product_title: LG : LSC27910ST 26.5 cu. ft. Side by Side Refrigerator - Stainless Steel
review_title: After searching and researching, I am very happy with this fridge.
review_text:
Note: I bought the black one, but I know most people prefer stainless steel, so I thought I would post this review for both fridges.

We are very happy with our fridge. It is huge on the inside, and very bright, and the shelves are sturdy and there is plenty of room to organize the fridge the way you like. The freezer is nice and roomy and the only thing I do not like are the 2 wire baskets at the bottom. I have a hard time pulling them out since items peek through the wire mesh and get caught with the items in the basket underneath or on top.

But the nicest feature is the fact that the ice maker is on the SIDE, on the freezer door. The only caveat is that you have to make sure not to place anything on the top shelf to block the connection to the side ice maker, but there is plenty of space on the top shelf, so it is not too big of a problem. According to manufacturer's specs, there is no more cubic feet in this model than the older one that had the ice maker inside the freezer (The model LG LSC27910SB and this one both have 10.24 cubic feet of space). However, I prefer have shelf space rather than a side drawer space. Plus, the pull-out ice bin on the side is really nifty and compact, and slides easily in. It is clear plastic so you can see how much ice is in it.

I also really like the tall dispenser. At first, I thought it was gimmicky until I had company and had to fill 2 pitchers of water several times through the evening. No tilting and trying to fit the pitcher under a short dispenser! It really is a nice feature. And if you have a fragile pitcher, there is a water button that you can use instead of pushing against the dispenser.

Finally, the digital display looks really cool. The numbers and symbols are this pretty blue color (not red, which would have been horrible), and after you get used to pressing the buttons to change the settings and not the display (for some reason, we kept doing this when trying to change the ice setting from crush to cube or vice versa), it is very handy. Aside from the forementioned button for Ice Type, there are buttons for setting the temps of your refrigerator (40 degrees for us-- at 38 degrees the juice froze) and freezer (0 degrees), a button for "Ice Plus", a feature that revs up the ice machine and makes more ice cubes faster (but don't forget to turn it off when you have enough ice!), and a button to change lock the display and deal with the alarm (an alarm can go off after 30 seconds to warn you you have left the door open). Also, the display of the temperatures is not the actual temperature of the fridge or freezer, which would have been really cool, but the settings.

The water dispenser requires a filter that the manufacturer recommends be replaced every 6 months, and they have a display with a monthly digital countdown for that! We have not decided whether we will replace it every 6 months, and if we do not, there is supposed to be a way to reset this timer so it won't bother you if you don't.

We bought the black one, and we love it. The handles are longer than the older model and look very sleek. The only odd thing about the black is that the doors are smooth black, the but the rest of the fridge is that textured black that fridges usually come in. At first, it drove me crazy, but now I do not notice it.

We are very, very happy with this fridge and would recommend it. We got it from our local big box hardware store (only one of the national stores carry it, the other does not carry LG), and we bought the extended warranty just in case. It was worth the $99 for 4 years of peace.

product_title: LG : LSC27910ST 26.5 cu. ft. Side by Side Refrigerator - Stainless Steel

review_title: Would give it 0 stars if I could

product_title: LG : LSC27910ST 26.5 cu. ft. Side by Side Refrigerator - Stainless Steel
review_text:

product_title: LG : LSC27910ST 26.5 cu. ft. Side by Side Refrigerator - Stainless Steel
review_text:
The fridge is great, does everything it is supposed to do, I don't have any complaints in that aspect.
My only issue was after changing the water filter inside the refrigerator, when getting water from the filtered water system, I had noticed what I thought to be an air leak since it was a hissing sound. I thought it maybe because of air entering the system after the filter change.
One day, I had gotten another glass of water, heard the his, but noticed a spray of water
coming from the back of the fridge. Keep in mind that this had been going on for about a month... When I pulled the fridge out, I noticed that the hardwood floor under the fridge was wet and beginning to turn black from mould. The water lines are made of plastic tubing and one of them had a small hole in it which caused the hissing noise.
I fixed this myself and replaced the flooring.
I was just surprised that with the amount of money this fridge cost, you would think that they could use something other than plastic tubing that's under pressure.
By the way, I also have their gas range, the over range microwave and dishwasher. I have absolutely no complaints with them...they work just fine.

product_title: LG : LSC27910ST 26.5 cu. ft. Side by Side Refrigerator - Stainless Steel
review_title: Stay away - finally replaced after 3.5 yrs
review_text:
This is the worst refrigerator I've ever owned. Purchased 3 1/2 yrs ago, and thought that the LG quality would be a good thing. In fact, as others have mentioned, the freezer simply does not freeze that well (ice cream was ALWAYS soft). The ice maker was a disaster. Constantly melting and refreezing then jamming. About 8 months ago the water service started delivering water at much lower volumes and the ice maker started making smaller cubes, indicating a low volume water delivery in the refrigerator. Tested the water supply from the home - very very good supply. Then, the refrigerator simply stopped making ice and delivering water. review_text: I purchased this model in black from HD two years ago. I loved the spaciousness, bright interior lighting, the deli drawer! and the bottom freezer. review_text: How this company stays in business is beyond me, far beyond. Our never-very-reliable-they-came-with-the-house washer and dryer finally collapsed under the weight of our laundry, it was time for a new set. Two weeks later Whirlpool delivered a dryer with a shattered door and a dent. Oops. Backorder, 2 more weeks and the glorious dryer sans broken door arrives! We installed it according to Whirlpools specs, admired how beautiful the pair looked side by side, and triumphantly shoved our first batch of accumulating dirty clothes in for a ride. And then, nothing. The dryer switched on, buzzed, whirred, the lights blinked on and off several times and, nothing. After my wife and I spent several hours bickering about the manual and 'you must of done something wrong' I called Whirlpool. The service tech agreed that something was indeed wrong, and dispatched service. Two weeks later service arrives and detirmines that we need 3 new parts for the never-been-used new Duet dryer. "I'll order these parts and be back on Tuesday". Did I mention the pile of dirty clothes threatening to crush my wife and I? This morning we received a call from service, one of the new parts we need for the never-been-used new dryer is on backorder until mid-August. Does anyone even sell clothespins anymore? The neighbors will be thrilled to see that hillbillies have moved into our yard when the clothesline goes up. Don't do it, don't drown in the Whirlpool, save yourself, save your money. If you purchase a Whirlpool dryer, don't forget to stop at the bank on your way home and pick up some rolls of quarters. Your going to need them for the local laundrymat. Bring a book to read and avoid eye contact with strangers. Thanks Whirlpool.

review_text:

If you are buying this machine for the "steamfresh" feature because like me you don't want to iron shirts that laid in the dryer too long--don't!

The cycle takes 20 mins to run, then it "fluffs" the clothes for 30 mins, then after removing them from the washer the manual says to allow the damp clothes to hang for 10 mins before wearing. ??? Now an hour has passed and you could've just ironed them or thrown them in the dryer would've done just as well! Not at all like the commercial!

My shirt came out too wet to wear (as it mentioned) and looked as if water had been squirted radomly on it. After all that, I ended up putting it in the dryer. The manual suggested you don't put 100% cotton clothes for the steamfresh either--which is exactly what i bought it for! (My husband's golf shirts)

As far as the steamwash feature--if you need your clothes shot full of hot steam because your clothes are unsanitary then you may need this. However, I used the steamwash today on hot water WITH bleach (I might add this cycle took 1 hr and 15 mins) and it still didn't get my socks clean!

It works fine to use as a regular washer, but my opinion is it isn't worth the extra $300 I paid full these extra features.

Also, the LG is very loud compared to the Whirlpool Duet. It has a loud whining sound when it gets ramped up. The first time I heard it I thought there was a motorcyle going by outside.

product_title: Whirlpool WTW6600SW Cabrio 4.5 Cu. Ft. Super Capacity Plus Washer
review_text:
I have been using my washer for almost 7 months. This is the precise model that I have, except mine is black. I have not had the problems others seem to have. It has only had an unbalanced load (UL) three times in that period, and each time, adjusting the clothes solved the problem. Below is the review I originally wrote for the machine, updated by these comments. It is still relevant in my case.

I will agree unconditionally that Whirlpool's customer service is CRAPPY. I tried contacting them several times (email and phone) for a part that I couldn't find for the matching dryer (to convert it from natural gas to LP gas) and NEVER got a response.

************************

November 10, 2006

This little wonder is as wonderful as Whirlpool ("WP") keeps insisting.

Now let me first say that every washing machine I have ever owned has been a WP - so there is some loyalty there. But bias aside, this machine delivers.

The 'space age' console that lit up like a Christmas tree was impressive enough, but WP added ease of operation. Use the pre-set wash cycles (turn the knob) or modify each to your liking (press the up and down buttons at each selection) - poetry in motion. One CAVEAT - I have not yet tried to programme a delayed wash, so I don't know how easy that is. The instructions in the manual seemed simple enough though.

LARGE TUB: The stainless steel tub is deceptively large. When I first looked in I noted the absence of the agitator but still I thought it wasn't as large as had been advertised. Then I put in what was in my old machine a "medium" load. My medium load became an extra small. What joy!

WATER SAVING: They do not lie! No more clothes swimming (pun) in water. This washer 'measures/weighs' the clothing (ain't technology wonderful?) and adds just enough water to the clothes to clean them. I was counting the savings (and apparently saving a tree in the Amazon) as I sat in fascination and watched my clothes wash. (Love the see through lid by the way).

CLEANING RESULTS: Clean the clothes it did. My whites were clean and fresh.

LOTS OF CYCLES: To suit every need. The BULKY ITEMS cycle is a gem.

LID LOCK: The lid locks as soon as you press the Start button. You can pause during any cycle by pressing the Pause/Cancel button once (twice will cancel the wash), then pressing Start to continue.

FEATURES: Too many to adequately expound on here. I love the THREE DISPENSERS - detergent (only high efficiency liquid or powder), liquid bleach and fabric softener. The end-of-cycle ALERT is indispensable and can be turned off, soft or loud. The machine is QUIET. Capital QUIET. Amazingly QUIET! (which is why you really need the end-of-cycle alert). The DRAIN AND SPIN cycle is great for those times when you start a wash and can't finish. The CLEAN MACHINE cycle - also a keeper.

The machine has a pleasing design and despite greater capacity and features, seems to take up less floor space than my older model washer.

I personally suggest using a surge suppressor with this washer simply because so many of the features are computerised and it is a large investment (would be a shame to watch it go down in flames).

I haven't had it long enough to comment on energy savings, but for every other reason cited above (and more), I fully recommend this washer.

review_text: I've had my Duet Sport pair for about a month and a half. So far, not any problems. I like that the dryer has a lot of options for drying. Before I purchased this pair, I read around and I thought the time of drying was supposed to be less, but this seems to take longer. But I don't really mind. I also like the Wrinkle Free Feature. It seems to help a little. Overall, pretty good!

product_title: Whirlpool WFW8500SR 3.6 Cu. Ft. Front-Loading Washer
review_text: This machine replaced a gwad awful Frigidaire that was less than 2 years old. So far, so good.  The Whirlpool can handle big loads and with the suspension system, vibration is minimual. Prior to this we had a machine that would literally rattle the windows. The only drawback is that "Whitest White" & "Sanitary" cycles are very long, 2 and 3 hour washes, and I would probabaly never use them for that reason. With the pre wash feature, I would like to be able to do it separately and then wash as opposed to having it wash in the same temp as the programmed load that follows the prewash. Other than that, it appears to be a great machine. It balances the load well and spins out most of the water / wetness. Something I find quirky, but not necessarily a nusiance is that when the door does latch is very loud.  I would highly recommend it.  I rated it 4 stars becasue of the pre wash feature.

product_title: Whirlpool WFW8500SR 3.6 Cu. Ft. Front-Loading Washer
review_title: Like MILDEW and spending $1,000 plus repeated tech calls?
review_text: I have had a Duet clothes washing unit for 4 years now (well before issues surfaced/where on the web, and with the price of this darn thing, who would have ever expected any issues to begin with.) The Duet was washing my delicates (expensive lingerie) in HOT (yes you read me right...can you say steam) H20 v. cold when just over a year old. The repairman came out and replaced the part that handles water temp. Now I've had the joy of experiencing mildew and funky smelling clothes. Likewise, as other posters mention, bleach doesnt work/get to the clothing intended. Went online, read about the issues, and much to my shagrin, I found my son's months old sock in the area between the bin and the door gasket (obviously the impetus and breeding ground for the mold all over my gasket.) Since not rinsing well, I have placed yet ANOTHER call into my repairman to see if perhaps another sock may be still be elsewhere in the unit blocking H20 flow for rinsing. Ultimately, I wish I had bought an LG or a Maytag. I will NEVER buy Whirlpool products again. Our 4 y/o Gold series dishwasher has been serviced 5 times since it was bought new with our house! The tech told me that Whirlpool KNEW the heating element was defective in our dishwasher and sold the units anyway (with the hopes that the part would last out the warranty period.) Additionally, our 4 y/o range has spillage down between the glass panels on the door which would indicate that it was not sealed properly. POOR quality control, POOR design. Lastly, dont waste your money on the optional base storage for this washer like I did...you see, Whirlpool's industrial designers apparently went to a two year online tech course school as they didn't bother to take into account standard sized laundry product containers when designing this base piece and thus, the unit is TOO SHORT to allow such containers to stand vertically/erect (which means you must lay things on their sides, risk spillage/fight to get things out). In short, expensive doesnt always equate into a better product. HEY WHIRLPOOL, MY SPOUSE IS AVAILABLE IF YOU WANT SOMEONE TO DESIGN A WELL THOUGHT OUT PRODUCT (he has a real I.D. and Masters degree) v. JUST AN AESTHECTICALLY PLEASING ONE!

product_title: Frigidaire 24 in. Gas Single Wall Oven – Black
review_title: I had this installed since it fit my 30 year ...
review_text: I had this installed since it fit my 30 year old unit and it fit well.  but the oven heated unevenly requiring some baked items to be rotated while baking  and in the 3 years I've had it repairs have been needed twice to the burner system.

product_title: Haier HLP20E Pulsator Stainless Steel Washer
review_text: I spent $40 a month in quarters at the laundry and I thought this could save some money. It did and it is okay. I gave it to my brother to use at college after I moved and got a full size washer and dryer. You have to be careful not to put too much in it goes off balance- my brother did it all the time. Also a little detergent goes a long way. The only other draw back can get annoying. It tends to tangle and twist the clothes together. For some reason the end of cycle is marked with a Jingle Bells tune that this washer plays. You will forever associate Jingle Bells with laundry after using this washer.

product_title: Haier HLP20E Pulsator Stainless Steel Washer
review_text: I've had this washer for a couple of years now and I would buy another.  The only problems I've had were due to my own negligence of not securing the drain hose.  -- There's quite a bit of water in there! -- This machine is reliable, compact, energy efficient and a pleasure to use. There's no agitator mechanism to wear on your clothes and linens. The clothes are agitated by jets of pulsating water.  The lint trap is a small bit of genius.  You will want to use something to filter the end of the drain hose though (as stated in a prior review - good idea!) or the sink itself.  If you hate the laundromat and have a little bit of space for this and a drying rack, your good to go. Highly recommended.

product_title: Haier HLP20E Pulsator Stainless Steel Washer
review_title: It does the job right and saves money
review_text:
I bought an used one and used it about 10 times a month. After 3 years, it still works like new.
I tested with a Kill-a-watt and found it costs about 0.13 KWH to run a full cycle which means the cost is less then $0.02 per cycle. It also doesn't need lots of detergent.

product_title: Haier HLP20E Pulsator Stainless Steel Washer
review_text: I bought this washer in 2006 (it's Jan. 2014 now) and have used it for all of my laundry (clothing, sheets, and towels).  It washes everything well, spins very dry, is gentle to my clothes, and is quiet.  Never overload it, place clothes loosely, add low-suds liquid detergent with a tablespoon measuring spoon, and be ready to occasionally redistribute clothes evenly for the spin cycle.  I wouldn't hesitate to buy another--  if I ever need one!

product_title: LG : DLGX7188WM SteamDryer Series 27 Front-Load Gas Dryer - White
review_text: Ok it never drys my clothes all the way the first time, even on the highest settings... for the $ I expect this dryer to work. It can't save energy if I have to use it 3 times per load. My cheap POS worked better and my clothes were warm and dry when I opened that one. Buyer beware, this dryer SUCKS!

product_title: LG : DLGX7188WM SteamDryer Series 27 Front-Load Gas Dryer - White
review_title: This dryer has almost never worked.
review_text: This product has failed to dry our clothes or get hot at all for half of the time we have owned it.  It will work for a month or two and then stop working for a month or two.  We had LG come and try to fix it when it was under warranty, but then it quit working 2 months later and they will not honor the fact that this was an 'ongoing' problem.  Imagine a $1000 machine that does not do its primary function half the time.  I will never buy another Lucky Goldstar product again!

product_title: LG LRBC20512WW LRBC20512WW Bottom-Freezer Refrigerator
review_text: Ours has been great! Love the bottom freezer! We have had it for 3 years without a single problem.

product_title: Whirlpool? WED5600SQ Super Capacity Plus Electric Dryer : White
review_text: Whirlpool has a terrible lint filters!!!! When you clean them it gets lint dust all over the top of your dryer. I hate my dryer because of it.

product_title: Frigidaire AEQ7000EE AEQ7000EE Front Load Dryer
review_text: I purchased this dryer with the matching washing machine and I couldn't be more disappointed.  It doesn't dry clothes very well and most times takes two cycles.  Clothes come out wrinkled and damp.  I have tried different settings and options and nothing improves its dismal performance.  The washing machine is not any better, actually, maybe worse!!

product_title: Frigidaire FTF530FS 2.65 Cu. Ft. DOE (3.1 Cu. Ft. IEC) Front Load Washer - White
review_text:
After I moved into my New apt. and had to pay for my water for 1st time I decided to buy a Brand New Washer & Dryer set,at the time I had a little X-tra money and seeing I was going to be on a Fixed Income now that it might be a good idea,washers & Dryers usually last at least 10 years or so and it was an Energy Star,save more money and being a single mom this was good.
Well things went well for awhile the washer cleaned well and spun so much water out they took no time at all to dry esp. in my New Matching Dryer,then one day I goto check my wash and find my Basement is Flooded & water is Comming out the Front Door of this Washer,so I run to shut it off,and clean up the water that I have to Pay for,then we try again and yep it still is leaking out and I end up having to call a Repair Guy,he comes and finds the problem but doesn't carry the needed part but charges me about 60.00,I order the part & Install myself to save a few bucks and it works fine,for awhile anyway...
A few months latter Again we have the Flow of Water out the Front Door of the washer but no real reason for it,and again I have to clean up water all over the Basement & then it seems to be fine and working.So a few months latter I throw in a load of laundry and when it was done I went to get it,well I can't seem to get the Washer Door Open and Nothing I did would get it to Open it's holding my wash Hostage and I was SO MAD Now What? I looked,I fiddled,I even called my electrician friend to see if he could by pass a switch or something but Nope that didn't work & I just didn't have the money to get the repair guy over again so I left the wash in there,either that or I break the door to get my wash & I allready wasted enough I felt,thank goodness I still had my old washer to use.
Not long after washer Nightmare I went to dry my wash and the Dryer was making a Horrible noise,so I look around inside mabey it's change or something,Nope,I was afraid to use it,it sounded that Bad.So after going to the laundromat a few times I said this is Stupid,so I went & took the Dryer apart to see if I could see anything,well let me warn you if U ever need to look inside yours be Carfull it's Super Sharp inside,guess they couldn't bother to grind the sharp edges,my son ran & got me a couple Band-Aids & I kept going,I didn't see anything wrong and put it all back together,the noise isn't as bad as before so I'm just gonna keep using it as long as I can unless I find a new affordable set.
I only used the "Set" for around 2 years & Less before I started having problems with Washer.
When they say it's Energy Efficient there Not Lying esp. when the washer uses No Electricity when it's Not Plugged In/Working & Great on Water esp. when it's no longer hooked-up!!
I wish I had the X-Tra 400.00 for extended Warranty but I could've bought a brand new one for that much.

For Sale Energy King,Queen: Broken Fairly New Washer/Dryer Set,Excellent on Water & Elect. Kidding....

product_title: Frigidaire FTF530FS 2.65 Cu. Ft. DOE (3.1 Cu. Ft. IEC) Front Load Washer - White
review_text: I bought this washer about 3 years ago. At that time I told the salesman that I wanted a washer that would do a good job and that would last.  Well, it does get the clothes clean but it recently developed a very loud roaring sound when spinning the clothes.  The repairman says it's a problem with the bearings.  Cost to fix it would be around $600 which is about the price I paid for it in the first place!  I emailed the company and of course it's not covered by the warranty after this long and they didn't offer to try and resolve the problem with me.  I'm very disappointed and would not buy this product again.

product_title: Frigidaire FTF530FS 2.65 Cu. Ft. DOE (3.1 Cu. Ft. IEC) Front Load Washer - White
review_text:
When we bought our condo this wash was part of the package, everything was ok for about 18 months and then a distinct odor started, a foul smell of mold. I thought we left a load in for too long and rewashed -nope the smell has been getting worse and worse. I started fishing around and discovered the rubber gasket or seal on the door and the metal "Sleeve" the gasket fits in - hold water! Close the door, you now have a dark airtight home for standing water - honestly, how did they miss this one? In their defense, some internet search reveals many, many front loaders have this issue - and the workarounds are ridiculous - "leave the door open always", "run a bleach load once a week", "clean the gasket after every use by hand", "use expensive anti-mold pucks" and more "Might help . . ."

Wow. This is washing machine and it has standing, moldy water in it all times, yuck.

product_title: Frigidaire FTF530FS 2.65 Cu. Ft. DOE (3.1 Cu. Ft. IEC) Front Load Washer - White
review_title: Great Value in a front load washer
review_text:
I've had this about 3 years. Bought it used with matching gas dryer. Not one problem. Great value for the price.

i wish the door was a little larger as it is a little difficult taking clothes out.

This definately uses a lot less hot water and gets clothes real clean.

As with all front load washers, if you don't use frequently the washer can have a musty odor as there is a little water retained in the drum. fix.. leave the door open, or use less softner, or there is a special chemical you can run thru to cleanse it out. I have just used clorox.

I'd buy again. Good value.

BTW i recommend the gas dryer to match. I have them stacked and they work well.

product_title: Frigidaire FTF530FS 2.65 Cu. Ft. DOE (3.1 Cu. Ft. IEC) Front Load Washer - White
review_text:
This review will be short and sweet. I've had this for a few years now, and it has been almost perfect. There was once an issue with the door latch (which may explain one person's complaint on leakage) and the repair was easy for the mechanically inclined.

The unit is not loud at all when washing clothes. But the 600 RPM spin cycle sure creates a whine! However, this washer is way quieter than a regular old top load.

You can add more clothes to the load, by stopping it first (push timer knob), wait a few seconds and then open the door. The water level does not exceed the gasket height. However, if you try to add more clothes while it is filling, wait at least 10 seconds between stopping the timer and opening the door.

The door opening is smaller than expected, which makes getting large items in and out a little difficult.

I also have the matching dryer. Love the set. The dryer has the lint filter very conveniently in the front and it also has an interior light.

Except for the door latch repair, this unit has been flawless.

Water and electricity consumption are definitely lower.

And yes, all front loaders require you to run an empty bleach load through once in a while. I find that the normal cycle of bleaching my whites does the trick.

product_title: Frigidaire FTF530FS 2.65 Cu. Ft. DOE (3.1 Cu. Ft. IEC) Front Load Washer - White
review_title: First one lasted 12 years with no problems, hoping for good luck with #2
review_text: In March 1999 we bought a Frigidaire Gallery stackable washer & dryer.  The washer just recently conked out on us - the bearings or struts or something like that broke off and the drum no longer rotates correctly.  I'm a little disappointed because I think 12 years isn't a very good lifespan for an appliance, but after doing some internet research, it appears 10 years is the average for a washer, so I guess I should appreciate that we apparently got 2 extra years out of it.  Our model number for the now defunct 12-year old washer is Frigidaire 417.39012890, but it looks the same as this Frigidiare  FTF530FS model (minus the blue highlights around the knobs).  Since we were happy with what we had, we're going the same route again and getting this FTF530FS from our local appliance dealer, even though it appears that most of the people posting reviews here haven't had good experiences with this model.

product_title: Frigidaire FTF530FS 2.65 Cu. Ft. DOE (3.1 Cu. Ft. IEC) Front Load Washer - White
review_text: I bought this washer and dryer set about a year ago. At first it was amazing - not only cute but cleaned well. After about a week though I noticed that my clothes didn't smell great after washing them. In fact, they didn't smell like they were even washed. I went online and found out that there are tons of people having similar issues with this brand. There are even class actions being taken. Not litigious in nature I have found that there are things to do such as using a hot water bleach cycle once a week to clean the drum, however, I find this rather wasteful and disappointing to have to use such measures on a brand new machine. I'm sorry I bought it. Otherwise it works fine...its just that the point of a washer is to actually get the clothes to look and smell clean.... not like mildew.

product_title: Frigidaire FTF530FS 2.65 Cu. Ft. DOE (3.1 Cu. Ft. IEC) Front Load Washer - White
review_text: We bought this same washer sold by GE. I was shocked today when the repair man said it was made by Frigidaire. Not only does a Company like GE. take it's jobs overseas, but it farms out it's appliances to other companies. Long story short, top load is the best, preferably an older top load without the 1/2 tub rinse cycle. All of these water restrictions have made these companies produce inferior products. This machine lasted 5 years to the day. Now I am told the pump and the bearings are shot. More than $600. to repair. According to Amazon, I can get this same piece of crap new for $29 more dollars. And talk about conservation, I will throw this machine away and buy another hunk of metal and plastic again in five years. That leaves us with a very full landfill, and Fridgedaire with full pockets! Take home lesson as told to us by the repair man, if you must buy this crappy machine BUY THE EXTENDED WARRANTY!

product_title: Frigidaire FTF530FS 2.65 Cu. Ft. DOE (3.1 Cu. Ft. IEC) Front Load Washer - White
review_text: My husband bought this washing machine (and matching dryer) as a surprise for me to replace my 15 year old top-loading machine.  He bought it at H&H Gregg.  The machine began to have problems after one month.  It started with the drum not spinning.  After fighting with H&H they covered the $300 + repair fee.  Since then we have replace the door latch - twice.  No warranty coverage.  Just replaced the draining pump.  $320.  No warranty coverage.  And was told the hinge on the door will need to be replaced soon.  The door must be left open between washings to prevent nasty things from happening.  I'm about to throw in the towel and buy an inexpensive top loader - 15 years and NOT ONE SERVICE CALL.

product_title: Frigidaire FTF530FS 2.65 Cu. Ft. DOE (3.1 Cu. Ft. IEC) Front Load Washer - White
review_text:
I noticed the very first time I used this machine that my clothes were smelling badly even when using bleach and liquid fabric softner. So I would re-wash the clothes and they still smelled badly. Then I dedided to watch the machine go through its cycles and found that if I put in a full load of clothes that they weren't even getting completely wet. So I tried a very small amount of clothes like two t shirts and they came out clean and smell free.
Determination, the amount of water to fill the drum is so small that the clothes dont wash at all and the rinse cycles were even worse with not applying enough water. Thats why they smell. They dont wash and they dont rinse with enough water. I have to get rid of this machine. In the mean time I fill the wash cycle with a garden hose then when complete I fill the machine at the start of the wash cycle as a rinse cycle with the garden hose and my clothes are clean and smell free. But that is two complete wash cycles to get my clothes clean. Or maybe someone can tell me how to increase the fill limit of the machine so it will work properly.

product_title: Frigidaire FTF530FS 2.65 Cu. Ft. DOE (3.1 Cu. Ft. IEC) Front Load Washer - White
review_text: This is the second FTF530FS we have  purchased and shame on us.  They both broke conveniently right after the the extended service protection agreement ended.  While the machine worked well, it is not durable.  Our first one, the basket broke and had we not been home, it would have been a disaster.  The second one, the timer broke.  Happening once, it is understandable, twice, shame on me.  Fridgidaire lost a customer for life.

product_title: Frigidaire FTF530FS 2.65 Cu. Ft. DOE (3.1 Cu. Ft. IEC) Front Load Washer - White
review_title: Two I've had die at 5 years old.
review_text: I had two of these. I bought the second one because I bought a stand for the first one and didn't want to spend $200 on a stand for a new model.  They both had the drum bearings go soon after the warranty expired. I'd say they have a life of about 5 years.  Otherwise, I didn't have problems.  We're only two people and if you had a big family this would have died after 2 years.

product_title: Frigidaire FTF530FS 2.65 Cu. Ft. DOE (3.1 Cu. Ft. IEC) Front Load Washer - White
review_title: 9 years and not worth the price to fix.
review_text: I bought this washer in Nov 2007, it stopped draining so I figured it was clogged. Had the repairman take apart the hose at the bottom of the machine. All this sediment was in there. We cleaned it out and it started working again. But it started making this noise. Then the spin cycle was obviously off center and the sediment came out all over the clothing. I would not recommend this washer besides being too small for more than 1 person's clothing and towels to clean. I got 9 years out of it for about $50 a year. This time around I'm purchasing a bigger washer and never a Frigidaire. Customer service doesn't even answer! Just can't believe my parents' washer and dryer both lasted 20 years. They don't make 'em like they used to.

product_title: Frigidaire FTF530FS 2.65 Cu. Ft. DOE (3.1 Cu. Ft. IEC) Front Load Washer - White
review_text: I had this washer now for about 22 years, one of the first over built washers, only issue , overloading. And pocket crap getting into the discharge pump . Not the crap they made after that. .he stays away from modern front loads . disposable box store junk.

product_title: Frigidaire Gallery Series GLEQ2152EE 27 Front-Load Electric Dryer - Black
review_title: Dries well, but destroys your clothes
review_text: We've had our dryer for about two years...like the other reviewer, we've had lots of trouble with the door trim catching buttons and our kids' overalls.  I was a little slow to catch on...my husband's dress shirts continually lost buttons, and my bras were mangled, but I didn't make the connection until I found a whole row of buttons, snaps, and hooks stuck in the door trim!!!  As for the drying, it dries fast and the clothes come out looking great...IF they don't have buttons to eat!  We got a fantastic deal on the pair (floor model clearances...less than half the list price), so I guess that sewing a button on now and then isn't too bad of a trade-off.

product_title: Frigidaire Gallery Series GLEQ2152EE 27 Front-Load Electric Dryer - Black
review_title: If I could rate it ZERO stars, I would!
review_text:
Let me start by saying that because of my experience, I will never again buy ANYTHING with the Frigidaire or Electrolux name attached to it. NEVER. I bought my dryer a couple of years ago, and thought that only a one year warranty was a little shoddy, but never did I expect that the control panels in these dryers are like self-destructing "screw the customer" systems! The dryer started beeping one day while not even turned on, and displaying error code E68, the code for a stuck button. There are no buttons stuck, and upon researching it a bit, I found hundreds of other people online with the same exact problem. The control panel shorts out after 2-3 years and will cause the dryer to think a button is being held down and won't run. Nothing is wrong with the mechanics, it's all just this stupid electronic panel. As I, and the hundreds of other people with these dryers, have found out, Frigidaire absolutely refuses to replace the faulty control panel unless you pay ~$200.00 plus the cost of a service person to come put it in if you don't know how to do it yourself!

They KNOW that they are selling dryers with defective control panels, yet hide behind their wimpy one year warranty as a way to milk a ton of extra cash out of their customers. Where is the recall, Frigidaire??? Hopefully the Better Business Bureau will care to urge them toward resolving this. In the meantime, I recommend that you DO NOT BUY THIS DRYER, OR ANY OTHER FRIGIDAIRE PRODUCT! THEY ARE SCAM ARTISTS!!!

product_title: Frigidaire Gallery Series GLEQ2152EE 27 Front-Load Electric Dryer - Black
review_text: Replacing the motor is 3/4 the cost of a new machine.  6 years seems lucky compared to some.  I have the matching gallery series washing machine and had error code issues and breakage during moving that were dissapointing.

product_title: Frigidaire Gallery Series GLEQ2152EE 27 Front-Load Electric Dryer - Black

product_title: Frigidaire Gallery Series GLEQ2152EE 27 Front-Load Electric Dryer - Black
review_title: No more Frigidaire dryers for me

product_title: Frigidaire Gallery Series GLEQ2152EE 27 Front-Load Electric Dryer - Black
review_title: Frigidiare front load washer and dryer

review_title: Good washer at a very good price

product_title: GE GTS18GCSBB 18.2 cu. Ft. Top-Freezer Refrigerator - Black
review_title: Repairs have already exceeded cost of fridge
review_text: We bought this fridge in 2006 and in the last 6 months have had two repairs, one to the defrost control, and one to the icemaker totaling over $500.  That's as much as the fridge cost.  Unacceptable.

product_title: Haier HC125FVS - 125-Can Beverage Center, Black
review_text: I shopped for several different brands and models of beverage centers in this price range and initially bought a Whirpool model from Lowe's. I was very disappointed in the uneven cooling as the unit had the thermostat sensor mounted on the bottom side. This wasn't acceptable and certainly seems a design flaw in the Whirpool.Therefore, the bottom would cool to around 42, but the top was 55 degrees! Be careful as it seems that some of these units are actually better intended for wine coolers than canned drinks since they don't cool as much as a refrigerator. All that seems to differ in some of those units is the type of racks for cans or wine bottles. I returned the Whirpool and got the Haier at Sams Club and can't believe the difference. It's made like a regular compact refrigerator but with more interior space. The thermostat is mechanical rather than digital so it is seems much better. review_text:
Initially I really loved this washer. It uses hardly any water and is very efficient. However, after a couple months of use, I started getting a mold/mildew smell in the washer drum and in my clothes. The smell won't go away no matter what I do. I have tried using bleach, vinegar, Affresh (manufacturer suggested product), etc. and nothing helps.

I've also tried wiping down the door after each use and also leaving the washer door and detergent tray open to dry out. Nothing gets rid of the smell. I use hot water on most loads and don't use fabric softener (I don't like it). I leave the washer door completely open in spite of the eyesore it caused sticking out into our main hallway. I do not use a lot of the HE detergent either.

Apparently this mold/mildew issue is a common complaint among owners of front-loading washers and there are several class action lawsuits out there for various manufacturers because of this issue. I've also heard from family members that the smell is worse down South because of all the heat and humidity they get in the summer. I heard about a class action lawsuit for LG washers (and other manufacturers) and signed up. I'm sick of the smell.

It's a great washer--if you want to live with the mold and mildew smell in your house and in your clothes. A top of the line washer SHOULD NOT have a major problem like this. Buyer beware!

product_title: LG : WM2016CW 27 Front Load Washer
review_text:
I have had this unit for 2 years now. It replaced the ubiquitous Electrolux/Frigidaire/Kenmore basic washer which didnt hold up well and had to be replaced at 9 years.

I like the electronic controls. The end-of-cycle bell could be louder (whereas my old E/F/K was so loud I would go to another room and close the door to avoid being near it when it went off). It washes well. Plenty of settings to chose from. I L-O-V-E the very high speed spin; the clothes come out almost dry. It takes about 1 hour for a permanent-press (almost all I ever use) wash cycle, but then it only takes 15 minutes in the dryer (which costs a --LOT-- more per minute to run so a huge net energy savings) to finish the load, so its all good.

I like that it has a sump drain/cleanout panel in the front in order to remove wayward pocket stuff. I dissolved 2 pennies and a nickle for 2 years in the pump of my E/F/K unit because you had to take it apart to get stuff out of the pump once it got in there.

I like the direct drive motor, which (should) last a long time and need little maintenance compared to a traditional "motor off to one side and power transferred by a belt" construction. It is pretty quiet even in high speed mode.

If I have one complaint, it would be that this unit can never make up its mind when enough water is let in. Instead of just opening the water intake valve and letting it run until enough water triggers a "shutoff switch" [like every other washer I have ever seen], this unit makes a meal out of it. Open Close. Open Close. Open Close. Open Close. Oooooooooopen Close. Open Close. Open Close. Open Close. Enough already! Heaven help you if you try to take a shower at the same time! It probably takes 5-7 minutes to get the water in, and considering frontloaders dont use anywhere near as much water as toploaders that is inexplicable to me. [stipulated that if you have a full load it is reasonable to have to add water 1 or 2 times early in the wash as the clothes soak it up - but this is probably 30 cycles or more!] Plus I am afraid it will wear out too quickly (or worse yet burst the inlet lines and soak my basement) with that perpetual banging open and closed on the water valve.

People [primarily those who've never actually used one] complain about it being "hard to empty" a frontloader but I find it easier to roll wet clothes out of the front of a frontloader than to have to reach way down inside a toploader and have to lift wet clothes out from around that big Maypole thingy in the middle. Additionally, I have a small stool that I sit on when loading/unloading the unit. Plus its fun to watch a frontloader run; try and get entertainment out of a toploader!

product_title: LG : WM2016CW 27 Front Load Washer
review_text:
We got this washer 21 months ago from Best Buy. It worked well at first and we were impressed with it, despite severe vibration during spin cycle (yes, it's properly leveled).
FIRST PROBLEM: Within 3-4 months time, a severe mildewy smell was becoming more and more evident, even though we would leave the machine open to dry after every use. It made our laundry room and our clothes smell. Cleaning and bleaching around the rubber gasket did not help. After doing TONS of research, I learned 2 things that fixed this problem: 1) don't use liquid detergents, they help form a sludge layer in unreachable internal parts of the machine. Use only powder ("he" type, of course. Sears makes several good ones). and 2) You must occasionally use Oxi-Clean mixed in with your detergent. The active ingredient dissolves that sludge layer which grows the mold and mildew. The same ingredient is contained in dishwasher detergent powders and some hot tub cleaners, but the oxi-clean is easier and is designed for washing machines. We had to run our machine empty with hot water and oxi-clean for about 10 loads straight before the smell went away.
SECOND PROBLEM: 21 months after purchasing the machine, the machine stopped draining the water out and we were getting error messages. Manually draining the machine and cleaning the drain filter, as per the manual and LG's customer service from India, did not help.(By the way- very poor design for draining the machine. There is a small rubber hose which is all the way down at floor level. The only way to drain it is to keep a small shallow pan under the hose, and constantly carry it away, empty it, and bring the pan back and fill it up again. It takes forever.)It turns out the drain pump was bad, a $325 repair, no longer covered by LG's 12 month warranty. The authorized LG repair person says that he replaces a lot of these and always tries to keep some on his truck. Luckily, our extended warranty coverage through our credit card should reimburse us, but this is very poor performance. You should get much more than 21 months of service before needing a repair that costs half as much as the machine itself.

My advice- STAY AWAY FROM THIS MACHINE! I would not buy another LG washing machine.

review_text: I didn’t buy this washer, but it came with the house we bought so I've owned it for a little over a year. I believe it is a 2009 model based on some manufacturer's labels on the inside but unsure of when it was purchased new.  Overall, I’m satisfied with its performance. When we moved in, the washer did have the mildew smell that I just couldn’t get rid of, even after a few "cleaning cycles" w/ bleach and/or baking soda.  A few months ago it started making these bad grinding noises and emitting a burnt plastic smell when spin cycling.  Me being a DYI'er, I decided to take it apart to see what the matter was.  The machine is fairly simple to disassemble, however to get to the common failure mode the machine has to be pretty much completely disassembled. The metal drum is enclosed in a water tight plastic two part tub and is mounting on the rear to a cast aluminum mount called the "spider".  This aluminum spider mount is internal to the plastic tub enclosure therefore is in contact w/ the water/detergent.  Without delving into the science of it... hot water, detergent and aluminum (especially cast aluminum) isn't long lasting.  This metal part eventually degrades and brakes.  This will cause the drum to become off balanced loaded and spin cycling, and will rub on the plastic tub (hence burnt plastic smell).  If left too long, drum will wear a hole in tub and cost you more to replace.  All in all, a new spider was ~$60, I installed new seals while it was apart ~$20, and a new silicone rubber boot (at door) for ~$80.  Hopefully I'll get a few more years out of this machine.  Lastly, ALWAYS keep the door open when not in use to that the insides can air dry.  If not, you're creating a great environment for mildew growth and accelerated corrosion (of spider).

product_title: Frigidaire King Size 3.5 Cu. Feet Front Loader Washer - Frigidaire ATF6000FS
review_title: Happy, with a couple minor issues
review_text:
I've had the Frigidaire Affinity pair for about 4 months now. Overall, they are nice and I have been quite happy with them. They do a great job at cleaning. And it holds more laundry than I expected. Plus it's nice that both cycles are about the same length. That's very convenient if you are doing several loads. And considering the very high RPMs of the washer, I was very surprised how quiet it runs. But it might not be the same for if you don't have a solid floor.

However it does have a few issues worth mentioning.

The most significant is that the washer door has begun to sag. It needs to be lifted in order to close smoothly. This could just be an adjustment. Will be calling the shop today.

The another thing, and this may be inherent to all front loaders, but it tends to leave a little water and soap in the gasket at the front of the washer. The instructions do recommend leaving the door open to allow it to air out. Not a big deal, but as a former top load user, it was surprising to see some residual water there.

And the last thing is that there are too many options for my taste. That's just a personal preference though. And that is also probably true of most new washers these days. For some that may be a plus. But for me, it's just one more manual to read.

Overall though, if you have a solid place to put it, it's a very nice upgrade. And I have seen a nice difference in both water and energy bills.

product_title: Frigidaire King Size 3.5 Cu. Feet Front Loader Washer - Frigidaire ATF6000FS
review_text:
We were going to open up some space in a crowded washroom by replacing our functional, yet oldish side-by-side, top load washer and dryer. This model was strongly recommended in several reviews of stackable front-loading sets, as well as the sales folks at Lowe's. In not more than a month or so, the rubber gasket was covered in mold and mildew stains and the washer had that characteristic odor. We scrubbed and scrubbed with bleach and formulated mold/mildew remover. It is impossible to get all off.

Now, we both are having problems with allergic reactions that bloom occassionally if we don't scrub this thing regularly to fight back the spore-producing mold.

It's a giant pain to constantly have to deal with this, not to mention the labor involved. For something that was supposedly designed to be more energy efficient, I think it fails here as well. The only tips I've gotten from sales and support folks is to weekly run empty, hot loads with a mold preventer. I'm wondering if that 50+ hot loads were included in the efficiency rating...I doubt it. Not to mention the additional expenditure to purchase this "specially formulated" mildew prevention detergent.

(We also experienced problems with the electrical panel of the dryer which went on the fritz after just 4 months - it was replaced. The technician says "it's pretty common". This did not reassure us.)

Do yourself a favor and stick with efficient top-loaders if you can. From what I have been reading, this problem is not unique to this model in the front-loading washer field. However, if you have to buy a front-loader, do a LOT of due diligence before making your significant purchase...

...And do yourself a favor. Skip this model or set completely.

product_title: Frigidaire King Size 3.5 Cu. Feet Front Loader Washer - Frigidaire ATF6000FS
review_text:
If it is possible to hate an inanimate object, I hate this machine. I've had it for a bit over three years, and I initially liked it. I knew that I needed to leave the door open between uses to prevent mildew problems. It didn't use much water and seemed efficient. I accidentally left the door closed just *once* and it had already developed that mildewy smell after only a couple of days. You are not supposed to leave the door open if you have small children, to prevent accidents. So it seems that people with children are doomed to have a stinky, mildewed washer.

Worse, after about two years of use, it gradually left the clothes wetter and wetter. The information that came with the machine offered no help, at least none that was relevant. I researched online and found that other people had problems with a filter that needed cleaning. A filter - you would think the product guide would tell you about it and that it would be easy to clean. But nooooo...my husband had to take the machine out of the laundry room so he could get to the side/back (I don't remember which, but it was definitely not the front) and there was not even an access door to get to the filter. It was a royal PIA to clean. This is for routine maintenance! If I had not found other owners' help online, I would have had to call a repair person, which would have been expensive, I'm sure. For a filter! The display that shows the time remaining before the load is finished lies. And usually by several minutes.

It doesn't clean especially well either. I've tried several different HE detergents and used prewash treatments, and still have stains that should come out relatively easily. My clothes sometimes smell bad, worse than before washing them, to the extent that I will not wear them without re-washing and hoping they come out better the next time.

I sent an email to the company when I first encountered the filter problem, and got no response.

The only reason I gave the washer two stars instead of one is because it hasn't completely broken down; it keeps working albeit poorly. Sometimes I wish it would break down and I could justify getting a decent washer.

product_title: Haier HC125FVS - 125-Can Beverage Center, Black
review_text: I shopped for several different brands and models of beverage centers in this price range and initially bought a Whirpool model from Lowe's. This wasn't acceptable and certainly seems a design flaw in the Whirpool.Therefore, the bottom would cool to around 42, but the top was 55 degrees! Be careful as it seems that some of these units are actually better intended for wine coolers than canned drinks since they don't cool as much as a refrigerator. All that seems to differ in some of those units is the type of racks for cans or wine bottles. I returned the Whirpool and got the Haier at Sams Club and can't believe the difference. It's made like a regular compact refrigerator but with more interior space. The thermostat is mechanical rather than digital so it is seems much better. Also the sensor is mounted in the top where it should be. The unit is cooling great and staying around 34-40 degrees fully loaded with it set on 6. The coolest setting is 7. At that temperature, it is safe to use as an extra refrigerator if you don't have many cans. The shelving is also handy with two that have flip tops to allow taller bottle placement. I couldn't be happier with this center. Please note the description below doesn't seem accurate and may be referring to a wine cooler or smaller beverage center. The unit weighs around 77 pounds.

product_title: Haier HC125FVS - 125-Can Beverage Center, Black
review_title: Does not deliver promises and NO auto-defrost
review_text:
I am extremely disappointed in this refrigerator/beverage center, HC125FVS. I purchased it at a local "big-name" store. Firstly, the drinks on the top shelf never got really cold, and the temperatures varied greatly from one shelf to the next. I have 4 thermometers, and this is what the temperature degree results were at for the 7th (coldest setting) - 6th setting (2nd coldest):
Top: 45-55
3rd: 40-45
2nd: 35-40
small bottom shelf: 30-35

There was an ongoing variance of 5 degrees per shelf. Also keep in mind that the average refrigerator should be at 35-40 degrees MAX.

I called Haier and the agent told me that 125 cans is the maximum and they do not recommend filling the center to capacity to allow the air to flow freely. (Then why advertise it as a 125-can center???) I had it only about 2/3 full of cans anyway, and there is no fan in the unit to circulate the air, so how can the air flow freely? No wonder there is such a temperature variance. (Go figure.) I decided to hold onto it for a little while longer to see if I did get any satisfaction out of it. (The only thing that made me really happy was that it freed up a lot of precious space in my main refrigerator.) So, I held onto it for a few more weeks.

The straw that broke the camel's back is that it is also advertised on the box to have auto-defrost. After I had it for about 2 months, it developed a thick layer of frost, and it never auto-defrosted. The manual made no mention of the auto-defrost and how it is supposed to work. So, I called Haier America and asked why it had not defrosted yet. I spoke with two different agents and both told me that they did not see auto-defrost as one of the options on this refrigerator. (Go figure, again.)

Oh, one more thing. This center was constantly running. Although it has been a hot summer, my electric bills have never been above $190 in all the years that I have lived in this house. I was shocked when my electric bill went from $170 one month to $260 the next month after the first use of this center. My next electric bill should be coming soon, and I am bracing myself. Although I cannot say 100% sure that this center contributed greatly to the big jump in my bill, but when I turned it off, my electric meter's wheel slowed down quite a bit.

It is going back to the store this weekend. Thank goodness I can return it after 2 months to my local store...

Well, I hope you find this review helpful.

P.S. I just ordered a Danby Designer 4.4 Cu ft compact refrigerator that it is Energy Star rated. I have seen great feedback (4.63 stars out of 5)on the Danby from over 40 reviews, and I have my fingers crossed that it works better. It's also 0.4 cu ft bigger than the Haier...

UPDATE: After I stopped using this beverage center, my electric bill went back down to normal levels on my October 2008 bill. I got the Danby, and I am so much happier with the Danby. Its auto-defrost works and it is energy efficient, which is the opposite of this Haier.

UPDATE 7/9/09: It's the following summer, and I still love the Danby. My electric bills are still at their usual levels of $170-$190. Therefore, I am convinced the Haier is the reason for the jump in my bill last year. As I previously mentioned, the Haier was running constantly.

review_title: Not cold enough for sodas, tea, juice or water!
review_text:
What a disappointment ! It just doesn't get cold enough.

We did everything the reviews say to do. We left the unit sitting upright for 48 hours before plugging it in so that any oil or whatever can drain back (in the event the shippers did not keep it upright since it should not be tipped over.)

Then, we plugged it in and set it at medium cool with only a couple of bottles of water and a coke inside and left it alone for 48 hours. But the drinks weren't cold enough so we turned it up to max cold and didn't open the door for 24 hour so it could do its thing. Still no good!

24 hours later, the top shelf was almost 50 degrees, middle shelf was 43 degrees. YUK! Not cold enough for cokes & beer. We didn't bother checking the bottom shelf temperature because we need more room than just the bottom shelf.

Also, the stores and the Haier website do NOT list the specs correctly. This unit is 32 3/4" tall--from floor to top of unit. We've seen the height listed on different websites as anywhere from 34" to 35" but not one got it correct.

If you only need it for wine, you might like this unit. Be we want our water, sodas, tea, and juice to be icy cold - not luke warm!

P.S. -- The manual and box say the unit is NOT to be used to store perishable food. Anybody know why?

product_title: LG : WM2233HW 27 XL Front-Load Washer - White
review_text:
Pros:
Efficient
Aesthetics
Good Cleaning

Cons:
Cycles are usually quite long
Too short to hide water lines, drain, and electric cord
Maintenance necessary to maintain proper function

Just received this washer and compatible dryer and am really pleased with it so far. Overall, it looks really nice and fits into a pretty compact space. The washer uses an extremely small amount of HE detergent and uses very little water.

The noise and overall vibration of these units is really low also. In the laundry room with the door shut, it is hard to know this unit is running unless standing directly outside of the door.

One key thing I learned about this piece of equipment is that there are four plugs that screw into the back of this device. When it is delivered, the delivery guy will remove them and admonish you that if you move the unit again, you have to reinsert the plugs. Keep this in mind if you plan on moving your unit to a different location.

As with all of the front load washers, regular maintenance is key to keeping it running smoothly and preventing mildew. I have found that wiping down the detergent tray and the inside of the unit with a paper towel after I am done using it helps to keep the excess water to a minimum. Also make sure to run it along the door seal as this area tends to retain water that can cause odors and potentially mold.

Overall, this is a pretty affordable unit from LG that has a lot of features to make washing your cloths enjoyable.

product_title: LG : WM2233HW 27 XL Front-Load Washer - White
review_text:
This is a great machine. Lots of flexibility . Rule 1 is RTFM (read the manual) . One of the reviewers notes that it has a bad smell. There's a self wash cycle for this. There are also a lot of other features in the manual.

What I really like about the machine is that it does the job. Wash comes out clean and well rinsed (second rinse).

One word of caution is that the fill cycle is constantly turning the water on and off. If your pipes are not property secured, undersized or the pressure is set high a "water hammer" and shaking pipes may occur. Reducing pressure or putting a hammer protector ( a vertical pipe section filled with air) should do the job.

The reason for the multiple bursts of water is to pre-treat the laundry for maximum cleaning.

The very pleasant two level done chime is a welcome relief from the cheap ring or silence of other washers.

Highly recommended.

review_text:
We remodeled an entire house last year with a complete new kitchen. As part of a package deal for being in a remodeled tour of homes, I was able to get the entire Bosch line of appliances for well-below MRSP. I had never had a gas range before, so I was not sure what to expect.

Since I am not a big cook, it's hard to compare this to what I did have - which was a flat-top glass electric range. What I do know is that I really love this oven/range. Some people have complained that the glass top is hard to clean - however, as a gas range - it's so easy to take off the iron burners and clean spills. I have had no issues cleaning grease, baked on spaghetti sauce, etc.. I have had to adjust to the heat of the flames - but that would be expected from any gas range.

The oven works great. I have used the probe several times to cook tenderloin and it's worked like a charm. I use the warming drawer at least 2-3 times a week and it's great at keeping my husband's meal warm and still edible when he gets home two hours after we've finished dinner.

I haven't had any trouble with the knobs - but I will be aware of that issue. They are plastic - but I didn't notice or feel like they looked cheap - maybe I'm not the appliance snob yet! ;)

So far, I would recommend this appliance. It has done everything it advertised.

The service tech and Bosch customer service both explain that the oven is vented through the panes of glass and smoke from cleaning can deposit. Bosch is unwilling to admit this is a huge design defect. The tech says he can clean the stain by removing the door and disassembling it for about $120. All Bosch ranges apparently have this design so I highly recommend staying away from all of them or at least get a guarantee this won't happen to you and that they will guarantee to replace the door forever if it does.

April 2014 update: I posted a question regarding my problem on Bosch's FaceBook page and received an immediate response from Bosch. He reviewed my pictures with his engineers and determined the glass was flawed when installed at the factory. Both the tech I had previously worked with as well as Bosch's own Customer Service rep had deceived me. A different service group was given direction to replace the glass under warranty.

review_title: Good range.  Works well but has a few quirks
review_text:
For all the important things, this stove/oven works very well. Heats up quickly, cooks evenly, looks good and seems well made. It also has a very nice and bright oven light. The quirks that made me downrate it one star are as follows:

1) The stainless rim that surrounds the cooktop looks nice and is sturdy, but is raised 1/8" above the cooktop level, making it annoyingly hard to sponge up all the debris that seems to accumulate on the stovetop.
2) There is only one large burner (the 3-way adjustable one) -- 2 seems a minimum a stovetop should have.
3) The control adjusting the 3-way burner is hard to set very precisely since the control knob can travel less than 1/3 of the circumference for each of the 3 burner size options. Instead of 9 marked settings (1->9) as is typical, on this burner, you have numbered marks at 1 and 9, and 3 unnumbered marks in between. In general, I think a separate switch allowing you to select the burner size is a better design.
4) Sometimes the off button is hard to get to activate. All the other controls work easily.
5) The designers felt it necessary to spend design cycles on building in a Sabbath setting. You've got to be kidding me.

As another buyer noted, the display light is red, not blue/green as displayed on Amazon's picture. We'd most likely buy again as the good features outweigh the annoyances.

it cleans ever so well, and you can watch your clothes tumble around on each other (no agitator to damage them).
i have never had any problems with it or its dryer counterpart. both possess easy-to-use displays and controls.

product_title: Bosch Nexxt 300 Series : WFMC2201UC 27 Front Load Washer - White
review_title: I'm sorry I ever bought this washing machine.
review_text:
I have had this washing machine for approximately 10 months. We first called in service to fix the problem of nothing happening when pressing the wash cycle button. It took service (2 separate companies) 7 visits to finally get the door, hinges, electronic panel replaced. Now it works most of the time - even the stop button, so now if I drop a sock, I can actually stop it and throw in the sock. Every once in a while it still won't start if the door isn't just perfect.

If you throw in a full load of men's long sleeve dress shirts, they are tied in knots, literally. You have to have a basket setting there all the time so that you can pull the whole load out, untie them, and then place them in the dryer. Blue jeans are just as bad.

One of the sales pitches we received was being able to cram the washer extra full and it could handle it. I've never done that. I still put in the same amount of clothes as my old washer. Their sales pitch is deceiving.

If you put a load on "Kids Care", expect it to take 2 hours, no matter how much you've put in there. I set of king size sheets (w/pillow cases) on hot water will take > 1 hour to wash - approximately 1.5 hours. Then if it spins out, you're lucky. It's frustrating to start a d

product_title: Bosch Nexxt 300 Series : WFMC2201UC 27 Front Load Washer - White
review_text: recently brought . runs quieter and clothes are cleaner than my old top-loader.easy operation.The most I like:does not have lots of functions to choose from.saves water.Buy it ,you will like it.

product_title: Bosch Nexxt 300 Series : WFMC2201UC 27 Front Load Washer - White
review_title: Scared by reviews, pleased with my Bosch.
review_text:
Pros: Overall, I'm very happy with performance on heavy duty cleaning, 1/2 the detergent, ease and very quiet. Plus I'm likely using about 1/10th of the water I was. (Really a 5 star but can't edit that)

Cons: fairly long cycles. Not a lot of options: cold, warm, hot then baby, delicate, heavy, 2nd rinse and bleach (which it adds later in the cycle for a better job cleaning). Could see it rocking on your floor if it's not solid (but we are built up on piers--not slab)

Usually research before buying, this time I did not. Got the washer home THEN read 2 bad reviews. So for the past 3 months have been expecting poor performance and/or a breakdown. Being a natural pessimist, I watched the laundry go around with what looked like almost no water and think "bah, bad design, my clothes will never get clean"

BUT my husband's filthy clothes got amazingly clean, much cleaner than with the old top loader. Expected wadding and twisting of clothes, neither happens. Despite being told in the instructions not to open the door during the cycle, I always stop the cycle and add clothes and the machine senses it and adds more water. So maybe the lack of options are compensated by the smartness of the machine. I'm sure there are lemons, but a good thing to bear in mind is that people who are pleased with a product tend to not review it. I mean, it does what it is supposed to do, right?

product_title: Bosch Nexxt 300 Series : WFMC2201UC 27 Front Load Washer - White
review_text:
We bought both the Bosch washer and dryer. My husband really wanted a front loading washer and a top of the line dryer to go with it. I had been very happy with my 25 year old washer and dryer that were totally reliable.
I gave in and we purchased these. I cannot even express how much I HATE the washer.
I am lucky if I can get a load finished and actually spun out so that I can put it in the dryer which usually does not finish drying and turns everything into one big lump of tangled laundry.
Right now I am on my third attempt to wash my duvet cover - it simply won't spin. I have re-started the load three times with different items in it so it can balance out. My laundry sink is now full of sopping wet items that I will need to re-start in hopefully the right proportions so it can get balanced.

DO NOT BUY THIS PRODUCT !!! If you really want one buy mine. I'll be happy to go look for an old Maytag that is totally reliable.

product_title: Bosch Nexxt 300 Series : WFMC2201UC 27 Front Load Washer - White
review_text:
Bosch Nexxt 300 Series Washer & Dryer
Pros: Good looks, quiet functioning, cleans clothing surprisingly well, low water usage.

Cons: Extremely long cycles for both washer and dryer. Is the trade off for water efficiency really worth the power it takes to run for an hour+/cycle for both washer and dryer unit (not to mention my time!)? There is no such thing as doing a quick load of laundry with this pair. Secondly, the max spin cycle can send it waltzing around the laundry room. A serviceman gave us four .50 rubber pads for the feet of the washer for a $40 service charge and they work with minor adjustments every several loads. Ugh. And lastly, and most significantly, there is a mildew odor to the machine that makes it the most offensive. I for one do not expect to clean or have someone clean my washing machine or to spend a dime on a product to eliminate mildew as was recommended by the serviceman. This is not the forever washer I had hoped to have upon ordering it and would never buy another front loader as the cons outweigh the pros. If you are doing your homework and reading this, good for you. I wish I had done so.

product_title: Bosch Nexxt 300 Series : WFMC2201UC 27 Front Load Washer - White
review_text:
Overall I'm pretty happy with it: it cleans stuff well and hasn't broken down (5 years and counting). I have the following gripes:

1. The door often requires a good push to shut properly, otherwise it doesn't lock.
2. The machine is supposed to adjust cleaning times based on load weight but I've not noticed it do this. Perhaps it does, I've not timed it.
3. If the load is unbalanced (e.g. when I stick in my bath mat) it sometimes won't spin because it detects an unbalanced load. Instead it tries to spin and repeatedly fails and so it can take a very long time for such loads to finish up.
4. The standard spin cycle isn't long enough. I have to manually make it spin a second time before the clothes are ready for the dryer.

Overall I'm happy with it. It's robust. It hasn't damaged my clothes. It cleans them well.

product_title: Bosch Nexxt 300 Series : WFMC2201UC 27 Front Load Washer - White
review_title: Five years, no major problems, efficient
review_text: After five years seeing code E02 coming up, but washer still works fine.  Cleaned out drain pump compartment, easy access, no tools required, just a rag and old toothbrush.  Pros: highly efficient, good clean, far fewer problems with the septic system since going to a front loader (family of 7, lots of water use.)  Cons: 1) Very low, need to raise it up.  Instead of $200 "Pedestal" I bought four cinder blocks and used a spare (very thick) peice of plywood with moulding around the edges to prevent slippage - it does shift slightly over time.  2) need to prop the door open with a rag to keep the gasket dry so it doesn't grow mold.  Helps to wipe door gasket out occasionally to prevent mold and grime buildup, not a big deal.  Cycle time can be unpredictable, but supposedly due to sensors and machine intelligence.  Normal cycle time starts out at 1:00, gets down to :50, then changes to 1:10.  Overall been a good machine. Switched from decades of loyalty to Sears/Whirlpool after getting really screwed by Sears.  Bought at Lowes, they delivered, installed, and took away the junk from Sears at no extra cost.  The 300 doesn't have the frills of more expensive machines, but has all the features you need to get your clothes clean.  "Kids Clean" cycle uses 150 degree water for tough jobs and sanitation.  The 300 series doesn't have 170 degree option if you really like your clothes cooked. If you like more bells and whistles, I understand another $500 could keep you happy.  If not, save the bucks and keep it simple.

product_title: Bosch Nexxt 300 Series : WFMC2201UC 27 Front Load Washer - White
review_text: This washer needs a baby sitter! The wash cycles are very long. (2hrs for 1 heavy duty load).There is no energy savings if you need 2 hrs for 1 load! The clothes come out smelly and partially dry unless I add additional water to the machine.I learned this after washing the first several loads of my young daughter's clothes. They still smelled of urine!!!  It is as if the computer cannot accurately gauge the correct water needs. I have had no success getting stains out, even with pre-treating clothes. Socks get trapped in the door well and have to be washed again. Sometimes the washer will alarm that the cycle is complete,  and the clothes are still saturated with water and need to be put on an additional spin cycle. Stay clear!

product_title: Bosch Nexxt 300 Series : WFMC2201UC 27 Front Load Washer - White
review_title: Worst appliances I have ever owned!
review_text:
Purchased a washer and dryer set in November of 2008. Dryer never dried correctly from day 1. Had the serviceman out 4 times for the same problem within 4 weeks. Bosch said I could not return the item since I had it past the return date. Told them it that's because the repairman had to come back 4 times to fix the problem and it still doesn't work right. They did not care. Luckily the manager at Lowe's said I could take it back to the store for a replacement. The replacement one works fine.

Now for the washer! I purchased the 4 year extended warranty. Came home last night, of course, 6 weeks after warranty ended to find my mud room flooded. Washing machine had stopped and was leaking out of the back somewhere. Pulled machine from wall and switched it to drain. Heard water pumping out. Then I switched it to spin. Drum would not turn. Took back off the machine figuring the belt had broken. Belt was good. So I took the soaking wet clothes out and restarted the machine. As the water filled the machine should agitate but it did not. Then I noticed water pouring out of the back again. Then I saw there was a crack in the plastic drum along the bottom and water was pouring out thru the split. The replacement drum housing and what ever is causing the drum not to spin will cost more than a new machine. So I will need to buy a new washer after 4 years and 6 weeks of use. Never have I had this many problems with any appliance manufacturer until a purchased a BOSCH product!!!! Lesson learned! NEVER AGAIN!!!!

product_title: Bosch Nexxt 300 Series : WFMC2201UC 27 Front Load Washer - White
review_text:
We purchased this washer in a set in 2004 and it still works great, for an 9 year old machine. It is still in one piece with no cracks, chunks of plastic falling off, no leaks, no stoppages, etc. For those of you worried about energy usage, watch your meter and compare the before usage against the running usage; you may surprised. Most washers are rated to last between 5 and 10 years and that rating still depends on machine care and treatment. When the time comes we'll be searching for another Bosch.

Pros:
1) It uses less water
2) It does an excellent of removing water from your clothes, which makes your drying time shorter.
3) It gets your clothes much cleaner.
4) It uses less detergent, softener, and bleach.
4) It is quieter.

Cons:
1) Balance. (this is mostly user error; loading done by my kids.) Sometimes the offset weight in the tub is loud for a few seconds when in a spin cycle. But, to be fair, that happens with most washers. (I've seen top load washers shake and jitter 2 feet away from its original spot.)

Bottom line: This machine is does as advertised. Treated with respect, care and general maintenance, this machine and any other will outlast the warranty.

product_title: Bosch Nexxt 300 Series : WFMC2201UC 27 Front Load Washer - White
