product_title: LG WM3431HW 24", 2.44 Cu. Ft. Washer/Dryer Combo (White)
review_text:
We got this a year ago after LOTSA research. To begin with, although widely advertised, nobody seems to actually have it for delivery. So we ended up ordering it 4 - yes, FOUR, times from Home Depot (yes, they will get it for you, you have to ask and insist...). Home Depot's computer automatically deletes orders not filled within a certain time. The item was always back-ordered, so our order was inadvertently deleted the first three times. We didn't even know it the first time, until I called to inquire about the delay. After told what the story was, I made sure we kept up calling and renewing the inquiry to keep the order in the computer. Finally, after 5 months and 3 weeks (not quite half a year, you see...), it finally arrived outside our door. Outside, because nobody wanted to put it inside and risk having to install. Which really amounts to: nobody wanted to read instructions. Just as well. There is nothing to the installation of this. Plug in, put hoses where the hoses of regular washer go. Done. For an added level of complication, we installed it under the counter in the kitchen where the dishwasher was. Steps: slide out dishwasher (you may need to take a pre step, to remove the 'shoe cover'. Big F deal...), discard. Unpack W/D; unscrew shipping screw (keeps drum secure during transport); unfold cord; insert hose in hole and other end in floor or faucet hole (sewer outlet); connect water hose or hoses (you can choose to use both C & H or only C and let the washer warm/boil the water - waste of time and electricity... I connected both cold and hot, helped that I had the same hookup with dishwasher); plug cord; slide W/D under counter. For aesthetics and stability: put shoe cover back. Done! Proceed to wash clothes!

It washes perfectly! Total euro style wash! Hadn't seen whites so white since grandma's last wash across the pond. It doesn't take any more time than the other washers, if you set it according to time. I don't follow the preset 'programs', I just set the temp, spin, etc. I want. Our washes take: 55 min for sheets and towels, 34 min for anything else.

We do the same for drying - just set the time. Otherwise the clothes dry awfully much. Best part, the clothes are a tad humid/not quite damp, when taken out, just enough to stretch and fold and eliminate need for ironing. You can leave the dryer working and go away. Regardless of how long you will be gone, the dryer will not stop and let clothes sit and wrinkle. After finishing its cycle, it will continue spinning the clothes every so often to keep them from 'setting'. When you are ready to take the clothes out, you have to press the button to release the latch. The machine will not allow you to open for as long as the steam/heat is at dangerous temperature levels. After about 3 min the key icon turns off and you can take the clothes out.

Washes require a little planning because clothes will need to air for a little bit before ready to be used. So if you only have one pair of sheets and expect to wash them before your girlfriend arrives, this unit is not for you. Sheets/towels need to air out a little after they are out of the dryer, before used or folded. We wash these items on a Saturday or Sunday morning to have plenty of time before they are needed in the evening. Because of this detail, not having anything way too dry, there has been no shrinkage of any clothing (think cashmere...) since we started washing in the LG. Which in and of itself is worth the entire price of this unit!!!

I have recommended this to anyone who asked - and will continue doing so without any reservation! Go ahead, buy it and enjoy it!

4 years later: I keep LOVIN' this machine, now have two of these - Read about the new one. Although the same model number, it is a bit different:

LG still has it, but they have changed the electronics a bit, without changing the instructions... We bought a second one for another apartment and didn't have a separate function for drying, so it seemed that we had to set the drying at the beginning of the wash and do it all in one scoop. I hated that because I wash all my clothes together (using 'Color Catcher' to avoid mishaps) but I hang and air dry most wearables, while I use the dryer for sheets, towels, etc.

After pouring over reviews and comments, I found out that you CAN run the DRYer SEPARATELY. Just set the washer on 'Rinse and Spin' and then turn off the 'Rinse' button. The machine will spin the clothes to remove any water first and then will start the drying cycle. Don't consider this an extra spin, as the older machine which has the functions separate, starts the drying with a good spin to get rid of the access water first.

10 Years later: The first washing machine (pictured here) developed a knotting sound when spinning, most likely a faulty/broken bearing in the main tub. This is a very expensive fix, (quoted $600) and not one under warranty. But the WD still works just fine, except it is to loud to have in the main house. I swapped the loud one from my kitchen and put in the guest house. Since it is programmable, can be set to work while nobody would be around. -- The second WD was bought in 2011, only 7 years young, and still quiet.

product_title: LG WM3431HW 24", 2.44 Cu. Ft. Washer/Dryer Combo (White)
review_text:
This is by far the worst washer or dryer I have ever seen, and I've seen my fair share when I was a poor college student traveling the world. A more accurate description of it would be a lint disperser and dampener. The wash function, while adequate at removing soil and stains, is somehow incapable of getting rid of those little bits of dust and hair that accumulate over a days wear. I will pull black shirts out and have to lint roll them before I can iron them. If you have pets, it has the unique ability to remove about half of the hair that gets tossed in the wash and store it just inside the rubber seal, creating a hairball that will randomly deposit itself into your laundry. As for the 'dryer' aspect, I think it would be quicker to just air dry your clothes. The dryer doesn't really dry them and I have yet to do a load that has not come out noticeably damp. As for that nice, warm, fresh, out-of-the-dryer feel, you can forget about it. All of my loads (even, miraculously, when I only washed a shirt and a pair of pants) come out wrinkled and knotted. It even managed to wrinkle some synthetic shirts that claimed to be wrinkle proof.

The icing on the cake is that the misery is not short lived, but takes 4-5 hours to do a single load.

product_title: LG WM3431HW 24", 2.44 Cu. Ft. Washer/Dryer Combo (White)
review_text:
This combo machine is an absolute last resort for anyone who does not have a way to vent a side by side or top/bottom combo machine.

PROS:
Looks good and will squeeze into most apartment or condo closets.
Has large timer display that counts down time left on cycle.
Uh - hmmm, that's about it for pros.

CONS:
Clothes will be damp at best for most loads. If you remove the clothes immediately while piping hot, the steam will dissipate and sheets or similar weighted items will dry if spread out. (I use a fan directed at the damp items to help finish off the drying process.) It is almost impossible to dry sweaters, towels and jeans. So, if you live in a climate where heavier clothes are the norm, you may want to take this into consideration.

Users will do better if they understand that you cannot employ the regular load washer/dryer mentality when using this machine. Mix the weight and size of the items - one sheet, two pillow cases, two bath towels and face cloths mixed in with a few gym socks or underwear.

It takes forever and a day to wash/dry one load. I've found that setting the cycle to wash and then opening the door even for a few minutes, THEN going back and starting the dry cycle cuts down the dry time considerably. Of course, this defeats the purpose of setting and forgetting a load to wash/dry un-tendered; but if you are a busy granny-nanny like me, it cuts down on hours of dry time. Plus, it's only an extra step and you still don't have to haul the load from the washer to the dryer in the process.

If you don't crack the door and let the moisture dissipate between loads, you may get this awful stench that is best remedied with a quick Chlorox rinse.

Lint accumulates around the rubber door seal and may re-deposit on the next load if not wiped down.

Our machine is less than two years old and has broken down completely once and at times will just shut down due to an uneven load, even with two equally weighted sheets. We will also get an arbitrary error message that can only be remedied by unplugging the machine or resetting the circuit.

Call me old fashioned, but I just can't be convinced that a few cups of water are able to get my grandson's cloth diapers cleaner than a couple of gallons in an energy efficient front loader or top loading machine.

product_title: LG WM3431HW 24", 2.44 Cu. Ft. Washer/Dryer Combo (White)
review_title: Great machine 5 years in- but do your homework before you buy!
review_text:
This unit has been the perfect solution for our situation: an urban couple in a tiny apartment (who absolutely HATE the laundry-mat!!), with no basement access to setup a traditional washer /dryer pair.

Important note: if you like to dry all your clothes in the machine (i.e. not hang most of them up to air dry like us) you will NOT be happy with this condenser dryer. You can only dry a few items at a time, and it will take about an hour and a half. As well, the rubber gasket that seals the door will impart a slight odour to the dried items until it has been used a while. We don't use fabric softener or strong smelling detergent so your results may vary.

The last drawback is that it is pricey. However, we have owned it for 5 years, probably running it 5 days out of seven, and it has been rock solid, with only 1 self-repair needed. After 4 years of light use of the dryer function,the clothes started coming out damp. Googling the problem, I was able to easily take it apart and clean the accumulated lint out of the condenser tube with a long bottle washer (like a thick pipe cleaner). Voila- back to normal, and still perfect a year later.

Replacement parts seem to be reasonably priced from third party vendors to boot. If you're handy, you should be able to keep it running for a good long time.

product_title: LG WM3431HW 24", 2.44 Cu. Ft. Washer/Dryer Combo (White)
review_text:
This machine does not deserve even 1 star! I don't often write a scathing review, but after 3 years with this machine, it absolutely deserves it.

Let's talk about washing first - the LG designer that wrote the program for washing cycles has apparently never seen or used a washing machine before. The machine has all sorts of extra back-and-forth gyrations between cycles, and with fairly long pauses - enough so that it adds about 10 minutes to what should be the normal washing time. The drain pump is called for whether it's needed or not and this goes on constantly. But the absolute worst of the worst is the spin cycle. The machine will not do well at all with small loads, so don't even bother, but that's not the main issue. The machine cannot achieve any kind of a reasonable balance and makes several tries - the amount of time can exceed 20 minutes or even stop all together with a time-out error. In short, if the machine was a person, that person is terrified of spinning.

Next is doing the drying - the dryer spin does not tumble fast enough to remove wrinkles from permanent press stuff. There is no user accessible lint trap, so it gets trapped in the internal hot air ducts and eventually plugs them. These ducts need to be cleaned at least twice a year, otherwise it burns a hole into the composite plastic duct and the back half of the drum chamber, creating a severe fire hazard.

Fortunately, I purchased an extended warranty when I bought the machine. As of writing this review, repairs have exceeded the original price of the machine. Even the 10-year warrantied motor did not last more than 2 years before the bearings wore out. The front panel circuit has been replaced twice. The drum and drum chamber (2 halves) have been replaced. The most recent failure was the 110 VAC power supply filter and relay; it melted due to inadequate cooling and heat sinking. Currently, the pump sounds as if it is on its last legs. I only hope it goes out before my extended warranty ends because the machine has to be completely dismantled to replace it.

I bought this machine because I have always had good luck with LG appliances, and it truth, the quality of parts used in this machine is good. What destroys this machine is an extremely poor design. Washing and drying in the same unit calls for some pretty exotic design choices and are not met in this unit. The electronics need to be protected better from the intense internal heat generated during the drying cycle. As a matter of fact, it would be better to give up the condensation drying and just use a fan and heating element - the clothes might actually get dry.

At this point, you might be asking how much I use the machine - two medium-sized loads per week, and using the dryer on only one of them.

Do yourself a favor and pass on buying this machine - it is nothing but trouble due to poor design, especially considering its initial cost.

product_title: LG WM3431HW 24", 2.44 Cu. Ft. Washer/Dryer Combo (White)
review_title: I hate it. Oh. So. Much.
review_text:
I guess I was spoiled. I had a vented, separate washer and dryer machines at my last place. This stupid machine was here when I moved it and the last tenant had used it for a long time. It was broken right off the bat. The guy who came to fix it says he "sees these troubles all the time" with these machines. Since I didn't buy it, he didn't feel bad talking smack about the machines. He said it was a bad investment and people hate the.

The fan or something didn't work. It was worthless. 8 hours and damp clothes. Capacity examples: two towels, 3 t-shirts and 4 pairs of socks, one pair of jeans and some socks, one sheet (if you overfill it beyond the recommended dryer line), 1 hoodie and 2 hand towels. Now that it's "fixed" the the cool down cycle, where it's locked and the screen says "CD" is also hours long. I tried turning it off, unplugging it, and you cannot open it for hours after the stupid machine beeps and tell you that it's done. I don't know what the point of "ding"ing hours before the cool down will allow you to take the clothes out. "Ding ding!" Hooray! Oh, wait. Well, I guess I'll wash 2 more towels tomorrow. Maybe I'll be done with these 3 loads of traditional laundry by next month.

It gave it 2 stars because it's better than nothing. I'm glad I'm renting and don't have to pay for the repairs. If I had to pay for the repairs then - zero stars. Invest in installing a vent in your house. Call a contractor. Today. Then use the vent. If you have kids, do a favor to your future self's sanity and don't buy this.

review_title: No complaints on a great washer
review_text:
My wife and I bought this washer 3 months ago, along with its companion dryer the DLG5966g, for use in a new "kitchen laundry cubby" installation on a new ceramic tile floor. We had concerns about having a washer/dryer in our living area because of noise, but they have been totally unfounded. One room away from the living room and TV, we rarely even notice it working as it goes through its cycles. Our other concern was whether we would have problems with vibration and the washer wanting to "walk" during the extremely high speed spin cycle of these new front loaders. The first few loads put our minds to rest. Even at the highest spin speed the vibration is hardly noticeable. LG has done a great job engineering this unit. Note, however, that this washer needs to be on a solid floor (concrete or ceramic tile) to work properly. I wouldn't recommend installing it on a wood or laminate floor. We purchased the optional pedestals, which puts these at a great height for convenience and comfort. Built-in drawers, too. Very large capacity, and there are plenty of cycle choices and options, but not terribly complicated to operate. My wife says it does a much better job of cleaning the clothes than our old top loader, using much less water and HE detergent.

The only drawback so far is that a typical wash cycle takes about 90 minutes. If you're used to much less than that, and if it's a critical factor for you, consider another washer. We're not in that big of a hurry. It does have a "speed wash" cycle which can run a load through considerable faster if you find yourself in a hurry. My wife also uses the "extra rinse" option, which adds a few more minutes. Probably not necessary, but it's there if you want it.

The only reason that I didn't give this washer 5 stars is because we haven't owned it long enough to know if it will hold up well over the years. It's direct drive, which was one of the criteria that made me choose it over other models. I'm hoping that this will also add to the reliability. If it's continuing to work well in a few years then it definitely deserves a 5 star rating.

product_title: Whirlpool : WED9600TW Dryer
review_title: 6 loads in a day, no problem!
review_text:
When we replaced our washer and dryer units I had to work hard get what I wanted. Exceeding my husband expectations of cost was the difficult part but it turns out the Whirlpool Duet front loader washer (GHW9150) and matching dryer (GEW9250) was a great investment. Without being a slave to the laundry room, I can get six large loads done in a day. Being Energy Star certified, the Duet units are extremely efficiently even with large loads. And, the washer conserves water by automatically adjusting how much is needed for each load.

But the decision was not an easy one as some reviews about front loaders discussed concerns of mildew and extreme entanglement of clothing. By actually read the manuals since our purchase (April 2005) we haven't had a single problem or complaint.

every day reasons to love them

- quiet

- quick

- easily cleans/dries large loads

- from delicate to heavy duty, you are in control

green reasons to love them

- uses half the water needed by top loaders

- uses half the energy of traditional units

product_title: Whirlpool : WED9600TW Dryer
review_title: $800 to fix dryer after only 3 years of service
review_text: I spent $90 on the diagnosis, and now they want $776 more to fix this dryer.  User interface boards (electronics) have gone bad.  Heard "lots of problems with the Duets".  I just started shopping for a new dryer and now my washer needs to be repaired - only $300 to fix it - bad "valve" letting water in.  Water keeps coming in, so I guess $300 is cheaper than all new floors, but I think I am done with Whirlpool.

product_title: Whirlpool WTW6400SW Cabrio 4.5 Cu Ft Capacity Washer (White)
review_title: Have used mine for 6 months and LOVE it!
review_text: I purchased my Cabrio 6 months ago and have been very pleased with its performance.  My clothes come out VERY clean.  I have yet to encounter a stain I haven't been able to get out.  Blood, oil, tomato sauce all came out in the first wash when I pretreated with a little detergent and used the presoak option.  I feel I am saving a lot of money in detergent as well...a jug of Tide seems to last forever!  I almost purchased a front loader but am glad I went with the top loader.  I have not had any problems with items twisting or balling up in the washer.  The clear lid is fun as well.  This machine does make different noises, kind of like a flying saucer taking off, so I've definitely taken a peak inside to see what it is doing.  I would purchase this washer again!

product_title: Whirlpool WTW6400SW Cabrio 4.5 Cu Ft Capacity Washer (White)
review_text:
We purchased this washer, described as "innovative, efficient, energy-saving, etc." I will say that it does perform reasonably well. It gets one star only because Zero Stars are not available under Amazon's rating system - because of Whirlpool's abysmal service!

We had the washer about one month when we started receiving error messages. We contacted Whirlpool and a Whirlpool-authorized technician was dispatched with ONLY a four-day wait (giving an 8-hour window causing my wife to lose one day of work). When he arrived, he indicated that he could not fix it, because the machines were so NEW, that the circuit boards were not yet available because Whirlpool was holding them to manufacture the original machines. THERE WOULD BE A FOUR-WEEK WAIT Repeated calls and emails to Whirlpool resulted in sarcastic replies about how only a tiny percentage of machines ever have problems (of course, it you have one of those machines, then the problem rate is 100%)

After repeated calls to the Whirlpool Customer Loyalty Specialist Line, we received a response that the parts would be shipped overnight to our home and a technician would come as soon as the parts arrived.

THREE days later, the package arrived. When we called the Whirlpool service line, we were promised that a technician would arrive in additional three days hence. (Interestingly enough, the parts were shipped from the same facility in Pennsauken NJ that housed the service technicians.) When the technician tried in install it, he discovered that the package supposedly containing the circuit board and harness was missing -- surprise -- the circuit board!

I even wrote to Jeff Fettig, CEO of Whirlpool, in total desperation. I received a call back from the same Whirlpool Customer Loyalty Specialist who was so "helpful" the first time. She stridently asserted that any lemon laws did not apply at this time, as they had not yet cycled through the multiple attempts required under the law to fix the product. She further stated that Whirlpool would call or email us when the part was available -- they would no longer respond to calls or emails regarding the situation -- OF COURSE, WE COULD ALWAYS PURSUE LEGAL MEANS SHOULD WE SO CHOOSE.

After several additional weeks, the product was finally repaired. Total out-of-service time on a washing machine that was in my home for only four weeks??? FOUR WEEKS!!! You would think that Whirlpool would have at least something to compensate for the cost of Laundromat service.

As a side note, you may not know that Whirlpool owns other brands. If you purchase these, beware -- you may get that same Whirlpool Service.

The brand names are: Amana, Estate Home Appliances, Jenn-Air, Kitchen-Aid, Magic Chef, MAYTAG, and Roper Appliances.

[As many who read my reviews know, I rarely take the time to post bad reviews. However, there is a big difference between a product/company that is not my taste and a product/company that delivers poorly]

product_title: Whirlpool WTW6400SW Cabrio 4.5 Cu Ft Capacity Washer (White)
review_title: great while it works, but broken right after warranty ended
review_text: we have this machine at our beach house.  it was great while it worked ... was a real workhorse, doing large loads of pool towels, linens and lots of kids clothes every week.  clothes got pretty clean.  and then the mysterious F1 error popped up.  am waiting for the repairman but am not holding my breath.  i "get" the fact that washers break down, but this shouldn't happen within the first year or two.  will never buy another one of these.

product_title: Whirlpool WTW6400SW Cabrio 4.5 Cu Ft Capacity Washer (White)
review_title: Nothing but problems. Can't do a load of laundry ...
review_text: Nothing but problems.  Can't do a load of laundry without the UL code coming on. product_title: Whirlpool WTW6400SW Cabrio 4.5 Cu Ft Capacity Washer (White)
review_text: We have owned this washer for quite some time now.  The controller was replaced twice under warranty (labor not included!!).  I have also had to replace the bearing (had to buy a $100 tool).  I am getting an error F50 and carefully followed the service manual which told me to replace the rps sensor.  It did nothing. product_title: Whirlpool WTW6400SW Cabrio 4.5 Cu Ft Capacity Washer (White)
review_text:
Great when it worked 100%. Electronics failed miserably - cycles all screwed up.

product_title: Whirlpool : ET0MSRXTB Refrigerator
review_text: I installed this above-deck in a boat galley that was designed to use a standard apartment-sized refrigerator at the time it was built.  This one is a little narrower than the old one but only a few inches.  Any fridge should have adequate airflow around or over the coils on the back if it's going to be expected to work correctly and have a long life, especially if it's in a hot environment like a garage or a boat that sits unused with the fridge running but air conditioning off most days.  In the case of the boat, it had been built with fans that blow over the rear of the fridge and out a vent so expect to need the same thing if you put it in any enclosed space.  It doesn't seem too loud and it looks nice.  Time will tell if it lasts but it was a good price.

product_title: GE Profile : PGSS5NFXSS 24.9 cu. ft. French Door Refrigerator
review_title: right door can't be closed after left door
review_text:
Unfortunately, I bought this frig based only on a photo and description on the GE website for my new home.

The right door must be slammed if the left door is already closed or it will stick at two different points instead of closing. This is a design flaw that GE will not take responsibility for. I reported it within two weeks of moving in and have had three service techs look at it over a five week period (along with many calls to the useless GE service and consumer relations department) and all of them told me it can't be fixed because it is a design flaw, but GE will not come clean and let me return or exchange it.

Try it before you buy it or you will be stuck with it like me.

product_title: GE : GTS18FBSWW Refrigerator
review_text:
Very loud fan noise. The fan on this refrig. is about as loud as a bathroom exhaust fan. I've never heard a new refrig with such a loud fan. The draws don't slide real smoothly.
On the positive side, the shelves are good, lots of room inside for tall containers, and the price is good for basic (but noisy) refrigerator.

product_title: GE : GTS18FBSWW Refrigerator
review_text: We're all trying to save a buck these days.  Sometimes it's worth it, and sometimes, well . . . you buy a Hotpoint refrigerator.  Principle gripes are, first, that this fridge is NOISY.  Is it so loud that it's useless?  No, but it's louder than any refrigerator I have ever heard, and it's certainly annoying.  Another irritant is that when you close the refrigerator, the freezer pops open.  Finally, the crisper drawers are hard to open and close, and make a plastic-on-plastic squeak when you do so.  It seems to cool things adequately, but it in other respects it's a let down.

product_title: GE : GTS18FBSWW Refrigerator
review_text: We bought this as a garage frig about 2 years ago. The delivery men were super nice by the way. It works great. It is plain with no frills and that was what we needed. No ice maker means the freezer holds a lot. I store a lot of drinks in the bottom and have to be careful where I put cases of water and soda because the shelves can't take slamming things in there. They will fall. If you take your time....it holds all though and I do put a lot of strain on them. The door shelves are big...and I love that. The door won't close if something is sticking out too far and hits the door shelves and I don't always notice that.

product_title: GE Monogram 30 in. Convection Double Oven
review_title: Failing Temperature Probes -- twice in 1 year
review_text:
Moved into a new house with this oven already installed. GE said it was "over a year old" when I bought the house and out of warranty, so pay $350 for service ($99.95 for visit + parts & labor.) They replaced 2 temperature sensors. 10 months later, same problem. Parts have a 5 year warranty, but the labor is gonna get you.

Set the EMPTY oven to bake 375 degrees, and get 285, set to 435 and get to 375. Set to 500 degrees and get smoke everywhere, with a raw prime rib for company. Can't even cook a chicken properly in this oven.

Their "customer complaint line" offer was to sell me a replacement, similar model for about 60% off of regular price. For what is now about a 2 year old oven used about 3-5 times a month, you can imagine livid is not the right response. I am not ready to spend $1700 to have GE replace their defective product.

In the end, I am "settling" for replacement temperature probes next week, and will have to pay the $150-200 "discounted price" for a service call.

Am I not wrong to suggest that a $3600 to $3900 double oven should last 20 years when used 3-5x/month no questions asked?

My guess at this point -- use self-clean mode, and the temperature probe fails. I figure it will take me another 6 months to prove that.

product_title: Haier HNSE045 Refrigerator/Freezer, 4.5 Cubic Feet
review_text:
This refrigerator is the perfect mini-fridge!
This is bigger than the average mini-fridge, but it is small enough to store in small places. I have it in my bedroom.
It has two and a half shelves inside, and two mini-shelves on the door (one of which is fitted perfectly for a 2 liter bottle of soda).
The freezer is perfect, too. It keeps things frozen, unlike some other mini-fridges out there. It also comes with an ice cube tray. I have kept ice, ice cream, and Italian ice in the freezer, and they all stay frozen. I use dipping tobacco, and I also use the freezer to store my dip in to keep fresh. It is perfect. Keeps things frozen, and has a mini door so the food in the actual fridge doesn't get frozen. Works without any flaws.
Inside the fridge, there is a thermostat. It goes from 1-7 (I keep it on 7), and off. This way, if you are going away and have nothing in the fridge, just turn it off.
It has a nice, simple design. I have seen people give it bad reviews, but I have no clue why. It's perfect! If you are looking for a nice mini-fridge, this is the way to go! You won't be disappointed.

product_title: Electrolux EW30DF65GS 30" Dual-Fuel Freestanding Range with Wave-Touch Controls and Luxury-Glide Ove, Stainless Steel
review_text:

product_title: Electrolux EW27EW55GS Wave-Touch 27" Stainless Steel Electric Single Wall Oven - Convection
review_title: 2 years of use but now replacement for a small part- BEWARE!
review_text:
We've owned this oven for over 2 years and though its use is infrequent, it's a great oven which we enjoy using. However, one of the oven lights burned out and its replacement per Electrolux parts dept. means buying a much larger part which costs between 55-67 dollars. It's ridiculously expensive and wasteful to have to buy a larger part to simply change a burned-out bulb. Since the part shown as the replacement has wires, it would seem to require taking some of the oven body apart or have some special tools and skills- or... incur the additional expense of having an installer come over.
It took a lot of research to discover it's a 40 watt halogen bulb- impossible to find this info on the bulb itself, in the oven or in the literature provided or on the web.
We eventually found a 35 watt double loop, G9 base bulb to replace the faulty one, cost: about 10$ It works just fine for way less. (Be sure to handle the bulb with tissue paper or cloth and not with bare hands when installing it.)
We only hope the other oven parts don't go out and cause such a problem. It seems the company wants us to purchase unnecessarily costly replacement parts. Not good for our pockets or the environment.

product_title: Electrolux EW27EW55GS Wave-Touch 27" Stainless Steel Electric Single Wall Oven - Convection
review_title: RUN Do NOT WALK away from this oven
review_text: Had this oven only since Sept 09.  Bought because of supposed good quality; willing to pay a little more than standard.  We don't use it that often but do bake at least 1-2 month.  From the very beginning, I thought it baked items too quickly, often drying them out when they should have had several minutes more before being done.  Didn't matter if I used convection or not; same issue.  I simply adjusted cooking times down and that helped a bit.  Last few times, I noticed muffins that had burnt bottoms but only on one side of the tin; that shouldn't be.  I inspected the oven and saw what looked like an "S" shaped puddle on the bottom left hand side of my oven lining.  Made a mental note to clean it up when it cooled down but it disappeared.  So I turned the oven on empty and saw that it reappeared. Disappeared when it was cool.  Called repair/service to come out.  The lining is practically burnt through and warped because the element shorted out and is malfunctioning.  It was probably something that occurred during manufacturing.  Electrolux will not offer me more than 10% discount on a new liner.  I still have to pay for the new element which costs about the same as the liner.  With 2.5 estimated hours of labor, it will total $800.  So this was a waste of money; we paid over $2100 with tax and installation 3 years ago and now another $800. So it cost us $706 per year for the life of the oven.  The worst part is how Electrolux positions itself as a quality oven and it's cheaply made and won't last even 5 years.  If you HAVE to buy it, get the extended warranty and make sure it covers the element and liner.  The repair man told me that not only was this issue a fire hazard, it was an electrocution hazard as well. Kelly Ripa owes me a refund. Bad product, stay away.

product_title: Electrolux EW27EW55GS Wave-Touch 27" Stainless Steel Electric Single Wall Oven - Convection
review_text:
This oven is just bad, and horrible customer support makes the experience of owning it even worse. It was the most expensive appliance I purchased when I redid my kitchen two years ago. Most expensive by a fair penny. I expected to enjoy its high end features, despite not using the oven more than a few times per month.

After the 3rd time I used the meat probe (just over a year after buying the oven), the plastic insulation split where it attaches to the probe, completely exposing the wires inside. As an electrical engineer, I have always taken care not to flex wires in ways that strain them, and this probe was no exception. It was just poorly made with no strain relief, and I suspect that material and dimensions are under-designed for their function. After a painfully long process of reaching the right person and explaining that a premium brand like Electrolux can't possibly expect a probe to fail after 3 uses, the representative finally agreed to provide a replacement rather than charging me the ridiculous amount that I have since blocked from my memory. However, they would not just ship me the probe. They insisted on having a service technician come out to inspect the broken probe and give me a replacement. I offered to send them the defective probe for them to inspect before sending the replacement, but they declined. Hence, I was forced to miss a morning of work and Electrolux was forced to pay a third party service provider to visit my home. Poor economics on both sides of the equation.

Then, yesterday, I was cleaning the oven. It's now a bit over 2 years old, and I was running the self-clean for the 2nd time ever. About 1.5 hours into the cycle, I heard a big bang. The middle pane of glass in the oven door had shattered. When I called Electrolux, the representative explained that the glass exploded because the temperature got too hot for the glass. I explained that, since Electrolux designed the self-cleaning process (and doesn't enable users to set self-clean temperatures) and since Electrolux specifies the glass used in the oven door, the problem she described sounds like a design flaw on the part of Electrolux. The outcome of a lengthy call (with a little discussion interspersed with longer times on hold), Electrolux agreed to give me the $258 piece of replacement glass at no cost, but they will not provide a new door and they will not cover the cost of the service call to have a technician disassemble the door to replace the glass.

I have gone back and done some searches on shattering glass in Electrolux ovens. This is not an uncommon phenomenon. Given the marginal increase in cost to use a more robust piece of glass inside the door, it is unconsionable that Electrolux has chosen to let even a small % of it's customers be exposed to this problem. I was cutting up pineapple with a very sharp knife when the big 'bang' occurred. I jumped, and easily could have cut myself. Beyond that, I have read about peope whose exploded glass was not contained within the door and could have caused other injury. For a product in this price range, it is absurd that the manufacturer does not spend a few more dollars (or SEK) on materials and add few more dollars (or SEK) to the price and just insure that its customers will not be exposed to this problem.

I hope to be able to get the door repaired without some of the onerous delays I've read that other people experienced, and I hope to get many more years of use from this oven. However, I do not intend to ever run the self-clean again, and certainly do not expect to ever purchase another Electroux product.

Note: I bought this from a retailer other than Amazon, but since most of my reviews are on Amazon, I am placing this one here, as well.

product_title: Bosch WAS20160UCAxxis 2.2 Cu. Ft. White Stackable Front Load Washer - Energy Star

product_title: Bosch WAS20160UCAxxis 2.2 Cu. Ft. White Stackable Front Load Washer - Energy Star
review_title: Unsuitable for more than one person.
review_text:
I purchased a Bosch washer (model WAS20160UC) and dryer (model WTV76100US) set in December 2011. This is the experience I have had with the Bosch appliances. It is a vented dryer, not the condensation model. This review is mostly about the dryer.

Pros: Stylish (witch makes no difference since the dryer is so poor)

Cons: This dryer takes very long to dry even small loads. It will get warm but not hot. A Bosch technician measured the temperature of the dryer at 122 degrees Fahrenheit. But, he informed me that this was normal for this dryer. In one test; two bath towels, two hand towels, and one facial towel were washed in the washer and rinsed on maximum spin to remove as much of the water as possible. It took the dryer 1hr. 20 min. to dry the load. After many phone calls and 3 or 4 service calls, they replaced the dryer. It performed as poorly as the first. So, I called an electrician to really find out what was going on. With freshly washed towels in the dryer, he observed the dryer drawing 10 amps (about the maximim rating) for 15 to 20 seconds. Then it went down to 5 amps for about about 30 seconds (he described it as half heat) then down to room temperature air coming out of the exhaust for another couple minutes. It repeats this cycle. At no time does the dryer actually get hot enough to remove the moisture from the load. It mostly just uses ambiant temperature air to dry the clothes. If touch the clothes in the middle of the load, they mearly feel slightly warm. While it is not practical for most people to use a clothes line, I think it would be just as effective as this dryer.

The thing that bugs me the most about this whole debacle is this: Both Bosch and the appliance store had the attitude that I should just accept the poor performance because it is a European design. I heard many excuses defending an appliance that I truly believe they KNOW does not perform as it should.

If you buy a coffee maker, do you expect it to make coffee in about 15 minutes? If you buy a blender, do you expect it to blend what you put in it? Well, when you buy a DRYER, you kind of expect it to actively dry.

In fairness, this washer/dryer set may be suitable for a single person who does small loads of laundry. You can expect a small load to take 60 minutes to wash and 80 minutes to dry. So you are right around 3.5 to 4 hours for two small loads.

Update: The appliance store has taken back the Bosch washer and dryer. I have replaced them with a GE unitized washer/dryer (model GTUP240EWH) This dryer completely dried the same load in 30 minutes.

I hope this review is helpful for you.

product_title: Bosch WAS20160UCAxxis 2.2 Cu. Ft. White Stackable Front Load Washer - Energy Star
review_title: Buy a Whirlpool. this is adequate but slow, noisy, poor design
review_text:
This unit (with its "take forever to dry" 220V dryer) fits a tight closet, like in our one BR condo. Thats why we bought it. Its attractive. Those are its pluses. But beware: Its small size makes it suitable for very small loads only, like one set of sheets from the bed or a couple bath towels. The wash quality is adequate.

Cons: It takes a long while to do a load as it spends half its operating cycle time reversing directions. The operating manual is horribly written, poorly laid out, general to dozens of models, and yet the washer controls are cryptic at best - but you will figure it out after a while, mostly anyway. I am sure there are some special features that this engineer has yet to determine.

We have not had a mold problem yet, but the door seal promotes water retention and you have to dry it after each use (this is obvious) - Bosch needs to ask a college senior design group to redesign what their careless engineers cannot.

I cannot recommend this unit unless it is your only option (we had to have something to fit a 24 inch space). Then it is adequate performance, but expensive for what you get with high maintenance after each use. I prefer our old Whirlpool.

product_title: Bosch WAS20160UCAxxis 2.2 Cu. Ft. White Stackable Front Load Washer - Energy Star
review_text: The rubber seal is a mold factory.  Smelly.  We call service about every six months.  Junking it.  Today I opened the door and about three gallons of water poured out.  Not supposed to happen. Stay away.

product_title: Bosch WAS20160UCAxxis 2.2 Cu. Ft. White Stackable Front Load Washer - Energy Star
review_text:

product_title: Bosch WAS20160UCAxxis 2.2 Cu. Ft. White Stackable Front Load Washer - Energy Star
review_title: Worlds worst clothes washing machine EVER

product_title: Bosch WAS20160UCAxxis 2.2 Cu. Ft. White Stackable Front Load Washer - Energy Star
review_text: Like with all major purchases, I researched the heck out of this machine and its competitors. My biggest issue is the fact that I'm in a condo in a busy metro area, and there is simply no room for a full-sized washer (much to my chagrin).  I'd been using the original washer and dryer that came with the unit--which was built in 1989! I will say, to Whirlpool's credit, that both were still working great; it was just time to upgrade to something cleaner and more energy efficient, and hopefully with larger capacity.  This machine really fits the bill. My laundry comes out smelling much more fresh and simply feels cleaner.  I've followed the advice of other front-load owners and left the door and soap dispenser open after wash cycles to allow them air-dry, and have had no issues with the foul smell (probably mildew) that other owners have complained of with this type of unit. Its incredibly quiet, which in a small condo is a big deal! The wash cycle is fairly long (circa 1 hour), but that's not been an issue. The only thing I can't do is wash my comforters; I still have to take them to a friend's house, but I have yet to find a 24" washer that *can* handle an item that large. Highly recommended!

product_title: Bosch WAS20160UCAxxis 2.2 Cu. Ft. White Stackable Front Load Washer - Energy Star
review_text: I don't understand the bad reviews. I've had my washer/dryer for almost 4 years with ZERO problems. I did my research before buying and I learned that front loading washers with a rubber gasket need to be left open for a day so it will dry out and not get moldy. I don't find this to be an inconvenience at all. I can't comment on cycle time because I have not had a ton of washing machines to compare it to, but it seems reasonable to me. I don't do laundry when I'm in a rush so I guess I don't notice how long it takes. I think it's a great, efficient machine. I have the matching dryer and that works great for me, too.

product_title: Bosch WAS20160UCAxxis 2.2 Cu. Ft. White Stackable Front Load Washer - Energy Star
review_text: They cannot figure out how to control the mildew that traps in the gasket area. Do not get sucked in by the cute size - there is NO WAY to win this mildew battle. And it just gets worse with time. I have owned 4 front loaders, all with gaskets that are similar to this and none of the others have this problem. DO NOT TORTRUE YOURSLEF.

product_title: Bosch WAS20160UCAxxis 2.2 Cu. Ft. White Stackable Front Load Washer - Energy Star
review_title: There are better bangs for your buck
review_text:
I've had this for 4 years and use it weekly and its worked reliably so far. It runs all loads and all settings just fine. I leave the main door and the filler drawer open after use to let everything dry out. No mildew or any weird odors but that doesn't mean it doesn't exist...I just can't see or smell it. In fact, I actually had mildew developing in my old top-loader so its likely that this will eventually get it also.

I miss not being able to use liquid bleach on my whites. All my whites are now various shades of grey. The spin cycle sounds like a jet engine which I actually like but others may not.

This machine cost more than some of the other brands and honestly I don't see how this is any better or worse than those. I would definitely shop around for a different brand next time around based on value. While Bosch is nice it doesn't warrant the extra monies.

product_title: Bosch WAS20160UCAxxis 2.2 Cu. Ft. White Stackable Front Load Washer - Energy Star
review_title: Better than the other reviews would have you believe!
review_text:
We have has the Bosch under counter washer and dryer for 10 years. The motor just burned out on the washer and we are replacing it with another Bosch.

All of the complaints about the smell are due to user ignorance. We had the same problem. I tried every method and product to eliminate it and could not. Then I came across one suggestion on the Internet that worked 100%. We switched fom liquid Tide HE to powdered Tide HE and within two weeks the smell was completely gone and never returned.

I agree it does not clean as well as a full size machine.....find me one that is better!

product_title: Bosch WAS20160UCAxxis 2.2 Cu. Ft. White Stackable Front Load Washer - Energy Star
review_text: The absolute worst product I have ever purchased. We paid big money for the set and it cleans and drys our cloths like crap; their customer service SUCKS also. product_title: Bosch WAS20160UCAxxis 2.2 Cu. Ft. White Stackable Front Load Washer - Energy Star
review_text: I didn't buy this machine myself, this washing machine (and the corresponding dryer) came with the house I live in. product_title: Bosch WAS20160UCAxxis 2.2 Cu. Ft. White Stackable Front Load Washer - Energy Star

product_title: Bosch WAS20160UCAxxis 2.2 Cu. Ft. White Stackable Front Load Washer - Energy Star
review_title: Worst washing machine ever!  DO NOT BUY!!
review_text:

We also now dry out the rubber gasket around the door after each load, which lets old water collect underneath and rot, but this alone isn't enough to fix the smell problem. product_title: Bosch WAS20160UCAxxis 2.2 Cu. Ft. White Stackable Front Load Washer - Energy Star

product_title: Whirlpool Duet WGD9500TC 27" Gas Steam Dryer w/7.0 cu. ft. Capacity (Chesnut)
review_text: I purchased the Whirlpool duet steam washer and gas dryer and I wish more than anything that I had not.  since this is a review of the dryer, I will only discuss the dryer.  Pros: none.  Cons: it takes FOREVER to dry your laundry.  the features including the auto dry and wrinkle shield do not work. I often have to dry my clothes longer than an hour and half! Also, clothes come out twisted and wrinkled especially jeans and long pants.  I still can't figure out any benefit to the "steam cycle" it doesn't do anything different.  I used to have a pretty standard maytag washer and dryer, which worked much better.  this is expensive and not worth the price. I have had this dryer for 3 months and will try to see if I can at least exchange it for something else.  Also, I have not noticed any decrease in my gas bill, either. Trust me, I was hoping more than anything that it would be great, but it's not.  sorry.

product_title: LG : DLE2516W 27 Electric Dryer with 7.0 cu. ft. Capacity, 5 Dry Programs
review_text: this machine does dry my clothes fine.  the downside is that it seems a bit cheap in construction.  overall, i regret buying it somewhat because i might like a stacked washer and the LG front-loading washers (which would stack the easiest) are reported to have mold problems (consumer reports and piles of online stories, including lawsuits) and i'm very allergic to mold.  i would prefer a washer with exceptionally high water temperature (near boiling) and better drain design to ensure that mold can be better managed.  unfortunately, i didn't really think all that through before i bought this dryer.  oh well.

product_title: LG : DLE2516W 27 Electric Dryer with 7.0 cu. ft. Capacity, 5 Dry Programs
review_text: We bought this washer and dryer combo right as our first child was born. Right from the start the dryer never dried our clothes. Unfortunately, we were so busy with the baby that we never had it looked at while it was under warranty. My husband and myself have both taken it apart in moments of frustration but still the problem persists. It takes at least two (sometimes more) 60 minute cycles on medium to get the clothes dry. However, we have never had the mold problems that I have heard others talk about. I would NOT recommend LG.

product_title: LG : DLE2516W 27 Electric Dryer with 7.0 cu. ft. Capacity, 5 Dry Programs

product_title: LG : DLE2516W 27 Electric Dryer with 7.0 cu. ft. Capacity, 5 Dry Programs
review_text:
Never had a problem...actually at my moms house using dryer now...and typed model number in to see who might still sell it...being I need a pair at my home. Speaking of model dle2516w dryer and wm2016cw washer...although I saw reviews and the washer dryer combo that also has my eye.

product_title: LG : DLE2516W 27 Electric Dryer with 7.0 cu. ft. Capacity, 5 Dry Programs
review_text: I own this pair washer/dryer for almost 8 years. They both work great and do the job wonderfully. I love smaller capacity as I do smaller loads, and these two are hardworking small horses. Kudos to LG!

product_title: Electrolux EW30ES65GSWave-Touch 30" Stainless Steel Electric Slide-In Smoothtop Range - Convection
review_text:
This is a dream of a range. The most beautiful, most versatile. Double oven. A perfect broiler while you bake french bread in the lower oven. The Perfect Turkey cooking setting roast a perfect chicken. I am looking forward for thanksgiving turkey.

The look is luxurious and the features are very easy to master. In this my first week I have used it quite a bit. Boiling water for pasta is a flash. I paired it with a 400CFM Bosch range hood.

I had the opportunity to get a new townhouse that had no refrigerator - got the 26' SS Electrolux fridge - kicked out the ugly white GE profile T-O-L range and microwave.

I am the happiest man. If you enjoy cooking this is the best. It matches premium gas cooking

product_title: Electrolux EW30ES65GSWave-Touch 30" Stainless Steel Electric Slide-In Smoothtop Range - Convection
review_text: I purchased this stove because I loved the features, racks and double oven.  However, I should have taken my time and looked at an "induction" cook top and stove as separate pieces.  I purchased this for 2599 and could have done beter buying an induction top and wall stove.  My parents have a ge cooktop which is easy to clean.  I am very careful with products and marked this cooktop the first week I had it. After taking the time to read the matierial on how to care for your cook top.  They sent cerama brye cleaner with this which i used to remove water from my mashed potatoes overflowing and it left a permanent fog mark on the cooktop. (after trying soapy water)  Then the numbers on my clock and digital tempature display starting to fade.  I called the customer service department and advised I used there cleaning products and it marked the top and the clock numbers are not fully displaying.  They sent me the two new parts and I am having an installer put them in next week.  I'm not happy that this needs to be replaced so soon.  I'm a very "worried" consumer of this stove and would not recommend it.

product_title: Electrolux EW30ES65GSWave-Touch 30" Stainless Steel Electric Slide-In Smoothtop Range - Convection
review_title: So far its like unbelievably COOL !!!!!!
review_text:
I bought the store display modal for $1100 with a full one year P & L warranty and so far after the first few days everything is absolutely A-OK. But so far, I have only used the burners a few times BUT HEY so far, so good. Some of the reviews have made me a bit apprehensive but at that price with FULL WARRANTY I am willing to give it a go. Richard

PS ... my first Electrolux vacuum lasted me 25 years without a single flaw and my current Electrolux vacuum is going on 18 years now and flawless !!! So Electrolux has a GREAT HISTORY of making quality products as far as I am concerned.

product_title: Electrolux EW30ES65GSWave-Touch 30" Stainless Steel Electric Slide-In Smoothtop Range - Convection
review_text: I purchased this oven over three months ago for my newly built home.  I love my oven.  It has a great design, lots of very cool features like dehydrate and perfect turkey options.  My favorite is the built in thermometer, I no longer have to guess if or when my meats are done, with a touch of the button it shows me on the screen what temperature my meat is.  I would have to disagree with the previous reviews that the ceramic top is not hard to clean compare to any other ceramic top.  Yes it takes me about 3 minutes after each cooking to scrub it good and I am a messy cook... and when I mean scrubs I mean I cook with oils, butter, wine, spilled water/milk, bacon grease cooked on and all. I would recommend anyone who purchases this item to read the instruction manual from front to back, FULLY, and follow all cleaning/maintenance instructions, it will save you from damaging the cook top by using inappropriate cleaning agents as well as save you headaches from guessing the operating instruction... After all this oven is highly sophisticated in technology and not your grandmother's oven. Only complaint that I have is the bottom over drawer does take a while to heat up, however, if you are like who uses both oven a couple time a year, it shouldn't be a problem.

product_title: Electrolux EW30ES65GSWave-Touch 30" Stainless Steel Electric Slide-In Smoothtop Range - Convection
review_text:
I was very pleased with this range and oven for about six months. However, the rubber seal around the ceramic top started coming loose and falling apart. I have an extended warranty at Lowes and the man who came out to look at the top said that it would not cover the repair as it was considered a "cosmetic" problem. After numerous tries to get a hold of Electrolux I finally got hold of someone through e-mail and they more or less told me it was my problem because I had a contract with Lowes. I asked them where I could get the rubber seal repair kit from so I could repair myself but never heard another thing from them.

I would not recommend this to anyone, especially given the amount of money it costs. To have things fall apart after less than a year is very disappointing.

product_title: Electrolux EW30ES65GSWave-Touch 30" Stainless Steel Electric Slide-In Smoothtop Range - Convection
review_text: We purchased this range just under 3 years ago.  I loved the design and looks....not a reason to buy...go for less things to go bad...old school from here on out.  From the start we had issues with the bottom drawer locking shot when in use...not great if you are trying to get something out before it burns.  Now the entire circuit board is gone in the range.  We did not get the extended warranty and now we cannot use the range.  It has an E15 error code.  The oven works, but you would have to listen to the continuous beeping of the E15 code while using.  Our certified Electrolux guy came out today and said the part is $428 plus the service call of $69.99 and then another charge to install this part.  There is no guarantee it won't happen again.  I can spend the money on the repair by a certified Electrolux technician and then purchase a $400+ warranty from Electrolux to get another 3 years of coverage...then what?  DO NOT BUY THIS RANGE...Very disappointed and it will be my LAST ELECTROLUX appliance.

product_title: Electrolux EW30ES65GSWave-Touch 30" Stainless Steel Electric Slide-In Smoothtop Range - Convection
review_text:
I've had this range for a couple of months now, and I haven't used the oven feature much, so I'm not comment on that.
I've really wanted a gas stove, but my kitchen didn't have the gas input and the space for the range was smaller than normal, so I ended up with this range as pretty much the default.

The range top is pretty hard to clean. I've had electric range before, and it used to wipe clean pretty easily unless there was burnt food. I need to clean this range with the ceramic range cleaner every day, and even then it doesn't seem to get completely clean. It's a little hard to reach the back cooking elements, and when I lean over to reach it, sometimes I end up touching the control panel and turning on or off other elements.

I'm also pretty limited to the type of cookware that I can use on the range. I've had to throw away a few of the cookware that I've used on my other electric range because it leaves marks on this one.

Although I haven't had any major problems with it yet, I don't really like the design of the range.

product_title: Electrolux EW30ES65GSWave-Touch 30" Stainless Steel Electric Slide-In Smoothtop Range - Convection
review_title: I would not buy it again

product_title: Electrolux EW30ES65GSWave-Touch 30" Stainless Steel Electric Slide-In Smoothtop Range - Convection
review_text:

I have liked this range, but it is not old enough to be this unreliable. For this price, you should receive higher quality.

Not recommended.

product_title: Electrolux EW30ES65GSWave-Touch 30" Stainless Steel Electric Slide-In Smoothtop Range - Convection
review_text: Wow.  Really?  Bought this in June 2011 for just over $2000.  Now, 3 yrs and 3 months later, after intermittent problems the whole time I've had it, we have repeated E15 error codes and is DOA.  Costs about $750 to repair with parts and service calls and no guarantee it won't recur.  Read the reviews online.  It will recur.  It's the components and the design.  I'll replace the range.  Should have lasted a lot longer.  Won't purchase any other Electrolux products.  Not ever.

product_title: Electrolux EW30ES65GSWave-Touch 30" Stainless Steel Electric Slide-In Smoothtop Range - Convection
review_title: We've had ours for three years and it's been great for cooking and baking
review_text: We've had ours for three years and it's been great for cooking and baking. Induction is pretty amazing. We do get sporadic E 15 errors on the touchpad (which all ranges seem to come with now) and we can clear them up only by powering it off for a minute or two. This happens about once every 12 months. Other than that, we have no complaints. I always worry about these computer controls dying, but I don't know if that isn't just the same across most ranges these days. When it finally does die, we'll have to look at cost of service versus replacement. I think we've only reset it four three of four times since we bought in 2011. In the meantime, it's like cooking with gas, but with the advantages of electric - instant control over power input. Lots of baking has gotten done in it and we don't even use the lower oven...but we could!

product_title: Electrolux EW30ES65GSWave-Touch 30" Stainless Steel Electric Slide-In Smoothtop Range - Convection
review_text: Love induction.  Loved this stove.  Now I will never buy another Electrolux product again.  A few months ago it started flashing E15.  I read the blogs and did the troubleshooting. January 5, 2015 the error code reappeared and it hasn't stopped.  I can get it repaired for maybe 1200.00.  If that doesn't work there is another 800.00 part that might fix it.  E15 is a common problem with these stoves and unavoidable.  I would recommend a different brand ad/or the longest warranty you can find.  Electrolux offers nothing as far as recall or assistance.  They know about the issue but they are not making any attempt to fix it.  I will be buying a new stove tonight.  Another induction.  Not an Electrolux.  Nowadays there are too many induction choices to overpay for a stove that doesn't last long. $3500.00 in 2011.  As much as I am from the old school of fix it and wear it out I just can't see putting that kind of money in this stove with no guarantees. I will buy a new stove for that same cost and buy a super warranty. Again, not an Electrolux.

product_title: Electrolux EW30ES65GSWave-Touch 30" Stainless Steel Electric Slide-In Smoothtop Range - Convection
review_title: Looks great, but is complete POS!
review_text:
I am going to make this quick, because I never write reviews.
This stove is a piece of crap, but yeah it sure looks sweet, I can admit that. I wanted to get a simple coil top stove because I knew they are very simple to fix. However, my wife wanted this beauty and I got on board because it is a very good looking stove.

I since have had down time with no stove. Replaced two control boards (luckily I could do this stuff myself) and the Main Power Input cable that you plug into the wall completely melted inside the unit where it connects to the lug and caused a phase to drop out. I also had to repair that. So far the stove is still operating.

The modulating cooktop design is crap. I burn stuff on the one burner when on low setting and the other one barely heats up on medium

IF YOU BUY THIS STOVE CUZ YOUR WIFE THINKS ITS PRETTY after reading this review, then you are one dumb sucker!

RUN LIKE HELL!

product_title: Electrolux EW30ES65GSWave-Touch 30" Stainless Steel Electric Slide-In Smoothtop Range - Convection
review_title: Beautiful range inside and out, but...
review_text: I did not buy this range thru Amazon, but it is my model, and I am writing to comment and to warn about using the self clean feature.  DO NOT, unless your oven is still under factory warranty.  It will perform the self clean feature with no problem, horrible fumes and all, BUT as I discovered, the oven may be dead following the self cleaning.  Officials I spoke with at Electrolux were all firm that the responsibility for repair is mine alone since the original factory warranty has expired, regardless of the fact that this was the first time I had performed the self clean feature, and by the way I used the Lite setting.  I am most annoyed that as a registered owner, I have never received warnings, advisories, or recalls about this possible occurrence.  Given the myriad of testimonial evidence I have since found in the public domain about this recurring problem, I find this fact reprehensible.

product_title: Electrolux EW30ES65GSWave-Touch 30" Stainless Steel Electric Slide-In Smoothtop Range - Convection
review_title: I've had mine now for over 10 years and love this stove
review_text:
I've had this stove now over 10 years. My model number is EW30ES65GSD and is no longer being made but similar stoves are being made. It's a "Slide In" so the controls are in the front where it should be. I hate reaching over a hot cook top and pans to adjust the temperature. I bought the slide in just for that reason.
It has worked flawlessly for the past 10 years. I use the cook top daily and the oven regularly. I have yet to use all the functions of this stove. It has so many things it can do.
I haven't read all of the reviews here but it really is a much better stove than these reviews reflect. As an electrician I can tell you that close attention should be paid to the wiring of this stove with a focus on proper grounding. I have never had an issue with my unit.
I love this stove and would buy it again

review_text:

review_text:

product_title: Frigidaire : FTF2140FS 27 Front-Load Washer - White
review_text:
When looking to replace my washing machine, I started out looking at the traditional top loaders. The cheap ones were around $300 and more standard quality ones around $400, and I saw some that were another $100 or more beyond that. When the salesman asked me about front load washers, I didn't give it much thought because they tend to be more pricey and out of my range. In fact, the first one he showed me was about $700. When I asked him what the cheaper ones cost, he showed me the Frigidaire FTF2140FS for $550, and seeing as they had $100 off deal, it was only slightly more than the standard top loader. So I took him up on the deal, ultimately paying $475 after tax, and so far I'm very happy with its performance.

I usually have two or three people who rent rooms in my house. The old washer took 40 gallons of water per load. The Frigidaire takes just 15 gallons! So right off the bat I'm going to be saving a lot on my water bill, as well as a few bucks on electricity as this washer takes less of that to operate, too.

The controls are pretty simple to figure out. Ten cycles, four temperature settings, you can set how fast you want the basket to spin, and there's a few extra options, too. Shut the door, hit start, and let it go. Just be sure to remember that you must use HE (High Efficiency) detergent.

The wash is very quiet and the spin dry sucks the water right out of the clothes. I can dry my stuff in half the time!

I did encounter one problem twice. When washing my bed sheets and blankets, I heard a beeping noise. The washer was stopped and I thought it was done, but it turns out my sheets were still soaked. I looked at the manual and apparently if the load in the washer basket becomes uneven, it won't spin (that's why it was beeping). So I just pushed the blankets a few times, shut the door, and on the cycle dial there's an option for Final Spin, which is just that, the final spin dry. So I selected that, hit start, and it worked both times. I haven't had that problem with any other load of laundry before or after that.

This was my first foray into the world of front load washers and so far I'm very pleased with the results! It's quiet, efficient, my clothes are clean and smell fresh, and most important of all to me, it isn't tearing my clothes like my old washer was. And for the price I got it at, it's a great value!

review_text:

The smell has gotten better, but most of my towels have a lingering odor several weeks now into the latest detergent. Don't even think of using powder because the dispenser only fills with ice cold water. I've ended up with hunks of half rinsed detergent clogs stuck in the drawer.

In short, this piece of junk has been utterly miserable. I've used 3rd hand junk store washers for a quarter of the price that worked better and lasted longer. I'm only on here looking for parts/information on how to repair this heap of garbage because it now does not spin at all and I'm presuming it's because the motor is broken (two years old).

I don't know if all front loaders are the same, but I most certainly won't be making the same mistake twice. What a pile of overpriced, overhyped junk. Europe can have this garbage back!

product_title: Frigidaire : FTF2140FS 27 Front-Load Washer - White
review_title: CANNOT ADJUST WATER LEVEL - Insufficient Water
review_text:
I had a Frigidaire front loader for 9 years that I loved. I replaced
it with this model. After the fact, I found out that the water level
could not be adjusted and it appeared that there was just enough water
to wet the clothes---someone told us that the new washers went from
40 gallons of water to 15 but I have not verified those figures. I
would always use the extra rinse and leave the door open after use
to prevent mold issues. Well after 18 months I noticed a mold smell.
There was NEVER a problem in the previous washer. I googled this
and found that it was a common problems in the new "energy saving"
(non-adjustable water level) front loaders. I talked with Frigidaire
and I will give them credit, they did replace the rubber gasket in the
door with a new one that has a mold inhibitor--at no charge even though
out of warranty. I will continue to buy Frigidaire but I will never
buy another front loader as long as there is not a water adjustment level.
I was told by an appliance salesman that in order to prevent mold issues
in these new energy (low water level) saving washers one must do the
following:
1. Only use warm water
2. Only use 2 tablespoons of soap if normal water
and just one tablespoon of soap if soft water
3. Always use extra rinse
4. Never use fabric softener
5. Leave the door and the soap tray open after use.

I now run the machine once with soap then run it again without any
soap to get the clothes clean and rinsed well. I will use it until
it breaks and then forget about buying another front loader.

I was told that the new TOP loaders have water levels that are
also NOT adjustable but that Speed Queen (made in USA) still makes one
that a person can adjust the level.

definitely don't go with this model.

product_title: Frigidaire : FTF2140FS 27 Front-Load Washer - White
review_title: Not what we expected in an HE unit
review_text: We have owned this unit for several years. Bought it new from a local dealer at a great price. Pros: uses very little water, spins out to nearly dry, price. Cons: detergent drawer can be cleaned if taken apart and soaked in bleach water, which must be done frequently because the alternative is hazmat level mold. The cavity that the drawer slides into can only be partially cleaned, and we've tried everything other than taking it outside and using a power washer, which we've seriously considered. The markings on the front of the unit indicating wash cycles, etc. have completely worn off--they should be able to handle a little window cleaner without dissolving. The detergent drawer face cracked and chipped off pieces of plastic over time, and not from severe use. Forget about soaking anything in this unit, as it uses the aforementioned very little water. In short, we hate this thing, so we got rid of it this week, replacing it with an efficient top-loader.

product_title: Frigidaire FMP330RGB 18 Portable Dishwasher - Black
review_text:
After moving into my new place, I decided it was time to get rid of the Danby countertop dishwasher and get a standing, 18" portable. I'd always seen the countertop model as a stopgap, because most apartments I could afford didn't have a lot of countertop, but the Danby did well for me during the time I used it.

I'd had an 18" Sears Kenmore portable about 20 years ago, and was planning on purchasing another Kenmore because I'd been quite pleased with that one. Then I received a $500 bonus from work, in the form of an Amazon gift certificate, so I decided to give up on Sears and see what I could get through Amazon. I found this Frigidaire, which seemed to have reasonably good reviews at other sites, and ordered it.

On first blush, it was a lot like my old Kenmore, except the upper rack had an additional, fold-down shelf for small glasses. Once I started using it, tho, I was disabused of the hope that it would be an improvement over my old Kenmore, or even over the Danby. Its drawbacks are:

1. It is loud. Keep you awake at night loud.
2. The racks are so poorly designed that I can't stack bowls in the lower level unless I leave 2-3 empty 'slots' between them. The upper rack has enough space to accommodate bowls, but not enough prongs to hold them in place so the spray can hit them properly. Furthermore, the extra level on the upper rack is useless since even the manual warns you not to block the spray by stacking items immediately above one another. This means that you have only one level there, rather than the 2 levels you initially anticipate.
3. The lower level design may be intentional, because the water spray is underpowered. If I stack dishes too closely, the spray doesn't reach between them, and the top half of the plate or bowl remains dirty.
4. The rack problem combined with the low pressure water spray to make it impossible to fully load the dishwasher. I can do about 3 place settings in a load - just about the same amount I could do with the much smaller Danby.
5. The water hoses and electrical cord depend on friction to hold them in place, meaning that I have to stuff them back through a small opening into their storage space after using the unit. Dragging the hoses & cord back out causes them to scrape against the opening, and it looks to me like that will shorten the life of the rubber/plastic coverings. I've decided to leave the electric cord hanging out, but the water hoses need to be stored to keep them from dripping. My old Kenmore had internal reels for these two items, making it easy to pull them out and put them back.

The one plus that the Frigidaire has over either of my two previous units is that it does have a "Hi Temp" setting, which heats the water during the cycle. This is important since the water in the building pipes doesn't stay hot between the stages of the cycle. The Hi Temp setting uses more energy, but does get the dishes cleaner than they were when I didn't use it.

All in all, I wouldn't purchase this product again. I do prefer having an automatic dishwasher to doing all the dishes by hand, so when I purchase my next dishwasher, I'm going to take bowls and plates with me to test the rack design and, if it's a portable, I'll look for a better cord management mechanism. The other problems probably can't be assessed in a showroom, so I'll just have to hope someone else writes a detailed review of the product I'm interested in before I purchase it.

product_title: Frigidaire AEQ6000ES Affinity 5.8 Cu. Ft. Super Capacity Dryer
review_title: If I could give it ZERO stars, I would!
review_text:
Let me start by saying that because of my experience, I will never again buy ANYTHING with the Frigidaire or Electrolux name attached to it. NEVER. I bought my dryer a couple of years ago, and thought that only a one year warranty was a little shoddy, but never did I expect that the control panels in these dryers are like self-destructing "screw the customer" systems! The dryer started beeping one day while not even turned on, and displaying error code E68, the code for a stuck button. There are no buttons stuck, and upon researching it a bit, I found hundreds of other people online with the same exact problem. The control panel shorts out after 2-3 years and will cause the dryer to think a button is being held down and won't run. Nothing is wrong with the mechanics, it's all just this stupid electronic panel. As I, and the hundreds of other people with these dryers, have found out, Frigidaire absolutely refuses to replace the faulty control panel unless you pay ~$200.00 plus the cost of a service person to come put it in if you don't know how to do it yourself!

They KNOW that they are selling dryers with defective control panels, yet hide behind their wimpy one year warranty as a way to milk a ton of extra cash out of their customers. Where is the recall, Frigidaire??? Hopefully the Better Business Bureau will care to urge them toward resolving this. In the meantime, I recommend that you DO NOT BUY THIS DRYER, OR ANY OTHER FRIGIDAIRE PRODUCT! THEY ARE SCAM ARTISTS!!!

review_text:

A few problems with the cooking results-- the Thanksgiving turkey bent the oven rack, causing it to magically roll towards me in subsequent uses. This was both dangerous and annoying. Heat in the oven was fairly even, but the right side definitely heated up more, necessitating a turn of whatever food I was cooking mid-bake.

Problem: my sensor and control panel continued to fail. I would receive the F5 and F10 error messages approximately 6 weeks after the sensor/ control panel combo were replaced. The only way of shutting off the oven (and stopping the annoying error-beep) was to cut off power from the breaker box. I was advised by Electrolux that using self clean or operating the oven at a very high temperature for pizza or bread can cause the sensor to fail. This was obviously very frustrating.

I'm hoping my new replacement unit is not a lemon like the first. If you can get a functional oven, you will get good results.

product_title: Electrolux EW30EW55GS Wave-Touch 30" Stainless Steel Electric Single Wall Oven - Convection
review_title: CHEAPLY CONSTRUCTED and Pricey to boot
review_text: I have the 27" version of this oven, otherwise it's identical so I'm reviewing this one as well.  Here's my experience; wouldn't recommend Electrolux to anybody. Had this oven only since Sept 09. Bought because of supposed good quality; willing to pay a little more than standard. We don't use it that often but do bake at least 1-2 month. From the very beginning, I thought it baked items too quickly, often drying them out when they should have had several minutes more before being done. Didn't matter if I used convection or not; same issue. I simply adjusted cooking times down and that helped a bit. Last few times, I noticed muffins that had burnt bottoms but only on one side of the tin; that shouldn't be. I inspected the oven and saw what looked like an "S" shaped puddle on the bottom left hand side of my oven lining. Made a mental note to clean it up when it cooled down but it disappeared. So I turned the oven on empty and saw that it reappeared. Disappeared when it was cool. Called repair/service to come out. The lining is practically burnt through and warped because the element shorted out and is malfunctioning. It was probably something that occurred during manufacturing. Electrolux will not offer me more than 10% discount on a new liner. I still have to pay for the new element which costs about the same as the liner. With 2.5 estimated hours of labor, it will total $800. So this was a waste of money; we paid over $2100 with tax and installation 3 years ago and now another $800. So it cost us $706 per year for the life of the oven. The worst part is how Electrolux positions itself as a quality oven and it's cheaply made and won't last even 5 years. If you HAVE to buy it, get the extended warranty and make sure it covers the element and liner. The repair man told me that not only was this issue a fire hazard, it was an electrocution hazard as well. Kelly Ripa owes me a refund. Bad product, stay away.

product_title: Electrolux EW30EW55GS Wave-Touch 30" Stainless Steel Electric Single Wall Oven - Convection
review_text: Took two people to safely lift but otherwise very easy to install if you know anything about 220 volt connections. The rapid preheat is amazing (preheats to 400 in about 2 minutes - old oven took about 20 minutes to preheat and then burned everything). Temperature is dead-on. Love the Keep Warm feature. review_text:
