When it works right, I am happy. The loads spin almost "dry" like which is less drying time.
I paid top dollar for the set and if I had to do it again I wouldn't. When this conks out, I am going back to a top load.
They handle more clothes per load and they are so much nicer to work with.
All in all , this has been a pricey , "lemony" laundry pair. TOO Much money for this kind of performance.

product_title: Bosch Nexxt 800 Series : WFMC8401UC 27 Front Load Washer - Silver and White
review_text:
I bought the 800 series washer front loader and dryer set. Had to have repair at year 1 due to a baby sock escaping from the washer bag (bag as recommended) and it shut down my machine. At year 2 1/2 the machine doesn't aggitate/drain - or one or the other or both - depending on the day. After 2 service calls it's not fixed. I'm replacing my washer with a top loader. Nevermind that the machine smells even with the door left wide open after finishing washing all loads. Towels will never smell good again. I think the smell is the case for all front loaders regardless of brand. But this machine cost a fortune and I'm replacing in a little over 2 years. Bosch wasn't helpful at all and in fact service calls took a while to book, and now I know why.

I haven't had any problems with my dryer so far (knock on wood). I have a Bosch dishwasher and so far it's okay too. However, I'll never buy another Bosch product.

product_title: Bosch Nexxt 800 Series : WFMC8401UC 27 Front Load Washer - Silver and White
review_text:
We had no washer dryer at all, so we went out one sunny day and bought a washer dryer set from Sears, they were KENMORE, NEVER AGAIN!!!
Those machines were bought just before we had a massive influx of house guests and oh yeah, our wedding.
They were out of order for the majority of the time they were in the house, 20 days or so of function and then weeks of waiting for repair man, parts and repair.
So we were eventually given new machines!!

I chose BOSCH, a reliable forward thinking brand, I've had various bosch products before with no issues, ever.
Then these beastly machines!
We got the washer and the dryer.
The dryer is fine, does it's think no issues.

I've not seen a top loader for decades before I came out to the usa (from the UK, remember the twin tubs, lol).
So of course I wasn't going to get an agitator to ruin my clothes.
The BoSCH washer has near on caused mental illness via the sheer agonizing, infuriating consistency of it's inability to balance and spin.
There's no spin cycle of itself, so you have to go through a slow and harassing process of pushing buttons, waiting, pausing, manually repositioning, wringing out and starting the spin cycle again and again and oh it's 2-3am and I still have laundry to do.
I would be better off with my late Grandmother's old twin tub, agitator included!

I cannot bear to spend more time and money on the consumer end of buying new machines, but I can tell you I am 100% looking forward to moving as we'll not be bringing this B*st*rd machine with us!!
I doubt we've saved any water with all the re-cycling (not to be confused with recycling) that we have to do to get the clothes or sheets or whatever out spun!!

The machine doesn't smell, we've never left it off with the door shut, I prop a spray bottle or something in the door to stop it closing when passing.
No other front loader I've ever owned has stunk.

If yours does stink I suggest cleaning it. This usually involves the hottest cycle or a clean cycle and a bottle of machine cleaning Clorox.
I've done that twice in 4 years due to the filthy stuff that we've put in there.
Clothes are always very clean.
We use tide free and clear and occasionally fabric softner, while generally just use dryer balls.

I llove the features of the dryer that allow you to flat dry delicates and the air dry only (no heat) option, as I'm happy to leave a dryer on when I'm out of the house if there's no heat involved...to avoid a common cause of house fire.

I'll be putting a pulley in my new house as the laundry room ceiling is high enough...look it up, big $$$ saver on drying.

product_title: Haier HBCN05FVS 4.0 cu. ft. Beverage Center, Black
review_title: Other reviewers should have done their research more properly
review_text:
Reading all the other reviews of this product......you have to blame the error of the customers and not the product itself.

If you have ever owned a Wine Fridge.....you know it is NOT a refrigerator....that is not its purpose. If the other reviewers wanted a beverage holder that was able to keep food in it or keep beverages below 40degrees....then they should have gotten a REFRIGERATOR...not a wine fridge/chiller.

So knowing that....let us give an honest and realistic review of this item based on what it was actually designed for.

This unit while not the highest frills of wine chillers is attractive with a stainless steel trim on the door and a glass front and a black body. The door is reversible and it has an internal blue LED interior light you can turn on/off depending on your mood. It does not have a Temperature indicator with a simple dial for temperature with MIN to MAX indicators. It is simple and attractive.....and given its price....thats to be expected. I purchased a suction cup thermometer that faces out and mounts to the interior of the glass door for like 2$.

It comes with 4 adjustable racks and the nice bonus of a bottom storage area rack that has not been present in other wine chillers I have purchased. It allows you to stack cans on the bottom on their side so they don't roll out.

My unit is new and I purchased it as it is replacing an old Urbina thermoelectric wine chiller that finally crapped out after 2.5 years (It was dirt cheap so no big whoop). We will see if this unit is the exception.

Lets be honest......these units don't tend to last more than 3 years on average so if you are worried about that a higher end unit may be to your liking....but you will pay a pricey premium for actual fridge-like beverage centers like GE's.....or just invest in a long extended warranty so you can be re-imbursed should it fail within 3 years (this is what I did).

This unit unlike my old model has an actual compressor and sealed coolant system which is a luxury at this price range....usually you are getting a thermo-electric cooling system at prices below 200$.

I will update my review in the coming months but so far my unit on MAX is cooling better than expected with an average of 33F below room temp:
(Current Results = Room Temp - 75F / Cooler Temp - 42F )
* NOTE: Cooler is in a shaded corner away from direct sunlight...and this is also one of the 'newer' models in stores now.

Hopefully this informed and realistic review will help others. This is good unit for the price if you want a beverage chiller. It is similar to units they use at bars and convenience stores on or near the counter. Your beverages will be chilled but they will not be ice cold. Your white wine will be in the perfect temperature range (depending on the temp of your home or room)......which is exactly what this unit was designed for.

review_title: Not bad for the price. Poor customer service.  Temperature and power tested
review_text:
Having read the reviews about the lowest temperature this gets to, I was skeptical, but decided to buy this one anyway. Mostly because of the price and the fact that it fit almost perfectly in the space where the old one was.

Although this is NOT meant for built in spaces, I had a planned workaround. Anyway, my first tests were with the fridge in the middle of an 80F room with plenty of air circulation and no direct sun. Note that this unit does not have a condenser fan (the fan on the back of most larger refrigerators). Instead, the coils are behind the side panels, so they do get very warm. Anyway, because there is no fan, you should not use it built in.

So how did it do? I used a temperature logging device with my laptop and a power meter. On the maximum setting, it cycles on for 30-45 minutes and then off for about 30 minutes. It uses about 80 watts when on (0 watts when off, unless you have the LED's on so maybe a watt) and the temperature ranged from 35F to 45F with a median temperature of 41 (that's what a can of beer or soda would be at any given time because of its thermal mass).

80 watts seemed like a lot of energy for such a small unit, but since Amazon doesn't provide energy data for these, there's no way to compare.

Just for grins, I tried putting the unit in the cabinets (with 1/2" side clearance, 2" on top and 4" in the back) with no modifications. While it did cool about as well as in the open, it ran almost continuously, turning off only for about 5 minutes every 2 hours. That would be a huge energy hog so what I did was put a ~5" diameter muffin fan in the side of the cabinet such that it drew cool air from an adjacent area (the drawer section) and exhausted it into the area where the fridge is. Since the only openings were towards the front, that gave good circulation all around. I had an old Sears Craftsman power switch that I wasn't using (the kind normally used to turn on an accessory when a tool is turned on) that now turns the fan on whenever it senses the fridge is running. The added fan draws 10 watts, but it keeps the fridge from running constantly so it will save electricity. In fact, it may actually may run less than when it was in the open because of the added air circulation.

I find the unit is quiet (sorry don't have a decibel meter), but it is in the family room where the TV is and is not objectionable. Even when it was out in the open and not in the cabinet, it wasn't too loud.

I wish it was more energy efficient, but considering the price it is a good buy.

UPDATE 8-9-12:
I found that having the blue LED lights on affects the temperature inside. That's because the power supply for the LED is in a section of the housing where the thermostat is. If you have the lights on all the time, they generate a small amount of heat which makes the thermostat think the whole fridge is warmer. Thus it will run longer and get the inside about 5 degrees colder. This could explain why some people say the temperature inside is too warm. If you want to get it colder, try turning ON the blue LEDs!

I lowered my initial rating from 4 to 3 stars because of poor Haier customer service. I needed to get a new plastic plug that covers the hole in the door left from reversing the hinges (it was jammed in so tight and it is soft plastic so it got mashed up when I tried to remove it). The manufacturer basically said too bad, you have to buy a new one! This is for a part that couldn't cost more than a quarter.

review_title: How to adjust your beverage cooler
review_text:
I purchased this beverage cooler with doubts in the begining, but once I received it I was pleased with how this unit was well protected. For those of you stating this unit will not cool lower then 39 degrees, I hate to inform you, but it actually will. I say this because I have manually adjusted the thermostat down to 33 degrees, I can go lower but I rather drink my beer then chew it. I will explain this process shortly, but to give you another example I called the support line regarding this cooler and just as I expected I was also informed it would not cool lower then 39 degrees. From previous post that I have read I saw a number of people stating it is adjustable...YES... it can be adjusted, and just in case you missed these posts, you have mine to read. This is how. 1st once you receive this unit please allow at least 12 hrs for it to run within the middle setting. After the 12 hrs locate a small flat head screwdriver and place it under the turn dial of the thermostat. With just a little force pull the knob with the help of the screwdriver and this dial should pull off completely. 2nd notice the small Phillips screw to the left of this dial, this is what you will be adjusting until you reach your desired temp. To give you an example, I set mine to start cooling when it reaches 39 degrees and to stop cooling at 33.5 degrees. (It can be done, just patience Daniel son)...The small Phillips screw will need to be turned clock wise a few rotations. Its best to turn 1 full rotation and allow the beverage cooler time to set the new adjustment. Continue this process until you have your desired temp, than place the turn dial back on and this is what you will be using to tweak your adjustments from now on. I hope this helps and the reason I didn't rate this as a 5 is because the wire racks are crap! Go to a glass shop and have your shelf's cut. Besides its a classier look. The blue light reflects nice with the glass.
Thanks and Cheers!

review_title: How to make it colder if you have the alternate version
review_text:
As most of you know this cooler does not make beverages cold enough to be enjoyable, and other reviewers have posted very helpful tips on how to adjust this cooler to make it usable. However there is an alternate version of this cooler out now that has moved the thermostat adjustment screw. If you pull the black control knob off the front and do NOT see the adjustment screw to the left that others have described, here is how to perform this same hack on this newer model.

(1) UNPLUG THE COOLER!
(2) If you haven't already, gently pull the black control knob off the front of the thermostat.
(3) Remove the three screws (Phillips) that mount the thermostat control box to the top of the cooler. There are two in the front corners, the third is in the center of the back.
(4) With the thermostat control box hanging lose, carefully pull up the metal control housing in the center of the box. You don't need to remove it completely, just enough to expose the small screw on the left side.
(5) Using a small-tipped Phillips screwdriver, turn this screw COUNTER-clockwise to make your unit colder.
(6) Reverse steps 1-4 to re-assemble.

It is very easy to accidentally turn your cooler into a freezer, so use a thermometer and check the temperature after several hours. It's best to make small adjustments until you get it right. If you can ensure that kids won't be getting into the cooler and getting shocked, I found it best to just leave the thermostat disassembled until I had the temperature correct.

Once you get it right, put everything back together and use the black knob to fine-tune.

It's a great cooler once you make this adjustment!

product_title: Electrolux RH36WC40GS36" Stainless Steel Under Cabinet Range Hood
review_text:
The image appears to be that of either the 30" or 36" dual-blower, under-cabinet range hood made by Electrolux. I recently installed the 36" inch version (model RH36WC40GS). Removal of the protective film on the hood's body and grease filters was tedious and time-consuming. Hard pounding with hammer/screwdriver was required to knock out the vertical duct openings for installation of 7" round duct. I was afraid that the pounding might have damaged some of the hood's electronic or mechanical components, but luckily that was not the case. The installation guide designates an incorrect location for the hole to be drilled in the cabinet bottom for electric-cable access.

The electrical connection (hot, neutral, and ground wires) must be made inside a plastic box that is too small. The work-arounds required to compensate for the small box depend on the particulars of the installation. In my case, I decided to insert a mere plastic shield into the access hole in the range top (rather than a cable clamp) and to create a cable-clamp at the two-inch-diameter hole I'd drilled in the cabinet's bottom shelf.

Installation of light bulbs with the required GU10 base was difficult because the light bulb blocks your vision of the two holes in the receptacle into which the two prongs on the bulb's base must fit. And, the only way to twist the bulb into its final resting place is to use some device, like double sticky-back tape on the bulb face, to get enough friction to twist the bulb.

The grease filter attachment is also user-unfriendly. There is no supporting ledge along the base of the range hood, front or back. Each filter's frame has two fixed tabs on the back that must fit into slots in the back wall of the hood (can be tricky). There is a spring-loaded handle near each filter's front edge which operates two movable (in-out) tabs on the frame's front edge. The handle must be held open to retract these tabs until proper alignment of the filter's front edge is obtained. Then the handle is released and the two front tabs pop out unto slots in the front wall of the hood. Care must be taken when removing a grease filter so that it does not fall onto your stove top. As you open the handle to release the filter's front edge, you should keep your other hand under the central part of the filter, because the filter will fall out of the back slots.

The LCD display is almost useless. Unless you are a really short person, you will have to stoop to make the displayed characters visible. This is an extraordinary shortcoming for a range hood that is this expensive and can only be tolerated because the display is not essential. The range light must be on or off.... no intermediate light levels. To use the highest (fourth) blower speed, you must punch the "up" button four times. Then, to turn off the blower you must punch the "down" button four times (my previous, less expensive Broan range hood had an on/off button for each of its three speeds... plus three on/off buttons for three different light levels).

Once the range hood is installed, and you are satisfied with the single light level and button-push logic, you are happy to find that the blowers are not too noisy (air-wise) and that the hood does a good job of ventilating your cooking. For me, however, there remains one significant complaint: The magnetic hum (120 Hertz) of the blower motors is a bit harsh. Now, many... maybe most people won't notice or be bothered by this hum. Electrolux says that the hum is normal. However, many fans and blowers use what is called a "permanent-split capacitor A.C. inductance motor". These are relatively inexpensive motors, and it is possible to design such motors so that the magnetic hum is negligible. I don't know what kind of motors this Electrolux hood uses. I do know that the blower motor in my previous Broan range hood had a somewhat quieter, softer hum than these motors in the Electrolux hood.

The build quality of this range hood is very good, and it has an attractive appearance. However, because of the negative factors mentioned above, and because of the high cost of the hood, I would not recommend this hood to a friend. And, believe me, I wanted to like this hood, having just un-installed the old Broan hood, installed 7" round ductwork to vent through kitchen cabinets out to a screened-porch wall, re-installed the Broan hood, decided to buy a new hood, un-installed the Broan hood again, and installed the Electrolux hood. That ain't easy for a retired 75-year-old engineer.

review_title: Worst Domestic Appliance ever purchased in past 30 years
review_text: This is singularly the worst domestic appliance we have ever purchased/owned. This month it is 4 years old and we bought this with a 1 year manufacturer warranty and 3 year extended warranty. I pity those who didn't. Today I took delivery of its replacement. I am a design engineer and everything wrong with this unit is a design flaw. The switch mechanism for stopping the ice production when the tray gets full is mounted at right angles to where it needs to be and never works. The result is it never stops producing ice. It literally fills the tray to overflowing then fills the freezer. When the defrost kicks in it part melts the overfilled tray that is now too near the defrost coils so the ice part melts and then freezes again as a solid block jamming the ice drawer completely. I could go on. The first time we didn't realize what had happened and tried to get it to dispense ice and the ice delivery motor went on fire. We have had the ice maker replaced twice, repaired twice and then gave up. The on/off switch for the ice is conveniently located behind the drawer that is now jammed because the ice has overflowed and frozen solid so it just keeps going unless you turn it all off and defrost it. The water dispenser freezes when the ice gets full and the manufacturers solution is to add a heater which then causes it to dispense hot water until you let it run for more than half a cup. I believe this unit was designed by a disgruntled employee or an utterly incompetent imbecile with no knowledge of basic engineering. I will NEVER buy another GE appliance. Everyone can have a problem but GEs refusal to take ownership of this disaster or to permanently fix it or recall and replace these lemons is disgusting. GE you have lost a customer for life. I wouldn't recommend this item to my worst enemy. PLEASE don't buy one of these or even look at a used one. BUYER BEWARE.

review_title: Nice, but I Wouldn't Buy it Again
review_text:
We got a very similar LG model 3 years ago. No major problems, but...

Door Closing: Unlike most refrigerators, you need to actively push the doors closed each time. Guests botch it. And household regulars miss it once in a while even after 3 years. The well designed door alarm resolves it usually, but not always. An active family is going to open and close the fridge door 80,000 times in 10 years. This minor hassle is not so minor.

Bottom Freezer: The model has a good energy efficiency numbers, but I wonder if those are closed-door tests. This one pulls the whole freezer drawer out into the room. Air circulates top, bottom, left, and right. It feels like a crazy amount of energy wasted every time.

Bottom Freezer--Part 2: The freezer also demands active closing attention. Once in a great while it's left 1/3 inch open...not enough open to trigger the alarm, but enough to tick you off when things are mushy the next morning.

Bottom Freezer--Part 3: The handle is about to break. There's a cracking sound every time we pull on it. Probably from having to pull extra hard when the roller-gear mechanism iced up due to Part 2 above.

Lots of good things about this fridge, and no fridge is perfect. But I think the french door + bottom freezer design has more hassles than benefits.

product_title: LG Electronics LFC23760SB 22.6 Cu. Ft. French Door Bottom Freezer Refrigerator, Smooth Black
review_text:
My entire life I have only known the standard, freezer door on top, one giant door below, refrigerator. About a year after we moved in to our house, it was time to buy a new refrigerator and there was a lot of things to like about this LG fridge.

Pros:

Width - we had a very set width we were working with, and at the time, this was one of the few french door models that would fit the size we needed.

Looks - overall, the fridge is aesthetically pleasing.

Size - the ability to adjust all the shelves and door compartments really allows you to maximize the internal space for your family's needs

Function - things are the right temperature and the freezer freezes. It's a fridge, it does what I hoped it would.

Freezer - I know from an energy standpoint the whole freezer pulling out, might not be the best, but if you want your freezer on the bottom, it's the best way to access it so you don't have to get on the ground to look in there.

Cons:

The doors require being PUSHED shut. Our guests leave the fridge open all the time. There is a door alarm which is a pro only because of this problem.

You need some extra space for the doors to open beyond the width requirement. Our one door is not able to open fully for this reason. Both doors have hinges that open just a little wider than the fridge itself.

Ice-maker - it works fine, but there's no filter for this fridge so your ice is only as good as your tap water.

Overall:

For our first refrigerator, we have been extremely happy with it. A couple minor quirks, but a lot of nice features and we got it a price lower than what is listed currently. After reading the other reviews, I just went out and gave all the handles a good tug, and they are all sturdy on my model. No complaints there. Based on my use, I would recommend it.

review_text: I purchased this model from a local dealer for our kitchen remodel that we had planned for a long time. product_title: LG Electronics LFC20760SW 20 Cu. Ft. French Door Bottom Freezer Refrigerator, Smooth White
review_text:
I will never again purchase an LG product and would suggest that all of you avoid them as well. Here's why:

1) Quality--Our previous refrigerator worked for about 25 years without ever needing a repair. Our LG refrigerator had a catastrophic failure in less than a year, becoming completely nonfunctional.

2) Parts availability--We were told that the electronics board, which is like your computer's motherboard, was on backorder for two months.. The refrigerator cannot function without it, but none were available.

2) Customer service--Perhaps even worse than the fact that LG makes an unreliable product and doesn't stock essential components is the fact that their customer service is absolutely abysmal. Literally every single thing that I have been told by a customer service representative, supervisor, or "resolution agent" has been contradicted by someone else in LG's system.

So far I have made 13 phone calls in the 12 days since the appliance died, since no one ever calls you back.

Everyone has agreed, since day 4, that the unit is under warranty, that LG cannot make us wait for so long for the unit to be repaired, and that the refrigerator will be replaced with a new one. But for some reason the case still had to "reviewed," which two people said would take 3-5 days another said 7-10 days, another said she'd mark "urgent" to expedite it, etc.

The exchange was then disapproved and the part that wasn't available until 8/25 suddenly would be available on 7/27 (or 7/31, depending upon which person was lying to me at the time). Since the odyssey started on 7/12, we didn't feel that waiting 2 weeks without a refrigerator was reasonable at any time, but especially during the summer.

We'd already had to throw out food, we'd been unable to buy groceries because we had nowhere to store them, we'd canceled a party for 30 people because we couldn't store things in advance of preparing them, and we'd spent money eating out each night.

I complained and the exchange was magically approved. But first it had to be assigned to an agent who would organize the exchange. I was given an agent's name and direct phone number. That agent has never called me, not even in response to the three messages I've left in the last two days.

So it has been almost two weeks already and although everyone has known that LG needs to provide a new replacement refrigerator, we still have no information about when that may be. Do yourself a favor and avoid the continuous aggravation and endless hassle--just don't buy LG products.

product_title: LG Electronics LFC25770ST 25.0 Cu. Ft. French Door Bottom Freezer Refrigerator, Stainless Steel
review_title: Crazy big, but everything we wanted
review_text:
As much as I liked a similar GE Profile model with LED lights, I couldn't justify spending $800 to buy LED lights (the primary if not the only distinction between this model and the GE). I specifically wanted this model because it does not have the door ice/water dispenser, which seems to be especially prone to freezing and other issues across all brands of French Door/Bottom Freezer fridges on the market.

This fridge is huge, as others have stated, both inside and outside. I bought it knowing it would never fit where the old fridge was--eventually, we will build a kitchen around this fridge. For now, it is great to have digital temperature controls, a very large freezer space, and, as someone who is very tall, it is great to be able to see inside the fridge without bending over.

The door pockets are very deep--enough so to hold a gallon of milk in either the left or the right door. The shelves slide out. There's 4 vegetable drawers and the fridge came with a "bonus plastic shoe box" as an extra crisper/box thingy. The compressor noise is very minimal--most of the time, the fridge is virtually silent.

Another reviewer mentioned the door alarm--yes, it's loud, but it doesn't come on until the doors have been for a few minutes--more than enough time to get jobs done. And from thereon, it seems to beep 3 times and then stay silent for 60 seconds. I think that's reasonable. The door alarm is important because these French Door fridges can appear to be closed but actually be open. That is a flaw across brands and seems intrinsic to keeping the gap between the doors sealed vs. visibility of the gap--so the door alarm serves an important purpose.

We've had this over a month and love it. The only complaints are that the finish marks easily (greasy fingers) and the lights are hot to the touch. But it looks sharp, keeps food cold, and has lots of space.

UPDATE Jan-2011: I've had this fridge for almost two years now and still like it. As other reviewers mentioned, you have to be active when closing the doors--by themselves they do not pull in firmly and guests can sometimes get this wrong, and the alarm doesn't always sound. But I think we've only had this happen once or twice. It's a little lame, but I think this is a problem with many french door fridges. I also had to try a mixture of stainless steel cleaners to figure out how to keep the surface clean, which is also a pain in the rear, but that's a problem with all stainless products as well.

review_text:

I've had to put folded towels under the crispers to give the unit more stability. Should that be necesarry on a 2 year old unit that costs over $1500???

The style of the fridge is great. Lots of room, deep door pockets. The shelves are a bit of a problem, lots of wasted airspace as there is limited shelf height adjustment. I would look at other brands if you like the french door style refridgerator. Our neighbors bought a Whirlpool and have not had any problems. A friend has the same LG fridge in stainless steel and is not happy with it at all.
Shame on LG for not offering assitance to customers on these refridgerators. I will not buy anymore LG products.

product_title: LG Electronics LFC25770ST 25.0 Cu. Ft. French Door Bottom Freezer Refrigerator, Stainless Steel
review_text:
The Good:
-Nice looking refrigerator
-Lots of space

The Bad:
-The covers of the veggie draws broke within the first couple of month. Not a big deal though you can always leave your veggies in the plastic bags. I don't know what you would do if you take paper instead of plastic.
-The ice maker was already replaced twice. Recently it broke again; I decided to not replace it a third time. The problem is always the same. The metal handle that stops the ice maker when enough ice is in the reservoir breaks when closing the upper drawer. It's not a big deal either you can always get ice from the supermarket and fill up the container.

And the Ugly:
-The cover of the control unit/lighting inside the fridge fell down recently. When I tried to reinstall the cover I realized that the heat from the lamps has partially melted some of the plastic that contains the control unit. This included parts that fix the cover to the unit and the unit itself to fridge. The light bulbs were the original bulbs that came with the fridge. I removed the original light bulbs until I can replace them with bulbs that produce less heat. The control unit and the cover have to be replaced. For all of you that are already proud owners of this refrigerator, consider removing the bulbs when the doors are open for longer times e.g. for cleaning or replace them with lower energy bulbs.

As far as LG goes, I'll take our former President's advice: "There's an old saying in Tennessee -- I know it's in Texas, probably in Tennessee -- that says, fool me once, shame on -- [pauses] -- shame on you. Fool me -- [pauses] -- You can't get fooled again.

Buy: If you enjoy repairing appliances, or if you want to support the economy in the coming years.
Don't buy: If periodic cleaning is all you expect to do with your refrigerator.

product_title: LG Electronics LFC25770ST 25.0 Cu. Ft. French Door Bottom Freezer Refrigerator, Stainless Steel
review_title: Nice, but I Wouldn't Buy it Again
review_text:
We got this model 3 years ago. No major problems, but...

Door Closing: Unlike most refrigerators, you need to actively push the doors closed each time. Guests botch it. And household regulars miss it once in a while even after 3 years. The well designed door alarm resolves it usually, but not always. An active family is going to open and close the fridge door 80,000 times in 10 years. This minor hassle is not so minor.

Bottom Freezer: The model has a good energy efficiency numbers, but I wonder if those are closed-door tests. This one pulls the whole freezer drawer out into the room. Air circulates top, bottom, left, and right. It feels like a crazy amount of energy wasted every time.

Bottom Freezer--Part 2: The freezer also demands active closing attention. Once in a great while it's left 1/3 inch open...not enough open to trigger the alarm, but enough to tick you off when things are mushy the next morning.

Bottom Freezer--Part 3: The handle is about to break. There's a cracking sound every time we pull on it. Probably from having to pull extra hard when the roller-gear mechanism iced up due to Part 2 above.

Lots of good things about this fridge, and no fridge is perfect. But I think the french door + bottom freezer design has more hassles than benefits.

product_title: LG : LMX21981ST 20.5 cu. ft. Counter-Depth French Door Refrigerator
review_text:
I bought this refrigerator/freezer in September of 2008, and by Sept/Oct of 2009 it was broken. Something in the door behind the ice container starting making a horrific smashing sound every time we closed the door, until the display lights on the door died along with the ice and water making and dispensing abilities. I called LG and they sent a technician not to repair the fridge but to replace some board in the fridge because of it's failure to be as energy-efficient as advertised. Turns out that the fridge was only energy-efficient with the ice-maker turned off. LG came to an agreement with the DOE to replace the boards and/or? to reimburse the fridge owners with a $21 payment/yr.

I was advised by LG that I should contact one of their authorized repair people who could repair the fridge. As of today (Dec 27, 2009), my fridge door is still not fixed and the technician was unable to diagnose the problem. He tried replacing the digital display and the door to no avail. I am not hopeful that there is a fix except replacement. For a fridge that cost me in excess of $3000, I expected much more, and you should too. So, I suggest you don't buy this particular item.

What I do like about the fridge is the double freezer drawers on the bottom. In fact, this was the major reason that I chose to buy this appliance.

As an aside, I had an LG gas dryer that broke within a year. It had the same problem at least twice more during it's 5-yr life until we decided to buy a new electic dryer. I think that buying an extended warranty on LG products would be a good idea. Maybe it would be an even better idea to stay away from this manufacturer altogether.

review_title: I LOVE MY LG FRIG, BUT MY BACK DOESN'T!!!!!
review_text: Ive had frig for almost 5 years, and it's been somewhat of a problem, but really not LG's fault.  I wanted this frig so bad I could almost taste it, and would have sacrificed almost anything to get, and I did.  I got solid white, swing door freezer.  I wasn't impressed with delivery/install folks.  They could not, or would not "install" ice maker because I did not have a cut off within 6 feet, it was about 8 feet away, but it does clearly state that it must be 6 feet and they cannot do it.  So, while two grown men watched, I connected the tubing and ice maker myself!  Anyway, to my point, I loved my new frig until less than a month later I broke 8 vertebrae in my back and for months and years now I have great difficult bending, turning and lifting.  So now,  getting to my ice maker and freezer is a REAL problem!  Can you imagine?  Not only the bending, but because of my bone issues, I have lost about 8 inches in height and can barely even reach the top frig shelf much less see what's there. As stated my health issues are certainly not LG's problems, but they have become and remain a huge problem for me, and really cannot afford to purchase another new frig.  The only problem i can speak to is that over time, the frig sounds seem to have gotten louder and more often.  Sometimes I literally think someone is in the house.  I see others have written about ice build up in the back of the freezer, and I have that too from time to time, but have determined it happens when I don't keep the filter and grate in the back clean, or something blocking.  If I spent alot of time, I would probably find maintenance also has something to do with the noises. My LG continues to operate as if it was new, it certainly keeps items cold, and things freeze rather quickly in the freezer.  The ICE PLUS feature works wonderfully when you need an extra boost for ice to fill up chests, etc.  Others have complained about the door alarm, but I have not experienced any problems with it; in fact, it has been very worthwhile numerous times in alerting me that I have failed to close the door completely, which is what it is meant to do.  It is very well lighted on the inside, and has more than enough temperature settings for any event.  The drawers and shelves are large, glass and see thru, something else I really like, and you can adjust and place them practically in any layout you want.  If I have to complain I would say the noise is somewhat irritating sometimes, and when my freezer is loaded, the drawer is very heavy to pull out (could be because of my weakness though), so being able to see what's in the freezer without pulling out the drawer is not easy.  And I'm clumsy I guess but I spill more ice than makes it to my glass, and it falls in places in the freezer that I cannot reach. And one last minor point, although my LG is while it is very easy to keep clean, but I have noticed at the top of the freezer door the paint seems to be starting to chip, dont know why, but for now, it is not a major issue, and it is not visible when door is closed.  I am pleased with my LG and were it not for my back injury, it would be GREAT, but keep in mind if you do have back issues, the bottom freezer can be a problem.

product_title: GE APPLIANCES PFSS6PKXSS 36 25.5 cu. ft. French Door Refrigerator, Ice/Water - Stainless Steel
review_title: This applies to all GE refrigerators
review_text:
I have owned (and still own) several GE refrigerators. This is an assessment of all of them: never, never buy a GE refrigerator with a built-in ice-maker. The ice-makers have been included for decades, and GE still cannot make one which is reliable. Ask any repairman: the ice-maker is by far the commonest source of problems, especially the ones with a feed through the door. The ice-maker requires a separate water line; it is noisy; and when the tray is removed, it may take hours to get it back into place. The ice itself lies open to the atmosphere of the fridge, and picks up foul tastes. The system wastes energy. When kids use it, ice ends up on the floor, damaging the wood and causing a hazard. The little flap at the top of the dispenser sometimes does not close, and then ices up.

The whole ice-maker and ice-dispenser is a disaster. It shows how engineers sometimes can design something which must have worked in their labs, but does not work under actual, real-life conditions. What is amazing, is that in all these years, they have never come up with a really reliable, workable design.

I have warned you! Now just let your wife or the salesman persuade you to buy one, and you can find out for yourself.

product_title: GE APPLIANCES PFSS6PKXSS 36 25.5 cu. ft. French Door Refrigerator, Ice/Water - Stainless Steel
review_title: Overall Good, with some things to realize before you buy...
review_text:
Okay, let me start by saying that I've had a GE refrigerator (side-by-side, ice/water in the door, quick access door) for over 15 years before this one. I always hated the side-by-side, but inherited it. The french doors and freezer on the bottom is great. I've got loads of space and can fit larger items into it very nicely. The deli tray is very convenient as is the little shelf in the freezer door. Also nice is the flip up shelf next to the ice maker and the slice back 1/2 shelf (had this on my s-b-s). That all said, here we go...

I don't mind the ice maker in the fridge at all, it is small enough not to take up much space and is a better option than Maytag offers on their models (where you lose the shelves completely from one of the doors. I haven't had any issues taking out or putting the ice try back, and so far, no knocking (tho it hasn't been 8 months yet).

Okay, now for the good, er bad stuff...

No egg container/storage provided. Water access in the door works fine, but is a poor design. You can't hold a glass upright as it will not sufficiently push the lever back to operate, and if you do push it back, your glass/container is tilted so you can't get an accurate read on how much water you have in your container. The water catcher tray at the bottom of the area is too small and the tube the water comes out of is too short (can't conveniently refill water bottles, something that should have been considered in anything since the mid-90s). There is no meat tray (I mean raw animal parts storage) in the fridge. You have a fruit and a vegetable drawer (yeah you can pile them up and put the meat into the other one, but then you waste a lot of space as it is too big for fresh meat use. The deli tray is also below it and for health reasons, the raw meat should be the lowest thing in the section.

The outside (of the Stainless Steel model at least) is NOT metal on the front, so there goes magnet space, be ready to use tape or something if you put kids pictures or schedules up there. The sides are, so if they are not blocked, you may be able to use that area. Me, I have a dented model and figured I'd put a magnet on the dented area to cover it, but had to resort to a sticker from the local hospital to cover the ding.

Again, functionally it is a good model, wish it had the quick access for milk and stuff, but that is a different model, so I'm overall happy. GE service in my area has always been good when I've needed them.

The rubber seal on the door came off and that required replacement of the entire door - twice -- which they put on crooked so when you look at the front of the fridge, one door is higher than the other. It also required a special order so we had to take 2 days off, one for the diagnosis and another for the actual repair. The humidity control on the cheese drawer broke. The pulls on the veg drawers cracked. The veg drawers fall out of the track if you put anything heavy in them like onions, tomatoes, carrots, or lemons. My drawers are just resting on the bottom of the fridge.

After 3 1/2 years the motherboard went - $600 (out of pocket).

When the doors are closed, the "Open Door" alarm starts beeping. Somtimes if you pull out and push back in the basket and the drawers in the freezer, it will stop beeping. Sometimes I have to open the fridge doors and press the two door buttons to get it to stop. Still haven't figured out what that is.

Having the water dispenser inside the fridge is not a good idea. The water pressure is too low and it takes too long. You have to stand there for a whole minute filling a water bottle with the door open. And if you fill two, the door alarm beeps. The ater filters are $30 each. You can get them as cheap as $26 - if you buy a case of 6!

One repairman said he spends 80% of his time fixing just GE Profiles. The model is poorly designed, poorly made, with inexpensive parts that wear quickly. I cannot reccommend this appliance at all. I know now, almost 4 years later, that it was a fad, something shiney, new, and novel, but not worth the box it came in -- like a pet rock.

product_title: GE APPLIANCES PFSS6PKXSS 36 25.5 cu. ft. French Door Refrigerator, Ice/Water - Stainless Steel
review_title: Avoid this fridge if you have children or an inattentive spouse!!
review_text:
Of all the refridgerators that I've owned over the years this is the first one that requires you to physically and consciously push the door, by hand, all the way until it seals shut. No more just setting the door in motion with a slight push and expecting it to close on it's own. With this fridge even a moderately forceful push will result in a partially open refridgerator. Even after leveling it per instructions it simply won't close without a fair amount of physical effort. Considering the dozens of times each day that my fridge is opened, this translates into alot of wasted electricity if my kids aren't paying attention to the door. Unfortunately the GE engineers, instead of actually fixing the problem and making the door more user friendly, they decided to install an "open door" alarm which is so quiet that if you're more than 7'-10' away from the fridge you can't hear it.

So to recap, GE designed a refridgerator whose door does not close all the way without force, the engineers recognized this and instead of fixing it, added a bell alarm that is inadequate. (Presumably these are the same engineers that created the faulty ice makers in this fridge that I've been reading about). It's too bad the GE is relying on their past, good reputation to sell a product today that has inherent problems that could be fixed. This lack of attention to detail, coupled with their poor customer service, will cost them in the long run.

review_text:
Most of this is fact but I have included some opinions.

I purchased a General Electric Profile refrigerator on 7/27/08 from Best Buy for $2281.23. It had been working acceptably until about the middle of April of 2012. We called GE repair and GE sent out a technician on 5/2/12, but he didn't have the part so he couldn't fix it the first time he came out. On 5/4/12 he came back out and did a few things including replacing parts WR55X10956, WR55X10490, and something called a REFER MAINBOARD Pkg. He said at first that he was sure it was the mainboard. The charges for the parts and labor was $324.91. Then when it wasn't acting the way he expected, he said he thought it might be the compressor but that we could wait to see if what he'd done fixed it. He ordered a compressor just in case and scheduled an appointment for 5/14/12 and told me if I got the compressor he'd come get it.. The refrigerator allows the consumer to set the freezer and refrigerator temperatures. We set them for the temperatures that GE recommends. The next day the refrigerator was maintaining the freezer and refrigerator temperatures so we canceled the 5/14/12 appointment. When canceling, we told the GE support person on the phone that he'd ordered a compressor to be delivered to my house. The support person said he'd canceled that too. Several days later we received the compressor that had been theoretically canceled. We never heard from the GE repair man about coming to pick up the compressor.

On 6/30/12 we noticed that the refrigerator was not maintaining the set temperatures so we called GE again.
They gave me an appointment for 7/6/12. Today he came out again but told me that they had not allowed him enough time to replace the compressor so he'd have to reschedule. The first available time for installing a compressor is 7/16/12.

I think GE is responsible for manufacturing a lousy product and having awful support of the garbage they manufacture.

product_title: GE APPLIANCES PFSS6PKXSS 36 25.5 cu. ft. French Door Refrigerator, Ice/Water - Stainless Steel
review_text: I own a GE Profile model PFSF6PKXBWW and I am now in discussions with GE about a replacement unit.  This refrigerator is less than 3 years old and the ice maker quit about 2 years ago.  I got water on the floor, and found that it leaked from the plugged lines after the defroster melted the frost from the unit.  The local repairman took the plastic cover off of the back of the defrost unit and the shielding between the defrost unit and the back of the refrigerator was not sufficient to prevent the unit from scorching the plastic on the refrigerator's interior.  Then the lining of the refrigerator cracked - the crack is about 4" long now.  The charing or burning on the inside of the unit is now brown and turning black from the defrost unit.  When the repairman talked with GE, they told him that they would send him white plastic tape to cover the crack.  The ice maker - which the repair man said was basically a "piece of junk" quit working and GE said that he wasn't to replace it at this time.  It makes 3 ice cubes a week whether I need them or not.  The unit certainly wasn't worth the initial purchase price, and now is worth nothing.  My biggest problem is what to purchase to replace this unit.  I know that GE is going to offer me a discount on a new unit, but I am not sure I trust their products after this ugly experience.  If you own this product, I suggest that you take the cover off of the back of the defrost unit, and see if you too have charing and cracks around the unit from the heating of the unit to melt the ice.

product_title: GE APPLIANCES PFSS6PKXSS 36 25.5 cu. ft. French Door Refrigerator, Ice/Water - Stainless Steel
review_text:
Our GE (made by Samsung) was purchased in Aug of '08 while moving into a new house.

Pros: Good looking, good storage space and features, keeps consistent temps.

Cons:
1). The compressor motor was not plugged into the wiring harness at the factory, so it took two weeks for GE to send somebody out to fix. Luckily we were moving in from out of town so didn't lose any food or $.
2). The ice maker died last summer and took out the main motherboard with it. Our 2 year extended warranty was over, so it cost $400 in parts. I replaced everything myself and avoided labor cost.
3). This past fall I noticed water building up in the bottom of the fridge. I finally tracked the problem to a frozen drain hole in bottom of the interior cooling coil area. You have to remove all the shelves, pull the back panel off (inside the fridge, not the back panel), use a hair dryer for an hour to thaw the frozen plug, then wrap some bare copper around the defroster unit and into the hole so it won't freeze shut again. Luckily I did that myself and it did not ruin the fridge or cost me $.

I would look for an option with higher customer rating or buy the longest extended warranty you can find.

product_title: LG LDS4821ST 24" Stainless Steel Full Console Dishwasher - Energy Star
review_text:
We are a family of five with standard home kitchen use. We wanted a dishwasher that cleans well, is simple to use, and has a steel tub. We wanted the stainless tub to avoid the ugly stains that every other washer I have ever owned invetibably got. However, an added bonus outside of looks, is that with a steel tub you can easily side mount the dishwasher, which is a must if you own granite or stone counter tops. We installed the machine ourselves and have owned it for a little over a month:

1. Super quiet at 52dB and does not interfere with conversations, tv, radio, or anything while running.
2. Very easy to use and simple control set up
3. Stainless tub and used to side mount
4. Bottom has wide channels for the water and electrical hook ups, which made installation much easier.
5. Water connection is in the front for easy access, again making installation easy.
6. Cleans our stemware and coffe cups better than any machine I have ever owned. Absolutely no residue.
7. Pots and pans cleaned well with no pre-rinse or scrubbing on my part.
8. The bowl placement for the top rack is not as good as it appears in the pictures, but the bottom rack handles them very well. Top is good too, but you have to space them every third or second post.
9. The top rack is adjustable and has mounts for stem ware, and as wine drinkers, I have loved this function.
10. I have never owned an LG before, but based on my experience so far, I would buy again and recommend to anyone.

They no-showed 3 times with no calls. And, I stayed home from work to be there to meet them during their 4 hour time window.

I complained to LG and at first they did nothing about it. I discussed this with the repair technician who came and he even said that if he puts in his own zip code where his business is located, he doesn't even come up in the search results.

product_title: LG LDS4821ST 24" Stainless Steel Full Console Dishwasher - Energy Star
review_text:
This piece of junk was purchased at Home Depot in 2009 for around $575.

The first major problem is it barfs up an "HE" code meaning the heating cycle is not working. The underlying problem is LG put the relay for the heating coil on the main circuit board. The relay can't take the 500-1000 watts or whatever the load is and simply melts. They actually had a recall at one point because it burned down a few houses. They blamed it on "poor soldering". Not really, it's poor design that will never work in a million years. You simply can't run that much power through a small relay and expect it not to fail. The thing never really dried the dishes anyway so it's hard to tell when it's not working. The "fix" is to replace the main circuit board which is around $125, if I do it myself. Having someone fix it would exceed the cost of getting a new dishwasher.

The second problem is the soap dispenser just quit working. The lid will not stay shut. We just pour in the soap, slam the lid, swear, and let it run.

The third problem is it is now making a horrific noise, grinding, whining, like metallic angry chipmunks. I stuff a old towel at the base to reduce the noise. There is not delay start so this thing can make it's noise at night. However, since it can't be trusted because sometimes it barfs up an HE code right away and you have to restart it, so instead of taking 2 hours and 4 minutes to do the dishes, you are up to 2 hours and 40 minutes.

The fourth problem is the metal clips provided to hold the dishwasher in place are way too thin, looks like 14 gauge steel at best. There is simply too much space between where the clips attach and where you screw them into the counter top. Raising the dishwasher by adjusting the legs you can only go so far up. At any rate after a year or so of loading and unloading dishes the clips popped out while both dish racks were pulled out causing the dishwasher to fall out of the cabinet spilling all the dishes and rack on to the floor. There's no lip or anything where you can just drive a big screw into the counter top to secure it, just those dang clips unless I want to re-engineer something. Just looking at it, who thought that design made any sense? It doesn't, it was probably the cheapest solution they could find.

Fifth problem the clips holding the rack wheels are brittle and crack. Luckily I robbed clips from the other side that are used for the worthless "adjustable" shelf feature.

Oh yeah, the first night we got it, it peed all over the kitchen floor. Turns out a seal was not install properly at the factory, so rather than calling service, I simply fixed it myself.

This thing is really nothing more than an assembly of the cheapest Chinese parts they could find. Even the silverware holder has worn through. Manufactures can make stuff that's "not quite right", but most learn from their mistakes like common warranty issues, complaints, and service people feedback. Good manufacturers take this feedback and improve the product. LG obviously has not done this since they are selling the exact POS that we bought in 2009. Consumer Reports feedback rants on this dishwasher and for good reason. Now I'm stuck, not worth it to fix it, even if I do the work myself, and a new dishwasher is not in the budget. Is it just me or it unreasonable to expect an appliance to last 10 - 15 years? I suppose that's what you get when the parts are made in China and assembled in Korea, probably a contract manufacturer at that who just slaps the LG label on it. I can't prove that but how can it come to be something is so poor that a company like LG is not aware of the problems?

I have fantasies of taking a pick ax to this POS.

review_title: Quiet, cleaning power is significantly reduced as a result

Because this unit attempts to be quiet, it doesn't use powerful jets on the dishes. It kind of drizzles water over the dishes, with expectedly lackluster results.

However, if there is ONE SINGLE THING you can do to get the best results available from this washer, it would be to ACTIVATE THE SANITARY RINSE FUNCTION. Activating that feature single-handedly increased cleaning results by nearly 100%. I even get decent results on the "quick" cleaning cycle, as long as the sanitary rinse mode is also activated. THIS MACHINE SUCKS! ALLWAYS HAS & ALLWAYS WILL! Do something fun with your $600-$700 because spending it on this machine will not be fun!

product_title: LG LDS4821ST 24" Stainless Steel Full Console Dishwasher - Energy Star
review_title: There is NOT a WORSE dishwasher out there!!!!
review_text: This is truly an awful dishwasher. It never has cleaned well. It has always left a white film on the dishes. I have had it for six years now and I have had it!!!. It started to not drain properly. There was always a pool of water when the wash was done. I took it out, and figured out that the little plastic box that controls the water level was covered in black mold!!!.It was disgusting to think that this has been building up since the day i purchased my DW. It is definitely not user error. Its the awful design. It is bound to happen to every single one over time. I cleaned out all the mold, replaced it, and now my DW is draining fine.What happened was that all the mold and gunk was keeping the bouyies from shutting the water off when it was supposed to.  I am in the process of looking for a new one. Definitely not LG.!!! Please stay away.!!!! I cant believe they are still selling this model on some sites. It also has started to make awful grinding noises after a year, and a cycle can easily take over 3 hours if you want your dishes somewhat clean. It is a wolf in sheeps clothing for sure. Looks great, but on the inside its a complete nightmare, with many design flaws. I just hope mine doent start a fire as I have heard many of them have.

product_title: LG LDS4821ST 24" Stainless Steel Full Console Dishwasher - Energy Star
review_title: diagnosis bad motor but said they don't do LG warranty work ...
review_text: Purchased this in Dec. 2012, June 2015 very loud noise started emerging while running.  Called local repair, diagnosis bad motor but said they don't do LG warranty work (out $85).  Called LG, got some "authorized" repair companies, came out, same diagnosis (out another $85) with a proposal to fix it at $428!!  It's $140 for the part.....  Called "customer service" back and they offered additional service companies - at the $85 service call rate, I can buy a new one soon.  Initiated a warranty claim, sent a copy of the receipt, which I had to go to the purchaser for and now LG claims they cannot read the PDF.  So fed up with this piece of junk and LG.  Buyer beware, wish I would have seen all these reviews for this specific model before I bought.  Repair people told me LG and Samsung are made in Korea, poor quality.  I also - have an LG side by side fridge, ice maker went within 12 months, repaired it myself.  Very disappointed!

product_title: LG LDS4821ST 24" Stainless Steel Full Console Dishwasher - Energy Star
review_text:
Purchased this dishwasher in 2009 from the the Home Depot. The dishwasher has done a good job washing and dying the dishes so we have not experienced the issues other people have commented about.

My main gripes about the dishwasher:
We intermittently received the OE error that corresponded to dishwasher not emptying water. After lots of troubleshooting I discovered the problem was with gunk getting stuck on a float that detects the water level in the tub. The dishwasher was draining fine but the float was not moving giving a wrong reading to the computer. The fix requires that you disassemble the plastic levels on the left side of the unit and clean them well.
We had an incident were significant amount of water started dripping from the dryer vent on the door. Looked online for help and identified the issue as having a clogged drain hose on the drying sistem. I fixed the issue by blowing an air can through the hose. A ball of paper gunk came out (I guess we washed something with the labels on).
The mounting brackets are flimsy and I have had to replace them because they failed (bended and cracked) with regular use. I finally decided to reinforce them with a thin metal plate.
The washing racks are severely corroded after 6 years of use. The corners and other parts are just falling apart.

These are all issues that I would consider unacceptable for a $500 dishwasher with 6 years of use. Based on my bad experience with my cooking range (bad knobs) and the issues with the dishwasher I will not buy LG appliances again.

product_title: LG LDS4821ST 24" Stainless Steel Full Console Dishwasher - Energy Star
review_text:
I am fixing it again and happened to see the reviews of this model (LDS4821ST). Yes, I agree. Bought it in 2010.

It was never put together correctly which resulted in it stinking. My wife and I pulled it out and took it apart. Some part on the side was filled with black goop. After cleaning that it stopped stinking.

etc etc etc ...

Plus we have to wash the dishes before putting them in the dishwasher.

It is a bad dishwasher.

product_title: LG : LSC27931ST 26.5 cu. ft. Side-by-Side Refrigerator - Stainless Steel
review_text: We bought this unit 3 years ago and have had nothing but disappointment and aggravation.  There have been many service calls and they usually end with, "Well, that is just the way they are".  The ice make is the worst aspect,  Seemed clever to have it on the door as a space saver, but it works very poorly.  It is slow to make ice and can't keep up if we have only a couple of guests in the summer.  The feed clogs often because it freezes up because it is on the door, and when it finally breaks free it unleashes an avalanch of ice on the floor.  Not only is the maker crap the rest of the fridge ain't so hot either.  We have had the main computer replaced 3 times, and it will randomly decide it is not cold enough and freeze everything in the refridgerator compartment.  I will never buy another LG product.  This one is going to the dump to be replaced by a Samsung.

product_title: LG : LSC27931ST 26.5 cu. ft. Side-by-Side Refrigerator - Stainless Steel
review_text:
Absolutely the worst appliance that I have ever owned. Cons: Ice maker useless, condensation leaks from door down front panel, brain damaged computer (decides on it's own whether to make cubed or crushed), ice dispenser breaks when used for the purpose it was designed for (dispensing ice ) We replaced the very expensive ice dispenser and it promptly broke itself again; plastic chunks came out with the ice until it seized. Temperature control for the refrigerator has now malfunctioned for the second time. I will not call a repairman again, it's going out the door.

product_title: LG : LSC27931ST 26.5 cu. ft. Side-by-Side Refrigerator - Stainless Steel

product_title: LG : LSC27931ST 26.5 cu. ft. Side-by-Side Refrigerator - Stainless Steel
review_title: You can find a better product
review_text: I've had this fridge for a few years now and it has it issues.  The main one is the bottom crisper drawer top is made of a very cheap plastic that cracks with any weight on top of it. product_title: LG : LSC27931ST 26.5 cu. ft. Side-by-Side Refrigerator - Stainless Steel
review_title: Flap on ice maker door never worked; allowing warm ...
review_text: Flap on ice maker door never worked; allowing warm air up into the ice bin and causing jams.  After a couple of years, the water dispenser stopped working. DO NOT BUY.

product_title: LG : LSC27931SW Refrigerator
review_title: Great Refrigerator but weak on Ice and Water Dispenser
review_text:
PRO:

We have had no problems with the refrigerator or freezer. It offers generous and easy access storage of fresh and frozen items. As with our previous Kenmore side-by-side, we purchased this LG model due to the ice-maker in the door feature that provides more shelf space in the freezer.

CON: Ice-Maker

Unfortunately, the ice-maker is a big disappointment. It makes ice very slowly (about 6 cube every 12 hours). The "Ice Plus" feature will double production but still agonizingly slow, especially if you are preparing to entertain people. You should plan on stockpiling ice for a week in advance.

CON: Water Dispenser

The water dispenser is very handy but has a serious dribbling problem. You will need to learn to keep your cup or pitcher under the dispenser for 1-2 seconds after you release the dispense button or you will end up with a wet floor. Additionally, evidently the water reservoir is much smaller than previous units we have owned. Except for a few glasses early in the day, the water will be lukewarm. The $50 filter does a good job making our local water more drinkable. The flow of the water became noticeably slower at about 5 months, but $10/mo for filtered water is still more economical than bottled water.

product_title: LG : LSC27931SW Refrigerator
review_text: LG fridge quits cooling after just 3 1/2 years of service, rusts before that around door water and ice dispenser. Icemaker flap would not close consistently so ice came out from time to time and fell on the floor. After four attempts to contact LG customer service about such a poor quality product, no success. "Live chat" had no record of email sent through company web site. Email provided by "live chat" customer service rep returned. Attemps to call on the phone ended in a "do loop." The service/repair number also ended in a "do loop".  LG poor product quality and no customer service! Buyer beware - LG does not stand behind its appliances or take care of customers!

product_title: WED7500VW Electric Dryer with 3.8 cu. ft. Capacity, 11 Drying Cycles
review_text:
The first Whirlpool WED7500VW dryer I received was defective. The drum was mis-cast and couldn't make a revolution without scraping and catching clothes due to a large gap along one side of the drum. How something like that could be shipped, or even produced is amazing. Returning it was a little unnerving because everything had to go through all parties involved, the original point of purchase store, the subcontracted repair people from Whirlpool and Whirlpool itself. In the end, we were shipped a new dryer but we were also shipped a myriad of repair parts which we're told will be picked up from the side of our front steps (no pickup date or time can be given). It's been over a week and no one has come yet and it's tedious to keep bringing them in and out each day, not to mention the security risk.

Anyway, the new dryer actually works which is such a relief. On the other hand, it's way noisier than any previous dryer I've ever used. It has an unpleasant raspy sound and does only an adequate job drying. I need to shift the clothes to make sure everything dries evenly - more so than on other dryers I've had. So I would have given this dryer two stars except Whirlpool produced it in such a small 24"W package so I bumped it up to three stars. On the other hand, if I had it to do over again, I might look into a dryer from another manufacturer, even if it didn't end up matching my washer. I would caution people against buying either this dryer or the companion washer reconditioned or used. Quality is not awe inspiring.

product_title: WED7500VW Electric Dryer with 3.8 cu. ft. Capacity, 11 Drying Cycles
review_text: Clothes come out terribly wrinkled even when the load is small, cycles don't fully dry loads always takes 2 full cycles, the drum capacity is miniscule. Parts feel cheap, plastic handle feels like it's going to break off when you open the door.

product_title: Whirlpool : GD5DHAXVY Refrigerator
review_text: Just bought this - works very well, and even I can adjust the temperature, etc. controls. Purified water, easy access ice cubes. I especially like the large size and that Whirlpool has the lowest repair rate for all major brand refrigerators.

product_title: Whirlpool : GD5DHAXVY Refrigerator
review_title: How do you keep the thing clean?
review_text: The stainless finish seems to pick up fingerprints like a magnet. Can anyone recommend a cleaner/sealant?

product_title: Whirlpool : GD5DHAXVY Refrigerator
review_text:
I happened to acquire this fridge for FREE with the purchase of a new condo. Let me tell you something... I've owned many refrigerators in my day, for the price, this one is the bee's knees. It is flawless except that it's not REAL stainless steel. It has satin finished aluminum doors, but has the look of stainless steel.
I'm not sure if all the models have the same features, but my model(ends in 04) has a crushed ice feature and a neat-o blue light I leave on all night. I feel like the prince of Norway when I ask my friends, "Cubes or crushed?".
The filters are $40, but being from L.A., I would pay twice that to be able to drink my tap water. I fill my empty water bottle every morning with the water from my fridge (which save me $1.75 a day). I use the water for coffee, recipes, cooking pasta, my cats, and even filling my fishtank. The filter in this bad boy removes a lot of crap my fish don't need.
As I said to a fellow Whirlpool GD5DHAXVY owner, to clean the "faux stainless" doors get the ZEP stainless steel cleaner. Not ONLY does it smell like lemons, it works like gang-busters on your entire kitchen.
So... DO IT!!! Pay the $1100 for this kick-ass fridge. Your friend will love you more.

product_title: Whirlpool : GD5DHAXVY Refrigerator
review_text: I can't express enough how disappointed I am in this refrigerator.  In less than a year, we had a catastrophic failure and the entire cooling unit had to be replaced.  Fortunately, it was still under the manufacturers warranty at the time.  Now 3 days after the manufacturers warranty expired (and less than two months after having the first failure repaired), we have the SAME failure.  I couldn't be more disappointed and upset with this horrible refrigerator.  Complete waste of money and time!

product_title: LG : LSC27931SB 26.5 cu. ft. Side-by-Side Refrigerator - Black
review_text:
This is by far the worst refrigerator my family has owned in thirty years. It was so bad that we thought about replacing it frequently, throughout the whole four years of our ownership. Now we are celebrating because we did; yesterday it just died for good, nearly ruining our Christmas groceries. Fortunately, we had taken in a back-up frige, expecting something like this.

The spectacular problems that we experienced are corroborated by many other spirited negative reviews at the LG website, especially the most frequent ones, which represent the owners who have had the product for some time; see http://reviews.lg.com/7676/MD00000251/reviews.htm. LG refused to provide support for the device, and it caused us to commit to avoid the brand for all our future appliances:
(1) Ice unfroze and refroze into single block, jamming device or stopping the whole frige
(2) Water constantly leaked from bottom of frige, and black surface rusted in multiple places (see photo for one)
(3) Cooling periodically stopped working--food would spoil and frige had to be "defrosted"

product_title: Whirlpool : GI5FSAXVY Refrigerator
review_text:
Let's put it this way, I had a Whirlpool double wide before and bought in to this French door stuff and will never buy one again. Please make sure you consider how you will access your frozen foods. Also consider how much space will be taken in order to get ice and water out the front door. Also note that you have to open both doors most of the time to access most of your foods. Here are the issues with this model:
1) Although the manual shows a onetime leveling mechanism through the wheels, in actuality you have to level it through leveling feet. Thus once you have it level you will have to unlevel it to move the refrigerator to clean. That is a pain and sucks they didn't correct their manual to show it.
2) The website graphics show a dairy bin, but in actuality you don't get one and you can't purchase one. Now we drop our butter in their soda holder which is useless anyways.
3) They give you this soda metal slide out rack that is at an angle for the sodas to roll out. The problem is that we don't have a need for two soda holders. You can't use the rack for anything else except sodas based on it design. We use it now to sloppily hold yogurts.
4) Although this is Energy Star, they have to put a dehumidify heater between the two French doors in order for moisture not to form on the outside of the refrigerator. This is a feature you turn on if needed and it only took a day to realize I have to keep this heater on all the time, so much for energy savings.
5) They use the Ice maker as a way to distribute the cooling into the refrigerator. Unfortunately things are so ergonomically tight that all the milk and water products freeze. The solution has been to raise the freezer temperature up from 0 to 4 degrees and seems to solve the problem. However, it is really just a poor design issue.
I am really disappointed in the poor design of the Whirlpool product and also in the fundamentals of French doors.

product_title: Whirlpool : GI5FSAXVY Refrigerator
review_title: No problems, just a great fridge
review_text: I haven't ever had any freezing of liquids in the refrigerator compartment. I've heard people complain about it, but all my foods have been the correct temperature, and I place my milk and juices right next to the ice maker. Yes, you do have to bend down to get items from the freezer bin, but that's not a symptom of this fridge, it's ANY bottom chest freezer. However, I've found that this refrigerator style allows me to place wider items in it (like a pizza box) with relative ease. With my old side-by-side, everything felt cramped. I've noticed the humidity problem around the door seals during the summer time if my house thermostat is set high, but the humidity button fixes that and I don't really notice any increase in my electricity costs. I think people are just splitting hairs when finding problems with this fridge. I've had it for 2 years now and it runs great. The shelves are sturdy, the soda bin is really convenient, and the door shelves are great for condiments and other items you want easy access to. They can actually hold Costco size mayonnaise and other items.

product_title: Whirlpool : GI5FSAXVY Refrigerator
review_text:
I really really dislike this refrigerator. We owned a Samsung french door fridge with the pull out drawer and it was awesome! This fridge is very poorly designed.

1. Everything freezes! I have to keep the temp at 42 degrees.
2. The fridge light only works if the right door is open which is very annoying and dysfunctional.
3. The can coke dispenser requires that you put the actual can box in the refrigerator for it to actually function, which is a waste of space and looks tacky.
4. The refrigerator inside is poorly designed, which does not provide enough space.
5. The freezer is tiny!
6. The ice maker does not have an option for crushed ice and the dispenser is not tall enough to fit a normal size glass so my water always spills when I get water because I have to lean it back so much.
7.The freezer drawer will not stay open by itself and the top shelf is really hard to pull out. The bottom is completely wire too which looks really bad.

I would never purchase this refrigerator.

product_title: GE : GFSL6KKXLS Refrigerator
review_text:
This refrigerator looks interesting, but be careful.
We bought a GE side-by-side refrigerator about five years ago. Since then we have had repeated problems with it, and had to call the GE repairman nine different times. The doors had to be replaced once. The ice maker was replaced four times, one time when it started breaking up and mixing shards of plastic with the ice. We could have been killed.
This last time the ice maker flooded the kitchen within two hours. We called GE for repairs and the repairman came several days later. He installed a new ice maker and said everthing was fine. He turned on the water and said "All set to go." When we checked a few hours later, there was no ice, the kitchen was flooding, and sheets of water were coming down from the ceiling in our rec room. The GE repairman never turned the valve of the water line on completely, so it leaked far far worse than it ever had before. Knowing to turn water valves completely should be Repair 101. I called GE back at 3:15; the operator said she would e-mail an immediate request to the repair people in our area. A taped message contacted us some five days later. By that time we had bought a new, very different brand.
I can understand a product having problems. But when the factory authorized repairmen make the problems far, far worse, that manufacturer should be put out of business.

review_text: All is good

product_title: Samsung : DV448AEW 7.4 cu. ft. Super Capacity Electric Dryer - Neat White
review_text:
1.0 out of 5 stars This dryer will quadruple your work!, May 31, 2011
By Judicious Jude - See all my reviews
This review is from: Samsung Front Load Dryer DV448AE
