The sheets and blankets end up dry, but wrinkled beyond hope. I've never been so disappointed or frustrated with a major appliance purchase.
I would not recommend this dryer to anyone!

product_title: Samsung : WF448AAP 4.5 cu. ft. Steam Front Load Washer - Stainless Platinum
review_title: Best washer/dryer we have ever owned!!!
review_text:
We purchased the matching dryer to go with this washer and they are fantastic! They are quiet, fast, and energy efficient. We purchased the drawer bases which give you more storage and raise the machines up waist level so you don't have to bend down when loading and unloading.

The only issue we had was with the brass "Y" included with the steam dryer for the cold water faucet. It leaked, but Samsung sent a replacement the next day!

We gave away an 8 year old set of Maytags that worked, but were both noisy...good ridence! These are so quiet and do a better job cleaning and drying our clothes than any set we have owned before. We have had GE, Kenmore, and Maytag. All good products, but these Samsung products are so far superior, it isn't even funny!

And don't let the "NASA" designed controls fool you, they are very easy to use with preprogrammed settings (e.g. whites, towels, perm press, etc.). And the steam in both the washer and dryer allow you to remove wrinkles and sanitize your clothes. This washer also has the ability to remove 99% of bacteria in cold water using silver ions.

Don't let our 5 star rating and the other person's 1 star rating make up your mind. We researched Consumer Reports and other web sites and read lots of consumer opinions before making our decision. Plus you get an energy credit on your taxes for purchasing these Samsung products!

One recommendation, purchase the extended warranty as these are high tech with digital controls. Ours are protected for 5 years along with a "lemon" warranty. If the other consumer who gave 1 star had purchased this, they could have already replaced the defective unit or got their money back. Although we are suspicious seeing that Samsung give a 1 year warranty and they claim they can't get Samsung to do anything about their washer...so do your research before writing off this product. We highly recommend this washer although it was the most expensive one we researched...worth every dollar!

product_title: Samsung : WF448AAP 4.5 cu. ft. Steam Front Load Washer - Stainless Platinum
review_title: Extremely low vibration and noise - great washer
review_text: Purchased this washer and matching electric dryer to replace brand new Whirlpool 9400 set we owned for less than 2 weeks.  The Whirlpool washer vibrated so bad I spent hours getting it perfectly level to no avail.  I even contacted Whirlpool who suggested that I re-inforce my laundry room floor with a seperate 3/4 inch thick sheet of plywood.  My laundry room floor is on the 1st level, linolium covered 3/4 plywood set on 2x10 joists 16 inch centered.  In other words, its quite solid.  The washer had been setup professionally, shipping plugs removed, leveled.  But when it went to high spin mode - watch out.  It vibrated the entire 20x20 floor. The Whirlpool merchant agreed to take back the Whirlpool units and the wife and I purchased these Samsung units.  The Samsung units were installed in the same laundry room without any modification to the floor.  They work great.  Extremely low vibration and noise.  My house no longer shakes.  The Samsung washer feet are different than the Whirlpool feet -  the Samsung feet grip the floor like a gecko.  Also, the Samsung washer incorporates "Vibration Reduction Technology" in all of its washers.  This VRT combined with the grippy feet really work.  The dryer works well also.  Both units are very solidly built and aesthetically pleasing.

product_title: Samsung : WF448AAP 4.5 cu. ft. Steam Front Load Washer - Stainless Platinum
review_text:
We have to prop open the door after washing to help prevent a mildew smell. Even with propping the door open, this this washer builds up a mildew smell over time. Mold grows behind the rubber gasket, so you have to pull that back every once in a while, and wipe out sludgy black lint. There are products on the market to help clean mildewy front loading washing machines, but they don't get out that sludge. The whole reason to buy a front loader is convenience, and I personally think this is less convenient than pulling clothes out of a top loader after every wash.

This is a problem with a lot of front loaders, but at least one other brand (Maytag) is including fans to help dry them.

I also would like to point out that this model has Vibration Reduction Technology-- but I am not sure what is reduced, my washing machine vibrates LIKE CRAZY. (BTW, this washer comes with protective blocks screwed to the back of them that you have to take off. When I complained about the vibrations they said to make sure those were taken off. I said, they were, and they basically said that's all they knew to tell me.)

product_title: Samsung : WF448AAP 4.5 cu. ft. Steam Front Load Washer - Stainless Platinum
review_title: Great when they work, expensive when they break
review_text: Unfortunately I love these machines when they work, and hate them when they don't.  I have had mine almost 5 years and am getting ready to put a 3rd heating element in it at $400 each time.  I have also had to fix the barrel before because it broke a wheel trying to dry bedding.  You will love them when they work, but curse the extra $ you put into them.  I had my last washer and dryer for 12 years before I had to repair anything. They are too expensive to replace, but way too expensive to repair as well.  Samsung customer service is a joke.  You are buying them at your own risk.

product_title: Samsung : WF448AAP 4.5 cu. ft. Steam Front Load Washer - Stainless Platinum
review_title: Just plain awful--and SAMSUNG knows it!  STAY AWAY FROM SAMSUNG APPLIANCES
review_text:
We bought this set of stainless steel junk on clearance from Sears against my better judgement. But the salesman pushed it so hard, and they didn't have the pedestals for the Kenmore set we wanted, so we gave it a try. Big Freaking Mistake! By the way, the matching dryer is just as big a piece of junk as the washer, but I will stick to this horrid mildew generator for right now. By the way, I have posted other negative reviews on this junk, but you can't find them any more. I suspect foul play.

First: From the very first load of clothes we have washed with this machine, NOTHING gets clean unless you use the 3.5 hour sanitize-and-extra-rinse with twice the soap and twice the fabric softener. Ok for towels, but not for clothes. I have tried everything. We have never ever left the doors closed on this machine because we were warned about that being the source of mildew. The machine was professionally installed and then professionally repaired twice and then re-leveled professionally and every time the installer told us we hadn't leveled the machine properly. Since the machine is on a level tile floor in a fairly expensive house, I don't think leveling is the problem.

We use the required "He" (I think it means "Low Effectiveness" soap. Only name brand. We use tide washing machine cleaner about once a month. That stuff is expensive, and of course, it is only a "temp fix". Now, I am almost 50 years old and I have NEVER IN MY LIFE HAD TO WASH A WASHING MACHINE. I have also never had a washing machine that didn't work for at least 10 years. And I for sure never paid over $1K for a washing machine of any type, but they have all performed better than this one in every way.

God forbid you put two sheets into this pile at the same time. They will turn into a stinky ball of mildewed cloth that will never ever dry. Blankets...you're talking about blankets? HAHAHAHAHA. You see, this thing, which supposedly has "VRT" will pound itself into the tile if you let it go and it becomes out of balance. I swear, I have seen it get out of balance with a load of socks. God forbid you have a load of towels in it. And here's the funny part--at one point in time the technician that came out to service it (for one broken part or another during its all-too-short warranty) told us the best way to get the towels not to stink was to stuff the machine full! DO NOT ATTEMPT THIS AT HOME UNLESS YOU ARE A TRAINED WASHING MACHINE WRESTLER!!!

There is a poorly-designed plastic door near the bottom left-had corner of the front of the machine that has a piece of stainless glued to the front of it. The first time I opened the door, one of the plastic pins broke, so the door just sort of sits in place now. The reason I opened this little hatch was to gain access to the "filter" because on about the third load of clothes, the machine stopped and said to check the filter because the unit was not draining. So I broke into the door, then had to pull the pin out of the 1/4" drain hose, and then sit there for however long it takes to fill buckets with a soda straw, only to still get laundry water all over when I removed the filter which had--I swear--ONE piece of string in it. However, when I dutifully reassembled the unit, it started working again. Now when I get the "not draining" alert, I just drain a cup or so of water from the soda straw and that seems to get it going again.

The soap dispenser tray is a joke. It has always felt flimsy, and sometimes the soap doesn't seem to want to leave the dish (admittedly, this is too rare to be the cause of every load of clothes being stinky). Did I mention we have to leave this door open as well as the front door of the machine to try to keep the mildew stink from recurring as fast?

Now, I am not an appliance mechanic. However, I have spent my entire adult life repairing electromechanical things, including very complex aircraft radar systems. I own an engineering company. I design and document complex things, which includes developing technical (instruction) manuals. I spent 20 years plus in USAF aircraft systems maintenance. Suffice to say, I can not only fix stuff, but I do read the literature that comes with it and I am generally able to solve problems. I also know a pile of junk when I see it. The saddest part is, I personally know two other people who have had the same exact issues with Samsung's garbage. And from what I have read, it is only a matter of time before this machine breaks terminally (pump housing attached to drum falls apart). Also, I have had the same exact experience as others with "my cycle" not working. If anyone could make this machine work, or could find workarounds for the problems, I think I could. And I would share that knowledge with everyone I could because, hey, 2500 bucks for a washer and dryer is enough for you to try everything. But there is no solution here without replacing the garbage.

I was going to write about the dryer, but suffice to say that it doesn't dry anything in any mode other than repeatedly running the manual dry setting for an hour. And yes, I clean the @#$! filter every time. And yes, my vent is clear to the outside of the house. The dryer is just junk too. It is, though, professionally leveled.

product_title: Samsung : WF448AAP 4.5 cu. ft. Steam Front Load Washer - Stainless Platinum
review_title: Worst washer I ever owned and Samsung has the worst customer service to match
review_text:
I bought this machine at one of the national big box stores while they had a "great" deal on it. The house was in the middle of a remodel so I stored the machine in the corner of the basement while all the various activities were going on.

This let me know that the machine did not wash the cloths well at all.
If that was not bad enough, after about 10 total loads this brand new a rather expensive Samsung stopped working. Looks like maybe a motor problem. Calling Samsung was like calling another planet, and one name WeDontCare. I live in Seattle and they did not have a single technician in the city.
Disconnected the Samsung, plugged in the old 1977 Kenmore and based on my experience with their support I will never buy anything made by Samsung.

Offered to send a repair person to fix machine that isn't broken!?! product_title: Samsung : DV328AEW 7.3 cu. ft. Super Capacity Electric Dryer - Neat White
review_text:
Only had our dryer about 17 mos and now having to replace the heating element (which, through Sears will cost approx. $74.00). While researching, discovered that many customers who bought this dryer are all having the same problems and early into ownership : heating element going out, belts falling off or breaking, thermostat breaking.

product_title: Samsung : DV448AEP 7.4 cu. ft. Super Capacity Electric Dryer - Stainless Platinum
review_text:
We purchased our set with a manufacturing date of 01.31.10.

I was a bit nervous about selecting these machines to purchase after reading a few complaints (overall, there weren't too many) about clothes not being cleaned, an occasional mechanics problem requiring resolution, noise, etc. and had decided the machines were either 'love it' or 'hate it.' I took the plunge anyhow and am so thrilled I did!

After owning the machines for a brief time, I can proclaim I'm definitely in the 'LOVE IT!' camp! Further, without wishing to offend anyone, I will even imply people who are in the 'hate it!' camp 1) perhaps have not read their instruction manuals thoroughly so they know how to properly use and care for their machines as well as understand their limitations, or 2) perhaps aren't using the machines properly. There seem to be some service / part replacement complaints from people, but those seem centered around models with earlier manufacturing dates than the set I own.

I have never been able to get my whites this clean without bleach or OxiClean or some other whitening agent, so I was truly impressed with the Silvercare feature (especially after wondering if it might be just hype and marketing). Silvercare really works, and works well! I can confidently sanitize things without worrying about using a great deal of resources other than cold water to do so, and ditching the bleach is a wonderful thing - I really don't think I'll need to use it anymore!

The steam features have already helped remove dirt and stains my last washer could never remove, leaving me quite impressed, and the refresh cycle on the dryer is a real boon when there isn't time to iron or quick-wash. I love being able to deep-steam more heavily soiled items like my son's soccer gear and have them come out looking pristine!

These machines are every bit as quiet as advertised - I can barely hear the washer (properly leveled) operating, and this allows me to do laundry at my convenience even at nighttime without disturbing the rest of the household. The dryer is dramatically quieter than my last one as well, and the lack of overall laundry noise is fantastic!!

I love the beauty of the machines - the polished understated glamor of the platinum set is fantastic. I'm very pleased to have them seen instead of feeling like I have to hide my washer and dryer from visitors who might enter the laundry room.

Although definitely not inexpensive, these machines are well worth the price considering the load of amazing features they utilize and the increased capacity of the washer and dryer drums. I'm very much looking forward to saving on our utility costs because of them! I would heartily recommend these beauties to my friends and family, and encourage anyone out there still on the fence to buy them with confidence!! I love them, and am confident if you read the manuals and use them properly you will too!!! =)

product_title: Samsung : DV448AEP 7.4 cu. ft. Super Capacity Electric Dryer - Stainless Platinum
review_text:
There is a chronic design flaw with this dryer (which I've had for
18 months).

That flaw is the design of lint screen, which is installed vertically.
Yeah, exhaust flows through it and lint is caught, but when you remove
the screen, gravity causes the lint to fall off the screen and into
the chamber below the screen. Laden with moisture, the lint tends to
mat there. Lint also flows around the screen, which has no rubber
gasket to impede this. This design virtually guarantees that lint
will escape in great quantities to the duct line and (due to the
moisture content, especially with these steam dryers) line your
exhaust ducting.

This lint then has three 90-degree turns before it is expelled out the
vent on the back of the machine.

Have one of these? UNPLUG THE MACHINE, then take your exhaust
duct loose from your wall duct and see how much lint is matted
inside it. Pull the duct from the machine (this is easy) and
see how much lint is inside the machine.

Need to clean it out? Cleaning out under the lint screen is a pain.
Get a vacuum with a nozzle. The nozzle will likely not come close to
fitting down into that chamber. I got about 2' of 1/2" flexible
tubing and stuck one end into the vacuum nozzle and then I could
snake that down and clean the chamber out pretty well. This also
worked well cleaning out with the duct assembly pulled from the
machine.

You can also take the top off, which only means removing the two
inner screws (not all six screws) and then sliding it off. You
can vacuum that out. The control board is mounted here and
is easy to take it loose so you vacuum all the lint off of it.

I'd appreciate hearing from others on their experience with lint
buildup in these areas to see if you're having the same problem.
I'm figuring on needing to clean this expensive dryer out twice
a year. I pulled a plastic grocery bagful of lint out of
this thing.

We had Kenmore basic dryer for years before this and NEVER had
lint buildup ANYTHING like this. Ugh.

product_title: Samsung : DV448AEP 7.4 cu. ft. Super Capacity Electric Dryer - Stainless Platinum
review_text:
This dryer is okay except for one serious problem: it lacks a reversing motor. Because the drying chamber is so big, large items like king sheets, comforter covers, and blankets roll themselves up into a knot within minutes. This means you have to constantly babysit the dryer, unwinding and repositioning these items and restarting so that they will dry completely.

I consider this a serious design flaw on a dryer at this price point.

product_title: Samsung : DV448AEP 7.4 cu. ft. Super Capacity Electric Dryer - Stainless Platinum
review_text:
Thumbs down. I've tried to like this dryer for 17 months. I have two complaints.

My first complaint is that the drum is too big. We purchased this size, the largest size, so we could easily wash king size bedding. It is not so easy. Everything rolls up into a ball and everything inside that ball stays wet. I imagine I've wasted more electricity running the cycle over and over again, while opening the door constantly to untie my laundry, allowing it to dry. The only other option is to dry one sheet or blanket at a time, which is ridiculous for a machine this expensive.

My second complaint is that the lint remover does not work. Once each week, I have to climb through our flowerbed to clear the exhaust so that our clothes will dry and the unit is not a fire hazard. Literally, I pull a fist full of lint from the exhaust hose each week. We never had this problem with our old dryer.

If I could make the choice again, I would not choose this dryer. Love the washer, but not the dryer.

product_title: Samsung : DV448AEP 7.4 cu. ft. Super Capacity Electric Dryer - Stainless Platinum
review_text:
I, too, am experiencing the lint trap problem. All of my clothes come out of the dryer covered in large clumps of lint, and when I try to remove the lint trap to clean it, the lint falls into the trap compartment. I've taken the advice of one of the previous reviewers and looked into getting the lint trap for model DV330AEB.

On Samsungparts.com, I searched for the lint trap for model DV330AEB and part DC61-01521A was returned as the search result. However, it is described as a lint trap that is compatible with many of their dryer models, including DV330AEB and DV448AEP. Does anyone know if this is the supposedly newer, better lint trap that may fix this problem, or is it the lint trap that comes with the DV448AEP?

product_title: Samsung : DV448AEP 7.4 cu. ft. Super Capacity Electric Dryer - Stainless Platinum
review_title: Good dryer, I like the steam
review_text:
Good dryer. I esp. like the steam feature. I use this setting with Woolite dry cleaning cloths for my dry clean only cloths. The steam helps the dry cleaning cloth penetrate into fabric and remove odors. Saving me lots of money by reducing my dry cleaning. Now I can dry clean at home every other time.

The auto sensor works well.

product_title: Samsung : DV448AEP 7.4 cu. ft. Super Capacity Electric Dryer - Stainless Platinum
review_text: Recently purchased returned (floor model) top of the line Samsung washer/dryer combo.. new condition, full warranty, etc from Lowe's.  Purchased extended warranty program as well.  Dryer came w/o owners manual.  Filled out necessary forms and provided proof of purchase to Samsung.  Received a call today that they will not provide owners manual, but we can purchase one from parts vendor for $19.95.  They also informed me that I can download one online.  Incredible.  Spent over $2000 on appliances, and can't even get a owners manual.  Had read reviews that Samsung customer service is lacking.  Now I know why.  Probably the last Samsung product I'll ever own..

product_title: Samsung : DV448AEP 7.4 cu. ft. Super Capacity Electric Dryer - Stainless Platinum
review_text:
I am NOT HAPPY with this dryer! I've owned it not quite 2.5 yrs and the heating element has broken again. Less than 3 months ago, we replaced it and found the machine and exhaust tubing full of lint. Now today, my dryer is not heating again. I shouldn't have to disconnect the exhaust tubing every month to clean that out since I faithfully clean out the lint trap every load.

product_title: Samsung : DV448AEP 7.4 cu. ft. Super Capacity Electric Dryer - Stainless Platinum
review_title: Good until NOW 3 years is too short
review_text: I've had my Samsung DV448 dryer and as many of the other reviews have stated have had a major lint problem.  The unit worked fine for 3 years and now has started to fail quiet often.  First to go was the tension wheel that keeps the drive belt tight.  One day it started making a grinding and squealing sound.  When I removed to exhaust duct to gain access to the underside of the drum the entire area was coated in a thick layer of lint.  I wrapped the exhaust tube with high temp metal tape to help seal the junction better and that seemed to help.  About 3 weeks later the heater element died.  I chose to replace the whole heater assembly instead of just the coils so I wouldn't have to pull it out in 3 more weeks to replace a thermostat sensor.  Like I said before I've had this unit for just over 3 years and believe this is way too many failures in such a short time.

product_title: Samsung : DV448AEP 7.4 cu. ft. Super Capacity Electric Dryer - Stainless Platinum
review_title: Continual repairs and poor customer service with Samsung
review_text: Purchased this dryer for almost $1200 and have replaced belts, shocks, has had grinding noise and continues to have lint build up even though the lint is removed every time it is used. The drum cracked after only five years and Samsung refuses to help us with fixing the dryer because we are out of warranty. We did purchase an extended warranty but that only last for two years. We do not recommend this dryer unless you want to have continual maintenance problems.

product_title: Samsung : DV448AEP 7.4 cu. ft. Super Capacity Electric Dryer - Stainless Platinum
review_title: Lint filter horrible compared to the Whirlpool top of cabinet long filter, but the dryer is otherwise OK
review_text: I purchased my 448 washer and dryer 9/2009 and haven't had any problems until 3/2015 when the heating element wire broke. I took the dryer apart after find help on-line and discovered that the entire bottom of the dryer was filled with a 1/2" layer of lint in addition to burnt lint inside the heating element assembly and the assembly socket on the back of my the dryer. I suspect the lint leakage is coming from the thin foam wrapped around the end of the exhaust tube that slips into the blower housing. Unsure of how to remedy this other than metal tape if I can reach it. I sliced my finger open on a razor sharp cross bar near the bottom.  I had been exhausting my dryer in a dryer lint box and with a sock on the end. Both need to be cleaned often as they are covered in lint. I never hooked up the steam, fearing corrosion or other failure. Meanwhile, I am reinstalling the 4" metal duct under the house with a booster fan and slow bending right angle elbows for less restricted air flow. By the way, Samsung support is like talking to a wall. That's another story!

product_title: Samsung : DV448AEP 7.4 cu. ft. Super Capacity Electric Dryer - Stainless Platinum
review_title: Lint can easily escape from the lint compartment -- and from the ...
review_text:
DO NOT BUY!!! --- MAJOR FIRE HAZARD!!!
The Samsung DV448AEP dryer is a poorly designed machine. Lint can easily escape from the lint compartment -- and from the poorly designed dryer drum -- and onto the bottom portion of the dryer where the electrical components, the heating element, and the motor are located. With a 12-month or less buildup of escaped lint a fire can occur - as did in our case five times. Four of the five times we called a repair tech referred by our warranty. The repair techs explained the lint buildup was the cause of the fires -- but - what they did not explain was the lint build up was due to the poorly designed lint compartment. Shocking! They're in the business of being able to detect poor design. And not one repair tech said - "Hey - major amounts of lint - like this - should not be located in this bottom area." It wasn't until our fifth fire - when we took the dryer apart ourselves that we discovered the design flaws. Any idiot can see where the lint is escaping. Why the machine was designed this way is beyond me. Why no one has contacted us about a recall -- or to tell us this machine is a fire hazard is beyond me. Why professional experienced repair techs did not know about this issue - or couldn't figure it out by looking at the machine is beyond me. Samsung should notify every consumer who has purchased this machine and offer a fix - or a newly redesigned dryer. You cannot tell me they don't know about this issue. Do not buy this machine. Or if you do. Don't go to sleep - or leave your house while it's operating - or you may wake up to - or come home to a burned down home. Good luck!
We purchased this machine 10/18/2009 - with four fire repairs over the first six years - the last fire in the seventh year of ownership.

product_title: GE : GSHL5KGXLS 25.4 cu. ft. Side by Side Refrigerator - Clean Steel Look
review_text: We purchased this refrigerator several months ago when the one in our new Coop broke down.  We did not shop around, but my husband and I both felt that "you really can't go wrong with GE" as we have purchased GE refrigerators and stoves before when we upgraded other properties we owned.  Boy were we wrong.  As soon as the refrigeator arrived we noticed that the quality was poor.  Where do I begin????  there is an awkward seam down the back of the fridge that is not even centered and looks as though someone glued two pieces together.  The clean steel scratches easily and if you look at at the top of the refrigerator you will note that the steel was applied as a sheet that covers only the front of the door and does not extend all the way to the edges (poor workmanship).  The water/ice dispenser sticks some times.  The glass inside the refrigerator is terrible quality and scratches easily.  The same goes for the door compartments.  Really, the quality is so bad that it makes me angry to think that we paid $1,750 total including taxes and delivery.  I would have gladly paid more for a quality product.  Again, we have owned other GE refrigerators that did not have these problems.

product_title: GE : GSHL5KGXLS 25.4 cu. ft. Side by Side Refrigerator - Clean Steel Look
review_text:
Last summer we decided to replace our very old freezer-on-top refrigerator with a side-by-side model that had the same storage capacity. After looking at many units in the store, we decided on this GE model based on size, price, and convenience features. We had it set up in our home on delivery with water line installation to the ice maker/water dispenser.

Pluses: it keeps food reasonably cold/frozen, it looks nice and is easy to clean, it is not loud, it was reasonably priced
Minuses: we can not fit as much in the refrigerator as we could on our old model; the drawers are oddly spaced and smaller than they appear (not as deep as you expect looking at the unit);the ice maker can't decide if it wants to crush or cube the ice, regardless of what setting we choose; you can't fit much in the refrigerator, it is not as deep as it appears as there is a LOT of 'insulating' trim; a GIANT dome light on top prevents putting anything taller than a standard gallon of milk on the top shelf; the door design with the soda can tray is ridiculous - another standard door bin would be much more useful.

If you have a large family and need a lot of refrigerator storage, I would look at other options. I wish I had gotten the french door model with the freezer drawer on the bottom. Live and learn!

product_title: GE : GSHL5KGXLS 25.4 cu. ft. Side by Side Refrigerator - Clean Steel Look
review_text: I bought this fridge through Sears seeing that they had it on sale. I am really happy with my purchase. I was skeptical at first after reading about the loud sounds that others said it made. It does make a loud sound like for 2 seconds randomly then it stops. I think it has something to do with the ice maker. I love the look and space I got with this fridge. If you see it at a good price then don't hesitate to get it. Oh my biggest draw back was the size. It was really hard to fit in the elevator and through my entrance door, but by the grace of God it did. Best Christmas gift I got this year.

product_title: GE : GSHL5KGXLS 25.4 cu. ft. Side by Side Refrigerator - Clean Steel Look
review_text:
I bought this model fridge about a year ago from Home Depot during
the appliance rebate nonsense paid for by your federal tax dollars.
Replaced a fridge that my parents had bought back in 1974, a old
2 door side by side Sears Kenmore. There was nothing wrong with the Kenmore,
it was still working. But I was getting tired of looking at it.. laugh.

I have seen comments from others here and elsewhere that this
thing makes too much noise. I can't say I'm bothered at all. Yes,
it does make more sounds than my other fridge had but it is doing
more. Some exotic cycling and fans popping on here and there. I suppose
if I wanted to sleep next to the fridge it might bother me, however it
is in the kitchen. NOT A PROBLEM. I can't hear any absurd loud noises.
Maybe I'm lucky.

Next, the ice maker. I've heard complaints on other sites back a year
ago when researching GE fridges of this general type and model range. People
complaining about the ice maker 'spewing ' ice out all over the place and making a mess.

THe only thing I can figure is those people are trying to get the ice dispenser
to toss ice in a small mouth glass or are failing to hold the glass close to the
dispenser chute. One will want to use a wide mouth glass or container. If ya have
to put ice in some small glass just keep a cheap SOLO type brand plastic
glass around to dispense ice into. No mess. No problem.
As for what the Ice Dispenser does. It is rather slow to dispense ice, but it works.

This model can dispense just lumps of ice (oblong half ovoid sliivers about 1/3-1/2 a inch thick
each) or it can 'crush' them so you have semi crushed ice. The crushing mechanism isn't
the best one might expect or desire. Sometimes larger nearlyi uncrushed bits of ice
arrive in your container. Overall it crushes good enough for me.

Water dispenser. Works. NOt as ice cold as some might want. CHilled fairly well.
If I want ice cold, I put ice in my water.

Water filter. I've yet to replace mine. Had it for a year now. No issues yet. YMMV as
I suppose my water supply, municipal, is pretty clean however our water has horrible chlorine smell.
The filter is still removing that so until it fails to do so I'll just leave the old one in.
Damn things are insane expensive. I will probably use the bypass on the one in the fridge when
it fails and buy a external to place in line that has sanely priced cartridges.

How well does it freeze and cool? It has been fine since I had it. No issues. I keep mine near max
cold on the settings. Freezer is somewhere below 10 degrees F on average (measured) and around 38-42 degrees F
in the refrigerator section as measured on the middle shelves.

Cleaning. Easy to keep this fake stainless clean. IT is not stainless it is a satin brushed steel finish with some
coating. Fingerprints do not show as easily. Nice feature.

Inside cleaning. I find this fridge much easier to clean than that ancient Kenmore from 74. No weird
seams to catch 'goop'. Nice glass shelves.

Shelf adjustment. Not as flexible as much pricer units but there are ways to move shelving around.
Good enough for my needs.

Freezer has some adjustable shelving too, door panels can be moved if you wish or removed. (pockets in door)
Pizza? no problem If you buy frozen large pizza you can store them vertically on a lower shelf. I can fit 6 for sure
with no issue on that shelf. I have seen other reviewers complain about that. I guess they never thought to move two
of the shelves and simply put the pizzas in vertical rather than trying to jam them in horizontal. LAughs.

There is a lower basket that one can slide in and out. I find it more annoying than useful but I leave it in.
Handy for dumping bags of stuff in on the freezer side that one doesn't use often or just for 'overflow'.

All the shelves on the fridge side and freezer side can slide out a few inches for those that have need of that.
To remove them is not too difficult.

One major complaint I've seen others mention is the crazy arse large dome light.
I agree. It takes up so much room it can be a challenge fitting big bottles of whatever on the top shelf. I had to lower
the top shelf to help with that issue. I'm tempted to break out the hack saw and 'fix' the issue but I'll save
that for some day in the future. Maybe I'll take a pic and post it. The dome assembly was some poor design work.
I'll say this for it, lights it up well.

Doors seem well made for modern area junk. Seals on the doors are still sealing a year later.

Overall. No complaint whatsoever.

Oh, as an aside. The guys that delivered my fridge had the task of taking the old one away to be recycled. They were
grunting and huffing to get the old one out. I do not knnow what it weighed but it was FAR MORE heavier than the new one.
I'd guess the new one is 1/4'th as heavy as the old one was.
Same capacity about.
Now the question is. Will this one still be working in 38 years? Hah.

For you kids today, we used to build things that lasted.
I only replaced it because the feds were willing to pay me 500 dollars to replace the old one if I proved I recycled my old one.
And I was tired of looking at it. In all those years that Kenmore, to the best of my knowledge, had never seen a
single repair man nor had any parts fail. However it did have a wonky thermostat that we learned to 'not touch'.

Oh, I looked up the old sales receipt my father had kept in records. He had paid 900 dollars back in 1974.
I paid with rebate just somewhere just below the 1000 mark. I'd say that is pretty amazing. I'll let a economics wiz
figure out what the old one would have cost factoring inflation. Quick guess.. around 3500 dollars.

hah.

product_title: Samsung : DV448AGP 7.4 cu. ft. Super Capacity Gas Dryer - Stainless Platinum
review_text:
I first purchased this unit about 7 months ago and if I wanted to dry a second load of clothes right after the first, it would shut off right away and not dry the clothes. product_title: Samsung : DV448AGP 7.4 cu. ft. Super Capacity Gas Dryer - Stainless Platinum
review_title: Large Capacity Promises, Low Capacity Quality
review_text:
We purchased this unit within the last year hoping its large capacity would help to clear up the log jam in our laundry room and for a while it did just that.

Lately the thing stopped working and we discovered a series of nasty surpises: A fried electornic control board, a broken drive belt, one of the four rollars that supports the drum having separated from its bearing and gone walkabout, and a torn drum seal. All this after a bit more than 6 months' family use.

We also found that although we live in an urban area with a lot of appliance repair shops, there are relatively few who work on Samsungs (and the one we found missed most of the problems). Then we discovered that parts for this thing do not seem to be stocked cy local sources and have to be ordered from Samsung direct.

With an unresponsive repair shop and laundry piling up, I went to replace the drive belt myself, which is when I learned that the design of this thing is such that you have to disassemble most of the unit to get to the motor. Not easy or cheap (and not helped by the fact that this product is new enough that most of the guidance for replacing Samsung belts on line do not apply to this dryer).

The final touch: the "stainless steel" trim on the front is already showing rust spots (the trim on the companion washer is worse: it is simply covered in rust)

Bottom line: we have a unit that though less than a year old looks like it is 10 years old and acts like it is 15. What a lemon!

product_title: Samsung : DV448AGP 7.4 cu. ft. Super Capacity Gas Dryer - Stainless Platinum
review_text: This dryer has been nothing but a total and complete hassle and waste of our money.  The dryer spins all of our sheets into a super tight little ball/roll and then shuts off.  Obviously, the entire middle of the roll is still wet, and we have to pull everything out, pull it apart, and then rearrange it when we put it back in the machine.  We have to do this 8-10 times per load.  I have called Samsung's customer service department a number of times.  The best suggestion they have has is to wash the sheets with wet, heavy towels. product_title: GE PSDS5YGXSS Profile 24.6 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel Counter Depth Side-By-Side Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_text:
We bought this fridge when our previous GE Artica side by side failed (unrepairable) after 10 years. At the time I seriously considered going with a different brand, but the feature we have become addicted to is the custom-cool drawer. If you are not familiar with this feature, it's basically a drawer that will chill wine and beer to 37 degrees in 15 minutes. There is no other fridge on the market with this feature, and in fact GE seems to be abandoning this feature as well since this is one of two fridges that still have it.

The nice things about this fridge that we enjoy:
1) The custom cool drawer
2) The sealed beverage pocket in the door that keeps drinks extra cool
3) It's nice looking
4) Digital temperature controls and monitoring (in C/F)

The things we don't like:
1) It died 7 months after we bought it. We lost a fridge full of whole-foods items. It took me two days to get hold of a person who could schedule repair, and it will take 2 weeks to fix it. Requires some special parts. The repair person told us to expect to perform the same repair every 2 years because it's prone to failing in this humid climate (austin, tx). The part is some sort of heater that prevents the cooling distribution from icing up. So in summary, I bought a fridge that will break every 2 years - as designed.
2) It's noisy, and I think this may have something to do with the icing up of the fans in the cool air distribution system. The fans sound like they are rubbing on something. It did this from the day we bought it (off and on).
3) The controls are aimlessly designed. In our old fridge, to turn on the custom cool drawer, you pressed a button once. In this new interface it takes 7 button presses. Home->options->refrigerator Options->Custom Cool->Express Chill->More time->OK. The person who designed this used engineering logic to organize the controls, they did not use any user interface design principles, and probably didn't test it with users.

Overall this would be a wonderful fridge if it didn't break down on us and ruin several hundreds of dollars of fresh food. If GE knows there are issues with the fridge, then it should be quick and easy to schedule an emergency appointment and that repair shop should have the parts in the truck. That would make it tolerable. Our current solution to this problem is to buy another fridge and place it in the garage as a backup fridge for when this happens again (and the GE repair man asserted that it would).

In Summary: Look elsewhere in you are in a humid climate.

review_title: DO NOT Buy Any GE Appliance & Avoid Frustration and Grief
review_text:

Two weeks ago the expensive GE refrigerator we purchased a few years ago quit cooling. So far we have had three GE technicians come for service and every time we call GE service, we have to wait another week for a technician to come. The first two technicians stated that there was nothing wrong with the compressor and replaced the same 'problem' board. Additionally, both technicians claimed that the refrigerator was fixed at the end of their service visit. The refrigerator is still not cooling.

Today a third GE technician came (it is always a different person) and this time the compressor was blamed for the problem. Obviously there is a lot of guess work going on here.

This last technician credited the $340 we paid originally, but now the bill has increased to $518 to replace the compressor. Supposedly they have to order the parts and we will be without a refrigerator for another 2 weeks.

Judging by the terrible reports from the countless dissatisfied and frustrated GE consumers, I am bracing myself for a long struggle with this abusive giant.

Ironically, my inexpensive 25 year old Kenmore refrigerator in the garage has never been serviced and is still working like a charm. If getting what you pay for is important to you, DO NOT BUY ANYTHING MADE BY GE!!!

review_title: BUYER BEWARE!!! - Stainless Steel RUSTS w/in 2 mo!
review_text:
I purchased this refrigerator April 2013 and was really happy with it initially. In June, I realized there were rusts spots on the front panel below where the water dispenses from. I tried to clean it off with the stainless steel cleaner, but it didn't come off. Bottom line response from GE customer service is that rust is "cosmetic" and not covered by warranty. Details below:

Contacted customer service in June and was told this should definitely not be rusting and that she would send a repair person out to assess the issue and either replace the door or the refrigerator. A repair person came out, confirmed the rust. His recommendation was that I use baking soda to remove the rust.

I followed up with customer service and talked to a supervisor who didn't know what to recommend until she 'reviewed her notes'. She has been in this position since 1989, yet never heard of this issue until reading up on it? This makes me assume that rusting is not normal and I may have a faulty refrigerator.

Her only recommendation was to treat the area with baking soda. Her only other offer to me was to buy a new refrigerator with a discount she would give me!! How often does GE expect customers to purchase new refrigerators? Every 2 months?

My concern is this, will my refrigerator continue to rust past the warranty and get larger, or expand to other areas. The stainless steel appears to be of poor quality, as I don't expect most customers to be satisfied with a rusty refrigerator.
I will never buy another GE appliance and I will be sure to let everyone know about my issue.

product_title: Samsung : RFG297AARS 29 cu. ft. French-Door Refrigerator - Real Stainless
review_title: Wonderful Fridge, Huge Freezer, Plenty of Ice
review_text:
I bought this fridge without investigating any reviews of it. While waiting for it to be delivered, I started to read reviews of the fridge and was scared that ice production would be an issue. I use a lot of ice in my beverages and live in Texas, so I go through plenty of ice. I have never had any issues with ice production. That included a week where five people were constantly using the ice. I simply followed the directions to set up the ice production.

The fridge has an incredible amount of space. There are plenty of shelves that fold, slide, and can be removed to store smaller items and bulky items. There are two large produce and fruit drawers that can easily be set to different humidity levels. I have found that these work really well. We use one on less humidity for fruits and the other on higher humidity for vegetables.

The freezer also has plenty of space. It is designed well with a top sliding drawer and a larger lower drawer that are divided into a couple areas. It's easy to arrange frozen foods based on what needs to be easily accessible.

Finally the controls and the look of the fridge are great. Its easy to set the exact temperature you want on the fridge and freezer. The temperatures hold well. Also, there is a nice alarm feature that will alert you if a door didn't close all the way. The look of the fridge is a major plus as we constantly get compliments on it.

The only annoying thing is that it does take a few days to get the ice maker set up for maximum production. After going through that process it makes plenty of ice.

product_title: Samsung : RFG297AARS 29 cu. ft. French-Door Refrigerator - Real Stainless
review_text: Do not buy a Samsung! I did and it's the biggest appliance mistake I ever made. Although they look great on the showroom floor, they start to fall apart immediately. Next I had to replace the condenser fan motor. Then all of the plastic on the inside liner started to crack and rot. Samsung made me pay to have one of their certified repair men come to my house. He did and certified that it was an unrepairable factory defect. Then the real fun began. I spent 6 months working my way through the customer service quagmire. I was told I would receive a prorated refund which never came. When I called back repeatedly over the following months I was given a variety of excuses. Talking about the filter; the comment on filter by another reviewer is spot on - expensive, never stocked at the local HD or Lowes, and needs replaced at least twice a year.  And the review regarding cheap plastic is spot on as well - a couple of the 'nice' doors inside no longer exist, broken and not replaced.  I could spend the rest of the review complainign about Samsung customer service but the story has been told.  We are not hard on the refrigerator but after 2 years, it is definitely worn out.  Plastic is low quality.  Except the stainless exterior - smudges but still looks nice with the other appliances in the kitchen.  If you've read this far, do yourself a favor and look elsewhere. If $1500 or $2000 is burning a hole in your pocket and you want to replace your refrig every couple of years, go for it.  It definitely looks nice. product_title: Samsung : RFG297AARS 29 cu. ft. French-Door Refrigerator - Real Stainless
review_text:

review_title: AVOID THIS FRIDGE LIKE THE PLAGUE!!!
review_text:
I bought a stainless steel GE bottom freezer refrigerator five years ago when I renovated my kitchen. It looked so nice and shiny and it worked fine until last year. Then the top section up and died.

I got on the GE website and scheduled a service appointment. The repairman finally came at 5:30 p.m. after I was home waiting for him all day long, but he did come on the day he said he would.

He inspected the fridge, told me the thermostat regulator for the top section had gone kaput, and installed a new one. I asked him how long that part was guaranteed for and he said five years.

I almost hit the roof. My previous fridge had been a top-freezer GE which lasted 17 years and was still in good working order when I tossed it. For $1300, I told the repairman, I expect everything in that fridge to last 100 years minimum and not a day less.

Anyway, the fridge worked fine again until last week, when I noticed it wasn't cold enough. Back to the GE website to make another service appointment. This time they sent the same guy but at least he came early.

He opened the fridge, and voila! The fan had up and died.

He replaced the fan, put everything back together nicely, and handed me a bill for $246.15. Labor: $194.99. Tax: $17.49. Fan: $2.98. I shelled out over two hundred bucks to replace a piece of plastic that cost $2.98.

GE, you've been warned. If anything else in that fridge conks out before 2025, I'm tossing the whole thing out and buying a Kitchen-Aid.

Judy Lind

UPDATE 8/15/11:

Holy-freaking-moly, would you believe this thing has conked out AGAIN?! For the THIRD TIME in SEVEN YEARS?!

Forget the repairman. Forget GE altogether. I'll be hanged if I'm shelling out another $250 to fix this dog. I will never, ever buy another GE product in this life or the next one. Kitchen-Aid, here I come.

Judy Lind

review_title: Nice but a little noisy and messy
review_text:

We set the temp to Deli and keep sliced meats and cheese in it and its perfect for that, wide but shallow so everything is visible. That drawer complements the usual 2 produce drawers which are directly above. Door storage is nicely adjustable. The freezer has an upper drawer that works well for storage.

Cons: The icemaker kicks the ice into the tray with a real racket. Our old Amana made some noise this way, but this one wakes me up some nights. The ice thru the door will splash the drink onto the floor if there is already liquid in the glass (maybe other models do this too). The buttons on the door for controlling the fridge and thru-door functions aren't very good. The buttons are part of a smooth face, but the lighted phrases that indicate the mode are not buttons, the buttons are around the edges and aren't lit. Most folks try to press on the lighted phrases, which is more intuitive. For instance, to get ice thru the door, you have to first look and see if the symbol above "cubed", "crushed", or "water", is lit, and if your desired selection is not lit, you have to press the button marked "ice & water", WHICH IS NOT LIT, until your desired selection is lit. I know how to work it now, but no one new figures it out without help.

I should caveat these cons with the fact that we chose this fridge without trying it out first. We went to a Sears scratch and dent store, where we were able to save $1000 off list, but the models weren't powered up for demo. If I could have tried them powered up and found another model with more intuitive door controls I might have chosen that. But overall it is a very good fridge, especially at the price we paid.

The high spin barely makes any noise and it does NOT walk across the floor like some of the other brands. The vibration reduction system works beautifully. In fact, when the spin cycle just starts you can see a little wiggle if you watch it but then it smooths out and your clothes come out with practically no water in them. I also absolutely love the silver care feature. This allows me to sanitize the washcloths that i use on my face without using a whole tank of hot water. It simply passes the water over silver plates to clean out the bacteria. I also love the delay start feature. If i don't want to wait up on a load to put it in the dryer i can just set it so that it will go off a couple hours before i wake up. That way the clothes don't set in the washer wet all night and smell musty in the morning.

I can't say enough good things about this washer. In fact, if my washer broke today i would buy it all over again. I've enjoyed using it so much.

product_title: Fagor Undercounter Glass & Dishwasher
review_text:
We selected this commercial product for home use, as we frequently entertain a large family and many friends. All was fine for a year or so, until it failed to heat water. The repair service, which is also promoting the item in the US, finally analyzed the problem as mice in the circuitry. At first, this seems reasonable and even embarrassing. But I am the only person in the world who has even had a mouse in a kitchen? What about all the other applicances that have never been so affected?

After numerous attempts to repair or replace the circuitry, the dishwasher was removed and returned to the shop. Inquiries were ignored until we eventually learned that this Fagor product could not be repaired. At all. No alternative was offered.

We are easy-going people for whom the hassle of additional pursuit, legal or otherwise, is not worth the effort, so I am contenting myself with simply alerting the dishwashing world: Beware of any product that allows normal kitchen events to render their expensive equipment unrepairable.

review_title: Bought it, tried 2 units, now no longer own it...
review_text:
We bought an NXR range at a local retailer. The good about the NXR range is that it has very nice burners, an infrared broiler and a large oven with very nice slide out racks. It also comes at a great price (1899 and always ask for the middle grate and ask for it to be free!).
The first unit arrived, in a box, and had a dent on the left front (note the oven door closes into a frame, it does not close flush like other ovens do) frame. The oven door itself was mounted crooked and the side had scratches.
Refused the unit, got a new one a few days later. Installed, tried, smelled gas. Turns out this unit had a heavy leak in the main gas line within the unit.
Returned that one as well and traded up to a Bertazonni range (slightly higher in price).
Also note that the NXR has fairly flimsy parts. The middle cover (between the burners) is flimsy and loose (it slides when cleaning). The back vent is flimsy at best. And in general it is not of high quality external materials when comparing it to a Bertazonni.
If the quality of the materials and the quality control were not so poor this would be a real steal! Alas, it is one of these "to-good-to-be-true" things.

product_title: Professional Series 30" Wide Freestanding Natural Gas Range 4 Sealed Burners 4.2 cu. ft. Convection Oven Manual Clean Extra Large Oven Window 4" Backsplash: Stainless
review_text:
We have had our NXR for almost exactly 1 year now.
We have the older model "NRG3001" mainly because we preferred the look of the older one. Only difference is the door handle is curved instead of straight and the panel the knobs is on is tilted up instead of flat.
I have heard NXR went from the 304 stainless (NRG) to the 430 stainless (DRGB)but can not confirm that myself, ours is 304 stainless.

The Range is very well made, is solid stainless steel on all sides & top, has heavy cast iron grates, heavy thick stainless oven racks.
4 excellent burners that are the exact ones used by Wolf, made in Germany and 15,000BTU each and all 4 are the same which I required.
I cant stand stoves that have 4 different burners, one big powerful burner one or two medium and then one tiny almost useless burner for just simmering.
That is just a total waste of a stove top to me.

I much prefer 4 really nice powerful burners where all 4 also become very low simmer burners, MUCH better configuration.
The burners are spaced enough apart to be able to use 4 large pots/pans at the same time.

Like ALL stainless it is rather easily scratched but other than that it is easy to keep clean and except for a couple tiny scratches still looks like brand new after a year of constant use 3X a day, 7 days a week.

Prior to buying ours last March this one review right here on Amazon was the one and only bad review I had ever found for this stove, and as you can tell has NOTHING to do with the stove itself but is a shipping problem.
Have since seen 2 others both complaining about the enamel on the inside of oven chipping badly. Both were the DRGB model and seemed like it was probably a bad batch of enamel.
Have only seen 2 reviews about that so must not have been wide spread problem.

The other review here from August 17th sounds as though they don't even own the stove just regurgitating something they have heard, which I have heard the same thing. But all they say is that it "can rust & spot", but apparently either they don't really own the stove or it hasn't rusted or spotted they just suspect it "might".

Not exactly sure how much difference it really makes between 304 to 430 stainless on a stove that is an indoor range and not some outdoor BBQ sitting in the elements. 430 stainless is only slightly less stain/rust resistant and I think the only molecular difference is 430 does not have the 8% Nickle that 304 does.
Technically the best stainless would be 316 stainless which virtually no one uses except for BBQs made for marine environments.

Anyway, we are very happy with the stove so far, cooks great, looks great and didn't cost an arm and a leg. We bought ours for $1799.00 total cost shipping included. A Kenmore we were looking at cost more and the NXR is easily 10X the stove that Kenmore would have been.

The Infrared broiler works very well, oven works great, knobs are nice, the door is heavy duty and even after having the oven on at over 400 degrees for hours the door is only just warm to the touch.

For the price there is NOTHING that beats a 30" NXR for value, not even close.
Can you get stoves just as nice? Yep, but you will pay dearly for it.
Only other stoves that are as good and even better in some respects than the NXR start at least $1000 more.

Blue Stars are decent, although I see a lot of complaints about them, Capital Culinarian is very good but both of those will cost considerably more.

product_title: LG : WM3988HWA 27 Steam Washer/Dryer Combo with 4.2 cu. ft. Capacity - DISCONTINUED
review_text:
We just got this unit yesterday, so have had it for a little over 24 hours now. We've washed about 4 loads of laundry so far, and we LOVE it!! Load #1 was a mix of jeans (4 pair), shirts, socks, & underwear, load #2 was a sheet set from a king size bed, load #3 was a blanket from a king size bed, and load #4 was about 6 pair of shorts. We also threw 3 wrinkled shirts in to try out the 20-minute steam cycle which removes wrinkles.

We've been having problems with our dryer vent. Our house was built in the early 1980's when they were using the flex plastic dryer vents. Due to the way our house is setup, it would have been some major construction and several thousand dollars to replace the dryer vent. We were having to run the dryer through 2 or 3 (sometimes more) cycles to get things thoroughly dry. This was making the electric bill higher than it should be. It also caused the heating element on the dryer to burn out and need to be replaced 3 times due to not being vented well. I did have the dryer vent cleaned out and it helped a little, but it still didn't work great. We had looked at the other LG combo units in the past, but didn't get one due to their small size and poor reviews. We decided to check them out again and found this new "full size" unit which had great reviews, so decided to take the plunge this time around.

It takes about 3 1/2 to 4 hours from start to finish to wash and dry a load in this LG, but that's not a big deal for us. You just start it up and let it do its thing. There are two people (including myself) in our home, so we don't normally have huge amounts of laundry to do. Instead of doing all the laundry one day a week, we've decided to do smaller loads a couple times a week. This new unit uses MUCH less water than our old washer, so the water bill should go down a little. Also, the electric bill should go down some since we won't be running a dryer two or three times per load. Another plus is that since it's just a single unit, we've put in shelving where the dryer used to be and now have a little more storage space!

The only drawback we've found so far is that there is no way to dry-only without washing. I would recommend that you thoroughly read the owner's manual before first use if you buy this unit. In our excitement to try it out, we ran the first load through without reading the manual and selected a cycle that washes only and doesn't dry. We then had to run the load through a wash cycle again to dry. The owner's manual has a chart in it that clearly shows what each of the cycles does and doesn't do. There are two or three cycles that will only wash and won't dry. Other than no option to dry without washing, I've found no drawbacks/problems with this unit and wish I would have bought it a long time ago.

This unit cost us much less (and no construction mess) than it would have cost to replace the dryer vent, and will end up saving us money on water and electricity. Thank you to LG for an awesome product!! We purchased from A.J. Madison which had the best price we could find anywhere, plus no tax (since we're not in NY) and free shipping!

UPDATE 10/18/08: I stand corrected! D.M. let me know that there is a dry-only option, and indeed there is! It's not listed anywhere at all in the owner's manual, so we weren't aware of how to do it. After you turn the unit on you have to press the Dry button BEFORE you turn the cycle selection knob, and it then puts the unit into dry-only mode. THANK YOU, D.M.!!! :-)

product_title: LG : WM3988HWA 27 Steam Washer/Dryer Combo with 4.2 cu. ft. Capacity - DISCONTINUED
review_title: This family of 5 can't live without it....
review_text:
After waiting for a very long time because of the cost we decided to finally take the plunge on this 2 in 1 unit after a brick and mortar store offered price match and no-interest for 18 months. WE are so happy that we went for it! I don't know how we survived without it. Well actually we do know how we did... our 3rd bedroom had a minimum of 10 laundry bags waiting to go out. It was an endless and vicious cycle that never came to an end.

The washing performance of this unit is impeccable! We have been using it religiously since December 2008 and are in love. There are many different cycles that offer a myriad of water temps,soil levels, spin cycle speeds and drying time variations. We basically use the Cotton cycle for most of our wash and the cold/cold water option. This machine is so efficient and works wonderfully with nothing but cold water. It truly does remove stains! Since it is a front loader and energy efficient, then you MUST use HE liquid. We have used the Tide 2X HE and Wisk 3X HE; personally we love the Tide scent but the Wisk offers you more bang for your buck at this time because it is 3X concentrated.

I read and re-read the reviews posted on here and another site and found that the machine *MIGHT* be okay for our family of 5. We are very happy to report that the machine keeps the wash in check in our household and we honestly average 3 loads a week. It is my husband, myself, 6 year old, 5 year old (asthma sufferer) and 2 year old. The machine has a large 4.2 cubic foot capacity allowing for an extra large load at a time. As others have pointed out, your drying capacity is not 4.2 but rather half, or half of the load that you have originally placed in. It was a trial and error of a few loads to figure the drying aspect of this wonderful machine.

I also wash my King comforter with the Bulky/Large cycle. There is no dry cycle for this setting because it is for very large items that would otherwise not normally dry in a dryer. It does a wonderful job of washing our bedding and removing all of the excess water for hang drying on our closet door. That specific cycle is 54 minutes long.

What works for us is to not always drying the loads. We have set up a tension rod in our second bathroom shower area and air dry our clothes. We truly cram a lot of clothes in there and it does a great job each and every time. Within a couple of hours the clothes are fully dried and ready to put away. If we are just doing our second upkeep weekly load we usually just dry because it isn't as gigantic as our original load. The dryer DOES indeed work and makes everything toasty hot. For others who claim it doesn't, then their machine must have been overloaded or it may have been a very heavy, bulky item. The dryer runs on steam so it sprays small amounts of water on your clothes. YES, it does wet your clothes to dry them; not sure how it does it, but it does work! A cotton/normal (average) wash cycle with added 16 minute pre-wash cycle, high spin and more dry will take you about 4 hrs. Unless you are watching the machine, you will not notice the time.

Pros:
*Ventless system that is a great set up for apartment dwellers.

*Many wash cycles and water temp options that really clean clothes.

*Energy efficient... we haven't noticed a difference on our electric or water bill as of yet. Keep in mind we are washing in cold water.

*Convenience of just drying without washing if necessary. Just select DRY after turning the machine on and select time desired.

*Being able to PAUSE any time during the cycle to either, add, remove, relocate or just check on your items.

*Allergiene and Steam cycles remove allergens for those that have asthma sufferers or any allergies.

CONS:
*Extra Large capacity drum does wonderfully washing but will have to be cut in half for drying.

*The wonderful PAUSE feature that I constantly use has an 8 minute time out. Twice I would be in the middle of doing something and time out... I would unfortunately lose the whole cycle and have to start either from the beginning or somewhere near that. Not really a con, but an annoyance. The reality is that you can not do that at the laundromat so the feature is a GOD send at the end of the day. Many times, I have the kids bring me articles 5 mins later even though I was screaming at the top of my lungs to BRING ME EVERYTHING. That feature saved me.

*Our floors in the kitchen aren't rigid enough so at times on the extra high spin cycle we have shaking and vibrating througout the whole kitchen. The only remedy for this is to have good flooring. We are researching whether the stand can buffer some of the vibration.

review_text:
After extensive research, we decided to take the plunge and invest a considerable amount of money in this machine. Our only regret is that we didn't do it sooner! It is amazing. Even our plumber, after he installed it, said "This is a beautiful machine!" --- and believe me, he has seen quite a few washers in his day. He plans to buy one for his own home. We live in NYC and our options were limited, both space-wise and in terms of venting. So that eliminated many choices that other people have. From reviews, which were mostly positive, I was afraid of low drying quality, low capacity, and possible odors since it is a front-loading machine. We have had ZERO problems with any of these. And I would disagree with the reviewer who said that this machine is not for a family of 4, 5 or 6. We are a family of 5 (two adults, 3 kids under 5) and this machine is perfect for us. I do loads about every other day, according to color/temperature, which are never that big anyway, so capacity is never a problem. However, when I have had to do larger loads, such as sheets and towels (for example, two towels and two sets of twin size sheets), everything comes out clean and dry with NO problem. The features are incredible, in terms of washing possiblilities and others such as pre-wash, steam, allergeine, and a wide range of drying cycles. The dryer will keep tumbling periodically even after it is finished in order to prevent wrinkles, which is great. Sometimes I prefer the clothes to be left slightly damp (I hate when normal dryers "bake" my clothes), and so sometimes they will be a bit wrinkled when they come out. This problem is very easily solved either by drying them a bit longer, or running the steam feature to eliminate wrinkles. It is so efficient that hardly any detergent (must be HE) needs to be used, and you will not notice a difference at all in energy or water bills (it runs on a 220 volt and is designed to use very little water. The amount of water needed for each cycle is tailored to fit the amount you need to wash by the machine).
I would recommend this to anyone who is interested in trying to reduce their carbon and water footprints---not just those with limited options, like us. It has a child lock, which really comes in handy with young kids. I also love the fact that I can program or delay a wash; often I put clothes in in the morning and they are washed and dried when I come home. Now they just need to make a machine to fold the clothes and put them away!!!
We have had no problem with mold or odors (I think because of the built-in dryer), no problems with capacity or with drying. I would highly recommend this washer dryer combo to anyone, regardless of their options or their family size. It's amazing and WELL WORTH the investment! Why have two, huge, bulky machines when just one will do?
THe only drawback I can think of, which is very small, is that, if I had separate machines, I would sometimes do two wash loads and then dry them together. Very minor inconvenience. I should also add that this washer/dryer is VERY kind and gentle to your clothes!

product_title: LG : WM3988HWA 27 Steam Washer/Dryer Combo with 4.2 cu. ft. Capacity - DISCONTINUED
review_title: Runs like a TANK +tips for other owners
review_text:
I bought this washer/dryer heavily used and 8 years old in the local classifieds, intending to install it in my 133 year old house that had no proper washer/dryer hookups.
If you own one of these or are looking to grab one second hand, I hope my experiences will help you out.

I've had this unit for almost a year now and I've got to give LG some serious props, this thing is built like a TANK!
When I first bought this unit, the previous owner lied to me and said it worked fine. I assumed he was lying but bought it anyways since he only wanted $300 and I'm pretty good at fixing things.
When I got it home I found that it leaked like mad, didn't dry anything, and I would routinely come home to a flooded laundry room and the washer full of water with a drain error on the screen.

First, I looked into the flooding. That turned out to be caused by the extremely restrictive (it had crossed bars in the bottom) 1 inch drain on the old laundry sink it was draining into. Lint would get stuck in the bars in the drain, clogging it up and causing it to fill up. Once the sink was full it would flood every time the pump ran, then water would get sticker back into the washer eventually triggering the drain error.
The quick fix for this was putting in an over sink colander to catch the lint. The permanent fix was to replace the drain with a more open one. Now the lint (which there in very little of, BTW) drains just fine. This shouldn't be a problem if you have a standard washer drain.

Next was the leaking/not drying issue, which turned out to be the same problem.
The dryer on this works by blowing hot air thru a tall shaft running along the back right corner of the washer, then spraying a fine mist of cold water down the shaft. The cold water condenses the hot moisture which causes it to rain down the shaft to the bottom where it is pumped out by the drain pump.
The problem occurred when the mist sprayer was getting too much water, which sprayed out the top of the condenser shaft and leaked everywhere.
Where the cold water comes into the washer there is a manifold with 5 solenoid valves that send water to different parts of the washer. The valve for the mister has a flow restrictor press-fit into the manifold output. The flow restrictor had become dislodged and shot down the tube to the mister. I reinserted the flow restrictor and it quit leaking but it popped back out a few days later. I researched this issue and found that it is one of, if not the most common points of failure on this washer and LG recommends replacing the entire manifold when it fails ($90). I instead, reinserted the flow restrictor, drilled a 1/8 inch in front of it and slid a piece of brass rod into the hole to keep it in place. That fix will not only outlive the washer but probably me too. Since reengineering the manifold, the washer doesn't leak a drop and drys everything just fine.

Once everything was running well, I noticed that the washer want draining as fast as I thought it should have. This just turned out to be a worn drain pump which was only $50 (and in stock) at the local Sears. I consider this regular maintenance on an 8 year old washer.

Since giving it a little TLC, this washer runs like a champ. That said, here's some pointers to make your experience better:
1. Drying efficiency is largely based on heat dissipation. Don't put anything on top of the washer and get the pedestal if you can, it makes a difference in drying (and your back will thank you). Also, if you get the black version (or paint yours black) it will dissipate heat better due to black body radiation (yay science!).
2. To run a dry only cycle, turn on the washer, then, without turning the cycle selector, press the DRY button (once for normal, twice for more dry), then press the SPIN SPEED button once to remove the rinse/spin cycle.
3. Clean your washer once a week! I cannot overstate how much of a difference this makes to how well this thing washes and drys.
Here's how to properly clean your washer/dryer:
A. Turn on the washer then hold the EXTRA RINSE button for 3 seconds to select TUB CLEAN.
B. Removed any clothes that are in the washer.
C. Fill the bleach dispenser with bleach.
D. Start the cycle. It will run for 30 minutes.
E. Once the cleaning cycle finishes, use a towel to wipe down the inside of the door, the rubber sealing ring, and the tub itself. (Now is also a good time to clean up any spilled soap to keep it looking nice)
F. Open the little door on the bottom left of your washer.
G. Pull out the drain tube and remove it's plug to drain any remaining water into a bucket. Please note, this is only possible if you have the washer pedestal, otherwise the drain tube is right at floor level. If you don't have the pedestal, I recommend keeping your washer on a catch pan. They are cheap and can save you from a wet floor.
H. Unscrew the drain filter and empty it.
I. Reinsert the drain filter, ensuring the open end is facing up. It only really goes in one way but my roommate proved that it can be forced in wrong, then it won't seal and you end up with a flooded laundry room.
J. Put the plug back in the drain tube and snap it back into its holder.
K. Close the access door.
There, now your washer is shiny and smells good.
4. Use service mode to make less of a mess. Under normal operation there is always a small amount of water in the bottom of the washer. This can be a pain when cleaning the drain filter. To put your washer in service mode, power it on while holding SPIN SPEED and SOIL LEVEL. Once in service mode press the start button to clicks through self test modes. The very first test mode will idle the drum and run the drain pump. You can use this to get nearly all the water out before pulling the drain filter. This it very useful if you don't have the pedestal as you can catch the remaining water by putting a towel under the drain filter when removing it.
5. I'd you want to clean your soap dispenser tray, you can remove it by pressing down on the right side of the bleach dispenser, then pulling it straight out. You can throw it in the dishwasher but I wouldn't recommend using the heated dry cycle if you do.

product_title: Whirlpool : RBS305PVS 30 Single Electric Wall Oven Stainless Steel
review_text:
We bought this oven's predecessor a number of years ago, and I'm writing this as a warning only because another reviewer experienced what sounds like the same problem on the current oven.

I'll describe my oven. You'll need to examine this oven to see if it has the same bad design features.

Here's the problem: To keep the waste heat of the oven from damaging the cabinetry, the oven uses a squirrel cage fan to suck fresh air in through holes at the top of the oven, below the control panel (but outside the over itself). This air is then blown out through similar holes at the bottom of the oven enclosure. If those holes, which aren't all that obvious, become obstructed in any way - with dust, grease, airborne cat hair, etc - the flow of air diminishes. This allows the oven enclosure to get too hot. Then one of two things can happen (both happened to us).

1. The thermal safety fuse on the back of the oven blows and shuts the oven off. The charge for this fuse, installed, is $150 - of which over $100 is the cost of the fuse itself.

2. Before that fuse blows, the extra heat rising to the top of the oven can deform the oven interlock assembly. This assembly includes a lock and a sensor that tells when the oven has been opened. When this is deformed, the oven will not unlock without disassembling the entire oven - not a good thing to happen in the middle of roasting something.

Our oven is (was!) self-cleaning, and the first time things failed it was during a cleaning cycle. The next two times it failed, it happened during ordinary baking, even though I was meticulous about keeping the air holes open.

When the interlock deformed I called Whirlpool. A new interlock would be $175, but they sold it to me for half price. When the second one went after only a few months I decided to remove the interlock and just not use the self-clean feature anymore (too dangerous to use w/o the interlock).

I wrote to Whirlpool and the CPSC complaining about what I thought was a flawed and possibly dangerous design. Whirlpool offered me a new oven for 10% off the LIST price. Thanks a lot.

The old oven works fine as an oven, though the broiler is really anemic, so I'll keep it until it gives out. There's no longer an interlock to deform, and there seems to be enough airflow to keep the thermal fuse from blowing at normal baking temps. I've gone back to EasyOff for oven cleaning, and that's a whole lot less smelly than the self-clean was anyway.
