product_title: 30" STANDARD CLEAN FREESTANDING GAS RANGES
review_text: This range is marketed as a dual fuel range because it can accept either natural gas or propane.  This is both false and potentially fatal.  I purchased this range from P.C. Richard and Sons; a big mistake.  The sales staff will tell you anything that you want to hear in order to have you line their pockets.  The customer service and warantee/repair service were completely useless as well.  The range was installed by a general contractor, not by the store installation people and that was a very costly mistake for me.  Apparently, the stovetop was set to use propane while the oven was not converted for propane but for natural gas.  This lead to failure of the electronics of the range as well as filling my house with carbon monoxide.  PC Richards was notified twice and repair men sent out twice.  The first time, the electronics were replaced and that was fine until I began using the oven nearly a year later.  This same problem was happening again and I made a call on the warantee that I had paid so much for.  This time, the repair man said that the range was inoperable and needed to be replaced.  Of course the scumbags back at the office would deny any responsibility for this because they had not installed the range, leaving me out hundreds of dollars.  I can safely say that I will never give a single cent to PC Richards or Whirlpool.  I wish nothing but the worst for both of you and cannot wait until both of your companies end up like Circuit City, obsolete and bankrupt.

product_title: Whirlpool : RBD305PVS 30 Double Oven - Stainless Steel
review_text: I have a similar model to this one.  It never kept accurate temperature and has now given up after we ran the self-cleaning cycle.  My husband called the service line and they told him they had heard of their ovens dying after self-cleaning before.  They don't want to say this is a known problem but that is what it is.  If you do buy this oven definitely never run the self-cleaning cycle.  Its bad news.

product_title: LG 4.5 CF STEAM WASHER RED
review_title: Design flaw allows mold, trashes clothes, high upkeep
review_text: I have owned my WM3001 LG washer for 2 years. In the first year using powder detergent mold grew between the drums that could not be removed. Tub cleanse cycle, bleach, baking soda, hydrogen peroxide, Whirl Out, vinegar do not remove the mold from between the drums. The problem is the rubber door gasket that is pierced with 3 holes in the center bottom that allows water to infiltrate and collect between the drums so mold grows. Mold also collects in the manual drain tubing and filter. Irony of all ironies there is a sticker on the front saying "Certified asthma and allergy friendly. Meets ASP-WM-01:07 Standard of the Asthma and Allergy Foundation of America". Well, mold IS my asthma trigger and my toddler has eczema. Our clothes and towels smell moldy when wet. I contacted LG to address this and was told to fax my original sales receipt. Then they claimed never to have received it. So I emailed them a photo of the receipt and I was told I would be contacted by extended warranty service for a 1 time service call. I never was contacted again. Customer service is indeed negligible. Regardless this washer requires unacceptably high upkeep and it is so harsh on clothing and towels (unraveling them after 3 washes) that only the gentlest cycle can be used despite all the fancy options. Not what I paid for. Still looking for some satisfaction on this purchase.

product_title: LG : DLEX3001W 27in Front-Load Electric Dryer - White
review_text: I am on my fourth lint filter for this LG dryer and none of the filters fit snugly.  The edges of the filter then chip, and the filter then catches, twists and tears holes in articles of clothing.  This dryer has ruined nine articles of clothing.  It is also supposedly environmentally friendly, which means it never gets very hot.  It can take up to two hours to dry a load of clothes.  I have been washing and drying clothes for forty years and have owned at least seven dryers.  This is the most expensive and poorest quality dryer I have ever owned.

product_title: Whirlpool : GU2275XTVQ 24 Dishwasher - White
review_text: This dishwasher has been a huge disappointment...it is very loud and does not dry the dishes. product_title: Electrolux : EIFLW55HIW 27 Washer Island White
review_text:
A vast improvement over my 22-yr.old top loader; clothes come out cleaner, less damaged, and judging from slipperiness and detergent perfume smell, the rinse works much better, and the spin gets clothes dryer.

I don't buy the sales pitch that steam injected into the wash somehow gets clothes cleaner or the one about 5 different ways to tumble clothes in a rotating drum. Save your money, like I did, with this model instead of wasting it on worthless bells and whistles.

I bought the liquid HE detergent recommended, but I wanted to use up my big box of powdered detergent--no problem; the manual says to take out the small dish from the detergent dispenser box and dump the powder where it was and it works fine. I use about half the detergent over the old top loader because this machine uses less than half the water and I haven't had any problems with foaming.

[Product details: Item Weight: 148 pounds, Shipping Weight: 247 pounds] is definitely screwed up; this baby must weigh close to 300 lbs and I'm glad the store wouldn't accept my offer of self-delivery/installment for 100 bucks off.

This machine is very quiet except when water is rushing down the drain hose. The controls are easy to use with a countdown timer to let you know when it'll finish. I didn't bother with the expensive pedestal thinking I could build one but after using the washer a few weeks, I'm fine without it.

(didn't qualify for Pennsylvania's $75 rebate for ultra efficient washers--June-2010)

product_title: Electrolux : EIFLW55HIW 27 Washer Island White
review_text:
We bought this machine five months ago after a long period of research. The clincher came from this reviewer at BestBuy who compared this machine to the Samsung and got better results. [...] Apparently, the steam and silver functions don't really help clean clothes better.

So far, the Electrolux has performed extremely well. It's effective, quiet and versatile. It can use regular as well as high efficiency detergent. It's very quiet when it operates, perhaps because it's heavier than competitors' models. The extra weight helps to keep it ultra-steady during the high-speed spins. The spin cycle is also quite gentle -- many of my shirts do not need to be ironed afterwards.

product_title: Electrolux : EIFLW55HIW 27 Washer Island White
review_text: I did not have a good experience with this washer.  While it was great for washing large items, and looks snazzy in my laundry room with its matching dryer, after a few months, my clothes started to smell.  It got worse and worse, and by the time I figured out what was causing it (mildew buildup in the machine where you can't see it) the one year warranty was up.  Fortunately, I bought the extended warranty, which I rarely do, and now Electrolux and the warranty servicer are refunding the full purchase price after two years.  Nothing I have tried gets rid of the smell.

product_title: Electrolux : EIFLW55HIW 27 Washer Island White
review_title: Good washer with one glaring problem
review_text: I have had this washer for nearly two years.  Over all, it's a good machine, but my major gripe with it is that whenever you put a heavy item in the wash, most times it refuses to spin.  Even when I have a bunch of bath towels in there, plus a heavy bath robe, it still refuses to spin, leaving me with a big load of sopping wet clothes.  At my other house, I have a Miele washer, and it always manages to wash and spin every single load.  If Electrolux offered a way of overriding this perfect blanace system at times, it would be a much better machine.

product_title: Electrolux : EIFLW55HIW 27 Washer Island White
review_title: So far. Everything I hoped for.

It also shook so badly it made the house feel like it was about to come down around us. Everything I read about this washer was true. product_title: Electrolux : EIFLW55HIW 27 Washer Island White
review_text: Great machine at a good price.  Amazon's price was $150 less than my local Best Buy.  I have had this machine for 3 months and it is working great.  Setup was easy. I like its large capacity, ability to get clothes very clean, and low noise level.  I would recommend this machine.

product_title: Electrolux : EIFLW55HIW 27 Washer Island White
review_title: Great for a family with 2 or more kids
review_text: I selected this product, after doing a review to meet the needs of a family of 5. My last washer worked well for 7 years, but due to to the large wash loads, the bearing broke. I wanted to make sure that the next washer I buy can handle large loads, be energy and water efficient. With the above criteria, I researched Washers to handle bigger loads, and zeroed onto the Electrolux EIFLW55HIW 27 Washer. I ordered this on Amazon after doing a price comparison, service handling etc. I received the washer, delivered to my basement by the shipping company, on time. I installed the washer myself in 30 minutes, and got it ready for operation. The washer performance is excellent, very silent, and features are cool. I recommend this washer without hesitation.

product_title: Electrolux : EIFLW55HIW 27 Washer Island White
review_text: I bought this washer after reading the many positive reviews at multiple sites . I am replacing a ten year old popular brand front loading washer that many of us have come to expect tens of years from. As you can see I will not be buying that brand anymore. The washer has plenty of features but the one I was most interested in is the perfect spin which works as advertised. This is what killed my old washer. This washer is hands down a better washer. It can complete a wash in as little as eighteen minutes and my clothes do not have a musty smell to them, my old washer always left a musty smell. I also have noticed that there is near zero lint in my dryer lint trap. I have owned this washer for just under three months. With that said, my expectations are high. I would  recommend this washer to anybody.

review_text: I purchased a electrolux washer and dryer about a year ago. The soap dispenser door on the washer does not stay closed anymore and I have to use tape to hold it closed. product_title: Electrolux : EIFLW55HIW 27 Washer Island White
review_text: I've owned my Electrolux washer and dryer for almost 5 years now. I have had NO problems with mine. The washer is so quiet and so efficient. My washer and dryer are in my garage and are subjected to some hot days. NEVER, EVER has my washer had a smell. I run the "clean drum" cycle every time it is suggested on the computer panel located on the front of the washer. I think Electrolux makes wonderful products!!! If ANY of their products fails to provide the customer everything promised by Electrolux, the full refund is issued. I have NEVER been treated as good by any other manufacturer.  There's not one bad thing I could say about Electrolux or their appliances. I WILL NEVER BUY ANYTHING BUT ELECTROLUX PRODUCTS.

product_title: Electrolux : EIFLW55HIW 27 Washer Island White

product_title: Electrolux EIFLW55HMB Front Load Washer with IQ-Touch Controls Mediterranean Bluea
review_text:
This washer basin is huge - 4.7 holds everything and we have a family of 5. We almost bought the Kenmore Elite HE5T with steam but found out the regular units are 4.4 but the sale unit only available in "barolo red" was only 4.0 - big enough for most but size was our major factor in a new washer. So we gave up the steam and went with Electrolux. Electrolux does not make a steam washer, the steam dryer is in the wave touch model ($300 more apiece than the IQ touch). The main reason to me for steam is stain removal; not so much wrinkle removal, so IQ touch was fine. Apparently Electrolux and Bosch don't think steam in a washer is necessary; neither offer it. This washer/dryer is fantastic. I was concerned about the doors (as many are) but they are incredibly sturdy and you should have no trouble with them, I got used to the 'push' feature immediately. The tops of the units do scratch - we lined them with the rubber foam liners so we can use the surface area (you can get the wide at Lowe's in the tool section). Both are very quiet - washer spins so fast you won't believe it. I was also concerned about the extended wash time with front loaders but with the size of the bin I can almost double my loads. Also, Electrolux offers an 18 minute fast wash cycle. Dryer time is incredibly fast because clothes are almost dry when they come out of the washer - 20 minutes for drying in most cases.

UPDATE 6/3/11 - I checked back and saw the comments and Electrolux began offering a steam washer shortly after our purchase. Our Electrolux IQ Touch Washer and Dryer are still going strong and we love them. No issues whatsoever, and my teenagers do their own laundry all the time.

product_title: Electrolux : EWFLS70JTS 27 Front-Load Washer with 5.1 cu. ft. Capacity
review_text: I own the set, matching dryer. Yes, it's very quiet, you can sleep next to it and it won't make a sound to wake you. The clothes always come out clean and very dry for less dryer time which helps to keep clothes looking new and in good condition. You also save on electricity.  It's definitely a water saver, it uses only what it needs. The many settings are excellent for the many different needs we come across, comforters, baby clothes, delicates, etc. The machine does what they say it does! However it feels "cheap" for said brand and the price point.  The liquid laundry compartment feels wobbly, (I tested others at the store & they felt the same), the latch to keep the door closed is plastic (and part of the door so if it breaks and you are not under warranty it's $100 dollars for that little latch). The doors don't close as smoothly, or even come open on the gentle push as smoothly. The buttons aren't as sturdy as I'd like them to be. I've had the machine 2 years, and I would have expected it to hold up a lot better than it has. Yes, I do use it maybe 3 times a week, and 2 years is a long time but at this price point I was hoping to use it for at least 7 years. So to sum it up, I originally thought this machine would be like my BMW X5; rugged but classy, tough but luxurious... instead it feels like my old Camry, reliable but it started to rattle after those 200k miles. Happy washing.

product_title: Electrolux : EWFLS70JTS 27 Front-Load Washer with 5.1 cu. ft. Capacity
review_text:
I am a mother of four and wife to a filthy (and I mean that lovingly) farmer/rancher. I do a WHOLE LOT of laundry. I bought this washer over a year ago based on positive reviews by well-meaning people who only owned it for a week.

At first, this washer was okay. We were replacing a Whirpool front-loader after the control board went out after only two years. It was comparable to the much cheaper Whirpool. The large capacity was nice, as was the quick-wash cycle (though that was ONLY for very small loads). Yes, there are a lot of fancy cycle options and a neat dial and all kinds of gizmos, but the washer itself was just okay. I didn't notice it getting anything more or less clean than any other washer we've owned. I was never gaga over it, but it did the job.

Fast-forward a year. We came home from our vacation, and the washer wouldn't spin. My husband ran diagnostics, and either the control board (which costs half or more the price of a new washer) or a pressure sensor are out. NOBODY will come work on this machine. We have heard multiple excuses, but what it boils down to is, nobody will come out and touch an Electrolux. I called Electrolux myself and was told, respectfully, that since it was a couple of months out of warranty, I was on my own. My husband even offered to load the washer up and take it to someone, but nobody would even work on it that way!

So, now, I am doing laundry for six with a 1970s-model "spare" from the in-laws, researching new washers yet again while my pricey Electrolux sits in the garage strapped to a dolly. I would not recommend this brand, or this washer.

product_title: GE APPLIANCES PT925SNSS Profile 30" Stainless Steel Electric Single-Double Wall Oven - Convection
review_text: This oven is great in that the double oven feature works great.  It is a great idea with one major design flaw.  All the controls (which are electronic) for the oven are in the top door, which has a row of slots along the top for ventilation and a slot on the bottom.  If you spill anything on the oven door (like we did) and it runs into these slots you will short out the entire oven.  Fortunately for us our oven was only three days old and GE covered the $600 repair. If you must buy this oven buy the maximum extended warranty available unless you never anticipate spilling anything on the top door.

product_title: GE APPLIANCES PT925SNSS Profile 30" Stainless Steel Electric Single-Double Wall Oven - Convection
review_text: The bottom rack in the lower oven cannot slide straight out without hitting the door and gasket - you need to tilt and lift the rack with the steaming, splattering hot turkey on it, and the turkey slides off the rear of the rack and into the oven. This is because the rack is too low. Nowhere is this mentioned in the instruction manual. To explain, when cooking a large turkey (18 lbs), you're instructed to use the offset rack in the bottom (A) position. However, you cannot slide the rack all the way out because the rack hits the oven door, particularly the gasket which is bad. Also, the rack bows with the heat and weight and ends up getting caught in the heating element, which further makes it very difficult to get the turkey out. There is no weight restriction listed for this rack; indeed, the owners manual describes an 18-20 lb turkey! I cannot recommend this oven for this reason. GE has refused to recognize that this is a design defect and so far has refused to do anything for me.

product_title: GE APPLIANCES PT925SNSS Profile 30" Stainless Steel Electric Single-Double Wall Oven - Convection
review_text:
If you need two ovens and only have room for one, this is a great oven. Yes, the lower oven may be a little tight if you're cooking an enormous turkey, but believe me, it's plenty big for a 15 lb turkey or a big standing rib roast. Both ovens preheat very quickly, around 10 minutes. It's also really nice to have the shorter doors, so you don't have to reach over as far (compared to a standard size oven) when you're loading and unloading the ovens. We use the smaller, upper oven the most. It's plenty big for baking cookies, muffins, pizza, meat loaf, Pillsbury cresent rolls, lasagna... It's kind of like having a big, commercial quality toaster oven. In fact, we decided to get rid of our countertop toaster oven and gained back that counterspace.

Each oven also has two oven lights, located in the back corners, so you can see inside really well.

In my opinion, the cooling fan really isn't that noisy. The exhaust fan above your range, set at the lowest speed, is probably noisier.

I agree with the other reviewer regarding the possibility of spilling liquid into the electronics located inside the upper oven door. GE should have designed the upper door with a drip guard, to keep stuff from falling into the slots. I would really rate this oven 4.7 stars.

My advice if you are considering this oven is to check it out first at the appliance store (we found it installed in the display kitchens at Lowes Home Improvement). Get a good feel of the size of the ovens and the rack positions. You get one rack for the upper oven and two racks for the lower oven. Make sure that will be enough for your needs. BTW, you cannot interchange the upper and lower oven racks. Ponder it carefully. Become "one with the oven". We did this 3 times, to make sure that it could handle the types of baking we do. This is a relatively expensive oven, so make sure it will fit your needs.

Again, we love it.

review_text:
As there is no need to repeat the positive comments made by the other 5-Star raters from this AND OTHER sites (with whom I totally agree), I'll just give a couple other comments/observations.

First, regarding the "noise": When I initially read these complaints - here and other sites (prior to purchase), I instantly thought, "Every washer I've ever owned makes that noise when the contents are very unevenly distributed". So I bought this model (based on the positive reviews); and I am s-o-o-o-o-o glad I did. Although NO washer I ever owned/used has been "SOUND-FREE" (SILENT), this one is quieter than ANY of the others - no "NOISE" - well, at least for the first 3- 4 days! Then there it was - a very LOUD THUMPING SOUND - "NOISE". This was my opportunity to test my theory. About 30 seconds or so earlier I had lifted the lid during the spin cycle; and apparently dislodged some items from their balanced positions. When I lifted the lid and saw that this, indeed, was the case, I simply rearranged the items (as with previous machines), closed the lid, and VOILA - problem resolved - back to quiet operation!!! Also, sometimes when tub is not centered, noise can occur - with ANY washer.

Second, I DO wish there was a TRULY HOT WATER option! This washer adjust water temp by alteranating hot with cool or warm to obtain what IT senses is the IDEAL temp for each load - based on the user's setting selections; however, I must admit that my "WHITES" DO get really clean. So I guess it's not a real issue!

SUMMARY: Not too fancy and/or expensive! Excellent basic washer (with some nice features - i.e. "extra rinse"cycle)! Does what it's suppose to do - gets laundry clean; and, does so superbly well! QUIET - WHEN BALANCED! I am extremely happy with this washer; and, would GLADLY recommend to my friends!!!

review_title: Simple, solid, good-looking, and works like a champ
review_text:
Ordered this to replace a 1980's-era Jenn-Air downdraft cooktop. We considered both conventional electric and induction cooktops when replacing our old one. This cooktop was our choice in the end and we're very pleased with it. The things that won us over:

* Appearance: Very basic and understated. We wanted something that would not quickly look out-of-style or dated.
* Functionality: We wanted a cooktop that included few bells and whistles, with simple controls and zero learning curve. This is the hands-down winner.
* Minimal changes required to install: Our install location would have made it difficult to install a separate vent hood or blower. Retaining the downdraft capability of the old unit assured us of being able to control fumes and smells predictably. This unit *DOES* require a 40-amp circuit though (as do most ranges in in the same size range). If you are replacing something more than 10 years old, make sure you take this into account for any replacement!
* Predicted reliability/maintenance. The low complexity of this unit (no high-tech components, no expensive timers/computers) means there is simply very little that can fail, short of physical damage. We really were attracted by the alternative of induction cooking, but the complexity of even a fairly basic induction cooktop made me just a bit wary.

After using it a few times, I can say that this unit is pretty close to perfect. It heats up MUCH faster than older electric cooktops with metal coil surfaces. Cleaning is simple. The exhaust fan is effective and quieter than we expected. Our installer ran into no complications at all when putting the cooktop in, and the understated, clean appearance makes this a purchase we're 100% happy with.

product_title: Frigidaire 24 in. Gas Single Wall Oven – White
review_text:
We just got this oven in black today and loved the look but were shocked to learn Frigidaire grossly misrepresented the actual interior size of this oven. They don't show these specs on Amazon, but AJMadison's website provided them, and we were counting on this oven being much closer to its reported interior size.

Our current old 24" gas wall oven is MUCH larger! Our old oven's racks are 17" x 19" deep as compared to this oven's racks being just 15" deep. That amounts to 4" less usable depth than our current oven of supposedly the same size has; and yet, it was advertised as having a depth of 18.5". However, my 17" cookie sheet does not fit.

We can't figure out how Frigidaire can get away with advertising 18.5" of interior depth - or 16" of height. They obviously ignore more than just the large broiler unit permanently installed. It seems they also ignore whatever comprises the walls of this oven, too! That is deceptive advertising. By this initial review, I just want to clarify these measurements for other buyers so they will know what they are getting BEFORE they buy it online like we did. Later, after we use it a while, I will add comments about performance.

Interior specs are important to know if you have other options than just replacing an existing wall oven of a certain size. Since our existing wall oven still works well, we did not need to replace it. We just thought it would help us sell our home more quickly if we had an attractive new, self-cleaning oven in its place. We had updated everything else in our country kitchen a couple years ago, but left this because it still worked so well and it was kind of quaint. If we had known we would be losing so much interior oven space by spending almost $1,600 for this one (with installation), we would have never ordered it.

Our 24" gas wall oven's usable depth is 20" - with an actual interior height of 14" throughout since it's broiler is in a drawer below. The width is about the same, 17". We thought we would be losing a little in depth but would gain some in usable height, based on the specs stated online. After all, this new oven is supposed to have 2.9 cu. ft. of space, which sounds large. In reality, however, it is not. It is the size of a large microwave, but with less usable height inside.

Frigidaire claims that the interior oven measures 18.5" deep x 17" wide x 16" tall. However, it's depth with door closed is only about 17" and it is only 13" tall at the highest point - which is nowhere near 16". In the rear third of the oven, there is less than 12" of height due to a self-cleaning gas component. If we had known this, we would have opted for a manual-cleaning unit, gotten more usable height, and save hundreds of dollars.

We think these specs provided are purposefully misleading. They make this oven seem larger and more useful than it really is. The broiler measures 2" high in the center x 10" wide and extends the entire depth of the oven - and is not removable. So, why else would Frigidaire not see fit to take it into account when giving an interior height? And the shallow depth! That just killed me to see because it is so much shallower than our old oven.

When it arrived, I was shocked. So, I measured it and called AJMadison immediately to complain and arrange to return it. However, they wanted to check with Frigidaire. When Frigidaire said (not surprisingly) that its measurements were not misleading, we were told we would have to pay 30% restocking fee if we sent it back - plus shipping. The restocking fee alone would be more than $300, so we are keeping the darn thing. This was a very expensive lesson for us.

I am a "detail person" and an experienced buyer, but I never imagined I could not trust the actual interior specs of an oven. I thought it would be black and white, but apparently, manufacturers will do everything they can to make its product seem bigger or better than it actually is - and Frigidaire did mislead us. With a depth of 18.5", I had good reason to believe I would be able to continue using my 11 x 17" cookie sheets, but I can't in this oven. Plus, with that upper broiler taking up so much of the height - in addition to losing another 3" of space underneath the lowest rack - one cannot bake anything more than 9.5" high. This oven is just too small to be worth the money.

In the future, I will never assume the specs of an appliance are real. If a spec is really important to me, I will always either measure it myself or call the manufacturer and get them to EMAIL ME the ACTUAL measurement - so I will have it in writing before I order it.

This oven looks nice enough, but it is really too small to serve as an only oven. At this price point and with the high cost of installing a gas appliance, one would be better off planning to put in a 30" range instead of replacing an older gas wall oven. The newer ones seem very inferior. Our really old Real Host oven still works well, but it no longer looks so good. Other reviews I have read on this oven on other websites say its oven temp needs to be recalibrated, so be sure to have that checked out when installing it if you happen to buy it.

Also, it does not even come with a broiler pan, and the lower storage drawer that used to be a broiler is still only big enough when opened to hold a 14"-wide broiler pan! Frigidaire never reconfigured the inside of this drawer for storage. It is still just 14" wide at the top and only 13" wide at the bottom, as if it was meant to hold a broiler pan. So, I am keeping our old one. Nothing else will fit into it, even though it looks like a 24" wide storage drawer. That, to me, shows how very little Frigidaire cares about serving the needs of those who buy this wall oven.

product_title: Whirlpool : WFG114SVB 30 Freestanding Gas Range with 4 Semi-Sealed Burners Black
review_text:
These stoves are known to have limited insulation and heat shielding causing the outside of the range to get hot to the touch and I can attest to this. Also these models make tons of noise (expansion and contraction) when heating up and cooling down. The single worst thing though is the computer control jobby! It must have been designed by lab monkeys or something. I have had 3 service calls and have a 4th scheduled right now all for the same issue in less than two months. Apparently moisture and/or condensation gets inside the control module and causes it to throw an error code. This turns out to be nice business for the local Factory Repair company since they get to bill Whirlppol every time they come out here; but it is an unbelieveable nightmare for me. After the warmup countdown the stove almost always throws an F2 (stuck key) error code. Meaning that I then have to unplug and power down the unit for at least 2 minutes. Anything less and it locks you out of the control panel entirely. While it is powered down this unit is useless as the electronic ignition wont work. Keeping the clock set is pointless as well seeing as how you are going to have to shut it down nearly every time you use the oven. The last time the repair guy was here he mentioned the moisture issue. This seems to be a situation that Whirlpool knows about and has done nothing to fix.

Update! Finally got a repairman who had dealt with this issue before and knew how to fix. Apparently the way the exhuast goes therre is an inherent risk of overheating the control panel. He manually bent the exhaust pipe or whatever it is called. Now when you run the oven the stovetop gets hot enough to melt anything plastic left on the range.....However, it know works like it should have from the factory. It appears that the design has a correctable flaw and that Whirlpool would rather spend money and waste the time of customers by making you deal with repeat repair calls for an issue they can and should fix before sale or at the very least on the first visit.

This stove is also a beauty to look at. Keeping it clean is difficult with the super gloss finish. After a scrub down with your cleanser and sponge of choice use a solution made from any common degreaser spray and dawn....A little goes a long way and then polish the range with a dishcloth. This is the only way I have found to keep it gleaming.

UPDATE 03/19/2011
This thing started throwing the SAME F2 code again! This things is a lemon! I have owned it less than 4 months and It still does the same thing after 5 0r 6 repair visits!!! I am filing BBB, Attorney General and Federal Trade Commission complaints! The Whirlpool company has now paid out more in repair costs than I paid for the range and I still don't have a properly functioning stove!

STAY away from Whirlpool Appliances! Look at other consumer sites and you will see that they are apparently slapping the Whirlpool nameplate on a lot of poorly designed and manufactured garbage!

review_text:

he told me that he had tried to repair these machines before, and they didn't get better.

might be my fault, that the floor wasn't "stiff" enough, despite the fact that it had worked
fine for a year, and that I had previously had a front load washer in the same spot without
issue for 10 years. I spent a lot to reinforce the floor, and the machine was no different.

At last, they told me they were giving up, they didn't know how to fix it. I have never had
anyone tell me they didn't know how to fix their own product and were just giving up. They
told me they would "buy it back", for a sum prorated for the life of the washer since it
was out of warranty.

They picked up the unit. I have yet to see a dime from LG. Every week I call them and it is
something else, the machine got shipped to the wrong place, the paperwork got misplaced, etc.
I am convinced they are trying to slow pay it.

I expected better from LG. This is a top of the line washer. It is also the last LG product
I ever buy. Everything points to the machine being an inherent lemon.

Scott Moore
San Jose, CA

review_text:
Purchased this fridge through Sears the end of February 2010. Looked good at the store. However, when set up at our home the ice maker didn't dispense from the start. Called Sears service. Told them ice maker didn't work. They sent out a repairman. "Yep! Ice maker doesn't work, but I don't have a replacement icemaker. I'll have to back order it."

Ice maker is left at front door by UPS about 10 days later. Arranged second repair call. Second Sears repairman installs new ice maker unit and leaves. Ice maker still doesn't dispense. (receipt claims warranty service would have been $239 if not covered).

Called Sears service who schedule third service call. "Yep! Ice maker still doesn't dispense, but the only thing left to do is replace the mother board on the back. But I don't have one. I'll have to back order it."

Sears left an automated call yesterday April 18 to reschedule the fourth service call set for today, Monday the 19th of April. I call them and they say OK when do you want the appointment. I ask whether they have the part. They say they thought I already had it. I say no I don't. They say I shouldn't call until I do. I say how about bringing out a new fridge. They say May 8 earliest.

The one repairman observed that this is Samsung's newest model. I would wait a year or two before buying one to let them get the bugs out and at least have parts in the pipeline. As for Sears. It's just mindboggling.

product_title: Samsung : RF265ABBP 26 cu. ft. French-Door Refrigerator - Black Pearl
review_text:
I would have given this unit a 2 out of 5 stars had customer service for Samsung been terrible but I am happy to say that they have been, at least, accommodating. I have owned this unit for about 2 years but only used it for about 1.5 years (as we purchased during the process of building a house which took longer than expected). About 6-9 months ago I noticed an odd odor coming from the refrigerator portion of the unit. Upon inspection I found that under the large drawer in the bottom a large amount of water had accumulated (enough to completely soak a regular sized bath towel and then some). I thought that perhaps someone had spilled something or somehow the door had been left open (though there is an alarm to help prevent that) and condensation had occurred. Just theories/rationalizations that there couldn't be anything wrong with our brand new refrigerator. I cleaned up the water, read the owners manual to make sure there wasn't anything else I should be concerned about and then didn't think about it again, for a while.

About 2-3 months went by when I began to notice an odd odor again. This time when I found the water I contacted a repair person (via phone) just to get an idea if this was something I needed to contact the company about and if there might be something actually wrong because I was fairly certain that no one had spilled anything and the door was not left open. The repair person indicated that this problem was one that he was very familiar with as he had seen it in other similar units; a problem common to these units. So I contacted Samsung and they at first informed me that the unit was no longer covered by warranty. I asked for a supervisor since the unit had only been in use for about 11 months at that point, and was granted a warranty extension.

A repair person came and diagnosed the issue and advised me that he would need to order a part and then he would come back and repair it. It turned out that particular part was on back order and I had to wait over a month to have the repair done. Now please be aware the leak is one that takes about a week to produce 1 Tbsp of liquid in the bottom of the fridge which is why it took me so long to realize there was a problem... because additionally there is a long drawer in the bottom of the unit so no reason to regularly check the very bottom of the refrigerator until I knew there was a problem. So the leak never caused a mess except having to clean up the water (which getting the drawer out is somewhat annoying due to the position of the unit but otherwise not terrible).

The part came and the repair person came and removed the back panel where I was able to see what the problem is with the unit. The drain was not clogged btw for those of you who are familiar with refrigerators and know that could have caused this issue. Apparently the cooling coils sit behind the panel in the back of the inside of the unit. Since the coils are right behind the panel as they thaw (especially if your power goes out as it is prone to do during storms and such) and cool condensation can form on the inside of the panel. Samsung tried to address this issue by having a piece of metal that angles in at the bottom of the panel and allows the condensation to drain into the drain which is directly below the coils. The flaw in this design seems to be two fold. First, the bottom of that piece of metal is only approximate to the drain it doesn't connect to it directly allowing water to flow over the edge of the metal and out the bottom front edge of the panel. Additionally, the design includes metallic tape to keep the drain portion "sealed" to the inside back wall of the unit (this is behind the removable panel I previously been discussing). What seems to happen is as this tape gets wet it begins to bubble which further enables the water to flow in the direction of the bottom front edge of the removable back panel.

I have now had two repairs trying to correct this problem and Samsung is still trying to make things right for us. Props for Samsung in that respect but I will remind anyone reading this that I did have to insist (politely) that they "make it right," by asking to speak with a manager.

What do I like about the unit? Well, I will tell you what I was looking for:
1. It doesn't have an in-the-door ice and water dispenser. I believe they take up too much room in the refrigerator and have more potential for future problems and messes. This unit actually doesn't have a water dispenser at all (there is one just like it that has one inside the door but I didn't want that feature).
2. A bottom drawer that is sturdy and allows easy access to both the top and bottom portions. This unit performs very well in that respect.
3. Smooth paint finish (even though finger prints show up more on a smooth finish I find it more aesthetically pleasing). In case you want to know the sides still have the older rough finish but mine is surrounded by built in cabinets so you can't see it.
4. Great amount of interior refrigerator space. I don't think I've ever filled it to where I didn't have enough room for something. I do own an extra freezer though so freezer space was not an issue and I never really considered it to be too small. I usually put our Thanksgiving turkey (when it's time for it) in the bottom drawer with still enough room to freeze other things as well.
5. Sturdily built. Despite the issues I've dealt with from the leak I still think it is well built and designed with the one rather annoying exception I have already shared the details.
6. An alarm if the door or drawer is left open. This unit has one and it's sort of musical and not too annoying.

Finally, I would just encourage anyone who is considering this unit to think hard about the issues I've mentioned and certainly be on the lookout for the leak. I would consider buying a unit from Samsung again but I would definitely not choose this unit or any that had the back panel design that this one does. I hope you find this review helpful.

Edited to add that the issues were finally resolved with Samsung replacing our unit with a similar unit different model number. No more issues have arisen in almost a year. Samsung's customer service along with our local dealer (The Appliance Center) working with them = nothing short of stellar.

review_text: A severe design flaw should deter you from purchasing this refrigerator.  This refrigerator/freezer worked well enough for 2 years, and then like clockwork, water slowly started to leak from the inside bottom of the refrigerator unit.  This water originated from the defrost cycle.  Normally, the defrosted water flows out through a drain located below the heater/defrost coils.  Because the system could no longer handle the water, ice began to form and plugged the drain.  The accumulated ice caused water to back up and rusted the drain plate.  I called Samsung to see if they would honor their warranty, but they would not pay for the repairman to fix the problem.  I had to pay $217 to fix this problem temporarily, plus the cost of replacing the food that spoiled.  Of course they did not cover that.  You see, the refrigerator door was open the whole time while the repairman ran back and forth to his truck while a lot of my food sat out at room temperature to clear space.  Who knows if this problem will happen again?

product_title: Samsung RSG257AARS 24.1 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel Counter Depth Side-By-Side Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_text:
We bought this refrigerator about a year ago from Sears. They just called to offer me an extended warranty, so I looked at the reviews again. Figured I'd put in my 2¢.

Here is my opinion after a year:

Plenty of space, absurdly quiet, keeps things very cold with uniform temps throughout, beautiful lighting.
Veggie drawers: Yes, they don't open far enough unless you open the door more than 90º and then pull them out with a little uplift to boost them over the stop. Not a big deal, unless you can't open the door more than 90º.
Ice Maker: We haven't found it to be too slow at making ice for normal use. But if you're having a party, you might want to save up some in a gallon ziplock plastic bag in advance. It does take a few seconds (1-2) for the ice to come out of the dispenser. The chute is poorly designed and can get blocked with accumulated frost and ice particles. So sometimes ( every 3-4 months, maybe) the thing will only dispense crushed ice and I know that it's time to remove the ice cube container and use the handle of a wooden spoon to clear out the chute in the door (or the bottom of the container itself, too). If you don't do that then eventually nothing will come out except the noise of the ice maker. This is actually not a big deal however. I would still buy this refrigerator even with the incompetently designed ice maker. It does make one wonder, though. Something like this isn't designed by idiots. product_title: Samsung RSG257AARS 24.1 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel Counter Depth Side-By-Side Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_title: Huge capacity, sleek and modern, easy to clean
review_text:
We purchased this refridgerator as a replacement. It's our first large appliance purchase on-line, and we were very satisfied with the delivery experience. The refridgerator was well packaged, with all stainless steel surfaces covered with plastic coating to prevent scratching.

The interior is very large capacity, shelves are easy to adjust. One shelf even slides back to allow us to put in extra tall vases or drinks. There is a wine rack - very cool - that you can also remove. There is a tip-out condiment rack we use to store hot-sauces, and one nice thing about all these racks is that you can adjust them and move them any way you want. Three big bins for veggies, fruit, and meats. Interior lights are bright, and no dark spots in fridge where old containers can linger.

Exterior door water is very nice, chills water and provides cubed and crushed ice. Crushed ice is fairly slow to load. Buttons on the front allow you to lock, but on the con-side they are also easy to accidently push (if the child-lock is not on) and screw up your freezer/fridge cooling settings (these really should have been put insider the fridge and out of the way of small children and tired adults getting water in the middle of the night). Ice maker is fairly quiet. Stainless steel surface holds smears and fingerprints like nobody's business and is difficult to clean, but that seems typical for this surface type.

Freezer cools very quickly. Fridge is wide enough to hold a standard pizza box in cooler and in freezer section, but just barely. Freezer has adjustable bins, allows you to see the ice (held on the door) but ice bucket is very difficult to get back into place. Lighting in the freezer is bright, but not as efficient at eliminating dark spots as in fridge.

Other exterior is pebbled grey enamel, looks good. Magnets won't stick to front, only sides. Kick plate at bottom holds dust bunnies relentlessly, you will need to get a brush to clean it out properly.

Overall we're very content with this - it's not perfect, but it's a really nice fridge!

product_title: Samsung RSG257AARS 24.1 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel Counter Depth Side-By-Side Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_text:
This fridge is not for everyone but after reading the reviews and doing my own measurements I decided this unit would work for my family. I'm rating a 5 because it delivers what I expected and a little more.

First, if you don't need nor do you value a counter depth model, I don't know why anyone would look at this model. Bigger models exist. I had a 25.5 Kitchenaid unit last time and it stuck out on my room all I could stand. In 12 years they actually got deeper and most units would protrude an extra 2 inches over my last unit; 4 inches over this unit. So I bought based on room looks which were important to my wife and I.

I think this unit is ideal for a family who has a second fridge to help with that Costco run and wants a slim line nice looking fridge in the kitchen. Quality of build and cooling performance are excellent.

On the ice maker. The total capacity of the unit is 1 gallon freezer bag. My last unit likely held 3 gallon bags of ice but in addition to eating 20% of my freezer, the ice got freezer burn. A gallon bag of ice is more then my family of 5 uses per day and our ice is fresh. Also note two more factors if you are a big ice family. 1) Icemaker is smaller then my old unit and 2) it is in the door so if you open the unit a great deal it will make ice slower. The ice maker meets all my needs but this fridge is not a world class ice maker by any means.

I worked on the shelves of the fridge so that I can get 3 gallons of milk in the interior of the fridge. Play with the shelf configuration options to find what works for your family.

Tonight I had to take a head of lettuce in and out of the fridge. I had to open the door fully and start to remove the drawer. Drawer is roughly 8 inches at the opening and a head of lettuce is bigger. The engineering could absolutely be better but the extra 15 seconds I spent on this task was not a big deal to me; especially since I measured before purchase and knew this was what I was getting.

If you can get along with the three above points and you want a slim line, nice looking, great performing fridge then this unit should be on the consideration set.

review_title: Parts difficult to obtain for repairs low quality
review_text:
I have owned this product for just over three years so I have some real experience with it. It is very attractive and the lighting is very cool inside. However, in less than a year, cracks appeared in the plastic molding around the tempered glass on several shelves. This is a common failure. It was fixed under warranty then they cracked again after warranty.

The freezer wouldn't get cold enough after three years 6 months. I made the mistake of getting a national firm, A and E Factory Service, who service samsung warranty and out of warranty Samsung appliances. I got them because it was possible it was a sealed system problem which is covered for 5 years. Two weeks later Tech shows up, waves a thermometer probe in the freezer side and declares it is the temperature sensor (thermistor) not keeping the compressor on long enough. I write a check for 80 something bucks for his time and for the part to be shipped to me. Then they would come out and install the part for $170+. Whoa--and it will take another two to three weeks. I put it in myself as it was as difficult as a light bulb. Freezer still not working properly--didn't fix anything. I then called a local repair guy I know who is competent and he came out, took some panels off the frig and determined that the recirculating fan was not working because it was getting no power(he checked that with proper instrumentation). The freezer was cool, not cold, because the compressor fan was working, but the recirculating fan was not.

Now I wait for weeks for the back ordered control board.

Stay away from all Samsung appliances. Do your googling and you will find many, many unhappy customers because of their lack of parts and frequent failures. Google A and E too. Even a local mom and pop appliance store stopped carrying Samsung because they were catching hell from customers who couldn't get their appliances repaired. I have learned my lesson.

product_title: Samsung RSG257AARS 24.1 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel Counter Depth Side-By-Side Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_text:
This review is addressed to Samsung; Dear Samsung,

I purchased your Samsung refrigerator model no: RSG257AARS/XAA, back in Dec. 2013 when I bought my first home.

While I am not customarily someone who uses ice in my drinks, there are certain beverages wherein I do use ice, such as with a soda or a cocktail. But for water and juices I do not require ice and as I rarely drink a soda or have a cocktail I can't say the ice maker on my unit has had much use considering I am a one person household.

This little to no use of the icemaker is potentially why this problem with the ice maker/dispenser did not appear until 6 months later, in July 2014.

I first noticed the problem when I dispensed ice and discovered a large white shaving of plastic floating in a glass of Coke-a-Cola. It was the size of a coconut shaving and so I removed this remnant and secured it into a plastic zip lock bag. Obviously, I disposed of the drink.

I then examined the ice maker machine and mechanism, removed the ice bucket etc. and discovered there were dozens upon dozens of plastic shavings sitting in the cavity of freezer below the ice bucket. Upon further examination I discovered areas on the left and right sides of the plastic housing wherein it was obvious the rotary blades (auger couplers) had literally shredded into the plastic housing and it was quite clear from the magnitude of the scratches, shavings and debris that this was a serious problem.

I received service to repair this problem in July 2014. However, the repair took nearly 4 weeks to conclude, two home visits, shipment of parts, and I had no ice available to me in that time. Moreover, I greatly needed ice to medically treat an injury. Thus, the repair was more than an inconvenience. While the repair included some new parts and a new ice bucket, after the repair, I was still hesitant and nervous to use the ice cubes for drinking and would look in each glass of ice.

Then just a few days ago on Oct 20, 2014, I found a SHARP solid chunk of white plastic floating in my drink. Again, I removed it and secured it in a zip lock bag for evidence.

Upon examination of the unit, I now find that the plastic housing under the ice bucket is again being impacted and hit, only this time the scratches and scrapings are at the front of the housing rather than on the sides. To make matters worse, on the evening of Oct 21st, I observed small white tiny powder like particles, sitting on the outside stainless steel dispenser tray, which indicates I have been ingesting and drinking micro particles of plastic. I have obtained a small sample of this particle by pressing my finger down onto it and then scraping this fine particle off my finger into a zip lock bag, but the particles are so small and fine that one could literally not pick them up any other way. It would be like trying to collect a single grain or flake of salt.

As of late, I have been enjoying one soda a day, in place of eating a desert, and have been having more iced drinks than usual. Again, this draws me to the conclusion that if only this icemaker and dispenser had had normal American household use this problem would have most likely occurred much sooner.

At this stage, my main concern is my HEALTH and how my body has been affected by ingesting micro fine particles of plastic used to make an appliance.

To be honest, I am more than upset by the gravity of the situation and I find your customer service to be sub-par. In my opinion, this unit is DEFECTIVE IN DESIGN. Any refrigerator that starts dispensing plastic for a HUMAN TO EAT AND INGEST SHOULD BE DEALT WITH IN AN APPROPRIATE MANNER, and does not even fall within the scope of an ordinary repair.

I can no longer trust this appliance to provide me ice! In addition, I will never again use it for drinking ice. NO WAY! NEVER! No matter how you repair it or pretend you did, it is obvious the that METAL BLADES are able to make contact with all edges of the plastic housing and therefore will ALWAYS HAVE THE POTIENTAL to feed me plastic.

Next time I see my doctor I will consult with him on this matter. In the meantime, feel free to send me the chemical composition with which this plastic material is made of and I will give that to my doctor. Alternatively, we can send samples to a lab and then I will bill and or sue Samsung.

I am outraged at this situation! Period!

The fact that you are again going to send me a service repair person whom has NO experience with this SPECIFIC problem is ridiculous. Moreover, two Samsung service repair technicians told me they had never heard of this problem. So all you are doing is putting a Band-Aid on this situation, waiting for the manufacturer warranty to run out so that you will not have to contend with it. So yes, I am outraged. I will never again buy Samsung.

In closing, I am attaching photos from last July showing evidence of the plastic shavings and impact to the housing. The current plastic particles are too small to photograph and while this is the same problem, the particles in fact are completely different now in shape and size. In fact the smaller particles and this current situation is way worse because I can NOT VISABLY see the micro-particles in a drink making this a blatant health hazard. Please review the photos carefully! I would like this case to be escalated and dealt with by your upper management.

UPDATE: On Nov 10 Samsung has agreed to authorize an exchange and or provide store credit for my refrigerator. I asked to be additionally be compensated some $70 for the two water filters I recently purchased (1 still new in the box as I can't return it to Amazon as I'm past 30 days) but Samsung executive care wrote me back saying they do not reimburse any additional cost or accessories! So not only have I basically lost 2 months of my life dealing with this situation and am still in need medical treatment, but I'm out of pocket for water filters as well. Mind you the ice dispenser uses the water filter and I had to dispose of gallons of ice in dealing with repairs and this situaiton. So I hardly see this as fair monetary compensation.

review_text:
Replacement fridge for our old side-by-side. We love the french door style with roomy interior. The drawers are NOT sloppy and get off track like the GE and Whirlpool models we looked at. The glass shelves with the spill proof border makes cleanup easy(the paper milk carton sometimes leaks).

The water/ice dispenser is on the door. Nice easy to read text/images on the computer screen above the water/ice. Water taste fantastic even though we have terrific tap water because it goes through a replaceable Samsung filter which removes impurities.

No problem with ice production. Good volume of ice, crushed or cubed. The computer readout above the ice/water dispenser is a nice blue text, telling what the features are enabled, what the temp is in the fridge or freezer, and has a little beep that tells when changing information. There is a little audible alarm if the door was left open which is nice because there are more efficient ways to cool the house.

Very pleased with this product.[[ASIN:B001P63PD2 Samsung RF267ABWP 25.5 cu. ft. French-Door Refrigerator with 5 Glass Shelves, Spill Proof, Twin Cooling System, CoolSelect Pantry, Power Freeze/Cool Options, External Ice/Water Dispenser and LED Display: White]]

product_title: Samsung : RF267ABWP 26 cu. ft. French-Door Refrigerator - White Pearl
review_title: overall good compromise on cost v quality
review_text:
Edit. Fridge crapped out after a few years. Samsung appliances are junk - wasted my money on their microwave too.

Ice/water dispenser - negatives: requires you to push a button to cycle through water, cubes, crushed. Dispenser allows a drip of water to fall outside of cup if you pull it away in a normal natural fashion (not enough to be problematic but still annoying). We might not have noticed this as a problem if we hadn't switched from a fridge that had ice and water dispensed from separate openings so you could get ice water one-handed. Cubes are a bit small and water dispenses slowly. Water filters are spendy. Positives: The icemaker is pretty compact inside the fridge and having a door dispenser does not hit seem to the unit's efficiency too hard. Water tastes good, and this is a relatively economical way to get filtered water. Has LED auto-on and auto-off light on dispenser

Exterior: the white handles look cheap, but they feel solid and nice. The freezer handle has to lift up to pull out, which my toddler figured out in about 4 seconds flat. If the fridge gripper feet are not tightened, the whole unit may move when you pull out the freezer - annoying if you like to have it loose to clean around it all the time; I don't like getting down there to loosen and tighten the feet. But it's a good compromise. The fridge front is quite convex, and it looks just plain colossal in our 1960s kitchen - definitely better suited to a newer home. I haven't tried to clean the finish yet, and I'd be surprised if it didn't scratch fairly easily with something like a Magic Eraser, but it's so slick that stuff should come off easy. The front is low so that only the very smallest toys can slip under there - I haven't had any of our plastic alphabet get lost.

Inside: lower-high-end to higher middle, was my impression after shopping. Nice solid shelves. I didn't go for the special wide drawer, because I could tell it would break with the abuse in our household, and it isn't very useful considering you have to open both doors to get into it. I'm glad I didn't -- however, there does seem to be some wasted headspace now. The door holds milk jugs, and there seems to be an extra rack/door box; I can't get all of them to fit in a way that seems practical because they are so deep. Humidity controls on the crispers really make a difference, nice! The drawer durability is probably about average. In the freezer, the movable divider on the bottom is so-so design - freezer has to be pretty much completely empty to move it. The wheels on the inner drawer are nylon and probably won't outlast the fridge, especially if it gets heavily loaded often, but they seem better than other brands in this range. The freezer feels spacious - you can pile stuff pretty high - I am very happy.

Has an alarm if you leave the door open (or you can turn the alarm off), which as you may suspect, means that it's too easy to leave the door open. The left hand door won't swing gently shut but has to be pushed. Interior lights are bulbs, which I think is a plus because who knows how long that LED stuff really lasts ... I *know* how to change a bulb.

I didn't want the digital display, but it seems to be the thing now, so I'm grudgingly enjoying being able to monitor the temp and set it exactly to a particular temp. It holds the temp really well even after repeated opening, and you can tell it to "power cool" the fridge or freezer if it gets warm. Oh, and there are control thingies under a panel at the front of the top of the fridge, which you can't see but it is very annoying if you like to store things for easy access on top of the fridge.

Overall I'm pretty happy with it - very decent quality fridge for under 2k, one of the more efficient ones with an ice dispenser, without an excess of unnecessary bells and whistles to break, and no more design annoyances than average.

review_title: Cooktop is nice - the exhaust unit is not
review_text:
My stove top arrived quickly and was well packed. It was replacing an earlier model (about 15 years old) of the same brand. It does heat quickly (about the same as our olderunit)and I like the improvements they made to make the surface area flat around the control knobs. In short, compared to our older model, there are much fewer places for dirt to collect. Our old model also had steel borders around the cooking models, and these wore out over time and looked ugly. This new model gets rid of the borders, which is also a nice improvement.

So I would give it 5 stars, except that there are issues with the down draft. First, the fan unit and exhaust hole protrude much futher down than the previous model. This gives 2-3 inches of less room to work with, which makes a HUGE difference. BY the time you put on the rectangle-to-round adapter, you are basically hitting the bottom of the cabinet. It was impossible to connect to the existing vent piping, which is very annoying since the old unit was basically the same model, etc.. as this new one. The only way I was able to get everything to work was to go to a smaller pipe size (down from 6" to 5") and run the 5" pipe a few inches into the existing 6 inch pipe, and wrap it up with ducting tape. In the end it worked, but I feel it is a design flaw to have the exhaust protrude so far down,which really limits your options if replacing an existing stove top. When installed in a standard countertop, you can expect to have less than 2" of room between the end of the exhaust adapter, and the bottom of the cabinet.

It also does not come with any clamps to hold it in place (the old unit had long screws for this). However I justkeep it in place by gravity,and this seems to work fine.

review_text: People you are CRAZY if you buy this fridge!  We bought ours a little over 2 years ago, worked fine till a couple of days ago.  Called out a repairman, he came out and I told him it wasn't cooling, he said "uh oh, I think I know what's wrong with it, common for these Whirlpool refrigerators."  So he proceeded to take the back off and check a few things.  Says there is a refrigerant leak in the "sealed system"  And he said that unfortunately they stopped giving a 5 year warranty on this, now they only warranty it for one year.  But the really bad news is its not repairable... they leak is in the coils between the fridge and the freezer, they are molded inside and you cannot get to them.  So therefore it cannot be repaired.  So I did a little research online... this is VERY common for Whirlpool side by side fridges... Found 100s of complaints and not one of them said Whirlpool took care of their problem.  Even found one website where someone used to work for Whirlpool and they know this is a design flaw but will not do anything about it!  That's why they changed the warranty from 5 years to 1 year!!!!  And its not just this model, its all the side by side models!  NEVER, NEVER, NEVER will I buy another Whirlpool or Maytag product again!!

review_text:
After posting the review below, I was contacted by a representative of Amazon.com. He agreed that Haier America's response to my dryer problems was not appropriate and was taking far too long. He said that he would contact Haier and request, on behalf of Amazon.com, that Haier immediately replace the defective dryer that they were taking so long to repair. Within days Haier contacted me and let me know they were sending a replacement for the defective dryer. Within another few days I received by new, and properly working dryer. I thank Amazon.com for making the effort to help one of their customers who was not being properly served by one of Amazon's suppliers.

While this dryer performed adequately when I first received it, after 8 months it abruptly stopped working. When I contacted the manufacturer they made arrangements for a service company to come out and repair it. After 3 trips they could not repair the dryer because the third part that was determined the dryer needed was not available from the manufacturer and was on back order. Eventually the service division for the manufacturer told me they would request a replacement for the dryer since they did not know when the part would be available. By this time 6 weeks have elapsed since my dryer stopped working. The manufacturer has still not given me any information as to when the dryer will be replaced or in fact if they will honor their warranty and repair or replace the dryer.

I also contacted Amazon.com to see if they, as the seller of the dryer, could persuade the manufacturer of the dryer to fulfill their obligation and replace my dryer. I was told by the representative at Amazon that they could do nothing.

I will certainly never buy another Haier product or any appliance from Amazon.com in the future.
[[ASIN:B001QLFFES Haier RDE350AW 6-1/2 Cubic Feet Electric Dryer, White]]

review_title: broken after 18 mos of moderate use
review_text:
When the time came, we replaced our Bosch dishwasher with this whirlpool model based on whirlpool's record of reliability. MISTAKE! After 18 mos of moderate use (family of three that eats-out often), the control panel stopped working and we found the basin filled with water.

We called whirlpool to report the problem. Because the product had been installed more than one year ago, the product was no longer under warranty and we were offered the repair plus one extended warranty for $270.

The service person replaced the thermal fuse. Three weeks later, the same issue occurred: control panel froze and standing water in basin. Because of the holiday and having to report each incident to whirlpool, the service date is one week out.

BTW: our Whirlpool HE toploader washing machine's control panel went out just shy of five years after purchasing it. Fortunately, replacement parts were covered. The service tech said it is less expensive to buy a new machine than to have this one repaired again. Not what you want to hear from your appliance repair tech.

What happened to washing machines and other appliances that lasted 15 years and cost less than $500?

review_text:
I bought this dryer along with the washer and pedestals. They look great and I like many of the features. The washer "talks" to the dryer and relays information based on the cycles you select so that all you need to do is throw your wet clothes in and it automatically sets the time for you. Sensor Dry is a nice feature as well. Relatively quiet units.

I bought them in March of 2009. The Smart Dispense system on the washer didn't work, so they had to send a technician out to replace a circuit board. Since then it's been trouble free....until now. The dryer drum stopped turning. I thought maybe the belt had snapped, so I was able to open the unit following some online instructions. Belt was broken, but it turns out the pully and the motor are also shot. 2.5 years old and we use it a few times a week (family of 5). Considering that I paid over $1000 for the dryer, you would imagine it would last much longer.

Now, GE wants to charge me $100 to come out and tell me what I already know - that the motor is dead. They said if that is indeed the case, they'd offer me $100 coupon to buy a new unit. If it comes to that, I'll probably simply get a Whirlpool and not worry about them matching or "talking to each other".

Lesson learned. Function > Form.

product_title: Electrolux EW26SS70IS 25.9 cu. ft. Side by Side Refrigerator w/Wave-Touch - Stainless Steel
review_text:
This refrigerator looks great, has nice features, but its design and functionality fall short of its physical appearance. I have had this refrigerator for almost exactly 3 years. When I bought it, it was $2300 (Best Buy...they had the lowest price), and as with all things electronic, the price has gone down some since then. My criticism begins with the water and ice dispenser. The water dispenses at an acceptable rate, but within the first month of installing the new water filter (which needs to be done every 4-6 mos and costs $50-60/filter, pretty pricey, but not as bad as buying bottled), the water pressure noticeably decreases to the point that by the end of month 2, it's painfully slow (I counted to 25 before I got an 8 oz glass of water). The ice dispenser is a disaster. It's almost impossible to get ice into a glass without ice going all over the floor. I suspect this is a combination of 2 things: the shape of the cube (they're elongated, and invariably they back up in the mouth of the dispenser or the glass or water bottle into which I'm trying to get ice because they turn sideways) and short length the chute out of which the ice is funneled--I suspect it needs to be longer. But these issues are more inconvenience which I can live with (although for $2300, I would expect these features to work as advertised).

Now for the actual malfunctioning. On month 13, the computer that controls the temperature started malfunctioning. Specifically, the water dispenser (yes, the dispenser that did so slowly) would NOT SHUT OFF. When I took my glass out from under the dispenser--get this!--it kept dispensing water. I nearly flooded my kitchen floor b/c I didn't know I could hold down the lock 'button' (there are no buttons--it's entirely flat touch screen) to override the dispenser. 3 weeks and a backordered part later, and the over-achieving water dispenser was fixed. (The technician, by the way, told me he's repaired some 10 or 12 units that have had the same problem.)

Fast-forward 2 years. The unit made some suspicious low groaning-like sounds. I knew this wasn't good. But they subsided. For a week. Then the sound came back, only exponentially louder now. Dog growling at this beautiful, sleek appliance that sounded more 747 than hi tech gadget, I called for repair. Same tech as before, identifies the problem as a leaking ice maker. Orders part. The next morning, the readout that should be displaying the freezer and refrigerator temperatures is instead reading 'EF'. Two unopened half gallons of ice cream are melted, and the refrigerator is clearly not cold. The bottom of the freezer however contains (thankfully) properly frozen food. Another call to Geek Squad (despite purchasing what I wrongly assumed was a quality product, I still opted for the 5-year platinum extended warranty, and now I'm so glad I did!), and they tell me this sounds like an entirely different problem.

Are the leaking ice maker and inability for the unit to stay cold related? Who knows. Frankly, it doesn't matter. I've had enough problems that I now know I will NEVER purchase an Electrolux refrigerator again.

Oh, and ease and efficiency of cleaning the unit? IMPOSSIBLE. You need tools (!) to unscrew the drawers to gain access to the bottom of the refrigerator and freezer, where debris easily collects and you can equally easily see.

From everything I've read and based on my experience with other major appliances, go with LG. If I have one more issue with this unit, I'm replacing it with an LG model.

***UPDATE 9/2/2012***

After having the refrigerator serviced for the issue I detailed above, it turned out the fan responsible for ventilating and cooling the unit was blocked by construction debris the builder failed to clean up prior to install. It's been working since the fan was cleaned, but the ice maker continues to leak in the freezer, where the water freezes into a large block in on the top freezer shelf, and the unit makes unusual buzzing sounds, which the tech has been unable to fix. My opinion about Electrolux refrigerators remains unchanged--I will not buy this brand when it comes time to replace it.

**************************

review_title: Great at first, then things go wrong
review_text:
I bought this dryer just over two years ago, along with the matching Samsung washing machine. For the first year and a half I was very satisfied with both: they looked great, they were quiet, and the washing machine doesn't use much energy. But then they both started making more and more noise. Things finally got to be too much just past the two year mark- when the warranty ended, of course.

Most recently, the dryer stopped working, and displays an error code ("HE") when I try to run it. Apparently I need a new heating element which I'll have to pay for, along with the service/labor expenses. Considering that I ponied up nearly $800 for this appliance just over two years ago, I'm less than thrilled about both the inconvenience of a breakdown and the bother/expense of getting it fixed.

Next time I'm going to look for something simple with a reputation for being a tank.

UPDATE: As it turns out, I was able to find online some very well-written instructions for how to fix this, and they include a source for the part: appliancepartspros dot com. (Check out shopping dot com, the instructions are in a review of the Samsung DV218AE.) The part arrived in two days, and I had it installed in half an hour. If you're somewhat confident as a do-it-yourselfer, this is not a difficult fix. I would, however, recommend replacing the entire heater duct assembly, not just a sensor or an element: it's a much easier operation, and you'll know that the heating element and the sensors are all brand new.

product_title: LG 3.5 CF WASHER FRONT CONTROL WHITE
review_text:
We bought a LG WM2010CW front loader washer in July 09 mainly to save water in our 17 year old country septic system. We had a still working 9 year old Maytag washer with a high capacity 45 gals per super wash and this new LG washer only takes 16 gals for the largest load (measured with the digital meter on our water softner). We are very satisfied so far after over a month using the new LG washer and also bought the matching dryer: with various dealer plus energy star [...] and selling our used older units for [...], the LG W/D combo only cost slightly [...] on sale including sales tax. Perhaps this Fall 2009 there will be US government "cash for clunkers" style additional [...] on new Energy Star washers, you may save another $50! We got ours on a special must by both washer & dryer for [...] total deal from a local appliance dealer.

This washer is very easy to use and gets the clothes as clean or cleaner then the old top loader Maytag that literally soaked them in water. It makes some strange noises and does take about 50% longer but they come out very dry on high spin (no noticable noise on a tile floor above a basement from that high spin either). Hopefully the JD Power top quality rating holds for us as my wife washes a LOT of clothes & towels so even with our kids gone it will get plenty of use. Only minor things to watch:

- Keep the door open an inch or so to dry out the rubber gasket. My wife occasionally wipes out the gashet and even the top detergent dispenser. You are supposed to drain and check the lower filter monthly. We just did and there was nothing there other than about a cup of water, so based on feedback from a friend with a front loader we may back off to a few times a year.

- If your house is like ours the old style W/D had the washer on the right and dryer on the left. All these front loaders seems to be reversed with the doors (not changeable on the washer) swinging so the washer should be on the left and dryer on the right. We have plenty of cord and hose to do that, however the dryer vent has to be re-drilled (through tile floor!) so we are trying it this way. We also skipped the ridiculously priced pedestals - bend at the knees and hang in there, it's not heavy stuff.

product_title: LG 3.5 CF WASHER FRONT CONTROL WHITE
review_text:
Growing exhausted from having to sit on and baby-sit my ancient never balanced top loader (no matter how scientific I loaded clothes) I decided it was time for a front loader. My primary objective was reducing shaking during spin cycles than reducing water usage. While there are models out there with VRT (Vibration reduction Technology) I was unwilling to pay the premium.
The spin cycle on a front loader differs from that of a top loader in a way that I had not expected. On a top loader the shaking is in a front/back side/side fashion making the machine walk when shaking and in my case making the machine join me in my office or the living room. A front loader on the other hand has a side/side Up/down shake. Though unbalanced loads are not as common the machine still has a vibration, and since the shake is Up/down this has a jack-hammer effect on the floor. So, on one hand the machine shakes far less than my old unit the shaking that remains propagates throughout the house more (crawl space). Anti-vibe pads did help allot later on (homemade from an unused 1/2" rubber mat). With that said the unit does not require me to baby-sit and with support under the floor or if placed on a slab shaking shouldn't be an issue.
VRT. My mother has a Samsung unit with VRT and it is noticeably better in terms of vibrations. Beyond that they both clean clothes just as well. Also, as advertised the unit is very quiet (except for the High speed spin cycle vibrations).
