review_title: Efficient but be careful with small children
review_text:
We purchased this washer 2 months ago because the new GE washer that came with our home was aweful and we got tired of calling service to fix it and getting the run around.

This washer is amazing in that it spins the clothes so they're practically dry before you need to dry them. (Maybe our other washer was just that awful, but this seems amazing!)

One time water did come out of the front door but I figured out I had loaded it too full (a twin comforter and a bit of clothes). I have had no problem since then, just didn't give enough room for water to move around that time.

The front loading idea was new to us and we didn't really think about the issue in regards to our kids pushing the beeping buttons. We were relieved that you can turn the beeping off if you want to and that there is a child lock on the buttons so the kids can't push them in a cycle. The PROBLEM IS there is no child lock for when the machine is OFF! Our son likes to go and fiddle with it and turns it on and then plays with the buttons. So, while he can't mess with the washer during the cycle he can before and after. :P Fortunately we can just shut the laundry room door, but even so, it's something we have to watch out for so keep this in mind if you'll have kids around.

product_title: LG 3.5 CF WASHER FRONT CONTROL WHITE
review_text:
I wish I were happier with this unit but it doesn't do what I want it to do. I live in the North so my cold water is quite cold. Also the washer is in the basement (60ºF) and there is about 20' of pipe filled with 60º water before any real hot water reaches the washer. This machine starts by squirting cold water into the machine--even for the so-called Hot wash which is preset to be something like 105º. So because of the very low water usage, enough hot water water can not be added to get it up to speed, besides which I want actual hot wash not 105º. The warm is preset to 95º but because of my situation it only reaches 75º. I tried using the Hot wash setting to get warm and it still did not get above body temp and then it only has a cold rinse which is pure tap cold which in Montana is just too cold to rinse properly.

As a note, to test the water temp, I let it fill and start washing and actually used a thermometer to test the water in the tub. Likewise for the rinse temp. I know you can't tell anything by what temp is running into the machine at a given moment.

If you are happy with tepid and cold temperatures, or maybe you live in Texas, this is a great washer. I have had another front loader which worked fine and I found out belatedly these were the reasons:
1. My other house had radiant floor heat so the machine was pre-warmed to room temp
2. machine was on main floor
3. laundry room was in center of house and h/w heater was in there, making it the warmest room in the house
4. brand new H/W heater
5. washer very close to H/W heater

The LG repairman told me I needed to get a model with built-in heater, but after I researched what the preset temps are, I know I would still not be happy. I think I am going to get the amana 7200 which has a true Hot wash (straight hot out of the tap although it will be lessened by the cold water in the pipes). The amana preset warm is higher than the LG and I am waiting to find out how it fills (does it start with hot or cold water?). I also have a call in to my plumber about inserting a valve to increase the temp of my incoming cold.

This has taken many hours of research and I am longing for the old days! So many features but not what I want and need! All I really want is about 105º wash and 75º rinse. Ideally (and my previous washer did this) I would also like a 75º/75º setting for wool. My other washer, which I regret leaving in the house I sold, had TWO warm/warm settings--one with a wash temp boost, one without. I set the un-boosted warm to be tepid; in the boost setting, it let in more hot water. It worked great for my needs. I rarely use a true hot wash, but when you need it--because of diapers, sickness, lice, whatever--you need it.

Aside from the temp. issue, I think this is a great washer. It has cycles that I want and is easy to use. It's kind of noisy in the beginning beacuse it starts and stops as it senses the load. One drawback is it doesn't save a favorite setting, so if you don't like the defaults on a cycle, you will have to push a few buttons each time.

product_title: LG 3.5 CF WASHER FRONT CONTROL WHITE
review_text:
We purchased this appliance Mid-Yr. 2010 to replace a top loader. Our 15Y old high end Kchn.Aid T/Ldr. would more than likely have kept on chugging along..however I attempted to wash a "Q" size quilt/comforter. Once wet...just became extremely heavy & finished off the thing. Rather than repair an old app., we purch. new. Found a terrific deal at Sears on a seemingly "last model on sales floor" of this type. Cost 350.+/- (200.00+ off reg). After researching these LG Frnt-LD washers.., alt. brands etc..including Samsung, Kenmore & others as well; we decided to purchase the LG. (Our 2007 LG 15,000BTU AC is a charm thus far)
As for the washer- After 6 months of daily usage we have no major complaints. The appliance works very well. Cycle choices & adjustments are helpful. Advises on "time remaining", chirps when finished and more. However to get the most out of the washer...brief the manual.
While reading reviews from others for this model some make note of issues with drainage or smells...but I haven't noticed anything actually worth mentioning. For the smell issue my wife occasionally either opens the door a tad for an hour..or a quick wipe around the inside door/seal. (On the same plane as emptying the crumb tray for the toaster) As for the drainage & vibrating pipe issues, we don't hav'em. Possible our plumbing application is configured where no pipe-vibes occur & the drainage door at bottom/front is never a problem.
So,while tomorrow may add new thoughts on this item...we are completely satisfied with it's operation/performance to date.
I believe that prior to the initial manuf. warr. expiring, we will purchase an extended warr. (mostly to cover the Digital/Dig. Operation/Readouts etc.)
One feature that could be re-designed is the LED readout. Though no issues, it could be expanded to show actual gallons consumed upon completion of any given cycle type...or even specific H2O temperature during cycles...or other certain "go-green" type data../Other brands may already incorporate this..i don't know.
Would recommend this appliance. VG op's & also a VG value as few brands average 2+ X the price...for features that might not be "absolutely" necessary. Why go over the top ?

If we get an average of 12-15YR or (*20,000 HOURS) of service from the unit...all the better.
It gets replaced despite it's condition at that time for newer technology.

May update review...once appliance sees 1yr+ usage.

product_title: LG 3.5 CF WASHER FRONT CONTROL WHITE
review_text:
I love my washer and dryer. I do 2-3 loads a week and I usually use the normal setting so I just push 2 buttons to get it started If you like to customize it doesn't remember your settings so you would need to push the settings you want to change each time you do a load. This doesn't bother me at all but if you do a lot of loads and don't like the preset settings it might be a bit annoying.

I use way less detergent than the recommended dose on the side of the box (basically half!) and my clothes are always perfectly clean.

This is a front loader so the cycles do take longer than the upright machines. About an hour or more for a normal cycle. I stuff my loads full so I'm not in a hurry to do another one and I find they are almost dry when you pull them out due to the excellent spin it's not a big deal to leave them in the washer for a few hours.

The finished sound is a nice bell sound and you can turn it off, plus it has a child lock and a self cleaning cycle.

It does get moist inside, I leave the door open after a load so it drys out inside. If you leave it shut after a load it does smell a bit. Plus, I do have to clean where the rubber gasket is around the opening of the washer as it gets hair and gunk built up from your dirty clothes. Not a big deal but a filter there would be nice. I paid $799 for the pair, so I am very happy with them!

product_title: LG 3.5 CF WASHER FRONT CONTROL WHITE
review_text: The only positive I can give this washer is it spins so good that the dryer works less. That said, that may be due to the fact the washer uses so little water there's not much to dry out. We've had this machine a year now. Many times clothes come out with spots, like the detergent wasn't fully consumed, we have used most varieties of HE soap and follow their directions. I imagine that's because the soap is added to merely damp clothes. I wish there was a mode to use more water. Squeamish alert, during cold season hankies need to be washed twice, that's right, there's still material there after once. ANY stain needs to be pre treated. Yesterday I had some very minor grass stains on my knees of blue jeans from working in the yard, they were still there and that was after Heavy Duty with large load amount of detergent.

product_title: LG 3.5 CF WASHER FRONT CONTROL WHITE
review_text:
I have had this washer for about a month.
I replaced a front loader Maytag Neptune - circa 1999 - which was a lemon.
I am hoping for a better experience with the LG.
I wanted largest capacity - fewer bells and whistles.
I am a heavy user - about 10 loads a week.
It is a little louder than I thought it would be.
I like that it tells me how many minutes to wash - usually 53 min - longer if I select heavy soil level.
But my only complaint - is when you select the type of wash - Cotton, Normal etc
it usually defaults to warm/cold, I prefer to wash most of my loads in cold /cold, and I have to scroll through all of the choices to get to cold/cold.
I love that you can select the spin- I washed my kitchen area rug and had it spin on low- it washed just fine - no out of balance.
If you have not made the switch from top loader - give it a try- you'll use less water and your clothes will be clean.
My house is very old - 100+ years and we have not had any plumbing rattling issues- as I saw in other reviews.
Overall very pleased- hope it is a work horse for at least 10 years

review_text:
I purchased this machine in March of 2010. I was looking to replace my 11 year GE washer, that still worked, but I wanted a new efficient machine for my new home. I did a lot of research on this LG washer before purchasing it. I based my purchase solely on (at the time) the MANY glowing reviews, the 10 year manufacture warranty, my history with OTHER LG products, and the great price I was able to negotiate. I loved it from first use and had ZERO issues with it........ until this week!
I noticed that it got VERY loud during a normal load in the last week or so. No codes were lit & not an "un-balanced" sound either, nothing sounded "off", just louder. Now fast forward to today......A very loud and sudden clinking in the spin cycle and the machine/drum seizes up?! The drum is immobile at this point. The clothes are wet but no water in the tub. After referring to LG's 800 number- they let me know it is OUT of warranty! After speaking to many others throughout the company I finally told me that if it WAS a motor issue that I would be covered for the parts-not the LABOR? Wow? So, long story short-After speaking with 3 different repair men (they ALL agreed from my description of events)IT will be a very Labor intense fix! At $350.00-$450.00 and they will not guarantee that it will not happen again? Apparently it has a "SPIDER" type mechanism that will corrode and disintegrate with some water types? According to the local repairmen I spoke with, this is happening frequently in my area! How many others are going through this?? I AM kicking myself that I did not get the extended warranty!! WHO KNEW this would happen after only 2.5 years? I will NOT be buying another LG! I am going back to my Tried and TRUE GE machines. At least if they break, I can afford to fix it and wont have to SCRAP it!!!!! DO NOT BUY this machine unless you have the money to replace it every few years!!

product_title: LG 25 CF FRENCH DOOR REFRIGERATOR SS
review_text:
My wife and I bought this model refrigerator 6 months ago when we moved into a new house, and so far we absolutely love it. We did end up taking one of the shelves out on one side to make a little more room for taller items as there's not much room for them using the standard configuration.

Pros: Looks great. Works great. It's quiet. It has plenty of room. The water dispenser is much faster than some fridges that I've used (good if you fill up water bottles often like I do) and it is even positioned so that you can get a large bottle or glass underneath it easily.

Cons: The shelf that can slide in half allowing for tall item storage is pretty useless, like I said earlier, we just took it out. The ice dispenser kind-of shoots the ice out in all directions... you get used to it, but the first couple of times I used it I ended up with a cube or two on the floor.

product_title: LG 25 CF FRENCH DOOR REFRIGERATOR SS
review_text:
We bought all LG stainless appliances for an full kitchen renovation. The looks on all (Fridge, Oven, Microwave, and Dishwasher) are top notch. Great fit and finish. My biggest problems with this fridge, and the other appliances, all center around seemingly avoidable design flaws.

First must be the location and functionality of the buttons/controls. The LED panel looks cool and at first seems quite functional. But after just a few days of use, the flaws showed. The labels are lighted but the button you press to change a function is not. So if I want to change from crushed to cube ice I have to turn the kitchen lights on to see the button. To turn the exterior door light on or off, you need to turn on the kitchen light to see the button. Also, other than the ice type and the light, none of the other functions need to be changed. I leave the temp stable all the time, so I don't think that is needed, but not a big deal.

The design of the ice and water dispensers is pretty poor. The water spout is too close to the push to dispense button and water dribbles on the button and then down into the tray. The ice dispenser opening is too big, even for a large glass and spills crushed ice everywhere. I need to wipe off the glass, the fridge, and the floor every time.

There is a flaw caused by two well engineered items. The doors hold an excellent tight seal and the wheels roll very smoothly. This causes the fridge to roll out when opening the doors unless you hold the other door handle to stop it. Not a problem when you have the hand free and a pain when you don't.

The final flaw is the very limited space for taller items. The space taken by the large in-door ice maker is the primary culprit as it eliminates all but one tiny door shelf on the left door.

I really do like a few things about this fridge as well. As stated before, the looks are great. I also agree with other reviews that the lighting is superb and second only to Samsung. Air seal and door closing is great. The door alarm works well. Adjusting the door levels was simple at installation. The freezer is huge!!!! It's easy to access and clean. I haven't noticed low ice output as of yet but there are only two of us using it.

Overall, a decent unit but I expect more from one of the most expensive units on the market.

product_title: GE : GFSS6KKYSS 36 25.9 cu. ft. French-Door Refrigerator - Stainless Steel
review_text:
I've had a single french door unit by Maytag before but this unit I'm using to replace a 12 year old side by side. I forgot how much more room it seems there is in the French door units. Anyway a few things:

Seems a bit louder during normal operation than my side by side (I still have that as a storage fridge/freezer until it dies)

He ordered a compressor just in case and scheduled an appointment for 5/14/12 and told me if I got the compressor he'd come get it.. The refrigerator allows the consumer to set the freezer and refrigerator temperatures. We set them for the temperatures that GE recommends. The next day the refrigerator was maintaining the freezer and refrigerator temperatures so we canceled the 5/14/12 appointment. When canceling, we told the GE support person on the phone that he'd ordered a compressor to be delivered to my house. The support person said he'd canceled that too. Several days later we received the compressor that had been theoretically canceled. We never heard from the GE repair man about coming to pick up the compressor.

On 6/30/12 we noticed that the refrigerator was not maintaining the set temperatures so we called GE again.
They gave me an appointment for 7/6/12. Today he came out again but told me that they had not allowed him enough time to replace the compressor so he'd have to reschedule. The first available time for installing a compressor is 7/16/12.

I think GE is responsible for manufacturing a lousy product and having awful support of the garbage they manufacture.

product_title: LG WM2101HW 27 Front-Load Washer 4.0 cu. ft. Capacity, 8 Wash Cycles - White
review_text:
A couple weeks ago we got our LG WM2101 washer and matching dryer.

I'm very happy with the dryer. It determines accurately when the load is dry without baking the clothes.

Unfortunately, the washer is another story. In the hot setting the temperature is regulated to a barely luke warm 95F. We thought the machine was broken and got a replacement. Same temperature! Then we called LG and had a technician come out. He determined everything is normal. LG says the range is 80 to 100F for the hot cycle, according to the technician who was sent to repair it. That is "warm" at best. BTW, this is not because our hot water supply isn't hot enough. The machine pumps in a lot of cold water to regulate it at 95F. I haven't seen any comments or reviews on this aspect. It seems most people don't check how hot their laundry is washed. I prefer 140F (60C) for hot.

The machine also has a sanitize cycle which is promised to achieve 158F. However, that cycle takes about 1 hour 45 minutes. Not really practical, nor energy efficient.

Sadly, we'll have to return the product and look for another manufacturer. Hard to believe LG can sell so many washers considering this issue!

product_title: LG WM2101HW 27 Front-Load Washer 4.0 cu. ft. Capacity, 8 Wash Cycles - White
review_text:
When our top loader died a few weeks back we decided it was finally time to try a front loader. After checking reviews on a lot of different sources (epinions, amazon, consumerreports, jdpowers, buzzillions) I decided on an LG but a different model.

I went to sears and they didn't have the model I had settled on - they directed me to this one. More checking of reviews ensued. I ended up buying this from Sears. On sale, + 5% off for using my sears account plus no financing for a year it was a reasonable deal. $665.00.

My husband did the pick up and installation and that was easy. (Don't forget to take out the shipping bolts!)

There were two things that stood out right away when we ran our first few loads -

1) The clothes were WAY cleaner than they had been in our top loader. I mean, seriously, I don't even know how to describe it. Just, wow, I didn't know a washing machine could get things so clean.

2) The dryer time was cut in half or better. A load of towels will dry in 20 minutes on the permanent press setting! AWESOME!

On the down side the cycle times are a little longer - Averaging just under an hour. The sanitize cycle is 1hr40-min. One reviewer had a complaint about water temperature. I have no idea how hot the water gets and will never have the energy to figure it out. I'm happy enough just seeing how clean everything is. Dish towels run in the sanitize cycle came out smelling clean. Yay!

The machine has a speed wash that will complete in just under 30 minutes. How cool is that? If you are behind on your laundry and just need to get some loads through you can have loads going through every half hour and you don't have to wait for the dryer because the clothes are spun dry so well their dry time is short.

The only real down side is that it is a myth to think you are now free to wash bulky things like king comforters. The load won't balance to spin and so the machine just keeps trying to balance it but it can't. However, I think it will work to wash the bulky items and stand by for the spin cycle. Just pull the clean comforter out and air dry it. (or squeeze it out yourself and put it in the dryer.

We debated on the 179.00 for an extended warranty. Based on the 10 year motor warranty and 3 year drum warranty we're skipping the extended warranty. I'll check back here if that turns out to have been a terrible mistake.

product_title: LG WM2101HW 27 Front-Load Washer 4.0 cu. ft. Capacity, 8 Wash Cycles - White
review_text:
I was tired of the old washer leaking all over my floor. The things that attracted me to this washer were the efficiency, the quietness, the high speed spin (dryer clothes), the direct drive motor (no mechanical gears etc.) and the sump to catch the water it does spill. Also It doesn't have a seal in the bottom of the tub to spring a leak, there is no bottom of the tub.
My experiences so far (only had it a while) are very good. No water on the floor. The sump drain only gets about a quart or less of water after a few loads. It is very quiet, though you do hear it at times. It is insanely simple to use. It may look complicated, but it isn't. You just dump your clothes in and your detergent in the reservoir, select the type of cycle you want with the knob. and push the go button. Now it will display a lot of lights in columns showing what options are default for the chosen cycle, if you want to change any of these you can use the buttons below the lights to toggle through the choices for that option before hitting go, but the defaults will get you through. It does get your clothes clean and it does get them quite a bit dryer. Also we set ours on our concrete slab floor and haven't had one iota of trouble with shaking at any time.

Still the thing is new and we haven't had it long, but we're very happy now.

product_title: LG WM2101HW 27 Front-Load Washer 4.0 cu. ft. Capacity, 8 Wash Cycles - White
review_text:
Unfortunetly I had my washer break and had to go get a new one all in one day because we live in a very small town and had only that day to get to the city so I had no time to read reviews. I'm a huge review reader so this was very hard for me. I used the online feature on my phone to look while we shopped, but still not the same. So needless to say I was very skepticle and tried my best to compare a few washers and dryers at a few different stores.
I'm very glad to say that after a few weeks, I am nowhere near dissapointed and had I had the time to review I probably would have bought these anyway. The morning after we bought these and before I unpacked them I did read as much as I could and I only got more excited. (We also bought the matching dryer) I take a LOT of pride in my laundry, and thought I was pretty good at it already. Our top loader was about 9 years old and it did just fine so I wasn't even in the market. My laundry is so clean and even more fluffy now and it smells amazing! I can actually smell the fabric softner better and it's evenly dispensed so not oily looking stains on the darks. I think I have washed everything in my house 3 times ;O) just for fun. My poor little kids are lucky to have clothes on them because I'm constantly looking for things to throw in the wash! I think the hot water setting and internal heater work just fine because the glass gets all steamy, however my hot water heater is on the other side of the wall from the washer so it doesn't have far to travel. I can see with the spurts of water how it wouldn't travel a whole house well and stay hot and that seemed to be some peoples complaint. Fortunetly I don't have that problem. I have also never expected complete silence from a washer and dryer... get a sound proof room if you need it that bad... it's laundry! As others have wrote... the water filling is louder than the rest of the cycle but I can't believe how little water it uses. The spurts come from the fact that this thing is so smart it measures just the right amount of water for each load! Think of the money I'm saving! And then to top it off my dryer is super "smart" too... it knows when the clothes are dry on the sensor dry and adjusts the time to it. The only problem I have had with that is not really a problem.. the sensor can't always tell when a blanket is still damp on the inside so it will lessen the time... I just adjust the blanket and use the timed dry setting instead of the sensor....
I hope this product still remains wonderful for years... it also has a ten year motor warranty on the washer! And I super LOVE all the "bells and whistles" AKA all the different choices I have for my differnt types of loads to include the time delay setting... cause lets face it... not all loads of laundry are the same!

product_title: Electrolux EW27EW65GS Wave-Touch 27" Stainless Steel Electric Double Wall Oven - Convection
review_text:
UPDATE: As of 8/11, I would rate this unit at 1 Star (Can't change on edit function of review)
Original refrigerator was just replaced with the newly designed icemaker model due to the issues with the original icemaker. Electrolux has been good, but this refrigerator's icemaker has really been a huge problem. I would look for other lines before Electrolux, at least until they can improve thier designs and engineering.

Original review with some edits:
We have been on a journey to find a great, stylish and functional counter depth refrigerator. We are replacing a perfectly fine Kitchen Aid side by side that we put in a second home. First, we chose a Samsung side by side, but were not satisfied with it's refrigerator temperature. We set it at 34, but it never seemed cold enough. Milk was never "ice cold" as we were accustomed to. We started monitoring the temperatures, and it was typically around 38-43 degrees. Samsung was unable to remedy this issue, even after sending out a new replacement. Then we chose a GE Profile model, but it was a similar scenario, with wide temperature swings between the setting of 34, and 44 degrees, so a return of the GE was in order after service was unable to remedy it's large temperature swings.

Now, onto the Electrolux. This was a favorite from the start when we were shopping, but we were scared off by some reviews. We decided to go for it anyway, and are pleased with that decision, so far. However, the first one delivered did not cool at all. A service tech was dispatched immediately, and he found that there was a broken line from the compressor, due to damage in shipping, no fault of the unit, and all the refrigerant had escaped. The dealer brought the GE back until another Electrolux could be ordered and delivered.

Upon recieving the second Electrolux, it is performing nicely. Internal temperature is as stated on the Wave Touch Panel at 34 and -4 degrees for the freezer (which, by the way, you can set to show the refrigerator and freezer temps at all times). The units appearance is of good quality, being stainless steel on all sides, sturdy handles, and a modern appearance with Wave Touch Controls, which are easy to use. The doors are simple to align or adjust if needed.

The interior of this unit is 22.6 cu/ft, so as counter depth goes, it is decent. With edgeless glass shelves, ball bearing glides on all drawers, a large temperature controlled drawer with digital programmed settings, 2 good sized slide out bins, and exceptionaly well done LED lighting, this unit's interior is impressive.

We especially like the temperature controlled drawer, which can be adjusted from 28 to 40+ degrees. The drawer is large enough for party platters, and can keep fresh meats at near freezing, or beer can be kept at a very nice 28 degrees, or wines at a favorite selected temperature. The ice maker does take up a fair amount of space, but for ice and water in the door, it is a worth while sacrifice.

The icemaker has had some negative reviews, but so far ours is fine. The cubes are rounded, with a divit. I'm not sure why this is considered "Drink Friendly", but they are nice. One issue is that the cubes seem to come out with some vengence. However, by simply putting your glass or ice bucket close to the dispensing chute...problem solved. We have seen no melted ice puddles in the catch basin. Water dispensing is simple, and functional. We have only had this unit for a few days, so I can't comment on ice production quantity, but it is supposed to be better than most, per Electrolux specifications.

The freezer has 2 deep slide out bins, and 1 shallow one, with dividers and smooth ball bearing slides. One of our wire dividers does not stay in place, but that is no big issue at all. Space is good, and well utilized. Lighting in the freezer is excellent.

If I listen closely, I can hear the unit running, but sound is not obtrusive or noticably louder than any of the other units we have had recently. I would say it is quiet.

Pros: Operates at accurate temperatures set, huge slide out temperature controlled drawer, Exceptionally well done LED lighting and appearance, Wave Touch Controlls, functional use of space. Looks and feels high quality. We finally have really cold milk again.

Cons: High end of price scale, Ice maker takes up some refrigerator space, and some door storage.

Electrolux was made aware of this problem and they have a retro-fix made available to their dealers to fix this. I addressed this issue prior to my purchase and it was corrected. The ice is cold and it does not drip. Putting the ice maker in the upper refrigerator does take up some valuable space. It's just enough room for my wife and I but for a family of four it would never work, it's just too small. This is a high-end refrigerator with all the bells & whistles. It is well built, quiet and real eye candy when placed in a upgraded kitchen. You will not be disappointed or regret this purchase. product_title: Electrolux EW27EW65GS Wave-Touch 27" Stainless Steel Electric Double Wall Oven - Convection

product_title: Electrolux EW27EW65GS Wave-Touch 27" Stainless Steel Electric Double Wall Oven - Convection
review_text:

At issue was inconsistent ice production, with the unit refusing to make ice for weeks at a time, then suddenly springing back to life. Apparently the software glitch has been worked out of the newer units, but we did not unfortunately experience this.

To their credit, Electrolux did send us a replacement unit and ultimately provided us with store credit. And you can't beat their friendly customer service, with Southern accent to boot. I'll keep buying their vacuums, not so interested in their refrigerators. No other manufacturer uses a second compressor to make ice inside of the refrigerator unit, to my knowledge. It is obviously first generation and has yet to have all the kinks worked out. And making arrangements to be at home for almost 2 work weeks for repair attempts is clearly unacceptable.

product_title: Electrolux EW27EW65GS Wave-Touch 27" Stainless Steel Electric Double Wall Oven - Convection
review_title: A great refrigerator... worth $3,500? Maybe, maybe not.
review_text:
I've never written a review on Amazon before, and after reading the reviews for this refrigerator, I was seriously doubting our decision to purchase an Electrolux unit. But we already had an Electrolux range, wanted things to match, and needed a counter depth unit. So we held our breath, and found this unit at the Sears Outlet for $2,100. To date, I've had none of the issues others have made mention of here. The top unit stays plenty cold, the ice maker makes plenty of ice, doesn't spit it all over the floor, it's not mushy, etc... etc. The unit does seem to run most if not all of the time, but it honestly just sounds like a small fan running. It's not loud or very noticeable at all. All interior lighting is through inset LED's that dim on when you open the door and drawer... a nice feature. I think there's nine LED's in the refrigerator alone... some inside the drawers so you can easily view their contents.

The glass shelves have a slight concave edge to them that keeps in spills and are very stylish. The only small problem we had initially was hat the seal on the freezer drawer wasn't sealing completely. We'd get some patches of frost in the freezer where air seeped in. Turns out the seal just needed to be massaged a bit to be a bit more flexible, and the problem has gone away. (it most likely got compressed sitting in the outlet warehouse) One gripe is that if you open the right fridge door, the water and ice maker stops until you close it. Open it while you're getting ice or water, and an alarm goes off after a few seconds.

FWIW, the ice maker makes ice in a "drink friendly" shape (Electrolux's term, not mine) The ice looks a bit more like store bought ice, in a bullet shape with a hole in the middle. Initially it just seemed like marketing fluff, but I have to admit, they do cool drinks rapidly, fit a bit better in bottles, and seem to also freeze faster. Set to "fast freeze" this unit makes a tray of ice almost twice an hour.

Now, as I said, we got our unit for a pretty steep discount at an outlet center, and at the price we paid, I'd call this a 5-star unit. I have to admit though, at a list price of $3,500 I could see some having a bit of buyer's remorse. If you can find a unit marked down a bit, or are comfortable with the price, this is an excellent refrigerator.

product_title: Electrolux EW27EW65GS Wave-Touch 27" Stainless Steel Electric Double Wall Oven - Convection
review_text: Very expensive.  Counter-depth model has a lot of wasted space and it is difficult to arrange the shelves to any satisfactory configuration  You have to open both doors to access any drawer.  Doors do not always close correctly.  Have had this repaired twice in less than six months.  Very unreliable electronic controls that are an expensive replacement, done twice under warranty.  Ice maker produces slowly, produces small cubes that are very light and "airy" and melt very fast.  Shelving in the freezer operates roughly and is difficult to arrange anything so you can find it.  The fridge has water dispensed through the door, but the water line runs through the heat-producing condenser area, so the water comes out warm.  It immediately melts the ice.  I called about this engineering wonder and was told this is the way the fridge was designed.  This is a very expensive, yet poorly engineered and shoddy appliance.  I will never buy anything made or sold by Electrolux again (this was my first experience with them).  You will be throwing money away if you buy this fridge.

product_title: Electrolux EW27EW65GS Wave-Touch 27" Stainless Steel Electric Double Wall Oven - Convection

product_title: Electrolux EW27EW65GS Wave-Touch 27" Stainless Steel Electric Double Wall Oven - Convection
review_title: Forget it if you want ice
review_text:
Our unit - purchased new about 20 months ago - and when it worked - it was fine. It looks nice. The major problem is the ice maker. Today the serviceman is here again - this is the 7th time in about 2 months. Thank goodness it is considered to be warranty. It melts the ice it makes and then leaks water all over the floor. Glad we have a tile floor, because it would have killed laminate or wood flooring. There have been at least 2 and perhaps as many as 3 hardware upgrades. They have upgraded my software with a new board about 1 month ago. The tech that installed it and has worked on it all 7 times says this is at least the 5th software upgrade he has seen with this model icemaker. Additional problems have been with the microswitch on the icemold mechanism. Their was a kit for that. The heater to eliminate condensation behind the icemaker was an upgrade and was installed; then it quit working and had to be replaced. I will say this - this is the fastest icemaker made. The volume of ice in the tray is marginal, but there are only 2 of us so we seldom deplete the tray. And, when we do it makes ice rapidly - when it works properly. Five software upgrades in less than 2 years indicates a significant problem with engineering and/or design. Don't chance buying this product at this time. They may never get it right.
Update: Item was replaced after I threatened a small claims court lawsuit. The new one is working - for now. If you get this product, buy the annual expensive extended warranty at $175.00/yr. or you'll be sorry. Very poor design.

product_title: Electrolux EW27EW65GS Wave-Touch 27" Stainless Steel Electric Double Wall Oven - Convection
review_text:
We've had this fridge for 5 months, purchased in April 2011. The ice maker reservoir is too small. We can only get about a cup and a half of ice cubes. It makes ice fast (11 minutes) when it chooses to, but not necessarily right after I've emptied the reservoir and actually need more ice. It spews crushed ice all over the floor, even when I have the cup/container shoved right up under the dispenser. The ice partially thaws in the reservoir and then re-freezes, locking up inside the ice dispenser, so nothing comes out. Thawed water leaks out of the dispenser into the overflow reservoir, which fills up, so water drips down the front of the fridge onto the hardwood floor. Having ice/water available on the front door of the fridge is TOTALLY NOT WORTH IT. The repair person has been here twice, is coming back to install the ice maker upgrade kit, which I'm pessimistic about.

Additional problems are: the crisper drawers don't open very wide, so I can barely squeeze larger heads of lettuce or broccoli into the drawers. The flap that seals the french doors close keeps flipping open, so I have to flip it back into place by hand before closing the door or else there's a loud 'clap' when I try to close the door. I imagine this will eventually damage the front of the opposing door. When swinging the right-side door closed (which everyone on earth with a fridge does multiple times a day), the door won't close all the way. Just stops, sitting open 2 inches. Needs a second shove to close all the way. The trays inside have edges that flare up a bit, supposedly to contain spills. These do, in fact, restrict the usable shelf space you have. The salesman said, 'oh some of your containers may tilt a bit, but it's no big deal.' Well, it is if you want to stack anything on top of said container, which you'll need to b/c the interior capacity is so small. I've now taken one of the shelves out completely, just so I can stack things higher inside. There is very little storage in the doors, especially b/c of the ice/water dispenser.

This is only the second time I've been compelled to write a review on Amazon about anything. I just wish I'd stuck with a traditional fridge with one fridge door (not french door) with no ice or water dispenser and normal flat shelves. But be warned, this fridge is JUST NOT WORTH IT.

product_title: Electrolux EW27EW65GS Wave-Touch 27" Stainless Steel Electric Double Wall Oven - Convection
review_text:
The long story short, is to make sure you get a serial number for this fridge that is at least 4A109* (meaning the 9th week of 2011). This supposedly ensures the new, redesigned ice maker.

We had problems with the ice maker in our original EW23BC71IS model, mainly with it constantaly dripping water out of the front and leaving a puddle of water in the front water/ice access area. We probably had 5-6 service calls to try many things to fix this (included putting thicker weather stripping around the ice unit, lowering water-fill pressure, insulation on water delivery pipes, many other things). Nothing worked. Finally submitted for a fridge replacement to Electrolux to give that a try. Electrolux accepted given the history on the unit and just as they approved we saw a comment on a Kelly Ripa Electrolux sweepstakes that the french door fridge had "party ice". That sounded new. A little research confirmed the ice maker was redesigned and now uses pyramid ice cubes (instead of bullets). New unit is a 5 star (and believe me I would have given the original a 1). I held back to 4 on this review due to the problems leading up to this (with the original ice maker), and also due to the LED light issue with the new unit (described below, fixed now) but we are very happy now. We were not before with the original unit. You may be able to get the new ice maker installed in your older fridge. If you have ice maker problems you may want to push for that. We've had the new ice maker for 3 months now and have had zero problems with it.

Mullion (Flapper) - on original fridge we had an issue where the flapper/mullion (between the doors that makes the seal) would sometimes stay open. This can be bad if one opens both doors and then shuts the left before the right (thus the open mullion hits the left door). If you have this issue, ask for a replacement flapper/mullion part to be installed. The repacement fixed the issue. I think there is some variance in the flapper/mullion parts. If the first one does not fix the issue, ask for another one.

Both the original and new unit had problems with the LED lights flashing and clicking when opening doors. We had a board replaced on the new unit and that fixed the problem.

I think you'll start to see the reviews on this model turn around as the new ice maker equipped models start to get some time in service. We also have a dishwasher, electric built-in range, and over-range microwave. We have been very satisfied with all of those and now the french-door, cabinet-depth fridge joins in that we are very satisfied with it now also.

product_title: Electrolux EW27EW65GS Wave-Touch 27" Stainless Steel Electric Double Wall Oven - Convection

product_title: Frigidaire FPHD2481KF Professional 24 Built-In Dishwasher - Stainless Steel
review_text:
On 24 June of 2010 we purchased a complete Frigidaire Professional Kitchen Suite from HH Gregg. We purchased the 5 year extended warranty with it.

Observations thus far: We have the Stainless/Fingerprintless version and love it. The finish is even amongst all the pieces and all are within tolerances for noise during normal operations. They're made by Electrolux, so the quality is in there.

Specifics:
Dishwasher (FPHD2481KF): Control board went dead shortly after installation, replaced by warranty in 3 days, flawless ever since. Quiet operation, simple homeowner installation.

Gas Range (FPGF3081KF): Love it... warming drawer is nioce, the griddle is a godsend.

product_title: Frigidaire FPHD2481KF Professional 24 Built-In Dishwasher - Stainless Steel
review_text:
For a mid-range (you might even say upper) dishwasher, this has been a disappointing experience. Dishes mostly get clean, but you do need to pre-rinse most things, and pre-scrub a couple of really tough foods (I'd expect most dishwashers to struggle with really tough things, like dried on egg yolk for example). They get about as dry as I'd expect, no complaints there. The machine is quiet enough; you can hear it but it's not bothersome. Where it goes off the rails is the basic design of the water path and seals. First, you should not be able to load the top tray enough to hit the rotor, but you can. Rather than make the edge of the door opening low enough to prevent you from putting dishes that high, this dishwasher allows you to shove whatever you want up there. The same problem exists on the bottom tray. Again, trivial to make the top tray (where the bottom rotor is mounted) with a bar that would prevent you from (or at least make you aware of) loading dishes tall enough to stop the rotors. Why is this all a problem? Because the door seals are not protected -- the door is not molded in a way that deflects water away from the rubber seal, so if you do load in something that stops the rotor from spinning, chances are good it's going to send a stream of water directly on the seal, and the seals are not designed to withstand that direct attack. Result: water on the floor. It's happened to us a half dozen times now. Even if you're careful, if something (spatula, for example) shifts and blocks that spinning wand, prepare for a leak.

I doubt we'll end up keeping this washer more than another few months. I can't plan on supervising every two-hour run to make sure it's not spilling water out. This is the only dishwasher I've ever owned that had leaking built right into the design.

product_title: Frigidaire FGHD2433KF Gallery 24 Built-In Dishwasher - Stainless Steel
review_title: Looks nice and sleek but is a pile of junk
review_text:
This dishwasher was actually one of the gifts given to the audience on one of the Ellen Degeneres shows. Our friend didn't need it, so she sold it to us for less than retail. Once it was installed, I noticed how cheap the sliding pull out racks were. I also noticed that the spray arms / wands were plastic. We have had better quality dishwashers over the years and as I recall, all the spray arms were metal. I must say that it was very quiet and worked fine for about three weeks.

After about the third week, the door started making a very loud and annoying "squeaking" sound every time it was opened and closed. I had a repairman out two different times. He tried lubricating the hinge but because the problem was actually deeper into the unit, squirting it with WD-40 only helped for a few days. (I was told later by an appliance tech that this model was not built with adequate wheel rollers that are used with the tension line which operates the counter balance on the door)

I finally convinced Electrolux (the mother company) to replace it, but nobody followed through for us for weeks. In the mean time, the spray arm located on the top of the unit fell completely off. I was able to snap it back into place because it is made of cheap plastic. It kept falling off again during use. I was so upset that I contacted Electrolux and insisted on talking to the furthest person up the line I could get to so I could honestly tell them that I was so surprised what a lousy product Electrolux would sell. I know it's got Frigidaire's name on it, but it is an Electrolux product. I told them that we have had one of their bullet-proof vacuum cleaners for 20 years, so assumed they were a quality company and couldn't believe they would sell such a horrible dishwasher. From that point on, I can say that their customer service kicked in and they stepped up their efforts and arranged to have it replaced qickly. The Gallery was out of stock so they upgraded me to the top of the Frigidaire line "Professional" series and it was delivered within one week. I had the appliance man carefully open this "top of the line" machine up and upon me seeing the exact cheap racks and plastic wash arms, I had him put the box back together and leave it with me. I sold it cheap, new in the box off Craig's list and am now again looking for a quality dishwasher just as you are. Do not buy this dishwasher! You will be sorry. I read the other review on this same model and could only shake my head.

product_title: Frigidaire FGHD2433KF Gallery 24 Built-In Dishwasher - Stainless Steel
review_title: Broken in less than a year!  Follow up review below!
review_text:
We purchased this dishwasher right before Christmas in 2009. It worked great until about two weeks ago. It made a horrible sound and then stopped draining the water. We were told that it is not considered broken just because the water doesn't drain!!!!!! We persisted and they FINALLY gave in and sent a repairman. He told us the pump was dead (in LESS than a year!) and he ordered a new pump. We are STILL waiting for the part. If I had wanted to do dishes by hand, I never would have bought this thing. It looks beautiful, but then, at this point, the only thing it is good for is it matches our other brand new stainless steel appliances. Thank goodness we bought a four-year warranty, although if it takes a month to fix it each time, I may just chuck it and buy something different. I will NEVER purchase a frigidaire again.

Okay here is a follow up three years later. The pump my wife wrote about above was due to glass that WE broke and a small amount found its way into the drain unit and jammed the pump. It was replaced free. We had a second pump go out (for the exact same reason) a year later. Knowing what to look for I told the repairman over the phone that it was the pump. He ordered one and showed up with it four days later. When he disassembled the unit he found a piece of glass jamming the pump. This time the pump was not broken just jammed from the glass. The repairman pulled the piece of glass and let me keep the new pump in case we ever have the problem again. All free of charge. I changed the one star rating to a four star rating.

product_title: Frigidaire FGHD2433KF Gallery 24 Built-In Dishwasher - Stainless Steel
review_title: Quite & Attractive but NOT WORTH IT!!!!
review_text: We bought this dishwasher from Lowe's because it was a good price, a good brand (or so we thought), and it matched the stove and fridge we bought at the same time.  I disliked it at first because the racks are poorly designed and hard to stack my dishes in, but I got over it becuase it operated so quietly.  Then after less than 2 months it started making VERY loud noises while running.  It was still under the 1-year warranty so Frigidaire replaced the motor.  Then less than TWO WEEKS after the 1-year warranty expired it started making the same loud noise again.  After 45 minutes on the phone I finally made Frigidaire understand why they should cover the parts and labor for the problem (the motor wasn't even 1 year old since the replacement!).  The repairman came out and said he couldn't find a problem, but when it made the noise again the next day I made a video recording of the noise and he agreed it was the motor again.  When I called Frigidaire to order the replacement part I was told the part was on back order (no ETA and over 500 parts backordered).  I told the repairman this and he agreed that it sounded like the motor manufacturer must have identified a problem with the motor that they were trying to correct.  To my surprise the new motor arrived at my house within a week.  When I called Frgidaire to question it they were confused too because the part is still on backorder.  Now I believe I have recieved an old leftover motor that will have the same problem that the first two have had and will not last another year - but there is nothing I can do at this point....except to write this review in the hopes that it will save someone else the trouble I have had with this dishwasher.  DON'T BUY IT!!!!!

review_text:

product_title: Frigidaire FGHD2433KF Gallery 24 Built-In Dishwasher - Stainless Steel
review_title: Great Dishwasher For An Even Better Price...
review_text: This is my second Frigidaire/Electrolux Tall Tub Dishwasher,the first lasting more than 14 years without a glitch or a single service call. What impressed me was my Frigidaire #1 was as quiet at 14 years as my new one is now. This is a fantastic product for the $379 price I paid. This dishwasher is very quiet when operating, in fact all you hear is the water splashing in the tub. When installed and used properly this dishwasher will provide years of trouble free service. The control panel is easy to operate and the automatic soil sensing system works great and produces gleaming clean dishes every time. I have had no strange sounds or escaping steam issues damaging cabinets at all. These modern units really need to be installed properly and then maintained and cleaned with Vinagar or "CLR" if you have hard water to avoid scale clogging and pump noise issues. This goes for any brand. I am very happy with my new purchase and would buy it again if I needed another.

product_title: Frigidaire FGHD2433KF Gallery 24 Built-In Dishwasher - Stainless Steel
review_text: Purchased: 9/30/2009.  In less than two years years, we have had numerous leaking issues with this dishwasher. Our dishwasher begain leaking from the bottom right-corner of the door shortly after receiving it due to the fact that both "splash guards" had become dislodged and were sitting in the bottom of the dishwasher. Service was called and the unit repaired. Then a short while after that, the dishwasher flooded our newly remodeled kitchen due to a faulty water pump. When the service technician installed the new water pump (replaced under factory warranty), he also replaces the two splash guards as he had noticed they had cracked (rubber split apart from the plastic tab). Less than six months later, the dishwasher was again leaking from the bottom-right corner of the door and the splash guards were again split apart. I replaced the splash guards myself this time, saving a service call. In my opinion, the dishwasher was found to leak during testing of the design and the "splash guards" were created to address this obvious design flaw. However, every time you roll out the bottom tray, the rollers run directly over the rubber on the splash guards, which causes them to crack and then allow water to escape. Now a few months later, the idshwasher has again flooded our newly remodeled kitchen, and like the previous reviewer, we are no longer using it and trying to get Frigidaire to replace it. I would highly recommend looking for a different manufacturer when looking to purchase a dishwasher.

product_title: Frigidaire FGHD2433KF Gallery 24 Built-In Dishwasher - Stainless Steel
review_text:
Came here to do a writeup, and was amazed at all the bad reviews...

This is my first dishwasher--we got a great deal on it from PC Richards. I had to get the machine serviced once; the serviceman found a bone in the works, so I can't blame the dishwasher. Otherwise it has been trouble free, runs quietly, and gets everything really clean. Like some of the other reviewers have reported, all the interior parts (trays and holders, sprayer arms, jets and strainers) are plastic, but that hasn't been a negative factor in performance or durability yet.

The reason I give it only three stars: about a third of the time, I find the detergent--the gel pack or "powerball" or whatever--hasn't dissolved. At first I thought it was because the water running into the machine wasn't hot enough. After making sure the water is boiling hot at the adjacent sink beforehand, I often still have the problem. I have to run the machine a second time, which is certainly not the objective.

product_title: Frigidaire FGHD2433KF Gallery 24 Built-In Dishwasher - Stainless Steel
review_text: Frigidaire completely dropped the ball on this one. Find another brand, as this unit is a bust. Won't ever buy Frigidaire again as they have been no help.

product_title: Frigidaire FGHD2433KF Gallery 24 Built-In Dishwasher - Stainless Steel
review_text:

product_title: Frigidaire FGHD2433KF Gallery 24 Built-In Dishwasher - Stainless Steel
review_text:
We got this dishwasher when we were renovating the gutted house we bought. I was doing so many things (floors/cabinets/walls/electrical/construction) that I just went into Best Buy and randomly picked appliances. The first year the dishwasher started leaking from the lower right onto the floor. The Frigidaire warranty was still in effect so I called them and they came out and replaced the side splash guards, the bottom splash guard and the door gasket. The side and door splash guards were visibly ripped. The leaking stopped.

2 years later the same leak appeared. So called the home warranty company and they came out and did the same thing, replacing those parts and the leak stopped again. So if you own one of these and are getting leaks out of the front, check the gasket that runs around the tub and seals to the door. Costs $8 to replace and its easy to push in and replace yourself. My 7 year old could replace it, its that easy.

The dishwasher was also very quiet when we first got it, couldn't even tell it was running. Well 2.5 years later and its louder. I asked the repairman about this and he said over time the quiet motors just get louder and louder.

Avoid this dishwasher, unless it is like on sale for like $20 then the $8-20 of parts you need to buy every year shouldn't matter too much.

product_title: LG : DLE2101W 27 Electric Dryer with 7.3 cu. ft. Capacity White
review_text:
It took a while to choose which dryer to get to go along with our LG SteamWasher (dryer purchased at Sears, washer purchased at Best Buy). We didn't feel the need for the matching steam dryer, since we have that feature with our washer. It slightly mismatches the SteamWasher, yet it doesn't "stand out" as a sore thumb. The control panel is different and the metal rim on the dryer has a bit more of a gloss finish than the SteamWasher (since they are different model designs). This isn't an issue for us, since the washer and dryer aren't on display in the kitchen area, and they are in a separate laundry room.

Other dryers I've owned before this one: Kenmore, Whirlpool and Amana (all large - super large capacity).

Household: 2 adults, 1 teen, 3 very furry Siberian Huskies as (indoor) family members.

Concerns: removing as much fur as possible, keeping clothing & linens in top condition, ability to do large loads, low noise, and perform for everyday use.

I don't LOVE the dryer like I do the SteamWasher, but I do like this dryer quite a bit. Yet, I have never loved any dryer that I've had. My main issue has been that some loads may take an extra cycle or two to completely dry. --This occurs with very large loads though. With other dryers, I've had to also run an extra drying cycle (with these type of loads; especially towels, comforters, pillows & stuffed toys). Much of this is most likely a learning curve, that I still need to work on, since I am new to front load washers & still playing with different spin settings.

--

Some "issues" I've read about LG electric dryers and my experience...

Lint screen - "lint screen falling appart?" My lint screen is very sturdy & I have had no issues at all with it falling apart anywhere...it is well made.

Dryer drum - "drum cracking?" I've had absolutely no signs of even minute cracking, & my dryer has gone through as many as 6+ loads in one day or 1-2 loads daily...high temp setting gets used as well. The drum isn't all metal (it's stainless steel main drum with rubber type "hands") , but it appears well made and sturdy. Our machine is also well balanced.

Dryer Sheets - "can't use dryer sheets due to it messing with sensor?" I use dryer sheets and have had no issues. One thing I have noticed though, I don't need as many dryer sheets as I use to use. Even with very large loads, 1 dryer sheet does the trick with keeping clothes static free.

Drying - "even small loads need an extra cycle?" For small loads, I have had no issues. Even larger loads of just sheets dry in one cycle. --With just making sure items are taken out of washer individually; checking so they aren't tangled or balled up (like what I'd do with any dryer)& this ensures less chance of wrinkling too. Larger loads and heavier materials, these do take a while longer to dry (extra 1-2 cycles, depending on how wet the items come out of washer too). Again, I am also learning my new front load washer spin cycles too.

--

With having Siberian Huskies, clothing and bedding can get quite furry (and their fur is super fly away soft!); even with regular vacuuming & husky grooming. This dryer picks up a LOT of the fur, that our washer misses (and the washer does get a good amount, and better than a top load) and sends it to the lint filter screen. This is very nice, and our LG dryer works a lot better with removing fur than any of my previous dryers. A typical small to average/normal load will be virtually fur free. Larger loads will have a little more fur, but still much, much less than our other dryers would perform.

The Cycles: 4 Sensor Dry (cotton/towels, normal, perm.press, delicates) and 4 Manual Dry (speed dry, freshen up, air dry, time dry). The 4 sensor dry cycles offer wrinkle care and damp dry options (with also ability to adjust dry level); while manual dry cycles offer the options of more time/less time and wrinkle care (as well as, the ability to adjust temperature settings & dry time).

Other features: child lock option, custom settings program option

LED digital display shows: settings, estimated drying time (and true time for manual dry settings), options & status message

Overall, this is a very nice dryer, easy to use, performs well for this family's needs and helps our clothing/linens stay in great condition. I haven't had any issues with wrinkles or any damages to clothing, linens, bedding or even stuffed toys. It's definitely not noisey while running & the beeper is loud enough for us to hear within the house (on low setting)...it plays a tune instead of an annoying BUZZ (which is another nice feature, and beeper can be disabled).

To get my sheets whitest white I use the special white cycle. You can also use a sanitize cycle for items like towels and bathmats. All of the cycles leave the items a bit twisted into knots, but if you shake them out before putting the items into the dryer they are fine. I also frequently use the extra rinse cycle if I am concerned about a packed load which may have some residue. Which brings me to the point of SIZE of load. I have stuffed 3 rooms' worth of laundry in one load-- sheets with 4 pillow cases each, and towel sets for two people. I can't believe how much laundry I can do in one load and and how white and clean they get.

It is important to use only the recommended amount of soap. I became heavy-handed with the soap and the experienced a system shut-down due to too much soap.

I think the washer looks great-- very space-aged and clean looking. I have the units stacked, which I didn't think was possible with such large appliances.

I also think the washer runs fairly quietly. The only time I ever hear it is when the spin cycle kicks in.

Both the washer and the dryer were expensive units but seem to be worth the money when it comes to heavy use and clean laundry.

I've now been using the units for over a year. They still clean and dry great. I only have one complaint, and it is kind of a big one. I started to notice that some of my sheets were torn-- some after only one wash. This kept happening, and happening. I finally discovered the culprit. The "peg" which starts the machine when the door closes is a metal fin which sits right in the middle of the area where your clothes inevitably get dragged over. The peg is just raw metal, no plastic coating, no soft, rounded corners. I actually had to take a (freshly torn) sheet off the peg. I am just stumped as to why this peg couldn't be coated with something protective. Now that I know the issue exists, I can be more careful removing clothes from the dryer.

review_title: A huge improvement over our former electric
review_text:
This range has been in use for about a month using natural gas. Installation went smoothly because we paid particular attention to measurements provided in the online installation manual, so it fits snugly and looks great in place. In use our range gives off a very slight odor, probably due to gas combustion. It is easily removed by our vent fan, but something we didn't have to do with the electric range.

Moving pans around is easy enough on the 'continuous' grates. The cast iron on this range is heavier than on some other brands we looked at, but not so heavy that you have a hard time removing it to clean the black-enameled underpan, especially when compared to the smooth schott-ceram surface on our former electric range. We like the different burner BTU ratings and use the burners accordingly, with good control over the heat level. The controls are easy to read and set.

Using the oven features is not 100% intuitive so we found a little time spent with the owner's manual helped us use it better.
For example using the Preheat feature means the oven is up to temperature in just a few minutes. Compared to our former electric oven it cooks at about a 25 degree lower setting. We haven't used the convection feature, clean or broil yet so I can't comment on those.

Anytime the oven is in use a fan blows room temperature air out the front beneath the control panel. My guess is that this keeps the electronics in the control panel cool. It is a noticeable amount of air, but we don't find the sound bothersome, as some have reported. It continues for some time after the oven is turned off.

The lowest oven shelf is attached to the door so that when the door is opened, anything on that shelf is pulled forward and easily accessed to, for example, check a cake for doneness or baste a ham. However, when we were baking sweet potatoes some gooey juice dripped down onto the oven floor and this shelf connection made it more difficult to clean up. We have used the split rack feature for roasting turkey and found it easy to remove and replace the section. The oven window is very large, and there are two bright lamps inside.

We were surprised that it did not include a broiler pan, something we felt should come with an appliance in this price range. It does have a removable wire rack "shelf" for the warming drawer, effectively doubling the amount of some foods you can keep warm, rolls for example.

We like the look as well as the performance and overall quality of this range. It has exceeded our expectations and is a huge improvement over our electric range.

review_title: Unsuitable for more than one person.
review_text:
I purchased a Bosch washer (model WAS20160UC) and dryer (model WTV76100US) set in December 2011. This is the experience I have had with the Bosch appliances. It is a vented dryer, not the condensation model. This review is mostly about the dryer.

Pros: Stylish (witch makes no difference since the dryer is so poor)

Cons: This dryer takes very long to dry even small loads. It will get warm but not hot. A Bosch technician measured the temperature of the dryer at 122 degrees Fahrenheit. But, he informed me that this was normal for this dryer. In one test; two bath towels, two hand towels, and one facial towel were washed in the washer and rinsed on maximum spin to remove as much of the water as possible. It took the dryer 1hr. 20 min. to dry the load. After many phone calls and 3 or 4 service calls, they replaced the dryer. It performed as poorly as the first. So, I called an electrician to really find out what was going on. With freshly washed towels in the dryer, he observed the dryer drawing 10 amps (about the maximim rating) for 15 to 20 seconds. Then it went down to 5 amps for about about 30 seconds (he described it as half heat) then down to room temperature air coming out of the exhaust for another couple minutes. It repeats this cycle. At no time does the dryer actually get hot enough to remove the moisture from the load. It mostly just uses ambiant temperature air to dry the clothes. If touch the clothes in the middle of the load, they mearly feel slightly warm. While it is not practical for most people to use a clothes line, I think it would be just as effective as this dryer.

The thing that bugs me the most about this whole debacle is this: Both Bosch and the appliance store had the attitude that I should just accept the poor performance because it is a European design. I heard many excuses defending an appliance that I truly believe they KNOW does not perform as it should.

If you buy a coffee maker, do you expect it to make coffee in about 15 minutes? If you buy a blender, do you expect it to blend what you put in it? Well, when you buy a DRYER, you kind of expect it to actively dry.

In fairness, this washer/dryer set may be suitable for a single person who does small loads of laundry. You can expect a small load to take 60 minutes to wash and 80 minutes to dry. So you are right around 3.5 to 4 hours for two small loads.

Update: The appliance store has taken back the Bosch washer and dryer. I have replaced them with a GE unitized washer/dryer (model GTUP240EWH) This dryer completely dried the same load in 30 minutes.

I hope this review is helpful for you.

review_text:

Pro: It is attractive, vents out back or side, and install was easy. The stainless drum is nice and the lint filter is easy to clean out.

Cons: It does NOT dry the clothes quickly. It gets warm, occassionally moderately warm (never hot), but then it does not stay warm for long. So a small load of towels takes a couple hours and still come out damp dry. Just not enough energy going in to remove the latent heat (i.e., not hot enough to dry the clothes in a reasonable time). Bosch says this unit uses "higher flow rate at a lower temperature," and I completely understand their intent, but it just doesn't seem to move enough moisture regardless of their claim.

Well, we have only had the unit a couple months and have yet to get a dry load.

Machine uses moisture sensors (near the lint filter). Repairman could not tell me if these have any control over heat level or just used to indicate level of dryness to turn machine off. There is good flow out the vent, so if it isn't the flow rate then it must be energy level. Repairman says - "normal" , but it was close to lunchtime. Or maybe it really is just a poor Bosch design.

This machine is a disappointment. Stay away from Bosch.

One year later. Still dries very slowly. But we have learned to keep the loads small (two bath towels, one hand towel, a couple wash cloths and bath mat take about 1.5 hours to dry). We also learned that the cotton, very dry setting is the only setting that works well. Lint filter fills up fast, so empty after each load.

review_title: Love our little bosch washer and dryer!
review_text: We built a little cottage on the water to replace our river house after it was destroyed by Hurricane Katrina.  Got the plans from the Lowe's website in August 2008 and built the little 700 sq ft cottage we now live in. Because of the dimensions, we were very limited in what kind of appliances we could put in.  The Bosch washer/dryer set stacked together exactly perfectly in the very small closet we had downstairs.  They remind me a lot of the washer and dryers you run across if you spend much time traveling in Europe or the Middle East.  Because of the cost of utilities overseas, these systems are designed to be extremely energy efficient.  They're also the quietest systems we've ever owned...they need to be, because not only are they in a tiny house, they're stacked in the closet immediately outside of our bedroom.  We never have trouble sleeping while they're running, as long as we're not washing or drying something like dog collars with a lot of metal parts.  They are unique for an American to use...unlike the dryer I grew up that just blasts heat non-stop, this system will take longer to dry your clothes, but that's not necessarily a bad thing.  It uses a little more gentle heat, and rather than running continuously, it runs silently for a few minutes, stops to let the heat it's built up continue to dry the clothes without motion for a few minutes, then runs again.  That's what makes it so energy efficient.  We've had ours for about four and a half years and have done nothing other than clean the filter with each load.  The only downside I've found with it is that we'd like to buy a new lint filter because the filter light is starting to stay on, and the bosch website is fairly useless for providing detail on how to purchase what I would assume would be the most often touched/highest wear and tear part.  You can find every single nut/bolt/spring on this device on the bosch website, but you apparently can't buy the filter there...that seems like more than a minor oversight.  Anyway, I would rate the dryer a five star for our situation.  I'd give the washing machine a four star, primarily because no matter how much you clean the gasket on the door, it develops large mildew spots quickly if you don't dry out the gasket, and if you ever decide to take the gasket off to try to clean it more, you need an SEC football offensive lineman to help you get the spring that holds the gasket in place BACK on to the machine.  Other than that, it's actually fairly easy to service a lot of the things yourself, and I've never thought highly of my ability to work on appliances.  We're building a bigger house now and we're going to go all Bosch on that one as well, although we'll look at getting a larger Bosch washer/dryer if they make them...but if it comes down to it, I'd buy the exact same ones again.

product_title: GE WHRE5550KWW 27 4.1 cu. ft. Top-Load Washer - White
review_text:
First, let me say that historically I've never bought G.E. appliances---especially laundry appliances. My youthful years spent working at Sears as an appliance delivery/installation technician (1986-1991) showed me more than a fair share of fairly new but recently deceased G.E. washers. I remember one customer who had only had hers about a year (and was obviously rich enough to simply buy another rather than repair it). I know that all of this was nearly 15 to 20 years ago and much can change with a company's quality (remember when Maytag appliances were still good and Hyundai cars were horrible?), still, it kept me away from G.E. washers for many years. Ironically, G.E. has built for many years probably the best line of refrigerators and ranges in the industry.

If you're reading this review then it's obvious that you know a thing or two about washers. I don't really need to go into the hows and whys, but I'd like to focus this review on what is unique about this washer.

1. Stainless steel tub!!! Hey, I'm a fool for a stainless steel tub, although I can't really say that they are any better than others. Remember the cool Speed Queens and their once-patented stainless steel tubs?

2. Lack of agitator/"Hydrowave." One benefit of front loading washers is that they can wash more clothes, yet get them cleaner and treat them more gently than a top loading washer with an agitator. Well, this machine is still a top loader but lacks an agitator---at least what we know as an agitator. I suppose the little "nub" in the middle of the tub is the agitator. At any rate, this machine employs what G.E. calls its "Hydrowave" system. Most likely, this is yet another industry buzzword.

3. Super capacity! According to the manual, this has a capacity of 4.1 cubic feet. That's big! Other "super capacity" washers are usually around 3.5 cubic feet. This extra capacity is achieved, of course, by the lack of the traditional agitator.

4. Quiet! In terms of quietness, this machine is what I'll call "library quiet." It really is wonderful not to hear the "clunka clunka" from the Maytag piece of garbage it replaced! It sits perfectly still like a good little church boy during the spin cycle.

5. Drier clothes. No, this is not a one-in-all machine like I've seen in motor homes and Parisian apartments, but this thing gets clothes drier after the spin cycle than any washer I've ever known. Drier clothes after washing means less time in the dryer and, ultimately, less energy consumed.

6. Options. In addition to the multiple cycles and settings on this machine, two extra "bells and whistles" that may prove handy are the "Extra Rinse" option and/or the "Extra Spin" option. I've not used them yet, but certainly see the benefit.

***** WORD TO THE WISE ***** Do not overfill your washing machine! 4.1 cubic feet doesn't mean that you can force 50 pounds of dirty laundry into the maw of this appliance---or any other washer. Nothing shortens the lifespan of a washing machine more than overfilling the machine, yet almost everyone does it. The rule is to fill it no more than halfway from the bottom of the tub. If fact, this washer only fills slightly more than halfway on "Super" capacity. This is probably the reason some reviewers have complained that the machine left some articles of laundry dry in their machine.

If I do not use the washer cleaners available (throw it in alone and it will clean the inside) my clothes smell as if I've left them in the washer for days. It has a ring just inside the door, where the dirty water goes in, I always find smaller items stuck in there...really gross to pull out wet soppy socks (or worse) knowing they have served as a filter for the rinse! The high spin is nice, but it essentially glues my clothes around the washer tub, so I have to pull them out, then they turn into this big "chain" of semi-wet clothes. I have to attempt to keep the chain together as I feed it into the dryer, but usually they start to break apart and fall all over the ground. So I've tried to pull them out, and break them apart from the "chain" so I can shake them a bit, to avoid the wrinkles--nope, wont work--still fall all over the ground. I do not notice the clothes being any cleaner...and most of the time they smell worse than when I put them in (unless I drown them in fabric softer to hide the musty smell). The clothes do come out of the washer fairly dry, but the irony is that I put them into the dryer for the 55minute HIGH cycle and usually many items are STILL damp!!?? Socks, jeans etc...I always have to add another 15minute quick dry, sometimes I'll have to do that twice. It's just not saving me any time, seems to be taking MORE energy--at least for me.
I also hate that I start a load, and if I walk through the house to find a "last minute item" I can't open the door and toss it in (it's locked and filling with water). I think I'd rather go back to the top loader.
