product_title: Frigidaire Professional Series : FPHC2399KF 36 22.6 cu. ft. Counter-Depth SidebySide Refrigerator
review_text:
I bought a Frigidaire FPHC2399KF in November 2009. It has never worked properly. Nor has the replacement unit Frigidaire supplied. That's right, 3 service calls, one entirely new replacement unit, and a new temp sensor later and I still don't have a fridge that works properly. My first unit had a large wave in the side that was noticeable, and even more troublesome both fridges have had awful temperature control. The freezer can not properly control temperature, and drops as low as -14 F several times a day (with a setpoint of 0 F). We were careful not to make any changes to the default settings on the second unit before observing this problem for a while because we were afraid that somehow we had messed it up. Only after watching the unit overcool for several days did we attempt adjusting the setpoint to +3 deg to see if maybe that would work better (it didn't). Not only does this excessive cooling make such things as digging through the bags of painfully cold veggies, or eating ice cream inconvenient (so rock hard that neither my husband or I have a prayer of scooping it straight from the freezer), but it causes some of our fresh food drawers to freeze because some air exchange occurs between the two compartments. Delicate items, like lettuces, have to be carefully positioned in the fridge to prevent damage. Even carrots & celery can't be kept in certain compartments because they got frozen all the way through and totally lost their crispness. To top it all off, the humidity adjuster on one of the drawers totally broke off.

Frigidaire's customer service is equally dissatisfying. I've spent hours on the line with them to be provided with no useful information. Originally they just told me to adjust the humidity control sliderson the drawers, but now they are just telling me to have my local service provider continue replacing the parts he is guessing are bad. They provide NO actual technical assistance from anyone who has any kind of in-depth technical knowledge of how this unit works. No one who might know what part really is defective so that I could talk to the repairman about replacing that part. Just the same routine over and over - they tell you to call your local servicer and continue with the repairs because the unit is fixable. But then my unit never actually gets fixed. I just waste time having parts replaced with no affect on my fridge performance. I've even had them tell me that my first unit didn't have this problem - apparently their rep didn't note that in my file. Fortunately, the service company did document that issue so I can prove that it is a recurring problem. The only helpful person I've spoken to was a corporate lady who was calling to follow up on a survey I filled out giving them horrible customer service marks. She at least sent me a contribution toward my food losses. But even she hasn't fulfilled her promise of having a product technical specialist call me.

product_title: Frigidaire Professional Series : FPHC2399KF 36 22.6 cu. ft. Counter-Depth SidebySide Refrigerator
review_title: Disaster, avoid this model at all costs! Part 2, How it ruined our wedding!
review_text:
We bought this unit with the matching stove, dishwasher, & microwave 6 months ago at the end of November, 2010. There was a promotion by Frigidaire to sell them, if you buy the stove and fridge they throw in the dishwasher and microwave at no cost. That should have told me something!

I won't go into the ridiculous water dispenser that makes it nearly impossible to hit the glass since others have already described it in detail here. Our 6 month old refrigerator just died completely! We heard warning beeps and the display showed temperature numbers that were going up and down. The refrigerator seemed to be holding a steady temp of 37 degrees, while the freezer went from what appeared to be zero or less, to higher than the refrigerator temp.

As it turns out, the whole unit had actually died, leaking water all over our new hardwood kitchen floors during the night and ruining them! We tried to call the toll-free Frigidaire help desk and only got the call back later message, it is only open business hours on weekdays. We will have to deal with getting this thing repaired and new floors installed with less than 2 weeks until we have over 50 guests here for a party. I couldn't be more disappointed and frustrated with a major appliance. I thought they would have figured out how to make a unit that ran and kept a steady temperature, growing up our basic fridge lasted my whole childhood. I only hope that our repair jobs are better than others have experienced, it seems the nightmare has just begun...

Part 2 of the story - Our refrigerator was repaired two weeks ago today. I was worried about an 8 month old refrigerator that needed so much work and so many parts replaced, but the service tech got it running...for a while. Less than two weeks from the repair date, and the morning of my wedding, the fridge died again!

It acted the same as before, warning beeps, temperature rising in freezer and refrigerator, resetting did nothing to make it cool. I called the repairman back who said he could come early in the afternoon, the only problem was that I WAS GETTING MARRIED AND HAVING CLOSE TO 50 GUESTS OVER TO MY HOUSE!!!!

We went to the ceremony and reception, then all of the guests arrived afterwards and were welcomed by warm beer, warm wine, no ice, and smelly warm food. As for the tradition of saving a piece of cake in the freezer for the one-year anniversary, that's been denied us by Frigidaire! We had to run out for ice during the party and find containers for makeshift ice buckets.

I called the local appliance store where I bought it (not amazon unfortunately) and got the same runaround as before. It only has a one year repair warranty, so you have to call Frigidaire. The service company (recommended by Frigidaire for warranty work) who worked on it 2 weeks ago still hasn't sent in their paperwork, so there's no record it was fixed once already!!! Frigidaire also gave me the same runaround as before when I called them.

I can't stress enough to avoid Frigidaire products. This pathetic excuse for a refrigerator in my kitchen is about 8 months old and has completely died twice already. I'm sure they will want to keep fixing it until the 12 month warranty expires then tell me tough luck for the last time. They have ruined two full fridge-loads of groceries, my kitchen floor from water leakage, my wedding and party afterwards, and my anniversary since I won't be eating frozen wedding cake! It doesn't get any worse than this!

review_title: GE quality is absolute bottom- refrigerators and ovens
review_text:
Our GE Profile refrigerator has all of the disadvantages I have read in the reviews here and more. Beginning with the day it arrived. The wheels on the frig are so small that given the weight of the thing, it damages floors as it rolls, even empty. They knew that and put down thick padding, but I didn't and when I pulled it out later when it started leaking, it put noticeable "track marks" on our oak (not pine!) floors. So get some padding to roll it on. And make sure every family member knows where the water shutoff to the frig or the house is. You'll need it.

Now to the tale of woe:

Twice now, the solenoid control for the water/ice-maker has started leaking. It is not that the line broke; the cheap little piece of Chinese crap began leaking from its own plastic casing. The frig wet our wood floor, damaging it. It damaged the drywall in the great room and its floor and walls below the frig. On both occasions. Since the leak was slow, and behind the fridge, we did not discover it until a lot of damage was done. Both new replacement parts were identical copies of the old ones- no effort to fix the problem even though the repairman says they fail constantly just as ours did.

The thing began to have temperature control problems. Took two visits for the repairman to figure out that the little plastic flapper that controls airflow between frig and freezer had broken. Replaced that. The one that came out I still have to show people. It looks like a 5th grade science project. The housing is styrofoam of the quality that your stereo came in, with a piece of plastic that is operated by a tiny motor. The "axle" on the flapper is barely bigger around than a toothpick, and the repairman admitted, "Oh, those things always break. This new one will break after a while." I wish I could post a picture of it.

Turned out that while the flapper was indeed broken, it still did not fix the problem. Fridge still would not cool properly and the left side was getting so hot you could hardly hold your hand on it. Some sort of computer board swapout was required. Very expensive.

The lever against which you push your glass for ice or water operates a valve for water. Any sticky contents from a glass will be splashed onto the valve and it will become stuck shut. If you are lucky. Ours also stuck open, with water pouring all over the place, though at least we were here to see it. Another repair visit. Even if you use nothing but empty glasses, mildew will form around the dispenser and is a nightmare to clean since it was not designed with smooth surfaces for cleaning.

The ice dispenser is so imprecise that it never gives a predictable amount of ice. You push the lever sequentially: No ice... no ice... no ice... a couple of cubes... then BINGO- full tall glass of ice and ice all over the floor. It all releases in a torrent. T

he water line for the water dispenser used to constantly freeze up, requiring that the temp in the frig be set higher until it thawed. Also, the buttons that switched among water, ice, and crushed ice began to malfunction. We finally got it back to ice and do not dare switching again. We stopped using the water dispenser and now have space taken up by a Brita pitcher.

I have put a water detector under the damn thing, but I did ask the remarkably candid repairman what to expect next. Said he: "Well, you see these water lines for the ice and water? Where they go into the solenoid I just replaced, that's near the compressor. It gets real hot right there because the cooling fan is not adequate. These things are not really made to be built in because not enough air gets to them. So these plastic lines break all the time." When that happens you get another flood. There is no catch pan, water alarm, or shutoff valve. If you are away for the weekend, good luck when you return.

We have friends who have a 1947 refrigerator in their basement that has been running constantly since they bought their house back then. Only repair: a door seal about 10 years ago. That GE puts out the kind of quality they do now is shameful. We're pilots, and are aware that they make aircraft engines. They know how to make reliable stuff- if they didn't in aviation, they'd kill people. But with refrigerators, they can keep selling us crap, and letting our insurance companies pay the thousands of dollars in drywall, paint, and floor refinishing. Of course, we policyholders pay in the end- in our premiums.

We have paid hundreds of dollars in repairs for this damn thing, and I wish I could just have back one of those old white things which you plugged into the wall, put your stuff in, it got cold, and you forgot about the box for 25 years at least.

Google "GE sucks" and other similar expressions of love you'd expect from irate customers. ("GE sucks" brings up a YouTube video of a Profile frig that pretty much covers it.)

Friends of ours have a Liebherr that people are raving about. German made, with the quality you'd expect from them. You'll pay more money, but deduct the cost of two ruined floors, walls, ceiling, etc. Beneath GE's stainless steel facade is nothing but the cheapest junk they can find. Had we known, we'd have gone with Liebherr.

Finally, ovens. We have two of the same type GE Profile ovens, one here and one at a country property. The touchpads keep going bad, (Google "GE F7 error," and "GE F0 error") and they have a knack for knowing when company is coming. Over $300.00 a pop. According to an independent repairman: "Electronics hate two things- heat and moisture. GE refuses to build in the protection for their electronics, so they all go bad. The more moist things you cook, the sooner it happens. They make a fortune off selling touchpads over and over."

What an embarrassment insofar as American productivity is concerned. And way too typical. Bosch dishwasher? Great so far- 10 years in. Everything they said it would do, and quiet as a mouse.

product_title: GE Profile : PFSS2MIYSS 22.2 cu.ft. Bottom Freezer Refrigerator - Stainless Steel
review_text: We've had our GE Profile bottom freezer for five months. No serious problems. We have an in-door ice and water dispenser. The water line to the door dispenser froze, but per the manual, we just increased the temp settings one degree to +1, +38 to get it working. Unit is surprisingly quiet compared to our previous GE Profile side-by-side. With a wood floor in the kitchen we invested in a set of nylon tracks that protect the floor when we roll out the refrigerator to vacuum behind it. Because the refrigerator is placed facing an island in a relatively small kitchen, the french doors give us much better clearance--we can stand in front of the fridge and swing both doors open--as compared with the previous model with a full-sized door. Can't say anything as to the reliability issues reported by others, but I'll update this note if we have problems. Note: Since we were rebuilding the cabinet surround anyway, we added an extra inch or two clearance above the refrigerator for good air circulation. That's become a handy place to store several oversized trays. As noted in other reviews, the french doors aren't self-closing. There's a piece of trim that pops out as you close the doors to create a good seal between the doors. This mechanism requires a firm nudge to seal the doors closed. We never thought of this as a problem.

product_title: Samsung : FTQ387LWGX 30 Freestanding Electric Range - Stainless Steel
review_text:
FTQ387LWGX
I was looking for range I could use for cooking and baking for about 6 months now. I bought Samsung FTQ387LWGX and I am very pleased with it. I came to US from Europe and I was not able to get range that makes sense for some time and my old 70's GE was falling apart. Let's cut down to the chase and list what it is that makes this Samsung FTQ387LWGX so special.

1. 2 single stage regular cooking elements for regular simmering.
2. 1 double stage element heating up very fast like for boiling water.
3. 1 triple stage element for cooking on big pots or oversized frying pan
4. Warming element for keeping mashed potatoes or gravy hot.
5. Top cooking elements come on full blast in about 15 seconds.
6. knobs are solid heavy cast metal, not some plastic replica
7. digi display for over is true touch with hard Lexan cover screen, not some ziplock joke soft plastic membrane like many others.
8. convection bake for bread that works like good old Italian pizza oven
9. proof for rising bread
10. convection roast for meat and poultry that works like rotisserie
11. regular bake traditional with hidden element for close container baking
12. broil for top meat top sizzle and Brie / Camembert over bread melting
13. convection over so quiet you cannot hear the fans
14. warming drawer with sturdy construction not some wimpy make-believe
15. solid steel one piece back not some combination of sharp corner plates
16. true stainless heavy oven doors and handle not some look-alike plastic
I was looking at Electrolux and Bosch, both nice units, and decided after close examination that Electrolux is too much of the Star Trek with potential problem if main board gets zapped and Bosch is too much of the plastic (so disappointed as I like the brand). I do use kitchen range to make my meal, not to just impress my friends. Never the less, Samsung FTQ387LWGX will still let you impress your friends, as it blends with GE and many others. If you are on the market for a range that will look certain way but you are only interested in boiling eggs and reheating baked beans, then this is not for you. Not a big deal, we all have our preferences. However if you are one of those people like me who need decent, heavy-duty, working and hi-tech range for preparing professionally seasoned tasty meal for one or sometimes fancy dinner for six, then you may want to have a look at this unit, just watch model "FTQ387LWGX". Samsung as manufacturer makes four varieties of these now, some budget, and to get all the goodies as specified, you need to trace this model to the letter.

product_title: Samsung : FTQ387LWGX 30 Freestanding Electric Range - Stainless Steel
review_text: There are not many good reviews on this site for this product so I wanted to add my input, since most people only leave reviews when they are dissatisfied. I have had this Range for about 5 weeks now and I just LOVE IT! I was really afraid of it when I purchased it and first used it because of all the reviews about how hard it is to keep clean and how easily it scratches. I have found that it absolutely shows splatters much more than my old coil range with the white top. It just made me realize how little I actually cleaned my old one because I couldn't see the splatters. Also, my old range had a black plastic top part that was very difficult to clean period. The top on this one is stainless and very easy to wipe down and the knobs are made of heavy stainless steel, not some cheap plastic. Also, the control panel has a lock button on it so you can wipe it down without accidentally pressing buttons. I use Dawn dishwashing detergent to clean the cooktop and find that while I am cleaning more often, it's not a big deal to keep clean. Dawn cuts the grease, plus I don't have to clean under the burners and around the ring of the coils. It heats quickly and I find no problem with the "low" temperature burning things. I appreciate the lights that tell which burner is lit, although you can just look at the knobs to see which one is not directly upright. I LOVE the two front burners that can accommodate various sized pots and pans.The warming burner has also been very handy. This is my first smooth top range and was very worried about scratching it but I haven't found that I have to use it any differently than my old coil burner range. The only thing I haven't done yet is use my cast Iron skillet as the bottom of it is not completely flat. I LOVE the convection oven! The entire oven itself is so much larger than my old one and I have had a lot of fun baking cookies, cornbread, homemade pizza and loaves of bread that come out perfectly in the convection oven and looking forward to making other things as well. I LOVE that the oven beeps to let you know when it's heated to the proper temperature and you can see at any time what temperature it is at. I must agree with another reviewer who said the oven racks seem to tilt when fully extended outward. That has me a little worried about putting anything too heavy on a rack while it's fully extended. I did a lot of research before purchasing this from Best Buy and was very happy to find this was the one with the most features for the money as I also have the Samsung four door, french door refrigerator and LOVE it! At first I didn't think I would use the warming drawer but have come to love it also. The oven heats much faster than my old Amana and the oven door window is HUGE! The lighting inside is also very good. The steam cleaning feature works well for me also. We got this Range on sale and my husband (who is not much of a cook) has even been excited to try it out. This is a BEAUTIFUL Appliance that instantly adds a touch of class to the kitchen and is very functional, with every feature I could ever imagine but never knew existed! I would definitely recommend this range to anyone looking for a smooth top with all the bells and whistles.

review_title: An innovative double oven from Samsung
review_text:
My Maytag Gemini double oven, which I estimate to be about 6 years old, (a previous owner of the home bought it,) never worked well. When I bought the home 3 years ago, one of the burners didn't work. It also had a gap between the door and the glass, so that drips went down into the inside of the glass rendering it uncleanable. Finally, the ovens stopped heating. I was able to "trick" it into working a few more times but unplugging it, but it finally gave up the ghost. Why am I talking about my old oven so much? Well, I knew I wanted to have another double oven. And it had a feature that I really loved: the oven racks. Those racks were so sturdy, and the bottom one had a section that remained stable in the oven, and another section that rolled out, making it perfect for that heavy turkey we have to hassle with once a year. Because of that rack, I started my search with Maytag. Unfortunately, reviews on that product were poor, so I was forced to look elsewhere.

I researched every brand that makes a double oven, and drove all over town to check them out in person. Sadly, none of the brands aside from the top-of-the line Jenn-Air had the type of rack I was wishing for. This was not my only quantifier, but it was a feature I was hoping to find.

I started looking at Samsung, because I recently bought the Samsung RFG298HDRS (not currently on Amazon), and it has been such an awesome choice that I decided to check Samsung for ovens. At first, I was disappointed, because it seemed that Samsung didn't make a double oven. Wrong! This cool oven is a single-door double oven that the user can convert into a double oven as needed. It also features a warming drawer. When the divider isn't needed, it slides into a slot in the top of the warming drawer so that it is still accessible if the user decides to put lids or whatever in the drawer. This makes me realize that Samsung is the Apple of home appliances.
So, why do I love it?
1) The super-cool option of being a double or single oven, and the warming drawer.
2) The burners heat up SO fast, and they cool down really fast as well. Like, REALLY fast.
3) I love that is has a steam-clean option so I don't have to super-heat (and stink-up) the house. Never fear, you don't need a water line to the stove; you just pour some water in the bottom. I haven't cleaned it yet though.
4) The warming zone.
5) The variety of options for burner sizes.
6) The professional-looking control panel.
7) The fact that it is a convection oven. My old one wasn't.
8) The cafity has two lights inside, so it is nice and bright in there when the door is open.
What I don't love:
1) I do miss the racks of the Gemini.
2) I was kind of hoping for an all-digital control panel for ease of cleaning.
3) I wish that the stove-top was a mottled pattern to help hide the inevitable marks I won't be able to get off.
4) Some of the setting are a bit silly. A chicken nugget setting? Really? Maybe I'm weird, but I think simpler is better.
Overall, I am really happy with this range and look forward to learning all of its features. Except for that chicken nugget setting.
One final note: Another reviewer mentioned that there aren't a lot of good reviews on Amazon for this item. I urge fellow shoppers to look for reviews on other sites as well, like home improvement store sites and such, because there are a lot more reviews elsewhere, and a large number of them are positive. Don't end your research here at Amazon.

review_text: You would think that this range would last longer than 2.5 years for the $1200 it cost!!!  Suddenly the oven didn't heat anymore and the controller and sensor needs to be replaced.  What a pile.  I would not buy this item again.

product_title: Samsung : FTQ387LWGX 30 Freestanding Electric Range - Stainless Steel
review_text:
If I could give this a zero I would. Please let me state upfront that I did NOT buy this POS on Amazon.com. I bought it from a local Lowe's. It is entirely possible that I got a lemon. A very expensive lemon, but useless citrus fruit nonetheless. You also have to have special pots/pans that are suitable for this type of cooktop. We had the unit professionally installed. My first issue with this is that the left-front burner is way too big, even for my Giada DeLaurentiis pasta pot. If you don't center the pot *perfectly* on the burner, you may get (as I often did), an "SE" error. "SE" errors are GREAT when you're trying to make a hot lunch in a hurry, right? God forbid you accidentally nudge your pot a teeny bit off "perfect position" on a burner. If you try to slide it back into position, you may get an "SE" error, as I very often did. My other issue? The other day I was trying to sear a roast before placing it in the oven. Well, the sensors said that the stovetop was too hot AND TURNED THE BURNER OFF. I had to put my roast on the small burner in the upper right of the field. It was great, realizing how much caramelizing ability and taste I was now losing...
Not only that, I've also experienced when the stove had been on, I ran the risk of not being able to turn on a burner because the unit might be too hot. Or, a la searing my roast, you might have 2 or more pots on the stove and have the entire cooktop turn off because it was too hot. Even worse was the placement of the burners. The bottom-left large burner was so large that it crowded out room to be able to have 3 small pots/pans on the cooktop without having them touch. We just had a Samsung gas stove installed today. Friends of ours have one and they have had zero issues. I have already seared a pot roast on the gas range - no issues, no SE error, just happy that the smell is causing my dogs to do their crazy little dances... ;)

product_title: Frigidaire FGEF3042KF 30 In. Gallery Freestanding Electric Range - Stainless Steel
review_text: We love the stove. Price was excellent. Shipping timely and without incident. All aspects of product work perfectly! Also bought matching fridge, dishwasher and microwave.

product_title: Frigidaire FGEF3042KF 30 In. Gallery Freestanding Electric Range - Stainless Steel
review_text: The stove is so hard to keep at a consistent heat. The display adhesives have let go and it is sinking down into the stove and we can hardly use the buttons. I have had problems with all my Frigidaire appliances. I will never even consider this brand as a future option.

product_title: GE Profile : PFSS9PKYSS 28.5 cu.ft. Bottom Freezer Refrigerator - Stainless Steel
review_title: GE Profile - not worth the money
review_text: Mine, and two of my friends have the same fridge and have had the same problem.  After 3 1/2 to 4 years, the motherboard goes and it's $660 to repair. The extended warrenty is $500.

product_title: GE Profile : PFSS9PKYSS 28.5 cu.ft. Bottom Freezer Refrigerator - Stainless Steel
review_text:
We bought ours from our local appliance store. I am told all refrigerator/freezers that are half way decent have mother boards. Do they go out? product_title: GE Profile : PFSS9PKYSS 28.5 cu.ft. Bottom Freezer Refrigerator - Stainless Steel
review_title: Great refrigerator with a lot of space
review_text:
We have used this GE Profile 28.5 cubic foot French Door Refrigerator with ice and water on the door for almost a year after a kitchen remodel. The refrigerator has a lot of space inside, with nice wide and deep shelves at eye level. The LED lights work great to light the space. There are some folding half shelves for taller items.

The pull out freezer on the bottom is like a large chest. There is also a smaller sliding drawer on top inside the freezer for frozen food boxes and smaller items.

The icemaker on the refrigerator door works great every day, though we use cubes instead of crushed ice...so the icemaker holds up. Also filtered water is dispensed.

Outside the stainless steel has a nice sheen/glow and it has a sculpted/curved look to the doors and handles. I hope the circuitry holds up over the years! This is by far the best refrigerator we've ever owned.

product_title: Samsung RF217AB 20 cu. ft. French Door Refrigerator with 5 Glass Shelves, Twin Cooling System,
review_text:
NEUTRAL: bottom freezer means fridge contents easy to see/access but freezer contents hard to see and older contents buried. shallow.

PROS: Attractive as these things go. Fits our space. Digital thermometers. Pleasant chimes sound out when pressing buttons. It seems to refrigerate and freeze enthusiastically and it is quieter than its predecessor. I trust it won't piddle on the floor like its predecessor did. It hasn't yet.

CONS: (i) Pull-out freezer door mechanism is very rough, metal scraping on metal. Floor models and most IKEA drawers perform better. QC? (ii) "EZ-Open Handle" on freezer drawer tends to detach in ordinary use. "EZ-Broken Handle" is nearer the mark. This looks like it may be a design flaw. This didn't happen with the floor models, but it didn't occur to me that the handle should fall off, so I never thought to push the point while in the store. (iii) there are very few shelf height adjustments allowed. Consequently we removed one of the shelfs in order to fit milk and other ordinary-sized bottles.

product_title: Bosch B22CS50SNS500 21.7 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel Counter Depth Side-By-Side Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_title: Returning it for the Second Time
review_text:
I replaced my 14 year old dead quiet white Maytag with a stainless steel Bosch. It has a nice, sleek look, but problems and more problems. The first Bosch refrigerator was different from the showroom model in Lowes (stay away!). The showroom model did NOT have two large vent holes on the top surface of the unit, and the refrigerator I received did--covered with stainless steel tape. I was told by the deliveryperson to keep on---a real pretty site, right? That was the first thing. Second is the constant-- I repeat, constant--and penetrating alarm sound/shrill beep that goes on 15-20 seconds (not one minute) after the door is open, and there is NO way to permanently shut it off. It can drive you CRAZY. Next is when you get water from the dispenser. No matter how careful you are, it leaks and drips onto the surface of the door, then drips AFTER you take away the drinking glass. In addition, the freezer shelves fill with frost VERY quickly. However, I noticed a crack in the interior of this unit, so back it went to Lowe's, and I received the same model as a replacement. Why I just didn't select another/different brand, well, I was naive. I have a space problem and need a counter depth refrigerator.
Anyway, the second Bosch refrigerator arrived, complete with the holes on top and all its other sundry faults I mentioned above. Now, the difference is that this second unit was so noisy, so loud, that I heard the noise from my bedroom, which is quite far away fron the kitchen. The noise was that loud and constant. Let me repeat: constant. I absolutely could not and cannot take it. I could not get a restful night's sleep. Mind you, the first refrigerator was quiet. This second replacement, as loud as can be, and extremely intolerable and unrelenting. Obviously, there was something wrong with it. I called Lowe's and they are picking it up tomorrow, and that is the end of my buying a Bosch refrigerator. I will have my money refunded. I am thinking about an LG. I hear that brand is the quietest. Any suggestions? Bottom line: please stay away, far, far away, from Bosch refrigerators. The absolute worst. Oh, one more thing: I have a Dacor range and microwave. The stainless steel on Dacor appliances seems superior in shine and durability to the much more duller Bosch finish. Don't buy Bosch. Ever.
Update: I finally found a refrigerator--a KitchenAid. See my review of this.

product_title: Bosch B22CS50SNS500 21.7 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel Counter Depth Side-By-Side Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_text:
Got our first Bosch, and it was great. Quiet and beautiful to look at. But a defect inside allowed the glass shelves to fall off their pegs, just as you put a gallon of milk on it. Bosch came out and condemned the unit. I was impressed. Out comes #2 refrig. Plugged it in and the compressor sounded awful. A metallic rubbing sound inside the compressor. Could hear it across the house. Ice maker did not work. Out came Bosch, who replaced the ice maker but said the compressor was fine. Well the compressor noise has gotten louder, and now the ice maker died again. Also the refrig has a door open alarm feature. Well, my kids left a fruit drawer out a little, which caused the door not to close all the way. I woke up the next morning to a refrigerator that was 50 degrees inside, and no alarm sounded. Out comes Bosch for the third time. He condemns the compressor, ice maker, and a computer board. I contact customer service and demand a new machine, as it is only 2 months old. "Sorry, our warranty says we fix it, so thats what you get" She also refuses to let me talk to anyone higher than her " I am as high as you can get" she says.
I purchased it from Fergusen Enterprises, a wholesaler to the construction market. Jeff at Fergusen in Downers Grove Illinois, stepped in and pressured Bosch to replace the unit. We are currently waiting for Unit #3 to arrive.

product_title: Bosch B22CS50SNS500 21.7 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel Counter Depth Side-By-Side Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_text: I so want to love this refrigerator.  It is beautiful and the space inside is incredibly usable...seems like more room than my last full depth refrigerator.  We did notice in the first few days that the interior temp was not accurate (different than the display temperature).  But, we simply turned down the temp a few degrees.  Two weeks later, a very, very loud squeeking/chirping noise started coming from the rear of the refrigerator.  We could hear it from outside.  We called Sears who were happy to send a repair person or exchange the frige since we had it such a short time.  Bosch was not helpful in the slightest.  Remarkably, the noise stopped.  I really hoped some sort of kink had worked itself out.  Today, the repair man came to take a look and apparently the fan blades had fallen off.  Apparently, the squeaking was when the fan was in trouble.  It quieted when the blades had fallen entirely off.  I'm just glad it happened during the 90 day return period.

product_title: Bosch B22CS50SNS500 21.7 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel Counter Depth Side-By-Side Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_title: Initially, difficult to get used to, but now happier with purchase
review_text:
I'm vacillating between 3 and 4 stars, but we certainly like our Bosch better than others who have written about it. The first point I'd like to make is that most reviews of larger appliances are really comparisons between what we had and what we just chose.

We moved down from a 25 cu ft GE Profile (counter-depth) that was 15 years old, and the only reason we did was that it was white (and a little noisy) and didn't go with our new kitchen decor. This wasn't exactly my idea, but I got dragged from appliance store to appliance store, and when I saw this one, I gave it my "seal of approval." The handles were less obtrusive than all the rest, and that for a galley kitchen was the clincher.

Pros: We've had it over a week, and time will tell, but so far it's extremely quiet, and it's good looking. It holds all our food because my wife got very efficient and economized the space, and we're only two people. We've measured temps on both sides, and each was right on the mark to the degree, 0° and 39°. It makes ice cubes very well and quickly.

Other things took a few days to get used to, and have gone from "Cons" to "doesn't matter." This includes the poorly designed ice and water dispenser. The water dispenser is well toward the front and for those used to putting a glass to the back of the dispenser compartment, you'll be cleaning the floor as often as we did in the first 3 days. On the other hand, our floor had never been so clean. As for ice, you should place the glass up against the to of the dispenser, push the button, and you won;'t get any shavings on the floor. To be fair, when it came to crushed ice, our GE used to spit out ice on the floor as well.

Cons: The shelf sizes are badly designed. The bottom shelf on the refrigerator door is almost useless. Maybe some sliced cheese and that's about it. I think it's just 2" deep and that's because, with the door closed, it abuts the vegetable compartment.

The refrigerator door has to be completely open to open some of the drawers all the way. The top shelf is okay for large bottles once you toss the completely useless and space consuming wine rack. There is one door shelf that will hold a gallon jug of milk, but right now we're wondering where we're going to put a Thanksgiving turkey. 22 cu ft either ain't what it used to be, or the extra 3 cu ft our GE had was space we never really appreciated.

If you just want a few ice cubes ADDED to a drink, and you don't want to splash water or soda by adding cubes through the dispenser, you have to pull out the ice cube bucket to get to the cubes. On the GE, there was a door that you could open to the ice bucket and just stick your hand in to get a few cubes out. We miss that door. Well, I miss that door. It's always been too high for my wife to see what she's doing. Is this really a "Con?" If you do this more than two or three times a week, yes. If not, then forget about it and move on to the real pros and cons.

We couldn't figure how to stop the alarm from going off and keep the panel lights on, but I suggest that, if you read the manual CAREFULLY, you'll get the answer. You can lock them out or on as the case may be. And so I'll add the manual as a CON. It must have been translated from the German because there are a few things that take some "interpretation" to understand.

The water filter is outrageously expensive ($70 retail, $50 through Amazon companies) and is supposed to be changed every 6 months. Our water is hard, but of good quality, and I won't be changing the filter but once a year if that. This is ridiculous. Our GE filters had to be changed every 6 months and cost $34 for two! I changed those every 8-12 months, and the water tasted fine.

Bosch gives you all of one sample cleaning cloth, and it does a fantastic job. No fingerprints show, but after application, use a T-shirt to clean off the oil residue. And note that the application of any cleaner makes the front of the appliance appear or actually be darker. Still, we will be buying the wipes and even after the two grandkids come to visit, we'll be able to simply wipe off whatever smudges they leave behind. (Our 2.5 year old grandson was born with 12 hands, so we're also looking for a good glass cleaner. P.S. A house cannot be kidproofed against a 2 year old little boy.)

Last, I'll be calling Bosch for an explanation as to whether this is stainless steel or clean steel (google, don't wiki this). A magnet will stick to the doors and that means clean steel. Clean steel will rust if scratched through, and I shouldn't be paying $2,400 for clean steel! IF manufacturers are using the terms interchangeably, then the practice should be stopped. And since our salesman knew the difference. but conveniently couldn't find his magnet, he should be stopped as well. We were assured that this was stainless.

Would we buy this again? Probably. Our favorite brand became LG, but there are people who hate LG. Others hate GE, and other love KitchenAide. We can't buy one of each and see who's wrong. Sometimes I think that reviews - even one like this - only tend to confuse. And some make you wonder how people could think that a refrigerator-freezer was going to play Beethoven's 5th every time you open the door.

All and all, we're getting happier about the purchase, but there are still some things that would need improvement and absolute correction for us to be "delighted." Let me put it this way: we're not unhappy with the purchase. That's 4 stars max. On a scale of 1-10, it would be a 7.5 or an 8, and those are pretty high marks, but we haven't had any of the problems the other reviewers have had. Maybe buying through "the mail" isn't such a great idea. If anything goes wrong, not only do we have the seller 5 miles away, we have the service center just 20 miles away in San Francisco.

product_title: Bosch B22CS50SNS500 21.7 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel Counter Depth Side-By-Side Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_title: Doesn't work for a small kitchen
review_text:
As part of our kitchen remodel, we selected all Bosch appliances - dishwasher, stove and refrigerator. The dishwasher is so quiet that we sometimes wonder if it's really on (but the spotless dishes let us know that it really was). The stove is beautiful. Ah, but the refrigerator. It's a good thing we held onto our old Kenmore side by side, because we haven't been able to use our new Bosch refrigerator at all. Why?, you might ask - it's because the refrigerator side requires a full 18.25" swing clearance to open the door to 160 degrees so that you can open the drawers. When we first started spec'ing appliances, we saw nothing about this swing door clearance requirement, and only found it buried deep in the specs after trying to figure out why we couldn't open the doors, and after the unit had been delivered and installed.
It's a beautiful unit, but all we could get from Bosch customer support was that the unit needed that full 18.25" swing clearance. We've thought of pulling out the bottom drawer and replacing it with a couple of Fridg Binz, but I'm concerned that this might have deleterious effects on the compressor. Any other ideas?
We've looked at other vendors' units since discovering this evident design flaw, and KitchenAid seems to address it well by having a cutout near the bottom of the door that allows the bottom drawer to open freely without opening the door past 90 degrees. Bosch could get me back as a customer if they did the same!

product_title: Bosch B22CS50SNS500 21.7 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel Counter Depth Side-By-Side Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_title: Why all the fuss about Bosch??
review_text:
You would think that with the name Bosch, you are buying something that has been expertly designed and engineered. I have to warn those of you who are considering the purchase of a Bosch refrigerator - DONT. Stick with a Bosch dishwasher or washer/dryer set if you must.

The drawer "hardware" is plastic and can easily break off when re-installing.
It is a LOUD appliance - what they call normal is not! I can hear it from two rooms away.
we had to have ours repaired less than 6 months after installation.
The shelves are also cheaply constructed and can only be adjusted minimally. Same with the door shelves. Not a very flexible arrangement.

So disappointed that we could not have moved our GE Profile counter-depth from our old house. It was a far superior appliance.

And by the way, the Bosch DW we have is also not the best. I'm not sure what everyone raves about. It may be quiet, but it does not clean very well, even with the recommended detergent.

product_title: Bosch B22CS50SNS500 21.7 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel Counter Depth Side-By-Side Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_text:
During my shopping process for a whole kitchen full of appliances, I noticed reviews are either penned by haters or lovers. That makes it hard for people trying to balance cost, function and reliability, because no appliance will ever be perfect. I was just now shopping on Amazon for a new filter for our fridge and noticed this product did not get very good reviews, I mean not at all. So I have to chime in and tell everyone this refrigerator is fine!

We've had this fridge installed for 6 months now. Two weeks after we put it in the ice maker went out. I immediately predicted gloom and doom and cited all the negative reviews we'd read here. But the warranty repair company sent someone out immediately. He told me this unit uses the exact same model as most other brands out there (like Jenn-Air, Thermador, Kitchenaid and GE, and all the icemaker units come from same manufacturer in China) and we just got a lemon ice maker and a gear was stripped out, which meant it wouldn't turn out the ice cubes. That whole unit got switched out at no cost, no problem. Since then we have had no issues.

Some pros, as I see them: the lighting inside is good, even being "not LED." Seriously, it's a fridge not an operating room. I really like the shelf that rotates up or down easily. I can do that to make room for something tall below without unloading the shelf. The doors do need to open almost all the way (like almost all side by sides) but the drawers slide in and out very smoothly. It is consistently very cold, and I love being able to adjust the temp on the lower drawer independently. Some weeks it holds meat at a lower temp, sometimes it's just regular stuff that's overflowed into the drawer. Also, we had an "oops" where my young son pulled the milk carton out of the door shelf too fast, and knocked that whole shelf out onto our tile floor. It hit pretty hard, and the silver rim came off, but it did not break or crack. (and the silver rim popped right back on.) Thank you, Bosch, for plastic strong enough to survive young families!

Now for some minor, picky cons: The very bottom refrigerator door shelf is useless. I think I currently have a baggie of pine nuts shoved in there, and that's really all it will hold. And the shelves on the freezer door are a little small too. This is a pretty compact unit! The control panel on the outside really takes some practice. If we ever have to do anything tricky it requires a trip to the manual drawer. I would never, ever use that panel for the timer function. Heaven help you if you set that thing. It's not intuitive. Most people who come to our house and try to use the water/ice function without a warning get their feet wet. The water dispenser is pretty far forward. This is a minor complaint, because you only make that mistake once, but I can see how people keep mentioning it in reviews because it is a little startling at first. I've never met an ice dispenser that behaved all the time, and ours does just what they all do occasionally. Crush when you've asked for cubed, spit a piece out spontaneously, etc. Very rare but it happens.

All in all, I'm really happy with this purchase. For a mid-price, sleek, stainless refrigerator, it's performing exactly as I'd hoped, which is to say that it does its job so well I usually don't even notice.

product_title: Bosch B22CS50SNS500 21.7 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel Counter Depth Side-By-Side Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_title: disappointed with interior space and quality
review_text: Just replaced our 13 yr old Kitchenaid Architect series fridge as obtained new Bosch dishwasher and db oven. Must admit, it seems flimsy with poorer quality materials/finish, and limited shelf adjustment flexibility by comparison. product_title: Bosch B22CS50SNS500 21.7 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel Counter Depth Side-By-Side Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_text: I have owned my Bosch side by side fridge for 3+ years and not a day goes by that I am not cursing it!  I have owned a Bosch dishwasher for 11 years and have nothing but praise and devotion for it so when the time came for a new fridge, it was a no "brainer" for me.  Bosch it would be!  I have to have a counter depth fridge and for those who don't know, the choices in all brands plummet to only a couple in each line.  I ordered this model from my local Lowe's store.  Within two weeks of installation the ice maker was giving me problems.  Bosch sent a guy out who without even running any diagnostics promptly jerked out the ice maker and replaced it.  Should have been my first clue.  Every couple of weeks I was calling Bosch complaining about having no ice and they would send someone out who would replace it with a new one. This appliance was new to the market so no reviews were yet posted with this complaint.  The people at Bosch tried to make me feel like I was doing something wrong and that the problem was on my end.  After having the third ice maker replaced, I finally gave up and accepted the fact that I had made a horrible choice and would have to live with this "crappy" refrigerator.  I will add that this is the most poorly designed and cheaply built appliance I have ever owned.  I don't have the noise issue others have described and it runs OK but I never know when it will decide to stop making ice so I always keep a bag of ice in the freezer we keep in the garage for emergencies. I will NEVER buy another Bosch refrigerator and am wondering if they have cheapened up the dishwashers to where the quality in them is gone as well. I may be the first human to serve time for murdering a high end kitchen appliance!  I suspect it would be worth it!!

product_title: Bosch B22CS50SNS500 21.7 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel Counter Depth Side-By-Side Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_text:
Why did I spend money to get a "top of the line Bosch" which barely makes ice, has cheap plastic internals, and after a short time has the stainless steel panels buckling. The refrigerator looks like it has been sitting on a golf driving range for 2 years getting pummeled.

product_title: Bosch B22CS50SNS500 21.7 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel Counter Depth Side-By-Side Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_title: Bosch has no clue how to make an appliance (any appliance)

product_title: Bosch B22CS50SNS500 21.7 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel Counter Depth Side-By-Side Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_text: Bought Bosh Refrigerator, Rang, Microwave, and Dishwasher less than two years ago.  All have something wrong with them. product_title: Bosch B22CS50SNS500 21.7 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel Counter Depth Side-By-Side Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_text:
Do not buy this refrigerator.
We chose Bosch because of it's reputation as a high end appliance. It looks sleek and modern.
But...it is terrible. We had to have the ice maker repaired FOUR times in as many WEEKS. They finally had to reroute a water line into the back of the refrigerator. This is FOUR times I had to rearrange mine and my family's schedule to be present for the repairman.
Some of the trim fell off a shelf inside immediately after we got it, not a big deal, but for the price we paid (at Dick Van Dyke) I expected it to at least stay in one piece for awhile. Also, some of the plastic shelves began cracking. Just last week, my 7 year old opened the fridge and an entire door shelf broke and it's contents fell out right on her. Luckily none of the condiment jars cut her when they flew onto my floor. It scared her and me to death. We paid $78 for a new shelf, which now I guess we can only put the lightweight condiments on as long as they are in plastic bottles!
The freezer is very small. The ice maker which makes about two cups of ice at a time takes up a lot of space and frozen pizzas and larger items are very hard to fit in there. I actually had to store food in my car outside while I was preparing for our Christmas guests.
Just today, I noticed the change filter light is on. Which means we'll need to buy one of those now. We've had this thing for four months and it has been one problem or expense after another. We walk on eggshells around it (literally) waiting for the next problem.
Also, at one point, the computer was all messed up and we had to push the light button to get water and the water button to get ice. We had to roll it out from the wall and unplug it for awhile and I guess it reset itself.
I basically begged Dick Van Dyke to take it back after the first two repairs (the first 2 days after I got it and the second the next week) and they absolutely would not unless I paid a 5 percent (i think) restocking fee. I think you shouldn't have to pay a restocking fee on something that was not working to begin with.
So, if you want to have an expensive, pretty fridge in your kitchen that is undependable, dangerous, and makes only a cocktails worth of ice at a time (because you will need a cocktail or two if you buy this) this is the fridge for you.
It is the worst money we ever spent and I really really regret it! I also would not recommend Dick Van Dyke.

product_title: Bosch B22CS50SNS500 21.7 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel Counter Depth Side-By-Side Refrigerator - Energy Star

product_title: Bosch 500 Series NIT5065UC 30" Smooth top Electric Cooktop In Stainless Steel
review_text:
Have used the cooktop for about three months. It has surpassed my expectations. I first saw induction cooking about 42 years ago in a high-end kitchen design store. Yes, 42 years ago. At the time, the units were installed randomly under glass that looked like tile. I didn't even know they were there among the other tiles on the counter. The Europeans are clearly ahead of everyone else in appliance innovation. It was demonstrated to us and I could not believe the concept of a burner not getting hot. I knew then, that I wanted to someday have this cooking method, but the price was always an issue.

It functions exactly as advertised and this brand or model does not make the loud humming sound I have read in other reviews of induction cooking. There is a slight hum at the highest cooking level, but it is not bothersome, especially, since I use my exhaust fan all the time. I only buy appliances on the rating of Consumer Reports, Amazon and Epinions, so I have never had a lemon for an appliance, yet. At the time of purchase, this one had a very high rating and was finally in a price range I could afford. It has all of the safety features you could want and I think it would be especially good for families with children or the elderly, as you cannot burn yourself accidentally if you turned it on and forgot to put a pan on it. It turns itself off without a pan or if you have a pan with nothing in it.

For me, the two best features are: 1. Nothing can burn on the cooktop if something spills over (including sugar) and 2. The temperature range is faster to reach than gas or a regular electric cooktop. With my old electric cooktop, it could take a while to cool down or get to a lower temperature. Gas looks like it is fast, but the grates hold heat, so reducing the temperature is not nearly as fast as induction. Now, I have to stay in the kitchen, to make sure I am there as soon as water starts to boil or a frying pan is heating up. It is that fast.

On the downside, you must use pots and pans that would stick to a magnet, so copper, aluminum and glass cannot be used. On the upside, I now have some new cookware to replace items I have used for over 25 years. The warranty starts to run on the date of purchase, not upon installation.

I found it difficult to believe that a company as established as Whirlpool would have such a policy.  I talked to supervisor and pressed him on the issue.  The answer remained - NO EXCEPTIONS.  If anything breaks after one year, it is your responsibility.  I understand normal wear and tear, but I expect the main bearing on the washer to last several years.  I am still stunned that a customer service supervisor would actually tell me that after one year (even a year and a day - as I asked him) they will do NOTHING.  Whirlpool does not care about anything after one year.  The service man that came and looked at the unit says this happens with Whirlpool often.  He said LG and Samsung have better bearings and will last longer.  I am still a huge fan of the front load washers and I will be shopping for a new one, but it won't be Whirlpool - never again.

review_text:

Also, as with any stove, make sure that the pots & pans are perfectly flat. Warped pans do not heat evenly, and if they spin easily on the cooktop, throw them out.

Also just found out (after our stove started to act up) that registering your stove doesn't necessarily mean you will be notified of any problems, or worse yet, a recall from the manufacturer. The manufacturer of our stove (Frigidaire)knew about said problem since 2008! We purchased it in 2006, but it first went out on us a month ago (Sept. 2013). We did have a service contract out on it, but after 2 visits for unrelated problems, they seem to have discontinued offering the service contract. Same thing happened with the dishwasher & the refrigerator. Same brand, offers of service contracts are no longer sent.

After "doing my homework" on the Internet, I learned that Whirlpool has bought out about 7 different company brands & own all of them. Guess what? Every single one of the different brands have the same problem with their smoothtop ovens!! This tells me that the appliance industry makes shoddy appliances either in another country, or with parts from another country. They really do not stand behind their merchandise either.

So, what is a person supposed to do??

product_title: GE GFSS2HCYSS 22.2 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel French Door Refrigerator - Energy Star

product_title: Frigidaire Affinity: FAQE7077KN 27'' Electric Dryer with 7.0 cu. ft. Capacity, 7 Drying Cycles, Auto/Timed Dry Cyles, 12 Options, Moisture Sensor, Drying Rack, Stainless Steel Drum and NSF Certified: Classic Blue
review_title: If I could give it ZERO stars, I would!
review_text:
Let me start by saying that because of my experience, I will never again buy ANYTHING with the Frigidaire or Electrolux name attached to it. NEVER. I bought my dryer a couple of years ago, and thought that only a one year warranty was a little shoddy, but never did I expect that the control panels in these dryers are like self-destructing "screw the customer" systems! The dryer started beeping one day while not even turned on, and displaying error code E68, the code for a stuck button. There are no buttons stuck, and upon researching it a bit, I found hundreds of other people online with the same exact problem. The control panel shorts out after 2-3 years and will cause the dryer to think a button is being held down and won't run. Nothing is wrong with the mechanics, it's all just this stupid electronic panel. As I, and the hundreds of other people with these dryers, have found out, Frigidaire absolutely refuses to replace the faulty control panel unless you pay ~$200.00 plus the cost of a service person to come put it in if you don't know how to do it yourself!

They KNOW that they are selling dryers with defective control panels, yet hide behind their wimpy one year warranty as a way to milk a ton of extra cash out of their customers. Where is the recall, Frigidaire??? Hopefully the Better Business Bureau will care to urge them toward resolving this. In the meantime, I recommend that you DO NOT BUY THIS DRYER, OR ANY OTHER FRIGIDAIRE PRODUCT! THEY ARE SCAM ARTISTS!!!

product_title: Whirlpool : GU3100XTVB 24 Dishwasher - Black
review_title: The beeping may drive you mad!
review_text:
Hello! At the risk of sounding completely neurotic, this dishwasher actually makes me come unglued with its beeping. It beeps when I open it (hello, I opened it, is it possible that I don't know that I opened it???), it beeps every two or three minutes while it's open (gone are the days of air drying the dishes and how could a person possibly not know that the dishwasher is open when it's laid out in the middle of the kitchen???) and it beeps when I close it (again, I'm the one operating the open/close of the dishwasher so I do not need a high pitched, completely annoying beep to let me know it's closed)! Because the kitchen is my haven, I have decided to simply hand wash the dishes most evenings because there are only two of us and a one year old so it's worth it to me to hand wash in peace.

Additionally, the racks seem quite flimsy, often off track and the silverware compartments do not stay in place well. The silverware compartments do separate so that you can easily remove sections to fit large items in the bottom yet still wash silverware but this is the only redeeming quality I have noticed so far with this dishwasher. Unfortunately, we have just bought the house and we are choosing to change other aspects of the house such as lighting so I'm stuck with this "beeper" until I can find one on craigslist that doesn't beep!

I am comparing this experience to the KitchenAid we have in our other home which is now a rental house. If the tennants didn't have four kids and need the peace and quiet more than I do, I would swap with dishwashers with them.

product_title: Whirlpool : GU3100XTVB 24 Dishwasher - Black
review_title: Good cleaning, mediocre design, right size
review_text:
This dishwasher has three positives: it fits in smaller than normal spaces, it has ample features (control options), and it cleans and dries well. It also has three negatives: relatively small capacity (understandable to accommodate the smaller exterior size), mediocre rack design, and the annoying beep when the door is open.

We've had this unit a couple months, and it's okay. I don't like the rack layout - it's not the most efficient design to stack dishes. I hate the beep. But the good thing about it is that it fits in the space we've got.

We originally bought a standard size dishwasher to replace our 15-year old one. When the guy tried to install it we were dismayed to see that it was a half inch too tall for our counter. A frustrating search for something that would fit led us to discover that the few available ADA-compliant units have a smaller height and width requirement. At that point, and even now, we're just glad to have one that didn't require us to replace our countertop.

I gave it 4 stars but that's only in the context of small dishwashers. If I rated it against standard size units it would have been probably 2 stars.

The bottom line is this: if your kitchen can handle a standard dishwasher, then don't buy this one. You'd pay more for it and have less capacity. However if you need a smaller unit then this is okay. It's not great but it's adequate, it got better reviews than the few other similar-size units we found, and it beats raising the countertop by a long shot.

product_title: Whirlpool : GU3100XTVB 24 Dishwasher - Black

review_text: For the price it's an ok dishwasher. But the beeping is one of the worst ideas ever. I cannot believe they made it impossible to turn off. It drives us nuts. It's also a little loud.

product_title: Bosch B22CS30SNS300 22.1 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel Counter Depth Side-By-Side Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_title: Seems great, but we can't keep it because of the noise.
review_text:
The delivery people dropped this off, and we unplugged it almost immediately due to a high pitched, headache-inducing noise when the compressor comes on (verified by visitors to our home). The service person from our vendor came the next day, agreed upon the noise and thought there was an issue with the compressor. He had our salesperson replace our refrigerator with another new one. The new one had the same problem, so we contacted Bosch directly and they sent their representatives out. They could not find an issue with it. Our vendor's service person came out again and called his Bosch representative, who noted a similar problem with a prior model and suggested replacing a board. The board was replaced, but the problem persists. Bosch and our service person had no alternative solutions and we are now returning the refrigerator altogether.

We purchased several other Bosch appliances at the same time (dishwasher, stove, washer, dryer) and found them all to be great; sturdy and quiet. We are extremely disappointed and unsure what we will end up buying. The only other Bosch refrigerators available to us are in the same series (we have 300, 500 and 800 appear to be the same except for more features) so we are afraid they will have the same problem and are looking at other manufacturers.

product_title: Bosch B22CS30SNS300 22.1 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel Counter Depth Side-By-Side Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_title: Ice maker a mess.  Compressor runs all day
review_text:
Only six months old- we were choosing between a GE and a Bosch and bought the Bosch because it was German made and seems well built. It certainly is attractive.

1) Long and short- spend any time in Europe and see how many Germans use ice makers-- none. Guess that's the reason Bosch has made such a mess of the ice-maker. Every time you go to get a few cubes, 10 of them fall all over the floor. Every time. 2) When it gets full, the ice-maker stops. And then never restarts again when it's empty unless you manually restart it. This means you spend a lot of time with an empty icebin (surprise...) 3) For no reason, 2 months ago the fridge started to run 24 hours a day, our of the blue. Our electric bill doubled during that time. We now need to get the vendor's service people out. What a hassle for a new fridge. 4) The alarm goes off after 1min. Incredibly annoying when filling the fridge... so we turn off the fridge to fill it. And... then often forget to turn it back on. A real design flaw.

Bottom line: Bosch hasn't figured out fridges for the US market yet. What a disappointment. Next time, based on our experience and the reviews in Consumer Reports, we'd pick the GE for sure. I wish that we never picked this model, or Bosch. We won't again.

product_title: Bosch B22CS30SNS300 22.1 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel Counter Depth Side-By-Side Refrigerator - Energy Star

So now it'll be three in the morning and the fridge alarm will be beeping.

If I could go back and get another fridge I would.

product_title: Bosch B22CS30SNS300 22.1 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel Counter Depth Side-By-Side Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_text: Bought our Bosch Linea 800 refrigerator at Sears a little over two years ago.  We have experienced issues with this unit since the very beginning - ice dispenser shoots ice all over the floor, then it jams and does not work at all.  The molding on the door shelves falls off from time to time (so annoying!).  The compressor makes strange noises from time to time that clearly are not normal operating sounds.  And this is all in year one under warranty, which Bosch honored.  Then, after the warranty ended, the LED lights on the water dipenser burned out completely and the temperature in the fridge dropped to the point where the alarm sounded.  Called repair shop and they came out and replaced the "control board/panel" for $400.  That didn't solve the problems.  They ordered temperature sensors and we are waiting for those to arrive so that they can come back and install them.  It is now 10 days that this refrigerator/freezer has been out of service.  We like Bosch products -- we bought their top-of-the-line dishwasher, oven, and microwave over the last two years and we have had no problems with those units.  But my faith in this brand has been damaged severely -- much will depend upon how they solve this problem at hand.  In the meantime, I cannot recommend Bosch products.

product_title: Bosch B22CS30SNS300 22.1 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel Counter Depth Side-By-Side Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_text:
We bought this thinking it must be the Porsche of refrigerators, judging by its manufacturer. It's actually the Fiat of iceboxes. Ours lasted exactly 30 days before both the freezer and refrigerator side died totally. The vaunted "self-diagnosis" test feature didn't work properly even though there was still power to the refrigerator, but never mind, I knew the reefer was dead--there was a big puddle of water on the kitchen floor where all the ice had melted and run out through the door icemaker. And as for that ice-maker, it never worked right anyway--dispensed either crushed or whole ice on a whim regardless of which button you pushed. Is Bosch manufacturing these things in Somalia, maybe?

Two-week-later update: I can now confidently say this is not only the worst refrigerator I have ever owned, it is the worst PRODUCT I have ever owned. Car, TV, coffeegrinder, chainsaw, power drill, computer, dildo...the worst. The icemaker makes so little ice that if we have another couple or two over for drinks and dinner, we need to first run up to the 7-11 and buy a $2 bag of ice. And if the freezer has had two or three days to make a minimal quantity of ice, you push the ice dispenser button on the door to fill a glass and nothing happens but a lot of grumbing/grinding sound. Then open the freezer drawer to try and get some ice manually and about a quart of ice cubes and crushed ice cascades out all over the floor. Great party ice-breaker, pun intended.

Bosch's contracted service people have, of course, been here. They left, shaking their heads, saying they'd have to consult with Bosch but that usually took a few weeks to get a reaction out of Bosch Central and they hoped nothing went wrong again in the meantime. "I HATE working on Bosch stuff," the service guy said. Me too.

Update: I've now had the refrigerator for 10 months. The above problem was solved (I hope permanantly) by totally replacing all of the refrigerator's electronics--two large circuit boards in compartments atop the refrigerator.

Now the ice-maker has failed. Zero. No ice. Two weeks ago, the entire ice-maker was replaced. Today, the new ice-maker has totally failed. (As for the above problem of the ice-maker making crushed ice when you want cubes, the service guy said, "Oh, yeah, they do that..."

product_title: Bosch B22CS30SNS300 22.1 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel Counter Depth Side-By-Side Refrigerator - Energy Star

product_title: Bosch B22CS30SNS300 22.1 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel Counter Depth Side-By-Side Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_title: Don't listen to Consumer Reports rating on this fridge!
review_text:
Bought this fridge in summer of 2010 since: a) Consumer Reports recommended it; and b) it was the only one to fit through the 29" doorways in our old home. Plus, it looks good and has the water and ice dispenser we wanted.

From the start, the door shelves have a plastic piece that keeps popping off. I've tightened them down with my hands because they're snap-on pieces, but they continue to pop off, sometimes falling into the fridge and generally becoming a nuisance.

Another issue: the warning beep sounds off to tell you when the door is left open too long. Kinda nifty, but I'd like to reprogram it to wait longer. Alas, there is NO WAY to reprogram a single thing on this fridge!

The biggie was summer 2012 when the control panel where I would control ice and water dispensing turned off. Nothing would reboot it (power on & off, service techs removing panel, etc.). Bottom line: the control panel is blown. In my book, that's fine. Just replace it. Technicians never called me back so I had to chase them down. When I got someone, they said they could not get the part. Seriously??? Thankfully I bought an extended warranty through Lowe's (only for big appliances like this!). So Lowe's cut us a gift card for the value of the fridge.

Now we have a dilemma: What to do with our existing refrigerator? I could pay to have the control board swapped out, but it sounds like it's only good for 1-2 years based on other web reviews. Plus, the board installed would cost me upwards of $500 (even a local tech confirms this).

I might see if I can sell this thing and just move on with life. What a hassle. My next fridge will not be a Bosch.

product_title: Bosch B22CS30SNS300 22.1 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel Counter Depth Side-By-Side Refrigerator - Energy Star

product_title: Bosch B22CS30SNS300 22.1 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel Counter Depth Side-By-Side Refrigerator - Energy Star

product_title: Bosch B22CS30SNS300 22.1 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel Counter Depth Side-By-Side Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_title: I feel like I won the lottery...
review_text:
The cabinet cut-out dimensions restricted us to buying a frig less than 69 inches in height by 36 width. I was extremely reluctant this was my only option after reading all the negative reviews. A local retailer gave me such a great price for a floor model (minor cosmetic door scratches and threw in a 5 year extended warranty), I figured what's the worst that could happen. I definitely didn't get a lemon and am keeping my fingers crossed things won't change after this first month.
Pros - Very Sleek looking (I hid the door scratches with contemporary magnets) inside and out
Very Quiet (only time we hear anything is when the ice drops into the reserve or adjust the temp)
Ice/Water Dispenser output is plenty for a family of 4 - no all over the floor issues (we use 8 to 12 ounce glasses)
Deli Fruit Vegetable drawers are big (no issue with opening doors all the way for access nothing to bump into)
Fridge/Freezer both get more than cold enough - the supercool feature is really nice after grocery shopping
No frosting problem in either the refrigerator or freezer unless I am constantly opening and closing the doors (self corrects)
2 of the door shelves can hold both gallons and 2 liter sized beverages
Unlike another reviewer, who stated 10 seconds, the door alarm only goes off after a minute of being opened - nice for
family members who cannot decide why they are looking in the first place
Cons - The door will scrape across the top of your foot if in the way when closing - only made that mistake Day 1 ouch
(The lower door was worth it to me instead of looking and having to clean an unattractive grill)
My older refrigerator was easier to move for cleaning
Egg holder only has space for 10 eggs not a dozen - I was told that's a European thing
A 6th shelf could have been added on the door for more condiments - there is wasted space
Bottom line - This is obviously a hit or miss / love it or hate it purchase - I do have the 2013 model - don't know if that makes a difference. The only reason I didn't give it 5 stars is because I am waiting to see if I feel the same way this time next year. Hopefully I can on my update

product_title: Bosch B22CS30SNS300 22.1 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel Counter Depth Side-By-Side Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_title: Bad connector in front door control panel in first 2-mos
review_text:

Much time spent to investigate issue. Bosch and dealer no help at all. They will not even supply me a wiring diagram so I can diagnose their stuff. There is a design flaw in the ice maker fill inlet heater. It has ample heat but evidently Bosch/Chinese engineers don't understand that reflective surfaces reflect heat also. I plan to put a fix out on the web for people to correct Bosch's engineering.
3. All control boards and valves are made/assembled in China. So much for German engineering and Q/C. As others, I switched from US to German made hoping to get a better product. So much for that theory going in the trash. The US made stuff at least will allow me to get a service manual for the appliance and it turns out many of the valves and units like the ice maker come from the same place as those in the Bosch unit.

product_title: Frigidaire Gallery 30 in. Slide-in Electric Range – Stainless Steel
review_text:
I like everything about how this stove cooks. The convection oven works well and is very accurated temperature wise. The controls are easy to use.
The problem I have had is with the finish. The "stainless steel" finish plate that surrounds the electronics control panel has been a problem. The finish has come off, I've been very careful to use a soft cloth and non-abrasive cleaners. A standard kitchen multi-surface cleaner took off the stainless steel finish. It is not covered by warranty, aparently non of the "non-cooking" surfaces are covered. But to find that out I had to talk to no less than 8 people. Each shuttling me to the next person, and often that person said I should have been helped by the person who forwarded the call. One man went so far as to say that they customer service department had "training problems" and lots of new staff. Not my problem. My problem is a surface that does not hold up to normal wear and tear and careful cleaning and a company that will not take responisibilty for it.
Now I have to pay $200 for a new part and figure out how to install it myself to save another $190.
Not happy with Frigidare.

product_title: Bosch B22CS80SNS800 21.7 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel Counter Depth Side-By-Side Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_text:
Got our first Bosch, and it was great. Quiet and beautiful to look at. But a defect inside allowed the glass shelves to fall off their pegs, just as you put a gallon of milk on it. Bosch came out and condemned the unit. I was impressed. Out comes #2 refrig. Plugged it in and the compressor sounded awful. A metallic rubbing sound inside the compressor. Could hear it across the house. Ice maker did not work. Out came Bosch, who replaced the ice maker but said the compressor was fine. Well the compressor noise has gotten louder, and now the ice maker died again. Also the refrig has a door open alarm feature. Well, my kids left a fruit drawer out a little, which caused the door not to close all the way. I woke up the next morning to a refrigerator that was 50 degrees inside, and no alarm sounded. Out comes Bosch for the third time. He condemns the compressor, ice maker, and a computer board. I contact customer service and demand a new machine, as it is only 2 months old. "Sorry, our warranty says we fix it, so thats what you get" She also refuses to let me talk to anyone higher than her " I am as high as you can get" she says.
I purchased it from Fergusen Enterprises, a wholesaler to the construction market. Jeff at Fergusen in Downers Grove Illinois, stepped in and pressured Bosch to replace the unit. We are currently waiting for Unit #3 to arrive.

product_title: Bosch B22CS80SNS800 21.7 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel Counter Depth Side-By-Side Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_text:
Looks beautiful but we've had multiple problems with this model

-- plastic shelf just broke off not holding anything too heavy
