-- water line freezes to water dispenser if not used for a week or so requiring turning off fridge/emptying freezer
for a day to melt water line for it to work again.

product_title: Bosch B22CS80SNS800 21.7 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel Counter Depth Side-By-Side Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_title: Not perfect when it works, but now it doesn't even work...
review_text:
After 7 months of use, I had semi-loved this refrigerator: nice to look at, intelligent layout of shelves. Have had a few minor problems:

- like another reviewer, the top cap on one of the shelves popped off and refuses to stay in place
- the ice dispenser seems to be trying to grind ice even when i'm trying to get full cubes
- the placement of the ice vs. the water dispensers are a bit non-intuitive and I'm always having to show friends how to use it so that they don't end up spilling water or ice all over the floor
- the bottom drawers in the refrigerator can only be pulled out if the refrigerator door is opened to 100%, otherwise it bumps up against the rubber gasket and cannot be pulled out.

But those are generally minor annoyances.

Then, at the 7 month mark, I woke up to an alarm going off with no explanation. Wasn't the door alarm. I turned it off and went to work. Came home and it was going off again. Opened the freezer to find everything melting. Used the manual's guidelines to do a self-test and restart the machine. Woke up to another alarm. Called Bosch and asked for a service appointment. They sent someone the next day, who concluded that the compressor or condensor was bad and that he could not do the work because it is a "closed system". Another day shot.

He referred me to another vendor who took the weekend to call me back. When I spoke to them on Monday, they informed me that they don't do work in my jurisdiction. Great. Another day shot.

Called Bosch again and they referred me to Vendor #3. They informed me that they can come out in two days, but that they would only come out to do a diagnostic and would then have to order parts and make ANOTHER visit out to install. So, Bosch's vendors cant even take the word of their own Bosch servicemen about what is wrong.

No resolution in sight yet, but I'm looking at THREE missed days from work now, and 10+ days without a refrigerator. All on a 7-month old refrigerator that cost over $2,000. I love my other Bosch appliances, but I don't think I'd buy another one after this experience...love the style, but I'm not very happy with the substance.

product_title: Bosch B22CS80SNS800 21.7 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel Counter Depth Side-By-Side Refrigerator - Energy Star

product_title: Dual Fuel Range
review_text:
I have had this stove for a few years and totally disagree with the other reviewer. The control panel is easy to learn if you follow the instructions a couple of times. It cleans in two hours beautifully (like most self-clean ovens, it has some ash you have to wipe after the door unlocks). The five burners are all different sizes and that gives you a lot of options. The delayed cooking feature is a gem for those who want to set up dinner and have it warm and ready at a specific time but you can't be home. Having two ovens below is great for holidays and multi-dish meals.
I did not have the bubbling on the burners and my stove is a few years old. You can clean the whole thing with Windex and then a stainless cleaner. I use a damp sponge to get the serious mess off, then Windex all over. When I'm feeling the need for it to be perfect, I use some of the stainless cleaner (spray kind only!) on the stainless portion and glass top. Put the burner racks in the dishwasher! Or clean in the sink with hot soapy water (any dish cleaner). Wash the buttons carefully as the writing can come off. You can always ignore the cleaning directions on appliances as they are invested in certain products.
Yes, it takes time but so did my all-electric dual oven Maytag. I hated the glass top when something burned on it as you needed to use a razor blade to get it off. Not so with this Frigidaire. The worst mess from cooking comes off with a damp sponge and/or Windex.
The only thing that needed replacement after 7 years was the door lock system when you self clean. My husband and step son did it themselves (they are very handy with motors; you may require a service call).
This is the best stove I have ever had. It is worth the money. The extra inches makes it so much easier to cook than a standard 30". We built our new kitchen around this range and gave it a gorgeous hood. It is totally reliable and has an accurate electric oven. The gas burners are a dream for any serious cook.
I HIGHLY recommend this appliance to anyone remodeling their home or who has the room for a 40" wide range.

review_title: 5 yrs. later, no replacement parts available.

There was no offer to further search other parts suppliers or no offer of a discount towards a new purchase. Or would a part from a new model work in my model? product_title: Dual Fuel Range
review_text: Does look nice, when you can actually get it clean between uses, and the little oven is handy, but the good stops there. The top is extremely hard to clean.  It's not possible to get all the spills/cleaning fluids used out from under the pans that are supposedly sealed, yet allow liquid to seep underneath.  I've had the previous model of this range for 9 years, and the new model here is essentially the same...panel and knob finish is a little different otherwise identical.  The biggest problem is the knobs on the cooking surface...pull them off and see how clean your cook-top really is. I'm stuck with it at the moment because the previous owner of our home was foolish enough to design the kitchen around it, and you can't get a decent Viking, Fivestar, Wolf, American or even GE Professional style range in 40".  Don't be fooled, spend $2-3k more and design your kitchen for 36 or 48 inch and you'll be much happier.

review_text:

Finally, the whole French Door thing was kind of interesting but after having one I'd rather have the side by side back. I use the freezer a lot and I hate constantly bending over to get things. With the side by side I kept what I used most (fridge or freezer) at the most convenient height.)

product_title: Whirlpool : GI7FVCXWY 27 cu. ft. Bottom Mount Refrigerator - Stainless Steel
review_text:

Ice maker is in the door, leaving good space open on fridge shelves.

Nice finish

Then the ice melts together into one blob (!)and will barely dispense out...in actual cubes anyway. The left door with the w/ice maker in it is very heavy so within seconds after you open it, it comes right back onto you. This makes it next to impossible to use the deli drawer, since both doors have to be open to pull the drawer out.

Door:
To keep the door from closing in, have tried re-leveling, etc nothing works. The techs who set it up said that it happened to them too. Thought it wouldn't be a big deal, but is actually very annoying trying to hold it open if you need two hands to get stuff out/in the fridge, and it folds in on you. I find myself using the right door only...may as well have my old have my side-by-side back (it was 16 years old and far bypasses this fridge in all aspects)

Motor:
We're on our second fridge in one month because the first one was making strange, loud, whiny-whirring noises each time it cycled on and off. Well, now the second fridge is also doing it. Definitely doesn't sound normal. Of course it's passed the time I can return it now.

Interior:
Compared to other fridges, the shelves and drawers are very plastic-y, cheapish with, rough-edged plastic shelves/drawers..don't look like they'll hold up long.

Finish:
maybe this is the issue with all stainless appliances? No matter what special cleaner I buy for it, the fridge is left with smear marks. Don't know, maybe I'm doing something wrong there.

Water Dispenser:
Okay, so the ONLY thing that I like about this fridge is the cool programmable water dispenser. Can allocate three different ounce volumes to fill a glass/bottle. It turns itself off after reaching chosen ounce size.

So, I guess what I essentially have in my kitchen is a $2,200.00 water dispenser!

I don't write many reviews on all the products I buy, but I am making a point to on this fridge because I want to warn others NOT to spend this kind of money on something that in NO way lives up to what quality it should be. There are plenty of other options out there. Samsung for one seems to do really well. Hard to believe that Whirlpool can sell these fridges in good conscience. It's too late for me but not for you :-) Good luck

product_title: Whirlpool : GI7FVCXWY 27 cu. ft. Bottom Mount Refrigerator - Stainless Steel
review_text:
Going on 6 months and refrigerator is working without problem. Maintains excellent temp in both frig and freezer compartments and is convenient to use with plenty of well-lit interior space. We mainly use the freezer for foods the kids need so the low drawer configuration is a good fit for us. Love the measured fill and large dispenser. Tends to be noisy when coming out of a defrost cycle, but quites down quickly. Overall much quieter than the one it replaced. Not as quite as other brands we looked at, but acceptable. Our only three complaints, and two of them seem to be common, are that the left door slams closed quickly (we open the left crisper drawer to keep it open), the ice in the ice bin tends to melt together (can't scoop ice out by hand, but the stirring rod seems to break it up when dispensing through the door) and the door open alarm is way too quiet (leaving the door ajar is a common problem in our house and the alarm hasn't helped at all). Overall construction is comparable to other brands in the price range we paid (did not pay full price) and the fact that the stainless front holds magnets was a wonderful surprise.

I would recommend this refrigerator to anyone looking for a good french door configuration with a few extra bells and whistles at a reasonable price, assuming it is priced near what we paid which was significantly lower than MSRP. I would NOT recommend this refrigerator at MSRP. There are much better choices in that range.

product_title: Whirlpool : GI7FVCXWY 27 cu. ft. Bottom Mount Refrigerator - Stainless Steel
review_text:
We've had this fridge for about a month and it has been an excellent performer. I must say however that when we first got it and turned it on, I was quite dismayed by the amount of noise. This turned out to be a temporary issue related to the fridge's start-up turbo cool mode designed to get the fridge's temperature equalized quickly. Once that happened, the fridge has been whisper quiet ever since.

We were torn between the Whirlpool and the Samsung RF4287 and after much research, we opted for the Whirlpool. Being an American made fridge, parts are easy to come by in the unlikely event that a repair is needed. Samsung has had allot of complaints in regards to parts availability that I can personally attest to. Six years ago we had a Samsung "Twin Cooling" fridge that took a dump after about a year and they had to replace it as parts were not available. The Samsung french door RF4287 is a beautiful fridge if aesthetics are your primary concern.

The features on this fridge are outstanding. Others have complained about the Ice-maker and we have had no problem. In fact, Wifey likes to make dietary Protein Shakes about three times a day and the Ice-maker is up to the task with lots of ice to spare. We also like the fact that the "in-door" design frees up a portion of the top shelf that is typically taken up with other brand's Ice-makers. The measured water dispenser is also another groovy feature not found on other fridges.

All in all, I highly recommend this product

product_title: Whirlpool : GI7FVCXWY 27 cu. ft. Bottom Mount Refrigerator - Stainless Steel
review_text: Plenty of space.  Excellent interior lighting.  Temp control and icemaking are fine.  Icemaker jams, but so did our GE.  It is expensive, but all are in this size range.  All in all, it's doing exactly what we bought it to do.

product_title: Whirlpool : GI7FVCXWY 27 cu. ft. Bottom Mount Refrigerator - Stainless Steel
review_text:
Nice Refrigerator with some caveats.
Things I like;
French Door is so Much better than side by side or traditional freezer on top. Ergonomically friendly set up eliminates bending down to that low drawer looking for stuff and plenty of wide shelves to place a tray of hors d'oeuvres. Great water dispensing system that accomodates large pitchers and dispenses measured amounts of water (oz,cups etc). 27 cubic feet is a lot of room. Magnets stick to it.
Concerns;
After 1 week had a loud noise problem, a technician came and said the fan was rubbing, he adjusted and no more noise. Ice sticks together, the dispenser generally brakes it up however we did on one occasion have a jam in the top part of the fridge (before it drops into the door) my wife stuck a wooden spoon up their and cleared it. She thought maybe it was a result of putting hot items directly into the refrigerator, maybe we should let things cool to room temp before putting them inside (the system has a turbo cool program that i'll use next time I have to put hot stuff, maybe that will keep temp low enough to prevent a reoccurence). Sometimes I hear the refrigerator humming lowly or the ice dropping into the door.

Over all I really like this fridge.

product_title: Whirlpool : GI7FVCXWY 27 cu. ft. Bottom Mount Refrigerator - Stainless Steel
review_title: A bit noisy, but love the large storage area and features
review_text:
We have had ours over a week so far, the fan noise is much louder than our old model, emitting a constant low-grade hum except when running. The hum is loud enough to be heard in the next room. We had a service tech out to look at it and he said it was normal.

Otherwise, we love it. We picked this particular model based on reviews that we had read, our experience with Whirlpool, the interior storage space, and the fact that we got it at a good discount.

There is a ton of storage space, far more than our old GE top freezer model of almost identical external dimensions. I was certainly a bit wary of the ice maker issues, but ours is working fine (even when delivering crushed ice) and we were happy to trade the larger ice capacity of some of the other models for more internal refrigerator storage space. It is keeping a perfect temperature as well.

Assuming the noise doesn't bother you, I would recommend this. I would add that we did spend $150 for an additional 3 year warranty given that I spent far more than that fixing my old GE during its first 4 years of service.

product_title: Whirlpool : GI7FVCXWY 27 cu. ft. Bottom Mount Refrigerator - Stainless Steel
review_text: We used to trust the Whirlpool brand when it comes to household appliances.  Not anymore.  This expensive product (purchased from Lowes) was a failure from the start.  All the negative reviewers on Amazon are correct in pointing out the hits and misses.  Our problem was with the water dispenser not working due to a frozen water line.  The service tech had to come out twice to replace the faulty insulation.  And of course we also experienced the infamous problem of solid mass of ice in the ice-tray.  The motor noise is louder than our last Maytag fridge but this maybe because the Whirlpool is a larger unit.  On the plus side we like the larger holding capacity and the aesthetic design and layouts of this fridge.  But overall, we are disappointed that Whirlpool did not thoroughly test this expensive product before pushing it onto us consumers.  Interestingly, Consumer Reports gave the Whirlpool brand of refrigerators a high rating.  I now have my doubts about Consumer Reports' ratings as well.  The only redeeming quality I hope will stand the test of time is Whirlpool's reputation for reliability.  We'll cross our finger but not hold our breath.  Not a good buy and not recommended!

product_title: Whirlpool : GI7FVCXWY 27 cu. ft. Bottom Mount Refrigerator - Stainless Steel
review_text: The Whirlpool #GI7FVCXWA00 that we purchased more than two years ago has more than worn out its welcome in our kitchen. It started immediately with the high pitched squealing sound from the machine, due to a poorly designed evaporator fan motor assembly. This was corrected with the redesigned replacement part. Then it was frost building up around the gasket that connects the ice-maker with the ice dispenser. "Big deal" right? Well, the frost build-up was just enough to compromise the seal just enough to let the temperature rise in the ice-maker just enough to cause it to defrost, resulting in water running into the drawers and out the front of the refrigerator onto the floor (it's just standing water on new hardwood--no big deal). This was remedied by yet another post-sale redesign in the form of a heater strip that keeps that gasket area frost-free. But that's not all...not by a long shot. Then it was the left door refusing to stay open, no matter how the unit was tilted. You see, both doors have to be open in order to access the (most often used) wide lower-most refrigerator drawer. You better know what you're taking out and exactly where it is, or that left door will hit you in the back-side over and over and over until you're ready to tear it off the hinges. Then, when you're finished in that big drawer and let that rotten left door finally close, you better not let the right door close without giving the left a good follow-up shove. You see, the pressure created by the right door closing, pushes the left door back open a little. It's just enough to make the temperature in the ice-maker rise sufficiently to defrost and...that's right...yet another flood. I would tell you how many times this thing has flooded our newly remodeled kitchen, but I have long since lost count. Now, even with that left door being closely supervised (and after shelling out $2300, constantly baby-sitting the doors is more than a little annoying), sometimes it would manage to get away with being open juuuust a little. This would result in the ice-maker delivering globs of ice (partially melted and then refrozen) that would jam in the dispenser and hold the dispenser door open, allowing the ice-maker to defrost sufficiently enough to...you guessed it...flood the floor. We have even had the appliance store owner here to get an up-front and personal brow-beating...but what good did it do? We're not getting a different fridge and even if we did, I think this thing is so poorly designed, we would have the same problems. I have finally grown so tired of the ice-maker that I have turned it off. That's right, we have an ice maker with an LCD touchscreen...that we won't use at all anymore...because it just isn't worth the stress. I would rather buy bags of ice...We used to buy nothing but Whirlpool. Times change. Companies change. If only we had known.

product_title: GE Profile : PHB925SPSS 30 Freestanding Induction Range, 5 Cooking Zones, Convection, Self Clean
review_text:
Powerful and fast is the best way I can describe the cooktop on GE's new Induction Range. It is so incredible it even surpassed all my expectations. It boils water so fast you don't even have time to get the food ready to go in before the lids rattling off the pot. Yet it heats so low that you can melt a large bar of chocolate directly in a pan without having to use a double boiler! It will have it melted and ready to use in 15 minutes, and you can leave it on for hours without worrying about it scorching. Now that's versatility! And the temperature change response time is instant. You can take that pot of boiling water with the lid rattling and reduce the heat to simmer, and the water instantly stops boiling and goes to a gentle simmer in a second. I don't mean in a few seconds. I mean right now! This thing blows gas away so bad it's not even funny. I've used both gas and electric, and gas being the closest contender doesn't even hold a candle to the power and speed of this induction cooktop. Now I can already hear the nay sayers out there saying no way, gas is the best. But seeing is believing. And this thing is truly amazing. That's not all though. It has even more tricks.

I use both cast iron and tri-ply stainless steel cookware on it. The stainless cookware gets used directly on the glass cooktop, but I'm afraid to use the cast iron on it for fear of scratching it. So I place a paper towel between the cast iron and the cooktop. You read correctly. I'm cooking on paper towels! Since the cooktop doesn't generate any heat at all, and the only heat the cooktop receives is the heat reflected back to the cooktop from the cooking utensil itself it doesn't get hot enough to ignite the paper towel. Then when I'm done cooking I use the paper towel to clean up the cooktop. This is a cinch because the cooktop doesn't get hot enough to burn anything on it anyway. Just a simple wipe with a damp paper towel or sponge and a quick sprits of window cleaner and the thing looks brand new again. I've found that a good streak free window cleaner works the best at keeping it looking new

The induction elements will make your cookware perform at the highest level it can. Since the utensil itself is the actual heating element instead of a wire coil or a ring of flame, there are absolutely no hot spots in the cooking utensil. As long as the utensil fits close to the size of the element circle, it will heat perfectly uniformly from edge to edge. The electro-magnetic energy field extends ½" beyond and above the element, so my 12" cast iron or stainless steel skillet heats perfectly edge to edge on the 11" element. And my 10 X 20" reversible cast iron grill/griddle works too despite the fact that the rim holds it about ¼" above the cooktop. It still fits within the range that the electro-magnetic field will respond to. And yes, I cook with it on top of paper towels since it is cast iron. It cooks very well spanned across the two 8" elements on the left side as long as you give it at least 15 minutes to warm up so the heat can spread out across it. The utensil size does not have to perfectly match the size of the element circle as the electro-magnet will automatically adjust to various sizes within a given range. And none of the element outside that range gets hot. Only the utensil gets hot. Think of it in the same way that a microwave gets only the food hot, the induction element gets only the cooking utensil hot. Not the food in the utensil or the cooktop itself, just the utensil. And in turn the heat of the utensil cooks the food that's in it just like it does on any other cooktop. It's just a microwave for your pots and pans! You can read all about how it works at this website: [...]. The 11" element can be used on a utensil with a bottom diameter as small as 7". The two 8" elements can go as small as 5 ¾", and the 6" as small as 4 ¾". You can also use a utensil larger than the element as well. I use a 14" cast iron pizza pan as a griddle on the 11" element and all but about the outer 1 ½" of the pan are evenly heated. The heat tapers off somewhat around the outer perimeter.

This thing is really built too. Weighing in at 240 pounds, it outweighs the Samsung induction range by 32 pounds and the Kenmore induction range by a whopping 50 pounds! We're talking impressive build quality here. The stainless steel is a very nice quality and is easy to keep looking good.

The control panel is a one piece glass touch panel with no knobs. It responds very well to touch and is easy to use. There is a slight learning curve since you're cooking by number instead of turning a knob. But I adapted quickly to it and don't even think about it anymore. There are 19 steps from low to high for each element. All 4 induction elements are high power and have a "boost" cycle that makes them quite capable of boiling a pot of water very quickly. There is also a fifth element that is a warming burner. It's a 120 watt electric radiant burner (not induction) with three settings, hi, med, and low. It is not designed to heat anything up, just to keep already hot things warm.

I haven't had much of a chance to use the oven yet, but from what little I've used it, it seems to work well. It has three heavy enamel coated racks that you can leave in the oven during self cleaning. That's a big plus because those big racks don't fit in the sink, so your only other option would be to wash them in the bathtub or take them outside. I've done it both ways with our old stove and neither is fun. So I'm happy I don't have to do that anymore with these. They also slide very easily in the oven too and there are six positions for them. This oven uses what is called True European Convection. Meaning that there is a third element around the fan itself. During convection cooking only this element is used and the fan blows and circulates heated air into the oven cavity. This particular system also reverses itself every 70 seconds which is supposed to aid greatly in the evenness of the temperature throughout the oven cavity. I have read that it works quite well so I can only assume great results when I really get a chance to use it. It also comes with a temperature probe that will come in quite handy when cooking whole birds, hams, and roasts. The convection fan is fairly quiet too. Much quieter than the one on my convection microwave. There's also a small fan in the cooktop that cycles on and off occasionally to keep the electronics in there cool. That too is very quiet and goes unnoticed quickly if even noticed at all. The kitchen has to be pretty quiet to hear it.

I have only had it a few weeks but so far I love it. The only problem I have had, if you can call it a problem, was trying to figure out a particular feature it has. If you own one of these or are going to buy one this may be of interest to you. If not interested, you may want to skip this and move on to the next paragraph. So here goes. I asked three different people at GE, the local rep, the email tech support, and the phone tech support and nobody had an answer for me, so I had to just figure it out myself. You see, the convection oven has a feature called "Convection Conversion". The user manual is written for many different models, but doesn't cover "convection conversion". It does however talk about "Auto Recipe Conversion" which is basically the same thing. They differ though in how the end result is executed. Both features when set to "on" are designed to automatically reduce the convection cooking temperature by 25 degrees since convection cooking is more efficient than conventional baking. This way you can just follow the standard temperature in a recipe, cook with convection and the temperature reduction is automatically taken care of for you. Sounds easy enough right? Well, according to the manual under "auto recipe conversion", (remember, there is no mention of "convection conversion") when you set say 350 deg and press start, you are supposed to see it say on the display, CON, 325 (the -25 deg thing) and then go to pre-heat. When it reaches 325 deg it will signal it's ready. But mine doesn't do that. If I set 350, there is no CON, 325. It just goes to pre-heat and signals it's ready at 350. So where's -25 deg's I'm supposed to be seeing? One GE rep said it was broken and wanted to schedule to have it fixed. I said no, I'll do some further checking myself before fixing something that may not be broke. The one at the store wasn't plugged in, so I couldn't see how that one worked either. So I decided to test it with my infrared thermometer since I don't have an oven thermometer to see if the actual temperature was 25 deg lower than indicated when convection conversion was set to on. Sure enough, with it set to 350 deg (and showing 350 deg on the display) it was actually 325 deg in the oven according to the infrared thermometer. When I turned the convection conversion off, the temp in the oven went all the way to 350 deg. Problem solved. And I prevented a repair man from tearing my new stove apart only to discover that it did the same exact thing again when he was done. Amazing that nobody at GE had the answer for me though. I guess this is a "new" feature that hasn't made it into the books yet, or anywhere else for that matter. Anyway, hopefully this has answered the question for someone else reading this that may be wondering the same thing too.

I am very happy I got this range. I had my heart set on getting the GE Café model because I really like the up-front controls and the pro look. But then I read the article in Consumer Reports on ranges and read about the induction cooktop. This induction range was about the same price as the GE Café model too. I had never even heard of induction before so I decided to do some research on it. Turns out induction has been around for about 30 years! In Europe, it out sells both gas and electric cooktops. It is also 90% energy efficient too because most of your energy goes directly into the cookware instead of heating the air. So your kitchen will stay much cooler in the summer too. It is far safer since there is no heat and no flame. And the element turns off automatically when the utensil is removed for a period of time (30 sec in my case), so there's no accidentally left on burners to burn your house down! So why hasn't it caught on here yet? The cookware. It requires cookware that is ferrous (magnetic) and apparently Americans are put off that they might have to replace their cookware for it. Therefore, very few company's here even sell induction cooktops let alone ranges, so the price for it remains fairly high. But thankfully that's starting to change and the prices are coming down to a more affordable level now. I believe that once people realize how great induction is they will get over this cookware thing and latch onto it. Induction is the next big thing since the microwave! It is well worth investing in some new cookware if you have to. Your cookware may already work anyway. If a magnet will stick to the bottom of your cookware, it is induction ready. If not, there is plenty of inexpensive cookware you can buy that will work. Try Ikea's 365+ line for starters.

I am so glad I read the article about the new ranges. If I hadn't, I would have spent the same money and bought the Café with an electric radiant cooktop since I can't get natural gas where I currently live and propane is not even an option to me (used them, don't like how they perform). Then I would have missed the boat on this wonderful technology. I believe in the next decade induction will be the next big thing here too. Let's hope.

Update: I have added a video review on YouTube. If you go to YouTube and type "GE Induction Range Water Boil Test" in the search bar, it should be the first video that comes up. (Amazon won't allow me to post a link to it here.)

11 Month Update:

After using this range for the last 11 month's I am happy to report that I still absolutely LOVE it! I have had no problems with it at all and we've since moved it into a new house. (New to us anyway). The speed of heating, instant temperature change response time, and heat uniformity across the pan are phenomenal. The glass cooktop looks as good as the day it was new. It is so easy to keep clean because it doesn't get hot enough to burn anything on it. You can clean up spills instantly while you're cooking because of this. And when you're done, a few spray's of glass cleaner and a paper towel and your cooktop looks like new again!

The element layout and size on this GE Range are perfect as well. I noticed a person mentioned that on their Samsung induction range their utensils had to be just the right size and perfectly centered, and if you bumped them off center or removed them from the cooktop for even a moment the element would turn off. Not so with the GE. Your cookware doesn't have to be centered at all and the element will just find and follow them. As long as you have at least the center of the element covered, it will locate and follow the pan as you move it around. The element will turn off automaticallyif the utensil is removed, but only after over 30 seconds from being removed. This gives you plenty of time to pick up and shake your food around the pan and set it back down without having to turn it back on. Also, a wide range of sizes can be used on the various elements. These elements are just not that picky.

There's a cooling fan in the cooktop to keep things cool in there that comes on from time to time. But it is so quiet that it quickly goes unnoticed. If your exhaust fan is on you'll probably never even hear it. Sometimes, depending on the utensil you will get a little buzzing sound. But that usually goes away after a few minutes. At any rate it's not annoying and is normal for this type of cooktop. Another aspect of induction cooking that you quickly appreciate is the fact that the setting used on one burner is exactly the same as on another burner. So if you're cooking something on a front burner on say 3 1/2, and you want to move it to a back burner so you can use that burner for something else, you just set the back burner on 3 1/2 and it is exactly the same setting as the front burner. And with no warm up time whatsoever! Because the pan is the part generating the heat, not the element. And the pan is already hot. The frequency from the magnet just keeps it that way. Same frequency = same heat.

The oven works equally well too. It cooks evenly and predictably. It's a little slow to warm up but not annoyingly so. And when using convection you don't have to wait for it to fully warm up anyway. The oven is very well insulated too. I've used the self clean feature 3 times now and this range doesn't get nearly as hot to the touch as other ranges I've used in the past. Although I'd still remove anything from the cooktop when self cleaning. The three oven racks are finished in the same enamel finish as the oven interior so I just leave them in while the cleaning is being done. This is a real time saver compared to my old range because I don't have to clean (read scrub!) the oven racks anymore. The enamel interior and racks still look like brand new after three cleanings. Just a wipe with a wet wash cloth to wipe the ash out is all that is needed after cleaning. I wipe the edges of the racks with a little olive oil and they glide like new. I expect the oven and racks will hold up for a long time to come.

I just can't say enough good about this range. It has been a wonderful tool to use for cooking. And the stainless steel pot's and pan's set I bought 11 month's ago to use on it still look like new because the induction cooktop is so easy on them. No hot spots, no burnt on food on the bottom, and no flames to discolor them. When I think of all the people that turn away from these induction cooktops because they don't want to buy new cookware I just shake my head. Cookware that works on these doesn't have to be expensive as anything that a magnet will stick to will work. It is a very small price to pay for such an exceptional cooking tool. No other cooktop at any price can compete with the performance of a good induction cooktop. That has been proven time and time again. Gas can't boil water anywhere near as fast, nor can it simmer anything as low. And electric doesn't even hold a candle to this technology. These have been selling in Europe for over 30 years now and have been exceptionally reliable. And why not, it's just an electromagnet with very little heat around it comparatively to cause failure. It's just so simple it's amazing.

20 Month Update:

It's been 20 month's now since I bought this range and it still looks and performs as good as the day it was new. I have had 0 problems with it. There are a couple of tiny scratches in the cooktop now but you have to look very closely to find them. Really, only a person cleaning the cooktop would ever even notice them. Also, the front edge of the brushed Stainless Steel that borders the cooktop is showing a little wear from things getting drug across it. But again you have to look closely to notice it. These are just the signs of a well loved range that gets used. And they are really only noticeable to the person cleaning it because you are looking for imperfections to polish out. You'd never even notice them by just looking at the stove.

The glass touch control panel and the oven still look and perform flawlessly. I have cleaned the oven about 6 times now using the self clean feature and it comes out looking like new every time. Just a little wipe out of the remaining ash with a damp rag is all that is needed after the clean cycle is done. The enamel finish on the oven and on the racks still looks like new. No signs of dulling or chipping as some have mentioned happening with "other" brands. And the enamel coated racks are WONDERFUL because you can just leave them in during the clean cycle and they come out looking great. No more having to remove the racks before self cleaning and take them outside to scrub on them as I had to do with chrome racks in my previous range. I just remove the racks when the cleaning is done, wipe the remaining ash residue off with a damp rag and apply a little cooking oil to the side edges of the racks and the rack guides on the oven walls and they slide in and out with ease again.

I still love this range and would never go back to a conventional electric or gas range unless there was no other option. For the money there is nothing that even comes close in performance to this range even from ranges costing thousands more, gas or electric. Even among the latest Induction Ranges available here in the US, from what I've read about them I still feel that this GE model is the best of the best. And two years in, the latest model from GE is still unchanged from the one that I own. However, they have added a "slide in" version now of this marvelous range for those that require it. It appears to be exactly the same as mine except that the control panel is on the front edge. Very cool.

product_title: GE Profile : PHB925SPSS 30 Freestanding Induction Range, 5 Cooking Zones, Convection, Self Clean
review_text: My range was delivered at the end of December and I've been using it for 4 months now.  It is everything that I expected and I am very happy with it.  It is so much easier to clean than any other range I've had, just a soapy, damp sponge to clean the grime, another wipe down with it rinsed out, and then some window cleaner.  My friends who come to visit are impressed with how fast it boils a pot of water, and the oven is large and accurate. It is so minimal that unless you are living in a monastery you won't really notice it at all.  What more can I say?  It really is the perfect range, fully deserving of all the positive reviews.

product_title: GE Profile : PHB925SPSS 30 Freestanding Induction Range, 5 Cooking Zones, Convection, Self Clean
review_title: Great Cooking Ability with some practical thoughts
review_text:
We have the same glowing reviews as others, but I am going to add some other things that people may or may not think of when buying a stove. If you have small children--beware of the handle on the bottom drawer. It is very tempting for our three year old to stand on it to see what we're doing. Obviously this is a safety hazard since she'll generally use the oven door as the thing to grab when standing on the drawer. She doesn't try it often, but sometimes if dinner takes too long or she gets restless in the kitchen, I see her standing there with her foot going up to it like she wants to stand on it or something. Most other stoves we have had with a pull out drawer do not have the handle.

Along with that point goes the bummer side of having stainless steel with kids around--fingerprints are everywhere on it. I never noticed how dirty our old white stove front was, but I notice every spot, drip or spill on the front of this. None of these minor things contribute to the functionality of the stove or oven in any way obviously. If you don't have the best house-keeping skills with children around, or perhaps do not have a house-keeper to run around after them wiping away fingerprints, and things like that are prone to make you a little more nuts than you were before, then perhaps find a stove that works as well and doesn't show all the spots as easily. It's not hard to clean it, one just needs to be more on top of it than I ever am these days!

Otherwise, it's all happy cooking! I am quite amazed at how fast it brings water to a boil. It's also nice to just know that "4" is the right pancake temperature, "3" is simmer without having to finely adjust the gas or electric stove all the time in the low-med-high ranges. I usually found the perfect spots on our old stove systems (which sometimes varied burner to burner), but just dialing in a number is nice and it seems consistent enough that I don't notice if there is a slight difference. "4" is perfect pancake heat on all the burners. "3" is simmer.

Overall we're very happy with it!

Update 11/4/2014: I still love this stove. The burners all heat pans at consistent temperatures and the oven is always true to temperature. However, the shiny front still drives me crazy. In our kitchen, the sun shines on it every day for a few hours and I can't ever seem to get it clean enough. There are always drips, fingerprints, smudges, wipe marks, etc. The old white oven door did not show all the smudge. The top part also gets spattered with oil or whatever every time I cook anything. I wipe it daily, but sometimes it's just a sloppy "Wipe it when wiping the counters" instead of a full on clean with an officially-approved-cleaner for shiny surfaces. If your stove is in a darker kitchen, it might not bother you so much. Or perhaps you have better cleaning skills? Really, the perks outweigh the smudges, but if there was a less shiny color, I'd go for that--with no drawer handle on the bottom.

review_text:

product_title: GE Profile : PHB925SPSS 30 Freestanding Induction Range, 5 Cooking Zones, Convection, Self Clean
review_title: Embarrassed to admit what I paid for this disappointment
review_text:
My wife and I gifted this range to each other for an anniversary. We replaced a perfectly good smooth-top electric unit because we both hated the ridiculous amount of heat that remained long after a burner was turned off. It was a hazard to us and potentially, our pets. An errant towel, hot pad or hand could have been disastrous. In retrospect, I think we would have gone a different way in buying a replacement, had we to do it over. I'll start with the positive.

Induction burners heat fast and cool much quicker than radiant coils. They don't have to heat the glass top and then transfer that heat to the pan. The temperature changes are near instant, plus, when you remove the pan, the power turns off. No need to worry whether you left a burner on after pulling off the pan. The burner controls are easy enough to understand and use, and it's generally a pleasure to cook on. Generally. My list of negatives starts here...already. The main (large) burner control has begun malfunctioning. When you adjust it, it may jump to HIGH or just turn off.

When we shopped this range, we nearly bought the better looking Electrolux EW30IF60IS, but the few reviews we could find scared us away. The top rating in Consumer Reports brought us back to this GE Profile, despite it's homely 1940's robotic looks. The fit and finish is not what I expected at this price range as the stainless panels on the doors are poorly aligned, and the sealer between the glass top and the metal rim looks like I shot it out of a caulking gun.
Also, when reading the owners manual, it's nearly impossible to determine if the features you're reading about pertain to the model you have, as it covers multiple ranges.

Getting back to the burners, the surface markings are hard to see, so you can't tell if your cookware is centered over the burner. To further complicate this, the top is so slick that simply stirring what's in your skillet will have it skating all over the place. You need both hands for this simple task, and that makes holding a dripping lid while you stir impossible. Even stranger, we discovered that our pasta pot with a couple of quarts of water in it will walk right off the burner by itself! You see, the burner coils buzz (we knew that going in), and create a vibration strong enough to move a heavy pot. That is unforgivable. Do they test these appliances at all before they stick us with them?

The control panel does have a nice sensitive touch to it, but unless you have good lighting directly above, the faint markings are hard to read. We solved this with an under-cabinet light. We have found that changing the oven temp on the fly is quirky. You must turn the oven off and reset the temp, but if you are lowering the setting, the unit senses an error and sometimes won't let you. Same goes for changing to convection at the end of a bake to speed browning. Sometimes it doesn't work. On the subject of convection, the range is supposed to have a programmable mode to adjust temperature for this, but when we followed the steps in the manual to activate this, the panel never displayed the "CON" that indicates you are using the corrected convection setting. We tried this several times to no avail. No great big deal here, as we have not found much of anything that improves with convection. Just burns the outside, and undercooks the center. I don't blame that on this range, just the technology.

You might think despite the negatives listed that GE could at least make a decent electric oven when convection is not used. You'd be wrong. We suspicioned that the temp was fluctuating based on cooking times and current temp readings that displayed when we changed temperature during cooking. I used my digital oven thermometer to chart the temperatures during preheating and through a two hour cycle. The oven indicated that it was preheated to 350* at eleven minutes, but in actuality, it had hit 350* somewhere around nine minutes, and was at 379* when the signal sounded. It continued to climb to 381* and then cycled and cooled all the way down to 324* at 23 minutes. It then continued to climb to 394* at 30 minutes and topped out at 401* at 37 minutes. You would expect the oven to then cycle and cool, but it held the temp in the 390's until one hour and forty-five minutes! At this point, I decided to up the temp to 450* to see how it responded. When the display changed from the current setting of 350* to the actual preheating temperature, it read only 320*! That's seventy-two degrees short of what my digital was reading!

This range also has a lower warming drawer that we have not used. Doubtful that we will since it basically looks like a storage drawer with an element above. It's not well sealed or insulated. It's probably perfectly safe, but the preheating time is almost prohibitive. Had we bought the Electrolux, we could have at least had an actual double oven for the extra money. Really disappointed with this purchase. Would not recommend this product to someone else, and for well over $2200, the sting is pretty severe.

product_title: GE Profile : PHB925SPSS 30 Freestanding Induction Range, 5 Cooking Zones, Convection, Self Clean
review_title: Meet Jane Jetson!  (same stove slide-in model)
review_text:
After much research, and driving far and wide to locate one up close and personal to look at, hands down this was the range for us.

It is beautifully made, very sleek and modern, and works like a dream. All fans on it (convection and component cooling) are whisper quiet. The control board is located on the front (unlike the free-standing model) and is very intuitive to use. It is definitely what I call "granny friendly," i.e. even those from the non-digital age will be able to use it easily.

The oven is very spacious and at high altitude only took 13 minutes to heat from cold to 425 degrees. I especially love the sliding rack and will be replacing the other two standard racks with those. Even at 425 degrees, the front of the oven door remained cool to the touch, suggesting that this stove is very well insulated. The first batch of cookies in it came out beautifully and the timing was +/- 1 minute from my usual recipe so I call that spot on.

The first time I used the stovetop, I put pan down, turned the heat to 5 and dropped in a pat of butter which began to melt *instantly* and I do mean instantly. Water boils in no time,(8 minutes for a large pot of water for pasta) and clean-up is a breeze.

The pans I am using are: Cuisinart FCT-10 French Classic Tri-Ply Stainless 10-Piece Cookware Set and they work fantastically with this stove.

I could not be more thrilled, and will update this review as time goes on.

product_title: Bosch : SHE55M12UC 24 Evolution 500 Series Full Console Dishwasher - White
review_title: Very Clean, Very Quiet, Very Happy
review_text:
(this is a copy of my review under the stainless steel exterior version SHE55M15UC...don't know why Amazon has them separated)

Installed myself. You will need a strain relief and power cord, and possibly an adapter to connect to your garbage disposal or pipe. The drain hose supplied fits up to 3/4". I needed 1". A $5 dishwasher drain hose adapter and a $1 3/4" galvanized steel pipe nipple solved that problem.

This thing is unbelievably quiet compared to our 8 year old previous 'quiet' model. You can easily carry on a conversation next to it. We have an open kitchen / living area that used to require turning up the television volume when the previous dishwasher ran...No More!

Dishes come out very clean. As others have said elsewhere, I think the Finish Quantum Powerball (sample provided) or another highly rated CR brand will make a huge difference in your results too.

The passive drying works extremely well. We will only have a few drops of water left on plastic.

I have seen the Sanitize light come on. It means that very specific conditions (time, etc as specified by the NSF) were achieved during the wash and dry. Note that the Sanitize light won't come on until the Drying cycle is complete, which is well after the Cycle countdown has reached '0'.

product_title: Bosch : SHE55M12UC 24 Evolution 500 Series Full Console Dishwasher - White
review_text:
Bought a new dishwasher after my 10 year old GE profile started leaking. Installed myself. Some hints,when moving the dishwasher, you will have the tendency to want to grab the metal flange of the dishwasher that is sticking out. Do not do that, that part of the dishwasher is really sharp and will cut you. Also buy a new water line to replace the old one. I tried to use the same water line from before, but it leaked. There is an O-ring in it and I guess it did not seal very well. The strain plate that you have to buy took me a while to find. It was called a combination connector in the hardware store I went to. What it does is clamp the cord so that if someone pulls on the cord, the stress will go to the clamp and not pull the wires out of the dishwasher. For wiring the electrical, no soldering is required, you just push the wire into the correct place and tighten the screw down. It is a 3 phase wiring. I forget which color goes to what, but you can find that online. Putting on the bottom grill was hard. You should align everything with a flashlight , then put the screws in.

Now to the dishwasher. After buying it, I had a bit of buyers remorse. The rack is great for loading saucers and plates,but it is hard to load cups and bowls. We used to load cups on the sides of the top rack, but on the Bosch, if you do that, you can't put plates next to it, unless you have ridiculously small tea cups. There are a lot of very narrowly spaced bars that don't work so well for big items and bowls. You can move the bars down, but if you can't nest the bowls, you really can't put many bowls in. There are some wider spaced bars for bowls on the top rack, but not many. Overall, it does not seem to hold as much as my older dishwasher because of these inefficiencies in loading bowls and cups. I also did not like the controls that much. When you turn the on/off switch on, it immediately starts the cycle. It doesn't allow you to pick which cycle. You can change cycles after it finishes. I'm still figuring this out, but I left it on auto mode, which seems to work.

Now the good part, this is the first dishwasher I have ever used that I can just put in really dirty dishes and it will clean them without pre-rinsing or scraping. I put in plates with stuck on cheese and pasta that I could not scrape off without a scotchbrite pad. After the cycle, they were very clean. They recommend using Finish quantum pellets, but I was using the cascade gel I was using from my previous dishwasher and it work fine. So this makes cleaning dishes much faster. Just wipe off anything loose particles and put the soiled dish in. I really like this about this dishwasher. Maybe all new dishwashers are like this, but I'm happy that this cleans so well.

I would give the Bosch a 5 if it had more rack space suited towards bowls and the controls weren't so fussy. However, bottom line, this dishwasher cleans better than any dishwasher I've ever used and for that, I am happy that I bought it. Also, I was able to get a $50 credit from the utilities for this since it saves water and electricity.

product_title: Bosch : SHE55M12UC 24 Evolution 500 Series Full Console Dishwasher - White
review_text:
After much research, we retired our 1992 Kenmore dishwasher in favor of a Bosch Model# SHE55M12UC. The Kenmore was still going strong, cleaning the dishes just fine, though noisy as from the day we bought it and a bit beat up. But, hey, it was 20 years old (and I will give it to Habitat for Humanity's Restore store and some one will use it some more years.)

We didn't wait for it to fail. We became very interested in using less water and less gas to heat the water and a much quieter appliance, and we assumed the dishes would be cleaned as well if not better than with our Kenmore.

In all cases our expectations have been met. It is a very economical appliance, the dishes get VERY clean (on "Auto" setting) and, my goodness, the appliance is so quiet we really do have to listen "closely" for its work.

You can hear the water going in sometimes and can hear water going into the drain and with ear to machine, you can hear the operations (hum of the motor, etc.) But, that's it. If two people are in the kitchen talking normally, they drown out the machine, not the other way around.

Yes, as some people have pointed out, the capacity of the machine is less than, say, a new Kenmore. So, if you have a really big family, then maybe you should choose less quiet and more capacity. That said, we had two guests last night and the Bosch handled all four of our dinner and desert and pan and glass and coffee cup and big bowl dishes. It may be we have to think a bit more about placement than we did with our bigger Kenmore, but that is OK for us.

Some people talk about lack of sufficient drying. I don't know what they are talking about. When the zero on the counter comes on, open the door and the dishes are pretty dog gone dry. (Except where concave surfaces have held "puddles" of water.

The ability to EASILY raise or lower the top rack seems really useful, as do all the various tines that are collapsible. The two utensil baskets offer lots of versatility.

What most impresses me is the build quality and that was the reason we bought the Bosch. During the installation you can see and feel the German engineering and the manufacturing quality done in the U.S. Without going into detail you can see HOW the quiet--47 DB--is achieved. If this machine fails I will be surprised.

One caveat, one negative, though it is not enough for me to knock the rating from a five to a four. If I could: 4.75. While the Bosch cleverly channels both the electrical wiring and the hot water inlet line to the front of the machine where they are secured, I cussed at the Germans for their method of installing the plastic toe plate which is used to help quiet the machine.

I had read another review about that "blinkety blank" toe plate. The engineering team did not take into account real life. Again without detailing why it was such a 45 minute problem, I will give those of you who do install this machine yourself a tip: Use masking tape to tape the 1.5" long screws (2) to the tip of your screw driver and then you will be able to insert the screws into the holes. You will know what I mean. I blinkety blanked the Germans on this part!

I have no other, but an old Kenmore, dishwasher with which to compare this Bosch. But, as an amateur handy man, I can unequivocally say this Bosch is the real deal.

Stephen Drinkard
Sandpoint, Idaho

product_title: Bosch : SHE55M12UC 24 Evolution 500 Series Full Console Dishwasher - White
review_text: We bought this dishwasher 18months ago.  It's been horrible.  We've had the rinse aid dispenser replaced twice b/c the light doesn't come on when the rinse aid is out. You just suddenly notice everything is soaked.  Would expect this on a lower end model, but not this one.  We're going to need to replace it again.  Our control panel has been replaced at least once and broke again.  You have to turn off the machine to change cycles or start the cycle and you have to move fast b/c the machine starts immediately.  Our plastics are now coming out with that awful white film in spite of using the recommended Finish items since the beginning and the dishwasher cleaner.  The Bosch support has been horrible.  We were missing some accessories and Bosch wanted to charge me for them stating they were not included in spite of the owner's manual showing the inclusion.  They actually wanted proof of purchase for $5 worth of stuff even though we had just had it serviced and they verified we did indeed pay for it.  Would have given 1 star except the machine is very quiet, the racks are very versatile, and it's great not having to worry about the plastics melting.  Do not buy this horrible machine. Bosch is riding on it's reputation, but having it's products made in China will soon ruin that rep.  Never again!

product_title: Bosch : SHE55M12UC 24 Evolution 500 Series Full Console Dishwasher - White
review_text:
We bought a Bosch dishwasher for about $700 shortly after the 2009 recall (dish washers bursting into flames due to electronics issue.) We thought that the quality issues were limited to a single electronic component, and previously the company had a good reputation.

The dishwasher cleans dishes... so we should be happy, right? In the past year, the control buttons and the plastic "countdown" window have popped out one by one. Today is my second round of DIY repair. The reason for repeated button loss is now very clear - the front fascia panel is made of a thin panel of ABS. This is not just a decorative panel - the stress of door opening with every use is applied to the panel, which is now cracked. Because of a design flaw, the cracks propagate right into the button area - so I no longer have a way to keep those buttons from falling out.

Parts are available on the Bosch web site. "only" $86 plus shipping for the fascia and the missing button. The replacement panel will have the same design issue as the original, so this may buy me a year, 2 years or three of intact dishwasher.

For environmental and financial reasons, I expect a dishwasher to last about 15 years. I am very disappointed by the substantial repair time and cost caused by an under designed appliance part.

model number: she45m02UC/53
part of doom: panel-fascia 478810

product_title: GE JKP90SPSS 27" Stainless Steel Electric Combination Wall Oven

product_title: GE JKP90SPSS 27" Stainless Steel Electric Combination Wall Oven
review_text:
Purchased this to replace a KitchenAid Architect Series since it had the same dimensions and would be an easy install in the cabinet. It has a lot less features than the KitchenAid, but still seemed to be a decent oven/microwave combo.

The microwave worked well, and we didn't have the paint peeling problem that many complain about (maybe not enough time has passed). The oven, however, has bothered me since the beginning. There is a blast of hot air and steam that hits you in the face when you open it that is not insignificant. When it first happened to me, I thought for sure others have complained about this. There are some reviews about it, so I know it isn't just my unit. I will put up with a lot and don't complain about products, but this really is bad. It's a wonder it hasn't been recalled. Basically, regardless of what temp or how long its been on, when you open the door, you get hit with a very hot blast of air and steam. I have learned to pull the door open and stand back. If something with high water content is there - veggies or potatoes, for example - you really have to watch out. One time my eyes smarted for a good minute after a blast. I now warn kids to step back, and remind myself. I didn't bring the issue to GE since I figure they'll not be helpful and frankly I didn't want the hassle of bickering back and forth, having someone come out, possible expense, and probably no solution. Based on other reviews I've read, dealing with GE is fruitless.

This week, the unit totally failed. The microwave emitted a 4-beep alarm every minute saying there was a possible short, service may be required. There was no way to stop the alarm every minute until my husband took the panel off. YouTube diagnosis suggested cleaning some of the wire connectors, but ours were totally clean. Checked all connections and disconnected power under the house. Plugged back in and then all appeared well. Used the microwave one last time, successfully. Then, it turned itself on for a couple of seconds and the alarms went off again with the same message. This has happened to others as well and I've read that GE is no help once outside the very short warranty period. I feel like I've leased an oven and lost my money. I'm not calling out service and facing a $300 cost for who knows what and possibly no fix. Besides, it won't fix that hot air blast that has irked me since the beginning.

Another minor thing that I've just dealt with: it cooks unevenly. But that, I figure can be solved by rotating the baking item. And, while I'm at it: the TWO clocks on the ONE display panel that have to be set separately and can keep different times (annoying when it's one minute off) is frankly just plain weird.

I'm so disappointed with the oven and I certainly don't recommend it. Disappointed that "durable goods" are even allowed to be made so poorly. Disappointed that I, the consumer, end up eating all the irritation and cost. Disappointed that I know GE won't stand behind the product. I'm sure GE will either yank my review or say failure is my fault (install or whatever), but I will try and inform everyone best I can to take the time to find a better product.

product_title: GE PGS975DEPWW Profile 30" White Gas Slide-In Sealed Burner Range - Convection
review_text:
I bought this to replace a 25 year old GE stand alone range that had finally given out. The new range looks great and works ok but there are a few issues.

One is that as a slide-in, when replacing a stand alone there is a gap from the wall to the rear of the range. In order to fill that gap, instead of simply providing what is an inexpensive strip of metal for such cases, GE requires you to purchase it as a separate piece of trim for about $40. If it were something more substantial, like an aluminum grating (which they used to offer) I could understand, but all it is is a painted strip of metal, which offers no method of adjustment, it either fits or it doesn't- which in my case resulted in still having a 1/16 in gap between the back of my range and the wall (leaving me to eventually fill that gap with stuff I bought from Home Depot).

Another issue is the heavy metal grill that covers the burners. It comes in two pieces that sit on the left and right sides of the top of the range. The ones I received were not quite symmetrical, leaving the bottom section (part of where they meet) looking uneven. Plus they did not sit on the range quite steady, one kept rocking back and forth causing me to use some folded up aluminum foil to prop up one corner in order to have it sit more steadily (as you would with a table that doesn't sit steady).

The controls sit more or less on the front top edge of the stove. At first I didn't realize this would be an issue, until I tried to cook some pasta. The front controls use up stovetop space, causing the burners to be pushed further toward the back. When trying to stir and access food cooking you have to lean over the stove quite a bit- even for items on the front burners- I have a microwave above my stove and it results in making it very cumbersome and difficult to access.

Except for the burner dials, the controls are touch sensitive causing some accidental activations whenever cleaning them. The oven has no up or down thermostat control, you have to set the temperature exactly each and every time you want to make an adjustment (want to go to 280 degrees from 300? That means "Cancel"... "Bake" "2" "8" "0"... "start").

Lastly there's an exhaust fan that stays on well (up to 40 minutes) after you press "cancel" with no way to turn it off other than pulling it out of its cabinet and disconnecting the electric. It's a bit noisy and having no control with turning it off can be annoying.

**Update 11/3/12**
Because the controls take up part of what would normally be the cooking area, the front burners are relatively close to the controls. As the largest burner is on the right front, if you set a large pot over it with a full flame, the heat generated begins to burn the control panel area. Such area is trimmed with: ...wait for it... PLASTIC. Who designs a gas-burning stove top with plastic anywhere near the burn area? The trim around the burner warped, turned brown/black and almost caught fire. The display then got condensation from the inside (making it next to impossible to access and clean). Despite the hefty price tag on this range, with a very poorly designed cooktop, it's just not worth it.

product_title: GE PV977NSS Profile 36" Stainless Steel Chimney Style Island Mount Range Hood - 450 CFM

product_title: GE PV977NSS Profile 36" Stainless Steel Chimney Style Island Mount Range Hood - 450 CFM

product_title: GE PV977NSS Profile 36" Stainless Steel Chimney Style Island Mount Range Hood - 450 CFM
review_title: Very nice range hood.  Works great.  Dependable.
review_text: I have had this range hood for five or more years.  It is on an average of two hours a day.  It has performed quite well, only a few light bulbs have burned out which is normal and they are easy to change. This unit moves a lot of air and that is what I bought for.  As far as noise, it produces quite a bit of noise on high speed but I seldom ever run it on high unless I am cooking something that produces a LOT of smoke.  I use the third speed out of five to fry a 1/2 pound of bacon or potatoes with onions.  The controls work great, the lighting is great and the quality of the stainless steel is better than many others I looked at that was very thin.  For things I don't fry I use speed one or two and it is pretty quiet.  Any range hood that is built with integrated fans (built into the range hood) will make a lot of noise when moving this much air.  If you want a quiet hood then look at a model that had the fan blowers on the roof.  This is a quality unit and must be vented outside.  I installed it by myself without any other help without much hassle in one day, but I am pretty handy and can do electrical, venting, most construction, remodeling and roofing work myself.  I can fry bacon, sausage or hamburgers and not smell it in the rest of the house and my kitchen stays such cleaner.

product_title: Whirlpool GB9FHDXWQ Gold 18.5 Cu. Ft. White Bottom Freezer Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_text: I got this refrigerator to replace a 17-cu-ft one that died on me.  I bought it off the net, and if I had had a chance to see it in person first I probably wouldn't have--the old, top-freezer refrigerator had much more freezer space.  The wire shelves take up way too much room, as does the ice container.  Good refrigerator otherwise, I like the additional room in the top half, but the freezer is definitely a disappointment.

product_title: Whirlpool GB9FHDXWQ Gold 18.5 Cu. Ft. White Bottom Freezer Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_text: We bought this refrigerator online and have been pleasantly surprised. The freezer is a bit smaller than our previous unit but very similar to all the other models and brands we looked at in this size, capacity and design.

product_title: Whirlpool GB9FHDXWQ Gold 18.5 Cu. Ft. White Bottom Freezer Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_text: My compressor broke in less than 3 months of regular use. They sent A&E to check it out. The techniican didn't even file a report and lied to me about what was wrong with the fridge. product_title: Whirlpool GB9FHDXWQ Gold 18.5 Cu. Ft. White Bottom Freezer Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_text: This refrig was 9 months old when it quit cooling. The frige ran and never shut off. Called Whrilpool and they first said a week before a repair person could come but they found another authorized repairer who could come the next day. I was surprized to learn Whrilpool seems to have only 2 repair facilities to cover Long Island. First tech said it was out of freon but was learning and did know how to recharge. Whrilpool shipped the compressor to my house overnight Fed Ex arriving Friday mid day, after I talked to a supervisor. Soonest the tech could come was Wed. of following week. product_title: Whirlpool GB9FHDXWQ Gold 18.5 Cu. Ft. White Bottom Freezer Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_text:
17 months old and there was ice forming on the freezer floor and water leaking onto the kitchen floor. Even though it was a holiday weekend I was given a service appointment for the next day, a Saturday. $208 later, I was encouraged to buy a 3 yr service contract for $200. 6 days later the freezer worked fine but the refrigerator wasn't keeping cold. Nothing helped: turning the temp control all the way up and turning the fridge off and on again got no results. I felt angry that I'd obviously bought a bad fridge, but pleased that I purchased a 3 yr service agreement. Until I called for service. When I was told the next available appointment was 18 days away I hung up in disbelief, called back from a different phone and said I didn't have a service agreement. I was given the next available appointment which was in two days. During that time the refrigerator randomly started working again.

The repairman called to say he was on his way. He said the charge for his visit would be a minimum of $100. When I told him I had a service agreement, he said he'd call me back. He didn't. I called him back - twice (caller ID is so handy). He finally arrived end of day, took the temp in the freezer and in the fridge and told me everything's fine. When I told him the refrigerator had stopped working for over 48 hours causing the temp to rise to 62 degrees, he told me next time it happens to just reboot by turning the circuit breaker off and back on. Like a computer. A computer? Really? I don't keep all my food and my prescription medication in my computer. And while having to reboot my computer might be annoying, it won't make me physically ill.

Whirlpool is not at all interested in me or my Whirlpool refrigerator's problems. Customer service told me to call their authorized service repair company and then asked me, "Is there anything else we can help you with today?" When I told them about the fraudulent behavior their authorized service repair company engages in, they said they were sorry to hear about that but they couldn't help me.

product_title: LG : LMX28987ST 27.5 cu. ft. French Door Refrigerator - Stainless Steel
review_text: My wife and I bought this refrigerator for our new home.  I am usually a big fan of LG products because of their focus on making them user friendly with some well-thought-out features.  However, this product has been a disappointment.  Less than 2 months after our purchase we had to have the computer control board replaced.  The ice maker frequently gets jammmed with refrozen ice cubes because of the design of the outlet which allows ice cubes to thaw and then refreeze at the outlet.  In addition, the top freezer drawer gets ice build-up that makes the drawer hard to open.  I thought defrosting freezers was something that was in the past!  To top it off, we have already had one of the door racks break.  This unit is far too expensive to have this many strikes against it!

product_title: LG : LMX28987ST 27.5 cu. ft. French Door Refrigerator - Stainless Steel
review_text:
We have had this in our home for a while now, and so far so good. Plenty of storage space, and uniform temperatures throughout. No cold spots or hot spots that I can find. It has a lot of well-designed shelf space, but the ice maker does consume the entire left side, except for small shelf suitable for a couple water bottles or something.

The ice maker and water dispenser is HUGE. I love being able to fill up an entire pitcher, or those big 48oz mugs without tilting them. We have not had any problems with the ice dispenser jamming up, and it holds a surprising amount of ice. The water filter lasts six months and has a nice visual indicator of the time remaining right on the front. There is also a handy control panel lock feature, which prevents any of the settings from being changed, and any features from being operated- including the ice maker and water dispenser. This is great when you are cleaning or if you have small kids in the house.

The automatic freezer drawers are fantastic. You can either press the buttons to open and close them, or push/pull them yourself and it will sort of "help you". There are a lot of nice touches like the dimming LED lighting, which really lights up the interior nicely. It's also very quiet. We really love this model so far, in every way. If it breaks I'll come back and post an update.

product_title: LG : LMX28987ST 27.5 cu. ft. French Door Refrigerator - Stainless Steel
review_title: Horrible refrigerators and horrible customers service
review_text: First month water filter cover broke.  slowly over the next year shelf brackets have broken and shelves have cracked.  I am 49 years old and have owened many refrigerators and have never had any of them break EVER until now.  Replacement parts would cost 150.00 and I refuse to put that back into a piece of junk.

product_title: LG : LMX28987ST 27.5 cu. ft. French Door Refrigerator - Stainless Steel
review_text: I waited several years before upgrading to a modern refrigerator and didn't mind spending some money for a better looking unit, and features that promised to make life nicer. Although this unit looks great and has some luxury features (the LED inside light is cool, moveable shelves), overall it is disappointing. The ice maker frequently gets jammmed at least twice a week with refrozen ice cubes and requires complete emptying to rebuild the supply with usable cubes. The bottom 2 freezer drawers are much less overall real estate space compared to my older, lower cu. ft. side by side unit from 15 yrs ago. Also, have 2 drawers means shorter space and having to shove stuff down to make room.. . . and I do not freeze ahead or freeze leftovers although I would love to. I am online today to purchase a 2nd freezer for needed space (or replace this unit all together).  If you don't use the unit or if it is in something like a vacation home, it's great. Otherwise, look elsewhere.

product_title: LG : LMX28987ST 27.5 cu. ft. French Door Refrigerator - Stainless Steel
review_title: Beware of LG's Lack of Customer Service!
review_text:
This comment is about LG's poor customer service and the unprofessional attitude of their management. We recently purchased a new LG stainless steel french door refrigerator, model LFX28978ST (the single freezer drawer model). We found our best deal at Home Depot and they delivered it promptly. It came well packed with blue plastic covering all of the stainless surfaces for protection. We inspected the unit to make sure it was in good shape, but left the plastic in place. We had to complete installing our new kitchen floor before installing our new LG, so we had the delivery folks set the unit out of the traffic pattern where it remained untouched for 9 days.

Once the flooring was finished, we installed the refrigerator into a custom cabinet where it fit perfectly. Once in place and connected to water and power, we removed the plastic on the doors as it cooled down so we could start putting things into it. It was after removing the plastic that we noticed a slight but very sharp diagonal dent about 8 inches long on the lower freezer drawer. Since we watched the unpacking and moving of the unit into our home the week before, this dent clearly occurred at the factory. We immediately called Home Depot, and they asked that we call LG since the unit is new.

We called LG, and to make a long story short, they said they would not do anything. Their position was that we have only 7 days (this was day 9) to report any damage. There is nothing on any paperwork that says this, but they said that this is their policy. We asked to speak with a manager, who said the same thing and added "let the buyer beware." This conversation lasted probably 15 minutes, but to no avail.

We then contacted Home Depot again, and they said they would take care of it for us. Home Depot is great! In fact, they were willing to replace the entire refrigerator. Since it was already installed, we agreed it would be far easier just to replace the drawer front. So, the manager of the appliance department came to our home personally with a replacement drawer front and replaced it for us.

While the story ends well and the refrigerator has been in use for several weeks now and we love it, had we known that LG was the kind of company that has no interest in customer service and their management has the guts to say "let the buyer beware" instead of resolving a problem, we would probably have purchased another brand. For those of you thinking about LG, think twice. And if you do purchase one, you may want to think about a warranty from an independent company, as you may otherwise have to experience LG's lack of customer service!

product_title: LG : LMX28987ST 27.5 cu. ft. French Door Refrigerator - Stainless Steel
