product_title: Frigidaire Affinity: FAQE7077KA 27'' Electric Dryer with 7.0 cu. ft. Capacity, 7 Drying Cycles, Auto/Timed Dry Cyles, 12 Options, Moisture Sensor, Drying Rack, Stainless Steel Drum and NSF Certified: Classic Silver (Coming Sep 1st, 09 )
review_title: If I could give it ZERO stars, I would!
review_text:
Let me start by saying that because of my experience, I will never again buy ANYTHING with the Frigidaire or Electrolux name attached to it. NEVER. I bought my dryer a couple of years ago, and thought that only a one year warranty was a little shoddy, but never did I expect that the control panels in these dryers are like self-destructing "screw the customer" systems! The dryer started beeping one day while not even turned on, and displaying error code E68, the code for a stuck button. There are no buttons stuck, and upon researching it a bit, I found hundreds of other people online with the same exact problem. The control panel shorts out after 2-3 years and will cause the dryer to think a button is being held down and won't run. Nothing is wrong with the mechanics, it's all just this stupid electronic panel. As I, and the hundreds of other people with these dryers, have found out, Frigidaire absolutely refuses to replace the faulty control panel unless you pay ~$200.00 plus the cost of a service person to come put it in if you don't know how to do it yourself!

They KNOW that they are selling dryers with defective control panels, yet hide behind their wimpy one year warranty as a way to milk a ton of extra cash out of their customers. Where is the recall, Frigidaire??? Hopefully the Better Business Bureau will care to urge them toward resolving this. In the meantime, I recommend that you DO NOT BUY THIS DRYER, OR ANY OTHER FRIGIDAIRE PRODUCT! THEY ARE SCAM ARTISTS!!!

product_title: Haier RRTG21PABB 20.7 Cubic Feet Top Mount Refrigerator, Black

product_title: Bosch : SHE55M15UC 24 Evolution 500 Series Full Console Dishwasher - Stainless Steel
review_text:
First wash with brand-new Bosch SHE55M dishwasher after installation disclosed a leak in door seal. Entire structure is very light, thin and flimsy. Seems the stainless lining easily distorts, being about as thin as a razor blade, but not as hard or springy. Door and cabinet are very flexible, which may be thesource of the ill-fitting seal.

This was touted as a very quiet unit, but we find it shrill. We can hear it from outdoors, through the closed kitchen storm door, 14 feet away.

product_title: Bosch : SHE55M15UC 24 Evolution 500 Series Full Console Dishwasher - Stainless Steel
review_text:
Agree with other reviewers; flimsy construction.

My issue was the top faceplate. It is used, with a cutout in the middle, to open the door. After it pulled away from the frame spewing the control buttons all over the floor, I could see that it is actually plastic. It is held on, if that's the word, with plastic tabs that click into slots in the frame of the washer.

The tabs can not handle the repeated opening of the door. (Gee-whiz, why would a customer expect THAT Bosch?)

The tabs WILL break in time. Mine occurred just after the warranty expired.

ALL of the Bosch Evolution Dishwashers are like this. Flimsy construction obviously driven by cost constrained MBAs.

As always YOU the Customer are the Test Lab.

product_title: Bosch : SHE55M15UC 24 Evolution 500 Series Full Console Dishwasher - Stainless Steel
review_text:
I bought this model to replace a prior bosch dishwasher that lasted 13 years of everyday use. This model does everything my last model did and more. I rarely do any pre-wash on the dishes and I have yet to have one come out dirty (same with my last bosch). To say this is quiet is an understatement. If there is any other noise in the room like a refrigerator or talking you will not hear this unit run (be sure to install the two bottom covers along with the noise insulation thats provided). Its very quiet. Lots of adjustments in the rack as well as height and many wash options. The front controls are a big plus and something I was looking for rather than the hidden. Most of the time I use the quick wash (approx 30 mins) and that is all thats needed. Plastics don't dry but that was the case with my old unit as well, everything else dries fine though. This was also the #1 ranked unit in CR beating out some much more expensive models. I am quite shocked by the poor reviews here as virtually every review on other sites are excellent. Not sure whats up with that but mine has performed exactly as I expected. If something changes I always update reviews and will answer any questions if someone adds a comment that needs a response.

One of the other reviewers stated the bottom rack will not hold heavy dishes. Makes me wonder if they have their models mixed up. The bottom rack actually does not have rails but rides atop molded runners pressed into the stainless steel sides. I am not sure what kind of weight it would take to have the rack come off but surely the rack would bend before the sides give out. I can push down on it will a lot of force and its solid. I would think you could safely load 50 pounds of weight in the lower rack without any issues at all.

Update 5/23/2012

I am close to a year owning this and have had no issues. Still quiet and cleans like it did on the first wash. Use it 3 to 4 times a week. I use the powerball tablets as suggested in the manual. No negatives to report.

Update 3/16/2013

Still running like new. No issues !

Update 12/5/2013

Still going strong. No problems or issues.

product_title: Bosch : SHE55M15UC 24 Evolution 500 Series Full Console Dishwasher - Stainless Steel
review_text: OK I've read the other reviews and they are inaccurate, I have owned this dishwasher since 2009 and we use it if not every day, every other day. It is the quietest dishwasher you will own. It cleans well, if you have hardwater and no softner you will need to clean it monthly (any dishwasher cleaner sold in the grocery store does just fine). I have NEVER had a repair problem, my biggest complaint is with loading the bottom rack, if the weight is not balanced you will have a hard time sliding it in and out, which sometimes get frustrating. Compared to others in this price range I would recommend it.

product_title: Bosch : SHE55M15UC 24 Evolution 500 Series Full Console Dishwasher - Stainless Steel
review_title: Very Clean, Very Quiet, Very Happy
review_text:
Installed myself. You will need a strain relief and power cord, and possibly an adapter to connect to your garbage disposal or pipe. The drain hose supplied fits up to 3/4". I needed 1". A $5 dishwasher drain hose adapter and a $1 3/4" galvanized steel pipe nipple solved that problem.

This thing is unbelievably quiet compared to our 8 year old previous 'quiet' model. You can easily carry on a conversation next to it. We have an open kitchen / living area that used to require turning up the television volume when the previous dishwasher ran...No More!

Dishes come out very clean. As others have said elsewhere, I think the Finish Quantum Powerball (sample provided) or another highly rated CR brand will make a huge difference in your results too.

The passive drying works extremely well. We will only have a few drops of water left on plastic.

I have seen the Sanitize light come on. It means that very specific conditions (time, etc as specified by the NSF) were achieved during the wash and dry. Note that the Sanitize light won't come on until the Drying cycle is complete, which is well after the Cycle countdown has reached '0'.

product_title: Bosch : SHE55M15UC 24 Evolution 500 Series Full Console Dishwasher - Stainless Steel
review_text: We have an older model similar to this and after 4 years, the handle is cracking and it's only a matter of time before it completely breaks. I called Bosch to ask about this and the guy I talked to admitted that there was a problem there but would not do anything about it. The replacement part costs $74 and obviously it would cost far more than that to have it serviced. I would look carefully at the handle design to see if the current models are made stronger before buying another Bosch dishwasher with the same type of handle design.

product_title: Bosch : SHE55M15UC 24 Evolution 500 Series Full Console Dishwasher - Stainless Steel
review_text:
This is an exceptional unit. I have had KitchenAid, Bosch and Maytag dishwashers previously, and each successive unit seemed more quiet than the one before. This unit replaced a Maytag that just didn't clean well anymore after about 8 years of operation.

I was a little concerned about this unit not being a self cleaner as I didn't want food recycling back onto the dishes -- a problem I have had in the past.

So here is the scoop.

1. The unit installs easily. Be careful with the door top though on installation as that can get scratched if you need to "jimmy" the unit in (sometimes if you have hardwood floors that don't go all the way into the dishwasher bay this can be tricky).
2. This dishwasher cleans as advertised. It washes dishes without pre-rinsing, and ones that have one day dried food also. It is a superior washer.
3. This dishwasher is quiet. Wow, is it quiet. Of all the units I have had it is probably half as loud. I have always aimed for good quality units, so the others were not bad. This unit makes less noise than the 2 fish tanks I have in my kitchen dining area. It is that quiet. Great job Bosch.
4. OTHER: The unit has LESS water wands than previous generations of dishwashers. My Maytag had 4 wands. This unit has 3 (well 2 wands, and a sprayer assembly on the very top). I suspect they use less for higher pressure. Whatever it is, this dishwasher cleans. It works! Great job Bosch.
5. OTHER: The food waste filter has not been an issue. Most little food scraps are getting cleared from the washer. Also, the filter is not getting grimed with grease as I had experienced with a previous unit.
5. Negative: not a biggie, but the wine glass holding facility is a bit weak -- you need to be careful opening the upper tray if you have wine glasses, or they will move and potentially break (yeah, I broke one).
6. Negative: you do have some flexibility in installing the unit on how far "out" the door protrudes. If you install it protruding too much, then watch out if you use the counter top above the dishwasher as you may rub up against the on button. If this happens, you will need to adjust the unit farther in.

Overall, I highly recommend this dishwasher. It cleans and it is quiet. It looks very sharp in stainless steel. And you don't need to wash your dishes beforehand in order for it to work!

product_title: Bosch : SHE55M15UC 24 Evolution 500 Series Full Console Dishwasher - Stainless Steel
review_title: Extremely Quiet, Washes Well. Capacity and Price May Be Factors.
review_text:
We've had this dishwasher just over a year, and I'm writing this review now because we finally figured out how to get it to dry dishes once washed.

First, it replaced an excellent LG (which we gave to our kids) because the LG was white and there seems to be some sort of law that you can't have a white dishwasher with a stainless steel refrigerator or range. The LG was the quietest dishwasher we'd ever had, often having to check it to make sure we'd turned it on. Well, this Bosch is comparable. It is extremely quiet in all but the "drain cycle." That's to be expected, and even that is quiet, well, as quiet as the LG and quieter than out old old GE.

We required the buttons be on the outside of the door, NOT on top so that they disappear when the door is closed. Believe it or not, this cut our choices in half. Another issue was the handle. In a galley kitchen (or not), we would not have a dishwasher with a handle that sticks out - even if you could have another dish towel hanging. We definitely wanted flush "handles" which, btw, is how we ended up with the Bosch counter-depth (flush) refrigerator.

The capacity is good, not great, one reason why I can only give it four stars. People talk about "holding place settings for 6," but they never mention what happens to those place settings when you add a pot or pan or a broiling rack or pan! But we're only two people and on a daily basis, this more than meets our needs.

Drying: Ah, drying. This has been a problem with many of our dishwashers. We've tried all the products for drying from Jet-Dry to a "cake" that was made to fit in the dispenser. We washed the dishes after dinner and let it go through the cycles and left the dishes and pots and pans to dry overnight. In the morning, there would still be spots that were wet though the dishes were dry and squeaky clean. Basically, we were running into the age-old problem on the lips of pots and the tops of cups filling with too much water for the machine to dry. Cups we dealt with by lying them on their sides, and that really worked. Pots or pans with lips we loaded on top when possible, and they were the first things we took out in the morning, and hand wipes the lips. And now - so we added 60 seconds to the unloading routine - all is well.

In the old days, dishwashers had a heating element in the bottom and did a better job of drying. But in the old days, you couldn't have a conversation in the same room as the dishwasher, they were so noisy. You learn to live with these things.

Washing, this gets 5 stars. Quiet, this gets 5 stars. Reliability, 5 stars. (Never a problem or repair.) Capacity and price ratio, four stars. Would we get another? Probably.

product_title: Bosch : SHE55M15UC 24 Evolution 500 Series Full Console Dishwasher - Stainless Steel
review_title: Cleans Well and So Quiet I Question if it's Running....
review_text:
I'll update this over the next few months, but after the first two weeks of using this Bosch my wife and I are nothing but pleased.

We have three boys who eat a lot and subsequently we run the dishwasher one or two times a day. The first time I ran this, I couldn't hear it at all and had to put my hand on it to verify it was running. Also opened it to make sure - water was dripping as typical when you open a washer mid-cycle. If it's quiet in the house, you can hear it running but barely. You can also hear when the washer is purging water before and after the rinse cycles through the drain but that's not bad either. But if you have the TV on or have kids in the house, you generally can't hear it at all.

But if it's quiet but doesn't clean, what's the point? We've had no issues with cleaning due to the washer. We have hard water in our area and the only issue we had some problems with spotting, etc. was when we didn't have the rinse agent in with standard detergent or using our usual special detergent. That was the same with any of the washers we or our friends have or have had.

Both the top and bottom baskets have lots of slots for things and at least 50% of them will fold down to accommodate whatever you are trying to wash.

Also, there's a timer to let you know how long the wash cycle has left. Not essential but nice.

Only issue we've had in two weeks is the door is extremely heavy (I believe a spring loose or missing). It has slipped or people new to using it have just let it drop. It goes fast enough I have worried about our dog. With the repeated drops the door has gone past horizontal. I scheduled a tech repair today and will update this once we see what normal should be.

But again, no issues with cleaning or sound. Both have been great for the first two weeks of use. You'd hope that'd be the case. Will update after we get the door squared away and again at the six-month mark.

--------------update on door-----------------
The door issue was as the comment from Lynn said - contractor screws that were too long. After the fix by Bosch (who's repairman said this was fairly common for appliances installed by contractors), the door is back to out-of-the-box condition.

New observations:
-the insulation on this thing is amazing. If the cycle is done running even two hours previous, the dishes and air inside is still really warm. I'm guessing once hot water goes in, it stays hot.

-drying dishes can be an issue if you run out of rinse agent or seem to run it on Auto Wash vs. Regular Wash. I'm going to keep a better eye on this as well.

-if you have any back issues, the bottom rack is extremely low to the floor. Likewise since the controls are on the door, there's more room in the top of the washer too. Again, lots of room for almost anything you could stick in it.

Again, overall satisfaction is high. We'll see where we're at in two more months.

product_title: Bosch : SHE55M15UC 24 Evolution 500 Series Full Console Dishwasher - Stainless Steel
review_title: SHE55M15U Dishwasher - Awesome after test driving
review_text: After much research, yes reading the GOOD and the BAD, we bought this dishwasher. Visually we're not happy: our old dishwasher, a GE, filled the entire space. The Bosch has a 1/2" gap all around the opening. However, it is sealed with a gasket that encloses the space. The interior is smaller than most dishwashers we looked at but the ability to configure the interior is what sold us. With the exception of two short rows of tines in the top and bottom racks all others fold "FLAT". This has given us the ability to wash pots, pans, large or oddly shaped pieces easily. The size has not been an issue. When we have parties we generally wash more than one load of dishes and this is no different. It took some time and frustration to learn how to load the dishwasher. Referring to the manual, with it's loading diagrams, solved the problem.....should have done this first. Our dishes come out literally sparkling. The dishwasher is so quiet I have walked over to check and make sure it was running. Unless you're standing right in front of the dishwasher you cannot hear it. There have been comments about dishes coming out wet which we experienced at first. However, again after reading the manual and loading the dishes properly solved this problem. It's the tilt at which you place items that makes the difference. Comments have also been made about the long run times but in our research they're not much different than any other dishwasher. Also we run it when we go to bed so the running time is not an issue. It took a few tries at loading, as I mentioned read the manual it's a big help, and I can say we're happy to have made this purchase.  NOTE: do not open the dishwasher to unload until the timer goes to 0 otherwise you will break the door seal and the dishes will not have dried properly. This could be another reason there have been comments about wet dishes.

product_title: Bosch : SHE55M15UC 24 Evolution 500 Series Full Console Dishwasher - Stainless Steel
review_title: Problems and Bosch doesn't stand behind their product
review_text:
We did a lot of research 15 months ago and selected this Bosch dishwasher. Consumer reports rated it high and the key drawbacks we saw were the smaller interior size compared to our previous dishwashers and the lack of a food "disposal" system. Many of the high efficiency washers have a filter basket that has to be removed periodically and cleaned out. That is the case with this one.

Shortly after our first use with the dishwasher we were smelling a lingering egg smell on the glassware. At first it was lingering and then it became strong and gross - like rotten eggs. We called Bosch. They told us to change detergents. Same problem. Talked to Bosch - they said we needed to turn our water heater temp up. Same problem. Talked to Bosch - we needed to remount the drain hose an extra 6 inches higher than the instructions stated. Same problem. Talked to Bosch - we should rinse our dishes better (what?!!). Same problem. Talked to Bosch - our water must be too hard... Huh? We never had that problem before. Same problem. Bosch said we cook with too much oil. $%@$^@$%@$???? Every time we called to get help they told us some other goofy thing to blame something other than their dishwasher. The one solution we found was to put white vinegar in the washer when it was in the middle of the cycle - that made things liveable. We would go through a gallon of white vinegar every two weeks.

Something we saw all the time was a gross, gooey sludge developed on the filter and the water that was left in the bottom of the dishwasher was dirty (high efficiency units leave a little water in the bottom under the cover). I would clean gooey yellow-orange-brown-sludge-butter-muck off the filter 3 times each week. Gross. No wonder the dishes smelled.

About 6 months into the ordeal (mind you, we are eating on dishes that smell awful but appear clean) we call Bosch and tell them we have had it and we request that they replace the dishwasher. We have a one year warranty, right, and clearly there is some type of defect with this dishwasher. What did Bosch say? "Oh, I am sorry to hear of your problem, but we don't have any record of you having any concerns with this dishwasher." What?!!! All the calls from our home, that they logged our home number with and provided us a log number - yet none of that was in their system. So what now? We need to start a process with a service call to get things in order. Great! In my mind, another delay tactic.

First service call: The repair man finds no problems - mechanically everything works (yep, we know). It took us 2 months to convince the service person there was a problem. At 10 months we were getting concerned that we were going to be stuck with this awful dishwasher so we called the reputable dealer where we purchased it. They told us "good luck, Bosch will never replace it." They were nice about it, but it was clear that others have had issues with Bosch and the company doesn't take care of their appliances under warranty.

The good news - we did buy an extended warranty at the time of purchase. On the day the extended warranty kicked in we started a 3 month process to show the dishwasher was defective/unfixable. The repairman was helpful and within 3 visits noted that the unit was unrepairable. We received a check to replace the unit. We purchased and installed an LG dishwasher and all is well. Smell is gone, dishes are clean. The dishwasher has more space and has a soft food disposer (no more filter cleaning). Turns out it wasn't my water heater or hard water or too much oil or too little rinsing or the detergent.... All that stuff is the same and the LG cleans well and doesn't leave a rotten egg smell on the dishes.

The reason I bought the LG washer was I read a review where a guy talked about researching appliance companies from the standpoint of how they treat their customers after the sale. His research showed that LG treats their product owners great. I researched the LG web site and found a lot of great resources and confirmed several of the points this gentlemen made. Then I contrasted that to the ridiculous way Bosch treated my family and me.

In a nutshell - the Bosch dishwasher I purchased was defective and the bigger issue was Bosch as a company treated me and my family horribly as we were trying to fix and resolve the problem. My experience causes me to stay well clear of Bosch appliances.

product_title: Bosch : SHE55M15UC 24 Evolution 500 Series Full Console Dishwasher - Stainless Steel

product_title: Bosch : SHE55M15UC 24 Evolution 500 Series Full Console Dishwasher - Stainless Steel
review_title: DON'T EVEN CONSIDER THIS PIECE OF EUROTRASH
review_text:
We made this unfortunate purchase 14 months ago, after searching through the Consumer Reports ratings and evaluations. They (CR) gave this dishwasher rave reviews for function, quietness, reliability and energy conservation. They downplayed the smaller interior as "insignificantly smaller". That all sounded good, so in spite of the grotesque price, we figured that it would amortize over a longer life, and heck, who doesn't want to save energy when it is feasible.

The ONLY positive thing I can say about this POC is that it IS quiet.

The interior layout is so goofy that it is virtually impossible to put a reasonable load of dishes into the baskets. The idiot that designed the interior must have been using doll-house dishes for sizing. It took two runs to process the same load of dishes that my previous Whirlpool would wash (CLEAN) and dry (DRY and SPOTLESS) in a single run. And it required 134 minutes to process one load.

And you have to keep feeding it this expensive Jet Dry rinse agent, or else you get a soapy film on the dishes, complete with a soapy taste as well. And the dishes are NEVER dry when the cycle is done.

There are options for shorter cycles. Because we pre-rinse our dishes, the short wash cycle got the dishes adequately clean (but not as clean as the longer cycle). The problem is that at the end of the short cycle, the dishes are soaking wet, and if you let them dry in the dishwasher by evaporation, they end up horribly spotted.

The alleged "automatic cleanliness detector" detected NOTHING; there was no difference. The "detector" cycle also ran the full 134 minutes. And all of that in spite of the fact that I have the hot water which feeds the dishwasher set at 150°.

So I wish some energy wizard would explain to me how it is saving energy to require twice as many cycles, each of which is longer than my Whirlpool, to do a given load of dishes and cookware, and not do them as well as the Whirlpool, with the additional requirement of frequently adding some energy-intensive chemical to the machine.

Based on the horrible experiences other owners have reported with respect to Bosch warranty support and repair service, I can say I am very thankful that this thing managed not to break in the 14 months we used it.

Bottom line, I hated the machine to the point I just would not use it often, and when my wife asked me PLEASE, for Christmas, PLEASE get rid of this thing, I understood and sympathized completely. So Dec. 23, while she was out shopping for Christmas dinner prep, I tore out this eurocrap tragedy and installed a new Whirlpool, which although it is NOT as quiet, it does its job remarkably well, and at roughly half the price.

Suffice it to say that she was EXTREMELY pleased.

product_title: Bosch : SHE55M15UC 24 Evolution 500 Series Full Console Dishwasher - Stainless Steel
review_title: Plastic Facia is used for handle; breaks quickly
review_text:
The design on our model is just plain stupid. The latch is designed to be tight, but their is no latch release mechanism. The designed way to open the latch is to pull hard. How hard? According to my fish scale, it takes 23 pounds (!) of pull to open the door.

On top of that, the handle on which you're pulling is held on by two plastic tabs which are each 1 inch wide and no more than 1/16th of an inch thick. They're bound to break, and when they do, all of the buttons (which are only held in by the facia) fall out.

So of course we're just barely out of warranty, but after I explain the major design flaw (and learn that they've apparently changed the latch part for that model since then), they offer to replace the handle only, not the latch which might prevent the problem from recurring.

To make things worse, they agree its a problem and agree to cover only the parts. That's fine because it would take me 10 minutes to change it (I've already had to disassemble and reassemble twice -- once to diagnose and try to reglue and once to take pictures to send to customer service agent) as opposed to all the time involved in waiting for a repairman. BUT WAIT, they'll only pay for the parts if I pay to have them installed by an authorized service provider. Yes, they'll send me the $45 part if I pay $85+ to have it installed.

review_text:

product_title: Bosch : WTVC3500UC 27 Vision 300 Series Gas Dryer - White
review_text:
Hooray!!! A dryer at last!

What I like:
*The inside is nice, high quality stainless steel.
*When I use the timed standard cycle, the towels are dry and fluffy.
*The window allows my kitty to watch the spinning textiles.
*The interior light illuminates beautifully when you open the door and goes off a few seconds after you close the door. This is so nice. No sock is left behind!
*The large interior allows me to easily dry quilts, blankets and bedspreads.

What I don't like:
*The end cycle signal is SOOOO annoying!!!! When your dryer finishes it will beep, loudly
beep beep....beep beeep...
beep beep....beeep beeep

and then after a few minutes the drum is activated and starts your load tossing about for 20-30 seconds then stops and begins the whole annoying beeping sequence again...this goes on until you turn the bloody thing off.

I miss the old dryer system model that defaulted to 'off' at the end of a drying cycle, buzzed once and was done with it.

If you put a load of laundry in your dryer, right before bedtime...unless you are deaf or sleep with earplugs or have your laundry in the west wing of your large castle, you will be compelled to get up and silence that beeping beast!

*Lint filter sensitivity: the dryer will stop and start beeping at you midcycle until you check and empty the lint filter (which sometimes has hardly any lint in it). This is annoying. Again, I miss the old 70's dryers that just ran and ran until their cycle ended, regardless of their full, half full, or near empty filter.

*The moisture sensor cycles are another waste of energy in my opinion. I do not use this feature unless I want my laundry to be slightly damp at the conclusion of the drying cycle.

The moisture sensor cycles also beep beep in the noisy end of cycle pattern mentioned earlier. This hardly conserves energy in my opinion. It seems like they could have left this end of cycle siren and spin feature out of the schematic.

Overall I am happy.

but:
It would be nice if we had an easy to access dial to adjust the loudness of the system signal.
I also wish we could push a button to turn on/off the moistere and lint sensor settings. This would keep our machine spinning regardless of the faulty sensors.

Alas, No more hanging towels like Wilma Flintstone, to dry over the tar pits!!! I like this dryer much more than the clothes line!

product_title: Bosch : WTVC3500UC 27 Vision 300 Series Gas Dryer - White
review_title: I agree with prior review on many points as well; overall very happy
review_text:
I purchased this dryer (along with the matching 300 vision series washer) two weeks ago at PC Richard's for $699 (free delivery) and am so far very happy. It works well and like the previous reviewer, I don't use all the different settings (the later model series like the 500 and 800 have even more settings, like steam cleaning, wrinkle reduction which adds a few shots of steam to the dryer etc.)...I just want my clothes dried quickly and without scorching them.
And this machine does what it says. I fill the dryer up about half full and the load dries in 30 minutes; clothes are nice and warm when they come out, not scorching hot, and they are dry but not wrinkled.

(Note to the previous reviewer (Davina), the 300 series dryer should let you turn off the annoying beeping alarm by depressing the two top buttons (the Econo-dry button and the other button right next to it) at the same time).

I have to agree with Davina that the lint screen is WAY too sensitive. The beep went off twice the first time I used the dryer (I had it set at cotton/regular dry) and it stopped the dryer until I pulled out the lint screen to clean it (I admit, the first time it went off, there was lint in the screen, but it went off again 10 minutes later with no lint). The folks at Bosch recommend that you don't use dryer sheets (which I wasn't) because the residue sometimes sticks to the sensor and that you makes sure the lint screen holder is free of dirt before you run the dryer. I haven't used the dryer enough to see if my "cleaning" the lint screen holder (by blowing in it) fixed this problem or not, but I did about 5 loads and it lint alarm hadn't gone off again (granted, for the first load, I set the dryer on the dampness-sensor settings; for the last four loads I simply set it up to dry for 40 minutes and the lint alarm didn't go off. That's fine for me.

So overall, I'm really happy with the dryer. It dries quickly and efficiently (by the way, my old dryer was electric and it ATE electricity; I'm looking forward to getting my next ConEd bill to see how much money I'm saving on this gas dryer).

product_title: Bosch : WTVC3500UC 27 Vision 300 Series Gas Dryer - White
review_text: This is the most annoying dyer I've ever owned. The obnoxiously loud beeping every few minutes when the clothes is dry is only the beginning of the problems (at least you can shut that off!). The ONLY setting on the dryer that is not high heat is the PermPress setting. And the sensor is set very wrong on that setting. It never ever dries anything on the first run. I've had to run it at least twice (and sometimes 3-4 times) to get it to dry my clothes. It is extremely annoying when you're doing several loads of laundry in one day. I know that it is not a matter of the sensor being gunky, I don't use dryer sheets and the sensor works fine on the cotton/high heat setting.  Now, to top the list of annoying things...after only 18 months the thermostat has blown out. I dried a load of towels last night and the entire machine and the load of towels became extremely hot and it smelled like burning electrical parts. Now today it runs but does not heat. From what I understand, Bosch only stands behind their products for 1 year so it looks like we'll either be paying a big fix it bill or getting a new dryer. Don't waste your money. You will hate this dryer and equally awful matching washer. Never buying their inferior products again!

product_title: Bosch : WTVC3500UC 27 Vision 300 Series Gas Dryer - White
review_text:
This is the most expensive gas dryer I have ever owned and possibly the worst. After only 5 years it is so noisy I hate to start it.
I took the back off to look for loose screws and it got a little better, but now gas won't ignite. Guess I'm taking it apart again tomorrow. I've had way better gas dryers at half the price but I guess nothing is made to last anymore, so you are better off with a cheaper model. The wrinkle block feature is annoying because you can't disable the function, so it wastes electricity. Annoying buzzer other people are complaining about is no big deal as you can turn it off. Just read the owners manual. Push both eco action and delicates buttons at the same time to enable or disable.

product_title: Bosch NET5054UC500 30" Stainless Steel Electric Smoothtop Cooktop
review_text:
The cook top was recently installed so I haven't much experience with it, although I have cooked with electricity for years.
I think the bridge element is a great feature. The control panel does not seem to be as simple as it might be and is not bright enough to suit me, but hopefully, I will adjust to it after a few weeks. If I don't have problems with temperature control and if it is as easy to keep clean as it appears to be, I would say it is a good choice for the cost.

product_title: Bosch NET5054UC500 30" Stainless Steel Electric Smoothtop Cooktop
review_title: Well designed and easy to keep clean
review_text: The cooktop arrived quickly, installed easily,  and works well. The feature that sold it to me was the "no knobs" design. Our old unit was much more difficult to keep clean. Grease and food would collect around the control knobs which took much effort to clean. This unit is very easy to wipe down yet the control design precludes accidentally turning on the unit.  Having a metal strip along the edges lengthwise should help prevent chipping  the glass top by sliding pans along the edge. A small chip on our previous unit eventually cracked across our old cooktop necessitating replacement. Replacement of the glass only is not economically feasible nor done without risk.

product_title: Electrolux Icon E23BC78IPS Professional 22.6 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel Counter Depth French Door Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_text:
Very nice french door counter depth refrigerator. Well designed. First version of this model had issues with the ice maker, but the new models have redesigned icemakers and are generally quite good/reliable.

Well designed interior. Well lit. Quiet. French doors offer excellent access and utility. Freezer is good and spacious as the icemaker is located in the upper refrigerator portion (so as to allow thru-door water/ice). Touch panel are tasteful blue as are internal temp adjustments.

Overall, impressed with looks/design (nice beefy "pro style" handles). Only "problem" is these counter depth refrigerators are relatively pricey since relatively few are produced (although I can't stand refrigerators that project out into kitchen walk ways).

product_title: Electrolux Icon E23BC78IPS Professional 22.6 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel Counter Depth French Door Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_text: I agree with the only other reviewer, except it's not just the ice maker that has quality problems.  I bought this model in March 2011 and have had nothing but problems with it.  This model costs $500-800 more than comparable styles in other brands and so we (mistakenly) thought it would be better quality than the rest. Not true. The computer board went out within 8 months. The ice maker has never worked right - unless you think it's normal to depress the lever and obtain 1 cube every 20 seconds. The frozen goods are always covered in frost and don't last nearly as long as they did with our old refrigerator. Afer a half-dozen visits from the repairman, he admitted they've had lots of quality problems with them, particularly the early ones.  I have to give them credit on one point, because after the warranty ran out they did authorize one more repair - but I'm not holding my breath that anything will really be fixed.  Also, I'd never again choose the in-the-door ice maker because it takes up too much space in an already small interior.

product_title: Electrolux Icon E23BC78IPS Professional 22.6 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel Counter Depth French Door Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_text:
I seldomly write a review for a product; but I can't tolerate this any more.

I bought electrolux French door refrigerator 3 month ago and it started leaking after 1 month.

I called service guy to fix it and they told me that all electrolux refrigerator have same problem; meanwhile the service attitude is very bad and you have to wait several hours to get someone answer your phonecall.

After 5 time service visit ; they didn't come any more and let refrigerator leaking and ruin my wood floor.

This company is a complete liar and I threw $3000 into water.

product_title: Electrolux Icon E23BC78IPS Professional 22.6 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel Counter Depth French Door Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_text:
I purchased the top of the line Electrolux Refrigerator, along with other Electrolux products. If there is ever a lemon, this is it. The Refrigerator is the worse appliance purchase I have ever made. Since the beginning, leaks on the water dispenser went unresolved. Ice maker problems during the one year warranty were several and visits from the repairman and drawer alignment were some some of the initial problems. After the one year warranty was over I have paid hundreds to have repairmen come out and repair it, specifically the ice maker. The last visit they said there have been major problems with these and they could not repair it. The refrigerator is less than 3 years old, stainless steel and cost over $3,600. I have receipts and plenty of correspondences I can prove every word of this.
I only like providing positive feedback, but this is so egregious I had to write it. I wish I was warned.
I like many of you thought I would save and buy great Electrolux products that I heard growing up were great, upper scale products. I thought I could pay for these and justify the difference with years of problem free appliances, although I have not had any problems with any appliances. I was wrong and have contacted the company many times and that has proven worthless. They offered me another one for half price. Why would I want another of their lemons.
The Refrigerator was made in Mexico which demonstrates to me they are taking what I thought was a great name and sacrificing it for profit. If you buy, get extended warranties and read the fine print.
The rest of my Electrolux appliances were made in Canada and the U.S., I have had NO problems. I can only advise do not buy Electrolux Refrigerators and after talking to customer service I would recommend not purchasing Electrolux at all.

product_title: Electrolux Icon E23BC78IPS Professional 22.6 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel Counter Depth French Door Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_title: Don't waste your money on ANY Electrolux purchase
review_text: I purchased a Electrolux counter top flat top range, wall oven, wall microwave/convection oven, and fridge all five years ago.  The flat top has had service 5 times, the oven once, the microwave twice and the fridge once and all of them falling apart.  I paid A LOT of money for this kitchen remodel and I am so frustrated and dissapointed.  DO NOT waste your money buying "top of the line" you will be hightly dissapointed!!  The worst purchases I have EVER made in my life.

product_title: Electrolux Icon E23BC78IPS Professional 22.6 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel Counter Depth French Door Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_text: I've had this refrigerator for about 2 1/2 years now. In that time i've had 20 repair calls. We are now waiting on our 4th repair call for the same problem. It is always the ice maker. It dose not work and no one can fix it. It is a very nice looking appliance, but if you want a refrigerator that will make ice, and you should expect that at this price, I would not buy this one. If you do, buy the extended warranty and expect to spend a lot of time waiting for repair people.

product_title: Electrolux Icon E23BC78IPS Professional 22.6 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel Counter Depth French Door Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_title: Continuous Icemaker problems! Don't buy it!
review_text: My icemaker has been "fixed" 4 times, not working again. After a lengthy argument with Electrolux CS, they agreed to pay for the repair, if it is the same problem, but they cannot find anyone in my are who us willing to repair it. I live 1/2 hour from Seattle and 15 min from Everett. What does this say about Electrolux appliances? The appliance repair people are unwilling to fix it. Kelly Rippa stored me wrong!!

product_title: Electrolux Icon E23BC78IPS Professional 22.6 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel Counter Depth French Door Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_text:
Bought new refrigerator May 12, 2012

Original ice maker died Sept 2012
Replaced under warranty

Replacement ice maker #1 died Sept 26, 2013
Electrolux assisted me in getting the ice maker replaced.

Replacement ice maker #2 died Sept 16, 2014
Here we are... another dead ice maker in less than a year.

We'll see what happens. Three dead ice makers in a little over 2 years. Wow.

product_title: Electrolux Icon E23BC78IPS Professional 22.6 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel Counter Depth French Door Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_title: An awful product with terrible customer service
review_text: An awful product with terrible customer service. Our ice maker has never functioned properly to a point where its not repairable. This review doesn't even deserve 1 star.  After numerous repair visits, we have finally started a process for a new fridge, which is already a nightmare. Their customer service reps are robotic and unfriendly.  We will NEVER buy an electrolux product ever again.

product_title: Electrolux Icon E23BC78IPS Professional 22.6 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel Counter Depth French Door Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_title: Seriously-don't buy this refrigerator. Buy the Electrolux oven, but not the refrigerator.
review_text:
Seriously. Take the reviews seriously-don't buy it. We liked the look of this refrigerator. We bought a top of the line French door bottom freezer Electrolux Refrigerator, an Electrolux Cooktop, and an Electrolux Oven in 2011. We LOVE the oven. Cooktop is ok except have to light one burner with a match if it is still warm and being relit. Refrigerator - SERIOUSLY want to kick it, often. Or unplug it. Seriously wish we had our 30 yr. old simple GE with no bells or whistles refrigerator back.

However, the customer service operators and engineers at Electrolux are very courteous and pleasant. I know. I have talked to them on many occasions :-)

Pros: looks, stainless steel doesn't show too many finger prints, separately controlled meat drawer that you can change temperature on, control panel outside refrigerator.

Cons: Icemaker, water dispenser have many problems, milk put in door sours quickly, configuration of inside seems awkward, freezer trays get off the tracks and freezer won't close often. There are not very many people who will service Electrolux refrigerators, even in a major metropolitan area (only 1 in the SF Bay Area).

We had read the poor reviews prior to purchasing the refrigerator, but liked the looks of it, and thought 'what are the chances of getting a bad one? How bad could it be?' And we like the oven and cooktop, and got a deal if we bought all 3 as Electrolux. We took our chances, and have regretted it greatly. After the refrigerator was professionally installed, we discovered it did not make ice. Apparently they forgot to hook something up properly. After a service call, it made ice, but would leak about 1/2 cup of water a day into the dispenser bottom, it would overflow and drip down the front of the refrigerator, causing a puddle on the floor. It took 3 more service calls and multiple calls with the Electrolux engineering department (who were very courteous) to get it to stop leaking and puddling on the floor. It is a good thing we had a tile floor. We had to leave a cup in the dispenser tray, and a towel on the floor beneath it for a month or two. Sometimes, we turned it off completely so the floor wouldn't get damaged if we we gone overnight. Finally, the leak was stopped and the dispenser worked.

Because of how our experience started and the many poor reviews we read, we bought the extended warranty. After the end of the warranty, we decided not to renew it because we thought it was expensive, and we don't find the layout of the refrigerator to work very well. Often, the trays in the freezer compartment shift into a different position, and the freezer compartment won't shut, so food has to be removed from the trays, the tray lifted and put back into position, before the door will shut.

HOWEVER, the control panel on the outer door is very nice. We have not had problems with it. It will alert you when the power has gone off, it will alert you when the temperature has become warmer than desired, one can easily change the temperature of the freezer or refrigerator with it, it will notify you when the filters need changing, and one can use the panel to turn off the icemaker - which is very handy as it is necessary to turn it off often! The icemaker often makes a loud, persistent buzzing noise. A search of the internet for this problem shows it is common, and many people have found it to be caused by ice buildup in an unreachable place. The common public solution is to turn off the icemaker for a few days until the ice melts. We have done this several times. Most recently, we turned it off for a week, but when we turned it back on, the noise was so loud and could be heard throughout the entire house, and it was even difficult to talk on the phone nearby. We read there was an Electrolux fix-free part. I called to ask Electrolux about it, and they said there wasn't one for our specific model. They said we could buy a $630 extended warranty to cover parts, labor or even replacement. We decided that a) we don't really like the refrigerator anyway--even if it worked, so we don't want to put another $600 into it b) we would rather have the $600 to put toward a non-Electrolux refrigerator that is less annoying and works. I told Electrolux we don't want the warranty, we just want to fix it.

They gave me the phone # for a certified repairman in the area (we live within 30 mi. of San Francisco). I asked if they could give me a second repairman to call, just in case. They said there is only one certified Electrolux repairman in the area (really? in the San Francisco Bay Area, there is only ONE certified Electrolux repairman?.)

I will call the repairman one more time. If it is more than a couple hundred dollars to fix it, we will go buy a different refrigerator.

We don't hate Electrolux. We LOVE or oven and would buy the same one again-it amazingly cooks a perfect turkey by doing nothing but placing a plain turkey in the over with a temperature probe it in, and pushing 1 button. The refrigerator is really annoying. I will say that the customer service people on the phone are very courteous, which is admirable, given the number of poor reviews their refrigerators have and the number of complaints they must get. I would have thought we just got a lemon, but from reading the other reviews, it sounds like many have the same experience.

product_title: Electrolux Icon E23BC78IPS Professional 22.6 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel Counter Depth French Door Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_title: ice maker problems here too!!!!! had to wait because it was on back order!
review_text: same problem with the ice maker. real POS. luckily it was within the first 30 days so i told them to take it away. so glad i didn't have to keep it. so upsetting.

product_title: Electrolux Icon E23BC78IPS Professional 22.6 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel Counter Depth French Door Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_title: Icemaker not only broke after one year, but seems to impossible to fix.
review_text:
We bought our Electrolux Icon fridge a little more than a year ago. We ordered it, then did some research and called the salesman at Coast back to say we did not want this model -- the reviews about the ice maker malfunctioning were compelling. The folks at Coast told us that they did not stock the model without the ice maker. If we wanted it, we would have to wait to get it and it would be more expensive.
Alas, we stayed with our original model.
For the first year the fridge was great and the ice maker worked.
Until it didn't.
Now, three repairman visits later, it STILL does not work. The repairman can't seem to figure out what is happening. It's not the motor. He thinks it's a control board issue.
Meanwhile, an icebound like me is opening the door, opening the ice drawer and taking ice out of the fridge on a regular basis -- ice cubes always ending up on the floor.
Going back, I would ABSOLUTELY NOT HAVE ORDERED THIS MODEL. Not only is it broken, as most reviews told us it would be (contrary to the folks at Coast Appliances advice), it seems to be virtually impossible to fix.
Buyer Beware.

product_title: GE APPLIANCES PGS968SEPSS 30 Slide-In Gas Range, 4 Sealed Burners, Convection, Self Clean - Stainless
review_text: Do not buy a GE gas range. Our new one which was re-jetted for propane will NOT BOIL WATER when the range fan is on high! The oven gives off terrible fumes when it fires up. The GE tech said " it is gas, so it smells" well why don't the burners that won't boil water give off noxious gases when they try to boil water?

product_title: Whirlpool W8RXEGMWQ 17.5 Cu. Ft. White Top Freezer Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_text: We have owned this refrigerator for 4 years. I very much like the handle less design and it turns out that is the only thing likable about it. It has a third small drawer that you can supposedly move around as needed and you can. Just don't try opening the drawer, even empty it sticks. The magnets in the door seals are falling out, the compressor sometimes sounds like its grinding nuts and when you close the refrigerator door the freezer door comes open just enough to thaw everything and make a mess. You have to put your hands on both doors and shove to make sure they're shut and if you're successful, you will then be using both hands trying to pry the freezer open. years ago I owned a refrigerator we found in the woods and it was a better appliance. This experience has led me to avoid not only Whirlpool but all of the other brands they make.

product_title: Whirlpool W8RXEGMWQ 17.5 Cu. Ft. White Top Freezer Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_text: Have owned this refrigerator for less than 2 years and it is already failing. The refrigerator portion hovers above 40 degrees (which is not cold enough). I had to fight with Whirlpool to get parts covered, and then the incompetent technicians in my area were unable to figure out what was wrong.(They overcharged me to not fix it...and patronizingly tell me that I was blocking the air vents although I made sure I was not blocking the vents.) Whirlpool has been incredibly difficult to get hold of. Their main suggestion was that I purchase a $300 1-year warranty extension...which is a long ways towards purchasing a whole new fridge! So I am stuck with a practically new, not quite working refrigerator. Do not buy this appliance!!!

product_title: GE PS968TPWW Profile 30" White Electric Slide-In Smoothtop Range - Convection
review_title: Poor design and difficult to clean
review_text: Can't wait to replace this range. The convection oven option is not deep enough to bake properly.The controls in front is a poor design. Food is trapped in the control panel and is time consuming to clean. The smooth top was chosen as we have cross ventilation with french doors on both ends of the kitchen making it difficult to use gas. Just a poor choice made by my designer.

product_title: GE Profile : PT960SPSS 30 Double Wall Oven - Stainless Steel
review_text: I am a professional Chef and am using this oven in my home kitchen. Great oven!  Convection in both ovens, preheats very fast, cooks evenly.  I've used for roasting, braising, baking and general reheating.  It has performed up to my expectations 100%.

product_title: GE Profile : PGS908SEPSS 30 Gas Range - Stainless Steel
review_text: I have one of the GE Profile gas ranges that preceded this one. I made the big mistake of falling in love with the 'black-on-black' model for about %1400 several years ago and have regretted it ever since. All the features still work. BUT IT IS IMPOSSIBLE TO KEEP CLEAN. If I had read the part in the manual which says the cook-top must not only be cleaned but POLISHED every day I wouldn't have bought it. Now the cook top is scratched overall in spite of my best efforts. When I saw this range which seemed to address the problems I jumped for joy. Fortunately I checked the web before rushing out to buy. There are no reviews (no negative reviews) anywhere! All the sites which list the range for sale say 'this product has not yet been reviewed"...come on. It's been out for over 2 years now and no-one has reviewed it? It seems that companies like Reputation Inc are suddenly dominating the web and removing or back-filling the review process. This range appears to be the exact same thing as my black-on-black model with the flaws corrected by SS. I'd love to buy one but I'm very leery of it. BE REALLY CAREFUL WHEN BUYING!

product_title: GE Profile : PGS908SEPSS 30 Gas Range - Stainless Steel
review_text:
We have owned this range approx. 3 years. I haven't noticed any problems with the oven or cook top burners, but I rated it low because of two reasons.

First, the cook top burners and grate are in an odd design. Both forward burners are too close to the front edge of the stove and to one another. This wouldn't be a big problem, except that these are the largest burners intended to handle bigger pots or pans. So, any of our large pots and pans are too close to sit next to one another or they hang off the front. The grate also has large spaces in it that will allow a small pot to fall through.

The second problem is with durability. Anything that has to be cleaned off the stainless steel portion of the top (nearest to the burners) will leave scratches. Ours developed so many that I now use #0000 steel wool to clean this surface. Also, even with gentle cleaning, the numbers have begun to wear off of the control panel.

I would not buy this range again.

product_title: GE Profile : PGS908SEPSS 30 Gas Range - Stainless Steel
review_text:
Having owned and used this oven/range for about three years, I can confidently write this review. I have to admit, I bought this oven because it looked nice....but soon found out that you cannot judge a book by its cover! I will just list the pros and cons:

Pros: Good looking, easy to clean range top, burners work well

Cons: Layout of the burners is not practical, the sizes of the burners are not very functional
(the 2 small burners are just plain too small)
the oven is not deep enough (often, I can't fit large baking sheets), the oven doesn't
cook food evenly, the vent on top (on the range) gets really hot when the oven is in use.

This oven overall is just ok....the price does not justify. I would give it a two star strictly on its functionality.

product_title: Bosch : SHE43P06UC 24 Evolution 300 Series Full Console Dishwasher - Black
review_text:
I took advantage of the appliance rebates earlier this year, but didn't install this dishwasher until I had a new counter put in this summer. I absolutely hate this dishwasher. It doesn't hold nearly what my old Maytag did - which had nothing wrong with it but was old and we figured we'd put in a new dishwasher when replacing the countertops. My Maytag held so much more. The Bosch dishwasher also doesn't hold things well at all. If you don't have the perfect dish set they show in their instruction manual - and have bigger plastic cups or deeper round bowls, they do not stack in the dishwasher well at all. It is aggravating to load it and big gaps in parts of the bottom that cups fall right through.

Does any REAL person test these products? And, unfortunately, you can't return products once they are installed, but you really don't know how you will like something like this until you use it.

I'm not that impressed with the cleaning - I have had to rewash some dishes that came out with spots - and one time none of the powder dissolved when the dishwasher ran and it was a big glob.

I've never seen a worse design and can't imagine being stuck with this for the next 10+ years. I seriously am thinking about taking the loss and replacing it, although can't afford to right now.

Take your dishes to the store and try to stack them in the dishwasher before buying! If you aren't using a perfect matched set of pieces, this dishwasher is NOT for you!

product_title: GE Profile : P2S975SEPSS 30 Dual Fuel Range - Stainless Steel
review_text:
We purchased this last Summer and are on our third set of controls.
Very poor design as heat from main oven / broil melts the plastic controls.
Our third set are a different material but now get very hot.
Also main control board failed so oven would not work, there seems to be moisture able to get in the oven control area.
I will not buy another GE appliance.

product_title: GE Profile : P2S975SEPSS 30 Dual Fuel Range - Stainless Steel
review_title: GE Profile Dual Fuel slide-in range 30"
review_text:
We purchased this range because of the favorable Consumer Reports reviews, and in the past we have been very satisfied with GE major appliances. But today, I cannot recommend this range.

This is our second GE Profile dual fuel slide-in 30" in four years. The first range had a serious problem with the gas control and we experienced 2' flames from the front right burner. The replacement range has an electrical short which will cost $500 to repair, the short has ruined the stove and now two months later GE won't fix it.

Change: 3/10/2013 - GE replaced the range with a factory fresh range including installation free of charge.

product_title: GE Profile : PDWT580RSS 24 Built-In Dishwasher - Stainless Steel
review_text:
We ordered this on Saturday of President's Day weekend and got a phone call that Monday night to schedule a delivery Tuesday or Wednesday. The vendor service was excellent.

I don't know if I'd recommend self installation unless you are mechanically inclined. The unit just fit under the counter and was otherwise a VERY tight squeeze compared to the GE it replaced. That extra capacity has to come from somewhere. Fortunately, there was a tile floor under the unit at the same hight as our hardwood, because I've heard that sometimes floor installers manage to box in the dishwasher during a kitchen remodel and you have to pop the countertop!

The GE Profile is very quiet. Had friends over and they didn't realize it was running in the kitchen until we heard the rinse cycle draining. We're very happy with the results.

product_title: GE Profile : PDWT580RSS 24 Built-In Dishwasher - Stainless Steel
review_text:
My spouse and I purchased this in spite of a couple reservations due to previous reviews. We had other GE profile appliances and were happy with those. When the appliance was received, it was damaged. We didn't want to install since it was damaged and unsure what the fix would be. When I called GE I was told it would have to be installed before they would send someone out so called the third party AJ Madison instead. They set up for a GE repairman to come out. He said it was factory damaged and would need to be replaced. (And I didn't have to install to get this answer). The new dishwasher came quickly and was installed.
However, now that it is installed I am NOT HAPPY with the unit. The racks are such that the dishes move around when sliding bottom rack in and out and have to continuously rearrange the dishes. When using the manual detergent dispenser the cleaning was more or less OK but decided to test the dispenser for holding a full bottle of detergent. I rinsed the dishes thoroughly, even though the manual says this is not necessary. I do make sure the water is hot before turning on the dishwasher and still had dirty dishes at end of cycle. I will test it again using the manual detergent dispenser but so far I would say if you want a dishwasher that cleans look elsewhere.

product_title: GE Profile : PDWT580RSS 24 Built-In Dishwasher - Stainless Steel
review_text: As a previous review mentioned, we also received this dishwasher as part of a new construction - we did not choose it. But now we are stuck with it. The space inside is useless. You might be able to fit one or two pots in the bottom. There are two rows on top for cups then a strange open midde section with little prongs that are useless. The biggest issue is that although I have run three separate loads, several items still come out dirty. I don't mean slightly dirty, I mean very dirty - as if even water did not reach them. Further, everything has water spots. Terrible dishwasher.

product_title: GE Profile : PDWT580RSS 24 Built-In Dishwasher - Stainless Steel
review_text: As others have said, this dishwasher does not actually wash dishes.  Almost everything that goes in either has to be rewashed.  Once, just for "fun" I didn't fully rinse something before putting it in the dishwasher.  I ran the wash cycle, which is 128 minutes.  One would think over 2 hours of washing would clean something, but it didn't.  I put the same dishes through for 3 cycles, 6 hours of washing, and yet, they were still dirty.  Even if the dishwasher really did wash dishes, the racks are useless.  There is no good way to load this dishwasher. product_title: Front load steam washer, Wave-touch controls, White
review_text:
It's a great machine but you can save four hundred bucks by buying an IQ-Touch instead. There is nothing a Wave-Touch can do that an IQ-Touch can not. The Wave-Touch has 4 distinguishing features over the IQ:

1. The Wave spins at 1350 vs. the IQ's 1200 rpm. No big deal. I don't think there's any practical difference in the amount of water extracted that will make a real dent in the drying time.

2. The Wave has an "Active Wear" cycle. It's not something you'd ever miss if your machine did not have it in the first place. You can use the IQ's "Casual wear" cycle instead, which differs from the Active Wear cycle by only 5 minutes.

3. The Wave's options are hidden in tedious to use menus and submenus, instead of the IQ's simple to use buttons. Buttons win here because you can see at a glance what options are active, especially useful for the next time you use the washer. With the Wave-Touch's menu style you'll be forced to scroll through the menus to see what options have been selected.

4. Wave-Touch has 3 favorites memory buttons vs. one favortie for the IQ-Touch. I have yet to find this feature useful. When one is useless to me, having 3 doesn't make it any better.

Construction-wise the two machines are otherwise identical.

Conclusion: The Wave costs $300 to $400 more than the IQ and delivers the same level of performance as the IQ. The Wave is for people who have money to burn. Okay, with a bit of sheepishness I have to admit I did buy a Wave instead of an IQ.

Now, let me review the Wave with steam function, since that's the one I actually bought.

The machine is exceedingly quiet when washing. The only real noise comes during the spin cycles.

As for vibration, make sure you balance the machine using a good quality level and follow the leveling instructions. Read the manual and it's imperative that the shipping bolts be removed per the instructions before using the machine!!! My house has a crawl space. My laundry room is on the first floor, where the washer would be perfectly capable of transmitting vibration if it was not leveled properly. So far it's been very smooth, in fact much smoother than my previous top-loader, with hardly much of any vibration. Keep in mind that every load is different and each load has its own vibration and noise characteristics. Some loads will be vibration free, other loads with a very unbalanced load (pillows and comforters, for example) will have some vibration. If it vibrates at all it's almost always during the spin up and spin down phase of the spin cycle. Once it actually gets into the spin cycle, there is usually little vibration.

This washer is quite ingenious in fighting vibration by ramping up to full spin speed in incremental stages. During the first stage, it slowly rotates the wet load counterclock-wise to test for balance, and also to pump out water. If it detects even the slightest hint of an unbalanced load, it will stop and reverse direction, i.e. spin clockwise, at the same slow rpm to let the clothes to shuffle in the drum. After a few seconds of this clockwise spin, it reverses direction again, i.e. counter-clockwise again, it then tests for balance again. If it again detects a poor balance, it will keep on doing this reversing direction routine until it redistributes the load evenly. When it's finally satisfied that the balance is good, it will then launch into high spin speeds in several stages. Frequently, after it has launched into a higher speed, it detects unacceptable vibration. It will instantly abort the spin and perform the shuffling routine again and again until it gets the balance right. It's not uncommon for it to go back and forth many times for as long as 5 minutes to find the sweet spot. As more water is progressively pumped out and the load becoming progressively lighter and better balanced, it will proceed to the next higher speed, finally maxing out at 1350 rpm, during the last 2 minutes of the spin cycle.

As for the steam feature, I've yet to find definitive evidence that it's the steam itself that gets the dirt out. The steam cycle essentially adds 20 minutes of wash time to any wash cycle using either warm water or hot water. Maybe it's the extra 20 minutes of washing in warm water in the steam cycle that does the trick. It's hard to tell.

It washes loose clothing very well while using little water. By "loose clothing," I mean items that are somewhat small and that will wet easily and shrink in volume as they are wetted. Items with these characteristics can freely tumble around one another inside the drum, as long as the machine is not overloaded. However when it comes to washing bulky big loads, such as pillows and synthetic fiber comforters, synthetic fiber bedspreads, etc., its miserliness in water use is its biggest flaw. With these bulky items, the water level is woefully inadequate to thoroughly wet the interior mass. And because they are synthetic fiber items, they don't shrink much in volume even when wetted, so they don't have much room to rotate inside the drum. The same side of the pillow or comforter then faces the drum and the center side doesn't ever get enough water. So, the side facing the drum surface gets cleaned but the center side doens't get cleaned. I bought this washer specifically to wash big bulky items such as pillows and synthetic fiber comforters, so it's a bit disappointing that it doesn't clean these items well. The way to get around this problem is to pause the machine after it's finished filling, and add water on your own either through the door or through the detergent tray. It works. Adding about 1 to 2 gallons of hot water fixes the problem.

I still love the washer, but only wish it had a "bulky items" selection which would allow it to have more water during the wash cycle. I believe this problem with washing bulky items is endemic to all high effiency front load washers and not just Electrolux. The real wish is to allow a separate button to vary the water level, like that found on my old Kenmore top-loader, but I don't think we'll ever see that water level selection switch on these high efficiency washers. I think the Electrolux designers' hands were tied by the stringent Federal energy efficiency standards.
