product_title: LG 4.2CF STEAMWASHER FRONT CONTROL WHITE
review_text:
Hi there. Firstly, the WM2501HVA is the same as the WM2501HWA with the only difference being the Graphite Steel color vs White. Big deal. In a lot of places, you'll pay $50 more just for the Graphite Steel color! WTF? Price for fashion I guess. I'll pass. I bought the white one and accompanying DLGX2502W after a couple of months researching steam washers/dryers(gas) reviews and prices on the interwebs and in person at the usual cast of brick-and-mortar retailers (Best Buy, Home Depot, Lowes, PC Richards, Amazon, Sears, etc.). I kept looking for great value in the duet (a.k.a., great reviews combined with a great sale).

I finally decided on this LG set and wound up buying from somewhere other than Amazon (BB) for $$509.99 (washer) and $569.49 (dryer) + after "instant" 15% advertised discount, plus $69.00 delivery and NYS tax for a grand total of $1,245.27 - all inclusive. The delivery came quickly and the delivery guys were very nice, very quick and very professional. I would have liked stainless steel but I wasn't about to pay hundreds more for aesthetics - eh...

On to the review...

The Good: Price! Value! Techno-wizardry interface, boops, beeps. I've never experienced such clean clothes from a single wash or any machine outside professional dry cleaners!!! Fantastic device in terms of cleanliness. Even my dress shirts that I either scrub excessively at the collar with stain removers normally before washing (and still don't get completely clean) came out spotless on wash #1 (with steam)! Wow. All the clothes have great, great smell - very different from my old clunky traditional top-loader. Very quiet cycle. Lots of features available at the push of a button. Certain programs disable certain options in an effort to not ruin certain types of clothing - nice. Lots of temp options unlike old ones where you're sometimes limited to certain temp combinations.

The Bad: Techno-wizardry interface, boops, beeps (takes some getting used to). It's not like the old-school turn 1 knob, select large-med-small, hot-cold and push to start. My wife was daunted at first but now she's happy with the setup. The wash time takes significantly longer than a "standard" top-loader - 15 - 20 minutes more maybe. Add steam, and you're looking at over an hour - yikes. I can live with it as long as my clothes keep getting super clean like they have been. A bit taller than normal machine but whatever.

In the end, I would HIGHLY recommend this product for anyone looking for a new washer. I have no clue why you would (and could easily) spend double on a steam setup. All the stores have the $1200 washers front and center at their displays - no thanks. I would have ranked this 5 stars except for the longish washing cycle times.

Enjoy...

product_title: LG 4.2CF STEAMWASHER FRONT CONTROL WHITE
review_title: Super Clean Laundry.  Whites never so bright.
review_text:
After our cheap-o washing machine and dryer broke down, we decided to make a Black Friday purchase and get both the dryer and washing machines from Best Buy. My husband and I researched the heck out of what was available on the market. We compared features, cleaning options, and prices. I came across one site that had over 1700 reviews for this machine alone - the average review was a 5 out of 5.

I could not be happier with the products. While it is true the washing cycle takes longer than a top load washer, the end result is amazingly different. The matching dryer seems to work more efficiently than our old one and makes up for the time difference between loads. My toddlers socks came out white and the dirt stains gone. Even some of the old stains were removed. There are a lot of fancy dials and sounds on the machine however once you get accustomed to the settings, it is very easy to use. The pre-wash and steam features are a nice bonus. I especially like the top area to load the soap and fabric softner. The load capability seems quite large to me. Several pairs of jeans, pants and tops can go in at once. While running, the machine is fairly quiet. This is a beneficial feature since our laundry room is located in the center of our home. Is it wrong to fall in love with an appliance? If so, guilty as charged. Now if only they could automate the folding process I would be in heaven!!

product_title: LG 4.2CF STEAMWASHER FRONT CONTROL WHITE
review_text:
I bought this from Home Depot, and have had it for 1 month. Loads take longer because the machine spins a bit, and stops. spins a bit and stops. spins a bit and stops... It's really annoying at the start of the cycle.. turns on water for 2 seconds and stops. more water for 2 seconds and stops. more water for 2 seconds and stops... just fill the frigging machine, ok?? as my water pipes clank from the constant and abrupt starts and stops.

i have used the extra water cycles, and have used the cleaned cycle. I wipe down the rubber gasket after the final load and promptly remove the clothes... there is still some kind of odor. Maybe I should get that Tide cleaner???

To me, these front load machines are like high maintenance prima donnas... If I had to do it over again, I would get a top load.

product_title: LG 4.2CF STEAMWASHER FRONT CONTROL WHITE
review_text: I recently purchased this item and the associated gas dryer at another retailer, with a price match to yet another retailer and a 10% coupon on top. While at first the wash times seemed rather long, there is always the quick wash option that reduces the wash time to essentially the time of a regular top loader. I admit that the short burst of water, spin a little, short burst of water, spin a little more, repeat, made me skeptical at first, the machine definitely does a great job cleaning everything I have tossed into it. Water usage has dropped incredibly and the clothes are so much brighter. All I can say is Wow! Wish I would have gotten one of these years ago. Definitely recommend this to others.

product_title: LG 4.2CF STEAMWASHER FRONT CONTROL WHITE
review_text:
We're a family of 3; with also 3 very furry Siberian Huskies. A large capacity washing machine was important for us. With moving last year, we chose to leave old Amana washer/dryer set behind and purchase new. Before the Amana set, we had Whirlpool. After much research and reading several reviews, we decided that the LG front load SteamWasher fit our needs. I was originally looking into the red and metalic colors, but they were $100-300 more. Best Buy had the white color on sale, about 6 months ago, so we chose to go with white.

I love this washing machine! Clothes come out much cleaner, & whites come out much brighter. The steam feature is really nice as well; whether you want to freshen up your clothes, use allergen control or sanitize. The bells and whistles to this washer provide just about everything anyone would need. Cycles include: *Steam Fresh, *Allergeine, *Sanitary, *Bulky/Large, *Cotton/Normal, *Perm.Press (*these first 6, all have steam feature; first 2 are exclusively a steam cycle), Delicates, Hand Wash/Whool and Speed Wash. Other features I enjoy are: steam, extra rinse/tub clean, stain cycle & water plus. I also like how I can adjust preference on: spin speed, soil level, water temp (all important for me). Not to mention, the beeper is not the standard loud and annoying beep most washers have...it plays a tune. Other useful options and features include: Delay Wash, Pre-Wash, Child Lock, and the option to turn Spinsense and Beeper on or off.

Clothes do take a little longer to wash (depending also on what settings you use) than most top load washers, but clothes come out cleaner, less soap is needed and less water is used. At first, I was concerned about the less water, since with a top load, using more water seemed to clean the clothes better. This is not an issue at all with LG SteamWasher. Most importantly, none of our clothes, linens, pillows or huskies' plush squeek toys come out torn or damaged, from washing! --We've had all too many items torn and warn down from top load washer's agitators.

Overall, this washer meets all of this family's needs. It's very quiet, very well balanced, has more warranty coverage than any other top load washer we've viewed, and it's a nice looking machine. I have nothing negative to say about it, even after 6+ months.

product_title: LG 4.2CF STEAMWASHER FRONT CONTROL WHITE
review_text:
Just got one of these a couple of days ago (not from Amazon, got an excellent deal elsewhere), to replace a Samsung front-loader.

I liked the interface and the SilverCare in the Samsung, but it didn't clean particularly well, and man did it beat the heck out of my clothes. This one is just a night-and-day difference in terms of cleaning power. I have an older white bathrobe that was starting to get pretty dingy-looking out of the Samsung. Even one trip through the LG brightened it up a ton, and a second trip through has made it look almost new again. I haven't even tried the steam cycle yet! Two runs on Sanitary (for the extra-hot water), and wow, what a difference. Same detergent, similar cycle times, but MUCH better results on the LG.

Don't know yet about clothes wear on this model, but Consumer Reports gives other LGs high marks for gentleness, so I'm expecting this to be good, too.

It's important to always dry off the seal and the inside of the door when you're finished with a front loader, and you're supposed to leave the door ajar to let the inside dry. This unit has a cool little stop that keeps the door slightly open, but holds it in place magnetically, so it won't swing any wider. I always left a towel in the door of the Samsung to keep it from sealing tight, and I won't have to do that with this unit. This tiny little feature makes me unreasonably happy.

If you're a laundry nerd (yes, they do exist :) ), be aware that there's no Favorite Cycle setting. If the built-ins aren't right for what you want, you'll always have to manually modify a cycle to do what you need. Doesn't bother me -- judging from the results I'm seeing, that machine knows a lot more about cleaning clothes than I do, so I just set the dial and push the button. One annoyance: the dial responds slowly. It doesn't matter how fast you spin it. The machine waits for the beep to finish each time it switches to a new setting, so you can't just crank it over to the right spot. You have to live through all the beeps in between. Mild grr.

As others are saying, it looks like this washer may be a little higher-maintenance than most; there's a drain filter on the lower front left that you're supposed to clean about once a month. The manual makes it sound pretty easy, but it is something to have to think about. For the results I'm seeing, I don't mind.

My only real complaint is that dial. LG, if you're reading this, modify your UI to let people spin it faster.

Can't speak yet to reliability or wear on clothes, but purely on the basis of cleaning performance, I'm really, really impressed.

product_title: LG 4.2CF STEAMWASHER FRONT CONTROL G STL
review_text: My wife and I wanted to get a front loader washer and after doing much research I decided to buy this washer.  What a mistake this was. Secondly, we were told this machine cleans exceptionally well in a much shorter time.  We don't find the clothes to be any cleaner and the time on standard loads is much longer then my other machine.  The main issue we have with this machine is the smell from the rubber seal around the inside of the door.  We were told by the sales person that this was a common occurrence with LG washers and they made cleaners to remedy this issue.  Well my wife has done everything possible in using different cleaners, drying the seal after each wash, leaving the door open after use etc., and the smell is still a problem.  We will be contacting LG shortly to complain, however based on other reviews I have seen in terms of customer service with LG, I have very low hope that LG will make good on this.  This will probably be my last LG purchase!!

product_title: Bosch : SHE43P15UC 24 Evolution 300 Series Full Console Dishwasher - Stainless Steel
review_text: We've own this dishwasher for about a year. I wrote a review someplace when I first got it describing how much I hated it, but after one year I've come to the conclusion that there is one feature that makes this dishwasher really, really nice.  You can take out the top rack, and then with a little piece ( that you have to purchase extra- online) you put it over the place that the water comes out for the top rack. It's just a cheap piece of plastic that makes like a water shower out of the back.  But what that does is make it possible to put really big items in the dishwasher to wash.  I wash my trash cans all the time in there and washing trash cans is one of my least favorite chores so after having this dishwasher for a year I realize how valuable that is.  I wash other large things too.  Without the top rack there is a lot of room in there.  The other really good thing is that it is very quiet.  It still is a major pain to load.  small cereal type bowls just can't find a good place to fit, and it doesn't hold nearly as much as my old dishwasher, even though that one had a post in the center, and it doesn't wash as well.  However, it does wash very good, just not as well as my old dishwasher. It's not really a "potscrubber"  With just the two of us at home now, or 3 when my son is home from college it is working out well.  So despite my scathing first review, the truth is I now like this dishwasher mostly because I can wash really tall things in it. By the way, I'm basing this review on the picture, this is what my dishwasher looks like, none of the other pictures match.

product_title: Electric Range
review_text: Bought this range when we remodeled the kitchen.  I would rather have had a gas model, but there is no gas available here.  This range with the convection oven get five stars from me.  Bakes  perfectly in both ovens.  The smaller oven is great for a single loaf of bread or broiled steaks for two.  The larger oven with its convection feature is fabulous for pizza, bread, large roasts and will accomodate huge pans.  the stove top with the five burners is most useful.  The left side of the cooktop can be used with a full size griddle since the normal space betweent eh burners can be activated as a heat unit.  The warmer burner is great for melting chocolate, butter, or just keeping food warm.  I'd buy ths again in a heartbeat.

product_title: Electric Range
review_title: Fit perfectly, cooks great, love it.
review_text: I had to get this size oven to replace one that fit between the cabinets.  I just had to get into the habit of using the small side oven for baking, not just storage.  Not having to heat up the large oven for a small pan of biscuits is great!  I didn't know if I would like the flat top cooking, but I really do. I went from gas to electric and a lot of people hate electric cooking but I have no problem with it.  Especially because clean up is so easy, but you do have to let the top cool before wiping up.

product_title: Electric Range
review_text: I bought this range recently and had it installed in a remodeled kitchen. It looks great, works great but the cooktop stains and marks way TOO easily. I have had a ceramic top range for years in another home and it was Samsung and the glass didn't have a mark on it.  We cook on it once per day and have a small family but if a splash or spill goes over, it is a frantic sprint to wait for it to cool and clean it. I had the technician out to look to see if there was a problem and he said it was cosmetic. I understand all that but why did that other stove never have any of that? It is a different surface obviously created by a different company so there is something they are missing, that Samsung had. There is no way to get it clean and we have had it for 3 months and every few days there is a new mark that will not come off. A pot of boiling water with pasta splashes over and a little pool went under the pot. I remove the pot and let the stove cool to clean and it leaves a permanent circle on that burner. Cosmetic?  Really.

product_title: GE GFSF6KKYBB 25.9 cu. Ft. French-Door Refrigerator with Water and Ice Dispenser - Black
review_title: The service tech said there's really nothing that could have prevented this as it's just a bad board and is out of warranty

product_title: Bosch : SHE5AL05UC 24 Ascenta Series Full Console Dishwasher - Stainless Steel
review_text: My Bosch dishwasher is 1.5 years old. The handle broke off. The parts are still under warrantee, but Bosch will not ship me the free part unless I pay a $130 service fee.

product_title: Bosch : SHE5AL05UC 24 Ascenta Series Full Console Dishwasher - Stainless Steel
review_text:

product_title: Bosch : SHE5AL05UC 24 Ascenta Series Full Console Dishwasher - Stainless Steel

product_title: Haier HLP21N Pulsator 1-Cubic-Foot Portable Washer
review_text:
I recently purchased this, though not from this vendor. My living space is on the top floor and the laundry area is down 2 winding flights of stairs. Someone suggested that if I could do laundry without having it pile up, my life would be easier. So now, this is the first week I have had this installed. Admittedly, I never have overly high expectations of machinery, but I am more than happy with this.

The instructions for the washer are fairly detailed. I ran into trouble over the sink hook-up, just because I did not understand standard terminology. When a friend came in to help, it took him all of 15 minutes (or less). Everything was tightened with a wrench, plus he tied the two hoses (in and out) with a fastener to position them securely. I ran the first load 5 minutes later. No leaks, in spite of what you might have read in other reviews of the same product.

I am not a big person and tonight, the load (at medium, the default setting) was:
1 pair of long pants
1 flannel pajama shirt
1 cotton sweater (in a laundry bag)
1 blouse
4 pairs underwear and 4 pairs of socks (in separate mesh laundry bag)
2 T-shirts

After reading many reviews, I leave it on the medium setting and don't overfill it. I also got these laundry bags to protect the clothing. The spin cycle does a good enough job so the clothes dry within 12 hours on a rack in the bathroom. It is also easy to hook and unhook from the sink, and comes with wheels that you can choose to install.

I am ***very*** happy with the ease of use, convenience, portability, small footprint.

January, 2012:
Update: Towards the end of the warranty period, there was suddenly a spark and the whole thing went dead. In spite of what you may read elsewhere, I did reach a real person when I called the number listed on the instruction manual. A local authorized repair person was despatched who diagnosed it as the motherboard having a short. Haier was supposed to send the repair rep. a part, but I heard nothing, until a call several weeks later from Haier, saying they were going to replace the washer outright. There were things I had to do and instructions to follow, like cut the piping etc. etc., cut a label, include this and that. When this was followed to a "T", I did receive a new washer, again some weeks later. This immediately malfunctioned and water overflowed. It was a huge mess and somewhat of an emergency. Because I could not wait, I did not call the company but took care of it with my own repair guy. We switched the water level sensor (wrong part on the new one!) with the one I had saved on the old machine. Since then, it has worked beautifully. However, should this malfunction again, I may look for another brand To cut a long story short: 1. Save all documentation. 2. The product is inconsistent. Why would the new washer immediately malfunction with an INCORRECT PART? This was troubling. 3. If you are not in a hurry to get it repaired, then Haier does come through. 4. If Haier replaces the machine, save the old one for parts, if you possibly have room. It is because of these hassles and the malfunctioning that I have downgraded the 5-star to 3.

product_title: Haier HLP21N Pulsator 1-Cubic-Foot Portable Washer
review_text: I purchased this item at a local store. I liked everything about this little machine.  Nice size, holds a decent amount of clothes.  Easy to assemble and connect.  Big Problem... product_title: Haier HLP21N Pulsator 1-Cubic-Foot Portable Washer
review_text:
I purchased this washer from Target through Amazon last month and I couldn't be more pleased with it. I have been reading the reviews of these the little Haier washers for several months so I was prepared for how the bottom plate works (it bulges out), for the fact that we would struggle a bit getting the screws through the plate and that we needed teflon tape and good pliers to really tighten the hose connections. All and all, the set-up was easier than I expected.

As far as using it goes, the loads are larger than I thought they would be, the clothes come out very clean and well spun out so they dry quickly. The controls are easy to understand and so far everything has worked as it is supposed to. Our household has three members, myself and two teenagers and so far it is keeping up with us and sparing us the hideous laundromat problems we had before. A load might be a pair of jeans, 3 shirts and 3 pairs of socks or a sheet, 2 pillow cases and a large towel. We have even washed some blankets.

If anything goes wrong or it develops major problems I'll try to remember to update here but so far I'm very satisfied.

product_title: Haier HLP21N Pulsator 1-Cubic-Foot Portable Washer
review_text:
I live on a boat. There are "boat-specific" washers that start at around $900, more than I can justify. I got the Haier for about $200 including free shipping. Packing was ok, there was a small dent in the case that I erased by rubbing the steel from the inside with a plastic screwdriver handle.

This was an experiment with a gadget that would fit in an available space and had reasonable reviews. My main concern was that the manual said it would not operate if more than 2 degrees out of plumb, hard to achieve on a sailboat even in a marina. That seems a little pessimistic, as it operates easily even when the boat is rocking 5 or 8 degrees. I bet if the drum was gently braced with foam rubber or something up inside the case, the operating range would be even greater. I have had two out-of-balance shutdowns, which are easy to fix and restarting from where you were in the cycle is trivial. I have run maybe 20 loads of increasing size through it using maybe a quarter cup or less of generic low-suds detergent, with good cleaning and the clothes well enough spun to air-dry quickly.

It's intended to be moveable and connected to a sink faucet, but I've bolted it into a locker space, and it's easy enough to connect the inlet into the boat's water supply and the drain to a through-hull fitting. It seems to use just a couple of gallons per cycle on the "regular wash" and middle water level setting, maybe half a gallon more for "high water" and "heavy wash." Runs about 20-22 minutes per regular cycle. Current draw when the motor is working hard is about 5-6 amps, not bad for a device with this much horsepower. It is what I would consider very quiet in operation.

There are slightly larger Haier models that were just too big for my space, though the extra capacity and features would have been nice. For me, for my application, I would consider this a good buy and a very suitable product. It's got a stainless steel drum and quality wiring and plumbing fittings. I hope it lasts as long as the ones others have reported on, several years at least. The "boat specific" ones might do that but they are a problem to repair and expensive.

product_title: Haier HLP21N Pulsator 1-Cubic-Foot Portable Washer
review_text: I am sorry but my washer arrived so damaged due to the packing  or transportation,that I sent it back right away.

product_title: Haier HLP21N Pulsator 1-Cubic-Foot Portable Washer
review_text:
I bought this washer through target's website because I had a gift card, but now that the price has dropped to around $180 I wish I had bought it here! I would use normal cycle for most things because it feels like the heavy cycle takes forever and if it's more than 3 items I don't think the quick cycle washes thoroughly enough.

product_title: Haier HLP21N Pulsator 1-Cubic-Foot Portable Washer
review_text:
I love how small this washing machine is. My apartment has big rooms but
the kitchen is miniscule a. I put the machine in front of the sink and hooked it up very easily. review_text: I purchased this little washer through a different vendor about two months ago and couldn't be happier. product_title: Haier HLP21N Pulsator 1-Cubic-Foot Portable Washer

product_title: Haier HLP21N Pulsator 1-Cubic-Foot Portable Washer
review_title: Is it possible to fall in love with an appliance?
review_text: I was hesitant to purchase this as replacement for my previous portable washer as it was considerably smaller.  But now that I have it, I couldn't be happier.  It is very compact, very efficient, very, very quiet and simple to use. It was delivered to my door and after about 30 minutes I was washing clothes. product_title: Haier HLP21N Pulsator 1-Cubic-Foot Portable Washer
review_title: Everything I needed and expected for the price!!!
review_text:
I bought this little washer over two months of tedious internet research. I needed a washing machine for my small two bedroom apartment and to do my sons' laundry and my own. There are many portable washing machines out there that are larger or smaller with varying functions and prices, however this machine seemed to fit my needs the best and it was the cheapest!. I just needed a small machine that would wash a reasonable amount of clothes with little to no hassle. I had read some of the other feedback about the machines noisyness, leakness, and hasslesome bottom plate, and extremely small basket and here is what I found....

I ordered the machine and had it within 7 days, I found that reasonable as i did not pay for shipping, it was also delivered with no damage to the machine or the box, I had it shipped fedex so i was able to track it daily.

The machine was very easy to put together out of the box, all I required was a phillips head screw driver. The bottom plate was hasslesome to install but I got it on, after that the rest was cake, I had it up and running within 22 minutes total.

I did a quick wash cycle and the machine ran smooth and strong, adding and draining water as nessacary. I didn't find the machine to be any noisier than any other washing appliance, the machine did rattle slightly durring the spin cycle but I have an area rug underneath it so it was neither noisy or disturbing to me. I experienced no leaks durring this cycle.

the clothes came out clean and wrung out, I was actually very impressed.

The basket size is actually larger than it may seem, I was able to fit into the machine about 3/4 of a standard wash!!!!!

All in all for the price and expectation I gave this machine 5 stars because it does what it say it will do, I have not experienced any hassles with it as of yet and actually I am more than pleased with the machine. I now look forward to never going to the laundry mat again or piled up laundry. I can see in the future having to go to the laundry mat once a month or two months for haevy blankets and rugs but all in all this little machine has handled my washes fine, to include sheets, light weight blankets, and jeans!!! Just distribute the loads carefully, remember one light weight blanket may mean one wash!!!

I am very pleased with this machine!!!! If you would like to see some pictures of it hooked up to the sink so you can get some perspective on it check out my face book page...jaime billiel in charlestown nh...............

product_title: Haier HLP21N Pulsator 1-Cubic-Foot Portable Washer
review_text:
I've never left feedback before for anything, but I figured that what I found might help others.

The washer arrived somewhat dinged up. The outer aluminum(?) shell had several dents, but I didn't mind. However, the plastic buffer/molded styrofoam combo piece that protects the guts of the machine in transit had been smashed. This meant a lot of crushed bits of styrofoam up inside the machinery, which had to be removed carefully. The apparatus appeared okay, so I assembled everything as per directions, used Teflon tape on the threads of all the adapters, and threw clothes in to wash.

What a dream! The machine started up happily, filled, and agitated all the clothes. Then it stopped. It seemed to think it was rinsing or spinning, because both indicator lights were on, but nothing happened. I looked all over the web for an answer, but didn't find anything encouraging. Apparently Haier's service is pretty shoddy, and all the combinations of buttons I'd tried on the machine didn't do anything.

I hand-bailed the tub, wrung the clothes, and set them aside. I unplugged the machine and unscrewed the plastic service cover on its side, thinking that something may have gotten damaged or jiggled with the rough transit. I couldn't find anything, but my sister put her hand in, felt behind the black pump unit, and located a loose wire. We unscrewed the bottom plate and just plugged it back in (it had a plug...no special skills required). And there you go, the machine worked perfectly! I ran 10 loads or so before putting it away the next day.

Fortunately, the washing machine is simple enough for anyone who is mechanically inclined to service. I'd recommend opening it up and looking around for broken or loose bits before chopping the plug off and getting a new one from Haier (not a guarantee, by the way, and a waste if you have a good machine with an easy-to-fix problem). It's likely that the wire will jiggle loose again through vibration and normal use, and I may go back in there and secure it somehow. If you don't mind unplugging the machine and looking around, you may be able to save yourself a few headaches.

4/5 for crap packaging, otherwise I'm happy as a clam!

UPDATE 9/29 - I changed the review to a 5/5. This is definitely the best purchase I've made all year. So easy to use, so convenient, and I can easily collect the rinsewater to water my plants with. :)

product_title: Haier HLP21N Pulsator 1-Cubic-Foot Portable Washer
review_title: For city dwellers (even in rentals) this washer's a MUST!
review_text:
I'd been looking at this washer for the past 2-3 months. I really wanted it, but, I didn't have a reason to justify it. This week, I got my reason. Doing 1 load of laundry here in NYC is (minimum) $5 - NOT including the dryer. A lot of people who live in apartment buildings have washer/dryers in their basements. People like me, who live in a brownstone/town-house DON'T. The other problem is - is it legal? A lot of landlords pooh-pooh the idea of getting washer and/or dryers in tenants apartments, because of the extra electricity drain (a lot of older buildings here don't have the greatest wiring), and the water hook-ups (the electrical costsis estimated at $14/year, based on 8 loads week.That's good for me!).

After studying the reviews - particularly the one from Witzkeyman "Louie Arrighi" - a fellow NYC'er, I felt that his enthusiastic thumbs-up (and wonderful video), I would 'take the plunge.'

Even though I ordered it yesterday, and they said I'd have it delivered by this Tuesday, I was VERY pleasantly surprised this morning, when FedEx rang my bell, and ... delivered it.

After learning the 'do-not's' here (particularly about installing the bottom plate correctly), I had the machine up & running within 10 minutes (not to put anyone down, but, I found that the people who did gripe - about putting on the plate the wrong way, etc. - would not have had these problems...if they just read the instructions, which, yes, I hate them too, but they were very easy and fast).

I'm one ecstatic apartment dweller now. This machine does what people like me need it to do; it does the day's load. The sheets from the bed. The towels & such. It's NOT a machine to give it a week's worth of laundry, and that's a blessing - to me. I don't have to collect dirty laundry all week, I can have it done, and ready for wearing the next morning.

When it's spinning the clothes out (jeans are a great clothing item to judge by) at the end of the cycle, it really, REALLY gets the water out - to the point that the clothes are only slightly damp, and not soaking wet.

Since it's been a really hot summer here in Manhattan, it's a perfect time to put this machine through it's paces. Every other day (color/white alternate), I'll put a load in after I've had dinner. Within about 15 minutes, the machine's finished, and I hang the clothes up to dry. By morning, they're good-to-go.

As I said, the reviews here on AMAZON are always very important to me, especially when I'm not familiar with the product. Besides Witzkeyman Louie Arrighi's helpful, informative video about the Haier (by the way - the name of the company is pronounced like 'higher,' NOT like 'hair.' If you ever see a commercial of theirs - overseas - they say 'dream, think, etc. Haier'), I also found Vlad from San Francisco's review helpful. I also took note of, because, while he had difficulties, he did say that AMAZON did try to help, and I strongly agree with those words. Another reviewer (name escapes me) addressed the drying question. He said that the clothes were so slightly damp, he'd dry them on a rack or a line. Saves money, and helps prevent wear on the clothing. He was 100% spot-on.

To all of you, I owe you a thanks for your advice.

In conclusion - I had a Haier air conditioner at my previous address, and got a new one when I moved here (see my review on that), and having had terrific experiences with Haier, and putting them through tough work, I was doubly-sure the Haier HLP21N Pulsator...Portable Washer would also make me happy. And it has.

review_title: this is the best purchase I have ever made!
review_text:
I have had good purchases and bad purchases from amazon, from receiving orders on time to not receiving them at all or receiving the wrong items. This machine is the absolute BEST purchase I have ever made. I researched this for days, read all the reviews and decided to make the purchase. I received it in a timely fashion and it was in perfect condition. Putting it together was a breeze. You screw on the bottom plate, level the wheels, hook up the water hose and put the drain hose in the sink. The manual is thick and I was worried about missing something, but it literally was that simple. I love that the faucet attachment that comes with it can stay on when you are done. I did some dishes after doing a couple loads of laundry and the sink worked fine. I hooked up the washer again after the dishes.

I did my first load this morning and watched it like a hawk, waiting for leaks or something major to go wrong. It worked perfectly. I did my first two loads on the normal water level and normal wash cycle. I find that you can fill up the drum loosely with clothes and start it. After the water has soaked the top of the clothes, I add a few more pieces of clothing. As long as you don't get too greedy, the washer will work fine. I decided that for me, I like to see the water fill up almost the whole drum (it feels like the clothes are being throughly washed with this much water), so I now use the high button for the water level. The medium water level works too, but only fills up the drum a little over half way with water. I use the normal wash cycle for every load, except towels, which go on heavy cycle. This only takes a little longer to wash.

As for the noise that some people didn't like, I find no issue with. All machines make noise, this one makes noise as the drum moves and when water is drained. Honestly, my room fan makes more noise. I actually like to hear some noise, that way I know it is working.

The machine is bigger than I thought it would be, but nonetheless, it is amazing. It is so much better than having to lug all my clothes to a laundromat and spend a fortune to wash and dry everything. I bought a dry rack and a standing tripod for clothes that go on a hanger, both from amazon as well, and now doing laundry is so easy. I have a small apartment so everything is perfect for me. This really is a great product. I am up to five loads today (yes I fall behind, another reason to have one here instead of driving somewhere) and still, no complaints.

product_title: Haier HLP21N Pulsator 1-Cubic-Foot Portable Washer
review_text:
I bought this item to avoid going to the laundry rooms at my apartment complex, especially in the summer as the room isn't air conditioned.

Overall? Awesome machine. Buy it if you're sick of laundry rooms and don't mind doing small loads throughout the week.

review_title: Use a Level to Avoid Unbalanced Loads - Love This Machine!
review_text:
I live in an apartment and absolutely detest our complex laundry room! It is rarely clean, and the machines are stinky! I have been looking at this Haier for some time and finally decided to take the plunge. And boy I'm glad I did - I love it!

It arrived on time, and was pretty easy to remove from the box and set up. One of the screw holes on the bottom panel (for noise reduction) wasn't flush, but as there are six screws keeping the panel in place, I figured one screw missing was no big deal. As I had no space for permanent set-up, I went for the wheels on the bottom. Easy to screw on and tighten with the small wrench that is included.
The first day, my new washer had a pretty tough workout. Nine loads, one right after the other, with no problems at all.

Load sizes - queen sized sheets, but one at a time with a few other small items added.
2 pairs of jeans, plus a pair of capris - no problem.
6 knit shirts with room to spare.
Bath towels? I fit four in and they came out nice and clean.
So you get the idea about how big your load should be...

Regarding keeping the machine in balance.
If you do NOT have this washer balanced, just like any washer it will shake-rattle-and-roll.
Here's a bit of advise for folks who live in an older complex, as I do. I have a small level, which I now keep with my laundry supplies in the pantry. On wash day, I take the level and place it on the top of machine, then roll the machine to the best location on my slightly uneven kitchen floor, then lock the wheels. Works like a charm! Sometimes the load still unbalances, like if I have a bath towel in with smaller hand towels and wash cloths. Easy enough to lift the lid and rearrange the load.

I highly recommend this compact washer for anybody who lives in a smaller space, and doesn't want their clothes smelling like a cruddy laundrymat!
Thinking about having one shipped to my sister!

product_title: Haier HLP21N Pulsator 1-Cubic-Foot Portable Washer
review_text:
Recently I moved with two kids to a slightly bigger home. Our last rental home had a washer and dryer, so we haven't owned one in awhile. It's a 10 minute drive, (65mph) down the main highway that cuts through town, to the laundromat. Our town's laundromat is usually dirty, understaffed, busy and people stand outside the door and smoke constantly. We started itching every time we wore freshly washed clothes from this laundromat. I started hand washing all our clothes in the sink and bathtub at home. (Anyone who's done this, knows how tiring it is.) I looked at different machines, not wanting to spend a fortune. Wondering, how would I move the unit, if I moved again? (I moved myself last time.)

I looked at state-of-the art high efficiency products at Best Buy, Home Depot, etc. But the price was scary, and the salespersons all said they are tricky to move. I found the Haier online and started reading reviews. Bought it last week, and had it delivered standard delivery. Within 30 minutes, it was up and running and washing a queen sheet. I was afraid to put too much in it. The washer seemed small. I soon realized that size doesn't matter too much. I washed 4 loads of clothes and towels next. The spin cycle really gets the water out. I was able to hang up the laundry and have it dry within a few hours. (Keep in mind, we live in the high desert, and are experiencing a heat wave.)

The Haier was easy to get into my small laundry room. I had a little water leak out of the connection hose, but carefully tightening it, stopped the leak. One time the machine stopped in the middle of a cycle. I reached in and untangled some pajamas from a wad of clothing, shut the lid, and it continued as normal. I like the fact it can sense such a small problem.

I have it connected to the cold water only, so I am using Tide Coldwater. White came out very brilliant the other day. The unit also fills very quickly (being connected to a dedicated water line). Instructions were pretty clear. I made sure the drain hose was elevated, as suggested, to prevent water back flow. So far this machine beats hand washing, and has exceeded my expectations.

12-03-2010 UPDATE: High pitched noise coming from unit while it is agitating clothes. Underneath the washer, I found a bunch of rubberized shavings. In the process of contacting Haier. ***Keep your receipt, they won't do anything if you don't have it.

review_text:
I purchased this product and was pleasantly surprised in its ability to clean most of our stuff. Its small and works very quietly in the background.

Our apartment is not huge, so its size was a consideration. The appliance fits comfortably next to our bath tub where it drains and takes up as much space as two standard chairs stacked.

It takes a load about half the size of the ones we used at the laundry mat and cleans just as well if not better since you can opt for heavy duty wash. I would however advise that you do not over-stuff the machine or it will not clean the clothes on top as well and will end up really stressing the clothes closer to the bottom agitator. Remember that this is a pulsar type of washer so it does not have the common agitator column many of us are used to hence why it is important that you do not over-fill it. We also opted for not installing the wheels that came with the washer since it is much more silent with the rubber bottom legs.

This almost completely eliminates the need to schlep over to the laundromat every week.

I would gladly recommend this product and simply suggest that you understand you are not getting a FULL size washer. If you have realistic expectations about this mini washer, then you will be happily satisfied.

Good luck and enjoy.

review_text: I'll admit I was wary - a washing machine at this price? review_title: A bit noisy, but a good washer
review_text:
I would give this washer five stars if not for a couple of things. First, it was a pain trying to get that bottom plate on. I ended up having to use longer screws than the ones provided, because the plate bowed out so much that the short screws wouldn't make contact with the body of the washer. Second, the machine can be surprisingly noisy. I find that it makes very little noise on big loads ("big" being a relative term here) but makes a lot of noise on small/medium loads, because the drum bangs around more without the additional weight of the water. Consequently, I end up using the higher water level on most loads, even when a medium amount of water would do. That said, I'm pleased with the machine. It gets my clothes, towels and even sheets clean and I like that you can put things through an extra spin cycle to wring out extra water. This is very helpful when you live in a somewhat humid climate and hang-drying things can take so long.

Also, if you find your towels feeling a bit "crunchy" after hanging to dry, give them a few shakes and snap them vigorously a time or two. This de-crunches things pretty well for me.

product_title: Haier HLP21N Pulsator 1-Cubic-Foot Portable Washer
review_text: I see some reviewers weren't so lucky, but mine arrived well packed & dent-free, and it's been working perfectly - I did about 15 washes with it so far. The "rinse" cycle isn't a true rinse-and-spin cycle like a standard full size washer, it is the same as the wash cycle but it changes the water first, so it doesn't spin the clothes while simultaneously spraying water on them. I don't think it's as good at washing clothes as side-loaders or washers that have agitators, but it seems to do allright anyway, using low or medium water level seems to swish/agitate the clothes more forcefully than using high water level. It's quiet enough although it does make some noise when it's swishing/agitating as the motor turns on and off as it changes direction. Hooking up to a standard bathroom sink was easy, I had to use teflon tape on both ends of the input hose. It's great to have a washer in a small apartment that has no hookups and to not have to share washers with other people - my clothes used to wreak of other peoples' scented detergent, and I no longer worry about toxins from whatever laundry detergent they used. This is the age of chemical poisoning, laundry-grade bleach (as opposed to food-grade bleach) and many other detergent products are so full of toxins that they should be banned, actually someday they surely will be. I'm keeping my fingers crossed in the hope that this washer continues to work for a long time.

review_title: Received Defective Machine.  Customer Service Ineffective
review_text:
I ordered this from Amazon. It arrived well packaged. It would have been a cool little machine if it had worked. Or if they had decent customer service. I ran into my first problem when the faucet connection did not fit on my faucet. So I took the connection down to Lowes and bought a new faucet. Don't assume that just because you have a new faucet that it will fit. There were several faucets that looked as though they would fit, but did not.

So then I connect the machine, and it works! The water flows in. And it starts washing. And the water keeps flowing in. The water never stopped flowing in. Periodically the washing stops and the machines kicks out water, while water is still flowing in. I watch it for awhile, wondering if it is supposed to do that. About 45 minutes later, I decide it isn't supposed to do that. The machine never gets to rinse or spin. It just keeps washing and washing and washing. And the water keeps flowing in and out. It never gets to spin cycle unless I switch it to spin cycle and turn off the faucet.

So I call Haier customer service, and they schedule a repair person from AR AC Refrigeration and Appliance Incorporated. I work during the week so we scheudle the appointment on Saturday. Unfortunately, the window is 8am to 5pm, so I have to spend the day waiting for the repair person which I'm not thrilled about, but agree to. The AR AC person calls on Friday morning at 8:30 in the morning saying they are in the area and can stop by if someone is home. I had already left for work, so I deleted the message.

The next day, I wait. And wait. And wait. And wait. I don't even take a shower since I was the only person home and I didn't want to miss the repair person. Finally I check my cell phone messages. The repair person called around 10:30 saying they had been trying to get ahold of me since 8:30 on Friday and to call back. I call back, and the rather unfriendly person says the tech was there at 8:30 in the morning. I inform him that the tech was not here at 8:30 in the morning, that I have been home waiting for the tech for 5 hours and no one arrived. He says that the tech was here at 8:30 on Friday, and I say, that my appointment was for Saturday. Then the person actually lectures me that I should have had the courtesy to call them back on Friday, that the tech is now back in Maryland, and can't come back out to Virginia, and won't be available for another week. Seriously? They show up on the wrong day and then decide to cancel my appointment on the correct day because I don't bother to take time off work to call them back? I say never mind, I'll call Haier and use a different service company.

I call Haier and ask for a different tech person. This time, rather than scheduling the appointment time for me, Haier says that this tech likes to schedule his own appointments, and will call me for an appointment on Monday. I figure they will call me later that day or on Sunday. Saturday ends. Sunday comes and goes. Monday comes and goes. Two weeks go by witout a call from the repair company. I decide that if it is this difficult to get service when it is being scheduled by Haier, what will happen if the machine actually breaks when it is no longer under warranty? So I decide to send it back to Amazon.

Then however, I get a call from the second service company. He troubleshoots the problem on the phone, determines it is probably a defective water valve. However, he doesn't know how long it will take to get the necessary replacement part, and says it often takes awhile. I decide to just sent it back to Amazon since at this point I am a couple of days away from the 30 day return window at Amazon. It doesn't seem right that Haier produces a defective machine but I have to wait an indefinite period of time to get it fixed. And the inconvenience of repairs if it should break down in the future just made the entire thing too difficult.

However, it is so large that I can't take it anywhere to ship, so I have to spend another day waiting at home for UPS to show up. They finally did today at 4pm.

So overall, I got a defective machine, a tech with a bad attitude, and an indefinite waiting time if I had chosen to have it fixed, and had to spend two days waiting around for people to show up. I would not purchase it again.

product_title: Haier HLP21N Pulsator 1-Cubic-Foot Portable Washer
review_text:
I received my little Haier 2 weeks ago from Amazon. It was packed very well, no dent, looks cute. The installation was very easy: I already had a Y adapter on my shower head, so I just connected the water hose with the Y adapter (do need some sealing tape), and threw the other hose in the shower tub. When the washer started to run, I was surprised to find it is even quieter than what is shown in the other reviewer's video, it sounds like a microwave. Later I found it was because the washer was put on my bathroom carpet, which makes a big difference, especially during the spin cycle. I was worried about the hose in the shower tub will start running like crazy when the water is out, but it didn't happen that way. I did put the U-shape connector at the end of the hose (which is not designed for that purpose) , not sure if that stabilizes the hose, anyway if I am away when the washer is running and worried about a flying hose, I'll just put a wet bath towel on the hose, it's heavy enough to stabilize the hose. I did have some trouble installing the bottom plate, the screws are very hard to use, and I still don't understand why the washer needs a bottom plate anyway. It comes with 4 wheels, but I didn't use them. One problem I had so far is that there is one time I put a lot of clothes in the washer, and it seems some important sensor got blocked, and after I started the washer, the water kept coming in and out non-stopping, and I lost all my detergent. But after I took two jeans out, it's back to normal.

========== update at 4 weeks =============
Today the water sensor stopped working again and I lost all my detergent again. Ok, I admit I was being greedy and put too much stuff in there, but it wasn't as easy to fix as the first time, even after I took all wet cloths out, the sensor still didn't work. I tried a couple of things, finally found out you have to slightly tilt the washer so that all water goes out (some water gets stuck under the tub), then the sensor will start working again. oh well, so happy don't have to return it or call the service.

product_title: Haier HLP21N Pulsator 1-Cubic-Foot Portable Washer
review_text:
Purchased this washer while I was procrastinating dragging 50lbs of laundry down 3 flights of stairs, into the car, across town, and to the laundry mat. We live in a tiny apartment with no laundry facilities. I read a few reviews of it leaking, being hard to balance, or generally malfunctioning, and felt a little nervous - but definitely ready to take the risk and try it out for ourselves.

The set up took about twenty minutes, and the instructions are great and really easy to understand. Personally, I was expecting a way smaller capacity(!), but it is definitely still on the "small load" side. I purchased a beautiful handmade afghan (double size) this afternoon from a thrift store nearby, and wanted to wash it before use. I was pleasantly surprise that I could fit it in our washer!

I have had no problems leveling the load, which I heard was an issue for some people. (Honestly, we didn't even use a level while setting up the machine as the instructions say since we didn't have one around)

I think the key is to be realistic with that you're expecting from this portable washer. I think it will definitely not live up to expectations if you're trying to jam it full of clothes, but if you're doing reasonable loads (maybe...1 pants, 3 shirts, some undies?) and follow the instructions for set up, I really don't see why this washer would not work.

It's extremely well built, the hookups are really easy to install (both initially and every time you use it), and it's really quiet!

Another plus is that the spin cycle is really effective and dries the clothing really well. So far, everything has been completely dry in about 12 hours - if you're doing an early evening wash, it will definitely be ready by the next morning.

This is the first review I've written for something I've bought on amazon, and it's for a good reason - this washer has exceeded my expectations and I'm really, really happy with it.

review_text:
I have washer/dryer connections in my apartment but wanted something small and portable enough that I can move it by myself when necessary (I'm not very big). This washer is exactly what I was looking for, and I wish I knew about it ten years ago! I don't believe it's mentioned anywhere else, but it will also hook up just fine to a standard washer's connection. You can buy additional equipment if you want both hot and cold water; I just picked cold, which seems to work fine.

What water level to use? I fill the washer by dropping the clothes in loosely one at a time, without doing any jamming whatsoever. If the clothes reach all the way to the top, I use High. Halfway to 3/4th of the way up, Medium. Less than half, Low. I've not had any problems with water overfilling or sloshing over the side on High.

It is a small washer, but for one person it's plenty. I had two week's worth of laundry when this washer arrived. I did one or two loads per evening for about a week, and then I was disappointed to have run out of things to wash - it is that cute and that fun. It can also do queen-sized sheets and blankets, but (probably) not comforters.

For other people who hang-dry, the biggest problem is running out of space to hang things. I've worked out that instead of separating clothes by whites vs. darks vs. towels, now it's pants/towels vs. socks/undies vs. shirts, with shirts washed last so I can use the hangers for the pants/towels first before they go into the shirts. As everyone else has mentioned, stuff comes out nearly dry already and it doesn't take long to dry the rest of the way.

One of the holes in the plate didn't match up with the hole on the bottom, so we left it off (the screw, not the plate). Haven't seen any ill effects yet.

It holds about half a "normal" load of laundry, which is what the average folding drying rack holds, which is great. No finding furniture to drape wet clothes over to dry! The pulsator design means no agitator for your clothes to get caught on and more room for laundry. The only change I would make to the washer is hooks on the back for the inlet and outlet hoses. There is a small hook for the power cord, but no where for the hoses. Currently, I put them in the washer tub and close the lid on them.

Overall, it's a great appliance for apartment dwellers, and with the money you'll save on laundry bills, pays for itself in a short amount of time.

product_title: Haier HLP21N Pulsator 1-Cubic-Foot Portable Washer
review_title: The BEST appliance I ever bought!
review_text:
If you are skeptical-DON'T BE, the washer works fantastic and it's exactly what apartment dwellers need. I read every review and was VERY skeptical and I'm still amazed at how well it works and I have had it for a few months now.

It arrived packed very well and was easy to remove. I read many complaints about assembling the bottom plate and it's not that big of a deal. All it does is protect the motor, it will not hinder the machine to operate properly if it's not perfectly lined up -just line up as best as you can and put the screws in tight. I am a female and I screwed it on with no problem. Yes, it takes some effort, but what do expect? It's a washing machine not a hair dryer!

The faucet hook-ups: They can't make the hose hook-up to fit every sink in the world. I used it in my kitchen and my bathroom. I did have to buy a thing to fit the faucet in the bathroom. Here's all you do if the connecter that comes with the washer doesn't work. Unscrew the little tip off of the faucet and grab the one that comes with the machine (metal funnel looking thing). Take it to Home Depot or Lowe's and get a double ended thread thing-someone will be able to help you. I have no idea what it is called, but one side will fit the faucet and the other will fit the hose connecter for the machine. You have to use the "washer" inside the large end of the metal funnel (I think that's what it's called the black round rubber doughnut thing) to prevent it from leaking from the faucet. The end of the black HOSE that connects to the metal funnel thing (metal funnel things is what actually attaches to the faucet), has this white plastic over top of I guess ball joints or something. I had a little trouble with it, but all you do is press it down using both hands and insert the smaller end of the metal funnel thing and then let go of the white plastic thing with ball joints and it will connect. This sounds strange, but you will know what I mean when you see it and try to attach.

Size: No it's not the full size machine you have used in the past, but it fits a good bit. Besides, if you have it, your laundry will not accumulate into huge piles because you can maintain it once you have a machine. I washed my queen size duvet cover and two pillow cases and it fit fine with room. Tonight, I washed two pairs of size 40 by 30 length men's pants (1 pair of jeans and 1 cargo pants) and a 2 X shirt, and again it fit fine.

The clothes: yes, it can twist the clothes up, but big deal. Just shake it out, a regular machine twists clothes up too. It's better than going to the laundry mat or making several trips up & down the steps to the laundry facilities in your building.

Noise: Excuse my constant sarcasm, but again, it's a washing machine it's going to make noise and cannot be fully silent. I initially thought that bigger loads made less noise because of the weight, but I have had bigger loads make noise too. I have a complaining neighbor below me and she has not complained of any noise from it. And I use it A LOT and at night up to 11:00 pm (I actually got a load in right now and it is 11:08 pm). Sometimes, the spin cycle can be a loud, but place the machine on a rug and maybe put a radio on for a diversion.

Overall, it washes clothes great; the spinning is amazing it really gets the water out very well. If you don't have a dryer, the clothes or towels and can be stiff, but I use a fabric softener and it helps a little. All clothes will dry stiff if they are dried indoors no matter what machine you wash them in. I have saved so much money by not using my laundry facilities and the machine will eventually pay for itself. I don't have to pay for water, and my electric bill has not increased at all and I do laundry for two people.

I wanted to write a very detailed review for the people who are like me and spend hours researching for the best machine- which is what I did for a month. If you end up with a defective one, send it back and get the same one. Anything you buy in this world can have a faulty defective item. Is it an inconvenience? Yes. But you will not regret buying this machine and you will be so glad you don't have spend half of your day sitting in a laundry mat! For the price you can't beat it.

Go Steeler's! Sorry, couldn't resist.. :-)

product_title: Haier HLP21N Pulsator 1-Cubic-Foot Portable Washer
review_title: Good if you need the space, but not up to par with regular washers
review_text:
I bought this washer to wash cloth diapers and baby clothes as I live in an apartment with no regular washer/dryer. For the most part, it served my needs, although if there were any way for me to install a full size washer I would have done so. The price is not that much less than some lower-end full size washers that I think would do a much better job and be more convenient.

Pros:
Small size
Actually fits a fair amount of clothes - there's no agitator so the bin is bigger than it would seem
Fairly good spin cycle makes hang drying possible

Cons:
Has to attach to sink with adapter (or directly to a water line). Maybe this should have been obvious, but for an apartment this made this a bit of a pain. I had the unit in my bathroom, and attached it to the bathroom sink and drained out the tub. There is a quick adapter included that does make attaching/detaching the washer from the sink fairly easy, but it doesn't contain an aerator so when the washer isn't connected water POURS out of the faucet. I bought a separate adapter that did contain an aerator, which made that a little better, but made filling the wash tub really slow. The result was that a "normal" load would take about 45 minutes, compared to 35 with the shared full size washer in my apartment complex.
Changing the cycles is confusing. The three main cycles (quick, normal, and heavy wash) are easy, but you are supposed to be able to change the rinse and spin cycles as well. I wanted to add an extra rinse for the baby clothes, but it was difficult to do without constant monitoring so that I could stop the washer at the right point in the cycle, turn it off, and restart it with the new cycle. Maybe I just never figured it out but I tried zillions of combinations and the manual wasn't very helpful.
Just doesn't seem to get things as clean as the bgi washer - again, maybe obvious but worth pointing out.

So, if you absolutely need a tiny washer, it works okay. But if you can I think you'd be better off with a larger washer.

product_title: Haier HLP21N Pulsator 1-Cubic-Foot Portable Washer
review_text:
I just purchased this washer and started using it 4 days ago, doing 2 loads everyday so far. I was a little worried because of a lot of bad reviews on this washer, but I was pleasantly surprised! We have a 3.5yo daughter and for 3 of us the washing can cost a lot in an apartment, but this is going to be a cost saver.

I had no problem like others say about the water level being at high. If anyone is that worried, maybe leave it on medium, but after the water reaches medium level, you can hold down the water level button to increase the water level a little more (it adds water on command by doing this). We have relatively hard water so our detergent doesn't sud as much, but we just use the cold water tide and it is all good. If we have softer water we would probably use he detergent for sure.

I also had no problem with water going everywhere like many others say. We have the washer on wheels, and we put the hose into the sink and put a 7lb weight on the hose. I suppose anything would work just so long as it is heavy enough to keep the hose in place :)

It got uneven once when it was spinning (I was washing a bunch of adults' pants), but once i stuck my hands in and evened the laundry out, it was all good. It doesn't re-fill the tank like others say - it just keeps going with whatever they were doing at the time. We also found it relatively quiet, and each cycle is quite quick anyway it has not bothered us so far. So so much better than the apartment washer and cleans things a lot better. Once done, we just wheel the washer back into the storage and we don't see it until we need it!

I highly recommend it to people who live in an apartment and feeling that they spend too much money on laundry. As long as you are fine hanging clothes out, it should be the biggest money saver. It is also the spot-on size for people who are doing cloth diapers like us! I gave it 4 stars because we haven't been using it for a long time, but we will see how it goes and report again.

product_title: Haier HLP21N Pulsator 1-Cubic-Foot Portable Washer
review_text:
We ordered this washer because we moved to an area that had no laundromats, and most people relied on friends who had washer and dryers in their homes. We didn't have any friends when we arrived so we didn't have anywhere to do laundry. For a while I was hand-washing clothes but that got old really fast! Finally we purchased this and it made my life A LOT easier! Here were some issues though:
Hooking it up to the faucet was a bit of a problem. We never figured out how to not have it spray everywhere when we turn the faucet on max, especially when the tub is done filling and the water gets backed up in the hose (hopefully that makes sense). We just got used to it though. I'm sure if you had a hardware store close by (we didn't) you could figure something out.
Also the clothes are always SOAKING when they come out. Obviously they are wet because it's a washing machine, but they were literally dripping. The spin cycle didn't do much. I usually reorganized the clothes and ran the spin cycle a few times. We didn't have a dryer either so I ended up hanging the clothes up on a line through our apartment. I suppose if you had a dryer the wetness factor wouldn't be an issue.

I would definitely recommend this product though. Although it's kind of bulky it fits in our bathroom and we can maneuver around it. We live in a tiny studio apartment so we're used to being cramped. In a regular-sized bathroom or apartment it really wouldn't be an issue though.

product_title: Haier HLP21N Pulsator 1-Cubic-Foot Portable Washer
review_text:
I am sort of laundromat-phobic so my husband suggested we purchase a Haier washer and dryer set for our new apartment. After skimming through about one hundred reviews and some deliberation amongst ourselves, we decided to purchase the HLP21N Pulsator 1-Cubic-Foot Portable Washer AND the HLP140E 2-3/5-Cubic-Foot Compact Tumble Vented Dryer.
I received this little washer in the afternoon and installed it immediately. I am very pleased with how easy it was to install the casters (rollers) and set it up in my kitchen. The instruction manual was lacking in information but the hardware was labeled for user convenience. Assembly was simple, given you have the proper adaptor/hook-ups to your kitchen faucet or other water line.
In no time, this washing machine was ready for use. I was cautious about how many articles I placed into the tub as it seemed unstable and rocked (for lack of a better term) from side to side. I'm sure this has to do with "balancing" the basin but for some reason I couldn't get the drum to sit perfectly in the middle of the machine. No matter, it worked fantastic and I probably had enough room for 3 more baby blankets!
NOTE: I opt to avoid overloading this appliance. I don't know if the machine is durable enough to handle heavy duty items like sleeping bags or comforters. I will still have to brave the coin-op place to get those "cleaned", eek!
I used the quick wash setting with hot water (turning on the hot water knob on the faucet) and the basin filled quickly. The machine automatically halted the water flow once it filled to the selected depth (I didn't have to turn off the faucet until the spin cycle started) and the drum began to agitate left and then right. I was so surprised by how QUIET the machine is even in spin cycle. The water drained into the sink with no leaks anywhere on the hose (a reoccurring complaint I found on other consumer reviews) and I found my clothing to be only semi-damp, not heavy, not dripping. Dryer ready!
It is a very efficient, space conserving, and from what I understand, a money saving machine especially if your complex has paid water utility, like mine. I won't have to go to the laundromat to wash our regular clothing or linens.
I do have a few concerns regarding the longevity and dependability of the Haier products based on both personal observations and consumer reviews. So far, the washer and dryer seem to be of good quality. This is my first review based on my maiden use of this washer. I will update this review with photos and my personal experiences in a month's time. I am hopeful that this product stays with my family for years to come.

review_text: I was really excited when the washer arrived. I'm looking forward to donating this machine when it becomes too much to stand.

product_title: Haier HLP21N Pulsator 1-Cubic-Foot Portable Washer
review_title: Better Than I'd Hoped It Would Be!
review_text:
I, like others, dithered for nearly a year before making the decision to purchase this appliance. I'd been getting by with a hand-cranked "Wonder Washer" but an increase in weekly laundry made using that option a bit onerous. I read all the reviews here several times, and Lou's wonderful report with video is pretty doggone accurate and was the thing that finally pushed me over the edge (after reading/watching it five or ten times!).

The box containing the appliance arrived in good shape--it was purchased from Amazon and shipped via Target--but for those trying to hide their purchase from their landlord, the box had a large picture of the machine on it in full color. It wasn't an anonymous beige box, not by a long shot.

I followed the instructions (using tips I'd picked up from reading all these Amazon reviews) and got the thing set up toute suite. I agree that having an electric drill makes putting on the bottom plate much easier--it went on without too much fuss and lined up well, but I could see where doing it manually might be a bit of a 'drill,' pardon the expression. I had zero difficulty with the hoses--didn't need to move the discharge hose from one side to another, so that was a plus, and the washing machine 'fill' hose screws on with no drama. The fittings to hook the hose to the faucet went on an underused sink in the bathroom with no issues. The hose clips on the faucet fitting snugly with no leaks.

I have to say that I can't believe how WELL this machine works. Despite its small size, it can do a decent load of wash--just don't pack the stuff in and don't be greedy. A normal cycle is just over a half hour, and the clothes come out quite clean. For people who are complaining that their spin cycle isn't working or they have water remaining in their machine, I would suggest they ensure that their machine is level before assuming it's defective. My machine spins my clothing so well that everything is dry in no time on an outdoor line, and the polyester stuff is almost dry as I pull it out of the machine. My machine is also quite quiet--and I'm betting this is because I have it positioned on a level surface.

If I had anything to gripe about, I'd say the smell of the hose is pretty nasty at first blush. It smells like burnt 'something or other.' The stink does dissipate over time, though, and it's not enough of a sticking (or stinking) point to cause me to lower my five-star grade on this item.

The price of this beauty has come down a good deal since I first started coveting it, and the price I paid was around two hundred bucks plus state tax (the order fulfiller, Target, does business in my state). So far, I have no complaints as to the delivery, the way the machine works, or the price. I wish I'd bought this thing sooner!

I am editing this review to add that I've had this item about a month, now, and I am even happier with it today than I was after the first week! When I think of the number of times I threw ten to fifteen bucks at a fetid laudromat, I regret having dithered about making this purchase. The "hose stink" I mentioned above is totally gone, the machine is doing a dozen loads a week without breaking a sweat, and I am overjoyed with it. At this rate it will pay for itself in no time.

UPDATE: I've now owned this machine for five and a half years (my, how time flies). I only use it during the summer months and the occasional weekend, as I have it at a holiday home, but when I am using it, I am using it a lot (several times a week, sometimes more than one load) and it continues to work superbly. This is probably one of my top five purchases from Amazon.

product_title: Haier HLP21N Pulsator 1-Cubic-Foot Portable Washer
review_text:
I was hesitant after reading the negative reviews, but with a big majority of good reviews; knowing this model is very popular in China, I went for it. I've only done two loads, but I'm impressed, and have some tips for your set-up.
I started going through the instructions, one step at a time, and realized the instruction book jumps around, so I advise reading it all through before starting. The instructions tell you to fasten the bottom plate with the six screws, then after that, it mentions re-routing the drain hose if need be to the other side of the machine, which you have to do before you attach the bottom plate. So off goes the plate to put the hose through the plastic-capped hole on the other side. I was prepared, from review reading, that the holes in the plate and machine wouldn't line up perfectly, and you kinda push thru the metal with the screws. I used plumbers tape at fill hose connections, as recommended. I didn't have any leaks. I replaced the leveling legs with the casters, and it was level w/o adjustment.
I followed the instructions to select low water level, start the cycle, and when it starts to wash, pause the cycle, open the lid and add your detergent/bleach, then clothes, and then select a higher water level before continuing. And I liked the advice to use the quick wash cycle, fast and clothes were plenty clean.
I'm very happy to not have to go to the laundromat, maybe to dry in winter, and can recommend this machine.

product_title: Haier HLP21N Pulsator 1-Cubic-Foot Portable Washer
review_title: Great for small spaces! Small loads
review_text:
After buying in February 2011, I used the washer at least 2x/ week. It is good for small loads or 1-3 days of outfits depending on body size. Word of caution: this is an appliance that takes water from your sink and while it NEVER overflowed, you should still be present during its wash cycle.
This item goes great with the compact dryer.
Here's what I did in my TINY Chicago Studio apartment: The washer fit right next to my sink. I hooked it up and drained it into the sink. I put the dryer by a window and bought two different vents from Home Depot- one to fit and exhaust out the window and one to vent indoors. Since both appliances use 120v, they were ok to use in my place without causing danger or needing a special outlet. There is a learning curve: they cannot be overloaded. Use the highest setting for water in the washer and hottest setting for the dryer. Since they are more likely to be used in smaller spaces...they do make noise, but not any more than a normal washer in a basement or closet.
You will be happy you bought these! Again...don't overload!

product_title: Haier HLP21N Pulsator 1-Cubic-Foot Portable Washer
review_text:
I've owned this washer for 7 months and love it. I do at least 5 loads of laundry every week and have had no problems with leaking or clothes not getting clean. The washer arrived double boxed with bubble wrap, and I had no trouble putting it together, even the dreaded metal plate on the bottom. As a gal with limited tools, I had it set up and working within 30 minutes.

Issues you might want to think about are:
- The wheels included are terrible. I went to Lowes and got wheels which make it easier to wheel the washer around the house (it lives in the kitchen but I use it in the bathroom).

- The spin cycle is very strong. The upside is that clothes come out nearly dry (I had to use the local laundromat and was stunned how wet the clothes came out of those washers). The downside is that clothes can stretch.

- Without a dryer your clothes will have lint on them. A cheap lint brush resolves the issue.

Overall, this is an excellent product that I would highly recommend.

product_title: Haier HLP21N Pulsator 1-Cubic-Foot Portable Washer
review_title: Give it a try. For the price why the heck not?
review_text:
All told, I spent 16.5 years in various apartments without washer and dryer hookups. That's a long time to go to the laundromat, and even when I didn't spend the time doing it in the laundromat, I paid a fortune for wash and fold. And about a year ago, I received this washer as a Christmas gift. I LOVED it! It took me a few times to figure out how to get it to complete a cycle (hint, all the lights have to be on, wash, rinse, spin. Otherwise, it will only wash). I found it held approximately 1/3 of a "normal" washer load, so for my family of 4, to keep up, I did 3 loads a day. It could even do King Sized sheets, but only one at a time. The only thing I couldn't fit were king sized comforters.

What I liked about it was it was super customizable. You could run any combination of cycles, water levels and you can even control the temperature from the sink. I was able to do a hot wash and a hot rinse. I've since moved to a house, and I miss that feature on my new full sized washer. Don't let the size fool you. This is a "real" washer, and your clothes come out clean and not sopping wet. I've never felt the need for the spin dryer step that other reviewers have mentioned. If you are really concerned about it, just run another cycle on spin.

PROS:

Sink Hook-up
Regular house current (110V)
Custom water levels and cycles
On wheels

CONS:
Small load size
The sink connection was sometimes leaky, but a washcloth over the faucet kept it from spraying all over the place.
On large or unbalanced loads, it is a little loud. We lived on the second floor, so we were careful to only do laundry when our neighbors were out.
