review_text:
UPDATE 2:

I've had this for 3 years. Working as well as the first day. I use it 3 times a week, some days several times a day. One of the best things I've purchased. Very convenient and saves water compared to a larger washer. Initially I made the mistake of choosing the small cycle for medium loads, which resulted in suboptimal rinsing. However, using the appropriate load size selection for my loads has eliminated this problem. Also, a BIG plus is that it has AN INBUILT SPIN DRIER. No need to transport washed clothes from one compartment into a separate spin drying compartment. You can put it in the washer and forget about it, go do something else. Great machine. It spin dries very, very well. Sad to see it's not offered here any more.

UPDATE 1:

I changed my rating to 5 stars because I've had this machine for 14 months now, and it has been running as well as the day I bought it.

I found that I don't have to run any cycle twice to get the detergent off. For the past nine months I've been running my small daily load using the low-water level only once each for each load, and I find this quite adequately gets rid of the detergent. Overall, it's a great machine.

ORIGINAL REVIEW:

I have had this for a month. Works great. Initially there was a water leak where the water entry hose entered the machine, but I read the troubleshooting portion of the instruction manual and followed the instructions by rescrewing the hose back on correctly, and there has been not a drop of water leakage since. This machine has saved me a lot of time and hassle, since I used to hand wash some workout clothing every day and didn't want to waste a lot of water by using a regular sized washer on small daily loads. I recommend this machine if you need to do a small daily wash load and want to save water but don't want to spend time hand washing.

product_title: Haier HLP21N Pulsator 1-Cubic-Foot Portable Washer
review_text:
This review is my first on Amazon.com. In fact, I didn't even buy this item on Amazon (see why below). But it has made such a difference in my life that I owe it to my fellow consumers, whose reviews I usually heavily rely on, to contribute to the conversation.
My husband and I decided to purchase this small washing machine after years of patronizing the local laundromat. Although we're still cool sharing the machines with the local park bums for heavy items like jeans, bed linen and bath towels, we felt the clothes of our newborn baby could use a more exclusive treatment. There's no hook-up in our city apartment, and no much space either to install a washing machine. We were thrilled to discover this Haier product. Not that vendors provide you with a dazzling number of options, mind you--which I find mind-blowing, BTW, especially compared to the European market; it's not like NO ONE in the U.S. lives in crammed city dwellings or in hook-up-less flats; but that's another conversation, I suppose.
Anyway, after reading all the reviews, we figured that if the machine we'd receive was faulty, we'd find out very quickly (Haier seemingly has a significant quality-control issue); we also learnt there was nothing to expect from Haier's customer service. So we decided to purchase our machine from a vendor with a brick-and-mortar location (Home Depot) so that we could simply return the faulty machine physically before the return policy expires... then order a new one.
Thankfully, there was no need for that. Our machine left the factory flawless--lucky us. As expressed by many reviewers before me, this device is a dream-come-true. It's been used once a day on average for the past 3 months and is still going strong. Once, the hose that connects to the faucet leaked. Extending it to the sink and back had loosen it up. All it took to fix it was to tighten it--that was 2 months ago.
In a nutshell:
This machine is a simple computer that only lets you choose the level of water and the length of the cycle (3 options). However, because it is hooked to your faucet, YOU choose the water temperature.
Because you can pause, switch, select Wash, Rinse, Spin at will, you can create your cycles at whim: skip Spin for your delicates (a good idea given how powerful this small machine's spinning capability is--leaves your clothes quasi-dry!); repeat Wash for a more heavily soiled load; repeat Rinse if you put too much soap. Sure, that requires you to be around and pay attention while the machine runs, but I find it a very small price to pay for the benefit of washing clothes at home.
We use this machine for baby clothes, but also for our underwear, shirts, T-shirts and other relatively light items. It's definitely one of the best investments we've ever made.

review_text:

Last week, the motor gave out and made a humming noise, and the tub didn't spin. I didn't realize there was a problem until I had put all my clothes in, and the water had filled to the top. When it didn't agitate the clothes, I realized something wasn't right. After watching it a while longer, I could smell something burning. I turned it off and unplugged it immediately. Then I plugged it back in so that I could drain out the water!

I called Haier customer service and learned that there is only a one year warranty on parts and labor, which meant I was out of luck. I found a repair guy who could come out and replace the motor for me, but I can't even order a motor without being charged an arm and a leg! At the end of the day, I would have paid as much as I did to buy this guy in the first place. Looks like it's going to the junk yard :(

It still gets 3 stars though because it worked well for the short time I had it, and basically paid for itself considering I would have had to pay $3/load if I used the public machine.

product_title: Haier HLP21N Pulsator 1-Cubic-Foot Portable Washer
review_text:
After reading all of the reviews and taking a deep breath we ordered this Washer 8 months ago...and since then it has paid for itself time and again! This little wonder has roughly the same weight and footprint of our vacuum cleaner-storing easily in our hall closet. It is the perfect size for 1-2 people.

While I do love my washer-it can be a bit temperamental. I have developed a rhythm of first plugging in the machine, then attaching the intake hose to the kitchen sink (this required a different adapter than the one that came with it), pulling the machine over and locking the wheels so the hose is taut, wrapping the exhaust hose around the intake hose (if you do not do this it WILL fall out of your sink and it WILL flood your kitchen), then turn on the machine (assuming the standard settings are fine, which they usually are) and press start, then turn on the faucet. When the drum is full of water the hose should automatically disconnect. Midway through the rinse cycle you will need to repeat this process. I have this process down to a science, I enjoy it and it works well for me-But I had to learn it from a few loads of trial and error.

This is a great washing machine for me, but it is important to note that if you are used to a more traditional laundry set up there will be a learning curve.

review_title: small, simple to use- everything I've wanted
review_text:
We wanted the convenience of having a washer and dryer but we have very little space (~650 sq ft apt). This was definitely our solution. It's small, easy to use and takes care of ~90-95% of our routine laundry. Between the 2 of us, we do anywhere from 1-4 loads/week. Some things to look out for- we do have 2 furry dogs. It doesn't take out as much of the fur as your standard-sized washer. You may need to wash it in smaller loads if clothes are really dirty. Overall, I'm still really happy with the purchase at almost 1 year later and given our current city accommodations, I would purchase the product again.

product_title: Haier HLP21N Pulsator 1-Cubic-Foot Portable Washer
review_text:
I bought this washer secondhand from someone who owned it for 1 year and I've now had it for about 9 months, and I couldn't be happier. I don't know what I would do without it, ESPECIALLY now that we have a baby! We live on the third floor of a walk-up building with laundry in the basement, and I can't imagine having to drag myself down there every few days (not to mention scrounging up quarters!) to wash baby clothes and burp cloths AGAIN. This machine is the perfect size for doing baby laundry - two loads (one whites, one colors) and it's all done! Including a baby blanket or two.

It's worked out wonderfully for adult clothes, too - I hardly ever have to use the basement machines unless we have a TON of dirty clothes or lots of towels or blankets.

An average load for us with this machine is one full-size bath towel, a baby bath towel, four adult shirts, and a whole lot of baby clothes (say, 10-12 items). It gets clothes just as clean as a regular washer, too - I don't notice a difference, and trust me, baby laundry can get DIRTY. The "normal" cycle is a bit long, but very thorough (I can hardly remember a time when the "heavy" setting seemed necessary), and for very lightly soiled items I sometimes use the "quick wash," since it really is much quicker.

Warning: If you live in an upper-floor apartment, do be VERY careful to set it up properly and don't leave it totally unattended, per common sense. I've never had the machine malfunction, but once I didn't set up the drain hose securely (my fault) and went to take a shower, and when I got out my downstairs neighbor (and the landlord) were NOT happy about his leaking ceiling! I've since become much more careful and made sure to set up a towel underneath the machine just in case.

product_title: Haier HLP21N Pulsator 1-Cubic-Foot Portable Washer
review_text:
I've had the small Haier washer for about a year now and it's definitely changed my life for the better. What used to be a huge pile of clothes that I'd haul to the laundromat every month has turned into a small and manageable pile that I just throw into the washer every day or two. As far as positive remarks go, I can't do much more than to simply say "it works." Unfortunately, I do have a couple of issues:

-It doesn't clean clothes as well as some conventional washers. I work outdoors and have a tendency to get my clothes VERY dirty by the end of the day. I ran my jeans through this a few times and was satisfied until I later put those same jeans in my mom's Kenmore washer (circa 1988). On a scale of 1-10, 10 being what came out of the Kenmore, I'd say the result of the Haier is an 8. Maybe even a 7. Normal clothes that I don't get dirty in seem to fare just fine.

-There's a tendency for the machine to get overloaded, even if it isn't. Whenever I wash my king size sheets, I have to be sure to run the top sheet and fitted sheet separate from each other, lest the machine shuts down in the middle of the spin cycle where it's sure to get unbalanced. Sometimes, it even thinks it's overloaded with only one sheet in there, forcing me to re-balance it to complete the spin cycle. This also happens if I run a load consisting of a pair of jeans and two sweatshirts, for example. I guess that's just a trade-off of living with a compact washer.

Beyond those two drawbacks, I can confidently give this washer two thumbs up. The bottom line is this - if you live in a smaller place that is incompatible with a conventional washer/dryer setup and are forced to visit the laundromat every week/month/whatever, then you should buy this. You won't regret it. (Even if you do end up with regrets, which you won't, just sell the thing on Craigslist. It'll be gone in 5 minutes flat.)

review_text:
I got this washer because I returned textbooks through Amazon and had money to use on an Amazon credit. I read many reviews and decided to go with this washer. I was so pleased with this washer. I am a woman, and while my boyfriend was at work I was able to set this up in under 30 minutes. Weird thing: washer arrived WITH water in it. I called Haier and they said to call Amazon to see why because it may have been a display model. This would have really upset me to get a USED washer and still paying $250, but my boyfriend said they might have to test them, so I settled with that idea.... Haha.

This little washer is a beast. I works really hard. It holds about 1/3 of a normal load. Remember, when clothes/towels are wet they weight a lot more, so the washer will not continue if you have overfilled the washer AFTER it agitates through the wash cycle and then tries to spin. This is annoying because then your clothes are soaking wet, but what I have done is remove the biggest item (pants, or towel) and let it spin once so the clothes in the washer are rung out, then put the big item back in. This has worked every time for me.

I have never been more pleased with a purchase. This washer spins the clothes as dry as a normal washer so they dry within 12 hours on a hanger. Make sure you have enough hangers when you buy this!

Set up just includes screwing a plate on the bottom of the washer and screwing in a hose to the washer that connects to the faucet. Read the directions for faucet installation, I didn't realize there was a small black ring inside the part of the hose going onto the faucet so it can screw onto outer threaded faucets.

Hope this helps, if anything messes up I will update this, although I don't see that happening!

review_text:

I purchased this washer as a gift for a female friend, it hasn't arrived yet, so I'll be updating these comments shortly.

2/12/2012
Here is my update for this washer....the biggest problem is getting the installation correct with the faucet connectors. The bottom plate was a breeze to install. Many people are complaining of a faulty washer because they aren't hooking it up correctly.

Here are some steps that may help
1.Find the correct washer that's going to sit in the connector being screwed directly on your sink. You can separate from the other piece, if its easier to do this way.

2.Hand tighten then turn your water on, the washer that doesn't leak is the correct one. The wrong washer will spurt water. Use a wrench after you've established the correct washer.

3.This is very important, attach the faucet connector to the piece you just screwed on your sink....the grey end of hose screws into faucet connector.

4.The white end of hose will go to your washer.

The washer works very well, cloths turn out so clean, there's no need to presoak most items.

product_title: Haier HLP21N Pulsator 1-Cubic-Foot Portable Washer
review_text:
I've had this washer for about a year, and use it for everything in a one-person household, even sheets (one full-size at a time). I like things rinsed really well, so I usually run two "normal" cycles, which gives one wash + three rinses, but I did this at laundromat too.

I do have a couple of less-than-happy things to say:

- It tends to tie sleeves or pants legs into knots that need to be freed up to prevent unbalanced spins (and to expose all parts to water for rinsing).

- The spin cycles seem a bit anemic, but I augment them with the use of [[ASIN:B002GEDBIG Centrifugal Clothes Portable Spin Dryer]] which removes ALL remaining water (several cups).

The combination of this washer with the spinner does a great job, and the clothes take only about 4-12 hours to dry on an indoor drying rack, even in the cold and humid time of year (SF Bay Area). It's a perfect solution for anyone without the room for a full-size washer, but keep in mind that it only does about half as much per load as a "normal" washer.

When combined with the use of the spinner (which has to be loaded rather carefully), it is more labor-intensive than using a regular washer, but the results are good and it's worth not going to the laundromat, and I calculated that in one year of use, these two devices have already paid for themselves in laundromat savings. It's been a great deal for me!

product_title: Haier HLP21N Pulsator 1-Cubic-Foot Portable Washer
review_title: Haier, good market niche but why are you still making a three star product when for 50 bucks more you could be 5 star?
review_text:
This is a 3 star product that could easily become a 5 star product with a little more polish and a little more effort.

If you understand beforehand the quirks of this product than it is a great buy and for this understanding the reviews...

First...it fulfills my needs. I live in a studio apartment and abhor taking clothes to a laundry...such a waste of precious time...so it gets the wash done...

Second...it washes well...albeit the fact that it tangles the clothes up by turning clockwise,than counterclockwise, than clockwise, than counter....takes a little too long to do a normal cycle...but this is no problem...

Third..it is real small...the pictures do not do justice to how small...so my weekly wash could easily be 6 loads of this machine...but that doesn't matter because it is working while I am at home doing other things...Note: It's size makes it an interesting purchase also for women who although own a big washing machine like to wash their delicate stuff separate from the rest...

Fourth...it has a nice electronic panel, does a full wash cycle, has two water levels, a quick wash cycle etc...so all of the functionality of a full fledged machine is there...

Fifth...The niche for the studio/efficiency apartment that needs a small personal machine is under-served. This is the only washing machine that I know of that targets this niche...and I actually only moved to this apartment after understanding that this washing machine would work for me.

I am a big fan of reviews and don't buy anything more than $30 that hasn't been reviewed and as usual the reviews explain well the pros and cons of this product and what you are getting so read a lot of reviews before buying this product and my intent here is to sum it up...

A lot of the issues in previous reviews like the water level sensor not working and other obvious mistakes have been fixed so this is a pretty stable product at this time.

Mine was wet on the inside when I got it and I contacted the seller pondering this product had water damage and they explained that the washers were tested before shipping...I didn't believe it at the time but after using this machine for a while, I believe it. The machine was wet due to testing...ok...

Important Cons:
Sixth
Why the assembly of the bottom plate? Why those terrible wheels...
How can a non handy person buy this product and just use it?
Why does the bottom plate have to be assembled later?
The bottom plate is no big deal but from opening the box to using the washing machine was about 3 hours and I am pretty handy and had tools etc....why?
Is there no other why to do this?
So if you are not considerably handy ...have someone come and install this for you...truly...

Haier: please rethink this and improve your product. Add +20 to the price and give me really good wheels, not the very cheap ones you sent....there is no reason for anybody to install a washing machine that connects to a sink without wheels...

Seventh
The connection of clean water from the sink to the washing machine needs work. This is a point of weakness for this product....The connection of the hose to the washing machine on the washing machine is way to weak...I bet that if you tighten the hose too much you will break the connection on the washing machine. I also bet this is a common error...why plastic? I let mine leak a little for fear of over tightening and breaking... There are better ways to do this, so please add 30 bucks to the price and change the hose and the connections on both ends. The sink end is also too flimsy and ify...
Again...if you are not handy don't try to install this washing machine because it is much harder than you would think ...oh, just tighten some screws and attach a hose...very deceiving...

The sink connection closes out the sink.
So if you want to wash dished and clothes at the same time you are out of luck.
I know that you can buy a connection to the sink that allows you to press a button and have water come out from the sink tap and still maintain the connection.

So...

review_title: FIVE defective washers in a row....
review_text:
Not sure if I just have exceptionally bad luck, but I purchased one of these locally a month ago, and have had one problem after another. The store delivered a fifth washer today (3/10/12), and it has mechanical problems. Summary below:

- Washer #1 had a fairly minor defect -- one of the supports at the bottom of the washer was mis-aligned, blocking one of the screw holes for the metal plate. In retrospect, perhaps not a big deal, but I wanted the metal plate to fit properly and securely, so I had a replacement brought out. I did not attempt to assemble or use the washer.

- Washer #2 fit together fine, and I did one washload consisting of a pair of jeans and a turtleneck, with the water level on "medium." The washer leaked - constantly - from three places: 1) from one of the seams on the back side of the washer, 2) from the water inlet hose, at the seam where where the hose meets the adapter which connects to the machine (it's not a seam that can be tightened) 3) Water was also coming from the bottom of the machine, leaking around the edge of the metal plate. I let the wash cycle finish, but had to mop up leaks the entire time. I had a replacement brought again.

- Washer #3 was from a different shipment. It had physical damage (a dent near the bottom, the nearest metal rim on the bottom was considerably warped, the nearest support foot was pulling slightly away from the edge of the washer, and there was a crack along the edge.) The washer was packed on a form-fitting styrofoam piece within a box, so I assumed the washer was dropped or otherwise damaged before being shipped, or perhaps not secured very well within the box.

- Washer #4 had mis-aligned support feet, and as a result, only one side of the metal plate lined up with the screw holes. Thus, it was not possible to attach the plate.

- Washer #5 has a mechanical issue. I did the same washload as before. There is a *very* loud clackety rattling noise that occured during the spin cycles, & it got louder with each cycle. The store salesman heard it over my phone, and thinks there is a loose screw or spring. Also, the washer leaks in two places near the water inlet hose: It leaks at the same inlet hose seam as washer #2, and it also leaks from the rubber seal around the water inlet. I put a washcloth around it, and it was soaked by the end of the wash cycle. I called Haier customer service regarding the noise, and they said that a service provider will call to schedule an appointment.

I can see that this would be a very handy appliance - if it worked properly!!

review_title: It's a Perfect Solution & I LOVE it!!!
review_text:
Oh my, where to start. This is one nifty little machine. It's very easy to assemble and operate. It weighs about 60 pounds and comes in a slide-off top type box. The metal base plate is in the top of the box. Lay the machine on it's FRONT side (per directions) & bolt on the plate. It is a little difficult to get the plate on but not impossible. I only had 2 screws and holes that wouldn't line up straight but I didn't see it as a big deal. The plate doesn't really have any function anyway except to muffle operation noise and protect the inner workings from damage if anything is shoved up under the machine.

The machine comes with leveling feet already installed but it also has casters, which I preferred. Just unscrew the leveling feet and screw in the casters if you plan on moving the machine around frequently. The casters do have flip locks on each wheel so make sure they are in the unlocked position for easy rolling. You can lock down the front 2 if you wish during operation.

Make sure you have a leveler on hand so you can get the machine as level as possible before operation. That helps tremendously with balanced loads. The hoses are easy to connect and make sure you have pliers on hand for and extra snug fit. It prevents the water leaks others complain about. The included faucet adapter did not fit anything in my house properly HOWEVER the water hose hooks up to the end of a garden hose perfectly!! I didn't have a way to run down to the store so I ran a hose through a window and got water to the machine that way. I really, REALLY wanted to use this machine and see how it worked.

I have a handheld shower nozzle in the tub so I used a small piece of rope to secure the washer drain hose to the hose in the shower. The water comes out in a pretty powerful stream and if I had just hung it, it would have come off. The drain hose has to be at least 31 inches high and no more than 40 inches high (also according to the instructions).

My final verdict....it's a wonderful little machine. It's compact but does what the big boys does on a smaller scale. I was amazed at how well it cleaned clothes. The digital panel is easy to operate and I love the clear lid on top.

If you do things right you should have a smooth setup and operation. Read the instruction manual FIRST, it's not very long and simple to understand. I was a bit surprised to have a little water come out of the hose when I took it out of the box but since that seems to be a common report with other consumers, I think that is just a side effect of the machine being quality tested before it's boxed for retail sale. It does not in any way make the machine not new.

review_title: Should have gotten this YEARS ago, some tips...
review_text:
I am a single professional that lives in a small apartment. I do a lot of biking and needed something to get the clothes clean more often. If you are looking at this machine, then you must hate dragging your clothes to the public machines as much as I do (did). I paid 50 bucks less for this model at a different site, but want to give some advice here if you do (and you should) buy this machine.

First off, you will get more clothes in this than you think. From the photo's, I thought that this thing would hold maybe one outfit, but because this uses pulsating jets, you can get a LOT in there. I washed a queen sized fitted AND regular sheet with this with good results.

Second, this machines pulsates water and gets the clothes MUCH CLEANER than the agitating type machines. I can really notice a difference... the whites are whiter and the darks stay dark. They also come out less damp. My clothes dry out in a few hours (the bike clothes are almost completely dry, jeans take longer), but I use a space heater if needed (see below). The pulsators will tie knots with sheets and long sleeves, just check during the rinse cycle if you are washing a lot of big items and untangle them.

Here are some tips that might be helpful...

-Make sure to secure the water drain hose to the water intake hose with zip ties. The water drains out fast into the sink with a lot of pressure during the rinse cycle, so I used 3 zip ties to secure it to the faucet hose so that the pressure does not move it from the sink. I make sure that I am always near by when washing just in case. After all, this thing uses many gallons of water during its cycles and would hate to be out to lunch while the washer soaks my downstairs neighbor!

-I always use fabric softener in the rinse with this machine. because this gets the clothes so clean, it leaves them a little stiff if I don't use the softener. I set a timer on my phone for 18 minutes after I start a normal load to remind me when the rinse cycle starts (there are no alerts on this machine when the rinse starts).

-I make sure to remove anything from the pockets. I had an issue with a quarter finding its way beneath the tub and it made a rattle. The bottom of the wash tub has a screw that is easily removed if something makes its way down there.

-I have a space heater in my bathroom. If I need something to dry faster, I hang the clothes on the shower rack, turn the heater on low and close the door. The clothes are usually dry in around an hour.

Overall, for a small washer, I find this to be pretty heavy duty. It is a solid little work horse that is made with quality parts and was shipped very securely. For the 200 bucks(shipped)I paid for this, I regret only not getting one of these years ago.

product_title: Haier HLP21N Pulsator 1-Cubic-Foot Portable Washer
review_text:
I purchased this item through a different vendor (J&R electronics) specifically because they do an excellent job packing items for shipment. They added extra air cushioning and a few layers of cardboard. Since the machine was getting shipped from NY to CA, secure packing was very high priority for me.

The machine itself is very heavy. I am a small woman who lives alone and I swear, I spent more time trying to muscle this thing out of the box than actually setting it up!

Attaching the bottom plate is not nearly as difficult as I was expecting. The "front" of the machine is the edge that has the control buttons directly above it. To easily attach the plate, hold the plate over the bottom and insert all the screws, inserting the screw furthest away from the last screw you inserted (e.g. insert the screw at 12 o'clock then the screw at 6 o'clock, then the screw at 1 o'clock, the 7o'clock, etc). Tighten all the screws 1/2 or 1 twist by hand. Then, going through the same "furthest away" pattern you did before, tighten all the screws halfway. Finally, tighten all the way being very careful not to strip.

If you simple go "clockwise" around the machine inserting screws, I imagine the plate will not go on/some holes will be blocked. If you sink the screws all the way in on the first pass, you probably will not be able to insert all the screws. As you tighten the plate and it becomes flush with the machine, you will notice some of the tough-to-tighten screws become easier to tighten, as the metal plate shifts.

I put all the screws in myself using a phillips head screw driver. This was probably a bit more labor-intensive than using an electric or drill.

Then, remove the aerator from your sink of choice. Screw on the silver piece, the "sink adaptor". Be mindful that your sink may be reverse threaded (normally things are lefty-loosey righty-tighty, but some older or fancy designer sinks are reverse threaded) Grab the intake hose, screw the white end into the machine. Take the brass fitting and screw this into the gray end. Press the little white ring/widget on the brass fitting towards the grey hose bit to quick release/attach to the sink adapter. Make sure everything is TIGHT. I did not adequately tighten the white machine connection, and got a soaking in return. If you're concerned, throw a dishtowel over the connections to prevent some of the spray.

Take your drain hose and hook it over the sink faucet, or nestle it in the sink. I flop mine over the intake hose and position it so that the opening to the drain hose hook is pointing a teensy bit up and at one of the sides of the sink, so that a "blast" of drained water will just push the hook around the sink. Be careful if you are using a bathroom sink, this puppy drains quick!

Follow directions for loading/operating the machine. Note that this thing does rebalance quite frequently and does the spinup-drain-spinup-drain-spinup-pause thing a LOT. No, it is not broken, it did not quit mid-cycle, it's just a quirky machine.

You do want to make sure you are using HE detergent with this machine, as otherwise it gets SUPER bubbly (we use All Free&Clear detergent plus oxy). After the spin cycle, it takes maybe 12 to 14 hours for clothes to dry.

All in all, setup was not terrible. If you're not handy, it will probably be challending but if you've ever asssembled ikea furniture, you can assemble your washing machine. I promise. Including time to remove the outer box(es) and a single "quick wash" cycle, it took 90mins to get set up.

It gets my clothes clean. because of the hose/other potential water-leak issues, I would not run this machine without being close by (meaning, 1 room away) and periodically checking on it unlesss the hose is totally secured/stationary to something solid. I don't have a good place in my kitchen to do this, otherwise I would be a lot calmer whilst running it. I took away a star because many of the materials used to make this machine (e.g. the hoses) are cheaply made and will need to be replaces probably within the next 12 months depending on use.

All in all, we are extremely happy with this purchase. My upstairs neighbor actually stopped in (he has been thinking about purchasing this model) and my description of the install process basically sold him. No trips to the hardware store. No power tools. Really, if I can install this properly, most people can. If you have difficulty, bring the part in question to your local hardware store (NOT home depot/lowes) and ask for help. Some of the parts/fittings/methods might be confusing to someone who is not mechanically inclined.

I plan to update this as my owenership goes on, but so far so great!

Edited to add:
As of 9/19/16, the washing machine is STILL going at it! The basket has become a little more prone to unbalancing over the years, and one of the pegs that hinges the lid cracked so you have to be careful when opening/closing the lid to ensure the peg is properly seated or the lid flaps a little (like flaps up and down <1CM near the handle). I attribute this partially to aging plastic and partially to us leaving the lid open with the hoses leaning against it at times. The peg broke about 2mos ago so roughly after 4 years of use. Next year we will probably replace the hoses per manufacturer suggested maintenance - I didn't think we would need to as I didn't expect this gadget to be in use for 5 years!

It has paid for itself many many MANY times over - not only in saving trips and $$$ to the laundromat, but in rent. We would probably have moved to a place with in-unit laundry, which would have run at least $100 more per month. Over the last 4+ years we have done an average of 1-2 loads of laundry a day (averaged over a week - 3 loads sheets/duvets, 2 loads pants, 2 loads athletic gear/sports suds, 2 loads work shirts, 4 loads socks/underwear/tees/pajamas, 1 load sweaters/misc, 2 loads towels & household linens. we are a household of two.). I have noticed a bit of buildup of cat hair (we have 2 short haired shedding machines) on some of our clothes, likely due to the fact that we air dry with a fan + dehumidifier rather than a 'regular' dryer. No issues with buildup in the machine itself.

The only items we found this machine has difficulty washing/must go to the laundromat are an ikea loveseat cover (Klippan model, 1 piece for whole couch), a heavy terry cloth hooded bathrobe, a queen size down comforter, and a 6ft by 4ft flatwoven cotton rug.

Edited to add:I bought this washing machine in 2012. It's still going strong (albeit with slightly more frequent unbalancing issues) almost 5 years later. Some of the LEDs go on the fritz and one of the plastic lid hinges cracked (you have to *carefully* lower the lid or pop the hinge back in line, could fix this with epoxy but I'm lazy). Our two adults + two cats household has done 99% of our laundry including queen size sheets & duvet covers in this machine. Worth every penny!

review_title: This little washer changed my life.
review_text:
If you are tired of going to the laundromat, putting money in someone else's pocket and don't have a washer hook-up/lack of space, this is the machine for you! I never liked the idea of washing my clothes in public machines. I've seen people pull some pretty strange things out them like horse blankets, tents and climbing ropes. I resented having to wait for an available machine and having little control over when I did my laundry. From the time I had my laundry stolen last summer, I have never felt comfortable leaving it left unattended. In these past three weeks, I have saved $30 towards the purchase price and gained priceless freedom.

The machine was delivered on time, in perfect condition and installation took about twenty minutes with the help of a mechanically inclined friend. It took me a little while to get used to how the machine operates. With just a few adjustments in the size of laundry load, the water bearing weight of the items and tangling/wrinkling of items due to the lack of an agitator, I am now operating this machine to its full capacity/efficiency.

A few tips I have learned are: Read the manual. It provides great information on how to navigate through the cycles if you need to re-spin a load or add an extra rinse cycle. Separate you wash loads by water bearing weight and by length. Long sheets, bath towels, jeans and long sleeved, shirts have a tendency to get tangled due to the lack of an agitator. I wash all of these items separately with smaller items such as socks, tee shirts and face cloths. Use less liquid laundry detergent/bleach. Set the water level to low and add it. Re-set water level to your choice and load your clothes. Adding two tablespoons of fabric softener to the rinse cycle can help cut down on wrinkles. The 'heavy' cycle has two rinse cycles so you can be sure all of the softener is rinsed out. I personally love the fragrance so I use all of the cycles indiscriminately.

I gave this washer as a four star rating only due the problems I had in contacting Haier. I tried to register my machine on-line, but couldn't enter the model number. I called Haier's Customer Service department numerous times and left messages with an answering service. I never received a call back. When I developed a leak in the water in-take hose, I repeated the same process and never heard back from them. Thankfully my mechanically inclined friend was able to fix the problem with tightening of the hose connection, but if this was problem only Haier could fix, I would be on my own.

review_text: I'm expecting my first child and I wanted a small washing machine that I could use in my apartment to wash my baby's things rather than my building's shared machines.  I bought this machine online and was a little skeptical on how well it would work as I kept reading about leakage, etc... I can say for sure that this washing machine is awesome! I've washed all of my baby's clothes, blankets, stuffed animals, various pillow covers and even a playmat in it.  One word of advice though is that a little soap goes a long way due to its small capacity. It took me a couple washes to figure out the right amount of detergent to use to make sure it rinsed all out.  Also, the machine does tangle up quite a bit with smaller items of clothing but if you lay the clothes folded together along the sides when you load the washer, it doesn't tangle as badly. Hook up was super easy and I had no issues with water leaking from the hose connection to the faucet.  The spin cycle does a great job of draining all the water out as well.  All in all, this washing machine is totally worth the money and a great addition to any home.

product_title: Haier HLP21N Pulsator 1-Cubic-Foot Portable Washer
review_text: I am into RV living and this machine fits right in I have decided to give up the dining table it is just a catch all anyways and that gives me a spot for a laundry center the machine is much quieter than I expected and does a great job you will have to figure out the amount of detergent to use that all depends on the brand you use. don't try to wash blankets but sheets work well I have washed two king size and they came out well. After a year with this machine I still have no regrets it has paid for itself several times over. It does make a bit more noise when the ball hits the side but livable.

product_title: Haier HLP21N Pulsator 1-Cubic-Foot Portable Washer
review_text:
I think that a lot of these reviews are from people who have never had a portable washer before and they give this machine high praise because of the relief it gave them from having to go the laundromat. Another thing is that many of the reviews state they've had the machine for a day or a couple of days or a week, so durability cannot be properly evaluated. I've only had it for a week myself, so can't speak to durability yet either. I'll update the review when it breaks. I will instead address performance and features (or lack thereof). My review will be from a little different perspective because I've had an Edgestar washer/dryer front load combo for 4 years, before buying this machine. I have something to compare it to, so I have a different perspective of features and performance than people who went straight from the laundromat to this machine. The reason I had to replace my Edgestar with this is because the pump started making a whining sound after 4 years of use (and I bought it used) and it sounded like a helicopter in the spin cycle. I didn't want to spend 1000 dollars or more on a comparable LG or the like, so I bought this Haier and the companion dryer. I bought them online from a local big box retailer and did the site to store option.

The reason I need a portable washer is because I live in an apartment without hook ups, and even though I live right across from the laundry room, the machines there are always broken and the wait for the 1 that works half way is horrendous.

My first word of caution is that you really need to make sure you have someone who has a truck to help you get the machine home. I thought it would fit in my 2 door Accord because it is so small, but it is double boxed and the boxes are huge. You've been warned :o)

I like the way it looks, but there are some important features that it lacks and they aren't clearly stated anywhere. The first thing it lacks is a water heater. My old one had a water heater built in, but with this Haier, the temperature must be controlled at the faucet. It does not mention this anywhere in the awful manual. The manual not only lacks details, but is poorly written with grammar and spelling mistakes. Another thing it lacks is a detergent dispenser. You have to add the detergents directly to the tub. It also lacks a count down timer, so you have no clue how much longer the cycle is going to last. That truly sucks! It also lacks a manual dial timer... the controls are electronic which makes advancing a cycle manually virtually impossible. If you want to skip to a rinse or change a setting in the middle of a wash, or add a second rinse (because the machine only does one rinse the normal and quick cycles and there is no option for a second rinse), you have to completely turn the machine off and then back on and press the same button multiple times to get what you want. There is no delay start option. There is no way to turn off the annoying beep. There is no hook for the hoses, but there is one for the cord.

The manual doesn't state how tight to screw the screw the wheels on, so when I attached them, I screwed them on as tight as I could get them. It was too tight and they wouldn't swivel. So, when I tried to roll the machine over an area rug, each half of two of the casters fell off. I had to flip the machine over and reassemble the casters and loosen all of them. Do not tighten them all the way.

This machine doesn't clean as well as a front loader would, but that is to be expected with a top loader. Front loaders have extremely long cycle times and a different wash action, and they just clean better. I had a shirt with ranch dressing on it and I had to wash it 4 times and pre-treat the stain with a Fels-naptha laundry bar and a half bottle of Zout to get the stain out with this machine. I could have washed it once in my old Edgestar and it would have come out fine after the first try (of course it had a 3 hour wash time, this one is only 20 minutes).

This Haier also has some pretty fascinating quirks. I was washing and I wanted to pause the machine to let the load soak, so I pressed pause. The machine stopped and I waited about an hour for the clothes to soak. Then I pressed the play/start button again. The machine washed for a bit and then stopped, beeped, and turned off to indicate that the cycle was done. The tub was still full of soapy water, and the machine should have gone through with finishing the wash and doing a rinse and spin, but it did not. It becomes unbalanced very easily, so know that before buying. When mine becomes unbalanced, it does not do the perpetual rinse and spin as the other reviews and manual indicate. It just stops everything and the rinse light continues to flash. I take out some of the clothes (and I do not over fill the machine ever), and then have to turn the machine off and then back on and start all over. Very annoying.

Another thing that you need to be aware of is that wall of the tub is ribbed, so buttons make an awful noise as the scrape against it. So does the Downy Ball, and you will need one because again, this machine lacks a dispenser and does not tell you when the rinse cycle is going to begin. I don't know about you, but I don't like to baby sit my washer... I like to let it work while I do other things. This one is not hands off.

The water inlet hose enters the machine on the top. Not only does that get in the way of the lid opening (depending on how you have it situated), but also looks bad. The other thing is that the cord comes out of the machine at the bottom right below the inlet hose, so if you have a leak there, it will drip right on the hose. Might be fun if you have a date over and want some sparks, but otherwise, that probably wasn't the best place for that.

The spin cycle is quiet, so that is a good thing! It doesn't get the clothes as dry as my previous front loader did, but it works pretty well. It spins for a few seconds, then stops to drain the water, and repeats that process until the final spin. The wash cycle is pretty quiet too, and the loudest thing this machine does (except for filling) is beep to let you know the cycle is finished (whether it's really finished, or it just got tired and decided to take a coffee break in the middle of a cycle).

The capacity is greater than I expected it to be (while still smaller than my old machine). I washed 1 queen sized sheet and 2 pillow cases and it did fine. I can also do a pair of khakis and a few polo shirts with several pairs of socks and underwear. If I were doing towels, I would put no more than 2 in this machine.

I know it sounds like I hate this machine, but really I don't. I've just noticed some quirks, and perhaps I was a little spoiled by my previous laundry processor because it was more fully featured. It also cost triple what that one did when it was new, so I may well be comparing apples to oranges. For the price, this is a decent little machine if it holds up.

review_text: We bought this lil machine for use in our 27' camper at the lake for summer use only. product_title: Haier HLP21N Pulsator 1-Cubic-Foot Portable Washer
review_text:
First I want to talk about Hi-Tech Media's customer service then I'll review the product itself.

When I received my washer the box was wet on the inside and there was water dripping out of it onto my carpet as I unpacked the product. There were parts falling off of the washer as it was unboxed and there was a dent in the front. Some of the parts were missing from the package and there was a piece included that was supposed to screw onto the bottom that did not even fit. The bottom of the washer had scrapes from where the casters had rubbed against it, which tipped me off that this was a used product (as if the water dripping out wasn't enough).

I contacted Hi-Tech Media's customer service through Amazon. They responded the same day and apologized for the mix-up. They reasoned that the machine was probably next to a new unit and was accidentally boxed up as new by accident at the factory. They then coordinated for the return of the product without my needing to do any work at all and even paid for the return shipping. Through the entire process their representative was apologetic, helpful and quick to take action.

Once my product return was confirmed a new machine was shipped out promptly and arrived in new condition with all of the proper packaging and parts. The new unit functions normally and I am quite happy with both it and the service I received from Hi-Tech Media.

Now on to the product:

This is a small washing machine that can be hooked up to a kitchen sink. I got it because I live in a studio apartment where washing a load of laundry in the apartment complex's laundry costs $3 a load. Plus the laundry room is on the 4th floor, which means I have to haul my clothes back and forth across four floors. That's not the only problem: Everyone in the neighborhood uses coin operated laundry and so the local businesses have a policy of not giving out quarters for the wash. So every other time I wanted to wash the laundry I had to get in my car and drive to the bank 15 miles away to get quarters, or sneak into one of the local laundry facilities that has a change machine and hope I don't get caught (I never wash my clothes there because they charge $7 a load).

With this machine, the [[ASIN:B002C8HR9A Wonderwash]] spin dryer and the [[ASIN:B000UWGLGU Haier HLP140E 2-3/5-Cubic-Foot Compact Tumble Vented Dryer]] I can wash and dry my clothes in the comfort of my apartment.

I also purchased a dryer exhaust vent kit that you put water in to trap the lint but I can't find the product link.

Here is how I do my wash:

1. The washing machine has casters on it, so I wheel it over to the sink, remove the water filter from the faucet and hook up the washer hose. I wash my clothes in the washer.
2. I take the cloths to the spin dryer and spin them for about two minutes to squeeze out most of the water. When they clothes come out of the spin dryer they are almost dry.

NOTE: If you buy one of these, get a screw driver and remove the board from the bottom that locks the motor during shipping before first use. They don't tell you this anywhere in the instruction manual.

3. Then I put the clothes into the Haier dryer to finish drying on the automatic cycle.

Pros:
- No more feeling like a thief because I need quarters to do the wash.
- Don't have to haul my clothes up to the laundry room and back down.
- I don't have to depend on the apartment laundry room having a machine available when I want to do the wash.
- The machine is small and easily wheeled out of the way when not in use.
- Clothes come out clean and smelling nice.

Cons:
- The machine is small so it takes several loads to do the wash.
- My apartment manager complained at first about using water for the washer until I explained it only uses about a gallon of water.
- Connecting and disconnecting the faucet adapter is a chore. I might get a two-way adapter so I don't have to remove my water filter every time.

product_title: Haier HLP21N Pulsator 1-Cubic-Foot Portable Washer
review_text:
This was the best investment I have ever made when living without a washing machine. It saved me so much time/money since I didn't have to go to the laundromat anymore. I was really impressed with how nice it is set up with all of the settings and alerts (like if you leave the lid open etc).

Only down side to this machine is that it can get your clothes really twisted up... It has a tendency to twist up bras...I had to used a lingerie bag for those items to keep them safe. Also, it doesn't have enough space for a comforter or large blankets... I tried that once and had to pull it out sopping wet because it didn't fit all the way...not fun.

Otherwise, I can usually fit quite a few outfits in it or a set of sheets (at most).

I did have to resort to hang drying everything...not so great if you have pets because the animal hair sticks to everything. I managed without a dryer by getting the drying racks from Ikea. Totally do-able!

Great machine!

product_title: Haier HLP21N Pulsator 1-Cubic-Foot Portable Washer
review_title: I am in LOVE with this machine.
review_text: Just like the other 95% of reviewers - I have to say this is a fabulous machine. I wish I would have gotten one years ago. product_title: Haier HLP21N Pulsator 1-Cubic-Foot Portable Washer
review_title: Love it Love it Love it!!!!
review_text:
I ordered this awesome machine one year ago from a different store (w**mart)for $200, which is cheaper than amazon. The setup was quite easy with the exception of the bottom plate like others have said. I have the washing machine in my bathroom which is 4.5ft x 5 ft excluding the space the bathtub takes. It fits into a corner leaving just enough space to move in and out of the bathroom. I also love that it has casters for easy movement around my tiny nyc apartment.

At first I thought I had to buy a special adapter for my faucet because the ones that came with the machine did not work. I tried one last time before I headed to the hardware store and lo and behold it worked! I attach the water hose to my sink faucet and allow the grey hose to release the dirty water into the tub. A few times the hose attached to the faucet popped off probably due to the amount of water pressure built up when the machine is done taking water for the wash. However, I just reattach it and turn the water lower.

I usually use the "quick wash" setting which takes about 25 minutes. Be warned, the machine will be loud noises if the laundry is not balanced! Usually the machine does a pretty good job balancing the laundry itself. I found that a dryer is not really necessary because I hang clothing in my bathroom to dry overnight. No more lugging laundry to the laundromat! The machine can hold a ton of clothing! One load is a week's worth of my laundry. I also wash my queen size bed sheet (I could probably fit two of those in there) and duvet covers. The only thing I really need to take to the laundromat is my comforter.

The machine is very efficient and I estimate that it has already paid for itself over one year. There is barely any noise when balanced properly and my clothing comes out nice and clean. Overall, this washing machine is a great value and has saved me so much time, money, and energy!

product_title: Haier HLP21N Pulsator 1-Cubic-Foot Portable Washer
review_text:
my wife loves it...it's been almost a year now it works perfect. we also had leak problem initially, we used teflon tape for that,it worked. washer makes sound only if it is fully loaded. we use this washer for all our small loads like baby bibs set, soft toys, wash cloths. we put five adult T-shirts for medium water level even if you add one more it makes noise.

product_title: Haier HLP21N Pulsator 1-Cubic-Foot Portable Washer
review_title: Why did I not purchase this sooner?!
review_text:
If you have read the other reviews...yes it can be noisy at times, and yes it doesn't hold a lot like a regular washer. But, if you follow what other reviewers have said...as in making sure the packing materials that get dislodged from shipping are removed from the inner works and you use less detergent...it is an awesome machine! I have washed everything in my small place - then hung on a line to dry...most of my items dry in 2-3 hours! I can wash my towels (2 regular and 2 hand and 2 washcloths) in the morning and they are dry in the afternoon when I get home from work. Another load may be my queen sheet set with 4 pillowcases - washed on high/heavy - they dry in about 2 hours! One thing to note is that most of us are use to putting our clothes in a washer in a swirly fashion. I find that if you casually place items in - and do an accordian type fold they don't make the machine become off balance! I did think I would need to get a dryer...well I don't anymore! EVERYTHING comes out damp...and drys so quickly! GOOD BYE and GOOD RIDDENCE to the laundrymat! LOVE THIS MACHINE!!! Also - I only use about 2-3 tablespoons of detergent...

UPDATE - I have now had this for 18 months - I have NEVER had a problem with it :)
I do about 1-2 loads per day and it is such a work hog! Just remember to not overload it and you will not have any problems!

product_title: Haier HLP21N Pulsator 1-Cubic-Foot Portable Washer
review_text:
I will re-review this product when I have had it longer. I got it last night.
It was easy to assemble thanks to previous reviews. Summary of those.
1. the metal plate goes on as if you are resting a cup on a counter, the bulge goes towards the floor.
2. The screw holes are not punched in exactly the right location. If you hold the plate and adjust it a bit it'll fit in there. I wasn't able to tighten the screws 100% but my plate doesn't jiggle at all and is silent.
3. If you are going to move the drain hose to the other side of the machine, do it BEFORE you put the plate on.

Wow, this thing is SO quiet, significantly quieter than my dishwasher. My clothes are really clean. I ran a few loads.
my problems...
I am having a leak that hasn't stopped even with teflon tape, though it lessened it. thoughts? I'm sure I just need the right configuration. I don't regret the purchase because of them. I will include pictures later. I have a leak where the faucet hose attaches to the machine.

How do you stop the quick sink adapter from spraying everything nearby when you unhook it when you are finished?

Like many others I could hear some water sloshing around in the machine when I got it. I think it was from testing at the factory as others have indicated. There is no indication the machine was a used return. It was immaculate. Is there any way to drain the water out completely when I go to wheel it into my closet?

product_title: Haier HLP21N Pulsator 1-Cubic-Foot Portable Washer
review_title: Poor quality machine and worst customer service
review_text:
I purchased the portable washer earlier this year to wash my newborn's clothes. I purchased it from Walmart online and had it delivered to my house. The first one arrived quickly. But it was wet inside, as if it's used. We called for an exchange, and got a new one. After a couple of months of usage, the washer started to make really loud noises when spinning. We checked the leveling, and it's fine. We called haier's customer service for repair since it is still well within 1 year warranty. We made the first call in August. Now it's Thanksgiving, and the machine is still sitting there. Among more than literally 20 phone calls to Haier and their service provider named Bobby Jones, I spoke with several customer service representatives, their manager, and the manager's manager. There are always approval needed, back order requested, etc. But still nobody shows up for a repair neither replacement. Haier probably has some issues with the vendor, but this shouldn't cause such a pain on customers. This is the worst customer service I've ever seen. We actually end up spending more time trying to have it fixed than actually using the washer. With a 7 month old, I'm still making calls between Haier and Bobby Jones, trying to have it fixed.
Bottom line: it is not a good quality machine and the customer service is worse. I am so dissappointed, and strongly suggest to stay away from it.

product_title: Haier HLP21N Pulsator 1-Cubic-Foot Portable Washer
review_text: Can't believe it's taken me 2 years to get one of these - I always thought that they wouldn't wash as well as the launderette but in fact they wash BETTER! My life is changed - I am so happy!

product_title: Haier HLP21N Pulsator 1-Cubic-Foot Portable Washer
review_title: Great for kid families living in apt!
review_text: I've used it everyday for over a month. It is super small, fits perfectly in our tiny bathroom. I use it to wash my 2yr old clothes everyday. It can also do adult clothes, like shirts, sleep wear, and bath towels, but not heavy outwear. The first thing to know is that if you place the drain hose in a bathtub without elevating the end of the hose, the water will drain out of the machine. If you drain to a sink, make sure the sink is large enough and drains quickly or you will have a big mess. The washer fills quickly and cleans surprisingly well. It is quiet during the cycle - until it spins. If the load is not perfectly balanced, the Haier makes quite a racket - and if even slightly unbalanced the machine beeps and stops spinning. Capacity is limited to a a pair of jeans, a t-shirt or two, and a couple pair of socks. A queen sized flat and fitted sheet together were too much. The touch panel controls are simple, but be careful pushing the cycle button or you may end up with wash only or rinse and spin. review_text:
I live in NYC, and my apartment building doesn't have laundry facilities. Until now, if I wanted to do laundry, I either had to wait until I had enough to justify a trip to the laundromat, hoard quarters, spend an afternoon there, and then lug everything back up, OR wash as much as I could in <a href="http://www.amazon.com/BRAND-NOT-SPECIFIED-Wonder-Washer/dp/B000BTDNEK/ref=sr_1_1?ie=UTF8&qid=1358208218&sr=8-1&keywords=wonder+washer">this</a>, a super small capacity machine with no spin cycle, which meant lots of time spend rinsing and wringing, and waiting for still dripping clothes to eventually dry on a rack. But that's all changed now thanks to this little machine, and I'M SO HAPPY ABOUT IT!

I received my Haier washer on January 7, and set it up January 12. It was pretty easy, taking all of about 10 minutes to get the bottom plate (which I believe is to dampen some of the sound) attached, and to swap the standard feet out for the included casters. I wheeled it over to the kitchen sink, and it only took a minute to determine how to do all the connections. I tested everything for leaks as I went along, and did notice some very slight water seepage at the connection to the washer, but nothing that a bit of Teflon tape won't fix, I'm sure, and I was able to keep it at bay by wrapping a piece of paper towel around it. My first load of laundry was a set of queen sized sheets (no pillow cases). I washed them on the medium water level (probably could've gotten away with low), and the normal cycle including wash, rinse, and spin. The machine took about as long a normal sized washer would, and I notice that it was a lot quieter than I was expecting. Even during the spin cycle, the machine really wasn't that loud - I'm on the 2nd floor, and I'm not concerned about the machine disturbing the neighbors downstairs. The spin cycle is impressive - when I took the sheets out, they were slightly damp. Definitely not dripping wet. I laid them on a wire drying rack in front of a fan, and they were bone dry in under an hour.

I've since done about 6 or 7 loads of wash in this machine, of varying sizes and types of clothing. The machine has handled them all perfectly. It did go out of balance one time (it beeps and pauses the cycle when that happens) but it was easy to rebalance and get started again. But I'm really impressed with this machine, and I'm so, so happy I got it!

product_title: Haier HLP21N Pulsator 1-Cubic-Foot Portable Washer
review_title: Decent washer with a few drawbacks
review_text:
I have had this little gem for a little over six months. I moved into a mid-rise apartment that has three washing machines per floor and with over 25 apartments per floor, it can be difficult to get laundry done in the PM hours after work. Also, I don't enjoy taking my dirty clothes outside my apartment. I looked at this machine for a long time before I made the purchase. It's a good little washer but it is quite temperamental.

1. Don't expect to use the large/heavy setting without problems. Often it will just shut itself off right before it needs to spin to remove the water. I don't do it often but I have washed a queen sized fleece blanket in this machine and occasionally it will just shut off for no apparent reason. This only happens when I use the heavy setting when the water is filled as high as the machine allows. For the most part, I only use the normal or quick cycles and I haven't had any problems with it shutting off midway.

2. This machine frequently becomes unbalanced and will shake, rattle and roll during the spin cycle. The way the clothing is agitated causes the fabric to knot up in the machine. This happens a lot with knits, sheets, cotton towels and denim. It can get a little loud so if you have neighbors, it can be a problem. I don't do laundry after 9pm for this reason. Usually you can fix the problem by shifting the clothing but occasionally it just won't be quiet. If it's severely unbalance, the machine will shut itself off.

3. My recommendation is to do small loads. I only fill it up loosely with clothes to about halfway. I also suggest batching your clothes by fabric type. Since the machine unbalances frequently, the machine seems to work better when the fabric type is similar.

4. Don't expect super stain removal. If you have stains, be sure to pre-treat before washing. Using the normal wash, you wash once and then rinse once. There aren't extra water changes during the wash like in a regular machine. I find that if something is really dirty, pre-treat and in some cases wash more than once. And, use a good quality HE liquid laundry detergent. I use Tide, Clorox 2 and Downy with great results. I tried a cheaper brand (Purex) and it did not clean my clothes at all.

5. Don't forget to switch the water over to cold when you use the fabric softener. Since the machine hooks up to the sink, whatever temperature you start off with is the one you'll finish with if you don't adjust it during the wash. I usually wash in warm and then switch it to cold as soon as the fill is finished (the first water fill on then normal or quick cycle) so I don't forget.

6. If washing towels, don't wash more than two bath towels at a time. The machine just isn't equipped to do heavy loads, like towels. If you want to wash sheets - queen or king sized, only wash one at a time. The machine isn't big enough and it will knot up like crazy. If your sheets are particularly heavy the machine with either shut off or unbalance. I wash queen 800 thread count cotton sheets with no major problems other than the knotting up issue.

7. Get yourself a really good lint brush. You'll need both the tape and the brush kind. This machine does nothing to remove lint. I have long hair and I also have two long haired cats, so everything comes out clean but with cat fur and my hair all over it. Anything very linty will also require some extra maintenance after washing.

8. I did not get the dryer that matches this machine because it has to be vented outside. I got two large folding drying racks from Ikea for under $25 each. You can set them up side by side to drape a queen or king sized sheet over it to dry and they hold a ton of clothes. In a pinch when I need something dried quickly, I'll set up a fan to blow it dry.

Overall this is a great little machine, despite the minor issues above. It has more than paid for itself over the last six months just in the amount of laundry I do. I probably do about 4 or 5 loads per week for one person. The machine is small enough to keep in my tiny kitchen and with the wheels, it's easy to roll it out of the way when necessary. I'm hoping this last for the next two years when I am ready to purchase a home (with laundry in unit!!). So far I cannot complain too much about this machine. Yes, it has issues but it certainly beats spending money on laundry and hauling dirty clothes up and down the halls.

review_title: Took Forever to Get Here, But Worth Waiting For
review_text:
I thought about this purchase for a year and researched it extensively. I knew there was a risk that I could get a machine that leaks, but overall most people seemed very happy with their purchases. Others were saying if it leaks you can just tighten up the connections and it will stop. This appears to be the case.

I ordered this machine on March 4. Amazon said to expect delivery sometime between the 8th and the 13th. When it had not arrived by the evening of the 14th I sent a message to the dealer, Wayfair. I got a message on Friday, the 15th stating that they had 2 weeks to ship the order according to Amazon, and it would ship on the 18th and arrive on the 20th. It did arrive on the 20th.

Today was the first time I have had an opportunity to hook it up. It took about half an hour to get everything set up, including installing the coasters. I am a 53 year old woman and it was not difficult. It just took a bit of effort to figure out the instructions. The illustrations are not terribly clear.

At one point I called the customer service number to ask a clarifying question about the directions, and the guy there told me I should have an installer come out if I couldn't handle it myself. He refused to answer my question at all, and I am certainly capable of putting this machine together. It is not difficult once you figure out what the directions mean.

The machine leaked the first time I turned it on at the coupling where the water goes into the machine. Tightening it with a pair of pliers did the trick. It is important to connect everything as tightly as possible.

The machine is very quiet, quieter than our full-size washer in the basement and much quieter than our automatic dishwasher. I don't know how anyone could have any complaints about it.

I'm very pleased with this product and I'm sure you will be as well providing you don't confuse it with a full-size unit.

The main reason I'm writing this is to mention, unlike the company's customer service department claimed, IT WILL work without being directly connected to a water source. Admittedly, it's easier if connected to a water line but not that much trouble to fill manually.

Here's how I do it: Fill the tub up with water, add detergent, stir the water to mix, add clothes. Next turn on power, select water height to high, press "CYCLE BUTTON" three (3) times for "wash only," then press start. The wash cycle takes about 15 minutes to complete.

Once wash cycle is completed press power button turning off machine. Next, push power button again to turn on. Press cycle button five (5) times for "rinse only." then press start, which drains the water out of the tub. After completed turn off machine and repeat the above "WASH ONLY" STEPS (listed above) but just fill with water. Let clothes agitate in rinse water for about 5 minutes and push the power button turning the machine off.

Repeat "rinse only steps" (above). I rinse clothes two or three times this way. When finished push power button off.

After rinsing is complete push power on, press "cycle button" six (6) times for rinse only, then press start.

There you have it. I use a separate spinning unit to drying the clothes as much as possible before hanging them to air-dry. When drying this I use multiple plastic hangers (at least three) so as not to put marks in the clothes.

Thanks for reading my review and happy washing!!!

product_title: Haier HLP21N Pulsator 1-Cubic-Foot Portable Washer
review_title: The review from 2010 about sounds is OUTDATED: Read this now!
review_text:
For those thinking the top rated review is accurate in terms of sounrds, you're viewing an outdated review from 3 years ago.

This updated washer is called the HLP21N. The previous version had a different letter designation at the right which also had variations on the top of the washer: Slightly different lettering, different colors on the button, there was even an internal lint filter (which the new model does not have).

I own the brand new 2012 / 2013 edition of this washer which people have been complaining about regarding the knocking, banging or extremely loud noises during the spin cycle.

My HAIER HLP21N makes these noises during the spin cycle, even with NO CLOTHES in the washer. It has nothing to do with balance: I purchased a balance from a hardware store and made sure the sides and front were balanced. Once it got to the spin cycle, not only did it make the extremely loud banging / knocking noises, but it was registering as "out of balance", meaning the machine would shut down.

I adjusted the rubber feet, added and removed the casters, and it's hit or miss: sometimes with no clothes it makes no knocking noise, sometimes it makes extremely loud noise.

Now with clothes some have been writing that the reason it knocks or bangs is because of too heavy a load. Sorry guys, you're wrong. The more of a load I put in, in fact, the quieter the washer is. However, no matter how light or heavy the load, once it reaches the spin cycle, the banging begins.

Finally, some others are posting that those complaining about knocking are complaining about the "regular noises during spin cycle". No, these are not normal, spinning sounds. These are literally knocking sounds as if someone is using a jack hammer on the machine during the spin cycle.

So please, those of you dismissing our complaints as invalid, just be lucky you don't have this problem.

If anyone has figured this out, please reply to this message, I'm all ears, because I've tried everything in my power to get this thing to not bang or knock during the spin cycle, and have failed.

---

UPDATE 5/30/13

I've now discovered that damage is being done to the washer every time it "bangs" or "knocks". Take a look at the inside of the drum rim. If you see any type of cracking happening, double check your clothing for white chunks of plastic which will now be stuck on your clothing and possibly ruin them, especially during the spin cycle. Pictures will follow in the next few days.

BOTTOM LINE: HAIER produces a very POOR-QUALITY washer which you literally have to stand next to for 45 minutes while it's operating, to make sure it doesn't flood out your apartment or scrape your walls down to the dryboard due to the unbalanced spin.

IF YOU LET IT RUN UN-ATTENDED, YOU ARE ASKING FOR BIG TROUBLE.

Put another way, have you ever seen so many comments with "helpful hints" as to how to use a plain-old washer ... technology that's been around for over 100 years ... so that the washer won't blow up, or burn out, or flood your kitchen (and anybody living in apartments below) ...?

WEIRD. BIZARRE. WHO NEEDS A "WASHER" THAT NEEDS "HINTS" TO OPERATE? You might as well wash your clothes in your bath-tub, which is EXACTLY what you'll be doing if you purchase a HAIER.

In my case, my front-loader HAIER was $699 plus tax, delivery, and set-up ... for a total of around $800, so I did my best to squeeze back my $800 by using it as long as possible. BUT IT'S BEEN NOTHING BUT TROUBLE. HAIER: NEVER AGAIN.
