product_title: Haier HLP21N Pulsator 1-Cubic-Foot Portable Washer
review_text:
Yup! I purchased this beauty on July 28th, 2011 and today is Dec. 21, 2013.

The packaging was an interesting touch. A big brown box with a shipping label and that's all. Nothing to describe what was inside, so if the landlord saw it, he wouldn't have a clue.

When I opened the box, I saw a nice layer of bubble wrap surrounding--yet another box with all the Haier logos and information AND inside that box was...THE MACHINE! Yes!

It was a very nice job of packing the gadget for delivery, so kudos to *Air and Water Inc.* and UPS for getting it to me with no damage at all.

Setting up the washer was a fun trip, but just using common sense and my ability to solve minor puzzles, I had the process completed in about 20 minutes. Also, *Air and Water* did most of the work prior to shipping. I just had to safely get the washer out of the packaging, install the infamous Metal Plate and stand it up! It was already leveled on the wheels (no wobbling).

The metal plate was just like most reviewers said. A plate with 4 holes for screws, that apparently was supposed to line up with four holes on the machine. No matter how I I turned the plate, I could only get three holes to line up. So, I installed three screws for a snug fit and tossed the fourth screw into my junk box...and that was that!

I read the owners manual from front to back and decided that MY best option was to use the default setting of Normal and go from there. As it turned out, I was right, but most of the time the water did not cover the clothes, so I would have to press the water level button till it stopped running. It got to be a habit, for both the wash and rinse cycles. Wait for the washer to fill and then press the Water Level button until the water stops running. Simple! :)

There is a slight glitch that developed after about a year of use. The timer on the Rinse cycle changed from about six minutes to 90 seconds. At first, I thought about going to the Haier site and see if I could get some specs that would show me how to adjust the timer, myself...but, I never did. I just compensated.

What's the big deal, anyway? 90 seconds of clean, sloshing water should get most of the soap out and then that insanely fast spin cycle will help too. And if my clothes still smell soapy after drying, I will just run them through the Normal wash, again, without using any soap...on the next wash day. Tis a no-brainer, folks! :)

By the way...you may be surprised by the amount of wet lint you will be generating and if you allow that stuff to go down your drain, it won't be long till your drain plugs up. So, I made a trip to the nearest supermarket and bought a pair of pantyhose and cut off both legs. Then I tied one of the legs to the drain hose that goes into my kitchen sink and it catches everything and you may not believe this but, i'm still using the first one, after 2.5 years. I just clean it out after every wash day and It works great!

Another thing I forgot to mention during the Setup, is the connection for the kitchen faucet. All I did was to remove the aeriator from the faucet and the connector that hooks up the water supply hose to the faucet. Then I took all those parts to Ace Hardware and showed them to one of the guys in the red shirts and he recognized it, right now. I said I needed to connect a water supply hose to the faucet and five minutes later I was out the door and on my way home...feeling about ten bucks lighter!

Cleanup is kind of a chore, but it has to be done.

First, I put a plier on the fitting that connects the water supply hose to the faucet and turn it SLOWLY! There is a lot of pressure inside the hose and if it pops off before you can get the pressure released, a little, You are going to get wet! So, be careful. Turn the plier slowly until you see water bubbling out and wait a few more seconds. Then it should be safe to remove it completely.

Second, remember to clean out your home-made lint filter. Just take it into the bathroom, turn it inside out and dump all that wet lint into the toilet and flush it. When the water fills up, drop the sock in and slosh it around a little and wring it out. Don't be a pansy about it. It's just water. And besides...Who's gonna know? Heck, you can always wash your hands afterwards, if you happen to be of faint heart.

Then be sure to drain the hoses. Just get a low sided pan and let the water drain into it. Then, put the hoses and power cord into the washer and gently close the lid. There will be a gap to help evaporate any water that might be left and you shouldn't have to agonize about any mold or mildew building up.

Get a BIG black plastic bag and pull in onto the washer and tear a hole in it for the fore-mentioned evaporation thingie, wheel it into a corner and throw some light stuff on top of it. The landlord will never see it. Out of sight, out of mind. Trust me...it works!

So...that's it. I have a washing machine that works and is dependable. I can dry the clothes on some lines I have strung around the apartment and because the final spin is so scary fast and the use of two pedestal fans to blow the air around...I can be ALL finished by 5:00 pm.

I'm not a shill. I don't work for Haier or Amazon. I did not get the product free for testing. I paid $251.94 with shipping and handling and I saved a heck of a lot more by not dumping a ton of quarters into a coin-op commercial washer.

Would I buy another one? Absolutely. Would I recommend it? Yes, I would!

What a great purchase!

review_text: I have this in my apartment next to my kitchen sink.  It's easy to use and quiet.  It washes small loads and does a fine job. What is unusual is that it doesn't wash clothes by tumbling them, like in a front loader, and it doesn't agitate them like big washing machines with the agitator thing that sticks up and moves back and forth.  Instead it has an smooth agitator on the bottom of the drum that turns quickly one way, then the other.  This makes the water in the machine swoosh up and through the clothes.  The clothes get tumbled around in the pulses of water.  For some reason, this action makes them tangle up with each other more than in other washing machines, though all washing machines do make you untangle the clothes in the end.  Another thing is that stretchy material llike t-shirts get stretched a lot by this action, somehow.  If you put them in a dryer they go back to the right size, but if you line dry them they may be stretched out.  Regular woven fabrics, like sheets and towels and undies and jeans and so forth come out perfect, because they aren't made of that stretchy -t-shirt jersey material.  So for me, this is a perfect helper in my apartment.  I can't tell you how many trips to the laundromat it has saved me and how convenient is is to do a wash any time I want right in my own place.  I notice there are some other similar machines on the market that look good, wash a bit more, cost a bit less.  But I haven't read reviews on them yet. Then I recalled using Vasoline to install a shower head some years ago. I put a glob of Vasoline on each connection. Turned the water on and it didn't leak at all even with the water on fully. Whew! What a relief! That was Tuesday. On Wednesday, I was prepared to begin washing clothes! I put a large towel under the washer to see if there were any leaks. Well, I washed three loads of laundry. I bought this washer 2 years ago. I had calculated out the cost of laundromat visits and 2 years was roughly when the washer would pay for itself. I'm happy to say it is still running fine. I've had no water leaks, it's still very quiet and does the job.

I do have one issue, I wish the rinse cycle was longer. On my machine it only rinses for about 2-3 minutes before draining.

One thing I have noticed is that in other reviews people seem to wash much more per load than I do, One pair of jeans and 2 t-shirts is a load for me. T-shirts alone I wash 5, underwear, 8 boxers or 12 briefs.

It doesn't take much in the way of detergent to get the job done, I use 1 TBSP per load and things come out nice and clean.

Overall, I'm quite happy, If you add in the fact I don't have to spend hours in a laundromat each week, it paid for itself a long time ago.

product_title: Haier HLP21N Pulsator 1-Cubic-Foot Portable Washer
review_title: Great little washer has made my life better.
review_text:
This was a major purchase. I put a lot of thought into it. Read many reviews. This little washer has changed my life after moving to the City (San Francisco) my studio apartment is tiny and I had to go to a laundromat. Now I can do small loads nightly after work, and I dry the clothes on a rack. I can do my weekly laundry a little bit at a time.

I placed my washer next to the sink. And use the water from the faucet and waste into the sink.

The washer is basic and materials inexpensive so don't expect something solid and heavy. I managed to balance mine so that the spin cycle runs ok. If I overload with towels I find spin doesn't work. So I can only do two towels or two jeans at a time. T-shirts, underwear socks all seem to wash well.

I found the connection to the faucet a nuisance.. but better than going to the laundromat. If I had to use the faucet connector I would. But I decided to plumb a line into my kitchen's cold water line and actually plumb the washer permanently to the water line, using a T connection. After 2 months of it being plumbed to pressured water the washer is fine. I even went on vacation without turning the water off, I was expecting maybe to hear a call from my landlord. But it was perfect when I got back. Having it permanently connected makes a world of difference as I don't have to unplug stop doing dishes etc. (Check your apartments rules and get a professional plumber to do this as it can be tricky and leaks are not great for your landlord or neighbors below.)

I still have to connect the waste water though and that is my next project to make this washer perfect.

Due to the connection issues, this is not a walk away solution you need to be around and make sure the sink does not over fill. Remember the sink is being used for dishes, food scraps and washing machine water. And if you using the connector there is always a chance the connection to the faucet you need to make sure it is properly connected.

I love the quick and easy options. The cycles are quick. And the clothes are washed just fine. The machine is easy to use. It is also fairly light, for a washer, so one man can carry it. I carried it from my office to my car to my apartment all on my own.

After owning this machine, I think I would prefer a more solid one. But for now it is great and working. And perfect for my Studio in downtown San Francisco.

product_title: Haier HLP21N Pulsator 1-Cubic-Foot Portable Washer
review_text: I got this Haier HLP21N Compact Portable washing machine as a backup for my regular machine that breaks down all too often. The instructions are crap, but the machine is awesome. First of all, the screws that they provide to attach the bottom plate wouldn’t go into the holes. (I’m an avid DIYer so it’s not operator error.) Luckily, I had some self-tapping screws that worked fine. Second, nowhere in the manual does it mention a piece of plastic that seems to be attached to the bottom of the motor. It’s not shown in the line drawings of the washer in the manual, but it’s not a very clear drawing so I assumed it belonged there. Wrong! After washing 6 loads successfully, this horrible noise was coming from the machine every time the tub moved. I stopped the machine, unplugged it, and removed the back panel. The superfluous piece of plastic had come off and was on the bottom plate just getting in the way. I took it out, replaced the back panel, and restarted the machine. No noise and no problem. There are no instructions on how much detergent or bleach to use, but I just used about ¼ of what I use in my large machine and it worked fine. Not having a fabric softener dispenser is a tiny drawback, but it’s very easy to pause the machine and add it manually. It does clean the clothes efficiently and can wash larger loads than I expected. It does tend to tangle sleeves, but it’s not that big of a problem. I love the quick connect attachment for the faucet. I have it in my garage hooked up to my utility sink. You will need to make sure you tightened the water hose well so it doesn’t leak and secure the drain hose to whatever sink you are using for the drain. I used Velcro Reusable Self-Gripping Cable Ties to secure the hose to the leg of the sink. I did buy a 3 year extended warranty, just to be on the safe side. So far, so good.

review_title: Anyway the machine is great, it could be a hassle it you overload ...
review_text:
I have used this for over 3 years now and I have had no issue with mines. Just recently though I noticed a small leakage of water showing up on the floor which must be coming from underneath the machine, havent had time to check to see if I can fix this or not. Just a note for people who plan on buying this. In the instruction manual I received it did not explain the cycling properly so I assumed the machine was broken. It seems as if you dont set they cycle properly, after the "wash" cycle it will automatically stop and want proceed onto the rinse and spin cycle. With this in mind you would think that the machine is broken but in reality it is not. If they had this in the instruction manual I probably would have not assumed it was broken. So if you come across this issue its probably because you didnt set it properly. Anyway the machine is great, it could be a hassle if you overload it, then you will find yourself babysitting it and wondering why the machine keeps stopping. If you put just the right amount of clothes in it you should be okay. I learned over time that if it does get off balance I simply put the heavy clothes on the bottom and the light on top.

I give this a 5 star as I have put this machine through some heavy loads and it is still going strong besides the small leakage of water showing up. The machine does get loud though during the spinning cycle, so if you have neighbors that leave their door open you probably want to close your windows. This machine basically runs itself, just leave the water turned on from the faucet and it will automatically add the needed water to your wash, no need to turn the faucet off it will stop the flow of water all by itself. Like I said before you will have to babysit this washer if you overload as it will get off balance during spinning cycles in which the machine will automatically stop and want begin again until you have fixed the off balance issue but if you put the proper amount of clothes in this thing you should have no issue.

review_text:
This review is more concentrated on the negative 'problems' listed in some reviews. It's really important that a buyer isn't so in a hurry to set the washer up that really important instructions and even simple logic are not missed. Firstly ,there isn't just one leveling leg there are four. Use a bubble level and follow the manual concerning how they work and tighten. I'm not referring to the castor wheels,I'm talking about the plain foot pads.

There is absolutely no reason to need plumbers silicone thread tape on either end of the hose. If, like some claim, they can't keep the water on between wash and spin cycles,they have simply not installed the hose connectors correctly. The white screw on connector end of the filler hose connects to the top of the washer. The grey screw on connector attaches to the faucet , BUT several things must be done FIRST. Totally strip the current nozzle that was on the faucet before the machine was delivered . Nothing but one of two things should remain after you prep your faucet ...

Either a hole should remain and that hole in the faucet will have threads inside, so you'd have to put your finger up inside the faucet to feel them, or you end up with just a slight one eighth inch of white plastic or metal threads protruding from the faucet,with the threads on the outside where you could see them even from 6 feet across the room. Page 13 in the manual clearly illustrates these two types of threads.

Why is that important ? Because if the threads are inside ... TYPE B ( you can't see them when facing the sink ) You would use all 3 washers that are inside the "SILVER FAUCET CONNECTOR" and yes they are tight but they are removable ... they remove because if you CAN see the threads because they are wrapped around the outside diameter of the faucet, you need to discard the thick top washer and use only the thin washer and the rubber cone washer (TYPE A) This failure to use the proper washer combinations is why some need teflon tape and others cant keep the water on because of spraying from the leaking connector.

Remember, the 'silver faucet connector' is your new sink faucet tip .. it must be the thing that is screwed right into your faucet, it does not have anything at all between it and your faucet. Nothing at all on your faucet except the threads described above will fit to the new silver facuet connector that comes with the washer. And before you drive yourself crazy, remember that the quick release new faucet tip screws on COUNTER - clockwise !!!

When screwing the WHITE connector into the top of the washer, do not tighten so much that the light soft white foam like washer that is on the machine already, slides out of round. hand tighten only,tool tightening will ruin the positive seal.

As to the gray connector end, hold the copper portion of the quick connector with needle nosed pliers, and tighten the grey coller toward the pliers which you are simply gripping with, not tightening with.Tighten the coller with your hands only, not using the pliers for anything but to grip the copper part of the quick connector. You will have no leaks, and you can then keep the water on from start to finish.

As to balancing the wash, fold pants and shirts into squares. and radiate all 'squares' from dead center of the tub outward evenly around the curved sides of the stainless tub. I've yet to ever need to rebalance ... but as stated earlier bubble leveling the 4 feet so the level is dead square when rested near the lid hinge is critical for silent spinning ... my washer in operation will not wake up a sleeping baby.

review_title: Way better than my Panda washer and spin dryer!
review_text:
I ordered this from Walmart. I was a bit upset because I had to order a iron with this. The cost of this machine was $229 with the iron. I paid $36 for a 3 year warranty because of the reviews I read and paid about $9 and some change for tax. I'm glad I got it shipped to my home b/c the box it came in was pretty big. The FedEx guy was nice enough to bring it in to my door-I live in an apt..

Getting it out of the box was a hassle. The way I took it out of the box was a good thing because there was a metal plate that needed to be attached to the bottom of the washer. It scared me for a minute b/c the bottom was exposed. I thought surely this washer didn't come like this!
Anyway, I drilled the screws in b/c I have no patience for a screw driver. I got the castors on and rolled this to my kitchen. I had to tinker with the connecting hose because of the huge washer it came with. I had to take that out b/c my faucet is funky and the washer was just too big.

From the reviews that I read and videos I've seen it was advised to tighten the hose that connects to the washer from the sink because it will leak. I thought hand twisting that hose as tight as I could would be the thing but no. I had to use vice grips to tighten it and I got no leaks. This is very important.

On to the wash:
I stayed by the washer to make sure everything was working and checked for leaks because it will if things aren't properly tightened. I started out small with a quick wash. Boy that quick wash was quick! I then did another bigger load and put the water level on medium and the wash cycle on normal. I then did a heavy full load. No problems with the first three.

I did manage to have to rewash some of my clothes because some of the instructions required you to turn the article of clothing inside out. You don't have to do this. I work as a cashier and I can either wear khaki or black pants. I chose black. I turned the pants inside out only to have to rewash them because when I turned them right side in all of the dirt seeped to the outside of my pants and I had to do a quick wash to get them clean. I had to do this with several articles of clothing.

Here's why I gave it 4 stars: After having to rewash a sweater when it was time to spin it began knocking real loud. It did so again when I washed my under garments. At that point I had to quickly turn off the power because of how loud it was and I do live in an apt.. I couldn't test out another load of laundry to see if it was because of how light the load was because that was my last load. In the near future I will have to make sure I didn't do anything stupid upon washing my clothes.

I washed about 4 medium loads of clothes-some I had to rewash-in about probably 3 hours. It probably would've taken me shorter than that if I didn't have to rewash some items and if I didn't leave my apt..

All-in-all this washer is better than my Panda washer because it has a spin and rinse cycle. With the Panda I had to manually rinse out each article of clothing and had to wring out the water with my bare hands. The spin dryer that I have I would've had to wait to wash all of my loads of clothing because it won't spin right if it's not jammed packed to the top. I will update my usage of this washer should anything change.

********************************UPDATE 3-8-16*********************************************************************
This washer knocks extremely loud during the last spin cycle. A local repairman came out twice and couldn't fix my problem so Haier sent me another washer. This washer did fine on my first load but it knocked real bad on my second load. After that I was scared to use it. Well, I have cervical vertigo and I don't go hardly anywhere so my wardrobe has been limited to PJ's but my underclothes was becoming a mountain so I had to bite my tongue and use this. I put it on medium cycle and I washed with hot water and the first two spins before the rinse went w/o a hitch. The third spin started to knock but it stopped because it was time for the rinse cycle. I put the water on cold and I stood and waited for the spin cycle. The first few spins were fine but then it started to knock. Someone told me that the knocking was the result of the drain hose. When the knocking started to occur I just positioned the drain hose a little and it spun for a few minutes with no knocking. The second long spin the same way. So I think that putting the rinse cycle on cold, keeping the washer's wheels unlocked, and positioning the drain hose to where it won't knock has calmed my nerves. It still get clothes wonderfully clean and I don't have to go to the laundromat.

I don't know, but I do know that as a senior on only Social Security I must cut it down and this little washer is I am hoping, helping me do that. I won't know until I get my next months bill. I know that I can use it sort of like a wringer washer of the old days. I wish I could find one, but as I have researched I don't think they make them anymore in the US. And the one I found was over a 1,000, not counting shipping. So what I do with this washer is fill it up about 5 inches from the top, add my detergent, and a small amount of bleach for the first load of whites. Now this is a little hard to do at my age of 65, the bending bothers me, but I put an amount of water in my tub, and once I allow the clothes to soak for a bit, and wash a couple of rounds, I wring them out and place them in my tub and rinse them, then wring the out all by hand, and then take them to my large washer and use the wringer on it to spin dry them before hanging. I can do all my clothes in the same wash water I started with by adding a bit more water as needed, because I can't wring them out entirely of all water before I place them in the tub to rinse. I figure by doing this I am using less than the water it would take to fill my large washer up for one load of the wash cycle alone. Surely this will cut my water bill down tremendously, if not I will be talking with the utility company on it for sure.

I have done even a queen size blanket and small rug runner's! I hang them up on the line outside when it is pretty and I hang them on my indoor line inside when it is cold, rainy, etc. I keep telling myself, when it sort of get's hard for me to do this, that my grandmother did it for most all her life, so surely I can too. Oh, I just place the drain hose into my tub and empty it . I really like that you can place the water in the tub by bucket's, and not have to fool with the hose because it gets messy, or did for me anyways, and I only want to use it sort of like a wringer washer could be used. Over all for the price this is a great product..

review_title: This is a BEAST! (in a good way)
review_text:
Not sure where to start - this has totally transformed how I do/keep up with laundry.
#1 - it cleans - wow does it clean. I have a high-dollar front-loader which I've suspected for a while doesn't clean well - so I took clean clothes (supposedly) and washed them in the Haier - unbelievable how dirty the wash water was! The quick fix for the front-loader is to manually add a gallon of water when I need it - which now, thankfully, is only with items too bulky for my Haier.
#2 - it's quick! Quickwash is done in about 20 minutes (high-dollar machine takes almost 50 minutes on quickwash); Normal is done in about 30 minutes; Heavy-Duty is done in about 45-50 minutes.
#3 - I like that it's tiny - I don't have to wait until I have a huge pile of clothes before it's worth the effort to wash. As soon as I get a medium load of clothes to wash, in they go, hang dry and put away - this has allowed me to keep up with laundry in a way no other washer has.
#4 - again - it's tiny - my large front-loader is in my basement and extremely inconvenient because I have family living dowin there - always something in the washer or the dryer, or the baby is sleeping, or whatever... I have my Haier in a small upstairs 1/2 bath - next to a room where I keep all of my clothes - never has washing clothes for me been more convenient.
#5 - allows customized washing - if I want to wash in hot, I just turn on the hot water faucet; if I want to rinse in cold, as soon as the tub fills with wash water, I turn off the hot and turn on the cold. If I want a prewash in cold, I use the wash only setting; then the spin only setting (usually just to drain it, I stop it before spin); then one of the wash cycles. If something needs just a bit more water, but not enough for the next level up, just push the water level button while the machine is washing - it adds more water without changing the setting. If you want 2 rinse cycles, use Heavy Duty - 2 rinse cycles are programmed in. The possibilities are endless.
Negatives or worries: If you overload it, it sounds like you've got a tyrannosaurus rex trying to escape, then it just stops - if this happens, it's much easier and quicker to pull out 1/2 and use the rinse/spin cycle, then repeat repeat with the other 1/2 - trying to rebalance the load is nearly impossible. But that's my fault for overloading - this is such a beast of a machine that it's tempting to overload sometimes. It leaked for a short while at first - but it stopped - I think the gaskets just needed to get wet and swell. My only worry is a major leak - because it's upstairs, it has the potential to cause a lot of water damage - I do turn off the faucets as soon as it's finished washing as a precaution. Things do tend to get twisted and knotted - the lower the water level, the moreso it seems to happen - bras are the worst so I just use a garment bag - problem solved.
So how much can you wash? Keep in mind, this is a mini washer - it's meant for small loads. Drop clothes in 1 at a time, no higher than the rim of the machine - then try normal cycle with medium water level. I've found that if I put so many clothes in that I need the high water level, then it's most likely going to become unbalanced during the rinse/spin. I'll wash 2 medium-weight towels with 2 washcloths and 1 hand towel at one time. I can wash thin microfiber queen size sheets just fine; thicker flannel queen sheets must be split into 2 washes. I can wash small blankets one at a time.
(Note: I purchased this washer directly from Wal-Mart because I wanted ease in returning locally if I had any issues.)

review_title: Best Portable Washer !!!!!! Order yours today!!!!
review_text:
I love this machine so much I wrote a review for it!!!!

I LOVE THIS MACHINE!!!!!! Was a total skeptic before purchasing one because I have always been a full size washer person but when I moved into a studio loft without washer and dryer connections I had to do something.

This machine will pay for itself within a few months. The laundromat was costing about $20-$30 dollars a week for 2 adults. That's $80-$120 dollars a month.

Don't wait to purchase this unit!!! It paid for itself in 2 months for me and I didn't really see any adverse effects to my electricity bill or water bill.

If it stopped working today I would purchase a brand new one without hesitation and if you need a washer now, order it today and get it in two days with Amazon prime!!! Order it today!!!!! You will not be sorry!!!

The machine is not difficult to move around and connects easily to the sink with a Quick Connect Faucet Adapter. I just went down to local Ace Hardware and purchased a new one for less than $20.00. Super easy and no leaking.

A note on the drain hose... I twisted my hose around the water hose so it would not slide out of the sink when water is emptying into the sink. There isn't a ton of pressure behind the water emptying into the sink but it is nice to know it won't move.

I do have to mention one of my biggest concerns was that it didn't have the tradition agitator in the middle like full size top loading machine but after I thought about it I realized the new front loaders don't have them either. Needless to say it doesn't make a difference. The clothes come out fresh and clean.

NOW...... FYI.........

You cannot do a 1000 pound load in this unit but my son and I just got back from a 7 day cruise and I'm doing my laundry as I type this and I fill this little sucker up...

As I pull this stuff out and switch it to the dryer I will give you a list of what is in there:

Load 1:

Ladies sweat pants
3 Mens XL Cotton Shirts
3 Mens Xl Polyester Golf Polos
Mens XL Basketball Shorts
5 Mens Cotton Underwear Boxer Briefs

2nd load

3 Ladies Cotton Shorts
2 Mens XL Shirts
3 Ladies Polyester Shorts
3 Mens Cotton Underwear Boxer Briefs
2 Ladies Polyester Golf Polos
Ladies Cotton Tank Top
Ladies Cotton T-Shirt
4 Pair Ladies Underwear

WOW... Now that I type that out I cannot believe what was all in there.

The other load was one I removed from the dryer before switching current load over.

This was all while running the unit on Normal Wash which is the cycle that comes up when you turn the unit on. All you have to do after pressing the "On" button is touch the water level button "1 Time" which moves the water level from Medium Water Level to High. Then press start to let water begin to run before adding laundry soap first and then the laundry after.

I have used powder detergent and liquid and even the pods. They all work fine just add the detergent prior to adding the clothes after running the water for a little bit so it has time to dissolve and mix up.

There must be a small reservoir under the tub because it takes a few seconds for the water to start showing up in the bottom of the washer which is why I wait to add detergent until I see water first.

If you are washing Jeans or Heavy Cotton Pants like Khakis, I only wash those 2 at time with 2 or 3 shirts on this same setting or I just do 2 pairs of Pants or Jeans alone on the "Quick Wash" cycle which seems like less that 10-15 minutes but I've never really kept track. If you try to do a large load with jeans and stuff it just becomes unbalanced and you spend more time readjusting the load so it is easier to just do them alone and faster.

When it becomes unbalanced the machine will make that loud unbalanced noise and pause itself and beep 3 times to alert you to readjust the load. Once you open the top and re-adjust the load it will resume running without any additional button pushing but stand there until it begins again to make certain you adjust the clothes evenly.

On heavier loads the machine will sometimes make a louder noise when spinning because it is close to off balance but not enough to shut it down. If the noise bothers you, then you can get up an re-adjust the clothing so it stops or just deal with the noise.

This noise will only happen on the spin cycle during the rinse and spins options because the clothing has gotten mixed up during the wash.

Otherwise if packed correctly, most if the time I don't even realize it is running Sometimes I even miss the end of wash alert beeps that let you know it is finish.

I have never had a problem with the smelling of mold like some of the new full size front loaders do. I do most of my laundry loads with 1/3 -1/4 cup of Gain Liquid Laundry Soap and Warm Water.

I do wash 3 Bath Towels or my King Size Bed Sheets at the same time with 2 Pillow Cases once or twice a week on Hot with a half or full cup of Bleach so maybe that helps but I just store it with the lid open after I use it and I might use liquid fabric softener a few times a week if I can remember to add it.

I am NOT into Ironing and I don't have to be either. There are some items I take right out if the washer and hang up and let air dry and I can wear them without throwing them in the dryer or ironing them.

Let me mention though. If you do plan on air drying then I wouldn't pack the washer that full so the clothes have room to move without getting all tangled up.

NOW!!!!!! If you are expecting the durability of a full size washer then just don't bother. Or if you are one of those very negative people that can find fault with everything in the world then don't bother.

Most of the negative reviews about most things are from people that can find a reason to complain about everything and anything and then the others who could afford to purchase a full size unit or get their laundry done for them but are too CHEAP to do it. Come On Guys .... You know who you are !!!!!

In conclusion, this is an amazing little unit and you won't regret purchasing it today. Great for college dorms too!

review_title: Well worth it for time saved
review_text:
First let me say, I did not purchase this on Amazon. I actually purchased one used at a local second-hand shop about two weeks ago for less than $100, which given the price made me seriously happy to find one!

I do not know if the new units come with this, but my unit did not come with the adapter to go from standard faucet to washer hose. This is, however, an inexpensive fix - Home Depot (or Lowes) is your answer. I picked up a two-piece quick connect - one stays in the faucet, the other stays in the hose and they snap together. Be aware though that you will have to pay attention and turn the water off and on - the adapter does NOT have an aerator.

Having read enough reviews, I have yet to try a load that will require more than a medium water level. I also wash twice due to chemical sensitivities so my three washes really equates to six. However, so far all my clothes have come out clean. Since we don't have a dryer, I just hang them up on the shower curtain bar to dry. I did one load last night and five out of six shirts were dry by morning (the sixth being slightly damp at the bottom, it's also the heaviest shirt I own, so this is to be expected and is not a reflection of the washer.) I was very pleasantly surprised by how well the spin cycle works. My only nitpick about this machine is I wish it had an option like the big washers do to add in an additional rinse cycle - then I'd be able to only wash once instead of twice. In the meantime though, I just use the quick wash on that second one, and it does the trick.

All in all, this is a life saver. My current living quarters are VERY small (efficiency), no washer/dryer hookups. The laundry room here is VERY inconvenient - only six washers, six dryers, all using a pain in the rear card system, and they're always either all full or half are broken whenever I need to do wash, coupled with short hours of operation that often are only open when I need to be at work. While I don't see myself using this machine for towels or the heavy blankets mainly due to size and my available space to hang-dry and my own preference, for keeping up with the clothes for two people this is going to be a serious lifesaver. And I would not hesitate to recommend it for someone who is just looking for something to help cut down on laundromat time.

********************************

Edited to add:

Well, about a month in, and this baby is still going strong. I have discovered a few things though through trial and error that I'd have probably known before writing my initial review if I'd purchased a machine with a manual!

1. I stated that there was no way to add a rinse cycle. However, there is, in a way. If you press the cycle button enough times you can not only change the water level, but also where the machine starts in the Wash/Rinse/Spin order of things to create an additional Rinse/Spin without the additional Wash. This also comes in handy those moments I space out and don't realize it's time to turn on the water.

2. I have now tested a load or two on the high water setting, with good results. I still would not recommend overloading the unit, Too many heavy items in one load will result in issues during the spin cycle.

Still happy with the unit, still worth the money for saving me time and money.

*******************

Added January 18 2018:

Just an update. I've now had this washer for about two years, and bought mine second hand. It's still going strong two years later. Since water and electric are included in my rent, the amount of money I've saved from not having to go to Laundromat has been well worth it. Highly recommended.

I was lucky enough to find this washer for $199 at a club store. The quick connect hose is convenient and can fit on a bathroom sink (which is what is easiest for me). I live in a small top floor apartment and DREAD laundry day. I work nights and am a slave to the laundry room hours which means I either get up early to do laundry or MUST do it on my day off. There is space between the tub and the inside of the machine so be careful not to overload the machine so that no water gets inside. I read about problems with the water sensor and have had none. My only gripe about the washer is that no matter what I do, it seems like the quick connect adapter ALWAYS leaks. I'll try some Teflon tape which might help.

The spin cycle is effective but can get loud. The entire machine will shake but it is effective and the pump is powerful enough to drain out all the water and doesn't flop around in my sink, which is good, because I can't connect it to the hose like the manual states. All in all, this is a really good product and being able to do my laundry at home and after work is a blessing. This would get 5 stars if the machine was a little more stable but hey, if I can get a couple years out of this thing for $200 then it works for me.

product_title: Haier HLP21N Pulsator 1-Cubic-Foot Portable Washer
review_text:
Washes my clothes. Nuff said.

Ok I have more to say, lol. First it's really light weight and small and good engineering design. It fits in my kitchen where a high chair used to be. I love how silent it is that sometimes I go to the other room and think it stopped washing because I can't hear it.

It washes a fairly decent amount of clothes in about 15 min on Normal Wash which it does a good job. It takes over 25 mins on Heavy wash but it washes and rinses the clothes very well. I usually add two full measuring caps of liquid detergent which is about 3/4 of a cup. I add one measure of softener (during Rinse Cycle when the water is pouring in) anything more and it doesn't rinse off well unless you're using Heavy Wash since it does two Rinse cycles. The Spin cycle practically dries the clothes. There is Heavy Wash, Quick Wash (11 min), and Normal Wash.

I love how you can choose the settings and how much water to use in each setting. Some settings automatically apply the water level but you can change it. Besides regular cycles It also lets you choose to only wash, only rinse, only wash and rinse, only spin, only rinse and spin. You can add water with the attached hose and faucet bracket it brings or with a bucket, the hose is easier. The washer rolls with ease if you attach the added wheels. I literally sit on my chair and watch the washer do its thing. Sometimes when the rinse cycle stars and water is pouring in I see my clothes tangled up and I have to pull them out all soapy and untangle them and place them back in. It's easy since they are already slippery. It doesn't happen often only when I add a lot of long sleeved clothes. I found out that if you add too much clothes it will stop the cycle until you remove some clothes. It does this during the end of the wash cycle when it's spinning to remove the soap, it starts banging inside basically telling you it's too much load. I keep a small bucket around just in case. You can add two to three man sized jeans in one regular wash but sometimes the machine stops and I have to remove one jeans. So I add a couple of t-shirts or soxs with two jeans and I have no problems. In an afternoon around 5-6 hours I washed 30 t-shirts, 12 underwear, 8 pair of jeans, 12 pairs or soxs, two sweaters, a long sleeved flannel button shirt and a pillow casing. It's reasonable to say I had a lot of hangers to hang them dry.

review_text:
I LOVE this machine. It does a great job and washes with WATER!, which is something our larger HE machine seems to think is optional. There are various settings for water settings, giving you control. If you have the water setting on low or med and feel it needs a bit more after it has started, simply hold down the water button and the machine will take a bit more until you let go. I also like that on the heavy setting it gives one wash and two rinses.
The machine is relatively quiet, easy to set up, and does not take up too much space. There is no 'delicate' cycle, but there is a 'quick wash' setting which I use for delicate wash in order to minimize agitation time. The spin cycle is also very good and leaves the clothes ready for the line or the dryer as dry as can be.
You will not be able to fit down comforters or bulky bedding queen size and larger, but regular sheets of any size are fine.
Occasionally, I put a 5 gallon bucket to collect the rinse water and use it for the following wash cycle (the high water setting takes more than what fits in the bucket so you need to be standing by if doing so on this setting).

review_title: A real washing machine that just happens to be portable
review_text:
I've been looking at portable washing machines online for years but never bought one because they didn't seem much better than washing clothes by hand especially since the clothes still had to be wrung out. The Haier HLP21N seemed like a better level of machine so I bought one and I am so glad I did! It's a real washing machine that just happens to be portable. Clothes get very washed, very rinsed and very spun to almost dry.

It's quieter than a blow dryer even during the spin cycle and has plenty of options for water level and cycle so you can do a quick wash (about 20 minutes) for lightly soiled items or a longer one (about 40 minutes) for seriously dirty stuff.

I use mine in the tiny bathroom of my apatment - water hose hooked up to the sink, drain hose in the bathtub - and it took me some trial and error to figure out the best way to position the drain hose into the tub: attaching the drain hose hook (included) to the drain hose and then hooking it onto the metal loop of my detachable shower head. That gave me the height the hose needs to drain properly and kept it secure throughout the cycle. If you do the same, just make sure you close your shower curtain as the flow is pretty strong and there will be splashing.

If I had to find a negative with this machine, the only tiny thing wrong with it is there is no dispenser for liquid fabric softender. Of course you can go old school and put it in during the rinse cycle yourself or start buying detergent with the fabric softener in it (I started using "Tide Plus A Touch Of Downy" liquid detergent and it works great).

I LOVE this washer! I'm a student so I can't afford too expensive models. I thought it would not clean my clothes very well considering the price but it actually clean my clothes better than the public washers in my apartment building.

The taps in my apartment are all weirdly shaped so I couldn't possibly hook the hose with the machine. I use buckets to pour water into the machine and it works just fine. The only thing is it can't rinse. I tried pouring in water and let it resume rinsing, or pouring water and restart the machine to rinse, but the first thing the machine does in a rinse cycle is getting rid of the water.
So in order to rinse, I let the machine go to rinse cycle, wait until it gets rid of all the water, and wait until the machine spins. When it's done spinning, the machine will want to try to get water. At this time I will turn it off, pour water into it, restart and let it run from the wash cycle to spin cycle. By letting your clothes spin once or twice before re-washing like I did will get rid of the soapy water, so it doesn't take much to rinse.

product_title: Haier HLP21N Pulsator 1-Cubic-Foot Portable Washer
review_text:
Living in a small apartment, this washer has been fantastic in the past two months, and it's probably close to paying for itself already compared to driving 20 minutes to the laundromat and paying for their machines.
It can wash a respectable amount of clothes for its size, but it is small. You can do a pair of pants, 2-3 shirts, and a fistful or two of socks and underwear per load pretty easily. A second pair of pants is fine if you cut back on the rest.
I haven't tried doing sheets yet but based on what I've seen, one would be fine, perhaps even two (full/queen). I've found that it does well if you fill it, gently, almost to the top of the barrel, it almost never had problems spinning.
It runs pretty quietly, too. The motor makes a slight hum both cleaning and spinning, but it's quieter than most home washers I've used.
We hang dry or clothes and the spin cycle gets clothes dry enough that just drying overnight usually makes them ready to use in a pinch, and they're dry by the time I get home from work. I have had a couple of loads that haven't spun out so well, but you can skip to the spin cycle and give them another go of that happens.
It's worth talking down a couple of mesh bags for delicates. Clothes seem to get tangled up more in this washer than others I've used, and can get pretty stretched.
Operation is easy. I hook it up to the kitchen sink as the water source and drain. It works fine with what comes in the box, but I bought a Y valve eventually for two reasons: to release pressure from the line when I'm done, and to be able to get water from the faucet while it's hooked up. Definitely worthwhile, if not absolutely necessary.

product_title: Haier HLP21N Pulsator 1-Cubic-Foot Portable Washer
review_text:
I have only had this washer for about a week, but I'm already in love with it. I live in an apartment complex that only has one washer and dryer for about 20 units, and it doesn't work 75% of the time, so I started looking into portable washers. I bought the Panda washer from the Amazon Warehouse, but it arrived totally messed up so I ended up returning it. I finally found a Haier HLP21N on Craigslist and bought it, and have been so impressed with it.

I did 7 or 8 loads of laundry on the first day that I got it and it carried on like a champ - no issues. Definitely read the manual before using though - it will save you some headache. I was worried that mine wasn't working because the water wasn't coming through, but that's actually how it's supposed to work - the water only comes through when it needs to and it closes off the valve once it has enough. After I found a manual and read through and realized how it worked, I was good to go. It can't take a full load of laundry that you would put in a full sized washer, but it is still pretty good for a little thing.

I love that you don't really have to worry about it after turning it on; it does the wash, rinse, and spin all on its own unlike the two side washers that you have to manually move. The spinner works really well too - my clothes are barely damp when I pull them out, and I just put them on a drying rack and they dry within a day with no stiffness.

It is a little louder than I expected but I think it's just my paranoia of bothering my neighbors. I live in a studio apartment so I can hear it if I'm in a different part of the main room, but if I go into my bathroom or closet it's barely noticeable.

Living in an apartment I forgot how convenient it is to be able to do clothes in your own home, but now that I'm able to I'm not sure how I'll go back. I would highly recommend this little machine to anyone living in an apartment who is tired of having to go down to the basement or to the laundromat to do laundry. Before laundry was a chore that I would wait so long to do it ended up being a disaster, but now I can just do a small load every other day and I actually almost enjoy doing laundry because I know it's not going to be a huge chore.

review_title: Great washer. Perfect for apartment. Pairs well with Panda dryer.
review_text: I was used to a full-sized washer that could wash more clothes at once, but as a newly single guy adjusting to apartment living I have to say I really like this little washer. It's fully automatic (fills and drains itself, washes and spins in the same tub) unlike some of the other brands. It uses only cold water so that might be an issue with white clothes if you must have them looking their brightest, but all my clothes are dark, and I always did set my full-sized washer to just use cold water always to help minimize fading. I used to get away with doing 1 load/ wk with the full-sized but this is smaller so I do loads 2-3x/ wk now which I discovered I actually prefer since putting away the laundry is less tedious now because there's less of it (putting away laundry had always been my least favorite chore). You can connect it to a regular w/d hookup or a sink (it comes with optional wheels and a funky hose). I just bought a regular hose and hooked it up to the w/d connection. Even though the water inlet is plastic, make sure to put the hose on extra tight or it will make a mess as soon as you turn on the water. Hand-tight is not enough. Use a wrench and do it at least 1/4 turn past hand-tight.  It Pairs well with the Panda dryer which they are small enough to fit together in a 3 sqft w/d room meant for a combo w/d (which I opted not to get since they are known to have issues).

review_text:
This has been a godsend for someone who has depended on coin laundry all my life. Unfortunately, after four years to the day, mine seems to have failed. Most appliance repair places won't touch it, and the cost of repair would probably exceed what I paid for my refurbished model.

If I can't fix it, I will gladly buy another. For all those who ask how much it will hold, you are thinking of it all wrong. This washer is not about how MUCH you can wash, but how LITTLE. If you're used to coin laundry, you wait until you get a full load together to get the most bang for your buck. The luxury of having my own little washer is I can throw my daily workout clothes in there and have them dry the next day, or just do a quick-wash load of the small microfiber cloths I use for cleaning and I don't want to mix with my clothing. I can wash one towel or one shirt if I spill something, and being able to wash something immediately reduces the chance of staining permanently.

I also find that the high load setting (the max water level) runs too noisily and tends to unbalance, so I keep my loads small. You'll keep up with your washing instead of having numerous loads to wash, fold, and hang.

product_title: Haier HLP21N Pulsator 1-Cubic-Foot Portable Washer
review_title: Not perfect, but I still give it 5 stars - here are the pros and cons
review_text:
PROS:

- In-unit washer
- Effective, at least for washing clothes that are not usually heavily soiled

CONS:

- Larger pieces of clothing get tangled (e.g., long sleeve dress shirts)
- Spin/balance issues related to the above
- Small loads (but you probably already know that)

I bought this machine back in June 2017, so I've had this for a good 5 months now. I wash all my clothes in this washer, including queen sized bed sheets, and towels. I use and store this in the kitchen.

I actually considered this purchase for a few months. I bought this for $215. Obviously not an insignificant amount of money. My primary concern was that this was a small machine, and what if it just stops working? So far so good, but I think the test is how long it lasts, and that's something I can't answer right now. In the meantime, I'll write about how it runs.

My clothes are not usually heavily soiled. Given that, this machine works fine for me. I have thrown more soiled clothes in, but have also put them in with a lot more clothes, and it doesn't quite clean that well when bunched with a lot of other clothes. So for soiled items, I'd recommend treating stains, and also washing it by giving it plenty of space in the tub. If you do that, I don't think you'll have a problem. The heavily soiled clothes don't need to be by themselves, but I'd make sure not to fill it up as you would normally fill the tub.

I use the heavy wash option each time - that provides approximately 26 minutes of wash time and two rinse cycles (each rinse cycle is only actually rinsing for about 2-3 minutes maybe). The most annoying thing so far for me is that, because I throw all types of clothes in the washer, I've discovered that the bigger pieces actually get tangled with each other. This is particularly a problem with long sleeve dress shirts. To mitigate this problem, I try washing at most 3 dress shirts in one load. And I try to be attentive in terms of throwing different types of clothes in there (socks, undershirts, long sleeve dress shirts, underwear, etc.).

What happens when clothes are tangled? Well, aside from my concern over wear and tear for the clothes, it actually causes the clothes to clump together, and that causes an imbalance when the washer starts spinning. While the washer can recognize these imbalances (in which case it will stop spinning), it actually takes a while for it to do so. At times, this causes pretty violent shaking before the washer stops spinning. So now what I do is I pay attention to the washer when it's doing the spin cycle, just so I'm ready to hit pause if there is an imbalance. And if there is one, then I untangle the clothes and throw them back in.

Given all that I've written, why do I give this 5 stars? Well, I still think it's a pretty awesome thing to have in my 1-bedroom apartment. I no longer have to wash my clothes outside my unit. It's a machine that washes my clothes effectively, and I can do that from the comfort of my own home. Given that I don't have hook-ups in my apartment, it's the next best thing.

But I also think people should know what they're getting into.

I already mentioned the imbalance issue. The loads are small, as you can probably see if you look this up on youtube. It's even smaller if you frequently have heavily soiled items. Also, I line dry my clothes because I don't have a drying unit. If you've line dried your clothes before, you probably know that the clothes come out somewhat "crispy" - it's just not as soft as if you dry them in a dryer. I personally don't care, but I do know that this may be an issue for some folks.

Despite all the above, I still highly recommend this machine.

UPDATE (07/16/2018):

I thought I'd write an update now that I've had this for a year. Someone previously suggested in a comment to my review that I could try putting clothes in mesh bags to prevent tangling. This worked great! I put all my long-sleeve shirts in mesh bags that I bought off Amazon. It's not perfect, but it has reduced the imbalance problem that I described above. Imbalance is still an issue, so I still feel like i need to be around when the machine starts to spin.

Other than that, I have no other comments except that I've now had this machine for a year, running it about twice a week, and have no problems. Still really like it and would make the same purchase again for the price that I paid. Happy to answer any questions about it if people are wondering.

UPDATE (05/08/2020):

Still running great!

product_title: Haier HLP21N Pulsator 1-Cubic-Foot Portable Washer
review_title: Portable, easy to use, and cleans clothes well
review_text:
I live in an apartment and got tired of the washing machines here, being so rough on my clothes and delicates, not to mention the expense and running back and forth to the laundry room. I thought buying this Haier washer might be a solution, because most of my clothing, I prefer to hang dry anyway, rather than put them in the scorching hot dryers in my facility.
I carefully unpacked it – found that the bottom of the box is separate – so you can lift the box off of the washer without tipping it over and pulling it out.
Assembly was easy, however there was a problem with the base plate – it came with no screws to attach it to the bottom of the washer. Even had there been the 6 screws that they state are needed, I couldn’t have used them as there were no holes on the bottom of the washer to screw them into. So, my washer has no base plate attached. It doesn’t impair the operation of it – probably its purpose is to keep dust out of the workings of the machine. This means I will need to periodically check under it and keep it vacuumed.
It wouldn’t work on the faucet that I have in my bathroom, so I took it into the kitchen to try it there. That was easy enough, but just be sure to follow the instructions about either leaving in or removing the little black rubber washer in the hook-up valve. Well, no matter how much I tried, it leaked and sprayed water all over my cabinets and counters. But no problem! I just draped a kitchen towel over it to catch the spray and I was in business. I stuck the drain hose down into the garbage disposal drain. It stays put when the water drains out, so no need to attach it to the water hose for stability.
So, after hooking it up to my kitchen faucet, I ran an empty cycle with detergent to clean the drum, as suggested. All went well. Time for clothes!
I set the water level to high and ran a normal wash cycle. Logically, you need to not pack the drum tightly with clothes. I placed my items loosely in washer and started it up. The whole cycle, start to finish, ran 35 minutes. The spin does an amazingly good job and leaves the clothes ready to hang dry anywhere with no concern of dripping. The wash cycle is about 15 minutes but the rinse is short – about 2 minutes. The rest of the time is for spinning, filling, and draining. I would prefer the rinse be a little longer, but with my using liquid detergent, I haven’t noticed any soap residue left on the clothes, so maybe it is okay.
I’m very impressed with how clean it got my white things. My white, cotton shirt was sparkling white and it had had some make-up stains on it around the collar. Fantastic! The clothes get pretty twisted, so I have found that I like to untwist them after the wash and rinse cycle before they spin.
Finally, a couple more things… it has a pretty quiet operation – quieter than my dishwasher. I also, saved the Styrofoam insert that came with it in the drum, to keep it stable for when I move it back and forth from a closet to the kitchen. It is on rollers, so moving it isn’t a problem.

After I’ve used it a few months, I will report back and let you know how it is holding up. As of this writing now, I have washed about 10 loads of laundry. I've found that it cannot be left unattended, so that the water can be turned on and then off when not filling. The water pressure may be too great to keep the water on when it isn't filling. (When the water was left on when not filling, the water valve shot off the faucet and stripped one of the threads on the screw part right off. I should get a new valve, but it works okay temporarily.) Also, it got off balance during the spin cycle once, and I was there to catch it immediately. I imagine it would be very hard on the machine if that happened and it wasn't stopped.

Update 11/18/19:
This is a great little washing machine. I've had it for 2 years now. About 6 months ago, the pump seemed to die.
I took off and inspected the drain hoses. Nothing was clogged in there. So I had to manually drain the washer on the porch for a while in order for the clothes to spin dry.

Coincidentally, in the summer, I started using Borax as a laundry detergent. Unbeknownst to me, this solved my issue. Borax is a water softener. I have extremely hard water. By using Borax in every wash, it helped clear the issue, and now the pump works again.

Just thought I'd put this out there in case someone else has this same issue. Now, after every wash, I put some warm water and Borax into the empty basket and let it go down into the system and sit there until I use the washer again, in order to keep the mineral deposits from gunking up the system.

Previous review:
I bought this to replace a 2006 Danby washer that had become leaky, and required babysitting while filling with water.

I bought this model based on the good reviews. I was not disappointed. While it does not hold as much as my Danby washer used to, I love the ease with which to use this unit. I no longer have to babysit during the fill mode (as I had to do in the later years with my previous washer), and it does not leak during use (previous washer).

It gets my clothes very clean. And the spin cycle removes most of the water.

I hang dry all year round using a drying rack.

A month or so ago, when the plumbing went south in the kitchen, which is where I use this washer, I was able to carry it upstairs and use it in my bathroom.

I used a 5-gallon bucket to fill it, and put the drain hose in my shower.

Once the plumbing in the kitchen was fixed, I carried the washer back down and resumed using it there.

Thumbs up for this little unit.

Between this washer and my two drying racks, I've spent only about $10 on laundry (not counting detergent) in those 4.5 years. I have had to replace the drive belt (in fact, that's why I'm on Amazon today), but I got mine as a refurb, so that may be a factor in how long the belt lasted. review_text:
Update 2- we moved into a nicer place a few months ago and have a full-sized washing machine and dryer now. Well this Haier is so good it still cleans better than the full size washing machine. So over 2 years later after purchasing this, I am still using this almost daily. It washes laundry like a champion champion and gives me zero issues.

Update- Over a year and a half later and this thing is still a workhorse that washes clothes perfectly for us each time. I have been using it almost once a day every single day due to having to cloth diaper two little ones plus other laundry that accumulates for our family of 5. We had an issue where it kept leaking and when we contact customer service we were pleasantly surprised to talk with a young man who actually helped us troubleshoot the issue. In the end, he suspected it was a cracked hose (suspected because after checking a few things he asked us to including our hose, we found the hose was not damaged that we could see). He sent out a replacement hose completely free. It did take 2 weeks to arrive, but upon changing the hose the leak stopped! Extremely happy with how that turned out and happy to be able to keep doing our laundry inside our apartment without having to go to a laundry facility!

Original review - We purchased this from a competitor since it was cheaper, about a month and a half ago. We had just moved from a home into an apartment and I wanted to cloth diaper again. Even after reading a lot of positive reviews from other moms and "Fluff love's" recommendation of this unit, I was still skeptical. After using this though for a month and a half now I can say it really does get my cloth diapers completely clean again. Here are some tips I discovered along my journey.

Fluff love recommends testing your water hardness. Anything over 180 ppm use borax or Calgon water softener. Anything under- the orange original tide powder works just fine. Our water is in the 100s so I stopped using Calgon and my diapers still come out completely, totally clean with no buildup or residue issues whatsoever. My daughter is about 20 pounds right now so I use Nicki's medium prefolds and Diaper Rite's large prefolds. One load fits about 7 of the prefolds, a large Planetwise wetbag, 4-5 cloth wipes and 3-4 covers. With those in there I am able to achieve the "stew" consistency. I first run a cold wash on heavy, high water level, which does the rinse and spin by default. I use line 1 detergent (Tide original powder) for this first one. I do make sure to let the water run and pour the detergent directly in the water stream every time so that it is well dissolved. Then when that cycle is done, I remove all the cd's, fluff them, shake them out and run a second heavy wash with high water level on hot water. To adjust the water temperature just open the cold or hot faucet and that's how the wash temperature is controlled. For the second wash I use a line 2 of the Tide. At the previous home I never had to shake off the solid waste (my daughter is a year and a half and completely on solid food now). I tested that on this Haier with just one soiled diaper, the rest were just wet with pee and it was not able to handle it. I had to pick off bits of orange carcass (the white stuff encasing the oranges) even after running 4-5 rinse and or heavy cycles. They just clung to the prefolds. My prefolds are a 55% bamboo with 45% organic cotton blend. Perhaps other non-bamboo prefolds would not have this issue, I'm not sure. So after having cloth diapered for over a year, I have finally learned to "dunk and swish" (there are YouTube videos on how to do this). I also purchased some organic fleece and cut them into liners. It takes about 5-10 minutes of dunking and swishing depending on what she eats per soiled prefold. Popcorn = 10 minutes to get all the kernal husks off. Strawberries = 5 minutes or less. I never thought I was the type of person who would ever do something so intensive or dirty, but I am surprised to find out, after having to do it I don't mind it so much now. It's just routine. So after getting 80-90%+ solid waste off, this Haier works perfectly.

Outside of cloth diapers I have also laundered my kids's clothes, our king bed's sheets, my spouse's and I's clothing as well. My spouse is 6'1 and over 200 lbs. I can fit about two of his pants and a shirt in one load, or 4 of his shirts if they are short sleeved. 2 if they are long-sleeved flannel and that is all when using high water level. I like to ensure the machine is not overloaded so I tread on the cautious side, perhaps more clothing can be squeezed in there. For the sheets in our king bed I do the fitted and a pillow case or two. Then the flat sheet separately again with a pillow case or something else that's small. I use the high water level for those as well.

Overall, I have found this machine to clean anything my kids throw my way- vomit, poop, pee etc. and to clean it very well. I use heavy for those heavy duty type cleanings, normal for almost everything else, quick wash for baby clothes and/or lingerie and underwear. Following the temperature settings outlined on those articles of clothing, combined with the wash settings I just listed, this machine churns out perfectly clean, undamaged clothes every time.

The only reason I docked a star is because of the price fluctuation (there seems to be over a hundred dollar disparity depending on the month), lack of agitation this unit has (I really would have preferred never having to dunk and swish since I didn't have to with my prior fully hooked up washing machine), and their poor customer service. When I contacted customer service because my machine kept getting stuck during rinse or spin, the young lady who answered was of no help. Her replies were along the lines of "hmm it shouldn't do that, I don't know why that is" or asking me, "Why do you think that's happening?". So I had to figure everything out on my own. At first, I was unsure if I had received a faulty machine or if it was user error. By fluke one of my cycles finished completely without getting stuck, which is when I realized it was user error on my part, and then proceeded to tinker with things till I figured it out. You have to use the white hook at the end of the hose (instead of just laying the hose down to drain) or it won't drain properly sometimes and pause the machine indefinitely. You also have to leave the faucet open for the entirety of the rinse (duh) and spin (not so obvious to me) cycle as well or it will again pause mid cycles indefinitely. So keep the faucet/water source on from start to finish (when the machine is done with all the cycles). The reason I say 'pause indefinitely' is because the machine does pause for a very brief amount of time during the spin cycles and such which is a normal pause. If the light is blinking and nothing happens (water fills, water drains, the machine agitates nor spins) for over a minute or two it means the machine is "stuck" in limbo.

review_text: I love Haier products .. they cater to a portion of people that most other appliance manufacturers do not .. people who live in small quarters or have no laundry hook ups! I used to live in an apartment with no laundry hook ups and I was too busy to make several trips to the laundry mat during the week. I seen this that came with the Haier portable dryer for about $400 .. I was skeptical of how well this would work at first. The setup was surprisingly quick and easy .. take it out of the box, screw a few things on, hook the water intake and drain hose and you are ready to go .. honestly took 10 minutes! Since there is no agitator but a pulsator ... it allows you more room for clothes. I was surprised by how much clothing I was able to fit in this little washer. I was also surprised by the array of fabric settings and loads sizes, including an extra spin cycle ..and a setting to allow for a long soak before the wash. There is even a countdown timer that informs how many minutes remain in the cycle and shows you which par tof the cycle it is on (fill, wash, rinse, spin) ...  Honestly .. I was amazed at how well this machine cleaned my clothes and with the pulsator .. it is more delicate on fabrics. Everything from the fill, wash, rinse, spin and drain worked perfectly ... the spin works just as well as a regular sized washer and the operation is pretty quiet .. as long as the washer is level on the ground .. there should be no issues. Now my reason I gave this a 4 star rating is because of the exterior shell. This is obviously not as strong and durable as a regular sized washer since it needs to be light weight enough to be "portable:" so I have had issues where if the unit gets banged by say the counter ... the outer shell can crack and the top loading door is not very durable either .. do no set anything on top of it or drop anything of heavy weight on it because it can and probably will break! I also had an issue where the area surrounding a couple screws/bolts on the exterior started to "spider web" crack around it. Now none of this affected the operation of the unit in any way, but the cracks can grow worse overtime. I personally know Haier customer service is great! Their warranty periods are pretty long, a few years, and they even have a separate warranty on the interior basket. If you have an issue with your unit .. they WILL send out a whole new unit if they have no Haier repair services in your local area. And they will NOT ask you to return the unit to them .. they will ask you to sign a letter saying you did properly dispose of the defective unit. I know some reviews state they had issues with the washer not starting after fill up ... this probably is because the washer is not level ... if this unit is even a small amount off level (even an inch) it will not run .. so adjust the legs accordingly.

review_text: I really wanted to love this washing machine. A friend of mine got one for her teeny NYC apartment to deal with baby clothes and raved about it. My building doesn't have laundry, so I thought this was the perfect solution for small loads. Trekking to the laundromat is such a time suck and an inconvenience. I can hear it when I stand OUTSIDE my front door. Also, the hookup to the sink is a major hassle. Even with the correct washers installed, I have to use a wrench to get it tight enough so that it won't spurt liquid every which way. I was using it in the bathroom for a while, which buffered the noise because I could shut the door, but had to stop because the machine was creating too much pressure on the pipes, which in turn caused a leak that dripped down into the apartment below. My landlord knocked on my door and I had wheel the contraband washer into my bedroom before letting him in, all while sweating like a guilty teenager disrupted in the middle of watering down their dad's stash of liquor. And last, but not least, is that it doesn't get clothes very clean. And yes, obviously, I do very small loads to avoid this problem, but the clothes are simply never clean enough. I've resorted to soaking a bit longer before washing, which isn't a big deal, but does add an extra step and on top of everything else is enough to erase the convenience. I had really high hopes and all this thing has given me is grief and anxiety.

product_title: Haier HLP21N Pulsator 1-Cubic-Foot Portable Washer
review_text:
I live in a small apt in a 4 floor walk up building going to the laundromat in NYC is awful. It cost me $8-$12 every 10-14 days taking trips to the dread laundromat and it's already paid for it self. I've had it for 7 months and this thing saved my life. Perfect for people in apartments RV's if you live alone or with another person, hate the laundromat.

At first I had the hardest time connecting the hose to my sink. I have a basic long straight arm kitchen faucet (no fancy curves or bends) and I found a really cool adapter called the Claber Koala indoor faucet adapter. Made hook up a breeze. It's pretty small I have it right between my dresser and a wall and it's out of sight. It cleans well it's more gentle than a normal washer which I actually like- Keeps clothes looking newer longer. Less pilling too! I roll it to the sink and hook it up in less than 2 minutes It fits a few days worth of my girlfriend's and I clothes. I use a tiny bit of detergent and unstoppable scent beads (I dilute those in hot water first) and my clothes come out super clean. From there the wash cycle begins and it is strong with a ferocious vroosh sound on each spin. I was worried it would be too loud and my neighbors complain, but it's not at all. We can still watch TV with it on close by. Next it automatically drains the dirty water then fills up with clean water again and rinses the clothes clean. At the end it begins the spin cycle and there have been times my clothes have come out bone dry no lie! It can knock when it spins which is loud and scary but it's preventable see my tips below. The control panel is great very simple, it allows you to have options to have heavier/lighter load cycles and options to select wash/rinse/spin cycles. Tips: Don't overpack it. Don't run more than 4 loads in a row (let it cool down). Pre-treat stains! That's important since it's more delicate and lastly you can always take a few clothes out and re-run the Spin cycle in two sessions to help assist with drying larger loads and helps prevent knocking. Rearranging clothes can help with knocking but spinning with less seems to work best. Overall great little machine that gets the job done!
