product_title: Samsung : FTQ307NWGX 30 Freestanding Induction Range, 4 Cooktop Elements, Convection, Self Clean
review_text: We purchased this range a few months ago. We tried out induction cooking with a small, portable burner. We loved that so much, we bought the full-size range. Our old electric range was awful at maintaining a constant temperature, and we were tired of having to lift the pan off the burner while waiting for the stove to cool down. I used to want a gas stove until we tried induction. We share the cooking in our house, and my husband says to me on a daily basis "have I told you today how much I love induction cooking". The stove is easy to use and very responsive. If you use the power burst setting, your water will boil super fast. Then, when you lower the temperature, the reaction of the food in your pot is instantaneous. No waiting, no lifting pots off the burners. The stove itself does not generate any heat. It creates a magnetic field which heats your pan. After you are done, the stove may feel hot, but that is just heat transfer from your pot. You can put your hand on the stove and not get burned (or lay your towel on the stove top and not start a fire).  Since the stove top doesn't get hot, nothing that boils over will stick or bake on. The stove wipes down easily with a soft cloth.  Also, the pot handles don't get hot. After cooking spaghetti, I can lift the pan up by its handles without the use of pot holders. If you leave your spoons in your pans, the part that sticks out of the top of the pan doesn't get hot either.  The convection oven is also easy to use and is very spacious.  I really love that the elements on the bottom of the oven are covered, so if something spills, it won't stick to the bottom elements. The range does make noise. There is a fan for the convection feature and little chirps and other noises for the induction. They are not loud or bothersome. This range has been a dream for us, and we would buy another one in a heartbeat.

product_title: Samsung : FTQ307NWGX 30 Freestanding Induction Range, 4 Cooktop Elements, Convection, Self Clean
review_text:
Have had this stove for about 2-1/2 years now and the cooktop went on the blink beginning of this month. I am totally hooked on induction top cooking and am putting an induction cook top in my new home. The oven part of this Samsung Range has been perfect and until this incident I have been totally pleased with this range in its entirety.

However, I live just south of Tucson and the only repair person qualified to repair Samsung ranges is located 116 miles away. To be fair they do come out and thank goodness I bought an extended warranty coupled by the 5 year cook top parts warranty by Samsung I am not paying anything. But without the extended warranty the trip charge itself would be $75.00 just to come out and diagnose the problem.

I hope there are no more problems with this range since I really have fallen in love with induction cooking and the perfect temp holding of the convection oven. I am giving it 4 stars due to the lack of local repair people. I did research before buying the new cooktop for the new house and there are many local authorized repair shops for this well known American brand. It is probably not made in America but at least they have quite a network of authorized shops unlike Samsung.

Please note that once you start cooking on an induction cooktop you will become hooked. The top does not heat up your house and that's a real good thing here in the Tucson AZ area. When I switched from the gas stove my electric bill hardly moved and my gas bill plummeted so it's very efficient. The temp changes faster than a gas cook top (incredible and didn't believe it until I used it) and low temps can be held perfectly. Oh, I forgot to mention you can boil a pot of water faster than a microwave. Two cups of water at 90 seconds!!!

By the way to some of the people that complained about the changing temps when using all 4 burners. Read the directions. It's right there explaining you cannot do high heat on all burners at the same time. Who cooks on high on all burners at the same time and what recipe calls for burning food!!!

product_title: Electrolux EIFLS55IIW 4.2 cu. ft. Front Load Steam Washer - IQ-Touch Control Island White
review_text:
Amazon says authors shouldn't review books.
But they didn't say anything about authors not being able to review whitegoods.

I'm an author. I'm also a feminist and I love my new washing machine.
The alternative - washing everything by hand - doesn't bear thinking about. How would I write The Next Amazing Novel (TM) if I was stuck in the laundry all day?

Ever wonder how Tolstoy wrote such massive books like War and Peace and Anna Karennina? I bet he never had to do laundry in his life.

Mind you, on the first day when this little love came home, I did sit in the laundry all day.
It was mesmerising. Clothes tumbling left. Stop. Clothes tumbling right. Oh the giddy majesty of it all.
1000rpm for the spin cycle. That's some serious torque right there.

But it's the "jetstream" fountain of sudsy wonderfulness splitter-splattering onto the clothes, making them all wet, that makes this washer so special.
Reminding me that I desperately needed to pee. You know, like at the end of that movie Titanic, when you've been sitting there for nearly three hours and your bladder is going to explode, and all you're looking at is water? Cold, icerbergy water that makes you want to pee!

That.

So, if I may advise anyone about to buy one of these fabulous products, don't sit there watching it all day.
You won't get any writing done, and you'll need to pee.

(I recently bought a 7kg Electrolux frontloading washing machine. Not this exact model, but one very much like it. And I really do love it.)

product_title: LG Home Applaince DLE2050W - 7.3 CF FRONT CTRL SILVER DR TR
review_title: Jingle your clothes dry in style!
review_text:
I bought this dryer with the matching [[ASIN:B003044XOC LG : WM2050CW 27in Front Load Washer, 4.0 cu. ft. Capacity - White]] washer (see my LG WM2050CW washer review). This is our first electric dryer from LG and we are happy to say that just like the matching pair of washing machine LG WM2050CW the DLE2050W 7.1 cu ft capacity electric Dryer is an excellent dryer appliance!

It is very easy to operate and has sensors (Sensor Dry System) and automatically adjusts the drying time for clothes which in my humble opinion eliminates the guess work one needs to do with respect to drying times for clothes. This saves a lot of money in electricity bills.

It has manual controls for timed drying cycles if you are not happy with the sensor based drying cycle. It boasts 5 Temperature Levels of High, Medium High, Medium, Low & Ultra Low and also another Wrinkle Care Cycle to Periodically tumble-dry clothes without heat to reduce wrinkles.

Product dimensions are (WxHxD) 27"x38 3/4"x30" (51" with door open) The machine is very well built and made in Korea and in my opinion should last many years!

PROS

[+] 7.1 Cu ft is large enough for most households
[+] Reasonably quick drying time (40-45 mins) for regular load of clothes
[+] Plethora of automated options for desired fabric care
[+] User friendly control panel which also has child lock
[+] Fairly large lint screen filter to capture lint.
[+] We like the musical jingle at the end of a cycle rather than a loud buzzer!

CONS

[-] Needs 3-wire (30AMP) 220V AC power cord to be purchased extra
[-] Needs a semi-rigid dryer duct to be purchased extra depending on installation location
[-] Does not include stand for drying shoes

Make sure that you level the Dryer properly for optimal operation, the included feet leveling screws may need tweaking to match the washing machine's height level.

If you have already bought the excellent energy saving washing machine model [[ASIN:B003044XOC LG : WM2050CW 27in Front Load Washer, 4.0 cu. ft. Capacity - White]] add this to complete your laundry pair - Highly recommended!

product_title: Samsung RF266AEPN 26 cu. ft. French Door Refrigerator: Stainless Platinum
review_title: Best refrigerator I have ever owned
review_text:
We have owned Kenmore, LG and Magic Chef refrigerators before purchasing this one for our new home, and we could not be happier. We bought the unit from Sears in May of 2012 (partly because the salesman raved about it). Since our purchase date is quite a bit later than the dates corresponding to the negative reviews for this item, perhaps Samsung has worked out the bugs for the RF266AEPN.

For example, there are several complaints about the ice maker. Well, the ice maker in -our- RF266AEPN is by far the best one I have ever used. It is VERY quiet - we rarely hear it, even when new ice drops into the tray. It also makes the best ice I have ever seen come out of an automatic ice maker. The ice tray keeps the ice at the perfect temperature - a difficult task in a defrosting freezer compartment. Each "cube" (they're actually moon-shaped) is perfectly formed, and they never melt and then refreeze to stick together. As a comparison, our LG would slowly turn the ice in the tray into one giant block via the process of melting and refreezing during the defrosting process.

The temperature is very even in the refrigerator compartment. Continuing the comparisons, both our Kenmore and LG units would freeze lettuce that was left in the vegetable compartment too long - this, even though we spent considerable effort to balance the cooling in both refrigerators. The Samsung has needed no such effort.

Generally speaking, our RF266AEPN is also very quiet - certainly MUCH quieter than any other refrigerator we have previously owned.

We like this refrigerator so much that we have decided to purchase Samsung again when we build our retirement home in 7-8 years.

product_title: Samsung RF266AEBP 26 cu. Ft. French Door Refrigerator - Black Pearl
review_text:
I really like this refrigerator; I've had it for 2 months now. This fridge looks great and has beautifully designed handles. Lighting is great inside, and the temperature is good. Shelves are easy to adjust and easy to clean. It's easy to find what I need in this fridge, even though it's so big. I'm impressed with how much longer my vegetables and fruit last compared to the fridges I had before the Samsungs. I LOVE the bottom freezer with a divider and a second pull-out drawer above it. I can throw my items in the freezer without fear of them getting lost way in the back.
I'd tried a Samsung before this, with door ice maker and water dispenser. I loved that one, but didn't like the amount of door shelf space lost to the ice maker. This one has solved that problem. I was concerned that it might be less energy efficient, since you have to open the freezer door to get to the ice and open the fridge door to get to the water. But a couple of months of using it and I'm not so worried. The increase in space compared to the model with the ice maker in the door more than makes up for that worry. The only difficulty I've had is that the deli drawer has gone off the tracks a couple of times, and it's a pain to get back on, especially if it's full.

I would buy this one again in a minute.

product_title: Samsung RF266AEBP 26 cu. Ft. French Door Refrigerator - Black Pearl
review_text:
My parents have had an older model in the same line of this fridge, and I was always impressed by it's functionality and looks. At 26 cu. ft., there is so much space for everything. I especially like the height adjustable racks for the taller containers. I prefer not to have the ice and water dispenser on the front because it just takes up shelf space in the interior. The ice maker is in the interior freezer rack. Though it does not come with its own ice scooper. I was pleasantly surprised to find out that this fridge had an interior water dispenser. It's on the left side of the main cabin and does not take up much space at all.

The picture shown for the product does not do the elegant black glossy finish any justice. Everyone is wowed the first time they see it. Fingerprints and streaks do linger, but you really have to be looking to see them. A minor nitpick is more related to my kitchen's layout, but the fridge has a sticker with the tag, model, etc. numbers on the left. That part of the fridge shows and is a small break in the fridge's otherwise clean and sleek finish.

My one complaint is that the bottom freezer compartment sometimes gets stuck. I have to yank the handle to get it open. Maybe it's just too pressurized.

product_title: Samsung RF266AEBP 26 cu. Ft. French Door Refrigerator - Black Pearl
review_text: We bought this refrigerator in early 2012. A year later the ice maker had to be replaced.  This summer, the ref part iced over and stopped cooling...tech said it was a fault in this particular model.  He cleared it, installed a better heating element (to prevent the icing over).  85 days later, it stopped working.  Overnighted a replacement motherboard but the day it was unplugged apparently re-set it...and it went on without a peep even without the new motherboard.  Next day, it died again. Unplugged. RE-set...compressor came on but not the fan..cooled the fridge but got hot.  Turned it off/on again and directed 2 small fans at the compressor...worked for 1/2 day...refrigerator has now stopped cooling altogether. Samsung won't offer anything but local repair info.  No answer OR callback.  I'm ready to chuck this!

product_title: Samsung RF266AEBP 26 cu. Ft. French Door Refrigerator - Black Pearl
review_text: Even though Samsung may rate high, this model is a POS. The first thing that went wrong was the icemaker after about a year and a half, just 6 months out of warranty. Soon afterward, we lost the ability to control the temperature with the push buttons at the top of the frig, they just stopped responding. Water started leaking from somewhere inside the frig and since we couldn't control the temp, it froze on the bottom shelf. We hired a guy (since Samsung didn't stand behind this particular product) and he put in a heating wire to address the freezing water. He said it was a common problem so he had a common fix (use a wire to heat the tube so it wouldn't freeze). It worked until about 6 months ago when it started leaking. We have a laminate floor so it ruined the floor underneath and around the refrigerator. Now we have to buy another frig, and I'm afraid it WILL NOT be a Samsung. I still like Samsung TV's (for now) and own three of them, but I'm afraid when it comes to refrigerators, I'll take my chances with an LG or GE.

product_title: Samsung RF266AEBP 26 cu. Ft. French Door Refrigerator - Black Pearl
review_title: It got worse and worse until it was so loud that I ...
review_text:
It's hard to imagine a single refrigerator causing so many problems.

I was bed-bound with a broken ankle when the machine starting making a racket. It got worse and worse until it was so loud that I couldn't sleep. Keep in mind that I couldn't walk and was stuck in a place without phone service.

I did a lot of on-line research and learned about a problem with Samsung refrigerators freezing up a solid block of ice behind the refrigerator section. This makes the circulating fan continually ding on the ice, until it is ultimately unable to move. The problem is caused by a drain at the bottom of the refrigerator section; it freezes over and then liquid from the defrost cycle can't drain.

The solution was to take everything out of the refrigerator, remove the shelves and drawers, and then unscrew the back panel to get at the ice. I did all of this standing on one leg and in great pain. The ice was so bad that the back panel wouldn't come off. It took about 24 hours for the ice to melt enough to remove the panel and for the remaining ice to melt.

There's a little metal clip-thingy that you can install over the drain hole to keep the drain from blocking with ice. I didn't have it on hand, of course, so had to reassemble the refrigerator without it. I ordered the part - it's cheap - in case the problem would reoccur.

Three months later: there is water all over my floor from the drain pan. It appears that the drain hole is plugged again. I will have to take all day, and possibly part of tomorrow, to go through the whole process of unplugging, disassembling, and waiting for the ice to thaw. Then I will add in the little clip to keep it from happening again - hopefully, anyway.

It's three days before Christmas. I have a lot of food in my refrigerator. Some of it will have to be thrown away.

Samsung - and any other manufacturer who reads this - we are tired of appliances with lots of features but low reliability. I need appliances that don't cause me a lot of stress, and don't require replacement after three or four years. Yes, I'm willing to pay more for a reliable refrigerator. I'd pay DOUBLE if it didn't mean having to buy refrigerators twice as often as is reasonable.

product_title: LG : LBC22520ST 22.4 cu. ft. Bottom-Freezer Refrigerator - Stainless Steel
review_title: LOADS of CONVENIENT storage! EASY to USE Refrigerator AND Bottom Freezer
review_text:
When our old coppertone refrigerator from the 1960's could no longer be repaired,
we had no idea what would be a wise choice on todays market.
We moved everything to the garage refrigerator and started the hunt.
After days of internet search and driving to most every store in the area,
this is the refrigerator we gained the most faith in.

We had listed our priorities:
1. BOTTOM FREEZER! -- SWING DOOR! -- NOT pull! -- Would like some storage on the door.
Pull out basket for easy reach. Ice maker, and a light in the freezer.
(Our coppertone was bottom freezer, swing door, with 2 shelves on the door, we loved it!)
2. WHATEVER BRAND that had the BEST REVIEWS.
3. BUY FROM a company that had a reputation of standing behind their product.
NOT JUST the manufacturer, but also the place of purchase,
and the quality and lenght of their extended warranty.
4. The COLOR we wanted was sacerficed, because cream with swing door,
bottom freezer is only to be found in TWO refrigerators on the planet!
(A)- Sears, and NOT the Elite line, so for us that was NOT an option.
On Sears own web sight it had only three reviews, and they were LESS then VERY POOR.
We looked at the display model at Sears and knew we'd rather switch
colors preference than buy that one.
Cheap looking plastic handles, etc.
(B)- G.E., a lower line that had less cu. ft. and ALL BAD reviews.

Most of a week was spent on the internet, with extensive notes.
We went from store to store for over a week, looking at ALL the display models,
the salesmen checked there store catalogs, we opened all the doors and drawers everywhere we went.
If you ask, the salesmen will plug in display models so you can hear the motor,
beeps, and see if the lighting suits you.
For us a BOTTOM FREEZER -- with a SWING DOOR, NOT a drawer,
is the ONLY convenient, accommodating style out there,
and there getting hard to find.
The pull out drawers are back breaking
with no extra conveniences to make it worth the hardship.
And of course there's no door to have storage on.
There are other stainless steel swing door models, in more expensive brands,
BUT those companys only make this style in a smaller size. Usually a total of 16 to 19 cu.ft.

We had read all 72 reviews for this model at the aj madison sight.
It stood out with a 4.4 star average.
So this LG-LBC22520ST, 22 cu. ft bottom-freezer is what we bought earlier this year.
The label inside the frige says, 'Made in Mexico 2011'.
(USED to be made in Soul, Korea)
For now, we have only good things to say about this model.

The refrigerator - freezer is Enery Star rated and has;
1. Dual digital temperature controls on the ceiling of the frige, that goes from 1-7.
7 being the coldest. The recommendation for top & bottom is #4.
Depending on how frequently the door is opened.
Using a refrigerator thermometer, our frige came in at;
#4 the frige cools to 34, at #5 it cools to 30 degrees.
At #4 the freezer cools to 2 above 0, at #5 cools to -2.
(At #5 it was VERY difficult to scoop the ice cream, #4 very firm & better for scooping)
The owner's manual states the unit will cool;
Refigerator; 32 to 47.
Freezer; - 6 to 9
TEMPERATURE GUIDELINES;
40 - 80 Warm.
32 - 40 Refrigerating.
0 - 32 Freezing.
-20 - 0 O.K.Freeze

2. FRIGE -- 15 1/2 cu. ft. has two bright 40 w bulbs, perfect lighting.
Three large bins. Split tempered glass shelves that can be re-arranged.
(they don't pull out) The door has 6 large capacity shelves, ALL of which are over 6" deep.
The bottom one is stationary but can be removed for cleaning.
The other 5 can be re-arranged. The shelves can hold several gallon size products.
Overall, the door holds a VERY impressive amount.
This model is not counter dept, you may want to double check how it suits your area.

3. FREEZER -- 6.9 cu.ft. has one 40 w bulb. Ice maker, has an on/off switch there.
Plus an automatic sensor that will immediately stop the ice maker when full, when left 'on'.
A large bin holds the ice.
When the ice maker pours the ice in the EMPTY plastic bin it is quite noisey,
but after there's ice in the bottom, it's much quieter.
Lining the bin with a rubber mat calms down the noise when empty.
Or if you have enough ice in the bin, it can be turned off at that location.
On the ceiling of the frige, between the digital controls there's an 'ice plus' button.
Pressing that will automatically speed up the ice production for a 24 hr. period.
The shelf DOES pull out. The large basket on the bottom slides on side rails, and also pulls out.
There's one shelf on the door, the LENGHT of the door, NOT just a small pocket like the G.E.

4. An alarm system with a soft 42 db, starts beeping when the door has been open for one minute.
It beeps 3x at the first minute, and then 3x every 30 seconds,
and it doesn't cancell until the door is properly shut.
If the door is left open over 6 and 1/2 minutes, the interior lights automatically shut off.
If you close the door and open it, the lights are back on,
they'll go off again in another 6 and 1/2 minutes.
I'm not crazy about these two enery saving features, but they aren't as bad as you'd think.
These features are some of the ways the industry is using to qualify for enery star quality.
This is an very quite running refrigerator, the motor is a gentle quite sound.

ST stands for stainless steel, the doors and the handles are, and magnets won't stick there.
The top and the sides are textured metal, painted medium gray, magnets will stick there.
The door handle comes on the left as pictured, but delivery men ,or you,
if you'd perfer can easily change to the right.
The gray 'plugs' on the door front are actually screws that are unscrewed
by the pressure of your thumb and twisting. You don't use tools on those 'plugs'.
Available in - black - white - stainless steel. Weight is 235.lbs.
The manufactures warranty is one year parts and labor, but 7 years on the sealed system.

We didn't experience a 'residue' left on the outside of the unit from the plastic film

product_title: GE Profile : PDWF800RBB 24 Built-In Dishwasher - Black
review_title: A decent dishwasher marred by poor quality control and a high price tag.
review_text:
I bought this unit to replace a 10 year old GE dishwasher that was noisy and whose racks were rusting. Since my house has an open floor plan, I was looking for a quiet unit. I seriously considered Bosch dishwashers, which are the industry leaders for quiet operation and low energy consumption. However, I was disappointed with their flimsy construction, small interior capacity, and poor lower rack design. This GE dishwasher is fairly quiet, with a good rack design and a very sturdy door. Since I am not a fan of hidden top-mounted controls, this model's front mounted controls appealed to me. So far, this GE dishwasher has been very good at cleaning. I am disappointed with GE quality; the front control panel is misaligned, and the screws on the door were quite loose. One of the tabs on the silverware basket broke within a week. GE quality control appears to be asleep at the switch. Also, GE's website states that this model has several features (cutlery tray, angled rack dry system) that are, in fact, absent on this model, which basically constitutes false advertising.

Pros:
* Cleans dishes well
* Good rack design
* Sturdy construction
* Generally quiet operation
* Well designed controls with remaining time readout
* Long warranty

Cons:
* Poor assembly quality
* False claims on GE website regarding features
* Expensive
* Not as quiet or as energy efficient as competing models
* Doesn't qualify for the "Cash for Clunkers" appliance program in Massachusetts

Bottom line:
A decent dishwasher marred by poor quality control and a high price tag.

review_title: Nice dryer but use with caution
review_text:
We bought one of these dryers in late 2011, and loved it: looks and works great.

Then we moved in 2013, and after installing the dryer in the new house, the lint inside the dryer housing ignited. Some of the lint must have shifted during the move, moving closer to the gas heater source. Luckily, the fire didn't cause major damage. I did some research online, and came across a class-action suite, "[...]", which seems to indicate that this was not just an isolated incident.

You need to take the back of the dryer off in order to see the lint buildup inside the dryer housing (around the drum motor, heater source, etc), and vacuum up as much lint as possible. My wife is meticulous about cleaning the lint trap with every load, so there may be a design issue involved letting the lint migrate inside the housing. We will keep using it, but will check the lint build-up often to make sure it is safe.

review_title: Clothes wash clean, uses little water, software upgraded
review_text:
I installed an LG wm2050cw, it is quiet and washes well. There was a software upgrade LG has done to models that now ship. I would prefer a longer spin cycle option, as I sometimes manually run an extra spin to really dry my clothes more, but it has the ability to do it. I bought it for under six hundred with tax and install, from a local "orange" big box store. Santa fe, NM also offered a four hundred eighty dollar credit, so it cost me in the end about one hundred sheets of paper. I also bought a basic GE gas dryer, and put both on pedestals I bought at an online auction site. With a little creativity it all worked out great.

The only downside is the door swings out a ways when you leave it open to dry the tub, some other models I looked at the door was stiffer and stayed where you put it. But the overall quality compared to the other models and the long 10 year warranty on the motor, lifetime tub, outweighed the inconvience. I also attach a bungee cord to the pedestal and it keeps the door tight when left open. If you obsessed with looks you may not like this. I like the functionality of it, even the delivery man said he never picks up LG washers for defects, but often picks up other higher rated well known brands, no regrets!

I guess though, you could always in anything get a lemon, but so far I have a peachy set up.

One last thing I went through customer service to confirm my serial number had the software upgrade, the call started overseas, collected some info, transfered me to someone in the states, checked my serial number, confirmed update, total call time under ten minutes. I did not need service, but they seemed fast and informed.

product_title: LG 4.0 CF WASHER FRONT CONTROL WHITE
review_text: Bought this machine a couple of weeks ago knowing that it had a software issue that LG acknowledged.  Even before they came out to do the software update, the machine worked beyond expectation.  The tech came tonight and performed the 5 minute upgrade and now I am confident that I will not have any issues.  The stacked unit resides in my kitchen which is next to the living room and I am able to enjoy TV while it is running it's cycle.  Some noise but not bad at all.  I would recommend this to anyone.

product_title: LG 4.0 CF WASHER FRONT CONTROL WHITE
review_text: I love this washer. I paid about $650 including delivery and 7% sales tax. This is my second front-loader. Do not be afraid of front-loaders. My first one was a Whirlpool Duet, probably cost about $1000 in 2003 and worked well for about 6.5 years -- so that's disappointing -- sounded like a bearing was broken and that costs a few hundred to repair so I figured I was better off buying new. This LG is so much better than my old Whirlpool. I'm guessing the front loader technology has gotten better since then. The LG has very little shaking and vibration, it is very quiet. The biggest concern with front loaders is the moldy smell, I have used my LG now for one month and no smell. I did occasionally get the moldy smell in my old Whirlpool and some mildewy stuff around the rubber part surrounding the washer opening which I wiped down occasionally, but so far nothing in the LG. The LG has simpler lines on the rubber thing so it looks like less nooks and crannies for water and mildew to accumulate plus it has drain holes so the water can drain away. Also, I learned with my Whirlpool front loader and I do this with my LG and you should do this with all front-loaders-- you must leave the washer door open all the time, leave the soap dispenser drawer open all the time, and never let wet clothes sit in the washer, move them to the dryer right away. I do at least a couple loads a week in hot water and use oxi-clean powder on a couple loads a week. In the Whirlpool, I found that the Tide product for cleaning the mold smell didn't help that much, I found that Oxi-clean a couple times a week does a better job. I usu do an extra rinse on all cycles and the cotton cycle takes about 65 minutes and extra soil cycle might take 90 minutes or so, so the cycles are longer than top loaders. I use only HE detergent for front-loaders and I use only the amount recommended by LG -- not the amt recommended by the detergent company. The LG has a user-friendly display panel, and the soap dispenser is clearly marked for correct levels of soap. This LG plays a cute little song when it's done rather than an annoying beep. It spins the laundry really dry, so the dryer cycle can be shorter. I washed a king size down comforter in my LG using the bulky cycle, no problem.  I just love this machine.

includes a "clean self" cycle)...and it is only available in white.

and just summarize by saying you won't find a better high efficiency washer for
your money than the LG WM2050.

product_title: LG 4.0 CF WASHER FRONT CONTROL WHITE
review_title: Beware of  "noisy door syndrome"  with this LG model
review_text:
This is my first front loader and I have generally been pleased. I was aware of front-loading issues like musty drums and moldy seals from the experiences of others. I leave the door open, wipe down the seal occasionally, clean the detergent bay and do my best to remember to clean the bottom drain.
The real annoyance has been the noise from the front door. The washer is on a solid floor and while the unit itself does not vibrate, both the door and door latch do. The noise travels throughout the house and you certainly cannot be on the phone while the washer goes through its spin cycle. The vibration did not start until after 500th load. The washer was close to its one-year anniversary when the rattle started and it just kept getting louder. I put in a service call and the service person the came was very professional and thorough in looking the machine over. He said that the noisy rattling door did not hinder the performance of the machine and repairs would not be eligible under the warrantee. As far as exactly what was wrong he could only speculate that the rubber seal on the door was "relaxed" or "broken in" to a point where the seal was not pushing as strongly against the door resulting in some "play" that allows the door to rattle (loudly).
While this noisy machine may not be considered defective it sure is a irritating. There is no way to run a load of wash at night without waking the entire house and you can forget about watching television when the spin cycle kicks into high gear.
Too bad.

product_title: LG 4.0 CF WASHER FRONT CONTROL WHITE
review_title: Good features and performance, poor reliability
review_text:
I have owned this unit for approximately 3.5 years with light use (~4 loads/week). I have been happy with the features and performance, except that the door seal builds up gunk and odors if not cleaned regularly. Also, laundry will mildew if left in the machine for more than a couple of hours after the end of the cycle. From my limited research, these seemed like common problems with front loaders back in 2010, so I wasn't concerned. The other problem I've encountered is that the detergent dispenser drawer seems poorly designed, because if you attempt to fill the bleach compartment, bleach spills out down the front of the machine. I'm not sure if I have a faulty dispenser, but I hardly ever use bleach, so I haven't bothered to fix this problem. FWIW, I have not seen some problems others have had, such as water spilling from the door seal drain and loud noises during spin cycles.

I would have recommended this machine until yesterday, when the unit suddenly started spewing water from underneath the top cover. Lots of water. Luckily, I was nearby and noticed it in time to shut it down and unplug it before much damage was done. It's out of warranty, so I removed the top cover and quickly discovered a massive hole in the rubber hose that connects the cold supply line to the main wash detergent dispenser. The OEM replacement hoses are absurdly expensive and appear to be poor quality seam-welded construction - lo and behold, the rupture occurred on the seam. I just went to the hardware store and got a 6' length of braided reinforced hose to replace all 4 of the inner hoses for about $5. That should fix the problem, but if I hadn't been standing right there, the water leak could have easily shorted various electrical connections inside the machine and started a fire. Major safety hazard.

product_title: LG 5.6 CF ELECTRIC RANGE WHITE
review_title: Great stove, very pleased with it!
review_text:
I purchased this stove after my Whirlpool stove failed after six months of use. I studied a lot of models, stayed away from anything made or OEM'ed by Whirlpool, and settled on this model. I was a little hesitant about buying a stove that wasn't from a bog box appliance store, but no one had them in stock locally.

The stove arrived approximately 4 days later on a palette, wrapped in styrofoam, cardboard and plastic. Not a scratch on it, I moved in into the spot formerly occupied by the Whirlpool and attached the stove plug to it (sold separately). I fired up the stove and noticed several differences compared to my old stove.

The first is a more even heating surface. The ring of coils heat up very quickly, and apply a very even heat to all of the pan, so that everything cooks at the same rate. This seems like it should be a standard feature, but the previous stove would have hot spots on the burner that cooked parts faster than other parts.

Second is the large oven space. I can get two baking pans side by side, which is important when it comes to making TV dinners for a family of 8. It also has a brilliant blue color on the inside, which just makes the inside of the stove cleaner looking.

Third, my electrical usage on the stove has gone down, again compared to the previous model.

I did have a concern about a clicking noise that I heard and called for warrant repair just to check it. They came out in a day or two and checked in, and the noise (not very audible) is normal. It's the heating coils getting up to temperature.

Overall, I'm very pleased with the purchase and even more comfortable buying big appliances on Amazon.

product_title: Samsung RF263AEBP 26 cu. Ft. French Door Refrigerator - Black Pearl
review_text:
Had it for a couple years now. The icemaker worked great for the first few months. Now it has become more noisy (refilling, motor, etc) and the cubes are sticking together and coming out broken into small pieces. But in my experience, I've never seen an icemaker that worked well. Still, not bad. It's well built, roomy and still operates queitly. I like the design and layout of the interior. Consistant temps, well lit, installed easily.

There is one thing that bugged me for a long time though... The doors - like any fridge - will automatically swing "closed" when you let go of them. However, on this one they have a hinge that stops them just prior to closing. WTF? Even if you give them a little extra shove, they will stop just before closing. You have to manually push them closed, or give them an extra push for them to swing closed. On my last fridge, all you had to do was let go of the door and it would automatically swing all the way to closed, so it took me forever to get used to this one. I was constantly walking away only to have the door alarm (good thing it has one) go off - go back and push the damn door shut. Now that I'm in the habit of pushing them shut it's not as big a deal, but it really bugged me at first. Don't quite understand that hinge design... I will say the alarm is a pleasant-sounding one.

But overall it's a very good refrigerator, has good ratings, and I feel I made a good choice.

Ours has several dents in the front panels, not sure if its because of cheap quality thin metal or ? but I find it interesting that this is our third fridge in this house all have been the same size yet this one is the only one that has developed dents.

Other minor gripes are that its difficult to get tall items in the fridge if its more than 8-9" tall and doesn't fit in a door panel your SOL. Yes you can adjust a shelf but what that does is make the 2 shelves above it worthless.

My final complaint is with the freezer drawer. Personally I feel that the drawer mechanism (slides and the tub itself) take up way too much usable room. Secondly stuff tends to get buried and if its mostly full you end up having to move everything to find what your looking for.

The freezer also has a small pull out drawer. We have used that for kids treats in the summer (ice cream popsicles etc..) but currently we are using it for our frozen veggies. works OK but the fact that the ice-maker takes up 50% means your not gonna get much of anything up there.

I have had some minor grievances with the ice-maker. It works fine but sometimes when you open the freezer drawer an ice cube or two fal out of the tray and then get jammed in the door mechanism which means you have to get on your knees and find and remove the cube.

We have always had side by sides and to be honest I miss them dearly. Our previous side x had pull out drawers and shelves. The freezer had several pull out wire trays and yes sometimes you had to dig for something but never like on this french door unit.

Next time I buy a fridge I'll take some soda cans with me to make sure i have room for my pop & beer.

Lastly why is it with the cost of LED bulbs now so darn cheap that refrigerators don't come with LED lighting?

product_title: Samsung RF263AEBP 26 cu. Ft. French Door Refrigerator - Black Pearl
review_text:
Ice machine broke just after warranty expired. $120 to replace
Does not make enough ice for 2 people let alone a family of 4

product_title: Samsung RF263AEBP 26 cu. Ft. French Door Refrigerator - Black Pearl
review_text:
I bought this fridge (but the stainless steel door) in May 2011 because of great reviews at consumer sites and here. When this fridge worked, it worked well although as some reviewers have mentioned its doors swing closed on their own but do not close all the way shut, luckily the alarm sounds so you can fix this. Same problem with the freezer drawer.

The big issue though is that it just stopped working with no warning. Evidently the chip and mother board blew. No lightning storm, no electric surges, no reason, just blew. It now needs to be fixed to the tune of over $500 because the warranty is only for 1 year. Because parts come from overseas, it also will take 1 week to 10 days to get them before being repaired. So not only did I loose a bunch of food, I also had to purchase a small replacement fridge to hold us over (and of course cannot store much in it so food costs are higher for us in the meantime since I cannot take advantage of buying in bulk). All in all I am really upset about this.

The repair guy told me that he gets a lot of calls from Samsung fridge owners. The issues are the water/ice maker and the electronics. He thought this was because Samsung has not had as much experience making fridges although they have lots of electronics experience.

A fridge can be a very expensive purchase -- I expect a new one to have no issues for at least 10 years. I am very dissatisfied and worried about how long this one will be running.

For all of you who already have this fridge, consider contacting Sears to purchase a service smart agreement (when it breaks) like I did so that it will be covered for service repairs (this is a service you buy after you already have a broken product and you do not have to have bought the original product from Sears). It will save you some money on repair costs. No I do not work for Sears nor does anyone in my family.

Update: I have had to replace the bar the pulls the freezer drawer open. While the bar is metal it is attached to plastic pieces that are screwed to the drawer and those have cracked. Because the parts needed to be ordered from the manufacturer I have had a long wait and it cost me another several hundred dollars with parts and labor. I would not buy a fridge from Samsung again.

product_title: Samsung RF263AEBP 26 cu. Ft. French Door Refrigerator - Black Pearl

product_title: Samsung RF263AEBP 26 cu. Ft. French Door Refrigerator - Black Pearl
review_text:

product_title: Bosch : SHE55M16UC 24 Evolution 500 Series Full Console Dishwasher - Black
review_title: Lovely machine  but  loading may be a problem
review_text:
We bought this dishwasher a month ago, and are generally pleased with it. It washes the dishes well, and is sufficiently adjustable to take tall items in either shelf. It is extremely quiet. It takes 105-120 minutes to run a cycle, but that's standard these days for energy efficient machines. I do wish that instead of a countdown, the LED display would show what part of the cycle it was at (wash, rinse, or dry).

Our major complaint is that the tines that separate and support the dishes aren't well suited for our dishes. They all slant, and they are fairly close together, so putting in glasses or mugs or pitchers is difficult, because you want them to stand vertically and the tines make this hard to accomplish. Because the tines are so close together, bowls will fit only if you lie them flat, taking up a lot of space per bowl. Our soup bowls are fairly curvy, not the flattish ones you find in elegant china, and there's really no way to stack them. (You can lie half the tines flat, but then there's no dish support at all.) Think about how _your_ dishes will fit in the dishwasher, before you choose this one.

product_title: Bosch : SHE55M16UC 24 Evolution 500 Series Full Console Dishwasher - Black
review_text:
After reading many bad reviews of Bosch dishwashers, I made the plunge. It is quiet, very high capacity, washes very well, dries at least as well as my old washer. We wanted an adjustable top rack but have not adjusted it in 3 months. Our washing schedule now depends on when we run out of dishes instead of when it is full.

If one stops the washer when the timer hits zero, it has not started drying, and the dishes will be wet. Just wait an hour and your dishes will be dry, at least as dry as old fashioned ones with an exposed heating element.

The high capacity means that the bottom is very close to the floor, so one must bend over to load and unload. Complaints about the bottom rack being hard to slide are because the door is not fully opened.

product_title: Bosch : SHE55M16UC 24 Evolution 500 Series Full Console Dishwasher - Black
review_title: Cleans well, but rack tine pattern makes loading options limited
review_text:
Ordered sight unseen from another online vendor. After unit installed, opened it to place dirty dishes, and realized (as another reviewer also has commented) that rack tines are great for cups and for plates, but not at all accommodating of our stone-ware type bowls. The bowls aren't particularly large, but are not the more delicately made or shaped bowls one would find in a china or corelle-ware set. Also, hard to figure out how to load pots & pans along w/ the plates in the lower rack.

Bottom line, we are sending this machine back and getting a newer model of the Kenmore/Whirlpool washer that we had (it quit working, thus the need for a new machine).

We did run the machine once, and it cleaned very well - even removing some of the residual white film our old dishwasher had been leaving on some of the plasticware. And, it was very quiet.

product_title: Bosch : SHE55M16UC 24 Evolution 500 Series Full Console Dishwasher - Black
review_text:
Like another reviewer, I'm puzzled by the very negative reviews of Bosch washers. I took Consumer Reports' word for it, and bought this one. So far, I have only done a couple of loads, but I can say:

1. it washes well. It even got stains out of the bottom of my teapot.
2. it is extremely quiet--useful if your TV is in the room next to your kitchen.
3. it is attractive. I don't see any part of it looking cheap, as some reviewers do.
4. The stainless steel interior does have a smell, but it's more or less a "new car smell," not a displeasing one.

However,

1. the interior does seem a bit small, and it can be tricky to load because of the angled tines set close together.
2. it's a little narrower (about a half inch) than my old Whirlpool. It comes with rubber "wings" or gaskets on the side that can spread out to fill the opening built into your cupboards, but it would look nicer if it fit perfectly.
3. you must always have rinse agent in it every time you run it. The dishes turn out beautifully if you do, so I'm not really complaining about that.
4. it has filters that have to be emptied and rinsed regularly (which I haven't done yet).

That's all I can say so far. I'll update if any other problems emerge.

product_title: Bosch : SHE55M16UC 24 Evolution 500 Series Full Console Dishwasher - Black
review_title: Very Clean, Very Quiet, Very Happy
review_text:
(this is a copy of my review under the stainless steel exterior version SHE55M15UC...don't know why Amazon has them separated)

Installed myself. You will need a strain relief and power cord, and possibly an adapter to connect to your garbage disposal or pipe. The drain hose supplied fits up to 3/4". I needed 1". A $5 dishwasher drain hose adapter and a $1 3/4" galvanized steel pipe nipple solved that problem.

This thing is unbelievably quiet compared to our 8 year old previous 'quiet' model. You can easily carry on a conversation next to it. We have an open kitchen / living area that used to require turning up the television volume when the previous dishwasher ran...No More!

Dishes come out very clean. As others have said elsewhere, I think the Finish Quantum Powerball (sample provided) or another highly rated CR brand will make a huge difference in your results too.

The passive drying works extremely well. We will only have a few drops of water left on plastic.

I have seen the Sanitize light come on. It means that very specific conditions (time, etc as specified by the NSF) were achieved during the wash and dry. Note that the Sanitize light won't come on until the Drying cycle is complete, which is well after the Cycle countdown has reached '0'.

product_title: Bosch : SHE55M16UC 24 Evolution 500 Series Full Console Dishwasher - Black
review_text:
We bought the Bosch based on Consumer Reports. It is very quiet and cleans the dishes well. We traded it for a Maytag after 3 months because our stuff wouldn't fit in the racks. We have two dishwashers in our kitchen sitting side by side. It is worth the extra $500 and giving up a little cabinet space. When one fills up you start filling the next. No more having to fit 2 more places in a washer already full or starting it 3/4th full because the dishes for the next meal won't fit. We also have 2 microwaves in our kitchen.
The Bosch can't handle cookie sheets or cassarole dishes. It was designed in Europe with smaller families. If you only have 2 or 3 place settings, you can put the cassorole dish on the top rack with the 2 or 3 cups and it's no problem. We have 6-9 around our table and can't give up so much of the top rack. We found ourselves putting the big stuff in the Maytag and the plates and cups in the Bosch but we lost our cyle effiency. The bottom Rach on the Bosch didn't work for cups. We like puttin the heavy glass cups on the bottom because our top rack fill up first.
If you have a small family, no cookie sheets or big dishes and like the quiet, this is a great dishwasher.
The best racks are Maytag so we have now have two Maytags in our kitchen.

product_title: Bosch : SHE55M16UC 24 Evolution 500 Series Full Console Dishwasher - Black
review_text: This dishwasher looks nice but that's about it.  The racks are terribly designed and difficult to load.  The worst is that I end up with at least one chipped dish or cup every time I run this dishwashed no matter how carefully I load it.  This never happened even with the cheap Whirlpool dishwasher that came with the house.  I would definitely not buy this dishwasher.

product_title: Bosch : SHE55M16UC 24 Evolution 500 Series Full Console Dishwasher - Black
review_text:
I bought the Bosch dishwasher model # SHE55M16UC to replace a 10-year-old Bosch that would inexplicably flood the wood kitchen floor without any apparent reason. OK, it was fairly old, so why not just replace it instead of a costly repair, especially when there was no obvious fault, such as a worn gasket or hose? This particular model is pretty much the same, but has a couple of additional and basically useless wash options, especially if you wash the food off of your dishes before loading as we do.

PROs: It is just a dishwasher, but a fairly pricey one at that. It is attractive, but nothing special.

CONs:
1. The racks are quite obtrusive. Some dividers are too close together and cumbersome, actually reducing the capacity compared with our previous model. I read that criticism prior to buying it, but I didn't believe it until I saw this machine on the hoof, so to speak. It holds fewer cups and glasses and it is a challenge to find space for a long utensil like a knife or cooking spoon. Bowls take up so much space that they infringe on the plate areas and do not fit into the dividers well.

2. The dishes come out wet, as there is no specific drying element, as there was in the earlier models. If you leave them overnight, there is just a bit of moisture on the glasses, cups, and racks. This is weird.

3. The machine smells faintly like garbage - and we are talking about dishes that have all been pre-washed with water and scrubbed with an abrasive cloth - unless you use the Finish soap cubes provided as a sample with the machine. Just tried them and they work very well, as compared to Cascade dishwasher detergent. I am sure that it is much costlier. I will check that out.

4. You have to let the water heat up in the sink before starting the wash cycle. Never saw an instruction like that before. It insures you are starting the cycle with hot water. That is about 3 minutes of wasted water down the drain before turning on this machine. Do other machines have this requirement? I have no idea. We never did this before, but the user guide tells you to do this.

We had a GE two houses ago that had more options and worked like a champ. The builder of our current house recommended Bosch. Not sure there is a rational basis to switch, although GE is even more expensive and other GE products have gone downhill in recent years. Cannot give a ringing endorsement to this product.

product_title: Bosch : SHE55M16UC 24 Evolution 500 Series Full Console Dishwasher - Black
review_text:
Have had this less than a week. Out of the box, the end of cycle alert didn't work. Will have a
repair person take a look/see. I have to say, this is the best dishwasher I've ever had. It is
extremely quiet. The glasses come out sparkling and it does a fantastic job on dishes. Just scrape
off the food (no rinsing) easily load dishes and start washer. There is plenty of room for everything
plus it has a half load option. Great item. If the end of cycle alert had
worked, I'd have given it 5 stars.

Look around for best prices and free installation possibilities.

product_title: Bosch : SHE55M16UC 24 Evolution 500 Series Full Console Dishwasher - Black
review_text: I bought my Bosch model SHE55M16UC about three years ago at the recommendation of a high rating from Consumer Reports.  Nine days after the one year labor warranty expired the cheap plastic control panel broke off when opening the door one morning spilling the buttons all over the kitchen floor.  To Bosch's credit they honored the labor warranty at that time however here I am about two years later with the same exact part failure!  I am not abusing the appliance, this is happening simply by opening and closing the door everyday, for routine dishwashing.  This time I am ordering the part (control panel cover) online and doing repairs myself. (the buttons are re-usable).  However when I have another part failure,(pump, etc), I will most definitely NOT be replacing the unit with another Bosch dishwasher that much I can assure you.  I gave it one star because it is quiet when it's not breaking apart...

product_title: Bosch : SHE55M16UC 24 Evolution 500 Series Full Console Dishwasher - Black
review_text: This is the worst dishwasher I have ever had in 40 years of buying them.  Dishes are not clean even after it's very extensive wash cycles. product_title: Bosch : SHE55M16UC 24 Evolution 500 Series Full Console Dishwasher - Black
review_title: I do not recommend anyone buying this product

product_title: Bosch : SHE55M16UC 24 Evolution 500 Series Full Console Dishwasher - Black

product_title: Bosch : SHE55M16UC 24 Evolution 500 Series Full Console Dishwasher - Black
review_title: Paid $890. 00 for this dishwasher only 4 years ...
review_text: Paid $890.00 for this dishwasher only 4 years ago.  The door panel cover is made of cheap plastic, which just broke.  Called to see what the problem could be and was told it could be the cleaning products I use to clean the plastic, What???  Bosch not very helpful. Do not buy this product.  Look for dishwashers that have a real handle on them.

product_title: Whirlpool Duet Steam WFW9750WW 27 Front Load Washer 4.5 cu. ft. Capacity - White
review_text: We purchased a front loading HE washer and found out they have mold problems. Think twice before you purchase any HE front loading machine. DO YOUR HOMEWORK!

product_title: Whirlpool Duet Steam WFW9750WW 27 Front Load Washer 4.5 cu. ft. Capacity - White
review_text: My wife and I bought a brand new Whirlpool washer and dryer set.  We loved it for a little over a year.  Then the main bearing and the pressure sensor on the washer went out.  The cost to repair would have been over $1200.  We didn't pay that much for the washer.  I called customer service and they told me that they would not do ANYTHING after the one year warranty period expired - "NO EXCEPTIONS!!"  I found it difficult to believe that a company as established as Whirlpool would have such a policy.  I talked to supervisor and pressed him on the issue.  The answer remained - NO EXCEPTIONS.  If anything breaks after one year, it is your responsibility.  I understand normal wear and tear, but I expect the main bearing on the washer to last several years.  I am still stunned that a customer service supervisor would actually tell me that after one year (even a year and a day - as I asked him) they will do NOTHING.  Whirlpool does not care about anything after one year.  The service man that came and looked at the unit says this happens with Whirlpool often.  He said LG and Samsung have better bearings and will last longer.  I am still a huge fan of the front load washers and I will be shopping for a new one, but it won't be Whirlpool - never again.

product_title: Whirlpool Duet Steam WFW9750WW 27 Front Load Washer 4.5 cu. ft. Capacity - White
review_text: DO NOT BUY THIS!!!!  I have the exact problem as another reviewer.  My washer was bought new directly from Whirlpool.  15 months later, the bearing is blown.  Repair person just left my house this morning and said that repair will be very expensive:  stainless steel basket, washer tub, motor belt, and front counter weight all need to be replaced.  I don't have written estimate but when looking at these parts online, the cost for just parts is over $800 and repair tech estimated about $250 in labor charges.  I have not called Whirlpool yet and dont have high hopes based on other reviewers' experiences.  It looks like I need a new washer, and it won't be Whirlpool!

product_title: Whirlpool Duet Steam WFW9750WW 27 Front Load Washer 4.5 cu. ft. Capacity - White
review_text:
have had this machine for 6 months and have had three service calls already. hot water shut off failed six weeks in, causing the hot water to run though the machine all night long. drum broke away from axel at five months requiring "essentially the entire inside of the machine" be replaced per the technician. took 9 days to get parts and have repair completed. most recently an interior seal has hardened and begun to deteriorate into my loads of laundry. Current repair costs have exceeded the retail cost of the machine by 100%. Thankful it's all under warranty, but fearful of what's to come once warranty expires. would take my 7 year old maytag back in a heartbeat if I could! whirlpool customer service has done nothing but read from scripts while refusing to consider replacing this machine - "unless problems continue to occur" at which point they "might" consider replacing the unit. technician said whirlpool is always looking to point fingers at consumers rather than take responsibility for problems with their appliances.

as an aside - machine is ridiculously noisy even when functioning "properly" and routinely ties clothes in knots during washing. have had numerous problems with the dryer from this set as well.

product_title: Whirlpool Duet Steam WFW9750WW 27 Front Load Washer 4.5 cu. ft. Capacity - White
review_title: Make sure you have a backup washer
review_text: When we first purchased this washer I was thrilled at all the features it came with.  But now it has been 6 months and we have had to service it twice.  The first service was simple, it sucked a baby sock into the water pump and would not drain, the service tech showed my husband how to fix since this apparently happens regularly. The second time a bearing has went out, it has been 5 weeks and the part is back ordered and they don't have any idea when I will get my washer back. We have three small children and a ton of laundry.  We lose our borrowed washer in 4 days and will have to purchase a new washer or lug my laundry somewhere else for who knows how long.  I am not a satisfied customer!

product_title: Whirlpool Duet Steam WFW9750WW 27 Front Load Washer 4.5 cu. ft. Capacity - White
review_text: Had washer for only 6 months and the bearings went bad. If I were to have had to fix it the cost would be over $1300.00. (Parts were over $1200.00)The repair man suggest I take out an extended warrenty as this is a very common problem with the Whirlpool Duet. I called Whirlpool why they wouldn't just replace the unit as it would be cheaper for them then to replace then to repair and they said this is their rules and could not give any other explanation. It took two guys to repair and 3 hours as the unit had to be completely taken apart. I would think twice before buying another unit from Whirlpool.

product_title: Whirlpool Duet Steam WFW9750WW 27 Front Load Washer 4.5 cu. ft. Capacity - White
review_title: Poor Quality - Same problems as everyone else
review_text:
This was a great washing machine while it lasted. We had ours for about 3 years and then the main bearing went out. Problem is a $15 bearing is integrated into the tub, so you have to replace the tub to replace the bearing. All in all it works out to be cheaper to just get a new machine.
If I was the only one with this problem I'd probably blow it off as bad luck, but when you ask around everyone is having this same issue. We paid over $1000 for this 3 years ago and were ecstatic and how well it cleaned the clothes, but for that much money the quality should be much higher.

product_title: Whirlpool Duet Steam WFW9750WW 27 Front Load Washer 4.5 cu. ft. Capacity - White
review_text:
We were ecstatic when we plonked $2200 for our set of Whirlpool Duet Steam Washer and Gas Dryer with matching pedestals. They have worked beautifully for us until recently the display just stopped working. We called for repair person and were informed the board had to be replaced at the cost of $500. Went online to research the issue and discover that this has happened to many others. Repair company informed us this was a common issue and he expected other issues to come up - we might want to just replace the washer. So we purchased a Maytag and 5 year warranty for slightly more than the repair of the duet washer would have cost.

Will never buy Whirlpool again.

product_title: Whirlpool Duet Steam WFW9750WW 27 Front Load Washer 4.5 cu. ft. Capacity - White
review_text:
This is the second (yes glutton for punishment) Whirlpool Front Loader that I purchased and the second to break after a little over one year of use...and, yes, the bearing issue is the culprit. I purchased the 4 year protection plan from Lowes the second time I bought the washer and am now going on three weeks with no washer while they try to find a service professional who will not run screaming from yet another Whirlpool Frontloader with a bearing problem...

I am disgusted with this product and urge anyone considering any Whirlpool appliance to learn from my mistake(s) and choose another company!

product_title: Whirlpool Duet Steam WFW9750WW 27 Front Load Washer 4.5 cu. ft. Capacity - White
review_text:
If you own this washer and have a recurring F35 code, understand that this can be caused by socks in the strainer or in the drin at the bottom of the door. However, it is more a symptom of a failing analog pressure switch. You can buy this part on amazon (Water Level Pressure Sensor Switch Replaces W10156252) and replace it yourself in 5 minutes for $75. Whirlpool has not ever contacted those of us who registered our purchases with them about the prevalence of these failures, nor have they briefed A&E that this failure is common.

Whirlpool - you invested a lot in getting us to be customers and nothing in keeping us! Bye Bye!

product_title: Whirlpool Duet Steam WFW9750WW 27 Front Load Washer 4.5 cu. ft. Capacity - White
review_text: After 20 months, I have not had any mechanical issues and it does seem to clean clothes sufficiently. That said, this machine loves to tie long sleeve shirts and jeans into knots. I usually do a load with nothing but jeans and when it is time to move them to the dryer, they all come out in one big ball that I have to untangle before putting them in the dryer. I am wondering how clean they can actually get being tied in a knot like that. Surprisingly, the matching dryer does not do this. My only other complaint is that it can get really loud on the spin-dry cycle. Part of the issue is that the OEM pedestal that it sits on is not very sturdy. Overall, I don't consider this to be a very good purchase for the money.

product_title: Whirlpool Duet Steam WFW9750WW 27 Front Load Washer 4.5 cu. ft. Capacity - White
review_title: The only thing I hate more than the washer is the dryer.
review_text: The only thing I hate more than the washer is the dryer, nevertheless, these are the problems you will encounter no matter how well it works. The washer stinks of mold all the time so you have to leave the door open to dry out. Even still you have to get the clothes out quickly or they immediately smell of mold so you have to wash them again. I've done all the tricks you're supposed to do and purchased the right detergent. It doesn't matter. The drawer at the top is dumb, too. Careful with using BLEACH because you need funnel to get it in there. And it's a pain in the neck to use too. Buttons buttons buttons. I had to type out instructions so everyone knew how to use it. Oops, (I'm not kidding here) I have to go turn the dryer on AGAIN, because IT DOESN'T DRY THE CLOTHES. As you can imagine, that plays well with the mold factory they just came from. Again with the buttons. It takes all day to do a load of laundry and if you don't babysit them you'll end up with moldy, wrinkled clothes. These things suck.

product_title: Whirlpool Duet Steam WFW9750WW 27 Front Load Washer 4.5 cu. ft. Capacity - White
review_text: I am posting this review as a service to others, I purchased both the Whirlpool Duet Steam washer (model WFW9500) and Dryer (model WGD9500) in December 2009 from Lowes and THANKFULLY also purchased the extended 4 year warranty.  Just after 1 year the door hinge to the washer broke. About a year later the bearings in the washer also went (previous reviewers have had the same problem).  They replaced all the parts and I was told the same thing as other reviewers, it's about a $1200 job.  This job was done in February. review_title: Worst Washing Machine Ever - Just Horrible
review_text:
I've used Maytags most of my life. Our wonderful Maytag Neptune front loader was ruined by storm damage and could not be replaced: Maytag is out of business. So we went for a Whirlpool.

One reason we picked this was that the Duet is one of the few washers that had (I thought) rational wash settings. Most of the brands now have cycles called "Baby", "Jeans", "White", etc. What are those supposed to mean?? Really, in the stores are whole rows of machines with a "Baby" wash cycle. How long do they expect people to have an infant? What is a "jeans" setting anyway? White is a color, not a cycle, people! Does a white throw rug get the same temperature and treatment as a white bra? I would hope not. Whatever happened to "Delicate", "Hand Wash", "Heavy Duty", "Wool", "Perm Press", etc?

So, onto this Whirlpool Duet SteamFresh Premium lemon. First off, what's the point of a 4.x cubic foot basket if it unbalances and dies all the time?? It can't handle one more sock than the smaller models, so right off the bat save your money and go for a smaller washer. The Neptune was 3+ cu ft and could easily wash a queen comforter and set of sheets. This Duet stops and starts and can hardly make it through just a comforter, no matter what setting I choose. The Neptune would re-asses loads, toss back and forth if it thought the load was unstable. The Duet grinds to a halt if a feather is out of place.

The washing selections on the Duet are lies. "Active Wear"? My active wear is sweats: the Duet stops dead. Apparently, my "active wear" is "bulky" or "heavy duty" or whatever. If I only put underwear in the active cycle the Duet spins them into pulp. And you are doomed if you ever mix cloth weights: want to put some underwear in with pants or sweaters? Error. Or, even better, it doesn't toss well enough to clean anything. Heavy stuff just sits there and light stuff gets ground to dust.

And now I have a perpetual F20 or F21 error code and I see online that I have to disassemble the case, root around for some internal filter, grab a bucket to catch a couple gallons of water, then dig into the guts to clear some drain filter. Are they really TRYING to make business for repairmen? WHO PUTS AN INTERNAL FILTER IN A WASHING MACHINE??

Other issues: The Duet runs the drain before it starts a cycle to "empty the basin". It ALWAYS has water in it. It's in the book. It never, never is empty. That seems like a recipe for disaster. It smells funny, musty even, if you don't use it for a week. The fabric softener cup is miniscule and will dump it's load at random points in the wash cycle. Most often when I close the door at the start. AND the book tells you to dilute softener first. WHY have a massive basket if it can only use a couple tablespoons of softener? You also do not have full control over cycle and temperatures. Some will allow warm water rinse, others will not. WHY??

It is such and unfair market where Maytag's Neptune recall put a great company out of business, and a venal, uncaring company like Whirlpool can sell $1200 washers with a 12 month warranty that fail at an alarming rate. Just researching the latest problems with this horrible Duet makes me feel for the people who had $1000 repair bills 13 months in. We've had the Duet Premium for about 18 months and I really, really regret buying it. I should have taken my chances on one of the other name brands with the stupid "Baby" cycle, or even just gone for a generic brand at half the price.

2. Washer - everyone in the house (4 of us) use the washer and each of us has at least once (for me countless times and why I am writing this) where you press the start button and you think it's started, only to come back an hour later to find dry unwashed clothes. (We have learned to wait the 30- 60 seconds for it to start and actually drop water into the washer, then it's confirmed that it's started)

3. I do not like to have the washer door open so that it can "air out" the moldy smell.

4. Probably not a big deal to many, but there are too many choices and not all combos can be picked. For example the super hot setting can only be used on the 2 hr cycle called sanitize.

5. Sometimes (not only when it could be overloaded, which I doubt) the spin cycle does not remove all the water. So okay, I'll run the spin cycle, except it's a rinse and spin cycle.

The dryer also has timing issues. I get it can not tell the exact amount of moisture in a load, but the estimated time left is crazy! I have sat and waited for 10 minutes when it tells me there are 2 minutes remaining. I have also had many occassions where it does not even come close to being dry but stops the machine... Once again there are too many choices and the combos I would like to make, I can't.

My clothes are not so much more cleaner than from my old washer to justify all the bells and whistles and the outrageous cost. While I am not ready for it to die, I do curse the machines often and am looking forward to a less complicated, less expensive machine next time.

Apparently the main shaft seal that protects the bearings from splashing water doesn't do much protecting. My rear (smaller) bearing was junk and I bought a repair kit to replace the bearings. Turns out Whirlpool had a change in their production run and the seal, bearings and another seal my on-line vendor thought was correct were all wrong. They were stumped, and apparently Whirlpool / Kenmore / Maytag are also stumped because they can't build a machine that doesn't destroy bearings after 18 months of service. It is obvious that they know there is a seal problem as the modification to the design they tried on my model didn't work either.

Guys, IF you try this repair yourself, be prepared for disappointment. Even though you tried to save the $600+ to keep this $1,000+ machine running more than 2 years, IT WILL NOT LAST! Try the stainless steel permanently sealed bearings from SKF to buy more time.

The other day I looked inside the rubber seal with a flashlight and it is covered with hardened BLACK MOLD! YUCK. I immediately contacted Whirlpool extended warranty and guess what, "Your extended warranty only covers mechanical and electrical. Not mold."
The transferred me to Whirlpool service to learn what I can do to remedy the mold and was told, "All we can do is order a new seal, 106.00 and send a service tech to replace it, labor 80 - 100.00. product_title: Whirlpool Duet Steam WFW9750WW 27 Front Load Washer 4.5 cu. ft. Capacity - White
review_text:
We try to buy US-made when we can. Whirlpool is mostly made in the USA, and they support Habitat for Humanity -- donating hundreds of thousands of new appliances to help new home-owners. So it's fair to say that there's no company that I'd rather buy my appliances from.

But this one ... oh boy. We've had problems almost the entire time that we've owned it. I currently have it taken apart (which is quite an ordeal), as I try to clean out all of the filters and pipes and sensors.

At any rate, when it works, it's great. But this one doesn't work, most of the time (probably 30% of loads fail), and that is pretty frustrating. It easily doubles the time it takes to do laundry :(

I will buy Whirlpool in the future, because they are a good company and US made. But I won't buy this model ever again.

product_title: Whirlpool WFW9750WL
review_title: So far So Good. The Wife Loves it.
review_text:
Going on a year with this unit. Installing it was not too bad, but if you don't have a very solid floor (2X10 joists with tile or simply concrete) you will find that the vibration with a large load can be pretty intimidating to say the least. I leveled the unit perfectly, and with no load the washer spins incredibly smooth at max rpm. With a smaller load, spin cycles aren't bad at high speeds. With large loads, watch out. I have 2X10's, and I added 2X6s to strengthen them. I also added a support under the crawl near where the washer is to prevent any bounce in the floor. I don't yet have tile, so I put a 3/4 inch piece of plywood under the washer and dryer for now. It's as good as it's gonna get on a wood floor. Once I put in cement board and tile I'll remove the 3/4 plywood and all should be fine.

Once installed the unit looks great and works wonderfully for my wife and I. She uses it more than I do, and with two young children it gets used nearly daily. I'm not holding my breath, but so far there have been no problems.

We ALWAYS take out the soap dispenser and leave the door open after washing. Zero problems with smells using HE detergent. To be on the safe side I do use the afresh cleaning tablets once every few months.

Hint: Use just enough detergent (HE seems to work best so far) to get the job done and let the thing dry out between washings.

Clothes come out very clean every time, and that is without using the steam cycle very often. Whites are white!

We'll see how this unit holds up. Whirlpool has sold tens of thousands and one can find a few dozen terrible reviews. A few dozen out of thousands is probably a good bet. Of course Whirlpool is not alone with bad reviews. When shopping for a washer and dryer I could not find a brand that didn't have negative reviews so I rolled the dice.

The matching steam dryer has also been great, and the steam cycle to touch up clothes before going out does work pretty good depending on the material. The dryer capacity is great.

Despite the size of the machine one cannot fully load it and expect it to get the job done. If it is too full the clothes simply cannot move around enough to get thoroughly clean. Don't overload it!

I'm not expecting it to last as long as an old fashioned mechanical timer top loader, but if I get a couple of years out of it before I have to repair it myself I won't mind. If when the time comes I need to get a part to repair it and the part is hundreds of dollars I'll be disappointed! Time will tell.

So far we love it and the dryer. The spin cycle can be crazy with a heavy load. Clothes come out clean. It's easy to use. It does hold a lot of clothing.

Update: December 3, 2012. No mechanical or electrical problems with the unit. We have also not had any smell problems as reported by some users on many makes and models of front load machines. We ALWAYS leave the door open and take out the soap dispenser after washing clothes to let everything dry out. When using powder oxidizer, we do notice a build-up of oxidizer under the soap dispenser, which is a minor hassle to clean. Other than that, the wife is still very happy with the machine. I'd still recommend and purchase this unit again. The matching steam dryer has also been a great product.
