product_title: Whirlpool WFW9150WW 27 4 cu. Ft. Front Load Washer - White
review_title: If I could give it a lower rating, I would
review_text:
We purchased our washer at Lowes in March, 2011. It was working great, I was happy over all, though I was a bit annoyed at the exaggerated advertising that this washer will hold 16 pair of jeans (5-6 is more like it). On September 11, the rubber boot pulled completely out of place and the wire wrapped around clothing and ruined them. I called the Service Center at Whirlpool and had them come out. They were out within a week. The repairman said that he would have to replace the boot and the part would take 2 weeks to get in. I was without a washer for 3 weeks at this point. They came and repaired it, and within a month it started leaking again. This time the boot was still in tact. We call the service center at whirlpool again, a week later a new company comes out and they declare it has the same issue - a leaking boot. They order the part and it takes 2 weeks to get in and installed. Again, we are without a washing machine for 3 weeks. A few weeks pass and I run a self cleaning cycle and the machine starts leaking yet a third time! I get on the phone with Whirlpool and demand a new machine. They refuse and tell me they are 'honoring the warranty and standing by their product by sending out a repair service'. The Service center tells me there is no one else to talk to - no case manager, no manager, no one at all higher up and the only way to get a new machine is to have a service repairman declare the machine is unrepairable. Yet a third company comes out and fixes some minor issues saying that's been the problem all along. They say they ran a self cleaning cycle and it was great - no leaks. They leave and that night I do laundry. The first load I run I know something is horribly wrong. It smells like burnt rubber. When the cycle finishes, I open the door and am greeted with rubber grit all over my clothing. They smell awful. I run the load again, thinking perhaps the grit was left from the service call. The smell during the second load worsens. When the load finishes, the grit is gone, but the smell is horrible. I dry the clothes, thinking I'd rewash them after the smell was gone from the washer. I run a self cleaning cycle with Affresh. Not 2 minutes into the cycle and the machine leaks all over. AGAIN. I call whirlpool the next morning and the soonest they can have someone out to fix it is a WEEK later!

Whirlpool by far has the WORST customer service I've ever dealt with. If you don't believe me, check out their facebook page. It is littered with people just like me. So far, Whirlpool refuses to replace my machine, and I continue to be a working mom of 3 kids who can't do laundry. Unacceptable, Whirlpool. My husband and I have missed 6 days of work waiting on repair service calls and our machine has yet to be fixed. We did the math, and at this point, we are out enough money it would have been cheaper to just purchase a new machine rather than miss so much work and do laundry at a laundromat.

Buyer don't just beware, RUN far away from Whirlpool and their products.

review_title: Don't Buy Whirlpool!!! The Duet Washer WFW9150WW is Garbage!
review_text:
Purchased new in July 2010. Brought home, plugged in and water spewed all over my laundry room from the soap dispenser. Called Sears, they sent a technician out who said Whirlpool had the hoses incorrectly assembled. He re-arranged where the hoses were run and our machine seemed to work properly.

We watch it filling with water...barely has any water. The water NEVER reaches anywhere near the rim like the commercial washers at the laundromat. (I went and checked them out, because our clothes did not seem to be getting cleaned.) I've only used Tide HE and our clothes are not coming out clean. During, "Add a Garment", I often wait until the water stops and toss in another 1.5 gallon bucket of water. This seems to help some, but doesn't alleviate the problem. (After I began doing this, I commented to a sales lady at Sears that our machine does not clean clothes well. She said she had the same one and had to add water during the "Add A Garment" stage to get her clothes clean. I told her that is what we had been doing!)

I often have to do a load 2-3 times...especially if Jeans. Stains easily transfer from one set of clothing to another...many items have been ruined. This would never have happened with the top-loader we had had for 18 years! Stains that would have come out with our old machine barely get wet with this one. We were able to load more clothes in our top-loader, also!

While under warranty, I called Whirlpool and told the rep that our clothes did not come out clean. My husband will be wearing a shirt and an hour later start wondering what smells...and realizes that it is his shirt. How gross! The rep said that even though the machine was under warranty, if a service tech came out and couldn't "find anything wrong" with the machine, we would be responsible for the $129 service call. After reading all the other negative reviews about Whirlpool online, we told her, "No, thanks!" Because their technicians would claim they all only use a little water and were working properly.

My husband ended up taking the machine apart and found that it was only adding 1.5 gallons of water for a full load of clothes! No wonder it doesn't clean well...it barely gets the clothes wet. We're still trying to decide if we are going to purchase a new front loader (NEVER WHIRLPOOL, ever again!) Or go back to a top loader...that you can at least allow clothes to soak in, when needed. The soak cycle on this front-loader is a joke when it barely gets the items wet.

Save your money, your time, and your disposition by purchasing from another manufacturer. My mother's LG works Great...maybe we'll change to that.

Look up other reviews online: [...]
BAD! BAD! BAD!

review_title: Good thing I got extended warranty
review_text:
I bought this from a Fred's Appliance (Spokane) and they have their own extended warranty - and they they are great; the machine is a lemon.
The machine is on visit 3 from Fred's.

I had a Kenmore 417.43142200 prior, its paired to a 628.9468213 dryer - still works fine.
It was a top rated model (CR) that was made by Frigidaire (GM), and in 3-ish years a badly corroded aluminum basket and bearing lead me to the descision to dump it.
I can fix these things, and I was prepared to, but I found out the repair components were made the same way and expensive.
I did extensive research on the matter, and learned that in this case, the Amazon reviews were more useful then the CR ratings - which are model specific only for new machines.
Overall, Kenmore is still good.

I e-mailed CR and explained their reviews failed me entirely, and in fact they still showed the unit as recommended, when I could see a YouTube explaining its fatal problem.
So its restoration didn't pencil-out.

The Whirlpool looked similar - so the issue of a non-matching pair was ameliorated.
I was happy...for a while. I had the same leak issue others had, and in fairness we aren't that kind to machines in this house.
I could hardly believe it when I read my receipt for the purchase date, I bought the extended warranty - never have before on a major appliance.
The second issue was done while I was on the road - I don't really know what was fixed.
Now it won't go through a cycle, for the 3rd inning.

That now about $275 worth of trips, but "free" to me, and we may hit 400 tommorow.
Right now I can here it beeping an error message, leading me to make this charitable act.

Before I got this unit I knew the risk.
I called a local repair shop I have used for 30 yrs.
I asked him is this normal (The Kenmore)? He mumbled out 4-5 years is normal.
We talked about the old Maytag that went 20 years, the Whirlpools that went 10, but were easy to fix.
He warned the Maytags are made by Whirlpool now (still a pretty good brand I thought, he didn't confirm.)
I asked what he'd buy, he said "LG makes a good machine, Samsung..."
I said, you'd think American industry would learn their lesson (cars), you mean were doing this again with appliances?

I went to Sears first, with my paper work, before I got this Whirlpool, they might make a deal...?
Well, no, but, I found they now private label Samsung and LG as Kenmore.
So they moved on, as I should have.

The Extended will probably get me through to a reasonable service life for the dryer.
If I'm not unemployed, I'll pick up a new set of LG's in 2-3 years.
If I am unemployed then, I won't be for long, I can fix these lousy machines 50hrs a week, and buy a dented pair of LG's.
I can't imagine how i might feel if I were out of work in my 20's, maybe springing for a new machine for my wife and kids, and getting this.

I belong to the American Society of Quality: I know much of this isn't due to our American labor as much as bean-counter management
Toyota can take our labor, at least the non-union variety, and make a Tundra in Kentucky that's perfect (no issues at 100K).
A US Camry (no issues at 180K), from Japan I had three Corollas, (no issue's at 180, 185K, but one, I bought used, had a problem at 150K).
We got a Lexus, no issues at 80K so far, that's a Japanese labor product, it appears to be perfect.
So 6 Toyota products, 10000 parts, and one $1400 repair -and I can't but a good domestic washing machine in two trys?

Most of those recalls in 2009 and such, were due to American parts from Toyota's plan to become more American, and on the American made units from there upstream suppliers.
Still, a Toyota made in Kentucky beats most American cars, however in terms of essentials, I think the quality issues with domestic cars tend to be minor.
I got my mom into a Focus, because used Toyota's were overpriced at the time - seems the a good car and well engineered.
That Ford engineering came out of: Ford EU....

I'm really glad Whirlpool doesn't make cars.

Maybe LG will have a US plant in a few years, so I can "buy American" - sort of.
That's my plan.

review_title: Pretty smooth-top and almost stainless finish...
review_text:

You can of course change it up or down by 25F increments. The stovetop has a control for all burners which is about as simple, too. Once again, the problem is stainless status and cleaning. To me, cooking is the thing and I don't fuss over a scratch or two, but for some, appearance is as important as function and they should avoid this series of stoves.

(that is, while it was still making ice in year 1-3) A little research on the net and I have discovered the motherboard breaks on these puppies and they stop cooling. If you figure one in every 10 people who have this same problem with their G.E. Profile's, write a complaint on line, then it's pretty much... yeah, everybody whose had one for 4 years. The brand is made in Mexico and no offense to Mexicans but it sucks! You'll be lucky to get 2 or 3 years from this machine. A word of caution: When looking on line for reviews, do not just count the # of stars people have given it and make your mind up based on that, you have to read the actual reviews because most of the people writing the reviews do so within a month or two of getting their appliance--sometimes the day it arrives. What the heck use is that, I ask you? (this is true of all appliances) Of course they're satisfied with their purchase in the first month. Read reviews from people who have had the machine for YEARS and that will tell you something. Now I have to figure out what to buy next because I'm not even going to bother fixing this junk.

UPDATE: I went searching for a new counter-depth, built-in fridg in stainless steel that would go with my gorgeous new kitchen and discovered anything counter depth (meaning it doesn't stick out in the room 6 inches beyond the counter like a giant cube) costs about twice as much as a regular depth fridge, and since there are no good brands made today left to buy--(they are all utter crap) I couldn't stomach paying a minimum of $2,000 for a unit that would last only a few years. Well, I decided to look on Craig's list for a used/older model counter depth, not sure if they even existed. I'm here to tell you, they do---I found 2 G.E. Profile counter depth refrigerators in my area on one night, which were at least 15 years old. They were in the price range of $75-150 and clean. I bought the one for $75 because it still looked new inside and was the right size, had well made drawers (heavy gage wire bins in the freezer), a lighted ice maker in the door that still worked, and NO COMPUTER running it. I took it home in December and I have had no problems with it, and if/when I do, if I repair it it will stay repaired because all the major problems with refrigerators today are associated with the computer brain. The same company makes mother boards for all the popular brands so they all have problems. The one I bought was almond in color, but I bought stainless steel contact paper at Loews (2 rolls, $14 dollars) and now you can't tell it's not stainless steel except for the ice maker on the front and the handles, but the overall impression is the same as the SS I had prior. It looks fine! The guy who sold it to me said he was the second owner and it has never given him a moment's trouble in 12 years. I think it must be about 17 years old. He just updated his kitchen and his wife wanted a new one---the same one I just got rid of! OMG, they are going to be soooo sorry in a couple of years. I hired a used refrigerator guy to move one out and the one from Craig's List in, and offered to pay him by giving him the 4 year old SS one I just got rid of, but he was very familiar with the new G.E. profiles and he only gave me $25 dollars for it. I had to pay $100 more for him to move them/ change them out. He says it's not really even worth $25! But so what, the whole thing out the door cost me $175, done and done. Anyone who doesn't want to spend thousands of dollars on a counter depth fridge (but still wants one) and is dead set against buying inferior products, and doesn't know what to do: Take my advice, either research/buy Fagor a european brand that you can get here at A.J. Madisons (it is the 5th largest selling appliance brand in europe and is getting rave reviews all over the world now. BTW they also make washer/dryers combos which you can buy on Amazon) also Summit is supposed to be a good brand. product_title: GE GFSS2HCYSS 22.2 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel French Door Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_title: Great for the budget and size
review_text:
I have had this fridge for just over a year now. I initially bought it because I had limited space; was restricted in width and also depth, hence needed a French door model to make sure I had enough clearance. I will also disclose that I am a GE employee (not the appliance division) and hence the employee discount was also very relevant in this decision.

On the whole, I have had no real issues with this model. When I first got it the freezer compartment did not seem to stay closed correctly (didn't seem to suction as har as I would have expected) and for a short while I thought I would have to return it/call for repair, but I think it was just because it was new? At any rate, that problem quickly disappeared.

Pros: Very competitive price, especially for stainless steel. Runs well, runs relatively quietly, has an ice maker in the freezer department. Crisper seems to keep my salads and herbs etc fresher for much longer than my older fridge. Looks nice and cleans up fairly easily, on the outside and inside.

Some Pet peeves:
1. The crisper drawer - the edge that runs on the tracks- cracked very quickly and easily and a piece broke off. Not a total write off as still works but you have to be more careful/angle it. It was a disappointment though to have something new which turns into something broken very quickly.
2. You have to open both doors to get into a crisper drawer. Not a huge deal but it would be nice if it could be accessed by opening just one.
3. As it's not a huge fridge not sure if much could be done to solve this one, but the shelving does not seem to have the right combination of height levels that would optimize the use of the space. No matter how i arrange it I can't fit a bottle of, say, cranberry juice standing up without having ridiculously small space on all other levels.
4. Biggest annoyance to me is the freezer space compartment. It's just one big basket in the drawer and I have been unable to find any kind of replacement which might have more dividers or separators, which would make it more accessible/storage easier. As it is, one has to dig through to find what you're looking for. This should definitely be an easier fix. Also, the space is pretty small for most families with kids, as you can't pile it up too high or it won't close, due to the ice maker and shelf to the side of the icemaker. We have our old fridge/freezer in the basement now which I find invaluable (for a family with 3 young kids and a weekend fisherman).
5. The icemaker drawer frequently "drops" ice from the back to the bottom of the freezer, especially when accessing the drawer. Ice falls out the back of the drawer, down the freezer and shoots out onto the kitchen floor (as the drawer is open). This is a pain, especially when it happens when the kids are getting ice and they don't "notice" (ahem). Then it melts and someone races through the kitchen, clips, and it all ends in tears...

Things I wish I'd thought about when buying:
Having three kids, if I was doing it over, I would have gone for a model that had the icemaker and water filter on the front door. This is partly because it's a pain to have a water jug inside the fridge door (space is tight, jug can be heavy for a 6 year old), and mainly because I would love to restrict my kids from a) - constantly opening the freezer to get ice, slamming it shut and running off without making sure it's properly shut (we have already had defrosting issues - no fault of GE's here), and b) - having my kids grab ice from the drawer with their hands (not always clean?). I have placed there a scooper, however would much rather prefer if it just came out of a shoot on the front door!

All in though, for my budget, I am very happy with my refrigerator. No buyer`s remorse here! I bought the extended service plan, as I have done for all appliances I have purchased over the past 5 years (all GE), but as with the others I have yet to need to use it (touch wood!).

review_text:
This model replaced a ten year old KitchenAid that was the worst disappointment of my appliance buying life. We've had this one about a month and it's made us realize the KA didn't work right from the beginning. We're happy with the Whirlpool.

This baby washes dishes in about half an hour though drying takes longer, but the KA took two hours. It heats the water superbly; a comforting cloud of steam wafts out when the door is first opened, and the dishes are too hot to handle. The best part is that even with an extended warranty, the whole thing cost about half of the price of the miserable KitchenAid.

The silverware baskets have slotted covers, so forks have to be stood tines-up (a major bone of contention in our household). I'm happy about that feature, though no one else is.

The installer warned us that this model might be a bit loud, but we haven't found noise to be a problem. It's fractionally louder than the KA, and--it actually cleans dishes. Actually, I find the sound of dishes being washed by someone or something else to be the most delightful noise in the world, second only to the sight and sound of someone else operating a lawnmower on my lawn.

The top rack isn't well designed for large cups, glasses and bowls and it doesn't hold as many dishes as the KA. Actually, both racks feel much more lightweight and cheesy than the KA. Still, since the KA didn't clean dishes well, that's not a deal breaker. The controls are not especially intuitive and sometimes the unit is hard to turn on, but it eventually does. I've found that a kind of sliding action seems to work best on the Start button.

Our appliance repairman warned us that dishwashers don't last beyond ten years these days so from now on we're buying inexpensive models. This one is very satisfactory. Plus the stainless and black exterior is snazzy.

review_text:
It's a good first kegerator for the money. I homebrew and I've used this kegerator for ales, IPAs, stouts, belgian dubbles, and lagers. I use the 5 gallon homebrew kegs, so I can't comment on the commercial couplers. If you like higher carbonated beer, you may want to get a flow control tap since this kegerator comes with standard taps. (I've had foaming issues with anything over 8psi. Then again, if you're having foaming issue, you can use longer line from what I hear) I did run into an issue with one of the taps sticking, but that's semi-normal for these cheaper taps. As far as temps go, it keeps the beer cold enough for me. I've even had a beer line freeze at one point.

Honestly, looking back, I wish I would have just bought a mini fridge. That's all this thing is in the end... a mini fridge with a two inch how drilled in the top so you can screw on the draft tower.

If I were going to do this again - I'd say just buy a good mini fridge and drill, baby, drill.

product_title: Haier Kegerator HBF05EABB-2 Dual Faucet Keg Beer Cooler Tap
review_title: With patients, this can be an awesome kegerator
review_text:
First, I'd like to address the comment "hope you like warm beer". Not sure what they're talking about. I have my thermostat set about 1 inch colder than "normal" on the dial. The fridge has two 1/6 kegs of Victory beer, both are ice cold. Initially I had it set much colder but the temperature readings were showing I was close to freezing. Ideally beer should be between 33F - 38F.

Foaming
I initially had foaming issues. There are two ways I know how to fix this:

1) Get longer lines - $10
2) Get a flow control tap - $50

Personally, I opted for the lines. Buy something high quality. I went with 10' of BevLex 200 3/16 for each line from a local homebrew store. You can also purchase it online. Start with 10' and trim until it pours the way you want it to. You want the beer to "fall" out of the tap. The top of the tower pulls off. Under that there is a piece of Styrofoam. From there you can remove the taps/line. Call the Beverage Factory if you need any help, they're happy to do so.

If you're worried about the beer sitting in the line, don't. 10' of 3/16 line holds about 1.5 ounces of beer, which is basically nothing -- I measured it. The beer is well carbonated and tastes amazing.

PSI/Regulator - Carbonation levels
Your best bet on PSI/Regulator settings is to contact the brewery that makes the beer. They can give you the target PSI they serve there's at. Then, you can use this chart [google for Solubility-of-carbon-dioxide-in-beer] to find out what you should be setting your regulator to. Most beers will fall between 2.40 - 2.57. It's important to know what the temperature of your beer. co2 has different pressures at different temperatures. **TIP** - place a glass of water in the fridge over night and temp that. It will give you a more accurate temperature than a free standing thermometer. Example: your beer is 36F, you want a target PSI of 2.40. Your regulator would need to be set somewhere between 9 - 10.

Overall, I'm very happy with this kegerator. Happy pouring!

We do love many things about this fridge, but that old saying "one bad apple" is applicable!
The video of the rust if AFTER my husband had used a grinder to get rid of all the rust - where it's silver in the video - was rust!
Our Side-by-Side Fridge (RS267LABP) stopped producing ice cubes approx. 6 months after we bought it - it would only crush ice (a problem I've seen in many reviews since + the ice production/quantity is really poor - we've often had to buy bags of ice to put in it! Without having to call Samsung, my husband repaired this problem (as he's very clever!) and we both enjoyed ice cubes again in our cocktails!
We didn't realize until about 9 months ago, the damage that had been done by the crushed ice melting and collecting in the dispenser tray.
Please see the video of our terribly rusted, not very old, fridge.
THE REASON WHY? Samsung don't bother to put a little bit of sealer between the tray and the dispenser surround. Therefore, water in the tray, gets under the plastic fascia and rusts out the door. I advise anyone to check if this has been remedied).
Sealing it would have taken about 20 seconds to do when being manufactured.
No one would tile a bathroom and shower daily without ever caulking it!
If this is the amount of care and time that goes into their appliances - we won't buy one again!

product_title: Samsung RF267AEBP 26 cu. Ft. French Door Refrigerator - Black Pearl
review_text:
Purchased this from SEARS Outlet as less than 1/2 original SRP!! Slight dent in door full warranty extended by Samsung 3 Months after registering!! Great Space and very quiet! Got rid of a 7.5 yr old GE (Profile) Lousy product!!
This is 26 Cu ft and Energy Star. Interior great and Freezer excellent with digital display. Only con is that the Water dispenser is too small and should be taller.

[...]

product_title: Samsung RF267AEBP 26 cu. Ft. French Door Refrigerator - Black Pearl
review_text: Like the fridg, but the right-door gasket tore after a year. Between the two doors, the gaskets have a wider flap that is very thin rubber, this extends past than the magnetic part, and is subject to wear. Supposedly, you can open either door first, but if you open the left side first, it puts extra wear on that flap on the right side gasket, and the flap tears. I don't think this flap  creates much of a tight air seal, but if you put a flashlight in the fridg and shut the door, I could see a hole with light coming through where that gasket is now torn off. I fixed ours with a piece of Gorilla tape, rather than spend $160 for a new gasket. The rubber flap should be thicker material, I don't think it will hold up well in other places now that I've seen how easily it tears. Other than that, this seems to be a nice fridg. Wish you didn't have to open both doors to open the deli drawer, but that's not uncommon in a french-door model.

product_title: Samsung RF267AEBP 26 cu. Ft. French Door Refrigerator - Black Pearl
review_text:
I would have to agree with the negative reviews. While I have not had the same problems I have not been happy with mine either, especially considering the cost. I was against getting one with an ice dispenser but got talked into it and sure enough, it broke. Something is causing the paddle to constantly open and close as if it is dispensing over and over. I will have to either replace the board or some part of the dispenser part on the door. Either way the unit was only about 2 years old and this started happening. If I do it myself the cost will be somewhere between $60 and $200, not sure which yet. That is totally unacceptable for such a new unit.

I also had the problem that is documented online where I had to disassemble it and de-ice it because ice builds up behind the panels and gets into the condenser fan which makes noise.

I like their phones, their TVs, etc. but I will never buy one of their appliances again.

product_title: Samsung RF267AEBP 26 cu. Ft. French Door Refrigerator - Black Pearl
review_text: We purchased the French door 26.0 cf Samsung unit just over 2 years ago and could not be happier. I saw all of the negative reviews and had to give my 2 cents. Honestly I have had nothing but problem free quiet operation provided by this fridge. I have kids and the door gets used frequently with no torn seals or anything. The only complaint I can agree with is the door opening for the water dispenser could be a little taller but is seriously not even close to a deal breaker.

product_title: Samsung RF267AEBP 26 cu. Ft. French Door Refrigerator - Black Pearl
review_text: I have alway been a big Samsung fan and when I saw this RF267AB french door refrigator, I loved it and, thinking Samsung being a great company, thought it would be a good quality product.  I did buy the extended warranty from Best Buy due to the high price of the product.  At about 2.5 to 3 years, I saw what looked to be grime in the crease below the ice dispenser.  I have always kept the refrigerator clean and wondered where the grime came from.  I tried cleaning it and realized it was rust not grime.  It wasn't terribly bad so I dismissed it.  However, now at 4.5 years the skin of the refrigerator is bubbling and the corrosion has gotten much worse.  I called Best Buy thinking my warranty would cover it, but when the tech came out, he said it wasn't covered.  So now I am rethinking my thoughts on Samsung products.  The last couple of Samsung items I've had I have had problem with. Other comments I've read about Samsung say the same, that the quality of their products are getting worse.  I will think twice now about buying another Samsung product.

product_title: Samsung RF267AEBP 26 cu. Ft. French Door Refrigerator - Black Pearl
review_text: We purchased this refrigerator in September 2011. We wanted the French doors and bottom freezer, though we subsequently came to realized that it is not nearly as roomy as you might expect. Still, that is not why we are so disappointed in this appliance. It failed completely last week, with both computer boards going out. We lost hundreds of dollars worth of food in both compartments and spent a goodly sum to get it repaired. Our last refrigerator, which cost a lot less, lasted 15 years! I e-mailed Samsung and got a return e-mail saying customer service had tried to call us; I don't believe it, as I work from home and have a phone machine so it's unlikely I would miss the call. They asked for more contact info, which I provided, and we have not heard another word. BTW, the black front also scratches and dents VERY easily and the water tastes terrible, despite frequent filter changes.

product_title: Samsung RF267AEBP 26 cu. Ft. French Door Refrigerator - Black Pearl
review_title: Head over heels for this Samsung French Door Refrigerator
review_text: I am a mother/wife of a family of 6. This fridge has stood the test of time through my family over and over again. No rust, no noise and absolutely perfect in every way! From the power burst to the space and the lighting and more! I feel like I am walking into the closet from The Lion, The Witch, and The Wardrobe! I can store all the food I need for my family and then some! I throw a lot of parties and the additional ice dispenser is a life saver for drinks! No need for additional mini fridges, ice trays/bagged ice, or deep freezers! I live quite a drive from the store as well so the power blast option is great for when I am rushing food in from my long drive from the store. It is absolutely beautiful as well and is a big conversation piece at my home. I love it! And for any woman or man who does a lot of cooking/fridge time... you will more than appreciate the ample lighting! You will not forgo the back of fridge items that often go overlooked until after they expire. At a glance I can see the majority of everything all at once! Best fridge I have ever owned/used in my life. BTW I'm 32! :D I highly recommend this fridge if you can get your hands on one as they are hard to come by and are most of the time sold out!

product_title: Samsung RF267AEBP 26 cu. Ft. French Door Refrigerator - Black Pearl
review_text: Never buy this. We purchased at Sears. Beautiful fridge but a nightmare. The fan in the back freezes up. It gate humidity. If you don't cool your food down to room temp it will start caking up with ice until it shuts down and won't hold the temp. Aesthetically well done. Lacks the ability to work.

product_title: Samsung RF267AEBP 26 cu. Ft. French Door Refrigerator - Black Pearl
review_text: This has been a great refrigerator. We have had it for over 3 years with no problems. Was surprised to come across the bad reviews, but I guess those are the ones that mostly write reviews. Anyway, I would recommend this fridge. Has great space, moveable dividers, and most importantly- it is reliable, does what it is supposed to.

product_title: Samsung RF267AEBP 26 cu. Ft. French Door Refrigerator - Black Pearl
review_text: We have owned this refrigerator for about 3 years now and it is not worth your money!  The ice maker doesn't work properly and leaves big clumps of ice burgs which freeze to the bottom of the ice tray eventually clogging up the entire assembly.  This happens on a regular basis - at least 3-4 times a day so now we have turned off the ice maker.  Luckily for us we purchased a used 1992 Whirlpool model last year for $25.00 at a garage sale that functions perfectly and makes fine ice.  I guess the Samsung Refrigerator wants us to get our exercise by making us walk to the garage every time we want ice.  I'm guessing the only solution is to replace the entire ice maker assembly, but will the next ice maker have the same problem?  Bottom line - Don't buy this refrigerator or any refrigerator made by Samsung.

product_title: Samsung RF267AEBP 26 cu. Ft. French Door Refrigerator - Black Pearl
review_text: I am having the same problem with the bubbling and rust on the doors as many other reviewers. And the piece at the top of the fridge that slides into the frame and seals the door has broken off. I went to an appliance store on Saturday looking for a replacement fridge and when they saw the pictures they were shocked. They urged me to call Samsung and since it was not the store I bought the fridge from, they weren't trying to avoid dealing with a problem themselves. I called Samsung this afternoon and got no help at all after 1 hour on the phone and 3 customer service reps. I'm so upset that this expensive appliance is defective and needs to be replaced and Samsung reps did nothing but read from a script telling me that the fridge was no longer under warranty so the only option was to send someone out at my cost. I kept telling them there wouldn't be a way to "repair" the problem even if I was willing to pay. We'd have to completely replace the doors. I am going to contact Lowe's, where we purchased the fridge, and see if they can help in any way. Needless to say, I will NEVER buy a Samsung product again. And I plan to check if other major appliance brands are actually owned by them (I believe LG is). So disappointed and frustrated :(

product_title: Samsung RF267AEBP 26 cu. Ft. French Door Refrigerator - Black Pearl
review_title: I also have severe corrosion around the ice maker. ...
review_text: I also have severe corrosion around the ice maker.  This is obviously a problem in this line - there needs to be a recall by Samsung.  I will not purchase another Samsung appliance because of this.

product_title: LG : WM3431HS All-In-One Washer and Dryer TITANIUM
review_title: Worst waste of $1700 I ever spent.
review_text: Don't waste your money. This washer dryer combo is a great concept idea, however, it needs to be perfected. I have had this unit for 1 1/2 years. It has broke down twice.The pump went out 5 months into ownership. It was under warranty. The repair people take one week to come out. I have a family of seven. We cannot go one week without our laundry being done. My husband repaired it. Now it is leaking water. It takes no less than 4 hours to do one load of laundry, due to the drying cycle. I found it faster to use just the wash cycle and hang the clothes to dry outside. Big problem in Michigan winters, so we do inside clothes lines. We will be replacing with a conventional washer and dryer. If you only need a good washer this is your baby. If you want dry clothes you will get cobwebs on you waiting for it to complete the dry cycle.

product_title: LG : WM3431HS All-In-One Washer and Dryer TITANIUM
review_text:
Pros - it is space saving, is gentle on clothes (more gentle than TL models with agitator) and looks nice

Cons. Really Badly designed. Gasket in front gets moldy because the water builds up in the channels and there is no drain. Even with wiping it out after every wash, leaving the door open to air out, running sanitize cycles and using powdered soap and no fabric softener (and running sanitize cycles with bleach or vinegar), I still get mold and then my clothes smell like mold. Very high maintenance to prevent the mold and not really worth the time considering how expensive this is.

In order to clean out the lint and buildup, you have to practically take the machine apart. Mine is in a built in custom kitchen and it is a nightmare to do this. All other part that might need a regular service are also similarly inaccessible so , in addition to the high cost of purchase, there is a very high cost of maintenance.

I had combo HE front loaders in europe and never had to do more than a moment's maintenance and never had issues. This one is more trouble than it is worth.

Drying time is LONG. Like for lightweight summer sundresses and underwear and not even a full load 1.5-2 hrs long. When I can hang my clothes outside I can just about bear this thing, but when I can't, I curse it's existence with all my heart.

It came with the house I bought, but I would never buy anything like this again. I dislike it sufficiently that I am considering removing it to get back some of my cabinet space and going to the launderette.

product_title: LG : WM2301HW 27 Front-Load Washer with 4.2 cu. ft. Capacity White
review_title: LG WM2301HW is a huge liability - problems galore!
review_text: LG WM2301HW caught fire internally.  This unit has been nothing but problems.  This model should be a recall!  LG WM2301HW is a huge liability for anyone who owns one.  The unit starts off working great however, aggressively, the performance becomes very poor - leaking water from door, error codes, poor wash quality and in my case ... a fire.  Please be careful with the LG Washing Machine - WM2301HW model.  One would think that LG would take responsibility for this.

product_title: Bosch B26FT70SNS800 25.9 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel French Door Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_text:
We bought a Bosch fridge 2 weeks ago after our 9 yr old Maytag fridge stopped working. NEVER buy a side by side Maytag fridge!! NOTHING but trouble 2 weeks after the 1 yr warranty was up. Compressor finally quit after 9 years, lost 100's of dollars in food, paid $100 to fix the fridge every 6 months.

Anyways, purchased a Bosch B26ft fridge w/french doors & water dispenser/ice maker. First of all, it is clean and beautiful in our kitchen. There is a lot of space for various sizes and shapes of food and food container. Maintains constant temperature with little fluctuation. I LOVE the water dispenser and ice maker. We had this in our other fridge, but the ice and water always had a background taste. The bottom mount freezer is fantastic. Very easy to organize items and therefore, you can store much more.

The only possible down side is that the exterior is easily fingerprinted/smudged. Considering the use of a fridge is to keep food stored properly, I am EXTREMELY happy with my purchase. I will update my review after 1 year.

[[ASIN:B0037X9990 Bosch B26FT70SNS 25.9 cu. Ft. 800 Series Standard Depth French Door Refrigerator - Stainless Steel]]

product_title: Bosch B26FT70SNS800 25.9 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel French Door Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_title: Alarm keeps my whole family up at night
review_text: Installed this fridge last week.  The alarm goes off VERY LOUDLY every hour or two, and won't stop until I come downstairs and push a button acknowledging that the fridge has gotten one degree too warm inside.  There is NO WAY to disable this function, and it's worse for my sleep cycle than a newborn infant.  So here I am, at 4AM on Sunday, writing this review on Amazon.  Please, for the love of God, DO NOT BUY A BOSCH FRIDGE.

product_title: Bosch B26FT70SNS800 25.9 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel French Door Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_text:
I purchased the Bosch refrigerator when the previous fridge died. It had the fewest on-line complaints and was actually made in the U.S. rather than Mexico. While it's really too soon to actually rate this refrigerator because I only just got it a week ago, here are some things that i've found:

1. The stainless steel isn't actually stainless so fridge magnets will stick.

2. The stainless look is on the doors only, sides are dark brown.

3. The ice maker makes plenty of ice.

4. The water line for the dispenser freezes often so no water comes out. (This doesn't seem to affect the ice maker though.) Don't set the controls below the settings shown in the manual. If your kitchen is cool the fridge temperature may have to be increased.

5. The produce and deli drawers take up a lot of room. So tall bottles aren't able to stand up. Also if you don't purchase mostly produce you'll be surprised at how little room is left over.

6. Both doors must be open to access any of the compartments.

7. The warning beeper sounds for about five (very long) minutes after you shut the door (if you've left it open too long). This is quite annoying.

8. The Sears installers will scratch the doors putting the handles on. (They don't level the fridge either.)

9. Six 12-pack cases of cans fit just right with no wasted space.

10. There is no positive indication that you've pressed any of the buttons and the mode selected is sometimes not clear.

11. It's very quiet.

12. The display shows only the settings. A thermometer(s) will still be needed to know what the inside temperature is.

13. Everything inside is very well lit.

product_title: Bosch B26FT70SNS800 25.9 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel French Door Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_text:
We have had this fridg for a month now and we love it with the exception of two things:

The ice maker CAN NOT KEEP UP with a weekend full of iced down drinks. The receptable holder is very small and after a morning of cokes and dp's it's empty! And it takes forever to fill up again. A real flaw for a product that costs this much.

Also, the alarm is a bit of a pain. It seems to go off in a hap-hazzard mode. Sometimes it waits the full minute when the door is open to chime. Other times you can just walk into the room and open the door to get out butter and it goes off. I find that annoying actually.

Otherwise, it's definitely state of the art. Lots of room and adjustable shelves and it's very classy looking and would jazz up any kitchen. We didn't need a new fridg, we are just upgrading and we kept our old Amana as well, for the garage. We are going to need the ice from that ice maker, I assure you. But I definitely would recommend buying this product if you really need the "french door" type of fridg to make it work. So much more "high end" than most of the national brands, and much better looking, inside and out. We also purchased their induction cooktop, which we hope we live long enough to have delivered NOT broken. So far we have returned three due to the glass being broken when in shipping!

product_title: Bosch B26FT70SNS800 25.9 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel French Door Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_title: Pleasant refrigirator, awesome design, large and well lit
review_text:
I purchased this from Sears with good discount. I was happy with the cost. It was scheduled for delivery after 20 days. I was nervous investing that much on a refrigerator. But when Sears folks delivered and installed it well, and I was not disappointed.

PROS:

1-Looks, it makes your kitchen a lot more sellable. Ready for HGTV?
2-Inside is roomy
3-Well lit
4-Ice and water outlet is flat and looks very modern. It is touch sensitive, not push sensitive. Just touch onto the buttons, they come off.
5-Water coming out of the dispenser is filtered and has very pleasant taste. Filter is inside the frig easy to access. It is very small, won't take space.
6-Flexible interior adjustment: you can move few thing around, and fit a Heineken keg easily.
7-temperature separated sections: Upper part has 3 temperature separated sections.a-Regular larger section b)vegetables section which keep veggies moist and cooler c) deli section, which keeps meat coolest.
8-Freezer is roomy with one large bottom section, and one drawer to put boxy stuff in orderly manner.
9-External light is pleasantly lit and ambient: yet to find a way to keep it lit nonstop, but blue water-ice outlet light is very nice in dark.
10-The Ice maker does not take the entire inside section of the right door where ice dispense is located outside. It is so well designed that you can still use the inside shelf located in front of the dispenser part of the fridge. most of the other brands use the dedicate that section for ice machine.
11-Best buy for a luxury frig under $2,500.

CONS:

If any..
1- Due to nature of french-doors, the doors do not self close, Therefore, you have to give a light push to ensure that the doors close, which outlines the alarm issue many users are complaining about. But, if you close the doors properly, alarm will not sound, period. So, close the doors.:)
2-A bit pricier than average regular frig, but this is not an average frig. This is a Bosch and this model cost twice as much in Europe.
3- Stainless steel stains, but this is the nature of the stainless steel. If this is a concern for you, avoid stainless steel fridges.

VERDICT:

BUY IT !!!!

product_title: Bosch B26FT70SNS800 25.9 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel French Door Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_title: Ice maker broke - straight up crazy water dispensor
review_text:
We bought this fridge for our new home (along with just about every other Bosch appliance) because we loved the size and bottom freezer design. From a design and functionality stand point the fridge has been great. As far as it's reliability....not so much.

First problem.

About 3 months after they installed the appliances the ice maker stopped working. Tech came out and had to order a new ice maker.

Second problem.

Three days after the tech was at the house for the broken ice maker, the fridge went straight up banana's on us and started pouring water onto the floor! Literally went crazy!! We were in the kitchen at the time (luckily) nobody was anywhere close to the fridge when all of the sudden the panel started beeping and settings started to change, then 2 seconds later water starts pouring out all over the floor. We had to open the door to get it to stop. We're standing there trying to figure out what to do with our possessed fridge when the water starts pouring out again!!! I had to hold a bowl under the water dispenser while my husband pulled the fridge out from the wall (scratching the wood floors in the process, not his fault)and turn the water supply off.

We have a call into the dealer now (they've been great thus far). Needles to say, I don't really want a water dispenser anymore. I don't even want to think about the mess we would have had if this would have happened when we weren't home.

Just remember, regardless of what you pay and whose name is on the door, the more "advanced" the equipment is, the more things there are to break.

product_title: Bosch B26FT70SNS800 25.9 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel French Door Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_text:
We live in Europe and the US. While we have had Bosch appliances at times, we've moved on.

Americans should understand Bosch appliances are the GE or Whirlpool of Europe. They are not good, not bad but little more than mass market appliances built to a price point. The premium price charged in the USA is supporting the marketing that goes into posturing the brand as some sort of upscale product. There are many European brands that are mass market in Europe but advertise and charge luxury market prices in the US. Sort of funny for us but be aware that this marketing strategy is used by many of the German companies.

In a nutshell, our experience: Bosch dishwasher are junk (poor space utilization and noisy, very similar to US brands but more expensive) refrigerators work fine but certainly not commensurate with the price in the US and the stoves/ranges are quite good in operation but, based on our friends' reports, not particularly reliable.

product_title: Bosch B26FT70SNS800 25.9 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel French Door Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_title: did they even test the ice maker?
review_text:
I chose this refrigerator because it seemed to have good fit and finish, and looked very nice.

However, the first one I got made one batch of ice... that's 8 cubes... and then quit working. Sears sent someone out to fix it, and it they decided it was broken, they needed a new one. Well over a month later (with no ice maker), the new one comes in, the guy comes out and installs it. It did not work--not even one batch of ice. So I called Sears and asked them to just take this one back and send us a whole new refrigerator. Several weeks later, we finally have a working refrigerator! Yay!

Almost two months later (that's right now), the ice maker quit working.

I don't understand how the ice maker could be that bad. I mean, did nobody ever test this after they designed it? It boggles my mind that the design is that awful. I don't understand how the repairs to the ice makers isn't bankrupting Bosch. I would have thought they would have quit selling this model as soon as the reports of the failures started rolling in, unless I just have exceedingly bad luck. But I don't think so--I notice someone else's review also says that their ice maker quit.

Anyway, I strongly recommend avoiding this model, and doing your research if you want a different Bosch model, to make sure it doesn't use the same broken ice maker.

product_title: Bosch B26FT70SNS800 25.9 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel French Door Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_text:
I would not buy this item. I bought this from Sears and finally was able to get them to switch it for a different model after the 5th repair in less than a year. The ice maker refused to work (and I have all new plumbing in my house and high water pressure - so that is not the issue) and what really killed the deal for me was the door alarm would go off randomly. I could wake up in the morning and open the door and instantly the alarm goes off. It doesn't sound like such a big issue, I suppose. But the fact is, it drove me nuts having the door alarm go off constantly. And if you did leave the door open a minute and the alarm went off, shutting the door doesn't stop it. You have to actually hit the mute button. Now what sense does that make?

It's a nice looking refrigerator, but the door alarm and ice maker suck. I would not recommend buying this model.

product_title: Bosch B26FT70SNS800 25.9 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel French Door Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_text:
Not happy with it at all. New fridge arrives and starts leaking from the dispenser. Technician comes in 4 times and replaces a few parts and is STILL happening. Hoping for a replacement, I call in and they tell me the policy is to have three FUNCTIONAL repairs before it is replaced. Apparently the first visit is a "diagnostics" visit and does not count. Anyway, now I am told the fridge does not have a gasket part and one will be put on the 5th visit. How in the world do you sell a new fridge without a required part????

It also seem to make a LOT of noise at times, quiet for the most part so it is not a major issue right now.

two stars because well, it does keep the food chilled. But honestly, I would go with a different brand right now.

Update: 10/13/2013
This Bosch has been moved to the garage as they could not fix the leaking after 11 visits nor will they take it back! An easy case in the small claims court for me to win, however like most of us, I lack the time. So off to the garage it went where now it RUSTED! yes, they market it as stainless steel but it rusted.
I ended up getting an LG which for the same exterior size, has 5 cubic feet more inside and it is overall leaps and bounds above the Bosch engineering wise. It feels more solid, ice machine easier to take out and better designed, the stainless steel is real stainless steel, better light, more compartments, quieter and just a much much better value for the money in general. Bosch feels like a cheap toy compared to the LG. Just try them in the store if you have the chance and you will see.
In conclusion do NOT make the mistake of getting anything Bosch (I have my "top of the line" Bosch dishwasher too, btw), LG is eating their lunch.

product_title: Bosch B26FT70SNS800 25.9 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel French Door Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_title: Chronic ice maker problems - stuck with a lemon
review_text: I have had model B26FT70SNS (french style doors, with freezer on the bottom) for about 1 year. From early on I had ice maker problems. Well...about 6 service visits and 1 entire ice maker replacement later, I continue to experience problems. Ice makers have been around for a few decades now, it seems that Bosch should have the bugs worked out by now. Some of the ice problems have included: busted motor, over filling, under filling, no filling of ice trays at all. It appears to be poor engineering and Bosch refuses to acknowledge that it is a poor design. The customer service representatives have always been courteous but have only offered sending out the repair service. I truly wish I could get a refund because after reading other people's reviews, they stated that their problems didn't go away even after having the entire refrigerator replaced. If you didn't care to ever use the ice maker, the interior storage and organization is very nice.

product_title: Bosch B26FT70SNS800 25.9 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel French Door Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_text:
I've had this piece of junk for a few days over a year. Changed the filter, and again, no ice. Water pressure is fine so it's not that. Not the first time it's happened either. First month I owned this same model, I had 3 service calls. item was replaced with this one. Same problems. I always thought Bosch was a quality brand but they should just start over or quit making these, especially if they plan on having an ice maker.

I did purchase an additional warranty and was told it only covers the compressor. I would NEVER purchase a Bosch appliance again. Paid BIG bucks, got junk. BEWARE!!!

product_title: Bosch B26FT70SNS800 25.9 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel French Door Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_text: FRIDGE FAILED TO RESTART AFTER A SHORT POWER OUTAGE. PROGRAMMING WAS LOST AND CAUSED ALL THE FOOD TO GO BAD. SERIOUS PROBLEM AS WE WHERE AWAY FOR SOME TIME SMELL WILL LIKELY NEVER COME OUT

product_title: Bosch B26FT70SNS800 25.9 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel French Door Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_text: We purchased a BOSCH counter-depth refrigerator (22 cu. ft.) in April of 2011 from Lowe's.  On December 18, 2011 the freezer side went out completely.  It took three weekends and three different service technicians to get the correct parts (the control unit and temperature sensor) for the freezer to start working again on January 14, 2012.  Luckily, we have an old 1999 KitchenAid in the garage to store our freezer items and that the Bosch fridge was still under warranty.  Overall, we are very disappointed with our purchase of Bosch refrigerator and will stay away from this brand.

product_title: Bosch B26FT70SNS800 25.9 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel French Door Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_title: Bosch Refrigerator a Piece of Junk - Do Not Buy!!!
review_text:
Purchased the Bosch B26FT70SNS refrig in November, 2011.

Pros:

1. Well lit inside.
2. Produce bins good size.

review_title: save $, buy Frigidair and have the same problems
review_text:
After 4 months with the fridge, its been a love hate relationship. Love the looks, hate the ice maker. in the 4 months, i've taken it apart 2 times to fix it. luckily its something that hasn't required a service visit and hasn't costed me anything except my time and a few stranded moments without ice. i know, first world problems.

here is the kicker which explains my title. after feeling ripped off that my bosch microwave was some cheap junk made in china, that suspiciously looked like a Frigidaire, i couldn't help but notice that my Bosch french door refrigerator, looked similar to a Frigidaire as well, both in and out. I checked out the reviews of Frigidaire FGHB2844L on amazon, lo an behold, identical ratings, and identical complaints; the ice maker sucks. I checked the reviews of the suspected Electrolux clone of this fridge and that has ice maker issues as well. I don't know which company is responsible for the original design of the ice maker, but you would think they would have fixed this to avoid angering customers from 3 companies.

bottom line, you can save a little over $700 by getting the Frigidaire. But be prepared to have the same issues.

------Update 03/31/2014
Its been a little over a year that we've owned this fridge. After learning how to take apart the ice maker from another reviewer on amazon i've been able to fix my ice maker 3 times early on in ownership in January of 2013. The last time was probably May of 2013, each time the same issue, a magnet on the ice bin sensor arm falling off and not resetting the ice maker cycle. The last fix i think was for good since it hasn't happened since.

Last month the ice maker stopped again, and i thought that magnet fell out. I opened it up and it was still in its correct place, so that wasn't the issue this time. Scared that i would have to get a repair guy in and take days off from work i reluctantly called service. The lady i spoke to suggested i changed the filter. Even though i was able to dispense water, apparently an old clogged filter lowers the pressure enough to push open the ice maker water valve.

Then i realized remembering how expensive the filters were, i kept resetting the timer since the water tasted fine. I changed the filter, and 1 day later it made its first cubes. 2 days later i got a full bin of ice again.

I learned a few things which might be helpful to others.
1. Change the filter. I got about a year out of an original bosch filter that came with the fridge. I don't know how others will fare.
2. I say others above because i tried out a filter from GE that had the same thread and connection pattern. Its been working for a month so far and no problems, if you do try this one it is at your own risk. GE MSWF Replacement Cartridge part #34-8710-7349-9. I don't think it was any cheaper than an original filter purchased online, but if you are in a pinch and need to get one, i found these at the blue apron box store. Make sure to save the filter grip handle part from the old filter before discarding. It won't be used on the alternate filter since the grip is built in, but if you want to go back to original bosch filters, you will need it.
3. Apparently the ice maker has a temperature sensor in it and will only make ice if the interior compartment is the correct temperature. This makes sense but wasn't obvious when i put everything back together and was expecting the ice cycle to begin. Having the fridge doors open and ice maker apart caused the temperatures to drop enough that the sensor wouldn't allow the ice maker to begin ice making.

So far its been ok, so i bumped up my rating from 2 to 3. regardless, we shouldn't have to deal with issues like this.

product_title: Bosch B26FT70SNS800 25.9 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel French Door Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_text:
I've had Bosch appliances for years, and used to have a very strong belief in their product line. If you purchased Bosch goods 10 or so years back, then you probably own a true, German made item. From my understanding, Bosch has since created a manufacturing plant here in the States, where there just isn't the same commitment to excellence in standards. It also seems that the tolerance of mediocrity is greater here in the US, as consumers seem to have been conditioned to accept/expect less and less over time.

This unit does boast tremendous capacity/storage, and is exceptionally well lit. It really does seem to keep foods, such as fruits and vegetables, more viable over time. The freezer is also commodious, though not quite so as the refrigerator itself.

I've owned this model for 3 years now, as of this writing.
Some problems are/were:
-After delivery, it became evident that the gasket around the freezer door was not properly attached and had to be serviced, albeit easily, though there was a great deal of condensation for a while along the freezer door, before the repair.
-The ice maker seems to make ice only when it is good and ready, and sometimes days will elapse before ice is available.
-The option of crushed ice vs regular cubes - it seems impossible to distinguish between the two, though no big deal.
-The water dispenser is super-slow and takes a while to fill even small glasses.
-A few months ago, there was a loud, vibrating sound that came on and off again, as if one of the fans were off kilter. I was going to call for service, but the sound stopped. I can't detect any difference in operation since the sound stopped, but fear that the fan, or its motor, just eventually blew out.
-The quality of the stainless steel is not the utmost, though decent enough, but just not for the money.

I would proceed with some caution when considering making this purchase, and keep your fingers crossed (which is really no way to go forward).
It may just be that there are some good and bad units of its type out there. I had looked at so many refrigerators prior to the purchase of this one and found that (possibly) for the money, it was about the best. It has the name, but unfortunately, that somehow means less nowadays...

2) In other forums, you will read about the frequent issues with the ice maker. This is an issue. Although it was never broke, we have had to reset the ice maker approximately every other week. It takes about 24 hours to get enough ice to use. The issue seems to reside in the trigger becoming engaged in the off position but will not resolve until a reset has been performed.
3) All of the lettering on the door that allows you to know what button does what task has worn off after 6 months of use and completely worn off after one year of use.
4) It is a noisy compressor
5) The portion of the door that keeps the two doors sealed together when closed, has broken. If you're not consciously checking this after closing the door, you have 1/2 inch of gap that lets cold air out.
6) The compressor has died after two years of ownership. For such an expensive appliance, this is unacceptable to our expectations. Normally, this part should last 10 to 15 years.

The compressor is still under warrantee, but we are required to spend another $250 to $450 to pay for the service to replace. As a result of all the issues noted above, we are opting to purchase a new refrigerator that will have better quality rating. And we are definitely not spending over $2000 to do so.

product_title: Bosch B26FT70SNS800 25.9 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel French Door Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_title: Ice maker needs defrosting to compensate for poor design.
review_text:
I bought this refrigerator in October 2010 for $2,390. It works, but this refrigerator sells for a premium price and is not a premium refrigerator, especially the ice making capability.

As many others have pointed out in their reviews, the ice maker often quits making ice. The problem comes from the ice maker not always detecting when the bin is full so additional ice gets jammed up in the mechanical mechanism and no more ice is made. What happens is that ice from the compartment gets caught up in the mechanism so that when additional water flows and freezes the ice in the mechanism becomes a big blob of connected ice cubes and binds the mechanism so no more ice gets made.

You can "fix" the problem by removing the ice bin, unscrewing the anchor screw on the left front side of the ice making mechanism, and sliding forward the ice maker mechanism where the top tabs align with cutouts. This allows your to drop the ice maker down to where you can rotate it the left and see the frozen mass of water inside that clogs up the operation. The connecting electrical cable from the mechanism to the back of the ice making compartment does not detach in any way that I can find. There is just enough slack in the cable to move the mechanism to the slots to let it drop down for inspection and defrosting. Since you can't completely remove the mechanism to do the defrosting, you have to leave it in the compartment and carefully use a heat gun or hair dryer to melt the ice blob enough to remove the ice that binds up the mechanism. I put several micro-fiber cloths in the bottom of the ice maker cavity and gently use a heat gun to melt the ice enough to remove the big blob of ice then dry everything out, put the mechanism back in place, and ice making works for a while.

Once you do this the first time it is pretty easy to do a couple of times a year if you are half-way handy. You only have to remove the one screw on the left side that holds the mechanism into the ice making compartment. You can also remove the top screw and gently lift up the mechanism top cover just enough to take a peek, but there are other screws in the back that can't be easily reached, so you may not want to take the risk of breaking the top cover of the mechanism. The mechanism is open on the right side, so rotating it to the left gives you access to heat up and defrost the ice that builds up and binds the mechanism.

Since the basic design of this ice maker is flawed, defrosting isn't a fix, but a temporary remedy to the problem. I hate to think how many people have paid to have the ice making mechanism replaced when all that was wrong was a frozen up mechanism due to this design flaw.

This product should have been better designed and tested before being sold, especially the ice maker. It is definitely not a premium refrigerator with this ice maker.

review_text: Have had this dryer since 8-11 and works great. It has many different settings that allow for many different fabrics and load sizes. product_title: LG 4.2 CF 24" COMPACT DRYER WHITE
review_text: We use this dryer for a family of 5.  It works great and drys as quickly as any other dryer we've had as long as we don't stuff it full.  The clothes need room to tumble.  The reason these dryers are much more energy efficient is two fold:  1.  It uses less electricity to dry the same amount of clothes as a vented dryer.  2.  The largest savings occur because it doesn't vent your home's interior air to the outside.  You spend a lot of money heating or cooling your home in the winter and summer, and a vented / "normal" dryer pumps that conditioned air outside at a high rate.  This dryer works by keeping the hot air inside the chamber, and then dehumidifies that air internally.  The water is either pumped through a hose to the same drain that your washing machine does, or it has an internal holding tank that you can empty.  It does not heat the room noticeably, even in the summer.  Can't recommend this dryer enough, and no, I don't work for LG; just a satisfied customer that cares about saving energy / money.

review_title: Drought-Stricken Californian's Dryer Adventure - a true tale of misery and pain
review_text:
Don't buy this. It's cute, small, dries efficiently and is pretty quiet for a dryer, but beware: it breaks down. 7 months after I purchased this item (I bought the set - no problems with the washer as yet) in April of 2014 after researching, researching and researching. I had very narrow perameters for my search. It had to be electric, it had to be small and it had to have a good service record. As far as I could tell, this dryer fit the bill. I had just had a horrible experience with a dryer of a different brand and finally gave up trying to get it fixed. The little dryer was great at first. I didn't use it much because I prefer to hang my laundry outside. But when it rained I used the dryer. I live in sunny, daought-stricken California so it doesn't rain much. The little dryer was hardly used. Then in November, a mere 7 months after purchase, it started to shut down at different times during cycle, start beeping and flashing a message to empty yje water container (it's the time of dryer that does not vent - it collects the water in a tray that you have to empty. Irt's great for drought-stricken Californians because i use the water to feed my drought-stricken plants). Anyway, the dryer flashed the message whether or not there was any water AT ALL in the tray. I would dutifullt check the container and restart the machine. 5 minutes later it would do it again. It was winter and it was cold and sometimes (but not often) wet outside and I wanted to use my dryer (besides collecter water for my thirsty, drought-stricken plants it also warms up the kitchen). It was still under manufacturer's warranty so LG helped me find a service provider for repairs. Thus began a parade of useless, untrained and unprepared service technicians from various companies who, for the most part, couldn't grasp the concept of an electric dryer. LG was sending out serive people who were clearly not qualified to work on the machine. After over two months of this, a technician came in to install a part - a wrong part - and knew right away what the problem was. The water sensor had malfunctioned. Two weeks later he came back and installed the sensor and the dryer began working again - yay! By this time it had begun to make a weird grinding noise but the tech said: "It's normal'. I asked him to check it out and he replied "I'm here to fix, not diagnose" Yikes. The dryer worked again, but the experience left me wondering how much LG actually cared about their products and their customers.

Over the next several months, the grinding noise got a little louder but the dryer kept working. Summer came and the drought continued. I used the clothesline a lot and the dryer rarely. Fall and winter brought actual rain to drought-stricken California and I was forced inside to use the quietly grinding but working dryer. And the, not a year after the first repair, it stopped working again. Again with the water sensor. Now LG's warranty had run out and I was covered by an extended warranty I had presciently purchased. After another parade of confused and untrained service techs visited my palatial estate and marvelled at the wonders within and then fumbled the job EVEN THOUGH I TOLD THEM EXACTLY WHAT WAS WRONG, aa new sensor was finally installed. Looking forward to another year of trouble-free drying I happily loaded up the machine and merrily pushed the start button. To my utter dismay the little dryer started beeping, now telling me to clean the filter. The filters are, of course, quite clean. So, after nearly two months of waiting for a repair I am now waiting for yet another. If I did not live in drought-stricken California I'm sure the dryer would have broken down down much sooner. I see that lots of people have very good things to say about this model. Maybe mine's a lemon. I called LG to ask them about that and told me basically to get bent because the dryer is out of warranty.

review_text: We've been using this dryer about once a week for the past 5 years, and it has been fine.  It will never be as wonderful and fast as the big vented dryer we have in our other house. product_title: Samsung : FTQ307NWGX 30 Freestanding Induction Range, 4 Cooktop Elements, Convection, Self Clean
review_title: Mine has been solid, albeit with a couple of warts, and relatively bargain-priced
review_text:
We've had this for 3 years with no unusual problems. It's hard to guess whether the company had quality-control problems or some of the problems were user- or site-related, but I'd very likely buy another one when the time came. I think that leading consumer-reports magazine gives the current model its best-of-the-bunch recommendation.

In our instance, the oven heats up quickly, we can use all the burners at once, they don't arbitrarily change their settings, etc. Our house is relatively new and there's good wiring (for a previous electric range), and we use only good-quality induction-rated cookware (with a sheet of parchment between pot and stove to keep it looking new).

Complaints: the sheet-metal could have used some sound-damping; it can get buzzy. I added some stick-on dampening material (from Lowe's) to the back exterior and tightened the screws a bit, so now it's mostly the heating drawer when it's not all the way in that can vibrate sometimes.

You can hear the electronics and its fans while the thing is cooking and cooling down afterwards, but it's acceptable to us. I don't know if other brands are quieter.

The large burner does demand a large pot, but that's clearly marked and mentioned in the manual and is more of a difference of opinion between the customer and Samsung's design department, not a failure. Some other brands allow for smaller pots on their largest burner, at considerably greater cost. I'd like that feature if it came without much cost.

On ours sometimes the large burner - which normally is perfectly happy boiling a large pot - won't re-sense it if I take it off and put it back a few seconds later. Pressing the master button off and back on fixes it but is a nuisance.

Spilling a lot of liquid on the stove top can generate a general "5E" error, but that's probably a useful safety feature. Press the master off to cancel the error, wipe, ready to go again.

There's a path that makes it not too difficult to get streaks between the two panes of glass in the oven door (I came here looking for comments on how to fix that - it seems simple enough to remove a few screws, but it's nice to be second when exploring).

There are lots more things I like than dislike - huge oven with 3 racks, many-path broiling element for uniformity, indirect baking element keeps incandescent temperatures (2000 degrees?) from radiating the bottoms of my baking pans, that wonderful heating drawer so I can easily serve meals on hot plates, the digital minutes-and-seconds cooking timer (which alas doesn't control anything but a bell), and all the benefits of induction cooking - how can anyone use anything else?

review_title: Good oven, not great finishes  GE JB850SPSS
review_text:
After having this oven for a few years .. i have any update to my review... they brushed chrome part on the back is really just a thin coating.. after regular cleaning this began to peel and now looks terrible. The stove we had before this was a GE profile with a grey speckled top. this black glass top looked great but has scratched and has burns that we can not longer remove.

it did not I purchased the model JB850SPSS it is the stainless steel model. I liked this one because i thought the smaller oven on top was an awesome option. We are a family of 5 and cook on it every day.

The oven works very well overall. When I first got it I had to adjust the temperature ( this is a feature of the oven) so that it worked the way my old oven did. I burned the first few batches of cookies, but now its the same as my old oven.

The upper oven has been a great feature, but you have to be careful about tall items like a bunt cake or roast that is tall. They may fit but if they are to close to the upper burner they will burn on top. I also can not get two cookie sheets in side by side, so one cookie tray at a time in the upper oven.

Some of the other features have been a disappointment. The oven windows became splattered in between the glass. So the glass does not look clean. There may be a way to take them apart, but I have not looked into it. The cook top has been the worst feature. Some burned on stains have become permanent. I am a cleaning machine, and no chemicals, razor blades or any scrubber i have tried have removed the marks. I have another GE oven before this one and it never had this problem. I think the cook top quality is not the same. The lower oven is a little tricky to use. Because it is so close to the floor it is harder than you think it might be to get your food out and up to the counter. If you cant do a squat while holding a ten pound roast in front of you this is not the oven for you. The Stainless finish on the back where the knobs are is only a thin finish, so do not scrub to hard or it will remove the finish.

If i had to buy this again and knew these issues, I would have spent a little more for better quality finishes. I definitely has the features but maybe not for a household who uses it as much as we do.

product_title: GE JB850SPSS 30 Electric Range - Stainless Steel
review_text:
This oven is great. I rarely use the larger bottom oven, but it comes in handy on holidays. It's nice, because the top oven pre-heats almost 2x as fast. The top burners are nice. I've owned the oven for 2.5 years now and did scratch the top sliding a pan across (doh!). I can buff it out if need be, but it's small and I can live with it.

The citric acid cleaning cream along with the razor blade make cleaning super easy. I do not have any stains on mine. I make sure my cookware is all ceramic top approved.

product_title: LG 5.4 CF GAS RANGE WITH CONVECTION WHTE
review_title: Great oven for people who like to bake
review_text:
Have used our LRG3095SW for several months now and have been overall very happy with it. Purchased it primarily because it was the only model that had a proofing mode that maintains a temperature low enough to let bread and other yeast products rise properly. The convection feature reduces the cooking time but it does take some trial and error to figure out how much to reduce the cooking times. When you enter a temperature, if you put it in the convection bake mode, it reduces the temperature 25 degrees. Bread and rolls come out with a crispier crust than our previous oven. The interior of the oven is a deep blue but that is not visible with the light off. When the light is on, it is much easier to see in the oven than other ovens we have used. If you go to appliance show rooms to see what the white unit looks like, good luck in finding one. LG apparently only allows dealers to put the Stainless models on display so we were never able to find a dealer with a white unit on display. In researching this product, one complaint we heard from people who had multiple LG appliances is that the some of the displays were red, some blue and some white, which defeated their attempt to have the appliances look like they matched. The electronic display on this unit has white numbers. The burners on the stove are very quick to light and it is nice to have a range of burner sizes available, although we do wish the smallest one had an even lower setting than it has. Other features that have been useful are the timed bake, so the oven will turn off when done. It also has a timer which can be set in minutes or hours.

The only complaints we have with the unit is the design of the knobs, which have grooves that can collect dirt and will be difficult to clean, and it uses far more electricity that it needs to. The clock consumes over 26 kilowatts per year and the oven uses a glo-coil igniter that draws over 400 watts whenever the oven burner is on. I can't fault them for the igniter because that is pretty standard in ovens, but there is no excuse for them not to make the clock more energy efficient.
