product_title: LG 3.6 CF FRONT LOAD WASHER DRYER COMBO
review_text:
This combo unit is amazing!!! With a very small home, this is great for a small space having an all in one washer dryer unit. It does take a while longer than the traditional washer and dryer setup, however it is worth the extra time.

product_title: LG 3.6 CF FRONT LOAD WASHER DRYER COMBO
review_text:
Just got my new LG combo unit and loving it. We had to replace and relocate our existing laundry area, so rather than buy two units that take up space, and run all new ductwork for a dryer, we bought this. I was skeptical at first, but I am really loving it! The machine is full size, ample for my family of 4. It cleans very well and is super quiet compared to my old Whirlpool. Pros: Saves space, easy installation, energy efficient, you can have your clothes washed a dried for you when you arrive home from work. Cons: You need to play with the dryer a bit to find the right amount of time needed; at first they feel wet, but it's mostly just steam-if you give it a minute to cool off they are dry. Takes a long time.
I will caution that I typically line dry my heavier items i.e. denim, sweaters, etc. So I typically pull them out before the dry cycle begins. If you typically put all your clothes in the dryer, this may not be for you.

product_title: LG 3.6 CF FRONT LOAD WASHER DRYER COMBO
review_text: This is the first review i have ever written for a product, mostly because the reviews for this product is what led me to buy it. This product is the perfect solution for any apartment where all you have is a water line. This fit into a small pantry in our apartment and we used the plumbing from the kitchen for the washer portion. You dont need a vent for drying, and the clothes come out dry. We were originally very worried because some reviews stated that the clothes come out damp, but that will only occur if you over stuff it. We are a family of 2 and wash clothes pretty regularly, and we can fit a normal sized load into the unit and it will come out dry. It does take abour 4-5 hours depending on the size, but if you go to work and come back you have dry clean clothes, same if you do it over night. Also the unit is quiet. We would definitely reccomend this to someone looking for a ventless solution to washing. Also, I dont think we would go back to a non-combo after experiencing the ease of this. product_title: LG 3.6 CF FRONT LOAD WASHER DRYER COMBO
review_title: Great machine, but a couple of minor flaws.
review_text:
I live in a small apartment and bought this machine to save space. Being ventless, it takes a long time to dry clothes, but I knew that when I bought it. I put a new load in each night after work, and as long as the laundry is done 24 hours later by the next night, I'm happy. It has lots of settings and, being ventless, plugs into a standard outlet and drains into the sink.

I bought the LG because I read on many different consumer sites that the other competing machines (like the Haier) have a lot of breakdowns and problems. The Haier is less expensive than the LG, but you get what you pay for.

But there's a couple of flaws. For one, if you wash too few items, it becomes unbalanced and stops. Sometimes, I just want to wash a couple of towels, and come home the next night to find that it's signaling an unbalanced load and didn't finish the load.

The bigger complaint is that the sensor that it has to tell when the load is dry and to stop the dry cycle doesn't work. I've had the repairman out a couple of times, and told me that the machine is working according to spec. So I use the timed dry setting instead of the automatic dry. But the problem there is that the maximum dry time it can be set to is 2 and a half hours, and that's not long enough. So my clothes are always slightly damp coming out if it. But the machine dries fine; it just needs more time to dry. If only the dry time could be set to 4 hours or so, my clothes would be perfectly dry the next day and the machine would be perfect.

product_title: LG 3.6 CF FRONT LOAD WASHER DRYER COMBO
review_text:
We ordered this unit on the last day of 2010 and it was delivered 24 January 2011. We've now been using it for about three weeks.
It's just the two of us in our household with no kids.
We found this unit because we were struggling with venting arrangements for a conventional dryer. This is ventless. And ventless means that you are not exhausting warm air from inside your home to the outside causing it to be replaced with cold air (in winter) that has to be heated.
We love the combined washer+dryer. Our laundry room is quite small and we did not want to lose any space unnecessarily.

--The lint mostly goes down the drain except for a trap that you have to clean out occasionally. And wipe down the door seal regularly. This is less troublesome than cleaning out a dryer lint trap each load. And no risk of fire from accumulated, trapped lint in the exhaust duct.
--We also love the fact it requires only an ordinary 120VAC power circuit. No 220VAC `pigtails' and plug configuration to figure out.
--And you just put in dirty laundry and the next time you open the unit door it is clean and `ready to go'. No need to transfer heavy, soggy laundry from washer to dryer.
We did read and comply with the directions about `similar lint' laundry items. For example, don't mix bath towels (high lint producing) with nylon underwear (zero lint producing). This seems to serve us well.
--The unit seems very quiet to us. It does not `act' as the typical power-sucking washer and dryer running continuously for lengthy periods of time. It operates briefly, then pauses. Then again. This may be disconcerting to some (like our cat) but does not bother us in the least. We know this is necessary to save energy while cleaning effectively. The unit seems easy to use. The pre-sets are easy.
--To know if the laundry is `dry', reach in and pull out a `sample' item. The air inside the unit may feel `damp'. Disregard this feeling of the dampness of the air inside the unit. When you remove the sample item and note that it dries nearly instantly as you give it a gentle shake, then you know the cycle is sufficiently long. This is often well before the machine says the cycle is complete. It is true that the dry cycle for bath towels is longer than for a conventional high-energy consumption machine. Remember that you are only putting the energy coming thru an ordinary 120VAC circuit into the unit. We think that is a good energy trade-off, tho. The unit is Energy Star-compliant and we got a $180 tax credit from State of Oregon because of its high efficiency ratings.

This unit seems ideal for small apartments, condos, and where venting is a problem.
This is a larger capacity unit than most `combined' units. Nice!
Cost of this unit may seem to be a disadvantage but don't forget to include the cost of pedestals (typically $150-200 each) for front-loader washer and dryer, plus extended warranty for each. When all was summed, our cost was about the same for a single unit as for the high efficiency separate front loader washer and front loader dryer. We did not choose to include a pedestal for this unit because we put laundry in dry and take it out dry -- no transfer from washer-to-dryer.
This unit may not necessarily be optimal for a large family with children if you have multiple loads `back-to-back' and need a washing cycle to be running simultaneously with a drying cycle of another laundry load.
And if you are wedded to the idea of your laundry coming out of a dryer `toasty' and radiating heat (and willing to pay the energy cost), you may want to think about whether this unit is the right choice. This dry method seems ideal for no-iron outcomes.
Only time will tell whether the unit is reliable but we have no reason to believe that the `combined unit' configuration will be a factor in that outcome. The motor does have a 10-year warranty. Will any service tech be mystified by the unit if repairs are needed? One financial feature we liked is that the extended warranty we purchased cost us for one unit rather than purchasing one warranty for the washer and a separate warranty for a dryer.
The guys that brought it did not leave the drum security bolts that are to be removed from the unit when it is `in place' for use, but kept and replaced before the unit it moved to a different home (to avoid transit damage to the drum suspension system). We had to get them to return the bolts. And we don't know if they removed the bolts in the proper order prescribed in the manual. Otherwise the deliver guys were very friendly and helpful.

review_text:
RUN AWAY! We bought this washer/dryer combo a little over 2 years ago. I wrote a review shortly after talking about the need to iron everything, the knots tied in shirt sleeves and the clothes coming out looking as if they were crumpled in a corner for a month. Here's an update:

review_text: The good thing about this machine is that it's two useless appliances, but only takes the space of one.  And it's beautiful too!  In true Rube Goldberg fashion, the machine goes on for 5-6 hours at a time, with beautiful LED readouts, wonderful spinning & gyrations, while accompanied by the gentle hum of percision engineering -- and amazingly enough, at the end of all this, your clothes are damp, dirty and wrinkled (even with a small load.)  It should also be noted that your patience is rewarded with the musty odor imparted into your clothes that apparently only a 5 hour dry cycle can achieve.

product_title: LG 3.6 CF FRONT LOAD WASHER DRYER COMBO
review_text:
I've traded up from a super crappy thin-twin stackable washer and dryer set, and let me tell you, it's one of the best things I've ever done. I read tons of reviews before I settled on this washer. One of the major complaints that most people talk about is how long it takes to dry, but I've found that it doesn't take any longer than a regular set, unless you're one of those people who sits and waits for the dryer to buzz. Personally, I stick my laundry in and forget about it for a few hours, and when I'm ready to think about it again...poof!...it's all clean. One other thing people talked about was that they didn't feel like their clothes were dry when they took them out. Because of the way the dryer works, there is steam left over at the end of the cycle. Once the dryer cools (it locks you out until the tub is cool enough to touch to keep you from getting burned) you take our your clothes, give them a quick shake, and they go from a little damp feeling to warm and dry. It's like a little miracle every time you do laundry.

I've had to get used to the way the machine sounds. It's not a constant hum, but a series of on and off cycles. I assume it's because it's supper energy efficient and its only drawing power when it needs to turn.

That's another really awesome thing about this machine...it runs on a regular outlet plug. Also the "Direct Drive" motor turns the tub directly, instead of through a series of belts, which means you'll never have to worry about replacing them.

Oh and another thing!!!! I had a shirt that I wore outside to do heavy gardening and yard work. It's been stained and dirty for more than a year, no matter how many times I've washed it. One trip through this new washer and it's as good as new! I use "Charlie's Soap" which is HE compatible, and only use 2/3's of a scoop. So little soap for such clean clothes!!!

I've only had the washer a few weeks, but so far so good. I"m really pleased.

product_title: LG 3.6 CF FRONT LOAD WASHER DRYER COMBO
review_title: Great unit, a few quirks, but below are the work-arounds!
review_text:
Cost of Operation

-Not sure as to the amount of water it uses (water is included in my rent)
-Using my [[ASIN:B000RGF29Q P3 International P4460 Kill A Watt EZ Electricity Usage Monitor]], and running a half full drum of clothes through a wash and dry cycle, it cost me $0.21. That's 21 cents at an estimated 12.2 cents per KWh. The entire cycle went through 1.72KWh.

Design/Size/Installation

-I had a very tight space to put this machine in, and it should be noted that the listed dimensions are the maximum values. The machine's front is 29 inches from the rear, and the circular knob on the front is what adds the extra .75". They do recommend that you have about 4 inches behind the machine for the hoses and stuff.

-I installed the machine by myself. It was very easy and it comes with a few sets of (the same) installation instructions so it's hard to go wrong. Make sure you remove the shipping bolts and retain them if you have to move the machine later. It is worth noting that if you have to tip the machine, as I had to, to remove the shipping foam from the bottom, LG tells you to tip it on its side, not on the front or rear (I am guessing to protect the drum). Having a second person to help move the unit would definitely make it easier, but if you note in the pictures I uploaded, LG added nice hand grips to the side to aid in moving the unit.

-The unit comes with all hoses, etc, necessary to connect the unit.

-The design is very nice. Although it stays in a closet, it is a very aesthetically pleasing unit. The LED readout is nice, and the buttons are big and clear. The chrome door is a nice touch as well.

Operation/Tips I've Learned

-There are a ton of different wash and dry settings on this machine, and I am sure you can read about them elsewhere, so I will focus on the quirks that you may encounter (that I have encountered) as you operate the machine.

-The machine plays a little tune when you start it up and a load finishes. (Warning: The tune may get stuck in your head if you do a lot of laundry.)

-If drying on the automatic setting I have noticed that when it gets down to "6 minutes remaining" it will stay there for 5, 10 maybe 15 minutes, before counting down. So if you see a 6 on an automatic dry cycle don't wait around for it thinking it will finish soon.

-The clothes come out dry despite feeling damp when you immediately open the door. The dampness is just in the drum itself, not in the clothes (unless you wash something heavy).

-When washing a queen comforter in the machine, we noticed some soap still on the inside after the dry cycle and we pulled it out. To combat this, I would recommend after the initial wash cycle of a bulky item, remove the item, move it around, and run another rinse/spin cycle (which is an option)
-Although you can do a wash/dry cycle at the same time, I like to do a wash only cycle (on extra high spin) then put a few dryer sheets on then go to a dry only cycle.

-There is a certain smell about the new materials in the machine, expect this smell in your clothes for a few washes. I would keep the door open once you install it to maybe dissipate the smell more quickly.

-After a dry cycle, the LED readout will say "Cd" which I am assuming stands for cool down or clothes done. The door to the dryer will remain locked and you will not be able to remove the items inside. If you wait for it to go away on its own, it takes a few hours. (I let it do it on its own once to see). The way to get around this is so just simply spin the silver knob once "Cd" is displayed. A few seconds later the door will unlock. It is nice to know though that while "Cd" is on, the machine will still rotate your clothes every so often to avoid wrinkles. Good thinking LG.

-I usually fill the drum about half way for every load. You can wash a full drum of clothes but then it says in the manual to remove half of the clothes for the dry cycle. After I wash a half drum of clothes and do the automatic dry, it has never taken more than an hour and a half to dry the load. Combined with the 49 minute normal cotton wash cycle, you are looking at about 2.5 hours or so to do a half load of laundry (washed and dried).

Final Thoughts

Overall this is a great machine if you are looking for a single unit that can wash and dry a full load of laundry while presenting you with the limitation of a smaller apartment, a non vented area, or an area without a 240V outlet. We experienced all three conditions and this was the best unit we could find to meet our needs. The full size drum is a rarity for this type of machine, and its worth should not be overlooked. The clothes come out clean and (after the first few uses, see my tip above) fresh. You will not be disappointed in this machine.

product_title: LG 3.6 CF FRONT LOAD WASHER DRYER COMBO
review_text:
We bought our LG all-in-one from US Appliance in March 2009 (don't think it was available on Amazon at that time) and got a 2 year extended warranty from Assurance along with it (on top of the one year mfg warranty). Long story short, several warranty repairs were needed after the mfg warranty ran out, including broken internal drain hoses, pressure regulators and sensors, and finally the motor went bad. Assurance refused to cover the last motor repair saying it was our fault and not an equipment defect.
Turns out the ventless dryer design does not have a lint screen, and with extended use the lint can accumulate in the drive motor, causing it to fail. I am still fighting with the Assurance extended warranty company on that issue, since even the repairman stated there was no way we could have either intentionally caused the problem (as per Assurance's bogus claim) or avoided it by operating it differently. US Appliance even went to bat for us until Assurance stopped answering their calls! LG customer service was no help at all, siding with Assurance's point of view.
Bottom line is this machine is best for light use only, until LG makes its design more rugged. And make sure to ALWAYS get the extended warranty.

product_title: LG 3.6 CF FRONT LOAD WASHER DRYER COMBO
review_text: I recently purchased this washer/dryer combo due to lack of space. I am House Director of a sorority in central Illinois and have a three room apartment on the second floor. After doing quite a bit of research, I chose this model due to other reviews plus the fact it doesn't need to be vented and runs on a regular outlet instead of 220. It does take longer to wash/dry, but you can continue to do other things since the time it will take is judged as it begins the cycle. I have had to hang some towels that were still a little damp, but this is not a problem either. I have suggested this to friends who are looking for new units and will continue to do so. Great idea LG. Love it!

product_title: LG 3.6 CF FRONT LOAD WASHER DRYER COMBO
review_text:
Washer Pros: Cleans great, perfect for our small space, no maintenance issues for the last 2 years. Great on water conservation! Good capacity.
Washer Cons: Many, too many washing options. For example, why would there be a separate "extra wash" button that give you an extra 3 minutes on your wash cycle? Too many wash cycle combinations overall! Furthermore, wash cycle takes forever! Don't forget to wipe-out the extra water remaining in the rubber inside tubing after EVERY wash cycle to avoid mold. Keep washer door open after every wash cycle to allow washer to dry.

Dryer Pros: Nothing extaordinary
Dryer Cons: Automatic dryer sensor doesn't work, especially on medium and small dyer loads. I had the sensor replaced within 1 month of purchasing this machine, but it made no difference. I therefore have to override the settings to be "extra dry" or run the machine on time-set.

In short, buy these machines for their small size, good maintenance records and quiet/efficient wash cycle. If these are not priorities, choose another model!

product_title: LG 3.6 CF FRONT LOAD WASHER DRYER COMBO
review_title: These need to be new standard in the U.S.!
review_text:
After seeing so many less than great experiences, I thought I should share mine.

I bought this model in the summer 2010 (about a year ago at the time of writing this). After researching all different kinds of units, I decided to give this one a go. None were remotely local, so I had to order blindly online. I was stationed in Germany, so I was aware of such units since they are pretty common place there and I had a friend that lived in a small high-rise place in Chicago that had this kind of washer/dryer (albeit, it was smaller, much older and didn't quite do the best job). I was a little concerned by some of the reviews I saw for this model, but decided to try due to being just one unit and the energy usage.

Right from the start I had great results. There was a learning curve though for using a unit like this. You MUST be open to it being different from what you probably grew up with and not try to cram it into that old way of thinking. How it works is completely different -- at least the drying side -- from all the conventional washers and dryers so many are familiar with. You will probably be disappointed, for whatever reason, if you don't take this into consideration.

That being said, I find it cleans clothes very well and dries clothes pretty darn well for using so little energy. On average, my loads take about two hours to wash AND dry. I don't think I've ever had a load go as long as three hours even. I do the auto cycles that calculate how long to wash and dry. I fill the drum usually about 3/4 full. If you cram it full to the point nothing care move, it will not clean or dry as well. THIS ISN'T AN OLD-FASHION UPRIGHT AGITATOR! You can't expect that really from new front loaders either. They just don't work that way.

product_title: LG 3.6 CF FRONT LOAD WASHER DRYER COMBO
review_text:
I did not buy this combo at Amazon. I found it cheaper with free shipping somewhere else. I have also noticed that most of the "bad" reviews came from people who had had it for a while and had some electronic or mechanical problems. These problems are actually to be expected. This is a complex machine, and it is difficult to service! It is one of the VERY FEW appliances where I RECOMMEND buying an extended warranty! A five-year (4 yrs extended) program is available from various sellers for about $140-180. LG's extended warranty is much costlier ~$350 for the same length (and therefore not recommended!).

Another problem is with people who haven't done their research but bought this machine even though they had other options. This machine is for people who have very limited space, no capability to vent and no 240V. For those who meet these requirements, this combo is FANTASTIC! There is no better solution (so far).

I refuse to give this combo 5 stars though. There are too many limitations and compromises that had to be made. If one wants to dry, then one cannot fill the drum more than 50-60% of capacity. A full load will simply not dry. The ventless drying uses a cold water line to a radiator, which condenses the steam from the hot clothes. This process is not too efficient, a bit noisy, and takes more than 3 hrs to dry a 1/2 load.
The lint from the process stays mainly in the clothes. Some get flushed in the drain and some get trapped in a filter located on the lower left corner. The manual recommends cleaning the filter every 2 weeks or so.

Thus, to a family that has many loads, I recommend washing every day, instead of having a "laundry day" that so many people seem to have. Those people that can run a vent should consider buying a separate dryer. It does the job much faster, and also more efficiently.

This machine is doing what it was designed for within its limitations. It is not a cure all, but for those of us who meet the requirements for buying this machine, THIS IS BY FAR THE BEST OPTION.

A side benefit of the ventless system is that in the winter, the heat that this combo produces will help in keeping the condo/apt warm. Even in the summer when the heat makes the a/c works harder, it is not a zero sum game. A vented dryer removes copious amounts of air to the outside, and this air is needed to be replaced, so the a/c will also work harder, though not quite as hard as with a ventless system.

And this brings me to my biggest concern. The radiator is located in the upper front right of the machine. When it is in dry mode, the spot becomes quite hot. Not hot enough to give someone a burn, but if the combo is in a closed space, I am afraid that it can cause a fire if a combustible item is left on top. I urge LG to install an insulating material over the radiator, attached to the top panel.

I have tried to publish my review on LG's website, but for some reason, it broke some of their rules even though I gave this combo a positive review. :(

05/16/12
I have had the combo now for a year and would like to expand on the lint problem that I encountered during that time. The lint assembles around the boot (rubber gasket around the tub). One needs to constantly remove the lint that accumulates there. If one does not do it, the lint will accumulate in the inner hoses and will clog the pump. LG recommends running the "clean" cycle with liquid bleach once a month (depends on number of uses per month). I recommend using this cycle WITHOUT bleach. Liquid bleach will harm the spider (the thing that holds the tub in place - a major repair if it needs replacement), which is made of aluminum. I recommend using bleach every 5-6 months. It is enough to clear the inner hoses and infrequent enough not to harm the spider too much.

I have gotten used to removing lint from my clothes all the time. There is really no solution to the excess lint :( , but that's life. :)

4/20/14
The machine is now almost 3 years old, and so far so good. I had no problems whatsoever. I assume that it is because I only have 2 loads/week on average. I cannot stress more strongly how important it is to clear the lint from the bellow. I work for a service company, and there are so many front load washers who get their drain pump clogged and the owners have to call for a repair that could have easily been avoided if they bothered to clean the lint at the end of the day.

Update: 2/5/2012
About four weeks ago the washer was on its final breaths. I decided to dive deep and learned about all sorts of horrible lint that builds up in the lines in the washer. Lint that accumulated above the pumps and caused them to fail due to stress. I did not know the strange noise was coming from a pump until I slid the washer on its side and did exploratory surgery. What I found is below. Know that the washer has had multiple issues with the pump and I believe it is due to the design and inability to easily access the location where the lint is accumulated.

There is easy access from the bottom and back of the washer. The back has a panel with four screws and the bottom has no panel at all. The large hose (3-4") coming from the soap dispenser down to the 'basin' under the washer is the problem child. This hose is used to receive the flushed soap from the soap compartment and comes down to the basin from the top left of the washer. There are two pumps at the bottom left of the washer right by the externally accessible lint trap. It appears that what happens is the spin cycle forces lint up the 3-4" hose and it clings to the side of the hose. This pushes it away from the pumps. However, the pump takes repeated damage due to stress of the lint at times. The lint slips down and constricts the pump openings. When I opened the back of the washer I removed two hose clamps from the 3-4" hose to check it out. I saw nothing...at first. Then I blinded put my hand up the hose and found a bit that turned into almost 2 cups of lint! I was shocked and thought I fixed the problem. The washer still had problems and I decided to replace one of the pumps ($30 or so on ebay). The pump is very easy to access and I had it replaced in about 15min. The washer is now 100%. Amazing that I almost tossed the washer for a new one. I am not sure how many washers that are side loaders have this problem, but it appears they all battle with it to varying degrees. Perhaps the material of the hose line is different in some not allowing the lint to adhere to the walls of the hose. Now that I am an unoffically certified LG washer repair person, we'll see how long it lives. The above information was pieced together from many sites and glued together with personal inspection and tinkering.
good luck!

review_title: Fantastic laundry option for the space-challenged
review_text:
When we bought our condo, the laundry hookups were in a (very) small kitchen, with space for a stacked washer/dryer and no space for any food storage. A coworker recommended the LG all-in-one washer/dryers to save space, so we did our research and ultimately bought this model. Since we were able to fit it in the nook for a stacked washer/dryer, we put a butcherblock counter on top, and shelves above, and have our microwave and pantry in the same space.

PROS:

+Cleans clothes well, with lots of options for wash/dry settings.
+No need to move clothes from washer to dryer. (We typically put laundry in before we go to bed, and have clean clothes when we wake up.)
+Gentle on clothes. I wash my nice work clothes, including "lay flat to dry" sweaters on Cold and the regular dry setting, and they come out beautifully without shrinkage.
+Fairly quiet. Our bedroom is located above the washer, and though we sometimes hear the water pump kick on/off (the loudest part of the cycle), it never disrupts our sleep.
+Energy efficient. Our water bills and electric bills are generally very low, even when we have done a LOT of laundry.
+Ventless dryer. The previous owners of our house had the vent line for the dryer run horribly wrong, and it was a fire hazard. It would have cost us several hundred dollars to fix it.

CONS:

-Clothes don't come out toasty warm. (They feel slightly damp, but are dry when you shake them out/fold them.)
-Can only handle small to medium-sized loads. (Clothes dry best when the tub is about half-full, to give room for air to circulate when drying.)
-Long dry cycle; we generally do the 120-minute dry cycle for all of our loads, which means that the total wash/dry time is 3 hours.
-No lint filter. We have 3 cats and the cat hair gets trapped/stuck to the rubber seal on the door, which is annoying to clean out.

Overall, this washer/dryer perfectly suits our needs and works very well for us (two large-sized adults with lots of laundry). It is great to be able to put laundry in before we go to bed, and wake up to clean clothes. It has also freed up valuable space in our small kitchen, and eliminated the need for costly repairs to the existing dryer vent line in our condo.

review_text:
First let me say I did not purchase this through Amazon so I can't speak to this particular retailer's service. I will say that the price I paid through a local appliance store was (after a bit of haggling) comparable to the price this retailer charges once shipping is included.

I've had this machine for about a month now and I've been very impressed overall. Living in an apartment that has no venting for a dryer, we needed something that was ventless so we knew that drying time would be an issue no matter what machine we bought. But rather than just getting separate units we decided to save some space and try out this combo to see if it would work for our small family's needs. So far, I'd say it's been very good.

The design is really quite nice - it has a space-age kind of feel, and the buttons are easy to use and most functions are clear and easy to access. My wife wishes it had been available in red, but the white is nice. The audio tones that play at startup and at the end of a wash are cute, but they may get to be a bit old after awhile. They're pretty subtle though, so I don't expect that they'll ever be annoying.

The washing and (more importantly) the drying couldn't be simpler. The unit can be used as just a washer, and it holds almost as much as any other front-loading washer. Before every wash the unit spins and weighs the load to determine the estimated time to complete the wash, and uses sensors to determine how dirty the clothes are. The unit automatically estimates the time to complete the wash, and then starts imeddiately after diong that. It can also be set to delay start up to 19 hours (in 1-hour increments) if, for instance, you want to set the washer to start in the mid-afternoon so that it's just getting done by the time you get home from work. The quality of the wash is really very good. We had been using an older top-loader, and by comparison this unit is much quieter, causes much less wear on the clothes and seems to get them cleaner, which really surprised me.

The drying feature is the main reason people buy this unit and I think it's great. There is a real advantage to being able to throw clothes in once, forget about them, and have them ready whenever you want completely cleaned and dry. It really puts an end to "laundry day" when you have to do multiple loads and constantly swap them between washer and dryer. Of course, there are some disadvantages, specifically that the capacity of this unit when drying is half that of the washer, at least that's what the instructions say. That means that if you load this unit full, you're supposed to unload half the laundry before running the dry cycle, and that means a lot more swapping loads if you're doing a lot of laundry. In practice though, this has not been my experience. I simply do smaller loads on a more regular basis and for the most part it's actually easier to deal with that way. Filling the unit about 2/3rds full, which for me is about 10 days worth clothes, seems to work just fine with the typical wash-and-dry cycle taking about 3-4 hours. Doing smaller half-loads, which for me would be about a week's worth of clothes, results in loads that take 2-2.5 hours. Again, because this can all be done automatically it means that I can just throw things in and go do other things, knowing that I don't have to be home to switch the load from washer to dryer or monitor it in any way.

A note about the timing of the drying: when the optional drying is added to the cycle, the estimated time display accounts for that time, and displays when the clothes will be able to be removed from the dryer. But this estimated time for completion is only a rough guess - the unit seems to use some sort of "fuzzy logic" to estimate the time along the way, so if it finds that your jeans aren't drying as quickly as expected, the timer will update continuously. I've had it add as much as 30 minutes to the total time of doing the load, so don't expect that the time it tells you it will be ready is actually the time it will be ready. This is both good and bad - it'd be nice if it were 100% accurate, but it's actually a big advantage for it to be actually analyzing the clothes as it washes and dries, and I prefer quality to accuracy. As for how well this unit dries, I would say it does a very good job. When I first started using it I would always set the dryer to "more dry" because reviews seemed to suggest this was necessary to get truly dry clothes. But lately I've just been using the regular dry setting and it seems perfectly fine, especially if you give the dryer some extra time in the "cool down" cycle to allow the steam to evaporate.

Overall this unit is pretty quiet and doesn't produce any smell, or even much heat. It's a very efficient washer/dryer too, with extremely low operating costs. It's ideal for people who live in apartments with no venting or limited space, and for a small family that is willing to do regular loads, it's the perfect machine.

product_title: LG 3.6 CF FRONT LOAD WASHER DRYER COMBO
review_text:
I am very disappointed in the LG machine. Besides being a maintenance nightmare, this machine takes forever to wash a load of clothes. It never really gets them dry, and anything prone to being wrinkled will come out looking horrible.

I have replaced the pump on my LG washing machine once again. The bad news is that I have had to work on this machine multiple times replacing substandard parts, hoses & pumps. The good news is that because of the repair frequency, I am getting very proficient and the pump replacement didn't take much time at all.

For what it is worth, the LG washing machine is a brilliant design but it is made up of very cheap, lightweight, parts that are prone to frequent failure. Our previous washer was a hand-me-down Maytag that ran for well over 30 years. I would never buy an appliance with the LG logo again. The new Maytag is scheduled to be delivered on Monday. :)

product_title: LG 3.6 CF FRONT LOAD WASHER DRYER COMBO
review_text:
I have been using this machine (actually the model before it) for almost six years, and I still love it! Yes, you have to remove your clothes when the cycle finishes or they end up wrinkled, but if you're not too lazy to do that... you will have super clean clothes every time ... with little or no ironing. If you do happen to miss the end of the cycle and they cool down completely, simply re-start the dryer for 30 minutes and then remove your clothes. This usually works for me.
I love the sanitary cycle - it's great for bedding, towels, and my husband extra-grungy t-shirts. They are stain free and oh so fresh!
I have replaced the water pump since I've owned the machine (last year, I believe). It was $40 to order online, and I replaced it myself. (yes, even a woman can fix a washing machine)
I highly recommend this machine if you have space concerns, or just want to save on water and electricity. One more thought - it would not work well for a young family, as there is a significant lengthening of the laundering cycle. It takes approximately 3.5 hours for a load to wash and completely dry.
I hope this was helpful!

product_title: LG 3.6 CF FRONT LOAD WASHER DRYER COMBO
review_title: Works, but takes around 7 hours for a single load
review_text:
I have this thing installed in my new construction condo and so far it's been working very well. The considerable effort I put into leveling it did a lot to keep the vibrations low. Still, my downstairs neighbor can hear it well and his ceiling shakes, but that's apartment living isn't it?

This is the ONLY solution on the market for a ventless dryer.

Washing performance is excellent.

Drying performance is acceptable, but it takes a solid 6 hours to dry a SMALL LOAD of around 8 lbs when there is a towel or two in there. I'm used to my old gas dryer blasting a 15 lb load dry in a little over an hour. This ia a major step down in laundry throughput.

I also don't know what people are talking about with 'energy efficiency' because combination washer dryers are extremely expensive to run compared to gas dryers if you pay for electricity. Here in NJ, the total cost of power is around 20 c per kWh and I expect my laundry energy costs alone to run into the hundreds of dollars per year.

As I said above, the LG combinations are the best out there when you don't have a vent, but still awful compared to gas because they are very expensive to buy and run. From the other reviews I read, they are also a maintenance nightmare (fingers crossed).

I'll be exploring creating a vent in my condo within the next year so I can install a proper gas dryer. Until then, this unit will have to do.

product_title: LG 3.6 CF FRONT LOAD WASHER DRYER COMBO
review_title: Seemed like a dream at first........
review_text:
We loved being able to put a load in before going to bed or leaving for the day - and this works really well if you only have 2 small-medium loads to do in any 24/hr day. If you are around during the day, you may be able to fit-in more loads (1 load for every 4-6 hours).

The best way to use this machine is to schedule one small-medium load for every 4-6 hrs, do not allow items to dry completely before removing them (to reduce wrinkling), and to remove one item at a time and shake the item a few times (amazing instant dry from a slightly damp). Also, use white vinegar in place of fabric softener. You might be surprised how much longer your clothes last, how less mildewy they will get, how much longer the colors will last and keeps the machine lines clean. When I follow these steps, I am fairly satisfied with my machine when it is working.

However....
We have had to do three repairs in 18 months.
Large loads will Never dry (larger loads will not dry even after over 20 hrs of dry time.
There is a trap where the lint collects and it is a messy process to clean that lint trap.

Good luck!

product_title: LG 3.6 CF FRONT LOAD WASHER DRYER COMBO
review_text:
I live in a small 550sq foot cabin with my husband and 4 dogs (yeah, we're a little nuts) - so, we are very limited on space. Our only option was to buy just a washer, or try this out. Knowing this background, here is my review

Pros
Washes very well
Easy to balance
Washes large blankets and sleeping bags without issue
Love the separate compartments for wash detergent, pre-wash detergent, softener and bleach.
Love the variety of wash cycle options - you can choose temp and spin level - the speed wash is great for a small quick load.

Cons
- Takes a very long time to dry - No complaints about this though, we knew this when we bought it. It's very dry where we live, so we hang our laundry outside most of the year and only use the dryer in the winter months. I have found that allowing the door to stand open for an hour or so after the wash cycle and then drying, helps speed up the dry process - makes it less humid in the machine.

- Gets clogged often - Here is my biggest complaint. There is no efficient way to collect the lint from the machine. The instructions tell you to wipe down the rim after washings, even doing this regularly, the machine gets clogged and fails to drain often. Granted, we do have a lot pets. Here is what I hate; when this happens, you have to drain the machine and this takes a LONG time. If you get impatient and unscrew the drain lots of water pours out. We thought we could be proactive and clean out the drain before a wash, but there is always standing water, so the only option to clear hair and lint from the drain, depending on how much water is in there, this takes between 10 minutes and 1 hour. The drain is located in the lower right hand corner of the machine, only a few inches from the ground. So you can't place a large tub under the drain hose and just let it drain, you have to use a shallow dish and empty it every few minutes. This is definitely worse in the winter when we are using the machine to wash and dry. I'd say, we probably do about 3 loads of wash a week and we have to go through this draining process at least once every two weeks.

- Makes clothes SUPER wrinkly - I'm not sure why this happens, but button up shirts and jeans come out of the dry cycle looking like accordions. Even when the clothes are promptly removed from the machine. Through the winter, when we are using the unit to dry, we have to iron our jeans before we wear them.

All-in-all it's what we need for the space we have, a stackable or separate washer and dryer are not an option in our space. However, if you have the option of a stackable unit or separate washer and dryer, go that route. I only recommend this unit if you have no other option, live in a dry climate (where laundry can easily be dried outside most of the year), and don't mind ironing. All of these downfalls are worth it to me - we live in a rural area and I hate the laundromat much more than this machine : )

product_title: LG 3.6 CF FRONT LOAD WASHER DRYER COMBO
review_title: Big Answer to a Small Problem
review_text:
For clarity's sake let me begin this review with a disclaimer: Back in the late 1950's (around 1958) Philco-Bendix introduced a washer dryer combo to the market. Both my wife and I had experience with that machine when growing up. So, we came into the purchase of this machine with an understanding of the limitations that this combination presents.

Flash forward 55 years...we are now retired and living in a condo unit in a high rise. Our unit was never wired or plumbed for a washer or dryer, does not have 220 service (it's an HOA thing), and would be impossible to vent. So, the question became: Use the laundry facilities in the basement (a non-starter with MRS.)--OR--find a solution for installing something in the condo. I discovered the LG online and read all the reviews. For us, it meets our needs very well and we are very happy with the purchase.

This unit fits into the small space we had available. It runs on 110V. It does not need a dryer vent. It is a full size front loading washer--in contrast to the "under-the-counter" tiny units available in Europe. It fit through the 27 1/2 inch doorway to our guest bathroom with a 1/4 inch to spare on either side. The machine could actually be put on wheels and rolled into and out of a closet. An accessory is available for connecting it to a sink faucet for water service and drainage rather like the older dishwashers.

Drying time can be a problem--especially if you cannot exercise the patience needed for a washer/dryer combo. It has a cool-down cycle for the dryer that helps to keep your permanent press clothes from wrinkling. Large loads need to be divided into two separate instances of drying. For a single person or a couple it is ok. I can see where a family with children would outstrip the capacity of the unit to meet the demand. In our case we just run down to the laundry facility in the basement of our building for any "hurry up" drying we need to do.

I like how the high efficiency washer uses so much less water. For clothing that is especially soiled, the machine has a pre-wash feature that adds an extra wash cycle. we have found the pre-wash cycle to be very handy.

product_title: LG 3.6 CF FRONT LOAD WASHER DRYER COMBO
review_text: Bought this used with some trepidation after reading the negative reviews on Amazon, though was curious why there were 24 five star and 24 one star reviews. I had a sneaking suspicion it wasn't so much about the product, but about expectations based on how we have washed and dried our clothes for so long. The instructions are very clear about size loads. It is an excellent washing machine with very low soap use, reduced water use, relatively quiet, great spin cycle and it sings to us when it is done. The dryer also works great on the normal dry setting and things come out dry. Some heavier items (cotton towels) feel slightly damp but dry almost immediately throwing them over a back of a chair for a moment. I'm not sure if this is because of what we are used to from a hot air type of drying verse this dehydration format. All my more high tech type of clothing loves this drying method and I would think they will last much longer. Bottom line this thing works great!!

product_title: LG 3.6 CF FRONT LOAD WASHER DRYER COMBO
review_title: not bad if you *need* an all in one
review_text:
This has been performing as advertised for almost 2 years.

In a situation where there's only room in a small condo closet for one unit, and no dryer vent, and only a regular 110v outlet, this unit is a great compromise to avoid expensive remodeling costs for electricity and venting.

Be aware, though; "as advertised" does not mean the clothes come out as dry as they do in a traditional, vented dryer. They come out dry enough, but not hot and bone dry as you're probably used to. The unit does a pretty amazing job at cleaning the clothes, though, and getting stains out. I'm very surprised at how effective it is - no compromise there at all. Loads take about 5 hours from start to finish... but that's washing and drying. You get a very cheery sing-songy beeps when it's done.

Not quite at the 2 year mark, this unit stopped responding completely. At first, I thought the breaker tripped - it was like it was getting no power. Fortunately for me, we have an appliance repairman in the family. His english-as-a-second-language diagnosis was "computer/electronics problem". He knows his stuff as far as appliances, just not english. I don't know how much this repair would have been if you had to call someone. I'm guessing a lot.

4 stars from me, though, because it was painless for me to get fixed - and it's worked flawlessly for almost 2 years now with pretty darn good performance. Impressively, it nearly rivals the performance of separate washer & dryer units - definitely worth the compromise IMO.

product_title: LG 3.6 CF FRONT LOAD WASHER DRYER COMBO
review_text: I purchased this at best buy.  Pros: if you don't have a dry vent access you have limited options.  it started out whisper quiet.  Cons:  pump repaired 3x under warranty, each time you have to sched a repair, then wait for repair date, then be home for repair man.  That's alot of time.... Right after the warranty expired, the bearings went out.  You know this is happening when the spin cycles get louder and louder.  Remember how silent it was when you purchased it?  it becomes ridiculously noisy as the bearings wear down.  As in, you cannot have a conversation or hear a television if the unit is 1 room away.  Seriously loud.  Wash dry times were long and the clothes came out damp and linty.  Keep in mind one of the functions of a dryer is to remove that lint.  There's no real way to do that with this system so as time goes by your house fills with dust because all your clothes come out covered in lint.  Shake anything dry -- cloud of lint.  That said, when we purchased we had no dryer vent so this washed clothes and saved us trips to a laundromat.  I would not buy this product again, and am very cautious buying any other LG washer dryer as I suspect the bearing failure is common to all their systems.  If you do buy, get a very very long warranty.

product_title: LG 3.6 CF FRONT LOAD WASHER DRYER COMBO
review_text:
Pros - uses 120v, washes great, almost silent operation, plenty of wash options, will wash fairly large loads of laundry, the power cord and the outlet do not get hot to the touch when running, uses way less soap and bleach than you are use to using, no problem with clothes tangling and turning into balls,

Cons - drying cycle is so slow, long long wash dry cycles, lots of maintenance on a daily and consistant basis, you can only dry half a load, clothes can get very wrinkled, heats up the area where it is in the dry cycle, clothes feel wet after the dry cycle,

Now I have not had this long enough to have the issues, problems, others have related. I guess I could wait 1 year or 5 to write a review. I have found that everything has issues after a few years. Most of the people with issues do little or no maintenance until an issue arises. I have run a number of loads in it trying different settings.

I have a vent for a dryer and wish this had the option of venting out while drying.

Pros expanded.

This washer washes clothes better than any machine I have ever used. The new laundry mat up the street with all new equipment does not wash as well as this machine.

This thing is so quite. You can sit in the same room and during most of the wash dry cycle you will not even know it is running.

I use less soap and bleach than I use to and the clothes come out much cleaner.

So many options on wash makes it great for all the different clothes. Shortest normal wash cycle I have found is about 2 hours. Longest is, that I have found so far, almost 4 hours.

This is one really nice feature. On seven of the cycles you can set it to wash and go straight to dry without you having to be there. Really saves time.

If you get your clothes out right after the cycle is done and shake them out they come out fairly wrinkle free.

I read of problems with clothes balling up or getting tangled. I have yet to have this problem even with draw strings in shorts or long sleeved shirts.

Cons expanded.

The problem is it takes forever to wash and dry a load. If you wash a full load the instructions tell you to only dry a half load at a time. And it takes forever to dry, about 2 hours.

I washed 1 towel, 2, medium heavy hand towels, and a load of ankle sports socks as a test. Less than half a load and after 3 60 minute timed cycles they were still wet, not just damp and I had to put it on high and run it for another 60 minutes before they were dry enough to take out.

I noticed the temperature on Timed, More and Normal all seem to be different. I did not take a temperature of the machine but you could feel the difference when you touched the machine. The timed modes seem to be the least hot. And on More dry cycle it get very hot, one person showed a photo with an external temp of 104*F.

If you leave clothes in after it is done washing and drying they will come out overly wrinkled, even with the 4 hour Cool Down that flips the laundry every few minutes to supposedly keep clothes from getting wrinkled.

Maintenance is excessive. You have to clean lint out of the door seal after every wash, least that is the recommendation, on a regular basis you are suppose to drain the water pump and clean the pump filter. I have yet to find a way to get the lint off the door seal easily. I think your suppose to wipe the door glass also. They recommend you store it with the door open.

Lint around the front seal is miserable to get out.

It will definitely heat up the area the dryer is stored and I would recommend some room around the machine to circulate air while it is operating.

Bottom line.

If you do not mind the long wash/dry cycles it is a nice machine. If you like really clean clothes it is great. If you like the idea of wash going straight to dry without you having to transfer from one machine to another it is great. Many a time I forgot about changing machines and the next day went oops, and had to rerun the washer to get the musty smell out.

I like it today. Would recommend it for Me and guys like me who are busy and can set it to wash and dry and walk away.

This is not my first front load or top load machine. It is better at getting clothes clean than anything I have had in the past.

It is the worst dryer I have ever had.

I would wash a heavy quilt or blanket in this machine but NO way would I try to dry it in this machine it would take a week.

OCT 17 2013

Having used this for over 2 months now I figure an update is due.

I cleaned the lint screen. It says to clean it monthly. There was no lint on it. Damn thing is probably useless at picking up lint. It is not a screen but a plastic thing with big holes in it. I drained about 2 - 3 cups of water out of the pump before i removed the screen.

This thing is great. I so enjoy setting wash and dry and then walking away.

So far, unlike some others, I have found that if you let it finish drying and then about a 20 min cool down clothes come out pretty much wrinkle free. If you leave them sit, like any dryer, they end up wrinkled and if you turn the dryer back on and run it for about 30 mins they unwrinkle a good bit.

I did sheets and no matter how I tried it they came out wrinkled like crazy.

The thing, maybe is is just me, stinks to high heaven when it runs. I thought that after about 3 loads a week for 2 months it would stop but it still stinks every time it runs.

I have not noticed any real increase in the electric bill. Maybe a few dollars but that is about it.

I must have missed the More Dry when I tested it. I put in 21 t-shirts, 6 pair of canvas shorts, 4 heavy small towels, I can not even guess how many socks and underwear and it was loaded and I mean jammed packed. Set it for More Dry, and when I got home everything was dry.

It is so convenient to set the wash, dry and leave it. If your single and like your freedom and clean clothes this is the machine for you. I swear it washes clothes cleaner than any machine I have ever owned and with less soap. It might even do well for a married couple who wash more than with a big washer, dryer set.

Dec 28 2013

Finally figured out how to clean the lint off the door seal and door.

A sponge soaking wet, squeezed just enough it does not drip, run around the seal will pull all the lint off the outer and inner seal nicely. Picks up most of the lint on first wipe and then rinse and do it again and all the lint will either collect on the sponge or end up at the bottom of the door seal. Takes about 1 min.

I found starting at the bottom and then either clock or counter clock wise gets all the lint either out or at the bottom of the door seal where you can pick it off.

Wet cloth, dry cloth, or squeezed out sponge will not do it.

Has to be saturated to just not dripping water.

product_title: LG 3.6 CF FRONT LOAD WASHER DRYER COMBO
review_title: Overal does wash & dry but involves a lot of maintenance and has a lot of issues for the price.
review_text:
So I read a lot of reviews before purchasing this and will now contribute based on my experience so far.

I did not purchase this new from Amazon but used off of Craigslist (about 1/2 the price) - supposedly it was bought in June of this year so it is only about 6 months old and still under warranty. The owner was selling it because he is a landlord who bought it for his tenant and the tenant did not like how long the cycles took.

I bought it because we have an old house and very little room - it was kind of a compromise between myself and my partner as a better option might have been for us to purchase separate compact washer & dryer but he wanted a larger capacity.

This machine is large - going from a compact portable washer to this was a big difference - make sure you have measured your space before purchasing. The combo will help us preserve vertical space but it did not help at all in floor/hall space.

So here is what I have found so far...

PROS:

* does essentially what it is supposed to do - washes with very little water and definitely dries (I have not tried to overload this and have probably only filled it between 1/3 to 2/3's so far but clothes have come out more than enough dry (on "normal" setting).

* feels fancy and fun with the lights & noise

* takes up half the space of two full-size machines

* a good amount of options for different kinds of clothes - although initially seems kind of complicated it's pretty straightforward to set up - and because it's front load will be pretty gentle on your clothes

* clothes come out dry when they're done ( no need to be there to change them from washer to dryer )

* being able to set it on timer is nice - I am not comfortable letting this be on while not at home yet but it's nice to set it to go off an hour or two before I wake up

CONS

* this is a very expensive machine and for the cost I would expect it to work MUCH better out of the box than it does - it will require regular cleaning & maintenance to keep it in top working order - much more than a regular dryer would (I will go into details below)

* it is difficult to level; or I should say - I have leveled it pretty well based on my level but it still started shimmying away when I had a larger load in - we do have the challenge of very out of whack old house floors but this machine seems to have issues when it comes to getting it leveled correctly. I found a good post here on how to deal with this (and it's on my to-do list): [...]

* I was pleasantly surprised that the first load I put in estimated less than 2 hours time (it was not a large load but based on what I'd read I was expecting worse) - however (and I have read this an issue for others) - when it got down to 6 min left on the display it stopped at 6 min for about 15-20 min before finishing and moving on; I looked this up and found others having this issue - I am not sure if it's a maintenance issue of the dryer not working well enough or a sensor issue - some LG dryer reviews said you need to wipe the sensors off but on this machine I am not sure where this is; so far what I have done to try and alleviate this issue is 1) make sure to wipe the lint out of the door seal real well (not easy - more below on this); 2) do the drain pump maintenance (pretty easy); and just to make sure I have all my bases covered I am going to go ahead and take the machine apart to clean out where the lint supposedly gets stuck - since I haven't been the original owner - I'd like to see where it's at now before I have to do it again

* lint lint and more lint: you have probably already read this is an issue. it very much is an issue. you will need to wipe the rubber door seal after each use and it is not an easy simple & quick thing to do as the seal has a deep fold in it that is not easy to get your fingers into and also lint will get stuck under the edge of the seal so you kind of have to go around and pull this up. plan on this taking a good 5 min and not being a fun task - this is an issue that really makes me have to give the machine a lower review - LG REALLY SHOULD DO SOMETHING TO TAKE CARE OF THE LINT collection because there is essentially none and, as you have probably read, it leads to a larger issue of the dryer eventually not working and requiring you to take apart the machine in order to clean it out (unless you want to hire someone) but a great instructions on how to do this are here: [...]

* the door rattle on high spin cycle - this is another big deal breaker for me in regards to giving this a good review. I have read it as being an issue with other people too - as far as i'm concerned there's no excuse for this - it is loud and annoying. I may be able to get it to be less of an issue if I can get the machine better leveled - and I have also heard of people making their own dampener by stuffing some cardboard in between the door and machine - either way - not cool LG. basically there is not proper padding between the door and it has wiggle room (when shut you can kind of push on it yourself and hear how it will sound if it happened multiple times).

* another note on noise: as others have wrote - the pump is noisy. nothing to say except that yes, it is, and it will go on and off throughout the whole cycle; think of it as a loud humidifier or old loud fridge motor noise; when the pump is not going off it's very quiet; our bedroom is upstairs and the noise will not be loud enough to wake us up - and if you have well insulated walls it may not be an issue for you either - but don't go into it thinking that this thing is going to be quiet if you have thin walls or floors

* smell: it smells a bit moldy/musty; I am just running Tub Clean for the first time today - will update later to let you know if the smell is alleviated - I am going to assume that the previous owner may not have done this at all.

* other random issues which I can live with: the instructions say to hold the spinsense button down for 3 seconds to activate - this is not working for me ( I read somewhere that it won't work if you have the dryer set to cycle on - I will try again and see if that solves it ); when I went to use the Spin/Dry cycle the timer showed it as going to take 5+ hours even though I put in a very small load and there was no way it should have taken that long - for some reason the machine didn't run it's own sensor but just automatically goes to 5 hours - you can solve this by choosing the timed dry instead "normal" or "more"

Overall I would NOT recommend purchasing this machine at full price. There are too many maintenance and glitchy issues to spend this kind of money. But, if you can find it on sale or used - it might be what you need to deal with space issues. Just make sure you understand that you will have to spend time to maintain it correctly and yes, the overall cycle times on a full load are going to be much longer than they would be on a normal washer/dryer. There is a big learning curve on the tiny things you run into that won't really be covered in the manual and for which you'll have to consult other reviews, internet search, etc to solve on your own. If you're the kind of person who doesn't mind doing this - then this machine may work out for you. But if you're looking for a low-maintenance machine that you won't need to worry about - this isn't it.

review_title: Garbage - great idea, bad engineering, won't last
review_text:
First, let me say that initially I loved this machine beyond reason. Single mom in NYC - it made life SO much easier. Hooking it up was a little more difficult than I'd initially anticipated as I had to figure out how to split the hot and cold lines under my sink, but once I did it was easy. The machine worked great for the first year or two. Yes, it takes a long time to dry and doesn't dry clothes in quite the way a traditional dryer does, but I expected that and it doesn't bother me. The lint issue is a little irritating, but I wipe the rubber gasket down with a bleach wipe after every cycle which gets the lint out and prevents mildew buildup. A little inconvenient, but also something I expected to have to do when I bought the machine.

After about 2 years the problems began. First the rear part of the drain hose suddenly busted open, spraying water into my downstairs neighbors apartment. We put a new, sturdier temp hose on that part and it held fine. Then a couple months later the part of the drain hose near the pump randomly busted open, also causing flooding. Since the machine was out of warranty, of course, I took it apart and replaced the entire drain hose assembly myself. The hose is really thin and brittle and I am surprised the LG engineering team didn't choose something that would last. I did not abuse this hose and there is no reason it should have failed after only a couple years of use. I would have gladly paid 10 dollars more for a better hose that would have lasted.

Now, a couple months later the pump is going bad and the machine is not draining. I will again attempt to repair it myself, but I should not have to. I've taken very good care of this machine, regularly clean lint from the drum/gasket as well as the coin trap at the bottom. Apparently the pumps are notoriously bad on these. Why LG didn't choose a sturdier design I don't know.

The basic idea of this machine is wonderful, and, again, I was smitten with it for the first couple years I had it, but don't expect it to last more than a couple years without having to do major repairs. I am in NYC, a place where these are pretty popular, yet there are only one, maybe two, LG technicians in the area (none of which have good reviews on yelp), so don't expect having an easy time finding someone to do repair for you.

product_title: LG 3.6 CF FRONT LOAD WASHER DRYER COMBO
review_title: Already at 4 service calls in less than 2 years
review_text:
I would absolutely not buy this W/D combo again, nor recommend it to anyone else. I certainly would not purchase it with anything less than a 4-5 year extended warranty.

We bought this unit after our stackable W/D unit broke and we bought this to replace it and save some space because our laundry room is very small and a stackable makes it difficult to access our furnace and water heater. A W/D combo unit sounded really cool at the time and would help us both save space as well as have the convenience of wash+dry without moving the load.

2 years later, we have now been through 4 service calls - the first occurring within 3 days of receiving the unit to replace the motherboard because it wasn't drying clothes properly, 8 months later because it wasn't draining properly (the pump had died), another 4 months later because the drain hose had a leak (possibly caused by the previous pump replacement), and now again after less than 2 years it appears the replacement pump has now died and makes no sound whatsoever when the drain cycle comes on. My parents had the same washer and dryer for at least 25-30 years at their previous house with little to no problems with the units. They certainly do not make them like they used to.

Thankfully, unlike some other reviews we've read, we purchased it from Home Depot and have a 4 year extended warranty covered through them (not LG) which has made getting repairs very simple after the 1 year manufacturer warranty expired. We are hoping they will reimburse the unit entirely and take it back so that we can get a different stackable unit from a different manufacturer. Furthermore, I would venture to guess that the pump is, probably, a common part on LG front-load washers, so I have no plans on buying any LG washer again. Since they come in pairs, I have no plans on purchasing a dryer either.

Pros:
* You can wash and dry in one unit. Being able to put a load in at night, have it start at 4AM and be done and dry by 8AM is really nice.
* Convenient if you absolutely do not have the space for a stackable W/D from a respectable manufacturer.
* 115V electrical with no venting makes it really, really easy to install.

Cons:
* It's expensive. The single combo unit by itself costs nearly the same amount as a similar 'quality' separate W/D stackable or side-by-side units. (By 'quality', I mean apparent quality by appearance and cost which in no way reflects the real build quality of the unit)
* 1 year warranty. LG clearly does not put any faith behind the quality of their appliances.
* As other reviewers have stated, it allows lint to build up in the pump and ruin the pump. This is a major design flaw. Based on our own and other reviewers' experiences, you can expect to replace the pump every 1-2 years minimum. We have a family of four and also were using cloth diapers for a majority of the duration we have owned it. It appears that with heavy usage the pump life is only 6-12 months.
* If you do not have a separate dryer, it takes a very long time to wash and dry a load, and furthermore when drying you can only fill it half way which means the volume of clothes it can take is half of what a separate large volume washer/dryer stackable could handle in one load, and when considering the extremely long drying time, it gives a separate washer/dryer side-by-side or stackable units a substantial advantage in capacity/time.
* Does not keep up with high volumes of laundry unless you are running it every day. For a family of 4, it is _very_ difficult to catch up if we let our laundry schedule slide for more than a couple days and nearly impossible to keep up when we were additionally using cloth diapers for one child on top of our normal laundry.
* Dries clothes inconsistently. Over the course of owning the unit, we have found when using the automatic "Normal" or "More Dry" settings for drying, that it has cycled back and forth between clothes being slightly moist when they come out (not wet, but not quite dry enough to fold and put away without hanging on a line for 4-8 hours) to very dry and hot to the touch for similar types of loads and volumes. For best results we have found that removing the clothes immediately from the dryer once the cycle completes guarantees the best results, but over time the drying time and effectiveness may vary.

BOTTOM LINE:
I would be fairly happy with this unit if it weren't for the continual service calls. Some of the other issues such as long dry times, smaller load sizes for wash+dry cycles and slightly damp clothes was a known issue before we purchased it (when we were a family of only 3). We had also purchased it planning to eventually add a separate stackable dryer on top. However, because it has been so unreliable I simply cannot recommend it to anyone except in the instance where there may not be hookups for a normal dryer and/or space to install stackable or side-by-side washer/dryer units. In the end, I wish we had just repaired our existing, less-than-stellar stackable unit rather than buy this piece of garbage.

product_title: LG 3.6 CF FRONT LOAD WASHER DRYER COMBO
review_text:
It takes a while to get used to this machine. However, I think it is worth the time to figure it out. It is excellent in the washing department. There are controls for extra water and rinse, both of which I use all the time. There is a quick wash which is under a half hour even with extra rinse. The finagling comes with the drier. There is damp (good for ironing) normal, more dry and the timed cycles. What you must allow for is the cooling down which is about two hours. Things feel damp when they come out, but some things just need a good shake and a few minutes in the air and they will be fine. Everything comes out lovely soft and you will only need a fabric softener if you experience static cling and then just a tiny amount.

But the cleaning is a bit of a pain. Our machine is down away from everything else and I must remember to bring a wet paper towel whenever it is time to unload. You can use a cloth, but then you have to wash a cloth filled with heavy lint. It is better to use the wet paper towel and then just throw it away. If you open without the cool down, be ready for a face full of steam. Take the time to give the gasket around the door a good wipe down. Get into all the folds and a pair of tweezers are good for that last bit that sticks at the bottom. Our machine is on a pedestal and I am so glad for it. It makes the clothing exchange very easy, and the gasket cleaning easier.

Then there is cleaning the filter. Have a bucket or something tall and pull out the little hose, position it in the bucket and take a walk, or a nap or have lunch. It takes the machine a half hour to drain and you do not want to mess with the filter until it has stopped dripping. Have a damp cloth on hand to give you some leverage with the screw that holds the filter. Without the pedestal, I'd be flat on the floor try to do this operation. With the pedestal, I'm just doubled over. Not fun, but we bought this so there would be no more transferal of heavy wet clothes into the dryer and from that aspect it is wonderful.

It is such a different breed of appliance it will take a while to become comfortable with it. It is best when you have stuff that does not need hanging up the second it is done. Picture putting dirty clothes in the washer before bed and pulling out dry things ready for folding before breakfast. Oh, it is HOT!! I would not suggest having this in your kitchen if your summers are hot, it will drive you out of the house. Ours is set apart and we can close off our kitchen so this won't be a problem. But think carefully about where you will place the monster. It is BIG and very heavy and needs at least two big men to set it into place, especially with the pedestal.

The problem is I really want a maid and this isn't even close. sigh. Once the learning stage is past I may like it better.

product_title: LG 3.6 CF FRONT LOAD WASHER DRYER COMBO
review_text:
I bought this washer/dryer elsewhere for the free shipping, and got a 3 year extended warranty on it (commercial), because we use it in my wife's nail salon to wash the towels used on the customer's hands & feet. LG's regular 1 year warranty does not cover commercial use, although we only wash towels in it - about 4-5 loads a week. Does a decent job washing & drying but it does indeed take about 5 hours to wash & dry.

However we have had 4 repairs in 2 years, with the machine out of service for as much as a month while waiting on the commercial repairmen to come out and diagnose the problem, order parts, then return and fix it. And the warranty does not cover hoses and other normal wear & tear items. Now the door gasket is torn (not covered) and the machine leaks water (could also be a broken hose under the machine again). I have never seen a machine where the internal hoses & pipes appear to break for no reason. Either LG uses a poor design or really cheap plastic, or both.

I also have an LG TROMM washing machine at home, and it too has had problems. The major item was a poorly-designed door gasket that left water puddled under the flap, so huge mildew/mold problems and horrible smell. Also had the infamous "tE" error code (faulty thermistor). So I read up on repairing it online, and ordered a gasket and thermistor and replaced them myself. Took about 3 hours, mainly struggling to get the wire band & spring that holds the gasket to the drum, back in place without the special tool LG says is required. The new gasket has a drain opening at the bottom, under the flap, so no more standing water & resultant mold problems. How come LG didn't think of this originally, and issue a recall on their washing machine? Obviously they didn't want to impact their profits..

I won't be buying any more LG products.

review_title: This is a good machine, but you need to understand its limitations
review_text:
I feel like all these people complaining have purchased this machine without understanding the trade-offs of a single washer-dryer machine, so to set the record straight:

1. re: mold; I have owned this machine for 3 years now and I have never had a problem. The trick is to keep the washing machine door and drawer OPEN when the machine is not in use. This way the inside of the machine dries completely. You also need to run the tub-clean feature once a month with a washing machine cleaner or just plain water/bleach. All of these are described in the user manual and if people just took time to read it then they wouldn't have a problem.

2. re: wrinkles and drying. This is simple, DO NOT OVERLOAD THE MACHINE. Again, this is stated in the manual. If your clothes are coming out damp, wrinkled, and taking too long to dry then you are overloading, plain and simple. If I am washing dress shirts and pants, I set the machine to perm-press and only load half of the capacity of the machine; for normal clothes I will put two-thirds full but that's it. I don't think this is a big deal; I don't wait for the weekend to do a big pile of laundry, I just do several small batches throughout the week. For bulky items like comforters, you may need to pause the machine mid-drying cycle and rearrange so that your comforter will dry evenly.

3. re: lint. The machine does not have a lint trap, so after each wash-dry cycle you need to take a damp paper towel and wipe the inside of the machine, particularly the rubber seal on the door. This is also why it is important to run the tub-clean cycle regularly. I have also needed to take a pair of tweezers and pull out lint from the soap dispenser (the orange thing where the soap comes out). I only needed to do this twice in the 3-year period that I have owned the machine, so again no big deal, you just need to observe your wash cycle if it looks like soap isn't coming out.

This machine has served me well and if I ever need to, I will happily buy another LG washer-dryer combo.
