review_title: If you're open to better laundry then read!
review_text: Guys listen...this is a great washer dryer and it will make you live with virtually NO laundry ever - here's the trick so many people don't realize. You put your clothes in - yes it takes three hours on average to wash and dry but you hit: DELAY START and keep adding a one hour delay until you do the math for when you're ready to fold your laundry. For example: I put my clothes in the washer/dryer and set it all up..I hit delay start six times (delaying my clothes to START washing in six hours) and when I get home from work, if timed perfectly...I walk into a house where the dryer's finish chime is just going off - viola! I put down my bags and then fold my perfectly dried clothes and never had to wait. I do the same thing while I sleep. I start a load that will delay, allowing me to wake up a 6am to MORE clean clothes that I fold and put away before work. So I never have to wait the three hours and live in a house with empty laundry baskets, it's really quite amazing. I will say it makes you look at laundry differently for example - there can be zero emergencies as in "I NEED THIS WASHED AND DRIED RIGHT NOW!!!" but the alternative for that is you just buy a few backups so you can avoid that. Also it's changed me completely from being someone who only tackles laundry on the weekend. I have weekends freed from laundry because I do a load every other day and fold when I wake up or when I get home from work. The last thing I'd like to address are the people staying it doesn't dry your clothes. Guys - it's a steam dry. When you put your hand in to pull them out you're NOT going to feel clothes to see if they're dry they JUST ARE DRY. The feel damp but they're not they're just literally still sitting in a little steam to keep them from wrinkling. When you pull them out an begin to fold you realize whoa they're now dry and it's only been like 10 seconds - it's a different feeling, yes, but one you can easily get over. The thing is - with every dryer your entire life you've had to think for your dryer. You've had to help it understand if the clothes are dry or not. This dryer doesn't ask you to think whatsoever. I believe this is b/c when the cycle starts it weighs your clothes and then calculates how long this particular weight needs in order to dry. You'll see there's no load size button - because it weighs it allowing things to be so incredibly accurate I'm surprised they even still make washers with that button. In my opinion, once you get used to completely revamping your laundry routine you'll be a happier person with this unit. It's just such a time saver you have no idea.

review_title: Great refrigerator at a GREAT price.
review_text:
Purchased for $1,439.98 as a still in-box close out as this model is discontinued. I have read many reviews that have noted a few complaints other have made, that I can observe but fail to see what the issue(s) is/are. It has been said that the ice/water dispenser is "too small" and not lighted. I don't find this to be an issue. Also it has TWO humidity controlled drawers, rather LARGE drawers, the documentation calls them VEGETABLE drawers. We use one for vegetables and one for cheeses and meats.

The funniest complaint I've read is that the ice cubes cause liquids to be splashed out. FUNNY, first of all that's OBVIOUS, second it WARNS in the documentation that this is probable.

I find this refrigerator attractive, pretty big, convenient and generally well designed. I'd buy another.

Double lower freezer drawers are REALLY nice... It means you don't need to bend over to look at the bottom shelves of the REFRIGERATOR. WE look in the refrigerator A LOT more then the freezer, and the double drawer freezer allows the least likely to be needed items to be stored in the lower drawer.

Completely silent, except for occasional ice maker noise when the cubes drop. There is a button to put the ice maker in hyper-ice mode (my words) and it seems to really produce.

If they still made this model it would be a bargain at the $2,000.00 Plus price listed here... I'd certainly check out the replacement model.

*NOTE* in the long run it's going to be hard for this product to beat the 26 year old GE that still worked when it was removed, BUT I have high hopes.

review_text:

product_title: Haier 13-Pound Combo Washer Dryer
review_title: Great if you know how to use it
review_text:
This is not your typical American washer or dryer.
You can definitely get your clothes clean enough in 30 minutes, but drying will take a bit of time.
The drying should take you about two hours. For me, as I only wash for myself and my husband, that's fine. If you've got the space for a separate washer and dryer, then that is what you should get. IF NOT...here are some tips to get the most out of your Haier combo...
1) Do the quick wash, 30 minutes...longer washes don't do much else.
2) Run an extra 9 minute spin cycle, that'll help dry your clothes out even more before the actual drying cycle.
3) Dry for the full 2 hours.
4) Take out as soon as it's done, as the humidity inside the unit will only make your clothes wet again if you leave them in there for hours.
5) If something feels damp, flail it around like a crazy person, odds are it's heat/humidity that's making it feel wet. If that doesn't go away, hang it up/lay it out for 10-15 minutes, it'll be dry.

Don't hate this unit because it isn't what you're used to. You're getting a combo unit because you need one, not because it's the cheapest option......because it isn't.
Learn to use it.
If you use this unit properly, you won't hate it as much as the other reviewers do.

review_text:

It basically has thin polystyrene strips at each corner, and the sides are protected only by a fairly thin cardboard. I was not surprised to see it damaged after opening the box, thankfully my damage was at the rear. As this is for my workshop I will not be retiring the unit and will live with the appearance of it.

This unit does not have a light. I was surprised by this.

It is about as noisy as the older refrigerator it replaced.

The ice cube tray is very small.

Whilst it states "it accommodates 2-liter and tall bottles" , it should be noted the bottle shelf in the door will actually overhang the door considerably, and the bottle is held in place with a special rack provided with the fridge. When the door is closed, half the bottle will be in the door area and half in the main fridge.

For less than one fifty bucks and shipped free in two days, it was better value than paying one eighty to get my old one fixed.

It is noisy (louder than full size refrigerator in my kitchen) and noticeably louder than the unit that it is replacing (Haier Aficianado Series 4.4cu ft approx. 2006 vintage).  Compared to prior unit - Haier has definitely cheapened up the product over the years.  Finish on exterior, lack of door lock, no interior light, and wire retainers for compartments on door.

Can't comment on longevity (yet), but everything else is great.

I personally don't have any use for the gallon-jug storage in the door (I bought it for an office environment) but I can see that as a selling point for those who'd buy it for a small apartment.

review_title: Solid product but could have improvements
review_text:
This product is a quality product overall. It is quiet, cold, and essentially provides all the benefits of a mini-fridge that you would expect. I got the 4.0 cubic size in order to make sure I can hold everything I needed. However, the general set up of the interior of the fridge is not setup well.

The fridge has a soda can rack on the door which is basically just a waste of space if you do not keep soda or beer cans in your fridge. It takes a good amount of space on the door that could be used for other items.

Also, the bottom of the main part of the fridge allows for barely any room to fit a larger item like a gallon of milk.

Lastly, the bottom shelve on the door has a bar that is held in by two holes on either side of the door, however, the bar provided barely spans the width of the fridge and falls out frequently. I had to duct tape the bar to the sides of the door just to ensure it would stop falling off.

All in all, this fridge is average-quality. It would be greatly improved by a redesign of the interior spaces in order for users to fit items that they want, not what the company thinks you may have. The can rack is simply a novelty add on that is unnecessary and wasteful of space.

It was horrible.  I called the authorized repairman out to check it.  He told me that it would cost me over 1100.00 to fix this unit.  AT that time, I paid 1200.00 for this machine.  I called Whirlpool to see what they could do.  They told me that it was out of warranty (by l mo) and that it was my problem.  They didn't even offer to sell me a new machine at a discount rate.  So, basically in 2 yrs and 2 mos, I had 2 of these machines and they both broke.  I was extremely upset with Whirlpool's response and that they didn't care about the customer.  I will NEVER buy another Whirlpool prod again.  If you choose to purchase this unit, make sure you get the 5 yr warranty.  guarrantee, you will use it.  I don't want anyone else to get scammed like I did.

product_title: Whirlpool Duet: WFW9470WW 27'' Front-Load Washer with 4.5 cu. ft. Capacity, 12 Wash Cycles, 4 Temperatue Settings, 1,300 RPM Spin Speed and Internal Water Heater: White
review_text: I have owned two Whirlpool top load washers in the past--one lasted 15 years, the other 12 years.  When it was time to remodel my home three years ago, I purchased the Whirlpool Duet. Last week, the spin cycle started roaring.  I called Whirlpool Customer Service and arranged for a $129. service call. "Bad rear bearing" was the diagnosis--an $1180. dollar repair. That is correct--the repair estimate was MORE than the price of a new washer. Thunderstruck, I called Customer Service, demanded a supervisor and was told, "You should have purchased an extended warranty." "After 27 years experience with what I thought was an excellent product," I asked, "why would I waste money on an extended warranty?"  DO NOT EVEN CONSIDER BUYING THIS PRODUCT. Despite a couple of poor reviews on Amazon, I'm replacing it with a Speed Queen. Overall, Speed Queen boasts the best warranty and customer satisfaction I've found in two days of researching top load washing machines.

product_title: Whirlpool Duet: WFW9470WW 27'' Front-Load Washer with 4.5 cu. ft. Capacity, 12 Wash Cycles, 4 Temperatue Settings, 1,300 RPM Spin Speed and Internal Water Heater: White
review_text: I bought this machine new on sale at Pacific Sales in October.  In the first week, on the spin cycle, it made so much noise the dogs ran under the bed. It seemed wrong to me so we called the certified repairman. He said it was fine. Last week it began making sounds like a bulldozer running over coke cans at a volume that would wake the dead. Then it started to smell like it was burning. When we opened the door shreded plastic from somewhere in the machine had fallen into the wash.  All the cloths smelled like they had been in a fire. Before buying this machine I owned a Maytag that took a family of six through almost 15 years of 2 to 4 loads a day without incident. I agree with all of the other reviews.  This machine is seriously defective. Oh, bye-the-way, Whirlpool has agreed to fix it but it will take 3 to 4 week for the parts to arrive. How nice.

product_title: Samsung RF266AEPN 26 cu. ft. French Door Refrigerator: Stainless Platinum
review_text: This will have been the 3rd one of this model fridge. The first one, they had to replace the main board and ended up getting a new one as it took out some capacitor on the compressor. Second one was DOA. This one, same thing in under 3years the main board went out. We just had that repaired, and now it's doing nothing but humming, I don't feel ANY air coming out of the fans, and the temp is remaining the same even with the power cool/power freeze options on.

product_title: Samsung RF266AEPN 26 cu. ft. French Door Refrigerator: Stainless Platinum
review_text: Bought this model in sept. 2011. After warranty expired, fan compartment iced over several times. After out of pocket and bad customer service, finally fixed. Today fridge stopped working completely. Again, bad customer service from Samsung. First rep barely spoke English, and just said, I'll get a call back. After no call, I called back and got someone who scheduled me next day, only to have the Mexican repair guy, who I could barely understand, tell me he's too busy to get to me, and I'll have to wait 4 days. On top of that, I also noticed, the water fill that located inside the fridge, created major rust rot behind the freezer seal. Too much money to pay for this piece of crap. Will steer clear of Samsung anything in the future.

product_title: Samsung RF266AEPN 26 cu. ft. French Door Refrigerator: Stainless Platinum
review_text: I bought this refrigerator new in Dec 2010. I did a lot of research before I bought it and I absolutely love it. It has been an awesome appliance - it's huge inside but "normal" dimensions outside, and works great. I like the water dispenser inside - it doesn't take up valuable door space. This is the first one I've had with the freezer on the bottom and I really like it - this model has an assisted closing sort of thing on the freezer door. So you don't have to physically push the door hard - which can be difficult when it's full of food. It's easy to clean too - even the silver finish is really nice. It doesn't show fingerprints, is easy to wipe off, and is magnetic!

product_title: Samsung RF266AEPN 26 cu. ft. French Door Refrigerator: Stainless Platinum
review_text: I did not buy this particular model of Samsung from Amazon but wanted to post to warn others about this model and brand.  Paid almost $2K for this in May of 2010.  Had a number of small issues with it right from the start but nothing dramatic.  When it was 5 years and 10 months old the freezer stopped working.  After having 2 services techs look at it (one dispatched by Samsung) it was determined there was an issue with the Freon cooling system of the fridge.  They said it was a leak.  Since refridgeator cooling systems are sealed there is no way to know how long it had been leaking but it must have been a very slow leak.  It would cost $350 for the parts and at least $500 of labor to repair.  Even the tech said it was not worth doing.  Calling Samsung and pointed out this leak had to have occurred over a long period of time and their cooling warranty ended at 5 years I felt they had some obligation for defective cooling unit.  They would NOT help and I got billed for the service call.  Did I just get a bad unit?  I don't know but I'm not buying Samsung again.

product_title: Samsung RB215ACPN 20.0 Cu. Ft. Stainless Platinum Bottom Freezer Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_text: Do not buy a Samsung refrigerator.  I bought one and it only lasted 3 years before the temperature gauge broke.  Had to pay for service and parts out of my own pocket because the warranty is only 1 year.  Buy from another company.

product_title: Samsung DMT300RFS 24" Stainless Steel Built-In Full Console Dishwasher - Energy Star
review_text: Classy look with controls on front not top. Child Lock out and simple controls make it easy to run.  May not dry dishes as fast machines but be sure to use a rinse aid. the manufacturer says this will help. My dishes are sparkling clean and well rinsed, even crusted ones.  Machine performs as advertised.  A big plus is the adjustable top rack which is easy to change accommodating a large pot or pitcher on bottom rack or tall stem ware on top. It is a VERY quiet machine.  Many great features for the price.  Price varies enormously, but watch out for other websites that offer a much lower price, but shipping/handling or in store delivery charge will make a hugh difference EVEN if you pick it up.  Installation is straightforward. IF YOU DO THE INSTALLATION YOURSELF:  Follow the installation manual! Samsung does not provide an essential fitting (an elbow) required to attach the washer to water source and they do not provide a hose clamp for the DRAIN HOSE.  Both of these parts are readily available and the size may depend on your particular installation.  NO strain relief device is available for running the power cord into the washers electrical box hook-up.  You may need to consider  purchasing one of those as well.

product_title: Samsung DMT300RFS 24" Stainless Steel Built-In Full Console Dishwasher - Energy Star
review_title: Control panel decals disappear within 3 months -- Big HASSLE
review_text:
I will not buy this appliance again. In a month, the decals for the control panel started to rub off from the stainless steel. So, we have to feel our way in order to start the dishwasher! What a hassle! And after one year, still cannot find replacement decals, not even from LOWES where we bought this item.

Kitchen Aid is a better more reliable brand. Don't buy this samsung.

product_title: Samsung DMT300RFS 24" Stainless Steel Built-In Full Console Dishwasher - Energy Star
review_text: We purchased our Samsung DMT300RFS after reading good reviews.  Our Samsung leaves film and food particles on our dishes.  We have tried difference detergents, rinse agents, plate and glass arrangements with no success.  Our salesman told us the dishwasher actually washed better when dirty and focused on the power of a built-in garbage disposer.  The wash cycle is long, even on the quick cycle.  If you want to use the Pots and Pans setting, plan of having the dishwasher run for 3-5 hours.  Our dishes never come out dry.  If you bump into the machine you will accidentally turn it on.  I HATE this dishwasher.  We had our Samsung inspected by a factory service technician.  He said the dishwasher would perform better if we used a powdered detergent, rinse agent, to run the sink water until hot and then turn on the dishwasher, to clean monthly with vinegar and defiantly, with this model rinse dishes.  We did all of the above and still have dirty, filmy dishes.  We have always been happy with our Kenmore dishwasher, regret giving Samsung a chance.

product_title: Samsung DMT300RFS 24" Stainless Steel Built-In Full Console Dishwasher - Energy Star
review_text:
I live in Boquete Panama with good water. I purchased this dishwasher locally at internet prices to replace a Frigidare PLD2850RDC0 whose main board had quit suddenly despite being on a whole house surge protector. This Samsung was relatively easy to install because I had plumbing parts from the Frigidare that I could use. I only had to buy a plug to fit the receptacle in that the Frigidare was hardwired. The old dishwasher would quit if a power outage (common occurence in my area) and would have to be restarted from the beginning. It was also noisy but cleaned well. The Samsung is very quiet, and if a power disruption occurs, it starts where it left off. It cleans dishes well as is but I will try and get some rinse aid if I can find it. Here in Panama electric dish washer soap is sometimes hard to find, so it will be a chore to find the rinse aid. I am very satisfied with this dishwasher. We will see how it stands up during the years. Unfortunately the Frigidare model was discontinued so I could not write a bad review on it to warn purchasers.

UPDATE: I went back to the states the end of October, and when I got back to Panama the dishwasher would not completely fill up and shut down. It took 1 and a half months to get it fixed by a Samsung authorized repairer who had to travel 40 miles to inspect it, order parts from the states, and then replace the parts. They replaced a motherboard and a water sensor. It works fine now. Cost me nothing but inconvenience. Most retailer sell their products here in Panama with a one month warranty. It is up to the manufacturer to provide warranty thereafter. The guy who came up to Boquete was the owner of the service country and very competent. I had a appliance repair license in California so I know. Sometimes warranty and quality of repair are far more important than price. I gave the Samsung dishwasher a five star rating originally, but give it a three star because it failed. I have rental units in Los Osos California and only buy cheap dishwashers because they get destroyed by the tenants. It usually costs more than a new dishwasher to get them fixed.

I would not install any electronically controlled (chip ) appliance without a whole house surge protector.

UPDATE: 1/18/13. I returned from visiting the states for 2 1/2 months. Dishwasher was not used while I was gone. SAME PROBLEM ALL OVER AGAIN! I now rate this item as a POS. Do not buy!!!
I don't care how good a dishwasher looks or how quiet it works, I expect it to work and last.

product_title: Samsung DMT300RFS 24" Stainless Steel Built-In Full Console Dishwasher - Energy Star
review_text:

I am hearing impaired, so being quiet wasn't even on my 'must have' features list. The dishwasher does not load easily. That feature was on my list. The dishes are not clean. I have changed detergents, rinse-aid products. I also pre-heat the water in the sink before starting the dishwasher. I have had it checked out. Bottom line, this appliance is not a dishwasher. If it was, it would wash dishes. And I spent $509.86 for this Samsung 'dishwasher'. :( I would not recommend purchasing this appliance.

product_title: Samsung DMT300RFS 24" Stainless Steel Built-In Full Console Dishwasher - Energy Star
review_text: I bought this dishwasher along with refrigerator and stove from best buy. I've only had it a little over a year. The panel lights have been out on my refrigerator for months now. product_title: Samsung DMT300RFS 24" Stainless Steel Built-In Full Console Dishwasher - Energy Star
review_text:
I have had this "dish washer" a few years and have been most disappointed. It does not clean dishes. I have accepted that its only use is to sanitize already clean dishes. Last week a spring must have broken the door. Now, if you don't hold onto the heavy door until it is completely open it will flop open with a house shaking thud.

I have tried every sort of detergent and rinse aid. If the dishes even have one tiny spec of food on them they will not come clean. I've had the technicians check it out and they insist nothing's wrong. Well...some thing is wrong when your dishwasher does not wash dishes.

I agree, too, with the previous reviewers who commented on the fact that you can accidently turn this dishwasher on just by slightly brushing up against it. I have a house full of teenagers and everyone is paranoid about standing in the corner of the kitchen with the dishwasher because we're afraid we might accidently start it without noticing (it's quiet). Also, these same teenagers live in fear of Mom finding even a spec of food on a dish that's been loaded in the dishwasher awaiting "washing". They know that all dishes need to be scrubbed completely free of food residue before being loaded "or else"...

Something with this picture isn't right.... Save yourself and your family a lot of stress and get a real dishwasher. I will give this "dishwasher" one star for its sleek good looks. I am willing to give credit where it's due. However, I will never buy this brand again.

review_text: I hate this dishwasher! My builders grade 10 year old whirlpool was far better. First, it is horribly designed. Fitting cups in the top rack is a nightmare. My last dishwasher never smelled. Lastly, it does not drain well. I often have to press the button to drain it again after the cycle is done. This is a more recent issue. product_title: Samsung DMT300RFS 24" Stainless Steel Built-In Full Console Dishwasher - Energy Star
review_title: Worst Dishwasher I Have Ever Used
review_text:
Dishes always have film and food specs, regardless of the brand or type of detergent, rinse aids, vinegar rinses, vinegar in the tub, additives (washing soda, Lemi-shine, Borax) ... nothing helps.
My first problem with it was there wasn't enough water circulating. The repairman told me that was not possible, because there was a built in sensor that would tell me if there wasn't enough water. I asked, "What do you have that tells me the sensor is broken?" I had already done a test with an upright cup in the top rack to prove there wasn't enough water even to fill that cup.
That repairman replaced the sensor, and at least I was getting water then, but there still were filmy dishes and food specks. I took apart the bottom of the dishwasher and cleaned the gunk out of it that had collected but that was only minimally better. product_title: Samsung RS261MDBP 26.0 Cu. Ft. Black Side-By-Side Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_text:
Although Samsung has a reputation for fine product designs, this refrigerator is not one of them. I have had this model for a few years now. The defrost issue with the freezer causing ice to form around the fan is the biggest problem, but there is a list of things to consider. Before I get into them, let me just say that I have had no problem with the physical use components of the design. The shelves and drawers are fine. Here is what is not good though:

- The LED interior lighting was intentionally placed in the back of the unit to make the more expensive models where there are more LED's and in better places more attractive. Once the refrigerator is loaded with food, most of the light is blocked and the interior is too dark.

- The water and ice dispenser requires excessive force to engage the switch. Once the ice dispenser is engaged, ice comes out quite rapidly. On occasion, ice does not drop down and the chute fills with ice cubes. This is annoying. It is also not uncommon for a couple of ice cubes to hang up in the chute. They drop out onto the floor several minutes later when they start to melt and work free.

_ If the refrigerator is run in energy saver mode, ice builds up around the freezer fan in less than a week and makes a noisy growl as the fan rubs against it. I believe that it defaults to this mode when plugged in.

- Freezer and refrigerator controls are on the main use panel on the front. I have kids. They have friends. It seems that someone is frequently changing the temperature settings in the refrigerator or freezer. Worst of all is when someone turns on the energy saver mode. That is sure to cause icing.

- In normal operation, the freezer eventually ices up and needs to be defrosted. This is very frustrating. To get at the fan and thaw the ice, everything has to come out and the back panel inside the freezer must be removed.

In summary then, this Samsung model has several design flaws that added up to an unpleasant experience for me. Since others are reporting the same problems, I just can't recommend it at this time.

review_title: Had for 1.5 years and its a great unit!
review_text: I have had mine for 1.5 years and it has worked flawlessly... Like one reviewer stated here,  initially when I got mine the product temp (ie a glass of water) was a bit high around 40 in fridge....I measured it carefully....as it turns out the installer didnt set the bar for the freezer at 5 bars (which can affect initial cooling of refrigerator as it is not a dual compressor design). The normal setting as buried in the manual is 5 bars for freezer and 4 bars for fridge....once that was set and left alone for a couple days temps started getting nice and cold. Subsequent power loss and cooling was much faster so I would guess a break-in period of 24 hours was needed...and makes sense, the manual does state it takes at least that for initial setup.  The freezer is powerful and amazing at the 5 bar setting....sub zero, with trips as low as -15F (air temp) and then of course you have your normal defrost cycles that increase that temp for a short period as high as 20+ degrees....so you have to log the temp over time to better understand the cycles when looking at the freezer temps. My refrigerator can go near 32 air temp but hovers around 36 or so...(it didnt at first). Also note that the fridge and freezer must be loaded a bit to add mass to the system.... air temp and product temps are not going to be equal...I measured water with a wireless probe inside the refrigerator part to simulate product temp.. and of course I wanted to know what the air temp was doing as well... Its been great, I make ice cream alot and I wanted a good freezer, got it and more. I accidentally left my freezer door ajar and didnt hear the alarm (my only suggestion for improvement is a louder and constant alarm) and it partially defrosted some food...closing the door and hitting power freeze mode took care of that blunder and saved the day. Hope this helps...

product_title: Samsung WF210ANW 3.5 cu. Ft. High Efficiency Front-Load Washer - White
review_text:
Purchased this locally, but sharing this review in case it is useful to anyone else. Even when I don't buy item on Amazon, I always appreciate the information that others share as I try to make purchase decisions.

This unit replaces a 12-y.o Whirlpool top-loader, which had some mechanical difficulties that made for loud operation. Right up front, the sound level is an amazing improvement.

Design: Attractive, clean lines, clear display. I like the front-load configuration, with some qualifiers. First, without the separate pedestal, you need to lean down, squat, or kneel to see deeply into the drum. Not bad, but a change from top-loader. Second, as dallas7 already noted, the access panel to clean the filter is near the floor, so without the pedestal, there will not be a lot of space for a pan under the drain hose. I don't find those things upsetting, and at some point may consider adding the optional pedestal, because I think the storage would help to organize my laundry room.

The door hinge is on the left side as you face the unit, and cannot be changed. This is likely to be best if your laundry room has washer on left and dryer on right. When I pull laundry out of top-loader, entangled pieces may fall back into tub. With front-loader, entangled items are more likely to drape toward the floor. Putting a laundry basket beneath the door would be practical to keep clean clothing off the floor (on any front-loader, I suspect). When I open the door after a wash load, a few drops of water fall from the door. Not a problem for us, but noting in case it matters to someone.

Operation: The washer senses load size. There are cycles for permanent press, heavy duty, normal, rinse & spin, quick wash, and delicate. As you turn the dial to select among these, lights show you what wash/rinse temp, spin speed, and soil level will apply for each. You can customize these options, and can save a custom configuration as "my cycle." You cannot set load size, which is a change from old machine. There's a child lock, implemented by pressing a two-button combination, and also a pause function to allow the door to be opened part way through the cycle. There is a digital display of time remaining in the cycle.

Performance: I've run 3 loads. I like the machine. I obviously can't comment on whether it will last 20 years, but I can tell you how it operated for me. First load, 12 pairs of adult jeans and a single-thickness sweat shirt, run on heavy duty. When machine was started, it displayed 1:30 run time. After it finished sensing, it upgraded the run time to 2:07. I'd read reviews that indicated that front-loaders use less water, and one reviewer complained that the machine did not fully soak the laundry. This was not my experience at all. I watched for awhile (yes, pulled up a seat and watched the dirty clothing go 'round). Clothing was thoroughly wet and pieces mixed while they cycled. As noted, operation was very quiet and there was no observable vibration. It ran very nicely.

Reviews on another site noted the improved spin efficiency, with less water left in laundry. This seemed to be true. Clothing was not drippy. More notably, I placed the load in the same dryer I've been using. Today, the seams and waistbands were not still cool or damp when the dryer buzzed. They dried completely, and the only change was the washer. I did not time the dryer cycle, but I run on moisture sensing, rather than timed, so it may also have run a shorter cycle.

Ran the second load on "normal." I think it started with a 58 minute run time predicted and it did not increase after the sensing cycle. The third load, towels, started with a 1:30 heavy duty cycle time and also did not increase. It appears that the machine noted the heavy load of jeans and adjusted, but otherwise ran default times.

Maintenance: I am pleased that the filter is accessible. That was not the case on old machine, and I think it is a good idea. I understand that I should run a "clean" cycle with a cleaner/freshener about once a month. Cleaning and odor seem to be a concern with front-loaders. I'm hoping that preventive maintenance will keep this from being a problem. Also considering leaving door open to dry for a few hours after last cycle.

I'm pleased so far. I paid a good bit less than the listed price here (search on "samsung wf210" for comparisons). Found a sale at one place that was ship-to-store, but was able to get price match at a local place that had in stock, with free next-day delivery, hook-up, and haul away of old unit. For the amount of the difference, I'd definitely recommend checking that option.

Hope that is some help. I really appreciate all the product information I have collected from this community over the years, thanks!

review_text:
Since I first bought my Samsung washing machine, it hasn't worked properly. It gets unbalanced, stops mid-cycle and locks the door about every 10 loads. Which may not sound like a big deal, except you have to get on your hands and knees and drain the tub manually with a bucket to get the electronic door to unlock, so you can adjust the clothes and run another rinse & spin cycle. Some single loads of laundry have required 4 or more rinse cycles before the cycle will complete successfully. Their repair services has been unable to fix the problem, after multiple visits. Their call center gives me the run-around, asking me to flip my switch on my breaker box 1000 times, even though, after 7+ calls to them, we have safely ruled out electricity as the problem. This purchase was a complete disaster.

UPDATE - After 15 months, when I paid myself for yet another visit from the repair man, the washing machine stopped in mid-cycle while the repair man was standing right there. He said "That never happens!" and I said "#$%#%#$^^%^$^#%$#%, it has been happening for 15 months!!!!" He said the only thing that would make the washer stop in mid-cycle, intermittently, with no mechanical symptoms, is a bad computer. The computer was crashing. He talked to Samsung and I talked to Samsung and they agreed to extend my warranty to cover the repair, since the problem existed from the first day I bought the machine, it just took them 15 months to figure out what it was. It has been repaired and now it works great. The repair man said that the trouble shooting flows they work with are all mechanical in nature, looking for a broken part, and that is why no one was able to match my situation to a flow that they knew how to fix. I think Samsung should update their flows to include the flow for a bad computer, since the computer is a pretty big part of what makes the machine work. I added a star, since my machine works now and they did extend the warranty. I don't know if I would buy from them again, though.

product_title: Samsung WF210ANW 3.5 cu. Ft. High Efficiency Front-Load Washer - White
review_title: Cleans well but "warm" water setting delivers cold water
review_text:
I've only had my washer for two months, so I can't comment on the reliability of the product. But I'd like to caution anyone thinking about purchasing the Samsung WF210 that when you select the "warm" water cycle, it doesn't use warm water; it uses cold water.

I checked my hose connections -- nothing wrong there; when I select "cold" I get a cold wash, and when I select "hot" I get a hot wash (well, kinda hot). Prior to turning on the washer, I also run the water in the sink next to the washer until it gets hot. I have the water in my water heater, which is also next to the washer, set at 145 degrees (ripping hot), so I know that's not the problem. But whenever I check the water temperature of a wash for which I've selected "warm," it's always cold. So now, if I want an actual warm water wash, I have to add hot water to the tub during the cycle.

I've since read other sites where others have noticed this problem, and one said that Samsung intentionally set the hot water usage low in order receive an energy star rating. Whether there is any truth to this, I cannot say.

To those who have given this product such high ratings, I'd be curious to know if you have checked to see whether it actually uses warm water when you select the warm water cycle. I have to take a star off, because I thought I was paying for a washer that gave me a "hot," "warm," and "cold" option.

Another problem that I had was with the bleach dispenser. I put a diluted mixture of bleach into the dispenser and washed a load of colored towels. I know that you're not supposed to use chlorine bleach on towels, but I like the clean smell and don't mind them being slightly faded. What I DO mind is spots! With my previous top-loader, I'd add the bleach to the tub and let it start to agitate before adding the towels, but you can't do that with a front loader. I thought that it would dilute the bleach even further before adding it to the wash, but I was sadly wrong. So now, a brand new set of towels is spotted. My solution is to add the bleach to a gallon of water and add that to the wash during the cycle.

Other than these two problems, I think that this is a good washer. My clothes come out pretty clean and they don't get beat up or tangled. But for the steps that I have to go through in order to get a warm wash or to use bleach, perhaps I should have stuck with my old-fashion top loader!

I hope this helps you.

UPDATE 8/30/2012
I contacted Samsung and explained the problem regarding the warm water setting. They were very helpful and actually arranged for a replacement washer. A technician came out and installed the new machine. Unfortunately, the new machine does the same thing; when I select "warm," the water still comes out cold.

product_title: Samsung WF210ANW 3.5 cu. Ft. High Efficiency Front-Load Washer - White

product_title: Samsung WF210ANW 3.5 cu. Ft. High Efficiency Front-Load Washer - White
review_title: I wish I had my old washer back
review_text:
We purchased this washer with a matching dryer to replace my broken-beyond-repair dryer, hoping that the washer would be a serious upgrade over my old washer. If I had to do it over, I would have kept the old washer, even though it used more water. The only positive I can offer with enthusiasm is that is does apparently use less water. It does appear to clean the laundry as well as my old washer. The negatives include 1)A large amount of water that has to be dried by hand after every final use for the day. The rubber gaskets all have to be wiped down, and there are several "layers" that must be dried in order to prevent mildew. 2) The washer and dryer both play an incredibly annoying electronic tune every time the doors are opened. I cannot find a way to disconnect that, and find I actually feel annoyed every time I do laundry. One has to push the off button in order to make it stop, which in the grand scheme of things is a small annoyance, but one that gets very tiresome after a full day of laundry. 3) I have to disconnect the hoses at least once a week in order to clean out the filters, which means moving the washer, shutting off the water, using a wrench to get the hoses off and then using the wrench again to retighten the hoses once the filters are cleaned. We do have well water, which may make this worse, but the man at Samsung I spoke with said he normally has to clean the filters on his identical machine at least once a month. I had to change the filters on my old washer only about once every 6 months or so. 4) The bleach dispenser did not distribute the bleach evenly, ruining several items of clothing.

For this being "high efficiency," I am disappointed that there is so much maintenance involved. I wish I had my old washer back, which required virtually none. I'm unconvinced that adding all the bells, whistles, and electronics is actually progress. I was told when we purchased this locally that this model could handle a king-sized comforter, but I have found that the load size is actually much smaller than that which my old washer did with ease. That error may be attributed to the salesman, rather than to Samsung. So even though each load may require the use of less water, the load size requires that I do more loads.

I would investigate thoroughly before purchasing an "he" washer and be sure you have the time and inclination to do a lot of regular maintenance. This particular machine had good reviews at the time of our purchase. (If you are accustomed to playing large amounts of video games that play the same tune over and over, you probably will not be annoyed by the electronic music, but I'm an old person and apparently getting grumpy.)

product_title: Samsung WF210ANW 3.5 cu. Ft. High Efficiency Front-Load Washer - White
review_text:

After spending several days researching washer brands it seemed that Samsung got the best reviews and had fewer mold complaints than other brands that I would have thought of first for major appliances. Anyway, after 2.5 years of use in Michigan climate, sitting in a basement (walkout basement), with no air conditioning my WF210 washer has had zero mold problems.

I do leave the door and soap tray open between washings. I use small amounts of HE powder soap, no fabric softener and once every couple months I run the machine on Hot with bleach in the bleach and softener tray. I also run it with some distilled white vinegar a couple times a year as the water is rather hard in these parts.

The machine is quiet and has very little vibration (it is stacked with dryer on top). It uses very little water but cleans well. I haven't had problems with water hammer in the pipes either - I had heard a few complaints about that with some machines ( seems like a plumbing problem not an appliance problem).

Overall the engineering inspires confidence. Of course my 22 year old super cheap top loader was still kicking without a service call when I replaced it - lets see if Samsung can top that.

Update May 2013 - still running well after 3 years.

product_title: Samsung WF210ANW 3.5 cu. Ft. High Efficiency Front-Load Washer - White
review_title: Faulty Washing Machine - No Samsung Support
review_text:
In the past three years, my husband and I have purchased the following Samsung products: two Galaxy S5 smart phones, three flat screen televisions, a front loading washing machine and dryer, flat top range, and microwave. For the most part, we've been happy with our purchases and have had no problems with anything but the washer (knock wood.) However, we have had a recurring problem with the front loading washer that we can't seem to get resolved. We get an error message that indicates a problem with the temperature sensor (tE.) We had the Samsung recommended service provider come out in September of 2013 to fix the problem, and they replaced the motherboard - a repair that cost us about $200. The problem seemed to be fixed until March of this year, when we got the same error. At that time, we were told that the thermister needed to be replaced, which we had done. About a month later - same problem. At that time, we were told that they had originally replaced the thermister with a "non-standard" part, and that they would be replacing it with the correct part, which they did. Now, we are getting the same error message again.

Having spent $700 on this machine (not to mention the thousands we've spent on other Samsung products,) it's infuriating to have this problem continue after having a repairman out three times to fix it. When we call the 1-800 number provided for Samsung service, we are given no indication that Samsung will pay for the additional service calls on this recurrent problem, or do anything to try to determine whether we have a faulty machine.

A quick Google search on "Samsung Complaints" yields a long list of people with various problems, most of whom sign off with "I will never again buy another Samsung product." I also note several class-action lawsuits against Samsung for problems with front-loading washers, televisions, and refrigerators. Frankly, I'm now very worried that it will only be a matter of time before one of our other purchases fails - probably shortly after the warranty runs out.

At this point, I don't know that there's much we can do, so we will pay another service technician for another service call, and cross our fingers that it works this time. And, we will hold our breath and pray that the other appliances and electronics will not give us similar problems in the near future. You should know, however, that we will be 1) telling everyone we know that Samsung does not stand by their products, and that the products themselves are not reliable, 2) contacting whatever law firms we can find who have handled class-action suits in Florida against Samsung to see if there is anything we can do and 3) discontinuing our loyalty to the Samsung brand in favor of another company that produces a more reliable product that they will back in the event of a problem.

review_text: My previous washer was a 17 y.o. Whirlpool that was still running so I was hesistant to replace. The dryer would run for hours if you did not manually stop it.  I was feeling a little superstitious (things coming in 3s and all that), so I decided to replace all three at once.  I needed something fairly compact but with a big capacity, quiet, efficient, reliable and reasonably priced.  Plus, I would only replace a working machine with an Energy star rated machine. It's fairly quiet but not as quiet as I would like.  If it were quieter, I'd give it 5 stars. The price was definitely right - around $500 with a rebate.  Time will tell how reliable it is.  I know it won't last 17 years because they just don't make machines like that anymore, but if I get 7-8 good years, I'll be pleased.

product_title: Whirlpool WTW5600XW Cabrio 3.6 Cu. Ft. White Top Load Washer - Energy Star
review_text:
I have to side with the people that love this machine for it's the best washing machine we've owned in our 35-year-old household. It does a great job on clothes, especially whites using the white cycle; they've never looked better. The accompanying dryer is just as good.

We've owned our machine 3 years, bought it new, and have never had service on it. It does 4-5 loads of laundry a week, usually on two different days, and has never failed. Since we converted from the old mechanically-driven washer whose tub was full of water to this electronic model that uses only a few gallons of water, there was a learning curve. We found you cannot overload this washer; indeed it works best with small loads. You have to follow the instructions in the accompanying booklet and do what it tells you to do. You have to leave the "eye" open at the bottom of the tank if you want the laundry to come out well.

While I can understand some of the people here than complain about breakdowns -- we also bought a Whirlpool refrigerator the same time we bought this washer and dryer and had to have it repaired once -- I cannot understand the people who say this is a piece of junk and/or doesn't work well. Our experience is exactly the opposite. This machine not only works well, it works 10 times better than any we've ever owned -- providing you use the correct detergent, fabric softerner and bleach and use the appropriate amounts and providing you adhere to the instructions Whirlpool gives in the manual.

One other thing: we did a major home improvement three years ago and switched all our major appliances to water- and electricity-saving models at the time. Primarily because of this washer, our water bill went down about 25 percent in a period where our municipality raised our rates. Our electrical bill also declined every year since we redid our appliances. We did not add a new furnace at the time (we live in Michigan where a furnace is a necessity) and in fact own a 50-year-old furnace that is about as inefficient as possible.

So here's a BIG vote of confidence for this machine that works wonderfully in our household. If you are having trouble getting laundry clean with yours, I'd recommend you read your owner's manual and follow the instructions, then try again. And DON'T OVERLOAD the thing since that could force water into the electronics inside the cylinder. This machine works best with small loads, so cut your loads in half if you are washing a lot of clothers all the time.

review_title: Stay away from Whirlpool Cabrio... didn't last 3 years
review_text: We relied on consumer reports as the primary source for a recommendation on this washer.  Just under two years old, it started making a noise, which suddenly went away.  Then one day the machine would not spin and drain, and we could not decipher the error code into anything useful. I turned the machine over to find that the drive belt was half-on/half off the pulley on the drive motor.  This caused the belt to ride against the belt guard and wear right through it.  I removed the belt and determined that the cause of the problem was that the large pulley on the drum was loose.  For some reason the nut which holds that pulley on was slightly loose, causing the pulley to wobble.  Not sure why they didn't use some loctite on that nut.  I put everything back together and tightened the nut.  No problems and I checked it a month later, everything was still good.  Fast forward to last week, when the machine was not yet 3 years old.  Same thing, washer would not spin and drain.  Tipped machine over to find that the belt had fallen off, the drum pulley was again loose.  But this time the belt had damaged the pulley on the motor.  I figured, no problem, just order a new pulley.  Well you can buy just the pulley on the drum, but the pulley on the motor is part of the motor, it cannot be ordered by itself.  The cheapest I could find the motor online was $250.  We decided to cut our loses and buy a new machine.  We will NEVER buy another whirlpool appliance (or anyone else's by the same manufacturer, i.e. maytag).  Our last kenmore washer lasted 23 years.  Oh but it had an agitator and wasn't listed as "HE" (High Efficiency), so I suppose the environmentalists would get the dry heaves thinking about the impact of that washer on the environment.  But it was useful for 23 years.  Now this "HIgh Efficiency" whirlpool is headed for the recycling pile.  Sorry, I think this hurts the environment more than an appliance which just works year after year.  Yep, they took a design that worked and now we have energy/water efficient washers that don't last very long and are so expensive to repair that the solution is to just buy a new one.

QUALITY
The build quality of this washer/dryer combo is inconsistent: On the plus side, the machine is heavy enough to stay put, and the drum feels so solid that you could wash bricks in it. Giving 10 years warranty on the motor is also a nice touch. On the other side, the entire front (including the secondary "glass" and shiny bezel around it) is made of plastic, the control panel gets hot (can't be good for the electronics), and I have observed kinks, such as a program starting in the middle maybe 1 out of 10 times, requiring an extra off/on.

THE WASHER
Front- loaders are only now making inroads in the US market, and if you believe "the internet", they are magical. I can confirm at least some of the claims in this specific incarnation: First, the washer is extremely frugal with all consumables involved: I'm down to 2 tablespoons of detergent and 1 of softener with no adverse effects; water is kept no higher than a puddle at all times, and the 1 hour cold cycle runs on a measly 0.1 kWh (or 3 cents for me). Second, the machine is easy on clothes: there are Delicate and Wool modes to give you an idea, plus I have successfully cleaned neoprene wetsuits (with special detergent), which are said to be shredded by agitators.

The major downside to the design is that the horizontal drum causes vibrations that many US homes cannot easily absorb. Consider my case, top floor of a pre-war walk- up, wood- based building: even on medium spin speed, the contents of the fridge next to the machine would rattle loudly, and I only saw some relief after I bought [[ASIN:B001JBLFWQ Sorbothane Silent Feet]]. I'm fairly content now, but I still feel the machine should have better built-in vibration reduction, especially considering that LG is the company that showed off a washer operating on 4 glasses a few years ago!

THE DRYER
The dryer is the weaker part in this package. For starters, a full cycle runs for 4 hours (on top of the 1 hour wash), which makes this machine unsuitable for big family laundry days. There is no lint filter, so you'll have to pry things out of the seal afterwards, and one low-temp cycle eats up 1.5kWh (= $0.50), somewhat negating the overall efficiency advantage. And as if all that wasn't enough, I swear I see more wrinkles than before, with my Brooks Brothers "wrinkle free" shirts now coming out in MORE need of ironing than regular shirts!

Now all that said... if you can navigate around those issues (also see TIPS below), the advantage of the combo design begine to shine: all you have to do is drop in the dirties, set the timer, go to work, and come back to a readily washed- and- dried package! I've gotten used to doing this during the week, and found that I have more clean clothes available than before at any time, therefore donated some, AND gotten rid of my large dirty- laundry container! That was an unexpected triple- win in the space department for me, and worth the trade- offs.

OPERATION
I find this machine easy enough to use, although there is room for improvement. Basically, you go from left to right: fill in the detergents, pick a cycle (cotton is the default), pick options (extra water, etc), select a dry mode, and press play. What irks me a little is that selections cross- interfere: for example, the machine may override your just-picked spin speed when you select a dry mode. Also, some drying combinations are missing: you can do time (30, 60, 120), dryness (damp, normal, extra), or "low temp", but no other permutations. For my wool pants or dive suits, a delicate wash cycle followed by 30 mins of low- temp drying would have been perfect, but nope....
One nice feature worth mentioning: you can interrupt the program at any time, change any setting or open the door, and then resume. Even with the Extra Water option selected, nothing will pour out (like I said, frugal).

NOISE
This machine is specifically marketed as quiet, an important feature when you want to sell to urbanites who perhaps plan to sneak it into their apartment (usually forbidden) . And yes, the direct- drive motor is a winner: all you get is a gentle hum at normal wash speeds. However, there are two problems (three if you count vibration, above):
- The water inlet valves open/close/open/close/etc... up to six times each time water is added, and this triggered building- wide "water hammer" events in my case. I used to think that this, too, was my building's fault, but I found that many people experience this with LG machines even in new construction. Thankfully, there is a solution to it: so- called "water hammer arresters" like [[ASIN:B000H5MQNM this Sioux model]] help out a lot.
- The pump that gets the water out is loud. That being a vague qualifier, I ended up measuring it (we've all got issues!): washing or drying registers around 60dB, but when the pump comes on, the sound level jumps to 70dB. For comparison, these numbers happen to be the range of human conversation: it's like someone speaking very softly (60 dB), then suddenly borderline shouting (70 dB). This keeps happening during the 4- hour dry cycle as well, not just the washing.

TIPS
After a couple months of use, here are a few practical tips I'd like to pass on:
- Use powder instead of liquid detergent. You'll be able to do a pre- wash this way as well as use the timer feature. The softeners is ok in liquid form and won't drip down.
- To save on electricity and ease ironing, make sure you pick the fastest spin speed possible, then shorten the dry cycle. For business shirts or synthetics, I'm getting away with as little as 30 min drying time.
- To run the dry cycle by itself: select "drain and spin" on the knob, set your dry option, then unselect the spin speed - et voilà! - you can dry your clothes some more or use [[ASIN:B0028OY2PK Dryel sheets]] this way.

RECOMMENDATION
One the one hand, this is the best appliance I've ever purchased: space- saving, efficient, and a heavenly luxury compared to the alternative which is an inconvenient and pricey "wash and fold". If you're in a similar situation, I predict you'll absolutely love this machine for what it does to your routine. On the other hand, there are some considerable flaws, mostly the noise level, slow drying, and the vibration issue. Overall, if you actually have the space for two machines, a separate washer / dryer would be the safer bet.

product_title: LG WM3455HS 24 Front Load Compact Washer/Dryer Combo , 2.7 cu. ft. Capacity - Silver

product_title: LG WM3455HS 24 Front Load Compact Washer/Dryer Combo , 2.7 cu. ft. Capacity - Silver
review_text:
I got this unit because I have space constraints in my apartment, and few other washer / dryers would fit near the plumbing lines without taking down walls or anything... If you live in an apartment where venting and space are issues I would recommend this. In a house, I don't think it would make sense over normal units.

As a washer-dryer it functions as you would expect and is really only slightly smaller than a standard sized unit. For a family, I could see the capacity being a problem, but for a couple or a single person living alone - I highly doubt you'd need more capacity than this machine provides.

-As a washer:
It has a number of different wash settings, functions as an HE washer (so use HE detergent), and does a normal sized load in about an hour.

-As a dryer:
I was concerned before I bought this as to how well this would function. It turned out much better than expected.

A key feature is that it is ventless, so no need to run an exhaust vent anywhere. It uses "condensation drying", not really sure as to the mechanics of how it is different, but I think steam builds up in the chamber where the clothes are loaded into, and the steam is slowly 'condensed' and pumped out from the drain line.

Other reviewers may have noted that the clothes come out moist, but this isn't the case at all... Upon removing clothes from the unit, a lot of residual steam is usually in the clothes chamber.

Remove the clothes, give them about 30 seconds for the steam to float away, and you'll notice they are *bone* dry... When I first used this machine, I used the standard drying settings, and noticed that my clothes came out overly dry (at risk of shrinking) because of how well the dryer worked. I've since set the machine to timed drying, and usually set it to about one hour.

The one caveat is that clothes do need to be taken out soon after the dry cycle is complete otherwise the residual steam in the chamber will slowly condense back in to water and leave the clothes a little wet. I haven't found this to be an issue, as I usually fold my clothes right after they dry anyway.

I load the machine with one full set of clothes (filling the chamber fully without compressing any clothes), no less and no more. I find it works well. Towels or jeans to dry and I might load it a little less.

For a complete cycle (washing and drying), I've found it to take just a little over 2 hours.

I don't know about the durability of this machine yet, as I've only had it for 6 months or so - but from what I understand, it's very important to clean out the pump filter (small hatch on the lower front corner) every month or so, and brush lint off the front door of the machine, as there is no lint filter. Without this maintenance, the lint will build up inside the pump or motor and cause a whole lot of issues - this seemed to be the cause of 90% of the repair issues from other reviewers I've seen on the web.

I bought the extended warranty just in case (I usually don't buy 'em), just cause this is a combo unit, and it does seem a little sensor / electronics heavy.

The only cons I've really experienced are as follows, and some of them can be mitigated:

1) I would recommended using water hammer arrestors, as the inlet valves turn on and off very abruptly when first starting cycles. In buildings with older piping, I could imagine this could (but not necessarily) be loud, and / or cause damage to the supply lines. Not really an issue with the water hammer arrestors installed - I haven't noticed any sounds / vibrations on the hookup lines.

2) Unless this unit is *perfectly* balanced, it will vibrate a lot, and make a lot of noise during the spin cycle. When it's not in the spin cycles, it sounds like a normal machine. When I ran the first spin cycle, it sounded like a low speed jet engine... I since leveled it as best as I could, got anti-vibration pads for the feet, and put in anti-noise / vibration foam around the sides which has dampened the sound somewhat... without taking these steps, I'm sure my neighbors would be complaining... even so it still is a little loud.

During the dry cycle, the drain pump is also a little loud, but that might be because I run my drain line to my tub while in use, and the pump may have to work a bit harder to get the water out.

If this machine ran quietly with the same functionality, I'd give it 5 stars. Without my custom mods, I'd probably give it 3/3.5 stars, because I could see neighbors complaining about the noise.

All-in-all though, the convenience of doing my laundry in my apartment trumps the hassle of setup. I'd recommend this machine to apartment dwellers.

_______________________

3 year update - had this for about 3 years. After each wash, I usually just do a quick wipe for lint which takes about 5 seconds. I checked the pump filter after 2 years for lint (had completely forgotten about it), and found absolutely no lint in the filter - meaning even just a basic check every now and then for lint will suffice.

I've had no problems with this machine whatsoever, and would definitely recommend for apartment dwellers.

product_title: LG WM3455HS 24 Front Load Compact Washer/Dryer Combo , 2.7 cu. ft. Capacity - Silver
review_title: Great Machine with a Few Flaws
review_text:
We have had this unit about 21 months at this point. Overall, it has been a champ. For 2 people & a dog, it is a great size and it cleans clothes really well. It wouldn't be the first option if we had room for full size laundry machines, but for a size-strapped city condo, it is a perfect fit. It takes about 3.5 hours from start to finish and clothes come out ridiculously hot and dry. So hot I have to give them a minute to cool down before removal. It dries them well (albeit slowly), but if clothes are not removed immediately, the wrinkling sets in. And boy, the wrinkles can be bad unless clothes are hung/flattened as soon as they are finished.

Aside from the wrinkles, this machine is great for day to day use. Really, it does a good job.

And for the bad:

-No timer. One would think a machine this pricey would come with a timer. Oh well.

-Water hammer. Just awful. It sounded like someone was shooting up our laundry room. It was so loud we bought the water hammer arrestors to help. And they do help, but that was an additional cost that should not be required.

-Flood-safe washer hoses are a bust. We had to go back and buy regular hoses. Hope they don't leak or fail!

-In the 21 months that we have owned the machine, we have had to call a repairman to clean out an internal duct 2 times. It seems lint collects in the bowls of the machine and this lint can not be removed without taking the machine apart. So, $100 a pop for those cleanings. I understand that lint has to go somewhere, but you think they could make that area user-accessible so we could do it ourselves. And additionally, it seems that it has backed up again, so I'll be calling the service guy again. That will be 3 times in 21 months it needs to be taken apart. Essentially, when this happens the dry sensor malfunctions and the machine thinks it is finished after the spin cycle (when the clothes are still sopping wet). Remove a fist full of backed-up lint and it runs like new again. Sigh.

product_title: LG WM3455HS 24 Front Load Compact Washer/Dryer Combo , 2.7 cu. ft. Capacity - Silver
review_title: Perfect for the space deprived student
review_text:
So I got this bad boy yesterday and was experimenting with it all day since I was off! I read all the reviews both on the LG site and here and was a little scared at first, mainly because of complaints of clothes coming out wet. There were a lot of people complaining about wash and dry times too but that didn't bother me. My mom has a washer and dryer that are older than me (25) and when I go over to do laundry it's at least 4 hours just to dry my clothes!
My apartment is super small and has more of a laundry closet without any venting so I had to get this one, I don't think the 27" would fit!)
Anywho I was a little scared with this machine as it's way more fancy and high tech than I am used to for a washer and dryer. It is super easy to use! The instructions made it sound a lot harder than it is! You just go left to right do detergent, pick a wash cycle, picck a dry cycle and then push play. It does require a little bit of common sense here like don't over fill the drum! This thing can wash a full load but can only dry half, says so right in the manual, I do a 3/4 load with no problems. Also for those who are afraid of the dreadded 4 hours: don't be. First off that's 4 hours you can be studying, working, going to the movies or something without the whole "OMG I left my clothes in the washer now I gotta wash them again before I put them in the dryer!" I also TRIED to get a 4 hour time and couldn't. The longest load took a little over 3 hours and that was 6 pairs of jeans. One reviewer on here recommends to not do the sense clean or whatever and just do the timed thing. product_title: LG WM3455HS 24 Front Load Compact Washer/Dryer Combo , 2.7 cu. ft. Capacity - Silver
review_title: Wrinkles, wrinkles and more wrinkles.  (Did I mention wrinkles?)
review_text:
Wrinkles badly! I'm a guy, and generally don't care much about a few wrinkles. But we find this machine unacceptable. I really wanted to like this machine, too- thought it would be perfect for our needs.

We bought this combo unit (actually the white one) to put in our dental office to wash our poly/cotton smocks. We've washed them at home for the last 15 years and never had a wrinkling problem, even washing 16-20 at a time. (My home washer is 3.1 cu. ft. capacity, so not much bigger than this machine, but to be fair our dryer has a much bigger capacity.) The washer part of this LG unit works great. But no matter how we set up the dryer, our smocks wrinkled unacceptably. We tried every setting there is. We tried drying 3 smocks at a time. We tried adding a small towel to the smocks. We tried with and without fabric softener. We washed on permanent press and tried lower spin speeds. We tried pulling the smocks out and shaking them before drying. We tried stopping the machine as soon as it said "CD". We tried letting them go until it beeped after 4 hours. Of course some of the settings and methods caused less wrinkling than others, but all of them were worse than hang drying. And even hang drying them leaves more wrinkles than my unsophisticated male taste would like.

I called LG- they sent a service person out who told me that the unit is working fine and the wrinkling is what you get with condensation drying in a relatively small drum. AC won't take the unit back or exchange it since it is not "defective". LG won't take it back. We're stuck with a very expensive washing machine. Bottom line is- if you don't mind really wrinkled clothes, or if you don't mind ironing, then this is a good little space saving unit, especially if you don't have a dryer vent. But if you want clothes that aren't so wrinkled that even a guy would notice, then look elsewhere. (BTW- if you want just a washer, LG makes the same unit without the dryer for $600 less. I would recommend that if you need a washer and have space issues.)

product_title: LG WM3455HS 24 Front Load Compact Washer/Dryer Combo , 2.7 cu. ft. Capacity - Silver
review_title: Great for 1 or 2 person space limited household.
review_text:
I have owned two other washer/dryer combos, a Splendide and a Bendix, so I knew the limitations of these machines, especially the dryer component before I bought it. Of the combo washer/dryers, in my opinion the LG is the champion. The fact that it uses 110volt and requires no outside venting means that you can put just about anywhere there's water and a drain. And, it can do laundry in much less time if the clothes are lightly soiled.

For wash and wear shirts and pants I use the Speed Wash setting and always use the fastest spin dry setting, then dry clothes to "damp dry", take them out and let them air dry on hangers to prevent wrinkling, and this takes about an hour. Only towels and thick cotton items do I allow to completely dry which can take up to an hour to dry.

If I had my choice I would buy a LG washer and a separate dryer, but I don't have the space.

product_title: LG WM3455HS 24 Front Load Compact Washer/Dryer Combo , 2.7 cu. ft. Capacity - Silver
review_text: I live in a RV, and I had grown really tired of laundry stacking up till my day off...then having to spend the day doing laundry....so I decided to try this LG machine.. product_title: LG WM3455HS 24 Front Load Compact Washer/Dryer Combo , 2.7 cu. ft. Capacity - Silver
review_title: Perfect for me, but with quirks
review_text:
Single guy who mostly washes gym clothes and towels. This ventless combo unit is perfect for me, once I got used to it's quirks.

Amazingly compact. Simple hookup - took me longer to get it out of the box than to actually hook up.

The biggest drawback is that drying takes forever. If you use the dryer mode, be prepared for a load of laundry to take 4-5 hours, and it will be very wrinkled. This is *not* a flaw in the unit, but a limitation of ventless dryers in general.

But, just buy yourself a $20 drying rack, and use the wash-only mode. Your laundry will be done in a fraction the time, will end up less wrinkled, and you'll save tons of cash on electricity. When you need to dry something, it can do it.

The unit is highly programmable, and can handle most things. But, wash smaller loads ... they actually go faster. Somehow the unit knows how much you stuff in it. If you overload it, it just takes forever, and the clothes are embarassingly wrinkled. Don't try to wash rugs in here. I've done a comforter though (without drying).

Wipe out the lint after every load. It builds up in the drum, because there is no venting.

One day I smelled a slight burning smell. Since it was under warranty, I called LG. They sent someone over THAT SAME AFTERNOON! He ran a diagnostic and figured that nothing was amiss with the mechanism. He ran a 10 minute wash with no clothes (in the washer - he kept his own clothes on) which loosened a big ball of lint. It turns out, the link can build up on the drum and cause the burning smell if you run the dryer mode. So ... wipe out the lint after every load.

product_title: LG WM3455HS 24 Front Load Compact Washer/Dryer Combo , 2.7 cu. ft. Capacity - Silver
review_text:
I purchased the LG WM3455HS in June 2012. After nearly a year, I can say that I am truly pleased with this product. We are a family of 4 (baby in cloth diapers/husband has uniforms) which makes having this machine a challenge - but definitely not impossible.

Pros:
* Space Saver! We needed extra room for the baby and getting this allowed us to free up a ton of space.
* Washes great. Love all of the wash options. Even the diapers come clean.
* Energy efficient. We noticed a savings of about $10/month on our water bill.
* I can set the machine before bed and it is washed a dried when I wake up. Makes me feel like I've accomplished
something.
* Built very well. With 4 family members, our machine runs ALOT. Typically, I do 4 loads a day. The machine is a work
horse!
* I no longer have skunky smelling towels, piles of dirty clothes, piles of clean but unfolded clothes. Since it takes
so long to do a load, I no longer let laundry build up. EVER. This has actually saved us all time and hassle.
Totally makes up for the long dry times.

Cons:
* Dryer does take some time. However, we try to line dry when possible. Wrinkles are an issue only if you forget to
remove your clothes or you dry too much at once.
* Vibrates. I've had other front loaders and they all seem to vibrate. With this machine, I notice it vibrates more
when I add oddly mixed items with varying weights (a load of t-shirts and a random pair of jeans...).
* Loads washed during the winter are "smaller" then during other months due to the bulk of the materials. just keep in
mind the weight limits.

Important Notes:
* You HAVE to run the tub clean monthly!!! The lint will build up in your machine if you don't. It gets all caught up
in the blower motor and requires either a service repairman or a handy spouse. Either way, just run the tub clean. I
run ours twice a month because we use it so much.

I truly like my machine. It does take some getting used to. The first week that I had it I wanted to return it and go back to my old jumbo machines. Now that I've retrained myself to keep up on the laundry, everything is fine. Love it!

product_title: Whirlpool WTW7600XW 27 5.2 cu. Ft. Top-Load Washer -White

product_title: Whirlpool WTW7600XW 27 5.2 cu. Ft. Top-Load Washer -White
review_title: Don't spend the money - it smells and its tough on the clothes!

product_title: Whirlpool WTW7600XW 27 5.2 cu. Ft. Top-Load Washer -White
review_text:
I had done months and months of research before deciding that the 5.2 cubic feet Whirlpool Cabrio would be our next washing machine. I knew I wanted a large capacity machine for our family of eight, and I also discovered that I preferred a top loader for many, many reasons. I hesitantly decided to go with the top-load HE, and ultimately the Cabrio, despite mixed reviews online.

First of all, it is a super quiet machine! I live in a very small house with the laundry just off the kitchen, and I can never even tell if it is on or not without looking. It holds and washes approximately three times as much as my old agitator washer did. It can literally handle at least 12 pairs of kids' play jeans with no problem. Everything comes out clean, fresh, and spun almost dry (if that is the spin speed I select). I do have to pay attention to the types of materials (denim? towels? sheets?) going into a load, the cycle I select, detergent and additives I use I truly feel the science and thought behind doing each load is totally worth it to save so much time, energy, and resources in the process!

It also works quite amazingly for my cloth diapers, even with hard water and then just as well after we added a water softener. I do a quick wash on cold with all natural, diaper-safe additive specially formulated for my hard water. Then I run a cycle with HOT water on the towels setting (because it uses the most water), a small amount of diaper detergent, and highest speed spin cycle with an extra rinse selected. Finally, I run one more quick wash cycle on cold with no detergent in place of an extra rinse. Yes, that takes a lot of time, but it uses no more water than a traditional agitator machine would in filling the basin all the way up several times. Once a month, I soak/strip all of my diapers in the "wash machine with affresh" cycle and Funk Rock soak.

I have and will continue to recommend this machine to friends, especially those with a lot of laundry to do. It has cut my time doing laundry in half or more! It also easily washes king sized comforters or a load of 15 full sized towels. It did have a slight learning curve for me to figure out what loads need liquid (oil-based stains), and what loads need powder (organic stains). I also know which loads will need a boost of oxiclean. But after reading the manual and paying attention to how my clothes look before putting them in the dryer, I have got to say that I have got a system that works for our house and everything is clean and fresh and done in half the time!
