review_title: Wake up people! What did you expect?
review_text:
People, come on. This is NOT a bad washer. First of all, the selling point of this and similar HE (High Efficiency) washers is that they use unconventional and cost-saving cleaning methods. In other words, these HE washers are nothing like what your mother or grandfather is used to. From my experience with this washer so far, it cleans clothing remarkably well considering the little water it uses. Because it's designed to use less water than normal washers, it periodically dispenses water over the spinning clothes instead of conventionally having them drenched in water. This method allows for a much lower level of water in the drum, thereby saving the operator some money. Due to the lack of an agitator, it's allowed to spin at a higher RPM than agitator-based washers without roughing up clothes. In other words, the faster spin means a bigger centrifugal force to "launch" away dirty water outwards. The spinning thing that replaces the agitator is called the "washplate", which creates a whirlpool (no pun intended) to help move clothes around and downward. In my opinion, the washplate and faster RPM makes up for the agitator to a respectable degree. However, some people may miss the ole agitator despite its roughness.

A benefit I noticed is that dyed clothing lose much less color than in conventional washers, making HE washers excellent for delicates.

A downside with HE washers is that more lint gets trapped in the folds of larger articles than with Non-HE washers, because the lint can't simply "swim away" in low water systems. DO NOT confuse this with dirt and think that your HE washer is a dud. However, a good dryer will suck that excess lint right out.

Seriously, if you're really worried about cleanliness, then play with the settings some more (ex. turn off 'ecoboost'; use 'deep clean' and 'extra rinse') or wash it again! I bet that even with two washes, this washer will still use less water and energy than a classic one.

*EDIT- USING THE "BULKY ITEMS" SETTING MAKES THE WATER LEVEL FILL ALL THE WAY TO THE TOP. THERE YOU GO. NOW THERE IS NO EXCUSE TO DISLIKE THIS WASHER.

Overall, I love this washer; it looks and cleans great and I wouldn't trade it for anything else. Remember, HE washers may look like your old washer, but they work in a very different way.

We replaced our perfect as new machine this Memorial Day weekend with an LG front loader.  This is not a good product.  The design also pools water that does not drain and causes a wretched mildew smell despite our best efforts with an extra cycle run with just bleach and leaving the lid open--hardly energy efficient to be running an extra cycle.  Don't buy this product.

product_title: Whirlpool WTW5700XW
review_text: We have WTW5700 for several months.  After reading all negative comments and knowing ourselves, we had decided to buy the model with glass lid, so we could observe the process, and see for ourselves, how the washing is done.  It does take a change of mind to accept high efficiency washers.  After studying the high efficiency washing process I have to say that it makes more sense than traditional machines.  How was washing done in old times?  By soaking clothes in water (as in traditional models, where clothes are floating in deep soapy water), or by rubbing it on the board (as high efficiency machines do)?  I cannot say that the washer is perfect, but if correct type of detergent is used, and the machine is properly loaded, the clothes come out clean.  However, if you cannot break the paradigm, and you cannot accept the process with very little water, you may be disappointed and be better off with the traditional models.

product_title: Whirlpool WTW5700XW
review_title: Yes, this HE washer is amazing technology
review_text:
I've read about as many reviews on the Cabrio line that I could, and still went ahead with buying one myself (WTW5700XW3), plus the matching Cabrio dryer. Instead of just being a cheerleader or basher...I'd like to just dive in and list some observations about what I see when I wash clothes in my Cabrio and then contrast it with what I read in all the negative reviews. You can be the judge on what you think.

First off, this Cabrio doesn't just shut off in the middle of a load. It actually pauses to let gravity drain the load for a minute or two and also does water level checks. Yes, it sounds like the washer just died; falling completely silent. Yes, your traditional washer doesn't do this. Yes, there seems to be a lot more logic in this machine making decisions for you along the way to optimize the washing process. In the end....it will continue on just fine, if you let it...

In the beginning cycle where it does the sensor stage to determine the load, you would think the sensor stage is done after a few brief spins with no water. I thought the same, but the sensor cycle is a little longer. The washer runs for a couple minutes with just a little water added, but it's STILL part of the sensing cycle (note the light hasn't changed to the wash cycle yet). The clothes are actually absorbing the first dump of water as the machine tosses them around. The washer will pause again and then add additional water after it has checked how much the clothes have absorbed. Of course, the water level will never be above the clothes like a traditional washer, since the clothes need to press against the bottom washer plate to be moved around. This is also the part that most are getting hung up on, or can't accept. If you watch closely between the clothes, you will see a level of water under the clothes. The clothes will churn out, under (into the water/detergent brine mix), and the back up the center.

The clothes actually do move throughout the washer from center to outside in a donut fashion, it's just in slow motion. If you are used to a traditional washers, where the clothes slush around gallons of water in a fairly fast pattern, then you will need to re-adjust your brain for how this HE process works......and yes.....it does work!

Now for big sheets/towels/blankets/etc.. the "bulky" setting is the one you want. It'll use much more water, but it will also allow the large items to churn in the wash cycle correctly. Using the Bulky cycle is next to worthless for regular loads, because the wash plate at the bottom will not come in contact with the clothes and move them correctly. It's tempting to set all your regular loads to Bulky to satisfy your old cravings for gallons of water sloshing around, but that is not how an HE washer works. Do that, and you will be frustrated (hence the gobs of negative reviews).

My favorite cycles are "quick wash" and "normal". Quick wash is really useful if you just have lightly soiled clothes. Let's say something like the clothes wore to an office, verses construction work. The cycle is pretty much identical to the Normal cycle, but runs about a one half hour only. The Normal cycle handles most everything else, plus whites. The washer has a whites setting, but then it burns hot water and runs a longer than normal cycle. If your whites are in hurting condition, then by all means go for the whites setting. For me, my whites are not in that much of a need for aggressive cleaning.

I have thrown just about every type of clothes at this washer (work, play, blankets, towels, sheets, etc...) and it has performed flawlessly. The clothes are clean! The water usage is low. The washer is reliable with no baby-sitting/re-balancing of the cycles required so far. Since my model of Cabrio (5700) has the glass lid, I can see the clothes churn several times down and around the drum; coming back up the center every 2-3 minutes. All clothes are cycling through the water/detergent brine several times. I have seen nothing that is left bobbing on top totally dry at the end of the cycle, like some other comments have said. Dryer time is also reduced significantly because the washer does such an excellent job on the spin cycle to remove most of the water from the clothes. The clothes come out of my dryer with no wrinkles. I can understand what folks are seeing when they take the clothes damp, to almost dry, out of the HE washer. The clothes will dry just fine in the dryer with the wrinkles gone. Again, folks with traditional washers might be used to their clothes being a lot wetter coming out of the washer; but I never found that to be a feature/benefit.

In conclusion, I don't fault the consumer as much as the companies that have designed these HE washers. They have obviously dropped the ball on educating the public about what really is going on with these machines. Just saying they use less water, and the water line will be below your clothes doesn't cut it. You make a new technology HE washer, and then the consumer sees it stop at times for minutes thinking it died, then not explaining the details of the cycles and what it's accomplishing (sensor technology? tell the consumer more about how it does this and the fill lines, the flow of the clothes, etc...), and then these companies just tell you it makes different sounds you not used to and all is fine??? ....well....to me this paradigm shift is like we're going from horse-n-buggy technology to gas powered automobile technology with these HE washers .....and the folks using them are still looking for the ropes to giddy-up.

I would highly recommend this HE washer to anyone that wants to significantly reduce their water consumption and have clean clothes. My water costs were high. This HE Cabrio washer put a significant dent in the water consumption. Now, if you can't get your head around what's going on inside these HE washers and agree with how they work, then stick with what you know. Buy a traditional washing machine that fills the bucket full of gallons of water, and be at ease with your decision. As for me, I look forward to doing laundry every time with my Cabrio, and the savings it brings.

UPDATE 1/25/2017: Well, it's been a few years and the washer is still going strong. Enjoy using it just as much as the first year. Only repair I had to make was a shift actuator module [[ASIN:B00DM8KQ2Y Whirlpool W10006355 Actuator]] that prevented it from spinning. This occurred about 3 years into having the washer. The part cost me about $30 on Amazon and replacing it only took removing a couple screws to replace it. About 10 minutes of work. Other than that one repair, it's been rock solid. Clothes still come out clean and everything functions just perfect.

UPDATE: 12/7/2018: Still going strong. Everything working great.

There does seem to be a tube that leads to a water level sensor. I've been thinking of extending the length of the tube, or widening, to get the level where I want it.

My suggestion to anyone that reads this, buy the least efficient Washing Machines, Dryers, Dishwashers and Refrigerators. Yes, your water and electric bill will be a little higher but the product will last 3X as long and actually work as you expect.

review_title: If I could give this washer a -100, I would.
review_text: This machines is without a doubt the poorest excuse for a washer I've ever experienced.  For a full load, it says it will take 74 minutes to run with hot water. That might be true if it washed efficiently without any issues.  Unfortunately, that is seldom the case.  1) the clothes, or sheets, or towels bunch up on one side of the tub which puts it out of balance thereby either stopping or freezing the cycle in whatever stage it happens to be; 2) When unbalanced, it doesn't spin fast enough to wring out the load and you open your freshly wet clothes to find out they are still full of water; 3) it doesn't get the soap out of the clothes.  When it rinses the clothes, the tub slowly spins while wetting the "washed" clothes while the tub fills up again.  Then the SHORT agitator tries to get the clothes to move for the water to effectively reach everything.  Unfortunately all that happens is the clothes stay piled on top of each other not allowing water to flow freely through all the materials.  The soap gathers on top of the water and stays there while the tub drains, leaving all the visible soap on top of the clothes. 3) I have found that it's impossible for me to wash more than 1 sheet at a time, and even then, the material twists and bunches up on itself.  Of course the tub becomes unbalanced and all the things mentioned above happen.  I always have to stop the machine between the wash and rinse cycles to untangle the item and lay it evenly and flat on the bottom of the tub.  By the time the spin cycle comes around, the same things happen.  Most times, I have to either run an extra rinse and spin cycle or an extra drain and spin cycle - or both. Sometimes it takes me between 2 and 3 hours to wash one load with this agitator, not to mention again the additional problems.  The fact that Whirlpool unleashed this sub-standard product on the public disgusts me.  Remember the good old days when you could wash an entire load in 30 minutes with a machine that has a tall agitator?  Well, that won't ever happen with this machine. DO NOT BUY THIS PRODUCT!!!!  YOU HAVE BEEN WARNED!!!

product_title: Whirlpool WTW5500XW 27 3.6 cu. Ft. Top-Load Washer - White
review_title: Worst I've ever owned. Incredibly bad. Zero stars.
review_text:
If I could give this a "0" stars, I would. It's hard to pick the most infuriating feature of this product, so here they all are:

I am all for eco-responsibility, but Whirlpool has taken this too far in order to get its "energy star" rating. The Cabrio doesn't get your clothes clean, and therefore, doesn't perform its only function.

The temperature settings are all wrong: "tap cold" --whatever that is--is cold. "Cold" is cold. "Cool" is cold, "Warm" is cold. "Hot" is hot. So either you boil your clothes or you wash everything in cold.

I find is really annoying to have a machine 'sense' how dirty my clothes are. The machine controls the water level, the temperature, and the 'oomph' of the wash and rinse cycles. With this washer you have no real control--Whirlpool has made all the choices for you. You have no choice about the rinse temperature you want, and if you want to choose another option, such as "soak" or "rinse and spin," you can only do that with cold water. You can't choose to wash your 'delicates' in 'warm' water, only in--you guessed it--cold.

The cool, sleek new profile is curved on the top, instead of flat, which means that if your dryer is next to the washer, you can't fold clothes and place them on top of the washer: they slide off. What was Whirlpool thinking? Don't buy this unless you have a separate folding table in your laundry room.

Whirlpool wants me to periodically 'clean' this thing with a product called "affresh" which is advertised prominently on the front of the washer.

Last but not least, you aren't allowed to just quickly throw one more thing into the load--a forgotten sock, for instance: you pause the thing and wait for 45 seconds while it makes up its mind to unlock itself before you're permitted to open the lid. I don't have time for this.

Cabrio has an extra rinse feature, and a 'clean boost' feature--whatever that is--and also an 'eco-boost' feature--whatever that is. None of these is explained well in the literature that comes with the product, so I believe these features are antagonists: eco-boost probably means colder water with a shorter wash-and-rinse, and less oomph in the wash and spin cycles.

I plan to unload this thing at the earliest possible opportunity--as soon as I can afford a different machine. Thank God I held onto my dryer instead of buying the companion to the washer.

A week later, a repair technician arrived, took pictures of the cook top, and left. He said there was no physical damage and that the problem was below the cooktop and should be covered under warranty.

We called back and were on hold another 45 minutes, then a Customer Service rep said after reviewing the pictures, they determined the problem was "cosmetic" and not covered under warranty. We asked for a Supervisor and were advised the customer service rep was a Supervisor. She only identified herself with first name and last initial. We asked to speak to a Manager. The Customer Service rep said that the technical group that viewed the pictures already made the decision and that they would NOT cover the warranty problem. Finally, she advised that someone from the Exec Customer Relations would be calling back within a week. While waiting for the call back, I researched this problem on the Internet and found many similar complaints of Samsung not honoring their Product Warranty.

They still refused to replace the cooktop despite the fact it is under warranty. If after one more call they still refuse to honor the warranty, we will file a complaint with the State Consumer Protection agency, and another with the Federal Trade Commission. We'll also send a letter to Consumer Reports magazine. I am VERY disappointed with Samsung Customer Service and the quality of the model FER300 glass cooktop stove.

My home has several Samsung appliances but we after this awful experience with Samsung customer service, we will NEVER buy another Samsung product. Buyer beware. Samsung customer service is absolutely not acceptable. Read the online reviews of similar issues and buy another brand as they have many complaints of NT honoring their Product Warranty.

review_title: Wonderful range for everyday cooks & bakers!
review_text: I cook everyday for a family of 5 and as I can not afford a viking gas range (my dream stove) and we were on a budget to upgrade all of our kitchen appliances, so we settled on this gem. It cooks 100% accurate, absolutely perfect and bakes evenly. Again, I cook often, and have cooked in fine dining restaurants for many years so I'm no novice. I also bake pastries and elaborate cakes (wedding cakes) as a side job/hobby and this range is PERFECT for all my recipes simple or complex! I love it, and I was pleasantly surprised by how accurate, even, and consistent it cooks. The features are simple to use, it heats up very quickly (burners and oven), and is very easy to clean. I have cooked and cleaned on 5 other glass/ceramic surface stoves, and when you get food or liquid and it cooks to the surface you will have to use a little elbow grease with any cooktop, and that's the case with any stove gas or electric. This range is by far the easiest to clean in my experience-my mother's requires a great deal of scrubbing if a tiny water drop gets on it (a 5 year old whirlpool). I read some negative reviews saying it looks dirty and has to be cleaned everyday and every time you cook,  but in my opinion you should clean your stove whenever you use it and when it gets dirty-no matter what brand, make, or model-but thats just me. It's a black surface so dust will show and I saw some negative reviews based on that, which is kind of ridiculous. I guess some people expect in 2014 a samsung range should literally do everything from picking out dinner, do the grocery shopping, and cleaning your mess and everything in between. I just want a solid & reliable product and if you take care of things they should not break. I read another complaint that the burners don't have a "simmer" selection and therefore you can't simmer cook with this range. Again people are unfortunately  stupid, it simmers beautifully between "LO" and "1"  on any burner of your choice. I guess since SIMMER wasn't actually written on the stove someone couldn't figure out how to simmer on this range, and that's stoves fault? I am a consumer that researches everything on anything that costs more than $50 and this is by far one of the best purchases I have ever made.

In the meantime, I recommend that you DO NOT BUY THIS DRYER, OR ANY OTHER FRIGIDAIRE PRODUCT! THEY ARE SCAM ARTISTS!!!

review_title: annoying in many ways, just ok at drying
review_text:
The most complimentary thing I can say about this dryer is that I don't hate it as much as I've hated 'advanced energy-efficient' appliances I've had before. My #1 complaint is, tho they may be energy saving & groovily computerized, they don't actually do what they're supposed to do very well, i.e. dry clothes (or get them clean). That said, this dryer is slightly better than the previous brand new dryer we had.

If you leave the settings at their default --and you have to re-set them every single time you do a load if you want to use any other setting (more about this in a sec)-- you get clothes so damp you either must then hang them up to finish drying (which sorta defeats the main purpose of having an actual clothes 'dryer'), or put them away & end up with closet or drawer full of mold & mildew.

So, you have to change the heat settings. Every time. Every. Single. Time. If you even pause it too long you have to re-do them all time; the cycle setting at least is a knob you turn. The default setting is medium heat, no cycle signal or "Wrinkle Shield" (which you would definitely need if you use the Med heat setting, or aren't poised to yank the clothes out the instant the dryer is done). Med heat doesn't dry anything but the smallest, flimsiest cloth. You have to punch thru "Low" & "Air Dry" to get to "High." I'm honking on about this because tho most people don't have serious pain problems with hands/wrists, it's a literal (for me) & figurative pain to have to re-punch the 'touch' setting(s). They don't set with a touch either; you have to mash them with a good bit of force.

& then there's the noise; perhaps to really show how robotically computerized & futuristic the thing is, you get an incredibly loud & annoying electronic "bee boop bop beep baboobareep!" medley of tones every time you turn the thing on, a different set of screaming electro-tones when you turn it off, & other random boopy noises at other times --& you cannot turn them off. It doesn't matter whether the cycle signal is on or off; the stupid thing has to let you (& half the neighborhood) know whenever you or it does anything. I've hunted around to try & disconnect the frigging speaker so I could do laundry when the rest of the house is sleeping, but so far no luck.

If I sound l like a dinosaurian Luddite, I am a bit of one. But I do embrace lots of up-to-date things, especially if they're good for the environment/use less energy. However, I firmly believe something that proclaims itself to be 'energy efficient' & GREEN should still do what it's designed to do without you having to use it twice, or twice as long. And that computerized things shouldn't shatter the quiet with screaming electronic tones just to prove how compu-groovy-modern they are.

review_text:
This range was in our kitchen when we purchased our home last year. The kitchen had been remodeled and the oven was brand new. I cook A LOT and it gets dangerously hot on the top of the range when using the oven - if you have young children like I do, I strongly caution you not to purchase this range. For example, if you're baking something and also using the top burners, and you've left a metal spoon on the top of the range, when you go to grab the spoon to stir what's cooking, watch out, if you forget to use a pot holder, YOU WILL BE BURNED and if you're like me you'll throw the spoon in the air after forgetting (again). On the plus side, if you need to defrost something quickly (currently defrosting frozen fruit while baking cookies), this is excellent. But, if you proof bread, don't leave it top of the range if the oven is on, IT WILL GET TOO HOT and kill your yeast!!

I called Electrolux/Frigidaire for months and had the range tested several times - it's just a low end model with poor insulation and no engineering fix to correct the excessive heat. So dangerous! And, the broiler is horrible - it's in the bottom of the range (where you typically store pots/pans), but you can't store anything in the drawer and good luck lifting hot meats from the bottom of the range (without burning the kids!!) without spilling everywhere - HORRIBLE design! Convinced yet? I just cannot say enough bad things....would NEVER purchase this model and brand again. Customer service also very disappointing - they do not take safety issues seriously or handle well at all (at their own admittance by the end of my ordeal!!).

review_title: Oven gets VERY hot on outside of range....
review_text:
I am extremely unhappy with this oven. The oven when turned on gets unbelievably hot both at the top of the range and on the front panel of the oven. I have had it melt thick Rubbermaid tupperware sitting anywhere on top of the stove, and the front panel is HOT to the touch. I was told by Frigidaire that it is normal that there is no insulation in the front door panel, and to keep children away from it. Try keeping small children away from that! This stove is dangerous!

Also, do not leave anything on or near the range while baking. The worst part is Frigidaire thinks that this is acceptable performance. I also agree that having the broiler in the bottom drawer is not good. The drawer is difficult and awkward to open and close, which is not good when trying to broil, well, anything. I hate losing the storage from that drawer as well. The oven also bakes uneven. There is a hotspot in the back left, and frequently the oven cooks faster or slower than it should. Anything you cook in this oven has to be babysat, and I keep an oven thermometer in the oven because I do not trust its temperature reading, it's been inaccurate so many times.

On the positive side, the range burners are ok. The Quick Boil burner does boil water quickly, and the grates are easy to throw in the dishwasher to clean.

review_title: RECALL REQUESTED - UNSAFE, DANGEROUS, BAD DESIGN
review_text:
Bad design, unsafe, should be recalled immediately. A poor design is one where a manufacturer takes a previously innocuous feature of almost every oven on the market, like a lower storage drawer, and turns it into a serious hazard. I recall the packaging tape saying do not use for storage. But, you know, past experience tells you that broiler pans and kitchen items are normal to put down there. Since that is what I've done with every range I've ever had or seen since childhood.

My babysitter, not knowing that the lower drawer was a A BROILER [who puts a broiler in a storage tray???] was cleaning up, put some cutting boards down there and proceeded to make tater tots in the oven. Something started to smell, we thought, oh, burn in. Well, flames started to shoot out the back and front. Not burn in ... FIRE! Luckily, our extinguisher was on hand. What should be a short story [use oven as an oven, and a bottom tray as a place for storing bulky kitchen items] became a smoke remediation nightmare in our new addition, with a babysitter and kids forever spooked about using an oven to make a snack. So, I looked up the feature online, and could not find another range on the market with a {I so want to drop F bombs here] broiler in the lower tray. Maybe they had warming trays or dual ovens, but a stupid BROILER. I'm usually very unforgiving of "user error" since it is in most circumstances, a user's stupid decision. But, this BROILER in the storage tray stumped every one I've asked. Have you ever seen one down there? No.

And, wouldn't you think they would permanently affix some label saying that the lower tray is actually a FLAMING BROILER TRAY????

I hate Frigidaire.

review_text: I had a similar model Frigidaire gas range installed new by the seller when I purchased my home two years ago. Because the oven is one year out of the (one-year) warranty period, the company would not replace the door: And the "corporate manager" I spoke to was remarkably unconcerned about the dangerous nature of this defect. If you search for "exploding oven doors," you will see that this has happened to other Frigidaire ranges in the past. As my friend put it: "Exploding oven doors should not be 'a thing.'" I will NEVER buy another Frigidaire product again.

I've now owned this refrigerator for almost 2 years. I'm not one to go out of my way to say bad things about a product, but I had to make an exception for this refrigerator since it costs so much.

Do not buy this refrigerator unless you want an ice maker that spits ice all over the place, and dies after a year. Or if you want to wake regularly to open doors and warm food because LG falled to build in doors that close on their own.

In addition to just failing to work properly, storage is horrible. Coming from a side-by-side, I feel like Im always fighting to find room in this fridge - partially because the top of the fridge is occupied by a HUGE light and water filter. One last nit, the freezer drawer regularly becomes dislodged.

It's junk. Pretty junk, but junk.

product_title: LG LFX28978ST27.6 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel French Door Refrigerator - Energy Star

product_title: LG LFX28978ST27.6 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel French Door Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_title: Beautiful, if only it was functional
review_text:
First of all, the good part: This fridge is a gorgeous piece of kitchenware. The stainless steel looks stunning next to my oak cabinets, and I've gotten quite a few compliments.

However, it's functionality does not live up to its fabulous facade.

So, here are the bad parts:

The water dispenser is separate from and placed above the ice dispenser, so that the drip tray (even if extended) will not catch any excess water sloshed about. It also confuses anyone new to the fridge and you'll end with water all over your floor. We've started keeping water in pitchers when we host parties to prevent this. Still, we inevitably end up having to hand out towels to at least one unfortunate soul.

The ice maker is horrible. The ice cubes stick together constantly, so that you have to bang on it a bit. Plus, we've already had to call and get someone to come out and put in a new ice cube tray when ours got stuck mid-rotation and started making strange grinding noises. Keep in mind, this occurred about 4 weeks after we purchased the fridge. The repairman said it was something about the way the doors close that caused all the problems with the ice cube maker. He said we wouldn't have problems if we didn't open both the doors at once. However, to access the bottom produce drawer, you have to open both doors.

The freezer holds a lot less than our old GE fridge (which was comparably much smaller in size). I'm not quite sure why.

The fridge cools unequally (more so than any other fridge I've ever owned or heard of). I've found that the upper part of the refrigerator actually gets quite warm, and anything placed there will go bad rather quickly. I'm not talking about a bit more warm, but the sort of hot-to-warm temperature that will encourage even preserved foods to sour. If I lower the temperature of the refrigerator to the point where things will keep relatively well on those upper shelves, the vegetables and fruits in the bins at the bottom of the refrigerator freeze.

The energy saver temperatures kept my ice cream melty and made my squash go bad.

The stainless steel looks great, but you can see every fingerprint. It's also horrible to clean. Windex or water will leave streaks. You have to rub them off with a microfiber towel or get a special stainless steel cleaner.

product_title: LG LFX28978ST27.6 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel French Door Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_title: My prefered brand is LG, this fridge has just one problem
review_text:
I like the way this fridge looks, and like all stainless appliances it shows streaks and finger prints, but it's worth it to me. If you are troubeled by that issue, don't by anything stainless. That isn't LGs fault, it's just a fact of the finish. I like that I can easily place a half sheet pan on any shelf and the fact that there are four separate drawers. All fridges are warmest at the top, so store less perishiable things up there.

It doesn't make huge amounts of ice, and the cubes are really small, but I don't have a large family so it isn't a problem for me. What is a problem is the way the left door closes. It is easy to have the mullion not go into it's channel, leaving the door open about an inch. It's true that it will beep after a minute or so, but if you grabbed your lunch out of the fridge on your way out the door, it will just beep all day and the fridge will be about 50 degrees on your return. Because I have never owned a french door fridge, I don't know if any other manufacturers have this problem. Could be a challenge for all of them.

I wouldn't recommend this fridge if you have children getting in and out of it for the above reason. If I had it to do over again, I'd buy this same model, even with the mullion problem. I just keep my lunch behind the right hand door now.

product_title: LG LFX28978ST27.6 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel French Door Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_text: Clearly the LG went with design style over function. product_title: LG LFX28978ST27.6 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel French Door Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_title: Great Refrigerator - Horrible Ice Make & Water Dispenser
review_text:
If I were only grading the refrigerator and freezer, this would have five stars. We seem to have much better temperature control than we had with our 6-year old side-by-side Kenmore. Our produce and deli meats seem to stay fresh longer. Our milk stays cold but does not freeze. Guess you can tell why we ditched the Kenmore!

HOWEVER, the ice maker is slow and of low capacity. Perhaps four glasses of ice water is all you'll get at one time. If you don't use the ice maker for two or three days, the ice all sticks together and the dispenser won't dispense ice at all - very annoying. Then you have to dump the ice container into the sink and start over. The water dispenser is even worse. While I appreciate the idea that this is supposed to make filling a pitcher possible, we get water on the floor all the time - even family members that use it frequently. We also have a lot of guests, and when they use the water dispenser, we see a puddle on the floor 100% of the time, until they've used it three or four times.

The ice maker and water dispenser absolutely are completely annoying - extremely poor design (water dispenser) and engineering (ice make and dispenser) - so much so that this otherwise fine product may not last as long as the Kenmore in our home. One star for the ice maker/dispenser and water dispenser gets no stars at all.

As far as noise goes - this unit is very quiet, except that it has a very low frequency, and noticable, hum. Four stars for noise.

Finally - while the water filter seems to work really well, the price of the water filter is way out of line - approximately $35. The manufacturing cost of this should be under $1 - shame on LG for their pricing! One star for the filter price.

Update: September, 2015. We have had this refrigerator for 3 years now. The mullion (the sealing spacer between the two upper French doors) spring broke. There is no standalone replacement spring for this model; they only sell the complete mullion assembly, at a cost of $46. Many similar models have a replacement spring for $5 or less. My rating for this refrigerator just went down to 1 star. This will be our last purchase of an LG refrigerator.

Update: August 2020: This refrigerator has been in our kitchen 8 years now. It is still generally working well. Found a much better supplier of water filters - REASONABLE price (1/3 the cost of a "genuine" LG) - at discountfilters dot com, and they are made in USA. The ice maker continues to be a DAILY annoyance. We use it several times each day, and 90% of the time we have to manually reach into the ice bin and mix the cubes around, so that they will dispense. Needless to say, I hate this fridge EVERY day this happens, but due to the cost of replacing it, I am putting up with it. It reminds me daily why I will never buy another LG product. The water dispense continues to put a puddle on the floor every time a guest tries to use it - doesn't LG test their products with real people? Just wanted to add this update to let folks know how much I have hated this LG product every day for 8 years.

product_title: Whirlpool WTW7300XW 27 5 cu. Ft Top-Load Washer - White
review_text:
I've had my WTW7300XW for about 3 months now.

It does a fine job of washing, with everything coming out clean. Delicates seem to be treated gently.

Wrinkling is perhaps a little more noticeable than my old washer. No matter the washer I use I always use a low spin speed for my clothes so I don't know how faster speeds affect wrinkling. From the get-go I discovered that even on the lower spin speeds, this washer does a great job of ejecting the water from the laundry, while still being gentle on delicates. So it has never occurred to me to use a high spin speed.

I also never ever use my dryer, preferring to just line-dry all my laundry and take my clothes to a laundromat for pressing.

My two peeves:

1. It often goes out of balance with loads of towels, say 3-4 towels along with a few hand towels or washcloths. I'm a single guy and I tend to wash smaller loads. I don't know how it would work with a larger load like I would expect a larger family might normally wash.

2. The stupid lock feature prevents me from adjusting my hot & cold water valves to get the water temperature in the ballpark. With my old washer I could adjust them while it was filling with water. This was necessary because with the cold open all the way, it was just way too much cold water for a warm wash. So I would need to dial it down. It it baffling that we are prevented from opening the lid when the washer is filling with water. I've never ever heard of a person being injured while a washer is filling with water. This is beyond stupid. I do close the valves after each use. I understand that this washer adjusts temperature automatically, but I don't think it can compensate for the wacky water valves I have.

I must edit this review. After more than a year with the thing I have to now say this is the worst purchase I have ever made. This washer is pure junk. Stay away.

product_title: Whirlpool WTW7300XW 27 5 cu. Ft Top-Load Washer - White
review_text:
We purchased this washer and matching dryer after our 9-year-old washer that was already bouncing all over for a couple of years had the sensor go and over-filled spilling water all over our floor (which it had ripped the vinyl previously, so water got under and had to have the floor replaced).

I read several reviews, but found it was just like when I wanted to purchase a new mattress. Nothing really got an awesome review. People either loved it or hated it, so I knew I couldn't go by reviews alone. There was a great sale on the items when we needed them, and we talked at length to the salesman. So glad we purchased them and didn't listen to the negative reviews!

It may be that the people who didn't like them are used to high efficiency washers and just want more bells and whistles. We were going from a 9-year-old machine that ruined our floor and bounced all over when it frequently became imbalanced, to this wonderful new machine. We love that it barely uses any water compared to the old machine. Love the different settings. It knows what is best for different loads and I don't have to think about it. It has a great capacity. What would've taken me two loads can now be done in one. Someone complained that it has longer wash cycles. The whites are a really long cycle, but it makes sense, since they usually need more sanitizing being your sensitive articles (underwear). I don't mind that some cycles are longer when I get the equivalent of two loads at one time.

To me, some people are just highly critical. I love these machines. They do the job well and I really don't need more bells and
whistles. Capacity is important to me, and they do a great job with that too. And another good thing that the salesman noted, they are made in the USA (I believe in Ohio). So if you do have trouble, it will be a lot easier than dealing with a manufacturer whose parts are out of the country.

product_title: Whirlpool WTW7300XW 27 5 cu. Ft Top-Load Washer - White
review_title: Not economical to repair when it fails
review_text: It is 5 years old now. Started hearing a new noise, like a scraping noise. A few days later, error code 51 appeared.  Had a tech in. He found that the single 1/4" hex bolt on the bottom of the motor assembly was loose. He tightened it. Ran a short cycle with no load. No error code. He leaves and I start a full regular colors load. 10 minutes into the cycle and error 51  appears again. The tech returns. He removes the motor rotor  that the 1/4" hex bolt holds onto the motor assembly. Magnets around the rotor have scratches. Obviously when the bolt came loose, the rotor then was wobbly. That wobbly rotor ruined the stator and motor assembly. $530 for the part! Apparently this 1/4" hex bolt is not glued on. It comes loose and destroys the motor. The tech also said this model  often has the main bearing fail. Water gets into the bearing and it rusts! I am reading reviews of the new Kenmore/Whirlpool models and am hesitant to buy another from them.

product_title: LG 25 CF French Door Refrigerator SS
review_title: Tier III Energy Star French Door refrigerator/Freezer
review_text:
We were looking for a replacement of our ten year old refrigerator which was very noisy. After researching the most energy efficient replacements, the LG LFC25776 seemed to fit our requirements, as it was rated as Tier III Energy Star. It uses exactly half the kilowatt-hours as our previous ten year old refrigerator.

Pros: The refrigerator and freezer sections are quite roomy. Aside from the high energy efficiency, the best aspect of the refrigerator section are the LED lights that are very bright, illuminating the interior. The compressor is very quiet. Compared to our last refrigerator, that banged and knocked loudly, the LG is extremely quiet. Also, the interior is a high quality with smoothly sliding bins and adjustable glass shelves. The large meat bin at the the bottom is the most useful one, even if it requires that both French doors be open to open it. The refrigerator doors have very thick foam insulation and that keeps door items cold. The temperature settings are displayed on the front of the refrigerator and the settings are accurate. There is a door alarm that goes off after about 30 seconds that is useful and necessary. The freezer section is large with two tub sections, with a nice pull out wire bin above the tubs and a smaller wire one on the door of the freezer that handles small boxes well.

Cons: There are a few aspects of the refrigerator and freezer that come up short. The main one is the spacing design of the plastic shelves on the French doors. The door bins are advertised to hold several gallon jugs, which is accurate. However, if more than a couple of gallons are stored in that door, there is no room for tall items on the remaining door bins. Plan B would be to use the main compartment glass shelves, but these are spaced with about 7", 6" and 9", from bottom to top shelf. There is no room for an upright open wine bottle, for instance. Back to Plan A, we keep those in the door bins but with four gallons of milk or water in the bins, there is no room. There are two solutions: keep fewer gallon jugs on the door bins or remove one of the interior glass shelves. We opted for the former since we are not willing to lose that much interior storage space. A better design with more adjustability for the door bins would be a big improvement. The vegetable and fruit bins are not very large or deep. Most weeks, we end up storing half our vegetables on the lowest glass shelf. Another issue is the shape of the exterior handles that dig into our hands. This is not too bad, but a more ergonomic design would be helpful. The freezer section uses a normal incandescent bulb, which seems strange given the extreme energy efficiency in the rest of the unit. Finally, the French doors require a little effort to shut. They do not swing closed but require a firm push. If you forget that push, the door stays ajar and the alarm goes off after about 30 seconds. While the alarm is loud enough, if you leave the room before the alarm goes off, it could be a problem. I'd recommend that LG come up with a phone app (they do manufacture cell phones, so it should be easy) to notify the user if the door is ajar, or if the internal temperature of the refrigerator rises past some selected limit.

review_title: Flexible design and large capacity make this a good choice
review_text:
My wife and I bought this fridge three months ago and have been very happy. Installation was seamless, and it has been working like a champ!

Pros:
+ Large: plenty of room inside for everything we need to store
+ Flexible: the shelf layout has been great. We keep one of the shelves folded up for tall items most of the time. Large door shelves also help.
+ Drawer is great! The deli drawer was never big enough in my old fridge. Plenty of room in the drawer. Also GREAT to access drawer without opening doors.
+ No full width drawers in fridge: Sounds like a negative, but actually a positive. When I go to the fridge I want to open the door with one hand and get my item with the other. With only half width drawers I can do this (not true in other french door fridges).
+ Easy to access Water & Ice: The light also turns on when you get close to the lever. On my old fridge you had to turn on the light separately (not good).

Cons:
- Love the drawer, but wish it pulled out a little further. Items in the back are covered by the upper doors. Still can get them, but no reason not to have full extension slides.
- As others have said, Ice dropping is especially noisy. Otherwise, fridge is nice and quiet.
- Like every other fridge I have owned, the water comes out with a lot of force. The small stream comes out so fast, it sprays water off the ice with close to the top. Why not put on a aerator like a faucet? Could still have good flow without the water jet.

Overall very happy with the purchase. Cannot overstate how nice the drawer is. Would not have gotten a french door style fridge without it. Also very happy it is a fridge drawer and not a freezer drawer. Don't know about you, but I get things out of the fridge a lot more than the freezer.

Be sure to check the size versus your old fridge. This unit is big! Same width and height as my old fridge, but about 2-3 inches deeper. Lucky I had room, but could see where that could be a problem it space was tight.

Three months in, so cannot comment on reliability, but hoping for the best.

review_title: 2 New Samsung Refrigerators, No Cold Food and a Wet Dog
review_text:
A little more than a month ago we bought a new Samsung RF4287HARS refrigerator. It is Samsung's top of the line model. It has many wonderful features. We love the center drawer with flex temperature control; the style, look and feel are great; the lighting inside is even better than anything else we saw. There was only one problem: It didn't work.

After a couple weeks the fridge just stopped cooling - the ice melted and drained water all over our floor, much to the chagrin of our dog who was sleeping nearby; the freezer defrosted, meaning it was steak night (with both corn and beans - hurray); the entire interior went to over 45 degrees according to our handy dandy thermometer. It just wasn't running. We had repair people come out twice, the second time they said it could not be fixed.

OK, that happens. Sears agreed to replace the unit with a brand new one. Three cheers for Sears!

The second new unit was installed and within a couple weeks we had the exact same problem. Warm soda and a wet dog - but hey, steak for dinner again. The service people came out and said it was a bad sensor. OK, that happens. So they replaced the sensor a week or so later (they had to order the parts, but the good news is that it is currently cold outside, so at least we had cold food for a while). After replacing the sensor it worked great for nearly a few days and then had the exact same problem again! By this point we have run out of frozen steak (and just about everything else), although our dog has never smelled better. But back came the repair people - this time the diagnosis is a bad mother board (although having watched several repair people work on this model it becomes increasingly clear that they do not really know what's wrong; at best, they are guessing).

We are now faced with the question of what to do next. Option 1: replace the second unit with a third new version of this model, and hope that the third time is the charm. My concern is that, as Einstein said, insanity is defined as doing the same thing over and over and expecting different results. Option 2: replace the second unit with a model from a different manufacturer. But here is a small problem - we looked at other units and found that the GE Profile models had many similar features and might make a good replacement for the Samsung version. But as we looked closer today we noticed that the one drawer GE was a little too similar to the one drawer and two drawer Samsung. If you look at them side by side you will notice that they are so similar that it appears they are actually made with identical parts. In an era where outsourced and contract manufacturing is common in many industries, this raises the concern that even the GE models would have the same problems as they may be made in the same factory with the same parts, leading to the same defects or issues.

For those of you keeping score, that is: Samsung refrigerators 2, Cold Food Zero, Steak Dinners 2, Wet Dogs 3, and spoiled food more than $300.

So in short, Samsung has included many great features in this unit. They only thing it seems to be lacking is coldness.

review_title: 4 Milk Jugs In the Side Door! Spacious, Versatile and Attractive
review_text:
My wife and I actually had a fridge that was working perfectly fine, but we just had our fourth kid in five years and suffice it to say we go through a lot of snacks and a lot of milk. With our other side-by-side fridge, we adjusted the top shelf so that it could hold milk/jugs of apple juice, but we'd have to unload the whole shelf to get what we were after, night after night!

We also found the space of our old side-by-side cramped and difficult to see, let alone retrieve items on the bottom shelf.

This fridge solves those problems and does so with style! The first thing worth mentioning is that the side door can easily hold four one-gallon milk jugs! The way Samsung uses the interior space is also impressive! There are sections that flip up vertically to accommodate our jugs of apple juice, and a separate shelf with a retractable front section to allow for, e.g., Costco-sized pickle jars.

This is accomplished not only through smart design of the shelving, but also through advanced insulation whose thinness allows for a full 28 cubic feet of interior space! Even the subtleties like the placement of the filter (which is long and slender and fits between the two shelves at the bottom to minimize its impact on space) are intentionally thought out to make it easy to fit everything you need into the fridge.

The kid's zone middle drawer is also nice, though a little tall for our three year old and under kids, and the button to adjust temperature is right in front, so kids have to be old enough to be over their fascination of pushing buttons to fully utilize the drawer.

For the bottom freezer drawer, I was a little worried that it would be hard to find our food given the big drawer nature of the unit, but I think it's actually easier to see everything than it was with our old side-by-side fridge. The space is big and open, you look straight down on everything and can see where it is at a glance with everything placed on its side, and there's an interior drawer on the top 1/4 of the space to hold items you're especially interested in finding quickly.

Again, the use of space is near perfect!

It's also attractive, with it's cool interior LED lighting, stainless steel exterior, and cool looking blue icon touch screen controls by the ice maker.

So far, I love the fridge!

One quick random tip, by the way: if you live in a dry climate, as I do, feel free to turn the "Energy Saver" mode on. All it does is prevent condensation, which you won't have a problem with if the climate is right. You may as well save the energy and little bit of money.

review_text: We bought this back in October when we moved into a new home. With the exception of a few minor flaws/problems we could not be happier. product_title: Samsung RF4287HARS Stainless Steel French Door Refrigerator with FlexZone Drawer, 28 Cubic Feet
review_text:
I bought mine about 8 months ago after my 9 year old GE Profile gave up the ghost. So far it has been great. I very much like the 4 doors and two cooling systems which are saving me on energy costs. I also like the way you can set temperatures in the middle drawer separately from the refrigerator part and the freezer. Also, the extra cooling power feature where you can press a button on the control panel and get boosted refrigerator or freezer cooling for several minutes after you have been to the supermarket and had the doors/drawers open for a while stocking the refrigerator. The LED lighting is very cool and the inside of the refrigerator is very well lit. The upper tray in the freezer being pulled part way out when I open the freezer drawer is a useful piece of engineering. The doors and drawers come off so the delivery guys can get it through a regular sized house front door and hallways to your kitchen. I compared this to a couple of other models by other makers with this general 4 door style, and I thought the quality on this one was clearly better.

Every 6 months or so many hundreds of gallons of water dispensed (I forget how many) you need to change the water filter which is located in the refrigerator part at the bottom center. I changed mine at 6 months when a warning light comes on the touch screen panel on the outside of the door. Changing the filter is about as complicated as changing a light bulb in a lamp, only easier. You twist the filter a half turn to the left and it pulls out. You take a new filter, insert it into the slot and twist it a half turn to the right. You do have to manually reset the change filter light, but that is even easier. On the touch screen, at the bottom left there is a spot that says Alarm/hold 3 sec for filter reset. You put your finger on that spot and hold it there for 3 to 4 seconds until the filter light changes from red to blue. Its not rocket science. The only tricky part is that the replacement filter part you need to buy has a slightly different number than the one that comes with the refrigerator. The original filter number is DA-2900020A while the correct replacement filter is DA-2900020B.

My only suggestions for improvements would be to make the middle drawer pull out a bit further so I don't have to reach to get to the back corners, make the sliding metal bar dividers in the middle drawer have a locking mechanism on the thingy where they cross, make it with an off white finish that will match many other kitchen appliances (I had to get the stainless steel), on the stainless steel model put stainless steel on the sides of the refrigerator instead of the dark grey paint for those of us who have refrigerators that have kitchen counter arrangements that expose part of the sides of the refrigerator, put a thin coat of magnetic material under the stainless steel so refrigerator magnets can stick to the stainless steel. These are all very minor and not worth deducting a star in my opinion, but they would make this an even more exceptional refrigerator than it already is.

review_title: Samsung Quality As Good As Competitors
review_text:
We recently purchased this Samsung model (almost 2 weeks ago) and not wanting to jinx anything (knock on wood), it is working flawlessly (right now anyway). The 2 biggest complaints I have is the intolerably loud noise the ice-maker creates when ice is ejected into the bucket. It's even more frighteningly loud when the ice bucket is empty as the sound amplifies upon impact with the hollow plastic container. I read other reviews commenting on this and thought it was an exaggeration, it's not. Samsung should really consider re-engineering the container by adding some sound deadening material around it to help muffle the noise (yes, it's truly that annoying). The other issue is relatively minor and indicative of all stainless appliances... the never ending battle against finger prints and skin oil smudges.

All that aside, the bottom line to any appliance purchase today is akin to betting on roulette and expecting to win (worst odds ever). Like many, I did an inordinate amount of product research and read countless customer reviews prior to purchasing. Opinions and experiences are all over the map. And this is a fundamental problem for all brands not just Samsung. As mentioned elsewhere there is much outsourcing going on and it seems almost impossible for manufacturers to attain consistent quality levels. BTW, I was surprised to learn (after purchasing) this refrigerator is imported from Korea. I bring this up only because it supports many customer complaints concerning long wait times when breakdowns inevitably occur. The delays are primarily the result of long distance parts delivery. Several service repair companies I contacted are not even qualified to work on these appliances as Samsung strictly controls the qualification process along with parts distribution (exporting from Korea).

To be fair, this Samsung replaces a 12-year old Maytag side by side (with ice-maker) which I can't begin to relate just how horrible and unreliable a refrigerator can be! It was the first appliance I ever bought with an extended warranty (reluctantly). It was also the first appliance I inevitably recouped my money from using that warranty (and then some) due to abnormally frequent repairs and parts replacement (both costly to the insurance company). What I learned from this is warranties can be useful for offsetting expensive service and food replacement costs but doesn't instill customer confidence or improve product reliability... it is what it is. Factor in countless hours due to lost work time; aggravation with incompetent CSR agents; delays and missed appointments with repair ppl and outrageous amounts of wasted food... you can easily see where this is going.

So don't hate Samsung just because it's not assembled in North America (who is?) or you see customer complaints online. In fact, check any brand and it's pretty much the same for all. CR may rate some models and brands higher but unfortunately (and inevitably) they all have issues. There are only a handful of companies (worldwide) making compressors and major components for refrigerators these days and every manufacturer is buying from them. So no brand is immune and "inconsistent" quality has been around for awhile now. The days of buying a refrigerator (or any major appliance) and expecting it to last for 20 years are long over. And spending more money doesn't help either. High end brands such as Viking and Sub-Zero are notoriously problematic and appear even more unreliable.

The bottom line is no matter how much research and regardless what brand you prefer or currently own... you definitely will be rolling the dice and taking a bigger chance than you might expect on your next purchase. The days of "Maytag reliability" are long gone (I can most definitely attest to that). Long term reliability is not the norm, it is an anomaly. Don't expect your next refrigerator to provide more than 7-10 years of consistent reliability (at most). Like other "tech toys" refrigerators have become trendy fashion statements, several high end models have built in flat screens with wi-fi, so don't expect them to last long. In fact, the tech will easily become obsolete long before the warranty ends prompting many to upgrade just to stay current.

The best advice I can offer anyone is cover your bets and consider an extended warranty and use AmEx or Discover (check their respective policies) to extend it another year. Because unlike back in the day, it may not take years to see problems develop in new appliances and 28 cubic feet of food spoils real quick and gets real expensive...

Update: 07-29-12
A brief update: After more than 7 months there is no significant issues to report and that is really saying something these days...

The refrigerator continues to operate flawlessly albeit with the following very minor issues. Every so often the unit makes a slight humming, mechanical or vibrating noise emanating from the rear. If I give it a slight nudge or push, it stops but returns infrequently. My suspicion is there may be a lose line inside the back that vibrates in sympathy with the compressor when it kicks on. Still its only sporadic and not repeatable enough to call out a tech... yet.

Beyond that all areas of the fridge appear to operate normally maintaining correct temps within acceptable tolerances. I installed 3 small digital thermometers within the upper, mid and lower (double door fridge, pull-out drawer & freezer) sections. Depending on time of day and frequency of access, the temps rarely deviate beyond +/- 5 degrees, which is really good especially with the unrelenting summer heat.

Our electric utility bills appear slightly higher than last year but the utility's "smart meter" indicates outdoor temps to be almost 2 degrees hotter these past months. Factor in our utilities super high rate pricing or "peak demand" for July & August (thanks SRP) and abnormally higher temps and it's tough to know if the refrigerator's efficiency gains aren't offset by our home's dual AC systems which cycle more frequently this time of year?

Lastly, the annoying ice maker continues to do it's part, still functioning normally albeit loudly. We have come to terms with it and now view it as a "feature" enhancement as you always know when its working. Guess you can get used to anything, all in all no real regrets...

Final Update: 07-01-14
Unless there is a catastrophic failure this will be my last update of issues and solutions we've experienced now that it's been more than 2.5 years with the fridge.

On 04-25-13 the infamous water drip began to appear. It started with several drips throughout the day, now we only see an occasional drip once per week or so. Over the course of the next 6 months I estimate about 3 techs, 2 water control valves (bottom back of unit), 2 hose connectors (under top door hinge) and a left door water/ice dispenser were all "experimentally" replaced. Remember, these were all trial and error exercises performed over weeks by various techs since none actually knew the root cause. While the net result of all these "fixes" yielded varying degrees of success I cannot say with certainty which really fixed the problem as none actually have. That said if I had to narrow it down to one "solution" I must say it was the one I least expected... the door dispenser. After each item was replaced we waited several weeks to observe and only after the door dispenser did I see the best result.

On 11-27-13 ice sheets began forming on the underside of the freezer pull out drawer (clear plastic storage tray inside freezer). I tried to thaw it out with a hair dryer but inevitably it reoccurred within 3-4 days. After fully extending the main freezer drawer and peering inside (between bottom of drawer and inside the freezer) a massive ice sheet had formed. Ultimately it was determined a clogged refrigerator drain tube was backing water up into the freezer where it spread and froze into a sheet. A tech was sent out to clear it and they say voila, no more ice sheets.

To summarize, all of these issues in an of themselves are really not significant but can be annoying and certainly time consuming to resolve so welcome to the new world order of appliance quality and ownership. As I initially stated way back at the beginning of this review don't go looking for long term reliability anymore. We purchased a Samsung dishwasher soon after and within about a year required replacement of a plastic upper tray lift release part that broke without ever using it. Later another recent acquisition, a Samsung microwave (arriving soon after the dishwasher) needed a new door due to a malfunctioning keypad. That's right the keypad isn't replaceable so time for a complete new door (handle and all)!

I still maintain if you plan to buy a new appliance, Samsung or otherwise GET AN EXTENDED WARRANTY! I promise you 2 things, I am not getting any commission or kick back for these (wish I were) and you will not lose money on it as it will more than likely pay for itself over time. After helping my sister about 6 months ago move into a her first condo I found a deal on a similar (slightly smaller) version of this fridge. I also made sure she purchased an extended warranty too. So far she hasn't needed it but I'm sure it won't be long...

Finally I'll leave you with this thought.
Remember life is too short so don't sweat the small stuff... it can always get fixed.

Good luck with whatever you buy...

product_title: Samsung RF4287HARS Stainless Steel French Door Refrigerator with FlexZone Drawer, 28 Cubic Feet
review_title: Great fridge! Love it more each day.
review_text:
Bought this great fridge in September. Absolutely love the capacity, French door convenience, two section freezer, but MOST of all, the cool drawer for beverages. My husband and I can fit 56 cans of pop and beer into the drawer. No need to open the whole fridge to grab a drink. We love the variety of temp settings and the ability to set the fridge, freezer and beverage drawer temps independently.

The freezer keeps foods at an even temperature, the coldest Ive ever seen in a non-commercial freezer. The whole unit runs so quietly we can never tell if it is running or not by the lack of sound. No more shouting at each other "sorry, dear, cant hear you the fridge is running!"

The only MINOR flaw is that when the icemaker dumps the ice its pretty loud, but we and our cats got used to that pretty quickly.

Unlike other stainless appliances, the surface is easy to clean without leaving streaks. A quick wipe with a damp paper towel or Windex does the trick.

This fridge has plenty of adjustible shelves, holds 2 gallons of milk in the DOOR easily and all the shelving and interior drawers are see-thru.

product_title: Samsung RF4287HARS Stainless Steel French Door Refrigerator with FlexZone Drawer, 28 Cubic Feet
review_title: Where's all the space? I think breathing puts fingerprints on it. I regret buying it.
review_text:
I was excited to upgrade the appliances in our kitchen to stainless--and especially so with this refrigerator since we were getting it for a lot less (due to a Lowe's sale plus a military discount) and I had wanted the French door option for awhile. However, if I could go back in time, I would never buy this model.

LOTS OF REFRIGERATOR SPACE? Ha. hahaha.

We had a regular side-by-side unit originally and we could fit SO much more in it it's unbelievable. (Granted, I do not know the actual square footage of storage space in the side-by-side, but the Samsung model screamed about how much space it had so I assumed it would hold at least the same if not more.) To start, even though the drawer is only about 6", that's a LOT of vertical space that comes out of the top, so all of the shelves are pretty low. Yes, you can adjust them, but I haven't found ANY arrangement that works better than the default. You can barely stack two short tupperware containers of leftovers on top of each other. Or an 18-24oz carton of yogurt or cottage cheese.

As far as tall things---in my old fridge, I could have fit at least 12 gallons of milk had I wanted or needed to (using two shelves) and still have plenty of room left over. This one? Six at most--and in doing so, you lose half of the bottommost right-side shelf (because you have to slide the split shelf back), half of the top most shelf (because the split shelf needs to flip up to accommodate the height of the milk), and half of the door space. I guess you could fit two more gallons of the door, but then you'd lose a lot of condiment space. In the old fridge, it was 12 gallons without losing any condiment space.

The old fridge? I could easily thaw a 24# turkey in a big bowl on the bottom shelf. This one? It's not deep enough or tall enough (though maybe you could remove a shelf, but then it's still not deep enough). Of course, part of the problem is the ice maker, which takes up a good portion of the left hand side (on both the door and the inner compartment). It's too shallow to fit a pizza box (which was no problem in the old one). I'm really not sure why the depth seems so off, since this one is deeper by our original one by a few inches...yet there's much less space.

THE DOOR RACKS DON'T HOLD MUCH, EITHER.

If you're used to the full length of door shelves to hold all your condiments, prepare to be severely disappointed. Yes, again, you can rearrange the shelves, but not much if you plan to use one of the shelves for gallons of milk (because you have to leave room to pull it out)--I have them as close as they can possibly be and I still have to really tip the jug to get it out. So in that placement, there's not even room on either of the other door shelves for a somewhat tall ketchup. You do get door shelves on the left-side, but half the space is taken up with the ice dispenser, so you get tiny spaces that aren't much good for anything except a horseradish or hot mustard bottle. And then in order to get them out, you generally have to pull out the other things in front of it. ANNOYING AS ALL GET OUT.

LOUD ICE--IT WILL SCARE YOU

We can hear the ice falling (being made) from upstairs in the bedroom and it scares the bejesus out of us--heaven forbid you are downstairs with it. It is the loudest ice maker I think I've ever heard.

DECENT FREEZER SPACE

It does feel like it has more freezer space than our side-by-side did, but it's just one shelf and one big drawer--which tends to let things get buried (think of those old chest freezers, where you dig to the bottom and find a foil-wrapped fish from 1973). I thought I'd like it, but after a month, I'd much, much rather have the easy viewing of the side-by-side.

STAINLESS--UGH--DON'T GET ME STARTED

Why did no one warn me just how horrible stainless steel is with fingerprints and swipes and drips and everything else? Certainly not the salespeople. Oh. My. God. I think you just breathe on it and it gets fingerprints. And of course they don't just wipe off. We tried the [[ASIN:B00029R8TK simplehuman Stainless Steel Microfiber Cleaning Mitt]] and it was absolutely useless. We ended up with the stainless steel spray cleaner. And as a busy mom and someone who hates cleaning, the last thing I needed was an extra step in my kitchen cleaning.

OVERALL

I would never buy this refrigerator again. Sure it looks pretty, but there's not a lot of good usable space and it's a bitch to keep clean.

product_title: Samsung RF4287HARS Stainless Steel French Door Refrigerator with FlexZone Drawer, 28 Cubic Feet
review_title: Best built of the French door fridges.
review_text:
Overview: We looked at them all: GE, Whirlpool, Electrolux, Kenmore, KitchenAid, Frigidaire, LG and Samsung.
In addition to the written ratings/reviews we looked at controls, shelf quality, plastics quality and features. GE, LG and Frigidaire utilize flimsy plastics on their covers & drawers; even on their top-of-the-line offerings. LG had the most flexible shelving (glass), but the Samsung was a very close second. LG also has a lot of reported ice maker trouble. Electrolux and KitchenAid were our second choices. The Electrolux were considerably more expensive in our area and not as nice as the Samsung. The KitchenAid had some illogical control placements i.e. the control for the 4th drawer/door was inside, above the drawer/door itself where any spill could leak in and short it out. Frigidaire did have the option of a black (as opposed the gray) cabinet with a stainless steel front; we wish Samsung would have offered that. Frigidaire's reputation as a "throw-away" brand discouraged us from looking further into their line. Kenmore and the very similar Whirlpool were more than adequate but overpriced for what they offered. GE was the flimsiest with the exception of their Proline which was adequate.

Samsung Pros: Fit, finish, heavy glass shelving, features (self-closing freezer, slide-out upper freezer shelf, fold-up tall bottle shelf, digital temp-control on 4th drawer/door), quietness (other than the ice maker), easy-to-clean, LED lighting & energy efficiency.

Cons: Very loud internal ice cube bucket filling. Ice dispenses very slowly. Water filter replacement indicator comes on after six months whether you use a lot or a little thru-the-door water; a scam to get you to purchase expensive replacement filters. Cheaper, after-market brands work, but don't fit snuggly. If you feel your filter is working, the filter timer can easily be reset on the control panel. Unit is not available with black cabinet. No egg compartment, no butter compartment, odd shaped door shelves, plastic rather than porcelain-on-steel interior (rare these days).

review_title: Had 3 weeks...and freezer has stopped working twice!!!
review_text:
Purchased this on June 12 - on June 29 opened the freezer to get the kids ice pops and noticed there were no pops; just slushies!! All frozen food was soft and pools of water puddled on top of all my food! Pushed the electronic temperature display and my freezer registered a whopping 38 degrees, 2 degrees higher than my fridge!!

Called Lowes where I purchased it from (do not recommend, customer service experience was dreadful) and cannot get service for 4 days, so reset freezer and good it seemed to work, until half and hour later when the electronic display stopped functioning ! Reset again -all good!

Three days later, we opened the freezer once again to see water pooled on top of packages of food and display registers at 38 degrees once again!! Repair man comes out -says he "thinks" its the main board which he has found to be a problem with this particular model in the past; it will take about 10 days to get a new one and then he would know for sure! As this was going on, my temperature shows as 33F - my freezer is a mess -caked in ice from the constant dip then rise in temperature! We have reset it three times today alone - and in 2 days time, it goes back to be replaced by a different brand through a different company!

This is not a cheap appliance, its one of the newer Samsung fridges that is the top of the line for store bought appliances (by store bought I exclude the Jenn Air, Sub zero type appliances )so you expect quality! At this point we are not sure what the problem is but we are not at all trusting of the appliance, or its ability to keep food at safe frozen temperatures!

The ice has also had to be thrown as it has an "off" taste; our tap water tastes fine so that is not the issue; the ice maker drips water every time you dare open the fridge door and of all the stainless appliances I have owned or currently own, this one is really not good with kids in the house as not only does it show up fingerprints remarkably easy - they do not remove as easy!

UPDATE: We were lucky that the store had a 30 day return window so it went back - delivery guys told us they had picked up 5 recently as returns, all for same issue. Switched to a GE which we have had for 9 months with great results!

product_title: Samsung RF4287HARS Stainless Steel French Door Refrigerator with FlexZone Drawer, 28 Cubic Feet
review_text:
Just had this delivered & set up this past Friday. What a great fridge!
I took off the storm doors spring hinge & decided to play it safe (and glad I did) so I also unscrewed the main door hinge. I have a 36" door opening & this Samsung beast came through w/ (maybe) 1/4" on either side!!
The installers placed it near it's final spot & hooked everything up & described the major features, then carefully pushed it to it's final spot.
The thing looks and works great!!
I did have some initial water drops coming from the water dispensor but upon reading the sheet that came w/ the instruction booklet it's shown that some initial drippage can be caused due to air in the water lines. Sure enough; the more I used the water dispensor the less drippage afterward (as all the air must have been purged out). Now there isn't a drop of residual water after using it.
I had read some reviews concerning the accessive noise from the ice dispensor, to the point of total distraction some would say. My living room is close to our kitchen and neither my wife nor I find the ice maker to be any more or less "distractive" than any other machine. It makes ice, and lots of it. We're happy and do not find the noice bothersome at all.
Overall I rate this a 5 all the way. Love the features, the led lighting, the touch screen controls on the outside of the machine and the overall quality.
One thing to add: I thought this was warranted for (1) yr. so I did get a 4 year additional coverage; upon reading the specs further it states that it's essentially (1) year 'bumper to bumper' if you will and (4) years for all sealed parts like the compressor, etc. so w/ the 4 yr. add-on I get (5) yrs. bumper to bumper & (9) years for all sealed parts. This is good as my previous fridge (a Maytag) finally died (compressor) after 12 years.
I don't want to fork out this kind of cash for something that could die in 1 year.
Do I like this Samsung? You better believe it.
Would I recommend it: You betcha'.

review_title: Samsung Refrigerators All Have a Fatal Flaw
review_text: Samsung refrigerators are designed so that they do not restart on their own after a power outage.  Instead, after a power outage of 15 minutes or more, they are designed to return to demo mode.  Demo mode is used in the store to demonstrate a refrigerator so it has the lights on, but the compressor not operating/cooling.  To restart the refrigerator you must to push certain buttons in a certain sequence.  This is a fatal design flaw because you may be on vacation or out of town when the power goes out, and not be there to push the right buttons to have it turn back on.  This will ruin all of your food and cause a terrible stench in your home.  I have been told of this "design feature" by both the Samsung customer hotline and by the Office of the President of Samsung in North America.  They say there is nothing wrong with my refrigerator as it is "operating per its design".  I'm sure that none of you want a refrigerator that cannot be relied upon to come back on following a power outage.  Please get the word out to all that you know of this fatal flaw.  If Samsung can't sell these flawed refrigerators, they will get things changed.
