review_text:
Nightmare of a refrigerator.
First off - all the complaints other reviewers have posted are valid. The fridge gets too dark,the controls are awkward and not intuitive at all so unless you use them daily keep the manual handy or prepare to spend time every time you need to readjust settings that take no brainpower at all on any other refrigerator.Also,every time you dispense water some spews all over the place and down the door all the way to the floor. the floor.
BUT THOSE ARE ALL MINOR ISSUES.
The fridge came with badly sealing ice dispenser flapper (the thing that closes the ice chute after the ice is dispensed) and so even if I don't use the ice dispenser at all snow forms inside the door ice chute. Now naturally that snow or ice breaks off every time the freezer door is open so even if you don't mind much not being able to use the Ice dispenser since the chute is always plugged you will sure as hell mind cleaning the mess on the floor every time the freezer door is open essentially rendering the whole freezer section useless.
Well and then the real fun started. I have called the Samsung repair department on June 11 2014 and instead of having the repairman call me they gave me a number to call for Big Island Climate Control. Well after numerous attempts I have reached the guy and he promised to get the part in about two to three weeks and call me back. I gave him almost two months but nothing happened. So after numerous additional attempts to reach him unable to even leave a message as his mailbox is always full I finally talked to him in mid August. Same promises made but nothing got done. Once being called at 7 am he apparently picked up the phone by mistake and immediately said he is not open until 8 am and that he will call me back. Of course that never happened. So I called the Samsung again and they promised to have somebody else to call me back in 24 to 48 hours.(After telling me this was their only representative in the area) You are guessing correctly that that did not happened either Naturally they also tried to tell me that my fridge is out of warranty even though they clearly know it is not as I called them on 6/11 2014 and told them when the fridge was bought. But it is close to running out of warranty so that is probably their plan.
Now that comes on the heels of having a really bad experience with a Samsung all in one laser printer CLX-3160FN couple years back that also arrived with defective scanner cover straight from the factory and started smudging prints as soon as warranty ran out. That was another Samsung $700 mistake.
Now I have bought this fridge only because it was on sale as the bad design and lighting was obvious even after casual look around but little did I know what a nightmare this will turn out to be. I guess my naivete sprang from the fact that as a builder who bought over the last 25 years at least as many refrigerators I have never -in all this time -bought a fridge that was broken straight out of factory and half of which was essentially unusable nor have I ever experienced such a shoddy customer treatment.So this would make this the worst Refrigerator I have ever bought by a wide margin. ( Keep in mind we are not talking two or three fridges here)
To think that a couple months back I have bought a Galaxy tablet fills me with dread and I for once will be hard pressed to buy any other Samsung product ever.
As of today 9/17 2014 the fridge is still not being fixed after more than three months of getting runarounds .
Oh and by the way -air breezing through the door ice dispenser can't be too good for the fridges energy efficiency either.
So there You have it. Do You still want it?

review_text:

product_title: Electrolux EI30EW45JS IQ-Touch 30" Stainless Steel Electric Double Wall Oven - Convection
review_title: Great price, free shipping, delivered unboxed right into our kitchen.  Cool features
review_text:
This replaced our 1999 GE double oven which had electrical wiring in the top catch on FIRE! OMG, good thing we noticed before too much damage occurred. The racks are awesome, the interior color is very unique. The double convection feature works awesome. Cooked better and faster than our previous oven so you may need to adjust cooking times down from older oven estimates. It's quiet, and doesn't get hot outside of the oven thus our cabinet above no longer gets hot.

We love the oven so far. A huge improvement over our old GE.

After the fire I was bummed because of the cost of replacing a double oven. I had an epiphany and decided to file a claim and see if they'd cover the fire under our homeowners policy. "Kudos to State Farm for handling our claim in a very quick painless fashion under our hazard insurance".

One thing of special note with installation is the electrical whip is at the bottom of the oven. We had to cut the drywall behind the oven for the whip to fit into when we installed the oven. The installation was very straight forward. The biggest thing was the weight. We purchased the appliance moving lifting straps and 2 of us were able to lift it the short distance to get it into the cabinet. We also had to build up the base with 2x4's and plywood and buy the optional larger base trim from Electrolux.

We also bought a 5 year square trade warranty which cost us $337 with a coupon they had. I'll take the gamble something will break in the first 5 years. This thing has a lot of features, it's worth the piece of mind. Square trade is awesome they are a no-nonsense insurer of electronics and appliances. We've had many claims paid out by them on everything from laptops to cell phones.

The shipping speed was very fast.

product_title: Haier Portable Ice Maker
review_text: We are avid weekend campers and have always gotten a bag of ice to take. We also have a non-icemaker refrigerator,so I've been making ice cubes the regular way for years. The Haier ice maker has been a WONDERFUL addition to my arsenal of appliances that I will not do without! I put in about 8 cups of water & press the start button to start making ice cubes in about 6 minutes. On the hot summer weekends at home I leave it on all day so we have ready ice. For weekdays I have the ice maker make enough ice to use up the 8 cups of water & put them in gallon ziplock bags to keep conveniently in my freezer. The 8 cups of water seem to make 3 gallon bags stuffed full of ice. I'm not sure how this equates with a bag from the store, but we used only 1 on a recent camping weekend. If you were to ask me a con to this product I would say that after you get ice you need to put a container under the spout because it consistently shoots out an ice cube after you turn your back. I use a glass measuring cup and all is well. I would recommend this highly!

product_title: Haier Portable Ice Maker
review_text:
I'm not sure what product the other reviews here are using, but it surely can't be this.

After opening the package and reading the manual (yep I'm one of those that do that). I had my ice maker set up on the counter and was ready to make ice. The first thing I noticed was the ackward way you must put water into the unit... with a funnel. They include this funnel but it was still a bit odd at first to think this was required.

After filling the unit with the necessary amount of water, I powered it on and began to see the unit function. I left it be to make ice for a while hoping to come back to a full hopper. This was definitely not what I came back to.

When I returned the unit was no longer running, and what ice had been in the hopper had either melted to almost nothing or spilled out the front where it pours ice into a glass. That's right, I came back to a puddle in front of the unit and melted ice chips. There is no insulation where the ice comes out to pour into the glass so it allows the ice to melt very fast even right after it is made. The puddle was created to ice cubes that had rolled out of the dispenser and melted on the floor.

As nice as the ice dispenser seems, do not purchase this product. This dispenser design ruins the functionality of the product.

product_title: Haier Portable Ice Maker
review_text:
Many people probably buy this due to the convenience of having a glass dispenser. I did. Don't be fooled.
I have had mine for 8 hours now and regret it. Small Ice Cubes and small cube bin. Stops as full too low in inventory if you ask me. If you are having guests over and plan for them to use this, after the first 2 glasses it will be empty. Here is the kicker, its not insulated. So, if it is hot, the ice melts before the next cycle of cubes are completed. I had to "jump" start it with other ice cubes to get the "bin" cold enough to maintain the cubes made from cycle to cycle. Get a larger unit, with an insulated bin and ice scoop.

review_text:
we just built a house (a horrible experience!!!) and needed all new appliances. product_title: Electrolux EWFLS70JIW 27 5.1 cu. Ft. Front-Load Washer - Island White
review_text:
I literally put 2 laundry basket full of clothes in this thing, and it cleaned them all, without a problem!
I don't know what the other review is talking about, I guess they just got 1 of the bad ones out of the bunch.
We have had nothing but happiness with this washer.
I literally sat and watched this thing do 2 loads, because it's so awesome to look at your clothes being washed with a bright white light illuminating everything.

I am not an engineering genius, I am only 23 years old and I installed this by myself, connected the hoses, leveled it front to back, side to side and it passed the install cycle within 5 minutes!
After that I did 3 loads in 1 day, BIG loads, and the washer still kicks butt.

THE BEST THING ABOUT THIS WASHER?
It has an OUT-OF-BALANCE sensor, so when the Spin part of the cycle starts, you will see the washer spin moderately to see if it is balanced, if it's not, it will come to a stop and repeat, until it finds the perfect balance, and then it goes to its 1400 RPM AWESOMENESS!!! This is the best thing any company could do to increase the longevity of their washers... I had a Maytag top loader whose suspension bars bent because I washed a comforter and it was out of balance and it decided to spin to its top speed. When I read about this Spin Balancing Sensor, I was SOLD.

Also, it has a deep clean + sanitize setting which is NSF(National Science Foundation) certified to kill 99.9% of bacteria!
What more could you ask for?
I have a little one on the way, and this was just the icing on the cake for me!
I knew I had to have this awesome washer.

It also has an Allergen option, which is NSF certified to kill 95% of Dustmites and remove 95% of pet dander!
I am allergic to cats and dogs, so this was a great addition for me, incase I visit someone who has them, I can come home, wash my clothes and know that my Electrolux Washer will keep me safe from the pet dander!
AMAZING.

P.S. The Department of Energy changed the way they measure the Cubic Feet of washers and dryers, so if you go to Electrolux, you will see that they have updated their size for this model to 4.42 cu Ft.
That may sound like a huge disappointment, but the largest front loaders on the market are 4.5 cu Ft. so they were all doing what Electrolux was doing, which was measuring from the Door to the end of the drum, now the measure from the Lip of the drum to the end of the drum!

This washer makes laundry fun... which I never thought was possible.
It is so silent you can't even hear it, until it gets to the spin cycle where it is moderately loud, but barely vibrates (if you leveled it great)!

I hope my review helps you in your decision!

product_title: Electrolux EWFLS70JIW 27 5.1 cu. Ft. Front-Load Washer - Island White
review_text:
The number of cycles, and options per cycle, are just staggering. At first, it's even confusing, since there are so many.

You select the cycles with the main central dial. From left to right, the cycles are: Favorites specialty, Deep clean sanitize, Heavy duty, Whitest white, Colors, Normal, Casual, Active wear, Fast wash, Delicate, Hand wash, Rinse & spin.

Then in the LCD window, you get the water temperature (7 levels), the spin speed (6 levels), the soil level (6 levels) and several other options that include: Add steam, Eco friendly, Allergen, Extended fresh, Shrink guard, Add more water, Stain pretreat, Fresh rinse, Extra spin, Pre wash, Warm rinse, Delay start.

But that is not all. When you select the Favorites specialty cycle, there are even more cycles available from the LCD window. There are two options displayed in the LCD window under the Favorites specialty cycle: My Favorites and Specialty cycles. Select the latter, and there you get more cycles by rotating the main dial: those are Jeans, Fast sanitize, Stuffed animals, Pet beds, Clean washer, Steam pretreat, Kids wear, Fast steam and Wool. Impressive, as would say Darth Vador!!

And then the fun begins, as you can combine all these options. But not always. For example, if you select the Deep clean sanitize cycle, you will obviously not be able to deselect the steam option.

You can wash almost anything in this appliance. The wash drum is big enough to easily wash a comforter.

The washer is very efficient on water consumption compared to a top-load appliance and the spin cycle removes a lot of water, so that the time in the dryer is well reduced. The clothes are very well cleaned, in a very soft manner that certainly helps protect them in the long term.

But the feature that impress me the most is the quietness of the appliance. The washer is in my bathroom, next to my home office. With my previous top-load washer, I had to close the door of the bathroom to be able to work. With this one, even with the bathroom door opened, I hear nothing. In the first few days, I even got up from my desk a couple of times to go see in the bathroom if the washer was still working. There, I couldn't believe that it was indeed washing!

The reason I give 4 stars rather than 5 is related to the Electrolux after-sales service. When I installed the washer, I made the mistake of placing the drain hose too deep inside the wall-pipe. That caused the washer to stop working on the very first wash I made with it, because it couldn't empties at the end of the cycle. An error message displayed in the LCD window said that the washer needed a service call, labelling the trouble Code 13, and displayed also a 1-800 number. It was on a saturday, so I called... Of course, nobody answered. The recorded voice message rather said that Electrolux office was closed and there was no option to leave a message... When I phoned back on Monday, the lady could only offer me to give a call to the store where I bought the washer... This is not an emergency phone number and it's totally useless...

Anyway, the appliance is just great and washes very quietly and so far, I am very pleased with it. As for the long term reliability, this is the only question I can't answer yet.

Yes, I would recommend it to a friend.

UPDATE 2014-01-12
I raise the rating from 4 to 5 stars for the following reason: I have a set of white satin bed sheets that had become yellowish with time, no matter how I washed them in my previous top-load washer. I have not count the number of times I washed this set in my new Electrolux washer, because I wasn't expecting such outcome, but after, I would say, 5 washes at the most in my new washer, they are white again.

It struck me the last time I took them out of the dryer: they were white again! I've never seen anything like that in my whole life, and I am over 50. I did not change the detergent or the fabric softener, I use the same popular brand of liquid detergent and liquid fabric softener. So it means the washer makes the difference. Very glad I purchased this set (washer and dryer), it has so far surpassed my expectations.

UPDATE 2019-10-05
I am surprised by the number of negative reviews this washer gets. After 6 years of EVERY WEEK use, this washer and dryer have been a work horse for me. I've had not a single issue with them in 6 years. Absolutely nothing failed on it, I have used many different cycles and I get very cleaned clothes every time. Could not be more happy with my purchase.

review_title: Major defrost problem leaves fridge section warm
review_text:
This unit came in our newly renvoated condo, so I didn't make the purchase myself.

A little more than a year after we moved in, I noticed the refrigerator section was not cooling (though the control panel still showed 36*F, the temp as measured was more like 56*F).

Some online research showed that this model has a known issue with icing of the fresh food evaporator.

Sure enough, this is the issue we were experiencing. I'm on my 6th repair technician visit, and still no resolution.

I'm an engineer and have some knowledge of how these systems work. I heard the tech on the phone with his Samsung professional tech support, and they are absolutely useless--no help to the repair tech. The Samsung people actually suggested replacing a thermal fuse (a one-shot safety device designed to shut the unit down permanently to prevent a fire if the defroster overheats) with a bimetal sensor (a self-resetting control device like what's in your home thermostat). They said: "is the plug the same? OK I wouldn't worry then." What?? Every plug in the fridge is the same! Who's to say the bimetal operates at the same temperature as the thermal fuse?! This thing could burn my house down, me and my family with it!

I'm now trying to get in touch with someone from Samsung who can actually confirm that this was an appropriate substitution (very doubtful!). What a nightmare. Steer clear!

review_title: This is a good refrigerator, but it has a serious design flaw
review_text:
I purchased this refrigerator in May 2014. I chose it because it was the highest-rated (by Consumer Reports) refrigerator that had the required dimensions and that did not have a water dispenser in the door - a feature I did not want.

I like this refrigerator. It fits the available space nicely, and it looks nice. it is not noisy.

However, I do not love it. And the primary reason I do not love it is the relative lack of storage space for taller items such as containers of milk, juice and 2-liter soda bottles. There are exactly two small shelves, in the doors, for this type of item. If you use a Brita pitcher, as I do, the pitcher takes up half of the available space. I can store the pitcher plus two half-gallons of milk - and that's it for the upright storage. Every other taller item has to go on a shelf on its side, which is not always practical or even possible.

Space for items such as bottles of ketchup, A-1, salad dressing, and the like is also very limited. Why? Because you either have to find a space in the doors (and there's not much of that) or you have to lay them on their sides on the shelves. The shelves only have about eight inches of space between them - and I have discovered that things like bottles of soy sauce and Worcestershire sauce are taller than that. The shelves are adjustable, but not by much. The entire storage compartment is basically designed for items that are less than eight inches tall. For the first time ever, when I go to the grocery store, I have to stop and think, when buying perishable groceries, whether or not the items will fit into my refrigerator.

I have a small household, so it's not a huge issue for me. But if I had a houseful of kids, I'd have to go to the store every other day for things like milk, just because of the lack of space in this fridge.

Update January 2015: There is another flaw with this refrigerator - frost buildup in the freezer compartment. I've had a repairman out once; he said the problem was that the refrigerator was placed too close to the wall which was impeding air circulation behind the unit. We moved it out and it was fine for a few months, but now I've got frost buildup again. I'm going to have to have the repair people out again while it's still under warranty.

If I had it to do over again I probably would not buy this particular refrigerator. It's not, in my opinion, living up to its Consumer Reports rating.

review_text:
I bought this thing for around $1500, if memory serves, from a local department store. I was sucked in by its beautifully spacey interior--the vertical strip of lighting--and the generally high ratings that Samsung refrigerators get from various organizations. (Of course, this particular model I couldn't find the ratings for.)

There is actually nothing wrong with this thing. But after having it for about 6 months now, my question is, is this refrigerator worth the $1200 difference between one of those old-fashioned white things we used to have. Yes, the head of lettuce no longer freezes up. (But I'll bet there are those cheap white refrigerators that don't freeze their lettuce either.)

I am amazed that for $1500 they still can't design an ice dispenser that 1) doesn't splash ice all over the floor and 2) make crystal clear ice like you get from dedicated ice machines. It doesn't seem like this would be too difficult to add to the refrigerator. (When manufacturers do add this, it will be a game changer for refrigerator manufacturers the way spell-check was for word processing programs -- everyone will want to upgrade.)

Also, this stainless steel is not magnetic, so the entire front of it is unable to be used for notes or anything. Also, the fingerprint problem has been horrendous with our kids. It requires constant cleaning (though wife did finally go get some stainless steel cleaner from the store and it looks brand new again). There is a model with a different surface called platina or something like that that is supposed to be magnetic and reduce fingerprints. Wish I'd gone with that model.

I believe that the way this type of refrigerator maintains its energy rating is because the bottom half of the refrigerator compartment consists of three drawers. When you open the door, no air escapes from these drawers. That's cool. On the other hand, having to open the drawers all the time to see what's inside is a hassle. (The fronts of the drawers are clear, but you can't seen what's in back.

With my old white refrigerator I used a Brita pitcher for water. This Samsung came with a filter of a brand I've never heard of. To me, it just doesn't taste as good as the Brita filtered water. Also, the temperature of the water, if you choose to drink it without ice is no very cold, as if it is just in the pipe outside the refrigerator until it gets filtered. You'd think that for $1500 they could make the water cold before it gets dispensed. I am also suspect of the filter because when water drips on the little tray under it, it leaves a big hard water spot. If the filter was working, shouldn't it not do that?

Anyway, I am really questioning whether I shouldn't have just bought one of those cheap $300 refrigerators.

Then it would dispense the ice in a rather slow manner with a lot of very loud clunking noises (my old GE unit made comparatively little noise when dispensing ice, and dispensed it far more quickly). The seller ordered a new unit and replaced it the following week. The front panel worked fine on the second unit, but the unit would not dispense the ice at all! Returned for a full refund. Samsung has made a very stylish-looking unit and for the most part it works well, but it does appear that they have some things to learn about manufacturing refrigerators.

product_title: RS267TDRS 25.5 cu. ft. Side by Side Refrigerator Twin Cooling System LED Tower Lighting Cool Select Zone In-Door Ice Maker and Wine Rack Energy Star Compliant: Stainless
review_title: Best fridge we have owned in 30 years
review_text:
This review is for a Samsung RS267TDBP which probably shares many similarities with its nearby model number cousins. I also published this review on Samsung's web site.

The review:

Temperature regulation seems to be excellent in both the refrigerator side and the freezer side. This unit is extremely quiet while running but the icemaker produces some strange (and funny) noises doing whatever it does.

Power freeze and Power cool features are excellent - our newly delivered and set up fridge cooled down the fridge to 45 degrees within a couple of hours. I forgot how long it took to cool down the freezer side, but it was relatively fast. Be aware if *both* Power freeze and Power cool are selected, the fridge side will cool down FIRST, then it will start to cool down the freezer. We thought the freezer side wasn't working, but after a few hours, the freezer side started to cool.

The design of the interior is very well thought out allowing easy and convenient organization and access to food/drink.

One complaint about the product is the pull out drawer design. They are much harder to pull out than they should be due to the plastic drawer design. The drawer runners/guide are simply plastic against plastic - there are no wheels or rollers. I noticed when fridge shopping as the price of the fridge increased, so did the ease of pulling the drawers in and out (and drawer quality). Looks like you need to get into a $2,000+ fridge to get a better drawer design.

There are many complaints about the LED lighting in this series of Samsung products - the primary one being too little light. The lighting is *very* well distributed up and down on both sides, but it is for a fact a little on the dim side. While a bit of a detriment, the other strengths of the product make this less of an issue.

Unless you use a very large diameter glass or cup, the ice dispenser will shoot crushed ice all over the place. This is the most significant design flaw of this product.

No regrets about the purchase and I would recommend it to others assuming they understand the weaknesses.

review_text:
As big fans of Samsung TV's, we were happy to buy this fridge 3-1/2 years ago. When I first used the ice dispenser in the door, I thought maybe it was me... but now I know it's this lousy design. It's spits out ice and ice shavings (even when you're set it to give you cubes) all over the place and occasionally spits out an extra cube minutes after I've left the room.

It has always made a HUGE CLUNK, which apparently is the condenser turning off and is normal!!! Yeah, right, waking us up at 3 AM when we're 60 feet away is normal.

I tried vacuuming the back coils (this is advanced handyman stuff for me -- never had to do it with another fridge in my life!) and got it down to 52 degrees, but that's 1 degree above the "food safety zone." I know that a repair person will cost hundreds and may not even solve the problem, from what I've seen in other reviews.

Given the horrible CLUNK issue, I'm inclined to ditch this CLUNKER. Ironic, because I've never in 40 years had a fridge break down. Our previous Whirlpool, which we relegated to the basement when we remodeled, is still going strong -- at 29 years old.

review_text:
Our side-by-side Samsung refrigerator, model RS265TDRS, was purchased in December 2010, so it's about 3.5 years old. About a month ago it got noticeably noisier. The noise sounded like a generator -- so loud, I was afraid something was breaking in there.

We moved the food into another refrigerator and freezer, unplugged this unit, and made arrangements with Samsung for a service call. (That itself was an adventure: Samsung rep never responded to email; the phone number in the refrigerator manual was for service on Samsung cell phones; the web form didn't work under several different browsers. I finally used live chat and had the chat rep fill out the service request form for me.)

Two weeks later, I plugged in the unit in preparation for the service tech's visit. No noise. The service tech called, and after discussion suggested we cancel the service call, because (a) with no noise, he can't really diagnose a problem; (b) chances are it was just ice buildup and may never happen again; (c) removing the panel to get at the fan means removing all tech, because everything is attached to the panel, and that means replacing the panel because you can't just put it back on after it's been taken off; and (d) something like his labor and the panel wouldn't be covered by warranty anyway after 3.5 years.

These are EXPENSIVE refrigerators. I think it's ridiculous that I should have to unplug my refrigerator every now and then to make sure ice doesn't build up, and it's ridiculous that this problem wouldn't be covered under a warranty.

If you have already purchased this refrigerator, watch out for this fan-sounds-like-a-generator problem. Don't bother with a service call; unplug it for a while and see if that helps.

If you have not bought this refrigerator, don't. It's a beautiful refrigerator and has some things going for it, but there's no way something this expensive should experience this kind of problem in three-and-a-half years. And getting support out of Samsung is a challenge at best.

review_title: Full of design problems, including one so bad that it inspired a class action suit
review_text:
Disappointment, out of the box.

The first thing I tried to do was attach a photo to the front with a magnet, but the front wasn’t ferromagnetic. Some printing on control panel is grey on silver—not easy to read in daylight, much less at night when getting a drink of water. No big deal, but these were harbingers. Here are the pros and cons I’ve experienced over my six-year history with it:

Pros:
• The blue LED display panel informs users of the freezer and refrigerator temperature, filter status, and the presence of problems.
• The freezer and refrigerator have separate cooling systems, so if the refrigerator side fails, you can use frozen items from the freezer to keep the refrigerator reasonably cool like an old-fashioned ice box. Read on to understand why this is important.
Cons:
• Filtered water comes out slowly.
• “Push bar” used to start water flow has such resistance that a guest broke a glass trying to get water.
• Long drop of ice cubes through dispenser mechanism broke another guest’s glass when the cube hit the glass rim.
• Invariably, 10% or more of the crushed ice ends up on the floor, not the glass.
• Ice maker is slow.
• Ice maker flap stays open unless I put my hand up to close it.
• After 4 years, the ice maker began making a clicking sound after dispensing that only stops after I open and close the freezer door.
• Someone stepped on the inside front of the freezer and cracked the plastic bottom.
• Doors often appear closed when they aren’t fully closed.
• Shelf broke and I had to replace (about $50).
• My (very experienced) refrigerator repair tech, when finished the with job, couldn’t reinsert the shelves over period of about 5 minutes and came close to breaking one.
• Motherboard failed.
• Coils froze (see below, from classactionlawsuitsinthenews[dot]com). These last two cost me half the cost of a new refrigerator when counting spoilage and repairs.

The Samsung refrigerator class action lawsuit complaint reportedly alleges that certain Samsung French door, side-by-side and bottom freezer refrigerators (model numbers RF266AASH, RS263BBWP, RB1955SH, RS2533SW, RS267LASH, RS267TDRS, RS2630WW) […] are designed and manufactured with heated coils that are intended to prevent excess frost from developing in the back of the machine, but instead of preventing frost, the coils allegedly allow frost and ice to build up in the refrigerators until the ice clogs and/or disables the machine’s fans, making it impossible for the fans to work to keep the machine cool.

I’m amazed that this refrigerator is still on the market. Please, save yourself the trouble and buy another product.

review_title: Fridge chimes, power cool goes on and off
review_text: I'm leaving this review to let those who have this fridge know how to resolve a common problem with this model.  The power cool feature will turn on eventually dropping the temperature to 30*.  It will chime as it turns on and off.  This is due to a malfunction in the power cool button of the LED display board.  It's about $100 to replace for a new  board (part #DA92-00201G ASSEMBLY PCB KIT LED) and is an easy DIY repair. Order the part and when it arrives unplug the fridge and remove the 4 screws on the bottom of the LED display. Remove the cover, carefully remove the 4 screws and disconnect the board. Install the new board with the 4 screws, reconnect and then reattach the cover with their 4 screws.  The new LED will be much brighter and the malfunction should be resolved.

product_title: Whirlpool EV250NXTQ
review_text:
We previously used 2 freezers - a relatively new 20 cf Kenmore chest and a quite old (R12?) 15 cf Gibson chest freezer. While our intent was to always use one freezer except for the time of year when we either buy a side of beef or store recently harvested venison, we found ourselves using both freezers all year long. The old R12 freezer which worked great was an energy pig (it would work in a cold or hot garage which is a benefit of these older freezers).

At the time of our purchase, both of our freezers were about half full, and needless to say, we really couldn't find anything in either of them due to their chest design. We then took everything out of both old freezers and put them into the new Frigidaire upright freezer. Much to our amazement, it sucked up everything from both freezers and we could actually see what we had!! My wife laughed when she saw that I had about 12 boxes of Toaster Strudel in the freezer. My excuse was that I got them on sale but the cold reality was that I never knew how many we actually had and sure didn't want to face the wrath of the kids if I ran out. We sent the old 15 cf freezer to be retired for recycling and kept the spare 20 cf for future use if needed. I expect we will rarely, if ever, need the 20 cf chest again but will keep it given we have extra space and we never know how much wild game we will harvest from year to year.

I have a couple of gripes about the freezer. First, and probably to be expected, the items stored in the outside door don't get as cold. The meat feels fully frozen but the ice cream is somewhat soft (almost the same consistency as what you'd get at the grocery store). I'd prefer or at least feel better if I could get the ice cream to fully freeze in the outside door. I have the thermostat set to the highest setting short of the fast freeze feature and this goal is still not accomplished.

The second gripe is that the freezer is noisier than either of the freezers it replaced. By all means, it isn't bad or extremely loud - it's just annoying. It has a higher pitched noise to it. My office is next to the room where the freezer is and I can work in relative silence if I close the door to the freezer room or my office. I mention this in the event that someone else might want to put the freezer in a noise sensitive area. The frequency of noise is most of the time, in my case, as I have the freezer on its coldest setting so it therefore seems to run most of the time.

I recommend this freezer and would buy an upright freezer from now on given the choice. The visibility of the items in an upright freezer clearly outweigh the benefits of saving a few bucks worth of electricity a year by having a chest freezer. By the way, I purchased this at Sears and have had it for a few weeks at the time of this review.

Review concluded - unless you want to read a horror story about Sears:

We had a bunch of problems with Sears Customer Service and Delivery. We ordered two appliances at one time to be delivered at the same time but due to a multitude of errors by them they delivered the freezer on schedule and missed the refrigerator. They tried to make up for it by promissing to have the refrigerator to us the next day by 8 p.m. Sears called to confirm the delivery for the next day between 6 p.m. and 8 p.m. and never showed or called even after they confirmed the delivery. Sears had the order marked - "Cancelled - Do NOT notify customer." Can you believe that?

A Sears representative then told us that we cancelled the order which we of course did not. Who would cancel a refrigerator order when your old one isn't working? They told us to see our original salesperson at the store which we did. He suggested that Sears has had a lot of delivery problems - duh! After a bunch more hassle trying to fix the mess (and being told by another salesperson that we cancelled the order), we gave up and told them to actually cancel the refrigerator order. Would you believe that Sears called the following week to confirm delivery of the refrigerator for the following day? Unbelievable!!! As as it was an automated delivery system, my wife had to spend a bunch of time trying to get a live attendant to tell them we had cancelled the order - a real pain. Although I would have felt guilty in doing it, I should have allowed Sears to try to deliver the refrigerator to our house while we were away. My wife earns sainthood for getting through to their CSR.

Based on my experience, I'd be very wary of purchasing appliances at Sears unless it is an in-stock item and you plan to bring the home with your own transportation.

review_text:

product_title: Whirlpool EV209NBTQ - White-on-White Whirlpool(R) 19.6 Cu. Ft. Upright Freezer
review_title: Nice design, but the seals got screwed up
review_text:
We've had this freezer for about a year.

It's the best upright freezer we've had. The top has a couple of shelves, and the bottom has deep drawers you can put stuff into. You can open the two sections independently, which is nice.

Like most stand-up fridges / freezers, you can switch the hinges (which we did). It runs quietly and reliably.

The only problem we had: after some time, the lower seal on the upper door got deformed. It no longer seals well, and we've had a consistent problem with icing as a result. I'm getting it repaired soon.

Pro:
- works great
- nice design
- quiet

Con:
- Door seal went bad after about 10 months, letting in moisture and causing icing.

product_title: Whirlpool EV209NBTQ - White-on-White Whirlpool(R) 19.6 Cu. Ft. Upright Freezer
review_title: Great if you want to grow mold
review_text: We've had this freezer for four years and have had 4 service calls on it.  Ice builds up (up to 2" thick) below the bottom drawer and we get frost over everything top and bottom in this "frost free" freezer.  The repair people say it's a design flaw that ices up the drain line, forcing the frost that melts to build up.  Add to that the fact that the door seal between the top and bottom doors grows black mold faster than you ever could in a biology lab, and you get the worst freezer we've ever had.  Only good thing about it is that it does keep the food in it frozen.

review_text: WORST refrigerator EVER!  Have had it 4 years and it just quit working!  Threw sparks while I was getting ice and now even won't cool.  DO NOT BUY THIS!  Electrolux is great....when it's not in need of repair!  And repairs aren't cheap for any of their appliances.

product_title: Electrolux EI27BS26JSIQ-Touch 26.6 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel French Door Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_title: Please do not buy an Electrolux refrigerator.
review_text:
We came to own an Electrolux refrigerator (model EI23BC56IS8) that conveyed with our new home in March 2014. Per the sticker in the unit, it was manufactured in June 2011 (less than five years ago).

For the second time in two years, it stopped making ice. This time the technician slid the unit out to get access to the control board which revealed what you see in the attached picture. Yes, among the giant rust spot, is a chunk of ice. Doing a little research online, Electrolux refrigerators are subject to failures in the coolant line or insulation that can result in what we experienced - basically a hole. Since we came to own this fine piece of refrigeration through the purchase of our home (i.e., it was "transferred" to us), Electrolux is choosing not to stand behind its product to do anything about it. Notably they have never expressed any interest in determining how this happened in less than 5 years - they simply do not care.

There are so much better refrigerators out there, please do not buy an Electrolux.

product_title: Electrolux EI27BS16JWIQ-Touch 26.6 Cu. Ft. White French Door Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_text: Do NOT buy an Electrolux refrigerator! My wife and I bought this model, in the stainless steel finish, when we purchased our home four years ago. The price was not cheap. The product, however, is. At the four year point (after the three year extended warranty had expired, of course), it died.  Apparently a major defect has been engineered into the appliance.  According to the repairman, during the defrost cycle moisture collects behind the evaporator panel. The circulation fan, which is also located behind that panel, is not sealed against moisture. It eventually shorted out, and when it did, it also blew the electronic motherboard in the control panel (and why does a refrigerator need an electronic brain, anyway? I just want it to cool my food, not to think). When the panel was pulled to gain access to then fan, it was also revealed to be rusting out. Why did Electrolux put a part made of metal that rusts where moisture will collect on it? Cost of replacing the fan and motherboard: $548.00. And because the underlying problem, moisture accumulating where it will cause rust and will damage the fan, cannot be "cured," the expensive piece of junk is a ticking time bomb that will eventually fail again.

product_title: GE Profile: PGCS1PJZSS 20.6 cu. ft. Counter-Depth French Door Refrigerator with 4 Adjustable Glass Shelves, Armoire Style Double Drawer Freezer System and External Water Dispenser
review_title: Ice tray spills ice all over the floor. EVERY TIME YOU USE IT!
review_text:
I purchased this appliance about a year ago and have regretted it every day. It looks great but the 2 freezer drawers are so poorly designed it completely overrides any good qualities with the refrigerator. The top freezer drawer is so small you can fit a pound of bacon or possibly 2 but not much else. The bottom drawer is where the real frustration is. It has an ice maker with a slide out compartment which holds the cubes. Every single time you pull the tray forward to get to the ice the ice hangs up on the upper tray and several pieces fall out onto the floor or worse underneath the bottom drawer where you can't get to it. The bottom drawer is deceiving in its looks. It has the slide out upper tray which is where the ice is leaving a very small bottom portion which is not very deep. If you put an ice cream container (less than half gallon size)in there it snags the top and bunches it up and the drawer won't close. The freezer is almost half of the volume of the appliance and yet it holds such a ridiculously small amount.
The refrigerator door hinges had to be replaced because one of the doors didn't close correctly and of course that happened as we left for the weekend. Unlike any other fridge I have ever owed, you really have to make an effort to close the doors. They do not seal if you just swing them shut. You have to push the door all the way until it comes in contact with the body of the fridge. It usually beeps when the doors aren't closed correctly which happens often, but not that time. When we came back on Sunday the inerior temperature was 64 degrees. Yep, everything in the fridge had to be thrown out. The hinges were covered under warranty but not the food or the 10 bottles of insulin which were in there. In fairness I think that the refrigerator has really good lighting but that just isn't enough when it comes to spending this type of money. This headache of a refrigerator will probably last me 30 long years.

product_title: 26 Cu. Ft. Gallery Series Side-by-Side Refrigerator
review_text:
As a Floridian, my refrigerator is one of the most important appliances in my house. This being said, I obviously want the best, most top-of-the-line product that I can afford. Fortunately, Frigidaire products fall in to this category! (or so I thought...). Upon my purchase of this fridge, I could not contain my excitement for the day to come that my new refrigerator would arrive, and I could once again enjoy the luxury of cold Cokes, and ice in my sweet tea! So I waited. And waited. And finally, it arrived! Ecstatic, I wheeled it into my kitchen and unboxed it, hooked up the water line, pugged it in, and opened the big double doors, expecting a blast of cold air...but what did I get? A FACE FULL OF POLAR BEAR!! This thing practically exploded out of the fridge, bowled over me, skidded across the floor, and out onto the patio and into the pool he went! Let me tell you, this was NOT a happy polar bear...I imagine he was hot and cramped from his ride in this fridge, going on trucks and in the cargo class section of an airplane. But anyways, I was mad. Because now, I had to put my new fridge on hold so I could take care of a polar bear that had hitch hiked to my house!! I did NOT pay over a thousand dollars for a pet polar bear! So, what had to happen was, I had to get this polar bear comfortable in the pool so he didn't hop out because he was hungry, and I brought him all the chicken nuggets and fish sandwiches I could buy from McDonald's (and apparently, polar bears like Micky D's... I had to make two trips!), then I had to figure out what polar bears like to do in their spare time, and guess what? They apparently like to play hide and seek in refrigerators in their spare time...but it is rare to not be found by their friends, so this was a once in a lifetime kind of thing! Just like getting a polar bear in a Coke bottle from the vending machine, right? So, I decided to keep him! His name is Pierre! As of now, I officially am a dedicated Frigidaire customer, because of this unique experience! Thanks, Frigidaire, for the great new buddy you sent me, and for the fridge! 5/5 stars!

P.S.- If anyone happens to know where I could get fresh seal or penguin, that would be great...I don't think my local McDonald's enjoys me bringing Pierre into the restaurant...he keeps eating all of their burgers and chicken. This is getting to be a huge problem, not to mention Pierre is also getting pretty huge...thanks in advance for any info on where I can get some!

product_title: 26 Cu. Ft. Gallery Series Side-by-Side Refrigerator
review_text:

review_text:

product_title: GE PSHS6PGZSS Profile 25.9 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel Side-By-Side Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_text:
Five years ago, when I bought a similar model GE Profile, it was a top-rated refrigerator with glowing consumer product reviews. Let this be a lesson to those who trust online reviews even from supposedly reliable sources.

On the whole, it's not the worst appliance I've ever owned but there's enough wrong with it to earn only one star from me.

For one, DON'T buy a 36" wide side-by-side from any manufacturer. What a mistake that was. I got two boxes which are too narrow to be useful for many common items. This goes double for the freezer, which isn't wide enough to store a decent-sized roast. Things like TV dinners have to be stored on end. A bag of meatballs occupies its own shelf. Adding an ice/water dispenser reduced the effective volume of the already too small freezer by at least 20%.

As for the GE, it never maintains a constant temperature. The fridge is be too warm one day and too cold the next. Part of the reason for that I believe is because the doors don't seal tightly. Even though it has an open-door sensor, it's very easy for a pan or a heavy bag to prevent the door from closing tightly and the alarm won't catch it. Next thing you know, you have a freezer full of frost, which takes the GE forever to lose.

After just five years, the fridge suddenly stopped cooling today so now I'm debating whether to write the GE off as a bad investment rather than fix it, especially after reading about all the trouble that others have had with the Profile.

The irony is that I moved the contents of my $1400 Profile to a 20 year-old, standard configuration, plain-jane Sanyo in the basement that cost me about $400 in 1992 and which has never needed a lick of maintenance. And despite the Profile being packed to the doors, the Sanyo is only half full with the same stuff. Sheesh.

review_title: So Far No Problems -- Looks clean -- Runs Well
review_text:
I was a bit skeptical after reading all the reviews. But as I was reading reviews for just about every refrigerator we were considering, I noticed that they were all pretty much bad -- which is understandable, as I usually go to the internet to complain when something I bought does not perform well. But even though we ended up purchasing this as a floor model at a store, I thought I would come back to Amazon and give it a positive review.

We bought ours in 2012, so I don't know if they fixed some of the problems that other people were talking about or what, but so far we have had no problems. Granted, we have only had it for a little bit. But so far it is running well and looks sharp to boot.

I have noticed the "whirring" sound that some people reported, but, to me, a fridge has to make certain sounds to operate and it's not a big deal. It is still way better than all the clunking and watery sounds our last fridge made. At worst, it sounds like air is flowing from the compressor to the compartments, which to me, is a normal operation of a refrigerator. At this price point, no, you might not get a completely silent fridge. But it's not crazy. You can go ahead and drop $2500 if you want an absolutely silent fridge.

Also, people rip on the ice maker. It's an ice maker... it freezes water rock solid and then the ice drops into a container. Just like every other ice maker, it only makes one row at a time, so if you just had a party and cleared the bin out, it's going to be dropping ice into a plastic container for 12 hours. That's just the way they operate.

Lastly, it's a side-by-side. Don't buy a side-by-side if you want to lay a DiGorno pizza flat. You'll need to buy a french-door fridge or bring your old fridge back from the 80's. But there is more to life than laying a pizza flat in the freezer. This side-by-side technology has been around long enough to know a 14" pizza in an even larger box is not going to lay flat. Don't be surprised by this.

But the bad reviews are all the same as what I've experienced, and you will find many, many, many more of them when you visit other review sites.

From the start, there has been a leak inside the refrigerator, where it connects to the ice machine. Huge chunks of ice build up there and have to be regularly pried off with a screw driver. The extra liquid pooling where it's not supposed to be also creates a black mold buildup ijnside the fridge that has to be cleaned up every few weeks.

But that's not the worst. The worst is that this refrigerator (and especially the freezer) WILL NOT HOLD A TEMPERATURE! If you buy this fridge, you're setting yourself up for food poisoning. Our freezer defrosts completely at least once a week without warning and for no reason. All of the ice in the ice machines melts completely. (We do not store things like meat in this freezer for this reason -- we use another, older freezer we're lucky to have downstairs.) Then everything will refreeze, again, but at a degraded quality.

And now the rubber gasket on the fridge has come completelly loose.

We're out of warranty (the problems for everyone always seem to start as soon as the warranty runs out), and I've read that a fix will cost at least $900 -- half the price of the original unit. Unfortunately we just married off our daughter and finished a remodel in the other part of the house, so we can't afford a new fridge. When we get one, though, there is NO WAY IN HELL that it will be a GE. I will be boycotting GE on everything for the rest of my life.

product_title: GE PSHS6PGZSS Profile 25.9 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel Side-By-Side Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_text:
I've spent about 6 months with my GE PSHS6PGZSS Profile refrigerator and I'm very happy with it. I was very dubious about purchasing a side-by-side model, but it's turned out to be very roomy and flexible. Frankly, I have no complaints about it as a fridge. It keeps things cool/frozen and makes ice very quickly. There are only a few minor flaws, and they are nearly insignificant, but I thought I'd list them:

- The hoses to the drink dispenser are plastic and exposed beneath the appliance. Unfortunately, this allowed some mice to gnaw through the hoses during a minor winter invasion. After trapping the mice, I was able to inexpensively fix the hoses (with a patch, but you can also cheaply replace the entire plastic water cooler they are attached to). Some protection (or better yet, copper lines) would be a helpful deterrent.

- The ice dispenser works, but not instantly, and the crushed ice is not a consistent size, sometimes containing whole cubes. It's definitely inferior to many other ice crushers.

- The curved profile at the top of the doors look nice, but serve no purpose whatsoever. You need to consider this for overhead cabinet door clearance. Kind of pointless, in my opinion.

- This is much quieter than my previous fridge, but it makes some bizarre noises that would be right at home in a horror movie (think "Blair Fridge Project"). I'm pretty sure it's the ice maker. There are also occasional taps and rattles, but nothing that would keep you up at night, and I have my television in the same room without any issues.

As I said, these are very minor issues. I suspect this model would have a much better rating on Amazon, but it looks like some reviews are directed more generally at GE and not this specific model. That's why I try to include the exact model number in my reviews (as did another reviewer who was unsatisfied). I am happy so far, and would buy this fridge again.

First Impressions

I am (mostly) impressed! While the refrigerator side offers amble room including three bins is which to store fruits, snacks and, and veggies, the freezer side is somewhat lacking in space. The price we paid for wanting an ice maker; the unit takes up ¼ of the upper portion of the freezer. And it doesn't help that the freezer is already 2/3 smaller than the refrigerator side.

However both sides are well lit with lighting along the sides of the compartments instead of one bulb lighting the whole thing. The push buttons on the door for water, ice (crushed or cubed) are attractively designed and back lit, however the lettering is not, so at night one has to turn on a light in order to know which button to push; bad design GE.

The lower drawer of the refrigerator compartment is humidity controlled and does a fantastic job of keeping veggies fresh and crisp, at least for a while. The drawer right above it we use for fruits and it too does a laudable job in keeping things fresh and editable for more than a week.

The shelves inside the body of the "GE PSHS6PGZ (25.9 cu. ft.) Side-by-Side Refrigerator" and on the door(s) are adjustable and spill-prove--whatever that means. And for the first time in a long time we actually have spare space in the refrigerator on an ongoing basis; wish I could say the same for the freezer wherein I have to constantly shuffle food around to make room. The big Purdue Over-Stuffer Roasters don't help, but hey when they are buy-one-get one free, who can resist?

Overall, I am happy with the GE PSHS6PGZ (25.9 cu. ft.) Side by Side Refrigerator, and will over time adjust to the limited freezer space. The design is attractive, the ice maker and water dispenser efficient and very utilitarian, and the veggies remain fresh longer than a week!

review_title: Great oven.  My wife loves it.  And I tested the temperature accuracy.
review_text:
At first my wife thought the oven temperature was not pre-heating accurately or quickly enough. But when I tested it with a thermocouple on an electronic multi-meter, it turns out to be very accurate. Testing it with a simple oven thermometer doesn’t give an accurate picture because the response times of those devices are much too slow.

It turns out that the oven was very accurate and in fact cycles above and below the set temperature by about 15°F. I.e., the 350°F temp is "held" actually by heating up to 365°F, then the gas goes off, it cools to 335°F, then the gas burner goes back on, and repeats this up and down. If testing with a simple oven thermometer which has a much slower response time than an electronic thermocouple, you get the average temperature. And you would normally want this to be the case for an oven thermometer.

I wrote up the above test results in case someone else, like me, was testing the time it takes to pre-heat the oven. Because of the slow response time of a standard oven thermometer, don't use it for that purpose. However, it does a good job as intended in monitoring the relatively steady state temperature in the oven. For an instant measurement, you need to use a thermocouple.

As a final note, on the initial preheat, the temperature (as read by the thermocouple) actually shot up to 390°F and then proceeded to the cycling of 350°F ±15°F as described above. I believe this is by design because when this oven's control panel says preheat is completed and put in the food, it knows you will be opening the oven momentarily to put in the food and the temperature will drop while the oven is open. This initial overshoot helps compensate for that loss.

review_title: A 5 star item - but is any oven worth $3K?
review_text:
I need to say I didn't buy this thru Amazon.

We initially bought this in Jan. of 2012. The main attraction was the fact the oven racks are on ball-bearings and slide out with the tug of one finger. Like all modern appliances, you have to be computer savvy to get the most out of this appliance. There are dozens of possible touch screen settings for operating the microwave as well as the oven. It replaced a 23 y.o. Thermador, which was definitely outdated. (It also had a matching microwave but was a separate physical unit.)
The easy slide racks are obviously not worth the extra $1K of the price of similar units. The excellent build quality makes it look, physically, better than most other units out there. This is a top of the line product. This was the only oven we saw with easy-slide racks. It would seem to me any mfr. could add this as an option for a couple hundred dollars.
After we had it for 9 months we had an accident and needed to run the self-cleaning function for the first time. It turned out there was probably something wrong w. the circuit board that wouldn't let us "turn on" the self cleaning function. The in home repair was covered by the warranty. When fixed, oven was thoroughly cleaned when self-cleaning was run.
Just cooked a holiday turkey using what is called "Perfect Turkey" function. It makes use of a probe and knows when to shut down the oven. Worked perfectly.
Microwave is not as high rated in watts as some others, but close. I would have thought an expensive unit would have the highest watt rating. The variety of controls is outstanding.
Conclusion - If you have a top grade kitchen or want a top notch appliance - put this on your "look at" list. This kitchen was in a condo with no gas service - so kitchen appliances have to be electric. Our cook top is a top of the line induction - which technology is somewhat new in the U.S. (It has been used for several years in Europe.)

review_title: Good overall, except for ice maker
review_text:
We bought this fridge about two months ago as a replacement for a horrible Samsung that flooded our house. So far so good on this one.

It's big, with good-sized veggie and deli drawers, lots of tall shelves (once we took an extraneous one out), and a deep freezer. Everything seems to be kept evenly cool, except for a cold spot in the top middle where we found inadvertently frozen condiments. Now that we know, no big deal. The french doors work fine -- the one that is supposed to be 'behind' the other will open/close independently with a bit of extra attention, and the alarm will let you know if you've forgotten it.

The only downside is the ice maker, which is ridiculously noisy both when filling with water and with chopping up the ice (or whatever it's doing). The capacity isn't nearly what you'd expect from such a big fridge; it runs out of ice after not many glasses. It has also jammed up with ice several times, requiring us to remove the ice from the top of the mechanism to prevent it from slowly melting into the little door tray all day. So - definitely not a win in that department. But if you're mostly using the fridge as just a plain old fridge, then it's a good one.

review_text:

HOWEVER...before the repair guy arrived I realized that the entire unit was warming up. The dripping was caused from the ice melting (and pouring out the dispenser, down the front of the fridge). The freezer contents were thawing and the milk and meat in the fridge section were spoiling. Helpful Whirlpool customer service suggested I "reset" the computer by unplugging and replugging in the unit. Surprise! The compressor had been off, which I didn't realize. The unit began cooling down again and I hoped it was ok. But when the service guy arrived the next day he read the temperature and said my fridge was 47 (I had it set at 33) and the freezer was 44 degrees (set at -1). According to him, the sealed system was flawed. They were going to need to replace the evaporator, compressor and all the freon. It would take a few days to order parts and be a long process to replace the entire refrigeration function of my 3-month-old fridge.
The AMAZING part: Lowes is REPLACING my unit (hurray!) within a day, the price has gone down so I'll get some $$ back. Hopefully it will not go into repairing the stupid thing in another few months. But I'm really proud of Lowes. Fingers crossed that I don't have a big piece of garbage in my kitchen.

review_title: Plastic Center Support for Veggie & Fruit Bins breaks apart
review_text:
We remodeled our kitchen in Feb 2012 and bought over 5K worth of SS appliances (and 5-year warranties) from Brandsmart in Deerfield Beach,Fl including this lovely-looking Whirlpool-Gold stainless-steel French Door Bottom Freezer refrigerator. Just 6 months later the plastic CENTER SUPPORT SNAPPED IN THE FRONT to cause the 2 vegetable/fruit bins it supported to 'fall' and become cockeyed (dropping inward, toward the center next to each other); this made the veggie bins hard to pull out and made the bottom DELI bin impossible to pull out (since the 2 veggie bins above it were now sitting upon the DELI bin below them).

There was no problem with Whirlpool Customer Service to send out a new plastic center support REPLACEMENT part since this was well within the 1-year warranty period from the Manufacturer (and the Brandsmart 5-year warranty period). Installing this part was easy and at first we chocked this up to 'infant mortality' where a somewhat defective piece of plastic had gone bad...(but we were WRONG!)...I say this because just 6 months after installing the REPLACEMENT part from Whirlpool, the same thing happened again...the same plastic center support SNAPPED IN THE FRONT to cause the 2 vegetable/fruit bins it supported to 'fall' and become cockeyed (dropping toward the center, and making the DELI drawer impossible to open).

Examination of the failing part shows a very weak engineering design concept in my opinion...that a 1/8-inch-thick piece of plastic that's about 1-inch wide,front to back could support the contents of not one, but TWO Vegetable/Fruit bins. Everyone knows that apples, oranges, pears, lettuce, lemons, and nearly every kind of fruit or vegetable has some WEIGHT that must be supported, and in this case the weight of a normal amount of veggies and fruits will cause the breaking failure of the plastic center support over time (6-months in my case). I have never owned a refrigerator with such a flimsy support system for the vegetable drawers or had to 'estimate' how many pieces of fruit or vegetables I could safely ADD to the two bins to avoid this CENTER SUPPORT SNAPPING failure due to their weight. So now I have an expensive piece of stainless-steel fridge that looks great on the outside but is very poorly designed inside with respect to the CENTER PLASTIC SUPPORT that really 'CAN'T SUPPORT' much weight in the vegetable/fruit bins at all.

To make matters worse when I called up Brandsmart Warranty services for a new veggie-bins center support the girl I spoke with told me "THIS ISN'T SUPPORTED BY YOUR WARRANTY TERMS AND CONDITIONS"- and that they would only support "ELECTRICAL AND MECHANICAL FAILURES of the fridge". When I questioned why a SNAPPING PIECE OF PLASIC THAT SUPPORTS TWO VEGETABLE/FRUIT BINS didn't fall into the MECHANICAL FAILURE category, she still denied my logic; when I asked to speak with a supervisor a man got on the phone and backed up the poor girl that first answered the phone... so I told the super I'd find a new place to shop the next time, and would never buy another Brandsmart Appliance or Warranty again! I reminded him that when I bought the FIVE-YEAR WARRANTIES for all my new kitchen appliances in January, 2012 the salesman told me they would cover "ANYTHING THAT WENT WRONG" with them...the Warranty Supervisor told me that I was "misinformed" and that I should have read the terms and conditions before purchasing the warranties. I told him that I'd believed their salesman to be an honest guy and there was no mention about 'not replacing broken plastic parts' within the appliances when he sold me the warranties. So much for Brandsmart Warranties!

The good news is that I was able to buy a replacement plastic center support part from a local appliance parts store for under $20 that included a "free replacement of the part for LIFE". I installed the new part and will now hope this replacement part will last more than the 6-month lives of the first two that broke! Honestly WHIRLPOOL, did you ever TEST for the breaking weight of this extremely flimsy plastic center support for your two vegetable/fruit bins before releasing this refrigerator for sale? In my opinion the only thing that will permanently repair this engineering flaw is a center support part manufactured from metal instead of the plastic part supplied. For this reason only I'm giving this refrigerator a '2-star rating' as the rest of it has been working fine so far. (knock on wood!!!)

product_title: Frigidaire FGHD2455LF Gallery 24" Stainless Steel Full Console Dishwasher - Energy Star
review_title: Poor quality - inferior engineering design and parts
review_text:
My wife and I were excited to receive our new dishwasher today, only to be sorely disappointed after opening the package.

The bottom rail system on this dishwasher is the epitome of why many people consider dumping their old dishwasher. It doesn't run smoothly and falls off the rail system the majority of the time. I'm surprised that after decades of one of the biggest pain points and complaints I've heard about old or shotty dishwashers is that the drawers get stuck, that Frigidaire would continue producing brand new mid-grade dishwashers with inferior parts and design in the rail system.

Even though the rail system was a major disappointment, we were just barely willing to accept this and keep the unit.

However, after further inspection of the unit, there was a glaring defect in the stainless steel front cover. In both upper corners, very detectible with just a glance, there was a major crease in the stainless steel sheet. It's as if during assembly of the unit, the front cover was forcibly compressed into a shape that it didn't quite fit into. This is an eye sore.

These are two major problems with the unit that we have seen. On their own, I might conclude this was a defective item. Finding these issues together on the same unit indicates to me that this is product is of poor quality; parts, design and manufacturing workmanship are substandard in my opinion.

We obviously returned this product and will not be looking for a replacement. Not sure if this is an indicator of all Frigidaire products, as I thought they were a reputable company. But I certainly will not be purchasing these types of items online in the future.

The only reason I gave this product as many as two stars is because we never did actually hook it up. Maybe it washes/dries dishes just fine, but we weren't inclined to install the unit to find out!

product_title: Frigidaire FGHD2455LF Gallery 24" Stainless Steel Full Console Dishwasher - Energy Star

product_title: GE Profile 27 In. White Built-In Convection/Thermal Wall Oven - PK956DRWW
review_title: Runs perfectly after over a year of use
review_text:
I am in love with this oven. Yes, I know that sounds weird, but I bake for a living and this oven is just the perfect piece of equipment for heavy baking/cooking.

Maybe I should have started off by explaining that this oven replaced my 17 year-old Viking. Baking with the Viking was always an adventure in temperature control-- easily fluctuating from 250-450. Still, that was gas and this Profile is electric. I wasn't sure how I'd feel about an electric oven, never having had one before. Having used it for a while I can't imagine ever using gas again.

The temperature is amazingly steady-- I have gauges in each of the ovens to keep track. The convection feature on the top oven is wonderful. Having never used convection before I was a bit leery of trying the feature at first. What I have found is that it does cook items slightly faster, but, more importantly, it seems to cook more evenly than the regular bake. I'm at about 7,800 ft elevation, so I usually alter recipes to a higher temp (about 25 degrees higher on average). I've found I don't need to do that with the convection feature.

The controls are clear and easy to read and understand. I like the fact that the control panel is easily cleanable. I do not care for the material that the handles are made from. It attracts dirt like a magnet. The Profile was more money than the other comparable double ovens (like Bosch) and I dithered endlessly before making the purchase. I can honestly say that this oven is a workhorse with no problems at all at over 1 year (knock on wood, of course).

review_text: While I don't use my oven daily, I do use it for a fair amount of baking so temperature control is important.  While I had to replace the control panel once already, I noticed recently when trying to bake small cakes that the temperature (based on a separate thermometer I had put in the oven once it seemed that things were not baking evenly) ranges 35 degrees above or below the set temperature.  Tired of messing with it - at this price the oven should be dependable.  Will not use GE Profile again.

product_title: GE PT916SRSS Profile 30" Stainless Steel Electric Single Wall Oven
review_text: I am greatly disappointed with my GE Profile single wall oven.  I would definitely not buy it again.  I think GE's quality control should be improved.  The temperature control is never correct.  I put in two oven thermometers that registered about 50-100 degrees below the temperature I set.  I was told by the warranty people that thermometers in the oven are not accurate assessments of the temperature of the oven.  It is just the food that tells you if your oven is off or not.  In other words when my scalloped potatoes for a dinner party came out raw after one hour, I then knew my temperature was off. After your food is overcooked or under-cooked then you know something is wrong they say instead of placing a thermometer in the oven.  That sounds ridiculous.  I just hope my other appliances work better than the oven.

product_title: Whirlpool WED4900XW
review_text: Like many other people, I usually research major purchases before I buy.  This Whirlpool dryer was highly rated among the sites I visited and the price was very competitive for the feature set. Delivery was as expected and I was called in advance to let me know when it would arrive.  I had no trouble connecting it and found that It has worked quietly and effectively so far.  It has all the usually-recommended features, like dryness sensor, end of cycle buzzer and a 'wrinkle guard' feature (it tumbles the clothes every so often after they are dry while the dryer is waiting for you to come and retrieve your clothes).  All these are options you can adjust yourself. There are other 'built in' features that I appreciate as well.  I like its large capacity for clothes. It has easily accommodated every load i have put into it.  I also like the size and placement of the lint filter. It is rather large and long and is accessible from the top of the unit. Unlike other dryers I have had, I never have any trouble cleaning all the lint out of the filter and I have not (up til now) ever seen the filter overloaded with lint.  I also appreciate that the door opens 'down'. This allows me to have additional surface area I can use when I am both putting in or taking out clothes. Of course these features are matters of personal taste but I have found them quite useful.  The entire experience has been very satisfactory!

product_title: Whirlpool WED4900XW
review_title: Hair and lint stay on clothes and in dryer
review_text:
We just bought this dryer about 2 weeks ago and for the most part I agree with the positive points mentioned in the other reviews: dryness sensor works well, 'wrinkle guard' feature is great, I like the pull down door. Overall a good inexpensive dryer.

But I am giving a three star rating due to my extreme disappointment regarding the lint filter. One of the reviewers points out that she has never seen the filter overloaded with lint. This is exactly the problem - the lint stays in the dryer and on the clothes!

This may be partly due to the fact that the fins on the inside of the drum are plastic, instead of metal. I find lots of lint and hair clinging to the plastic from static. It's possible using softener sheets in the dryer would eliminate the problem, but I don't like using chemical sheets and never had to with my old dryer.

I have several cats and the lint filter on my old GE dryer was always packed with cat hair and I even would use the dryer to de-fur stuff from time to time.

After using the new dryer a few times I was surprised to see how little cat hair was captured in the filter, so I inspected the drum, and lo and behold, the interior of the dryer was full of hair and fuzz! Now I know to clean it after a load, but what a pain, and there is still lots of cat hair left on clothes after drying. Not good!

The lint filter was below the door in my old unit - I wonder if the position of the filter in this machine makes it less effective. I really don't like the fact it is on top of the dryer - I tend to leave things on the dryer and it's a bother to move everything to clean the filter. Although the way this thing filters, I only have to clean it every 3rd to 6th load.

Luckily we are going to convert to gas soon, so I will be able to replace this dryer with another model. Any recommendations for good dryers (and washers) for pet owners?

review_text:

product_title: Whirlpool WED4900XW
review_title: Good "old school" clothes dryer; could do better at getting lint off clothes
review_text:
After reading hundreds of complaints in regards to front load washers and dryers reliability, not to mention price, my wife and I decided to stay "old school" with the traditional steel top load washer and flip-down-front-load dryer. As we recently moved, our old dryer was gas and the new house had no provisions or cheap way to retrofit the electric-only hookup. In addition, I wanted to keep the same style as the washer because I'm anal retentive about things matching. This dryer was the closest thing that would match our washer (the dark grey paint color has lightened on the new models). So far, I've found it to heat and dry the clothes better than any previous electric dryer I've ever used (owned or laundromat). The only complaint is that it doesn't seem to get all the lint like our Whirlpool gas dryer did - maybe its because this is a slightly larger capacity. However, it's an inconvenience, as small as it may be, and should be noted (as someone else has). Another gripe, but we purchased knowing that it didn't have the feature is the inability to use a drying rack.

Please note that with any electric dryer, you'll need to purchase and install an electrical cord that matches your house hookup and a dryer vent hose if you don't already have one.

product_title: LG DLG2141W
review_title: Good dryer with all the basics
review_text:
My wife picked this dryer out after researching for several days. We've used it for maybe a dozen loads of laundry so far, and are quite happy with it.

Pro:
+ reasonably quiet. I wouldn't call it silent, but neither is it so noisy that you can't watch TV. Best of all, the sound doesn't particularly carry and vibration is low.
+ sensor does a great job. Like any dryer it still gets confused if you throw towels in with the load, but with just clothes on their own, it does what you want, which in my case with normal dry, have the clothes 'barely' dry, rather than cooked to a crisp. Everything came out looking about the same size it went in, which is nice :)
+ easy to operate. When you look at the picture of the control panel it looks pretty daunting, but the reality is, it's just a couple buttons and a dial, with an inefficient way of showing your selection.
+ nice enough looking

Con:
- it's a little deeper than I was expecting, so it sticks out further from the wall.
- the control panel is unnecessarily complicated IMO. They could have figured out an easier way to convey the few settings
- it estimates the time left for drying. This would be handy if it actually did a good job with its estimates, but so far when I've looked it's been off by quite a bit.

Overall it's a reasonably good dryer. I'll update this review if any surprises pop up.
