product_title: GE GTWN5050MWS
review_title: Follow the directions and it's a great washer!!
review_text:
This washer is NOT the typical top loader agitator style washing machine. READ THE FURNISHED MANUAL AND FOLLOW THE DIRECTIONS!!!

We purchased this washer as part of a matched set along with the GE electric dryer [[ASIN:B0046MH7RC GE GTDN500EMWS 27" Electric Dryer with 7.0 cu. ft. Capacity, Multiple Drying Cycles, 4 Heat Selections, Sensor Dry, Wrinkle Care, Stainless Steel Drum and Quiet-by-Design Performance]]. We are VERY happy with this washer dryer set as a matched pair!

My list of points to keep in mind with this washer after our initial experiences:

1. READ THE FURNISHED MANUAL!!! And read plenty of reviews first!!
2. ALWAYS USE LIQUID HE DETERGENT for HIGH EFFICIENCY Washers!! Use anything else such as high sudsing powder detergent (is that really a word??) and you are likely to experience problems such as white detergent scum on the clothes!
3. Always add the appropriate amount of LIQUID HE DETERGENT, start the washer to begin water flow, then load and run as usual. (At least during our initial learning experience we used a small magnet to keep the switch activated so we can do this with the lid open - caution do NOT do this if you have cats, children or other small pets or absolutely anything else that can become harmed while the machine is running!!)
4. Do NOT expect to be able to add more clothes once the water level is set ie once the machine is running. The first time I tried this and restarted the washer it drained ALL the detergent water out first, then replenished the water level. Therefore my newly added liquid HE detergent was on TOP of the clothes, not down in the water where it belongs. LESSON LEARNED: just because it's a top loader, don't expect to add more clothes once the machine is running, same as a front loading washing machine more clothes cannot be added later once the machine is running and has water up on the seal of the door. (I called the GE answer center, they report once START is pushed clothes cannot be added to the washer at all since the auto-water-level sensing is the first aspect that completes.)
5. Noise level - this machine is a different technology than the old style agitator top loaders therefore makes a completely different sound when running and pauses during the cycle. It is not LOUDER than our old Amana, just different.
6. Balance - So far we have no experienced any balance issues, just be sure to load the wash AROUND the nubby "agitator", not on top of the agitator (same concept as a typical washer where you would NOT load clothes on top of the agitator either so on this machine just think of it as a shorter agitator!)
7. This washer has a stainless steel drum. This is a PLUS for dying clothes (I love to tie dye! - but I'm not certain this particular washer would be useful for dying clothes I will update once we try dying some items.)
8. Due to concerns with soap residue from ANY and ALL washers, we have always used the extra rinse (even with our old washer) and the extra spin (simply set the selector dial in between both). With this high efficiency unit we will be conserving more water than the typical household as this will save water on THREE fills, not just the typical two. If you are like us and have always used the extra rinse cycle, you will also experience further water use reduction.

As we have only washed a few loads and are still in the learning curve I will update this review in a few weeks once we have more experience.

Happy Washing!!

PS I gave this washer a FOUR star review simply due to trepidation over the learning curve on how to successfully load and run this washer - it simply is a different technology. If this machine proves itself over time I will likely upgrade this to a full FIVE star review. I could not give this washer five stars at this time since it is requiring a learning period which again is simply due to a different technology than the old standard agitator washers - and I somehow would feel better if there was an option to add MORE water... sometimes the amount of water just appears to be so low.. yet so far all the clothes are coming out perfectly clean.

GE Parts: 1-800-GE-Cares
GE Answer Center: 1-800-626-2000 Option 3 (Questions about operation, etc)

UPDATE Dec 2011: I have upgraded this washer to five stars since it has been functioning flawlessly and continues to prove itself worthy. If you "cheat" like us and use a magnet to cause the machine to run with the lid up, for whatever reason it often won't finish the final spin cycle. Stop using a magnet, close the door and the washer will continue to work flawlessly! ;-)

product_title: GE GTWN5050MWS
review_text:
We bought this for our Mom who is in her 80's, so simple and efficient operation was important. It was advertised as being quiet, and the spin cycle is amazingly unobtrusive, but it screeches during another part the cycle, which alarmed Mom at first because it sounded like it was having mechanical difficulty (i.e. not the sound of a smoothly operating appliance). Having to go out and buy a special type of detergent was also a thumbs-down (although I understand the reasoning behind it). People may have their distinct favorite brand after several decades of doing laundry, or they may want to use coupons or buy detergent on sale if on a limited income and not be obligated to a higher priced item.

One day I came over to did the laundry for Mom. I am fascinated with new technology so I peeked inside the tub mid-cycle trying to see how the odd-looking agitator worked. I was surprised to see barely any water in the tub, and the clothes on top were out of the water. I thought maybe I had forgotten to change the Load Size setting from small to large when I put in the load. Guess what? No setting for load size--it automatically fills so you can't add more water even if you wanted to. Then I noticed actually printed on the machine "It is normal for some of the load to be above the water level". Hello. Last time I checked, you actually have to have clothes IN the water for them to get WASHED and eventually, clean. The machine is advertised as high-volume capacity but what good is that when you can't fill the water up to that capacity? The concept is that the agitator will eventually rotate the clothes on top down into the water, and push the others out of the water. So, I get it, you use only half the amount of water necessary by making the clothes take turns getting in and out of their bath. But....are you really getting the clothes clean swishing them around in half the water, which is twice as dirty? And the clothes are getting washed only half the time that you think they are, because half the time they are waiting their turn to get rotated in?

At the end of the cycle, there was just a little bit of detergent residue (using the high efficiency detergent) but the clothes still had dog hair on them. I had to redo the load which of course, negated the energy star effects for both water and electricity. Maybe if you never check the laundry afterward and just throw it into the dryer, you'll land up with more lint because the extra stuff got blown out instead of washed out. I understand you might not get everything out if you have tons of dog hair in there but it's not like she owns a kennel or anything, she has one little 15 pound dog. I have 3 dogs and my Kenmore (that actually uses enough water to wash the load) gets everything fabulously clean. So I think this is an example of a company being so excited about their new technology that they put it into production right away so they could be the first on the market, but actually thought it was not important to test it thoroughly first. What were they thinking? Truthfully, I wouldn't even get this machine it it were at the Goodwill.

product_title: GE GTWN5050MWS
review_text: The tub broke loose (probably belt broke) and banged against the washer walls that I thought someone broke in my house!  I have a very small family, wash once a week, and it still broke down after only 3years. product_title: GE GTWN5050MWS
review_text: I purchased this washer as a replacement to an LG front load that "walked" across my floor in the spin cycle.  I was excited to get back to a top load machine.  That excitement ended quickly as this is the worst washer I have ever had.  After an average load, some of my clothes are not even wet because they were not agitated below the water surface. review_text:

Remember once you remove the oven door, and racks, turntable, it is about 150lb which is not too bad.

Observations: - Very quiet operations, the microwave is very powerful and very quiet. - the oven: I thought that the fan would be noisy and was very surprised how quiet it is for such a large convection fan. Heats a little slow, but, cooks much faster than my old oven. on 400 degree. I placed two frozen pizzas on two racks and both cooked well, for about 15 mins. - I like this one better than the non-profile; the oven door's glass is really dark unless you turn the light on. Looks real nice. One thing that I thought kind of odd, it has two clocks that you have to set separately, the interesting thing the bottom clock does not ask you for AM/PM unlike the top one! design flaw?. - I had good luck with GE in the past and I am sure there will always be parts for it.

product_title: Samsung DV520AGW
review_text:
We bought this dryer (Platinum/Stainless Steel color) DV520AGPwith the matching washer when my local store had it on sale, about half off Samsung list price.

The washer/dryer combo has been great. They do a good job of washing and drying. The dryer has left my close a bit damp but it's due to the cloths/sheets getting twisted and wrapped up, any dryer would do that and my old dryer did that. The middle of the heap is still a bit damp.

My biggest complaint was that the dryer was making a loud buzzing noise while running after a couple months of owning it. It seemed like every time it was heating it made the noise. I called Samsung about it and was told that it was normal operation but it seemed to loud and too frequent. After some discussions, it was agreed to send a repair person to look at it.

The repair man came and ordered a new gas valve and would come back 2 weeks later to install. I received a call out of the blue from Samsung support to talk about my repair ticket and they told me the noise was normal operation behavior. I went to the dryer and had them listen, they stated it was normal. I asked about the repair call, they stated he shouldn't do any repair. I asked how do I return the dryer because if it's this loud I don't want it. They told me to work with my local store for that. This made me quite upset that they are trying to tell me that this faulty unit was working as expected.

Regardless, the gas valve was shipped to me and the repair man came anyway. Supposedly, once the repair person is called, it's out of Samsung's hands, thankfully! He took 15min to replace the gas valve and the loud buzz went away. He stated it was definitely a gas valve struggling to work properly. He felt there will be a recall on gas valves soon from what he has been seeing. Thankfully this happened within my year warranty.

So, if your gas dryer is buzzing really loud through out the cycle, it could be a bad gas valve.

Shame on Samsung for trying to pass this off as "normal operation".

Otherwise, I'm pretty happy with the product and would recommend people to buy, just watch for the bad gas valve.

review_title: Does not rinse well, rough on delicate clothes
review_text:
I have high expectations for a washer because I use cloth diapers on my children. I was extremely happy with my previous traditional Kenmore Elite which did a fabulous job of getting diapers and clothes clean. When the agitator quit working the repair job was going to be a few hundred dollars less than new, so we thought we'd go with new. I wish I had spent the money on the repair.

I did lots of research and felt the GE was the best of old school and new. I wanted a top loader to be able to soak, but I did not want a locking lid. I wanted an agitator and I also wanted to be able to control the water level and the temperature. Despite the HE components like auto sense load and auto temp, this machine still lets you choose the water level so I thought I made the best choice. I also thought it was a great price compared to the new fancy machines with all the bells and whistles that I don't need in order to do a simple task like laundry.

When it was installed and I washed my first load, I was pleasantly surprised at how quiet it was. After a few loads however, it started making a bad squeaking sound that I knew was not normal. The big blue home improvment store that we bought it from was excellent about coming to replace it quickly. I could have chosen another machine, but I still felt this one had all the features that I wanted so I just got another one.

After a few more loads I had to figure out how to make the machine do what I really wanted it to do. Because of new government restrictions, hot is barely tepid. To get the machine to fill with all hot water from the water heater without getting diluted by cold water, I have to leave the lid up. The downside to this is if I forget to put the lid down, the load never starts. I've gotten use to it, but everyone once in awhile I forget long enough that the water cools down and I have to start all over. It's ridiculous to me. Hot should mean hot. I HAVE to wash diapers on hot and their version of hot is completely unacceptable.

To get the water level I want, I have to set the dial one to two loads above what I think it is. Large is really more like medium so if I fill the tub up with clothes, I have to select super to get as much water as I want. Don't change the dial while it's filling up because then the tub empties all the water and starts all over. Sort of defeats the water saving feature if you ask me.

So all of this was inconvenient and maybe annoying, but if it was cleaning clothes then I figured I could live with it. Wrong again. I was use to basic food or playground stains coming out with a little pre-treatment or something. Not with this machine. I have to put something through at least twice and I'm still not sure that the stain will come out. I've also had items like gym clothes that come out still smelling like sweat or a mixture of detergent and sweat. Yeah, gross.

It also cannot handle delicates. With my previous machine I could put in items that said hand wash and they would came out clean and in good shape. This machine leaves holes at the seam line in clothes that say to wash on gentle despite chosing the delicate cycle. I've also noticed that many of my kitchen towels and bath towels are starting to shred at the ends. Granted I've had some of these towels for years but I find it odd they ALL starting fraying after we got this machine.

The final straw with this machine is that it does not rinse well. My kids are not overly sensitive to detergents, but I've noticed that they have been scratching or are otherwise irriated after we've had this machine. I've noticed a difference for myself too. The biggest tell-tell sign is with diapers. It is very important that diapers are rinsed well so that leftover detergent doesn't irritate baby's skin potentially leading to a rash. Even when using the second rinse feature, or the fabric softener option, diapers are NEVER rinsed well. I can smell the detergent when I pull them out. And yes, I am using HE detergent. I've tried powders and liquids and the results are the same. I can run a load of diapers without new detergent and suds will float to the top of the water. To get my diapers as clean as they should be I have to run at least 3 hot loads while manually scooping out the suds. Consequently, I have grown to loathe this machine.

Now that we are expecting a third child I MUST have a machine that can handle cloth diapers. With three little ones, I will not have time to babysit this machine and scoop out suds. My wish list is still the same so the search continues. If you need a machine to do some heavy duty cleaning, keep looking. This machine can only handle ligth weight laundry and even then I'm not sure I would recommend it.

review_text:
This washer does a great job cleaning clothing and running quietly, while offering many settings to choose from. But I am the type of person who likes to run a regular cycle, then before it rinses, change the cycle to gentle and throw in a few items that need to be gently washed. If you do this with this 4250 model, it will drain out all your soapy water (wasting it) and then begin refilling your machine for a totally new cycle- your gentle cycle. I have spoken with GE technicians and repairmen to verify this and have been told, "You cannot change the cycle once it has begun."

If you like to have the option of changing the cycle, check out the 18, 180, and 2800 models.

Another caveat, if you open the lid a few times too many during agitation, to add a few items say that you found laying around, the machine usually will drain all your water and end the cycle. What gives with that? How is this efficient? I was told to use the "pause" button each time I want to interrupt the cycle to add laundry, but I was also told "you shouldn't be interrupting the cycle once it begins." Seems there are sensors (as opposed to 'mechanical' workings) that have a mind of their own. These sensors are set to end the cycle when there are too many interruptions.

I prefer managing my machine myself, but if you are the type that likes to load it up and leave it, then go for it, bkz this machine does a great job, runs quietly, and has lots of options for cycles!

We called back and spoke to Jeff and he said someone would be here at our home in 3-5 business days at 4:00 pm and would call to confirm and we should keep a log of all money spent at the Laundromat. I was here every day at 4:00 pm.
No call, no repairman.

I called back on Tues am Oct 16 to the corporate office to complain about the lies told to me by the Customer Service Dept about sending someone out to repair the Haier washer. Spoke to Karen who said she was the Vice President. When she was told about the runaround and the lies, she said she would call us back the same day in the afternoon at which time she said she would either find someone to fix the washer on the 17th, or would arrange to have a new washer brought to us and the defective washer removed.
No call, no repairman, no new washer, still have the old.

Karen said that if she couldn't find someone to repair the washer, she would start the process of MAYBE replacing the DEFECTIVE WASHER with a new one because she would have to get that approved. These empty promises change with every breath.
I am greatly surprised that Amazon would do any kind of business with this type of company. review_text:

I am ordering a new pump ($40) and will install it myself this time around, but I will not buy another Haier washer when I replace this one.
All in all, plus two stars for being an effective washer but minus three for ongoing drain pump issues. I expect I will be replacing that drain pump once every year or so until I replace the unit.

review_title: Be Careful...very, very careful with your money
review_text:
We bought this stove in 2010 for a newly remodeled kitchen project. It was bought from a national specialty store and took 4 weeks for the 1st delivery (incorrect stove delivered and picked up a few days later). The 2nd delivery came 4 weeks later and was broken when the delivery guys unpacked it. 2 weeks later the correct stove (undamaged) was delivered. Oh, by the way the warranty begins on the date of purchase not the date of delivery (per Frigidaire). About 9 months after the date of purchase we noticed the oven fan running an hour after the oven was shut off. A service call (under warranty) by one of the Frigidaire local service firms yielded a "nothing is wrong with the stove" verdict. In October of 2011 (2 months out of warranty) the ovens seemed to not be heating up. We placed a thermometer in them and found neither was heating to the set temperatures. In fact neither would go over 200 degrees. We goofed around with the adjustments as suggested by the owner's manual to no avail. We contacted a local dealer (thank God there are still some old school stores and repair guys) who agreed to have one of his repairmen take a look (our next and future appliances will be purchased there). After replacing the main control panel once it was determined that the stove was built with a flange that made contact with the wiring causing a dead short. Because the moron (licensed electrician) allowed a large breaker in the range position of my service panel, it would not "trip" off unless someone tried to wire NY City through my service panel. The result was that the stove was "partially functional" in that the burners worked and the oven came on but would not heat to temperature. Only dumb luck prevented a house fire. Of course this entire "discovery" is on my nickel. Parts are still on order and of course the response from Frigidaire is "well it is out of warranty you know." Thank you so very, very much. Never again... and no more Frigidaire products... EVER.
Oh did I forget to mention that when the oven(s) were working, the steam from cooking foods was directed to discharge on the left set of control knobs. The plastic is starting to discolor and we have used the stove for about 3 months of the 16 months we have owned it. Good luck if you bake (if your oven works that is).
Bottom line...spend your money wisely and buy something else.

review_text:
We came to own an Electrolux refrigerator (model EI23BC56IS8) that conveyed with our new home in March 2014. Per the sticker in the unit, it was manufactured in June 2011 (less than five years ago).

For the second time in two years, it stopped making ice. This time the technician slid the unit out to get access to the control board which revealed what you see in the attached picture. Yes, among the giant rust spot, is a chunk of ice. Doing a little research online, Electrolux refrigerators are subject to failures in the coolant line or insulation that can result in what we experienced - basically a hole. Since we came to own this fine piece of refrigeration through the purchase of our home (i.e., it was "transferred" to us), Electrolux is choosing not to stand behind its product to do anything about it. There are so much better refrigerators out there, please do not buy an Electrolux.

review_text: Had this fridge for 4 years. IT looks nice... but that's about it. My experience with Electrolux appliances have been horrible, from central vac, to my bar fridge to this fridge. The freezer door jammed within 3 months, rails replaced under warranty. recently the freezer defrost element stopped working so ice builds up in the condensor and blocks the airflow, resulting in a warm fridge. In diagnosing the problem, I realized that the freezer temperature is fake, there is in fact no thermometer in the freezer section, it just gets as cold as it gets, controlling the temperature of the freezer does nothing. Case in point, I had the freezer open and had a hair dryer blowing hot air on the ice build up in the condensor, after 30min when all the ice melted, I put everything back together and turned fridge on... guess what ? fridge said the freezer was at -18C... product_title: GE GFWH2405LMS
review_text:
Have had the GE 'Adora' front load washing machine for 5 years, and it has been one headache after another. The biggest problem, not counting everything on it rusting out, is the door seal, or 'boot'. Not only does this leak water, the design is so poor it allows socks, colorfast sheets, washcloths and the like to slip around the seal, and make their way to the pump suction. This in turn clogs the filter, does not allow the pump to pump out, leaves you with a washer drum full of both water, and soaking wet clothes, and the only remedy to clear the clog is to remove the filter cover, and, thanks to the miracle of gravity, all that water in the drum pours out the filter basket, and there you are, trying to catch it in a funnel and bucket arrangement, and trying to either swap out one bucket for another when it fills up before it runs all over your floor, or screwing the filter cover back on, which often results in a garden sprayer effect, causing water to go inside the bottom of the machine, and getting everything under the washer soaked. (sorry for the run on sentence, but if you do this just one time, you'll understand.)
If you have the pedestal, as I do, this constantly is filling with water, making it useless for storing anything but rubber duckies.
Even on it's best days, the pump fails to pump to the height in the specifications, making this washer unsuitable for most basement applications.
The washer rarely is able to crank itself up to full spin speed. I've tried running smaller and smaller loads, and that only seems to alleviate the problem somewhat. Not a lot of sense having a 'high capacity' washer if you can only fill it about 1/4 full.
To add isult to injury, this week, after discovering a flooded floor, found that the door seal is full of holes, rips, and tears and is leaking like a seive. I know I could take this piece o' junk apart, and replace the seal, but it just isn't worth the trouble, since all the same problems are still going to exist.
In short, run away from GE Adora.

review_title: A good value, but some details can be improved.
review_text:

Pros:
1. Very nice modern looks.
2. Huge usable volume in the refrigerating compartment.
3. Ice-maker is not in the freezer, thus eliminating odors in the ice.

4. Freezer generates a noticeable amount of frost.

It does not have a drawer for meats or dairy so I had to buy a bin for those foods as well. product_title: LG LMX25964ST 36 24.7 cu. ft. 4 Door French Door Refrigerator - Stainless Steel
review_title: Very Good Refrigerator, But Some Drawbacks.
review_text: The LG LMX25964ST 24.7 cubic ft refrigerator was recently purchased to replace my GE profile that went into cardiac arrest after 7 years.  A $600 dollar fix, that was too much for a 7 year old frige.  Having said that, I can tell you that this LG Refrigerator has performed as advertised.  A huge Refrigerator cabin was the real selling point for me.  It is both deep and and wide, providing more than ample room, for those large platters and pitchers.  The right side door has deep compartments inside the door, that can more than store your gallon milk containers and 2 liter bottles.  The blue tinted LED lighting is evenly distributed throughout the cabin.  The freezer also provides ample storage space, with the bottom pullout door being the deeper of the two.  I personally, like the idea of the Ice maker inside the left sided door.  Although it takes away rack space inside the door, it allows for more storage space in the main compartment or freezer.  Most Ice makers are located in the freezer, which means everytime you want ice you have to fetch it in the bottom freezer.  It is nice to have the ice inside the door, at eye level when you need it.  The filtered water system dispenses water and ice through front of the left door.  The water dispenses cold and fresh, and Ice can be allocated directly into your glass.  The ice however, is not crushed, but will dispense 3 to 4 half moon ice cubes at a time.  The refrigerator does have some drawbacks.  The water dispenser is a tad small, thus, a full size glass cannot fit into the dispenser unless you remove the bottom spill base which is easily done.  The water filter lasts about a year, and is easily accessible in the main compartment in the upper left side .  A simple screw on and off application.  The water filter comes with the appliance, but there after a year, the replacement goes for about $35-$40 dollars. The electric status board on top of the water dispenser will tell you when to change it.  It is basically a built in Brita filter system.  The frige comes with an audible alarm, that will sound if a door is left ajar for more than 30 seconds.  This comes in handy if you have kids.  The doors need to be shut physically, because they won't shut by them selves with a half hearted push.  The alarm can also be disabled.  Now back to my GE profile frige that died.  No matter what modern day frige you buy, I would recommend you get a 10 year extended warranty, which in my case was $200, or $20 per year.  It is not the compressors that usually fail. but these appliances are all computerized, and if a mother board goes, that is a $500 fix.  Not to mention everything else that could go wrong.  One service call will pay for itself.  Gone are the days when mom and dad purchased a frige and it would last 25 years.  Most sellers will tell you that you will be lucky to see 10 years out of them.  Having said that, I can tell you that I have been very satisfied with this purchase, and would recommend it to anyone looking to replace an older unit.

product_title: Bosch WTE86300USAxxis 3.9 Cu. Ft. White Stackable Electric Front Load Dryer
review_title: Hey, I think I figured out how to fix this POS...
review_text:
I recently moved into an apartment with this dryer, and like many other reviewers, I found it was completely worthless. According to the manual, this thing is actually designed to NOT completely dry clothes, since that supposedly damages them. However, I prefer my clothes to be mildew-free, so here's what I did to get this thing to properly dry my clothes:

-Stop trying to clean the sensors with vinegar. It's a complete waste of time--use the vinegar to clean your coffee maker or espresso machine instead.
- Next, open the panel below and to the left of the door and remove the plastic drawer-looking thing after twisting the two tabs on the corners. You won't be needing this thing anymore, but place it on top of the dryer or someplace nearby so it doesn't get lost/discarded. Someone else who wants their clothes to smell like mildew may want this at a later date....
- Next, don't close that panel door if you want to do laundry. Obviously, you can close it between loads, but you will always run the dryer with this panel open. If your dryer is in a closet with a door, carefully make sure the closet door closes without slamming into the dryer panel door when it is open. My unit is in a very small area and the closet door wouldn't close without hitting the panel door, so I cut a piece of string to a very specific length and then knotted it to make a loop so the panel door is open at about a 30 degree angle when looped around the panel latch and either of the metal pieces that make up the locking mechanism in the dryer door. This may take some trial and error, and you can do it anyway you want, but the panel door absolutely needs to be open when you're doing laundry. If you have a closet door, I'm just guessing you want that closet door to be closed, but obviously that is up to you.

- Next, take out the lint screen, remove any lint, and wash it with hot water and shake it off to dry. Even if it looks clean, it may not be, so rinse it with hot water.

- This next step is optional, but I found it severely reduced the "filter" light warnings I was getting. Turn the lint screen over and notice the screen mesh covers the hinged area in the base of it. Take a razor blade and cut through the screen at the base (i.e., between the plastic along the hinged base). This may not look like a big deal, but it will dramatically increase the airflow through the lint screen while still allowing the lint screen to function and collect lint. Again, this part is optional (and it does permanently modify the lint screen), but I found it significantly reduced the number of times that the filter idiot light comes on.

- For regular maintenance, I only wash the lint screen with hot water and shake it out to dry when the filter light comes on. I think the mesh is so fine that it gets clogged by stuff that's hard to see, so don't trust your eyes. When the filter light comes on, take out the lint screen, remove any lint, wash it off with hot water, and shake it to dry. Also, I used to rinse off the metal condenser thing in the drawer behind the open panel, but I don't think that matters, so I don't even do that any more, but if you run into any problems, you may want to rinse that off as well.

- Lastly, I always use the Regular/Cotton--Extra Dry setting, with the "Low Heat" push-button option selected. Unfortunately, it can take an hour or more, but it always dries my clothes that way. The clock is never right--it starts at 2:37 but then updates continuously and I'd say it takes about an hour or so, I haven't tried a lot of the other settings, but they may work as well.

Hope this helps. Feel free to add your experience/comments/thoughts/ tips below.

UPDATE 9/18/14
Now 10 months later and still working beautifully. The unit is quiet, consistent temperature (by thermometer). The stainless steel paddles for the ice maker and water have scratched a bit but they are METAL not PLASTIC and I can deal with that. The in the door ice maker does have a limited capacity but at the gain of no intrusion into the refrigerator compartment. If I am anticipating a need to a lot of ice for entertainment, I dump the ice into the ice bin in the freezer and viola, plenty of ice for the occasion. review_title: buyer beware on LG refrigerators & appliances
review_text:
Our LG french door with ice/water dispenser which cost us $2212.00 has been an eye opening experience. We've purchased other LG electronics and had good experiences and thought that this brand was reliable. Our 4 y/o fridge burned out a wire that blew 2 circuit boards in the ice/water dispenser. We paid $427 to replace both circuit boards before they figured out that the wire was burned & we also needed to replace the entire door for another $360. The repair man suggested that I ask LG to foot the bill for the door. LG service refused consider my request because it was out of warranty (the warranty only is 1 year)so I demanded to speak to a supervisor, It was only at this higher level that I finally got them to consider my request. They made me jump through hoops producing the original sales receipt etc and taking over 3 weeks to respond. LG finally conceded and replaced the door but that was only after I told them that I was going to tell everyone i knew not to purchase their appliances.

During the 3 weeks i was waiting for LG to make up their minds if they would help me or not, I began speaking with my friends about my experience. I found that almost everyone I spoke to who had an LG appliance that was out of warranty had failure of those appliances and had to replace them. It seems that LG is making their products to last through the warranty and then fail. Refrigerator condensers seem to magically fail only months after the warranty expires. I've spoken to people whose driers failed after only 6 months of use, and my friend with a 3 year old LG dishwasher said it sounded like it would die any second and she couldn't find an appliance repair that would service it when they found out it was an LG. It finally died 6 months later and she has replaced it with a GE. Another friend's LG microwave died a month after the 1 year warranty expired.

The lesson here is that although LG appliances will work wonderfully for the first few years you own them, you should expect that soon after your warranty expires you will find that the appliance will fail and you will be footing the bill for costly repairs or replacement. this is not such a big deal if it's a cell phone, but when you are spending $2,200 or more for an appliance you expect it to last longer than 4 years. I now fully expect that the compressor will fail on my refrigerator shortly after it is 7 years old (end of compressor warranty).

Even though LG finally did the right thing and replaced the door, It was only after I demanded to speak to a supervisor and demanded that they do something for me. I will never purchase another LG appliance and I'm warning you about this. Before purchasing LG appliances I suggest you talk to everyone you know and learn their experiences. I'm certain that you will begin discovering that many people have had similar experiences as I & my friends have had with LG.

review_text: I was very excited when buying this stove. As a fairly careful shopper, I read a number of print and online reviews, and finally decided that a LG LD3017ST stove was what I wanted. The lure of the double oven and the infrared broiler won me over my trepidations of a stove with 0 dials, all touchpad. We were still remodeling when we bought our shiny new stove, it was used less than a half dozen times before we moved in for good. After approimately 2 weeks of daily use the touch pad for setting the clock and oven functions quit working for the 4,7,9&0. Called LG as stove is under warranty. A week later a local service company umder contract shows up, tech is nice enough, but just takes my word for what is wrong with the stove, doesn't do any sort of "running it through it's paces" but does ascertain that the touchpad does not in fact, work properly. Tech calls LG, they tell him what part he needs, he tells me someone will be back to install the new part. Over a week, different tech, installs part ( new touchpad), still doing the same thing. LG puts him on hold forever, tech finally leaves, says someone may come back sometime, someday. ( I waited 5 hours for him to arrive on that day!) My wife and I go into Home Depot where we purchased the stove, they tell us it's between us and LG. Am 3 weeks and waiting without a functioning $1500 stove. Have bought appliances from Best Buy and Lowes without issue previously. Lesson learned, LG does not back defective products in a reasonable fashion. And don't buy large ticket items from Home Depot. If I had bought the same stove from a certain local retailer, they would have sent their own techs out to take care of the problem and I have found them to be far more knowledgable about their work then the techs working for the company doing service work for LG. It would have cost me another $100. Stupid. Stupid. Price is not everything, and I KNOW that, just tried to save some $, since the remodel was running higher than planned. As a respected craftman in the trades ( residential construction) I will have ample opportunity to help others from making the mistakes (LG and Home Depot) that I have made.

review_title: COOKTOP STOPPED WORKING IN LESS THAN 1 YEAR! Lg Electric Double Convection Oven...THINK TWICE before YOU BUY
review_text:
Lg Electric Double Convection Oven w/ Infrared Grill and Smooth Cook Top 5 Burner: There are 5 smooth cooktop areas for cooking set under the glass cooktop...I've found them easy to use & much easier to clean up then the old style coils and they glow this cool looking orangy-red color when hot; be sure to apply your cooktop special coating supplied upon shipment/delivery prior to using your cooktop heating elements...I found that out after reading the manual. Simple to use the plus/minus settings to adjust heat setting; further the elements can be adjusted in size for larger or smaller pots/pans. Reads "HS" for "hot surface" to remind you not to touch when still hot from use!
The smaller top oven section has 2 modes (No convection mode in the smaller top oven): speed grill/broil & regular bake mode. The inferred grill/broil is excellent for grilling steaks, fish & poultry with a nice crisp crust to it while retaining the juices as well being faster by about 1/4 less cooking time then a regular oven/broiler. This upper oven section also does regular "bake" mode which is very convenient if you don't want to heat up the larger lower oven and maybe just want to bake a pizza or something of low profile...very nice..I use this section the most ; )
The larger lower oven has "regular bake" and "regular broil" modes as well as "2 convection modes", for "convection baking" and "convection broiling". Convection means the oven utilizes a "fan" located inside the lower oven's back wall to evenly distribute the heat which prevents hot and cold spots inside the oven...resulting in shorter cooking time and a nice crispness to the outside of your meats & poultry, etc while preserving the flavor, juices and tenderness inside foods.
There are also several other features/modes on both oven sections that I have yet to try, they include "Kids Meals", "Favorite" and "Warm"...I haven't been interested enough to read up on them yet...I want to get the basics down before trying these other settings.
You adjust both of the oven temperatures by touching the different "1-2-3-4-5-..etc" touch pad numbers to enter in your selected oven temperature; if you use the "convection" modes (bake or roast)only found in the larger lower oven, it will automatically adjust the temperature downward to accommodate for the higher more even heat distribution the convection modes provide. Convection baking & broiling require less cooking time because of the more even heat distribution...no need to turn meats or cakes and other dishes...but I still check frequently while getting used to this new oven.
The glass to the oven doors has a slightly pinkish/rosey hue or "rainbow effect" as this is an "oxide coating" that's applied during manufacturing to "redirect the heat inwards" and prevent heat loss through the glass ports/windows.

7/24/2015 UPDATE: Cooktop burners NOT working...just short of being 1 year old! The burner was clicking at a rapid rate yesterday...but this morning...not turning on at all! NOT HAPPY!

review_text: I have used this freezer for 6 months now. It was purchased to be converted to an ultra low energy chest type refrigerator. Using an external beer thermostat that can handle the lower temperatures of refrigeration, you plug the chest freezer into the external thermostat and then plug the external thermostat into the wall socket. When the desired temperature is reached, the power is cut off to the freezer, essentially making it into a fridge with a huge amount of insulation. This type of conversion uses about 140 watts of power a day vs 2500 watts of power per day with my upright fridge and requires no modifications to the chest freezer. The chest freezer itself is high quality low power and I would recommend it to anyone who wants a small freezer. By the way, based on Killowatt meter readings, a freezer that is outside in the garage during the Colorado winter uses about half the energy of a freezer in a heated space. I state this because many places on the internet state that freezers do not work properly in very cold temperatures and actually use more energy, but this is completely false. I have tested it with two different  freezer models.

review_title: good product but beware the poor factory warranty service
review_text:
Purchased the matching washer and gas dryer in December 2009 at the local Home Depot. All this time (now is November 2011) I have used them only for basic washing drying of cotton based laundry and both units worked great until 4 weeks ago. I cannot comment on the fancy new features because I have never used them.
Four weeks ago I open the dryer and strong smell of burned electric wires comes out. The shirts are shredded with large holes as if burned by the iron. Inside the dryer, the stainless steel drum is covered with a blue/gray film that cannot be washed away with a wet cloth. Oh well, stuff happens and that is why I purchased the 4-year extended warranty
And that is where the problem starts. The current warranty provider is A&E Factory service and that is where the problems start: nobody picks up the phone at the other end. After a few days of unsuccessful calling I drive to the Home Depot and they dial the same number but this time somebody actually answers. Coincidence? You be the judge when that happens to you!!!!. Of course the next available appointment is a week away, technician shows up, sees the damaged drum, can't find the cause but nevertheless orders a replacement drum. Another week goes by and the replacement drum is at my house. Service technician shows up a few days later and upon opening the package finds that the new drum is crushed and therefore unusable. Not a problem! He orders a new one to be delivered immediately and promises to come back when the replacement to the replacement is back. The replacement drum does arrive 3 days later but the technician forgot(!!!) to make the appointment in his busy schedule. Now I am waiting for the next appointment a week from today. And the only thing I know is that he will replace the drum not fix the problem that caused the original drum to burn my clothes. Which of course begs the question: How many more drum replacements are there in the future before (if ever) the actual problem is identified?
So let me draw a line, $2500 invested in washer-dryer and extended service plan, $300 worth of damaged shirts, one month of tracking to the nearest Laundromat. And the ordeal is not over yet.
Do you think it is worth your pretty cash? I thought so 2 years ago but the factory service from A&E is definitely a deal breaker.
Next time I will just buy the cheapest washer-dryer machines and never again buy the extended service plan. When they break down just take them to the curbside and get new ones. It's got to be better than this.

review_title: Works like it should, but it still has a few gotcha's
review_text:
Pros: This cook top has a lot of nice features, and they all work just fine. I also like the fact that there are no knobs or anything sticking up that can break off rendering one of the burners useless. The Warmer feature of the unit is a nice touch, and even though we got the 30" unit, there is plenty of space to use all the burners without issue. The touch on/off feature and touch settings have a small learning curve, but quite easy once you got it. This unit has a fan that blows upwards to cool it during operation and come on from time to time, nice but kind of loud.

Cons: The burner area has got to be the most disappointing part of this unit in operation. (I say that because there was an even bigger disappointment overall that I'll get to a bit later.) The burners are the same glass surface as the rest of the surface. I shopped for this one, and didn't notice or didn't think anything of it during operation. However, you should be aware that if you move, shake, rotate, or do any type of movement of the pot/pan on the glass surface, it will scar the surface. The directions state this right out of the box, so be careful while using it! The Push on/off button. While you must press and hold to turn the unit on (which isn't a big deal), it does have a tendency to turn on while you clean the surface, that doesn't require you to press and hold. Seems odd, but it has happened to me more than once. So again, pay attention to this as well. The only issue about this is the sound it makes. Now, for my biggest disappoint, well there is a housing all around this unit, and even though my hole from my previous 30" unit fit just fine, this housing adds about 3/4 of an inch, so be prepared to cut your counter top to get it to fit. Additionally, they also included locking tabs on this housing, and if you ever want to lift or take this unit out again, you better remove those tabs, because it will lock it in tight! I removed mine. Other than this, the electrical hook up was a snap.

Warmer Function: Updated 11/26/2015. Took this long to finally have a need to use this feature. Don't let the wording on the unit fool you. You must read the manual to get this feature to work. On the device itself, it has a pad that says "Warming Zone", well this isn't for the Warmer Function of the unit. The warmer function of the unit is every other pad but this one. Seems dumb to specially print "Warming Zone" on one pad, and it is the only pad that isn't used for this feature. Other than that gotcha, the Warmer Feature worked perfectly.

Overall: This is a good overall unit, and I'm hoping it will last as long as the old GE. I can recommend this unit as a good buy, so long as you are prepared for the gotcha's I mentioned above.

Good Luck!

product_title: GE DCCH480EKWW 24 Ventless Condenser Electric Dryer with 4.0 cu. ft. Capacity
review_text:
I've owned this dryer for about a month now and am very happy with it. I spent months researching and hemming and hawing about buying a condenser dryer to replace my traditional dryer. I purchased a condo year ago and despite it being sold as having a washer/dryer hook-up, I learned that the dryer was venting into the condo and I had to use a bucket system in order to keep the lint from floating around my house. Running the dryer was miserable, but I couldn't find a condenser dryer that had decent reviews so I held off on buying one.

Finally, I got fed up with the bucket system and gave this GE a chance despite the lack of reviews. I couldn't be happier with this dryer. I was expecting the worst, but this dryer turns out to be great.

Drying clothes takes longer than a traditional dryer, but this dryer is definitely able to get clothes completely dry. I would estimate a large load takes about 2 hours to dry completely. Usually, the dryer stops before the clothes are completely dryer. Then, I switch to a manual setting to give it an extra 20-40 minutes of dry time. The clothes come out completely dry using that method.

The dryer has a bunch of settings and it's simple to select which ones you want to use. The link trap is large and works well. I have this dryer connected to my washer's drain, so the condensate goes down the drain, but you can set it up so the water goes into a tub that can be emptied into a sink.

This dryer is smaller than most vented dryers, but it works for me. It can fit a king sheet set, but not a king sized quilt.

I purchased this dryer with the matching washer (WCVH48). I'm also happy with the washing machine. With a condenser dryer, if you have an older washer, you'll likely want to replace it since the spin speed of the washer is important in drying times. The matching GE washer spins at up to 1400 RPM. This whisks a lot of the moisture out of the clothes before they even reach the dryer. When washing delicates, I set the spin speed lower, but do fewer clothes in a load, otherwise the dryer has a difficult time getting everything dry.

The dryer does emit dry, tepid air into the house. Unlike other condenser dryers I read reviews for, this one doesn't release hot air into the home, so it can be used year round.

Overall, I love this dryer and am so happy I made the switch from a traditional dryer. If you need a condenser dryer, this one seems to be great. However, just be aware of what you're getting when you buy one of these dryers. If you have the option for venting outside, I think a traditional dryer would be better, but if you don't have that option, this GE is an excellent choice.

review_title: It works, but total pain to work around "smart" sensors, stick to timed dry
review_text:
The dryer does eventually get clothes dry but you have to use timed dry. So all of the whiz bang programs are completely worthless.

I moved into a new building with new appliances so I am the first user. The dryer has been in use for 3 weeks as of this review.

The accompanying washer is also wretched.

When you chose a drying program, say "cotton" it pops up the temperature, adjustable, and the dryness sensor, NOT adjustable. It also shows you expected time to complete the cycle. Using a cotton example, the machine states high temp, dry for wetness sensor, and time 1:20. So, imagine my surprise when I came back to the dryer in 45 minutes to find the load "done."

The clothes are not dripping, but no one in their right mind could call them anything other than damp - imagine 15 minutes walking to work in a light but steady summer rain . . . without an umbrella. You aren't quite dripping, but you are definitely damp.

So not only had the sensor shut off the dryer before time elapsed, but it wasn't even accurately sensing dryness. Boo.

If you try to run the cotton cycle again, it will shut off even faster. Damp is what this dryer considers dry. Poorly designed. The clothes are entirely too wet to fold and put away. They would need another few hours to open air dry. Never mind that the point of a machine dryer is to erase the need for open air drying....

None of the programs seem to allow you to override the wetness sensor. Stick to timed dry.

review_text:
I purchased this washer (less than 2 weeks ago) at a major discount home improvement center, along with the matching dryer, and they comp'ed the pedestals (to match another discount electronics store). I've always had good experiences with LG before, so chose it over a Whirlpool/Maytag similarly priced.

I wish I hadn't. The washer doesn't use anywhere near enough water to carry the dirt out of the clothes. Using the "water plus" feature doesn't add much more. In fact, at the end of the prewash cycle with "water plus" turned on, and a full load of jeans, sweat shirts, wear guard work pants and tee-shirts (work clothes), some of the items weren't even wet yet. The "Load Sense" indicated the load was only three-quarters full, even though nothing else would have fit in the washer. Stopping the washer and re-starting it sensed the extra weight of the somewhat wet clothes, so the second pass "load sensed" as full. But the clothes still came out dirty at the end of the 2 hour and 20 minute wash with pre-wash and "water plus".

Also, you can't use "water plus" and program any extra rinses. Setting one cancels the other. So if you want the extra water, you have to run a wash, then run a "rinse and spin" cycle after the wash finishes.

I called to complain, and they did send a tech out in two days, good turn around time. But the first thing he did was fill the washer on a Large/Bulk load instead of normal clothes. The manual indicates Large/Bulk is for things like pillows, bedspreads, comforters, slip covers, etc., not normal clothes. Also, the spin and water temps available on that cycle are restricted. So by the time he tried to test for my original problem (dry clothes at the end of pre-wash), the clothes were already wet. When he called LG to find out about the "water plus" cancelling the extra rinse, and vice-versa, they said that was what it is supposed to do.

Will I return it? Probably not. Will I buy another LG appliance. Definitely NOT.

UPDATE: After two service calls, the second one from another company, it still doesn't completely wet full loads by the end of the pre-wash. And it usually "weighs" a full load as only being three-quarters (load sensing). The second service company did replace the water level sensor, as they agreed it doesn't take on enough water. But that only raised the water level about an inch, still not anywhere near enough to wet the clothes at the center of the washer. product_title: LG WM2350HWC
review_title: A front-loader is nothing like a top-loader...however, the LG is great!!
review_text:
Its a washing machine, nothing magical. I love it. Quiet, and it washes my clothes like it is supposed to do. User-friendly and moderately priced as well.

First of all, you have to educate yourself about front-loader washing machines. They are designed to NOT fill up with water like old top-loaders do. That is why they are more water efficient. Top-loaders filled up with water and cleaned clothes by agitating; front-loaders filled up with just enough water, and the clothes rub against themselves (friction, like you would do hand-washing) to clean.

Second, you MUST leave the door open so it can air out. As with anything where water will be sitting, mold and mildew will soon follow. If you see reviews about people's clothing smelling like that, its because they 1) probably shut the door immediately and do not allow the water (hot or cold) to air out. They also probably never clean the rubber seal, and underneath the seal, around the door.

Third, there is a valve/hose that has to be drained out every other wash cycle, as well as a filter/catch-all that needs to be checked frequently ,too (for coins, earrings ect). If you do not drain the house often, the water will get backed up and that is not good.

If you aren't willing to take on the extra work, don't buy a front loader. If you think that leaving the door open so the washing machine can air is hazardous, buy a top-loader. While some negative reviews are serious issues, a lot of people are just lazy and don't use common sense. If you think you might be interested in a front-loader, ask people you know if they have one, how they like it, what brand they have, ect. A lot of stores also have return policies, so if you are not satisfied with the washing machine you can return it.

review_title: Super Powerful BTUs, Grates Stain Easily.
review_text:
This Whirlpool cooktop is probably about average in quality and ability compared to its rivals. I bought it because it has rather shallow undercounter needs, needing only 4" below the top, allowing for a drawer below the cooktop. Plus it was inexpensive.

Pros: Super powerful burners. White enamel cooktop easy to clean: simply pull off knobs and remove grates to completely clean the cooktop surface. Immediate ignition when lighting the burners. Shallow undercounter dimension.

Cons: The grates easily stain and are impossible to clean completely. In a year of cooking, these grates will be blackened and look like crap. Really disappointed in the quality of the grates. Also, the smallest BTU burner is placed in the front left. That's fine if you need a slow simmer frequently, but for us, we use the medium BTU output burners all the time. Unfortunately, both are placed in the back of the unit, making it a bit of a stretch to reach over taller pans and inconvenient when frying/sauteing. Why not simply use the high output burner or simmer burner? Because they're at the extreme ends of the spectrum: the lowest setting on the high output burner is almost too high, while the highest setting on the simmer burner is too low.

Any cooktop in the $400 range is going to be of middling quality, so we should have expected some tradeoff between price and quality. But geesh, the basic components of cooktops hasn't changes in decades. One would think Whirlpool would have gotten a non-stain coating on the grates right by now. It was such a pain to install that we'll simply keep the unit and not return it, awaiting a full kitchen remodel to replace.

product_title: Whirlpool WET3300XQ 8.4 Cu. Ft. White Electric Washer/Dryer Combo
review_text:
I took delivery of mine (from a local dealer) on December 31st of 2014. The FIRST one was delivered the previous Friday, that one's washer did not work at all. Yes, it was brand new. The second one works, but don't buy one until you read this entire review.

The washer is a failed attempt at saving water. I have no clue how any engineer or marketing team could be this stupid, but I have a feeling the WET3300 is not the only dud out there - since it uses the same pressure switch as many other models, and it is the pressure switch (and how it is configured in the WET3300) that makes this washer so awful in performance.

The washer, when set to "LARGE LOAD" will only fill with 6.5 inches of water. If you load this thing like a normal top loader, it it not going to perform well. Running small loads, it works fine - but read on.

The rinse cycle is horribly designed. On the "LARGE LOAD" setting, the tub fills with only 3.5 inches of water. This means the rinse is not complete (I have read reviews where people said they had to rinse twice with one of these, I see what they mean.) But there seems to be a way around this - liquid fabric softener, with so little water, will stain your clothing. So, for those who use liquid softener, Whirlpool put a switch on the control panel. By leaving the Fabric Softener switch on, the system fills to 6.5 inches on rinse!

If you only load the machine tub 1/2 full, run the machine on "Large Load" setting, and run with the Fabric Softener switch on at all times, you will likely be happy with this machine. Doing this, the machine is effective in doing one thing: Saving space. IT does not save water because you can't load the machine very much - but it DOES save space. If you have a family, htis is not the machine for you! A single person (like me) or maybe a couple can get by with it - but you will never wash blankets or large items in this machine.

If you really want to save water, but a front loader - they do the job of saving water AND cleaning clothing very well. The top loader, let's face it, is on it's way out. As I said before, the pressure switch in this machine is the same as many others -so either it is employed differently in other machines (likely) or else all new top loaders are junk. I simply don't know.

Beautiful, until you use it! I have had this cooktop for about a year and though it was gorgeous when new it has since proven to be a very poor choice. I upgraded from my 30 year old electric coil stove top which served to cook many batches of homemade jam and soups and stews, to this gorgeous black mirror finish top. While the top cooks well it is impossible to keep clean, scratches easily and is discoloring at the burners! Water, food or anything that spills over or drips on the top becomes burned on and usually requires the baking soda and vinegar treatment and often a razor blade scrapping to remove. Reading several sites about these cooktops I found warnings about spilling sugary substances on the top, but in my experience anything can become a problem. I ridded myself of my old pans, buying a rounded edge pan with smooth bottom to minimize scratching, but I seem to get a new scratch every time I use this top. Any moisture on the bottom of the pot discolors the top, if the spoon you are using drips you have a new burned substance to scrape off.
The provided plastic scrub pad is nearly useless at removing residue, the ceran cleaner doesn't actually buff the top, just cleans it a bit, and the discoloration at the burners is irreversible.
I think this cooktop has significant drawbacks and I can't wait to get rid of it. Spending 30 minutes trying to clean the top after each use is not my idea of an upgrade. My friend has a ten year old GE with their grey flecked top that is miles ahead of this top for ease of use and maintenance.
Okay, buy it if you wish, I tried to tell ya! I wish someone had told me!

review_text:
Our 17 year old 24" GE wall oven/microwave had a catastrophic failure and new parts are no longer available. I chose this 27" wall oven/microwave because: 1-It would fit in the old kitchen cabinet with some modification, 2-Electrolux is a good brand, 3-The reviews (although only a few) are good, 4-The price was very good, 5-Free shipping.

This unit weighs 250 pounds so requires at least two people to put it in place (I had to widen the old cabinet opening and expand it by lowering the bottom of the compartment about 3"). I got it installed a few days before Thanksgiving so wanted it use it to roast our turkey using the "Perfect Turkey" setting. We baked a cake first to make sure everything was working properly. The turkey should have taken about 3 hours but it stopped cooking after about an hour-and-a-half. We continued to cook the turkey on the regular roast mode. When I eventually carved the turkey I discovered the problem. When I inserted the probe I was careful but the tip of the probe went all the way through the meat and just into the cavity where the stuffing was. The probe measures temperature and stops the cooking when 180 degrees is reached. The stuffing got hotter sooner so the cooking stopped sooner. The lesson, make sure the probe is inserted properly so that the tip is in the thickest part of the meat and isn't touching bone or in an area of fat. The probe should in only as far as necessary so that the tip of the probe is at the thickest part of the meat. The location of the tip of the probe is critical. You may want to try cooking a roast before you try the "perfect turkey" setting because it would be easier to place the probe properly in a roast.

The oven itself was well packed but tape residue was left on surface. I sprayed WD-40 on a soft paper towel and the residue came right off. Of course this left an oil film that had to be removed with a mild solution of soap and water on a soft paper towel. All of the labels on the doors peeled off easily except one. I had to use a painters/window washers blade to gently remove that large label. I got the scraper, which uses a one-sided razor blade, in the paint section of Walmart for about $3.

The microwave works well but a jet of air blows out the front while cooking and for about two minutes after it finishes. This is somewhat annoying since it blows in your face or hair and is rather loud.

Nonetheless, we are happy with this product. It is stylish, has advanced electronic controls, works well and is a great replacement for the old oven. Anything larger than 27" would have required a larger cabinet and major changes to adjacent cabinets and counter-tops. I'll do an update if I discover any new issues or features. Oh, it appears that this model is no longer being produced but there is a similar 30" model which wouldn't fit in our old cabinet.

review_text: We bought this dryer after first asking for the next model down, the DV330AEW.  This one, the DV331AEW, has "steam technology," which is really just a water connection that allows a fine mist spray into the hot dryer.  Having tried it, I must say it really works.  I have plain cotton shirts that wrinkle a lot, and have always needed thorough ironing after being thru a dryer.  Using the "Refresh" cycle, 15 minutes with a small water (steam) spray, all I had to do was touch-up iron the collars & pockets.  In addition, there is a 90 minute "wrinkle prevent" option that tumbles clothes every few minutes and keeps lots of wrinkles from setting in.  Installation is easy, but still a few comments.  The dryer specification says it is 38.6 inches tall.  (We bought the one without the booster drawer underneath.) Really, with its plastic feet, it is 40 inches.  No big deal?  It was for me, as we had already built a counter that had exactly 38.65 inches clear, so I removed the big plastic feet and put a square of 1/4 inch plywood under each corner.  Samsung furnishes water hoses and a wye fitting to get cold water from the washing machine faucet.  It would have worked OK, but to reduce the clutter, I ran an extra water faucet from the crawl space and up behind the dryer.  The dryer's lint filter is well-designed and has all rounded corners to avoid catching clothes, which had been a real problem with our old dryer.  It also has a door over its lower half, which avoids spilling lint while removing to empty it.  By the way, as many people have already learned, some shopping around gets better prices: the vendor I bought dryer from was asking $859.00

When I hear the inevitable thump thump thump of the created wad of fabric, I go shake it out again only to hear it wad up again. Woe to me if I am not right there to monitor. I found a mega wad of several items of clothing yesterday, wound so tightly that I could barely get them unwound. This after the inevitable wad of sheets that I didn't have the time to monitor because, I don't know, I have a life with kids and dogs?? I wish I had thought to look up these issues when the thing was new--others are reporting the same exact thing. I'm not in any way overloading the machine--ONE set of California king sheets, or ONE king sized blanket, folks. Not a log jam. review_text:
This dryer takes forever to dry laundry. First of all, the sensor dryer doesn't work. When wet items are on the sensor dryer cycle, the dryer shuts down after a few minutes and the clothes haven't been dried at all. So despite all the fancy settings on this dryer, there's only one that I use: Timed Dry - HIGH - usually for one hour...and a majority of the time, even after this first hour, the load STILL has to be dried longer. I'm not overloading it, and sometimes there's only four or five items, but no matter what, the dryer time is so long. I haven't even bothered to try the stream dry because I don't expect it to work anyway. If it wasn't too late to return this, I would return it.

Also, once you turn on the dryer and choose a setting and hit "start", it's impossible to change the setting (for example, to change it from "medium heat" to "high", or to change the drying selection. To change it, you have to completely turn off the machine, turn it back on, and then select "high" instead, or turn the dial. Also, once your load is finally dry, the dryer completely turns off as soon as you open the dryer door. So if you want to put in another load, you have to then turn it BACK on again. It's not a very smart machine. I totally regret retiring our old Whirlpool dryer (which still worked, and dried clothes VERY well compared to this one, but my husband wanted a newer-looking dryer to match our new washer).

product_title: Whirlpool 3.5CuFt Top Load Washer 5 Water Levels Direct Inject System with Dual Action Agitator
review_text:
Either they have the incorrect picture or incorrect model listed here. I own a Whirlpool WTW4910XQ(0) and I can state they do not match up. See my customer Pic.

The following review is a copy from my review at at C o s t c o w e b s i t e where I paid about 1/2 the price listed here.

I would like to address the one comment by a reviewer who wrote that he/she was unable to add cloths after the machine was started. Unless I have a newer model, I am able to on mine by pressing the START button. Whatever cycle the machine is in it stops and unlocks the lid. Press the start button again and proceeds on the cycle it was in. Press and hold the Start button for three seconds, and it cancels whatever cycle it is in.
Now to the details. The group of switches on the far left is the Load size, ranging from EX Small-Small-Med-Large and Super. Next is the Temperature control which has the settings of Cold-Cool-Warm and Hot. On the right of that group is this odd Fabric Softener On or Off with the option of an Extra Rinse . Fabric softener is dispensed from inside the agitator
The large dial to the far right is the washing cycle with Normal Heavy-Regular and Light and Casual Normal -Regular and Light.
Two interesting features also on the Dial is the Drain & Spin and a Rinse & Spin.
Drain and Spin is for thick items like comforters and towels than you may want to remove excess water before you place in the dryer. There is no water used in this function
The Rinse and Spin is a great option for me if you have pet hair or sand in your laundry and want it to go through an extra rinse cycle.
Now my machine has two options that are now displayed or mentioned in the manual and that is a Soak cycle and a Super Wash.

Laundry tip # 1: To retain the color of newly purchased clothes add 1 cup white distilled vinegar in the agitator (the fabric softener dispenser) and set to RINSE & SPIN or do what I do and save an old 1 gallon milk jug add 1/2 cup vinegar and fill the jug with cool water. Place the new dry garment(s) in the washer, pour the vinegar-water solution over garment(s) and set washer to DRAIN & SPIN.

Laundry tip # 2: Do you ever get those dark oil-grease stains that are almost impossible to remove from Laundry? Purchase a can of liquid lighter fluid and pour a small amount on the stain, enough to cover and wash as usual. I can almost guarantee those stains will come out.

The only complaints I have with this model is that there is no detergent dispenser. The manual just calls for you to dump the detergent in first then add then add your laundry. Second complaint is the small tub. Smaller than my last washer.
Over all I am fairly pleased with my machine . It cleans sufficiently; I would purchase again.

Update: I have two corduroy shirts that are a lint magnet. I put them both in the washer and ran the Rinse-Spin cycle. Most of the lint was removed (about 95%). Nice option to use.

Features:

Normal - Regular Cycle
Normal - Light Cycle
Normal - Heavy Cycle

Other uses for White distilled vinegar in laundry.

Prevent lint from clinging to clothes by adding 1/2 cup white distilled vinegar to the wash cycle.

To remove soap residue that makes black clothes look dull use white distilled vinegar in your final rinse.

Get stained white socks and dingy dishcloths white again. Add 1 cup white distilled vinegar to a large pot of water, bring it to a rolling boil and drop in the articles. Let soak overnight.

Some stains on clothing and linens can be soaked out using equal parts milk and white distilled vinegar.

Before washing a mustard stain, dab with white distilled vinegar.

Attack spaghetti, barbecue, or ketchup stains with a white distilled vinegar and water solution.

Remove perspiration odor and stains on clothing, as well as those left by deodorants, by spraying full-strength white distilled vinegar on underarm and collar areas before tossing them into the washing machine.

Forgot that you left wet laundry in the machine and it now smells moldy? Pour a few cups of white distilled vinegar in the machine and wash the clothes in hot water. Then run a normal cycle with detergent.

Remove smoky odors from clothes by filling the bathtub with very hot water and 1 cup white distilled vinegar. Hang the garments above the steaming water and shut the door so the steam can penetrate the fibers.

Keep the steam iron clean and in good working order by getting rid of mineral deposits in steam vents and spray nozzles. Fill the water chamber with a solution of equal parts white distilled vinegar and distilled water. Set it in an upright position and let it steam for about 5 minutes. When the iron is cool, rinse the tank with water, refill and shake water through the vents onto an old cloth. Test before using.

Remove scorch marks from an iron by rubbing it with a warmed-up solution of equal parts white distilled vinegar and salt. If that doesn't work, use a cloth dampened with full-strength white distilled vinegar.

Remove musky smells from cotton clothes by sprinkling them lightly with white distilled vinegar and then pressing them.

Get water and salt stains off shoes and boots by wiping them down with a solution of equal parts white distilled vinegar and water.

Give patent leather shoes and bags a better shine by wiping them down with white distilled vinegar.

Get cleaner laundry! Add about 1/4 cup white distilled vinegar to the last rinse. The acid in white distilled vinegar is too mild to harm fabrics, yet strong enough to dissolve the alkalies in soaps and detergents. Besides removing soap, white distilled vinegar prevents yellowing, acts as a fabric softener and static cling reducer, and attacks mold and mildew.

Note: I don't like to use conventional liquid fabric softener because of the buildup on the inside of the machine; plus it makes my clothes feel gummy. I use vinegar in the fabric softener dispenser and it really makes my clothes soft. Also I like Ecos all natural laundry detergent

Eliminate manufacturing chemicals from new clothes by adding 1/2 cup white distilled vinegar to the water.

Remove soap scum and clean the hoses of your washing machine with white distilled vinegar. Periodically run the machine with only a cup of white distilled vinegar in it--nothing else added to the wash cycle.

Bring out bright colors by adding 1/2 cup white distilled vinegar to the rinse cycle.

Fluff up wool or acrylic sweaters (hand- or machine-washed) and rid them of soap smell with 1/2 cup white distilled vinegar in the last rinse water.

Get rid of the tiny holes left along the hemline when you take out the hem of any garment by moistening a cloth with white distilled vinegar, placing it under the fabric and ironing.

* Be no more than 70 inches tall

Would like:
* French Doors
* Available in white

product_title: Samsung 30 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel Side-By-Side Refrigerator - RSG309AARS
review_title: A disaster. Don't buy anything form Samsung because service is awful.
review_text:
We had a top rated GE refrigerator for 9 years. It had a great layout but did not hold temperatures well and required frequent repairs. It conked out and we had to buy a new fridge quick so we looked at Consumer Reports and since we had not time to shop, we went on line and purchased the top rated Samsung without eeing an actual model. Wished we had read the reviews first. We wanted white but it wasn't in stock so we got stainless steel. Big mistake. It is stainless only on the doors. Sides are an ugly dark grey.

Manual poorly written. No info on how to clean stainless steel which quickly becomes a mess. Manual really only tells how to set up fridge. No info as to where the water filter is.

Do not have option of not using water filter which we don't need because our water is great to begin with. Other brands allow user to plug filter hole so no need for filter. Can't rearrange door shelves which results in wasted space. Limited rearrangement of interior shelves. The icemaker is unique and great but water dispenser doesn't dispense cold water. Temperature controls are great. Can get precise temperatures. Lighting is LED which is energy saving but doesn't give off enough light. Covered storage compartment on refrigerator door is too small to store anything. Needs to be two inches higher in height. The bottom door tray is useless. Fridge has a lot of interior space but because shelving is poorly arranged, too much space is unusable.

The fridge door has three big shelves which are the only place that gallon milk cartons will fit as well as liter bottles of soda. Not very useful if not used for this purpose. Can fit either two gallons of milk on each shelf or three liters. Would much rather have smaller shelves to store jams jars, salad dressings, pickle jars, barbeque sauces, etc. Instead have to store on regular shelves which is very inconvenient. we bought plastic baskets to put these items in but it is a hassle to use them. So although this fridge has al lot more space than most fridges, more space is wasted. And it comes with a wine bottle rack which we find useless.

Another problem is that the ice maker keeps jamming up with ice and it takes 15 minutes to get all the ice out of the storage and dispenser. Eventually, the ice maker completely jammed and could not be removed. It happened one day after the warranty expired and Samsung charged me over $300 to fix it and it took Samsung five months to fix it. The replacement ice maker failed after nine months.
