product_title: Samsung RF4289HARS
review_title: The fridge all your friends will want to play with...
review_text:
Purchased this Samsung fridge as the final appliance to wrapup our change-over to stainless steel. For first 10 days, the refrigerator didn't seem to be keeping items cold in the refrigerator section. Freezer was working great (ice cream was rock solid) but refrigerator would not stay at temperature set on computer display. If I set the temperature for 34 degrees, the inside was anywhere from 46 to 55 degrees most days. Experimented for several days disabling energy saver and running on Power Cool, but nothing seemed to be a permanent fix.

I called Samsung was very disappointed with their response. They don't know much about this model yet. Level 2 support told me that I couldn't use a thermometer to measure the inside temperature. They told me that I could not use a mercury or digital thermometer because it would have to be calibrated for the fridge. When I asked what type of thermometer I could use, they could not give me an answer. I was told to trust the refrigerator to do it's job -Sure! They can eat the spoiled food! They told me that a few degrees was normal (which I accepted) but not 10 to 12 degrees all the time.....any, to make a long story short I decided to "reboot" my fridge.

Yup, it's a linux OS that runs the system and all the apps. I decided to pull the power plug for the first time since I installed the fridge and voila. The refrigerator started working correctly. Temperatures started reporting within 2 to 4 degrees of the set temperature on the control panel. So, if you buy this frige and have this problem, remember to reboot your fridge after a few days if the temperature doesn't hold.

As for the apps. yup, Pandor, Weatherbug, AP news, Picasa web album (SD Card or photos from any DLNA network device in your home), Epicurious and more all work via WiFi. Since my wife can no longer magnetically hang a calendar on the stainless steel, I showed her how to sync her IPhone with Google Calendar which puts all her appointments and reminders on the refrigerator screen for her to review every morning. Very cool. Also the NotePad option allows you to hand write notes and messages on the screen or with a keyboard. Very cool too. While the Apps are interesting and work quite well, I can't see myself reading the news or twitter feed on the door. The screen saver mode allows you to display all or some of the specific feeds.

Finally, there is a "Smart Grid" feature prominent on the display that nobody at Samsung Level 1 or Level 2 can tell me about. When you select the option, it gives you a warning that tells you a little about smart grid. It then displays an error message saying you don't have the SmartGrid modem. When I called Samsung support, they told me to just "go buy a modem". When I asked, what type and where do I "plug in" the modem board to the refrigerator, they came up blank for answers..... I suppose once enough people call and complain, they'll provide tech support with a better response.

Samsung support is outstanding! Call Samsung first before calling the retailer. They will send somebody onsite, no questions asked, to repair a $3000 refrigerator or a $350 microwave (which I bought a few weeks before which came with mfg cosmetic defects).

REFRIGERATOR: Oh yeah, how do I like the appliance as a "refrigerator". The refrigerator compartment is well lit with LEDs and spacious. Some of the door shelves needed getting used to when switching from my old Kenmore side-by-side as only certain bottles of certain heights will fit in specific locations. Seems more cramped on the doors. Inside shelve area, I can't seem to fill it with food or leftovers. The top right shelf (lowered one notch) is the one place tall enough to store bottled waters and some cold beer bottles. I would prefer to have them somewhere on the door, but they just don't fit.

COUNTER HEIGHT DOOR: The "counter-height" door is just silly. The sliding divider in the showroom seems like such a cool idea, but in practice, if you don't have solid block objects larger than the spacer, things are falling in between compartments as you poke around. COMPLAINT- The middle drawer does not come out far enough to easily see what's in the back section of the drawer. You can reach items, but you have to poke around and bend down.

FREEZER: Works rock solid and never had a problem. My wife and I complain that the ice cream is just too hard now. That's a good thing. Has section organizers but main section is just a big dumping place for stuff.

ICEMAKER: Works great but 1/4 the capacity of our old Kenmore and VERY NOISY when the ice drops into the bucket. Yeah...VERY noisy, otherwise you don't hear a thing from the fridge. Wife empties the ice bucket every morning with 3 "Big Gulp" type cups of ice she brings into work. My old Kenmore would half fill an Igloo Playmate. .

WATER DISPENSER: Works great and high pressure. Wife complains because the first few seconds the water is warm. This is because the water tube runs inside the door, behind the touch-screen computer. Water is cool after a few seconds. WARNING: Been about 3 week so far and the water still tastes and smells like the plastic reservoir. Looking forward to not having "that new fridge smell".

PRICE: Shop around. Purchased for $3300, then price discount a week later took off about $200. Then a competitor ran a Samsung 25% discount the next day and we saved another $600+ . Thank you Best Buy Price Match Policy.

AUGUST 2011 UPDATE: Refrigerator is performing flawlessly. Several software updates over the past few months have been pushed down and all the problems appear to be resolved...knock on wood. Counter-height door continues to be silly use of space with divider, Freezer is still a disorganized mess and we've gotten used to the "You've got Ice" plunk :-)

January 2014 UPDATE: Refrigerator going strong. No problems. Sorry to hear of those with problems. Remember, it's rare to find people taking the time to write positive reviews. Negative ones are much easier to pen.

product_title: Samsung RF4289HARS
review_text:
I agree with many things the first reviewer had to say and yes, I rebooted my fridge as well although as I had the opportunity to read his review, I did it on the second day and now, temperature is basically spot on. All three compartments, fridge, drawer, freezer are usually +/- 1 degree of set point. I think the temperature sensors simply needed to stabilize and then calibrate with a reboot. I don't know that it wouldn't have happened on it's on as I didn't give it a chance.

Lighting in this thing is awesome. LED's all over the place, in every compartment so it's very easy to see what you have. Fit and finish seem excellent and it's EXTREMELY quiet. With any background noise in the kitchen at all I have to really listen to hear it running.

It's pretty cool having your fridge connected to the Internet, I particularly like having the Weatherbug app on the display and the wife likes having her Google calendar syncing with it.

I guess the only complaint I have and the reason I didn't give it five stars is the ice maker, and where it is. I would gladly give up having ice dispensed through the door (although water would still be nice) to have the ice maker mounted in the freezer to gain the lost space in the fridge. Most manufacturers however do the same thing. I can only recall one and I think it was Amana that had water only dispensed through the door and the ice maker in the freezer. Still, we moved from an old KitchenAid side by side with 25.0 cu/ft and this Samsung is 28.0 cu/ft so all in all, even with the ice maker in the fridge, we gained a HUGE amount of refrigerator space, so I don't complain too much.

I would buy this refrigerator again in a heart beat. Deals are to be had if you look

product_title: Samsung RF4289HARS
review_text:
Agree with above reviews. Reboot fridge (unplug, wait about a minute and plug back in) after a few days from the time you first plug it in. Ours had wild temp swings prior to the reboot. Sometimes display said 15F in fridge, but thermometer said 38F. Other times display said 38F but fridge was actually 45F. After reboot it seems to be accurate again. Also, have heard some people (on other sites) say touchscreen doesn't work well (or not at all). I had this problem with a display model I was looking at in the store and was ready to pass up this fridge and go with the version w/out the LCD. But, I performed the touchscreen calibration and it worked perfectly after that. I especially like Weatherbug and have programmed my home weather and also weather for my family in another state. I really like the flex-space drawer as we can put sodas in there and cool them down to almost freezing temp. Nothing like drinking a Coca-Cola at 33F! Can't do that with a normal fridge as it's not good for lettuce and etc. The fancy sliding divider is useless. If they really want to improve it they need to make it so that you can lock it in place. It is so loose, it allows stuff to move around. We plan on getting some plastic tubs to organize it better. I'm going to see if I can remove the sliding rail system altogether. This thing is quiet! Way quieter than our 8yr old Maytag wide by side it is replacing. Like everyone else says...when the ice drops into the bin, it is loud. Most fridges are loud when this happens, but this one is especially so. It's been 2 days and the water has that "plasticky" taste. I hope the lines and filter purge this eventually. I wanted a fridge that would "WOW" my wife every time she looked at it or opened it. This one does that for sure.

Update: 12/13/11. So far the refrigerator has been great! I purchased a refrigerator thermometer and the temp has been spot on in all 3 parts of the refrigerator. I do notice, it takes a day or so to stabilize temp after you add a bunch of groceries. Maybe it's the energy efficiency programming. But, you can use the "power cool" setting and it cools down quicker. We are still running the flex-space drawer at 29F and enjoying sodas nice and cold! The longer we have the fridge the better we like it. We flip the "flip-up" shelf and put wine there. Also, when the right door is full of milk & OJ, we can slide the right middle shelf back out of the way and store a gallon of apple cider there. Really handy!

Update 6/10/12: Fridge is working perfect. Temps in all compartments are spot on. So far we are extremely happy! I'm about to order my first replacement water filter.

Update 7/13/12: Ordered new water filter. This one gave great tasting water right away. The original filter was part # DA29-00020A, whereas the new filter is DA29-00020B. Samsung must have changed something between the two filters.

product_title: Samsung RF4289HARS
review_text:
I purchased my 26X series Samsung French-door refrigerator and also had the good fortune to remember to buy a Lowe's 4-year extended warranty.

Samsung products are junk, plain and simple. Once Korean-made quality products they are now made in China and are garbage. Samsung does not support their products unless you know how to create trouble for them.

Just a month after the Samsung warranty expired the icemaker reservoir did, too. That was repaired under the extended warranty the first, second, and third time. The bottom freezer gasket failed and was replaced. The freezer light switch failed and was replaced. Five days after the technician replaced the entire icemaker system the water dispenser failed. After replacing the main circuit board in back, the front control panel, lines, water switch and water reservoir with no luck the technician declared the refrigerator "unrepairable."

After the icemaker failed for the third time and the lower gasket and switch and the main CB had failed and been replaced I sent an email to Samsung Support from their website. What I got in response was that Samsung considers these types and numbers of failures within less than two years since purchase "Normal wear and tear."

Chatting online the representative apologized but refused to escalate my issues to a higher level ("Not allowed").

I contacted Lowe's Home Office and advised them of my problems and the fact of so many negative reviews in Amazon as well as the Class Action lawsuit against Samsung for selling several models of refrigerators with KNOWN defective compressors. Lowe's promised to look into the matter.

I waited a few days and then did another online chat. This time my claim was routed up the chain and I was assured I would get a call "within 2-3 business days." On the fourth business day I went back on the Chat Line and I got a call several hours later.

Suddenly, Samsung was "very concerned" and was willing to issue me a rebate for the depreciated value of the unit. All I had to do was send them a copy of the original sales receipt and invoices for the repairs. I did that and was told it would be 17-21 business days for my refund.

About a week later I got a call from a TV repair shop asking to set up an appointment to "inspect a Samsung unit." I told him I did not have a Samsung TV and he said he would cancel the call. I found out later that Samsung has no appliance service techs in my area and they then cancelled my claim.

Got that straightened out with the promise of another call to Lowe's Home Office and now I am SUPPOSED to be getting my depreciated rebate soon. The Lowe's Extended Warranty folks confirmed the "unrepairable" status with the technician and they are issuing me a Lowe's gift card for the full purchase price plus tax.

...and the icemaker gave up the ghost for the FIFTH time last night. Rather than try to sell it or give it away I am going to have Lowe's take it away and junk it.

Again, DO NOT BUY A SAMSUNG PRODUCT OF ANY KIND.

product_title: Samsung RF4289HARS
review_title: Run away! Run far! Run fast!
review_text:
Never, ever again will I buy a Samsung major appliance. I have three of their televisions, and love them, but this fridge is a steaming piece of crap.
Repairmen out 7 times since I bought it, all to repair problems with the freezer. Main board replaced. Then (less than two weeks later) main board AGAIN replaced, along with all the sensors in the freezer section. Then daughter board and more sensors. Then the door display panel. Then the main board replaced for the third time - and blamed on me because I was running the freezer empty, so they charged me for it. Like I was going to trust this freezer after that many failures until it had run reliably for a good long time? I'm still arguing with Samsung over that one. This morning I woke up to find my kitchen and dining room flooded - the water chiller tank in the fridge is broken, there's water everywhere, and the fridge is a frosty 65 degrees.
The best money I've spent on a fridge in the last year is the cheap one I put in the garage. It's never broken down, and it works even in the summer in an uncooled garage. This thing? Unless you've got a masochistic streak a mile wide, a bottomless checking account, a love of throwing away food that was perfectly good when you went to bed last night but the fridge managed to destroy while you slept, and someone to stay home all day long waiting for the repairman again, don't even consider it.
I'm either going to call the repairman again, and hope that I get the one guy at the Samsung Authorized Repair Center who actually knows anything about Samsung refrigerators, or I'm stopping on the way home to get a new fridge and toss this thing on the junk heap, where it belongs. It's a toss-up right now.

review_text:
I waited a little bit over a year to write this review since I wasn't sure how reliable this appliance would be. I'm very pleased with the fridge so far. I chose this fridge based on the features and price. I like the fact that I can browse the news in the morning, and later listen to Pandora while I cook dinner or entertain guests.

Pros
-Definite wow factor - most of the guests that see the fridge are impressed with the technology
-Middle tray makes access to deli meats/cheese , soda etc very convenient. Sliding divider bar keeps item organized.
-Bright interior lights, well designed shelves and trays
-LCD is a great way to pass info. (esp. the calendar function since it syncs with my Google calendar and my wife's)

Cons
-Weak WiFi reception. My router is on the opposite side of the house, but I believe I should have better signal. (my PS3 gets excellent reception and is farther away.) I'm assuming I can remedy the situation with a simple wifi signal booster.
-Android operating system will crash after every 2-3 months requiring fridge to be unplugged and re plugged in.

At the time, this fridge was cheaper than the fridge without the LCD and the 4th door, so I bought the 3 yr extra warranty, an appliance surge protector(since it has circuit board), and still saved a few hundred compared to the lower model. I also took notice that a lot of the reviews on Amazon were the same people spamming angry reviews at the entire line of Samsung fridges and not any one fridge in general. To be honest I wouldn't have bought the fridge without the extended warranty, but am very glad I took a chance.

product_title: Samsung RF4289HARS
review_text:
This fridge has the worst software I've ever used in my life. Let me give you just a small inventory of the problems I've encountered with it:
1. The home screen shows you news headlines whether you want them or not. I was getting a drink of water the other day and my fridge had a headline about Bill Cosby being accused of rape. I don't need to read about celebrity rape scandals when I'm getting a damn glass of water. Then I had friends over, and my fridge was telling us about a chlorine attack at a furry convention. Okay, well, at least the fridge was successful at being a conversation starter about how ridiculously terrible my "smart" fridge is.
2. The photos feature doesn't work. I put an SD card full of perfectly valid image in the fridge. The entire fridge software hung for about 5 minutes. During this time, it showed each image on the card failing to be read. Then it hard crashed so that I had to use a toothpick to reboot my fridge.
3. The Picasa Web Album integration doesn't work at all. I'm guessing that Google has changed their API at some point in the 4 years or so since they used the name "Picasa" for Google Photos. Samsung has not updated their software to fix it.
4. The Google Calendar integration does not work at all. When you try to log in, it gives you a nonsensical error message about "Please check your email on Google Calendar website". Again, Google has updated their APIs in the last few years. Samsung support blames Google and says they are working on fixing it, but that's clearly bulls***.
5. The epicurious integration is frustrating. At least half of the photos are rotated sideways because the software doesn't understand how to read EXIF metadata. And the names of dishes are truncated or malformed because the software doesn't decode Unicode properly. It treats UTF-8 as Latin-1 probably. But the most frustrating part is that if you see a recipe you want, you can click it and then... it disappears. What am I supposed to see a recipe I want and then Google it on another device? How the hell am I supposed to use this?
6. The twitter integration is crappy. Half the time it's just blank. What could they not find any tweets to show? And then when it does show, lots of tweets have links or embedded media that can't render, so it's pretty worthless. On top of that, there's no emoji support, which is just kinda lame.

I hate this fridge. It would be better without the computer or touch screen at all. I wish someone would figure out how to root it so I can put Android on there or something. How did Samsung even manage to write software this bad? I shudder to imagine.

product_title: GE JB650STSS 30" Stainless Steel Electric Smoothtop Range
review_text:
Sure it's beautiful with handsome styling, but it's also so much more.

Some of my favorite features include the two multi-size burners, warming zone, and melt function. All the burners, including the power boil (yes, that's right) heat up well and function very efficiently. Along with the electronic display are some stainless knobs that I think lend a richer look than the black ones.

The oven cooks evenly (there were some minor fumes briefly during its first use). And of the two cleaning options this model offers, I'll definitely choose steam clean as opposed to the energy hog self clean. It's also nice that GE engineered the heating element off the oven floor.

I haven't had any difficulty at all keeping the black cook top clean. But if I do, I'll just use Wieman Glass Cook Top Cleaner, which out-performs Cerama Bryte (comes with GE ranges) by a mile.

Now if this model had a dedicated clock pad, it would be absolutely perfect. Then, I wouldn't have to push so many unrelated buttons to set, display, or turn off the clock.

All things considered, though, this is a great looking / performing range and I'd definitely recommend it.

product_title: GE JB650STSS 30" Stainless Steel Electric Smoothtop Range
review_text:
I use stove burners everyday and the oven almost every day. Replacing my well loved range was a difficult thought and I researched the options endlessly. I'm pleased with the results.
My favorite feature is one I didn't know I was getting. You can set an oven timer to turn off the oven at the end of the baking cycle.
The steam cleaning is an interesting idea, but it really doesn't work well. If something has spilled over while baking, the steam cleaning won't touch it.
The warming burner is very handy. Mine burned out within a month, but was replaced without fanfare.
The smooth top has been easier to keep clean than I feared. I'm the world's messiest cook and whether or not to get one was the hardest decision when choosing a new range. It's been fine.
The largest burner fits my 7 quart canner perfectly.
The drawer is nice and big.
The oven bakes very evenly and can fit 2 Baker's Secret 12 muffin pans on the same shelf- a truly large oven. The oven is very slow to preheat- it takes 15 minutes to get up to temperature.
There's only thing that drives me nuts. Because the top is black, it shows every grain of salt and crumb that constantly get on it.

product_title: GE JB650STSS 30" Stainless Steel Electric Smoothtop Range
review_text:
It works great. Digital controls are intuitive, and it still has some dials for the stove top burners. A big improvement over our old range from the 70's.

My only disappointment came when I discovered -- after reading the manual -- that several of our pots and pans were not recommended for use on a smoothtop.

product_title: Whirlpool Gold GSC25C4EYY 36 24.5 cu. ft. Counter-Depth Side by Side Refrigerator - Stainless Stee
review_title: don't believe all the negative hype
review_text:
I almost didn't buy this fridge after reading the comments on this and other websites.
Even though I did not purchase through Amazon, this is the site with the most comments and I wanted to put this where others in my situation would see it.
Counter-depth fridge choices are limited, and if you don't want to spend an additional thousand dollars (or two!), then the options are really limited.
I have been extremely happy with my Whirlpool refrigerator. It is VERY roomy for a counter-depth. The LED lights are pretty and illuminate well. The stainless is a great look and the sides are gray, which blend in better than the black sides that some have. Magnets do stick to the front and sides. The shelves are glass with a nice lip to prevent spills, the plastic drawers feel sturdy. Operation is quiet. My ice maker works great, I like the smaller cubes. I have not had any issues with ice shooting onto the floor, or with things freezing on the top shelf. I did turn the fridge temp up 2 degrees since things were REALLY cold, since then I've had no issues.
Downsides - ice maker is loud, especially when the bin is empty, you can hear every cube. Stainless smudges easily (duh).
Overall, this has been a great purchase. I'm sure there are some lemons out there, but after talking with numerous sales and repair people, I am reassured that Whirlpool has a pretty good repair record.

review_title: I agree with the other reviewer - It is a nice refrigerator
review_text:
I commute to and from San Antonio for work, so while in San Antonio I live in an apartment. The apartment came with this refrigerator and I have to say that I am very pleased with it. I was surprised with all the features that come with this fridge for its size. It just so happens that the fridge went out in my real house and I started price shopping this fridge and ended up on Amazon (surprise, surprise). I was dumbstruck by the 1 star rating that was given. Perhaps the other reviewers are over exaggerating but to give a one star rating in my book it has to be pretty crappy. I will be buying this fridge today (4/09/2013) with no worries of performance based on my experience of using it for six months at my apartment in San Antonio.

The fridge itself gives you a lot of "big fridge" options but in a small package. My wife also loves it as well, and she is pretty picky. Ice maker, great use of space so there is plenty of storage, filtered water, pretty to look at both inside and out. I love the door open chime as it has saved my bacon (literally :) several times. I have also quit buying bottled water, well, I have cut down on my bottled water usage thanks to the dispenser that serves up cold filtered water. I don't really know what else to say about it other than my standards are pretty high when it comes to value and taste and this refrigerator certainly satisfies both areas. I would recommend this refrigerator without pause.

I paid for the warranty on the matching washer. It is leaking. A service technician came out two months ago and said the area where the bleach goes in needed cleaning and that was the problem. Both the washer and dryer work fine when they work. I think about the old washer and dryer I replaced that worked great for over 10 years and all I had to do was replace the heaters in the dryer and maybe a washer belt. They just don't make them like they used to. I give the dryer (and really the pair) 1 star because it doesn't matter how good they work, when they work, if there are numerous repairs to deal with.

product_title: Samsung DV520AGW
review_text:
We bought this dryer (Platinum/Stainless Steel color) DV520AGP with the matching washer when my local store had it on sale, about half off Samsung list price.

The washer/dryer combo has been great. They do a good job of washing and drying. The dryer has left my close a bit damp but it's due to the cloths/sheets getting twisted and wrapped up, any dryer would do that and my old dryer did that. The middle of the heap is still a bit damp.

My biggest complaint was that the dryer was making a loud buzzing noise while running after a couple months of owning it. It seemed like every time it was heating it made the noise. I called Samsung about it and was told that it was normal operation but it seemed to loud and too frequent. After some discussions, it was agreed to send a repair person to look at it.

The repair man came and ordered a new gas valve and would come back 2 weeks later to install. I received a call out of the blue from Samsung support to talk about my repair ticket and they told me the noise was normal operation behavior. I went to the dryer and had them listen, they stated it was normal. I asked about the repair call, they stated he shouldn't do any repair. I asked how do I return the dryer because if it's this loud I don't want it. They told me to work with my local store for that. This made me quite upset that they are trying to tell me that this faulty unit was working as expected.

Regardless, the gas valve was shipped to me and the repair man came anyway. Supposedly, once the repair person is called, it's out of Samsung's hands, thankfully! He took 15min to replace the gas valve and the loud buzz went away. He stated it was definitely a gas valve struggling to work properly. He felt there will be a recall on gas valves soon from what he has been seeing. Thankfully this happened within my year warranty.

So, if your gas dryer is buzzing really loud through out the cycle, it could be a bad gas valve.

Shame on Samsung for trying to pass this off as "normal operation".

Otherwise, I'm pretty happy with the product and would recommend people to buy, just watch for the bad gas valve.

It was not. I suspect this is a problem on most modern refrigerators. Manufacturers want to get ultra high efficiency ratings, so they probably test under ideal conditions. product_title: LG LFX31925SB30.7 Cu. Ft. Smooth Black French Door Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_text:
So the obvious part of the review is that this is one of (if not *the*) biggest fridges on the market. It's got a bunch of neat-o features, like an in-door ice maker and an air filter to keep your fridge from smelling funky.

After living with this fridge for a year...
1. I'm surprised the price hasn't really gone down after a whole year!!
2. I'm a bit disappointed in the ice maker, which tends to turn all of its ice cubes into a giant ice block if you don't use it for a day or two.
3. Like the first review, I suspect my fridge is a few degrees warmer than the temp control settings claim.
4. The ice maker had a random meltdown once (literally!), with an error code and everything, but after I unplugged the fridge for a minute, it hasn't had a problem since... !?!

Minor annoyances aside, this fridge is huge!! We've never even come close to needing more space, and it's easy to store veggie trays, pizzas, or watermelons or any other odd-size thing that usually had to go in the extra "garage refrigerator." Honestly, it's probably bigger than we need, but it fit nicely into our kitchen's fridge-hole.

Some other pros: The LED lighting is great. It's leagues quieter than the ca. 1998 Kenmore that it replaced. The control panel on the front has reminder-lights for when it's time to change the filters, and the filters are pretty simple to swap out (although we need to pull out the top shelf to change our water filter - maybe not an issue for you, since you can put the shelves in at any height you like).

Would I buy it again? I could go either way. Depends on the competition, probably, and the prices. We were watching the sales and got ours for several hundred dollars off of retail at the time. I don't have any regrets, but if a competing fridge had a better sale going on, well...

The freezer is a little tight, but it's organized, and I can find things. It has multiple areas. Three bins, two drawers, and even an area for tiny things that would have been lost forever in my old freezer.
I only gave four stars because of the freezer size, and the stainless 'skin' seems a little fragile. I think if I had little ones with 'pounding' tendencies, I'd have a dented up refrigerator. Just my impression.

review_title: If I could, I would get something else
review_text:
Had to replace the dishwasher in a new house. Looked into many models, and decided to go with this model (bought at a local BestBuy). Used for 5 months prior to writing this review.

Pros:
1. Washes dishes well.
2. Supposedly saves water (not sure if I can check this claim, so I am taking it as is)
3. Supposedly saves energy cause it's not using dry-heat at the end of the cycle but rather FINISH rinse agent (more on it in #3 of Cons)
4. Nice looks and easy to operate. Mainly use the AUTO wash - set it and forget it. Also we use 3hr delay so we don't get bothered with noise (later about the noise).

Cons:
1. It is much smaller than other dishwashers we have owned and/or operated (primarily Kenmoore and Whirlpool). I think this Bosch's basic model was made smaller on purpose to make you buy a more advanced washer that is sized properly. For a family of 3, we turn the dishwasher on at least every other day, sometomes daily (when we have guests and such)
2. Maybe I got a defective dishwasher, but mine is NOT QUITE. Again, I compare with kenmoores and whirlpools that I have used and/or owned. We set the 3-hr delay so that in the evening we can watch the TV in the living room without having to turn the volume up.
3. This dishwasher goes though FINISH [[ASIN:B0026WRHK6 Finish Jet-dry Rinse Agent, Original Liquid, 32 Oz]] lightning fast. We set the use of FINISH to the lowest, but the LOW indicator lights up every three or so weeks. Maybe the dishwasher is saving water (see #2 in pros above) and energy (see #3 in pros above), but last time I checked water is much cheaper than FINISH liquid. With Kenmoore, we had to refill the liquid no often than once every 3-4 months.

All things considered, we aren't getting anymore BOSCHs. Next time around I am getting a Kenmoore from Sears. They all are regular sizes and don't consume FINISH at lightning speeds.

product_title: Bosch SHE3AR55UC Ascenta 24" Stainless Steel Full Console Dishwasher - Energy Star
review_text:
This is the 2nd Bosch washer I have bought from a local home improvement store. The first one was an entry level back at our old house replacing a noisy cheapo whirlpool in 2006. We bought Bosch because of how quiet they ran. Now in our current home we are replacing another cheapo whirlpool (dead) with another entry level Bosch but the price point is a couple of hundred less than 5 years ago. First, this has a stainless tub with a plastic bottom, whereas the old one was all stainless.

Now we get to how quiet it runs - on my old Bosch you had to put your ear next to the washer to hear it - the new one you don't have to, you can hear it pretty clearly but i would not describe it as loud by any means - you will not have to adjust the volume of a TV set in the kitchen or have to talk over it. I would guess its on par with or a bit better than most dishwashers at this price point. I am guessing Bosch is now using how quiet a washer is to set price points on their washers.

It cleans very well and dries better than the last one. Let me share what I know about a Bosch washer and how it Dries. You do not have the traditional vent on the countertop for steam to escape it goes through the drain - so you need to use a rinse aid like Jet Dry. The washer will heat the hot water supplied and has a hidden heating element under the Plastic/Poly bottom. It is possible to turn the heating element off - you need to consult the manual to adjust this and or the amount of rinse aid dispensed. With the heating element on, sanitized selected and using a rinse aid - all my dishes are dry in fact it dries better than the old model - the dishes are so hot right after a cycle that they are too hot to handle.

FYI - Many dishwashing detergents have been forced to change their formulas (remove phosphates in the past 12 months) some traditional detergent brands are now terrible to the point where people are buying new dishwashers when they only need different detergents - I have found the best results with Finish tablets.
This washer is made in the USA and i do not expect it to last as long as my mother-in-law's still running trouble free 16+ year old German built Bosch. The stainless steel outer door feels a bit flimsy when you wipe it down.

All in all I think I got a fair product for the money and do not think I would have a better product for the same $ I spent on this. The only thing else I would say is that it does not have a solid food dispenser and if you want near silent operation you and your wallet will need to step up the Bosch line.

Pros
bang 4 buck, made in usa, cheaper $

Cons
made cheaper

UPDATE 6/27/13 - I am still getting consistent performance out of my dishwasher. If I had to do it all over again, I would have spent a bit more for a 100% stainless tub as this does not live up to its name in terms of quiet performance. All in all though I do feel as though I did get a reasonable bang for the buck. I did have a Bosch front load washing machine that I wound up replacing after 3 years, so Bosch will only get my money for dishwashers, wiper blades & spark plugs from now on. review_title: Rusts on the inside; stains on the outside
review_text:
Two years after purchasing Bosch's "stainless" steel "rust-free" dishwasher with a "lifetime warranty" against rust, we discovered... rust. It was in a very specific area, where the metal filter attaches to the interior tub. We called Bosch and were told that it was our fault, that it was our water, our dishwasher soap, our flatware--anything but the dishwasher. We persisted, explaining that we use a water softener and a reverse-osmosis system and that our water is no worse, and probably a bit better, than average. Furthermore, if it was merely our water, then we would expect to see rust everywhere. As for our dishwasher soap--well--it comes from Costco, and I'm sure they'd take exception to Bosch's claim that it promotes rust. We offered our own theory, which is that the metal used in the filter is dissimilar to the metal in the tub, resulting in a galvanic reaction and corrosion to the metals. Basically, the two different metals, pressed together in an aqueous environment, results in a battery. But for Bosch to admit this would be to admit a design flaw--the sort of admission that leads to a class-action lawsuit. We already know Bosch uses a variety of "stainless" metals. For example, the metal used on the door is a very inferior grade of stainless steel that is easily streaked and spotted. And the way you can tell is to use a magnet. If the magnet sticks then it's ferrous metal and more prone to staining.

This section is taken right out of the manual: "Stainless Steel TallTub: A rust-free, hygienic interior surface with a lifetime warranty." Bosch routinely advertises a "lifetime rust-free warranty". The sales reps will tell you that the unit comes with a lifetime rust-free warranty.

Yet Bosch claims they don't actually guarantee the tub to be rust-free; they only warrant against "rust-through", meaning you will have to live with the rust until it eats a hole through the metal--until water starts pouring into some part of the dishwasher where it doesn't belong (hopefully not endangering you, your family, or your home, in the process). When you consider that Bosch basically expects you to use their rusting appliance until there's a catastrophic failure, you realize that the advertisements, selling points, and sales pitches regarding "rust-free" and "lifetime warranty" are all fraudulent.

Bosch offered no remedies and suggested that the rust can be removed (on our dime, of course). The problem is that even if we use a rust-removing product, the rust will return in time, because the source of the rust--a design flaw--remains.

review_title: Read this if you are considering ANY Bosch dishwasher
review_text:
A repairman just left my house after an unsuccessful attempt at repairing a five-year-old Bosch dishwasher. It needed a new control board which was discontinued, unavailable, recalled, and the recall had expired. In other words my not-so-old, very expensive dishwasher is JUNK.
I'll not be looking for another Bosch. Would you?

product_title: Bosch SHE3AR55UC Ascenta 24" Stainless Steel Full Console Dishwasher - Energy Star
review_text: We recently purchased this dishwasher at a local big box store. It cleans and drys well and looks nice and is relatively quiet. We are a two person household so the size is fine.  HOWEVER, it makes a very irritating high pitch sound throughout the entire cycle.  We exchanged the dishwasher for another one thinking and hoping that we had simply received a bad one the first time around. Unfortunately, the second one makes the same horrible noise. I can't believe no one else has complained about this. We even added a piece of foam behind the foot plate but it didn't dampen the noise enough.

product_title: Bosch SHE3AR55UC Ascenta 24" Stainless Steel Full Console Dishwasher - Energy Star
review_title: Rust on inside of SS door after only 2 months
review_text:
I did a lot of research before purchasing this dishwasher locally. It seemed to work Ok for the first few weeks, but then the soap dispenser would not open and drop in the Electrosol Tab (the recommended product) into the dishwasher. So now I just place the tablet inside one of the utensil trays before running it. Then yesterday when I opened the dishwasher door after running a small load, I was surprised to see small rust spots all over the inside of the stainless steel surface of the door. I first tried just wiping the spots off with a wet cloth, then tried cleaning it off Tilex spray, then Stainless Steel spray cleaner...but the spots would not budge.

This morning I called Bosch customer service for their advise on addressing the problem. The first response was that this was just a cosmetic issue not covered after the first 30 days. Second, that if I had ever cleaned the surface with Chlorox it could cause the surface to rust. Since I would have no reason to try and clean rust stains from the inside of the door until today, that was no help. The final advice was to try and clean it with a product called CLR, a product recommended to clean mineral and rust stains...otherwise, since this was just a cosmetic issue it was not covered under the warranty (period).

All of the major, and most of the minor appliances, in my kitchen are stainless steel, and over the past 15 years none has ever had rust spots appear on them...so this was a big disappointment with the new Bosch. Otherwise the dishwasher does run very quiet, and seems to do an adequate job so far. Just not too happy with the rust spots, and the cool brush off by Bosch customer service.

product_title: Bosch SHE3AR55UC Ascenta 24" Stainless Steel Full Console Dishwasher - Energy Star
review_text:
I'd be interested to hear whether any of the other reviewers have had this problem, but a couple of months after installing this dishwasher, it started to smell terrible. After months of trying to keep the filter clean and living with the terrible odor, I called a repairman since it is still under warranty. He came and cleaned out the filter and sold me some dishwasher cleaner and told me that it is normal to have 1/4 inch of water under the filter after running the dishwasher. That is the source of the smell. He ran the dishwasher with the cleaner and a couple of hours later... still stinky! I've googled it and this seems to be very common to Bosch owners. I will absolutely never buy a Bosch dishwasher again.

Pros: *It does a decent job cleaning the dishes, though it's not perfect. There is often food stuck to the dishes after running.
Cons: *IT REEKS! *The dishes come out sopping wet unless you use Jet Dry, which is expensive. *It could definitely be roomier. My last dishwasher was a builder-grade basic one and I could fit a lot more dishes in it.

product_title: Bosch SHE3AR55UC Ascenta 24" Stainless Steel Full Console Dishwasher - Energy Star
review_title: Wheels fall off, food gets stuck in jets
review_text:
I have had a mid-price Bosch that was recommended by consumer reports for two years now, and I can't understand why no one else has complained about it. It cleans great at first, and is quiet. But the wheels are constantly falling off - we've lost 4 of the 8 of them. When you pull out a full bottom rack it skittles across the dishwasher door and every time I worry that the whole thing will crash on the floor.

The water flows through jets in two different spinning arms. The tiniest bit of food - often a scrap of lettuce or something unidentifiable - will get stuck in the jets. This signifiantly impacts cleaning. I struggle to pick it out with tweezers. I DO rinse my dishes before loading them!

product_title: Bosch SHE3AR55UC Ascenta 24" Stainless Steel Full Console Dishwasher - Energy Star
review_text: I do not own this model exactly, but I want to make all consumers aware of the NIGHTMARE you will experience if have any problems after purchase of a Bosch appliance.  This company does not stand behind their products, from Day#1, under-warranty, of ownership. We bought their top-of-the-line dishwasher that performs worse than a bottom-line budget special. Bosch has refused, from the first day, to acknowledge any problems; going so far as to doctor their repair records, of which we have an un-doctored copy, to redact service techs' comments regarding non-performance of the product. It has been like dealing with a fly-by-night, street-corner hawker, who disappears after the sale is made.  They have tried their damndest to dissuade us from service calls, and each time we call for repair they have questioned us in an accusatory manner about how we load the dishes, what brand and how much detergent we use, temperature and pressure of the water, etc.  Each repair person who has checked the machine has determined we are doing everything correctly, but each time we call Bosch to report that the machine still does not work, they act live we've never called before and start the same aggravating, time-wasting routine.  Their customer service reps' attitudes are very defensive, no doubt because they are handling nothing but complaints about quality all day long.  BUY ANOTHER BRAND, ANY OTHER BRAND!!

product_title: Bosch SHE3AR55UC Ascenta 24" Stainless Steel Full Console Dishwasher - Energy Star
review_text: We have had our  Bosch dishwasher just over 2 years.  The sanitizer light stopped working a couple of weeks ago, and the dishwasher seemed to be working overtime - a longer cycle and unclean dishes at the end.  The repair main told us it was because the electronic circuit board had burnt out. Apparently the water coming into the dishwasher when it was turned on was not at maximum hotness, and so the dishwasher was having to work overtime to get the water to the correct temperature.  The dishwasher we had before for 20 years showed no such necessity, and I had never considered this requirement before - nor had I been told about it. Disappointing.

product_title: Bosch SHE3AR55UC Ascenta 24" Stainless Steel Full Console Dishwasher - Energy Star
review_text:
We have the She3ar7uc

product_title: Bosch SHE3AR55UC Ascenta 24" Stainless Steel Full Console Dishwasher - Energy Star
review_text: I bought the new Bosch Ascenta because it was highly rated by Consumer Reports for performance and reliability, but the lay out of the machine makes me wish I'd bought another model. The control panel is needlessly complicated compared to my old model. One needs to reselect the setting each load. And the rack layout is very frustrating. If I have a casserole dish to wash, it can only go in a place that blocks off the racks for the plates. The owners manual shows various ways of loading (only dishes) that are models of Teutonic order, but where are the casserole dishes? Kids's cereal bowls? Who lives like that? Also, should you have to open the door while it is cycling, you will get a face full of water from the upper jet. Also, the soap dispenser won't lock shut if you get even a small bit of dishwashing powder outside the tray. The springless door is not very user friendly, and the lower dish rack goes clanging off the tracks if you open it more than 3/4 of the way. Bosch designers need to buy a Kenmore and take notes.

product_title: Bosch SHE3AR55UC Ascenta 24" Stainless Steel Full Console Dishwasher - Energy Star
review_text:
I recently bought the white exterior version. So far, so good, but with a few caveats, which are enumerated below.

It replaces a 14-year-old Kenmore [KitchenAid, I believe] unit that evidently rusted through the interior door panel, causing a short in the control circuit board. Instead of attempting a repair and risking future water-induced electrical failures or even a fire, I shut off the power and water supply and decided to replace it. Installation was VERY easy, and the instructions were clear and easy to follow.

1) I greatly miss having a "progress row" of LEDs, telling me which cycle it is on. (That will be another $200 for a higher-end model, please.)

2) As others have noted, the soap door is somewhat flimsy and temperamental, to the point that I treat mine VERY gently.

3) I also greatly miss having a rinse-and-hold cycle. (That will be another $200 for a higher-end model, please).

4) I got the hang of cycle cancellation ala Bosch (treat it like a computer and hold the on button for awhile), but the Kitchaid had a convenient and much-appreciated drain-and-cancel button.

5) The lower rack's wheelset is flimsy, and it is VERY easy to get it off track. This was never an issue with the KitchenAid, for which I do not recall ever having a rack derailment.

product_title: Bosch SHE3AR55UC Ascenta 24" Stainless Steel Full Console Dishwasher - Energy Star
review_text:
Like many others here, we purchased the Bosch SHE3ARblahblahblah Ascenta on the strength of Consumer Reports (a company frequently wrong about computers and now dishwashers), and also the recommendation of our local shop.

It is quiet. It does circulate water throughout the compartment and produce clean dishes. It doesn't come to life and attack the family. It's shiny. That's about everything I can say about it that I like.

Whomever designed the inside of the dishwasher has simply never used one. Standard-sized dishes cannot be placed next to one another; the "back angle" placement of the main racks on the bottom compartment ensures that space is grievously wasted; forget about putting in large anythings; bowls pretty much are restricted to a single size (are there special Bosch bowls that one can buy for use with this dishwasher?) and, uh, you cannot load wine glasses.

Let me repeat that last one for people who drink wine: YOU CANNOT WASH WINE GLASSES IN THERE. This dishwasher will load the tiny sherry or port glasses, but that's it. Anything larger will need to be hand-washed or you risk breaking them, especially since the bottom tray basically falls out of the unit rather than glides out as was the case for all my previous dishwashers.

Also, it smells weird, and it is a pretty strong odor. This might go away after many washed (we have used it three times so far with a variety of kitchenware), but maybe not. A friend of mine anecdotally told me that stainless steel dishwashers can retain an odor.

Anyway, it is terrible. This is the dishwasher I would build on my first-ever try (I am not handy with tools). To think it was researched and pored over by Bosch technicians makes this an actual insult. There are a thousand dishwashers out there: stay clear of this one.

product_title: Bosch SHE3AR55UC Ascenta 24" Stainless Steel Full Console Dishwasher - Energy Star
review_text: I purchased a Bosch Ascenta dishwasher in 2010, my first Bosch.  It is very quiet, although as the years pass, it is not nearly as quiet as when new.  I was quickly disappointed in how ineffective their "drying" process is.  You will need to read up on them to learn that they don't really have a "drying" cycle as such.  The result is that your dishes will come out fairly wet, especially plastics. My problem with this is that since we live in a humid climate to begin with (Florida) the lack of a drying cycle just exacerbates our humidity battle.  When I start the dw after dinner on regular cycle, it takes 2 hours 19 minutes, and that means it finishes around bedtime.  So I like to wait until the following morning to unload it.  But that results in a lot of my flatware and cooking utensils having tiny rust spots already!!  Even good grades of stainless!!  Interestingly, a couple of years after we purchased this Bosch, we purcased a summer home up north that had a working Bosch dishwasher in it already!  I was very concerned that I would have more of the same problem!  Not so!  That  particular dishwasher was an older model (circa 1999) and apparently it has a dry cycle as my dishes there come out sparkling clean PLUS they are dry!!  And that is when I open the door.......so it is not just that the climate there is less humid than Florida!!  I have concluded that the older models are superior in this aspect.  I do hope Bosch eventually goes back to the way they built dishwashers in the 1990's.  The dishwasher at our northern home does a fantastic job all around, and in less time than the new one.  Lesson learned, newer is not always better!  When it comes time to replace any dishwasher at either home, I will be looking for one with a dry cycle, as this is the first time I have ever had to deal with the issue of rusting in just a few hours.  Go back, Bosch, to when you got it altogether right!!!  And I will gladly purchase another dishwasher from you!

product_title: Bosch SHE3AR55UC Ascenta 24" Stainless Steel Full Console Dishwasher - Energy Star
review_title: The best thing about this dishwasher is that it is extremely ...
review_text: I purchased this dishwasher because of the Bosch name and my daughter-in-law has a Bosch. My GE was so rough on my dishes that it chipped the edges of cups and bowls.  I was not able to see this particular model in person so I took a chance and ordered it. Not through Amazon but from a local store.  I will not purchase another.  The best thing about this dishwasher is that it is extremely quiet.  However, it is small on the inside and would never do for a family.  The tines on both racks are positioned in such a way that it is very difficult to place dishes or glasses and cups.  The utensil basket is OK.  I like the piece that sections it so that spoons do not get stuck together.  The clincher for me is that after 2 years the main board went bad and it cost almost $300 to repair.  That's just for the part.  I had a Maytag in a different house that lasted over 5 years with no service.  I wish I could have brought it with me when I move.  A more expensive model may be built better, but not this one.

product_title: Bosch SHE3AR55UC Ascenta 24" Stainless Steel Full Console Dishwasher - Energy Star

product_title: GE JB705STSS 30 Freestanding Smoothtop Electric Range - Stainless Steel
review_text: This range has a lot of fine features and seems well built.  Unfortunately, GE ships it with some sort of acrylic binder on its oven fiberglass insulation that has to burn off with the first few uses.  The smell from this burning is nasty, and probably toxic.  GE recommends that you self-clean the oven to get rid of the smell, and open the windows.  So don't buy one in the winter.  I'm left with the feeling that GE cares little for the health and well-being of its customers - all they would have to do is plug in and run the unit at the factory (preferably outside) yet they don't do this.

product_title: GE JB705STSS 30 Freestanding Smoothtop Electric Range - Stainless Steel
review_text: I was hesitant to buy any smoothtop stove but I am glad that I did buy this one after 18 mos of research and talking with others.  I love it.  So many features on this one.  Power boil, 3 ring burner, warmer, convection bake, convection roast and 3 baking racks.  So much for the money.  Shop during holiday sales (presidents day, black friday) and save hundreds!  The top is easy to clean with the ceramabryte cleaner that comes with the stove and also sold on amazon too!  The rangetop has a speckled design which diguises dust that lands on your black stovetop.  I do have a small scratch on mine after 4 wks dont know how that happened.  Cons:  you cannot use cast iron or corningware and I have lots of corningware but I would buy again. Its beautiful, made well and matches my kitchen perfectly.  The convection roast crisp up pizza, crepes, skin on chicken perfectly.  Rangetop heats fast, oven is slow to preheat due to heating element being hidden under oven floor but that makes the oven easier to clean, just make your adjustments.  Timer ring is low volume but I guess you should stay in vicinity while cooking anyway.  Love Love this beautiful stove. There are also lower level GE models with less features that have same quality and beauty for less money.

product_title: GE JB705STSS 30 Freestanding Smoothtop Electric Range - Stainless Steel
review_title: Nasty Oder and HIGH surface temperatures
review_text:
I too had the problem with this GE range (but the Black model) and like you GE was as useless as they were for you. I had to run the Self-Clean procedure 4 times at 5 hrs each time in order for the smell to go away even when trying to cook something in the oven at 350 degrees.

Be aware that when doing the Self-Clean, the top of the oven (where the burners are), the metal of the electronic controls (where the knobs are and the keypad), and the front of the oven will get to over 180 degrees. The sides of the electronic control panel during the Self-Clean cycle will get to over 220 degrees.

Also when cooking something in the oven at 450 degrees the metal of the control panel with the knobs and electronics get to over 125 degrees and the side of the control panel gets to over 155 degrees.

I asked GE if this was expected or normal and they brushed me off and said that is how they designed it.

I do not know if all hidden-element, glass-top ranges are like this but GE would rather not have customers know this.

product_title: GE GDWT668VSS 24" Stainless Steel Fully Integrated Dishwasher - Energy Star
review_text:
I researched dishwashers like crazy and decided that I would just go with the same "updated" model of GE. Prices compared, it is about the same.
I had several things that I wanted. One was the potential for the same length of a normal wash cycle (114 minutes with added heat). Secondly, I wanted hard food disposal and loading flex. I'm very easy to please.

All the newer models available had a little of this, a little of that. And the cycles were torturous in length because new and eco friendly uses less water and energy. It does not appear by reviews to help with cleanliness. In as much as the specs for the motor in this machine(GDWT 668) are the same as my old machine,(PDW 8480) the features do not work the same.

The positives, thus far, are that the dishes are shinier than I remember and the glassware sparkles! It does run more quiet than the old DW. The decibel level went from 53 to 52. And, as the new dishwasher only came with a pittance of insulation, I took my old insulation which wrapped the entire machine and re-used it, so this surely adds to the sound barrier. The dishes are clean, yes, and it runs quiet...but there are negatives in general.

The basket lay-outs have changed and actually gotten smaller. Most machines I researched did not have fold down tines and I wanted this feature. I have folding tines in the lower rack, but it doesn't help to improve loading capability like the old DW. I have a large fry pan that I was able to load upright on the side. Now, it won't fit with the tine placement and if I put the tines down, there is no support to keep the pan upright and save loading space for seven peoples dirty dishes. I cannot fit two rows of coffee cups easily on the top basket, either and I could before. Again, smaller features. I was going to try and take the old lower basket and use it, but it's larger, sadly. I'll get used to it.

The silverware basket has a lovely cover system of holes that makes it so each piece can be cleaned without nesting. Frankly, if I had that kind of time, I would do without a darn DW, so I don't use it!

The final thing is that the added heat and drying do not work the same at all. The Manufacturer recommends Jet Dry. So, because it came with, I am using it. That being said, I have not opened any load of dishes to find them dry, glasses and mugs in particular. Nor is the door of the DW completely dry as with my old PDW8480. It's quite annoying, but not a deal breaker. I am not going to uninstall the darn thing because it sucks at drying stuff. I'll just be grabbing a towel and be glad it's all I've got to do!

I just hope that paying the $819.00 will last me 7 more years. I don't agree with any of the eco friendly technologies because in reading reviews, those people are paying more for less all the way around, with the exception of emotional comfort that they are helping to save the environs. This is why I chose the near identical DW hoping to get the same work out of it. I am practical and what works for me, may not work for others. Nothing is perfect, so it gets 3 stars. It cleans well, is quiet, and looks count.

product_title: GE GDWT668VSS 24" Stainless Steel Fully Integrated Dishwasher - Energy Star
review_text:
I didn't purchase this dishwasher on Amazon; I bought it elsewhere. Hopefully that doesn't discount my review at all.

That said, we're really happy with our dishwasher. We did all of the research on Consumer Reports and read all of the consumer reviews from retail places like Amazon and Best Buy. The best thing to do is to just find one with the features you want and hope for the best. That's what we did and it worked out nicely. The consumer reviews are pretty polarizing: "1 star this thing is terrible and noisy!" or "5 star awesome unit!" Rarely do people actually go into good detail with it (except with KitchenAid's and their broken racks).

That said, here's why we bought ours. It has a self cleaning food grinder. We plan on renting our place out rather than selling after we leave, so things like a food disposal are more tenant friendly. None of the Euro brands have a food disposal so keep that in mind when your friends brag about how quiet their unit is. It means that they have to clean a waste filter by hand. No thanks.

This dishwasher also has nice features like steam clean, heated water, sanitizing confirmation, etc. Our water is already pretty hot so the only one we use on a regular basis is sanitize. I'd say it works really well, but honestly I have no idea if it's working. Steam clean works, but we rarely use it unless we're lazy (or tipsy) when doing the dishes. Overall it's quiet so that's a nice plus. The water pump in this unit is really good and that's honestly the loudest thing in the cycle. Not the pump itself, but the sound of the water dumping into your disposal or p-trap. Nothing GE can do about that though.

The blower for the top rack is nice and gets all the glasses completely dry. The only exception is plastic cups. Nothing gets plastic cups dry.

Overall, a nice dishwasher that we'd recommend.

product_title: GE GSM2260VSS Console Dishwasher
review_text: Only option for a dishwasher due to the way the kitchen was built, so I had to either buy this or remodel the kitchen.  Overpriced for what it is, comparable to a $200 dishwasher in features and quality.  Ordered the stainless steel model and the lower access panel cover came white so I now have a tri-finished dishwasher.  Black on top, stainless in the middle, white just below, then black.  If I spend $950 on a dishwasher, at least put the right parts on it in the factory.

product_title: Samsung FE710DRS 30 In. Freestanding Electric Range with Ceramic Cooktop and 5.9 Cu. Ft. Flex Dual Convection Oven, Stainless Steel
review_title: Good features but poor quality in cook top
review_text: The oven cooks excellent but the steam function on it doesn't really clean nothing, you still have to go with the 2 hours self cleaning in order to get it clean. You can definitely save time by cooking two meals at the same time with the separator. The separator works great cause you set different temperatures for both dishes and both cook perfectly without changing the taste cause the flavors do not get mixed up.I only gave to 3 stars because of the quality of the cook top . After a week if cooking and cleaning it with the solution recommended that came with it it's got already scratches .So I blame that on poor quality.Otherwise the cook top boils very fast and cooks good. Overall I am satisfied with it but for the quality of the cook top the price is a little high, even if Amazon had the best price once again on the market 500$ less then any other store.It comes with one year warranty from the manufacturer but I would suggest get the extended plan from Samsung before your year expires so that way in case your cook top get scratched pretty bad you can have it covered where you don't have to buy a new stove again and again.

product_title: Samsung FE710DRS 30 In. Freestanding Electric Range with Ceramic Cooktop and 5.9 Cu. Ft. Flex Dual Convection Oven, Stainless Steel
review_text: I’ve had this range for four months and am extremely disappointed with it.  Although the oven works fine, the black glass top is amazingly cheap for such an expensive range.  It is impossible to keep clean and scratches very easily.  I had my old GE range for 10 years and it still looked like new when I replaced it with this Samsung. In just 4 months, this range looks old and worn.  Every pot scratches the surface.  I only use the pad and cleaner supplied with the range and even that scratches the surfaces.  Plus, any spillovers go down into the vents and streak the oven door glass.  I contacted Samsung and they sent out a technician who took pictures and said Samsung would call me.  It’s been 3 weeks and no call.  I finally got ahold of Samsung's Executive Customer service today and they said no cosmetic issues will be covered under the warranty.  I would never but a Samsung kitchen appliance again.

product_title: Samsung FE710DRS 30 In. Freestanding Electric Range with Ceramic Cooktop and 5.9 Cu. Ft. Flex Dual Convection Oven, Stainless Steel
review_text: Bought this to replace a Kenmore Elite range that lasted several years.  Main selling point was the double convection oven.  What a mistake!!  I bake frequently and this oven cannot be compared to a Kenmore.  From the beginning, I have had to rotate the item half way through baking so that it would baked evenly.  Anything that can be flipped (cookies, biscuits, etc.) will be much darker on the bottom if you don't flip during mid-cycle.  Never had these issues with Kenmore.  And to top it off, the main circuit board went out just a few months after the one-year warranty ended.  Samsung would not consider fixing this for me.  Instead offered (for full price) the extended warranty, which I bought since it cost less than replacing the circuit board.  I first called Samsung the second week in November.  It is December 15 and the part still has not arrived.  I am told it will not be here before Christmas, so am scrambling to try to rent a range before family starts arriving for Christmas.

product_title: Samsung FE710DRS 30 In. Freestanding Electric Range with Ceramic Cooktop and 5.9 Cu. Ft. Flex Dual Convection Oven, Stainless Steel
review_text: Love my new stove!!! Even during the biggest sales of the year at all the appliance stores, department stores, home improvement stores and online this was by far the cheapest price. Came delivered by truck all packaged nicely and dropped at my door. Love that you can cook at 2 different temps and it has the warming burner. There is so much room on the inside and 3 racks.

product_title: Samsung FE710DRS 30 In. Freestanding Electric Range with Ceramic Cooktop and 5.9 Cu. Ft. Flex Dual Convection Oven, Stainless Steel
review_text: The convection oven(s) work great.  We have enjoyed those.  However the burner tops heat slow, much slower than our previous glass top GE range.  Also the "fast boil" burner is a joke.  There is no fast boil there, in fact it is slower than the other burners.  I would not buy again.

product_title: Samsung FE710DRS 30 In. Freestanding Electric Range with Ceramic Cooktop and 5.9 Cu. Ft. Flex Dual Convection Oven, Stainless Steel
review_title: Do not buy this oven, will not hold temperature
review_text:
We bought this stove in December 2014, we noticed within about 2 weeks that it just didn't seem to be cooking at the right temp. We started testing with our digital temp sensor and verified that the oven would preheat to the proper temp, but once you open the oven to insert your food item, it never recovers the temperature. If preheated to 375, it will drop to 320 and never come back up. You have to reset the temp, like you are starting over and it will come back up. We had it serviced, they replaced the board in the back along with a temp sensor, but it didn't fix it. The problem does not appear to be related to the unique double oven, but to the electronics.

Its not worth the risk in my opinion to buy this model.

product_title: Samsung FE710DRS 30 In. Freestanding Electric Range with Ceramic Cooktop and 5.9 Cu. Ft. Flex Dual Convection Oven, Stainless Steel
review_text:
I purchased in January 2015. The idea was great. Two ovens! I bake a lot and wanted two temps for two ovens. This thing is horrible. I cannot even bake a pizza in it. Top oven only has convection. Pizza has to be rotated to get done on each side. The outside of the pizza will get very brown and the center will not be done. So I tried the bottom convection. Same thing except the bottom gets brown before the top. Tried the conventional setting on the bottom oven. Pizza gets burnt on the bottom and not done on the top. Have to move it to the top oven because it is the only one with broiler. The broil has two settings, hi and lo. Do not use hi. You will burn the pizza quickly. It has a pizza setting. That doesn't work very well either.
So with this being said, I can't even bake a frozen pizza in this thing and I have been baking for years!
As for the stove top. The glass is hard to clean. I had a glass cook top before and it wasn't as hard to clean. The eyes do not keep good temps. There is either super high, boil it to heck and back, or low is basically a warming unit.
I hate this range. Trying to return it.
Update: two service techs came out and waiting on a third. Second tech admitted that the temp on one side was 350 and the other was 260. He suggested that I take out all of the racks and bake that way. I asked if he could fix it and he said no. I asked if he would tell Samsung that it was not able to be repaired and he said no. Why won't they do something about this stove? I'm going to ship it to Mr. Sam Sung's front door!

product_title: Samsung FE710DRS 30 In. Freestanding Electric Range with Ceramic Cooktop and 5.9 Cu. Ft. Flex Dual Convection Oven, Stainless Steel
review_text: Bought this due to the potential "double oven" feature. I have used once, and worked well. Rapid boil is fantastic. The broiler however, is less than steller. Good for toasting breads, but, really terrible for meat. Food in the oven comes out evenly cooked and cooks faster due to the convection feature. Also love the warming burner on top. The controls take some getting used to because of all the features on this product. Overall, I'm satisfied with this product. Might not buy again however because I use my broiler a lot and was quite disappointed.

product_title: LG LSC27925SB26.5 Cu. Ft. Smooth Black Side-By-Side Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_text:

product_title: LG SteamDryer Series DLEX2450R 27 Front-Load Electric Dryer 7.3 cu. ft. Capacity - Red
review_text:
I purchased the LG 2040 steam washer and dryer in combination, and could not be happier! Prior to this, we owned an old whirlpool agitator washer and drier, which worked great, but after 14 years, were starting to have some issues. In researching washers and dryers, we decided to go with the steam versions due to their excellent ability to wash more efficiently, reduce wrinkles in clothing, and reduce allergens. However, never having had any experience with the steam option on washers and dryers, we were not really sure what to expect. Well, after using them for about three week now, we are very happy with the results!

I must say, the steam option in a dryer is a must have feature, at least for my family. I was not at all sure that would be the case before buying this machine, but it has proved its worth to me. You can add steam to normal drying cycles to reduce static or improve ironing conditions by removing wrinkles. Bottom line, this feature works, and works well. Importantly, with the LG model, water is added to a reservoir on the top left panel before the cycle begins. This is very convenient, and doesn't require a separate water line hookup like other steam dryer models do. I am currently in the process of learning how to properly steam dry my dress shirts to minimize ironing and reduce the dry cleaning bill - so far with really good results. This dryer also has a steam fresh cycle for already dry materials in need of a good de-wrinkling and refreshment. The steam sanitary cycle works great for already dried clothing or other items that cannot be washed, but could use a good sanitation. The rack works great on sweater and shoes. There are lots of features, and I am still trying to figure them all out.

The dryer, whether using steam or normal drying procedures, is fantastic! We've had tremendous results, and our clothing has never felt fresher. The machine is overall very quiet and smooth. It will take lots of experimentation, which can be quite fun actually, to understand all the features of this dryer. Highly recommended!

product_title: LG WM2450HRA 3.7cu.ft. Steam Front Control Washer, Red
review_text: Make sure you remove the 4 bolts with the rubber bushing on the back put there for shipping before washing clothes otherwise you will watch the machine dance down the hallway when it starts the spin cycle. Also where the water lines  connect on the back they are plastic and are very hard to get the hoses to seat and seal properly. It still shakes a little on spin cycle but just make sure you have the legs adjusted right. I also got a rubber gym mat and cut it into 4 squares to place under the legs. Other than that I love this washer.

product_title: LG WM2450HRA 3.7cu.ft. Steam Front Control Washer, Red
review_text:
I purchased the LG 2040 steam washer and dryer in combination, and could not be happier! Prior to this, we owned an old whirlpool agitator washer and drier, which worked great, but after 14 years, were starting to have some issues. In researching washers and dryers, we decided to go with the steam versions due to their excellent ability to wash more efficiently, reduce wrinkles in clothing, and reduce allergens. However, never having had any experience with the steam option on washers and dryers, we were not really sure what to expect. Well, after using them for about three week now, we are very happy with the results!

The steam option on the washer (which can be difficult to fully appreciate) definitely has benefits. The primary benefit is the ability to reduce allergens on the "Allergene" setting. It is great to know that items are getting thoroughly sanitized in the wash. Steam also reduces the amount of water being used (which is already quite low in the front-loading machine). Finally, don't worry about steam shrinking the clothes. Basically, the steam comes from above, while there is cooler water in the bottom where the clothes are located. The steam gives a deeper penetration with superior cleaning, while the cooler water keeps your fabric protected. It also minimizes wrinkling problems by softening the fabric. We've had excellent results in experimenting with the steam washer option.

Another feature we love in the washer is the load sensing capability. In this process, which takes about one minute at the beginning of the cycle, the washer spins a couple of times, judging the weight of your load (the material must be dry for this to work properly), and estimating how much detergent you should use. Bottom line, this will save you lots of money on the HE detergent required for these machines. Most loads, which look like full loads due to their volume, actually only require a half measure of detergent. The machine lets you know exactly how much to put into the load before beginning the cycle. This is a genius feature!

The washer, whether using steam or normal washing procedures, is fantastic! We've had tremendous results, and our clothing has never felt cleaner and fresher. One note: the machine does wobble a bit in the spin cycle, but is overall very quiet and smooth. It will take lots of experimentation, which can be quite fun actually, to understand all the features of this washer. Highly recommended!

product_title: LG WM2450HRA 3.7cu.ft. Steam Front Control Washer, Red
review_text:
cant agree more with the other two reviews! I've own this washer for about 4 weeks now, and I'm loving everything about it, especially the steam and load sensing features :) Our clothes come out really clean, soft, and smell good! product_title: Samsung RS261MDWP 26.0 Cu. Ft. White Side-By-Side Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_title: WARNING! Defected  freezer evaporator circulation module put on units made before june of 2013
review_text:
Refrigerator units made before june of 2013 have defected freezer evaporator circulation modules on them, which is the biggest cause of ice developing on the back of the inside of the freezer unit, that forms around the circulation vents that clogs the vents up which will not allow proper airflow to circulate throughout the refrigerator unit itself. These defectives units are also responsible for ice build up to occur around the evaporator fan in the freezer which may cause the fan to develop a loud noise when the evaporator fan kicks in.

Samsung redesigned the freezer evaporator circulation module for these units starting in june of 2013. if you have one of these units that were made prior to june of 2013, you should call samsung and demand them to replace the defective freezer evaporator circulation module unit or file a complaint to the better business bureau if they don't do anything about it.

product_title: Samsung RS261MDWP 26.0 Cu. Ft. White Side-By-Side Refrigerator - Energy Star

product_title: Samsung RS261MDWP 26.0 Cu. Ft. White Side-By-Side Refrigerator - Energy Star
