product_title: Bosch SHE3AR52UC Ascenta 24" White Full Console Dishwasher - Energy Star
review_text: First I want to make clear that I am referring to the BOSCH 50dBA. We purchased this dishwasher because of the Bosch name. We had several criteria which this dishwasher met: It is very quiet and the dishes come out clean. BUT: The bottom rack does not roll out properly. It falls into the rut and I have to lift it out....pretty easily when the dishwasher is relatively empty, but still it clangs all of the dishes and I know a dishwasher should not do this. It also holds a very limited amount of dishes. If you use any sized pots and lids or large plastic containers, this is not the dishwasher for you. It does come with a diagram suggesting loading patterns. Even this is misleading. If you want to put in full-sized plates you can't put anything else that's sizable in the bottom shelf...including salad bowls. That is annoying. Most significantly, the dishwasher always smells awful. From the first use. This is not due to trapped food. This began after the first use and we keep the trap clean. I have had many dishwashers and this has never been a problem. The dishwasher cost just under $600. I couldn't be more disappointed!

product_title: Bosch SHE3AR52UC Ascenta 24" White Full Console Dishwasher - Energy Star
review_title: Good In Spite of Some Bad Reviews Here
review_text:
There are a large percentage of reviews on Amazon that rate this product low. There are percentage reviews on other sites that are much more positive. I found this dishwasher a good deal, easy to install, built well and cleans dishes well. I look to Amazon reviews for my purchases, so I was concerned about this product. The Bosch name is good and they make more expensive ones. I don't think the relatively high number of negative reviews here gives the right impression.

Pros: Stainless steel interior. Solid door that closes well (self closing when running I think).
Relatively easy to install (I did it myself to save 150.) However, installation takes much more than plugging in a toaster and you run the normal risks doing so.
Cleans well. Absolutely quiet.

Cons: Some cycles work better for washing and drying.
Not the best for drying dishes.

I think Bosch dishwashers use less water, so using less detergent actually prevents spotting. I use the normal wash, not auto. This machine perfectly cleaned baked on pie from the bake pan with just a half container of detergent.

It was easy to install. You can connect the electricity and water after putting it inside the cabinets. But the outflow need to be connected first (it's in back). Try 3-4 wraps of Teflon tape (provided!) for the water inflow.

The unit does not have a heating element on the bottom. The dishes get 95% dry when running the sanitize feature. If absolutely dry dishes are necessary for you, I would look elsewhere.

Remember, less detergent and try normal wash, not auto with sanitizer on.

product_title: Bosch SHE3AR52UC Ascenta 24" White Full Console Dishwasher - Energy Star
review_text:
My household installed this dishwasher four weeks ago and have run it between one and three times daily since. I was satisfied from the first load but waited a month to review due to mixed reviews in case problems cropped up.

In short, this was a marvelous purchase. It is super, super quiet and cleans extremely well. The hidden heating element protects any small items that fall. We use tons of flatware, so we appreciate the ample (but removable) silverware bin. Those in-door silverware holders would be inadequate. I like the countdown timer.

Regarding complaints of other reviewers: We have had no problems whatsoever with unwanted odors, wet dishes, or self-starting. (The entire appliance should be powered off between washes, anyway.)

The tines that hold dishes in place are laid out differently than other dishwashers I've used, but after a couple weeks, I had a good system going. I actually like that the rows on top vary in width. It holds different size cups more securely when the person loading can place each item where it fits best. There is plenty of height on the lower rack to hold a blender carafe or other tall items.

The machine does require rinse agent to operate properly, so be sure you have some on hand.

product_title: Bosch SHE3AR52UC Ascenta 24" White Full Console Dishwasher - Energy Star
review_title: Bosch sure beats GE in the dishwasher department.
review_text:
This Bosch DW replaced a brand-new GE that was basically DOA with failure to close, three service calls with a fourth pending. It was cheaply made and rather than replacing it after the second service call we were pushed to accept a third and fourth call for the same exact issue. Terrible customer relations. I would never buy another GE dishwasher.
Bosch SHE3ARF2UC pros:
1. Made solidly. You can tell the engineering was well thought out and implemented unlike the GE.
2. Stainless steel tub with polypropylene bottom and a manual filter. This aspect eliminates noise of the grinding and pump to achieve the 50 dB it advertises.
3. Cleans dishes amazingly well. You can set the amount of jet dry solution from off to 5. We have our set 3.
4. Superb selection of wash cycles. We love the express as it only takes 30 minutes. In a two-person household with minimal dishes throughout the day, the unit is only 1/2-3/4 full by the evening. As one reviewer commented, you do not want to use excess amounts of dishwashing powder. 1 tablespoon suffices for this size load. Never fill the cup unless it is jammed full and the dishes and pots are heavily soiled. We always prerinse and scrape our dishes.
5. After the Express 30 minutes cycle, we allow the dishes to dry with the door closed for the first half hour then open up and pull out the racks to dry overnight. There is always a little water on the bottom of the cups turned upside down. A quick dab with a dishtowel prior to replacing in the drawer/cabinet is all that is needed. Silverware is sparkling clean and glasses are spot and streak free. It is probably best not to use any of the DW gels in this unit.
Cons:
1. Capacity may be a little small for a household of 4-6 people. You would likely have to run this unit twice a day. You may want to opt for a bigger cabinet.
2. While some bemoan the lack of a track for the wheels on the bottom rack, that's simply a matter of getting used to. There is a nice convenient handle that sticks up in the center of the rack and you should use that to pull the rack out and push it back in. It tracks perfectly well that way. It would appear to me that trying to engineer some tracks for the wheels would introduce crevices that reduce the efficiency of the washing and allow for moisture accumulation and therefore odors. I like it the way it is. The present design therefore is not a con in my opinion.
3. The only beef we have is the design of the racks. It is supposed to be "the European design" whatever that is. There are very narrow tines and some that are not so narrow at right angles. The upper rack has an indentation in the front that actually removes some of the capacity. It is designed as a handle to pull and push the rack in and out of the cabinet. The upper rack in the back has female openings into which male openings in the back of the cabinet would fit for introducing the water pressure to spin the spray arm underneath the upper rack. It is really an ingenious design and apparently works quite well if the upper rack is restored to its proper position before closing the door.
All in all, a terrific machine. Hinges have some springs on it to allow positional opening as well as rapid closure of the door. The clasp for closing is secure and engineered beautifully compared to that GE dog with it's plastic clasp and the cheap hinges attached to thin metal frames. Take it from us, get a Bosch but don't buy a $1500 model with all the bells and whistles. $600-$800 is plenty of machine for most of us.
Well we did not buy it through Amazon, we got it through a local bricks and mortar, privately held appliance Center but even then paid over $350 more than we should have as we got no benefits from installation rebates or store credits as we would have from a local big box store. Mom-and-pop appliance stores want to compete and what they have to offer is superior service and personal interest in its customers. When they fail in that respect and in getting your repeat business, they are not worthy of your future business. Such was our scenario for nearly 4 months dealing with the defective GE DW with the local dealer. Finally we got the unit removed and a replacement ordered and installed only after many weeks of dealing with GE customer (non-) service and the local dealers business office.

review_text: Bought the dishwasher in July 2015.  There is door switch which works a depression in the top of the door. When you close the door it clicks shut and the door switch is engaged.  Long story short, in October 2015, the switch didn't click and the dishwasher didn't work.  Bosch factory warranty repairman was dispatched. He unscrewed the dishwasher from the counter, pulled it out,  bent the top frame downward with his hands, saw that the door then "clicked" and put "adjustment" on the warranty invoice. What did I know?  I thought that was a strange way to handle the problem.  I asked him about it and he said that's how it's fixed.  Okay, fast foward to February 7, 2016. The unit stopped working again.  I called Bosch and they said they would dispatch the same repairman.  Instead, I found an authorized local service company to do to the warranty repair.  The repairman took the unit out of the counter and saw that the top of the frame (housing the door switch) had been bent down.  He asked about that and I told him.  He then further dismantled the unit, did his tests and said that he needed to order a new door switch and control panel.  It seems that the "adjustment" made in October by the Bosch guy put the unit out of spec and was bound, sooner or later, to destroy the door switch and control panel.  It took three months for that to happen.  Buyers, beware.  That experience is unacceptable.[[ASIN:B0057YO0IM Bosch SHE3AR52UC Ascenta 24" White Full Console Dishwasher - Energy Star]]

product_title: Bosch SHE43R55UC
review_text:
Bought from a local retailer, but love it enough to share a review:

Our house is designed with the kitchen right out in the open, right in the middle. We like it. What we didn't like is the noise our former dishwasher made, a "quiet series" dishwasher. Or the noise from the one before that, also billed as being very quiet. This Bosch? It really is quiet, except for the barest announcement when the cycle changes. Thanks to the light at the base, you know it's on. But you wouldn't know from listening unless you press your ear against the door.

Even though this dishwasher and our previous models shared the same interior size, this one does hold more on two racks thanks to a better layout of the tines.

Our former machines utilized the age old heating element on the floor of the interior to heat the water. And over time, that heating element became calcified or coated with dishwashing soap or something -- who knows. I know that over time, our machine did a poor job of heating the water, ergo, a poor job of washing the dishes. In this machine the water heats at the entry, instant-heat hot water. It seems more efficient. It's hot.

No matter which settings we chose, our former machines ran for ages, only to present barely clean dishes. We scrape the dishes, load this washer and set for "auto clean" and "sanitize," and while I haven't tested with a timer, it seems to operate in about half the time of the other dishwashers we owned. That's efficiency.

The only thing it doesn't have (although some Bosch models do) is a delayed timer. I made good use of that in our other machines so that we weren't disturbed by the noise. It operated in the middle of the night, away from our bedroom, away from us. This machine doesn't have the timer, but it's a moot point since it doesn't make any noise. I turn it on, then we have a conversation, watch television, listen to music, all undisturbed.

Great price for a quality product. Now. If someone would just explain to me why dishwashers need to be cleaned, I'd be happy.

product_title: Bosch SHE43R55UC
review_title: Great replacement for a builder-quality unit
review_text:
Thirteen years ago, our new house came with a decent but no-frills dishwasher - AKA - Builder quality. It worked for all those years but eventually, when we decided to go with all stainless steel appliances in the kitchen, we searched hard for a top quality replacement. Using several sources and with the assistance of an outstanding sales rep at our local Sears (Bob in Rockaway, NJ) we settled on this Bosch unit. While it is not the top Bosch model, it has many more features than our original and all we really need.

The two we are loving after a few months of hard use are the stainless steel tub and the whisper quiet operation. Seeing the gleaming stainless "tub" after a wash tells me that the dishes are really clean and sanitized. Also very important - Our old unit was so loud that you had to go into another room to use the phone. How quiet is the Bosch? So quiet that they have to provide a small red light projected on the floor (our cat loves it) to remind you that it's doing its thing. How cool is that?

As has been mentioned by another reviewer, the detergent used makes a significant difference. Bosch provided a sample of their recommended detergent (Finish tablets) and we have to agree - using our regular "Cascade" powder, there was a residue on the dishes. I suspect that I am using too much and will experiment to find the sweet spot because we have a near full box in the pantry.

This unit does a good job on pots and pans too. My wife doesn't mind scrubbing the pots but I hate that job and sneak them in whenever I can to get them done and put away. So far, every pot, pan, strainer, etc., has come out clean and caked-on-food free. Shhh! don't tell my wife.

Summary - dishes come out clean every time - 2 stars. Pots and pans come out spotless - 1 star. As quiet as a churchyard at midnight - 2 stars. Total 5 stars...

For overall quality, value and performance, you will have to go a long way (and a pay a higher price) to beat this Bosch unit.

Highly recommended.

product_title: Bosch SHE43R55UC
review_title: Wheels fall off, food gets stuck in jets
review_text:
I have had a mid-price Bosch that was recommended by consumer reports for two years now, and I can't understand why no one else has complained about it. It cleans great at first, and is quiet. But the wheels are constantly falling off - I've lost four of them. When you pull out a full bottom rack it skittles across the dishwasher door and every time I worry that the whole thing will crash on the floor.

The water flows through jets in two different spinning arms. The tiniest bit of food - often a scrap of lettuce or something unidentifiable - will get stuck in the jets. This signifiantly impacts cleaning. I struggle to pick it out with tweezers. I DO rinse my dishes before loading them!

product_title: Bosch SHE43R55UC
review_text: For my family of 3 and for the price, happy with dishwasher. Been using for a month. Verrrry quiet, which I love! Have to double check sometimes to make sure it is running. Dishes come out sparkling clean. The negative is the design of the baskets. It is not easy to load and I cannot get as much in as I did with my other dishwasher. With only 3 of us here (most of the time), that's not a big deal. Because it cleans so well, is efficient and quiet, I don't mind running it more often. As recommended by all dishwasher people in the know, we do not rinse our dishes before loading-just scrape off the food before putting in. I've even left them overnight and they still come out clean. The way the dishwasher cleans is more important to me then how it loads. Compared it to other dishwasherws and found this to be the best buy per price and reviews. Not disappointed.

product_title: Bosch SHE43R55UC
review_text:
We went to not having a dishwasher to having this one. It cleans well and the racks are versatile enough. It is super quiet. We have close quarters and we hear it for some cycles, but most of the time we don't even know it is on. The beeping for the end of each cycle was super annoying and so we turned it off by following direction. The red light on the bottom is a nice feature because as I said, you can hear it most of the time and the red light indicates that it is still cleaning.
The biggest complaint is the rinse well indicator light stopped working within a month or so. The compartment for the rinse aid doesn't seem to work quite like it was intended either. When we first used it, it would slowly us the rinse aid and when the light went out a couple washes down the road, we would refill. Now it empties with each wash. We still fill it up because it does help tremendously with the cleaning and drying of the dishes.

product_title: Bosch SHE43R55UC
review_text: We bought this to replace a GE that was just three year old - enough said. The Bosch does a good job and is super quite. On this model though there's no rinse cycle and no way of knowing how far along the wash cycle has run, so 4 stars.

product_title: Bosch SHE43R55UC
review_text:
Yes and No. I see all these great 4- & 5-star reviews and yes, I do agree with most comments. The machine is quiet, it cleans and dries quite well (except for certain plastic items). Though I didn’t notice it mentioned, the upper (3rd) rack for silverware is more convenient and loads more easily than the lift out baskets which take up considerable room. There was a short learning curve to puzzle out the operating instructions but after a few weeks I gave it no further thought.

But my experience relates more closely with the 1-star rating. Certain similarities in that review immediately caught my attention; i.e., Consumer Reports, old Maytag, rack design and broken glasses. I also made the purchase based on Consumer Reports; but sometimes those reports don’t mention an untested important feature. In this case the problem is the upper rack design.

There is a picture in the Bosch instruction manual that shows glasses loaded all in a row. I tried that as well as other placements but found no consistent way to avoid broken glasses. Never had that problem with our 20+ year old Maytag; in that machine I never broke even fine crystal. In no way would I trust our crystal in the Bosch.

Bosch shows on-line video tips. But though they mention preferred ways to load cups, plates, bowls and large items, they don’t mention drinking glasses. Each time I load the machine I am frustrated and disappointed on that one point alone. If it weren't for that problem, this would be a 5-star review

product_title: LG LFX33975ST32.5 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel French Door Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_text:
This is a great product. We have a family of 5 and it is truly amazing how much more storage we have in this fridge then our last one.
The general build quality seems very good however only time will tell how well all the seals, lights, and electronics hold out.

Some of my favorite features.
Miniature ice cubes no need to use the crushed ice feature unless maybe you want a mixed drink.
Lighting is great even when full of food
Condiment storage is adequate. We seem to have lots of little jars and the design allows for storage in front of the door gallon storage bins this is very helpful
The little storage compartments on the bottom of the fridge for cheese sticks and quick grab items for the kids. They are deep and easy access for the little ones
The sliding shelf for tall products like a 2 liter or pineapple this is used more then I thought it would be. We almost always have this shelf slid back

The Freezer is great the three shelves might be the best part.
On the top we keep ice cream, extra ice, and things to that nature I have never had ice cream kept hard but soft at the same time "love it"
The middle shelf all the bagged and boxed veggies
One the bottom it is so deep there seems to be no bottom. It is large enough to hold a rack of ribs flat front to back

Not so favorite.
The ice maker is truly the slowest thing I have ever seen. Even on fast ice it can not make a full bucket in one day.
Now that we have had full ice we don't run out but we still keep the bottom bucket full just in case.
The touch buttons are sensitive to where they are touched or the touch area is just very small. We use the child lock all the time and it is hard to set and unlock without paying close attention to where your finger is.

I give this 5 stars quiet, great space, not much larger physically then my last fridge, but so well designed there is much more usable space everywhere.

product_title: LG LFX33975ST32.5 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel French Door Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_text: This refrigerator has all the room you will need. Only problem is lack of space for larger items such as 2 liter bottles and milk. One shelf folds in half to make room for the taller items, but it still isn't enough. Removal of the whole shelf is necessary. The right door has room for tall items, but the temperature is higher there. A cold cuts drawer is full width of the interior making it impossible to open without both French doors opened. Two half width drawers would be more convenient. This way you would only have to open a single French door. The temperatures shown on the front door LEDs is lower than what I actually get with my two separate thermometers. The paddle that switches the ice and water on is easily marred. This happened the first time we used it. Just like getting a scratch on the hood of your new car on the first day. Polishing didn't help. We have a cabinet above the refrigerator that cleared by less than a quarter inch. Make sure you have at least 68.88 inches of height clearance. The manufacturer boasts a 10 year compressor warranty, but only includes a single year labor warranty. Ten or one year compressor warranty, you still need the extended warranty that covers it all for up to 5 years including labor. Most extended warranties will let you extend the length beyond the 5 years and include up to $100 for food spoilage. The ice maker alone will pay for the cost of an extended warranty if it goes out. Our ice makers have been replaced in the past. The doors are the only stainless parts, the rest is painted gray. This covers about all the negative items I found in the first two weeks of ownership. Overall, this is a very large spacious refrigerator. It looks great inside and out. The two extra drawers in the freezer are great for items like TV dinners and pizzas. A bucket is included for storage of extra ice. I found nothing negative about the freezer section. If the above items were addressed, I would give this refrigerator a full  5 star rating.

product_title: LG LFX33975ST32.5 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel French Door Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_text:

review_title: Unreliable product, horrible LG customer service

If the board is not ready by 06/29, they will start the process again. This means: 1. wait 14 days, then 2. wait more days. This is so ridiculous. product_title: Haier HPIM26W Portable Countertop Ice Maker, White
review_text: We purchased this to put on our 30'sailboat.  It makes enough ice at night when we are plugged into 30 amp shore power to fill the cooler so we have cold drinks all day long.  I leave it on the salon floor at the bulkhead and the cord is long enough to plug into the 110 volt outlet in the head(bathroom) or at the portside outlet.  By plugging it in to the outlet in the head, we don't have to step over the cord and the door to the head clears the cord, so that the head can be used while the machine is plugged in.  Also,  the unit is short enough that the salon table can be converted into a bed without having to move the icemaker.  When we leave the boat for a few days, I  drain the unit into the bilge, eliminating the need to lift the unit to drain it.  This ice maker makes cruising more enjoyable for us -- who like a warm drink on a hot day!  I haven't tried to run it off the inverter,  but I believe that it could be run off the inverter, as we have enough house battery to keep our onboard refrigerator running for 48 hours using battery power.

review_text:

One note about the first days batch of ice...yuck. Had a plastic kind of taste. Actually, the entire machine smelled like it tasted. I just let it make baskets of ice all day the first day and discarded all of them. The next day, the odor was gone and the ice tasted fresh and clean. I use filtered water. The ice is really soft - great for crunching!

I use mine at work. It sits on top of my mini fridge. It's perfect!! The window on top is neat, but the really neat part is watching the ice get dumped into the basket. It's cool! My coworkers love it too!

product_title: Energy Star Affinity 3.26 cu. ft. Front Load Washer in White
review_title: Failed after a year and a half
review_text:
Note that the following is regarding FAFW3577KW1, a previous iteration of this model; perhaps the current model has improved.

My tiny 1970s-construction laundry closet isn't deep enough for most current models, so (not wanting to remove the closet door) I had limited choices at my local dealer in 2011...basically, this was it. The installers had a terrible time stacking the corresponding dryer on top of this washer and installing the set in my closet, so I hoped it would last many years. I read the manual, followed all the instructions, and took good care of it. Since it's just me, I do wash once a week at most.

However, about a year and a half after installation, the washer started beeping. It wasn't even in use! All its lights (including the panel and interior light) were flashing on and off too. Was it possessed? To get the beeping and flashing to stop, I had to unplug the machine.

The Electrolux warranty is one year (they've got it down to a science), and the repair was for 2/3 what the washer cost. Fortunately, I'd used VISA (which covers an extra year for repairs). Electrolux agreed to cover the parts, so the untimely problem mostly cost me time and headache.

The local Authorized Service Center guys (Bay Appliance Repair, yay!) replaced the control panel and said this machine breaks down all the time. (They suggested I sell the set and get a better one, like Whirlpool Duet--which I already knew wouldn't fit in my closet, as it's what the dealer originally sold me).

Jumping forward to the first pandemic year, 2020, another issue cropped up with this washer. Troubleshooting indicated the door lock. I bought a generic door lock assembly on Amazon (about $6), watched a video on the repair, and had my friend (by phone!) walk me through fixing it. It worked! So, while some learned to make sourdough, I learned to be a handy-person!

It's now December 2021, and I can happily report that the door lock is still operational. (Time to learn how to make sourdough.) The washer control panel is still going strong too. Do they build the originals of these things with parts from the Rejects bin or what?

One other thing I've noticed with this washer (which may be common to modern washers) is that the delicate cycle leaves the load somewhat waterlogged. I run a spin cycle afterward, and that does the trick. This probably nixes much of the benefit of the delicate cycle, but hang drying takes less time that way. I suppose I could use the normal cycle on cold instead of running two cycles. Whatever.

I'd rather have spent twice as much for something that's not crap but isn't ENORMOUS. I'm aware of the European models like Bosch, but the capacity is smaller. If anyone knows of a reliable normal-capacity (US) set that's 29-and-3/4" deep or less, I'm open to suggestions.

review_title: Still love this washer a year later
review_text:
It is now May 2014 and I've now had the washer for a year of hard family use, and am still absolutely loving this washer. Highly recommend. (Maybe the other reviewer here who leaves change in his clothes...maybe that is what eventually broke the glass door of his washer?)

Anyway, here is what I wrote in May 2013:

This is my new washer. It is an HE front-loader, and since I didn't buy the optional pedestal (too expensive!), the washer requires only the same space as a conventional top-loader washing machine. Perfect.

It is my first front loader, and is easy to use, just a quick perusal of the instructions in the manual, and I was washing my first load. The machine is so quiet, I went down in the basement a few times just to make sure it was running, because I could not hear it from upstairs! (The horrible, awful GE machine that it replaced sounded like a broken jet airplane when it ran.) This beautiful Frigidaire washer doesn't even vibrate. It's so sturdy and stable.

I saved the best for last: it cleans beautifully! Even in our hard well water, clothes look and smell clean, bright and fresh, even the half-dirty clothes that hadn't been getting clean, not really clean, with my old washer. The appliance dealer told me use just a tablespoon of HE detergent, no more, and that is what I do. Works great. A bottle of Tide lasts more than a month of daily or twice daily loads.

As a side note: there are several reviews here bringing the star rating of this washer down, and it's misleading people looking for decent reviews. At least one of the reviews is for a DRYER! One is for a different model! So, don't go by the average star rating on this, read the individual reviews on this product and the other washers you are considering.

Recommendation: Yes, two thumbs up for this beautiful, quiet and efficient washer.

product_title: Energy Star Affinity 3.26 cu. ft. Front Load Washer in White
review_title: Repairs after one year, Total Failure After Four
review_text:
You saw my headline. Avoid this model.

But I have to say, until it broke down, it was an awesome unit. It got clothing SUPER clean, especially with the sanitize option. It was a gorgeous ice blue color, and it was extremely quiet. That's why I bought it. But a couple repairs and then right after the warranty ended, the glass front of the washer shattered. I was in shock. And of course, before then it failed repeatedly because of the change left in my clothing, which got trapped in the coin trap--which is extremely easy to access in most models, but not in this one. $200 repair.

I spent over $1000, easily, in repairs during the few years I owned it. I became good friends with my repairman Carlos, and that's never a good sign. Here's what Carlos said: These Frigidaires are putting my kids through college.

I adore Carlos, and I want his kids to get through college, but you paying for Frigidaire repairs is a bad way.

And the matching dryer kept shorting out, too, and had lots of repairs. Nothing but problems with Frigidaire. I'd go with Whirlpool, which is American made and works great. In the four years I've had the Whirlpool (I'm a landlord and own lots of models in my tenants' units) I have not had a single repair.

product_title: Energy Star Affinity 3.26 cu. ft. Front Load Washer in White
review_title: If you love tearing your washer apart yearly then this is the washer for you!
review_text:
Do you enjoy taking things apart for repairs annually? Do you find entertainment value in appliances that need constant maintenance? Do you find clamping/unclamping drain hoses relaxing? Do you have a strange fetish with cleaning filters out? If you answered 'Yes' to these questions, then this is the washer for you!
I found some amazing things in my washer's pump trap, such as children's socks, hair, rings, dollar bills and coins... even 2 quarters! I would like to know how all of that stuff even made it through in the first place (magic?!). But at least now I know that the washer really is responsible for those missing socks...
I love getting to spend 3 hours tearing my washer apart once a year when it stops draining, just to see the amazing treasures waiting for me inside. If you also love drain trap treasure hunting, then do not hesitate and buy now!

UPDATE: December 2014- My washer stopped draining again and I had to tear it apart and clear the pump intake. This time I found 2 of my teenagers short socks, A gold dollar, 2 quarters, a penny and an ALL color catcher sheet that I rarely use. This is the 4th time in about 6 years I have had to do this, this time I made it 15 months. I have 3 kids who are all at least 5 foot tall, so no baby socks and they usually check their pockets before doing their laundry.

I did update the star rating from a 1 to a 3 because while this is a pain in the ass, the pump, surprisingly has not burned out! I have actually not had any other issues with this, but the matching dryer destroys anything with a strap.. there is a snag point on the lint catcher.

product_title: Energy Star Affinity 3.26 cu. ft. Front Load Washer in White
review_text: The first thing I noticed was that my clothes on the cold cycle come out warm. This thing uses so little water that it barely clears out the pipes, much less get to cold water. Then the Normal cycle stopped working. Then the Bulk cycle stopped working, both seemed to start fine, but no water was ever added. Then, I put in a twin sized comforter, and it barely even gets it wet, much less clean. I hate this machine and regret buying it.

product_title: Energy Star Affinity 3.26 cu. ft. Front Load Washer in White
review_text: This is a mold breeder.  I use washing machine cleaner once a week with hot water.  Clean out the gasket with Clorox wipes every other time I use it and have started keeping the door open when not in use.  (NOT A GOOD IDEA IF YOU HAVE CHILDREN)  Nothing works.  I am so sorry I bought this machine.

product_title: Energy Star Affinity 3.26 cu. ft. Front Load Washer in White
review_text: You'd assume it would last a few years. we have electrical problems after just a little over one.  In our case, We lost normal cycle, and the dial doesn't work properly. Review would have been fine if i would have got 4-5 years out of it, but one isn't acceptable to me hence the low review.

product_title: Energy Star Affinity 3.26 cu. ft. Front Load Washer in White
review_title: One of the worst purchases I made for my new home
review_text:
This washer does clean clothes pretty well. When it works, which is about 10% of the time, it really works well.

Like everyone said, after 4 years completely breaks down. All I want for Christmas is a new washer.

Simply put, the washer does not advance to the next cycle. 90% of the wash loads I start do not progress. I have to manually set 'spin'. Just recently it just says 'paused' and will not progress.

DO NOT BUY THIS WASHER.

product_title: Energy Star Affinity 3.26 cu. ft. Front Load Washer in White
review_text: This machine hasn't lasted a year.  6 (SIX!) trips by the repairman to try and get it working (stops spinning because of a communication error). The warranty is about to run out and it still does not work correctly. This has been the most frustrating purchase (and caused more lost work days) than any other purchase I have ever made.

product_title: Energy Star Affinity 3.26 cu. ft. Front Load Washer in White
review_text: I rarely write a one-star review for any product, but the Frigidaire Affinity really is in a class of its own in terms of poor quality. We purchased ours (new) from a local appliance store about a year and a half ago and it's truly an awful product. Previous reviews have summed it up: the machine's gasket grows mold even if you leave the door open when the machine is not in use; the detergent compartment fills with water and does not drain; the door leaks out the bottom even if you close it carefully. And worst of all, the machine periodically shreds articles of clothing that become trapped between the gasket and the spinning drum. I really can't think of any positives about this machine, and we are planning to get rid of ours as soon as we pick out a different washer.

product_title: Energy Star Affinity 3.26 cu. ft. Front Load Washer in White
review_text: Worst purchase ever. We spent more on parts and trying to fix it in the past five years, that it's not even worth fixing anymore. product_title: Energy Star Affinity 3.26 cu. ft. Front Load Washer in White

product_title: Energy Star Affinity 3.26 cu. ft. Front Load Washer in White

product_title: Energy Star Affinity 3.26 cu. ft. Front Load Washer in White

product_title: Energy Star Affinity 3.26 cu. ft. Front Load Washer in White

product_title: Whirlpool WDT910SAYH Gold 24" White Fully Integrated Dishwasher - Energy Star
review_title: A bad machine from the start.  Avoid.
review_text:
I'm writing as I'm about to junk this thing after two years. As far as washing goes, it is a poor performer. Any dish that egg has touched must be washed by hand. We have tried many detergents, using pot scrubber mode, pre soaking, pre washing, you name it. Nothing works. Same goes for starchy foods, especially potatoes and rice. If you cook either of these things and then put the dish in the dishwasher, the entire load will be covered in a white film. Pot scrubber mode does not scrub the pots well enough to avoid hand washing afterwards, so there is no point in using it. Dishes always come out wet even when using jet dry. Every 6 months or so it breaks a glass.
The racks themselves are not strong enough to hold up to normal use. The first year was okay, but since then every 3 months somethin has broken-- we have gone through 3 tine clips and a wheel. And these flimsy plastic parts are not cheap to replace. Apparently this is an issue across many whirlpool products, so please do your research before buying a Whirlpool or KitchenAid dishwasher.
After 2 years the machine has started leaking water when filling the tub. Considering how much the repair will cost, the constantly breaking dish racks and the poor washing performance it's just not worth fixing.

review_text: I love that I can choose the 1 hr. wash cycle.  It has been just as efficient as the longer one if I use heat to dry. This dishwasher also holds more than my Kitchenaid did. The only complaint I would have is that I can't see where I am in the cycle.

product_title: Whirlpool WDT910SAYE Gold 24" Black Fully Integrated Dishwasher - Energy Star
review_text: Very nice looking and seems to work well so far.  I pre-rinse my dishes and use the Normal, then Pre-scour, then heated dry and dishes have come out clean with no spots.  Use Rinse Aid also.

product_title: Whirlpool WDT910SAYE Gold 24" Black Fully Integrated Dishwasher - Energy Star
review_text: We purchased the W10331043A in 2012 and we are very disappointed with it. It leaves residue on bowls and if we don't unload the clean dishes right away they spoil and smell terrible. We have had to re-wash loads because they smell so bad by the time we get to them (within 24 hrs.) It takes forever to run a cycle and "dry", but the dishes are never completely dry after the heated drying cycle. Additionally, crud accumulates all over the bottom of the dishwasher and behind the silverware caddy and smells. Dishwashing powder residue is always present and the door to that compartment has never shut well. I don't notice a difference in cleanliness of dishes when I use the "power scour" feature. Skillets always have a residue after they've been washed. My grandmother has a less expensive version of this dishwasher and she does not have these problems with hers. Clean dishes can be left for a couple of days without the dishwasher developing a spoiled odor. I wish I had saved the extra money and gotten her version; or better yet, gone with another brand. We did our homework on Consumer Reports, customer reviews, etc so go figure. This is my last Whirlpool purchase.

product_title: Whirlpool WDT790SAYW Gold 24" White Fully Integrated Dishwasher - Energy Star

product_title: Whirlpool WDT710PAYM Gold 24" Stainless Steel Fully Integrated Dishwasher - Energy Star
review_text:
After attempting to research dishwashers to replace our broken one - I was more confused than ever, if that is even possible! Each web site contradicted the previous one. I realized that most happy people do not bother to write reviews, so thought I would write to share our happy review of this one.

I would describe our decision process as a crap shoot. We did not want to spend $900 on a dishwasher, but did not want a piece of junk either. Don't get me wrong, I would love to have one of those elegant designer dishwashers, but not at the cost of my first born. (maybe I should reconsider that - ha ha). Anyway, based on a Consumer Reports rating, we were looking at a few dishwashers, Whirlpool Gold being one of them. This is not the exact model they were rating (not avail at our location), but close enough for us. Over all, we felt this was a safe bet because our last dishwasher was a Whirlpool and it lasted 17 years before it finally bit it and went to dishwasher heaven. This one was in stock at our local home store and we could install right away. Others we would have to order and wait 7-28 days depending on machine.

One of our requirements was that the machine was quiet. This one is advertised at 55 db. I can safely tell you, as I sit 5 feet from the running machine, that it is pretty quiet! I can hear it but it is a low hum. Not completely silent, but very quiet. Absolutely acceptable in our open living area.

It seems to clean very very well. It was 4 days between the old one breaking and the new installation and those dishes were ick. Dried on egg, cheese, and cake mix among other things. They came out beautifully. I could not ask for better in the cleaning department. I do not rinse the dishes before they get washed, just scrape off the scraps and throw them in, they were pretty dirty.

Installation went pretty well, took a couple of hours to get out the old and have the new completely hooked up.

Overall, we are happy with this machine so far. Clean dishes and pretty quiet, our 2 big requirements.If anything pops up, I will update.

product_title: Whirlpool WDT710PAYM Gold 24" Stainless Steel Fully Integrated Dishwasher - Energy Star
review_text:
I purchased this dishwasher from the local home improvement store, and I couldn't be happier with it so far. I was initially looking at the [[ASIN:B005BHSW3Y Whirlpool WDT910SAYM]], but the only meaningful difference I could see was that model had a stainless steel interior for an extra $200. Maybe it's worth it, but I don't know. Clean dishes are clean dishes, in my mind.

Installation of this dishwasher is also pretty easy. You have to buy the inflow hoses and connectors, but the home improvement store knows this and they have a kit already prepared with every connector you'd ever need. The Whirlpool dishwashers require a larger brass connector than other brands, but it's in the kit and very easy to hook up. Also, there are several good videos on youtube showing how to install this very model. It took me a couple of hours to take out the old unit and install this one, but I was washing dishes much more quickly than I had anticipated.

My only concern about this dishwasher is the latch. It works fine (for now), but it's a plastic latch. It's actually in place out-of-the-box, but I thought it was a temporary shipping latch. I even went back to the store to look at the latch on the floor model to make sure I wasn't missing something. It's there already. All you do is pull. I thought it should have some sort of "lock" on it, but it doesn't. Just push shut and pull open (the first couple of pulls are a little stiff). Because it's plastic and easily removable, I'm tempted to order a replacement part right now while I'm thinking about it. Who knows? The latch will probably work fine for 20 years?

As far as noise is concerned, this unit is MUCH quieter than the freight train that was my old model. Simple conversation or watching TV in the same room while the dishwasher is running isn't a problem. You can hear it, but it isn't overly intrusive. As far as cleaning is concerned, like the other reviewer I don't "wash" the dishes before putting them in the dishwasher. So far, everything has come out spotless. There is also much more room in this thing than I had in my mid 90's model Kennmore. I don't pay much attention to changes in dishwasher technology over time, but all this additional room has been a welcome surprise.

Obviously, I won't be completely sure of the durability of this unit for many more years. However, I am very pleased with this unit so far.

review_text:

product_title: Whirlpool WDT710PAYM Gold 24" Stainless Steel Fully Integrated Dishwasher - Energy Star
review_title: Cleans great and holds lots of dishes.
review_text:
This dishwasher is great. It easily holds 2 days of dishes for a family of five. Everything comes out super clean, except the silverware. By having the silverware container on the door it saves lots of space for other items on the bottom rack and I love that. But the silverware often come out dirty. I'm sure this could be remedied by using a basket on the lower rack, but I haven't had the dishwasher long enough to play with other ideas.
The buttons and lights are all on the TOP of the door. I like this because I don't bump them by mistake, but depending on how your counter is built, you may not have enough room to view these once the door is shut. It does take a few extra seconds of my time to crouch down and peer between the granite and top of dishwasher when I am selecting the wash. My spouse really hates this feature.
The only other concern is that it requires a $4 part to install that is NOT included. It took 7 Home Depot employees to find this part while I was in the middle of installing the dishwasher. Be prepared, go buy this before you begin install. But really, Whirlpool should just include it.
It runs smoothly and quietly, and for the price, I would buy it again.

review_title: As far as the bad reviews I have read on this Dishwasher

product_title: Whirlpool WDT710PAYM Gold 24" Stainless Steel Fully Integrated Dishwasher - Energy Star
review_text: If performance is what you want, look elsewhere than this dishwasher. With today's energy efficient appliances everything is less - which is NOT more. product_title: Whirlpool WDT710PAYM Gold 24" Stainless Steel Fully Integrated Dishwasher - Energy Star

product_title: Whirlpool WDT710PAYM Gold 24" Stainless Steel Fully Integrated Dishwasher - Energy Star
review_title: Horrible product; will avoid Whirlpool and there "gold series" from now on.
review_text:
Have had the dishwasher for about 1 year now; whirlpool obviously made this model to make large profit margin and fail after about 1-2 years of use. 100% in-excusable that a dishwasher in this price range would have this low of a mtbf.

Make no mistake; company as large as whirlpool knows exactly the MTBF (mean time between failures) and use the KPI vs cost before releasing the product.

1. All the plastic has turned brittle; replacing top shelf tabs and wheels is normal occurrence; about 6 months life span before you have issues.
2. Dishes come out dirty; constantly re-washing. Silverware is the worst typically.

Bottom line; spend the extra 200 and get a bosch; life will be good for about 5 years instead of 6 months.

Apparent that whirlpool does not care about keeping customers and is applying "lean/lean" concepts to increase stockholders earnings at the price of customers.

Update; 2 years now; have spent over 500 dollars keeping the machine going. Have now replaced the top rack twice and the bottom rack wheels 3 times. Worse product I have ever purchased... Unbelievably disappointed with whirlpool.

Sent whirlpool a letter with rcpts from the first 2 years of use on keeping this pile of junk running; they basically said "we dont care" in a very nice way.

Upgrading to a Bosch this week; will have a whirlpool free house going forward.

product_title: Whirlpool WDT710PAYM Gold 24" Stainless Steel Fully Integrated Dishwasher - Energy Star
review_title: I've had nothing but problems with this dishwasher. I ...
review_text:
I've had nothing but problems with this dishwasher.

I bought the dishwasher about a year ago and I'm on my fourth repair. product_title: Whirlpool WDT710PAYM Gold 24" Stainless Steel Fully Integrated Dishwasher - Energy Star
review_title: THE WORST Utensil Basket in the History of  Dishwashers
review_text:
The dishwasher itself works OK, nothing special, good or bad.

Now to the real problem with this model (apparently discontinued). The utensil (knives, forks, spoons, etc.) basket.

I have used probably 10-12 different dishwasher utensil baskets in my life, while living in different apartments, homes. I don't remember any of them. I will never forget this one.

The one that comes with this Whirlpool model (and maybe with other models) is in a class by itself; a BAD class.

It is hands down the worst utensil basket ever made in the history of dishwashers.

How much do I hate it? Let me count the ways (apologies to Elizabeth Barrett Browning) :

--If you put it in the door mounted position there are many problems:
.....It is basically impossible to load the utensils in this position, to try, you have to contort your wrist into non-human positions
.....If you do manage to load it on the counter, and then mount it on the door, the weight will slam the door down barking your shins until you know better
...........To anticipate the person who says, 'well just adjust the door spring to compensate.' If you do that, then to bottom rack won't stay
down when you try to load it, the door spring is too strong and lifts the empty rack up.
.....It is also very difficult to unload from the door mounted position
.....Finally, the basket handle is bent to make it easier to place into the door, however the handle blocks the two of the slots make the loading process (already very difficult) even more difficult to accomplish for those slots.

Another MAJOR problem is that teaspoons, salad forks, and occasionally a table spoon will fall down crossways and get hung somehow between the 'slots' . I have a teaspoon and a fork which, so far as I can see, would require power tools to get out. They are permanently hung in the basket. No amount of shaking or jostling will remove them.

Now the weirdest problem of all. Uneven cleaning. One utensil will be shiny and sparkling, while another, right beside it (but not nested) will look as if it had never been washed. And I'm not talking about baked-on crud, rather, rice, peanut butter, mashed potatoes, etc. I don't even know how it's possible for it to do that!

If you are thinking about buying a Whirlpool, look very closely at the utensil rack before you do. I certainly wish I had.

review_title: A pretty decent contender in the stainless tub dishwasher game!
review_text:
I bought this dishwasher at ABC Warehouse, last month. It was on sale for $404.10.

Pros: SUPER quiet, solidly built, "anywhere" silverware basket (I keep ours on the lower rack, NOT the door), indicator to see the rinse aid level, indicator lights indicating what part of the wash cycle the dishwasher is in.

Cons: "Anywhere" silverware basket, rack tines arent meant to be adjusted, no just rinse option (That I have yet discovered).

Ok so the first thing I would like to emphasize in my review is how unbelievably quiet this dishwasher is; so quiet, in fact, that after we installed it, we kept going up to it and trying to "hear" if it was running or not! The only true way you can hear it work is when it drains the water. And the only noise you will hear is from your sink, NOT the dishwasher. So it gets A+ in the sound department. IMO, it is a strong competitor to Bosch and the other virtually silent high-end dishwashers.

So moving on, I should disclose Ive had the dishwasher a month. However, I am quite the dishwasher aficionado. Buying this appliance was a VERY involved process for me, in fact I believe the salesman at ABC Warehouse truly believed I was mentally ill, as I had to come and "look" at the dishwasher 3-4 different times before I actually committed buying it, lol.

With that being said I never thought I would dislike the "anywhere" silverware basket - but after using it once or twice, what a dumb thing. On the door, my silverware didnt seem to get the exposure to wash water and detergent like it does on the rack, so I removed it from the door and placed it on the lower rack. I notice my silverware doesnt have that weird smell now, like they did on the door. I recommend moving the basket. The silverware basket holes for the silver ware are also an afterthought - if you have thick handled silverware, you are going to have to flip the top of the basket and place the silverware in directly.
The racks are very well build and do not feel cheap. The tines arent meant to be bent, but I was able to easily move one. The controls on the front are easy to use, and the indicator light will let you know what stage the dishwasher is in. There isnt a rinse only option, that I have read about or discovered yet, bummer. I really liked that feature in my last dishwasher. Guess I missed that in my research!

Whirlpool recommends Cascade Platinum tabs, they even give you two of them as a promotion with the machine and I did go out and buy some, however I find that Cascade liquid works just as well if not better. Downside- the liquid leaves stains that look like hardwater stains. Vinegar takes it right off.

When Whirlpool promises you can fit 15 place settings into the machine, or whatever their wild promise is, they arent making things up. The lower rack is HUGE and will seriously fit 15 plates easily. The upper rack fits most cups nicely.

Last but not least, the stainless tub seemed thinner than my last Kitchenaid. Either way, dishes ALWAYS come out dry (I use the non-eco heat dry option & sani-rinse) and the plates and glasses are piping hot at the end of the wash.

All-in-all, I strongly recommend the Whirlpool WDF750SAYB. For the price, you arent going to find a machine as quiet and flexible.

review_text:
I bought this gas stove less than 5 mo. ago and have run into a very serious design flaw. And thought I have to tell folks about this.

You know how you have to push the knobs in & turn to ignite gas burners- well these knobs need VERY, very little depressing, and they turn very easily too, and a slight turn or bump releases gas without causing the auto ignitor to go on, plus they are high output burners- the combination makes for a GAS LEAK.
It has happened several times to both my partner & myself without noticing until we smell gas. Happens when we're cooking, sometimes happens we reach up to use the microwave above the stove, happened when our dog tried to stove surf-which really freaked us out.
Just yesterday a friend was over and began fixing a cup of coffee on the counter, next to the stove. I guess she may have grazed it with her body as she moved, within a few minutes we all began to smell gas, and we knew just where to check. Sure enough, the damn knob(s).
Some of the knobs seem to protrude out slightly further than the bar/oven handle-so the handle offers no protection of the knobs getting bumped.
Not sure if this problem is limited to our stove, but I would seriously check this stove out in person at a store first before purchasing.

I am not sure where/who to report this potentially deadly problem to, but thought I mention it here first where there is a significant amt of traffic.

review_text: DO NOT SPILL ANY AMOUNT OF LIQUID ON THE STOVE TOP. You will ruin the entire range!!!! After a couple minutes we started using paper towel to absorb the hot grease. It took less than 10 minutes and all seemed well. We used the burners after cleaning up and even turned the oven back on. We used the oven for 2-3 weeks and then last night while cooking a lasagna for over an hour at 350 we started smelling a really weird "plastic" smell. Then smoke started comming from under the stove top and was burning our eyes and throat. We turned off the oven and left the door open. The smoke continued for over an hour even though you could touch the inside of the oven with your bare hand and it wasn't hot. After it cooled we took off the cook top and saw a cantalope sized black charred insulation under the back left burner. No other burners showed any sign of oil. Oil had apparently seeped under the burner when it spilled and soaked the insulation. When the oil spilled it barely made it up to the base of the aluminum burner where it meets the cooktop. The oil was spread evenly across the cook top below the grates yet only one burner leaked the oil. It is obvious they didn't tighten the burner when they assembled the top. If they had then none of the oil would of leaked. We have talked to Frigidaire three times now and they sent out a tech to look at it. The guy said that Frigidaire never covers any oil spill damage. I asked, even if it is because they didn't bother tightening the burners down at the factory, basically he said yup! So we called frigidaire back and they said call another tech in if we didn't think the first one did a fair job. We called two more techs and they both said the same thing, if it has anything to do with oil spilling, they will not cover it. Even though we keep calling frigidaire, they obviously would rather have their factory authorized techs waste their time rather than just saying what the techs keep saying. We don't care if we messed up, we will not take responsibility for a design that destroys the range if you spill a little oil!! The repair will bee $450- $525 to just cut out the charred insulation and replace with a piece. Frigidaire sold a range that wasn't put together properly, they couldn't care less and every one of the repairman said STAY AWAY FROM FRIGIDAIRE or any of the Electrolux brands as they have horrible warranty policies and Frigidaire sees alot of problems throughout their gallery line especially! I made the mistake of buying a Frigidaire Gallery refrigerator, range, microwave for our kitchen remodel. I WILL NEVER DO THAT AGAIN!!! NEVER!!!!!!!!!! Thank God I bought a Whirlpool diswasher after we returned the Gallery before we installed it. One and two star ratings for the dishwasher was to big of a risk! I will Electrolux will NEVER pawn their crap off on me again. I remodel kitchens and bathrooms for a living and I will ALWAYS warn against using such junky appliance made by such a pathetic company!!!!!

review_text: Everything was working fine on this stove when it was new about 4 years ago but slowly over time I had to push harder and harder on the push button display for it to work.  After a year I was pushing the commonly used buttons several times just to get the thing to work.  After a about 2 years it became nearly impossible to use because even when I'd manage to get the bake button to activate, after punching in the baking temperature I was not able to get the start button to actually turn on the stove.  Some of the numbers would fail to work also at times so I was not able to bake at desired temperatures and had to use the next closest temperature I could get the buttons to work for.  At first I thought the contacts were worn out and thought I'd have to replace the digital display push button panel but after removing the ribbon cables from the circuit board to the digital control panel and re-connecting them again the control panel miraculously worked again.  I've now had to do this a second time.  It seems like this problem is progressive and worsens to the point of having an inoperable stove every couple of years.  I was originally going to give this stove 1 star for this reason but since the work-around only has to be done every year or two and is relatively easy I've decided to give this stove 3 stars instead.  I should not have to troubleshoot and fix my stove within two years of buying it and have to repeat this ever year or so.  The other problem is the heat from the burners is enough to slow warp the face of the plastic control panel over time.  Mine now has noticeable ripples. The plastic is permanently deformed due to heat.  The best thing about this stove is the center griddle.  It lets you cook two pancakes at a time and you can keep stuff warm on the edges.  It cleans up easily.  The oven bakes evenly - no complaints there other than it seems to cook at a bit lower temperature than what you think you are at.  I find I have to go 25 degrees higher than a recipe says or increase the bake time by about 25%.

product_title: 30 in. Gallery Series Freestanding Gas Range with 5.0 Cu. Ft. Self Clean Oven - Stainless Steel
review_title: Great value in a range-wonderful cooktop power and even baking in the convection oven
review_text:
I had this range installed about 6 months ago. It replaced a nine year old Frigidaire gas range which was generally satisfactory but I was always frustrated with the lack of speed of the burners, despite the fact that it had what was, at that time, about the highest BTU burners available on a regular gas range. Water took ages to boil, and with pasta, it almost never came back up to a real boil before the pasta got soft and stuck together without the benefit of a proper boil.

This new one has a more "pro-style" appearance, much sturdier iron grates, and wow, the burners! The 11,000 BTU burner in the old one has morphed into a 17,000 BTU in the right front, and the next more powerful one is 15,000 BTU in the left rear. That means the fastest burner is nearly 50% more powerful than the old one, and boy, does it show! Water boils so quickly I can scarcely believe it. I can stir fry in a wok! There is a long oval center burner that I've not had occasion to use. The grate for it can be replaced with an included griddle, for pancakes, eggs and bacon, and more. I expect it will be very useful for making my Thanksgiving turkey gravy. The roasting pan will fit very nicely on it.

The convection oven is terrific, but I have found it takes longer to preheat than the beep would indicate. I've no idea why I would want a "pizza" setting, however. I've not tried the broiler as I use an outdoor grill, but I expect it would work as well as any gas broiler, moderately well. I've also not yet the need to use the self cleaning cycle but as it worked very well in the old range I expect it will do so with this one. I love to bake and have found the convection oven allows me to actually bake three pans of cookies at a time very evenly. I expect to put the flexible half shelf to use this Thanksgiving, stacking the stuffing and vegetable casserole to the side of the turkey, and that will give me a chance to try out the temperature probe (and undoubtedly the self cleaning feature!).

My only caveat about the rack that pulls out when the oven is opened is to be careful of it. It must be the lower rack, and it will make it easier to burn your hands as it is raised up higher than the oven door when the door is open. Just be aware of it, and know that you can disable this feature if you choose to.

I feel that there is excellent value in this gas range, and as an avid and skilled cook and baker, I'm enjoying it to the max. I paid about $900 for it. A great price for an excellent range. I cannot imagine how a range costing twice as much could improve my cooking. I couldn't be happier!

product_title: LG WM3550HWCA
review_text:
Pros:
--As of Feb 2012, this is the most efficient large capacity consumer washing machine according to the EPA. Google 'EPA washing machine' to see their website.
--This unit costs $10 a year to operate!!!
--Gets clothes really clean. I use the ultra efficient 'tap cold' setting every time and I haven't had a problem yet getting out tough stains (like blood)
--The steam mode is a nice bonus feature I think, but I don't really use it very often. But when i do, it's on a blanket on a cold day, and it's refreshing.
--The aller-genie mode (get it? as in allergy-fighting mode) does sheets very nicely, and I notice a real difference from my old washer
--Each load takes 1/2 the detergent I would normally use with my old top-loader.
--According to Consumer Reports, LG is the most reliable washing machine brand, and we haven't had any problems yet in last couple of months we've owned this machine.
--Easy install, setup, and operation. I'm not good with electronics, but it's easy even for me.
--Auto balance will determine the size of the load so you don't have to. It weighs it, which is interesting to watch!

Cons:
--Expensive.
--This is my first-front loader, and I hate that I must wipe the front rubber seal after each use. I have tenants who live in my house, so I worry that they'll forget to follow instructions and I'll have mold some day.
--Some wash modes take a long time! A full 'heavy' soiled load takes about 1.5 hrs.
--There is such a thing as too many options; there are 10 different wash modes! It can get a little overwhelming, but luckily 'normal/cotton' seems to work for just about everything
--As with all high efficiency washers, it's recommended that you use the special HE washing detergent, but I refuse to pay extra for my washing solution. Just use less of the normal detergent (so this is actually a positive if you ignore the advice).

I was hesitant to buy this washer as it's not very common and I could only find one review online. The more expensive LG 3875 seems to be far more common here in the USA, but there are 2 reasons why this model is better:

(1) Cheaper and
(2) More efficient

I was not disappointed. It has not leaked or otherwise malfunctioned. I love this machine, it makes washing fun, and I high recommend it!

review_title: Don't waste your money on LG washers
review_text:
Don't buy LG.
We bought the top of the line LG front load washer a few years ago. It was great for a year, and then the problems started. We've had repair people in several times and repairs are always a hassle because all LG parts must be ordered from CA.
The smell started the second year, and it has been a continual problem. You may hear about wiping the door seal, using different detergent, and other solutions, but we've tried them all, as well as products to eliminate the smell. The only reliable solution is to use the bottom drain line located inside a small compartment on the front of the washer after every load. Yes, the small door that is not mentioned in the manual contains a drain line, and we drain the left over water into a small bucket after each wash.
Our clothes don't smell, but this process is absurd. We've contacted LG, but it's a waste of time. The only thing they haven't told me yet is their washer is better than washing clothes on a rock near a river.
Our washer is now 5 years old, and the bearings are bad. My wife called the repairman and the estimate is over $500. I am thrilled, I can now throw out this piece of junk and buy something that works. I struggled to throw out a $1500 washer that worked, but it's an easy decision to toss it now. Good bye LG.
Once again, don't buy LG products until they learn how to build reliable products and develop some customer service.

product_title: LG LFX25974SB 24.7 Cu. Ft. Smooth Black French Door Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_text:
We bought this refrigerator in Nov. of 2011. We were initially very pleased with it, and it looked lovely in our kitchen. Once summer came we quickly found out how poor at producing ice the icemaker is and does not keep up with the demands of a family of 6. We bought this large refrigerator because we are a big family never questioning that ice production would be an issue. It seems in hot humid weather the production slows down and ice buildup appears along the inside gasket. It leaks water from the door into the refrigerator. We did call LG and they sent a serviceman out who did nothing but change the settings on the panel. The problem was not rectified and here we are a year later in the hot summer with the same problem. I will now have to pay a repairman to come out and examine the problem.

We have developed another problem on the refrigerator this summer and that is rust. The ice/water dispenser leak water and it seeps along the lower edge causing rust to form. The paint is bubbled and looks awful for a refrigerator that is not even 2 years old. I called LG about this problem and they have informed me that it is a cosmetic issue and even if we had purchased the extended warranty it would not be covered. I explained that it really is a functional issue which has become cosmetic due to the leakage. They would not hear of it.

I think is is disgraceful when you spend over $2000 for a refrigerator and it looks awful after 18 months and the manufacturer does not stand behind their product in the least.

Also note that with 4 children in the home our refrigerator gets a lot of use. I am a fanatic about keeping things clean and find that the smooth surface of the refrigerator doors are not kid friendly. They show any scratch and finger prints. You are better off to stick with the textured doors if you have children!

I think maybe both doors need to be left open for the alert to sound.  The icemaker does not work 80% of the time.  Either it's simply not producing ice or the ice is stuck and will not come out, in either case it is extremely frustrating.  Also, the drawer in the freezer comes off the tracks often.  Sometimes it only slightly comes off causing us to not realize that the freezer is not 100% closed and then our food starts to defrost. After owning the refrigerator, I can say with 100% certainty that I would never buy another LG refrigerator again.  Please learn from our mistake.

review_title: No replacement mullion spring available for this model so cannot recommend.
review_text: VERY frustrated because the mullion spring broke on this fridge and while you can replace that same part on other similar LG models, they do not sell the mullion spring for this particular model.  The ones for the other ones (MHY62044103 and 106) do not work. I am not even sure that buying the entire mullion (for $80!) will ensure I get a spring, it isn't visible in the parts diagram for Sears parts or anywhere else I looked; nor is there a PN in the parts diagram for the spring for this refrigerator.  Have spent hours on this issue, including buying and trying to install the other two springs, did not work. This was confirmed by a half-hour chat with Sears parts; they were also baffled, but no help.  This alone is a good reason not to buy this, in my opinion, otherwise it's a perfectly ok refrigerator, but mullion springs do break and what the heck to do?

review_text: we got a great deal through best buy. we paid around $600 and got a 4yr service aggrement through them. We got this washer around Christmas with free shipping. My wife uses it everyday with 8 kids in the house.Its been 9 months and we have not had any problems.I am glad I went through Best Buy.They messed up our shipping date so they kept us quiet with a $100 gift card.

product_title: Whirlpool WFW9151YW
review_title: Bad machine, but at least you'll replace it quickly.
review_text:
I've had this machine about nine months. It replaced an old Frigidaire front-loader that worked fine, but was 10 years old and starting to leak from the tub.

The washer has extremely long cycle times. It takes about 90 minutes to do a load of whites and 72 minutes for a regular load. If I had known, I'd not have bought the machine.

Also, it has frustratingly poor rinse performance. The machine is so stingy with water that I often have to do each load twice: once to wash the clothes (with extra rinse turned on), and once again (the full wash cycle with extra rinse) without detergent to get the suds out. Yes, I use HE detergent; yes, I keep the tub clean of residue; and no, I never use more detergent than the amount for one load (usually less). It is just that the machine doesn't so much rinse the clothes as dampen them.

Look elsewhere. I don't care how much you save; if you do more than one load of laundry in a day, the savings won't be worth it.

Update: I've finally had enough. As of August 2014, the machine just leaks too much and requires too many extra rinse cycles. There is NO water savings. This thing is impossible. Off to the junkyard after about 2 1/2 years. The Whirlpool WFW9151 is a total failure of a machine. No more Whirlpool for me. Ever.

product_title: Whirlpool WFW9151YW
review_title: Quiet, water efficient, but damages clothing
review_text: This washer is reasonably quiet.  It is just off my bedroom and does not bother me to run it while I sleep.  The clothing comes out very clean, but I do have to use the extra rinse cycle to properly rinse the clothing.  My biggest frustration is that it makes pulls in the fabric of clothing.  One table cloth was completely ruined by large thread pulls.  We cannot determine where the fabric is catching in the tub.  We do not feel any sharp edges, but it continues to happen.  I am very careful that nothing is caught in the door when I close it.  As others have said, the front gasket grabs small items (like children's socks).  It also retains a lot of water, so you need to dry the gasket with a paper towel when you are done with a day's laundry to prevent mold building up inside the gasket.

product_title: Whirlpool WFW9151YW
review_text:
Had this washer replaced 2 times and the inner rubber keeps breaking off and it leaks all over the floor.
Called Whirlpool.... not much help there either. I spent over $800.00 for a product that broke within 30 days of use.
too bad I thought this was a good buy ....

product_title: Whirlpool WFW9151YW
review_text:
Purchased this machine as it was the only washer that would fit into the laundry room built in cabinetry. 2 weeks later I am putting this on Craigslist since I am unable to return ("it is operating as designed"). Small items get stuck in the front door and cannot be fixed until the cycle is over - then you have 2 dripping wet socks to deal with.

Delivery guy told me to leave the door open after using to "avoid the mold problem". THE MOLD PROBLEM? Seems that the poor design also leave substantial water in the front gasket of the washer and forms MOLD.

Seriously, give this machine a pass - even if you have to spend $500 rebuilding the cabinetry in your laundry room.

product_title: Whirlpool WFW9151YW
review_text: Whirlpool is not the same company it was a few years ago.  We bought a Duet washer and dryer to replace our 20 year old Whirlpools (which still worked perfectly).  I fully expected to get 20 years out of these given Whirlpool's reputation and the cost, but no such luck.  The tub bearings and basket shaft went bad in the washer after just 5 years, and the replacement parts alone (no labor) are nearly as much as a new washer.  After doing some research, I discovered that this is a very common complaint.  Needless to say, I will never buy another Whirlpool appliance.  There are much better choices out there now (i.e. LG) from companies that are interested in building brand loyalty by standing by there products.

product_title: Whirlpool WFW9151YW
review_text: We bought this machine about a year ago. Doesn't rinse clothes. Constantly throws error codes. We bought it to replace the cheapo Goldstar top loader we had before. That thing was ten times the machine this one is at 1/3 the cost. Now its back to the 60 year old wringer washer we use every time another new washer craps out. Thanks for the lesson in caveat emptor whirlpool.

product_title: Whirlpool WFW9151YW
review_text: This washer managed to make just past the one year warranty, then the pump broke.  $200 repair bill later, It began having all kinds of errors, usually E2 F7, then stopped.  Then the pump broke again, and it began ruining clothes by leaving black dots on everything.  I replaced the pump again, then it started having an E1 F6 error instead.  I give up.  I've only had it a year and a half and I'm getting rid of it.

product_title: Whirlpool WFW9151YW
review_title: although some reviewers had even worse luck. Its other issues are common to front ...
review_text: It doesn't deserve one star.  We spent $971.+ on 7/11/2012, and replaced it on 11/11/2015 with a boot torn in 3 places, and in need of a new inner basket and outer tub with bearings.  Parts alone exceeded $600 without labor.  We are a senior couple with minimal to average laundry needs, we took care of the machine, and followed directions.  We did not have the extended warranty.  The performance was just fair, even when brand new.  It is unacceptable for such a machine to fail in just over three years, although some reviewers had even worse luck.  Its other issues are common to front loaders:  even with regular cleaning, as recommended in the manual, and leaving the washer door open when not in use, the odor and the build-up were disgusting, even with a water softener.  No matter how good a Black Friday deal, beware of this model, and be careful of Whirlpool.

review_title: worst appliance i have ever owned
review_text:
Within months of buying this fridge the plastic shelving and drawers started cracking and breaking. Fine while it was under warranty. Not so cool after that. I had a one year old fridge that looked about 20 yrs. old. Honestly, I have seen cheap kids toys made out of better plastic than this.

product_title: LG LFC25765ST24.9 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel French Door Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_text:

So my advice? Find another appliance company to buy from. One that will show good faith and responsibility when you actually need them.

product_title: GE Cafe CGP650SETSS 36" Built-in Gas Cooktop
review_text: When my wife wanted to change out our old cook top I of course completed research ad nauseum. We did not want to spend more than $1500.00. This bad boy is excellent.  The 20,000 BTU middle burner is awsome. I cooked a four gallon pot of Shrimp and okra (yeah we are cajuns)gumbo today and the middle burner made quick work of it.
