product_title: Frigidaire FGEF3055MF Gallery 30" Stainless Steel Electric Smoothtop Range - Convection
review_title: Excellent Quality At A Mid-Level Price
review_text:
The appearance of this range is very upscale. Not just "professional looking", but obviously built to higher standards than lower-end models. Looks fantastic in the kitchen. This is a mid-level range, with features placing it in the top of that category. We've been using it every day for 3 months now.

The oversized oven window was one of my must-have features. It's very nice, indeed - but the tinted glass and dim interior lighting hampers your visibility somewhat. Perhaps a brighter light bulb will help.

The 5-element cooktop is perfect for family use. Warming element works great, we use it often. Quick-boil feature definitely heats faster than the other burners, and works really well with small-to-medium size pans/pots. Large pots of boiling water still take awhile, but no worse than a coil-element burner. Elements heat fast, controls are precise. Those familiar with smoothtops will be right at home. Small scratches aren't noticable from a distance, and it usually takes no more than a few minutes for routine cleaning. We still prefer the old salt-and-pepper surface, but this black version cleans up just as easily. It's unforgiving with dust particles, but this doesn't affect cooking performance or require special cleaning.

The oven is fantastic. Control panel looks a bit daunting, but the basic controls are straightforward. We mastered the layout and display very quickly. The oven status graphic is very useful. Touch controls are smooth, alert beeps are effective without being annoying. Very well designed. The brushed stainless console is easy to clean, a spritz of Windex is all we need for most splatters. The cooktop knobs are very easy to clean, and won't discolor like plastic.

Baking and roasting times are noticably faster. Preheating is fairly quick, but doesn't seem any faster than our old gas oven. The fan is acceptably quiet - puts out a steady humming sound that's neither loud nor obnoxious. Browning ability (ie; a roast) is superb - nice bark on top with even browning - including the bottom. Several features are available for baking/roasting, all helping to insure good results. Everything we've turned out so far has been nearly perfect. Temperature probe and automatic keep-warm work as advertised, and are very useful for daily cooking.

We've had 3 self-cleaning ranges over the last 27 years, and this one beats 'em all. While experimenting with the broiler, I created a MAJOR greasy mess that covered the cavity and racks. By the time smoke began to pour out, the grease was hopelessly baked on. I did my best to clean up that mess, but it was a lost cause. Didn't expect much from self-clean, but 4 hours later I couldn't believe my eyes. It was sparkling! I did have to soak/scrub the racks, but the oven interior was like brand new. Very, very impressive.

We feel we got our money's worth. If it proves as durable as professional-grade, this is one sweet bargain.
UPDATE 7/19/17: After 2.5 years of constant use, still looks and cooks like new. Solid choice.

review_title: Please do not buy an Electrolux refrigerator.
review_text:
We came to own an Electrolux refrigerator (model EI23BC56IS8) that conveyed with our new home in March 2014. Per the sticker in the unit, it was manufactured in June 2011 (less than five years ago).

For the second time in two years, it stopped making ice. This time the technician slid the unit out to get access to the control board which revealed what you see in the attached picture. Yes, among the giant rust spot, is a chunk of ice. Doing a little research online, Electrolux refrigerators are subject to failures in the coolant line or insulation that can result in what we experienced - basically a hole. Since we came to own this fine piece of refrigeration through the purchase of our home (i.e., it was "transferred" to us), Electrolux is choosing not to stand behind its product to do anything about it. Notably they have never expressed any interest in determining how this happened in less than 5 years - they simply do not care.

There are so much better refrigerators out there, please do not buy an Electrolux.

product_title: Electrolux EI23BC30KSIQ-Touch 22.6 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel Counter Depth French Door Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_text:
I posted this review for our fridge, the model number of which is no longer on Amazon (EI23BC36...). This is a repost with update. Original review was October 2012.

My family recently did a complete kitchen gut renovation and although the contractor purchased all the appliances directly, not through Amazon, we want to share our thoughts now that we have lived with them for over 6 months. See our other reviews for the other products.

BACKGROUND
This is the final in our series of kitchen appliance reviews from the remodel. In some ways we spent more time looking at fridges than at anything else. Every fridge seems to offer just a slightly different set of features and it was difficult to judge in advance what set would make us happiest. In looking we found that fridges can fall into 4 categories:
- Really really expensive (eg Sub Zero and similar at above $5,000). We came to the opinion that you are paying for the brand and brand alone with these. They did not offer more or better features and our friends who have them do not give them exceptional reviews. I suppose if you plan on selling your home and need to say it has Sub Zero or Liebherr, then the value is worth the price. Otherwise it is not.
- Mid range ($2,000 to $4,000 approx). Most, not all but most, in this group seem to be the high end of the mass market brands and it was here that we found fridges that had the most thought put into design and functionality. We chose the Electrolux because the features and design worked for us but we suspect that if you end up with another one in this range that works for you in terms of looks and functionality that you will be equally impressed that the designers have put good thought into their designs.
- Low end, mass market (under $2,000). Here we found a lot of GE's and similar brands that probably have all the reliability you need but few features and just don't look as good.
- Eurotrash Pretenders (under $2,500). This is the category to be careful of. We almost fell into here based on finding fridges that looked great, seemed to have good feature sets but were flimsy and poorly made. I say "Euro" based on what they seemed to be designed to look like, but the worst offender seemed to be Fisher Paykel which I believe is a Kiwi brand. Be very very careful if you are buying something that seems too good to be true - a fridge is not where you want to find out that you've bought something that looks good but works poorly.

So we ended up in the "mid range" and are very happy. It worked out well for us. The details that we believe to be salient on this unit are:

THE GOOD
- Looks great. At counter depth and in stainless steel, plus the exterior design elements that are not overly "faux-commercial" all look great.
- Fit and finish are strong. The doors line up, open and close without hitch, etc. And this is not small thing. Take a look in the showrooms for all the french-door fridges where the two doors are not exactly at the same level. Every Samsung we saw in every showroom had misaligned doors.
- Easy to clean.
- Easy to customize shelf levels.
- It is so amazingly quiet. Sometimes we are not even certain it is on.
Note that we selected the version without the door dispensing ice and water. We did so based on looks alone as we wanted the cleaner lines of not having that functionality. But in doing so we also gained quite a bit of interior space.

THE BAD
- Easily smudges on the stainless steel front. They are easy to clean off but look unsightly until you clean them up.
- Ice can and does fall behind the freezer drawer causing the freezer door to fail to close, and if the ice is of just the right size the door will close enough that the alarm won't go off but not enough to keep the freezer frozen. It happened to us.
- The water and air filter replacements are expensive. If, like us, you use the water filter only for ice, the expense of replacing a filter at the recommended 6 months seems onerous.

SPECIAL NOTES
1. Don't let the ice bucket get over filled. Just turn on the lever to make ice when you are almost out and turn it off the next day. For us we turn it on about once a week and it works fine and we therefore do not have ice falling behind the drawer.
2. Don't overstuff the freezer, for the same reason of the door not closing fully.
3. We run both the fridge and freezer at 2 degrees above the recommended level mostly just to save a few cents on energy cost but we find that everything is a fine temperature.

COMMENTS TO OTHER REVIEWS
There seem to be several comments related to the ice maker and to noise. We have not experienced any noise at all other than the ice falling from the maker to the bucket.
We have also had nothing but good results with the chill drawer, though perhaps because we run the fridge 2 degrees warmer than recommended.

UPDATES JUNE 2013:
The fridge is working really well. Overall we are very pleased. We are especially pleased with how easy it is to clean and how durable it is. Our only quibbles are:
- The only area that is difficult to get to to clean is the back of the freezer section and things seem to collect back there.
- The plastic molding on the top of the freezer door is cracking. Not sure if we will replace it (the molding) or try to repair it. Not a huge deal but a bit of a pain.

The product failed from the front panel controls, both ice makers (top one would not shut off when the bucket was full continuously jamming the machine, the bottom ice maker (in the freezer section) fills half the large container and then dumps ice out of that container and down the back and ice would come sliding out from underneath the basket all over the floor when the drawer was open, a reoccurring loss of temperature control continued to increase until the freezer indicated 50 degrees F and we lost most of our frozen goods, shelf slides broke numerous times during normal use, etc. These are just a few of the failures we encountered with the machine, since the variety of failures extended from one side of the unit to the other and are too numerous to mention. review_title: Had To Replace Fridge Right After Warranty Expired
review_text: I bought this brand because it was rated the highest in reliability. But shortly after its extended warranty expired, it stopped cooling. We had to throw all our food out, a $300 waste. When the repair tech pulled it away from the wall he had me touch the back coils on the heat exchanger. They were cold. They should be warm. He then pointed to the 3 foot vertical rust and ice line on the back metal wall of the f.ridge. He said I have a coolant leak spraying the inside back wall. It stopped cooling because it ran out of coolant. Because it is an internal sealed system it was not repairable and we had to buy a new fridge. It irks me that friends with cheap fridges have lasted 20 years but this premium brand only a couple of years. If you buy this fridge, set an alarm on your smart phone for a month before your warranty expires and check the back for rust lines. Demand a replacement if you have them. Don't wind up like me.

review_text:
We needed an 18 inch dishwasher. We looked at the comparable 24 inch machine at Lowes. The reviews on Lowes and some other sites have this dishwasher rated very highly. We also looked at Amazon and considered buying it from here, but Sears at the time was offering 15 percent off the sales price so we bought this dishwasher from Sears for about $650 (excluding taxes).

For starters, it took 6 weeks to arrive, as it needed to be special ordered. That is fine as we knew about that going into the deal. Some stores, like Lowes had told us it would take about two weeks. When I asked the guy at Sears about that, he alleged store like Lowes got the dishwashers from the same place as Sears and they liked to give people a lower than probable estimate as to when the product will likely arrive and then adjust the estimate later whereas Sears tells you when the product would actually arrive. Based on past experiences with Lowes, and with what the Sears guy said, I suspect that this is probably true.

When the dishwasher arrived, it was light and compact enough to easily put in a small SUV (I didn't pay the $50 extra dollars at Sears to have it delivered). I lifted it myself into the back of a Subaru. The dishwasher is beautiful to look at and seems to be sturdy. It is stainless steel inside and out. However, it is not exactly the same as the 24 inch model (as some pictures on Electrolux suggest). For instance, it is missing handles on the inside trays. For me, that was not that big of a deal.

Second, installation was easy enough. However, unlike with the last dishwasher I bought from Fisher Paykel about two years ago for a different house, I had to purchase some hoses and an electrical cord. Apparently, you are supposed to use the hoses and electrical cord from the old dishwasher, but there was no dishwasher there before. Not that big of a deal, but still a pain. We ordered those things on Amazon for better quality parts at a lower price than the boxed stores by us.

After installation, the dishwasher worked great. I really loved this machine. For its size, it holds a lot of dishes, and does a real nice job cleaning them. In some ways I found I preferred this small dishwasher to the large ones. I found we were filling the dishwasher up every day, and running it. That meant there were no dirty dishes that we wanted to use just sitting dirty in the dishwasher. Another nice feature I like about the dishwasher is it displays this pretty blue light underneath the unit to tell you when the dishes are done. It also is fairly quiet as far as dishwashers go.

This love affair lasted for about six weeks. '

All the sudden the electronic control panel froze after running a load, and after about ten minutes the lights started blinking. Resetting the machine by unplugging it did not solve the problem. Moroever unlike the Fisher and Paykel dishwasher I purchased before, the instructions did not tell you what the various combinations of blinking lights meant. I couldn't find this information anywhere.

So, I called up Electrolux. To its credit, the customer service was friendly. The representative spoke English. She gave me a list of repair people in the area to call, which I did. About three days later the repair guy came out. About two hours before he came, I plugged the machine back in and all the sudden it was working. Go figure. Shortly after the cycle started, however, water came rushing out from underneath the unit. This didn't happen before, but I had removed the floor plate earlier to look under the unit, and suspected that maybe it was releasing water before, but I just didn't notice it.

So, the repair guy came, and found that the basin holding the filter was not properly secured. He speculated that the water was coming out the basin, and it caused some sensor that detects low water to trip thereby shutting off unit and displaying the blinking lights I encountered. So, he secured the basin, and the dishwasher did in fact operate properly. That is until later that night, when the blinking lights and frozen control panel problem reoccurred. We called the repair people again. Three days later, another guy showed up and said he thought the control panel was toast. He said he had to order the parts, which would take about 5 days. Currently, we are waiting for the parts to arrive. So, we waited a month to get this dishwasher. It worked great for about six weeks. Then it was out of commission for about a week. It then worked for half a day. Now we are waiting for a week for it to possibly work again.

I called Electrolux to express my dissatisfaction. The representative claimed that at this point all they could do is repair the machine. She, however, did agree to extend the warranty by six months.

I read online that some other people are experiencing the same problem. For some of them, they had to remove the dishwasher, tip it on its back, access some panel, and tighten it. I am capable of trying that myself, but I don't think I should have to for an $800 dollar dishwasher (even though I paid less). It will be interesting to see if replacing the control panel fixes the machine.

UPDATE: I raised my review one star. The machine is fixed, and working great again. Three weeks running now. Had I not had issues I would rate it five stars. When working it really does do s great job.

The repair guy told me it likely was a design defect the company knew about and fixed with the new part it sent. He also told me a Korean company makes all of the 18 inch dishwashers and the name brands just design things like the trim and controls.

As previously said, Electrolux did pay for repairs and extended the warranty by six months. They also gave me an extra year warranty that covers just parts on top of that.

UPDATE 2: OK this thing has to be the worst dishwasher on the planet. When it is working it is great. However, now every few days the control panel has a light that lights up and freezes. When this happens nothing one can do will fix the issue. Generally in about a day it will start working again. Right now it has been out of commission two days. This machine makes me want to do unspeakable things. It has to be the worst overpriced purchase I have ever made. Go with the BOSCH.

review_text: I didn't know a simple gas oven could have this bad of a design.  Obviously it's designed by some engineer who has never cooked.  When you use the oven a fan runs the entire time, blowing hot air out the front right on you and also out the back heating up the entire kitchen until you can't stand it.  Then the fan runs for 30 to 40 minutes after you turn the oven off making sure the inside of the oven is cool and comfortable, but the humans in the kitchen are dying of heat stroke.  Shortly after we purchased it, the fan in my oven starting hitting something so there is an irritating loud buzz the entire time the fan is on. review_title: Deserves ZERO STARS!!!!  DO NOT BUY THIS Piece of....
review_text:
This was a terrible purchase. I actually admired it in the showroom for a year before I purchased it. Boy do I regret it.
I replaced a Kitchen-Aid Superba that just had problem after problem. When the computer finally went out I purchased this one.

What a disaster from the start.

My first (baked) meal was prepared on a cold Chicago November evening. And to think... I was actually cooked out of my kitchen (that has an open floor plan and vaulted ceilings). After much research, the issue is how the range is designed.

There's a gap in the front of the range above the door and below the controls. Also, there is a fan that starts on the oven to blow hot air to prevent the controls from melting. I called Electrolux and they told me that this is how the range is engineered and they know that it will heat up your kitchen 7-10 degrees.

All I could think of was being cooked out in the winter, I will never be able to use my oven as soon as Spring hits.

I complained to my sales guy and he agreed to take it back from me and I purchased GE Cafe 30" Stainless Steel Slide-In Gas Range With Baking Drawer - CGS985SETSS This one doesn't leak heat.

Other notes: the oven did cook beautifully.... but I can't tolerate the heat loss
When I open the oven door too fast its like it blows out the flames and suddenly I get a whiff of gas until it re-ignights.
The oven drawer only goes up to 170 degrees, which your food can cool off pretty quick if you try to use it for very long. I have more luck storing things in my microwave turned off than using the bottom drawer "warming" oven.
The details on the stovetop dials rubbed off within a month.

As another reviewer noted, the large burner is difficult to regulate.... especially for simmer which supposedly it excels at.

I have no idea what test market actually approved this product to be built and sold, but I'd be surprised if you found anyone who is an avid cook that actually LIKES this thing. Congratulations team--I will never purchase another Electrolux appliance again.

product_title: Whirlpool: WRT771REY 21.1 cu. ft. Top-Freezer Refrigerator with SpillMizer Glass Shelves, Humidity Controlled Crispers, Full-Width Pantry, External Water Dispenser and Ice Maker
review_text: I bought this frig two years ago.  It was more than I had ever spent on an appliance and I was thrilled to have an automatic icemaker and water in the door.  Unfortunately, there is a manufacturing problem with this frig.  The plastic tubing that goes to the frig at about level with the icemaker does not stay in place.  I've had the repairman out three times in two years for this single problem, and I sit here now waiting for him to return for the 4th time.  They have tried everything - putting a bracket thingy on it to hold the plastic tubing in place and tightening it down with screws.  But nothing works.  A week ago I was standing at the kitchen counter when a spray of water came over the top of the frig.  The tubing had slipped out again.  I hate to think what would have happened to my oak floors if I had been at work at the time.  I've decided this is the last time I will pay for a service call - they are quite expensive.  If it happens again (and of course it will) I will disconnect the water feature and make my own ice cubes and forego the water.  I'm so disappointed in this refrigerator.  My advice to anyone shopping for a frig is to make sure the water connectors screw in securely.  Anything else will ultimately not be able to stay in place. In every other way, this is a reasonable frig.  Nothing fabulous, but fine.  I did not purchase this through Amazon, but since they sell it I thought I would share my experiences.

product_title: LG LFX25991ST 24.5 Cu. Ft. Counter-Depth French Door Refrigerator with Smart Cooling Plus
review_text:
We've had this fridge for a few months now and it's forced us to reevaluate food expiration dates. The first thing we noticed was the produce was lasting two to three times longer than in our previous fridge (a 2004 Whirlpool Gold). We just made a salad from two week old lettuce and it was almost as fresh as the day we bought it. Green onions, fresh cilantro, fresh parsley, and cucumbers have all at least doubled their shelf lives. We then began to realize that our deli meats and dairy products were also staying fresh longer. We used to have to throw out the milk within 3-4 days after the sell by date, when it started to smell. I just drank a glass of milk that was 11 days past the sell by date and it tasted and smelled the same as it did the day I opened it. The sliced turkey, ham and sliced cheeses have also been lasting significantly longer. I don't understand it, but it's awesome.
Everything else on the fridge has been great. Love the LED lighting, the counter depth, the easily accessible water filter, the in door ice maker, and the bottom drawer freezer. The stainless is a pain to keep clean, but so was our last fridge. I had read reviews on other sites that had complaints about the ice maker jamming. This has happened once to ours in the first week and was a quick fix. I just took out the ice container and banged it on the counter to break up the ice. It hasn't happened again. The counter depth for us has been great. Our previous fridge had gaps on both sides and stuck out farther into the kitchen. This one still leaves a small gap on one side, but is 3 inches shallower while giving us an extra 4.5 cubic feet of storage. The 3 inches doesn't sound like much, but it made a world of difference in the look of our kitchen.
The only negative thing I can say about this refrigerator is the high price. I couldn't imagine spending that much money on any appliance, but the wife talked me into it. After using it for a few months, I figure since it's saving us at least $50 per month in food costs, it should pay for itself in a few years. If you're looking for a counter depth fridge that keeps food fresh longer and looks great in your kitchen, this is the way to go.

product_title: LG LFX25991ST 24.5 Cu. Ft. Counter-Depth French Door Refrigerator with Smart Cooling Plus
review_title: really great refrigerator, but don't underestimate the burden of counter depth
review_text:
Ours has worked perfectly; ice-maker and water dispenser are great. And the whole ice/water package is in the door freeing up a lot of space. That's really important because even though this thing is only abut 4" less depth than a standard unit, it's a little tricky to get food arranged in it. We had to load and unload it a few times to get enough fresh food for two people in it. The trick is that everything thing as tall as a normal beer bottle must be in the right side door. All the tiny mustard bottle sized stuff must be in the left side door. Then you'll have enough space for the usual things in a fridge on the shelves.

The good news is that the doors have shelves that are really large and it is possible to keep a six pack, a couple of bottles of wine, and a gallon of milk in the right hand door.

A design choice that I don't care for is that vegetable bins are too small because there is a drawer for junk food under them. I would have skipped that wide short junk food drawer under the veggie bin and made the veggie bins deeper (if funny shaped).

The real problem IMHO is that the freezer is too big. We don't eat frozen food, and the icemaker is in the fridge, so this huge freezer is wasted space. Normal people that eat a lot of frozen food are going to get just about all the freezer space a standard has, but they'll really need the space in the fridge more. If they made the freezer about 4" shorter you'd get back all the space in the fridge you lose from the counter depth, plus you could put a six back on the shelves rather than in the door. There is a fold up shelf but the part that folds is too small to be realistic; the six has to go sides ways across the fridge.

As it is, there isn't space for more than 2 six packs, so probably not the fridge you want if you entertain...

LG forces customers to call LG and LG sends a repair person who charges 2-3 times the going rate, and LG charges sky high prices for parts. review_text: I bought this brand because it was rated the highest in reliability. But shortly after its extended warranty expired, it stopped cooling. We had to throw all our food out, a $300 waste. When the repair tech pulled it away from the wall he had me touch the back coils on the heat exchanger. They were cold. They should be warm. He then pointed to the 3 foot vertical rust and ice line on the back metal wall of the f.ridge. He said I have a coolant leak spraying the inside back wall. It stopped cooling because it ran out of coolant. Because it is an internal sealed system it was not repairable and we had to buy a new fridge. It irks me that friends with cheap fridges have lasted 20 years but this premium brand only a couple of years. If you buy this fridge, set an alarm on your smart phone for a month before your warranty expires and check the back for rust lines. Demand a replacement if you have them. Don't wind up like me.

product_title: Whirlpool WDF510PAYS 510 24" Stainless Steel Full Console Dishwasher - Energy Star
review_text:
I just purchased this dishwasher to replace another one that lasted 8 years. I could've repaired the other one as the pump wore out, but for a bit more, I sprang for a new one. I read the reviews about people complaining about the utensil basket in the door. Well, if they read the instructions, the basket can be mounted elsewhere. That's why they call it the "Whirlpool® Dishwasher with AnyWare(tm) Plus Silverware Basket". AnyWare(tm) Plus Silverware Basket means The basket fits in three places. Put it on the front of the rack or in the door for 100% usable rack space, or use it in the bottom rack for maximum flexibility. Here's the link http://www.whirlpool.com/-%5BWDF510PAYS%5D-1020680/WDF510PAYS/
I found the noise to be quiet and not that noticeable. It cleans really well and I have not had a problem. As with many appliances, you have to supply the power cord.
I found the installation easy. I reused the appliance cord from the one I took out and bought a universal dishwasher installation kit. It had the 5' steel braided supply line I needed and the connector to connect it. It worked perfectly and made it easy. It took about 20 minutes to install and I am no professional, just an Average Joe. The drain line comes with clamps and I connected mine to the garbage disposal. Installed and running with no leaks. Only tools needed were a screwdriver (electrical connections and mounting screws), channel lock or adjustable wrench (tightening the water supply to the machine) and that was it.
Several loads have been put through and all were cleaned well. I like the price, simplicity and am happy with the way it works.

product_title: Whirlpool WDF510PAYS 510 24" Stainless Steel Full Console Dishwasher - Energy Star
review_text:
We bought this dishwasher to replace an aging Kitchenaid (that one lasted over 20 years). Our old dishwasher quit suddenly just before Thanksgiving and I scrambled to find a dishwasher I could pick up and install that day. I soon discovered that stores don't stock many dishwashers. This model was in stock at our local Bestbuy store for right at $300, we like our other Whirlpool products, so I went with it.

Likes: the tall tub, energy star rating, it is very quiet, and it has done an excellent job of cleaning the dishes. We use the "normal" cycle, not the quick wash. I am ashamed to say that our dishes were noticeably cleaner and the glassware clearer after being run in this washer, apparently our old one wasn't doing a good job anymore. I like the controls and the options, it is easy to use.

Dislikes: predominately the silverware basket hanging on the door. I haven't read the instructions yet, so I'm glad another reviewer remarked that there are other options mentioned, I'll check that out. The tub is plastic, but I'm not sure that is a big disadvantage, and I wouldn't expect stainless at this price point. Non adjustable racks- we don't miss the height adjustment of our old upper rack, but we have had trouble loading the dishes as efficiently as before. That may be a matter of time to discover the best way to use it.

Basically I am very happy with the way it looks and the way it works, and for this price I think we did very well. Over $500 like some reviewers mentioned? That seems a bit much for this dishwasher. We had a Bosch in another house that we paid around $550 for and the build quality and features were much better than this. Even now I see this model on sale for about $360 at Bestbuys. If you can find it under $400 okay, not a bad dishwasher- get one, if you can't- keep looking.

product_title: Whirlpool WDF510PAYS 510 24" Stainless Steel Full Console Dishwasher - Energy Star
review_title: Run, Don't Walk, Away from this Machine
review_text: I purchased this model in November 2012 to replace an existing dishwasher.  For the first month, the unit worked well.  Then a few dishes started not being clean.  Silverware still had food on them.  We thought it was the detergent, so we tried a few different brands.  That helped temporarily.  We tried loading the dishwasher differently, no change.  Then, right after the warranty expired, the Sanitize indicator light on the front panel started blinking instead of staying solidly lit at the end of the cycle.  The dishes, while never really dry at the end of the cycle, were becoming even less so.  A horrible odor started coming from the unit.  We thought it was the drain, then we thought it was the garbage itself, before discovering that it came from the dishwasher.  The dishes that were clean appeared to be washed, but they smelled terrible.  I would have to air everything out.  The few unclean dishes became several; 50% to 75% of the silverware stayed dirty.  The silverware rack is a terrible design and constantly came apart when lifting it up to empty it.  I called Whirlpool, to no avail.  [The one thing that is nice about their customer department is that it is in the U.S.]  So, I called a local repair person who first replaced the heating element, which did nothing  to fix the issues.  Then he came back and said it was the relay switch, so the motherboard needed replacing.  Between the two repairs, it would be near the cost of replacing the unit itself.  I now have to buy a new dishwasher.  SO disappointed in Whirlpool right now. Sad thing is, with my budget, and the fact that Whirlpool owns several brands, I probably will have to buy another one.  I will be getting an extended warranty, though.  I would recommend that no matter what brand you buy -- nothing is built to last anymore.

product_title: Whirlpool WDF510PAYS 510 24" Stainless Steel Full Console Dishwasher - Energy Star
review_text:
Disclaimer: I'm a bit sour.

Granted, the number of reviews on Amazon are significantly lower than those on Lowe's or Home Depot, but I am upset to see how strikingly different the reviews are on Amazon. They are overwhelmingly positive every where else, but quite low here.

The big issues I noted on the negative reviews here:
* Washer does not dry
* Utensil rack attached to the door is annoying
* Is overall cheap

My response:
* Washer does dry. In fact, it dries well. I wonder what the disconnect here is. Not using a drying agent? Not loading the washer properly. I just don't know. I will say some plastics did not come out 100% dry, but I have never had a dishwasher where everything came out perfectly dry. I've used about 6 other dishwashers over the course of my time and they are all the same

* Utensil rack is certainly different. I can't say "50% of the rack is useless," as that's just plain not true. It takes some getting used to but once you do, you grow to like that it's on the door to save space on the bottom rack for other items.

* Can't speak to the "cheapness" of this washer. Seems just like any other one I've used. If anything, I've heard good things from Whirlpool.

Thank you, reviewers, for stressing me out pretty much over nothing. YMMV, but mine's been pretty good.

product_title: Whirlpool WRF560SEYM 19.5 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel French Door Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_text:
Overall this fridge looks great and has performed well (I've had it about a month). I do have some complaints though. If you are constrained to 30 inches, I think it's a great contender, but if not, look for something else.

On the plus side, you get benefits of a French Door fridge in a 30 inch space, including
- eye-level refrigerator compartment
- better energy efficiency due to the door configuration
- through the door water dispenser
- more attractive styling (in my opinion)

In addition, it has good, modern fridge features like LED lighting, a shelf with a sliding part that can be moved away to accommodate taller items from the shelf below, an air filter that controls odors (no more baking soda!), moisture control (basically a heater which evaporates condensation on the door seal), humidity-controlled drawers, and some other things. Nothing unique or outstanding, but I'm glad it has them.

However, there are a number of things I'm not thrilled about:
- Fridge space. I still can't get as much stuff in this unit as in my old top-freezer model, despite that they are both approximately the same advertised cubic feet. I'm sure this is partially because I have not yet figured out the optimal way to utilize the space, but there is also a significant gap between the front of the main shelves, and the door compartments (when closed). In my opinion, the shelves should be an inch or two longer so you could this space.
- Freezer space. Same deal here - there is nearly a 4 inch gap between the top of the sliding upper freezer shelf, and the the top of the freezer, creating a full cubic foot of difficult-to-use space. If you have a single tall item, you can put it there, but you can't pile multiple things all the way up, because the shelf's back does not come up that high so things will fall off, requiring you to squat down and retrieve them before you can close the freezer. Also, the ice-maker bucket is stupidly large given the size of this fridge. It's literally twice as big as it needs to be - about 20% of the total freezer space. I'd much prefer to have half as much ice and 10% more space for food.
- Water temperature. The water tubing that leads from the cool water in the reservoir to the dispenser is outside the fridge on the back, So the water in the tubing warms up to room temp as it sits there. Thus the first cup of water is warm to cool-ish depending on the size of your cup, and then the second cup is then colder. Whirlpool suggests discarding the first cup of water. Not only is this very wasteful, but it also take a long time since water already comes out relatively slowly from fridge dispensers (due to the 1/4" piping). Better to use some of that excessive ice in the freezer to cool down the first cup!
- no butter compartment
- the lighting strip has a bulge in the front, which blocks access to stuff in the center of the top shelf, making them hard to reach.

That said, these faults are all things I can live with and I do not regret the purchase. More than anything I wish I had more than 30 inches of width in my kitchen so I had more fridge choices!

review_text:
I purchased this unit in Feb. 2013 to replace a 20+ year old GE side by side. I was very excited about the updated technology especially the electric bill savings. It worked flawlessly for about 4 months. We had some chicken spoil. There was nothing noticeably wrong with the refrigerator so I assumed it was just bad meat. Two weeks later we had more meat spoil. Up until this point the unit had remained on it's default cooling settings. I adjusted the temperature 1 "snow flake" up from the default 3 to 4. within 24 hours half the items inside were frozen. I then went back to the default settings. I also purchased a refrigerator thermometer to keep tabs on the temps inside. On the default cooling settings they were ranging from 40 to 50 degrees. I submitted a service request to Whirlpool. When the tech came out (around a week after the request) everything was working as it should and the temps were ranging from 35 to 40 degrees. He found nothing wrong and said to call if it acted up again. He came early in the morning. We left just after him and did not return until later that evening. The temps were back up to 45-50 degrees. I submitted another service request. This time he ordered a new thermistor. The first part was the wrong one so we waited over a week for the correct part to arrive. After replacing the thermistor we noticed no change in the temperature or behavior of the unit. We were now using the maximum cooling setting. The temperatures remained around 30-40 degrees for several months. Occasionally we would have partially frozen vegetables or other items that were in the very back of the fridge. It is now Jan. 2014 and for the last couple of days the unit will not cool below 40 degrees going as high as 50. I am in the process of another service request. With all of the great reviews on this unit I assume I just got a "lemon"...

4/5/2014 update

The ice maker is no longer working. The temperatures are still all over the place. The small thin rubber(?) door seal on the right door has completely fallen apart. It started as a very small tear near the bottom. Over a few weeks it continued tearing to the middle of the door. And the best part... the warranty expired in February...

I've had the same white Whirlpool Princess Series 14 cubic ft. refrigerator for 27 years. By the way, it's still working perfectly and I never once had to have it repaired! My mother also has the same refrigerator, but in beige. She never had to repair it either. Yes, I needed more room as the years went on and my family grew...but I managed somehow, not wanting to discard an appliance in perfect working order. However, an opportunity arose to "upgrade" to a larger-sized refrigerator with an icemaker and filtered water dispenser. Upon the passing of a family member living in the first floor of my home, I renovated the apartment and relocated my old Whirlpool to that kitchen so I could treat myself to a new one.

With only 32-1/2 inches width available in my refrigerator opening among my kitchen cabinets, I found my options extremely limited if not non-existent to purchase a French-door refrigerator that would fit. Following an extensive internet search, I found only two models available with French doors, a stainless steel finish and outside water dispensers that were small enough to install in my kitchen. The other model was a Maytag, which appeared to be practically identical to this Whirlpool model. Lucky for me, my nearby PC Richards Appliance Center had this model in stock. Still, I wandered the appliance aisles in search of other options; none were to be found. Most refrigerators of this kind are 32-5/8" or 32-3/4 in width. There is nothing smaller. I was initially disappointed that the icemaker wasn't part of the front panel dispenser. The icemaker only works inside the bottom freezer, depositing cubes into a large bucket in the top drawer. However, I've had this refrigerator for two weeks and am quite happy with that configuration. Everything works beautifully, so I was quite shocked to see the bleak reviews given in Amazon for this product. I felt compelled to post a good review, as this product performs as intended. I would like to tell prospective buyers, though, that you will have to take out one of the shelves on the right door if you want to store 1 liter bottles of soda or a gallon of milk on the door (there are three shelves on each door). It runs very quietly and I have no complaints with this product. I find it ironic that after 27 years, I'm with yet another Whirlpool refrigerator! I only hope that this one endures as long as my original one. I think it's wonderful that they cornered a market for a product that people really want that only have a small space for a refrigerator. I have a stand up diner bowl apparatus nearby for my large dog at a right angle to my refrigerator, so the French door style works great for me as it avoids that area. I am very happy with my purchase.

review_title: Do your research and check reviews first.
review_text:
Hindsight is 20/20
We bought this as a Christmas gift to ourselves. We were using a Gibson refrigerator that was 34 years old. It still worked but we thought we were living on borrowed time. So off to Home Depot for the holiday sale they had. We went from an old type of fridge with the freezer on the top and not a lot of room in it. The Whirlpool offered much more freezer space but we weren't used to the freezer being on the bottom. I have to say, in hindsight, we should've gotten a side by side or another top/bottom instead of this. We have a little more room in the freezer but it is next to impossible to organize. I find I have to pull things out to get at what I want. And when trying to figure what to make for dinner, I could no longer stand and look in the freezer and say, "oh, I can make this or that" because now I have no organization. Even trying to keep like foods together is almost impossible as there are only 2 "bins". I find that now I have to keep a mental list of what I have and what I need. As far as the refrigerator, I wish there was more "headroom" for the taller items kept in a fridge. Like milk, soda bottles, even large ketchup bottles. This has a shelf that half of it slides back to put taller items there but sometimes you have more than what fits in the door or that one space. When I was making a holiday dinner, I didn't have enough room to put a 12 lb. turkey to defrost. It wouldn't fit. And figuring all the make ahead dishes you make for the holidays, there's just not enough room to hold them all as well as your normal fridge items. There is plenty of room on the door shelves but again, not a lot for taller items. I do really like the drawers in the fridge as you can control the humidity in them for maximum freshness. And the see thru shelves are nice to have, especially when you have someone in the house that doesn't like to move things to find something ;). They are also easy to clean. It has the filtered water dispenser but we haven't hooked that up yet as we don't have an existing water line in that space of the kitchen so I can't comment on that feature. Never having had a stainless steel appliance before, I didn't realize what a pain it was to keep it fingerprint free, but with a certain glove that was recommended by a friend, it's not a big problem. But it would still be nice if I didn't have to go through steps in order to keep it shiny. We have some measurement requirements with our space which limited our selection of refrigerators so this one fit with only a ½" to spare. In hindsight though, had I realized my real time issues before I even started shopping, I would not have bought this fridge. But hindsight is 20/20, right? Were it not for Home Depot's very shoddy return and exchange policy (they only give you 48 hrs. and will only take it back or exchange it if something is wrong or broken), we would've tried to exchange it for a side by side or another top/bottom. I do like that it was made in America.

Addendum-I wrote this review on January 30, 2018 and originally submitted directly to Whirlpool by request. They have yet to post it.
It should also be noted that their website definitely needs improvement. I wasn't able to register it online but instead had to snail mail to card.

product_title: Whirlpool WRF560SEYM 19.5 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel French Door Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_text: This appliance was virtually new when we bought this house 3.5 years ago.  The water hadn't even been hooked up. It was a lot smaller than I was used to, and there was definitely a LOT more space available, but the previous homeowner I guess was just looking for a cheaper one to put in the house to sell it... Anyway, it's got good modern features. The only issue we started having was after we hooked up the water, we started having issues with the freezer not closing. We realized over time that the water connection was loose, dripping under the freezer drawer, and creating a slab of ice building. Once we rectified that, the problem was solved. We've now just upgraded to a MUCH larger appliance , and are selling this one, but I had to give this one a decent plug since it has been fine for us the last 3.5 years.

product_title: Whirlpool WRF560SEYM 19.5 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel French Door Refrigerator - Energy Star

product_title: Whirlpool WOD93EC0AS 30" Stainless Steel Electric Double Wall Oven - Convection
review_text: We upgraded our kitchen with the builder and this is the double oven that they included. A fan comes on when you turn the oven on to heat up, stays on while cooking, and remains on for quite a long duration afterward while it cools down (ie baking for 1/2 an hour leads to approximately 1.5 hours of fan noise in the kitchen).  With an open floor plan, it's difficult to hear the TV or converse with guests while this oven is on. After much searching online, it appears that the fan is required to keep the electronics cool.  Am quite disappointed and would prefer old-school dials over the noisy but fancy electronics.  Too bad it's such an expensive oven or we'd just replace it right away.

product_title: Whirlpool WOD93EC0AS 30" Stainless Steel Electric Double Wall Oven - Convection
review_text: I love this oven! My whole family can't stop baking. The warming feature is divine.  It's beautiful to look at, too!

product_title: Whirlpool WOD93EC0AS 30" Stainless Steel Electric Double Wall Oven - Convection
review_text:
We purchased this double oven 6 months ago and it has been a big disappointment for us because of one feature.
When you turn off the oven, the fan keeps running (in order to cool the oven down and protect the electronic components according to Whirpool)
and it makes a very annoying howling noise for at least 30- 45 minutes after the oven is turned off.

It makes dinner much less pleasant than it would be without the noise. I checked with Whirlpool and they do not have a replacement board that would turn the fan off when the oven is shut down. This is unfortunate since the oven is stylish, full-featured, easy-to-use, and bakes well. But all that does not make up for having to eat meals with the annoying noise. I hope they solve this problem in the next version of the oven; in the meantime we'll do more grilling and less baking.

product_title: Whirlpool WOD93EC0AS 30" Stainless Steel Electric Double Wall Oven - Convection
review_title: Great except for fatal design flaw
review_text: The oven is great except for a fatal flow in the door where grease can get down into the door and cause streaks on the glass.  The only way to clean it is to take apart the door which is difficult.  It is not covered under warranty.

product_title: Whirlpool WOD93EC0AS 30" Stainless Steel Electric Double Wall Oven - Convection
review_title: We love the looks of the oven
review_text: We love the looks of the oven, and works just fine.  However, as others have noted, this oven makes a LOUD whistling noise whenever either oven is turned on.  The service techs have no answer, and have replaced both fans, to no avail.  If we had known about this problem ahead of time, we never would have purchased this oven.

product_title: Whirlpool WOD93EC0AW
review_text: I am currently fighting with the dealer to return this poorly made/dangerous product.  The oven blows so much heat out of the bottom vent that it heats up my whole kitchen. The oven has a very small metal hood at the bottom of the second oven where the heat blows out.  This little metal plate gets so hot in a short period of time that eventually someone is going to get burned and sue Whirlpool - won't be me or my family as I am getting rid of this thing.  I called Whirlpool to complain and they said "you just need to keep your kids away from the oven." Easy for them to say when my kitchen is totally open to the living room and my table and chairs are next to the oven. Wasn't expecting to have to return something like this - I really wanted to love this oven. It is beautiful to look at, but not worth the risk.

product_title: GE GLDT696DSS 24" Stainless Steel Fully Integrated Dishwasher - Energy Star
review_title: Worst appliance I have ever owned
review_text:
firstly I did not buy this from amazon, I bought it locally, along with a ge fridge, washer, dryer, and microwave. In all my years, in all the houses I have lived in, and all the firehouses I have worked in, I have never truly hated an appliance until I bought this piece of junk.

cons

product_title: GE GLDT696DSS 24" Stainless Steel Fully Integrated Dishwasher - Energy Star
review_text: This thing is tiny! It came with the house we recently moved into and it's so small compared to my old cheap Maytag (and every other dishwasher I've ever owned or even used). We've estimated it is at least 1/3 smaller than a normal dishwasher.  I started researching it to find out what size it was, I cannot believe this is considered a standard size dishwasher. The top rack is so shallow, it's useless for anything other than short cups...forget about wine glasses!  The previous owner kept receipts on everything so I know this is fairly new and yet I'm constantly pulling dirty dishes out after it runs.  And for the price, I'm shocked it doesn't have a hard food disposer.  Far cheaper models include this.  This is definitely first on the upgrade list!

product_title: GE GSC3500DBB Console Dishwasher
review_text: as some others have indicated, this dishwasher seems to do very little, if anything, in the way of actually cleaning dishes.  :(  i don't mind the noise level a bit; i guess i grew up with noisier dishwashers than some people did. but running it at all is kind of pointless if it's not going to get the dishes clean.

product_title: GE GSC3500DBB Console Dishwasher
review_text: This machine is great for storing your dirty dishes in a concealed, out of the way spot until you are ready to wash them by hand. It can also be used as a draining/drying rack after you wash those dishes by hand. What it is NOT good at is actually washing dishes. It is SLIGHTLY better if you run it when it's no more than about half full, but that's not very environmentally friendly. Today I opened it to find small plates with literally all the same crumbs on them. Mind you, this was not tough, stuck-on food - just crumbs from toast. You know, the kind that brush off really easily. But it hadn't even managed to remove those. If I did not clearly remember putting detergent in, hooking it up to the faucet, etc etc, I would seriously think it hadn't been run at all. I'd say it is WORST at silverware. I've tried with more detergent, less detergent, but no matter what you do, you end up with an icky filmy residue on them. I'm willing to use them at that point but would definitely be embarrassed to use if I had guests. Then if you DO use them that way, though, after a few cycles, that film has built up to the point where it's significantly more work to remove (by hand) than if you had just washed them by hand to begin with. It is highly disappointing when you are used to a good-performing non-portable. I don't know if there ARE any good portable dishwashers in existence. I do know this ain't one.  James Dyson, are you listening? Could you save us poor renters by inventing a portable dishwasher? Because unlike you, apparently GE doesn't think things should work properly.

product_title: GE GSC3500DBB Console Dishwasher
review_title: Decent at washing, bad at longevity.
review_text: Unlike others here, I had no problem getting dishes clean with this dishwasher. It was excellent at that. review_text: I bought the gth17jbcww which has now been replaced by the gth17dbdww.  My purchase was less than two years ago. product_title: Whirlpool WFC130M0AW 30" White Electric Coil Range
review_title: Everything I need including a low price!
review_text:
When we found that we were going to replace a washer/dryer, range and refrigerator all at the same time, price quickly became one of the top 5 priorities. I purchased mine at a home improvement store during their rebate drive for major appliances. (so I can't rate this seller) In speaking with the sales person I found that if you are into canning, a smooth surface is not for you. ( I also fry in a cast iron Lodge = high heat) He owns one and said that while they love the look of the smooth, clean-up can be an issue - say with boiled potatoes over flowing. Those two scenarios are the reason I chose a standard coil element.

At first I wanted a self cleaning oven, however, I only use the feature once a year as I live by the old rule of clean as you go. So the extra $$$ for the feature was put to better use on another appliance. I bake/broil about 4 times a week and have not had any issues with simple clean up of the oven. We were not fans of the plastic knobs and almost purchased a Frigidare for the same price that was sitting right next to it, until we opened the oven door. This range has much more heft in the handle and opening mechanism (since I use my oven this is a key item) and the oven view larger. So we opted for this model and we deal with the knobs and the cheap drip pans( I can buy those)

I prefer a gas range BUT I have to say the response time for heat up and cool down is excellent on all the elements of this model. When boiling you do not need to remove the pot should you come close to overboil, turn it down, wait and then replace the pot. Same with the oven. The broiler is fantastic, heats up quickly and steaks are done in just a few minutes. Broiler is within the oven, not the bottom drawer, which I prefer.

It has the basic features of an oven timer, oven light, glass door, 2 large/2 small burners, bake and broil. I paid $359.00 and had it delivered and set-up the next day. We purchased it in black, which is actually not any harder to keep streak-free than the white. All-in-all, thumbs-up great baseline stove AND it's made here in America.

product_title: Whirlpool WDF310PAAW 24" White Full Console Dishwasher - Energy Star
review_title: Cleans Exceptionally Well, A Great Buy -  Readon...

3) One Hour Wash - To use this (and it cleans perfectly), I go to - One Hour Wash and then press start/resume. And in one hour, my dishes come out sparkly clean.

4) Basic model that has TWO RINSE ARMS. And not too many bells and whistles. This is a BUDGET MID RANGE MODEL, not a top of the line, but worth the price.

**True stars: 4.9

product_title: Whirlpool WDF310PAAW 24" White Full Console Dishwasher - Energy Star
review_title: For this price, this is a bargain!
review_text:
I was in the market for a cheap, but good dishwasher, and this was a perfect fit for my needs. Originally, I was looking on craigslist for a used bosch dishwasher, as my mom has a bosch, and it works great. As you can imagine, one of those isn't exactly easy to find used at a cheap price because of their popularity.

Finally, I decided to look at some of the new, low budget, dishwashers for sale at lowes. This one had great reviews, and for good reason. For the money, it washes almost as good as my moms bosch dishwasher. I mean, you can't put dishes in it with food chunks all over it, but if you wash off the dishes first, and let the sticky ones soak, it does a great job. I use the normal and sometimes pot scrub settings.

It has all the best parts a good dishwasher should have, like the two wash arms, without all the expensive options I really don't need. I used to hate the old style dishwashers that would have that thing coming up through the center to spray water into the second wash arm. This one, thankfully, doesn't use that idiotic design, leaving you plenty of room for dishes.

It's true that your dishes may still be a little wet when they are done, but coming from a guy who use to have to hand wash them and stick them in a drainer, who cares! I just open the dishwasher door a bit, and let them finish air drying. At least it gets the water hot enough to sanitize the dishes.

If you're on a budget, and aren't some spoiled snob who has to have the best of everything, than this might be the dishwasher for you.

product_title: Whirlpool WOC95EC0AS
review_text:
Caught in Whirlpool of Horrors

I have made a conscious choice to remove baked food from my diet back in early 2013. That has not stopped my wife from pursuing her passion for baking from time to time. It goes without saying that baking requires a well functioning baking oven. The one that came with our home was a Whirlpool Wall Oven/Microwave combination. Sometime in early 2014 the Oven broke down. I had no choice but to replace the combination. After doing some online research and a couple of trips to stores like Sears, Home Depot and Lowes, we decided to drop 2700 of our hard earned dollars on a brand new Whirlpool WOC95EC0AS wall oven microwave combo to replace the old one. Lowes sent someone home to take measurement to make sure that we ordered the right size for the slot in our kitchen. 2 weeks after the purchase, around March 27th or 28th, we had the Microwave oven installed in our kitchen by some Lowes provided. After installing the appliance, the technician demoed both the microwave and the oven part of the combo. Everything looked good and we were happy to see the shiny new appliance adorning our kitchen. Little did we know then that this would start a seemingly unending horror story.

For the first 3-4 weeks we used only the microwave and it worked as expected. Then one weekend, my wife decided to do some baking. The dough was prepared meticulously and then came the first surprise the oven refused to turn on - "Feature not available" the message scrolled across the LED display. And horror of horrors, the microwave started giving the same message immediately after. We looked online for solutions, and we found one that suggested that we try breaking the circuit for 1 minute and turn on again - we tried it to no avail. And now we went from having a working microwave/broken oven to no microwave/no oven.

We waited till the next day or so before placing a call to the customer service number provided in our warranty receipt. By now the 30 day return guarantee had expired and it was the end of April, 2014. Product was now under manufacturer's warranty. Whirlpool/Lowes customer service scheduled a technician to come take a look at the oven.

My wife took a day off from work and waited for the technician. The technician from J&H appliance repair of SJ came home took look and then tried breaking the circuit and turning it on again after a minute; of course, it did not work. After consulting with someone on the phone, he decided to order some parts - the main circuit board. He promised to come back after the part arrived. We did receive a call from J&H to schedule an appointment to install the part and schedule a time we did. J&H decided to no-show us on the appointment and my wife wasted another day of her time-off from work.

We called customer-service again and this time they decided to send in a technician from a Sears owned company called A&E Factory Service. A technician came home and he went through the same steps as the earlier technician from J&H. This time, it was my turn to stay home and welcome the visitor. Finally when there was no trick up his sleeves to try, he decided he is going to order the main board. A&E technician did something different - he ordered the part to my home. I called him as soon as it arrived. We scheduled a time and he arrived to install the part. I stayed home again. Well, result was no different and the appliance was in no mood to oblige to our coaxing and cajoling - "Feature not available" it continued to bleep out. He ordered 2 more boards to my home. I stayed home again to welcome the technician and he arrived again to install the 2 new boards but the result was no different than the last time - "Feature not available" the zombie appliance screamed. He told me that there is only one that remains to be done - which is to replace the front panel circuitry - so he ordered it. By now it was end of June. We hadn't used the oven for 3 full months and the microwave for 2 months.

First week of July, a new technician from A&E showed up early in the morning to install the newly ordered front panel. Surprise, Surprise - Feature not available screamed the shiny lemon sitting in my kitchen wall. The technician asked me if I will be home the whole day and I said yes. Another technician, a supposedly senior expert came by that afternoon. He tinkered with it for sometime and like all who came before him, he surrendered. He said there is nothing left to do with the oven and that he is going to recommend that the oven be replaced.

He left me a voicemail next morning saying that I need to call Whirlpool myself and apprise them of my experience and ask for a replacement. So I called the customer service - after a long 1 hour talk with customer service rep, followed by a conversation with his rude supervisor, I was told that Whirlpool no longer deals with A&E - that they broke their relationship with them as of June 31st, 2014. I failed to understand why that was my fault. I was told they need to send technician from another company - can you guess the company whirlpool recommended? It would be funny, if it wasn't incredibly painful to deal with horrible customer support representatives - yes, it was the the no-show company J&H. I told him I'd have nothing to do with J&H. So they recommended their only other option - a company called AGO.

AGO technicians started showing up at my house since early July and I waited with baited breath for them to suggest a way forward to a resolution. Well good thing that I didn't hold my breath for that to happen. AGO technicians have made 8-9 visits to my home during July and August with the last visit being on Aug 20th. They replaced all the boards that A&E guys had already replaced the previous month. On August 21st, I received a call from AGO rep saying that they have given up - that the product is irreparable. They gave me a reference number and asked me to call Whirlpool for a final resolution.

I called Whirlpool customer service on August 22, 2014 and Spoke to Jennifer and her supervisor for 32 minutes. They want to restart the whole process of sending technicians to my home. It would be funny if they hadn't stolen $2700 of my hard earned money + all the lost hours and productivity + vacation time lost + headache they caused + the pain of not having a working Oven/Microwave in our kitchen + dealing with rude "customer service" reps, I lost it. I threatened to put the whole recorded conversation on YouTube. The rude inconsiderate supervisor hung up on me.

I called back after a few minutes and spoke with a more reasonable rep named Ashley. At least, she had the patience to hear me out without barking at me about what my rights are as a customer. Well she had no better solution than to suggest another technician appointment - what was the excuse this time? That the last technician from AGO didn't call Whirlpool's tech support line while he was at my house. As if that is my fault. I agreed and we setup an appointment for Wednesday, August 27, 2014 between 8AM and 12PM with the same old company J&H who no showed me once. Goes to show you who Whirlpool's associates in business are. They had only two companies providing repair services in San Jose - AGO and J&H.

I took the morning off from work on Aug 27, 2014 and waited till 12 noon and there was no sign of technician. So I called Whirlpool customer service number one more time. As you would expect by now, a rude customer service person named Eva from Michigan picked up my call. It was reasonably clear to me during that conversation that the J&H technician no-showed because appointment was not communicated to them. She emphatically claimed that my warranty is not a product replacement warranty but a "repair" warranty and that she needs to send me a technician to take a look at the product. Can anyone believe it? She told me I have only one option either to accept the perpetual technician visits or she will note that I have rejected their offer to service the product. I told her I am not rejecting anything, just exploring all my options. She assured me I had no other options. The arrogance of these people!

So here I am, several thousand of my hard earned money stolen by Whirlpool and I still have no working product. Adding insult to injury, 2 weeks ago I received a letter from Whirlpool pitching me to extend my 3 year extended warranty to 5 years. They want to inflict more pain and charge you for the privilege.

I have more options than Eva would want me to know. Luckily I have legal coverage under my benefit plans at work. Even more importantly there is social media and internet. I am pursuing those options at the moment.

Here's the summary:

Lowes takes my $2700 on March 13th.
A total of at least 15 repair visits are made to my home ( I have started losing count)
Time since product purchase: > 5 months
# of times the oven has worked : 0
Hours spent talking to rude customer service reps: 4-6 hours
Time spent at home baby sitting repair technicians : > 100 hours

UPDATE - 9/17/14

Within a few hours of publishing this post (on 9/2/14), I was contacted by both Lowes and Whirlpool via Twitter. Both the companies seemed genuinely interested in resolving this issue. After I DMed my appliance and contact information via twitter, Melissa from Whirlpool called me and left me a voicemail on Wednesday, Sep 3rd, 2014 informing that they have decided to replace the oven. I was told in that voicemail that I should expect a call from Whirlpool on the details of the exchange before end of day on Friday (Sep 5th). I was contacted by Lowes and I informed the Lowes rep that Whirlpool has agreed to replace my oven.

I thought I would really be able to make a single update to the post informing the world that Whirlpool really made amends and tried to hard to correct the failures of the past. It is 9/15/14 today and I haven't received any updates from Whirlpool about the how/when of the exchange. I made 2 customer service calls to Whirlpool last week. I was unable to speak to Melissa the first time, but did speak with another rep. She told me she will pass the information on to Melissa and ask her to contact me. She connected me to Melissa's voicemail and I left her a voicemail. Melissa's voicemail greetings suggested that I also contact her via Whirlpool's customer service email for faster response. So I did that too.

On Thursday 12:37PM pacific, I received a call from Melissa. She had no useful information to share with me. She is waiting for some paper pusher to do his/her job and could not make any promises as to when it will be resolved. My "file" is stuck in one of Whirlpool's many bureaucratic bottlenecks. This is no personal indictment of Melissa - it is just evidence that Whirlpool's is not serious about customer satisfaction. My experience is not isolated as evidenced not just by this event but also by the number of people ranting on their social media handles. Here was an opportunity to rectify its mistake and win the confidence of a customer back and so far Whirlpool seems to be uninterested in any such thing.

12/2/14 Update:

We finally had the combination replaced by Whirlpool at the end of October. Both oven and the microwave has been working fine. The Microwave seem to have less power than one of the portable Microwave we have had for over 10 years. It takes longer to warm stuff in this Whirlpool versus the 10 year old Panasonic. review_title: ALL Hidden Element electric ovens suffer from a defective design and this Whirlpool oven is no exception
review_text:
I bought this wall oven from a major brick and mortar retailer because I have purchased nothing but Whirlpool appliances for my homes since 1978 and had excellent luck with them. After having to arrange for installation myself, because the local store had recently lost their only installer, my and wife and I began to use the oven only to see the interior temperature swing wildly around the set point and take forever to cook a pot roast, burn a pizza and in general cause a great deal of angst about purchasing a defective product.

Whirlpool warranty service sent out a factory authorized service agent who monitored the oven with a portable thermocouple and determined that the oven was performing within specifications. The problem centers around the control thermocouple regulating the oven temperature, its in an upper rear corner so it senses the highest heat in the oven (most of us should know that heat rises) and thus during the preheat mode where the oven is cycling between heating with the bake element and the broil element ( a thermochemically stupid idea) the temperature in the center of the oven and the bottom of the oven will be much lower (and so it will not cook the way you expect if you put food in the oven to cook until it is thoroughly pre-heated). The computerized controls indicate the oven is preheated when in fact it is not. The service technician advised us to install oven thermometers and to preheat the oven for roughly twice as long using the oven thermometers as an additional control mode. This does seem to have solved the problem (I have yet to cook a soufflé in this oven so this is not an absolute corrective prescription).

The technician advised that the hidden bake element design was instituted so homemakers could more easily clean the oven bottom (read homemakers more concerned about cleaning than cooking). This necessitated placing thermocouples to regulate the temperature in the oven cavity. I have a PhD in inorganic chemistry and I have used ovens and furnaces for chemical synthesis and preparations - research where precise temperature control was absolutely essential to the success of my research. Putting a control thermocouple in the top of the oven suggests the oven was designed by electrical engineers and computer programmers who do not understand the chemistry of oven cooking, which requires an isothermal (even temperature throughout) oven. I asked the technician if this was a problem common to all hidden baking element ovens, because I was seriously considering returning the oven. He assured me the problem is endemic and common to all brands including high end brands (Note: replacing a burnt out hidden element now takes three to four hours instead of simply plugging in a replacement element).

My research ovens and furnaces utilized control thermocouples placed in the middle of the rear wall. Its my suggestion that Whirlpool and all other appliance manufacturers keep in mind that heat rises and place the control thermocouple(s) in more chemically reasonable locations inside the oven cavity - maybe even consult a cooking chemist or a chemical engineer instead or relying on electrical engineers and computer programs, i.e. get professionals involved with the design of an oven who actually understand the chemistry of cooking (BTW thermocouples are not that expensive).

review_title: Not perfect, but would buy again
review_text:
We replaced our 20 year old oven with this one when we had our kitchen remodeled 2 years ago. I am generally happy with it but I will share a few bullet points that may help you with a decision:

1) Even though the oven has the same outside footprint, it is several inches wider than the old one. That is very nice.
2) The controls are very intuitive and easy to use for the most part.
3) This oven seems to be extremely slow to preheat. For anything above about 300, I feel like I need to allow for a half hour (although I haven't timed it precisely and don't have a lot of other ovens to compare to. It seems to take a long time to cool down as well unless I leave the doors cracked (I assume that means some pretty good insulation).
4) I did just have my first big issue with the oven. I ran self-cleaning cycles on the top and bottom ovens back-to-back. About half-way through the bottom oven, it blew a fuse up in the control panel that is designed to shut the oven down when it gets too hot to protect the electronics. That was a $250 repair. The repair man basically said to never use the self-clean cycle that he replaces these fuses all the time (I think he meant that for all ovens, not just this one.
5) There is a fan that blows any time the oven is on to disperse hot air out into the room. It is quite noisy, especially in a small kitchen. (this is and the slow preheating are my main reasons for taking off a star).

In general, I'm a little nervous about all of the electronics in the control panel - they are bound to go out at some point and the parts alone are $5-600, but pretty much all ovens these days are made that way.

Generally though, I'm happy with the oven, generous interior space and the temperatures seem to be accurate (and there's a calibration if something is off).

I would probably buy it again if I had to replace it (unless there was an old-fashioned kind without all of the electronics available).

Whirlpool provides only a one year warranty so they would not replace it or repair it.
While it was working, we had several problems:
Takes extremely long to warm up to 275 degrees.
Oven would advise that the oven was up to temperature long before 275 degrees was hit.
The oven would periodically lock out all functions and report "function not available." You have to turn off the circuit breaker to reset that.
The clock can not survive a power outage, requiring frequent reset. I *hate* that.

If you will Google these Whirlpool ovens you will find constant reports that the self cleaning cycle doesn't clean the oven at all. Even worse, self cleaning will blow the control panel fuse and require a repair. The self cleaning feature should be considered marketing hype, you will not get any benefit from it.

You will also find many reports of the porcelain shattering, as ours did. You will also find that Whirlpool will resist making an adjustment for this, calling it "cosmetic" damage even though compromised porcelain will make cleaning the oven impossible.

The only path forward is to fight back. Don't buy Whirlpool. Look for something with a reliable track record. Whirlpool ovens do not have that.

The new machine has been a clunker since the day it was installed! It’s extremely loud, it does not rinse properly, and now it’s leaking water and black soot from the bottom on the machine.

I’ve been washing clothes for almost 30 years, and I’ve used many different washing machines. This is the only one I have any complaints about. It is truly the worst home investment I’ve ever made.

I contacted GE Appliance Service and scheduled a service appointment. When the repair technician removed the front of the machine, he immediately saw that the machine is leaking and is rusted out. To fix it, he needs to fully disassemble and rebuild the washer, including the transmission, tub seal, bearings, tub assembly, tub ring, inner and outer basket, and probably other parts. This is a new machine, only 6 months old!

Given my experience, I do not recommend this machine. Following is a more detailed description of the problems:

1) The washer leaks – Water and black residue (looks similar to black dirt when it dries on the floor) are leaking from the bottom of the washer on the left-hand side.

2) The washer is extremely noisy – My neighbors can hear it spinning from outside of my condo unit, even when they are a full flight downstairs. It sounds like a train roaring down the tracks! The noise interferes with phone calls and TV, and it definitely doesn't make me popular with my neighbors!

3) The washer does rinse properly – With just two regularly-sized bath towels in the washer, the washer will not rinse properly. Even after running it through an extra 2 - 3 full wash/rinse cycles without soap (which takes a lot of time and wastes energy!) there are a lot of suds left in the water and there are suds on the sides of the tub after it spins. To wash towels, I have to skim out the soapy water by hand. I currently use high-efficiency (HE) laundry detergent, but the problem occurs with both HE and traditional laundry detergents. As for the question of whether I'm using too much soap, I’ve reduced the amount of soap and it didn't resolve the problem. Also, I've been washing clothes for almost 30 years, and I've never had this problem with another washer, so I don’t believe the problem is related to too much soap; the problem is with the machine and the way it rinses.
