product_title: Whirlpool WFE510S0AS 30" Stainless Steel Electric Smoothtop Range
review_title: An exercise in really bad user-interface design
review_text:
We bought a refurbished house and it came with this range. The good thing about this range is that if you can get it to do what you want, it works and it works very nicely. But the user interface on this thing (and all the Whirlpool ranges in this series) is a textbook example of what not to do. No I mean what NEVER to do. Actually I mean about 20 things NEVER to do. Really, I could teach a short course on bad design using just this range. Where do we start?

First of all, the center touch panel is recessed and it's dark. It almost defies attempts to make it light enough to see. Because it's recessed, there is a constant shadow on the top of it. If you install this with the companion overhead microwave oven you'll have both a blessing and a curse. The curse is that the microwave will cast a shadow from any overhead lights you may have, making the control panel essentially unworkable in anything but the brightest side-lit sunlight. The backhanded blessing is that the microwave has a light beneath it that you can use to slightly illuminate the control panel - but this light is pathetically dim, it's mounted almost directly above the control panel, and once again the shadow due to the recession of the panel makes even this very close light almost worthless, leaving the top half of the panel in total darkness. So you'd better keep a very bright flashlight near your stove, because you are likely to need one both day and night.

Making matters worse is the fact that the control panel has several very similar-looking buttons, requiring you to look very carefully at them. This problem with the similarity is compounded by the staggering darkness of the thing. If you are older and your eyesight is not really up to par, you will find yourself constantly putting on or taking off your glasses and/or sticking your head over the cooktop and squinting to read the tiny type, since the dark images are entirely insufficient to make clear what almost any button does.

There are more problems with the control panel but I don't want to make a book out of this.

The cooktop has four heating elements arranged in a square. But the four control knobs are in a straight line, providing no hint as to which knob controls the front vs. back burner on each side. In order to determine which burner each knob controls, there is a tiny, tiny image near each knob. Unless you have 20/20 vision at this distance, you are going to be leaning over and squinting just to see which burner you are turning on. You might expect that after a year I would have memorized which knobs go to which burners, but I haven't.

I would guess that 99% of the population would say that you should design a burner control knob so that turning it clockwise makes the burner hotter, but no, on this oven all of the knobs make the burner hotter by turning them COUNTER clockwise. Well, almost all of them. It gets even crazier.

The left front burner has a center element surrounded by an outer ring. You can turn on just the center, or the center and the ring together. Very nice, except again for the controls. Once you figure out that the leftmost knob controls the front burner, you have to squint again to see the tiny, tiny images on the left and right sides of the knob. One shows just a circle (indicating the center element) and the other shows two concentric circles, indicating both elements. These images are so incredibly small that one simply has to wonder whether the designer had some sort of telescopic vision.

After you have leaned over and squinted sufficiently to determine the side towards which to turn the leftmost knob (you select either one or both burners by using either the left or the right semicircular heat range), you then have to worry about whether to turn the knob clockwise or counterclockwise to get the "high" or "low" heat setting. Incredibly, these are opposite on the two sides of the knob. So if you are using just the center of this burner, you rotate the knob one way to make it hotter, but if you are using both elements then you rotate it the other way to make the burner hotter. A nasty contradiction in just one knob, and remember then that the side of this knob that heats up clockwise is also in contradiction with the other three knobs. Think of it. A stove on which the knobs use different rotational directions to mean "hotter". And think of it you will, every time you decide to adjust a burner. You'll squint and you'll think.

If you want some idea of how much you'll be struggling with this thing when you buy it, I suggest you look at Amazon's biggest-magnification image from a normal screen viewing distance and imagine yourself trying to figure out exactly what to do. It's very similar to standing in front of the real thing. Unless you have the eyes of a sharpshooter, you'll be putting your face right up to the screen and squinting.

The entire panel on this range is a ridiculous exercise in bad design. If I were teaching a design course and a student turned in something like this, I'd fail him and advise him to pursue another career. Really, how something like this could have made it out of the lab, let alone into production, is beyond me. And from Whirlpool, no less.

review_title: Never. Again. It's a lemon, and LG has sour customer service.
review_text:
Run. That's all I can say. Run as fast as you can from LG. Mine was not an Amazon purchase but I feel obliged to help others make an informed decision, and all I can offer is my own personal experience with this product and manufacturer.

Purchased this dryer 11/02/13, with matching washer WM3470HVA.

The "steam fresh" and "steam sanitary" cycles stopped working. I got an "Ie2" error message. But at least it dried clothes. LG customer service said that either I'd have to A) "preheat" the drum for 5 minutes (which pardon me if I'm wrong, but doesn't that defeat the purpose of having an HE machine?) or B) select the "big" setting for those two cycles and just can't use the other two garment settings. Then they told me that the current cold weather is causing this issue and I should wait until it's warm outside before calling to complain again. I insisted that I was getting the error message when it was over 70 degrees out. I live in Atlanta. I'm wondering, according to LG, do people in colder climates just have to live with error messages 6 months out of the year if that's the case?

I insisted on a service call. They obliged. BTW, the service tech has been extremely sympathetic and professional. I get the feeling he's genuinely embarrassed by LG products and customer service. His first service call didn't fix it. So he ordered replacement parts and scheduled another visit a few days later. That still didn't fix it. He said my only recourse at this point was to call LG and see what they could work out with me.

I called customer service and remained calm, but the person on the other end ("Tish") was smacking gum or food in my ear and proceeded to read a prepared statement about the cold weather causing these issues. I got frustrated and told her that's unacceptable, that a $1000 machine should work top to bottom no matter what, especially 3 months old. And it isn't like I live in Siberia. I live in Atlanta. She got condescending with me (something I've read is not unusual for LG customer service reps). I was still calm, until....she said I was getting upset for nothing. So 2-1/2 hours on the phone with customer service, missed two days of work for service calls, and to her it's "nothing." Not only that, she said there was nothing they could do, and there was nothing they were going to do. She said it was my problem. I have cut out a lot of the terrible exchanges between me and LG. Suffice it to say every call but one was this bad or worse, and nobody wanted to help. By the way, this thing is under warranty until 11/02/14.

Today it just stopped drying altogether. Oh it will turn on. It just won't heat up. Ever. Called customer "service" and have a new error message, "H5." I now have a THIRD service call in a couple of days.

I'm out $1000, have had this less than three months, and the headaches have only just begun. I pray the washer keeps working.

Bottom line: Don't do like I did. Do your homework. Read up on reliability of dryers by all manufacturers, and please take into account how customers are treated AFTER the sale closes and issues arise. If you don't believe me, you can look up something called customer service score board and LG. Read for yourself the nightmares. Look them up in the better business bureau of Huntsville Alabama. I can assure you I'm not alone.

For your sake, don't make yourself their next victim.

UPDATE: 5/6/14

If you google LG TE2 error, you'll find a video of someone who fixed the issue with a $5 part from Lowes/Home Depot. LG never knew about this, or if they did they aren't owning up to the dryer not functioning properly. That small, inexpensive part (dryer vent valve) fixed the problems I've had with this blasted machine. However, despite it working fine now, LG customer service proved to be such a horrific, maddening, traumatizing experience that I'd sooner lock myself in this very dryer and go over Niagara Falls in it than ever speak to them again.

review_title: Very nice fridge, one significant design flaw
review_text:
I've owned the LG LFX31935 for a little more than six months, and overall it has been great. It has a cavernous interior with very flexible storage options. It does a great job of keeping food cold/frozen, and it's very quiet. The material and workmanship is top notch, and it looks great. There are two things worth commenting on in more detail: the wine chiller and the ice maker.

WINE CHILLER

This unique feature is a big plus, and honestly a big selling point for my wife and I. We don't have a wine fridge, and it's nice to be able to chill a bottle of red before drinking it. This "blast chiller", as it's called, works well - it chills a bottle of wine from room temperature to ~62F in 8 minutes. You just pop open the blast chiller door, slide the bottle in cork first and rest it in cradle, close the chiller and the fridge and then press the button on the front panel. Most of the time, the thing just starts to work - the cradle gently swirls the bottle while the cold air is circulated through the chiller's chamber (it's a bit noisy while running, somewhere between a dishwasher and a stand mixer). Sometimes, however, the chiller refuses to start and affirms its obstinance with a red light next to the start button. According to the manual, this can happen when the fridge is not down to temp, which kind of makes sense. But the behavior seems more random than that - it has done this a half dozen times at least, sometimes when I'm pretty sure nobody has been in the fridge for hours. In fact, it seems to happen whenever have guests over and are trying to show off our #$%*&@ wine chiller! Otherwise, though - it's a very slick feature and one we use all the time (though it would NOT be a good idea to use on a bottle that should otherwise be decanted due to sediment).

ICE MAKER

The ice maker on this unit is completely contained in the left-hand door. This leaves the main compartment wide open and unobstructed by the ice maker, which is great. The ice maker itself if rather small, as is the bin - it's capacity is probably less than half that of my old side-by-side Kenmore 25 cu ft with the ice maker in the freezer. But the real problem is the dispenser. When you push a glass against the dispenser plate, an electric motor lowers a trap door in the dispenser chute and then the dispenser mechanism starts pushing ice down the chute. It works great until one of two inevitable things happen: ice cubes jam up in the chute (the jam can be freed by poking a finger up the ice chute - effective, but somehow feels wrong), or ice delivery stops because the ice in the bin is frozen together (which requires opening the left door of the fridge, opening the ice maker door, and breaking up the frozen ice mass in the bin or discarding it altogether). This is not an occasional problem, it happens almost always the first time it is used in the day.

I've had the factory-authorized service company out several times. The last time, they replaced the entire ice maker assembly (and the control panel as well, for some reason). No joy. This problem is not going away until some aspect of the current system is redesigned: either the ice chute is not wide enough, the chute door doesn't open far enough, the ice cubes are the wrong shape, the ice doesn't stay cold enough, or maybe even a combination of several things.

In all, I'd say the positives significantly outweigh the negatives, but on a fridge that costs three times what my previous one did, I guess I expected more. I'm still hoping that LG will take an interest in the ice maker problem and provide a field upgrade, but I'm not holding my breath.

product_title: LG WM2250CW3.5 Cu. Ft. White Stackable Front Load Washer - Energy Star
review_title: An incredible upgrade from a top-loader
review_text:
I LOVE this washing machine. Seriously. I finally dumped an 18-year-old noisy top-loader for this sleek new digital wonder and couldn't be happier. To address some of the complaints I've read on this model, first, you don't have to clean any filter daily or after every load. There IS a water pump filter on the lower left corner of the machine which is LG recommends you clean monthly, depending on use. I've checked the filter twice in a month and haven't seen any build up yet. Second, the machine does its best to balance an awkward load of heavy wet items in the spin cycle. If it starts to spin and is too off-balance, it will give up, try to readjust the items with some low-speed spins, and try again. The machine WILL vibrate some as it first starts spinning and the clothes are heavy with water. As the clothes start to lose their water, the spin will even out and become nearly vibration free. Regardless, it is MUCH quieter than my old top-loader.

I actually checked the noise level with a dB meter and compared them to what my old machine used to put out. My old "Lady Kenmore" top-loader would top-out at about 80 dBs, usually during the wash and spin cycles. The LG WM2250C tops-out at 50 dB, while injecting water into the wash drum, or during the first part of an awkwardly balanced spin cycle. As a reference, 50 dB is about the same noise level you'd get in a busy park or face-to-face conversation with someone. I also installed two "water hammer" arrestors on the water inlets for about $15 total from your local hardware store which "cushion" the water column in your pipes as the fast acting valves used in these types of clothes washers inject water into the wash drum. Without the water hammer arrestors, the valves switching on and off (they do so a dozen times during a wash cycle) might produce a loud thud in your water pipes, which is annoying and could cause damage to your plumbing. The water hammer arrestors reduced the noise level during the water injection another 5 dB, making the loudest part of this washing machine an off-balance spin cycle.

The clothes coming out of this washer are incredible. There is much less odor in the clothes from residual soap residue because the rinse cycle is much more efficient and the washer needs much less detergent than a top-loader to start with. Also, the high speed spin option gets the clothes so dry they need significantly less time in the dryer, increasing your utility savings. After drying, all my clothes and bedsheets and even towels feel softer and more supple, with less detergent smell. I am extremely happy with this. The washer also has a handy magnetic door holder which keeps the door semi-closed and out of the way while allowing air to move in and out, preventing mold or mildew growth.

The few drawbacks I can think of are a longer wash cycle (normal cycle with normal soil level takes about 45 minutes) and the fact that you can't open the door at all during the cycle - unless you unplug the washer. I found the silly electronic chimes that the washing machine plays at the beginning and end of the cycle to be annoying, but it was easy to permanently turn them off. Overall, anyone graduating from an old, noisy, inefficient top-loader to this sleek digital wonder will be extremely pleased.

product_title: LG WM2250CW3.5 Cu. Ft. White Stackable Front Load Washer - Energy Star
review_text:
Let me start off by saying this washer is really, really good at cleaning clothes. I've never had whites so white, or towels so fresh, as this thing provides. It's easy to use, and has a pretty big capacity drum, so a weeks worth of my laundry would fit in one load. Amazing.
However, there are a couple things about this washer that drive me absolutely insane. I'm not sure if it's just my particular machine, but here are a few issues I've had:
1) After a few months of use, the washer became very noisy. Not the pump or motor, but the suspension. It would creak and squeak at any change of motion (eg. when the drum switches rotational direction). I opened the washer up and found that the shock absorbers in this machine are completely plastic, and were the cause of the noise. LG had a tech come out and was unable to validate my concerns, even though I told him what I thought it was. He said the suspension wouldn't be a problem unless there was a vibration or balance problem. Which brings me to item #2.

2) This washer is terrible with vibration and balance. Even though it has the "true balance" system, it takes forever to balance loads, and sometimes when it spins you can hear the drum vibrating so badly that it shakes the floors (in a one-story home). Oh, and that causes the suspension and cabinet to be noisy as well, so not only do I have a vibration problem, but it squeaks, squeals, and creaks for the duration of the spin cycle sometimes. Keep in mind my washer has been completely level since day one (validated by LG tech) and this still happens. Replaced the shock absorbers, and while it's not as noisy, the balance problem remains.

3) The stainless steel drum, while corrosion resistant, is stupidly thin, and susceptible to dents/dings. I threw a dog collar and leash in the washer (something I've been able to do with family members FL washers of competing brands with no problems), and the drum got dinged up in many places. Noticeably dinged - it looks terrible. I mean, come on, it can't handle a dog leash and collar mixed with regular clothes?

4) After about a year of use, the motor started getting super loud on spin cycles. It's normally no quiet soul, but now it sounds like a giant vacuum with a high-pitched noise at speed. In addition, the pump has developed a relatively severe rattling sound at startup, which kind of worries me. I take perfect care of this machine, cleaning the pump filter religiously every 20 loads. It should not be doing this.

5) The steel top cabinet for the washer was formed incorrectly from the factory. It is visibly tweaked and is not flat on top. Not dents, but a result of the top being manufactured incorrectly or being the incorrect size.

6) The washer sometimes does not turn on. It takes unplugging and re-inserting the power cord to get it to respond if that happens. I hope it's not a sign of bigger issues with the control board.

As much as I like this washer, and as well as it washes clothes, I'm not going to be buying another one of this brand in the future. All these little things (the noises and electronic quirks) make the washer an annoyance to use. Other people seem to have had great luck with this machine, so I'm not sure if it's the fact that my machine is made in China (this model is manufactured in both South Korea and China) or what, but it definitely has been a less than stellar experience with this washer.

review_text:
I purchased this dishwasher from the Sears Outlet here locally. Wanted to have a local presence for this item. I read some reviews of the white/black models that they had and was overall fairly impressed. The installation went great, was super easy and the unit REALLY does a good job of heating up the water and washing.

The removable tray in the rack helps if you have lots of dish loads and its very convenient when you have lots of silverware/utensils to clean. The racks are slightly changeable in height, but its not significant and the default size is more than enough for all of our largest pots/pans. Cleaning quality is good on all our dishes, so far we've not had to pre-wash/soak anything. There are filters at the bottom of the unit, plastic catches and whatnot, that are easily removable from the bottom of the unit. These can be cleaned of any debris and food, etc. Seems to work well from what I've used so far. They recommend cleaning it at least once every 3 months, but there's a frequency information in the owner's manual.

As to the electronics, there are 3 wash cycles (Heated Wash, Normal Wash, 1 Hour Wash). There is a 4 hour delay on the unit so you can leave it to wash later in the evening when everyone is sleeping. Also there is a heated and unheated mode for drying. I've not experimented much myself with these modes, but they seem to be fairly cut and dry. Really like the options, and they are simple and self explanatory.

The unit is slightly loud, I'm guessing above 50db reaching towards 60. However, I think this is more an issue from the installation and the tile floors we have really echo in what is quite a small house. I think the unit is on par with anything else in this range. However with the wash quality as it is, it's hard to fault this thing in the slightest.

I think overall this is a fantastic washer, that has the necessary features, heats the water well, cleans well and has a decent amount of space to really capture all your messy dishes. What more can you ask for? Additionally, installation was a snap with everything being in place within a day (I was a little slow due to removing a cabinet for this). Seriously consider this dishwasher, its worth it for the pricetag.

My coffee mugs likewise do not fit in a logical manner but we keep trying to find the right combination of items to keep the upper rack from being a mess. We haven't found it yet.

The silverware tray is removable and that is about as useful as it gets. No matter what we do, we cannot find a way to put our silverware in to our satisfaction. The very narrow part that is clearly designed for knives is so wide that they end up falling over and can actually slip down onto the floor of the section. There are other sections, none of which is very large so it allows for dividing every type of utensil into its own space but the useless narrow part makes some of these sections even smaller than they already are limiting how many of each type can go in a single space.

It runs well, although it takes a long time to cycle through a complete wash. I like it but there are some very clear design flaws that simply do not make sense whatsoever.

product_title: LG WM3470HWATurboWash 4.0 Cu. Ft. White Stackable With Steam Cycle Front Load Washer - Energy Star
review_text:
We've only had this, and its matching dryer, for a couple of months, but so far we love it. Writing this review is almost difficult because it's so easy to use and works so well that I hardly think about it. We always have the TurboWash feature on, and loads are done so quickly that we are often surprised when we hear the end-of-cycle buzzer. There are plenty of cycles and options, so I never find myself wondering whether my clothes are being washed with the right settings. The wash capacity is great--sometimes we start sorting out items from a basket of laundry for the first load, only to realize that the entire basket fits, with room to spare.

The only downside, if it is one, is that water sometimes pools in the ring around the door. We had a front-loader before that had the same problem, so we just left the door open after each load to allow it to dry out. LG thought about this problem, and added a little magnetic plunger on the bottom of the door. It's a little hard to explain, but it basically makes it easy to prop the door open after each load, just enough to allow it to ventilate. From the outside, it's hard to tell it's even propped open, and it provides little enough resistance that you don't notice when you actually intend to close the door.

Speaking of the door, it's very sturdy and has a good, solid feel when opening and closing. This is especially notable because many of the other brands do not provide this feeling. We visited multiple stores, comparing many makes and models when we picked this one, and the door ultimately sold us. When opening or closing a Maytag or Whirlpool, for instance, you almost get the impression that you're breaking it, as it sounds and feels snapping a piece of plastic. The LG has a solid metal tongue, pushing into a metal latch that just feels right.

And with all this said, the LG cost us less than the others. By the time we were done comparing all our options, there was no other choice.

Every few loads, there are pools of water under the machine. There must be a major engineering flaw that allows suds to escape from the machine on a regular basis. A suds error code has not once come on to prevent this from occuring. At least if suds are able to leak out the air vent, the suds error code should kick in and shut the machine down before water ends up all over my laundry room floor. Laundry has become quite a pain, running and checking every load to check if I need to mop up. (I do ALOT of laundry for my large family, so I am doing a lot of running and mopping). I am very unhappy and unfortunately I bought the machine from a company that does not allow returns on a major appliance. review_title: Buy only if you love ironing. The end-of-cycle signal sounds like a child's ...
review_text:
Buy only if you love ironing. The end-of-cycle signal sounds like a child's toy and is so feeble, even on its loudest setting, that you can't hear it unless you're in the same room and there is no other noise. Furthermore, when the cycle is done, the dryer just stops, rather than continuing to tumble so that the clothes won't wrinkle. There is "wrinkle care" option that is supposed to keep the drum tumbling for a little while when the cycle is over, but it only turns the drum a quarter-turn once every minute, not enough to stop the wrinkles from setting in. Even worse, the "wrinkle-care" setting inexplicably disables the end-of-cycle signal completely. If you don't want to iron, you basically need to pull up a chair next to the dryer and sit there the whole time.

The dryer also has a special cycle to take the wrinkles out of a dry garment using steam. It shoots steam into the drum alright, but also plenty of liquid water along with it. So when the cycle is over, your shirt will be wrinkle-free but will have one sopping wet sleeve, for example.

It's pretty clear that LG doesn't have a clue about how laundry appliances are actually used. Avoid this brand.

review_title: A fix for the water leak.
review_text:
I’m responding to the review by Mumofmany as air vent was the leaking problem. Thank you Mumofmany!
I bought the same front load LG washer back in 2013. The leaking has been an intermittent problem since then.
I’ve had an LG service tech out to look who said not to fill the detergent higher than the normal fill line. We were sure to fill below that line and still had leaking issues that leaked on our 2nd story laundry room.
I bought the washer and dryer at Home Depot and they couldn’t help me either.
I literally saw water and foam coming out of the air vent in back of the washer toward the end of the wash cycle which is the rinse and spin cycle.

First, I removed the rubber gasket around the mushroom fitting in the air vent but that didn’t do the trick. I put the rubber gasket back.

I finally had enough of that and removed the vent cover on the back of the washer. I replaced air vent fitting with a 1-1/4” pvc connector. I needed to make the hole little bigger so I had a 1-1/4” knockout punch to do that.
I bought a 1-1/4” Electrical locknut to secure the connector. I connected the air vent hose to a threaded end of the 1-1/4” pvc plumbing connector to the washer. Then, I installed a reducer fitting to 3/4” and threaded a 3/4” hose connector to that and connected a 3/4” hose. I cut in a “Y” fitting to the 2” laundry drain pipe. At the “Y” fitting, I reduced the “Y” to 3/4” and threaded a 3/4” hose connector. Connected the hose and I haven’t had any more water leaking. All the vent water goes down my drain pipe now. I’m very satisfied with my solution!
I don’t think the original air vent was designed correctly. Thank you.

product_title: LG LFX28979SW27.6 Cu. Ft. White French Door Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_title: Love it so far, with a few caveats
review_text:
We got this fridge a couple of weeks ago, and love it so far. Pros and cons as follows:

Pros:
- Large capacity.
- Good (but not perfect) ergonomics.
- Available in white finish (many are stainless and/or decorator colors only these days we found).
- Bright LED lighting.
- Large lower drawer contains smaller nested upper sub-drawer for convenience items and the second ice-maker tray.
- Audible alarm if the door is left open too long.
- The doors and drawers open and close easily, and will almost always close the rest of the way if partially closed.

Cons:
- The housing for the LED lights sticks down significantly from the top of the interior of the fridge, making it an obstacle for taller items and needlessly limiting what you can put in the upper shelf. The light housing could easily be half as thick as it is now.
- The upper ice-maker in the door holds only a small inventory of cubes in its bin. The lower ice-maker makes a lot of cubes, but you have to open the drawer and get them manually, they aren't dispensed out of the door. Not the end of the world, but inconvenient when there is heavy ice utilization, such as when entertaining.
- The water and ice dispenser are in the left door, and if you open the right door they will not dispense. This just seems like a silly design oversight, since there's no reason (I can think of) to not dispense from the left door just because the right door is open. Again, not the end of the world, but noteworthy on a high-end unit.
- It's a bit difficult to arrange the door and interior shelves to allow for taller items. Some fridges have shelves that will partially retract for those times when you need to store taller things, then extend other times. This fridge doesn't have that. We knew that going in, but it's been a bit annoying trying to allow for the occasional wine bottle without arranging the shelves inefficiently for everyday use.
- The time for the door alarm is not configurable, and often goes off during grocery unloading, etc. It can be disabled completely, but we'd rather set it to a higher number of minutes instead of taking the risk of leaving it disabled, then leaving the fridge ajar without noticing it.

Note that the 'con' list is mostly nitpicks and not fatal flaws, and in some cases may not even been negatives for other buyers. However, for this kind of money we feel justified in doing a little whining about things that are not excruciatingly perfect in our estimation.

But, if we had to do it over again, we'd get the same model, hence the five stars.

product_title: LG WT5070CWWave 4.7 Cu. Ft. White Top Load Washer - Energy Star
review_text:
Okay, I tried posting this review on LG's website and it was rejected...go figure:

I had this machine installed a week ago, and I've had nothing but problems from day 1. I HATE IT AND WANT MY OLD MACHINE BACK! The salesman is convinced we got a faulty unit because he says this is his top seller and the best machine on the market. He is going to replace it without even sending a tech out. I get another one Friday. I don't have high hopes. But, this is the route to be taken before I can get something else.

Here is what I'm seeing (in no particular order):

1. Unbalanced loads - I've seen the drum knocking HARD on all four walls of the washer and the washer visibly moving across my concrete floor. The washer did not stop, I ran in and shut it off before it could error out. I'm not sure how long it was going to go before it stopped, but I didn't want to find out. I've had issues with this washing jeans and bedding.

2. Water HOG on bulky/bedding, towels and perm press cycles - my tub filled to the rim with water on each load. Loads tend to get unbalanced when the tub is full and the machines remedy for an unbalanced load is to fill the tub and try to balance again. This is rarely successful, especially on the bulky cycle, which tends to wad up the blanket into a ball. Also, pausing the cycle to add a garment seems to override the load size sensing feature and the tub fills to the max. I'm not 100% sure this is what is happening, but it is my best guess at this point. I think this is why the tub filled on the towels and perm press cycle, but I haven't had a chance to try those cycles again.

3. Bleach dispenser doesn't always empty - a cycle ended with it completely full of water. It remained full for another complete cycle and then emptied in the last 5 minutes of the spin cycle. Thankfully, I wasn't using bleach for the first load, or I would have had some ruined clothes.

4. 20 minute spin cycles - I watched a load on the normal cycle spin for 20 minutes??? Really?

5. Waveforce - what waveforce? I have yet to see the washer perform this function like what was shown in the store demo. Oh, and the waveforce functionality is only available on the normal and heavy duty cycles.

6. Clothes don't circulate in the washer. I have watched the same clothes sit on the top of the load the entire wash cycle and rub against the tub wall, completely dry. They do eventually get wet in the rinse cycle, but I don't see how this can be considered "clean". Saw this with a garment bag too. The garment bag remained on top the entire cycle, so only one side of the items was exposed to the friction that is supposed to clean the clothes.

7. The bulky/bedding cycle is in no way efficient, this cycle overrides the load size sensing feature and automatically fills the tub to maximum. I see a huge water bill in my future as I do wash a lot of bedding. The recommendation is to only wash one blanket at a time, so this will really use a lot of water. Also, this does a terrible job washing pillows. I followed the instructions in the manual and washed two queen sized pillows on the bulky cycle. The washer filled to the max and left my pillows floating on the top like a couple of marshmallows in hot chocolate, pressing on the glass lid. When the machine started to swish, I could see that since the pillows were floating so high, they were going to hit on the metal water tray and I was going to have either a ripped pillow, or broken machine. So, I stopped the machine and manually pressed out all the air from the pillows.

8. There is a sticker on the front warning NOT to wash any water-proof or water-resistant clothing in the washer even if the label says it is machine washable. I contacted LG about this and asked if this included things like jackets, snow pants, rain gear, and mattress pads (not the ones with the vinyl back). They essentially gave me a generic response saying the machine can trap bubbles of water during the spin cycle and this can cause serious damage to the washer...WHAT???? Now the salesmen says I should be able to wash that kind of stuff??? I have a feeling this has to do with the recall on the older model.

I don't see how there can be so many positive reviews on this machine. My fears are this machine is operating as designed.

product_title: LG WT5070CWWave 4.7 Cu. Ft. White Top Load Washer - Energy Star
review_title: The money I paid was good, but this washer is not.
review_text:
Washer tries to wash a full load of laundry in 3.5" of water. Clothes cannot move about in that little water so they come out with some areas clean and others not. Company says "Oh, it's high efficiency. That's the way it's supposed to work!" The "impeller" (its alternative to an agitator)severely twists and knots clothes, an extra step is needed to untie them prior to tossing washing in the dryer. The washer is placarded against washing any waterproof items, so no shower curtains, no GoreTex rain gear, no shoes, no rubber-backed carpets. If clothes aren't evenly distributed at the end of any cycle prior to spinning, the washer will repeatedly refill with water and agitate again trying to even the load (not so high efficiency). If it can't even the load, it will simply shut down and fail to finish the load. Nice surprise when you come in expecting your wash to be done and you have to start it over. I want my money back and I want a machine that does what it says it will do. I did due diligence and this machine was highly rated, but it is inherently defective. Don't buy it. As you read reviews for it, notice the length of time people have had it before they review. The good reviews are mostly from new owners, the bad ones from folks who've used it a while. It is not just this machine, most of the new HE machines are receiving similar feedback. I have had very few disappointments with a major purchase in my life, but this one is near the top. They took my money and gave me dirty clothes.

So... I was able to return this machine for a refund. I bought a simple Whirlpool machine that lets me set the load size, wash temp, and cycle strength manually. Both it and its companion dryer cost a little less than one-half the cost of this washer and its companion dryer. The Whirlpool should last long enough for the makers of HE machines to work out the bugs and in the meantime, I have $1,000 back.

review_title: So far so good, but what does this button do
review_text:
I have had this washer for 3 months and have not had the problems some others have experienced, and I hope I never do. It cleans well but is cryptic as to what some of the settings are. The user manual does not clearly describe many functions, but I was able to find most answers I had on the web. Here are some notes.

"Cold" setting will mix hot and cold to come to a temp around 65.

"Tap Cold" setting will use the tap temp without adjustments. If your water is very cold, then your detergent may not activate/work properly.

"Coldwash" performs some magic agitation that gets clothes as clean as a warm wash by using cold water. I guess you should use this when using the cold settings. The manual states this option eliminates the built in heater, but this is a mistake as it has no built in heater.

"Warm" can go to 120-130F degrees. Um, OK, to me this is hot. I am not sure about "Hot" then as my water heater is set to about 120F.

"Eco Warm" is around 90F.

The "Cotton" cycle uses very little water and this can be not so good for clothes that wrinkle easily. It seems like this is very aggressive and clean clothes very well however.

The "Towels" and "Perm Press" cycles seem to be good all around cycles ans use reasonable amounts of water.

The "Wool" is actually the delicate/handwash cycle.

If I figure out anymore about this washer or have any issues, I will update this post.

Now, another complaint I have is that the clothes come out extremely tangled...all of the time, thus very wrinkled. What does this mean for me...well...for every load of laundry that I wash I have to remember to go into my laundry room about 5-10 minutes after the load has started and push the 'water plus' button at least 2 times in order to feel comfortable that my family's clothing is actually getting washed.

Terrible product, I wish I could get my money back and find another brand.

product_title: LG WT5070CWWave 4.7 Cu. Ft. White Top Load Washer - Energy Star
review_text:
Probably the worst purchase we’ve made in a long time. We've had this washer for over two months, which is long enough to form an opinion and get to know it. The washer does a great job cleaning clothes and its washing load is larger than our dryer capacity; something we didn’t think about! It was top rated in Consumer Reports. However, as many others have complained on other sites, this washer goes out of balance very easily -- too easily! (Its physically level side-to-side, front-to-back. I checked it three times!) The worst part is there is no audible alarm to tell you the washer has stopped washing! The first you’ll know something went wrong is when you go to do second load and discover the first is not done.

The washer will try to rebalance several times. This entails filling the basket with water and agitating then flushing the water and trying again. This process can happen many times before it gives up completely. This totally defeats the water saving benefits for which one would buy a high efficiency washer!

It seems counter intuitive, but the larger the load the less the chance of going out of balance. The problem seems more common with smaller loads of somewhat dissimilar items. Let’s say you’re washing bed sheets and find a cotton towel you missed when washing all the towels. You add the bath towel to the sheets. That one cotton bath towel will hold more water than the permanent press sheets. When spin time comes, the washer will go out of balance. One pair of jeans with some permanent press casual shirts - forget it.

Even with similar items it sometimes has trouble. I got called out of town on short notice and needed to run a very small load of underwear and socks. Much to my dismay the washer got out of balance because the clothes didn’t evenly distribute around the tub. Frustrating.

I gave the lowest marks for value since a washer that doesn't run to completion 1 out of 10 washes is not meeting my needs and therefore of low value and a continuous irritation. I can’t recommend this washer.

review_title: NOT A GOOD WASHER - PROGRAMMING FLAWS
review_text: The washer was delivered on a Saturday and we did our first load of laundry within an hour.  On the very first load the washer filled to the top of the drum with water on the rinse cycle.  We didn't think this was normal so on our second load of wash an hour later the washer filled to the top of the drum on the wash cycle!!  We did a couple more loads of laundry the next few days and the machine was doing the same thing.  I called for service...the service tech came out and said "there was a loose wire" and that he fixed it.  I asked him to stick around for a bit to watch what happens but he was in a big hurry to leave.  We did two morre loads of wash that afternoon and the same thing was happening.  We sent the first unit back and had the exact model delivered about a week later (thinking we got the one-in-a-thousand lemon)...the second washer is doing the exact same thing...over-filling the tub which is using about 40% more water than our old "inefficient" washer.  Also, we noticed that if you use the PAUSE option to unlock the lid for whatever reason during the wash cycle (let's say you want to add something or you want to untangle the clothes) it messes up the water level sensor and the tub will fill all the way to the top.  Sometimes it fills up completely all on it's own (when washing sheets or towels) but using the PAUSE function during the wash cycle will guarantee a full tub of wasted water...and with the clothes floating around in 35 gallons of water in a washer with no agitator the clothes just...well...float around and don't get washed.  Most loads we are having to PAUSE the wash cycle so that we can hand-agitate the cloths just to make sure they are getting cleaned because they are floating on the top of a full drum of water.  The washer will be going back and we will be trying a different brand in a HE top-load before going back to the more efficient "low-efficiency" version.

review_title: I've only had the LG 5170HV for 1 wk
review_text:

This is a stupid concept since the huge laundry capacity is so that I don't have to do multiple loads of laundry. So, I will have to agree with some of the previous reviewers from the Amazon and the LG website. I would add at least 1/2 a pitcher of water to your laundry for half loads and at least 1 pitcher of water for full loads in order to trick the sensor if providing more water in the wash. So far, my laundry seems cleaner that my old Whirlpool Calypso laundry washer (which apparently was the worst washer ever made per every appliance technician that ever came to my house, so I don't know if this is a good comparison or not). I am also annoyed by the residual water that remains in the Liquid Bleach container after the wash. I have to wipe out the water after each load and throw the towel into my dryer.

I am seriously considering deducting the review down to 2 stars

product_title: LG WT5070CWWave 4.7 Cu. Ft. White Top Load Washer - Energy Star
review_text:
Purchased this at Home Depot about 2 years ago because I loved how it looked. I also liked the extra large capacity.

I use this machine to run 2-3 loads every week. Sometimes 2 load and sometimes 3, depending on my load. I haven't had any mold or odor problems and I haven't noticed any lack of water. If anything, I think it puts in more water than it should because the machine rotates the dry load to sense how big it is. Problem is that rotating the dry load makes the load higher in certain areas, which is why I think I get more water than needed.

As for how well the machine cleans, I don't have any complaints. My clothes come out clean.

There are 3 issues though:
(1) there is always water in the bleach reservoir, which is annoying. After reading a review, I think I know how to clean it out now.
(2) the agitating motion really twists your clothes toghether. It's a struggle getting the clothes out of the dryer because they are all tangled together. This means it's really heavy to take it out as one huge clump. Or, you have to really work at untangling items. I'm good about putting my stuff into washer bags so I haven't had any issues with knit items stretching out.
(3) Lint and other gunk collect along the top rim. I'm not sure how to clean that out because the tub clean cycle definitely doesn't do it.

review_title: Drying sensors are a joke, and clothes don't "toss" properly
review_text:
Now that I've finished bashing the matching washer, it's time to turn my attention to the faults of this dryer.

First of all, the so-called "sensor" is a joke. Don't even bother using them; just experiment with whatever Timed Dry setting does the job for you. When I first got the dryer I set it to Casual, which on my former Duet came out to 36 minutes. Worked fine for a load consisting of one queen sheet set (top and bottom sheets + two pillowcases). Casual setting for the same load in this dryer was "supposedly" dry in 20 minutes (What the..???!!?). Naturally everything was still wet.

Speaking of Timed Dry, this machine does NOT let you choose the amount of minutes that you want! There are only pre-sets, and the only useful (ha) ones are 25 mins and 40 mins. Hello???? My old Duet let me set the exact number of minutes, which usually ended up being 37 for 95% of the laundry that I do. But this machine basically forces to you run it for 40, even if your laundry would be perfectly dry in 35 or 37 minutes.

Ours is stacked on top of the matching washer. Although the pair is absolutely level, the clothes "congregate" at the front door and continually wipe against it during the entire dry cycle. What's up with that??? When I complained to Electrolux they told me that my unit must be perfectly level. Well, my 18" spirit level says that it is. Then they said that this happens with "oversized loads". A pair of queen sheets plus 2 pillowcases is "oversized" for this machine? Seriously?????

Honestly I don't know which is worse, this dryer or its matching washer. They are both a huge disappointment and annoyance. My only hope is that I will have sold this house before either of them breaks or the second-year warranty expires.

product_title: Frigidaire 24" Gallery Series Orbit Clean Built-in Dishwasher - Stainless Steel
review_text:
We purchased our house in 2009 with a brand new Frigidaire dishwasher included.

Last month, my husband and I woke up at 1 a.m. to our fire alarms going off and a strong smell of burning plastic. We quickly grabbed our toddler and baby, ran outside and called the fire department. Turns out our 4 year old Frigidaire dishwasher's electrical panel caught fire. Now we have $15,000 worth of damage to our house due to smoke damage, water damage, and a charred dishwasher area. I've attached the picture of the burned dishwasher. Home owner's only covers so much, and we're paying plenty out of pocket, eating fast food to try and keep things cheap, not to mention dealing with the inconvenience of not having a kitchen with two young children. (Ever tried scrubbing bottles and dishes in the bathroom tub?)

When we contacted Frigidaire, they gave us the run around and then basically told us without a receipt for the item, they would do nothing. It was installed by the contractor who sold us our house, so we don't have a receipt. Frigidaire also went on to tell us that they reuse serial numbers on their appliances, so there is no way to track their products. Upon doing some research online, fires with their products specifically dishwashers, are all too common (google `Frigidaire Fire'). But there is NO recall on this product!

I would seriously reconsider buying Frigidaire with this kind of product defect history, plus lack of customer service.

product_title: Frigidaire 24" Gallery Series Orbit Clean Built-in Dishwasher - Stainless Steel
review_text:
Seeing some of the other comments here, I'm a bit leery that eventually I may have to come back and revise my words here and add into the chorus of 'I really don't like this thing', but for now I'll keep myself in the cautiously optimistic range and say that wife 2.0 and I like this appliance.

Sadly the 10+ year old Kenmore dishwasher that it replaced had gotten to a point that it just stopped functioning as well as it should have. It worked, but not nearly well enough to rely upon, and with each use it seemed to be a total roll of the dice as to whether or not the dishes that were in it were clean. It had put in years of service and it did cost me a little along the way to replace the baskets (trays, whatever term you want to use) in it after some of the plastic coating on the wire frames within had worn off. Once that happened the wire frame started rusting and rust staining dishes that were in it so it was imperative to replace those trays. I don't remember for sure, but I'd guess that somewhere near half of the service life came after replacing those trays.

Enough about the old appliance, at least temporarily. On to the new...

Ooops, not so fast since I need to take a few minutes to compare the two and note some of the areas where I currently do have to say that I don't absolutely love this new device (and wife 2.0 doesn't absolutely love it either). The older Kenmore device that it replaced had trays that didn't include all of the ability to customize and arrange things that this appliance does. The top rack/tray/shelf in this appliance lets you flip up or down a few pieces that give you some options to arrange the dishes you want it to clean differently as necessary. On the one hand, that adds a lot of potential functionality but on the other hand it also tends to give users something less than the best of either configuration. It can be very handy if you can conform your usage to the configuration that this best offers, but if you can't make your usage fit the pattern this is aimed at, then you may find that the trays aren't nearly as convenient as you'd wish for.

The same applies to the bottom tray. There's a lot of ability to arrange things there, but if the arrangements that are offered don't work as well as you hope for then you may find that you wish for perhaps a different manufacturer's offering.

There is a lot to potentially like here, with a fairly deep cleaning area to work in. The lower tray offers a good bit of height above the tray, though it is not without issues since there's a rotating arm up there that needs to move freely to spread the water that is used for cleaning throughout the upper portion of the chamber. The upper tray sits a little lower than where the tray sat in the Kenmore that my family replaced. That means being able to put a few more items up there and that is always handy given the number of items that we wash that are either marked top rack safe, or recommended to not be washed in the dishwasher because of the potential high heat that comes into play.

Wife 2.0 and I both find ourselves happy with the 'clean' indicator light on the top front panel. We used to use a magnet that was placed on the front of the old dishwasher to show that the contents were either clean or dirty. With this new unit the 'clean' indicator lights up orange (amber?) and is clear enough to show other family members that the contents are clean and ready to put away (assuming no one opened the door once the cycle completed and the contents were clean. Once the door is opened the indicator goes away, so if someone does open the door they really need to put away the clean dishes and not just take out one glass or other item from within).

We (wife 2.0 and I) both find ourselves wishing that the controls were on the front of the panel and not the top of the front panel. While they hide under the counter, they are not as easy to make use of or see as they hide under our counter top. If the controls and indicators were on the front rather than on the top they'd be easier to see and easier to make use of.

The brushed stainless look on the front of this dishwasher is nice and does a good job of keeping away fingerprints. While other appliances in our home don't match (we have a mix of Black, White and now this Stainless looks) it blends well enough and is neutral enough to live with. (We were going to buy a model with the Black front but the appliance store we purchased it from was sold out of that model.)

The Sahara dry feature promises to dry the dishes that have been washed in some super impressive manner. Unfortunately it didn't seem to make a difference for the pockets of water that sit in the top of some glasses and mugs that we wash in the top tray.

We don't remove the utensil tray from our dishwasher (it stays in place, we just remove the cleaned utensils from within and put them away directly). Not pulling that tray in and out should help keep it from breaking into pieces and coming apart from such handling. I'm not sure that such fragileness doesn't deserve to be slammed a bit here, but at the same time I'm not sure that would be considered a typical usage case.

One other comment here - the old Kenmore had a nice layer of plastic covered insulation all around it. This Frigidaire included a thin layer of insulation (like what was between the plastic covering that was on the old Kenmore unit that it replaced) and that insulation wasn't covered with any plastic. My dad handled the installation of this unit for me (thanks again dad!) and when we were doing the install we wound up pulling off the covered insulation that was on the old dishwasher and placed it on top of the layer of insulation that was on this unit (cutting out an appropriate area in the top right rear of the unit). We both expected that in adding that extra insulation it would help make the unit's operation quieter. I suppose that means that any comments I can make on how quietly this unit operates aren't quite fair, though am not certain it would make that much difference -- assuming you install correctly and make certain you've set the feet appropriately and bolted the unit to the underside of your counters so it doesn't get a chance to vibrate (and in turn make more noise).

Again, this is admittedly a fairly early review (a few weeks in now) of this item. Our opinion might change over time and if so I'll certainly revisit and update accordingly so please, if you want to hate on this unit and you disagree with my review because you think I've just been lucky so far, hang in there and check back later.

product_title: LG WM3470HVATurboWash 4.0 Cu. Ft. Graphite Steel Stackable With Steam Cycle Front Load Washer - Energy Star
review_title: I think Amazon reviewers are being a little hard on this washer
review_text:
I bought this washer a few days ago. I absolutely LOVE it. It's quiet (except for some vibration and "jet engine" noises when the spin cycle is getting revved up, which is a common issue with ALL front loaders which spin 1200 RPM or faster) when washing and rinsing - I can literally hardly hear it at all, and it's right outside my bedroom door in the hallway.

I did a TON of research and settled on this washer as the best compromise of price (in my case on sale for $800), capacity, features, and "Brand Reliability." LG scores well with reliability, although there are some horror stories about some of their top-load washers (see the videos on the #1 ranked video web site - search "LG washer exploding".) Samsung and LG are about head-to-head in reliability and features, although in technology, Samsung might be a bit ahead - they have a washer now with an 8" touch screen which handles all functions and is wi-fi enabled. But it's also about $300-$500 more expensive than this LG WM3470HWA washer.

This is one of the top-rated models according to a well-known consumer testing agency. It also scores well on websites which sell a lot of appliances - you can search for the results yourself.

The washing experience is great. Tons of options when it comes to choosing what cycles to use for which clothes. The 4.0 cubic feet rating means it can wash a LOT of clothes in one load. It has the TurboWash feature which can get a load finished in about 25 minutes, if the soil level is not too bad and you are in a hurry. The 1200 RPM spin speed means many clothes come out virtually DRY. Polyester polo shirts? Practically dry. I washed a thin blanket and it went straight from the washer right onto my bed - just slightly damp.

You want to be cautious if you have this on a second-level-or-higher wooden floor, as the spin cycle can get noisy for people below. There are rubber "vibration reduction feet" you can buy on this website if you need them. On a lower-level concrete floor, you'll be fine.

One other common issue with this washer seems to be "water hammer" problems. With older plumbing, or higher water pressure than normal, this washer might cause your pipes to "bang" or make noises when it fires it's internal water jets during the wash cycle. This can be easily solved with $20 worth of "water hammer arrestors" which can be purchased at most hardware stores, and also here on Amazon. I bought myself a pair of them, since my apartment complex is "older" and I just wanted to make sure this problem did not bother either myself or the neighbors. So far, I have heard NO pipe sounds with the arrestors installed. The go on at the back of the washer, between the water hose and the washer. You can web search and find all this information.

I did buy a 5-yr extended warranty to cover myself in case of problems, but the warranty was very inexpensive. The motor is warrantied by LG for 10 years, the stainless steel tub for lifetime, and all else for 1 year.

I'm only giving this washer 4 stars because of the potential for water hammer noise and the fact that it might not be perfect for laundry rooms on the second floor or above which have wooden floors. As far as performance and how much I love it, 5 stars for sure !!!

product_title: LG WM3470HVATurboWash 4.0 Cu. Ft. Graphite Steel Stackable With Steam Cycle Front Load Washer - Energy Star
review_title: Good features, but it will leak eventually.
review_text:
You can read all of the good stuff I wrote when I first bought this below. After five years of light use it started leaking. If you call the LG support line the system will ask you if the unit is leaking (hint: a lot of these units must be leaking). They instruct you to run the tub-clean feature three times consecutively. If you buy an LG front load washer, run the tub clean once a month or it will build up debris that will eventually cause it to leak. Also, I have to replace my unit because it will never complete a towel spin- stops dead and reports unbalanced every time. Service people cannot determine why. My recommendation: Buy a Samsung instead.

One of the first things that impressed me was the load sensing feature. This is not your grandma's washer. The drum is direct drive, so it responds immediately to the electronic instructions it is given. You will see the load turn once clockwise, immediately reverse direction and turn counter-clockwise, and so on as it tests the weight of your load to help it determine how long to run and how much water to use.

This is very efficient- it is not like the old school laundrymat washers that fill with water. You will probably not see any water at all through the transparent door, but your clothes will get clean. I love the fact that you have so many choices. For example, if you want to use cold water your clothes will get just as clean as with warm or hot: the machine just runs it through more cycles.

I was very impressed when I pulled out my first load. I was prepared to heave out the heavy wet towels (as with my conventional top loader) only to discover they were practically dry!

Fairly quiet and smooth running. Just make sure you level the thing and take out the shipping bolts. Oh, and dry the seal with a towel after every use and leave the door open to let things dry out- I hear that front loaders are prone to mold growth if you don't.

product_title: Samsung RFG296HDRS 29 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel French Door Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_title: So far, so good, with minor complaints
review_text:
One week into ownership...

I went into a giant appliance retailer to purchase an advertised RFG297..., and was baited, and switched, to the RFG296 (because I'm not sure I can get that one, there is only one left.) The sales lady was extremely nice, and good at her craft, but did work me over a bit by showing me a unit with a Cool Pantry and skinny ice maker, then handing me literature that said the cool pantry wasn't included in mine (on page 3 in small print.)

All that said... I have a food thermometer in the fridge and it is keeping the temp steady as advertised on the digital display. Seals are good. Water is tasty. Workmanship seems solid. It's cold, quiet, and beautiful.

I have minor complaints that seem fixable by the design engineer's.
1. No egg tray? Come on Samsung, don't you realize Americans keep eggs in the fridge? And no place to put the carton except on the main shelves. The cartons don't fit in the doors. (Hence, provide me a 3x4 egg tray in the door instead.) Easy Fix. (I'll buy 3x4 egg trays when I can find ones under $20.00.)
2. LOUD when the ice falls into the ice maker. Not a big deal as the ice trays are rarely empty, but when they are, it's crashing loud. (The fridge itself is very quiet.)
3. You have to hold your cup under the water dispenser for an extra second or two after you shut it off or water drips out and onto the door. Easy to get used too, annoying that I have to.
4. This is more of a requested feature than a design flaw: Why didn't you design the water dispenser to allow for a pitcher to be left there to fill up unattended?
5. Edited: 6/28/12: The doors don't swing shut easily. I'm sure this can be improved. With many units I've owned, a little push and the door closed on its own. With this one, a little push won't cut it. Again, minor issue, but notable.

Overall, I really like the unit, and as you know, it looks great. I recommend it. I had to buy because I had my old one break down, so I wasn't as careful as I usually am, and therefore got surprised by the missing features. Pay attention to model #'s and features, and I believe you'll be happy with your purchase. I'll update this review if anything changes performance or quality wise.

review_title: Wish I had bought a different brand.
review_text:
There was not much info on this refrigerator when I bought it. Only the Samsung site had reviews and they were all good. Wished I had waited because the Samsung site obviously is not objective.

Things that I like.
The French door design makes it easy to get things in and out quickly.
Looks nice.
Keeps food fresh.
Large size.

Now the bad.

As mentioned on other sites the ice maker is loud. Loud enough that we can hear it from our bedroom with the door closed at night. Our bedroom is across the house 3 rooms away. At first it was alarming since we were not used to the noise but we have gotten used to it.

Ice maker comes unseated and won’t produce ice. Opening the door and reseating it solves this.

Ice get stuck in the shoot and backs up. You have to open the door and poke at the ice while depressing the ice lever to clear it. Invariably whatever glass you have is not large enough and the ice spills all over the floor.

Items fall behind the freezer trays and can hold the freezer door open. We found our freezer half thawed and have covered in ice when this happened. Apparently the door alarm does not work for the freezer door, or not when it is only slightly ajar.

Problems we have had with the fridge in the first year.

Two of the door bins have broken and fallen off – leaving our 29 cf fridge with 26 cf of usable space. The bottom trays from the right and left doors are broken and the upper right tray is showing signs of failing. The plastic that holds the bin on the door is thin and brittle. Cracks form which cause the shelf to fail. A gallon of milk and some salad dressing bottles prove enough weight to cause the failure. The french design of the fridge is such that the only place you can put milk and other taller items such as a pitcher of juice or 2 liter bottle of Coke is the door. The thin plastic of the bins in my opinion is a design flaw and will not hold the weight causing the bin fail and fall off the door. It is common enough that they sell replacement bins on Amazon.

The bar seal on the left door is malfunctioning. When you close the right door 1st the bar on the left door hits the right door when closing. At some point something will break entirely.

The right vegetable draw gets stuck open. It appears to get wedged due to the rollers getting out of the runner. You have to use a combination of force and wigging to get it closed.

When I pay top dollar which I'm willing to do - I expect quality.

I used to purchase all LG appliances and 55 tv. No more. I just bought a 32 cu/in fridge by Samsung and a Kitchenaid dishwasher. Two sales LG lost because they lost my faith in the quality of their product. We'll see how these companies play out.

Update: They tried to make me get a service call so that they could send a tech out to snap in a cap for me. I rejected the suggestion. Finally they referred me to a parts distributor. product_title: LG WT5070CWWave 4.7 Cu. Ft. White Top Load Washer - Energy Star
review_title: Only owned 1 month, but are very pleased so far.
review_text:
We bought this washer (and its matching dryer) to replace an 11-year old Kenmore (with center post agitator). Our immediate observations have been:
1) The machine is taller than the the one it replaced, by about a couple of inches.
2) It runs very quiet. Most of the time, we can't even tell it's running (except for the spin cycle, which does have a soft-whine that can be heard outside the laundry room).
3) The wash cycle is fascinating. We watched the entirety of the first load we ran through it, from start to finish, through the see-thru lid. It's amazing how well it cleans clothes with a minimal amount of water.
4) We washed the large comforter from our bed. I don't think that comforter has been this clean in years. Same is true for the electric blanket we washed next.
5) The cycle times are a little long. What took 39 minutes in the Kenmore, now takes a little over an hour in the LG.
6) The high-speed spin does a nice job of water extraction. It is also almost vibration-free, once it gets up to speed.
7) The end-of-cycle signal is a catchy tune (not a bell or buzzer), but it is not very loud (even on the loudest setting), so it's hard to hear if you are not within earshot. (The dryer also plays the exact same end-of-cycle tune; I'd have appreciated something different, so we can tell which one is shutting off.)
8) My wife believes that the laundry is coming out smelling fresher from this washer, as opposed to the old one. I haven't noticed this myself, but my wife is more sensitive to smells than I am.
The bottom line is that the clothes are coming out clean, with no damage that we can tell, while using a minimal amount of water. With the much larger tub, my wife does larger and fewer loads. After 1-month of usage, we have so far been very pleased, and have not regretted the purchase.

product_title: GE GTWN2800DWW 3.9 Cu. Ft. White Top Load Washer
review_title: Free at Last from the Throes of HE Machines - Clean Clothes and No More Stink
review_text:
This basic machine is sold by the big box retailers also with only a change of a couple of letters so they have some sense of exclusivity. For all practical purposes they are the same. GE offers one of the largest 3.9 cu ft conventional washers now available. The offer an HE model, an EnergyStar model with agitator, and they offer the nonEnergyStar conventional machine which actually has some more desirable features than the more expensive brethren.

This machine has been the beginning of a new and better life at our house.

We installed a new LOW efficiency clothes washer with as big a tub as we could find and all mechanical dials -no electronics - complete with manual temperature controls and with no electronic override on hot cycles which often tempers even HOT cycles to only 110 deg F washes. Our still-youthful, very large deluxe main brand HE washer has been relegated to basement storage -after draining all the stagnant water out of it which HE machines cling to in between washes..

You may read that this model is noisy - it is not. It is quieter than our old HE, which also played a symphony depending upon the stage of the cycle - very irritating. So unless you have your washing machine installed in the den right next to the TV, you may not even know it's working.

Does it fill the tub? Oh my - on LARGE load setting it fills to within a couple of inches of the top of tub-very satisfying.

Is hot water really HOT?-yep, just like it comes out of the heater. Likewise, warm is warm, cold is cold. How about that?

We had already decided we wanted a very large machine, so a 3.9 cu ft was the one for us. Over the last six months our family has bought three GE 3.9 cu ft machines. One was an EnergyStar rated for a rental property. No complaints from the tenant on that one. My son-in-law spoke highly of this nonEnergyStar model. He had replaced a deluxe HE machine which smelled and needed sanitizer regularly, whose pump broke down three times, and which yielded dry, unwashed clothes sometimes on the BIG wash cycle. The dirty little secret (not so secret anymore) about HE machines is that most of that large stainless steel drum goes basically unused on the wash cycle, therefore the big numbers for size are misleading....and they hold onto significant amounts of old rinse water in name of efficiency which sits and festers waiting for your next load of unmentionables Remember that the next time you wash clothes contaminated with lawn and garden chemicals, oil and gasoline or other work related substances.

So, I was leaning toward the GE 3.9 EnergyStar Model. Then, I met a lady at Lowe's who was trading hers back in after a few weeks. To Lowe's credit they were allowing her to do so. She said that the agitator only turns very little, that it would not fill very much with water and the water never reached a high temperature on HOT cycles.

Some research told me that she was right on two out of three counts. A GE spokesman wrote online in a reply to similar complaints that the EnergyStar machine tempers hot water to a maximum of 110 deg. F. One can culture bacteria at 110! GE also says that some of the same models may have a problem with the manual override not allowing it to fully fill the tub-hers must have had that problem. The third complaint about the agitator; I took a chance on that. It does turn slowly and quietly but it thoroughly agitates the clothes, if there is enough water.

Worried about durability? - Buy the extended warranty. The price is already very competitive at most places. No machine is going to last like the old 40 year-old Maytag your grandmother used..or is still using.

I now enjoy the pleasures of fresh smelling towels and sheets, and jeans that actually get clean....and the wife not complaining because the cycle is lasting too long, and about large loads coming out with dry unwashed spots, and having to use Afresh every couple of days to keep the machine from smelling like an open sewer. Sometimes progress is stepping back a bit and finding something that works.

product_title: GE APPLIANCES GTWN4250DWS, White
review_text:
I, like so many others, was horrified when my washer finally died after 22 years. After reading all the reviews, virtually no washer available got what I considered really good marks, even those that were well over a $1,000. Consumer reports is starting to get silly on this environmental stuff so they didn't even review washers with agitators. Geesh! Amazon is starting to be more and more reliable and is quoted quite often by reviewers with the advantage of being able to read each review. After balancing reviews, costs, and using a little common sense, I decided to go with this washer.

First thing everyone needs to understand, these new style washers do not fill with water. When the wash cycle starts, the wash basket spins slowly while water is sprayed onto the garments, thus soaking the garments. You need to place the detergent in the washer before the wash starts since there is not enough water to disperse the detergent in the same manner as the old washers. I think that is what is worrying so many people...it's just different. There are also separate dispensers for bleach and fabric softener; I have used the one for bleach and it worked beautifully.

Reading the manual is a must because it really lays out what exactly the washer does and it's easy to manipulate the settings to do what you'd like. There's even a setting for just blue jeans. Or, you can override everything and just do long washes filled with as much water as the machine allows...but I doubt the wash would come out any better. Also a big plus, most regular loads have come out really, really dry. It's almost bizarre of how rung out they are and it has cut down on drying time. It is also very quiet...at least compared to our old machine.

Of course, I have no idea how long this washer will last but it has really exceeded my expectations. I honestly am very surprised at how well this washer works. My only advice for reading reviews on these new washers is realize they use much, much less water and spin really fast so complaints that are the results of those two realities, like clothes being twisted due to the fast spin, you almost have to ignore.

This is a very, very good washer and the price makes this thing a best buy, in my opinion. I honestly couldn't be happier.

2.26.13: Just as a quick add-on as I've now had this washer for over 3 months. I live in the country and am on a well system for water. Due to our filtration system I can see how much water we use. We use so much less water now I am shocked. Now, for me, I'm not that big on the ecological stuff as I find most of it to be misleading. However, if you want to use less household water, this washer has made a significant difference. If water conservation is a concern, then this is a good washer for that reason alone.

review_title: The Worst Washing Machine Every Designed.
review_text:
My machine was purchased from Lowes on December 14, 2012. Lowes finally delivered it on January 4, 2013. The following comments are offered after using it for the past 2.5 months.

1. No matter what load setting is used on initial start, the machine will not put in more than a few inches of water. It requires either filling with a bucket or recycling through another start cycle. If you recycle by pushing the "Stop" knob, it will beat the clothes with inadequate water resulting in torn clothes. It is best to unplug the machine instead of pushing the "Stop" knob.

2. If using the hot water setting, the water comes in VERY slowly (water pressure is sufficient and screens are clear) and will not fill to the required setting. Again, either unplug it and fill with a bucket or cycle the timer through the start cycle about 3 times until sufficient water level is assured. The GE repairman came and stated the machine is designed to assure low hot water flow during filling. Someone should inform the designers of their incompetence.

3. Any time the machine is turned off, the agitator will whip the clothes violently. If no one is watching to assure an adequate water level is present, damage to clothes is highly likely. DON'T EVERY LEAVE THIS MACHINE UNATTENDED!

4. When water empties at the end of the wash cycle, it does not spin out the dirty water and soap. This results in retaining a large portion of the soap and dirty water. Therefore, the rinse cycle is immediately contaminated by an unnecessary amount of dirty water.

5. When the rinse cycle begins, the tub will only fill to about 20% of the required rinse water. If left unattended, this results in more clothes damaged due to agitation with very little water. The rinse cycle, again, requires either filling with a bucket or cycling the timer enough times to assure there is sufficient water in the machine.

6. Since the machine failed to spin out the dirty wash water, it is necessary to start another wash cycle in order to properly rinse the clothes. Without this step, the clothes remain dirty because they were never rinsed in clean water. This extra wash cycle requires the same monitoring and manual addition of extra water to prevent destruction of clothes.

The process of washing a load of clothes takes about 1.5 hours and the machine must be constantly monitored. If the above was the intent of the GE design team, they need to seek other employment.

A positive comment: The machine looks like a normal top-loading washer.
