review_title: Easy hack to fill it 3 holes down from the top with water:
review_text:
Got this machine a few days ago via the Thanksgiving promo.

So far it seems alright, will keep my fingers crossed. It is more quiet than the previous very basic GE washer that we had. Also, the clothes are spun to a drier state, thus faster drying time.

A lot of people don't like that it never fully fills with water. While on Super the water seems to come up about 5 holes down from the rim. Now, this is not all it can do. While playing with the settings, I've figured out how to fool it to get as much water as it can, which is about 3 holes down from the rim.

The sequence is the following:
1) start some wash with the water temperature you desire, and wait for it to fill the drum a bit
2) cancel the wash by holding the button for 3 seconds
3) start the wash again by pressing the button
4) if it starts draining, press the button for 3 seconds immediately, to cancel the draining
5) start the wash, it should start filling, and this time it will fill up to how much the sensor can take

I've had the water setting on "Large", and it filled the drum to 3 holes down from the top by doing this sequence which it should not have had done for "Large".

Consider this a manual override for "special" occasions. For having to do this silliness I've taken 1 star off.

review_text:
It breaks my heart to say this about a GE appliance, but let me count the ways I hate this machine. First of all, let me mention that my grandparents bought GE appliances. So did my parents (my dad worked for GE for years). I continued the tradition, and my daughter’s first appliances are, you guessed it, GE. I proudly own GE stock.

First of all, the washer doesn’t use enough water. The clothes come out a tangled mess, and I have actually had some that were torn to shreds. So now I am forced to sit by the washer and wait until it stops filling. Then I add enough additional water to make sure that the clothes can move freely and won’t be destroyed.

The PerfectTemp feature obviously doesn’t work as intended. The warm water is way too hot, the “colors” setting makes it too cold, and when I use the hot setting, it apparently thinks my water is too hot and adds cold water.

Oh, and don’t make a mistake and start a load on the wrong setting. Just this morning, I started a load of colors, and forgot I hadn’t changed the setting from my previous load, which was delicates. The washer was ¾ full, I changed the setting, and the washer drained. It drained. Along with all the detergent and additives I had put in. HUGE waste of money literally down the drain.

If you accidentally lift the lid before the washer stops spinning completely, the drum comes to a screeching halt. This can’t be good. There should either be a lock on the lid to prevent it from being lifted to soon, or some sort of indicator light to let me know when it’s safe to do so.

The additional settings are on dials instead of buttons, so it makes it difficult to choose the options I want for each load. I find myself choosing one or the other for things like a second spin, auto soak, extended spin or power rinse for when I use fabric softener.

I do like the fact that the agitation is much gentler than most machines I have owned, and that it has a way of redistributing the load to avoid the spin being off balance.

The dryer it comes with has a few flaws as well. Drying large items such as blankets, sheets and quilts is a chore, as you have to stop the dryer about every 10 minutes, remove the ball of tangled items, and then redistribute them (it) to make sure the inside of the “ball” gets dry. Otherwise it works fine, and if I use the auto dry setting, it drys normal loads completely the first time, on any temperature setting.

All in all, I would return this pair if I could. As it stands, I’m stuck with them for the next 10 years or so, which is about how long any major appliance lasts these days. I’m still a fan of GE appliances, but next time I’ll be much more choosy when I shop for a washer and dryer.

product_title: GE APPLIANCES GTWN4250DWS, White
review_text:
UPDATE - FINAL REVIEW

Here is my actual review of this washer. I did go out the next day after writing the "pre-review" and bought the washer and matching dryer. Writing the pre-review convinced me to go ahead and get the set.

First, I must amend my comments about this not being a HE (High Efficiency) washer. It is a HE washer but lacks the locking lid so it can't be called HE.

The locking lid is a necessary safety feature because the tub spins at 700 rpm during the spin cycle which is really fast. The lid on HE washers locks until the spinning has stopped to avoid injury if someone were to reach in while the tub is still spinning. It would take off a finger, a hand or even an arm. It's dangerous. I'm giving it a 5 star rating with the understanding that it can be a dangerous machine. Believe me, I don't even think about opening the lid during the spin cycle. I don't even open it during the wash cycle. (Opening the lid during the wash cycle aborts the wash cycle, empties the water from the tub and you have to start all over.)

Also be sure that you use only HE detergent and use it sparingly. This washer doesn't need the usual amount of detergent.

I expected the controls and settings to be baffling at first and they were. Eventually I got the hang of them and I hardly think about the settings now. It's a moderately steep learning curve. The learning isn't helped by a poorly written instruction booklet. It's basically a generic set of instructions that cover about half a dozen models similar to this one. I've read them so often that they are dog-eared.

The controls give you a lot of choices and flexibility. What was surprising was the number of settings for water temp. There is "cold only", then you have about 2 or 3 settings of slightly warmer water, then you have warm and hot. You have many settings for wash cycles but eventually you'll mainly use the Color, White and PermaPress settings. It also has LEDs on the control panel that light up to show which cycle the washer is in. Nice touch.

The clothes are very clean and nearly dry when they come out of the washer. I can wash a very small load, I've even washed a single item on occasion. On the other end of the scale, I tried washing a comforter (single bed) and it came out beautifully with no protests from the washer. I'm doing more laundry than before and my water bill is actually a bit smaller. This really does save water.

I think the most important issue is to be sure the washer is perfectly level. My installers did a good job and I later re-balanced the washer. The high speed of the spin cycle demands that the washer be very level. If it's out of level, it will make loud noises and "walk" itself across your floor.

I've used the washer heavily in the time I've owned it and it has operated beautifully. Just beware of opening the lid while the tub is spinning. Bottom line is that this is a wonderful machine. It cleans well. You add soap and softener first, then add clothes, set the controls and push Start. Then you walk away for an hour or so and the clothes are ready for drying. Washing is almost fun.

I've not said much about the dryer. It's more conventional and does a fine job of drying quickly. Just be sure to clean the lint filter after each use. Cleaning the filter allows the dryer to dry clothes quickly and with the least amount of power. It also prevents lint buildup in the exhaust hose, which causes fires.

Thank you, Ed

====================================================

PRE-REVIEW

I'm seriously thinking about buying this machine but haven't actually purchased it yet. This is a "pre-review", not one of a washer that I own. At least I don't own it yet.

I've noted in many of the reviews that people think this is an HE (High Efficiency) washer. IT IS NOT an HE washer.
It is an Energy Star rated machine. Energy Star means that it meets certain standards to reduce energy and water used to operate the machine.

An HE washer takes energy efficiency to a much higher level. HE is much more automated, takes longer to cycle, makes noises not usually associated with washers and uses a different method of washing and cycling than a traditional machine.

Neither is it this washer the washing machine of just a few years ago. True, it does use less water. Using less water is one of the requirements of attaining an Energy Star rating. If this makes sense, then you'll see that there is a big difference in Energy Star rating and an HE rating.

Interestingly, the reviews of this model on Amazon are largely negative. In comparison, the reviews on Home Depot are just the opposite. They are mostly positive. I take both the bad and the good with a grain of salt. It's telling to me that there are 578 reviews on the Home Depot site with an overall rating of 4.0 stars of a possible 5.0 stars. There must be something good about a washer where almost 600 people agree that it's a fine washer.

I suspect that a lot of the negative reviews were related to not fully understanding how the machine operates. It has electronic controls which give you a very wide choice of settings and all of these choices can also be confusing. Also, since it has to conserve water in order to get the Energy Star rating, it "looks like" there is not enough water in the tub to wash clothes properly.

Again, I read in a number of the positive responses that the clothes came out very clean and the users were happy with the results.

As I said, I'm seriously thinking about getting this machine. One of the local dealers is offering it for under $500.00, delivered and installed through 3/26/14. This the best price I've found. It's a machine with many good selling points. For me, the stainless steel tub and the generous 3.9 cubic feet of capacity are pluses. The Energy Star rating is another big plus for me. In addition, it features lots of cycles and variations on the basic cycles and I like the 700 RPM spin speed (drier clothes out of the washer). Another selling point for me is that the cycle times are substantially less than an HE rated washer. I also like that I can customize the washer to wash just as I want it to. The bottom line is that it seems to give a lot of "bang for the buck". It's a good value at this price.

I rated the washer with only four stars because I don't yet own it and have had no experience with it. I'll return with a followup review after a good trial of how it works. I may just earn a 5 Star rating.

Thank you.

review_title: Computer programming flaw: You have to have unusually high water pressure for it to fill up
review_text:
I bought a house with this washing machine in it. It was filling with a thimbleful of water no matter what setting I put it on. I had to do tiny loads. I was freaking out over this lemon and thinking that with the "high efficiency" it was designed to not be able to wash.

Then, reading these reviews, I see half and half that it fills up great versus that it doesn't fill and uses a thimbleful of water.

I went through troubleshooting it as if it were broken. And, I got it to fill with water. Anyone who was told by a repairman or company employee that this won't fill up and that that is how high efficiency machines work had a dud repairman or General Electric employee lie to you. This washer is supposed to fill. However, it has a computer programming oddity to where you need to have high water pressure for this to happen. It allots a certain amount of time for filling up, and if the washer isn't full, the washing machine just turns water off and goes into the wash cycle without ever waiting to fill up completely. You can see in reviews, some people say it fills up great. Some people say it won't fill. That's probably a difference in their water pressure.

Anyway, here's how I fixed mine.

Mine was filling up to the bottom few dots along the side. It would fill with maybe 3 or 4 inches of water in the bottom no matter what setting I put it on.

I first started from the view that maybe the pressure sensor had gunk or build up in it, since I got the washing machine about 6 years old. The pressure sensor is something in every washing machine that has a tube and water goes up the tube and raises air pressure in a bubble at the top of the tube and when the pressure is too high, the washer knows it is full and stops filling with water. You never want to take that thing apart, because if you mess it up, then your washer can not know when it's full and can overflow. What I did is ran a load with a gallon of vinegar added. Vinegar dissolves hard water deposits. Mid load, I lifted the lid and left it open to leave the vinegar water sitting in the machine. Next I ran a load of plain water. Next I ran a load with a half gallon of bleach added. Bleach dissolves cotton and human hair. So, I figure between the two of those, that will dissolve most gunk. The plain water in between is because bleach and vinegar together will make chlorine gas, so you want to clear all the vinegar before running bleach through and vice versa. After I did that, the washer would fill up to about half way on hot water wash, but still just a few inches on cold water wash. (Both vinegar and bleach will damage rubbers, so this is not something you would want to do on a maintenance schedule. Once in a while is no big deal, but doing this regularly would be a bad idea.)

I disconnected the hoses, and tested running water through them by connecting them to the garden hose spigot outside to make sure water was flowing. The hot water hose was to where it would shoot water across the yard. The cold water hose was more like a faucet tap, so flowing freely but not spraying. This made me think that there was hard water build up inside the hoses. (You want to replace your washer hoses every 5 years anyway, to prevent risk of them popping and flooding your house.)

I got new hoses. After connecting the new hoses, the washer fills up about 3/4 of the way full if I do "Super" wash. That's the most water I can get the machine to fill with with my water pressure, and the water pressure is totally fine in the house. I know for sure that the washer is supposed to fill up to two dots from the top of the drum when it's on "Super" wash, because if I start it going, then spray a garden hose in along with the washer fill, the washer will cut off water when it gets to two dots from the top.

What is going on with this washer is this: The pressure sensor (measures how much water is in the machine) is only talking to the washer to tell the washer to turn water off at the end of the fill. The washer has some kind of timed cycle where step 1 is a combined fill and soak. If filling up takes longer than the preprogrammed allotted time for fill and soak, the washer doesn't wait until it's full. Instead, it just moves into a wash cycle with too little water. So, if you have any kind of lower pressure water at going into the washer, then it won't fill up in time. You have to increase the water flow into the washer. The washer will recognize when it's full, and cut water off to not overflow, but if the washer is mostly empty, it doesn't care and just goes "time's up, time to go to the wash cycle". For me, connecting new hoses worked to get a satisfactory wash, but I don't have enough water pressure in my house to actually fill it. (And like I said, water pressure is not at all a problem in my house.) My only option would be to use an actual garden hose (with a bigger hole in the middle) as a fill hose, and that would be risky in case of rupture since washer hook up hoses are intended to hold lots of pressure for years, but a garden hose no one cares if it pops and they aren't designed to hold pressure for years and years. My washer is in a garage where all my stuff is up on shelves with feet, so flood is not a big deal, but in a room in a house, I would have no way to get more water pressure, and even in the garage I really can't risk it. It's a really bad design flaw with the washer - that thing were it starts the cycle after a set amount of time whether or not it's full with water. Like I said, I don't have any water pressure problems, and I can't get it to fill to where it is supposed to for a "super" wash. By increasing water pressure the best I could, I wash able to get a big improvement. I hope that helps anyone wrestling with this lemon. It's not as bad as a high efficiency machine that simple won't fill, but if you don't have super high water pressure, it may as well be.

By the way, when it comes to high efficiency machines and water use, the EPA had new regulations kick in for personal use machines in both 2016 and 2018 to where now they really can't use water. This machine couldn't be sold after 2016. This machine, the GTWN4250DWS, is the "good old days". It's not a good machine, but you can't buy a new one that is better. You have to get used. The EPA allows about 1 and 1/2 times as much water to be used for commercial machines, and if I hadn't been able to get this working, I would have bought a Maytag Commercial or a Speed Queen TC5000 (reversed the changes in 2018 where Speed Queen tried to do a fast wash cycle and the machines from 2018 just weren't cleaning). If you want clean, you have to repair the older machines like this one, or else you have to get a commercial grade replacement (which the government allows to use more water). Washing machines got regulated to where even though this GE washer is a lemon for computer programming and not especially well made, it's better for cleaning than anything you can buy new for under $900.

Honestly, the house this came with - the family that lived here had 4 kids, and I have 4 kids, and this was made in 2012 and now it's 2020, and it seems to work just as it did the day it was new (ie. badly unless you have super high water pressure). I think it probably was an OK machine, but I wish that GE would have fixed the computer programming to where it would check and make sure it was full before starting the cycle, and that GE employees had not just lied to people and told them that "this is how high efficiency machines work" when the bad computer programming caused problems.

product_title: LG WM3070HRATurboWash 3.7 Cu. Ft. Wild Cherry Red Stackable With Steam Cycle Front Load Washer - Energy Star
review_title: Get ready to love doing the laundry - REALLY!
review_text:
Ok, so I didn't think I'd be so thrilled that I'd actually be writing a review for a washer, but, nonetheless, here it is! This is the first front load washer I've owned and I can say that I will never go back to a top load again. The short list consisted of this washer and a Samsung. The Samsung I was looking at had PowerFoam as a feature, but was a little over $700 more than the LG. To be fair, that washer was a 4.5 cu. ft. size as compared to the 3.7 cu. ft. size for the LG. I'm sure the Samsung washer would have been a great washer; I liked the idea of PowerFoam. However, I'm a family of three and so the 4.5 cu. ft. load capacity wasn't really something we needed. 3.7 is more than large enough for my family's needs. Also, as cool as PowerFoam sounded, I liked the idea of the Allergiene cycle that uses steam to remove 95% of common household allergens. My wife really suffers with her allergies and I really liked the fact that this wash cycle could help mitigate some of her suffering. The SpeedWash, TurboWash and ColdWash features were also big selling points. Couple that with the Direct Drive motor (as opposed to pulleys) for the movement of the drum and I was satisfied that I was getting a washing machine that would more than satisfy my needs. So in considering this machine and the Samsung, I very quickly realized that while both machines were quite good, I would be almost able to purchase both the LG washer and dryer for the price of just the one Samsung washer. As a side note, the smaller capacity Samsung washer (the one that would be more comparable to the LG I purchased) did NOT come with the PowerFoam option, so in a more apples to apples comparison, I feel the LG washer outshines it's similarly equipped/sized Samsung competitor.
With regards to performance, this machine is the best I've ever owned. I had high expectations, but I was also somewhat skeptical as to what a front load washer would really be like. I was sure it would wash clothes and that it would do a good job, but would it really be a noticeable improvement over my old top loader? YES! If you've been on the fence, time to move. I do not regret this purchase at all.
I've had the LG for about a week now and I've used it daily. First, the machine is extremely quiet during operation. Our laundry room is located in an open nook just off of the kitchen. There is no door to close to dampen the noise. Prior to this, we'd always have to adjust the TV volume accordingly when washing clothes. The only real intrusion I've noticed is during the initiation of the spin cycle. During the actual washing cycle, I don't even hear the machine. It doesn't intrude in conversation or TV viewing. It's amazingly quiet. Don't get me wrong, you can hear it if you choose to attend to the noise, but it becomes so innocuous in the background that it's easy to forget the machine is even running. Of course, once you hear it's end of cycle signal, you remember you had clothes running! Once the washer is spinning, it returns to very quiet operation, too. I just notice the difference when it moves from the wash cycle to the spin. And that's really if I'm even listening for it.
Since I'm speaking of the spin cycle, this washer does not walk all across the laundry room floor either. It's very stable and has not even vibrated the floor, house, windows, etc. even once - not even a hint of vibration. Given that front load washers can spin at some pretty impressive speeds, I was surprised by this. The TrueBalance system on this machine is definitely impressive and effective!
With regards to performance, I was thrilled at the difference between washing in the top loader and this LG. This LG replaced a Maytag that, at the time of purchase, was a top of the line washer. I nicknamed the Maytag the Washing Dead because it refused to die. It was 16 years old and still going strong. It was undoubtedly a relic. The agitator was a pain when it came to washing comforters. I can't begin to count the times that a small load would get out of balance and the machine would just stop until I manually balanced the load. Sometimes it would get out of balance and quit again within 5 minutes. This was annoying, but if I was home it wasn't a big deal. This would be a problem when I'd set clothes to wash when we were leaving. It was never a good feeling to come home only to find that the machine hadn't finished the job. Say goodbye to that problem. This machine completes the job every time.
After several loads of clothes, I can say that my clothes feel cleaner. I could tell the difference with the first load of clothes I washed. However, because I didn't want to chalk it up just being excited about a new appliance, I waited several days to make a judgment. I have no doubt that our clothes are cleaner with this machine than they have ever been. Things just "feel" cleaner and on a deeper level, too. Another plus is that my clothes are not being beaten up by the agitator any longer. That means that clothes will look newer for a longer period of time. A front loader is just going to prolong the life of any garments washed in it. Another thing that amazed me about this washer was how dry clothes came out of the washer. I'm used to jeans dripping wet coming out of the old Maytag. That's a thing of the past. This machine spins as much water out of these clothes as possible and with such effectiveness that it reduces the amount of time (and therefore energy) needed to dry the clothes. That's a win-win scenario in my book!
There are a multitude of programs and cycles available in this washer and I don't believe any of them are gratuitous. In a little over one week, I've found that I've used a great deal of them. About the only consideration I gave with my other washer was hot, warm or cold and then moving the slider to correct position for the size load of clothes I was washing. That's about it. With this machine, I can wash small loads or bulky loads. I washed two full sized comforters at the same time and still had room to spare. I've loved the ColdWash cycle and have found it to be just as effective as the warm wash cycle. I've used the Allergiene cycle and my wife commented that her sheets, pillowcases, and comforter never felt or smelled better. While there are a myriad of options available for washing, I have not found any to be gimmicky or unnecessary. I can see a use for all and have already used most.
I purchased the matching pedestal to go with this unit and I highly recommend it. It brings the machine to eye level and eliminates stooping down to load or unload the machine.
All in all, I'd buy this machine over again in a heartbeat! It's been one of the best appliance purchases I've made in years! The dryer that goes with this washer is also amazing and I have reviewed that as well. My wife and I both love the Wild Cherry color. It sounds awkward to refer to such a mundane appliance as sexy, but nonetheless the red is just that. It pops nicely against our mocha paint in the laundry/kitchen area. So not only is this unit visually stunning (again - hard to believe I'm talking about a washing machine and not an exotic car with such jargon!), but also incredibly efficient and effective. While the options are numerous, a quick read of the instructions manual or PDF online will have you up and running in no time. The automatic dispensing of HE detergent (liquid or powder, but I recommend liquid), fabric softener, pre-wash, and bleach takes all the guess work out of cleaning your clothes. I've found the pre-wash to be very effective at helping clean some of my red clay soiled jeans. I also got some dark cherry juice from cherries on a white t-shirt out without a trace. I didn't get a stain on the shirt intentionally, but I figured this would be a good litmus test for how efficaciously the washer cleaned clothes. It worked like a champ!
When they first released appliances other than TVs, I was skeptical of Samsung and LG. I once remarked, I don't want my refrigerator made by people who specialize in TVs. I can honestly say, I have been proven wrong. I would have no qualms buying a refrigerator or washer from either company. The highest compliment I can give LG is that they completely exceeded every expectation I had for this machine. Nothing feels cheap at all about this machine. It is truly a fantastic washer and, for the first time ever, everybody in the house wants to do the laundry!

product_title: LG WM2650HRASteamWasher 3.6 Cu. Ft. Wild Cherry Red Stackable With Steam Cycle Front Load Washer - Energy Star
review_text:
We bought the LG Front Load two years ago - my husband's impulsive Black Friday purchase. Two years into it, here is what I can say:

1) The machine starts out by doing a test spin to determine the volume of laundry, and adjusts the water supply accordingly. However, there have been times when that machine was FULL, and it still showed only two bars for fullness (instead of three). Consequently, I have washed an entire load of clothing, only to take it out and discover that the clothing in the middle of the load was BONE DRY.

2) It leaks. It leaks little tiny river trails from the bottom of the lid. This can be annoying.

3) The spin cycle on it is RIDICULOUSLY unbalanced. We leveled the unit per the instructions, our floor is level, etc., but when the spin cycle kicks in, the entire house shakes. I've learned not to do laundry when we have people over, otherwise, our guests get scared thinking there is an earthquake.

4) Speaking of spin cycles - sometimes, for no apparent reason, it just doesn't drain all of the water. I guess that is why they have a separate "spin" you can put the setting on. The manufacturers must have known this happens.

5) This is the only washing machine I have ever owned that requires regular maintenance to keep it from getting gross. In no time at all, the inside rubber gasket rim gets full of gross crud, as does the inside of the clear lid. On a traditional top loader, I would have to clean the inside lid maybe once a year. On this thing, it really needs to be cleaned once a week or more.

6) Speaking of gross - don't make the mistake of leaving the lid closed when not in use. You will come home to a stink factory. This is particularly annoying, if, like me, you like your laundry room buttoned up and tidy. But nope, gotta keep that big old door hanging open. This leads me to wonder, if a simple closed door can breed so many organisms that the entire laundry room will smell, just how sanitary is the entire unit? You know, a unit designed to make things clean?

7) Speaking of clean - clothes come out OK, but not stellar. I was expecting stellar from all of the advertising LG had been doing on these machines. The only way for me to get clothes as clean as I prefer is to do a prewash, a stain cycle, and an extra rinse.

8) The large capacity is misleading. At full capacity, the clothes do not come out clean at all. At half capacity, the clothes come out okay.

9) Additional annoyances: The writing on the buttons started to flake off after about 6 months. Really, LG? Really? The cherry red coating on the plastic components (like the soap dispenser drawer) started melting off after about 6 months also, meaning each time I open that little drawer to pour in the laundry soap, my fingers get coated in red melted goo. Note: this drawer needs to be cleaned out regularly, too!

10) Positives: It looks nice with the red. The accompanying dryer is AWESOME and FAST.

11) Bottom Line: After noticing that my drain pan was full of water this morning, I just couldn't take it anymore. We are moving this set into the garage and buying a Kenmore or Maytag top loader set.

product_title: GE GFWH1200DWW 3.6 Cu. Ft. White Stackable Front Load Washer - Energy Star
review_text:
We wanted a front-loading washer because we like the performance of the front-loader in our previous house, and we like the feeling of using less water and getting cleaner clothes in the bargain.

First Impressions

I am impressed! This washing machine has a lot of button and lights and at first glance one can be intimidated by the controls. However, the "GE GFWH1200DWW" makes most of the selections for you depending on what setting you chose via the rotary dial which includes the following selection: Whites, Colors, Sanitize, Delicates, Speed Wash, Drain + Spin, and Basket Clean. There are push button controls for "Soil, Spin and Temp" with a wide range of selection, however these are made for you automatically depending on your rotary dial choice.

You are free to change them of course, but I have found that letting the washer chose the setting for me tends to work best. So controls that once looked intimidating aren't and washing a load is just a dial setting away.

GE recommends using only High Efficiency (HE) detergent with the GE GFWH1200DWW and we settled on Tide because it tends to get our cloths cleaner. The detergent dispenser is situated on the left hand side of the washer and has a compartment for detergent, fabric softener, and bleach. The compartment is removable and good thing since the fabric softener compartment tends to fill with water after each wash and needs to be emptied.

The GE GFWH1200DWW is fairly quite though you know when the door is being locked or unlocked. Speaking of which, the washer can be paused during the wash cycle to permit to adding of additional cloths; the start button is actually a Start/Pause button.

Conclusion

With its 3.6 cu. Ft. capacity, the GE GFWH1200DWW can and does swallow a lot of cloths. The average wash cycle last 1:25. We opted for the optional pedestal/ storage unit and I'm glad we did because it raises the washer off the floor to just the right height where we do not have to bend over to add and retrieve clothing.

Overall I (we) are quite pleased with the "GE GFWH1200DWW Front Load Washer"; it does what it is supposed to do with minimum fuss and at the end of the wash cycle and alarm will sound at 1 minute intervals until you come an retrieve your wash. Nice touch GE. And while I would have preferred another color, blue, or red perhaps, the white is not unattractive, and it gets the job done.

If you are looking for a sub-$1000.00 front loading washer ($839.00 at Amazon.com believe it or not; they sell everything!), the GE GFWH1200DWW should be on your list.

review_text: I am so disappointed with this product. I can't believe it is a GE. I had to replace our wonderful Asko after many years of good service. Because our counters are 1/2" too low for standard height dishwashers and we live in a remote area, I had very limited choices available that I could buy online and I couldn't actually see it before I bought it. The racks, rollers, utensil baskets and spray arms are made of flimsy plastic. Although the unit is the same size as the Asko, the racks are only 17" deep (instead of 19"). The top one only pulls out part way, reducing capacity and making it hard to load and unload. I don't know what "fully integrated" means. It does NOT mean quiet. After rattling and roaring on for nearly 2 hours on the first load, the wretched thing created a further commotion by flashing a whole string of green lights and making intermittent beeping sounds to celebrate the fact that it had completed its cycle.  This continued until I got up and manually turned it off. I'm glad it was happy, because I just wanted to cry. As for Square Trade, the jury is out. They promised "same day" shipping on July 19. It shipped on July 28 and finally arrived on August 4. The 3-year Square Trade Large Appliance Protection policy has yet to arrive. Somehow, I suspect I'm going to need it, although I might be happier just letting the thing die an early death. I would wait to write this review until I had more to report, but I've given myself only 48 hours to think about how annoying this dishwasher is before I pretend it just doesn't exist.

product_title: LG LDF7551BB 24" Black Fully Integrated Dishwasher - Energy Star
review_text:
We bought this from Best Buy and had it professionally installed. It has been up and running for a few weeks now. After the first run I was disappointed with the cleanliness of the dishes and the effectiveness of the drying cycle. However, after trying the "powerscrub" and "extra dry" features, I was very pleased with the outcome on both counts. Just be aware that with these features, a run will take about 3.5 hours. The washer is VERY quiet. During the first run it made a very pitched whine during the whole cycle, and I was like "I can't live with that!" However, since the first cycle it has not made such a sound.
The washer dries the dishes without a heating element. Instead it pulls moisture out of the unit with a fan. It REQUIRES a drying aid, like JetDry, or something of the sort for adequate drying of the dishes, and the instruction manual informs you of this. The downside is you have to buy a drying aid. The upside is you can put plastics on the bottom rack without fear of the plastics melting or deforming. Another upside is that the dishes are not hot to the touch when the cycle is done, so you may empty the washer immediately following the cycle. In addition, you get energy efficient drying and you don't heat up your kitchen with steam pouring out of the washer like you do with a heated dry washer.
The filter in the bottom of the machine is very easy to access and very easy to clean.
I like that the buttons are like touch screen buttons and will not wear out after years of pressing.

product_title: LG LDF7551ST 24" Stainless Steel Fully Integrated Dishwasher - Energy Star
review_text:
I bought this dishwasher from Home Depot and the drain pump failed within 2 months. No big deal, stuff happens. It is a small part, easily replaced. I called LG and they have said they do not have a service technician in my area (Lexington, KY). They said it would take 3-5 days to identify a company that could they could contract the work out to. So, basically, if you don't live in a town with a certified LG repair technician, plan on waiting a week for any repairs to be done.

I told them to just send me the part, I'd do it myself. They refuse to do that as it would void my warranty.

I decided to just get the part myself. I went to an appliance parts store who said that LG parts are only available online. Most sites do not carry parts for this model. When we found one that did have them, we spent twenty minutes combing through exploded views of the dishwasher trying to find this particular part. It was not listed.

I removed the failed part in 5 minutes with a screwdriver and a pair of pliers. If I could just get the part, my dishwasher would be working. My next thought is to head to Home Depot and steal it off a floor model. Somebody distract that sales clerk...

UPDATE: After 5 days, a service tech did come out and confirm what I already knew- that the drain pump was bad. He said he would have to order the part directly from LG. He said most service companies do not work on LG because LG doesn't allow them to stock the parts- everything has to be ordered. I guess I convinced him I was somewhat mechanically competent because he asked if I wanted the part shipped directly to me. I said that I did. I took 3 days, I received it on a Friday night. Had he not done that, it would've been Monday or Tuesday at the earliest for it to be installed. Instead I did it myself and got it running 4 days sooner.

The bottom line remains: You can't get LG parts. If it breaks down you're going to be out a dishwasher for 2 weeks.

For every DW where I found a good review there was another site saying how terrible it was. From reliable resources this one had pretty decent reviews, albeit plenty of bad ones. You have to look at the whole picture so here is my take after a few months. I installed this myself and should not have compared the build to my Kitchenaid. review_title: 0E error and how to fix it
review_text:
The machine is okay, but we suffered from perpetual blockage errors (0E). Read other reviews if you're thinking of buying this machine because this review is more for owners who are frustrated by the 0E error and are wondering if anyone else has this problem.

0E caused by a blockage in the exhaust pipe and stops the cycle. The problem is that you may not be able to find out where the blockage is and so may think you've dislodged it, only to find it come back. It can also be the cause of strange sounds at the start of the cycle. Sounds familiar? Read on.

Okay, so to fix this you're going to have to pull the dishwasher out from the enclosure and get to the bottom of the unit (by the way, if it is still in warranty then call up the repair technician and they'll come and fix it for you). You will need a pair of pliers, but that's about it. Most of the parts are just plastic and rubber. Once pulled out, I tilted my machine up from the front with the water hoses still attached (remove the power!). You want to look for this part here (ABQ73503002 Dishwasher Case Assembly) - it's sold on Amazon if you need to buy a new one. You will also need a shallow bowl to catch water released when you remove the hose.

The drainage system of this washer is actually quite simple. There is a small sump which feeds to an impeller (a pump / spinny thing) that drives the dirty water out of the washer and down the pipe. The impeller is inside the above mentioned assembly, which is only about 2 inches across. If your machine is making weird noises or you're getting the 0E error, then there is probably a foreign object in this unit that got passed the filters. The first time this happened to us it was a grapefruit pip. The second time it was a stiff fish bone.

Unhook the assembly by removing two black rubber squarish figure eights. Then remove the exhaust hose (the narrow gray ridged hose) by using pliers to move the spring clamp up and then pull the hose off the assembly. It will spurt water, so catch it in the bowl. If you like you can blow down the hose (the technician did this) to make sure there's no blockage on the rest of the exhaust pipe. Then take the assembly and twist off the bottom part. It should be possible to do this just with your hands. You should now be able to see the impeller and whatever is stopping it from moving or jamming it up. Remove the object and screw the bottom back on. Plug in the hose and move the clip over and hook the assembly back on.

Once you have put the machine back and plugged in the power, throw a load of water into the base of the machine. When you start a cycle, the first thing the machine does is pump out any residual water. This will flush out the pipe.

I'm pretty much resigned to the fact this may happen again. I can't recommend you buy this machine if you haven't already. We bought it because it matched the fridge and the reviews at the time were not so bad! Hope this helps someone!

review_title: Hate this dishwasher.  Wish we'd gone with another Maytag.
review_text:
We bought this because it was quiet. Unfortunately, that is the only good thing about it (ok, besides the little song it sings when it is done washing-- or, in this case, sort of washing).

Every time I load the dishwasher, I regret buying this. The biggest problem by far is the tines although it doesn't clean well either. The easy rack system is terrible. The tines fall over constantly and it is so frustrating. The tines are also spaced badly: they are either too close together or too far apart. The ones for plates can only fit the thinnest possible dishware. Anything but the thinnest and most delicate china flops over. The spacing for bowls is weird: the only available space is huge--way too big for a normal soup bowl-- or plate sized.

The interior space on this is huge but with the racks being how they are, it makes no difference. You cannot fit much in ths thing. Also there is no tiers for double stacking like our old Maytag had. I'd say that we fit about 60% of what we could fit in our old dishwasher and this one has much more space inside. Go figure.

Finally, this LG dishwashher is very finicky about cleaning. You seriously have to rinse every bit of food off for anything to come clean. I don't get it. As annoying as this problem is, it is still less annoying that the horrible "easyrack" system.

If I could do it again, I would buy the loud but functional Maytag we used to have.

product_title: LG LDF7551ST 24" Stainless Steel Fully Integrated Dishwasher - Energy Star
review_title: I hate, hate, hate this dishwasher!
review_text:
This dishwasher came with our house. It looks great, and matches all of the other LG appliances in the kitchen.

I hate it.

Actually I hate each and every one of the LG appliances that came with the house for varying reasons, but I digress....

I despise this dishwasher. It doesn't clean. It doesn't dry. And if I don't leave the door open so that it can air out between uses, the kitchen begins to smell like a swamp.

I have tried different detergents, different rinse aids, different settings on the rinse aid, running the tap before starting a load to make sure the water is hot, nothing works. Even when I use the extra dry cycle, the dishes are always wet when the cycle is done. And if I don't open the door immediately after the dishwasher finishes so things can air dry, metallic items begin to rust. I had a fantastic set of kitchen knives that I've had for decades completely ruined just because I turned on the dishwasher before going to bed. When I unloaded the dishwasher in the morning, everything was dripping with rust. Okay, so maybe they weren't the highest quality stainless steel, but they were always safe in a Whirlpool or a Hotpoint or a Maytag or a Kenmore or a KitchenAid (I've had a few dishwashers over the years).

The hybrid drying technology used in this dishwasher needs to be abandoned. It's developers, flogged. It doesn't dry, it just creates a sort of ultra humid environment with the hopes that the water will lose interest in clinging to your dishes. We live in Arizona. The relative humidity here is like 3%. Everything dries out here. Everything except items in this dishwasher that is. Had I known then what I know now about this dishwasher, we would have bought a different house. I hate this dishwasher that much.

Thanks for listening.

review_text:
I observed the Frigidaire FFBD2406NW with a prevailing online retail list price of about $400 when I was shopping for a dishwasher end of June, 2012. With its features it seemed priced correct there versus comparable models. Which might be to say, it wasn't a complete bare bones econo model, ie, a cheapie landlord's model for rental units. This model was a step or two above that.

I ended up finding it in store for $269 (...this model must be near retirement. It seems to be listed at $269 everywhere now), which IS a bare bones price. So I bought it. I have not been disappointed. It installed easy and runs well. At the price I paid, I got enormous value.

I hope the following comments are useful:

It's a two spinner model. 3 cycle choices with delayed start.

Dishwashers seem consistently rated for noise at about 60db, as is this one. In practice, this is not noisy at all. This Frigidaire runs quiet.

Door has a lightweight feel, as they all probably do these days.

Wash cycle runs 1 - 2 hours. Seems like a long time, but I confirmed this is normal.

Dishes come out clean. No films or stains observed.

Dishes are still a little wet at end of heat dry cycle. Taken in perspective, I think this is fine. It's an inexpensive unit.

review_title: Truly, a marvel of modern appliance engineering.
review_text:
It is rare to find the perfect combination of inefficiency and poor design in one appliance, but the folks who created this dishwasher have managed to pull it off.

No matter the configuration I try, I simply cannot get a true full load of dishes into this appliance. There are always spaces in both top and bottom racks as well as large empty spots in the silverware rack. Additionally, the silverware rack takes up one full side of the bottom dish rack, so no matter what you will not be able to arrange the bottom rack to accommodate all your dishwashing needs. Additionally, the top rack has to be loaded in such a way that taller items like travel coffee containers are toward the front, because if you load them too far back then the rack won't slide back into the machine. Everything is exactly the wrong size for normal-sized dishes. Oh, and if you actually expect your dishes to be clean, well, then you need to make sure you've selected the high-temp wash, which of course takes a toll on your hot water supply and/or heater.

The trolls who engineered this marvel must have done the math to ensure maximum frustration for the appliance owner. This takes true skill and precision. Kudos to the designers of this appliance--you have done something I never thought possible.

product_title: LG LFX28968ST27.6 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel French Door Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_text:
First let me preface this by saying that I first bought a Frigidaire refrigerator with most of the same features as this LG. I was working on replacing all of my appliances to stainless. I have a Bosch dishwasher, but my oven is Frigidaire so I thought I would try to at least match those appliance brands. After a couple of days, the Frigidaire had not produced any ice whatsoever. This was the first appliance I have EVER purchased without research. Had I done so, I would have seen the horrible reviews it received, mostly because of the ice maker. So two days later, it went back to the store.

NOW to the LG. I spent HOURS online researching reviews on all refrigerators with the features I wanted after my Frigidaire fiasco. I narrowed my search to three. This LG, a Whirlpool, and a Samsung. This one won. The reviews are astounding on this product. There are very few appliances that receive 5-star ratings, but this one did over and over and over again.

I told the sales associate of my new choice and he said I would not be sorry. He apologized for the Frigidaire and said that, even though Frigidaire is trying to move their production back to the U.S., the quality in refrigerators is still not there. He told me that he and his coworkers have been blown away by the positive reviews and quality of all LG appliances. According to him, they had never seen 5-star reviews on products as consistently as LG as well. I knew before I went to the store exactly what I wanted, so he said 'I want to show you something'. He turned his computer screen to me. It showed the number of service calls they made for mechanical problems over the last fiscal year on all LG products. The number was ZERO. He said this was not just refrigerators, but washers and dryers as well.

The features I like most about this refrigerator, aside from the absolute beauty of the stainless steel, are the:

~refrigerator size~ There is a lot of space on the shelves. On shelf is 'retractable', meaning that half of it slides back in under itself so that you can place taller items in front of that shelf if need be.

~freezer size~ The drawer is deep and divided, will hold a lot, and food is easily visible and accessible. The added pull-out top shelf holds an ice bucket for additional ice storage if necessary, as well as a good amount of room for more.

~ice maker~ The ice maker is on the door rather taking up any space inside the refrigerator. The Frigidaire I had bought originally had the ice maker inside the refrigerator itself. I didn't realize how much space this actually consumed until I saw the LG. No wasted space here. It only took a few hours to make the first batch of ice. The manual says that it will make 70-210 ice cubes/day. That's plenty for our family of 5, but there's still the huge ice bin that is located in the freezer. I keep some on hand for guests and spur-of-the-moment large gatherings.

~compartments~ The door compartments are great for holding milk, 2 liters, and other most frequently used items. There are two large storage bins for fruits and vegetables. There is a large, refrigerator width drawer that holds deli-meats, sandwiches, meats to cook etc. This drawer keeps foods at a different temperature for safety.

~quiet~ Unlike another reviewer's experience, this unit is extremely quiet. Mine is virtually noiseless.

I just can't say enough about this refrigerator. I did pay an extra $145 for an extended warranty, but based on what I've been told and shown, I should never need it.

There was nothing wrong with our other refrigerator that we've had for 15 years or so, other than it was white. As I previously mentioned we were slowly replacing our kitchen appliances for stainless steel and this was our last one needed. We were in the home improvement store to get a new water heater when I made my first impulse buy without any research whatsoever. Why I would do that on something as big as a refrigerator I will never know. BUT it all worked itself out. I learned a big lesson and I ended up with a first-rate refrigerator. This is a purchase I'm sure I will not regret.

You can't set the cup/glass in the unit to dispense water, like you can the ice. You have to hold the glass up to it, to get water.

There's plenty of freezer space at the bottom, but we have to be careful to stay self-organized. The fridge part is very large, with several drawers and a variety of door shelves for short slim bottles, short fat jars or tall slim wine bottles. She also likes the digital display. review_text:
In the past 7 years I have had two LG refrigerators. The first one failed after about 3 years. It needed a new part. LG no longer made the part. They did the right thing and gave me a partial credit towards the purchase of new refrigerator, so I bought another LG.

After two and a half years the replacement is having problems. When the technician arrived he didn't have to spend any time trying to figure out the problem. He said, "I think I know what the problem is because the fans in these things fail all the time." He said he would replace the fan, but, if it wasn't the fan it was the electronic control panel and he couldn't know for sure until he replaced the fan. It was going to be two weeks before he could get the fan because there was a large demand for the part and LG wasn't able to keep up.

Further, none of the parts nor the labor was covered by the warranty, even though the refrigerator is not even three years old. So I have to pay for the replacement of the fan and if it didn't fix the problem I would have further expense as he worked he way to fix it. Meanwhile I don't have a working refrigerator.

I decided to buy a new refrigerator rather than take the chance that I would have to poor money into repairs only to have a buggy refrigerator. This refrigerator cost almost $3,000 and now only two and a half years later I am buying another one.

I got a letter from a law firm a few weeks ago telling me that as an owner of an LG refrigerator I was party to a class action suit regarding the unreliability of this product.

All in all dealing with LG has been a very expensive and unpleasant experience. I feel that I have an obligation to my fellow consumers to share my experience so that you may take this into consideration before you spend a lot of money on an LG refrigerator that may not live up to your expectations.

product_title: LG LFX28968ST27.6 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel French Door Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_title: Lots of space with great organization & visibility
review_text:
After 17 years of using a 25.1 cubic foot side-by-side fridge with an ice maker that took up a good portion of the freezer space we decided an upgrade was in our near future. We wanted a French door style so we looked around at a lot of places and eventually landed on this one as it had all the features we were looking for and was an open box deal which was way cheaper than even the Black Friday deals. We've had it for about three weeks now and so far we absolutely love it!

I smile inside every time we open the doors because there's just so much space and everything is so brightly lit and easy to see. We now have two shelves that can hold tall items as opposed to a single shelf in our old fridge. This is thanks to one of the shelves being able to convert into a half-shelf, meaning that the front part can be pushed back half way so you can put tall items on the shelf below it while still having a shelf in back to hold shorter items. Every shelf is adjustable and if you line them up side-by-side then the sides snap together. We kept the top ones like that but the ones under those we toggled to give different height options on each side. Whether snapped together or not, all the shelves are sturdy.

There are two half-width drawers that are side-by-side which can be adjusted for either fruits or veggies, then one long drawer under those. All of these drawers are on wheeled tracks so they glide open with virtually no effort. The fronts and tops of the half-width drawers are transparent so it's very easy to see what's inside. Not being able to see well into drawers or to the back of shelves on our other fridge led us to forget what was there, which in turn meant that food would often end up in the trash.

On our old fridge the automatic ice maker took up a lot of room in the freezer and had a large bin which held a lot of ice, a bin that wasn't sealed off from the rest of the freezer so the ice would soaking up odors and end up leaving an unpleasant taste in our drinks once it began to melt. It got so bad that we started using metal ice cubes kept sealed in a separate sealed plastic container. This new fridge has a much smaller ice bin and it's built right into the fridge door, out of the way so it doesn't take up any shelf space and completely sealed off from both the fridge and freezer so the ice won't absorb any odors. No longer do we have to worry about nasty-tasting ice or messing with metal ice cubes! And even though the ice maker is in the door, there is still shelf space there! Granted, it's not very deep but it works.

The ice and water dispensers are also nicer than our previous fridge as these have an area which allows very large glasses to be filled. I think this is due to having the water dispenser above the ice dispenser instead of next to it, allowing for extra width on either side to fit large containers. The dispenser tray even slides out so you can set a large glass or mug down while filling it. There is a safety feature built in where the dispenser won't operate if one of the doors is opened. This can be annoying if I'm trying to use it and my wife opens the other door to get something. I haven't yet looked into finding out if there's a way to disable this feature.

The freezer is also a source of joy as we can now spread things out and see everything that's in there. The wide drawer slides out easily and all the way so nothing is hidden, and there's a smaller drawer inside to help keep things organized so everything isn't just stacked on top of each other. It comes with an ice bin in case you need more ice than the ice maker can hold, but so far we've just used it to put small food items in. We like the pull out drawer way better than shelves because everything is easily visible and in easy reach without having to pull stuff out, put it on the counter, grab whatever in the back, then put the stuff on the counter back.

One thing we weren't aware of when we bought this is that stainless steel isn't magnetic, so on this fridge only the sides are magnetic. Now, this could be a good thing or a bad thing. We used to have our fridge covered with various papers and things and there was just no room to put them all on the side, especially since we only have half of one side available due to a wall completely covering one side and a counter covering half the other. On the plus side, the front of our fridge looks nice and sleek and not covered in junk we really didn't need displayed.

I can't speak to the longevity or durability yet since we've only had it for a few weeks, but it feels pretty solid and so far we absolutely love this fridge so here's hoping it will last! If anything new developments come up I'll be sure to update this review.

review_title: Most expensive mistake in a long time, purchased July 2013
review_text:
This washer (note the matching dryer is great) is one of the worst investments I have made in a long time. Aside from the delivering dealer's service being absolutely horrible, the machine has been a constant irritation from day one, and warranty service has not really improved things. The machine imbalance is terrible. Warranty service determined a "bolt" was missing from the balance assembly (it was just a large screw), which seemed to improve things somewhat. The machine has been "leveled" to death, but just the flexibility of the Samsung pedestals and the cushion of the rubber feet seems to be enough to allow for incredible vibration at high speed, and the machine literally rocks while clunking at lower spin speeds with any load size. It is so bad that I don't know if this balance part is still working or not.

The amount of water to fill is usually inadequate. Any fabrics that soak up water such as towels, sheets or jeans, the machine will only put enough water to make a damp-to-wet ball that thuds back and forth. Synthetics are the only clothes that don't abrade in enough water for more of a sloshing action. I use He detergents by the teaspoon in order to get adequate rinsing with an extra cycle, and the cold-only rinsing makes things worse. Bleach is dispensed only 7 minutes before the end of a wash cycle, why I have no idea.

If I had the chance to do it over again, I would not follow test organization ratings in choosing a washer, but get a machine where users have stated they can get around problems by having more manual settings such as load size to overcome some of these bizarre behaviors. I would never recommend this machine period, much less on any floor but concrete. I would insist on more than a 30-day return policy, no strings. I would demand being able to purchase an extended warranty after the 30 days, when you realize the machine will probably vibrate itself to oblivion. The only plus, wherever you are in your house you will know when your load is done, no need for the chime at all!

product_title: Samsung WF457ARGSGR 4.5 Cu. Ft. Onyx Stackable With Steam Cycle Front Load Washer - Energy Star
review_text:
I read the first and only review on this product and I can almost guarantee that reviewer doesn't even own one. First, the "smell". It's a new product. I didn't notice any smell. It's probably the smell of the Home Depot he checked out this washer at. As for parts not lasting - I'm not sure where this person came up with that one. I would like to read some more details about his/her experience on these unreliable parts. Third, expensive parts. This is a premium product. It's like buying a Mercedes over a Chevy. But to be more realistic, appliance parts are expensive to begin with. I've never heard anyone say "wow, the part for my washer/dryer was dirt cheap!".

Now for the review itself: We upgraded both the washer and dryer with the Samsung products and couldn't be happier. The number of options and modes that it allows you to chose when washing clothes is just unbelievable. The touchscreens are huge and very visible. The washing/drying is extremely quiet. I actually had to go back a few times to check if the machines were even on because they were so quiet! The ability to connect the units to wifi and your smartphones is an added convenience. You have the ability to control the units via inside the house using your smartphone or in a remote location. Some people may say this is a stupid idea but realistically, it's an added "convenience" and for some, they will benefit greatly from this feature.

I plan on writing another review after a couple of weeks to see how things hold up. So far, so good. I couldn't be happier with my purchase. It's quite surprising how far washers and dryers have come even from 5 years ago.

Update (09/13/2013): Still loving the washer but discovered a big oops on my part. I threw into the washer a soaking wet towel. When I mean soaking wet, I could have squeezed about 2 cups of water from it. Anyway, I put it in the washer and just left it there for a few hours without running it and long and behold, the washer leaked the water out and onto the floor. Now, before you see this as a flaw: Front loading washers have a huge mold problem. Fortunately, this washer has not had that problem. So the keep the washer mold free, it has to "open" everything up inside to let it breath. With that said, if I were to dump a bucket of water into the washer without it actually being on or on wash mode, the washer itself wouldn't know and the water would leak right out. So this is totally not the washer's fault. It was my stupid mistake. Who leaves a soaking wet towel in a washer anyway? Right there you're already asking for mold/mildew problems.

review_text:

I was hesitant to purchase a more expensive high efficiency washer because I wasn't sure if the gentle motions would clean as well as a normal cheap washer. Well it has cleaned everything I have thrown at it, and the flip side is that my expensive clothes have barely faded at all. This has saved me hundreds of dollars on clothes because I work in an office and have to dress professionally. This is in addition to the noticeable drop in my electric bill (my electric company sends weekly emails with usage charts and I no longer see spikes during the hours when I do laundry).

One family member who lives on campus about 1.5 hours away will bring her clothes here just to avoid using the conventional washer at her campus apartment. The reasons she gives include the Samsung being more gentle on her school clothes, she doesn't like to hear the noise of the washer in her apartment, and she likes the "Sanitize" feature for her medical scrubs.

The only negatives I have are that I use the gentle/delicate cycle when washing the expensive clothes, but it forces me to use the low spin speed which extends the dry time slightly. At the same time, the dryer automatically shuts off when it detects no moisture so there's no extra dry time compared to my old dryer that ran until the timer finished. Also, when drying my king size sheets they sometimes ball up even with the "Bedding Plus" option. If I don't check and unwrap them, the center of the ball will still be wet when the cycle finishes.

I did have one scare in the first few weeks. The washer worked but it would accumulate a pool of water when sitting for a couple of days. I called and Samsung sent a technician. It turns out it was because the Best Buy installers barely opened the water valve. It's not intuitive, but he said it was because there was no water pressure. All he did was turn on the water valve and was on his way in a couple of minutes--it was under warranty so he didn't charge me anything. I have had ZERO problems since then. I did learn that the Samsung support was very courteous and professional, but I was left wondering why they couldn't have suggested opening the valve over the phone?

review_title: Don't be put off by old, bad reviews.
review_text:
I was initially put off by the Amazon reviews on this model and similar models but our fridge went out and this was the best type for the money for us. We did not want a door ice/water thing and I did want a bottom freezer (husband didn't care). We had a 17 year old GE side-by-side.

People said the refrigerator made weird popping/cracking sounds. Like 'gun shots', some said. Dogs were alarmed, said others. Some could not carry on a conversation in the living room or sleep through these horrible sounds. Now, that's alarming.

But I knew this could not actually be true since it defied common sense. If every Samsung refrigerator buyer attempted to return/constantly service every unit, they would stop selling them. It wouldn't be cost effective to keep trying.

I'm not saying some people haven't got a lemon but I refuse to believe they are all like that. I have waited with baited breath for my new fridge to suddenly begin shocking us with weird sounds. So far, it's a quiet as our old one. Oh, and we have done a bunch of party stuff involving opening and closing the doors, digging in the freezer, and generally just using it.

Here's what I think: when it's a big ticket item people have more expectations and a much lower tolerance for any little thing. I had no unusual expectations (it's way better than my old one) and it's no better or worse than my old one in terms of noise. Actually, both were/are quiet.

Don't be put off this model due to the reviews (many of which are years old). If there was a problem, it looks like Samsung has fixed it. It's a wonderful unit for someone who does a lot of from-scratch cooking or who entertains a lot (I do both).

review_text: I absolutely adored this refrigerator for the first couple of years. Spacious, easy access with the french doors, etc..Then the noise started. It's a grinding noise at times, a hum at others. At it's worst it's a jack hammer and drives me out of the kitchen. Along with the noise came difficulty opening the cold cut drawer and water in the crispers. My mechanical husband looked and said there was frost in the back panel.So we took all the food out to let it"defrost". Didn't I buy a frost free refrigerator? But we turned it off and hit with the hairdryer. And mopped up all that melted. We put it back together and it was frost and sound free for about 3 weeks. Then here we go again. The noise starts and even louder to the point where I'm having to turn up the TV volume. I really want to hit the thing to make it stop.So Mr. Mechanic gets on YouTube and discovers that this is especially common to this fridge. The drainage hole at the back of the fridge is too small to accommodate the amount of water and it freezes up. This guy suggests a copper wire down the hole to keep it open and flowing. I don't remember all the particulars but we decide to try it. Here we go with the defrosting mess again. So the wire is place and for 2 weeks we're good. And then the noise is back on and off for about a week. Then it stopped. So either its so frozen the circulator fan won't spin or it died. Fridge is still cool enough to keep food but not cold. We are shopping for a new fridge. We have read that Samsung will not recall it and it definitely is defective so stay away! I'll buy a Samsung phone, computer or TV but not an appliance!

product_title: GE PFE29PSDSS Profile 28.6 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel French Door Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_text:
Bought this after most review sites highly praised it and most reviews (like this one) liked it. No matter where you look you will always find someone who isn't completely satisfied.

First off, check your doorway dimensions. Even if you take the main doors off this beast it is still 30.5" deep. Older doorways might be tight to move it through. I was able to take off the freezer door tracks (8 mini-bolts/screws) and it brought it back down to 29.25". The delivery guy wouldn't do it so it sat in my living room until I figured that part out myself.

It assembles pretty easily. The directions are pretty straight forward, just follow the book (but you have to follow them backwards as there are no assembly instructions only dis-assembly instructions). You can do it with 1 person but there are a few steps that make it a LOT easier with 2. The doors aren't actually set to level at the top as it was explained to me by the installer that the Left door is built about 1/8-1/4" taller to factor in sag over time since the water/ice maker/dispenser is built into that one. Makes sense but you can adjust it yourself to make them even.

The overall appearance of this monster is beautiful. It is a shiny/polished stainless steel front. The side panels state that they are a slate/dark grey but to me they actually look more dark chocolate but it could be the lighting in the room. No magnets will stick on the front due to the high nickel count of this stainless steel but they do stick to the sides.

The doors open and close very heavy. Gone are the days of the thin doors. They are actually pretty loud (no whisper action here) when they close but that is mainly due to the left door seal that expands/contracts as the door opens. Be warned: they will wake a sleeping baby or the family dog if you open them during a late night raid of the fridge.

The interior lighting is wonderful. It 'warms' up after a second once the door(s) are opened. Not super bright until they all warm up. Most other fridges in this class seem to only have overhead or back lighting which makes a lot of the food shadowed and dark. Not this baby. Theater lighting all the way around provides a clear view of everything inside.

The door shevles are a little different. They don't quite fit 'American' food. I wonder if that falls under the European influence. The one flip up door shelf would be perfect for a dozen eggs, if they only came in 10 instead of 12, deep enough but not wide enough for the carton. Some of the others on the Left door are considerably smaller due to the ice maker so they get to catch nic-naks (perfect for mini-wine bottles). You will need to re-adust them a few times until you can find the best configuration for your usage.

The interior shelves are very deep. Upgrading from a 18cu. ft. model to this model makes it look like I don't have any food in the fridge. The shelves are adjustable. The right rear top shelf items seemed to be a little colder than the rest of the items in the fridge so be warned.

The interior drawers are spacious BUT you have to have both doors open to access them. Kind of a bummer. But they are deep and hold a lot of items are are lit too. The full width Deli drawer is nice for storage of just about anything. All come with separate temp controls too.

The Freezer drawer is deep and split into 2 side via a plastic tube. I see forgetting about certain items in the bottom after awhile. The 2 pull-out drawers work perfect for often accessed items (smaller one on the left holds 2 loaves of bread (or extra ice) & the larger right drawer is perfect for ice cream and other frozen treats). The little tip-out shelf on the backside of the freezer drawer is nice for frozen cans of juice.

The water/ice cube dispenser is a nice feature even if the ice cubes do come out at weird angles (make sure to keep your container (glass) right up against the dispenser or you will be cleaning up ice cubes off the floor). The autofill works awesome of small containers. I put an empty Gatoraid bottle under it and did the Autofill and it stop about 1/8" from the bottle neck. Perfect. The water does fill kind of slow (personal opinion) but better than splashing all over coming out too forcefully. No matter if you use the Autofill or just manually fill it tells you on the screen how many ounces you have dispensed which is kind of cool. Having the water filter accessible but still hidden in the door itself is a nice option too. It comes with a by-pass plug too incase after you find out how much the filters cost to replace you choose to no longer filter your water.

You can upload images to the LCD screen thru the USB port (no mention of it or how to use it in the manual) located in the top left corner of the water/ice dispenser. You can load up to 99 images (depending on the image sizes). Your images have to be in the home directory (no folders or sub-folders) of the device you are pluging in to it. It will automatically copy the images to the mini-hard drive for the screen. It will cycle them as a slideshow in the order that you uploaded them in, no random feature, anytime you use the water/ice dispenser.

Some reviewers have 'mentioned' (code for complained) about the noise it makes. The compressers are high efficient so they run more often than some older models. I used a Sound Meter app on my phone and they peaked between 42-48dB. Not that loud but you will hear it. If it is in an open area the sound will travel to the next room. It will take some getting used to but being more efficient comes at a price. It is quiet but not silent. Older models ran louder but turned on/off more often. The newer ones run longer but use a lot less power. But the sound is something to consider with this model.

The door handles are quite thick and show fingerprints very easily.

The shipping shrinkwrap is kind of tough to remove, especially since I think they put it on before some of the door handle hardware so it leaves little flakes at the joints, tweezer-worthy to remove them. We actually left it on the pull out tray under the water/ice dispenser. It is a cool looking blue and anything to draw attention to it adds to the look of it.

The water hookup is pretty easy along with the power plug (if standing in front of the fridge the water hookup is on the left and the power plug on the right).

It does roll forward and back pretty easily for a fridge of this weight but not side-to-side as the wheels don't pivot.

This beast is a prime example of fashion and function. It can handle anything you put in it and look beautiful in any kitchen.

I call it a beast as this was a huge upgrade for our house (18 cu.ft. 1995 model to this 28.6 cu.ft. monster).
