product_title: Electrolux EI23BC35KS IQ-Touch 22.6 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel Counter Depth French Door Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_text:
I owned the Electrolux EW23BC85KS counter depth french door refrigerator for four years. I would think the issues apply to both wave and IQ touch models.

Short version of this review:
Do not buy this appliance. If interested in another Electrolux refrigerator, I would be very wary if the ice maker is similar to the one in this unit. I had issues with the ice maker for 3 of the 4 years I owned this unit. The ice maker would leak and/or stop producing ice very often. The warranty company serviced it twice. The second time, they decided the unit was NOT REPAIRABLE and sent us a check for $3000 to replace it. I'll be honest here. I was relieved when they said that. My warranty expires in about 10 months and I was dreading have to pay for all of these repairs myself.

The good:
- No problems with the compressor. Freezer was always at 0°F, fridge at 37°F.

-There was what I called the "beer drawer" that kept at 33°F. I thought that was fantastic. Beers and sodas were that much better. However, refrigerators at a lower price point put this into a separate door below the french doors (look at the Samsung models) and are almost $1000 less.

- I really liked the ice that the machine produced. They were dome-shaped. The sliver-shaped ice that other machines made would tend to "bunch up" at your mouth when drinking a beverage, preventing the liquids from entering your mouth (I know this sound silly). But the dome-shaped ice from this fridge prevented that from happening.

- For it being only a 22.6 cu ft fridge, I found that it fit a lot of stuff. Maybe it was the placement of the shelves that we chose, but I didn't feel that it was "that small." I could fit 5 gallons of milk on the bottom left-hand side of the unit. I think that is really good for that size fridge!

- There was never any build-up of frost in the unit (expect for when the freezer door broke)

Now for the bad:
- After the 2nd year, the ice maker began having a leak. Water would drip down from the ice maker and out the dispenser. This would happen slowly, but about once/week, I would wake up in the morning to a puddle of water in the door dispenser.

- Around that same time, the ice maker began to have trouble producing ice. It would work great for about a week, and then it would just stop making ice, even though the tray was empty. I would turn off the ice maker entirely, wait about 8 hours and then turn it back on, and then it would create ice again.

- I got service for the ice maker problems last year. The tech fixed it, but it started to leak water into the dispenser after 6 months. This latest visit discovered that the ice maker (which is a separate unit) dislodged over time from the fridge wall - a common problem - which meant the cooler air from the fridge made its way into the ice maker - not good. As for the ice, a gear which churned it out broke - it was cheap plastic, and according to the knowledgeable service tech, very common.

And the ugly:
- "Something" happened to the freezer door. It no longer closes. I pulled out all the freezer trays, but I cannot see what the problem is. The service tech mentioned something happened in the back wall of the machine which caused the wall to bubble out, and dislocate the shelf. The door no longer seals. This resulted in a frost buildup inside the unit.

- At the same time, the ice maker started to only produce crushed ice into the dispenser, no matter the setting.

- We paid for the 4-year warranty on this appliance to cover repairs. After the technician came to check on it again last week, it was deemed "unfixable" and the warranty company sent me check to replace the unit.

review_title: Nice Fridge but a Couple Minor Issues
review_text:
I have had this Electrolux EI23BC35K Counter Depth Refrigerator for about two weeks now, so I am ready to give it a review. Some things that I really like about it are:

Looks great, doors and drawers all open and close smoothly.
The LED lights come on and transition from off to full brightness in a couple of seconds.
Rounded pyramid ice cubes from the door dispenser, and near half moon shaped cubes in the freezer, plenty of ice. So far, the ice makers are working perfectly.
Temperature readings on the front display appear accurate.

What I don't like about this refrigerator:
The compressor and fans run constantly. I have only heard it shut off once, for about 15 minutes. Even after not being opened all night long, it is still running non-stop in the morning.
It does have, as other reviewers have noted, a slight, high pitched whine coming from the compressor. It's not too loud, but noticeable. Since it never cycles off, it can be a bit annoying if you have good hearing and your kitchen is open to the living area.
The water filling the ice makers makes a loud whoosh noise, much louder than my previous fridge.

The refrigerator arrived in decent time, considering it had to be shipped from the east coast to the west coast. Upon arrival, the packaging appeared good, and once the cardboard was removed, it all looked good so I accepted delivery. After I completed the tedious task of removing the protective film from the stainless steel front, I found a small dent in the exact middle of the freezer door. It wasn't visible with the film on, and the film took a long time to remove as it was like peeling duct tape off. The blue film on the handles come off easily, but the somewhat clear film on the doors was a royal pain to remove, taking about 40 minutes to finish. I did not make the delivery people wait while I did this, so could not mark it as damaged in shipping, so I get to live with it.

That being said, I am overall fairly happy with my purchase, but would really have to think twice about buying a major appliance this way again. I saved a couple hundred over buying locally, but lost out on having the slight damage repaired. The savings I made were used to buy a SquareTrade extended warranty and new water supply line. If I have any issues in the future, I will update my review.

review_text:
This review is largely in response to the previous review bashing the dryer.

The dryer does a good job drying clothes, and our comforters, with exception of our 1 king sized comforter. The washer will wash it, but, the dryer leaves it damp. I believe this is a limitation of dryers that are meant for residential use, there is just not enough space for the air to circulate with the dryer 80+% full.

With regard to the other reviewer's mention of the "customer service scoreboard" - I did actually look at this, and, noticed, every company that makes dryers has >94% negative reviews... You must keep in mind that people only contribute when their experience was bad - good experiences rarely seem worth praising - the device has already required a call in to customer service after all.

And, with regard to the other reviewer's dryer being broken: almost all complex devices show a U curve failure rate - a bunch of failures when they are new decreasing to few failures for most of the normal working life, increasing failures when they get old. I will agree that not having the option to have your dryer replaced is a pain, however, even local stores won't pick up big items for free - at least that's what I found buying my lawn tractor from a big box store. product_title: Electrolux IQ Touch White Front Load Washer and ELECTRIC Dryer Laundry Set with Pedestals EIFLW50LIW_EIED50LIW_EPWD15IW
review_text:
Okay, I really hate to bash a product, but this washer is a piece of misery.

Bought a washer dryer set late November 2012. The washer developed a major leak in the first month. Given my personal circumstances at the time, I insisted that the local vendor (a nice independent store) replace the unit. They did. 7 months later the 2nd washer starts to make a loud noise whenever the drum spins, which is quite often in a front loading washer. I recorded the problem with several short movies on my cell phone, then looked for an authorized repair service.

There are only 3 authorized service repair facilities in all of Southern California for Electrolux. That should be a clue. The YELP reviews on all of them were horrible, so I picked the closest one. The first technician they sent watched my video but incorrectly diagnosed the problem. I waited a month for the part he'd ordered to arrive. It didn't. I asked the service shop to send another technician. This fellow took one look at my videos and knew immediately that the problem was with the bearings. They were failing. So he orders the two big expensive parts to effect repairs. Now the real fun starts.

The relationships between Electrolux and the authorized repair shops is best summarized as fraught. I've learned more about it then I care to or should ever have to know. Since early August, I've had at least 20 conversations, including emails and conference calls, between the repair service and manufacturer. This has gone on for over two months and is not resolved. The repair service is required to purchase the replacement parts through a vendor, usually Marcore. Marcore doesn't have the parts in stock. Electrolux does, but will not sell them directly to the authorized Electrolux repair service. Go figure. The local repair guys have to spend extra to acquire the parts from Electrolux through Marcore, and they aren't happy about that. The tub assembly that arrived was damaged in shipping so it sits in my garage until someone comes to fetch it. A second tub assembly has come and is also sitting in the garage. The box looks suspiciously bashed up but I'm not going to touch it until the repair man gets here. The other part, outer basket, has yet to make an appearance. It is supposedly in Florida, but I haven't seen it or a shipping order for it. These parts get shipped directly to me, the consumer, not the repair shop. That means being here to accept delivery and having room to store the 3 foot square boxes. The repair won't get done until both parts are on hand.

Like I said, the problem is still not fixed. But once it is done, effectively the washer will have been rebuilt. That's not encouraging. If you've ever had a car go through a major accident and repair you know it is never the same. I've got my doubts about what will result from this repair.

When I did my homework on washers, I liked the Electrolux for its size and appearance. It's still big and looks nice, but right now, that doesn't cut much slack against the miserable customer service and poor quality. Oh, and the soap dispenser dish doesn't drain (the cup is always full of water) and there is always a crust of soap in the cup after the wash cycle is complete. Yes, I use HE soap in the correct amounts.

Furthermore, both the local shop and Electrolux have chastised me for not buying an extended warranty. Call me old fashioned, but I rather thought that a washer costing over $1000 should work at least for a year or two. I certainly did not appreciate being made to feel guilty for not purchasing the extended warranty.

Maybe you will have better luck then I have, but I would still heartily recommend not buying this machine.

Temperature fluctuations are a bit higher than expected - despite being full of beverages, which should stabilize. I have mine set to Celcius - and it cycles plus/minus 3 degrees Celsius off setpoint. In other words, don't keep your milk in this one. Good unit otherwise.

*** April 16, 2014 update
Thought I'd let you know that it's a quiet unit - built in. Still fluctuates more than I'd like, and I keep it stocked with lots of soda cans and other beverages, so the thermal mass is there. I think that Electrolux set a wide deadband on purpose to make it more energy efficient - rather than let users opt for a more frequent cycling to manage temperature swings better. review_text:
This is one review from Sears website:

"If it were not for the one problem that I had with this machine I would have given it 5 stars. It does an excellent job of cleaning the clothes and has a large capacity. It is also very quiet. The problem is that the dryer damaged the clothes due to a badly designed seal between the rotating dryer drum and the stationary front pannel. This was a problem that another review wrote about but I decided to get the machine any way. Small buttons (the ones on the front of button down shirts) and drawstrings (like on sweat pants and hooded sweatsherts) get caught in the unsually large gap in the front seal. The repair technition that came out and looked at my machine was VERY supprised at such a large gap. When he called back to where ever he called they told him that there had only been one official report of this type of damage to clothes. The fix for the issue was to tilt the machine backwards. He did this and so far I have not had any more damaged clothes. However, in my opnion this should only be a temporary fix and I am hoping that GE is redesigning the front seal and will issue a recall to fix the machines already in service. Tipping the machine is not a fix for a design flaw. Also, the installiation instructions state that the machine should be level for operation so I don't know if the tilting will cause damage to other parts of the machine (like the washer) over time. The loads that had damage to my clothes were a small load and a medium load so the dryer was definitely not over loaded."

This is 100% accurate, please keep in mind of this issue. I have yet to try the tilt thing, but I hope this works because I can't continue to deal with damaged clothes.

review_title: Love the 5th warming burner with 3 adjustable levels (100 watts) and the hidden oven element but wish oven controls were simpler

After shopping around for a new oven, we fell in love with this oven overall far over and above similar ovens - it has the simple 2 racks (ordered a 3rd for baking purposes) in a very roomy oven (5.9 cubic feet). The large window reveals a true convection oven - the rear of the oven has a fan with another heating element for up to 30% reduced cooking time - keep this in mind when following recipes and cooking directions on prepackaged foods!

Features that would improve this freestanding range, in my opinion:
* The bridge element for using with 2 burner griddle. I can use it the way it comes anyway, but it would be nice to include on future models.
* A turn knob for the warmer element (currently has pushbutton controls)
* Simplified oven controls - such as up and down buttons for selecting temperature instead of numeric buttons (some people will see the numeric controls as a huge feature)
* The controls on the 2 dual burners both go from OFF to HIGH to then lower temperatures, yet the regular burners are OFF to LOW to HIGH, with the controls being opposite this could be a hazard to older (or younger) cooks.

All in all I believe we are going to love this range over time, it simply has an adjustment period from the older range.

review_text:
Samsung suggests cleaning the stove for 1 hour or more before attempting to use the oven which I did. They suggested using good ventilation during the cleaning process which I did during the cleaning. A strange odor emits from the stove. My house is two stories and the smell traveled all the way to the second floor. I could not escape the fumes. I had a stomach irritation for 4 days following this exposure.

As I delved deeper into the instruction booklet (page 14) I saw a warning.

This product contains a chemical known to the State of California to cause cancer, birth defects, or other reproductive harm. This appliance can cause low-level exposure to some of the substances listed, including benzene, formaldehyde, carbon monoxide.

I decided to do a little research on these substances to see what impact it may have on my health and here is what i learned.

Benzene:
• Benzene works by causing cells not to work correctly. For example, it can cause bone marrow not to produce enough red blood cells, which can lead to anemia. Also, it can damage the immune system by changing blood levels of antibodies and causing the loss of white blood cells.
• The seriousness of poisoning caused by benzene depends on the amount, route, and length of time of exposure, as well as the age and preexisting medical condition of the exposed person.
Long-term health effects of exposure to benzene
• The major effect of benzene from long-term exposure is on the blood. (Long-term exposure means exposure of a year or more.) Benzene causes harmful effects on the bone marrow and can cause a decrease in red blood cells, leading to anemia. It can also cause excessive bleeding and can affect the immune system, increasing the chance for infection.
Formaldehyde:
• The major toxic effects caused by acute formaldehyde exposure via inhalation are eye, nose, and throat irritation and effects on the nasal cavity. Other effects seen from exposure to high levels of formaldehyde in humans are coughing, wheezing, chest pains, and bronchitis. (1,2)
• Ingestion exposure to formaldehyde in humans has resulted in corrosion of the gastrointestinal tract and inflammation and ulceration of the mouth, esophagus, and stomach. (1,2)
Chronic Effects (Noncancer):
• Chronic exposure to formaldehyde by inhalation in humans has been associated with respiratory symptoms and eye, nose, and throat irritation. (1,2,4,5)
• At exposures increasingly greater than the RfD, (Reference Dose) the potential for adverse health effects increases. Lifetime exposure above the RfD does not imply that an adverse health effect would necessarily occur. (6)
Cancer Risk:
• Occupational studies have noted statistically significant associations between exposure to formaldehyde and increased incidence of lung and nasopharyngeal cancer. This evidence is considered to be "limited," rather than "sufficient," due to possible exposure to other agents that may have contributed to the excess cancers. (1,6)
Long Term Effects of Carbon Monoxide Poisoning
Carbon monoxide, also known as CO, is a potentially deadly gas that can have devastating effects upon your life – assuming, of course, that it doesn’t kill you.

The reason why carbon monoxide is so harmful is that it displaces the levels of oxygen within the blood, which results in the death of cells and damage to major organs, which are subsequently starved of oxygen. This lack of oxygen in the blood is known as anoxia. This can lead to a range of symptoms and effects, both short term and long term depending on the levels of gas breathed in and the duration over which you are exposed to carbon monoxide.
The long term effects of poisoning by carbon monoxide can be extremely serious. The long term effects of breathing in carbon monoxide can affect:
• memory
• brain function
• behaviour
• cognition.
It can also cause permanent damage to other major organs within the body, such as the heart.

It is thought that the hippocampus, which is the section of the brain that deals with new memories, can be particularly susceptible to long term damage from CO poisoning.

Because of my longstanding health issues this stove is being exchange for a good old fashioned electric range.

review_text:

The box had no damage. I went ahead and accepted it, big mistake, as it would be hidden by the counter. The store even refunded $50 for the dent. However, after the first use, which was a couple of days after performing the burn-in, the glass in the oven door shattered. Since this was within a week of delivery, the store replaced the unit with no issues.
Now, just be sure to check that everything on the stove works within the first few days so that you can avoid the experience that I just went through with Samsung Support. The wife tried using the right rear burner on the second stove in October. Just didn't have a need to use it prior. The burner did not work. Contacted Samsung Support and after three service visits over a two week period it was fixed. Turns out the coil in the burner had a weak spot and it burned out when it was turned on. However, the Service Tech ordered a replacement on the first visit, but when it arrived two days later, the ceramic ring was broke in several places, so a second replacement had to be ordered. That part also arrived in about two days, but then the earliest a Service Tech was available to install it was another week out.

So two lessons learned:
1. Do not accept a new appliance with any type of damage, even if it seems to just be cosmetic.
2. Test everything just as soon as you possibly can so it can be addressed by the store that the item was purchased from.

review_text:
I unknowingly purchased this unit and immediately discovered that the outside of it heats up to dangerous temperatures. The outside of the oven glass as well as the rim around the cooktop get EXTREMELY hot. I did some research and this is what I discovered:
This unit features new self-cleaning technology that essentially uses a steam system rather than an incinerating system (traditional self-cleaning technology where the oven heats to 700+ degrees to basically incinerate all the cooked-on grime). This means that the oven does not need to heat up as much, and therefore does not need to be built to withstand as much heat. Following that, the unit is not insulated as well as ovens with traditional self-cleaning technology. The manufacturer even stated that this range is built to heat to 172 degrees on the OUTSIDE. The manufacturer is aware that this range heats to an excessive degree on the outside, as this is simply the way this unit is built.
In addition to this danger, one of the oven vents is placed under the range control knobs. So, when the oven is on, the knob to the furthest left becomes unusable because it is so hot.
This is a very poorly designed appliance. Small children (or other vulnerable populations) can get burned very easily by touching the outside of the oven or rim of the cooktop when the oven is on. I would not recommend this product to anyone.

product_title: GE GDF520PGDBB 24" Black Full Console Dishwasher - Energy Star
review_title: WORST APPLIANCE I EVER OWNED - TWICE!!!!!
review_text:
If I could I would give this ZERO stars! This is my second go-round with this exact model (originally purchased through Lowe's). When the first one failed to clean the dishes (sometimes they looked like we didn't even turn the thing on after a cycle, it was that bad) we wanted to return it to the store under warranty. Since it was only 3 months after purchase they sent out a GE repairman who treated me like Ihad never owned a dishwasher before. I'm nearly 56 - this is not my first dishwasher rodeo, Mistah! He blamed me for every issue as follows:
1. Our water wasn't hot enough - though we had it set at 125 degrees he said his thermometer was only registering it at 120. We proved was set higher but we set it to 130 degrees. He said we needed to run the hot water to maximum temp before turning on the dishwasher so that "the tub did not cool the water off." (Um...doesn't that defeat the purpose of "energy" efficient?)
2. We did not use the right dishwaster detergent...apparently ONLY Cascade Platinum with Dawn will work with this dishwasher and ONLY JetFinish rinse aid.
3. If we rinsed our dishes of major particles before putting in the dishwasher, then the reason they weren't getting clean is because there was nothing for the soap to "stick to"...HUH? (Now that's a new one - I wonder if GE has scientifically proven that clean dishes will not get cleaner in a dishwasher?)
4. If we used the steam option, the temp boost option or the sani rinse option, it will only "cook" the food onto the dishes and make it harder for the unit to clean them properly. (Then why do they have those options if you aren't supposed to use them, I asked. "Because that is only for commercial applications when you need to sanitize the dishes to get rid of bacteria," he replied. "I didn't know this was a commercial grade dishwasher and so it must be my misconception that this is sold as a residential kitchen dishwasher and that normal kitchens don't have problems with bacteria." (That earned me a stupid, blank stare.)
5. The and kicker...it would be better if we ran the dishwasher at night before we went to bed because if we started up the cycle, then used the cold water in the kitchen sink, that would also reduce the hot water temperature and prevent the dishes from getting clean.

But...for the heck of it...I made all the changes he recommended, took pictures of the still dirty dishes and Lowe's was nice enough to offer me the option of either getting a full refund or an exchange.

So...I exchanged it. It was nice and quiet (that's the one star) and I thought perhaps GE had just produced a lemon, which happens to everyone occasionally. Last month I had it installed. Nope. Just today I decided I have tolerated a ramping up of the same problems I had with the last one, even though I am still implementing the recommendations of the GE repairman.

This IS the worst appliance I ever owned in my entire life.

review_text: This sounded like a wonderful dishwasher with lots of great features at a great price point. GE sent a technician to check it out and he plugged in his computer and checked the error codes. He said the pump works fine, so nothing wrong that he could tell. He also explained that this is an entirely new type of dishwasher that functions on only 0.8 gallons of water and senses the dirt in the water. The hose was shorter then our old dishwasher, but we went ahead and shortened it as much as physically possible. It didn't help at all and the dishwasher continued to retain water after a wash. Then we had another problem, the tub filled and leaked out the seals all over my kitchen floor. I can tell you, without a doubt, this dishwasher uses more then 0.8 gallons. review_title: correct facts and fixes to issues.
review_text: I installed one of these a month ago for my Girlfirend's daughter and everything is working fine now.  I'm  writing this to explain a few negative things mintioned in a prevsious reviews and to explain a problem and how we corrected it.  First, the .80 gallons used, is only reffering to the amount of water the unit keeps stored in the bottom of the unit at all times to keep the pump primed and the seals from drying out. Obviously a dishwasther uses more than  this when actively running through a wash cycle.  Second, we also noticed the pump making an odd sound, (we also have an extra long drain hose on ours) but after a little observation, we found that is was simply the pump  vibrating against the floor while it was pumping. Sure it's an issue that should be addressed by GE with regard to the mounting location and method of the pump, but we quickly resolved the issue by placing a small foam pad between the pump and the floor...."issue fixed".  We also experienced water leaking from the unit when we first tested it.  After making sure it was level three times, and with three sets of eyes watching for the source of the drip and some nimble fingers  feeling for signs of water while the unit was running, we determined the water was coming from inside the door (not the seals between the door and i the main unit). We disassembled the door and found that the water was coming through  the openning where the soap dispenser comes through inside wall of the door.  Appearently the o-ring seal isn't enough to withstand the typhoon inside. So we used some clear silacon on both sides of the soap despenser unit and sandwhiched it all back together... let it dry an hour and that was the last of the water leakage.  Everything has worked great since then.  Everyone loves how well it cleans and HOW QUEIT it is.... so much that my girlfriend is now wanting to replace her existing dishwasher with this model.  I agee that any unit you buy new shouldn't have any issues and that's why I'm only giving this unit 4 stars.  But considering how things are manufactured now, I'm surpised  there aren't more problems in all products we buy.  So when ranking this unit on it's preformance, I'd give it 5 stars (It's very quiet) but on it's construction, I'd give it 3 stars.

product_title: GE GDF520PGDWW 24" White Full Console Dishwasher - Energy Star
review_title: Mostly pleased but a few issues
review_text:
UPDATE 2/2105:

Still running strong. The only new issue is that the door is hanging low so I need to try to adjust it. We also noticed after staying in several vacation rentals that this dishwasher takes about twice as long as other models. But it is quieter!

UPDATE 9/2014:

The washer stopped filling with water after 17 months. I bought a fill valve, but that wasn't it - turns out the water height float was stuck due to gunk collecting in there. To fix, removed the filter and poured hot water over the column inside. Problem solved. Otherwise, still running great with 1 to 2 loads per day.

Original review:

I have the GDF520PGD0BB model which is identical to this one but in black. We have had the dishwasher for about 4 months now and so far are mostly pleased.

We wanted a reasonably priced quiet dishwasher to replace our Kenmore Elite which was getting older and failing. This one didn't have all the features but had high ratings online for its low noise level and effective cleaning.

When I installed it I noticed there wasn't much exterior soundproofing. Nevertheless it was quiet, but not as quiet as the Kenmore Elite. The sound of the water splashing inside was a plastic thunk, markedly different from our old stainless steel interior. I took the ample soundproofing wrap from the old dishwasher and added it to this one. It fit fairly well and this dishwasher is ULTRA-quiet now. I recommend adding extra padding around it if you want super-quiet. Standing right in front of it now I can barely hear anything at all.

The dishwasher seems well made except that one leg was screwed in wrong on the bottom at an angle. It looked cross-threaded but I couldn't get it to go in right; I ended up having to bend it to make it straight.

It isn't very deep. So it easily fit the dishwasher spot with plenty of room to spare, but inside it isn't quite as deep as the old one. The interior is grey plastic, not as nice as stainless steel but better than white plastic.

The door has no release lever - it auto-latches closed and you just need to pull a little hard to release the latch and open the door.

It fits lots of plates. They are very close together but generally come out clean. The top rack has no height adjustment and the shape is irregular so I have some trouble fitting things in the top rack.

The silverware basket is a pain. It can mount on front of the bottom rack or on the door. Either way, it ends up in the same spot and the silverware doesn't always come out clean. If I use a cheap detergent it doesn't always finish dissolving because the silverware blocks the water. Cascade doesn't have this problem for us though. I found that I could put the silverware basket on the right side of the bottom rack instead; we lose a little space but the silverware is cleaner and the detergent dissolves.

Still, loading the silverware is awkward. You can put each individual utensil in a slot, but this takes time and not everything fits into the slots very well. Plus if you put soup spoons in adjacent slots they don't come out clean. Alternately, you can fold up the basket covers and just shove everything in together. But this doesn't work well either because the dividers are far apart and the basket is short so they fall over.

When running there is no indication of where it is in the cycle and no time remaining display. It does quietly beep when it's done though.

If you interrupt the cycle by opening the dishwasher it doesn't automatically restart when you close it, but beeps until you press the button to continue. I like the auto-sense to determine wash time, but you can also choose light, medium, or heavy wash.

The dishes usually come out very clean. I sometimes add a little TSP to boost the detergent now that detergents are low phosphate. We are on a septic so there's no danger of polluting waterways - it just fertilizes the soil. There's no sani-rinse but there are 2 levels of extra heated wash you can select.

However, even in our dry climate the dishes always finish very wet unless we use heated dry. On our old dishwasher only the plastic items would be wet - perhaps this is because of the plastic dishwasher interior but I'm not sure. We just leave it open for a few minutes to let the water evaporate so we don't waste energy on drying.

There is an easy to remove and clean filter at the bottom which only needs to be checked occasionally.

All in all, a fine inexpensive, effective, and very quiet dishwasher.

Pros:

Quiet
Cleans effectively if you move the silverware rack to the side
Fits many plates
Heated wash cycles
Easy to clean filter
Autosense cycle

Cons:

Takes about twice as long as most dishwashers
No time display showing remaining minutes or even which cycle it is in
Not as deep as I'd like
Silverware is hard to load and doesn't always come clean when basket is in front
Dishes finish very wet unless heated dry is used
No Sani-rinse
No drain cycle but you can start a cycle and then cancel to drain

review_title: Quiet, but rack is poorly designed
review_text: This dishwasher is extremely quiet compared to the 12 year dishwasher I replaced.  The "Hybrid Stainless Steel Interior" means that the interior part of the door is stainless steel, but the interior tub is plastic. I knew that when I bought it and I don't have any issues with that being that way, but if all they say in the product description is "Hybrid Stainless Steel Interior" then I can see why it is misleading to someone who hasn't physically seen the dishwasher first.  The issue that I have is the rack design and its component parts.  The metal rack materials seem strong and sturdy and well protected by its coating, but the silverware baskets and flip down racks are extremely flimsy. In one respect I do like the way the basket have lids with holes to insert the handles of the spoons and forks, and the blades of the knives.  I'm assuming that makes it more efficient to clean them.  The problem is that the doors on top of the basket are extremely flimsy, difficult to close, and likely to break in a year's time (although none have broken yet).  The slots for the knives are so close together that the handles get in the way of each other.  We were having problems getting all the dish washer soap to dissolve until we figured out that the soap dispenser is blocked by the silverware baskets.  If you put a lot of silverware directly in front of the soap dispenser, it blocks the water going into the dispenser and it leaves residual soap, even when using the recommended Cascade ActionPacs.  There are flip down racks that are used to hold up wine glass stems.  The are removable and that's the way we keep it 98% of the time otherwise they just get in the way.  But now I have to store this racks somewhere so that when I do want to use them, I can.  I find that really annoying.  I find it really annoying to load the dishwasher because of the rack space.  For dinner plates, the prongs are so far apart laterally that it can really only take large plates and does not work well with the square plates we bought at the same time.  The top rack has a recess for the sprayer that protrudes into the upper rack space, making it almost useless for stacking small bowls and plates.  Don't even think of using the middle of the rack to put glasses.  I feel like the design takes away about 1/3 to 1/2 of the capacity of what the upper rack could hold if it were designed properly.

review_title: Mediocre; identical, I think, model but with plastic tub
review_text:
Ours looks just like this except it has a plastic tub, and it shares most of the same failings as mentioned in other reviews.

To get all dishes clean on Normal wash cycle, I use both the Steam option and the Boost Water Temp option. I would have expected to save the Steam option for occasional use but without it cleaning is not reliable. Boost Water Temp, I have read, is often needed on various dishwashers. In our case the pipe to the dishwasher from the water heater is along run—I'll stand at the faucet for 30-60 seconds waiting for hot water to arrive. But use of these two options certainly increases both energy usage and time take to do a load. It is nearly 2 hours.

I never use the heated dry option (to conserve energy and avoid damaging plastic things) and so I guess I cannot complain that when I open it after 2 or 3 hours things are still damp and water collects in concave items and on the top flat racks. I try to remember to open it when I hear it shut off if I'm still up, then leave it open for a couple of hours and things will be dry.

My pet peeve is the rinse-aid dispenser which seems to give no clue as to how full it is. The little window is dark all the time. So I have to periodically remember to open it and pour in the liquid carefully so as not to overflow it. This seems so simple to fix in the design process,and our previous one certainly had a visible indicator. We have hard well water and use Lemi-Shine rinse aid to lessen hard water spots.

The utensil racks are like the ones criticized by another reviewer: one part has separate slots for each utensil, though you can open the lid and put things into a small open cage. The part of the rack in front of the soap dispenser can only be used for short items such as paring knives since tall items will block the opening of the soap dispenser (which, btw, has only one compartment).

I saved utensil racks from our previous dishwasher and use one to expand capacity (but it takes up space where 3 plates or other things could go). Probably I could relocate the dishwasher's own utensil rack, from its insecure spot hanging on the outside of the bottom rack, to standing in the bottom rack, at the cost of losing more space. More likely now that I am thinking about it, I will use cable ties to affix the utensil rack to the front of the bottom rack.

For our most-used dishes the bottom rack is not well designed and so I never end up running the machine totally filled with dishes on the bottom. If I did, probably the crowding would further reduce the cleaning efficiency. Now the items that don't get clean are mainly silverware.

Yes, tall glasses do fall over on the top rack unless something with a broader base or shorter height, like a mug, is put next to the last one. The manual said, as I recall, not to hold glasses up by putting them over the upward prongs, maybe because water force might torque them and cause breakage, so careful loading is the only option.

If manufacturers would pay more attention to comment pages such as these, they could no doubt make appliances that pleased users much more. Appliances are one very expensive purchase that you cannot test before buying!

If I listed PRO and CON, I'm afraid there would be no PRO section. I chose it partly because of the options for Steam and Boost Water Temp, which I though would be useful once in a while. Its poor performance makes them necessary each time to get reliable cleaning. I've never used the height-adjustment on the top rack but sometimes the levers get bumped causing the rack to lurch downwards. Oh, it is fairly quiet, I can say that, just to end on one positive note.

review_title: once you get used to it, it is better than average
review_text:
we used to have the best dishwasher ever, quiet, cleaned anything and everything, no rinsing etc and after 15 years my 7 year old finally managed to jamb something in the pump where I couldn't get at it.

I looked at a lot of dishwashers because the basic requirements for me are internal food disposal, pots and pans cycle and water heat. I was amazed at how many more expensive units didn't have all of those features. All in all this dishwasher works really well except the dish layout is a little frustrating. It is made to hold a 12 piece dinner place setting. If you aren't loading a 12 piece dinner place set the tines are too close together if you don't over load it it cleans pretty well with an occasional item that doesn't get everything.

The silverware bins are truly annoying but if once you figure out that loading silverware in like groups, all spoons together for example, the it is easier to load and unload otherwise the utensils get stuck on the flap and well... also don't put any forks or knives too close to the soap dispenser of they might block it from opening.

One really nice feature with kids is that you can lock the control panel so they can't start and stop it just by hitting button ( we have had that happen plenty of times )

the water temp is not as hot as my old unit, hence why it does not get as clean. Also the heated dry tends to create condensation when it is done so if you don't take them out and get third degree burns then they are wet when you do particularly plastic items.

this dishwasher is also very quiet. In fact on occasion if there is some noise in the room, sometimes I am not sure it started.

one more advantage I almost forgot is the rack height that is one other place It does have my old unit beat you can put really large stuff in the bottom without interfering with the spray arm.

So all in all compared to a dishwasher I would have given a 5 and bought again if they still made it I give this one a 4. If they made the racks less complicated and the water temperature hotter then I would have said goodbye to the old one happily.

review_text:
I have been using this dishwasher for about eight months. I replaced an Asko dishwasher with this LG model. Honestly, I loved my Asko, but parts could not be found to fix it, so I had to replace it. Asko appliances are hard to find. . . and almost impossible to have worked on. So in the end, I chose this LG model. But there are “trade-offs”.

The good:

This is . . . by far. . . the quietest dishwasher I have ever heard! I thought my Asko was quite, but the LG is amazing! You really don’t hear it at all!

The racks are “adjustable” and they also fold down. This makes it very easy to place pots and pans in the dishwasher. You can place the cutlery basket on the bottom. . or on the top.

Speaking of cutlery basket, there are “holes” to place the cutlery so they are not “nesting” next to each other. So all of your cutlery is clean. But if you don’t really like that, then you can simply raise the cutlery basket cover that has the “holes” and dump all of your cutlery in as you would any other dishwasher. But I prefer the “holes”.

I have never seen a dishwasher with so much SPACE! The bottom is 14” and the top is 12”. I put HUGE pots in the bottom. I don’t know how they get so much space in there. . . but it’s GREAT!

The listing on Amazon shows two spray arms. . . but there are actually three. One on the bottom. . One in the middle. . . One small arm on the top.

This is something I haven’t had to use, as I haven’t had any “issues” with my dishwasher. . . but. . . . if you have “issues” then there is an app which will transfer information from your dishwasher to the app to help diagnose the problem before service has to be called. That sounds really cool. Again, I haven’t had to use it (thank goodness) so I don’t know how well it works. . . but it is a cool feature.

The “not-so-great”:

Before I start to list these. . I have to say. . . and I hate to keep repeating this. . . but I have been using an Asko for over 20-years. So there are certainly “advantages” to Asko. . . but. . . to have to weigh the cost and everything else.

I didn’t know this until I read the manual. . .but. . . each spray arm sprays separately. In other words, they don’t all spray at one time. Kind of “odd”, but that’s the way it works.

I’m assuming, due to each spray arm spraying separately, it takes a LONG time for this dishwasher to go through a cycle. I rinse all of my dishes first. Just a habit that I have done since I was a kid. But even with the “quick wash” it takes almost 1.5-hours. With a “regular” wash it’s well over two-hours and pushing three.

This dishwasher does NOT heat the water. That’s one thing I really liked about Asko it heated the water. But because the LG doesn’t heat the water, you must keep your hot water heat to at least 120 degrees. That’s a LOT hotter than you would have to keep it if you didn’t have such a dishwasher. So though this dishwasher might be an “energy star” dishwasher. . . I don’t know if they considered that you’re going to have to keep your hot water heather much higher than if you didn’t have such a dishwasher.

FYI. . . . This can all depend upon how far your hot water heater is from your dishwasher. . .but. . . I found out, after first use, that I needed to run the hot water in the sink until it was scalding hot before I started the dishwasher. Otherwise the water that was going into the dishwasher was not hot enough and so the results were poor.

Cleaning. . . . Hmmmm.. . .. this is a hard one. But personally, I don’t really think that it cleans nearly as well as my Asko. Granted. . . . I rinse all of my dishes anyway, so I don’t have any problems. But if I didn’t rinse them, then I think that I would. But if you rinse. . . and if you load the dishwasher correctly.. . then I think you will be fine.

It uses a lot of rinse aid, even on the lowest setting.

In summery. . …. . .

This dishwasher is supposed to hold up to 14-place-settings. I find that hard to believe. Even as a single person, I run a load almost daily. . . but. . . .I really hate to wash dishes in the sink, so my motto is “if it can’t go in the dishwasher. . . throw it away and find something that can!”. Hahaha So for me, it’s easy to fill a dishwasher.

Overall.. .. . Even with the “not-so-great” things about this dishwasher. . . I’m happy with it. My electric bill and gas (hot water) bill are still quite “normal” running the dishwasher daily. Oh… . .and if you’re not familiar with LG appliances. . . they “jingle” when the cycle is complete!

product_title: LG LTC24380ST23.73 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel Top Freezer Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_title: I wish I had done more research before buying
review_text:
update:
An appliance service repaired this problem and to possibly save someone the $100 - it turned out to be the switch just inside the fridge that senses when the door is closed. The serviceman said the switch has electronics inside it. He popped it out and replaced it. I decided to open the switch and see for myself. Lo and behold there are no electronics just plain vanilla single contacts. One could easily clean or adjust the contacts or just buy a replacement sw.
None of that tells me why a switch that should last for a million cycles would fail so soon. Lousy Quality control I assume.

Original Review: This has been installed just a couple months over the 1 yr warranty period and is on the fritz already. (!?) I have owned other fridges years on end without any problems ever. Maybe its just my time, statistically speaking. The interior lights blink off then sometimes on when the door is open. The motor is switching off with the lights which would possibly indicate a relay or thermal cutout. PLUS, it seems like they could be (sometimes) on while closed, heating my food nicely. In addition in researching the problem you see similar issues in the past including a recall. LG was absolutely unconcerned about me or my fridge on a chat today. Suggested I call the appliance repairman (when I asked about documentation or tech literature).
Too bad I went on a spree last year and bought LG washer dryer too. Maybe this is the one-off.

product_title: LG LTC24380SW23.73 Cu. Ft. White Top Freezer Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_title: I love my LG--GREAT APPLIANCE FOR THE PRICE!
review_text:
I love my LG refrigerator. I have had mine for 15 months now, and have not had any breakage problems. I love the top two door shelves which are large enough to accommodate 1 gallon water jugs as well as my 4+ qt. OXO Good Grips containers that hold my coffee beans. The lower third shelf I find useful for holding soda cans and condiments such as mustard.
I have stacked the bottom two shelves low and do wish I had more room on the bottom shelf; however, I find the center of the bottom shelf is tall enough for me to house a store-bought rotisserie chicken. I do not overload the fruit and vegetable crispers and have not had problems with them.
My refrigerator was advertised as being stainless steel, but I discovered that it is actually the stainless steel look. Stainless steel is capable of holding magnets and the front of my refrigerator cannot, though the sides can.
I paid $100 more for mine and it was on sale at the time. This refrigerator is not big enough for a family of four, but works well for 1 or 2 people. I positively love the built-in icemaker that came with mine. It has not given me any problems the way other icemakers have and it works fast!

product_title: LG LTN16385PL 15.7 Cu. Ft. Platinum Counter Depth Top Freezer Refrigerator
review_title: Who knew I'd have such warm feelings for something so cold.
review_text:
The main benefit of this refrigerator is that you are basically getting a gorgeous, counter-depth (or just slightly deeper) appliance without the ridiculously high price the counter-depth units command. My counter is just over 25 inches deep, and the two inches this fridge protrudes is barely noticeable. The color is a bit darker than my stainless GE range and dishwasher, but since they are not on the same wall, it all seems to work together. The finish looks like a slightly darker version of stainless steel -- if you're very picky, I would make sure it's not immediately beside a true stainless product. Keep in mind that the storage space you lose with this fridge being shallow is made up for with the added height -- so be sure to measure the available height in your kitchen. There are also three nice-sized racks on the interior of the door for extra space.

The only negative I've found is that, because the freezer door also has deep racks, those racks push into the interior space when the door is closed -- so if you do not shove your freezer contents as far back as possible, your food may block the freezer door from closing as the racks push into it. Before I figured this out, I was stumped as to why the freezer door wouldn't close fully. THIS IS NOT A BIG ISSUE once you become aware of it.

Oh, and note that this refrigerator does not have an ice maker -- but since I've had ice makers leak and cause costly damage to my kitchen floor, for me, this was a plus (though your needs may be different, of course).

Overall, though, this sleek appliance with its beautifully curved handles is nothing short of a work of art that keeps your food fresh.

product_title: LG WT4870 4.5 Cu. Ft. Ultra Large Capacity Top Load Washer Featuring Powerful StainCare Te, White
review_text:
.
We've had this about 3 years and find it a big improvement over our 1998 Kenmore washer.

- - - Energy Savings - - -

The EnergGuide label shows it to cost $15/year with a gas water heater...only a few dollars per year more than the best front loaders (see Note 1 for more EnergyGuide data). (If your water is heated by electricity, the cost difference is greater.)

In our area (San Diego) it qualified for rebates from the power company and the water company... $135.

- - - Noise - - -

It's not quieter than our old Kenmore, just different. The spin cycle does remind you of a jet engine...but a really high quality jet engine, and not an offensive sound.

- - - Controls - - -

The controls are organized and mostly sensible. You can rotate the knob to one of 7 settings, or select your exact preferences with push buttons (water temp, short/long cycle, spin speed, etc.) The pre-set selections don't quite line up with our eco-desires, so we work the buttons before each cycle. You can program (save) one custom cycle to your own wishes, which is nice.

Most of the "normal" soil level (wash time) selections result in a 52-57 minute cycle.

- - - Setting Confusion - - -

There is some confusion over settings which I find annoying and inexcusable. What's the difference between "Tap cold" and "Cold"? Between "Warm" and "Eco warm"? It says the "ColdWash" setting is for small loads only (8 lbs max), but it does not explain why. And does that also apply to manual selection of Cold or Tap Cold? Or just to the cycle enacted by the special ColdWash button? None of these reasonable questions are answered in the 32 page manual, or anywhere.

Come on, LG, it's 2013. The information age. We're supposed to care about energy efficiency, and you've spent millions of dollars engineering an efficient machine. But you can't explain what each button does, or what the trade-offs are?

The owner manual is clear and complete on many things, but they should have finished the job.

- - - Shopping Tips - - -

Our local Sears store had all the machines plugged in. Nice, if you want to check out the controls. Our salesperson at Sears knew a lot more about the machines than the reps we got at Best Buy (maybe random luck).

The 35-page owner manual can be downloaded from the LG site if you want more details.

- - - Top Load - - -

After years of front-load mania, top loaders seem to be getting more popular again. It seems much easier to load and unload. Larger door, no stooping, no hide and seek.

- - - Cleaning Effectiveness - - -

I don't know. According to Consumer Reports (August 2013) this model is "Very Good" but not as good as the best front loaders.

- - - Capacity - - -

The drum seems huge. The stainless steel part is 22" diameter x 17" high (no agitator in the middle). The total drum is 21" high (probably not all usable).

- - - Details and Overall Quality - - -

This machine feels like quality. Shock-absorber feet...beautiful stainless steel drum...dampened lid hinges (lid closes gently when you let go of it).

- - - Pricing - - -

This model goes on sale for $600 at all the major outlets every few months (free delivery, free haul-away). Check camelcamelcamel for a look at price history (hit the Best Buy tab). Amazon merchants can't quite match this, apparently.

- - - Notes - - -

Note 1: EnergyGuide label:

- Assumes 8 loads per week, 10.65 cents/kWh electricity cost, $ 1.218 per therm gas cost.
- $24 yearly operating cost with electric water heater (lowest model is $10, highest is $71)
- $15 yearly operating cost with gas water heater
- 225 kWh/year electricity use

product_title: LG WT4870 4.5 Cu. Ft. Ultra Large Capacity Top Load Washer Featuring Powerful StainCare Te, White
review_text:
When our 10 year old kitchen aid washer went out, I was shocked to learn that the new washers had no agitators and the door locked and they used much less water. So my husband and I started researching washers, reading dozens of reviews and asking everyone we knew about their washers. We learned a lot and decided that this LG washer/ dryer was the best value for the money. We have had it for almost 2 months now and have been very pleased.
It cleans well and is very quiet. The loudest part is when the water enters or exits the tub. We both enjoy listening to it and often leave the utility room door open so that we can. We never did this before... I know it sounds weird.......but it is just cool hearing what sounds like an airplane ( a quiet one) take off in your utility room and the melody played at the end of a cycle!!!!
A few recommendations: 1) read all installation instructions before installing and follow them. 2) make sure it is level and on a good solid floor (it does spin very fast). 3) after washing, pull the detergent dispenser out to release trapped water and leave lid open for a while to dry out and avoid smelling. We have not had this problem but some reviewers said they did and i want to avoid this. 4) place clothes around the center in a balanced formation and put in similar items per the directions, towels and sheets really don't work well together. 5) if you are buying the washer go ahead and buy the dryer because they are most efficient when used together ( and look great too).
And best of all, 6) Be sure to check with your electric company for rebates on new high efficient energy appliances. Ours offered a $100 rebate on this washer. We bought ours on sale at Sears, picked it up and installed ourselves and received the rebate. So we feel we got a great deal and a really high quality product for the money. Other washers with similar features were $300-$400 more.
Best wishes!

product_title: LG WT4870 4.5 Cu. Ft. Ultra Large Capacity Top Load Washer Featuring Powerful StainCare Te, White
review_text: So here I am, three months later, & I hate this machine more than ever. The place where you place the bleach leaks - all over my colored laundry! product_title: LG WT4870 4.5 Cu. Ft. Ultra Large Capacity Top Load Washer Featuring Powerful StainCare Te, White
review_title: Bought as a set with Dryer
review_text:
I wanted to wait to review this until after I used it for a month or so. I read the reviews on this set prior to purchasing it and I'm glad that I did.

Many seem to not like the extended wash time so I was prepared for 1 1/2 hour cycle. However, I found that the increased space that this machine offers equals 2 and maybe 3 loads of my old unit. This means I'm still saving time because instead of doing laundry 3 X per week I'm only doing laundry once.

I love the direct drive and how the spin cycle really spins out the water. This equals less drying time.

One thing I used to like doing is to set my machine and let items soak and then close the lid and finish the wash. With this unit, you cannot fill the machine and let a few items soak. The machine fills the tub according to how much laundry it senses is there. So if there is only a few items it will know to only fill the tub to a certain level. I will need to experiment more with the soak option.

As an allergy sufferer I can say that my sensitivity has gone way down. Also a reason I got the direct drive. No belts to contend with! The belts emit dust.

Many have commented about the noise during spin cycle and I must say that this machine is 100% quieter than my belt driven old unit. I don't even hear this running! I have to leave my utility room door open to hear it chime when finished. And the chime is so fun to hear :))

product_title: LG WT4870 4.5 Cu. Ft. Ultra Large Capacity Top Load Washer Featuring Powerful StainCare Te, White
review_title: Update: It's been 18 months or so... still runs well. Cleans, agitates, spins, pumps. So far so good.
review_text:
I've had this model for about a month. I had some installation issues that needed to be fixed. And the spin does vibrate more than my previous washer. Other than these, it does a very good job.

Why did I buy this washer? My old fisher and paykel was needing repairs a bit too frequently... I wanted to replace it with the same kind of technology... the direct drive inverter. F and P have it, samsung too. I was pleased to see lg also has direct drive. This is why this machine is more powerful and efficient than standard washers like whirlpool,etc. Notice in the reviews a lack of any mechanical issues? Bingo! Most of the issues have to do with load settings.

How well does it clean? Very well. It is doing all cycles like I expect. I don't normally use detergents (gasp!... I have a device that oxygenates the water before reaching the washer). I spot clean when needed. Laundry is still a choir... There's no magic. Unicorns and rainbows don't return with each load. Now if the could make a washer that could load itself, that would be something.

product_title: LG WT4870 4.5 Cu. Ft. Ultra Large Capacity Top Load Washer Featuring Powerful StainCare Te, White
review_text:
This washer is so picky when it comes to the loads you put in. It's supposed to be true balanced, but that never works. I would say half of my loads become unbalanced and I have to manually adjust them. Want to wash just one set of sheets? Nope! Want to wash a small load of clothes? Nope! Want to wash a comforter? Nope! If the load is too small or light you have to add more to the load in order for it to (possibly) run without becoming unbalanced. But then on the other hand I've tried to wash a comforter and it becomes uneven then too. And sometimes its completely random. I have a toddler and even though I'm washing a week's worth of clothes, it is not heavy enough for the washer to run properly. I read a ton of reviews on this washer before buying, but I honestly didn't think it could be this bad.

Also, when the load becomes unbalanced it takes super long for the load to finish. If you want to throw a load in after work and it becomes uneven, you'll be up all night waiting for it to finish. I love the matching dryer for the set, just wish the washer wasn't so sucky.

product_title: LG WT4870 4.5 Cu. Ft. Ultra Large Capacity Top Load Washer Featuring Powerful StainCare Te, White
review_text:
This washer replaced a 12 year-old GE select that I liked very much. The GE was a workhorse and never gave us any trouble at all--until it started leaking. We chose to purchase a new washer rather than repair. Believe me, we got our money's worth out of the GE.

I read the reviews and selected this particular LG washer, mainly because of its capacity and overall ratings (especially from Consumer Reports).

I was surprised that the LG actually had a much larger capacity than the GE. It's huge. One reason is that it does not have an agitator like the old GE (which means nothing will get torn up either). The only thing preventing me from doing even larger loads now is that we still have the GE Select dryer (fingers are crossed--don't want another large expense!), and even though I thought its capacity was quite large it turns out it doesn't come close to the LG.

I wasn't looking forward to the digital display (everything was mechanical on the GE), but after getting used to it, it's not that big a deal. It is a bit intimidating at first though.

We had a pro deliver and install the washer, and we're glad we did because I can see that it does need to be balanced just right. Speaking of that, the only complaint I have so far is that we get the Unbalanced signal when we have larger items like blankets in the washer.

Overall, the washer has cool sounds and does a great job of washing the clothes. No regrets.

product_title: LG WT4870 4.5 Cu. Ft. Ultra Large Capacity Top Load Washer Featuring Powerful StainCare Te, White
review_text:
Edit: July 11, 2014.
I still dislike this machine. I've found that I have to almost always switch the spin speed to medium or it will go off balance. The biggest kicker: it has a 'tub clean' setting. When we use liquid detergent, the machine begins to smell within a week(despite keeping the lid open), so I ran the tub clean last night with one Affresh tablet. Note my surprise when the wash setting that was DESIGNED to run EMPTY shut itself off! Why? It kept saying it was off balance! There weren't even clothes shifting in it. I've checked all levels...it is not out of level.
This washer is a joke.

I've owned this machine for almost a year. It replaced an old agitator style that suddenly died. I saw rave reviews all over the place for this machine. To be honest, I am not sure why.

Pros:
It holds a lot of clothing

Cons:
It becomes unbalanced VERY regularly. Probably 50% of the time, and it really doesn't matter how many or how few items are in it.

I use powdered HE detergent, as it keeps down the slimy/smelly buildup on the outside of the drum. It will NEVER rinse out all of the detergent during a regular cycle. It might get it all if you use the 'extra rinse' feature. Be ready to see a 90 minute wash cycle.

The wash timer is woefully inaccurate. I understand adjustments, but I've never seen a 57 minute load actually take 57 minutes. It is more like 70. Even more with the extra rinse cycle.

Maybe this is the nature of HE washing machines. Personally, I don't like it, and my husband despises this machine. We have seen no difference in our water usage...probably because you have to use 'extra rinse' for it to work properly.

I hope that when this one dies, they still make water-guzzling old school machines with agitators.

product_title: LG WT4870 4.5 Cu. Ft. Ultra Large Capacity Top Load Washer Featuring Powerful StainCare Te, White

review_title: Took me awhile, but it grew on me
review_text:
My experience with this washer was rough going for the first month or so. Many of those first loads had a horrible odor...the clothes and the tub.

I like the function of the settings. I like that it's programmed to a 'normal' setting that we typically use. One of my children thinks every load should be on quick wash (which I don't like). On our old machine, I wouldn't notice that he had turned the knob until I had done a load or two. On this machine, he can put it on quick cycle and it will automatically return to the 'normal' setting that I like for the next load. After I run whites set on bright white with hot water, the next load automatically goes back to the preset program.

I like that it's top load. That's one less bending stress that my back doesn't need. I've never liked the front load. I like the see-through top. It's interesting to me to see just what's going on in there. I guess it's the child in me. Even though the barrel is deep, I have no problem reaching in to unload. I'm 5'6", but two of my children are several inches shorter. They have no problem removing clothes as well. The child in me also likes the tune it plays when a load is finished. It does take longer to run through the cycles, but that's okay with m because the clothes come out much dryer. The spin cycle really gets the water out, which takes less time to dry.

Initially I gave this a 3 star rating. That was completely based on the 'stink'. The only problem is that I simply could not believe how bad they smelled at first. I've done a lot of research on this and have found that this is often a problem with high efficiency machines because they don't use as much water. My previous high efficiency washer never left clothes smelling at all...never ever. To manage that, I sometimes add vinegar to the bleach compartment. I know sounds crazy right? Vinegar has a million uses. This is annoying to be sure. Were it not for that, it would be a 5 star for sure. I gave it a 4 star, however, because of its rocky start.

I should finally add that now, after a couple of months, I haven't had any loads that were unbalance or smell at all. I've also washed tennis shoes a couple of times and it was not a problem at all.

So all in all, its' turned out to a great washer.

Appears to be a design problem because to activate the ice dispenser you have to tilt the top of your cup backwards which allows the small ice cubes to miss the cup. To solve(somewhat) hold the cup upright and press ice dispenser with your finger.

Did have delivery issues as delivery company did not arrive on the day they said they would and then arrived 4 hours after the time they said they would on the day they did deliver it. Also, they initially would not deliver into kitchen and were going to leave on porch even though it was clear when I bought the refrigerator on Amazon that it would be delivered to room of choice. product_title: Electrolux EI28BS80KSIQ-Touch 27.8 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel French Door Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_title: Please do not buy an Electrolux refrigerator.
review_text:

For the second time in two years, it stopped making ice. This time the technician slid the unit out to get access to the control board which revealed what you see in the attached picture. Yes, among the giant rust spot, is a chunk of ice. Doing a little research online, Electrolux refrigerators are subject to failures in the coolant line or insulation that can result in what we experienced - basically a hole. Since we came to own this fine piece of refrigeration through the purchase of our home (i.e., it was "transferred" to us), Electrolux is choosing not to stand behind its product to do anything about it. Notably they have never expressed any interest in determining how this happened in less than 5 years - they simply do not care.

There are so much better refrigerators out there, please do not buy an Electrolux.

product_title: Samsung WF435ATGJWR 4.3 Cu. Ft. White Stackable With Steam Cycle Front Load Washer - Energy Star
review_text: We needed a new washer and based on my research, I selected a front loading washer from Samsung.  I work in the field as a technician and get pretty dirty at times. I have noticed the clothing is cleaner and the technology is superior to the old agitator machine that we replaced.  One thing to note: I have noticed the lint filter in the dryer does not load up as much as before.  I think this is a testament to the fact the front loader tumbles the clothing and is not as hard on the fabrics as the agitator was.  I would certainly recommend the Samsung washer as a great appliance addition to someone's home. The 4.3 cubic feet capacity is another nice feature.  We are washing larger loads and including bedding that we sometimes washed by hand and then would hang it out to dry. The spin feature on the washer gets the water out before going into the dryer or out to hang dry.

product_title: Samsung WF393BTPAWR 3.9 Cu. Ft. White Stackable With Steam Cycle Front Load Washer - Energy Star
review_text:
I've only been using this washer for 2 months, but it has performed really well thus far. It is large and easily holds LOTS of items per load. We aren't having to do laundry as often. It uses very little water and detergent. Be careful not to over-do the detergent. The washer is quiet, including spinning. It takes a while to get the hang of which cycles/temps/spin speeds are the best for various uses, but once figured out it's smooth sailing.The My Cycle makes customizing your settings easy. Wash cycles that heat water to a higher temp take an hour and a half, but the hotter water has been worth the time . The Sanitize setting really cleans up those sour dish cloths, kitchen towels and washcloths. The Delicate cycle is very gentle--to the point where I decided to do some delicate items on Perm. Press instead. I have not had a problem with odor in the machine. I dry the grey rubber seal at the end of the laundry loads and then keep the door propped open with a rolled dishcloth so the machine can dry out. I gave this machine 4 stars because you can't engage the extra rinse without canceling the cycle and starting over...which I guess is also one way to get rid of excess suds.

The dryer that goes with the set has been a revelation. It dries perfectly without over cooking anything. An unexpected bonus for certain.

Like I said, great so far.

product_title: Samsung WF365BTBGWR 3.6 Cu. Ft. White Stackable With Steam Cycle Front Load Washer - Energy Star
review_text:
We bought this washer and its matching dryer in December of 2012. I immediately loved them as they are such an enormous upgrade to the terrible, cheap top loaders I was using before. The sanitize and steam settings are fantastic for a family with three children and a husband who sometimes forgets to switch the laundry before going to bed.

The unit is also pretty quiet, it doesn't rattle or make any annoying noises like I've read about in other product reviews for other machines. I especially like the "singing" alarms which are a far cry from the noxious buzzer sound I'm used to hearing.

All that being said, I give this machine a 3 star rating because of one very odd problem : the lettering wipes off when one tries to clean it after the control panel has had fabric softener or detergent dripped on it. I discovered this when I tried to clean some Downy off of it, using a plain white washcloth dampened with water. Some light researching yielded many complaints about this issue, and I'm concerned Samsung will not be able to do anything so I'll have to use my extended warranty where I bought it to get a new washer (which seems silly). Apparently they didn't bother to put a clear coat over the lettering on the washers so exposure to certain chemicals -- particularly the ones used to clean laundry -- will cause the markings to wipe away. This wouldn't be so terrible if the control dial and buttons didn't add up to 20+ individual words and setting combinations. If they expect me to happily print off a picture of what it looked like "before", just so I can use the darn thing properly, they're wrong.

I will try to come back with an update on how my email to Samsung turns out. If they actually have a solution that doesn't involve putting another of the same in my house (with the same problem), I will bump this up to a 4 star but leave the warning. No one should have to worry about their machine being ruined by a liquid that is used *in* the product on a near-daily basis. And doing returns/exchanges is always a pain I like to avoid.

UPDATE, 1/16/14 : As of today, they continued to blame the control panel wiping off on me and refuse to admit fault. One rep did say they would pay for it, then the next guy who spoke to me after I emailed my model number decided they wouldn't do it after all. I saw another reviewer say going on Facebook and Twitter helped, so I will be trying that and come back with another update. Highly recommend getting a clearcoat if you buy any of their products and promptly treat the control panels as Google searches found problems with Samsung dishwasher and refrigerator panel lettering wiping away with water as well.

product_title: Samsung WF365BTBGWR 3.6 Cu. Ft. White Stackable With Steam Cycle Front Load Washer - Energy Star
review_title: Consider your needs v. your wants.
review_text:
We have had this set for more than a year now -

First of all it looks and operates really nice. People have commented on how nice it looks (on the pedestal. Looks are good, but operation is important, as well as cleaning (for which you buy this type of machine). We bought the combination washer and dryer, so they would look nice. It would be a mistake to buy a front loader without buying the Pedestal to elevate it high enough to avoid bending over to take out and put in laundry. After a number of months of use, we found out that you should not overload the machine (too much) because the belt will come off in it's operation. That was a dumb move on my part. The energy and water you save is nice (although it's not a huge amount), and we like the different selections of operation (which gives us a huge amount of choices when doing our wash). One important note; this machine will not clean your cloths better than a "tub" washing machine. You can also load a larger amount of clothing in a "tub" machine. Cleaning is very important to me, so if I had to do it again, I'd find a nice looking "large tub" machine and go in that direction. But if your sold on the front loader - I'd recommend this product. I mean, good looks, and doing the job is important, but looks aren't everything to me.... but doing large loads and getting them clean is.

product_title: Samsung WF365BTBGWR 3.6 Cu. Ft. White Stackable With Steam Cycle Front Load Washer - Energy Star
review_title: Quiet, Energy Saving, Cleans Very Well!!
review_text:
I purchased this washer from Home Depot and received it with no scratches.
It is a very gorgeous washer (and dryer combo). I did not purchase the pedestals
because I am only 26 years old and I just can't see the extra money for nothing
more than convenience.

Pros- VERY quiet (at full spin speed I really had to verify it was on), cleans thoroughly,
empties the detergent tray every load (easier cleanup). So many wash choices for various
situations (most of which I'm sure I'll use frequently), including PureCycle. PureCycle
allows you to sanitize the washing machine, killing any mold spores inside.

Cons- It seems like the wash cycles take quite some time, my average load runs about
57 minutes (the sanitize cycle of the washer requests around 2 hours 27 minutes).
My son loves to put his face to them and smudge the chrome.

This is a very versatile washing machine; at this point I do not think I could have made
a better choice. ALSO: The music is pleasant; functionality is not nearly as complicated

I realized this after a few loads as the clothes are hardly even damp when the wash cycle is complete. I have had no issues thus far. Be careful when you pull the filter (you should do this often) for cleaning, make sure you pull the hose first and have some kind of bowl nearby to catch water.
