review_title: Junk - Threw away after 16 months and 3 repairs
review_text:
I purchased mine as part of a set from Lowe's in October 2012. We had been happy with our Maytag Neptune set for 11 years but our new home required stackable units so we purchased this set. We were excited b/c of the features and it being a newer and prettier set than our 11 year old Neptunes. We had them delivered and installed by Lowe's.

We were initially happy b/c the sensor functions worked better than our Neptune set and the capacity was slightly better. The washer worked ok although this dryer does take longer than our old Neptune.

We started having issues in June 2013 when we opened the dryer and a 3 inch wide by 6 inch long gash appeared in the drum. It was very sharp and very dangerous. It completely shredded a pair of my basketball shorts. Fortunately, it did not damage other clothes. The dryer was completely unusable. This is where the fun began. We contacted Samsung and could not secure an appointment for TWO WEEKs. We had already had a service appointment once on the washer (less serious issue but still a warranty issue) that had taken nearly a month to resolve with 4 different trips. Samsung, the global conglomerate that makes mobile phones, many makes of video monitors / televisions, countless other consumer electronics, hundreds of consumer electronics such as watches-phones-music devices-etc used a sub contractor to work on their appliances that was nearly 4 hours away from our home despite us living within 1 hour of two 800K person cities and 45 minutes from a 250K person city. They would send a tech from Columbia, SC to Beaufort, SC but not from Charleston, SC or Savannah, GA, or Hilton Head, SC....this led to many long lead times and trips back and forth when the techs could not figure out what to do. To add insult to injury, there was a 1 month back order on the drum (they had to replace the entire drum to address this). After 68 days, they finally addressed this with a new drum and we were able to dry clothes again.

Now (February 2014), only 17 months later, we have a dryer that shuts off after about 2-3 minutes running. No matter what setting we use; it just turns off after about 2-3 minutes. If we stand there long enough re-starting it it may run 10 minutes. Drying one load can take 5-6 hours and require you to start and re-start over and over. We contacted Samsung and were told we would wait about two weeks to see a tech, again from Columbia, SC; and we would have to pay for this honor.

So long Samsung; your equipment was picked up by our recycling folks in Beaufort. We have learned our lesson...no more Samsung equipment period. We even wrote letters to your office of the president and to customer care people who helped us before and got NO RESPONSE after two weeks. We called both 800 numbers and got nothing but "we are sorry" and run arounds. So, we bought new electrolux equipment and we will never ever buy Samsung anything again. Shame on you for building junk and then not supporting it...and finally for not even acknowledging our communications with you.

Buyer beware. I would not buy Samsung unless you buy some type of long term warranty or have the energy and time to do your own work on their equipment. They clearly do not care enough to support their products in market by having anyone able to respond to emails or letters and dispatching sub contractors from 200 miles away. Unbelievable.

product_title: Samsung RF263BEAEBC 25.6 Cu. Ft. Black French Door Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_title: STAY AWAY FROM SAMSUNG Please Read and you will see why
review_text:
Let me start off by saying I give every manufacturer a chance to correct a mistake I don't expect everything to be perfect and issues can occur. However with that said Samsung should stick to making Phones and other consumer electronics.

I bought all new appliances for my house at the end of March 2013. This Samsung refrigerator and a Washer and Dryer.

The refrigerator has been decent except for the amount of noise the compressor makes which is due to a variable speed compressor according to two different appliance repair places, scratches in the ice maker area, and water filter replacement. The first appliance repair guy allowed one of the tubes that goes to the compressor to continue to push against the back of the units cover making a terrible vibrating noise. It seems the "authorized" appliance repairmen are hit and miss, some know what they are doing and others do not. the Customer Care line at Samsung would like you to think they care but they do not. My refrigerator arrived with scratches in the ice maker area and a dent in the door. The place that sold me the appliances said they would take care of it, otherwise I would have refused it in this condition. They ordered two different doors the first one was put on and has 3 deep gouges in the ice maker area. The tech told me this is normal and that it would get scratched up anyways. This was a BRAND NEW refrigerator I just paid over 2,500 for this is unacceptable. The second door came in and was even worse it looked like someone had taken a scotch brite pad to it. The tech stated again this is normal he then proceeded to take my cell phone go outside of my house and talk behind my back to the place that sold it to me "Page Appliance" and told them it was a customer issue and that he was losing money. When I asked him why he had gone outside of my house with my cell phone he tried to lie but I called him out on it saying if he didn't have anything to say about me then why would he have to go outside he then basically owned up to it and said it was considered a "customer issue" meaning I was being fussy and unrealistic. I asked him if he would accept a new car with scratches on it he then said no but that many cars come that way and they can be touched up he then went on to tell me that many of the appliance retailers have full time touch up guys in house to repair dents, dings, scratches and missing paint on BRAND NEW APPLIANCES!

I have found their is a very limited number of repair shops that are authorized to work on Samsung appliances and some of them that are authorized cannot even do simple troubleshooting or know how to enter the diagnostic modes on the Samsung appliances.

Calling Samsung customer care gave little results. They fought with me about sending a new door and finally agreed to do so (this was the second door) which they said they would pull and personally inspect (they must have been asleep) because it looked like a scotch brite pad attacked the door. When the door is shipped it is wrapped in plastic all across the front except for the ice maker area which is black plastic. They do not cover the ice maker area with any protective film. This area scratches extremely easy. Since March the paddle to my ice maker is riddled with scratches and scuffs from normal use, I do not jam glasses under there nor have I been rough with it in any way. Samsung refused to send any more doors for the refrigerator. The second door was never put on the fridge and the appliance repair guy left it in my kitchen and said I could put it out on the curb and scrappers would take it (THIS IS A BRAND NEW DOOR!). The place where I bought the appliance could only offer me the door to their floor model.

At this point I threw in the towel over the frustration and time wasted dealing with this issue. I also did not want a floor model that had a door that had been opened and closed multiple times a day for viewing and kids hanging off the handles. Samsung stated it was not a warranty issue so they refused to do anything more even though they previously sent out a door. The technician that came to the house reported to Samsung that I was basically a difficult customer and downplayed the condition of the doors. I reported him to Samsung's department that authorizes technicians because he was clearly incompetent and rude. They never got back to me and nothing ever happened with it. This same technician also worked on my SAMSUNG washing machine that was squeaking terribly and never noticed all the legs were not turned all the way up into the machine when it was seated on its pedestal. More on that on a review of the Washer which I will write separately.

Samsung's support and finding something as simple as a Water Filter is an absolute joke as well.

I needed to replace my water filter so I started out by reading the manual that came with the Refrigerator. Most manufacturers put the water filter replacement part numbers in their manuals, Samsung however does not. I then went to the Samsung support website to inquire about my filter. It lists no specific information on the website for the water filter. it then refers you to another website setup to look like it is part of Samsung. When putting in my model number on the website it comes up with a water filter that says it has been discontinued. I then decided to click the link that says live support to initiate a chat session. The individual told me the correct filter was located here http://www. samsungparts. com/PartsList.aspx?Catalog=Parts_and_Accessories&PartSearch=DA29-00020B which is the DA29-00020B it does not list my model as a "supported" model at the bottom of the page when I brought this to the persons attention they (Marcia)immediately closed the chat session (very unprofessional). I then called 1-800-SAMSUNG who then referred me to another 800 number which is 1-800-627-4368 which is J&J international which is an authorized parts dealer for Samsung. According to them Samsung does not sell parts directly to the consumer. They want double what the filter costs here on Amazon.

Needless to say I will NEVER buy SAMSUNG again. Incompetent rude technicians, a rude subcontracted parts department with inaccurate information on its website. Samsung's lack of putting something as simple as a water filter replacement number in the manual (you'd think since they want you to use ONLY their filters they would advertise them more in their own manual). Along with the fact many places selling the appliances now have little to no experience with Samsung so the delivery and setup guys don't have a clue how to properly set it up.

I will be writing a separate review for my Washer from Samsung which has been nothing short of an Epic failure. and include a link to it here in the near future.

And to top it all off you cannot buy the DA29-00020B water filter at your local LOWES only Home Depot carries it.

review_title: I loved it up until this past Friday
review_text: I bought this refrigerator 3 months ago from my local Electronic Express. I loved it up until this past Friday. I thought the interior was nice and spacious compared to my old side-by-side and it was brightly lit by the LED. On Thursday I went grocery shopping and spent $200. The very next day the refrigerator was making a loud noise, like it was running high and it was warm inside the refrigerator and the freezer. I tried manually lowering the temperature with the controls but it wouldn't cool down. The display was saying the fridge was 65° and the freezer was 57°. I read the whole manual and tried resetting it by unplugging it for ten minutes and then plugging it back in but it didn't work. I had bought an extended protection plan for it, so I called Electronic Express to find out who I needed to call for a repair. They said I needed to contact the manufacturer since it was under a year old and they supplied me the number. I called Samsung on Friday and they said their technicians work Monday-Friday, so the soonest they could get someone there would be Monday. I made an appointment and was told I would receive a call from the tech 24-48 hours in advance to set a specific time. Well, now it's Monday and I haven't heard anything. I contacted Samsung again and was told a technician had been assigned for today and I would receive a call shortly. I asked if the warranty covered spoiled food and I was told it only covered parts and labor, and they understood my frustration but at least I was getting the service for free. So I have $200 worth of spoiled food since it was 3 days before they could come fix my BRAND NEW refrigerator but I should appreciate that the service is free basically. I wish it was over a year old because the extended protection plan I bought through a 3rd party does cover spoiled food.  Horrible policy, if your product doesn't work and costs me money I should be reimbursed. I have an entire refrigerator full of spoiled food because of this bad product.

review_title: If you are coming from a conventional, top-loading washer, be aware of the following.
review_text:
So I got this top-loading LG HE washer as a replacement for my 14-year-old top-loading Kenmore washer that eventually failed. This LG was the highest rated washer by a leading consumer reports magazine, and that's why I bought it.

Can't say that I am thrilled with this new machine :(

Pros:
Supposedly uses less water and electricity.
Higher spin speed gets more water out, resulting in shorter drying times in dryer.
Quieter, and less vibrations at high RPM.
No need to manually set water level; it supposedly figures the right amount of water to use.
Glass window on top, to see what the washer is actually doing.
No back panel like other washers; easier access to front controls.
Electronic controls (not mechanical dials and knobs).
Clothes look and smell clean after wash, but are they really cleaner? (see cons below).
Larger capacity.
Gentler on clothes.
Gives you an indication of remaing wash time in minutes, that could increase during the cycle depending on certain conditions.
Soft-closing lid (doesn't slam).

Cons:
Takes twice the time for a wash. (So where's the energy savings?)
Does all kinds of rotations with the clothes, without water, to try to balance the load before water-intake.
And still gets out of balance during spin (uE code), and does an unnecessary rinse again (during spin cycle), lengthening wash time, to try to re-balance the load.
The Owner's Manual states" "Always try to wash articles of somewhat similar weight to allow the washer to evenly distribute the weight of the load for spinning" (page 30). Really? What BS! All this because of the higher spin RPM? How do I find something similar in weight to my white bathrobe, as my other whites? It was very, very rare for my old washer to ever go out of balance.
Don't watch the clothes too long via the top glass window, or you might get dizzy.
Absolutely needs HE only detergent.
I've seen the same bathrobe pocket on the top of the other clothes at the beginning of the wash, and at the end of the wash. Sometimes smaller items get enclosed in the bathrobe. Are these indications that the clothes are not moving around properly in the water? Never had this problem in my old, agitator-based washer with sufficient water.

Update:
After a couple of months of use, I called the LG Tech Support to look at why I was getting so many uE (unbalanced load warnings). The technician came by and immediately replaced the rotor (with magnets around it), saying that there was a batch of them that had magnets that were not exactly identical in power causing some issues. Well, I still see uE warnings today. He did not indicate that my machine was not level or anything like that. He did say to avoid the default (cotton/normal) cycle because it uses very little water (to qualify for the washer HE rating), and that tends to cause more instances of unbalanced loads. Use Bright Whites, Pure Color and Bulky/Bedding is what he said.

2nd Update:
The washer is ripping our clothes in a different way than my previous agitator-based washer did.
If I use medium or high spin speed, the wet clothes can occasionally get stretched/pulled during the spin cycle, and this causes rips in strange places. I have to manually switch to use low spin speed with every wash load now, and that negates any energy savings of getting the clothes a little more dry by the higher spin speeds.

3rd Update:
I have figured out a way to get more water in the Pure Colors wash: simply pause the washer once it begins washing, open the lid and push/pull/move the clothes around manually, maybe add an extra item to wash. Then close the lid and resume the wash cycle. In a short while, it will intake more water until the max limit, and continue the wash cycle.
It is a pain to have to do this with every wash, but clothes move more freely and tend to wash better this way, I think.

product_title: LG WT1101 4.3 Cu. Ft. Ultra Large Capacity High Efficiency Top Load Washer with SlamProof, White
review_text:
I waited a few months before I wrote a review on this product. I wanted to have time to come to understand how this washer performs and what it's challenges were before I wrote down my thoughts. I think this is a very good washing machine, not worthy of five stars, but surely worth a solid four stars.

This machine has several cycles ranging from 35 minutes to over an hour. However, the actual time is longer than the 35 minutes if the load goes into imbalance and the machine resets itself. This might be frustrating to some but the technology wants the machine to correct itself. Aside from the wash cycles there are rinse and spin or spin only cycles. Do not put waterproof items in the washer as it will damage it.

The most prominent thing you will immediately recognize is how quiet this washer is. Standing next to it you can barely hear it washing. Spin cycles are a little louder, but if your laundry is on the main floor of your house, the machine will not disrupt your activities. The machine advertises that it saves water and energy which may be true, but without submetering your water or electricity, it would be tricky to come at a firm number. The fact that it spins at a high rate of speed (there are four spin settings: high, medium, low, and none) removes a lot of water meaning that your dry times will be faster than a conventional washer with agitator.

To operate the machine simply place your items in the drum and add detergent to the dispenser and select a cycle. The machine will determine load size and the amount of water needed. Note that if you fill the machine plumb full, it will likely go into imbalance mode. If the machine cannot correct the imbalance, it will shut down. This may lead some people to criticize the design, but keep in mind it is not a commercial washer at a laundromat. Think through how much you put in the machine and do two loads if necessary. Again, some will say this will not save as much, but overfilling a conventional washer will not get the clothes clean and cause excessive wear on the motor. Save yourself the hassle and do not fill the machine barrel more than half way. It has a large capacity, 4.3 cu. ft. so you can get a lot of clothes in it.

When I was considering a new washer I knew I wanted something different than the old standard agitator machine. Front loaders seemed too low to the ground if I didn't want to buy the base for an additional $200+ so the choice came down to Samsung or LG. I settled on LG and have been generally pleased thus far. I say I'm generally pleased as I have overloaded my machine and had it stop. I've selected lengthy cycles that seemed to take forever to finish. I've loaded only towels and had the machine go into imbalance. I've learned from my earlier mistakes and am not displeased with my choice. I did purchase a warranty plan from my local appliance dealer because this technology is still relatively new. I may have wasted my money but it seemed like a good idea at the time.

So four or five months into my ownership of this washer I feel like I've gotten to know this machine relatively well. Would I buy it again? Yes. Would I switch to a different brand? Not necessarily. As I said at the start of this review, it is a very good machine, but it's not perfect. I did not buy this from Amazon as I felt more comfortable buying it from a local dealer who can also service my machine should it need repairs. I like this machine a lot and do not regret my selection.

product_title: LG WT1101 4.3 Cu. Ft. Ultra Large Capacity High Efficiency Top Load Washer with SlamProof, White
review_text:
We purchased this LG top load front panel washer and matching gas dryer to replace old Kenmore units. We needed them to fit in the same space. The new front loads would not fit and sit higher. This design was perfect for our space. The lid opens to stay below the wall cabinets. The front panel controls are really convenient.

We were concerned about several reviews that criticized the long cycles and "balancing" at the start of the wash cycle. Some said this step would result in the cycle stopping and forced a reset while you manually re-distributed the load. After 6 weeks of operations including whites, colors, large bed comforters, small loads, etc. we have not had any problems. The washer goes through "dance" at the beginning as it senses the load size and weight. This does take time but seems to work well.

This is a HE washer. So it uses less water .. no center spindle to beat up your clothes. A large load of white underwear with bleach and "soak" cycle can take over one hour. But the closes come out clean and white and the spin cycle can be set on high and they are de-watered completely .. taking less load off the dryer.

We did wash a king bed comforter on cold water, gentle. Looking through the top window you can see how the washer uses little water and the comforter is sitting above the water line. But it works and works on it until it seem happy. The comforter cam out clean and spun dry.

The matching dryer has also worked well. Like the washer there are many combinations of settings. Large loads have come out dry .. if you figure out the right settings.

We have no idea if the warranty service is any good. We purchased our set from Pacific Sales and they say to call them if we need service.

So far we are very pleased with our new washer dryer pair. They also look cool!

product_title: LG WT1101 4.3 Cu. Ft. Ultra Large Capacity High Efficiency Top Load Washer with SlamProof, White
review_title: After 6 months I am buying a different washer.
review_text:
I am taking the loss on my $750 and replacing this washer after only 6 months of use.

If everything works perfectly it takes more than an hour to wash a load, if the load becomes unbalanced, which happens FREQUENTLY, you can be in for 3, 4, or even more hours.

The manufacturer recommends that you wash garments of "somewhat similar weight to allow the washer to evenly distribute the weight of the load for spinning" - in plain language, don't put jeans and shirts together because that will fail about half the time.

In fact according to the manual, The UE code (which means the washer has stopped completely until YOU fix it) can appear because "Heavy articles are mixed with lighter items" or "The load is too small". Sorry, but it is not my fault that you designed an inferior machine, other washers can handle these situations without difficulty.

The software that runs the washer is garbage. When the washer becomes unbalanced it will either stop completely or refill with water to try and balance. It will even refill with water if it is in spin cycle only mode. This creates a loop of fill-spin-fail that repeats endlessly.

My money is down the drain - don't follow with yours.

product_title: LG WT1101 4.3 Cu. Ft. Ultra Large Capacity High Efficiency Top Load Washer with SlamProof, White
review_text:
After WAY too much research into the subject of which washer to buy, we took advantage of the big orange store's deal on the LG WT1101CW; $629, free delivery and pick up of old washer. Also liked the 10 year motor warranty.

Leveling was simple, just used a 3' carpenter's level per the set up instruction sheet. The drum looked evenly spaced from the edges, so I hooked up the water, plugged it in, and threw a load in the huge, stainless drum. I mean, there's room for you and several large friends in there.

We've only had it 4 days, but we've run 6 loads of different sizes and composition, including a load of bathroom-type rugs and towels. Whites, colored, all came out clean and spun pretty darned wrung out, too.

Zero problems with balancing loads so far. Plenty of water in the wash cycle. Tried the "add garment" thing (the "add garment" light has to be lit, per the instructions. You just pause the cycle, wait for the lid to unlock, and toss it in. It does a little re-balancing dance and then takes off again.)

It is very quiet and, yeah, the loads take an hour plus. Thing is, you can run easily twice as much per load, so the time may be a... wait for it... wash, to do your laundry.

i'll update later, but for now we're pretty happy with it. It offers plenty of flexibility in the cycle options, so it will just depend on how reliable it is. Got a feeling that the 15-20 year Whirlpool/Maytag washer days are gone, but it is what it is.

Bummer for those who seem to have gotten a "lemon", but ours seems okay. Be nice if you didn't feel like you were rolling the dice when spending good money on what should be a reliable appliance.

product_title: LG WT1101 4.3 Cu. Ft. Ultra Large Capacity High Efficiency Top Load Washer with SlamProof, White
review_text:
After reading the great reviews in consumers, we were happy to get a good deal on this machine.
It looks good, and has a window so you can watch your clothes get washed, for those of you who may not have cable.

What a mistake, I am not normally writing reviews about washers. I dont normally care. But this thing is making me crazy. It needs to be constantly monitored, and even then, it barely works. There are days when only 1 load can get done, because it shuts off constantly. We have tried every setting. Big loads, small loads. different temp water. Lighting candles and chanting. Still, nothing works. I am writing this now because it was either vent in this review, or take an ax to it!
We have owned this washer for over 6 months, so I have given it a fair chance.

Since 10 am this morning (it is now 4pm) it has been on a single load. For the past 3 hours I set it to "spin only", at the lowest speed. It said 18 minutes. Every time I walk by its full of water again, or turned off or...I just checked, it says 10 minutes to go! Lets see what its doing in another hour.
Listen, you have many fine choices you can make with your hard earned cash.
This piece of crap should not be on the market, period!
You have been warned.

product_title: LG WT1101 4.3 Cu. Ft. Ultra Large Capacity High Efficiency Top Load Washer with SlamProof, White
review_text:
I am beyond happy with this top load HE machine! Had Maytag Neptune for 10 years with little to no issues but was ready for a top load when the Neptune died.

I guess I do the perfect load size because balance issues have been nil. In eight months I've had it read "uneven" one time-- when I crammed it full with sheets and towels that were not evenly distributed. (We do about 6 loads of laundry/week.)

It's is not a huge tub at 4.3 but VERY huge in comparison to my old Maytag and plenty of room for my 14 year old's entire laundry basket or a king size blanket for better reference. It's also very quiet and smooth when running at a full spin cycle.

I am surprised to read so many recent negative reviews. This machine has been awesome.

product_title: LG WT1101 4.3 Cu. Ft. Ultra Large Capacity High Efficiency Top Load Washer with SlamProof, White
review_text: I have had this washer for about 7 wks.  It takes an hour to wash even a tiny load.  You have two options.  Clothes come out wet, looking and smelling exactly as they went in.  Or you get clothes that are coated with detergent and need to be re-rinsed.  The washer "balances" and flattens the clothes to the outside of the drum.  Then the water and the detergent spill into the CENTER of the drum, avoid the actual clothes.  There is only at best a  50/50 chance your clothes will get enough water and/or detergent to get clean.  The efficiency then goes out the window, since you are continually re-rinsing, re-spining, and yes, at times re-washing all of your clothes.  I now have a service call in, since Lowes won't accept return after 30 days. product_title: LG WT1101 4.3 Cu. Ft. Ultra Large Capacity High Efficiency Top Load Washer with SlamProof, White
review_title: DOES NOT CLEAN WELL AT ALL
review_text:
My washer in the 3.6 size is horrible. I wish I had listened to the reviews on here. And had found the LG website reviews before purchasing. We are getting ready to return it. I am so bummed that I didn't fix my old one. Now I can't get it back. JUST FIX YOUR OLD ONE IF YOU CAN. THESE NEW HE WASHING MACHINES ARE PROBLEMATIC. I could get the clothes cleaner by hand!! This washer leaves lint, PET HAIR and soap residue ALL OVER THE CLOTHES!! They don't come clean AT ALL. I normally hang my clothes to dry. Now I am SPENDING MORE MONEY drying clothes that I don't want to fade or shrink just to get the washing machine residue off. Or spending money on lint removers (which don't even remove soap residue well). Clothes look way worse when they come out then when they went in. These clothes aren't even visibly dirty. I haven't tried anything that is truly soiled yet! I've tried all of the trouble shooting stuff too....more soap, less soap, extra rinse, bulky load, tub wash, smaller loads, like items together....NOTHING WORKS!! DON'T BUY THIS MACHINE. YOU WILL REGRET IT!!! OH YA, and it has a very WEIRD mildew type smell. We've only had this washer for about two weeks!! All that being said, we haven't had any balance issues. Maybe they fixed that! I almost wish that was our problem, it might be fixable!!

UPDATE #1: I have now had this machine for two months and it is not performing any better. I tried the green scrubbie and the vinegar that LG recommended to other reviewers on their website. I have now learned another valuable lesson, it is almost impossible to return a poorly manufactured appliance. I am now working with LG to get a return authorization. Mine is the only poor performance review on here for this size, the other purchasers just got lucky. Read the poor performance reviews on Amazon for the bigger machine and on LG's website for this sized machine. I am not the only person having problems. I have read every review and tried every "fix it" trick recommended. I am not using my machine improperly. Other reviewers have recommended learning how to use the machine! The very first load was not clean and every load thereafter. I would sell it on Craigslist or Ebay but will just have a huge mess on my hands when my purchaser gets ticked and wants to return it to me. I'll end up in a lawsuit!! I CAN NOT re-sell this machine with a clear conscious. I may end up being out the $670.19 I paid after tax and extended warranties. A new service guy is coming out in two days. I've already had one here that threatened to charge me if he came out again for a false alarm. He hooked his computer up to it which indicated that it is still within factory specs and is working as manufactured....go figure!

UPDATE #2: The new service man tested my machine and it is again working within factory specs with no repairs needed. I now have figured out that if I do two extra rinses (hit the extra rinse button twice) the clothes come out 90% "clean". The soap residue is mostly gone, but the pet hair is not. I can't wait to see my new water bill. This is using a lot more water than my old dinosaur. I watched it fill up three times to do three complete rinses! So my tub fills up four times now instead of two. How is this energy efficient? I also had a soiled item I washed twice in hot water that was pre-treated with an Oxy Clean Stain stick and it did not come clean as it would have with our old machine. This one also still winds things up, like bra straps even though it has the new agitator design. I'm concerned about trying to find a new one. All of them that I've looked at have issues. I can't imagine any machine working worse than this one though. You also can't soak items for any length of time. The water drains out of the washer within a very short amount of time. You end up with clothes that now have a mildew smell that you thought were soaking in water!!

UPDATE #3: LG has told me that they will not authorize a return since my machine does not have an actual defect that is easy to repair. The supervisor accused me of having buyers remorse. It blows my mind that a company this big does not stand behind their products. I choose to ignore the bad reviews concerning balance (there were no reviews about dirty clothes then) when the salesman I bought this machine from assured me that I could return it. The company where I bought it has since fired that salesman due to the promises that he was making to customers that did not follow company policy. Appliance Factory Outlet will not ever take returns on appliances unless the manufacturer authorizes a return regardless of what a wayward salesman may tell you. Apparently no appliance store can take a machine back and get reimbursed for the machine without the manufactures authorization. They can take them back, repair and/or re-sell though. That is up to the individual stores policies.

PROS: The only good things about this machine are the fact that it has a lid lock (I run a licensed home child care center) and that it is extremely quiet.

review_text:
AVOID AT ALL COST! Oh my gosh, can a washer be considered a nightmare? YES...this washer qualifies. First LG appliance, and I can definately say it will be our last. Purchased last December, and it has been an endless hassle. Looks pretty,functions terribly.

I can't remember the last wash cycle that actually managed to get completed on its own without having to go in and redistribute the clothes 2, 3, 4 or more times. This washer will indicate "Ue" (uneven) while running,which them prompts the washer to try to rebalance itself using loads more water and electricity, the progress to "UE", which means the wash cycle has been interrupted and it has shut itself down. Go in, redistribute the clothes, try again.., more water/power. A wash load that should be completed in 35 minutes can stretch on for 3-4 hours!!! Yes, I have followed all the guidelines: keep loads with similiar weight/type fabrics, don't only wash one or two items at a time. It does not make any difference.

Give me my old, plain, reliable Kenmore washer ANY day...you could throw anything in there, not all the crazy limitations, and it NEVER stopped in a wash cycle.

Bottom line: looks pretty, plays a nice tune at the end of the cycle (if you can ever get to that point, it's like the movie "Groundhog Day") but is an epic fail in the land of washers, keep away if you don't want to drive yourself crazy in the laundry room!

review_title: So far, I'm bummed I bought this machine.
review_text:
I plan to give this washer a chance, but after my first couple loads, I'm not happy.

1) Detergent type. I've got bad MCS allergies and can't use most laundry detergents; BioKleen works for me. What I didn't realize is that this washer wants you to only use particular brands of detergent. The BioKleen label says to use 1/2 a capful for high-efficiency washers, so I assume BioKleen is OK for high-efficiency washers. The instructions to the LG say I'm supposed to be looking for a certain, HE logo on every detergent product. Similary, LG's instructions say nothing about using white vinegar (against odors, mold, and for softening) or Borax. They just say "Oh only use our products, because other stuff might affect the sensors in this machine." I guess this is fine for people who are willing to use nasty, smelly chemicals like Tide. For me and my kids, it's not ideal.

2) Following instructions as best I could -- the half-capful of BioKleen detergent put in the little drawer, and I did add a very small amount of vinegar and some pre-dissolved Borax straight in with the clothes -- I selected the "heavy duty" cycle for clothes after we'd been camping in them. I filled the washer fairly lightly, because I'd read that this washer comes unbalanced easily. The load was pretty quiet and everything seemed fine... until I got the clothes out of the dryer later. They have a peculiar set of wrinkles, and they smell like campfire. Some are stained. Heavy duty? Hardly.

3) Trying to pre-soak clothes the way *I* want to wash them seems surprisingly difficult. If I want to soak a bunch of clothes in a tub of water with some BioKleen oxygen bleach or Borax or whatever, for 20 minutes, and then have the washing machine rinse it down, with old-fashioned washers I was used to being able to do that. Then I could add normal detergent, add some more clothes that didn't need the pre-soak, and run a normal load. This washer doesn't seem to want me to presoak at all! LG says on Bestbuy's site, replying to similar customer confusion, that the "Soak" cycle includes a 30-minute soak -- as part of its mysterious high efficiency cycle.

4) I asked the salespeople multiple times about LG's famed "Allergeine" allergy cycle, and supposedly it's in this machine, but there's no button or indicator that says allergy. Haven't sorted that out yet.

For what it's worth, I did a lot of research before purchasing. I'm unable to use front loaders because they tend to become mildewy more easily than top loaders, and I have a Severe Mold Allergy. Buying another old-fashioned, energy-inefficient washer seemed like a bad idea for the environment and for our water bills. But so far, I'm bummed I bought this washer and dryer. At this rate I'll be doing half the wash by hand in the bathtub, because at least my tub allows me to soak a bunch of clothes if I freaking want to.

product_title: LG WT1101 4.3 Cu. Ft. Ultra Large Capacity High Efficiency Top Load Washer with SlamProof, White
review_title: Kinda wishing it would break so we can replace it with something else. Anything else.
review_text:
First off, I purchased this machine at an actual store and not through Amazon. It is, however, the same model. As I know people check the reviews on Amazon as they research products, I wanted to pass on the knowledge we've gleaned after owning this thing for about a year now. We're a family of 4 and seem to accumulate a rather startling amount of laundry on a weekly basis. This machine has a few "Pros", but some major "Cons". Be aware before you buy.

Pros:
Huge capacity is great. This machine can eat through our Mount Laundry Hamper in just 2 loads, compared to our previous machine's 4 or 5.
Cleans well. Cold cycle is a plus. I've never had anything go in dirty that didn't come out completely clean. No complaints there.
Very quiet. Our L.R is right off our kitchen so a quiet machine was important to us.
Smooth running. No "jumping" or "walking" issues. It doesn't even shake the floor during high speed spins. No complaints there either.

BUT.......
Cons:
Nearly impossible to keep loads balanced: machine runs on computerized wizardry that is heck-bent on keeping the machine in balance. If a load shifts during one of the (many) spin and "back and forth" cycles (which is a common occurrence), it will throw a "uE" code and start refilling with water. Even if you're wash time is down to the final 10 minutes, it may suddenly go off balance and start refilling again, adding an additional 10 to 15 minutes while it attempts to shift the load and balance again. If the "uE" attempts to re balance the load fail, you'll get a "UE" code which will stop the machine. It will wait patiently for you to come and toss the contents (salad, anyone?) and get it going again.

Once a load starts to throw codes at you, you are in for a long laundry day: seriously, no matter what you do, it will keep throwing the stupid "UE" and stopping, or you'll be dealing with constant refilling. I once spent a full 4 hours washing a load of whites. One load. Seriously, true story.

Loads need to be large: That whole Large Capacity thing sure sounds great. However, it's less of a perk and more of a requirement if you want this machine to run well. Too small of a load? Sorry, it won't stay balanced. (Codes galore). Too large of a load? Sorry, won't stay balanced. (Codes galore). I feel like I spend a LOT of my time attempting to find the sweet spot between too small and too big. It's a time wasting endeavor that makes me hate doing the laundry.

Some things refuse to cooperate in there. I can wash quilts. I can wash comforters. But blankets? Forget it. Not gonna happen. Whether I put the blankets in the machine alone or with other "similar weight items", ( per the manual's tips), I can anticipate a few hours of good old fashioned code throwing fun.

Manual tips are ridiculous. The manual suggests loading the machine with materials of the same weight; however, in our family, and I would suspect in many families, that makes the load size too small for this demented machine. If you try to mix the fabric weights, you may get the invite to the dreaded Code Party. Some loads go through without a hitch, others are like the ghost of some awful cooking smell that you just can't get rid of. No rhyme or reason to it.

LG Customer Support is no help. I've tried telling them what I'm dealing with. Their response is a chipper "I can help you with that! Be sure all the loads are of the same weight!" Thanks. Helpful.

In short, this is the first washing machine that we've owned that I find myself hoping will break. And believe me, we will not attempt to fix it when it does. If I had known how impractical it was at the time we bought it....if I had read the reviews a little more thoroughly, this beastly thing would not be taking up space in my home, or on our credit card, right now.

review_title: Intentionally designed for SMALL loads. . . (unwritten advice from LG technician)
review_text:
UPDATE: I returned my LG Wt1101 and am returning to a conventional washer with a central agitator. The fact that this huge washer is DESIGNED for small loads and has no effective setting for more typical medium-sized loads was central to my decision. The first thing I did with my new machine was to re-wash many of the clothes I'd done with this LG HE washer because they reeked of soap and fabric softener.

ORIGINAL POST I've had this washer for two weeks and am still deciding whether to keep it. My complaint, like many other people, is that the water level is so low that clothes are not pulled down into the wash water. After an hour on the phone with a LG technician, I learned this: the different cycles are designed to use different amounts of water. Ignore the given names (e.g. Cotton, Heavy Duty) and think of the cycles in terms water levels.

He said that two cycles, Cotton/Normal and Heavy Duty, are designed to add water only up to 1" above the silver knob in the center bottom of the tub. That equals 5" of water measured from the deepest pockets in the bottom of the tub, but an average of only 4" throughout most of the tub. If you put in more clothes than this, the clothes on top might not get pulled into the water. I put in six long-sleeved t-shirts and the top one did not get pulled down into the water in the Cotton/Normal cycle. Apparently this [stupid] design helps LG qualify for the low water/high efficiency rating on this machine. It would take 54 minutes to wash those six shirts.

Two other cycles, Bright Whites and Pure Color, are designed to add a bit more water. I measured it as 2" from the top of the silver knob and 6" from the deepest pockets in the bottom of the tub, averaging about 5" deep throughout the tub. In addition to the six long-sleeved t-shirts, there was enough water to add three lightweight sweat shirts using the Bright Whites cycle. Together, this load was smaller than what I could do in my old-fashioned 2.4 cubic foot washer with a central agitator. The was cycle was longer than an hour.

One cycle, Bulky Items, is designed to fill the tub and it does. It works well for large loads.

The technician recommended always using small loads and selecting Bright Whites, or using very large loads and selecting Bulky Items, and then manually setting the water temperature, agitation, and spin speed to create the wash I want. There are buttons for water temperature and spin speed; the Soil Level button sets the agitation (more "soil" adds more time and uses a stronger agitation; it does not add more water like I thought). There is no easy way to wash a medium-sized load on this machine because the cycles provide too little or too much water.

He also said it's important to use the Fabric Softener button if softener is used in the Cotton/Normal or Heavy Duty cycle (the manual also mentions this). In those cycles, the default setting uses a spray rinse that will not remove fabric softener from the clothes. Again, this is a trick to reduce water consumption in order to qualify for ratings; it does not provide an effective rinse. By pressing the Fabric Softener button, you override that default and the rinse will "fill" the tub with water in normal rinse fashion. Apparently the other cycles always "fill" the tub during rinse so the Fabric Softener button is not needed for them.

The last thing he said is that the Load Sensing period that occurs before the wash begins is simply an attempt to distribute the clothes evenly; it has nothing to do with judging the weight of the load or assessing how much water will be required. By the way, I've washed some heavy items and have never encountered the unbalanced load problem that others report. I think the trick is to load the clothes as if there were a central agitator in the middle, spreading items around the edges of the tub.

So the bottom line is this: this huge capacity washer works best for very small or very large loads, and the "smart" specialty cycles need to be overridden for almost every load of laundry. I'll try a few more loads now that I have this information but I'm not pleased.

One last word of advice: the washer does not have a way to filter and remove lint or dog hair from the water. I washed a load of dog bedding and then, as I explored this topic of water level, I ran several loads of just water (no clothes) to see how much water entered the tub. Even after filling, spinning, and draining several cycles of water, there still was dog hair floating in the water. The only way to remove it seems to be doing another load of laundry and having it stick to clothes, and then being removed by the dryer. The matching dryer, however, is great at removing lint and dog hair as the clothes tumble dry.

It was getting so bad that I was told to make my current pair of underwear last, because there was going to be no more washing until the washer was fixed. Something had to be done!

review_text:
We bought this washer at Home Depot based on the insanely high number of good reviews, and it was a huge mistake. At least the truth is out here on Amazon! Please listen to all the 1 Star reviews and do not buy this washer. It cannot stay balanced to save its life. I wash a very normal amount of clothes, and it gets to the end of the cycle end with no problems about 1/4 of the time. It very easily goes off balance and cannot spin the clothes dry. But it doesn't simply stop and wait for you to balance things. It quickly re-fills with water to balance the clothes itself. It's trying to save you the effort, but in doing so, the energy efficiency goes down the drain. How is it using less water if almost every load gets an extra rinse? Even if you catch it re-filling, and start again with a "spin only" cycle, you have a problem. Spin only means "spin until I get unbalanced, and start that extra rinse thing again." I basically have to babysit this washer when I do laundry, and I hate it.

UPDATE: After months and months of hating my washer, my hubby was basically offering to buy something and start over. I said how about you just call LG and bug them until they help us (we should not have to spend hundreds on a new washer!), and he did. After a couple calls where they told him to call a repair man (he tried, no one was reasonable and most didn't even want to look at this washer), they finally offered him an LG repairman for $200 flat rate with a guarantee that it would be fixed. Finally, something worth trying. On his first visit, he replaced the "brain," the computer panel and the button panel at the top of the machine. Supposedly the software was out of date which could be causing all the UE codes, extra rinses and loads that could never spin. The load he did worked, but the problem was just the same for the 2 weeks following. So we called again - we want our guaranteed fix! This time he replaced the motor which also contains the sensors. Finally we have a working washing machine!!!!!!! It has not gone UE since. My husband is convinced it was bad sensors this whole time. The wash was never unbalanced or unable to spin, the sensors were going nuts and causing all the problems. I agree, and I think LG should contact EVERYONE complaining of this problem and replace their motor/sensors. If they did that, I would change my star rating, since my washer does work now. However, I think they have a glaring problem in manufacturing somewhere, and they don't care. I would warn people away from buying this washer until that gets fixed.

review_text:
I would like to share my experience with this machine. For the sake of honesty, I purchased the machine from a "brick and mortar" store, but felt compelled to place my review everywhere and anywhere I could if it can save someone the hassle of owning this machine and the ABSOLUTE NIGHTMARE of dealing with LG's customer service - which if I may say is the WORST I have ever dealt with, EVER!

Honestly, this machine worked flawlessly for 8 months. It cleaned the clothes very well regardless of load size. I have no idea why so many people are having trouble with unbalanced load errors; I only had it happen once in 8 months and I reset the clothing, restarted the machine, and it finished without further issue.

Now comes the "warning" for potential purchasers. First and foremost, if you EVER have to deal with LG customer service, my sympathies go out to you because they will just give you scripted responses to your questions that are meaningless and unhelpful in any way, shape, or form. Their only response to a warranty repair request is "we are trying to locate a service technician in your area" and if you check, you will find that many reviewers who have requested service complain about getting the same identical response from LG I did no matter where you live. That is the response I got for 5 days in a row. It took a lot of yelling and threatening to get them to put me through to a manager who was able to authorize service for my machine.

Now on to why I needed service and my current situation. The machine was leaking water all over the place. When we finally got a technician out to check out why, he determined that the plastic "outer basket" was leaking. Not a hose, but the outer basket itself. Upon checking his parts listing, he found no listing for a replacement part. He called LG who told him that they "discontinued making replacement outer baskets" for these machines and the technician stated LG would call me on Monday or Tuesday (this was on a Saturday) with an authorization to get a new washing machine because my machine (this same identical model listed) was "unrepairable" according to LG and the service technician. Although I was upset, I was okay with that particular outcome. Before the technician left he recommended I DO NOT get the same model because some parts for this particular machine are "obsolete" rendering the machine "unrepairable". It is now Friday of the same week and no call from LG as of yet.

My recommendation: DO NOT buy this machine! Because if you should ever need service, LG customer service will do their best to run you around in circles, and some parts for the machine are "obsolete" according to LG themselves. Why is this machine still being sold if some repair parts have been discontinued and are no longer available???? The unfortunate part is, even if I did not have to deal with LG customer service for a warranty repair, I would still be stuck with nothing more than a "doorstop" because I could not get it repaired due to the fact that the particular part I needed was "discontinued" and therefore unavailable, basically rendering the WT1101 "obsolete"!!!

If you never need service, the machine is a wonderful machine, but do you really want to take that chance? For me, I now have a $700 paperweight and am making plans to buy another machine not named LG and hoping I get more than 8 to 9 months out of my next washing machine. Too bad LG does not care about their customers because I really did like this product up until I had this problem and had to deal with a customer service department that does everything in its power to basically blow you off. As the title says, BUYER BEWARE.

EDIT: It has now been 6 weeks since I initially called for service and 5 weeks since LG was informed by their technician that the washer is "unserviceable". I still call them almost every day to no avail, and suspect I will get absolutely nothing out of it considering the plethora of reviews around the internet describing the exact same "customer service" experience that I have had. I have since bought another washer, obviously NOT an LG product. I will say this again, do yourself a favor and avoid this company's products at all costs; unless of course you believe you will never have an issue with what you bought! Why take that chance???

product_title: LG 3.6 CF FRONT LOAD WASHER DRYER COMBO
review_text:
I did not purchase this unit from Amazon, I purchased from Living Direct.
I came with all the necessary attachments and tools. (did not have to pay extra)
I also purchased the extended warranty considering how expensive the unit was.

If you are hard core hot air dryer addict, then you probably won't like this unit.
Vent-less drying means it dries clothes like an air-conditioner via dehumidifying / condensing.
Clothes will have a slight "damp" feeling when you first pull them out, but in a minute or two they are dry.

Pros - keeps your home cool because it does not radiate heat
- it is extremely cost efficient.
- clothes come out incredibly clean and NO soap residue
- you don't have to move laundry from the washer to a dryer YAY
- uses extremely small amount of water! Incredibly environmentally friendly!
- it's great for limited space, or apartment living where washer/dryer hook-ups are lacking
- no risk of a dryer fire breaking out!
- perfect for delicate fabrics that are easily damaged by heat
- much less shrinkage of clothes
- colors do not fade like they do from heat drying
- clothes still come out soft without using fabric softener, but even more so if you do.
- no more dryer sheets to control static cling! OH YEAH!
- clothes do NOT come out wrinkled if you remove them within an hour or so of finishing
- the powerful spin cycle means clothes hung to dry will dry fast even when indoors
- only need space for ONE UNIT.. instead of 2
- does not require exterior venting (huge plus factor!)
- say goodbye to public laundry mat
- it sings an adorable tune to let you know your laundry is done =) Not annoying.

Cons - no.. you cannot throw something in and have it come out dry 10 minutes later.
- it can take double the time to dry items than a conventional dryer (but sill less $$$)
- lint.. you must manually remove the lint or do a load w/o drying to wash out lint
- you cannot leave the laundry in the machine for an excessive amount of time.
.. of course.. even with a regular dryer leaving laundry sit is bad news...

NOTE: YOU NEED TO FOLLOW MANUFACTURER INSTRUCTIONS AND RUN THE CLEANING CYCLE EVERY MONTH!
If you don't then problems can and probably will arise. (I have not had a single problem)

I recommend leaving the door open after use to completely dry out the interior.
Remember that it is based on a wet system so just use some common sense.

DIRECT DRIVE means a turbine engine on steroids. It spins hard and fast.
YOU MUST MAKE SURE THE UNIT IS PERFECTLY LEVELED or it will bounce and get damaged.
When leveled, it functions smoothly and quietly. Some vibration on highest spin cycles.

Yes, it will wash comforters and quilts up to double/queen but won't let you dry them.
You must hang them to dry but due to the spin cycle they dry in no time when hung.

There is an incredible array of features and options that are easy to use except for one.
The setting for washers on wooden floors to suppress vibrations (it works fantastic), but it
requires holding the stain button down for a couple of seconds and listening for beeps.
It's hard to know when it's on. That's my only pet peeve.
They really should have created a separate button for this function.

I've had it 8 months now and never had a problem.
Customer service was great when I called in for assistance with the vibrations suppressor.

review_title: Ok dryer, terrible LG customer service
review_text:
First, the is a review of the LG dryer, not of the seller.

I've owned this LG dryer for 8 months now, and it functions (mostly) okay. All things considered, it is over-priced for the features that we use. I didn't find the steam function effective at all and ended up using an iron on the items I tried. The moisture sensor routinely stops the dryer early even when adjusted to dry longer. The moisture sensor is only reliable for items of the same density (all towels, etc.)

My major complaint is with LG customer service. The white paint is peeling away from the entrance for the clothes (right next to the lint trap), exposing metal beneath. These little white chips of paint end up in my clothes. I contacted LG customer service. They told me this was a "cosmetic" issue and would not be covered under warranty. After speaking to a "manager", they agreed to send a technician out to look at it... who charged $78 to tell me the same thing. This dryer is not inexpensive, I expect better quality in this price range. I've had a handful of dryers over the past 20+ years (cheaper than this one), and I've never had an issue like this. At issue here is the "cosmetic" label, which gets LG out of warranty coverage.

Based on this experience with LG customer service, I will not be purchasing an LG appliance again.

review_title: Nice fan, questionable customer service antics.
review_text:
After our cheapo vent fan bit the dust, we wanted to get something much better. This fan has a cool look and I love the simplicity of the push-button controls. The grease trap is simple to remove for cleaning. The fan also offers back-vented, top-vented and recirculating mounting options. The dual halogen lights are much better than the cheesy 40 watt bulb our old unit had. This fan moves a lot of air (rated at 300 cfm) when you need it to and at it's highest setting you can still hold a conversation. The cons are minimal, in my opinion, but they are worth mentioning. The top surface sticks out further than I anticipated, I believe this is so the recirculating vent is exposed, if needed. It is about 2 inches proud of the cabinet face frame. It is also about an inch and a half shorter, so we had to fill in the backsplash, that was a minor inconvenience. I'm pretty sure the dimensions are given, I just didn't compare them. All in all, I am very pleased with the look and functionality of this fan. There are many options in this price range and I'm glad I chose this one.
A few weeks ago, one of the buttons fell into the housing. I contacted Frigidaire and they tried to weasel out of a warranty job by sending me the part, calling it a "cosmetic issue" that wasn't covered. I kindly requested them to send a repair man and they did. The repair was made under warranty.

review_title: Repaired LG LFC23760 (not cooling fridge and freezer)
review_text:
My parents LG refrigerator and freezer had stopped cooling completely and we could hear a clicking sound which led us to believe that the compressor was not starting and that we needed to replace the start relay or the capacitor. When I tried to look up the start relay I could not find anything that looked correct ( I was looking for the original piece with slots for the capacitor to plug into). After reading many reviews on multiple sites I realized that LG had changed the start relay so instead of getting the old piece you need to order this Overlay and the start relay LG Electronics 6748C-0004D Refrigerator Start Relay (also on amazon). The two pieces fit together to replace the original 3 pin start relay on the LG LFC23760 and also once you get these pieces you no longer need a capacitor.

That last confusing thing was figuring out where the plugs in the back go as now there are 3 slots and the original had only 2 slots. I found a review online which said " Replaced the start relay and overload. I had only a blue wire and black, no pink. I put the black wire on the relay terminal toward the inside of fridge. The blue went on the overload." I followed this persons advice the refrigerator and freezer are now working perfectly. [[ASIN:B00AUDA0GQ LG Electronics 6748C-0004D Refrigerator Start Relay]]

review_text:
I purchased the LG LFX25991ST as part of a whole-house remodel and was sold on the French Doors and the spacious interior for a counter depth fridge, even though the price was pretty steep. I am a little annoyed by a few things:

1) The stainless-steel doors have an imperfect curvature to them that makes them look dented in. I thought it was a result of careless installation, until I noticed the LG refrigerator in the commercial had similar imperfections.
2) You can't stick magnets on the stainless steel doors! There's maybe a hot spot or two where you might be able to put up a magnet, but it's so weak you can't expect it to hold up much. We've sadly had to tape pictures to the fridge. I never thought this would be an issue, but it is.
3) The water dispenser is awkward to use since it comes out of a different spout than the ice dispenser. I've had plenty of embarrassed friends and family spill water all over the floor. The lever that activates the water dispenser also scratches easily.
4) Both the fridge and freezer sections lose their cool fairly quickly. I typically find a layer of frozen droplets throughout the freezer compartment from condensation.
5) As other reviewers have pointed out, the ice maker can get stuck every now and then as there isn't a proper mechanism to break up the ice once it's fuses together.

While most of these issues aren't enough for me to return the fridge outright (I'm a pretty low maintenance guy, what can I say), I also wouldn't recommend this fridge for the reasons above. My produce is pretty fresh, and with a little Tetris, I can get all of my groceries to fit pretty easily. But for a fridge this expensive it should be amazing, and amazing this is not.

product_title: LG LFX25991ST 24.5 Cu. Ft. Counter-Depth French Door Refrigerator with Smart Cooling Plus
review_text:
My background is fixing restaurant, refrigeration & commercial AC equipment. This review is for the LG LFX25991ST & includes a BACK to BACK comparison with the Samsung counter depth side by side model RSG257AARS/XAA.

PROS

High cubic foot capacity among the 36" wide french door, counter depth models.
Looks good, nice sliding action on the drawers, nice lighting.

CONS

Known defect in defrost cycle, this is VERY important; all modern frost free 'fridges enter a defrost cycle to rid itself of frost / ice.
Ice is accumulating on the back panel of the freezer, near the evaporator coil & fan.
They (LG) tried to engineer a fix but it's only partially effective, they will replace the main circuit board, the new one will have a LONGER defrost cycle (it will now use more energy than what your yellow energyguide sticker said) & change out that back panel which includes two fan motors (one is for the ice maker).

Even though our house is always between 30-50% RH ice still accumulates.

The compressor has started vibrating, causing bottles & misc items within the fridge to rattle.

The leveling system is poor & contributes to make the fridge unnecessarily wobbly when the doors are opened & closed, I made wood shims to help but it doesn't eliminate the wobbles, no matter the surface - I compared on concrete & my kitchen's wood floor. It really gives a flimsy feel for an otherwise nice looking fridge.

Controlling proper temps & humidity in the fresh vegetable drawers has been very poor without blocking off cold air ducts.

French door design is in vogue but it has a lot going against it...think about this compared to a side-by-side...

* You remove the entire contents of your freezer whenever you open it. Hope you don't plan to have that 'fridge in your retirement years. It also exposes all the freezer contents to outside air, moisture in the air quickly turns to frost on your contents & drawer. It requires more effort to find things in the freezer which tend to be buried like a chest & you are in a hunched over position looking for them.

* The freezer drawer sliders are more complex than a simple hinged door, they carry a lot of weight & break much more frequently. Simply pulling from the side of the pull handle (asymmetrical force) instead of the center can cause the drawer to go off kilter & make trouble.

* There's more gasket surfaces meaning more areas that can leak or for condensate & mold to form on, plus a cheesy center partition that can develop condensation (because it's not heated) & is susceptible to failure.

* In order to have ice in the door the ice maker is in the refrigerator section so it's not uncommon for ice to partially melt & clump together causing dispenser jams. A separate ice maker fan forces freezer air via ducts to the ice maker - not the best engineering to go about making & delivering ice - more stuff to go wrong. The SBS actually has the ice & ice maker in the freezer, BRILLIANT!

* MANY times it is necessary to open BOTH doors to get something out when it used to be only one with a SBS. Organization is not that good in these.

Three service calls & LG has agreed to replace - our point of purchase is getting a full credit from LG & we can now pick another brand/model from them - we are going back to a SBS. The irony is we're as happy to get away from this fridge as we were when we got it! :^)

UPDATE

We've only had the new replacement, a 24.5 cubic foot Samsung SBS model RSG257AARS/XAA for a few days so this is only an early impression but we do like it MUCH better.

Now this is IMPORTANT & something other reviewers CAN"T comment on...We've had BOTH fridges loaded with the same groceries BACK to BACK & the difference is HUGE...

PROS

MUCH BETTER use of space, we transferred everything out of the 3/4 full LG, put it in the Samsung & it was AMAZINGLY less full AND better organized. Plus, enough room for all the condiments AND a gallon of milk in the door (not so with the LG). Space is a BIG deal when considering a counter depth fridge, we would have never believed it without owning both but the Samsung side by side EXCELS IN SPADES over the LG FD!

Everything is easier to ACCESS, the difference is not slight, we are happy to ditch the "French door" style, ooo-la-la, good rid-dens.

Exterior door display is MUCH easier on the eyes at night.

Two out of three people say it looks better, the third (me) is undecided.

Can place it more flush against the back wall, per the mfrs spec, this is partly due to how it draws condenser air, the Samsung draws air from the front & the side ensuring that heated condenser air isn't recirculated, the LG draws & discharges condenser air from the back, so you will definitely get recirculated condenser air if you're placing against a wall especially so in an alcove. Samsung includes a flat angled type wall plug on the power cord so you push it back further if your receptacle is behind the fridge.

Quieter - vibrates & is noisy at initial start (warm box) but completely acceptable when temps are at normal operation. Ice dropping into bin (especially an empty bin) during the harvest cycle is somewhat loud but infrequent & really a non-issue.

Doors can open wider so be careful not to open them into nearby items like pantry doors or an open dishwasher.

Costs less.

CONS

Leveling system is no better, just two leveling feet in the front, fridge wobbles a bit but not as bad as the LG.

Lighting is not as bright as the LG since food items tend to block a lot of it, lighting does ramp up on this one.

Exterior fit & finish is good but the LG has the edge there.

For those with pets, periodically accessing & cleaning the condenser coil on any fridge is a must, this one is more difficult to complete that task than the LG.

A lot of people complain about the drawers not opening far enough but they DO open ANOTHER increment if you open the doors all the way, in that case they open plenty. Limiting how wide they open for normal use helps prevent stress & potential for breakage. We are totally OK with this design. The drawer rollers aren't as smooth as the LG.

I hope this helps :^)

7-6-14 UPDATE: Still happy to have ditched the LG for the Sammy CD SBS.

review_title: Best Counter-Depth French Door Fridge Available
review_text:
After doing extensive research with Consumer Reports, reading hundreds of reviews and playing around with dozens of fridges, we decided to take the plunge and purchase this fridge (through Amazon). We bought it from the HCcost which did a great job of communicating with us about the delivery. Delivery took about 2 weeks, which is pretty standard. HCcost gave "white-glove" service where they will deliver the fridge to any room in the house and will take away any boxes. For $40 more, they took away our old fridge too. Prices on Amazon were substantially lower than the two major home improvement stores even when they offered their annual sale on appliances.

THE GOOD:

Style: The fridge is beautiful. The front of the fridge is slightly curved out which means that it will almost always capture some light from your kitchen and shine (similar concept to a diamond). The LG in the top right corner is not very obtrusive and blends in well with the front. The front display panel and water/ice dispenser blend in well with the stainless steel front. The sides of the fridge are matte gray and also blend in fairly well with the stainless look (though in most installations you will not see most of these).

Fridge Space: This fridge has the highest amount of storage space in a French Door Cabinet Depth as of early 2014. On top of this, LG did a superb job of laying out the space in the fridge. The in-door ice-maker is flat and level. This allows you to put tall condiments in all areas of the left door (something you can't do in the Samsung model). This also means the top left shelf inside the fridge does is not impeded by the ice-maker.

Freezer Space: I went from a Side-By-Side (SBS) to a French door. This unit does have less freeze space than the SBS units, but does do the best job I have seen of any French door of organizing the space. The freezer opens to reveal the main lower drawer and automatically pulls out a second smaller drawer within it. There is also a third fairly large drawer you can pull out at the top. Having these three different drawers makes a huge difference since you don't have to pile food all in one giant drawer and just dig around to find anything. This is the only French Door cabinet depth model that has this feature (don't be fooled by the 4 door models - the 4th door is always fridge space, not freezer space). There is also a separator for the main drawer to help with organization and a tiny fold out shelf for spices.

Lighting: This fridge has excellent bright LED lights everywhere. Many other models have trouble lighting the different drawers, or the top left shelf (where lighting can be blocked by the icemaker). Even the freezer has good lighting on all shelves. The front panel lights be set to turn of after 15 seconds or so of opening the fridge except the ice indicator (cubes vs. crushed). The water and ice dispenser both turn on a light which makes it easy to see the water level in clear/translucent glasses at night.

Ease of Use: The freezer has an easy-open handle which breaks the air seal making it easy to open the bottom drawer (many units lack this feature). The top doors both open easily, though the right door is much easier to open than the left door. The ice-maker door is easy to open and the ice container is fairly easy to remove. Inside the refrigerator section, the largest drawer can be set to three temperatures and can be opened with both of the top doors open just past 90 degrees (some of the French doors require you to swing both doors open 120 degrees or so to access this drawer.

Noise: I am very sensitive to noise and wanted to get one of the quietest fridges out there. It is impossible to test this in person in any store since they don't have them turned on and the stores are usually noisy anyways. According to Consumer Reports, this fridge scored tied for the best rating for noise as of 2013 (Samsung was the other manufacturer they tied with).

That being said, the fridge is still a cooling unit and requires fans/compressors to run. The LG unit uses two compressors (one for the freezer and one for the fridge). Both of them are very quiet. One of the fans on my freezer that circulates the air does make a little bit of high-pitched whirl which is a tad annoying. My fridge is not within an alcove (many kitchens have a three walled spot for the fridge), so this may be one of the reasons I can still hear a small amount of noise (or it is possible the fan is defective). But in any case, this is likely about the quietest fridge you can buy today.

Smell: There is a carbon-based (de-odorizing) air filter on this unit. I thought this was a major gimmick, but it does actually keep the air smelling fresher. Note that this is primarily an odor filter, not a particle filter (like for your house AC). This filter is a huge money-maker for LG as you now have to purchase two filters from them every 6 months (water and air). If the smell never bothered you before on your fridge, you can simply not replace the filter for several years (since it is primarily an odor filter and not a particle filter it will not heavily impede airflow). However, if you are going to spend the money on a cabinet depth fridge, you can probably afford to replace these (I think they are about $12 a filter). I am sure in the future there will be some generic brand that you can get for even cheaper (they have several now for the water filters).

THE BAD:

Ice Quantity: The amount of ice that can be produced per day is fairly low. The unit does come with an extra ice pale in the freezer so you can dump the top container into this if you are expecting to have a party. I do not use ice except for making mixers, so this is not a problem for me. If you have a family of four that likes ice in every glass of liquid they drink, this may be an issue for you. Note: the cubes that come out are smaller than normal fridge ones. I like these since there is less of a chance of them freezing together into one big block of ice in your glass and you are not forced to imbibe crushed ice chunks.

Water Temperature: The water that comes out of this unit is cool, but not cold. I personally like room temperature water, so this is a plus for me, but most people expect water to be cold. The water filter does a good job of purifying the water, so the water does taste good (and thus does not need to be chilled for taste reasons). If you want cold water, you will have to add ice and therefore you may run into the above issue of the unit not producing enough ice per day.

Ice/Water Paddles: These two paddles that you press your glass against are not designed well for two reasons. First, these two paddles scratch fairly easily. If you get a new unit, I would advise putting ultra-clear package tape over these two panels (or some other type of protection). These paddles can likely be replaced if you need new ones, but it really seems like a design oversight. Secondly, these two paddles are not angled towards your glass. This means you have to press the very top of your glass directly against the paddle to get ice or water. If you re-fill your glass, this becomes a sanitation issue as you press the area where your mouth touches the glass against the paddle. My work around for this is to hold the glass in place and then press the paddle down with my other hand (this actually works for both issues). Again, this is a design flaw. You could easily add some one-sided gray foam tape to fix this problem (if you can stomach the look of it).

Non-magnetic Front: Yes, this unit has a stainless steel front. No, you can't attach magnets to it. This is true with almost all French Door stainless fridges. This does force you to have a very clean looking front of the fridge which I personally like. If you like to use magnets on your fridge, you can stick them on the side of the fridge or you can tape on a magnetic board. For Christmas cards and the like, we attach paper clips and hang these on a horizontal string up along the wall.

CONCLUSION:

Overall this is a very well designed fridge and in my opinion is the best available Cabinet Depth French Door fridge on the market. It is quiet, well organized and designed. There are some ice quantity limitations and minor issues with the water/ice dispenser paddles. However, it really excels at it's primary function of keeping food persevered and accessible.
