product_title: GE CFE29TSDSS Cafe 28.6 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel French Door Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_text:
PROS:

1. Innovative FEATURES

2. Nice design

3. LOTS of room

CONS:

1. (Major) Horrible refrigerant cooling system design, function, durability and reliability(the WHOLE point of a fridge to begin with)

2. (Major) Very loud, disturbing noises after a few months

3. Fridge is not made to last - would be surprised if they lasted more than a year. Mine lasted 4 months with light use, and being babied.

3. (Major) GE Customer Service - will take a miracle to get them to do anything and even to respond to calls.

4. (Minor) Doors should lay flush against the fridge cabinet, when open, to easily remove drawers for cleaning.

5. (Minor) No feature for auto fill, convenient for multi-tasking when cooking.

6. (Minor) Hot water dispenser only holds about 9 oz of hot water. This feature is kind of a waste and unnecessary, I still use my tea pot.

REVIEW

My husband and I bought the GE CFE29TSDSS, Cafe refrigerator with hot water dispenser in May 2013. We have paid for it dearly.

When it was first installed this fridge ran wonderfully, was quiet, and a joy to have. We loved all of the "features".

Four months later, the fridge started to make grinding noises nearly 24-7, as well as sounding like an airplane was taking off in our kitchen. We called GE to have a tech come out and look at it.

The next day we received a box from GE that contained parts for the repair. GE did NOT communicate with me that they were doing this. They also failed to inform their OWN technician they were doing so. When he arrived, he was very apologetic, but informed us that he was not going to be able to fix our fridge for another week. GE hadn't allotted him enough time for our fridge repair, which he said would take at least 2 hours. GE only gives their techs 1/2 hour for each service call, unless the tech lets dispatch know in advance that the call is going to take longer. Our tech couldn't do that because he didn't know GE sent the parts box.

The day of his 1st repair visit he was 1 1/2 hour late. I tried calling GE several times to find out where he was, and no one was able to put me through to their dispatch unit. None of the GE customer service reps seemed willing or able to help me. They just told me to wait and that he would be here soon.

He was also late the next week. This time when I called GE, they told me that they didn't have an appointment scheduled for our fridge until the following day - yet the automated system confirmed our appointment for when the tech told me he would be here.

So, I was waiting around, wondering if the tech was even going to arrive.

He did arrive that day, but he was again late. Please, it is NOT the technicians fault, he has to follow the dispatcher's instructions, and is given very little time to complete jobs, which means he is constantly overbooked and short on time.

He started the repair and accidentally broke the copper refrigerant line. We do not blame the technician, since GE used the cheapest copper they could get their hands on for this fridge. The slightest touch broke it in half. This discouraged us, we expected more from a $3000 American made, high end appliance.

So, the tech had to reschedule again since he had to order the part that he accidentally broke.

He came back the next day, did the repairs, which took nearly 3 1/2 hours, and started the fridge up.

He told me to give it 24 hours to start cooling again. I thought that was odd because it started cooling within 2 1/2 hours of delivery and installation. Well, long story short, it never cooled down. The internal temp of the fridge stayed at 62 degrees.

We called again, and we had to wait another two days for the tech to come out again. The poor tech spent another 3 1/2 hours trying to fix it. The fridge at this point was beyond repair, and he informed us even the GE manufacturing plant would junk it - they wouldn't even scrap it for material.

So we have a broken fridge, were given a case number, and given the name of our case manager. You'd think the case manager would have called us, right away, when she saw the notes and situation.

Wrong. WE had to contact GE to initiate replacing or refunding our money. I have talked to GE over the course of a week about 12 times, and have left message after message for OUR assigned case manager to give me a call. She STILL has not called us back.

Because this fridge is on back order where we live, they wanted to to replace our $3000 fridge with a less expensive model and NOT reimburse us the difference. When I declined, they then offered me a more expensive model, and I asked them if they were going to eat the cost, they said I would have make up the difference. Either way, GE was asking for more money from us on a product that was faulty the minute it left the factory floor - our technician admitted to that fact.

I did, however, manage to get through to one of the reps who I hope will help us through their buy-back process. I am still awaiting confirmation she received our faxes to start the process. I can only hope she comes through.

On top of this, we had MAJOR food loss over the course of 3 weeks, over $500 worth of organic produce and food. GE wasn't going to pay for any of this, we literally had to fight with them to get even a portion of this loss back. We did our best to keep our food cool in a cooler, but most food needs to stay dry as well, which is difficult to manage in a cooler. Produce is particularly vulnerable to wet conditions.

I could literally go on and on about this experience and the lies and runaround that GE IS currently putting us through. Our next step is to write a letter to GE Corporate Headquarters and seek legal counsel if they don't respond to us soon.

I would NOT recommend this product, nor any GE product, to anyone, not even my worst enemies.

review_title: Best refrigerator I have ever owned.
review_text:
I have had this GE cafe for 10 months, so plenty of time to form opinions.

Pros:
* Has the straight, clean lines of professional refrigerators that are $6000+. I had a hard time finding a fridge that I liked aesthetically, that was not $7000, so this fit the bill.
* Monster fridge - I can never complain about not having enough room to hold everything.
* Love the 3rd fridge drawer that you can temp set. There are 5 or 6 options to set to the perfect temp or your needs.
* The other 2 vegetable bins hold fruit and produce perfectly. No more frozen lettuce with this refrigerator.
* Over 9 cubic feet in the freezer. Plenty of room for the summer berries I freeze every year.
* Front door dispenser. What a surprise. I have never had one and really did not want, but my other fridge was broken and I needed to pick out something quickly. I use this so much more than I ever thought I would.
* Love the hot water button. Quick, hot, filtered water.
* Love having filtered cold water as well as filtered ice in two size options.
* Turbo boost - for cooling the fridge or freezer. Cools down a pot of still warm soup really fast. Also turbo boost for the air filter. Put some spicy food in the fridge. This will eliminate smells asap.

Cons:
* The salesperson, the installer and I separately measured to make sure this big fridge would fit in the space I had. Well it did not because no one accounted for the front door hinges that require about 2 more inches than the box height that was listed. I had to have my cabinet raised. What a pain.
* Wish the front doors were more low profile. Not sure I have ever seen door that thick.
* Yes, there is noise from the motor as other mention. It is not that loud and my kitchen is on another floor from the bedrooms, so no issues.
* Still not a big fan of french doors. I love a single door. Impossible to find single door refrigerators that fit the space I have that were not super high price wise.
* There is a shelf that you can drop down (below what I assume is the butter shelf) in the right size of the door to use. Great idea, but it drops too low for me. It would be super functional if it had an adjustable height that you could use.
* Upload pictures to the front of the fridge. Silly, but I am sure someone likes it. I would rather have clean lines, so I do not use.

Pros totally outweigh the cons. Best fridge I have ever owned...

review_title: The reason GE is on the decline
review_text:
Like 60s and 70s technology?

Well, here’s the prize for you.

Unfortunately, it’s not quite what I had hoped for.

It took me nearly 3 months of waiting in order to finally get this unit only to discover it’s new-old stock. Turns out this was a Canadian bound washer from 2019 as evidenced by the labels on the unit. Not only that, but the product registration cards were addressed to a Canadian source. As an afterthought, somebody was nice enough to tape an American registration card on the box.

To be fair, this unit made the trip from Canada to Florida without a scratch, although some things were missing.

For example, the instructions for installation stated a hose was to be included. Nope, that didn’t happen. And what if you call the manufacturer like I did on a previous GE product? “Sorry, about that, we’ll mail you a part – you should get it within 4 to 6 weeks”.

4 to 6 weeks? My installer wasn’t planning on living with me for that amount of time so I ended up having to pay $36 extra for parts that should have been included.

I was also supposed to get an instructional manual on how to operate the unit. Nope, not there, either. Fortunately, easy enough to get off the internet, but still these things should be included.

Installation was a no-brainer.

And that’s where the fun begins. This unit comes with no insulation blanket but, to be fair, some just don’t come with one. Believe me, you’ll want it later on.

Why? I live next to an airport that has 707’s flying in an out. This will drown them out.

More on that later.

Now for the 60s and 70s quip above. Remember the rotary dials you used to have on washers and TVs back then? The type that sounded like you were grinding coffee as you turned them? Well, you got it here.

So, you turn and grind until you hit the cycle you want and then close the latch.

Clunk number 1. That’s the audible signal the washer is starting. It’s not a beep or chime, it’s an audible thump akin to closing a car door.

Now comes the water. No doubt it’s working, you can hear it sloshing inside.

Clunk number 2. Best as I can figure, that’s the soap dispenser opening.

Shake and shimmy. This washer has the most vibration I have ever experienced in a dishwasher. It vibrates so much that it actually loosened the level supports on the bottom. I have to physically put those levelers back to floor level after every couple of washes.

Slosh, slosh and slosh again. Rattle, rattle and clink (that’s the dishes clanging together sometimes) and then silence.

Waiting for the end of cycle beep? Nope, for $400 you don’t get that. You’ll have to guess when it’s over or take a look at the dial.

Some of you may have noticed you do have a heat dry option along with the option to shut it off.

This does work, but unlike my previous washer, it doesn’t lessen the cycle time. Instead of skipping the 20 minute dry cycle, this machine just stops sloshing water and lets the dishes air dry for 20 minutes. Sure, you can open the washer and take the dishes out at this point, but you’ll have to close the latch again to complete the cycle. Either that, or use the “grind it till you find it” rotary dial.

Now, to be fair, this unit cleans and cleans very well. I have no problems there. It’s just that this unit is over $160 more than I paid a year earlier for a digital unit without the issues and vibrations.

And the icing on the cake? It's not rated as energy efficient so if you're expecting a rebate from your utility company, dream on!

If you can wait, please do yourself a favor and get a different unit.

Since I'm not interested in spending $200 on repair parts for this trash every year, I'm replacing it. It's a dishwasher, not a subscription service.

Don't be fooled into thinking that because there is a manual dial and it's lower tech that there is less to go wrong and it will last longer. The gears in the timer are cheap plastic and wear out quickly, causing the machine to not switch cycles properly. If it gets stuck in draining mode just a little too long the solenoid will burn out, or maybe even your drain pump. It's a known issue with this machine. The whole thing will burn up due to a crappy cheap timer.

You've been warned.

product_title: Frigidaire EFIC102 Counter Top Ice Maker, Silver, 26lb per day
review_text:
I received this rather slowly, but after unpacking it, it was extremely simple to operate. No guesswork, and only a few buttons.
I plugged it in, filled it with a couple of quarts of water, selected "small cubes" and in about 8 minutes the first batch was delivered, and every 8 minutes after that until the bin was full and "ice full" lit up on the control panel. I emptied the bin into a freezer container and pushed "start" again. It takes about an hour and a half to fill the bin, which is equal to about two ordinary ice cube trays, which is about a quart of water, so in three or four hours, you have the equivalent of four ice cube trays to store in your freezer.
The "large" ice cubes are about 50% bigger than the "small." Neither is really large, but I prefer the small size. They also work better in my ice crusher (Hamilton Beach) for even finer ice for super cold drinks.
This machine does make a little noise from the fan and when it empties the ice into the bin, but it's a kind of reminder that it's on, because if you leave it in the ice maker, it will melt and then make the same ice over and over, which is terribly wasteful. It is not a freezer. You have to get some plastic bins from 99 cent store or Walmart and then find a place in your freezer.
Occasionally the ice will be melted slightly, causing it to stick together in your plastic containers. If you get a metal ice scoop you can break the ice apart with that. Even better is a meat tenderizer mallet which will break it apart in just a couple of whacks.
This is small enough to fit in an out of the way place (on a low table, for instance) yet big enough and fast enough to make plenty of ice for everyday use or parties.

product_title: GE CYE23TSDSS Cafe 23.1 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel Counter Depth French Door Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_text:
We wanted a cabinet depth refrigerator as we don't like our fridge sticking out too far from the cabinets. We had a GE prior to this one and I swore I would never buy another GE refrigerator again. It was about 10 years old and was their top of the line cabinet depth back then. Thank goodness for extended warranty as we had numerous calls on it which unfortunately continued after when we had to pay about another $400 to keep it running. Ferraris have this sort of maintenance needs, not GE appliances....

I was looking at Samsung and LG options and was sold on going that route when my wife found this model online. I was not thrilled about it, but agreed to look at it since she liked the looks and features. A local large box home appliance retailer said they could get it for me and the price was right - with their 5 year extended warranty - so I went ahead with it.

So far it has been a very nice refrigerator. I really like the LED lighting. It really lights up the interior so much better than the old incandescent bulbs of the past. And it gives it a rich look. The LCD panel on the front is an attractive feature and does things like tell you how much water you're dispensing in ounces. Very nice, for example, if you want need 8 ounces of water. It counts it off for you. It also has a neat animated background when in use. Just a nice detail that makes it feel "rich" without being gimmicky.

The hot water dispenser is a very unique feature I have not seen on any other refrigerator. It is good for tea, soups, etc. It takes several minutes to warm up, as you may expect, but is more convenient that boiling water on the stove. So far we've only used it a few times, but I can see where this would be a handy feature once you remember you actually have it.

It runs quiet and efficiently. The ice maker works very well. It took about 8 to 12 hours before ANY ice was made so don't be alarmed if you don't see any ice making activity for the first 6 or 8 hours. I was ready to call service on this but it must take time for it to get started. (Yes, I know ice doesn't freeze instantly.... It just seemed to be a long time until ANY was made.)

The freezer has multiple levels and 2 pull out drawers, so organizing your food should be easy. Going from a side-by-side to this will take some getting used to, but we don't have a ton of freezer stuff and we have a second refrigerator in the garage where we keep items less often used, so ours is still mostly empty. You will have to judge this based on your own habits.

The "fun" feature is the ability to use the LCD panel as an electronic picture frame. I am a gadget person so I tried this out. There is a USB port under a rubber cover where the ice/water dispense. THIS IS NOT documented in the manual so I had to find it on my own. It immediately recognized the USB drive and uploaded the pictures. Note, it only does a full overwrite of what is on there, so you can't simply add or delete pictures. Load your pictures on a USB drive, plug it in, and it simply replaces everything on the fridge with what is on your drive. When you use the panel for water or ice, it will then display your pictures for some period of time as a slide show(not sure how long - 10 minutes maybe?) Unfortunately GE engineers don't allow any customization of this feature. It's just an upload and display item; you can't adjust anything about how they display. There is NO documentation in the manual that I could find so if you like this feature you will have to sort this out on your own. (See my reply below with a more detailed explanation of this process!)

Overall our first month has gone well. The store explained that the manufacture of GE refrigerators has moved from Mexico back to the US and they've seen an uplift in quality. (I did look and my old GE was made in Mexico and this one is made at Appliance Park in Kentucky.) So will see how that plays out long term. Given the Cafe line is supposed to be their best, I anticipate much better service than the Artica model I had before.

product_title: GE CYE23TSDSS Cafe 23.1 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel Counter Depth French Door Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_title: Love the special features, but don't love the space/configuration issues.
review_text:
I have had this fridge for just over 3 months and bought it because I have really like my GE Cafe gas stove. There are things I love about this fridge and things that are disappointing.
First what I love…
The hot water dispenser, it's fairly quick and gives me the temp I need. I thought it was silly at first, but am amazed by how often I use it and have come to love it.
The cold water and ice dispenser, I love that it measures the water for you, the water is COLD, unlike my last in the door water fridge. The ice functions are great, crushed is crushed, cubed is cubed, cubes are a standard size, pretty straight forward.
The digital picture function, I love it, and will admit that I thought at first it was a little ridiculous and overkill for a feature. BUT now that I have had it and used it for a bit, I love having the pics on the fridge without cluttering up the front of it.
Deli drawer, I love the fact that it is so wide and has a wide range of choices for temp setting. Easily this is one of my favorite features.
Door alarm may save us millions in wasted power.

Now for the disappointments…
The freezer, its drawer does not pull out nearly far enough, you have to have both of the fridge doors also open to get into it. Also, it has a tip out shelf against the front of the drawer that you practically have to do a handstand to see into. Even the tip out feature does not help. The two smaller drawers within the freezer are ok, but again hard to get into without opening the whole fridge up to get into.
Interior space, UGH, the veggie and fruit drawers are tiny, not nearly enough space for even basic salad makings. Because the ice maker is on the inside of the front door, the shelves are not nearly deep enough. This fridge has the same useful cubic measurement of my old side by side, but you would never know it. The shelves on the door that holds the ice maker are impossibly shallow, fine if you use teeny tiny containers of condiments, but anyone else will likely be disappointed.
In summary. The lighting is great, the outside dispenser is great, I have had no issues with noise as mentioned in some of the other reviews, I love the way it looks and much to my surprise, I love the hot water and digital frame features. The Deli drawer is the best. BUT the draw backs are pretty important to me, space and access to the freezer.
The extra features are great, but I would probably not buy this model again because of the size issues and like I said it is supposedly the same size as my last fridge, but the set up makes it seem smaller and less accessible.
Unfortunately, the things I don't like are things I didn't notice until after I had lived with it…

product_title: GE CYE23TSDSS Cafe 23.1 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel Counter Depth French Door Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_text: Bought this a month ago when the kitchen renovation was complete. Did extensive research on competing models and brands. We looked at ALL models that were: french-door, counter-depth, single freezer drawer, with thru-the-door ice cube, crushed ice, and water dispenser. This model nails all of those requirements and bested what few competitors there were, typically one competitor from each manufacturer. First, the refrigerator looks fantastic. Great fit and finish, LCD display and control organization. Second, the ice maker and water dispenser is in the door! Don't underestimate this feature. Earlier side-by-side models always had problems with the icemaker and water dispenser because there was a physical connection between the door and the ice/water maker in the body of the refrigerator that would get separated every time the door was opened. The door is thick, but it contains the water filter easy to pop out), the ice maker, the grinder (for crushed ice), and the ice storage. Incredibly convenient and easy to use/maintain. Also, the angle on the water dispenser is just right, no splashes and plenty of room for large cups /bottles. Third, the lighting on the interior of this model vastly outperforms its competitors. Importantly, the LED lighting basically shines from the outer edge of the interior inward, as opposed to downward from the top of the interior (like many competitors). This configuration ensures every shelf is equally lit, and big items don't prevent lower shelves from being lit. Fourth, the compressor almost never runs and when it does, it is whisper quiet. Fifth, temperature is consistent between internal compartments and door compartment, which are large enough to store 1 gallon of milk / 2 liters of soda + additional stuff. This is greatly appreciated. Finally, the hot water feature is helpful for teh occasional quick cup of tea. Does 10oz of hot water (at user specified temperature) at a time, with a heat time of about 2 minutes. I maintain this is the best counter-depth, french door, single-freezer drawer, thru-the-door ice/water refrigerator there is. Not cheap, but worth every penny.

review_text:

product_title: GE CYE23TSDSS Cafe 23.1 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel Counter Depth French Door Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_text:
UPDATE:
I'm updating this review since this piece of junk is even worse than I'd thought.

First, the hot water dispenser was broken the day it was delivered. It just never worked properly. After 6 service calls, GE finally decided to replace the damn thing after they basically replaced all the electronics in the fridge, to no avail.

The new fridge is just as loud as the first one, but sometimes, it's much louder. It's like having a Harley running in your kitchen. It measured it with a decibel meter and the sound level came in at about 75 dB.

Worse, the fridge doesn't keep the temperature. I have all the temperatures set at the "recommended" settings, but the actual temperatures are WAY OFF. In short, EVERYTHING is FROZEN in the fridge. The water line doesn't work because the WATER IS FROZEN. All our vegetables have freezer burn and we had to throw them all away.

ORIGINAL REVIEW:
A lot of people complained about the noise... I didn't think much of it when reading the reviews, but now I regret that I should have. Others have said this already: that it's normal, that it sounds different because of the variable-speed compressor. However, there's no excuse for it to be so loud.

Also worth mentioning is that the hot water dispenser is flaky at best. I've tried to make hot water 3 times, and 2 out of the 3 times, the fridge comes back with the dreaded "Hot Water Disabled" error message. Google this; others have had this problem. So I have to go to the panel and cycle the circuit breaker to get hot water to work.

The stainless steel is also quite cheap for a Cafe--it's something I'd expect on the mainline GE. It's the thin, shiny, with lots of coarse grain, nothing like more polished SS found in higher-end appliances.

And, just after one day, the cover on the touch panel for the temperature-drawer bin has already started peeling off.

review_title: Great fridge, but like most things, it's not perfect
review_text:
Purchased this in November for our home and have zero regrets. I did SO MUCH research on the best in-door water/ice maker refrigerators and I will say LG was on the top of my list until I heard about how backlogged they were with fulfilling the orders.

I purchased this without looking at it in person and even then there were little reviews.

Things to consider when purchasing this model:
- Yes, it gets noisy. This only started happening (5 months after purchase) when it alerted me to change the odor and water filters. i have yet to replace them
- Yes, the SS is hard to clean and you'll get fingerprints EVERYWHERE. no big deal for me - just a wipe and surface is clean.
- Yes, the ice maker is slim to accommodate the in-door design and sometimes the ice misses the glass. no big deal - put the glass closer to the spout.

I thought I would use the hot water feature more often than I do today - which is very rarely - but it is faster to run my electric kettle with higher volume than run this feature.

Additionally, I use the precise fill every time I make my son's bottle and the letters are starting to fade. I don't mind this so much because this does not affect the functionality.

I've read other reviews that say you have to open both doors. This is only true if you need to open the ONE drawer that is the length of the fridge. Otherwise, you can make do with one door open.

All-in-all, I do love this fridge and get so many compliments on how "fancy" it looks!

review_title: 6 repairs in 8 months to the brand new GE Cafe.  GE agreed to replace it yesterday.
review_text:
We bought this refrigerator and had it delivered the first week of Jan 2014. It sure is nice to look at... and that's it. Today is Sept 2, 2014 and I have had GE come out for repairs on this refrigerator 6 times. That's right folks, SIX REPAIRS in 8 months. When I said I wanted a new refrigerator to the tech, he laughed and said that GE will only do repairs - no replacements! Let's see if I can recount all the reasons that they have come out so far:

1) The horrendous noise level, (two calls so far but should have been more). They ended up installing a "noise kit" to reduce the noise in this "known problem". (Again, how did this product make it on the shelf.)

2) Ice build up in the "frost-free" freezer. Yup. Even 5 minutes with my hot hair dryer didn't melt all the ice near the fan in this freezer. It's awful. The technician spent almost 45 minutes clearing the ice from my freezer.

3) If you use the crushed ice feature it clogs the ice maker and you have to take it apart and pick the ice out. (One call)

4) Loud noises from the fan in the freezer. Turns out the thermistor in the freezer was installed incorrectly - which the tech said "happens all the time" but then said this might not fix it. (OMG)

5) (Small but listing) The ability to load pictures on the screen doesn't work. Tried 2 different USBs but says it's unreadable. Sigh. No phone call on this one but still it's annoying.

To summarize, please do not buy this crappy refrigerator. Your money is better spent elsewhere. Go look at a whirlpool or something.

OH wait. I forgot to list the PROs!

1) The hot water works ok. But you only get 10 ounces at a time. (I drink a lot of tea.) If you want more it has to heat for another few minutes before you can get it. A nice start to "instant hot water" though.

review_text: Believe the reviews!!!  We did not and we are paying the price.  I would not buy any GE product again after this purchase.  It may look okay but the quality is ridiculously subpar.  The service from customer relations is even worse.  We have had this refrigerator for all most 11 months now, and we have had 3 service calls for a number of reasons.  First of all, the refrigerator is loud.  I didn't believe most of the reviews on this and thought how loud can it be.  Well it does sound like 100hp compressor is operating in this refrigerator.  The first issue we had was with the refrigerator icing up and causing an even louder fan noise.  The second issue was with the refrigerator and freezer not keeping temperature.  Everything was warm one day and we lost most of the food.  This supposedly got fixed.  The next issue was with this unit keep things too cold and freezing everything in the refrigerator.  The temperature on the frig read out stated 37°F but the thermometer we put in there after the last incident said that is was 29°F.  I had had enough.  I asked GE to replace this refrigerator.  They then told me that they no longer make the model we had, but they could replace it with a new model that is smaller.  I told them that we could not afford to lose space in the refrigerator and we would need the same model.  They searched a little harder and found one of our models.  They shipped this to us which took about a week.  When the refrigerator arrived at 9:15pm they brought it into the house and set in the kitchen.  We then saw that the whole rear corner of the refrigerator was smashed in by a clamp truck.  This was no cosmetic damage.  It might as well been pushed off the back of the truck with damage like that.  Now they had to return this one and...this was the last straw.  I told GE that I wanted my money back.  After many phone calls and waiting for approvals on this, keep in mind we have a refrigerator that does not keep temperature, we final got GE to agree to buy back our refrigerator.  However, GE would not reimburse us for the full price we paid for the refrigerator.  At first they told me that we would be reimbursed for the MSRP price.  They said the check would be sent to the delivery company and they would deliver the check when they picked up our defective refrigerator.  A few days later I received a message from GE stating that I need to submit receipts for this refrigerator or they will not reimburse us.  I completely understood this and wondered why it wasn't done this way from the beginning.  So I submitted my receipts for the frig which included an extended warranty.  GE then told me that they would only reimburse me for what the refrigerator cost.  They would not reimburse for any taxes, state fees, or warranties.  I had already checked with the warranty company and they told me the warranty was nontransferable so the warranty was useless if I returned the refrigerator.  We are still arguing over this issue I plan to take this as high as it has to go until GE decides to stand by their product and reimburse us for the money that we laid out for this lemon of a product.

review_text:

Still working flawlessly as the "garage 'fridge".

review_text:

When we needed a new one 3 years ago, we bought what we thought was the same style and quality we'd had in the past. It was, of course, more expensive than we'd paid before, but we hadn't had any problems with others so quickly decided to just do it.

This one has never performed "normally"! Food in the fridge freezes; the ice cream in the freezer is essentially soft-serve. Anything left in the freezer for longer than two weeks comes out freezer-burned. Today, we discovered the defrost drain pan has spilled over. Unfortunately, access to the pan is via the compressor --> the refrigerator has to be shut down and the compressor removed before gaining access to the drain pan.

I can't tell you how disappointed I am with this refrigerator! I'm glad to know the model (WRT1L1TZYW) has been discontinued, and I most likely will *not* purchase another whirlpool.

review_title: Great if you like wet clothes
review_text:
I've had many different driers over the years, and they've all dried clothes. The only differences were capacity, heat source, and features. It didn't matter the capacity, the heat source (gas or electric), or the features, they all had one thing in common, they dried your clothes. The permanent press cycles are nice, the cool down cycles are nice, infinite temperature settings are nice, but they are all worthless if it doesn't ultimately dry your clothes in a reasonable amount of time.

Then there's this drier. It is the absolute worst drier I have ever used. It will not dry a load of clothes on one dry cycle. Doesn't matter how many clothes are in the drier, how long the cycle is, the temperature of the cycle, items never come out dry. And I don't mean a little dampness or slight cool-to-the-touch around the waist line, I mean wet. It always takes at least 2 cycles, and often more, to get them dry. Especially towels. I will be up half the night restarting the drier every 75 minutes or so just to get one load dry! It must have 15 different drying cycle types, and it doesn't matter which one you use, everything is still is wet on completion.

This is the only computerized drier I've ever purchased, and it will be the last. Give me a good old mechanical dial for the amount of time and a 3-position switch for setting the temperature any day.

product_title: GE GTWN5650FWS 3.9 Cu. Ft. White Top Load Washer
review_text:
I had an old whirlpool washer from 2001. The last 7 yrs it's had really heavy use especially since that model had a smaller tub. I have a tight laundry space that only allows certain dimensions, so this was the most important factor when picking out a replacement. I went to Best Buy and bought a new set that was still a manual model for approx. $1100. The very next day I happened to stumble upon this machine at Menards for only $400. It was an upgrade from what I originally selected and let me tell you how happy I am. I've had this machine about a week so far so please keep that in mind. What I love:
-Set Up: It's very easy. In fact, I don't think there really was a "set-up" to say. Basically the technician installed it and said it was ready to go.
-The tub: It's Stainless steel and for a smaller machine, the tub seems huge.
-The panel: VERY VERY easy to select your wash cycle. I also LOVE that you can override the pre-set selections to customize your wash which is not possible on a lot of more expensive models.
-Agitator: Really love that there is an agitator. I read a ton of reviews prior to getting this machine and it seemed a lot of complaints on the ones that don't have an agitator were due to clothes not getting clean and severe wrinkling.

The things that I wish were a little different are very minor but in fairness feel they should be pointed out.
-Detergent cup: this may or may not apply. I have the laundry soap where it has a spicket. On my old machine I would pour in the detergent and rinse out the detergent cup in the water so it was always clean, then add clothes. You can't do this on any of the newer machines (not just this model). Once you start the water, you can still add clothes but the water stops filling immediately making it so you can't rinse out the cup. Small annoyance. I will switch to a different method of detergent to avoid this or deal with a messy cup.

-Noise: It is a small tad louder and more noticeable than I'd like. Don't get me wrong, my last machine sounded like Air Force One was landing so this is a huge improvement, but you can hear the water splashing around and spinning. In a way this is a blessing because most negative reviews complain about the low water level so the fact that I can hear this splashing against the lid is reassuring that the tub is filled with water.

Again these are small annoyances and because they are pretty common on all machines I won't deduct for it. I haven't tried the delayed start yet which is a feature I was excited about, nor the bleach dispenser so those weren't factored into the review. I would highly recommend this washer.

While waiting for our appointment day, the freezer stopped cooling. This time the service fellow found that not only had ice formed around the fans again, but the entire defrost cycle was not working. IN addition, today as I am writing this, it has been 3 weeks that we have had to cope a malfunctioning fridge and no freezer unit. We've dealt with  cancelled parts orders, last minute cancelled appointments by GE, and a lie about the time of day the rescheduled appointment was going to be. review_text:
Update: two years later and I still love my fridge. The ice maker has a brain fart once in a while but resetting it by turning it off and back on corrects the problem. Have had absolutely no other issues. Highly recommend this fridge!
Though I have only owned this fridge for a little over a month, I wanted to go ahead and write my review. I found this fridge in Lowe's and fell in love with the design so I searched all over the internet to read reviews and find the best price before purchasing it (from Amazon). I read many negative reviews and took them in to consideration, I understand that not every item we purchase can be perfect so I believe there's a risk when purchasing ANYTHING especially online. So far, I have no issues and I am very pleased with the amount of storage I have now. I didn't think that there would really be enough space to store all the groceries and leftovers for my family of 5, but there is more than plenty and at this point... product_title: Whirlpool WFW86HEBW Duet 4.1 Cu. Ft. White With Steam Cycle Front Load Washer - Energy Star
review_text:
This review is for those who are accustomed to seeing your washer fill up with water, agitate, drain, spin and repeat. This front-loader does more of a tumble, tumble, drain and spin but the big surprise is how little water it uses.

Your laundry will be soaked, but there is no extra water sloshing around in the tub. Just wet laundry being tumbled, making you think that it cannot be working. However, we have discovered that our clothes come out looking and smelling great, the towel setting produces great results, and we are pleased. The only negative is that we usually do an extra rinse to make sure the soap is out, but that is more a personal preference.

A big positive is that the machine spins so much water out of our laundry that our old dryer runs for a little less than half the time it did before. This translates into big electricity savings for us. We are also enjoying the fact that we can wash 12 pairs of jeans and jean shorts in a single load, maybe an hour or so, and then dry them in 20 minutes. This machine is easy to use.

I take away a star because I think it does a good job, and I reserve the extra star for products that are spectacular.

10/3/2013 As a follow-up, we've been using this machine for several months now, and still like it. Points of interest: It has not broken. It has a lot of buttons and lights and does a lot of work, so i won't be surprised when it does, but so far no problems. We've never seen a sock get stuck, never seen it leak, none of those things. It does have very sesitive controls. If you lean against the machine, or sometimes throw a towel on the machine it can touch the power button and stop the machine in mid-cycle. Also, we run the "Clean" cycle less than is recommended by the soap-selling manufacturer and still have never once smelled mold or mildew or anything except soap - a pleasant surprise.

review_title: Looks great, but doesn't wash the clothes
review_text:
I bought this washer, locally not online, about 4 months ago after our old maytag gave up. After reading many positive reviews both by other owners and by appliance "experts" I decided this was the one.

First let me start with the good. I love the look of the washer. It really looks like it's stainless steel and the front panel controls give it a really clean look. It has a huge capacity, way more than our older dryer can handle. It is super easy to operate and is really quiet, almost silent. It also spins the clothes really dry. I've read some reviews from people complaining about unbalance errors, UE, but I have only had that happen once and it was with a large bulky comforter so it's a non-issue for me.

Now for what I don't like about it. My biggest complaint with this washer is it doesn't wash the clothes. I mean come on, it's called a washing machine for a reason right? We have people in our household that are out in the dirt and grease daily and their clothes get very dirty. It doesn't matter how much spot treatment or presoaking is done, the clothes don't come out even remotely clean. They are literally just as dirty after they are "washed" as they were when I put them in. Any money that you save from the reduced water and energy usage is more than offset with the cost of spot treatment and new clothes. The wash cycles also seem to be excessively long, especially for the pitiful amount of cleaning that is done. Lastly, and not a big issue, but the tub is very deep and I had to make a step for the ladies so they could reach the bottom.

To be fair, this is the first "high efficiency" washer that we've had and also the first without an agitator, so the poor cleaning performance might not be exclusive to this machine, but it doesn't do a very good job of cleaning that's for sure. If I could have given it 2.5 stars I would have. It is very nice looking, quiet, and has a lot of different cycles and options with a huge capacity, so if you're someone who doesn't get their clothes very dirty, it might work just fine for you. I will be buying a simple "cheapie" washer with an agitator to wash the dirty clothes and use this for the less dirty clothes and bulky items like bedding and towels.

Hopefully this review was helpful

product_title: LG WT1201CV 4.5 Cu. Ft. Ultra-Large Capacity Front-Control Top-Load Washer with SlamProof Lid Â– Graphite Steel
review_text:
I have owned this washer (and the dryer that matches) for about 3 months now. I LOVE it. Some background:
Household Occupants: 6 + a dog, cats and other sundry animals.
Location: Rural hobby farm
Usual Cleaning Needs: Outdoor dirt, farm dirt, average amount of cat hair and women hair (shoulder length or longer)
Usual Load Size: Large
Child ages: 8-23 no, we are not the Duggars ;)
Replaced Washer Brand: Maytag Neptune (Worst machine I ever owned - did not clean well and twisted the clothes terribly when spinning out - but after 10 years with no mechanical issues I give Maytag credit)

I did try the Samsung almost top of the line model but it shook like crazy when spinning out and made weird rubbing noises when washing. I sent it back and a replacement was dented so I just figured it was a sign I needed to go with a different brand.

Enter the LG. I LOVE, LOVE, LOVE this washer and the matching dryer (my old dryer did not have enough cubic ft. to match the washer so I sold it and installed the LG. Make sure you think about that before you replace your washer alone)

Negative Issues:
Cleanliness: NONE
Unbalanced load: RARE (seems to happen with smaller loads so if you usually do smaller loads don't buy this machine. It's a waste of your money. If you do occasional smaller loads, just be cognizant of when the load is running and check on it to see if it gets unbalanced in the spin cycle. Not all my smaller loads do it.)
Tub Reachability: If you are 5' 6" or taller - NONE

Other Points to Consider:
Ease of Use: Very easy to operate. Some might not like that you have to push the Power On button every time you do a load but it's a non-issue for me. Everything is self explanatory and for all other things there is the manual.
Noise level: AVERAGE TO MINIMAL - This machine does make some noise when ramping up for a spin but really nothing that I wouldn't expect from any other washer and it is definitely quieter than my Maytag was (everyone though a rocket was lifting off for space). We have 2nd floor laundry with our bedrooms very close to the laundry area and we have no issues if the washer is working when we go to bed. When washing it is very quiet. It also does not have that annoying buzzer when the load is done, it plays a very nice little song. I don't think you can change the song (my friend has a front loader that has song options - this one does not) You can choose to turn it off completely.
Water amount needed for load: Good to Great (I like more water as the clothes do get cleaner and rinsed better)
Amount of space needed: A bit more than my last washer but worth it
Recommended Cleaning Detergent: I have used all natural powder soap as well as tide liquid soap and have had no issues. I did have an issue with the powder PODS. They don't like to break down in the detergent tray. They also don't like to break down when placed directly in the washer. So I would recommend you get loose powder if you are going to use powder.
Load Timing: Varies from 35 min (speed load) to 1hr 20min (soaking load)
Effectiveness of Spin: PHENOMENAL

Other things to consider would be if you do a lot of waterproof items or rugs with rubber backing. Check with the manufacturer to see if their product allows this. Some do not at all and some say ok if you low spin your items. This one is ok as long as it is not a lot of items in a load and you low spin them.

Also love the feature that lets the tub breathe without having to have the lid up. I have family that have front loaders and they stink to high heaven. ugh! You don't have to worry about that with this washer. Very well thought out.

Only drawback I have had so far is that you cannot choose every option for every load type. Some loads you cannot choose hot water for and some you cannot choose low spin for.

Otherwise I love the washer. Love the look, love the performance and love the pair. If you get this washer do seriously consider the matching dryer. It used to take 70 minutes in my Maytag gas dryer to dry my loads, now with this gas LG it takes half that time or LESS. Seriously, that much less. I am saving a ton of money on gas and electricity usage here. I NEVER have a load of wet clothes waiting for the dryer to finish anymore.

We purchased this at a local retailer.

Feel free to ask any questions - I would have no problem answering them.

product_title: GE GTDP200EFWS 6.8 Cu. Ft. White Electric Dryer
review_title: It has operated fine for me
review_text:
I have owned this model for 10 months. It has operated fine for me. I only use the timed setting, but there are also options for Permanent Press and Cottons. 60 minutes gets clothes dry, but you can run it up to 80 for larger/thicker loads.

I never wash extra large loads of clothes, so I'd probably be safe putting two washer loads in this dryer at the same time without exceeding the rating. My washing machine is only designed to handle 3.9 Cu. Ft., and this dryer is rated at 6.8 Cu. Ft.

The nicest feature of this dryer is the light inside the tub that is triggered to come on when I open the door. A light is such a simple, but thoughtful addition. That extra illumination ensures I don't leave a sock or some other small article of clothing behind.

The biggest design flaw of this dryer is location of the lint filter. It's positioned just below the access to the tub with no screen between the filter and the door. Whenever I open the door, the suction from the door causes bits of loose lint to come flying out all over the floor. Thankfully, I have a separate wash room. If this dryer was in a hallway, I'd need to vacuum after every load to keep the lint from getting all over the house. Having the filter inside the door like that might be a good reminder to clean out the lint after every load, but that's about the only advantage. If I were buying a dryer today, I'd go with another model due to this particular flaw in the design.

I purchased this dryer from Lowes when they had it on sale for $399. I bought the extended 3-year warranty, so the total was approximately $460. This model is currently priced $440 at Lowes without the warranty.

UPDATE 7/31/16: I am updating this review and reducing the rating from 3-stars to 2-stars. I have now owned this dryer for two years. About six months ago, the On switch became finicky and would not start the dryer. I finally figured out I can get it to start if I twist the button counterclockwise. I will be calling Lowes to see if they will repair this problem under the extended warranty I purchased at some point. All in all, my impression of this dryer is that it's not the greatest design, and the parts are cheap.

review_title: Steam sanitize cycle not what i thought
review_text: I have had this dryer for almost 6 months and am mostly satisfied.  I bought it based on reviews and features.  I like the anti-wrinkle and steam refresh cycles.  The dry-sensor is more accurate than on older models.  What I don't like is the manual.  It is not helpful.  I was having a problem with the refresh cycle. Following the manual exactly, the clothes were still coming out with big wet spots.  I called Samsung and a technician told me that the manual was wrong, I needed to put more items in the load.  Problem solved and those steam cycles work great.  But when I first used the steam sanitize cycle, it shut off after a few minutes.  The manual does not tell exactly how to use this cycle.  I was under the assumption, and so are many people judging by online comments, that this cycle was intended for dry items, just as the other 2 steam cycles are.  I wanted to steam some pillows. Luckily I have an extended warranty, so a technician came. He said it needed a new panel.  When this didn't fix it, he talked to his supervisor who said the items need to be WET.  This makes no sense to me. This cycle simply dries at a very high temp, then shoots out some water at the end.  I don't see how the result is any different from the regular sanitize cycle.  The moisture from the load plus the high heat would make steam.  I am very disappointed. I am writing this review mainly to make people aware that the steam sanitize cycle is not what one might expect.

product_title: Frigidaire Electric Washer/Dryer Laundry Center – White
review_text:
Purchased this item brand new from Lowe's, end of January 2013. This is my first washer/dryer combo with no center wash agitator.

When the machine is running properly, it's fantastic. The wash cycle is significantly quieter than other machines I've used. The knob selections leave you with very limited options as far as being able to influence the actual wash duration. I've noticed that the "normal" wash cycle typically takes up to an hour, which is significantly longer than other machines I've used.

The spin cycle on this machine is another story... It may very well be that I have a faulty machine, but when doing larger, heavier loads (i.e. towels, blankets) the machine gets extremely finicky. Sometimes it will run smoothly, but the majority of the time, it makes horrific clanging noises as if the wash bin is loose and thrashing around inside the machine, and the entire unit shakes and rattles wildly. Doing "normal" loads (shirts, pants etc.), I can load the machine to 80% capacity and it usually runs okay. But with heavier loads, if it's not under 50% capacity, the machine goes berserk.

I even had an authorized repairman take a look at the machine. He opened up the front panel and examined the machine under load and could not locate the source of the clanging noise.

Another limitation of the machine are the knob selections. For example, "rinse" and "spin" are a single selection. You can't just run the spin cycle to wring wet clothes, you are forced to run the clothes through a rinse cycle as well. This of course caused problems for myself and the repairman trying to trouble shoot the spin cycle because now we had to wait 10 minutes for the rinse cycle to complete...

Pausing the machine mid-cycle for any reason is also a no-no. Pushing the button to halt machine operation (for example, if the machine is banging around during spin cycle) will pause the machine, shortly after which it "resets" the cycle. So for example, if you pause the machine with 10 minutes remaining in the wash cycle, and you let it sit too long (3-5 minutes?), when you "resume" the wash cycle, it will just start all over again.

Regarding the lint trap itself is very small and clogs quickly. Is this a limitation of the dryer or are my clothes just linty? :p If the trap gets fully clogged, I would recommend clearing it and running the dryer cycle for a few more minutes or so in order to catch remaining lint.
Also, the dryer door has a spring in it which causes the door to close slowly when opened. This is extremely irritating when trying to put clothes into or take clothes out of the dryer.

PROS: Quiet operation (when it's working properly)
CONS: Noisy spin cycle (when it' not working properly), lack of options on the knob turn dials, small lint trap, dryer door automatically closes.

I will try to post a video shortly.

product_title: Frigidaire FFHN2740PE26.7 Cu. Ft. Black French Door Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_text:
UPDATE: Still in the endless holding pattern of warranty service company ordering parts. Check the last comment for details. I honestly feel like Electrolux is being ripped off by these guys. The 3rd service person on the 8th service visit, decided to replace to whole sealed system without doing ANY testing on it. I guess I'll get my money from Electrolux one way or another but is any of this going to fix anything? Doubt it.

Never buy a Frigidaire product again. This refrigerator simply does not work. There are a number of issues with all the Frigidaire french door models, in both quality control and design.

First of all let me say I have 3 Frigidaire products I've been happy with. But please understand that these were simple designs that have worked since the 50's. A chest freezer, a 18cuft refrigerator, and an apartment fridge/freezer. So when looking for a nice big fridge for the wife Frigidaire seemed like a good choice. It wasn't.

This is an Electrolux appliance, so consider that they also sell this model as a Tappan, White-Westinghouse, Gibson and Kelvinator. First of all, it doesn't cool. As myriad other reviews, even on Frigidaire's own site have pointed out, the fresh food compartment can barely make it to 40 degrees. Even if you never open the doors, it still won't get below 40.

There are four reasons for this, all are design flaws. The first one is the mullion strip, in order for the doors to open the gaskets around the door have a relief to clear the strip. The attempt to solve this was to add a small gasket to the top and bottom of the mullion. However all this does is push the door gaskets open. Goto a store, find one, it's on all the models of Frigidaire, and close only the door with the mullion, look at it edge on. You'll notice quite a gap, you might think like I did that once both doors are closed it will be compressed. This is not true. After weeks of frustration I placed a flashlight inside the fridge and closed the doors. Seeing the light around the top and bottom of the mullion confirmed my suspicion. This can be mitigated by adjusting one door high and one door low, which causes the gaskets to overlap better. It helps but does not cure the problem.

The second design flaw of the fridge compartment is the airflow. Being a bottom freezer it has to push the cold air up. It has a very underpowered fan, with a constricted air column. It's actually made of a styrofoam piece with a 1/4 inch channel that runs from the damper door to the top of the compartment. There are four vents near the top of the column which are about 1/4 wide by and half inch tall. This is on the back wall of the fridge. There can be as much as a 10 degree difference between the back and the door shelves. The cold air never makes it to the doors. Even if it does, the poor seals let it escape.

The third design flaw is where the thermistor is placed. It's on the back wall of the fridge, half way up from the bottom, inside the plastic cover for the air column. It's like putting your house thermostat in a closet next to a register. The rest of the house will never be at temp. No matter how warm the fridge gets, the sensor can't tell. If anything it should be on the roof of the fridge.

The fourth design flaw in my opinion, this one is mostly opinion, is the compressor. It's "smart" so when it does actually get close to temp it slows down to save power. Which makes it run ALL THE TIME. And ours squeaks when it runs. The warranty service tech won't even consider touching the sealed system. So we're stuck with it until he gets done swapping out control board after control board. Now in the service/repair manual FROM Frigidaire it states that with an ambient temperature of 68 degrees the compressor will run 35-40% of the time. At 90 degrees it will run 100% of the time.

The freezer never really stays below zero either. It can and will get down to zero, but most of the time it is around 10. Strangely the temp settings on the freezer only goes to -6 but on the fridge it goes into the mid 40s. Which of course is completely improper for food safety. The danger zone of things like e-coli as an example, is 40-140. A properly working refrigerator should be about 38-39 at least. And a freezer, if you don't want freezer burn should stay BELOW zero. -10 to 0 is the safe zone. If your food is above zero when the defrost cycle starts, it'll thaw just a little, then refreeze and dry out causing, freezer burn. From what I've seen the freezer gets up to around 20 degrees at times. I can't be sure if this is after a defrost cycle but seems to be so. Every time I've noticed it the compressor is running, which it shouldn't during a defrost cycle. So I'm guessing it's just completed one. Seems to defrost about once a day. With such poor airflow it may have excess frost buildup and could also be a factor in the freezer not being able to stay cold if the has to defrost more. I don't have it hooked up to a meter to tell for sure when it's in defrost. It almost never shuts off.

Quality control issues that I can see are; The door handles were rusty out of the box. The finish was also streaked, mostly on the ends. It suggests to me they have a bin piled full of handles laying around and just spray paint them rust and all. I haven't bothered to ask Frigidaire to replace the handles since we've been focused on the cooling issues.

But if you look under the doors you'll see pieces of excess spray foam, you know the stuff in the cans, leaking out from where the plastic seams are. Doesn't look like a well finished product from the bottom or the back. After the first bottom control board was replaced. The compressor fan quit working. I came home to find the the fridge up to 48 degrees and the freezer at 20. The compressor was making an unhappily loud hum and was almost too warm to touch. So after trying some resets by unplugging it for 6 minutes. I placed a desk fan on the compressor and called the service tech back first thing in the morning. Turns out that the compressor fan was stuck on a piece of the poster board, yes, poster board, that is used as an air baffle around the coils. The fan had moved when he was working on it since there seems to be almost nothing holding it in place. Strangely enough, it cooled better with the desk fan on it. He's ordered a replacement fan.

The shelves and the drawers on this model are about the only good things, they all glide nicely. One thing to look for on the freezer door is a toothed wheel on the side track, this keeps the drawer from racking and makes it easier to open from the side. The fridge shelves all slide out a few inches so you can reach things in the back easier. But it's like having a sports car with a lawnmower engine. It just looks good.

The inside really doesn't have that much usable space, it's big but you can't really fit that much in there. Wine bottles are a real problem as you have to remove at least one shelf to make room. The crisper drawers are just a bit too big. shouldn't be quite so deep and you can't open the left side unless you open both doors because of the mullion strip. You can move them around just like the shelves though.

The freezer is the same, the ice bucket takes half of the top shelf. Kinda pointless and really kills the space. However the ice maker takes about 3 hours to make a round of ice, so it takes days for it to fill up. It also doesn't push the bar off when it does fill up but I've never had an ice maker that did shut itself off. There is still more empty space in the freezer than storage space. That seems to just be the way all bottom freezers are. Looked at other models in the store quite a bit now. At this point I'm hoping Frigidaire will refund my money as I can't return it. If you get one DO CALL THE STORE, DON'T CALL Frigidaire. Just RETURN IT ASAP. That's what I should have done but now I'm being taught a $1600 lesson. It smarts. Worst of all I'm going to have to buy another fridge, so it double smarts.

I do want to point out that dealing with Frigidaire on the phone has been hassle free, and I commend them for that. My advice to them would be to take a very hard look at their design, move the thermistor to the top, expand the air channel and get another factory or do some serious house cleaning down there and put QC inspectors in place. Otherwise they might as well pack it in. This fridge was made in Mexico like almost all are these days. But QC is what matters, not where it's made.

review_title: LG WT1201CW top-load-washer: very happy with it
review_text:
I read alot of reviews (on Amazon and elsewhere) on many makes and models, which led me to buying this washer (LG WT1201CW). In reviews I read people's most frequent complaint about High Efficiency (HE) washers seems to be they don't add enough water to cover the clothes. I found this to be true, seeing about 1/4 to 1/5 the height of the clothes being left exposed when beginning the wash cycle in a 'normal' mode. It seems strange especially when coming from a traditional non-HE washer (my old one broke down) that fills the tub enough to leave the clothes swimming in it. So for this new HE washer, what could I do to get more water in the wash cycle if I wanted it? I learned of a few tricks from others and from reading the manual/guides:

1. The quick reference guide that comes with the washer says to hold the Extra Rinse button for 3 seconds and it will add more water. I'm not sure if this added more water up front (seemed like it didn't) in the wash cycle, but tapping the Extra Rinse button once or twice did add noticeably ore water in the Rinse cycle (it allows up to 2 increases).

2. Start the machine, let it fill with water in the wash cycle. Shut it off. Start it again and it is tricked into thinking there is a heavier load (the weight sensor is what gages how much water the machine adds).

3. Start the washer in 'bulk' mode, which is used for bulky stuff like blankets and pillows. In this mode a lot of water is added, like is done with a traditional (non-HE) washer. I did this with my usual clothes load and it was like I had my old washer back. This feature alone would make all those complaints about lack of water go away.

4. Get a bucket of water and add it in with your clothes before hitting the Start button. This is easy if you have a wash sink nearby or another tap. You can add just enough water to top the clothes but even this extra amount will still result in using much less water than what you'd have by running in 'bulk' mode. You'd be semi-HE I guess.

If you find the machine's standard water-fill adequate, then by all means leave it alone because that is where you get your savings. Maybe having more water is only a placebo for those transitioning from the old traditional water-generous units. Then again it might not be.

As far as operation goes, I really like how quiet it runs, and it runs smooth with very little vibration. When vibrating it feels damped, and this is probably due to the excellent suspension system this machine seems to have. When installing the machine it's best to make sure it is as level as possible. You can use the legs to adjust each corner. The basket should look centered. I used a level to check it and the bubbles were centered even with the basket visually slightly off center. So its good to eyeball the basket too and try to perfect the level. I found it worth the extra effort.

Another tip I was told is that in HE machines you use very little soap and fabric softener, like 1/3 of what is used for a load in traditional washers. I reduced my usage this way and the clothes came out clean and fresh.

Finally, it is very worthwhile to read the manual even though the machine can be used intuitively. The manual tells you how to optimize its performance for the various types of fabrics out there. Or, you can keep it simple and run it like your old washer by using 'bulk' mode for everything.

I gave this LG washer 5-stars because it works great and it shouldn't be penalized for annoying 'water efficiency' that is mandated by the US Government.

product_title: Samsung RF31FMESBSR 31 cu. ft. 4-Door Refrigerator with Automatic Sparkling Water Dispenser
review_title: We're sending out the announcements any day now
review_text:
Update 5/3/14: Still in love with this fridge. The two of us are still on our first SodaStream canister. We love the flexibility of the snack drawer (currently "marinate the steak" drawer), and have adjusted the shelves to best suit us. I scraped a glass bowl along one of these shelves and it didn't scratch--hooray! The fridge continues to be quiet, except when dropping ice cubes, and it took a day for the dog to quit barking and us to sleep through. It's really not that loud, just a new sound. The ice cubes themselves we think are a huge plus for this fridge. They're softer than hard ice cubes--something we were expecting with the maker in the fridge and not the freezer. I can munch on them all day. It is important to note, unless you very strictly follow the setup instructions for the ice cube maker (shake the bin every hour after cleaning and reset), you will be enjoying a mix of cubed and crushed until you rest it again. We really love how bright it is. It is packed with food and containers at the moment and not one of them is hidden from my hungry eyes. Produce is staying fresh days longer than the previous fridge.

My husband and I are thrilled with our new addition. It came very securely packaged and with easy to read manuals. Most of the setup is common sense (hook up water, plug into wall, peel off plastic, etc.). The carbonator was an easy find at Target and we received a rebate for a SodaStream with the manuals.

Soda has three different levels of carbonation (1-2 Pellegrino, 3 Perrier). It takes a few minutes to fill the reservoir, but it's not inconveniently long. The Samsung website has a chart that actually breaks down how much sparkling water is made at which level and how long it takes for each in the FAQ section. The cartridge pops into the door; not a lot of force required.

Very roomy and well-lit. The lights on the side in the interior really ensure I can see all my Tupperwares all the way to the back. We're having fun with the middle drawer--do not put glass in it! This is not for wine storage. Our thermometers say all temperatures are within ideal range on suggested settings. The ice maker does make noise when making ice, but otherwise there is no obnoxious noise coming from it. No coils on the back that need to be vacuumed either. Water filters are easy to find at Home Depot and install.

This fridge is 410lbs before groceries and replaced our 100lb fridge. We live in an older home and reinforced the floor just to make sure we wouldn't find it in the crawlspace the next the morning. Not sure if it was necessary, but couldn't hurt. Overall my husband and I are thrilled to welcome the new member of the family.

product_title: Samsung RF31FMESBSR 31 cu. ft. 4-Door Refrigerator with Automatic Sparkling Water Dispenser
review_title: Love It. And Not Just For the Sparkling Water....
review_text:
We bought this fridge about two weeks ago, and we really love it.

1. It's enormous and holds a ton of stuff. It also feels like a very high-quality product. The doors are like 4" thick, and when you open them, it feels like you're opening the vault at a bank.

2. It's versatile. In addition to having adjustable shelves (as most fridges do), this fridge has two very helpful "flip" shelves that enable you to store tall items easily. Also, the deli drawer has a cool adjustable compartment and independently adjustable temperature controls.

3. We totally love the deli drawer, and it's the primary reason that we chose this product over others. We used the deli drawer a lot in our previous (Kenmore Elite) refrigerator. It's great to be able to access stuff in the deli drawer without having to open the fridge. Also, in most fridges, the deli drawers are made of relatively flimsy molded plastic, whereas this deli drawer has the vault-esque qualities as mentioned above.

4. It's quiet. It's way, way quieter than the Kenmore Elite refrigerator that we replaced (and relegated to the garage as a beer fridge). On Consumer Reports, this fridge gets a "very good" rating for noise, which is shy of an "excellent" rating. The problem with buying a fridge is that they aren't plugged in at the store, so you have no way to compare the noise and actual functionality of the products. But, I'd be surprised if there's any fridge on the market that's noticeably quieter than this one, as this one is really dang quiet.

5. We also like the sparkling water feature, and we've been using it quite a bit. That said, people, don't buy this refrigerator "for" the sparkling water feature -- or if you do, hedge your expectations a bit. This product is *not* a soda fountain or a Coca-Cola bottling factory with a refrigerator attached to it. Rather, it's a *refrigerator* that has a little sparkling water *feature.* I know that Samsung is really overhyping this feature, and because of that, it didn't meet many people's expectations and those people are now ranting about it. Ultimately, it's fine and it's a nice convenience, nothing more and nothing less. We lucked out, and we got this refrigerator for an amazing price, and for even less money than the model that does not include the sparkling water. So, for us, the sparkling water is just a bonus. If we hadn't got this refrigerator for such a great price, we would've likely opted for the model that does not include the sparkling water and saved a little money. I wouldn't have paid an extra $150-ish for the sparkling water.

Bottom line, so far, after about two weeks of use, I really don't have anything bad to say about this fridge. My one word of advice, however, is to measure the area where you'll put this fridge very carefully and make sure that you give yourself about 1/2" of leeway to accommodate the published width of this product. When I took the measurements at our house, we "should have" had about 1/4" of wiggle room for the fridge. However, when we actually installed the fridge, it was a smidge wider than the published dimensions, and it just barely fit in our space. I was sweatin' it....

Good luck with your purchase.

review_title: IF YOU ARE BUYING IT FOR THE SODASTREAM, DON'T
review_text:
We purchased this fridge last year, May of 2013, and from the get go, the sparkling water dispenser was a disappointment. It is advertised to be the same carbonation level as Perrier. That would be true if we were talking about a Perrier that had been open for 8 hours, while sitting in the sun. This is the way it works. In the door, there is a mechanism that fills a bladder with one liter of water, then it injects the CO2 into the bladder. For some reason this process takes about 15 minutes. Then someone comes by and fills a glass with, lets say .85 liters of water. Then you go by with your glass, end up with a 1/2 cup of semi-bubbled water, the machine goes "FFFSSSSSHHHHHHH", empty. Fast-forward 15 minutes, again not sure why, and you are set up to be disappointed a second time. That isn't the worst part. We noticed after about 2.5 months, that the mech wasn't expelling a full liter anymore. Maybe 3/4 of a liter... Then 1/2 liter... Then 1/4 liter... Finally after about 3.5 months it would just spit at you and "FFFSSSSSHHHHHHH".

We requested a repair order in DEC of 2013 and our repair man was very nice. After messing with it and talking to tech support for about 30 minutes, he finally just ordered a replacement unit for inside the door. That worked great for a while, we had the same mediocre level of bubbles a liter at a time. Until it went to 3/4 of a liter... then a 1/2... then a 1/4...then "FFFSSSSSHHHHHHH". Nothing.

We have since purchased a counter top SodaStream. We are out of warranty now and are being told that the parts, even though this is a sealed unit, have no warranty of their own. Bad business, Samsung.

The only other real (first-world) problem is the ice dispenser. If you select crushed ice, you get nicely crushed ice. If you select cubed ice, you get poorly crushed ice and a few cubes. And the ice capacity is terrible. If you have more that 2 people in the house that enjoy a frost beverage, buy a bag of ice.

The rest of the fridge is fine, plenty of storage, the Flex-zone drawer is nice. The lighting is fantastic, it would be a magical puppet show theater.

All in all, buy a model that has all the features except the SodaStream. You can get a great fridge and a countertop SodaStream for much less than this thing will set you back, especially if you assign a cash value to frustration and the number of times you hear "FFFSSSSSHHHHHHH".

review_title: This fridge gave me a buyer's remorse hangover times ten!
review_text:
Lesson learned. I will never buy another Samsung appliance. They make a mean phone or tablet, but this refrigerator is a gorgeous piece of dead weight.

To its credit, it's beautiful. It maintains a perfect temperature and stores lots of stuff. That's the good. Now....

The ice maker leaks. Apparently there's a service bulletin out on it, because of a small seam in the bottom left corner that allows the warmer air from the refrigerator section to get in and melt the ice & interfere with the freezing process. That means you will not get many whole ice cubes: even on the "cubed" setting, I get little pieces of ice and not anywhere near the "10 lbs of ice a day" that it advertises. I plan on sealing the seam with silicone gel to see if that helps. Oh by the way: I'm on my second ice maker, it's crap and I've only had the fridge 15 months!

So where does all this leaking water go? There is a tiny drip tray in the fridge door, and that's where it goes. The engineers at Samsung, however, decided to make it a NON-REMOVABLE drip tray. It doesn't drain anywhere... it just fills up and then you have to take a sponge in there to sop out all the water every few days. Very much a pain in the tailpipe, folks.

Next: the compressor is now making a God-awful noise, and I'm 3 months out of the 1-year warranty. I did get a 10-year major component extended warranty that covers the compressor, but not the service call, diagnostics or labor. Which means we're going to be out even MORE money on an already costly fridge.

Next: the Sodastream function works well enough, but good luck fitting a Sodastream bottle in the door straight to use it! No, again those pesky engineers designed the opening below the water spout too short for you to stand a 1-liter bottle up in. I've gotten very good at angling the bottle in and measuring the right amount of sparkling water into the bottle, though. If you still choose to buy this fridge, get used to it.

It's extremely heavy. I can't even budge this thing, which means that I have to wait for the service technician to pull it out and service the compressor before I can put a refrigerator surge protector in the outlet. I highly recommend this because the compressor is a very specialized one, and not many appliance repair companies will even touch it. So if you're going to spend this much on this fridge, spend a little more on a surge protector. They're available on Amazon. The problem is that if it ever trips, you'll have to pull this monster out to reset it... so now I'm having second thoughts about installing it. We're hosed!

In summary, given the chance to go back in time 15 months and talk to ourselves while we were looking at this shiny, beautiful appliance, we would do so, screaming "NOOOO! RUN! STAY FAR AWAY!" You can surely do much better for the money that this dog of a fridge, and I cannot possibly recommend it to anyone I like. And I like you.
