review_title: CO2 tank change to much bigger one.
review_text:
Addendum DEC 2015: Have lived with the fridge for about a year. Our experience has been good. Fridge is quiet and problem free so far. The addition of a 20 pound CO2 tank has been great. Copious amounts of very fizzy water. Did not have any ice maker leaks that other reviewer had. One little issue arose when quests came and somehow the fridge was placed into showroom or demo mode, shutting off the compressor. Absolutely no help from the manual. Fix was to simultaneously long press top two left buttons, ie., Freezer and Alarm, which turned the compressor back on. Thanks to all the people on the Internet! Why this isn't stated in the manual is idiotic.

Original review:

We bought the counter depth model. Just the two of us, so it is plenty big.

So the important thing is my wife loves sparkling, fizzy, gassy, water by any name. The original. little, tiny, soda stream CO2 tanks just wouldn't do, so I had a look at it and have now attached a standard 20 pound CO2 tank with regulator, to the refrigerator, stashing the tank in an adjacent cabinet. Works well !

So far great fridge, we haven't had any problems, but see other reviews, all the rest is about CO2:

If any one is interested, I used 6mm PU tubing, a CO2 regulator and two connectors, to go from the 20 pound CO2 tank to the fridge. Surprisingly simple. It seems that the soda stream regulator is built into the metallic gas bottle connector, so I just by-passed it, connecting my 6mm tubing, from my regulator, right into the push to connect fitting in the fridge, where the tubing from the soda stream originally connected to the fridge. Only a couple of screws need to be removed to access the carbonator and fittings in the fridge.

The tricky part was routing the tubing through the top of the door. There is a plate on top of the door, above the dispenser, which when removed, reveals plenty of space, and I drilled from the edge of the door above the handle [ not the hinge side], into this space, through the plastic, down to above the carbonator, and ran the tubing down. All I hit with the drill was foam, but yes, i was a little nervous.

I then ran the tubing back to the hinge along the top of the door, and underneath the plastic piece on top of the fridge and back to the cabinets.
The tubing is covered completely from sight, though if I was to do it again, I would use black tubing instead of orange. Would make routing easier.

Set my regulator to 80 psi originally, but bumped it up to 100 psi. Works well with about 14 feet of 6mm tubing. The PU tubing can easily handle these pressures, but is surprisingly flexible. All parts were bought on Amazon, except 20# tank which was bought locally, filled with CO2, but everything was about $200. I see Amazon sells several sizes of CO2 tanks, though, of course, they are empty. 5 or 10 pound tanks may fit cabinets better. Tank has to be upright to get gas out of the top.

This review is only for educational purposes, and I would never suggest that anyone actually do it. There is some confusion about CO2 out there though. CO2 is not under the pressures SCUBA tanks are, at least in beverage tanks, maybe 600-800 psi, and after the regulator, about 80-100 psi is used. Beverage type of CO2 is a liquid with an overlying gas phase, and not as dangerous as a SCUBA tank, which is 3000 psi gas [air].

You have to get a beverage tank, which dispenses gas from the overlying gas phase, and not a "siphon" tank, which dispenses liquid CO2, from the bottom, which the paintball people use to refill their smaller tanks. Under no circumstances should you ever get a high pressure compressed gas CO2 tank.

The beverage tanks are sold everywhere. Always use a nylon washer between your tank and regulator. Also use flare washers on all flare fittings on the regulator. I went from a flare fitting directly to a 6mm push to connect fitting at the regulator. Not as complicated as it sounds. Some companies are making money off of "food grade" CO2. Not necessary. A clean tank is all you need.

I am now looking into a small, post carbonator, sparkling water storage tank, to fit into the original Soda Stream tank space. Haven't figured it out yet. This space is other wise wasted.

review_title: LG Doesn't Stand Behind Its Products
review_text: A week or two after I took delivery of the LFX29927ST/01, the freezer door, supposedly stainless steel, began to develop what I can only call rust spots (strike 1). They would mostly rub off with a lot of elbow grease, but would always return, getting worse and worse each time, until virtually the entire freezer door was discolored. I called LG and they sent a technician. He admitted that he had never seen anything like that before, took pictures, wrote a report, and told me to follow up with LG after about a week, as LG would NOT be calling me (strike 2). He also recommended that I ask for executive customer service if I wanted quicker results. I followed his recommendation and ended up speaking with one Sherry Thompson. After trying to blame me for causing the rust stains (strike 3) by not following the owner's manual (untrue), Sherry said she would refer the matter to her supervisor and get back to me. I even emailed her the photos taken by the technician, which she claimed not to have. I waited for 2 months (strike 4) before calling back. The new executive customer service agent looked up my file and told me that all Sherry had written there was that she had told me to read the owner's manual. That was it. No indication that any follow up was ever intended (strike 5). The new agent, who was quite sympathetic, then talked to her manager and reported back to me that I would not be given a new freezer door because the rust was not affecting the functioning of the refrigerator (strike 6). She then offered to send me paint to "cover" the rust spots. review_title: So far so good but quite different from my previous GE convection oven
review_text:
I had a GE profile double wall oven with top oven convection for 20 years and it was good although I had to have the electronics or touch pad replaced several times. A new kitchen rebuild and we bought one of these (local, not from Amazon). NOTE - my oven is the CAFE' model which is identical except for the shape of the handles.

It is bigger and besides requiring a bigger cabinet (we put it in a 33" cabinet) it requires a 40a circuit, whereas the older 27" oven required 30a and I shoehorned it into a very narrow cabinet, replacing a 27" GE single wall oven.

The cooking modes are significantly different. The older oven had two convection modes - convection bake, which utilized the heater surrounding the fan in the back of the oven, and convection roast, which ran the fan but used the top broiler element. This latter mode was great for roasts, chickens, etc. In either convection mode the fan at the rear ran at full speed, and I never had any trouble with it. You could bake (bottom element) or broil (top element) without the convection feature.

The new oven has more modes. Besides the non-convection modes, which are the same as the old oven, there are new options for convection cooking.
Convection bake (similar to old convection bake but the fan cycles from off to slow)
Convection bake multi rack (the fan runs faster but still cycles? More like the old convection bake)
Convection roast (nowhere near as good as the convection roast in the old oven, slow fan speed and uses all three heating elements, as far as I can tell. The old oven would cook a chicken in a little over an hour at 325 convection roast, the new one 15-20 minutes longer and it doesn't brown as well)
Convection broil (hi, low, or "crisp") the low broil is most similar to the old convection roast but you can't control the temperature.

The remote feature is OK, mostly good for us couch potatoes with poor eyesight who don't want to get up and go over to see what the oven is doing. It took me several days to get it working, apparently the software update app that I downloaded was corrupted and I eventually deleted and reinstalled and then it worked.

Yes the fan runs for a long time after the oven is done, but I view that as protection for the electronics up top.
The vent for the ovens is under the bottom oven, a big improvement from the previous arrangement where the oven vented directly under the touch pad and electronics.
Note that you need to run the meat probe almost all the way in, otherwise it is influenced by the oven temperature and will prematurely signal that cooking is complete.

I spent a couple of days calibrating the ovens - they were pretty close as it came, and all 3 probes I have were pretty close too (the old probe works in the new oven). I undid the "auto temp correction" which subtracts 25 degrees from the set temperature in convection mode because the oven is just barely "convection" in the convection bake and convection roast modes.

Yes, the oven does look good but I'm more interested in how it cooks and how it holds up.

review_text:
The seller did a great job packing the oven. It arrived with no damage at all.

I really like the look of this oven. It is very sleek and the materials used appear to be above average. I consider myself a somewhat hands-on person so I did the install myself. My first install but was able to get it done in about an hour. Most of that time was relocating the power cable junction box behind the oven since the oven would not slide all the way back.

Once it was in everything worked great. I am not used to the hidden element on the bottom of the oven but like that feature a lot from a cleaning standpoint. I would imagine that will also make for an element that will last longer than an exposed one. During pre-heating the oven does make a little extra fan noise but not overly so. It does seem to take a little longer to come up to temperature, but it cooks way faster than my old one (and I did verify the temperature with an oven thermometer). I think it is due to the convection-like action with how the heat is circulated. Frozen biscuits cook about 5 minutes faster and have much more even browning than my old oven. I would recommend that you monitor any new dish the first time to make sure you don't overcook.

The only thing I am having to get used to is the timer. I am finding myself putting the timer on for 10 hours instead of 10 minutes. I am sure I will get used to that in the coming months though. One great feature about the timer is the subtle chime that is heard one minute before the time's up.

review_text:
Want to be clear that this review is for the OVEN and the company I bought it from, however ASK WHO will be delivering it. If it's A&M Trucking ("AJ Madison") in the San Francisco/San Jose bay area, READ MY WARNING BELOW.

I am a baker. I'm a stay-at-home-dad and because I like to eat yummy stuff I've had to learn to bake great treats (cooking - not so fun for me; I'm terrible at tracking more than one item at a time; timing). I bought this primarily for the baking functionality - the double oven, the digital panel, and the ability to both set "Cook time" and "Delay start" times. If I could I'd have an oven I could use an app on my phone to activate & control, but that doesn't exist (yet, though I do know for a fact it's being tested). This range is amazing. Just this morning I was standing over it with my coffee in hand wonder what the heck I was ever going to use the warming zone for? I have two kids who are yanking on my clothes anytime I'm preparing food - there's never a need for me to keep food warm, it's one the plates the moment it's done.

Suddenly I had to step outside for a moment and without much thought I turned the warming zone on "Hi" and placed my ceramic mug down on it. When I came back (nearly an hour and 1/2 later... got side tracked) my coffee was nice and hot. Not "burn the roof of your mouth or tongue" hot, but pleasantly hot where you can take a nice sip or small gulp and tolerate the heat. It was awesome.

I had this experience after having the oven for nearly a month already! I was already in love with this oven/range. Like most of my purchases, the wife thought I was insane wanting to spend $1200+ on a range, when we rent an apartment! However it's been very very much worth it. This oven will go anywhere we do - and it's not typical to own your own appliances in the SF bay area when you're a renter.

Worth EVERY PENNY. (FYI - I recommend you get the SquareTrade warranty that comes up as an option upon checkout/cart adding. On-site service for 4 years? Amazing!)

Now, for the shippers. A&M Trucking ("AJ Madison") tried to extort money (cash) out of me upon delivery. I bought from HCcost here on Amazon and THOROUGHLY reviewed all shipping polices and charges PRIOR to purchasing. Knowing we live in an upstairs apartment I scrutinized the HCcost's shipping policies for ANYTHING to do with additional charges for stairs. Nothing. The email they sent me acknowledging my order and delivery status even read, "When your appliance is delivered it will be brought into your room of choice and all packing materials will be collected and removed, if you choose."

When A&M pulled up they informed me there was a charge for stairs. Being no dummy I happily said, "okay, just let me know how much I owe." They pulled the oven off the truck and opened it up so I could inspect - they informed me this was so they didn't carry it all the way up to my place only to have me discover a defect. They then carried the oven up and placed it in my kitchen. After removing a little more packing material from it they took it upon themselves to proclaim they don't normally remove the packing materials but they could for a fee. I explained the policies from where I bought the oven said all packing materials would be removed but said if I needed to return the oven for any reason it might be advisable to keep them just in case. I told them to just leave them downstairs (where they removed 98% of it) and I'd put it in the recycle bin/trash. Then when I walked downstairs with them they said I owed for 47 stairs. They said the first two "flights" were free. I asked what constituted a "flight" and they said 7 stairs is a flight. (Most places recognize 16-18 steps in a flight). I had counted the steps on my way up, 35. Big difference. I told them I had no cash, which they insisted on. I offered to pay by credit card, but they said, "cash only." This seemed VERY fishy. I told them I never carry cash (I don't, I'm all plastic, all the time). They actually said to me, "Well I wish you would have told us that before we started because we would have never carried the appliance up then." I told them to have their company bill me for anything they believed I owed, as I didn't not contract them for delivery, I simply purchased it from a company who contracted them.

20 minutes later I got a call from someone claiming to be from A&M trucking asking for my credit card number. If the company had any authorization to charge me for anything additional they would already have this information so I told the man I would happily pay anything they felt I owed AFTER I inquired with the company I bought the appliance from. The man got very belligerent all of a sudden. He told me I owed for 47 stairs. I told him they guys who delivered said I got the first two flights free AND that there were only 35 stairs. He told me there 47. I offered to video myself walking up the steps and counting them and to put it on YouTube for him so he could verify. He cursed at me and hung up. After emailing HCcost the details of my problems with A&M Trucking the apologized and confirmed there was not supposed to be any additional shipping or delivery charges.

review_text:
It looks beautiful and the double oven works well but this range has some serious shortcomings; if I had known then what I know now, we would have bought something else. If LG would give me our money back, I'd gladly take them up on it. They refused to print my review on their site so I'm posting it here.

First, there is very little space at the bottom rear of the range for the stored heavy 220 volt electric cord; I had to move our outlet under the floor to get this range to slide all the way back against the wall. Second, I hate the touch-type electronic "on-off-adjusting" feature for the "burners"; it takes much longer to go from 10 to 4, for example, than twisting or turning a knob. I think there are too many small "burners" and not enough medium sized; the left front, for example is either "small," "large," or both, the rear two burners are very small, and the right front is the only "medium/large." It also seems to take longer for the burners to get "hot" than our old range, and the top surface is much harder to clean than our old range.

Then, there is a major fault with the ovens: each door has an opening that the "latch" fits into when you close the door. In the first week that we owned this range, something spilled while taking it out of the oven and got into this opening; it then ran down the inside of the two glass "windows" when we closed the door and looks like hell now. There should be a seal inside the door to prevent this from happening. (We called LG and they refuse to admit the design flaw and say we would have to pay to have that taken apart and cleaned.)

We paid a lot of money for this range and it is definitely a big disappointment.

He gave me a case number and while he was there I called GE and for sure they confirmed it was a go and would have the trade out info for me in two business days. First let me say that I am dealing with one of the most reputable Appliance Dealers in Tucson, Christie's Appliance. Second the service tech was always on time and courteous and tried his darndest to fix it. This appliance dealer's service department is a designated GE service company for Tucson area. product_title: GE JK5000DFWW 27" White Electric Single Wall Oven - Convection
review_text:
When my Jenn Air convection wall oven finally died, I began the search for a replacement. After having 3 touchpads fail in the time I owned it, I was not looking for another Jenn Air. I had already replaced my Jenn Air ceramic cook top with a Kenmore one, which has been excellent, and my Jenn Air microwave with a GE Profile model, which is the best such device I have ever used. However, since Consumer Reports rated the Whirlpool oven the best, I looked at it first. Two things drove me away: the noise issue and the slow preheat reported by many. Since there is often a big difference in the reviews by magazines and those by people who actually live with the product, I place more value on the latter, at least when they are thoughtfully given. Noise is a big issue for my wife, and whether it was a quality control issue (some being quiet enough, others noisy), or just some owners being more sensitive to noise than others, it seemed like a bad risk either way for us. We are sensitive to noise, and I don’t care to play games of chance with such an expensive item. So we reluctantly gravitated to the more expensive GE, which at least would match the GE Microwave which sits above the oven. Also I hoped that the extra cost was for better quality components (like fans) and a robust build quality.
So far I am impressed. The new wall ovens have concealed bottom elements, which makes keeping them clean with a simple wiping down with dish detergent or vinegar a very easy task. This almost certainly means a slightly longer preheat time, however. Nevertheless, where my Jenn Air took around 10 minutes to reach 350 degrees, the GE took less than 13 minutes. Not a bad trade off in my opinion. The temperature actually reached was 352 on my Fluke thermocouple. This oven automatically adjusts the temperature when using convection, and does so differently when you choose single rack baking or multi rack. My Fluke showed temperature control to be excellent. It is also very quiet in my experience. Off course, when turned off the fan will continue to run for quite a while. As with my old Jenn Air, I simply leave door open until it cools off to speed up the process. But in this case not because of excess noise, but because I am just fussy about using more power than I need to.
Being a bread maker, a feature of the old Jenn Air I really liked was the ability to set the temperature as low as 100 degrees. This was great for proofing bread and making yogurt. Most ovens don’t allow you to set a temp below 170 degrees – a bad idea in my opinion. This oven, however, has a proof setting which gets around this. Also leaving the oven light on in an oven once it is around 100 degrees will usually keep it just right for making yogurt or rising dough.
So far this oven meets my expectations. I installed it myself, so I can confirm that it feels solid and well made. It is quiet and the controls are easy to use. Time alone will tell how durable and reliable it proves to be. But I will continue to update this review, as it can be very difficult trying to decide among such expensive items with so little shared information available.

product_title: GE JK5000DFWW 27" White Electric Single Wall Oven - Convection
review_text:
I am extremely disappointed in this oven. We have had it for two months now, and I have yet to get the temperature regulated. I've adjusted it up and down several times, and it still varies quite a bit. I have now come to the conclusion that it simply doesn't hold the set temperature correctly.

On top of that, the temperature reading is off. For instance, if I have it set for 375, and I want to increase it to 400, when I reset it for 400, the temperature that shows on the readout may be 362 or 370. If I already had it set for 375, why is it starting out at less than that?

The buttons are a real frustration, because each one has a different touch sensitivity. The temperature setting is very sensitive, so even a light touch inputs a setting. The timer buttons require a heavy touch, and the others are somewhere in between. I spend way too much time setting, canceling, and resetting.

The preheat is incredibly slow. That wouldn't be a big deal if there weren't other major problems. But, it is an added aggravation.

I have been baking for over 40 years, and I have used a number of different types of ovens, including gas and electric, so I know what I'm doing. I bake a lot, both personally and professionally, and I thought I had chosen a good oven for my needs. Unfortunately, I could not have been more wrong.

product_title: Samsung RF24FSEDBSR Stainless Steel Counter Depth 4-Door Refrigerator, 24 Cubic Feet
review_title: Some Pluses and Some Biggish Minuses
review_text:
I have no major complaints with this refrigerator after owning it for six months. It seems much better made and much better designed than my previous $8000 GE Monogram built-in which was a pile of junk (beyond belief awful in almost every way).

Let's start with the PROS. The counter depth is wonderful if you have narrow countertops and don't want the refrigerator sticking out past them and into your kitchen workspace. A really cool feature that works great are the fold up shelves that enable you to put very tall items into the refrigerator either temporarily or permanently (e.g. a turkey or wine bottle). There's a surprising amount of usable space (much more than the absolutely awful $8000 side-by-side GE Monogram). The refrigerator is amazingly easy to move in and out of its space for cleaning and servicing thanks to well-designed wheels that don't damage flooring (in my case, hardwood).

CONS: That said, there also are several issues that are consistently annoying. First, as others have noted, the angle of the spigot on the water dispenser makes it difficult to use for any container larger than a drinking glass (e.g., a measuring cup or SodaStream bottle) and even with drinking glasses you have to be pretty careful or you'll get water all over the place. Ditto ice dispensing. In addition, removing the ice dispenser bin from the refrigerator for cleaning or dumping is extremely difficult to do. The worst feature of the refrigerator that I've run into is the so-called replaceable water filters. First off they're ridiculously expensive (list price about $55.00 each). These items need to be replaced every six months so the cost over the life of the refrigerator is significant. Worse yet, the filter housing is very, very picky. After market filters (which are cheaper) don't always seal well and massive leaks are a possibility. Even more worse, although you can buy supposedly Samsung factory-sealed boxes of filters for about half what Samsung (and Best Buy) want for them, if any problems arise (and in my case they did - flooded kitchen and refrigerator), Samsung will turn their nose up at you unless you paid full price and bought the filter from their one and only approved distributor, PartStore.com. If you have a problem with your unit and are using factory parts purchased anywhere else, Samsung will deny all responsibility. Their excuse is that such parts may be knock-offs for all they know.

On the whole, I'm a lot happier with this refrigerator than I was with my grossly overpriced GE Monogram built-in but there's room for improvement. For my money the single biggest thing Samsung needs to do is cut the price of their factory filters (from their approved source) in half and they could improve the friendliness and cooperativeness of their Customer Support. I had to get Best Buy's people to contact them before they would even speak to us seriously about the filter problem.

review_text: In March 2014 we bought a Samsung counter depth refrigerator RF197ACRS from Florida Builder Appliances.  We are not sure when it first started happening but in December 2014 we noticed water in the crisper drawers and upon removing them to empty the water we found a layer of ice as this is just above the freezer.  So after contacting Florida Builder Appliances who did nothing, I called Samsung and they sent out a warranty company, Lakes Electronics.  I live in a gated community so when the gate called I decided to go out to the driveway to meet the technician.  I found it odd that he was walking up my driveway with a huge part under his arm.  I thought to myself that is odd, as an engineer myself I would think that a problem needs to be diagnosed before bringing new parts into the equation.  So after an hour the technician announces that it is all fixed but being an engineer I wanted to know more.  The technician was very reserved and would not offer much information.  I did get him to say that once this new part was installed he'd never seen this problem reoccur.  So again my engineering kicks in and I decide they had a design problem.  Well 2 weeks later same thing, and I call Florida Builder Appliances and they do nothing.  So I call Samsung and had to go through this all over again.  Amazing Lakes Electronics sends the same technician and this time he puts on a "leak" kit and tells me that Samsung instructed him that the refrigerator needed to be tipped from front to back.  Folks you don't have to be an engineer to understand that this is what we use to call a "kluge" in my business. Little did I know that it is all over the internet that there is a class action lawsuit against Samsung refrigerators since 2011?  I asked Florida Builder Appliances to give me a full refund and they have refused.  Their management is selling a product that doesn’t work; they know it and don’t care.

review_text:
We've had the refrigerator around three weeks. We're still adjusting to the different storage configuration vs. a 2-door frig. The only real disappointment is the ice maker - we never looked at the ice tray before buying; it looks pretty big but in reality it's perhaps one quarter of the capacity of the old GE frig. we had before - at most, would hold two of the old manual ice cube trays. I take a six-pack cooler of drinks to a job site several days a week; the ice for it was no problem before, but I'm very skeptical about this one making enough ice. And, there's no ice tray in the freezer to store a buffer supply of ice for high-volume occasions - a serious flaw. Even Samsung may have intended at one time to provide an ice bin in the freezer for storage - it is suggested to transfer ice to it in the manual - except there isn't one!

We've had no trouble with spilling water or ice from the door dispenser; it all seems to work fine. The counter depth fits well, it's a good-looking unit, well-lit inside. The temperature displays are convenient, and it is quiet. Overall mostly pleased, except for the ice supply.

product_title: Samsung RF24FSEDBSR Stainless Steel Counter Depth 4-Door Refrigerator, 24 Cubic Feet
review_text:
We bought this refrigerator from Home Depot and we bought it because we wanted a countertop depth size. We had heard of Samsungs 'good' reputation and reviews of the product. There only two of us and we felt that we could easily make this work. So it is nice, and there are a few quirks, like anything else, however, From day one, the ice maker never worked. We read the documentation and went through all the steps to make sure the problem was not caused during the installation. Turns out we had a few problems, and we fixed them all. We were told by the delivery folks that we had to run about 2 gallons of water through it to make sure the pump for the ice maker would work. So we did, and them fix something else, and try it again. We finally decided that we had to call Samsung. The folks were great but they told us we needed to run 5 gallons of water. Through multiple conversations, we made sure we ran through all the steps to make sure everything was correct, and at the end the put me through a tech rep. From there, everything went downhill. After the first conversation, I could barely stand it, after the second one, we were told that the problem was not caused by Samsung but by the delivery team. Please keep in mind that this whole process took about 2 months, and the fridge was still not making ice. We finally contacted Home Depot and they took charge of the problem, and dealt with Sansung. We did get it fixed, but it took another month. Now the ice maker works, but it is pretty lame. When dispensing ice, it throws it all over the place. There are two settings, one for cubes and one for crushed. Makes no difference, it all comes out crushed. Most of the time, we have to wipe the floor.
So the good:
Very esthetically pleasing
Well illuminated
Nice display on the door
Plenty of room inside for our needs, although keeping the same depth, they could have made it taller by six inches
Nice cheese drawer
Filter is well located and easy to replace
There's a shelf that splits to create a taller space... Works well when so needed

The bad:
Really poor customer support... As in frustrating and insulting - tech rep probably means that they have been trained to deal with the customer when all other options have been exhausted and avoid blame
Ice maker is too small
Ice maker does not dispense cubes even though it should
There are two levers in the door, one for ice and one for water, and they are on top of each other. One is half the length as the other which makes it inconvenient since you keep hitting it when wanting the other.
Water keeps seeping out after having filled a glass and spills on floor

My impression: Samsung should stick with TVs. I would not buy another fridge from them. Very disappointing overall due to customer support experience, but also, the water dispenser and ice maker just never worked properly.
Home Depot has really stepped up, and had it not been for them, we would have taken it back. They had the unit fixed, but unfortunately, just never really performed. I gave it two stars, because everything else is fine, although I still wish it was taller. I just hope nothing ever breaks again.

product_title: Samsung RF24FSEDBSR Stainless Steel Counter Depth 4-Door Refrigerator, 24 Cubic Feet
review_title: DON'T DO IT! Shame on you Samsung
review_text:
We bought this Samsung refrigerator when we remodeled our kitchen a couple of years ago. For the first year we loved it and had no problems with it. We started having problems with the ice maker after that. The ice maker was not making FULL ice cubes and water was leaking from where ice dispenses from. Best Buys Geek Squad came out and replaced the entire ice maker. A couple of months later the same thing started to happen. We could hear the fan inside of the ice maker area making noise. It turned out that ice accumulated near the fan and began to rub against the fan blade. Again, Best Buy sent guys out to fix it. They ordered parts to repair the entire ice maker again. This time the repairman caulked the area between the ice maker housing and the inside wall of the freezer. He said that there was a problem with warm air getting in between the wall and ice maker housing and that is what was causing the ice to melt. He said that we would not have another issue after he sealed it. Three months later it started to leak again. Geek Squad came out again. This time they only ordered sealant and a relay switch. Repairman fixed it again.
NOW, we are experiencing another issue. The ice maker has decided NOT to make ice. Now, the display is showing "Ice off" indicator. I didn't even know that the display had this function till now. I called Best Buy Geek Squad to get it repaired again. I explained to the Service Repair scheduling guy that the refrigerator is a lemon. He was apologetic about ALL of the issues we were having with this refrigerator. But, told me that it was too late to return the fridge because we had it so long. He said that Best Buy wasn't very happy, as well, because they are having to spend lots of money to continually come out to fix the fridge. I explained that Samsung should have to repair this problem FOR LIVE knowing that their
refrigerator was having ice maker issues. I shouldn't have to purchase extended warranties to cover my ice maker since they knew it was an ongoing issue. I explained that it is wrong that Best Buy has to foot the bill for Samsung's crappy fridge.
We had always bought American made refrigerators in the past and had good luck with them.
I gave this a 2 star rating because it is a nice looking fridge and we were looking for a counter depth fridge to go with our new kitchen. The fridge is somewhat small for our family of five. Although, the ice maker doesn't stay up well with the consumption of ice that we use. I read that it is supposed to make ice every 45-50 minutes. Ours only makes ice approximately every 2 hours. Maybe this is another problem that I don't know about yet. Meanwhile, I have to wait another 5-7 days to have a repairman come out. Meaning that I have to buy ice till then.
Does anybody know if there is a CLASS ACTION LAWSUIT out there for this product? If not, we need to start one.
SHAME ON YOU SAMSUNG for selling a faulty product and not backing it.
I would stay clear of purchasing this refrigerator. You WILL REGRET IT!
Frustrated customer.
D.S.- Glendora, CA

The water dispenser does in fact fire the water at a 2 - 3 degree left angle. No real problem. Haven't switched the ice machine to the "Crushed" setting yet. We like cubed ice.

The three section layout is good for our needs. The center drawer has a 3 - 4 degree up or down temperature capability.

The ice maker is in the upper left-hand corner of the top refrigerator section and not in any freezer section. How it makes ice in the refrigerator section is unknown to me.

review_title: Do not buy if  you use ice
review_text:
Do not buy a Samsung RF24FSEDBSR/AA refrigerator if you use ice. I have had one for 2 years, and my ice maker has never worked properly. I have had it serviced several times, but they cannot make it work properly. It leaks water through the refrigerator door. It makes wet ice. After a while it forms ice in the mechanism which clogs it, and it stops working. I try to pull the ice maker out to break up the ice which is clogging it, but the ice accumulation prevents removal. I increase the freezer temperature to melt some of the ice. I try again and again to remove the ice maker. Eventually it comes out. I pick off all the ice, defrost it, replace it. It goes back to its normal poor operation until it freezes again, and I have to repeat the procedure.

I purchased an LG LFCC22426S for my second home. I specifically avoided any model with a which has through-the-door ice or water. As an Engineer, I think this as a complicated mechanism, and I have owned a few that never worked correctly. The LG has an ice maker in its freezer drawer. It dumps ice into a rectangular tray. It is a much simpler mechanism than a through-the-door ice maker. It has worked perfectly for 5 months. It is easier to use than the through-the-door ice makers. You just pull the freezer drawer open and grab a handful of ice. No waiting while the ice maker churns and churns trying to spit out a few wet cubes.

The Samsung RF24FSEDBSR/AA refrigerator has its through-the-door ice maker in its refrigeator compartment. It reduces the refrigerator shelf and door space on one side. The LG LFCC22426S has significantly more refrigerator space even thouhg it has essentially the same exterior dimensions as the Samsung.

The Samsung refrigerator cost over $2000 only 2 1/2 years ago, and I am almost ready to give it to the Junk Man.

product_title: Samsung RF217ACWP Energy Star 19.7 Cu. Ft. 33 In. Wide French Door Refrigerator with Freezer Drawer, White
review_text: I purchased this refrigerator at Lowes in late August of 2012. By June of 2013, the paint was peeling off the handles and the vegetable bins were filling with water. The ice maker had completely quit working. This refrigerator is in a 2 person household, where both adults work full time jobs and rarely entertain at home. It does not get a work-out at all. I did purchase the extended warranty, figuring I'd never have to use it, but boy am I glad to have it. The first round of repairs took 2 visits and a complete emptying and shut down of the refrigerator, forcing me to take time off work as well as find a friend to store my food for me. 6 months later, I am having similar problems, but apparently this time it is some coil that freezes over and must be replaced. I had to wait 8 days to receive the part and am expecting the repair man to come next week. For this repair, I must empty my refrigerator and freezer and leave it unplugged for 24 hours before he can fix it. The refrigerator leaks, which has also damaged my laminate floors. I have contacted Samsung about both the peeling paint and the ice maker and the leaking into the vegetable bins. Their response was maddening -- "we understand your frustration and stand behind our product. Unfortunately, you are no longer under warranty...yadda, yadda, yadda." I have also contacted the Better Business Bureau and a group of attorneys that are handling a class action lawsuit against Samsung Refrigerators. This particular model is not listed in the lawsuit yet, but according to an internet search, Samsung has just changed the model number without fixing the complaints. I so regret this purchase and I am so fed up with the people of Samsung for not standing behind their product. I really wish I would have bought an American made refrigerator (if there is still such a thing). I know had I bought a Kenmore or Whirlpool or Electrolux, I would not be experiencing the frustration and waste of time this heap of junk has cost me.

review_title: with the white-hot passion of a thousand burning suns
review_text:
I hate this refrigerator with the burning passion of a thousand white-hot suns during the apocolypse.

Men, if you're looking at this review, think of this: you'll be home after a long day at work, ready to tussle in the sheets. Your woman will be ready, too, and then she'll remember: "Hey, Honey! I can't do that right now. I've got to DEFROST THE FREEZER.

My husband and I aren't monkeys, I don't think. Well, I didn't think. Before we bought this refrigerator we actually prided ourselves on having graduated with Bachelor's Degrees. We wrongly made the assumption that we could operate a piece of machinery that everyone owns. Built in the 21st century. Looking all sleek and wonderful.

How wrong we were.

I look back upon our days of naivety, our days of wine and roses. Back then, we had a refrigerator that would, say, hold TWO gallons of milk in one side of the door. Our old refrigerator wouldn't have vegetable and fruit drawers that would RANDOMLY FILL WITH FILTHY COLD WATER FOR NO APPARENT REASON.

Our old refrigerator didn't have an ice maker, and we just filled the ice cube trays the old fashioned way like everybody else. Was this good enough for us? NO. We had to go and get all high-falutin', buying a deluxe model that made ice for us.

Does it actually make ice? No. Not any more. The ice making portion isn't portioned off, so if a random child stuffs the ice cream back into the area that is supposed to be used for ice making, CRAAAAAAAAAAAAAACk! Ice maker arm broken. For the record, we've become frequent members of a refrigerator repair site. We're racking up points because we've replaced the ice maker arm THREE FREAKING TIMES.

I used to think that people who wrote such angry, seething reviews while everyone else was happy were basically just clueless morons who weren't working the thing right.

If that's true, I've joined the masses. SUCK IT, SAMSUNG.

product_title: GE CZS25TSESS Cafe 24.6 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel Counter Depth Side-By-Side Refrigerator
review_text: I have had this fridge since 2010 - so the model number changed once they upgraded the lights to LED, but that is probably the only difference. During the first 5 years (warranty period) I had it serviced at least twice.  The serviceman was kind enough to order me extra parts so I could have them on hand.  There was a leak in the bottom of the fridge from the cooling system.. Anyways, recently I noticed the ice cream wasn't freezing, it was turning to mush, but somehow I still had ice.  So, I paid the $99.98 to have GE service out for the 3rd and final time.  They were able to assess that it wasn't cost efficient to fix.  Basically, the closed cooling system (coolant) is leaking. This would be cost prohibitive to fix - may as well get a new machine.  I am highly disappointed that such an expensive piece of equipment doesn't operate for at least 10 years without the need of service.  GE doesn't give me a break on the cost, when all the guy has to do it plug in his diagnostic tool and immediately tells me it's a lost cause.  7-8 years and done.  Anyways, buy this machine at your own risk.  My parents had the SAME refrigerator for AT LEAST 30 years, and never had any work done on it - and barely ever pulled it out and cleaned it - so I'm saying they didn't take care of it that well.  It seems completely unacceptable that today's workmanship is this bad.

product_title: LG LDG3036ST Freestanding Gas Range, 30-Inch, Stainless Steel
review_text:
I've had this dual oven for a while now and all things considered, it is a very good looking unit and the performance outside of the center burner is very good.

The dual oven feature is great and helps when cooking multiple items. I've used the convection on the lower oven a few times now and has worked well with both desserts as well as dinner items like casseroles and lasagnas. The upper smaller oven heats up quickly and although the grate doesnt slide as well as it should, the oven works quite well.

The main beef I have with this unit is the low BTU output (8k) of the center burner. When speaking with multiple associates about this, they say it isn't supposed to be your main cooking option and that's why the output isnt great. I kind of took this with a grain of salt but after using the center burner and griddle combo for a little bit of time now, I have unfortunately concluded that its just not enough heat emitting from it. I was trying to be patient the first few times and didnt write this review until I gave it a fair shake but after using it this weekend 2 more times, I sadly have to say that it just doesn't have the punch to really cook something sufficiently. I'm not looking for a super high sear or a charring effect but when it takes 2+ minutes to finally have the bubbles of a pancake surface, I think that is just a little too long. Also since this griddle is a little thin compared to the other brands (GE and KitchenAid were much thicker and heavier while Samsung was roughly the same density), there seemed to be a couple more hot spots (near the back half) than I would have expected.

I don't want to knock this oven entirely since most of the competitors are between 8k-10k BTU's as well so this might just be the industry standard. Again I would have just wished that the heat output be just a little higher in order to give this center burner a little more versatility than what it currently is.

Outside of this, the oven looks great and performs quite well.

review_title: Just installed this last week and LOVE it. Burners have a strong flame
review_text:
Just installed this last week and LOVE it. Burners have a strong flame, light quickly and consistently, and boil rapidly. Burner grills form a continuous surface across the entire range for a ton of cooking/warming space that is wasted on other stoves. The long center burner is a nice extra, and comes with a high quality griddle surface you can overlay. The top oven preheats quickly and is the perfect size for cooking pizzas or keeping a pan or casserole warm. The lack of a drawer means the lower oven is still more than adequately roomy. The convection is a great feature as well. Can't comment on cleaning mode yet, as we've yet to try it, but we love everything else about this unit so far.

This cost a bit more than units that don't have all of this to offer, but if you have a family and enjoy cooking, the investment is more than worth it. It's cheaper than a traditional range/oven plus an additional convection oven, it takes up only the space of a traditional model, and the build quality is really impressive. I don't often gush in Amazon reviews but my wife and I highly recommend this LG oven/stove combo. We are thrilled with our purchase.

On another note, the oven on the bottom does not cook evenly at all. I cooked a layer cake in there and the sides of each of the layer cakes cooked faster on the wall side of the pan. review_title: I love this oven so far (one week in)
review_text:
UPDATE (12/2/16) - The knobs on this range are plastic and falling apart. It seems I can buy a replacement knob for $23.99 from LG, which is ridiculous considering how much I paid for the range. Also, when I said the alarm/timer is 'cartoonish' -- it's not just annoying. We don't use the timer because the 'melody' that plays is so annoying. Bought an egg timer with a "ding". :)

I bought this range from a local dealer to replace a KitchenAid range, which the computer died ($600 job to repair). I love this oven so far (one week in). I'm sharing items in my Cons only as a heads up. I would buy this range again. If the Cons were a true deal breaker for me, I would simply increase my budget and get a Viking or Wolf range (not an option for me unfortunately).

Pros
- I really like how quiet this oven is. The convection fan is quiet and with both ovens @ 425F there isn't any other fan blowing heat. My former range would turn on fans when it heated up and the convection was quite loud. I'd gotten used to it and this LG range is a pleasantly quiet.
- Burners are large and the low settings are very low. Nice range from high to low on burners.
- Oven racks have a small handle making it a bit easier to pull them out. Thoughtful and small things like this are nice.

Cons
- I knew it when I bought this range that I'd be losing a storage drawer. Not an issue, but something to think about. I'm currently using one of the ovens to store metal baking sheets. Works fine.
- Really small item -- the timer alarm is a small music melody. Some might like this. I'm slowly getting used to it. I'd greatly prefer a pleasant chime or tone for notification than a sing-along-song musical tune. Seems kinda cartoonish to me.

review_text:

The top oven is the only one we've had need of so far. With the baking dish we used was just a tad tall and it had to be slid over to the side due to the position of the broiler. Not a big deal, just a geometry issue.

The one thing that keeps it from being a 5 star is that the recess in the back of the range is different from all other ranges we have had previously. Our gas pipe stuck out of the wall 4-5 inches on the right side, while the recess was only 2 inches deep on the left. So we had to have someone remodel our gas pipe in order to push it back toward the wall. It still sticks out an inch from the wall due to the flexible hose trying to fit in the recess too.

I'm glad we bought the range, but I would have liked the usual recess in the back.

We have only had it for a few weeks now, but boy do our dishes look so much clearer and cleaner. I read some reviews that mentioned that it was difficult to hook up, but it was the same as any dishwasher I have ever installed. The only thing we needed was a hose adapter 90 degree elbow to install it and some wire nuts. You can buy a dishwasher install kit at Lowes or any other home improvement store that will include what you need.

The only thing that surprised me is how long the cycle takes. Almost a couple hours for the regular cycle. However, we run it at night and don't do more than one load per day so, no worries. In the past, I have bought a few cheap dishwashers and I am very happy that I didn't do it again. Think about it, this thing affects every meal and drink you have at your house. Spend some money on a good one so you don't waste your time and money washing dishes twice, or getting sick from the residue the washer leaves behind.

Not only does it clean the dishes very well, but the door springs work well, it makes almost no noise when running and the silverware basket comes out and goes back in easily which is nice. My old dishwashers made it difficult for whatever reason.

We are now only using the 3 in one cascade packets and it is much easier and again, the dishes look amazing. Even my 8 year old daughter mentioned how much cleaner our cups look after just two times through the wash. I definitely recommend this washer, it has been wonderful so far. Also, it shipped quickly and came in perfect condition.

product_title: GE GDT580SMFES 24" Slate Fully Integrated Dishwasher - Energy Star
review_title: Quiet like the gentle falling of the rain
review_text:
Aesthetics:
So very eye pleasing with no controls that can be bumped or but not reset by a passerby. With two curious American Bulldogs, that was a must.

The slate finish doesn't show finger prints. I LOVE my stainless steel. I don't love a stainless steel dishwasher.
I cannot tell you how many time I would open the dishwasher with wet finger or greasy fingers and bemoan that I would have to clean it YET AGAIN. It actually was a ritual, keep as many dishes in the sink, load the dishwasher 1 time before running it, clean the dishwasher, unload it, clean it again. I could pull my hair out.
The finish has completely alleviated that frustration. No more dishes in the sink either!

Features: the top rack can actually accommodate my full size day to day dishes!! Seriously. Granted they are light weight and in some cases plastic, I can get so much in this thing, it's incredible.
The top basket easily maneuvers to either accommodate those dishes on the top or slides up to let me put in a full size cookie sheet.

I really love the sanitize feature as well.
It almost feels like appliance abuse, but if we use our dishwasher for more than dishes (make sure dishwasher or autoclave safe)
My rose pruners get sanitized in this, nail clippers, scissors, anything that touches either plant or person that can be sanitized goes in here. As a super nerdy chick, I had to see if sanitized was really sanitized. To that effect, I put my nail clippers in, and swabbed them after the cycle. The swab was swabbed into some agar and set to let grow what will be there (it's like the middle school experiment where you swabbed your school desk to see how gross it is)
Guess what. No contaminates grew after 48 or 72 hours.
That's really sanitized!!!
The wash cycle can be set to either the top or bottom only which adds convenience for those little loads.

The entire interior is stainless steel, not plastic, which means, it won't readily absorb odors. This is both good and bad.
Good: you know of your dishwasher is clean because it doesn't smell
Bad: you've never had a dirty dishwasher smell and this REEKS to high heaven and you don't know how to make it stop stinking.

Here's the solution to that "bad". In the bottom of the tub is an easy access filter that with a 1/4 turn comes out. Rinse that thing off (I do it everytime I wash) and pop it back in. Poof! Smells are gone.
It's not time consuming and I treat it like the lint filter in my dryer. It's easy when that's your mentality.

Hook up was very simple and this unit, unlike many others, comes with a new drain hose.
You WILL NEED a elbow connector that is not provided. A quick trip to lowes with the manual and they plucked one off of a nearby shelf. They are well aware of this as MANY new units need it to install.

How quiet is 48 dbs?? The manual says its like hearing the rain outside. Great because the rain is only ever one volume... It's like a gentle rain or the printer in the adjacent office working that you o lay hear if the air conditioner is off. It really is very quiet. So quiet that I actually made my husband pull it out because I heard the water dripping down the drain and thought the unit was leaking.

My favorite little part: the "all done" chime. Like a sweet little song, it chimes that it's done and the light that was once orange (depicted in my pictures) is now green.

product_title: Whirlpool WTW5800BW 3.8 Cu. Ft. White Top Load Washer - Energy Star
review_title: The Worst Washing Machine ever Manufactured...by anyone...
review_text:
This washer is defectively engineered. Whirlpool wanted to create a top loading, water sparing machine, so their idea was to come up with a tiny agitator on the bottom of the tank and allow it to "wobble" to force the water through the clothing. The water used for washing does not cover the clothing, and the agitator kind of tries to move the water through the clothing.

That does NOT happen. The clothes do NOT come out clean. I suppose it is possible to wash similar size, small items like underwear in it. But you can't mix clothing or bedding types in the same load.

Compare this pathetic machine with a modern front load washer that uses gravity to tumble the clothes against each other in two directions, as well as allowing them to soak momentarily on the bottom of the tub with each change of direction. You can't help but wash the clothes.

Cabrio runs the clothing through a very thorough rinse cycle, trying to make up for the deficiencies of washing. The clothes get all tangled and knotted up. It also unbalances easily as a washed sheet will eventually gather up smaller items into a ball and the agitator will just smash against that ball of sheet and underwear.

I submitted my review to Whirlpool and I suggested they redesign the washer and tilt the clothing tub to a 35% angle, which would start to use gravity...but that would expand the footprint of the machine. They said no-way and took my review off line.

I sent mine back after 4 days and paid the restocking fee. It is the worst washer made. You'd be better off using your great-grandmother's washer with an attached hand wringer. (Watch your fingers). There have also been technical, electrical and mechanical problems with it, even after a short term of ownership.

I got a Maytag front loader instead, and it works great.

I think the Cabrio is best used as land-fill.

product_title: Whirlpool WTW5800BW 3.8 Cu. Ft. White Top Load Washer - Energy Star
review_title: Do not purchase this HE washer
review_text:
I tried to post review on Whirlpool site but it never was approved. That would explain majority of the positive reviews on their site. We purchased our washer/dryer set at Costco since they have a wonderful return policy. This set is going back because of the washer. The actual washer model is 5810BW which is made specifically for Costco. It is the same as 5800 BW sold here. This washer does not rinse the detergent out of our laundry. After the first use whole family was itching because of the detergent left in the laundry. We have been using the same detergent for many years and in fact we used up most of this bottle with our old washer. I also am aware of differences between HE and regular machines and specifically checked instructions on the amount of detergent to use. It is Kirkland Signature HE detergent so it is designed for this washer. After the first fiasco I started using less detergent - 1/2 to 1/8 of recommended amount. The itching stopped but if our laundry had any stains they would not come out. With our old washer (also Whirlpool and also from Costco) I just had to pre-treat with a Shout spray and toss it in the washer. All stains would usually come out. With this washer I had to wash one t-shirt 3 times to get a stain out. How is this saving water? I also use additional rinse cycle for all of the loads because I have no desire to itch again. How is this helping with the water use?
I took a video of the washing cycle since the washer has a glass lid. You can clearly see the white item sitting on top of the load throughout the whole washing cycle. Small items do circulate through detergent but larger items stay in one position and do not move. When I hand wash items I also do not submerge them in to the water and rub. I use a little detergent and rub the item against itself, but this is not what this washer does. The washer just moves its "washplate" back and forth and wet items just vibrate on it.
I use dress shirts from Costco which are treated with water repellent. This washer cannot get this shirt wet on normal cycle. I have to use deep water cycle to even get the shirt wet. First time I did not believe my eyes - had to open the lid and make sure that part of the shirt was dry at the end of the wash cycle! The heavier items like bath towels do not get clean and stink after the first use. This rarely happened with our old washer. And don't get me started on the "spray rinse". I am not sure who came up with this concept and what it actually rinses. If you watch videos of Samsung or LG HE top loaders, these washers have a nozzle which sprays water ON your laundry that is stuck to the sides of the drum after a spin cycle. I can see how this can do something like rinse. This washer just pours water at the center of the drum from where it happily drains in to the holes in the bottom. How this can possibly rinse anything is way past my understanding. There is no way to overwrite any of the settings or add a little water.
The sensing process is unreliable. If I put few small items, the washer will add a lot of water, 5 inches or more, and the items would be swimming. It I put larger item, like a towel, it will absorb all the water and there would be almost no water in the tub. Ether this technology is bad or Whirlpool's implementation is bad.
The only good thing I can say about this washer is that it spins laundry very well. The laundry comes out much drier and therefore dryer does finishes much faster. This is well compensated by washer taking more that twice as long as our old "inefficient" washer did. I should have fixed our old washer instead of buying this new one, more so since I already diagnosed what the problem was. We thought to update our 14 year old set with the new one - what a mistake.

As I understand it is the government that is mandating these water and energy savings. How about starting from the government itself? On my way to work I see on-ramps being watered every morning, being that it is drought in California and all. How about saving water there? Also mandate more water efficient landscapes instead of planting grass everywhere. I wish the government would stay the heck out of my laundry room.

product_title: Whirlpool WTW5800BW 3.8 Cu. Ft. White Top Load Washer - Energy Star
review_title: Wonderful results if you can unlearn what you “Know” about washing
review_text:
It has only been a short while, but I love this washing machine. It uses fewer resources (water and soap) and my clothes are cleaner.

I have read the critics of this machine. I want to respond to some of the complaints. First, it IS louder than my traditional washer. This is not a big deal to me. Is it really a big deal? Next, each load may take longer. What is your rush?
I may get flamed for this, but my guess is that the folks that have an issue with this dryer are not following the directions and/or are clinging to lessons that were true with earlier washing machine technology. In many cases, they return perfectly good machines. This drives up the cost of all of us. I would like to see folks study the manual and call for help before demanding the retailer take back a perfectly good product.

Some people claim it leaves soapy residue. My guess is that they were using up their non-HE soap. In general, HE likes liquid detergent. Powders, which have traditionally been more effective, struggle to dissolve properly in this environment. Try skipping all the powders and see if you are happy. (Sorry Oxi Clean). Also, it is important to use LESS soap. This is hard for some of us that were brought up on MORE soap=CLEANER clothes. This was true. It is not true with HE washing machines.

Other people complain that their clothes were still wet after the spin dry. My guess is that they used the wrong cycle. I have not seen any evidence of this problem, although it was mentioned by reviewers on other boards.

All in, this washing machine is a great, entry level HE washing machine.

However - it's probably a year old and it looks it. The stainless steel around the controls on the front has been scratched - someone cleaned it with the wrong type of pad. The burners also have burnt stuff on them that I couldn't remove with conventional cleaners. I was frustrated each time I cleaned the stainless steel around the controls on the front, because I had to first clean it with a damp sponge and soap, then with a damp sponge without soap, and finally buff it with a dry cloth to remove the water spots.

But what I really disliked about it was the fan. It blows warm air from the front door while it cooks and for 15 minutes afterward. I think it is designed to keep the door cool so it won't be a hazard. But it seems like this range would really heat up a kitchen in the summer.

review_title: Looks great and seems to be of high quality
review_text:

product_title: GE PS920SFSS Profile 30" Stainless Steel Electric Slide-In Smoothtop Range - Convection
review_text:
Great stove, been using it extensively since we got it 2 weeks ago and are very happy. Boils water very quickly, oven works great and the auto temp probe is a great tool. Warming drawer is great for heating pies. Flat top is easy to clean, with no knobs to clean around. We saved several hundred dollars over purchasing in Home Depot/Lowes/Sears, and the stove was delivered to our door in perfect shape. Very pleased not only with the stove but also with the entire transaction on Amazon.

Follow up review after about 1 year of using this stove: Still working great but one thing to watch out for is to not spill an excessive amount of water on the cooktop as there are vents along the front and rear. Inside those vents are circuit boards which do not mix well with water. We did blow one out after a pot boiled a lot of water over the edge and it was covered under warranty. Just something to be aware of.

Also, my initial fears that a family member or one of our cats might accidentally push a button and turn a burner on have proved pointless, it would seem very difficult to do at best. Lastly, there are audible beeps when a button is pushed which is also a good thing. We weren't sure of this before purchasing.

product_title: LG WT5680HWA TurboWash 5.2 Cu. Ft. White With Steam Cycle Top Load Washer - Energy Star
review_text:
After our front load washer broke 4 times in 8 years, I decided it was time for a change. Now I can only wonder why we didn't do this sooner!

After pouring over reviews and consumer ratings on multiple sites/sources for days, I finally decided to purchase this machine for several reasons. Hopefully, the amount of research I did prior to our purchase can help someone else limit theirs. ;)

The first reason I chose this machine is because it's a top loader. I never loved our front loading machine because of the maintenance requirements, and consistent stale smell from wet lint, dog hair etc. that would be left behind in the rubber gasket.

The next reason was because this model has a soak cycle available. When I gave up 'soaking' at the time we purchased our front loading machine, I had no idea how much I would miss having it. With active kids, sports stains, etc, it was a must-have for us.

The last reasons I selected this machine was it's huge capacity (for handling our king size bedding) and warranty.

I admittedly was concerned by the 'out of balance' reviews and comments indicating the lack of water used in these top loading HE machines... I just couldn't help but wonder if it would be enough to get items truly clean. So much so, I almost opted for another front loader but ultimately decided since this model offered a 'water plus' feature (essentially allowing you add additional water) coupled with Best Buy's 14 day return policy, I would give it a shot. After muliple loads of wash, including several very large loads, I can honestly say I have no concerns whatsoever by the amount of water being used and am thrilled with how clean the clothes have come out.

All in all, I'm very happy with the purchase. Although it was expensive and I haven't gotten to use all the cycles yet, this machine appears to be a keeper. We did purchase an extended warranty, which for us, is uncommon. But, based on the track record of appliances these days, especially our prior washer, it's piece of mind if nothing else.

Good luck!

product_title: LG WT5680HWA TurboWash 5.2 Cu. Ft. White With Steam Cycle Top Load Washer - Energy Star
review_text:
My (Front Load) Whirlpool Duett broke down after 8 good years of great service. I was told it would be too costly to repair and that all front loaders stink. So in good faith I started to look at the alternative...a top loader! I did my research online, looked at different machines in the store and came up with a favs list of the things my 'new baby' had to have. I decided on this LG. I read alot of the reviews, too! Once it was delivered, I read the manual, loaded it just like they say in the book (because ppl online kept complaining about the wastefullness of water to balance the load and how long it would take to wash one load due to that fact), then I started washing different types of loads..big and bulky, sanitary, heavy duty and of course the normal. People were right, it is very deep. I am not a short person, just average 5'7, but I really had to stretch to pick up the stuff from the bottom of the drum. I stood there and watched this thing do its job... making a long story short, I don't like to use the word hate, so I will say I VERY MUCH DISLIKE this machine! While in sanitary, my clothes just floated in water while the tub was sloooowly going around and around and around. That went on for quiet a while until I got borred and walked away, came back to watch it float some more and left again lol
Then I washed my sons cheap, very thin and lite nylon/polyester full size summer comforter, fitted queen sheet and 2 std sized pillow cases. This water wasting beast required THE WHOLE TUB being filled with water. I mean come on now...5.2 cu. Ft of water for just a small little maybe half size load? I am sure my Utility Co would love me for using all this water, but my pockets aren't that deep! The manual says it weighs the load in the beginning? Well I guess the scale was incorrect in my case!? The rest of the other loads I washed came up short too. Most of my clothes were barely moved during the cycles. Coming from a front loader, I am used to see my clothes being tumbled around, all equally being swooshed and turned in the water. If I wanted my clothes washed gently and barely wet, I would have used the delicate cycle. So neatless to say this machine has its water usage all mixed up and I am exchanging it today for another front loader. So happy about my 30 day exchange policy!
When the sales man that sold me this machine saw me and I told him how much I 'disliked' the LG, he told me "Once a front loader, always a front loader" I just wish he would have told me that before, not after the fact!

review_text: We bought an LG top-loading washer in Nov 2015 and since the first load we have noticed issues. The washer leaves stains, debris and discolorations on our clothes - the come out dirtier than they go in! We have had technicians to our home 3 times and have tried a variety of fixes per their suggestions - try more detergent, try less detergent, try tub cleans, try water softeners, try less clothes, try more clothes. Nothing has helped. The last technician came and admitted the washer is not working normally, but he could not diagnose an actual problem. After waiting days for customer service to call us about a follow-up (which they assured us would happen), we called them and were given a similar run-around. Today we spoke to a supervisor in customer management and he said they get complaints like this a lot and "can't replace everyone's machines". His solution was to send another technician out to look at the washer. We told him at this point we needed them to do something more he said he could not help us. He could not give us any details on what the technician would be looking for this time, or what a possible solution could be - basically he told us there is no solution, even though we are dissatisfied and under warranty. LG is not standing behind their product or providing satisfactory customer service.

review_text:
Hopefully, for the last time, I have learned my lesson to not succumb to a pretty face. I did a partial kitchen remodel and because I wanted to leave the wall behind the stove exposed for artwork, I decided to get this stove which has the controls on the front panel. Bad decision on my part. The location of controls is just one of many poor design features of this stove and I lament that I spent this much money on such a product. The control panel is in a vulnerable position that seems to attract every drip, spill and splatter, and the flimsy clear plastic sheet over the digital read-outs is already wrinkled. As many other reviewers have already noted on other vendor sites, the right front burner is impossible to regulate. In fact, I had a service person come to my home and he replaced the control mechanism for that burner, and it made no difference whatsoever. There is a design flaw in that burner. The most irritating thing about this stove, however, is that it requires an inordinate amount of time and energy to keep the surface clean. Personally, I do not want to have to spend so much time applying the special cleaner, scouring with the special plastic scrubber, and scraping with the special razor tool that is provided for the task. It is a nice looking stove, but I strongly recommend that you don't support GE's effort to perpetuate the manufacture of such ill-conceived products.

I must add, however, that the customer service provided by GE was outstanding in every way. If only the product, itself, reflected such conscientiousness.

review_title: Solid range with ineffective burner layout
review_text:
The range works well. Materials are solid, assembly and finish are good. However, it is needlessly bulky. The area with the knobs and oven controls sticks out more than needed. I would not recommend it for smaller kitchens.
Burner controls are solid and precise knobs. Unfortunately, oven controls are all digital and require lots of button presses, even for simple operations such as adjusting oven temperature.
My main gripe is with the distribution and layout of the burners. The range has 5 burners: 2 identical small burners, 2 identical large burners, and 1 power burner.
- The 2 identical small burners are underpowered. Boiling a small pan of water takes too long. The range would have been more useful with 1 mid-size burner in addition to 1 small burner.
- That second small(er) burner should also have been in the back, not in the center of the range.
- It would be more practical to have the two larger burners in front, with the power burner in the center.
I understand that cooking needs and styles are individual -- but do pay attention to the burner layout and the oven controls before you order this range. Once it is delivered, we found, it cannot be returned.

review_text:
Update:

Still a great stove functionally speaking. Unfortunately, the burner labels (showing which burner the knob controls, light, high, low, etc) have completely worn off or are almost worn off. I have only used water and occasionally glass cleaner to get off grease. I'm disappointed in this aspect and given the location of the knobs (get dirty easy) I would not have expected them to wear off in 3 years of use). I will be contacting the manufacturer.

We purchased this stove when we moved into a new home. I did a fair amount of research and it was tough because there are a LOT of good gas ranges out there. I eventually settled on this one. We were able to buy it at a local appliance dealers massive warehouse sale, something we didn't even plan on going to until the last minute but ended up buying all our appliances there at far below the lowest prices we could find online.

It looks high end and bigger than it is. Its what people comment on first when they enter my kitchen. So far (3 months of heavy home use) I've had no complaints with any of the cooking functions and I've used all of them except the self-clean. My favorite part is how the range sits on top of the counter and covers that little crack that is usually between the stove and counter. The oven seems to cook very evenly and the convection mode when using more than one rack means no rotating pans which is nice! I have not noticed any excessive heat out of the vents. The stainless cleans up very well. Yes, it will scratch like all stainless does. That doesn't bother me. I love to cook for fun, and I cook nearly all our meals from scratch for a large family. My appliances and kitchen gear get used hard! Scratches are just part of using stainless and I don't think it degrades the look at all.

My one negative would be the control panel. While its easy to use, because of its location and angle I tend to spill things on it quite easily. That said, I didn't want controls on the back, nor would I want to lose stovetop space either, so the logical place is there. I just wish it sat more flush with front of the oven and didn't catch my spills so easy.

review_text:
I purchased this stove and the Amazon installation service. The installer arrived without the necessary attachments and hoses. He was required to remove the old stove. He did not since he came in a car. The old stove sat in my garage till we removed it ourselves. He also did not check the stove for to insure that it was operating properly. That process would have involved turning on the oven and running it for 10 minutes. He would have determined that the fan was not working.
I used the oven once, and the house filled with gas.
After multiple phone calls with Amazon over a three day period, they ordered another technician to check the stove o determine if it was defective.
He was not able to come for two days. We now had been waiting for a resolution for one week. When he did arrive he determined that the stove was defective.
At that point Amazon contacted the retailer who advised that I had to pack up the stove in the original packaging and send it to them.
They also wanted the technician's report, which was finally provided. When they received it, they emailed me that a GE technician would have to evaluate the stove to determine if it was defective. After three weeks, the stove remains, and I am without a resolution.
What is so disturbing is that Amazon had no process in place to remove a defective product, and the responsibility lies squarely with the customer.
I still cannot believe that Amazon expected me to repackage this stove in the original packaging and send it back to the manufacturer.
I strongly urge anyone considering a purchase of this cost and size to bi-pass Amazon and go to a local retailer, especially since in this case it involved safety issues and the proper installation of a gas powered product. To date the stove remains.
My family and I are beyond frustrated and disappointed especially since Thanksgiving is next week, and plans for dinner had to be canceled.
