product_title: GE PHS920SFSS Profile 30" Stainless Steel Electric Slide-In Induction Range - Convection
review_title: EXCELLENT RANGE - BUT BEWARE PAN SIZE REQUIREMENTS!
review_text:
I ordered this GE induction range from another retailer and then spent a few hundred dollars on a brand-new set of Circulon Symmetry induction-ready cookware. I was loving my new induction range and how FAST it boiled water, until I tried to use one of my three new "10-inch" pots/pans that came in the set on the dominant front right power burner, which the manual says requires a "minimum 8-inch" pan size. The 10-inch pans would not work, though they worked on the smaller burners. Meanwhile, my 30-year-old 10-inch cast iron pan worked fine on it, but I'm reluctant to use it due to its rough bottom that could scratch the cooking surface. Also, the 8-inch induction conversion disk I bought heated up just fine.

I called GE for a service appointment but in the meantime, I continued to try & troubleshoot why this was happening because it made no sense. I finally figured out that you have to measure the BOTTOM of the pan, not the top, so beware of the fact that every pan in the world is advertised and sold is by its top diameter, not the bottom part that touches the stove. I called GE customer service and the best they could do was offer me a $50 rebate certificate if I want to buy yet another GE appliance, which I have no need for. It will cost me much more than that to buy a 12-inch induction-ready frying pan so I can actually use this power burner which occupies one-third of the entire cooking surface. As most of us are right-handed, I'd assume, like me, most of us favor the front right burner for most of our cooking. You won't be able to do that with this range. So if you choose to purchase it, don't buy new cookware without measuring the BOTTOM of the pan if you want to use the dominant power burner. The Circulon frying pans have a flat bottom that is at least 2 inches in diameter smaller than the top diameter. Amazon (and other retailers) sell a 2-pan package for $59.99 that includes a 10" and a 12" pan.

Other than this issue, I do like the range. Burners heat up super-fast. I roasted a lamb shoulder last night and it smoked like crazy, I had to put my fan on high and open the terrace door a couple of inches...but I'm not sure if it had anything to do with the oven as much as the minced garlic I brushed on it at 450 degrees for half an hour. It stopped smoking after about 45 minutes and the roast came out great. So after 3 1/2 weeks, I guess I'm liking it, so far...

(Update):

OK, it's now 6 weeks later and I'm LOVING this range. I guess the above dilemma turned out to be a big "duh" but GE should definitely state that the critical pan size is the stove surface contact diameter, not the "pan size" as most manufacturers advertise, nor even the actual interior cook surface diameter. With this technology, appropriate pans must have a perfectly flat bottom. Since most pans curve outward from there, this builds in a discrepancy. (GE, please add this to your advertising specifications!)

To address other comments I've read here and elsewhere: When I clean it, I do usually turn the burners on accidentally but this is no problem because (a) they don't generate heat, and (b) after 30 seconds or less they turn themselves off anyway. The only exception is the oven control, but hey - the illumination is a big clue and all you have to do it touch it to turn it off. The same thing happened in cleaning my old electric range touch controls, or with any touch microwave oven control.

Mr. Burns' review stated that the oven racks are difficult but I do not have that problem. My installer, a general handyman, put the special ball-bearing slider rack in in 10 seconds without even reading the instructions, and I've subsequently moved it myself with no problem. I love the ball-bearing sliders. The other two racks slide easily for me as well, so...(??)

I do get the buzzing sound when using certain burners at certain heat settings but it's not really an issue. The benefits of the super-fast heating outweigh that and you're soon enough distracted with the act of cooking. With the new 12" Circulon pan I bought, the power burner works great...and I'm delighted to finally have the super-sized fry pan I always wanted :). My old, and luckily magnetic steel spaghetti pot works fine on it as well.

I have also used the oven several times subsequently, and no smoking or odors. I think the instructions state that "first time" there may be some odor from surface finishes burning off. I do not have that now.

Also, the built-in meat thermometer is great - but has a very short "leash." I wanted to use it on a chicken roasting near the bottom of the oven while I had an appetizer on the top rack, and the cord wouldn't reach. Next time, I'll reverse the order but in this case the oven was already hot. When roasting in the normal position, i.e. centered in the oven, it's great, because it will alert you when the meat temperature is achieved. In the above case, I just used a stand-alone instant meat thermometer instead. Not a problem.

I also love the extra-large oven window. And finally, I love the soft blend of the dark charcoal-gray color with the stainless steel. It's a welcome relief from the stark black-and-stainless look of the past 20 years.

product_title: GE PHS920SFSS Profile 30" Stainless Steel Electric Slide-In Induction Range - Convection
review_title: Researched for 6 months and chose to get the GE. Here are my thoughts.
review_text:
On GE's implementation of induction:

Please read up on how induction works before buying an induction range. It's nothing like ordinary electric cooktops.

- The induction range is amazingly fast and responsive. With a very thick, 7-ply Demeyere skillet (which normally takes a while to heat up even when empty), the medium-sized burner can boil 1cm water in under 10 seconds. When you turn the heat down, the response is nearly instantaneous -- even with the large heat capacity of this skillet, the water slows its boil in less than 3 seconds, and that's on a smaller burner that does NOT have the "power boil" feature.
I read numbers like this when I was researching induction and they didn't impress me. Really you have to see it in action to realize how much time it saves.

- I heard complaints about "buzzing" on GE's previous model of induction range. Some people even returned it for that reason. Here's the skinny:
> When on low heat, below 5 1/2, the range "clicks" as it (presumably) turns on and off. The click is about as loud as lightly tapping a Bic pen against the counter. I don't find it distracting or annoying.
> When on high heat, you can hear an "electric" sound. It doesn't sound much different to me than the sound I hear when I turn on high-powered standard electric cooktops, except that the electric cooktop is usually silent after a short time while the induction range keeps making the sound.
> The sound itself isn't loud, and I wouldn't describe it as "buzzing." What it sounds like is an electric transformer. I'm sure you've heard one before -- they are the giant grey cylinders on some power lines. You hear the same sound near high-tension power lines. It's exactly like that (in fact, the sound is probably coming from a transformer in the range), but it isn't as loud. I don't have sound measuring equipment, but i'd say that it's noticeable in the kitchen but not in the adjacent dining room except for when everything else is silent.

- While arguably the greatest benefit of induction is that the range can vary temperature with even greater control than gas, this range does do the "on/off" switching at low settings (those below 5 1/2 out of 10). In practice, this hasn't reduced temperature or caused hot-spotting like it does on a electric glasstop, but it might when using very cheap, thin pans.

- GE's range detects pan sizes and won't turn on if the pan is off the burner or is too small. This prevents accidentally heating a stainless steel wedding ring, for example, or a steel spatula. It also prevents you from using small pans on large burners, though this isn't a problem in practice... Except for the very large burner. We don't have any pans large enough for it to turn on. Not a problem though, the other burners work perfectly (Update: We now have a few pans large enough for the big burner and they heat up even faster than the other burners. According to the C-Net review, the large burner is the fastest-heating burner they have ever seen by quite a bit).

- On changing pans: This was surprisingly cheap and easy for us. T-Fal has a whole set for under $99 (as if this writing) that works perfectly on induction. See http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B000GWL8T4/
We have some "nicer" pans, like Demeyere, but they don't seem to work any better and cost a fortune (A single skillet, while clearly well made, cost three times more than the entire T-Fal set!).
You still want to do your homework on induction. If magnets do not stick to your pan's bottom, they probably won't work at all. The pan's bottom surface must made from one of: Most types of stainless steel, mild (ordinary) steel, or cast iron. Aluminum pans work only if the bottom is made from one of the above--all aluminum or all-copper pans do not work at all

On the oven:

- If you are worried about changing all your cook times with a new oven, note that you can adjust the thermostat of the GE to match your old range.

- The racks don't seem to be especially well designed/manufactured, The slide-out rack was very difficult to fit into the oven, even with significant force, and scratched its sides a little. The other racks seem to be a little too wide as well and are difficult to pull out. They also make a rather unpleasant grinding sound as they slide along the oven walls.
(UPDATE December 2015: The racks have "set" and are now easy to slide in/out. The aforementioned scratches were not deep and did not penetrate the protective powder coating of the inside of the range).

- The oven doesn't preheat especially quickly, but it does tell you its temperature in realtime as it heats.

- We haven't used it much at all and probably need more practice, but we did try cooking two pizzas at the same time with convection mode. The top pizza did not cook as much as the one on the bottom, though it did have slightly thicker toppings. Technically for 2 pizzas, we are suppose to position two racks equidistant from the center of the oven. We kept the 3-rack configuration because, as mentioned above, shifting racks is awkward.

- The oven's window is larger than almost any oven's I've ever seen. It seems larger in person than the photo makes it look.

- The oven light is near the door of the oven, so I guess it's easy to replace. I've never had to replace an oven light, though, so this is speculation.

- The convection fan is audible but not loud, high-pitched, or distracting. It sounds more like white noise.

On the controls:
- The entire control surface is capacitive touch glass, like on a smart phone. It works very well and rarely misses a tap. It is a little sensitive, though. When leaning over the oven (which admittedly is not done often), it sometimes thinks the "set timer" button has been pushed. The controls do have a lock-out feature to prevent this from happening and presumably to prevent kids from playing with it.

- Range settings start at 5 of 10 when you turn them on. You then change the power with +/- buttons that shift the value by 1/2 with each press. Thus, it's slower to set the a burner to "2" than it is with old-style knobs. This problem is partly resolved by special buttons. One burner has a "simmer" button, which immediately sets power to 2. Another has a "Melt", which sets it to 1. The large burner has a "Power broil" button, which presumably sets it above 10/10 for a time. (Update: It just sets it to 10/10)
In practice, changing settings is still pretty fast. The GE Monogram cooktop has a slide-to-set feature which I like even better, but it hasn't trickled down to the mid-range line.

- Overall I am happy with the design of the controls. They feel intuitive, and give you hints as for what to do next. For example, when you set the timer and enter the time, the "Set timer" button blinks to remind you to tell the oven that you are ready to start the timer. There are many small touches like that which tell me that the GE engineers spend some time thinking about how to make their range easy to use.

UPDATE: After two years, we have had zero problems with the unit. The glass surface still looks good, with only some very minor scratches.

product_title: GE PHS920SFSS Profile 30" Stainless Steel Electric Slide-In Induction Range - Convection
review_text:
UPDATE December 2017 - 4 years in, it's still immaculate, and everything still functions perfectly.
UPDATE December 2015 - I've had my range for 2 years and the current cooktop on it for 1.5 yrs. The range continues to operate flawlessly and the glass remains 100% scratch free, there are not even any tiny little "you have to look at it just right to see them" scratches. Follow my glass care tips below and you should see similar results. I remain completely satisfied with my range. I've bought more pans of different brands this year and none of them buzz below about level 7.5, then only mildly, if at all. If yours buzz all the time, they're either really cheaply made pans or you're cranking the heat too high. Turn it down! I seldom cook anything over setting 5 on any hob. In fact, I usually begin on 5 and turn it down to 3.5-4 once food is added. Except my hand-made wok, that baby gets cranked right up to 8 and stays there. And of course, I boil water on High, because I like water that boils in just a couple of minutes. I don't like waiting for Spaghetti Carbonara!

ORIGINAL REVIEW - I can't believe I haven't reviewed my range yet. After waiting for this model (slide-in) to be released, I took delivery of mine a year ago and have used it daily since. I've had excellent performance. The induction cooktop is the star of this show and GE got it right. TIP: shop layouts and coil sizes before committing. I really like having the largest hob in front, along with a mid-size burner. These are the two most used. I also insisted on a slide-in range, because I want all my controls up front. I had a free-standing model once, and hated having to reach across hot pots to reach the controls. Never again.

Controls are pretty intuitive and very easy to use. For each hob, heat ranges from L to H, with half step increments from 1-9 in between. That's 19 power levels per burner, if you're counting. Power Boil takes the largest hob straight to it's highest setting and Simmer moves the mid-size hobs to level 2. The small induction burner has a Melt button which sets it to 1. There's also a Warming Zone, a small radiant burner that is designed to keep sauces warm. Note that 5 (med) is the perfect starting point. If you're using higher heat for most applications, it's time to rethink the way you cook. Medium heat will get most any stovetop job done right. I have a hand-made Cen brothers Cantonese carbon steel wok. My big surprise is that I can use it on a mid-size burner, with it's wok ring turned upside down. I never need to go higher than 8. My wok begins to smoke in under a minute. This means there's no need for a flat-bottom wok, if you prefer traditional round bottom woks. At the other end, bakers will love this range because on the lowest settings, it's possible to melt chocolate without a double boiler. Another neat induction trick; when melting butter to toss croutons or for wings, I melt it right in the stainless steel mixing bowl I'll be tossing the bread or wings in. Be sure to use an oven mitt, the bowl will be hot!

Don't forget that this is a more powerful cooktop than most. Your average electric coil or radiant cooktop will have burners with max wattage ranging from 1200W-2400W. Gas cooktops have similar numbers, but expressed in BTUs. GE's induction cooktop uses 2500W-3700W. "Medium" heat takes on a whole new meaning. Dial back the heat from what you're used to. You'll be glad you did.

The oven is just as easy to use as the cooktop, and GE takes steps to make things very intuitive. After selecting Bake, for example, the buttons to select temperature light up, leading you to them naturally. This is true of all functions: the buttons for the next step light up so you'll know what to choose next. The one flaw the oven has, and shares with most others, is that the temperature it displays when it's finished pre-heating is not accurate. I strongly recommend an inexpensive oven thermometer, like the Cooper-Atkins, that can be left in the oven and used to accurately gauge temperature. http://smile.amazon.com/Cooper-Atkins-24HP-01-1-Stainless-Thermometer-Temperature/dp/B00125TABM/ref=sr_1_1?ie=UTF8&qid=1421244143&sr=8-1&keywords=oven+thermometer

The oven will heat to 550ºF, hot enough to make a pretty nice pizza. If you're still buying frozen, you ought to check out fresh. Dough is readily available, and even using jarred sauce will (but it's so cheap and EASY to make your own) give you better pies than all but the best take-out joints. My pizza stone lives on my gliding rack, up near the broiler. BTW, this oven is quite large, and will take the largest 28-30lb. turkey with tons of room to spare. My racks all slid very well until I cleaned the oven before Thanksgiving, now they're a bit sticky, but not worth losing a star over. (update - after ordering and applying some graphite, as suggested by Neon Cactus in the comments below, my oven racks glide effortlessly).

I've got standard cabinets with granite tops. My range fits well, with only a small gap between the counters and the glass cooktop. We had to adjust the legs to get just the fit we wanted, but that was (with the aid of a level) a 2-minute job at most. Easily done. The only 2 features I haven't used are temperature roasting with the probe (we use a grill thermometer or our Thermapen) and the warming drawer. The warming drawer is very roomy, though, and easily stores my various broiler pans and small sheet pans for easy access.

A word about cleaning. If you're new to glass cooktops, you'll want to buy a few microfiber kitchen towels. After wiping down the glass with soap or soft scrub, I dry it, then use glass cleaner (I make my own, so cheap) liberally and wipe it with microfiber towels that I use for this one purpose only. This is the best way I've found to keep it streak-free.

To avoid scratches, wipe the pan bottom with a towel, your sleeve or your bare hand or arm before setting it on the glass. Make sure there's nothing on the glass, either. Finally, if you have rough cast iron cookware, lay down a paper towel or sheet of parchment or newsprint. At high prolonged heat, the paper will burn (but not catch fire), but it will still protect the glass. Lift pots to move them, don't slide them. It's not hard, taking only 1 second for every pot or pan. It's become automatic to me. My first glass top broke. I've had it's replacement for 6 months and it remains scratch-free, not even any fine scratches. Clean it every night after dinner, wipe dust/grit off your pans, use paper when needed, don't slide pans, and you'll have a gorgeous cooktop.

Finally, I'll say a few words about cookware, to help you avoid some of the mistakes I made. People will tell you to test pans with magnets, and that works, to a point. But it doesn't tell the whole story. Poorly laminated clad and disk bottom stainless steel pans can emit a nasty buzzing sound, especially at higher power levels. Many, if not most, aluminum pots and pans have questionable amounts of magnetic steel in their bases, and may not work, or will only work poorly. All of the brands I list below do very well.

If you're a fan of aluminum nonstick cookware, I advise going with Circulon Infinite or Anolon Nouvelle Copper Aluminum. These are the only two lines I've found that appear to work well on every induction top. Check reviews here for other brands, there isn't another aluminum line I've found with universally excellent induction ratings. Other pans work great on some cooktops, but not on others, or they work on them all, but they're slow. Or they only work on smaller hobs than they should. I don't have the Circulon pans, but my small Anolon Nouvelle saucepan is the one I reach for when heating thick, creamy sauces or making oatmeal. It never, ever scorches and cooks like a dream.

For really good clad cookware that won't blow the budget, consider Cuisinart French Classic, anything by Zwilling, or my personal favorite, Vollrath Tribute, a commercial line that outperforms all but the very top end of high end clad cookware. It blows away All-Clad and does it at a killer price. Buy it at Wasserstrom.com or your neighborhood restaurant supply store. Honestly, although it's never going to be mistaken for stove jewelry, you'd have to pay about $200 more per pan to get better performance. All-clad, Calphalon, Cuisinart MCP and most of the boutique store brands (Sur La Table, Le Creuset stainless, etc...) also work well with minimal/no buzzing on high power. If weight and budget are no issue, go with Demeyere Atlantis/Proline or All-Clad Copper Core. They're the only pans that best Vollrath Tribute.

If you like disk bottom saucepans, consider Vollrath Optio or Update Interantional SuperSteel (same pans), another restaurant line. It's a bargain priced workhorse. Check Staples.com for excellent prices on Vollrath, the Update International can be cheaply had here on Amazon. Bonus - the lids fit Tribute pans. For a bit more, you can get the very nice Anolon Nouvelle Copper Stainless. It should be almost the equal of it's aluminum twin. For high end bullet-proof stuff, try Paderno Grand Gourmet or Demeyere Atlantis.

review_title: Works Well, but smelly on break-in.
review_text:
I did a great deal of research on slide-ins before buying this for our new remodel. We do baking, roasting, broiling, and cook-top cooking regularly. Actually, we are quite pleased with the unit on the whole. Broiling is very effective (watch your food carefully!!). Baking was simple but read the oven manual! Took us a while to figure out how to use the probe. The elements on the cooktop are excellent. Our other one had a kind-of turbo boil, but had a time limitation to prevent electronics from overheating. This one has a quick boil that will stay in super mode until the pot boils over (yes, my wife still has not figured out NOT to walk away from the stove when boiling stuff!). It is fast! The warming tray below is nice, but we principally use it for storage. The display is easy to read and after reading the manual (please sit down with coffee, etc. and take the time!) things are generally intuitive.

Why the missing star?? Smelly. It's been used for a while now and you can still get a whiff of "out gassing" of hot internals. It is really pronounce when it was first used a few times. We had to air out the kitchen, in fact. We kind'a knew this would happen because we bought a similar product for my daughter. We were REALLY concerned something was frying inside (besides the food, that is!). So brace yourself - it will eventually go away.
Another thing is a mixed blessing. It is quieter (fan noise) than others, but the caveat is that the panel gets very warm; close to hot. I am concerned for the electronics... The alternative is to get one that is cooler, but sounds like a jet warming up. I'll take my chances on the heat.

product_title: GE PHS920SFSS Profile 30" Stainless Steel Electric Slide-In Induction Range - Convection
review_title: Fast cooking but lots to learn.
review_text:
I was so excited to receive this product. I had been dreaming of an induction range for years and when we updated our kitchen I thought the time was right. It was a little slow in arriving, but that was just a lesson in patience for me. Two days after it arrived we had modified the cabinet space for it so it would fit and I started cooking on it. I was blown away. So fast. Water started to boil in a fairly large pot in less than a minute and was at full boil in three minutes. I love how easy the cooktop is to clean. Matching the pans to the correct diameter cooking area is easy because you have four different sizes to choose from.

The convection oven takes a little getting used to. The waves of heat coming out of the door when I opened it were surprising. And it took forever for it to cool down. I checked and rechecked the controls because it felt like the oven was still on. When I used the oven as a conventional oven I didn't have that problem. Also, a cookie sheet actually blew over the edge of the oven rack when I opened the door using convection. I will probably use the oven in the conventional mode more. It heats up much more quickly than the convection mode too.

I say I will probably use that feature because I don't know what will happen after the service technician gets here next week. I read so many reviews on this range and most were good. There will always be some bad reviews, but I wish I had paid more attention and definitely wish I had purchased it locally so I could return it. Just eight days after it arrived the cooktop failed, in the middle of cooking breakfast. The lights came on and blinked and then shut off. Later the same day it was working fine. Still later the problem had returned. Eight days! And during that time we were out of town for three days so it didn't get used at all while we traveled. So really this very expensive induction range lasted all of 5 days and very few meals. I could not be more disappointed. GE will be sending a service technician out next week, but in the meantime, we have no way to cook. Thank heaven that we have a microwave and a toaster oven that can handle most jobs. I would not recommend this range to anyone. Take the bad reviews to heart and stay away!

UPDATE: While the GE service man was here we discovered that the problem wasn't in the range, but in the plan placement. By moving a pan less than a quarter of an inch it caused the burner to "catch" or "lose" the pan. You need to be VERY aware of pan size and placement on the top of the range. This can result in not being able to use all the burners if you don't have exactly the right size pan to fit. Yesterday I had to use a much bigger pan than I needed because the smallest burner was already taken and the next size burner would not recognize a small pan. This is explained in the owner's manual, but I didn't realize how precise the size of each pan on each burner has to be. I will probably need to buy a few more pots and pans to accommodate the various size burners.

product_title: GE PHS920SFSS Profile 30" Stainless Steel Electric Slide-In Induction Range - Convection
review_title: BEWARE! Induction cooking is great but REPAIRS CAN BE EXPENSIVE
review_text:
First the Pros.
First my GE induction range was an earlier model with the backlit control panel at the back of the range, but my comments, in general still apply..
Cooking with Induction is great. Water boils almost instantly, pots and pans stay relatively clean on the outside and the added counter space the cook top offers is a plus. I used this range for 2 years 10 months before the motherboard had a major meltdown. I'd had signs there were problems with it as early as 1 year after my purchase when my main large burner failed to boil water or sear stakes as efficiently as I could do on my smaller burners. However, I procrastinated calling for a service call as I thought it may just be the induction qualities of my cookware. I loved cooking on induction but there are a few things you should be aware of if you are considering purchasing an induction range. The only major con of this range when it worked properly was that the back-lit control panel was very hard to read. Sometimes it took pure guesswork to select the right item on the panel for a given function because the function selections were extremely dimly lit.. The most important issue I wish to address is the cost for repair. After only 2 years and 10 months my induction range went out entirely. I put in for an Authorized GE Service call. When the serviceman arrived their was a standard $108 diagnostic fee which I was fine with if my range could be repaired. When the technician finished the diagnostics I was advised that the morther-board was fried and the replacement part would cast me over $1100 plus labor cost to install it. Since my wife did not like the induction stove at all because she felt the controls were to complicated and too difficult to read, we opted to purchase a new Gas range. Induction can be a very efficient and a great way to cook, but if you choose to go that way, be aware that repair cost can be extremely expensive. I paid around $2800 new and only got 2 years 10 months of use out of my GE Induction range. If you invest this kind of money, I'd recommend you purchase a 5 year service warranty to protect your investment. Induction is great, but a good Gas range meets my needs also, and Gas Ranges are much less expensive to repair. For the record, I went with a new Samsung top of the line, Slide in Gas Range and love it. I also purchased a 5 year all inclusive extended warranty.
Hope this review is helpful

review_title: Major quality control issues with this dishwasher.
review_text:
We bought this dishwasher from Home Depot rather than Amazon, but wanted to give everyone our experience nonetheless. There appears to be quality issues with this model. The first one delivered had a defective door hinge that we detected just prior to installation. The helpful delivery people came back to pick it up and drop off a replacement machine. Shortly after they left we discovered the second machine had some broken stems which connect the plastic tub to the frame. We called and a few days later a third machine was delivered. At this point everyone including the delivery people decided to really give this third machine a close inspection. Sure enough, yet another defect was found. Some of the insulation on the junction box wires connected to the power cord was damaged, exposing bare copper wire. Left undetected, such a defect might have caused a dangerous short circuit.

The problem could easily have been fixed by us with some heat shrink tubing. However the delivery people agreed that three defective machines in a row was indicative of a serious lack of quality control. The question raised in everyone's mind was what else could be wrong that cannot seen? What else could be broken but not revealed until after installation? Will this thing fail in a few weeks or soon after the end of warranty? Reluctantly we decided to return this third machine and go for another model from a different manufacturer. We just ordered a Whirlpool WDF760SADB from Home Depot to be delivered next week. Hopefully it will be better quality.

In retrospect, we learned that the appliance division of GE was sold to AB Electrolux of Sweden for $3.3B in September 2014. In July 2015 the Justice Department sued in Federal Court to block the merger on grounds that the deal would hurt consumers. Morale at the GE appliance division must be terrible right now and the lawsuit just adds more uncertainty to their fate. The takeover, whether is happens or not, has most likely had a detrimental effect on quality control at the beleaguered appliance division. This consumer was adversely affected.

P.S. - We installed the Whirlpool on August 5 and it's running great. Also designed and made in the USA.

This is a pricy unit, with low capacity, and isn't effective at completing it's sole purpose for existing. review_title: ... Bosch compact pair (each 24 inches wide) has been great for 15 years
review_text:
A Bosch compact pair (each 24 inches wide) has been great for 15 years, and the dryer just died, and I replaced it with this unit so I could still plug the old Bosch washer into the dryer for power. Bosch is only making ventless dryers now, and I bought this against my better judgment because the reviews of the ventless dryers have been terrible. Bosch apparently went to ventless because of new regulations about lint fires in ducted dryers.

This dryer is great! The automatic sensor is adjustable for different levels of dryness. It is faster than the previous vented Bosch dryer, and the clothes come out perfect. The fact that the washer spins to 1200 means the clothes are already pretty dry. If your washer does not spin at 1200, that might explain why clothes would take a long time to dry in this dryer. The condensation unit at the bottom of the dryer drains into a hose which empties into the same drain as the washer. (If you have a 3 prong outlet, the manual shows how you can rewire the dryer for a 3 plug cord, or you can replace the outlet) . Some warm dry air is emitted from the dryer and we use it to help heat the house when it is cold.Why waste this source of heat? In the summer I will direct the warm air into the garage or turn on the exhaust fan in the laundry room.

In short, we are thrilled with this dryer. We have only had it a short time, and hope it will last as long as its predecessor.

product_title: Bosch 500 Series WTB86201UC 24" Ventless Electric Condensation Dryer with 4 cu. ft. Capacity, LED Display, Reversible Door in White
review_text:
I am surprised by the negative reviews here. I have owned this dryer for over a year and my experience has been very positive. Coming from a conventional, vented gas dryer, I expected long, slow drying times but did not get this at all. We changed from large, conventional washer and dryer to the European-sized models so we don't cram every possible piece of dirty clothes into one load. I typically run 4-5 smaller loads per week: dark, light, white, towels and jeans, and dress shirts. This dryer does a great job of drying all these clothes types, especially if you take advantage of the special settings. For me, the key is to remove clothes immediately at the end of the cycle. This is true of all dryers, IMO, but especially with this one. It *does* leave a small amount of residual moisture in the clothing, depending on setting. If you pull clothes out while they're warm, then fold or hang immediately, almost all the wrinkles disappear without ironing.

If I have one complaint, it's that the dryer only rotates one direction. This means very large items (california king sheets, for instance) can get tangled and not dry evenly.

There is one MAJOR advantage to this dryer. Living in a drought-prone area, I put the drain hose into a bucket and recover one to two gallons of water from each load that I use to irrigate my garden. Clean clothes, happy tomatoes. What's not to love?

product_title: Samsung DV50F9A6EVW Electric Front Load Dryer with Steam Dry, 7.4 Cubic Feet, Neat White
review_text: We bought a $1000 Samsung model #DV52J8700EP/A2 dryer just over a year ago.  The dryer comes with a 1 year warranty, but naturally, things start going wrong after the warranty expires.  The dryer was making a squealing noise that sounded like metal grinding on metal.  It would make the noise periodically, but got worse over the course of a couple of weeks.  All of a sudden, there was a loud bang and the drum wouldn’t turn any more.  First thing I thought of was that the drive belt had broken.  When I removed the back panel to inspect it, the belt was fine – it was the tension pulley that had broken.  I should say, rather melted.  A cheap plastic pulley was what kept the belt tension tight.  It had been melted by the friction on the bracket it is mounted to.  Even more scary was the fact that there was a wiring harness directly beneath it.  Had the pulley melted and gotten hot enough, it could have burned through the insulation on the wires and caused a short or possibly a fire.  I called Samsung to explain the situation and how dangerous it was, and all they said they would have to send a technician (about $150) to inspect it (they direct you to another website to schedule service instead of talking to you).  The whole bracket assembly is held together with 1 screw and 1 spring.  I managed to locate the part at an appliance store, but had to spend $40 for the whole bracket assembly for a $1 plastic pulley.  The person at the appliance store said that they were cheaply made and he had people buying them all the time for the same reason.  It took about 10 minutes for me to replace using only a screwdriver and a pair of pliers.  I would have been really upset to pay a technician that kind of money to remove a screw and spring and then put it back on. The whole situation could have been avoided had Samsung spent a couple of dollars more and used a metal pulley instead of a plastic one.  All of the parts are cheaply made, and I expect more repairs in the future.  The pulley will last about a year under normal circumstances, so I expect to spend another $40 in about a year, provided I will be able to find the bracket again.  Their customer service was a joke.  All they did was constantly apologize that there was nothing they could do but send a technician and offered no help whatsoever.  In my opinion, spending $1000 on a dryer that is made in China with cheap parts – I’ll never buy a Samsung product again.  Don’t waste your time or money on them.

You're given a pump spray bottle that you fill with water and use to soak down the oven; then the oven just heats to about 200 degrees for 20 minutes and it is done. Yes, that's it! Then you have go in and not only clean it but first sop up all of that water that served no purpose whatsoever except to turn grease into a gummy mess that still won't come off. So you know what? Service plan costs $400 - about the cost of the board, so after trying to get LG to replace for free or partial, we give up as it's close to Thanksgiving and have company arriving. LG contracts with a local company, who in turn subcontracts with another company.They guy arrives and fixes it in 15 minutes ... the connector to the board was bad from the factory (his assessment), he snips wire and puts on a new connector. So I just paid $400 for a .10 part!! Technician says LG have a lot of board problems.

We tried to get LG to compensate us, but customer support refers us to warranty, who refer us back to customer support. After about ten phone calls I gave up - maybe that was their intent all along. LG used to be a good brand, but based on this product, and my interactions with them, we could not recommend any LG brand.

Update 4/2018 - broke again w F9 error, this time a main wire into the connector block (where main power comes into unit) melted and broke off! product_title: Frigidaire Gallery Series FGGS3065PF 30" Slide-In Gas Range with 4 Sealed Burners in Stainless Steel
review_title: Nothing but problems and poor customer service
review_text:
I will begin by saying this is a beautiful range but has a very loud fan that you cannot turn off and gas burners that are not responsive. I have had terrible customer service with Frigidaire and Pacific Sales was unwilling to help us when Frigidaire would not. We only had the range for 11 months, still under manufacture warranty, and sold it to buy a Samsung.

The issues we had began back when we received the range in October 2014 from Pacific Sales (Best Buy). We were unable to use it the first four weeks as we were having construction done in out kitchen. Once we finally connected it, we noticed that the cooling fan was very loud. I called Frigidaire and they informed me this was normal but after much discussion agreed to send a tech to look at it.

The Tech agreed it was a bit louder than usual and was able to make adjustments to it which made a slight improvement. But after cooking a standard meal at 400 degrees, the fan would continue to run for 45 minutes after we turned off the oven. So every time we used the oven, we would eat dinner, clean up, and sit down to watch TV, and the fan would still be running. And this is not a subtle fan, you must speak loudly to talk over it. And three days later the fan became very loud again. I called Frigidaire back and they agreed to send someone to look at it again. He came out said he needed to order a new fan and would have to set up another appointment. This was very difficult as my wife was very pregnant and we both had very busy schedules. He came back a couple weeks later and changed out the fan. It again sounded a little better but still much too loud and ran much too long after using the range. This was very annoying, but we could not return it as we were past the two week period.

A few weeks later we noticed that one of our burners wasn't very responsive when we adjusted the dial. I again reached out to Frigidaire and they agreed to send someone to look at it. I asked if the tech could please bring all of the necessary parts to fix it on the first visit as we now had a small infant and was difficult to plan our schedule. The tech came and again explained that he would need to order a part and we would need to set up another appointment. He returned a couple weeks later with the part and slightly improved the burner.

We then decided to check all the burners and noticed that none of them are responsive. For instance, as you turn the dial there seems to be four different settings; high, medium, low, and very low... but there is no proportional control.

I again reached out to Frigidaire and they again sent someone to look at our stove. This time when he looked at it he said that this is typical of a Frigidaire range and there was nothing he could do. I feel this is unacceptable as the entire purpose of us changing to a gas range was to have better proportional control than an electric range. Now we had very little control over the temperature while we are cooking at all.

I called Frigidaire back at that time to explain that we wanted a different range and they told me there was nothing they can do unless the tech considered it unrepairable. In my eyes it was unrepairable because there's no proportional control over the gas heating element and is also no control over the loud fan that runs for 45 minutes after we are done cooking. I was informed to leave the oven door open after we finished cooking to reduce the time of the fan running. That did not sound like a smart solution with an infant learning to crawl, not to mention the excessive heat. Frigidaire did not agree and once again I moved on as they said there was nothing they were willing to do.

Then, about five months later we were cooking and we had F30 error appear and the oven would not work. I was extremely upset and immediately called Frigidaire again to have it repaired. They explained that they were completely booked for two weeks and they would see if they could expedite it and would have someone call me back within 48 hours with a sooner time. After I got off the phone, I realized that the fan was still blowing on the oven and would not turn off. I eventually unplugged the range and plugged it back in and the fan turned on off.
I didn't hear back at 48 hours and after 72 hours I called back they said they had scheduled an appointment for us on September 2. We had two problems with this. First of all, that was they original date (two weeks out) that they told me when I originally called and secondly we had were not available that day. I explained that was not acceptable so they were able to get us an appointment on August 31st.

A few days before they were scheduled to come out, my wife was able to turn on the stove and the error was gone. I canceled the appointment but I know that there was some type of problem in our range computer. We then noticed that the drawer on the range was not sitting straight and it appears to have a missing screw which was one more thing that irritated us.
That is when I decided to go to back to Best Buy to see if there was anything they could do to help us out as Frigidaire was very clear that there was nothing they were willing to do.

We had only had this range for 11 months at this point and have already had techs come to our house eight times in an attempt to fix it. I had spent ours on the phone and had to open our schedules to work around techs to fix a brand new range that we spent $1,600 on. It is not as if we purchased the least expensive range on the market. We had problems with the fan, burners, computer, and the drawer, and are completely unsatisfied with this purchase. We had no confidence that this is going to last us for reasonable period of time. We wanted a refund.

I went to back to Best Buy and I spoke to the Pacific Sales manager and explained the many problems I've had with the Frigidaire range we purchased 11 months ago. I informed him we wanted a refund so we could purchase a different range. He said he would reach out to Frigidaire and see what he could do. A customer service rep from Frigidaire emailed me and asked what they could help me with. I wrote a very long email (similar to this review) and explained everything that had happened. They suggested that I buy the extended warranty and were unwilling to do anything else.

I reached back out to the Pacific Sales Manager and he said he could not do anything about our Frigidaire range, but would give us a great deal on a new range. But it turned out that his great deal was still more expensive than the same range at Home depot or Lowes. I asked if could could at least get if for half price, but he said the best he could do was match the price at Home Depot. We bought a Samsung range at Lowes the next day and it is fantastic. I will never shop at Pacific Sales or purchase a Frigidaire product again and I suggest you stay away as well.

review_title: Terrible Performance for such an expensive stove!
review_text:
I had some basic expectations from this two thousand dollar stove. The pros are it looks great, it is a slide in and it has a meat probe.

The cons are it lacks basic functionality that even a 200 gas stove has. Basically when you turn the burner control from the lowest setting to the higher settings the flame jumps around like a roman candle. Not only that but on the power burner there are basically two settings 1. extremely low 2. extremely high. There is no middle ground. So when you start to turn the knob from low to high you find that nothing happens until you are about 90% of the way back to the highest setting, then the flame kind of explodes back to high. On the Plus side the fireball can help get rid of those annoying arm hairs you have, however it can be a bit surprising.

Tried to get service from Frigidaire. .. they referred me to a local repair guy who insisted everything was 'normal' needless to say I returned the stove and now enjoy NXR brand that works great.

product_title: PAIR SPECIAL- LG Turbo Series Ultra Capacity Laundry System With Steam Technology (WM3470HVA,DLEX3470V,WDP4V x2)
review_title: Excellent purchase in every respect, so far.
review_text:
First, let me say that I rarely write a review unless the purchase/product is exceptionally good or exceptionally bad. Happily, this purchase falls in the "exceptionally good" category. So, let me run down the reasons that I have been pleased so far with this purchase:

1. Shipping speed. We ordered this set around noon on a Tuesday. Within an hour or so, I received the shipping confirmation. The next day, Wednesday, I received a call from the trucking company to set up a delivery time for the following day, Thursday. The washer/dryer set was delivered before noon on Thursday. That totally blew me away!

2. Packaging. The washer, dryer and two pedestals were, as I expected, packaged separately. What I didn't expect was the quality of the engineered packaging. It was pretty amazing and, as a result, these heavy units came out of the packaging completely unscathed.

3. Installation instructions. They were clear, fairly concise, and not cluttered up with pages and pages of "lawyer speak" safety instructions which often seem to be designed not to make the product installation safer but, rather, to limit the manufacturer's liability in case of an accident.

4. Energy efficiency. Yes, I knew that these were HE appliances but when I read on the Energy Guide that the total cost to operate the washer for a year was only $12, I was in disbelief. Honestly, I'm still somewhat skeptical but that's what it said.

5. Operation. I would never have believed that a washer/dryer could be so quiet if I had not heard it (barely) with my own ears. They are amazingly quiet. Our wash room contains the washer, dryer and a large upright freezer. Honest to goodness, I can hear the freezer running over the washer and dryer. I can't really tell if the clothes come out any cleaner but my wife says that the time to wash and dry is considerably less than our old set. She also loves the ease of operation as well as the extra storage space provided by the pedestals. If she's happy (and she is) then I'm tickled plumb to death.

6. Long term reliability. This one I can't answer yet. Only time will tell but, based on our overall experience so far, I'm expecting good things.

One caveat regarding installation is that these things are HEAVY. I think that the washer and pedestal weigh in the neighborhood of 275 lbs. So, this would be a good time to have some big strong friends to give you a hand.

If we experience reliability problems, I will post an update to this review but I'm really not expecting that to happen.

review_text:
I purchased this from Home Depot and it was delivered last week. Within the first hour I knew it was going back. I do not expect a refrigerator to be silent. However, I didn't expect it to give off a high pitched noise. It's an annoying sound that will make you look outside to see if someone is sawing metal because it's somewhat muffled. My inner ear was numb. Also, since it has a digital inverted compressor, it runs almost all of the time. Which was unfortunate because the high pitched noise lasts for 30 minutes per hour before it cycles down to a quieter mode. During the high pitched sound the refrigerator also has a noisy hum/buzz.

After this experience I went to the store and started investigating the other Samsung refrigerators. I love the look of Samsung and didn't like any of the other brands. I realized that this model has two vents (one on each side of the refrigerator) which I believe is the cause of the noise issue because you can hear everything from these vents. We turned it on in the store and could hear the same metal/high pitched sound coming from the vents.

After checking out all of the Samsung French Door refrigerators, I decided on the RF31FMEDBSR 31 cu ft because it does not have the 2 side vents and when I tested it in the store it seemed quieter. (although it's hard to hear clearly in home depot). I was right, it's MUCH quieter. Most of all, it does not have that metal sound. Also, it doesn't seem to run full throttle as long as the other refrigerator. It was a little noisier the first 3 or 4 hours when it was cooling down at first but it's great now. It's only about 1.25 inches longer so upgrading to the 31 cu ft worked out better anyway. Lots of room, great lighting and I love the middle drawer!

review_title: Great at first, but wait a few months
review_text:
Purchased in February and it was great. However, in July something broke and it will no longer switch between crushed and cubed ice. Since this was not a big deal I procrastinated and didn't contact Samsung support. That has now become a three week nightmare. Still have not had a service person scheduled to even come out and determine what is wrong. Samsung customer support is probably the worst support I have ever dealt with. They originally assigned the ticket to one local company that I was never able to get in contact with. Then a week ago Samsung called me, I explained the situation and was told they would assign to another company. Called Samsung yesterday as I still have not heard from anyone and the ticket was never transferred. The person with "Executive Customer Relations" told me she transferred the ticket, called the Authorized Service Center herself, and that I would be contacted within 24 hours to schedule the service call. Plus she would call me back to follow-up. Well, here it is over 72 hours later and zero calls.

I just want people to be aware of what they may be getting into.

Follow-up: Well, after all the issues getting someone to look at the refrigerator, I finally had a service technician out to look at it on Nov 26th. Turns out that the "ice box" which houses the motor for the auger and the mechanism that opens the door for cubed ice had ice built up inside of it. No indication of this on the outside of the assembly. The ice build up was preventing the solenoid from being able to work correctly to open the door, and caused the solenoid to burn out. The technician at first thought that the heater inside the assembly that is to prevent the ice build up was not working. After testing he determined that the electrical connection was probably not properly connected at the factory which prevented the heater from working. He ordered a new assembly unit and on Dec 4th it was installed. Ice maker has been working properly since. Of course I have no way of verifying if the heater is working or not, just hoping that it is.

And, although Samsung told me they would follow-up, I have heard nothing from them since the repair. Just another example of poor customer service from them and the lack of quality control at their factories.

product_title: SAMSUNG RF28HMEDBSR French Door Refrigerator, 28 Cubic Feet, Stainless Steel
review_text:
We've only had this fridge installed for a couple days, but I already love it. Firstly, installing it was WAY easier than the old fridge (which was a 13 year old Samsung). They have improved the ease of removing and re-installing doors 100-fold (at least). Since the unit can't get in the house without removing the doors and re-installing them, that was a big deal.

Beyond that, the unit is beautiful and has great features. The ice maker filled up very quickly (once I ran the water for a while to fill up the water line). The "flex drawer" is way more useful than I thought. It has plenty of space for drinks and also items like yogurts that used to fall out of the fridge and break on the floor, splattering everywhere. So that's a nice feature. The main refrigeration area is really well laid out so that you can use the space effectively. The shelf that flips up and the other one that retracts make it so much easier when there's a tall item. You can fit it without having to take everything off the shelf and adjust it. The door shelves are great as well, with some more small and narrow to hold smaller items and make them easier to find (these are the shelves they managed to fit around the ice dispenser area - so there is still storage even in that area - great use of space). The clear plastic also makes items easier to find.

I thought the ice maker would take up too much space in the refrigeration area, but it really isn't an issue at all so far. I thought the freezer would be difficult to organize, as I was used to a side by side. But the freezer has the drawer and the little storage bin on top, plus a separator in the main compartment. So it's really not a problem to keep organized. I didn't even realize that it was going to have a fancy touch screen control panel when I bought it, but my daughter was pretty jazzed about that. The water/ice dispenser is really tall for filling water bottles. The LED lighting is recessed and out of the way, but really brightens up all the spaces. Plus we can use the LEDs in the water dispenser area as a night light. Lastly, I had heard others complain about how loud their refrigerators are, but this one is barely audible to me when the fan and compressor are running. I was even concerned at first it wasn't working, but it's cooling beautifully!

It is a little expensive, which is the only downside I've found. But I guess you get what you pay for (I got a really great deal, though, so thanks Amazon)!. Overall, a really great appliance and I'm happy to have it! I don't know about reliability yet, but consumer reports did have Samsung listed as the manufacturer of refrigerators with the lowest number of repairs required of all the manufacturers in their survey. Our old Samsung lasted 13 years, so I feel good about it.

product_title: SAMSUNG RF28HMEDBSR French Door Refrigerator, 28 Cubic Feet, Stainless Steel
review_text: Personally, I would not ever buy a Samsung refrigerator again.  Reason: it is designed to be not fixable.  Okay, first issue: there is a class action lawsuit against Samsung for the ice maker.  The icemaker has leaked, causing it to freeze the ice tray in place.  And, we've also developed a noisy fan in the icemaker.  We had the repairman come out and he told us the icemaker was out of warrantee, but he also said the fans tend only to be noisy, but not to go out.  So, we decided to live with it.  More recently we've developed a new noise, seemingly involving the fan for the refrigerator itself.  This is a much louder noise and we can't live with that - way to interfering.  So, I took a look at what it would take to see if I could fix it (I'm an expert home repairman).  But, the housing on the fridge is all designed to be interlocking elements so that even trying to see what is the problem (such as by taking the back panel off the refrigerator) is not possible.  Essentially the fridge doors need to be dismantled; then the main shrouding removed; then maybe you could have a look.  Further, it looks like the main shrouding was designed to be dropped in from above; so, it looks like it would require high clearance above in order to avoid bending the shrouding at its top corners.  All of this is much more difficult than it needs to be.  Even a small problem could easily result in a very big repair cost because of the difficulty getting at things in order to repair them.  We haven't yet decided if we are just going to consider this a bad investment and replace it, or bite the bullet and see if repairs can be done with less-than-outrageous cost.  Anyway, Samsung won't see us again.  We certainly understand that things can break.  But, making it exceedingly difficult to fix them is poor design and poor customer relations.

product_title: Samsung RF28HMEDBWW Energy Star 28.2 Cu. Ft. French Door Refrigerator with Counter-Height FlexZone Drawer and Freezer Drawer, White
review_text:
This is a nicely conceived refrigerator/freezer. Many of the features are exceptional and the overall design is pleasing. You can open a humidity controlled drawer at the refrigerator level by only opening one door. Many of the other manufacturers don't make the produce drawers so they can open without opening both french doors. Of course there is the flex drawer which has separate temperature control and is nice for a variety of goods; like sandwich meats and snacks etc. Finally, there is the separate refrigerator and freezer temperature controls located on a display above the water/ice dispenser. Ice cubes are readily available as either cubes or crushed ice, though the crushed ice comes out almost as powder - mostly unusable.
Now for the bad news.
Generally speaking, most people never actually check the temperatures in the refrigerator and compare them to the manufacturer's design. I have gone through two brand-new refrigerators with exactly the same problem; a problem that Samsung has no idea how to fix or even acknowledge needs attention. Samsung sent out an appliance repair service and they confirmed the problem existed on both units but could not determine that anything was functionally defective. Samsung's solution was to indiscriminately replace parts hoping to find something that worked - a process that would ostensibly take many weeks. So what's the problem you ask?
The refrigerator temperature set-point is adjustable down to 34F with 37F being the recommend temperature. The actual refrigerator doesn't get below 44F. There seems to be a 10F discrepancy between the temperature set and displayed and the actual temperature. If you set the freezer at 0F, the recommended setting, it will end up at about +5F (soft ice cream). The temperature settings on the flex-drawer are off also, and pretty much match the refrigerator. By the way this was all checked with precision temperature indicators because of the short life of the contents of the refrigerator. The temperature problem acts as though the temperature sensor is located too close to the evaporator so that it is reading the refrigerant temperature and not the air temperature - that's just a theory though derived from the temperature state if you use the "power cool" function. Here the power cool function will bring the indicated refrigerator temperature down to 23F. You would think everything would be frozen, but the actual refrigerator temperature never goes below 38F. Best circumstance; set the freezer temperature to -5F and the refrigerator to 34F. Doing this results in a refrigerator air temperature of about 40F and a freezer temperature of about -1F. Not great, but useable.

We love the deli drawer. Our only issue with that is that the divider is always moving. We may figure out a way to keep it in position. Love the bottom freezer drawer. The light in all compartments is great. No excuse for losing anything in there!
The only con I've come up with so far is that the smooth white paint (?) on the doors/drawer fronts is very easily scratched/nicked. There is a tiny nick on the front of one of the doors from when it was delivered and a couple of small scratches that I put on it with a magnet. review_title: Terrible design causes huge freezing issue
review_text:
This is an attractively designed refrigerator which is reasonably priced, but this fridge line has an endemic issue with its internal defroster which causes water to pool inside under the crisper drawer.

This will result in giant hulking slabs of ice, way too much humidity inside (veggies going bad too quickly!) not to mention the need to cart out giant chunks of ice.

Seriously look how much there is, with a nice can of Red Hare Juicy IPA for size comparison. This much builds up about once a month. It even blocks the crisper drawer from closing all the way.

The issue is caused by way too small of a heating element in the back of the fridge, which isn't able to keep up with the cooling. This allows condensation to build up, then freeze and block the drainage lines.

The fix? Just unload your whole fridge and use the power defrost cycle, or simply disassemble the rear wall and use blow dryers.

Terrible design flaw. I cannot believe it is still sold with this problem.

Buy a different fridge.

product_title: Samsung RF28HFEDBSR Energy Star 28 Cu. Ft. French Door Refrigerator with Cool Select Pantry and Freezer Drawer, Stainless Steel
review_text: Was ok for a year or 2, then turned horrible.  I was excited to finally have a fridge with crushed ice.  It is the slowest ice dispenser (note it was always slow, from the very beginning).  It can take up to a full minute to fill a normal size glass with crushed ice.  What is worse is the ice maker freezes over and then clogs so after a few weeks, you will have no ice in the tray unless you check it daily and clear any jams.  You then have to completely defrost the icemaker to get it working again.  I bought a heat gun for something else, but found it works good for defrosting it quickly.  What is even more terrible than the above is the fridge freezes over behind the back wall and there is a fan that starts hitting the ice and makes a terrible buzzing sound.  You then have to defrost the entire fridge which entails taking everything out and putting a space heater inside it until the inside back panel defrosts enough to be able to remove it, then use a hair dryer to melt the rest of the ice.  After that it will be good for 4 or 5 months (maybe).

review_title: AVOID! Component failure / defrosting required or fridge stops cooling
review_text:
It is my view that Samsung is negligent having failed to advertise this fridge as requiring defrosting, and selling these fridges with full knowledge they are not performing as advertised - and in fact fail to perform the purpose they are intended for, for a period of time that is well within reasonable expectations. I bought this fridge in Sept. 2014 and it needs defrosting periodically. The cabinet housing the fans builds up with ice to the point the fan stops and the fridge ceases to cool effectively.

The internet is filled with people having the precise same problem as I am, and videos on how to remove the ice build up (hairdryer works) so I have to believe this is not a singular problem I am having but a characteristic of their fridges. There is a class action in the USA.

Samsung does not include info on how to defrost in their manual nor do they offer any workaround, or information such as "where will the water come from as it defrosts". Yet the call centre folks don't even need to consult a manual to tell you how to defrost it ... you have to put it in something called "shop mode" and wait 24 hours.

They offer this product with a 10 year warranty, which I took as a company willing to stand behind their product, yet this commonly experienced design problem is not covered. I believe as a consumer I need protection from this company's shoddy design and lack of responsibility for their malfunctioning product. And so it seems does anyone buying a Samsung fridge. The model is the RF23HCEDBSR.

review_text: Please, Please, Please do not buy this fridge. Ill go as far to say, do not buy any Samsung fridges. Basically they didn't design the seal on the ice dispenser (in the regular fridge) well enough and it causes the ice to not be cold enough so it will melt. Every time you use that dispenser you will get a pleasant surprise of ice and water dripping on your floors. soon after that starts to happen, you will get a large chunk of ice build up which will cause a very loud fan hum that can be heard throughout your entire house. You will then contact Samsung, they will charge you 600-800 to repair something that will constantly come back every few months needing the same replacement. At that point you are just going to replace a 1-2 year old fridge because of it. This is very well documented, i wish i did better research. I will never buy another Samsung product as long as I live because they are unwilling to recall or fix this issue that is due to a design flaw. I will not pay their crazy fees to "fix" the issue that cant be fixed. be my guest... look up Samsung french door ice maker issues and this will show up 10x at least on your search.

review_text:
We bought and installed this refrigerator as part of a kitchen remodel and now that our refund is safely in the bank I can write a review on it. The problems we had were:

1) Design. This was our first side by side refrigerator and will be our last. There wasn't as much refrigerated room as our last frig and the layout of the refrigerated space wasn't very good. The bottom 40% was taken up by 3 large draws when really 2 would have been sufficient. We would have preferred more shelf space.

2) Reliability. We installed the refrigerator in late November and 5 months later both the refrigerator and freezer stopped cooling. The compressor seemed to be running and there were no error lights on. We tried adjusting the temperature and powering it down and up again but nothing worked.

3) Service. This was the worst part. Samsung gave me a total run around even saying that the company I bought it from (Home Care Corporation) wasn't an authorized dealer so it wasn't under warranty. Eventually Amazon interceded to settle that. After the repairman they finally sent out couldn't fix the problem they agreed to refund the purchase price. Even then I had to send Samsung a form with pictures showing the cut power cord and the removed interior tags with the model and ID numbers.

We got the refund about a month after the frig broke down. They said they would take it out but have yet to contact us. We just paid $15 to have Home Depot take it out when they delivered our new one. I wouldn't take any bets on the chance of getting that money from Samsung but then I also wouldn't take any bets on them getting more of my business.

I am really really frustrated with the company and the situation. Really really unhappy overall. Awful that you get told to get the repair and they will reimburse you, and then after the fact they can't do anything about only reimbursing you for a partial amount. NEVER buying a Samsung product again and recommend you don't either!

review_text:
My 30-year-old Kenmore dryer (wow!) was on its last legs, so I researched on line reviews and Consumer Reports. The Samsung DV56H9100GG was well-regarded, but CR listed it as #1 which sealed the deal for me. I bought mine at Home Depot and they delivered it within the week.

I've been using my new dryer for several months and it is quite a step up over the old Kenmore. It is very quiet and energy efficient. Plus there are a variety of spiffy drying options that weren't there in the old days: a "Wrinkle Prevent" to keep clothes looking good if you can't get back to the dryer in time; "Wrinkle Away" for clean stuff that just needs a spritzing and tumble dry; a variety of settings for anything from light blouses to heavy towels and bedding, and an illuminated drum so you can see what you are doing. They even include a drying rack for tennis shoes, toys, etc., though I usually just stick stuff like that out on the back porch to dry.

The Samsung dryer is several inches taller than my old Kenmore, which makes me glad I didn't buy the pedestal that raises it off the floor; I don't think it would have fit in my available space and I certainly couldn't fold stuff on the top surface. In any case, check the dimensions of your laundry area before buying.

This Samsung dryer looks O.K. (shrug, it IS basically a big box) and appears well made. It sounds cute soft musical tones and tunes to signal different features. The "load finished" tune is rather long and resembles (to me) an 8-bit version of a "Pirates of the Caribbean" drinking song. ;) The lint trap is tucked on the door edge for easy access. Unfortunately, my new dryer door opens to the right and it appears to be a tremendous hassle--possibly impossible--to change the hinge direction.

This is a pricey critter and if I ever have a problem I'll post an update immediately. I doubt I'll get 30 years like I did with my old Kenmore, but this is a really nice clothes dryer. Five stars.

product_title: Samsung WF42H5200AW Energy Star 4.2 Cu. Ft. Front-Load Steam Washer with SelfClean, White
review_text: Perhaps the reason for all the negative reviews is a front load learning curve problem... this is my first front loader, and the transition from water-soaked top load agitator washing is apples and oranges.  No, it doesn't use a tub full of water, float the clothes and beat them to death.  On my first front load, my clothes and towels smelled dirty and felt like cardboard after the washer/dryer cycle.  Here's what will give you front load success.  Switch to powder detergent (HE only) for a short time -buy a small box- and don't use more than line 1 on the scoop for any load.  The powder is more forgiving if you use too much detergent, which is exactly what I was doing.  You CANNOT use the amount recommended on the detergent container.  Less water = less detergent.  DO use fabric softener, half capful.  Don't be afraid of gumming up your machine or other horror stories.  The high spin speeds render clothing less than desirably soft, although dramatically cut down drying time!  In the dryer, use MEDIUM heat and your MOISTURE SENSOR, which works very well (I have the matching dryer).  The towels I thought I had ruined by blasting them dry on high heat and a timed cycle are now soft and fluffy again.  My whites have NEVER been so white, and I do not use bleach.  I also do not use vinegar that so many seem to swear by in the rinse cycle.  I use the Normal cycle for most loads and use HOT for whites, STEAM for extremely nasty items (anything sweat or dirt-soaked), and WARM for everything else.  Cycle time is around an hour except for steam, about 1.5 hours.  Dry time is 45-55 minutes for HUGE loads.  My laundry is sweet-smelling, clean, fresh and soft again.  I'm never going back.  My water bill is down $10 a month and I've reduced my loads from 10 a week to 6.  I've run the clean cycle once and just got the reminder to do it again, which I do while I'm sleeping. I clean the detergent drawer and leave the washer door open when I'm done for the day.  Bottom line - if your stuff stinks, you're using way too much detergent. Be patient - it's going to take several powder loads to get rid of all the excess that's stuck in your clothes, but you will win in the end : )

review_title: You will repair this washer every 2-4 years
review_text:
I bought this on Amazon around four years ago. I am repairing this machine for a second time for the same problem. It has a defective design on the central drum bearning. That's the part that allows the drum to fit in the motor/drive housing and spin. Over a two to three year period of running normally these bearings will go out and they will need to be replaced.

You can buy a new bearning kit for around $80 and repair it yourself if you're VERY good at repairing things. You will need to:
1) Completely dismantle the machine.
2) Lift the drum assembly which is very heavy. You must use a pully or have other people help. You will likely get hurt if you try this without ample help or equipment.
3) Dismantle the drum assembly and remove the bearings. This requires a machine press or a hammer and pin and lots of patience.
4) Insert the new bearing with the same amount of equipment and patience.
5) Reassemble the entire machine (all of it... the gaskets, hoses, shock absorbers, wiring harnesses, control panel, etc.).

Or, you can do 90% of the disassembly noted above and spend $300+ on an entirely new drum assembly.

Or, you can spend even more than that to have a professional repair it or buy a new machine.

I would advise against buying this machine.

If you have this machine already and hear it sounding like an airplane taking off then chances are this problem is happening to you. If you have the persistence to fix this as I've mentioned above then I suggest you look online for a video on how to do this repair. I bought the service manual from Samsung (which is a horror story all by itself) but it didn't help as much as the videos online.

review_title: Terrible Service on Model This one Replaced
review_text:
I would highly encourage anyone reading this to avoid purchasing any LG product, given our recent experience. A technician came out to fix our year-old refrigerator under warranty and proceeded to damage it beyond repair in the process. Now, LG will not provide us with a replacement. Here was our experience with them and their customer service.

In March of 2014 we purchased a LFC25765ST French Door refrigerator. We received a great deal on the fridge at a price of $1,367. In July of 2015, the fridge suddenly stopped cooling. Below is a timeline of the ensuing events:

7/14/15: Called LG to set up a repair appointment.
7/16/15: An official LG technician came to our house and determined three different components that could be the cause of the issue. He informed us he would replace the most likely component, and if that didn’t fix it to call him to come out and replace the second component. We needed to give the fridge at least 24 hours to cool.
7/18/15: The fridge remained broken, so we called and made another appointment for the technician to return.
7/21/15: The technician came out to our house and repaired the next component. He informed us that if the fridge still wasn’t repaired, that the issue must be the compressor, and he would return to replace it. Again, we needed to give the fridge at least 24 hours to see if it would cool.
7/24/15: The fridge remained broken, so we called and made a third appointment for the technician to come out.
7/28/15: The technician returned to replace the compressor, noting that this repair would certainly solve our issue, but early in the repair process, he snapped a loop component in the fridge and stated that that particular component could not be repaired, effectively bricking our fridge in the process. He asked for our original purchase receipt, which we promptly provided, and said he would send it in to LG so that we would receive a reimbursement or a new fridge.

Keep in mind that my wife had to take time off of work for all three of these repairs in addition to our being without a working refrigerator for two weeks (and still going strong). In the end, LG has offered to provide us with a store credit at the location where we originally purchased the fridge, but for the original purchase price, not including tax or delivery, which together total an additional $200 in our original purchase. As this refrigerator was bought for an amazing--and now unavailable--deal after several days of research and shopping, even purchasing the exact same model would result in an additional expense of $500 at least.

I called LG's escalation center stating that I didn't want a store credit. I simply wanted them to send us either the identical fridge or the current model of it. It absolutely sickens me that they would send an official technician into my home, who would then effectively break my property, and expect me to have any out of pocket costs, let alone over $700. Bear in mind that customers are required to use LG repairmen, otherwise, the warranty is voided. When I asked the escalation center representative how he would feel if I came into his house, broke his property, and only paid him for a portion of what it would cost to replace it, he said, “But we paid you back for what you paid.” I said that I understood his viewpoint, but that an individual of his company destroyed my property and that an ethical solution should not cause any financial impact to me.

Based on this customer service, I would never purchase any LG product again. I have worked in a similar industry and we would always either cover our customer's replacement costs in these situations or, ideally, provide them with a new, identical product at our expense. No one should ever incur any out of pocket costs when a corporation is at fault for destruction of property. Beware all LG products. Not only did this fridge last 16 months before needing repairs, the company that made it clearly doesn't value its customers or ethical business practices.
