review_title: What good is an oven that is horribly inaccurate
review_text:
What good is an oven that is horribly inaccurate?
OK, I know it takes 30-45 minutes after an oven reaches temperature for the temp to become "stable", and I know opening the door releases heat, and I know that the oven cycles on and off so it tries for an "average" temperature with a +/- 25 degree swing. But mine has an 80 degree swing. Set at 350 and it goes to 390 then down to 310, then back up. Cannot bake a cake or anything accurately unless you go for "forgiving" food like a baked potato or ham. Why spend $2200 for this oven when the temperature is so erratic. Yes, I used a scientific air-temperature probe from Thermoworks for a high degree of accuracy. The only way to bake is to constantly turn the oven on and off to try to keep it within about 20 degrees of where I set it. Have to go now and turn the oven off and then on again to get it back up to temperature before my cake is ruined. PS. both lights burned out in the first 2 months probably because the assemblers at the factory used bare hands on the halogen light bulbs during installation - which is a no no. Alarm on timer is uselessly quiet.

review_title: Poor quality and has some design shortcomings (noisy fan, blows warm air)
review_text:
We recently replaced all our appliances w/ Bosch. Sadly this oven is poor, and if I had it to do over, I'd go with another brand like Kitchenaid.
Pros: Looks great and cooks well. Controls are pretty intuitive and easy to use. Has some nice features.
Cons: Lousy quality & customer service. And the cooling fan is noisy and blows warm air into the kitchen.
Details: When either oven heats up, a fan turns on, blowing warm air from under the touchpad. This is a bit annoying, since it's at chin to face-level for many folks. The fan is also rather noisy. These are somewhat minor issues, but I'd expect a $3000 appliance to not have annoying design shortcomings. Plus, it's not great to have an appliance blow warm air into my Florida AC-cooled kitchen.
In addition, the oven had serious design/quality problems from the start. Whether on or off, it would randomly beep and flash 'convection bake' on the display. Then if the oven was on, it would turn itself off. This was totally random - sometimes every few minutes, sometimes up to 2-3 days. The Bosch factory service guy called Bosch, who told him this was a 'known problem' and they expected to have a fix in ~2 weeks. 3 weeks later, they had 'identified the problem with the touchpad, and expected to have a replacement part soon'. 3 more weeks, the guy installed the new touchpad. No change - problem just the same. The next day, he confirmed w/ Bosch that they'd sent the same old touchpad, and expected to have a replacement part in another 1-2 weeks. 3 more weeks... no new part available.
Finally, after nearly 3 months, 4 repair visits & 20+ calls to my local dealer, Bosch customer service, and their repair guy... Bosch agreed to replace the still non-working oven. The new one is in and working ok so far for about a month.
Overall, I'd avoid Bosch's ovens & microwaves. (We also replaced a built in microwave at the same time. It was DOA and was replaced promptly. It also has a similar noisy fan design issue.)

Sadly, now that I’m looking I see that I’m not the only one that has had this happen.

Bosch customer service was friendly when I called about the panel light but essentially told me it wasn’t their problem and offered to give me service repair phone numbers. Really? We spent more than $1200 on this microwave oven. You would think Bosch would stand behind their product especially since it appears that this issue is not unique to just our microwave. review_text:
We bought the Samsung RH299000SR side by side refrigerator on 6/26/14, during the 4th of July sales. It was delivered, at our request, on July 7th. The refrigerator design is elegant, sleek and modern. The handles are flush with the doors which gives it an interesting cleaner look. The refrigerator door has the Showcase feature which is like a double door allowing access to items in the door by opening the Showcase door cover, without having to open the door to the main compartment.

PROS: the space in the showcase door is very roomy and flexible. It has 3 shelves with dividers, 2 open drawers with dividers (you can roll them out when the Showcase is open) and a shallow bottom shelf. All dividers can be moved out of the way to allow full use of the space.
The Ice maker is really efficient and the ice bucket has a great capacity. The bucket is easy to remove from the door for maintenance or just to empty and save the ice into another container.
The electronic controls for the basic functions are easy to use.
The interior led illumination is bright and very effective.

CONS:
We don’t know how the ice dispenser works because ours was defective. The flap to allow the ice to exit worked but the motor to turn the ice didn’t.
The one sided handles are very awkward and counter intuitive. You have to use your left hand or twist your right wrist to open the refrigerator door on the right. It is not obvious which part of the refrigerator handle to pull to open the main door of the refrigerator or just the Showcase door. It will take time, practice and frustration for it to become second nature.
The compartments of the showcase door do not keep temperatures consistent with the interior of the refrigerator. The temperature at the bottom shelf was more than 50 degrees and slightly progressively cooler on the others depending on their position.
The refrigerator door with the Showcase feature is very heavy to operate even when empty. If you don’t guide it gently when closing it, it slams.
There are only 2 drawers in the refrigerator and one of them is not full size.
The freezer has four shelves and only 2 drawers, a third one would be more convenient.
The actual consumption of the water filter is not displayed, only when it is exhausted an indicator will turn on. My 12 years old Kenmore showed the percent left on the water filter life.

Conclusion:
Based on the awkwardness and temperature control problem of the Showcase door of the side by side, the ice dispenser malfunction and the other issues we decided to return it to the seller. We replaced it with Samsung’s 4 door RF30HBEDBSR model on July 30th. It has 2 french doors with Showcase in one of them, a Cool zone drawer and a spacious freezer drawer. I have been monitoring the temperature in the different compartments of the refrigerator, the doors, the Cool zone drawer and the freezer and everything is fine. The Ice maker and dispenser work well. We will have a more comprehensive review of this model when we have more time to evaluate it, but, as of now, we believe it was the right decision.

The oven is VERY SLOW to preheat, in contrast to my former GE oven which preheated in a fraction of the Bosch time.  The kitchen timer is practically useless!  It's so quiet, you can barely hear it from another room ... and turns itself  off after about a minute, so if you've been outside or in another room, well, too bad.  When baking cookies, the back ones are done more than the front row.  On the plus side, the probe function works well.  In hindsight, I should have purchased the GE Profile.

product_title: Bosch HDI8054U 800 30" Stainless Steel Dual Fuel (Gas) Slide-In Sealed Burner Range - Convection
review_title: Look elsewhere, this product will give you headaches.
review_text:
Not very happy with this appliance, we have had it about 18 months and it needs repair for the 4th time. The first time it went wrong, we were without an oven for a month as the part wasn't available. It failed again shortly after and took two repair visits to get it fixed. Today when running the self cleaning oven mode, the inner door glass just shattered. I will probably replace this myself as it is not a complicated job, but for such a new oven it is quite unacceptable. We will soldier on with it for a while longer, but to be honest we are already researching replacements, an oven that goes wrong every six months is an inconvenience to say the least.
When it does work, it cooks quite well, just wish it was more reliable.
As a previous reviewer said, Bosch customer service isn't very helpful, you will end up tracking down your own repair guy.
I would not recommend this appliance, I always regarded Bosch as a quality product, but my experience with this product has me thinking again.

product_title: Bosch HDI8054U 800 30" Stainless Steel Dual Fuel (Gas) Slide-In Sealed Burner Range - Convection
review_text: Given the negative reviews about reliability, I was nervous about buying this range. But I did, and added the extended warranty. I've had it for a few months, and so far so good. Everything works, including "Pizza Mode." I won't claim to be that guy who chooses an oven primarily because it has a dedicated pizza mode, but I was attracted. And for sure, my frozen pizzas come out notably better than before. German engineering at its finest. Also, the center gas burner is truly intense -- I can't imagine needing anything more powerful. No issues thus far.

product_title: Bosch HDI8054U 800 30" Stainless Steel Dual Fuel (Gas) Slide-In Sealed Burner Range - Convection
review_text: Excellent range for the money. I am a contractor, my wife is a professional baker and we are both impressed with this.  You could spend $2000 more and not get much more in return.  The convection oven works great.  My wife literally cooks three times as much (3 batches of cookies at a time) at once.  The stove top is easy to clean.  The controls work great. I have installed a dozen of Viking and wolf ranges and they are good but not worth the extra money.  They are a bit heavier feel but that is the only difference I notice. I have had great luck with bosch brand.  Power tools, dishwashers, even water heaters. This range was no exception. We have had it for a month now and are very pleased.

product_title: Bosch HDI8054U 800 30" Stainless Steel Dual Fuel (Gas) Slide-In Sealed Burner Range - Convection
review_text: Fabulous range, highly recommended, if you can get warrantee service. We needed help with a small item, but no one in out area would service it, using their warrantee terms. So sad.

product_title: Bosch HDI8054U 800 30" Stainless Steel Dual Fuel (Gas) Slide-In Sealed Burner Range - Convection
review_title: Stove top great, oven never worked right
review_text:
Bought in 2014, had to wait 3 months to receive it.
Oven stopped working in 12/14, then started working again. Repeated every summer and every Christmas. Had certified technicians look at it, they replaced a fan. It still didn't work. They couldn't figure it out and said to just replace the control panel. That didn't make sense as it worked except in the summer and at Christmas. Had an electrician look at it, he said it was fine. Contractor who installed it checked installation, said it was fine. Now, in 2018, after a summer of not working, the oven only broils. Bosch says get an appliance person to come find out what the problem is. The problem is that it is a LEMON. So, about to pay $200 to see if it can do something other than broil. Please, save yourself the trouble.

product_title: Bosch HDI8054U 800 30" Stainless Steel Dual Fuel (Gas) Slide-In Sealed Burner Range - Convection
review_text: Can one be in love with a stove? Well I act like it, just gazing at it with hearts in my eyes. I read review after review on all sites, and called Bosch before buying it, just to make sure that they'd fix the loud oven fan. Well, first of all, once it was installed and operating, I tried to decipher the source of a whispery sound heard and suddenly realized that it was the oven fan - so it's barely audible. Oven fan sound apparently is no longer a problem. The stove is beautiful to look at and minus the clunky rear panel of most American made stoves, allows for a more open feeling in my small kitchen and even some art on the wall. I've put up with cheapo Kenmore and GE stoves for years and years. They were reliable for sure, but the burners would click and click filling the kitchen with gas until they'd catch with a small explosion and there was always a gap between stovetop and counter that allowed for the collection of years' worth of gunk, unreachable by any kind of cleaning implement I could find. I just figured it was something I had to put up with. Well...NO MORE. The burners pop right on and the dials are incredibly sensitive. Just a touch and the flame is at the level I was seeking. And the stove has a stainless steel lip on either side that fits right over the counter so that there is no gap at all, as it accomplishes the built-in look as promised. No more digging out popcorn kernels and attempting to clean up spilled spaghetti sauce from a mini chasm, but chasm, nevertheless! Yay! And as you can see from the photos, the oven baked two perfect loaves of bread, my big first test. So far, so reliable. Just make sure before buying that your counters and stove will match height-wise. As one who has always loved to cook, my only regret is that I didn't recognize years ago that buying higher end appliances was well worth the investment! This one is for sure!

product_title: Bosch HDI8054U 800 30" Stainless Steel Dual Fuel (Gas) Slide-In Sealed Burner Range - Convection
review_title: Do Not Expect a Trouble-free Appliance.
review_text:
I bought this stove from a local retailer. I love the stove top and the five burners, but I wish they had included a double ring burner which heats large pans more evenly.
The electric oven is another story altogether. Right out of the box, the oven cannot seem to regulate the heat. It can vary by as much as 50-60 degrees. A certified Bosch technician ordered a new oven sensor. When he came to install it, he noticed a more serious problem with the gas connector within the unit. It was bent and twisted., and he could not remove the stove back or there would be a possibility that the oven problem might be fixed, but I would be left with a non-functioning stovetop. He said that the internal gas component was safe and not leaking. I’m going to have to take his word for it or maybe have the gas company come and check.
I looked into getting the stove exchanged, but Bosch informed that I had to have the repairs done before they would authorize an exchange and then promptly disconnected the chat. So much for Bosch quality and customer service on a brand new item.

product_title: Bosch HDI8054U 800 30" Stainless Steel Dual Fuel (Gas) Slide-In Sealed Burner Range - Convection
review_text: I've had this range about 2 years and can't begin to express how much I regret the purchase.  Don't count like I did on excellent engineering from Bosch - the grids on top will not accept small pans as many of mine are and unlike some people's comments I think the grates and stove top are very hard to clean.  But most of all, I am blown away by a design that causes the control panel to go out every time you use the self-cleaning oven feature.  This has happened twice on my stove!  Bosch's customer service agent hung up on me when I answered her question "What is the problem?" by saying that their engineers failed to insulate the control panel from a feature that they placed on the stove (self-cleaning feature.)  So don't count on any real help from Bosch they appear to only be interested in getting more money from you by making their parts unavailable to third parties.

product_title: Bosch HDI8054U 800 30" Stainless Steel Dual Fuel (Gas) Slide-In Sealed Burner Range - Convection
review_text:
I bought my Bosch range because I wanted a unit which would stand the test of time. Unfortunately, this one is malfunctioning after just three years. One of the burners will no longer ignite, and I can see the igniter is cracked. I looked online about how to replace it, and found that the heavy range will have to be slid out so the front and top of the range can be disassembled so the igniter can be replaced. Not the quality I expected from Bosch or a range that cost $2500.

Another thing I have learned is the oven is very difficult to operate. It may be good for a professional baker, but I have to refer to the instruction manual every time I use the oven. If it's pizza, it's on one rack, if it's a roast a different rack, and the racks and temperatures are different with every item I want to cook. Be aware.

product_title: Bosch HDI8054U 800 30" Stainless Steel Dual Fuel (Gas) Slide-In Sealed Burner Range - Convection
review_title: Stay clear from Bosch oven ranges, appliances
review_text: We have/had oven range since 2015. We have been using the oven daily. Although, it looks great, the range it is very poorly engineered. We had manty, many problems. Not sure where to begin.  For instance, none of the electronics are surge protected, and as result, we had to replace the electronic panel. (Was caused buy outages).  So far, we have 4 repairs, and these were costing us about 1000USD each. Today, the oven is not working again. For all the money we had spent,  we could have easily bought two Viking ranges. Do yourself a favor and stay clear from Bosch appliances. You will be much happier, unless  you just  like to look at it and not use.

product_title: Bosch HDI8054U 800 30" Stainless Steel Dual Fuel (Gas) Slide-In Sealed Burner Range - Convection
review_text:
Delivered Oct 29, 2021. Clock runs very fast and needs to be reset daily on this $4,000 oven.
Do bicep curls to have the strength to yank on and pull out the oven racks., which is no longer a problem because the OVEN STOPPED WORKING in January. Bosch says they will exchange for a new one but when? No date in sight! 5 months, $4,000 later, and all I have is a worthless piece of junk. Do not buy!

product_title: Bosch HDI8054U 800 30" Stainless Steel Dual Fuel (Gas) Slide-In Sealed Burner Range - Convection
review_text: we bot the dual fuel range August 2000. We immediately had a problem with one of the large burners going out and then coming on with a burst of flame when we opened the oven door. The repair service looked at it, said they would call Bosch and reported back that Bosch was aware of the issue but didn't consider it enough of a problem to be dangerous. I would disagree because the flames shot up about 6" and nearly burned me. Thank goodness I was quick enough to move my hand and the pot. Yesterday I turned the oven on and within minutes smelled an electrical fire and the house filled with smoke. I turned the range off along with the circuit breaker. Now I am without an oven and have no way to prepare dinner.  I expect it will take an extended time to get the parts and since Bosch only offers a one year warranty it will cost me a pretty penny.  Oh sure, I could have purchased an extended warranty but if Bosch only has confidence in their product for 365 days, do I really want their range? It is a blessing I was at home and not outdoors because the entire house could have burned down along with my pets. I'm not going to trust Bosch again and will be looking at my options with other grands.  Stay away from Bosch.

product_title: Bosch HDI8054U 800 30" Stainless Steel Dual Fuel (Gas) Slide-In Sealed Burner Range - Convection
review_text: Have this oven  HDI8054U.  Gas burners are fine.  Electric oven is a pain!  Very long time to get the oven to temperature, then it goes all over the place - up and down - from there.  30 to 60 degree swings. Replaced the sensor and the relays on the control board. Somewhat better, but not much.  Next would be to replace all the broiler burner, oven burner and convection burner even though the test fine with a ohm meter.  Some have said the convection burner is the issue. Don't know?  Debating as to whether to sink more money into this 5 year old expensive piece of junk or just buy a new and different brand?  Leaning towards the latter. Some parts can be difficult to find. Convenient for Bosch, I guess!  As I said, if you are considering this, or going to buy it.........GOOD LUCK!

product_title: Bosch HEI8054U 800 30" Stainless Steel Electric Slide-In Smoothtop Range - Convection
review_text:
This is a true story. I posted this review on the Bosch Canada website as well (waiting to see if the company will post it).

First stove: I purchased this model of Bosch stove in October 2015 on sale from Lowe's Regina (Saskatchewan, Canada). I paid to have it delivered and installed by Lowe's. According to the installers, sparks flew out of the stove when it was plugged in. I heard the noise but did not see where the sparks came from. The stove control panel was still working so the installers continued with the installation. Later, when I went to use the stove, two burners were not working. I also realized the installers had installed the stove so it was resting on my quartz countertop (which it should not because the stove weighs about 250 lbs). The countertop was damaged in about four places as a result. Lowe's is responsible for the countertop (still unresolved) and Bosch arranged for a stove replacement.

Second stove: The replacement stove was delivered and installed by Lowe's in November 2015. At time of delivery, the following issues were evident: 1) bubbles in the control panel finish 2) warped glass stove top and warped metal trim (photos attached). I needed a stove, and given the concerns with possibly damaging the counter top further, it was decided to repair the second stove rather than replace it. Numerous phone calls and emails later (weeks would go by with no response from Bosch Customer Service US), arrangements were made for a service technician to complete the repairs. In the meantime, I realized the oven fan was not working properly. The speed of the fan cycled erratically. I went to Lowe's and listened to the floor demo to compare! I found many bubbles in the oven finish as well. When the Bosch service technician visited my house (twice), he confirmed all of the above issues. This process has taken about two months. Now it's the end of January 2016, and it's been determined to order a third replacement stove.

Additional issues:

1) The Bosch installation manual says, under "Parts Included”, that foam tape should be included "unless already installed on underside of cooktop sides". For both stoves, no foam tape was provided by Bosch, nor was it on the underside of the cooktop, to protect my countertop. When I mentioned this to Bosch Customer Service, the supervisor replied that the installers should have not installed it without the foam tape! I purchased and installed tape for the second stove installation which seemed to help slide the stove in more easily.

2) Also, for both stoves, the chemical smell of the oven finish was extremely strong when the oven was on. Eventually, the smell dissipated, but until it did, I did not cook any food in the oven.

3) I find the stove top elements do not simmer at all well.
4) Lastly, it’s tricky to move the stove because of it’s weight and the lip on the sides of the stove top.

Funnily enough, during all this, my Bosch dishwasher was recalled for a fire hazard issue with the plug.

You may be asking yourself by now, why would I get a third replacement stove by Bosch? I'm hoping the company will get it together and send me a quality stove? The price I paid was a really good deal. It matches my made-in-Germany dishwasher (which did not give me problems). Are there other stoves out there much better in this price range?

Needless to say I cannot recommend this stove, especially not at full price.

Good luck with your stove shopping.

product_title: Bosch HEI8054U 800 30" Stainless Steel Electric Slide-In Smoothtop Range - Convection
review_title: Nice Range- But widen the stainless vent in the back!
review_text: I did not have any of the problems posted by other reviewers. This stove looks wonderful and performs flawlessly. The glass quality is German made and second to none. The only issue I have is that the back of the stove stainless vent does not extend to the very end like the glass top, thus exposing a gap in your counter on each side! This is a bad design, hopefully Bosch will correct with the next model as other reviewers say the same thing! The warming drawer was broken upon delivery but was replaced by the vendor with a new one. I don't think the spring and plastic mechanism that releases the door is very well thought out either. I have cooked about a month now and have no issues. I cook a lot of pizzas on pizza stone and using the pizza function on this stove it cooks at a lower temp (400) for a longer time but the results are excellent- crispy crust without even pre-heating the stone first! I did not have any loud fan noise as others have posted as well. Simply put, this stove performs and looks great!

product_title: Bosch HEI8054U 800 30" Stainless Steel Electric Slide-In Smoothtop Range - Convection
review_title: Beautiful and sleek, but not worth it.
review_text:
I purchased a showcase home and was impressed with the Bosch kitchen appliance package that was included with my new home. Within two weeks of using the stove, our teapot melted on the stove when accidentally left unattended. OK, this was our bad and no fault of Bosch, but we were surprised how powerful this stove is that it could melt a teapot! Several months later we noticed the two large front burners started to get discolored and cannot be scoured, cleaned or scrapped with a razor blade to return it to it's original finish. We have lived with a white char marks on the stove ever since. Earlier this week while sliding a plate off the top of a frying pan on the stove (we did not have a lid large enough) , it was accidentally dropped on the glass surface which chipped the edge of the glass on the stove, but the plate did not break. Since this incidence, the chip has turn into a crack that has run the entire length of the stove.

We have a 2nd residence which we purchased a Samsung glass top slide in stove for. We have not had any issues with the glass discoloring, chipping, cracking or overheating of the elements. I don't normally write reviews for products, but the $600.00 price tag to replace this stove top was my motivation. Far better choices out there than this stove, do your research and stay away from Bosch.

product_title: Bosch HEI8054U 800 30" Stainless Steel Electric Slide-In Smoothtop Range - Convection
review_title: Lovely but very difficult to keep cooktop clean and unstained
review_text: Let me start out with the fact that my boyfriend, who loves to cook big meals, does make a mess in the kitchen.  My job is to clean up.  So I very hurriedly wiped off my new Bosch cooktop with Weiman daily cooktop cleaner the last 3 times he cooked.  Wrong.  I'm guessing some oily foods such as olive and grape oils got sort of baked into the glass cooktop, and the top was left with big smears that would not scrub off with the daily cleaner.  So I ordered Weiman's heavy duty cooktop cleaner plus scrubbing pad on Amazon.  Better, but smear residue was still apparent. The manual said to use the razor blade/holder which came as an accessory.  Yes.  I scraped and scraped, and finally every inch of the cooktop was clean and shiny, after about 1 1/2 hours of scrubbing.  This was about six months ago, and fast-forward to today - the same mess happened!!  My fault for not carefully cleaning after each use, but I just now spent over an hour with white vinegar, Weiman's heavy duty cleaner, and a damn razor blade to restore the perfect look.  Giant, annoying hassle!!  I don't know if this is a Bosch quirk or if it's true of all electric cooktops, but who has time for this type of unpleasant task??  True, we have sloppy cooks in my house, but sheesh!

product_title: Bosch HEI8054U 800 30" Stainless Steel Electric Slide-In Smoothtop Range - Convection
review_title: Dial indicators rub off within a year
review_text: A little over a year of use a the numbers rubbed off around the dials!!  I only used a sponge and dish detergent.  No abrasives or scrubbing.  Stoves are supposed to last for years.  Not worth spending extra for the Bosch name.  I used to like the brand.

product_title: Bosch HEI8054U 800 30" Stainless Steel Electric Slide-In Smoothtop Range - Convection
review_title: Remember to wipe down the inside of the oven and run it at 350 for 30 minutes before using
review_text: So far it works very well. Have used  the oven for warming already cooked foods and for baking. The cook top works super  well. I clean it every day with Cerama Bryte. Seems like cleaning up every little spot right away will keep it from becoming uncleanable. The oven did give off a very strong burning petroleum kind of smell the first time I used it, even though I ran it at 350 for half an hour after it was installed. I did forget to wipe down the inside first, which I was also told to do. So maybe that is why. Over all I am very happy with the purchase.

product_title: Bosch HEI8054U 800 30" Stainless Steel Electric Slide-In Smoothtop Range - Convection
review_title: Don't buy any Bosch appliances.  Internal /external parts will break. Cheap stainless
review_text:
My control Display panel for this electric stove broke last month. The display started to show wild lines, and numbers. The stove top worked and the and oven seemed to work, if I could press the buttons in correct order. but there was no way to see what oven temperature was being set. I wanted to replace the part on my own, but being not sure what the issue was I ended up paying $300 for a $140 part.

A month later, the other computer board inside broke, which I'm can't seem to figure out the part number and plan to be twice the prince of the display unit I replaced.

I will never buy Bosch again.

product_title: Bosch HEI8054U 800 30" Stainless Steel Electric Slide-In Smoothtop Range - Convection
review_title: ANOTHER TRUE Story about this same BOSCH model HEI8054U
review_text: We had an almost identical situation to the 2016 Review when our new BOSCH HEI8054U Electric Range purchased at SEARS was installed - as soon as it was powered sparks flew and spit all over - clearly defective.  When the replacement arrived, installation went okay but we purchased an additional TWO YEAR Warranty from Sears. Unit appeared to function properly and as a neat freak, I kept to the manufacturer's recommendations using only the procedure/products used to keep the glass top and oven clean. Two months after the warranty expired, the OVEN began burning food - going way higher than the temperature I set. Then the oven door repeatedly LOCKED w/Error Code E115 displayed. One large cooktop burner does not regulate itself well & stays so HOT that it has a gray/whitish ring now that won't go away. My GE PROFILE Range cooktop NEVER did this. On a budget so I've gone without an oven for months now while saving $$ to afford that. Had always thought BOSCH a quality product; deeply disappointed and thought other potential consumers should know before purchasing.

review_title: Really disappointed in our Bosch appliance package we got two years ...

product_title: Bosch B22FT80SNS800 21.9 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel French Door Refrigerator
review_title: overall it's a great machine and we love it.
review_text:
we've had this refrigerator for about a year (bought through best buy).
It's been a great appliance so far. it's quiet, keeps food fresh, makes ice, dispenses cold water.
we did not get the in the door water or ice because we don't like the look of that and from what we read it can be very loud.
the finish has held up nicely for us. I use a stainless steel cleaning product about once every month or two to take off smudges and get the new luster back.
I love the meat and cheese drawer at the bottom. it makes room for much more above. the shelves are easy to adjust and wipe down to keep clean.
the water filter works nicely, but replacements are expensive as I'm just finding out. so far the cheapest I have found is $90, but am just replacing it for the first time in a little over a year.
the ice maker works well.
the door alarm doesn't seem to be working and a couple of times it has been left open and frozen crystals appeared on the cooling element. that disappears after a while when you figure it out and shut it back up. opps.

the size if more than adequate for two adults.

product_title: Bosch NET8666SUC 800 36" Black Electric Smoothtop Cooktop
review_title: We love it. It only took about a minute to ...

review_text: I love it!!!  so sleek

product_title: Frigidaire FPGS3085PF Professional 30" Stainless Steel Gas Slide-In Sealed Burner Range - Convection
review_text:
I had some basic expectations from this two thousand dollar stove. The pros are it looks great, it is a slide in and it has a meat probe.

The cons are it lacks basic functionality that even a 200 gas stove has. Basically when you turn the burner control from the lowest setting to the higher settings the flame jumps around like a roman candle. Not only that but on the power burner there are basically two settings 1. extremely low 2. extremely high. There is no middle ground. So when you start to turn the knob from low to high you find that nothing happens until you are about 90% of the way back to the highest setting, then the flame kind of explodes back to high. On the Plus side the fireball can help get rid of those annoying arm hairs you have, however it can be a bit surprising.

Tried to get service from Frigidaire. .. they referred me to a local repair guy who insisted everything was 'normal' needless to say I returned the stove and now enjoy a strove from NXR brand that works great.

product_title: Electrolux EI24ID50QS IQ-Touch 24" Stainless Steel Fully Integrated Dishwasher - Energy Star
review_text: Had a Dishwasher and Microwave go out on me over the holidays. I seem to be burning out dishwashers at an alarming rate, the computer goes bad or motor goes out, leaks, not having good luck. So getting away from Kitchen Aid and Whirlpool and seeing the problems the new Samsung was having (people pushing chairs up against the door to keep it closed) I decided to go with this dishwasher as it was rated number one on some testing something on another site. They glorified the thing as god's gift to the dishwasher community, so okay. Ordered from Lowes, took it home and installed it. The inside is a little smaller than my last Kitchen Aid so that takes some getting used to as I like to stick car size things inside, huge pots for making spaghetti for 20 people like five gallon stuff, doesn't fit. Regular home, will not have a problem with this dishwasher, I over do it. It cleans better than any of the dishwashers I have had in the past. zed Glasses come out cleaner or more clear, well everything you can see it, I am surprised. Drying kinda sucks. I had turned off my water softener to fill fish tanks and if you use hard water, it does not dry the dishes very well. Turned on the softener, use Jet Dry and it does okay sometimes I got to shake a few things to get them dry when I take it out. The controls is something else I don't like. Press the start button and nothing indicates you made it happen. However if you put your ear to it, it makes a little beep beep sound, very faint. Then you close it and does a little faint song as to say its going and you know its going. For the amount of money I paid for this dishwasher and how well it cleans, I am willing to overlook the small things and I don't mind drying one or two things by hand, but others might see it differently. I like it and its doing good, so 5 stars. One more thing, I do BBQ and no other dishwasher can get some of the meat pans clean. I usually wash them in the dishwasher just to make it easier to do it by hand. This dishwasher actually cleans the pans first time out. Makes me wonder how long my dishes are going to last getting blasted clean like that, but I like the less work that is involved.

product_title: Electrolux EI24ID50QS IQ-Touch 24" Stainless Steel Fully Integrated Dishwasher - Energy Star
review_title: Thought I was buying quality, but instead nothing by heartache.
review_text:
I would strongly advise anyone to avoid the Electrolux line of dishwashers. While the machines runs great for about a year after the initial warranty wears off the real heartaches begin. I thought by spending big bucks for what I wrongly assumed was a top of the line brand that I would get quality AND a company that would stand behind their products. I was mistaken on both counts. The machine is now almost 4 years old, and I have had 2 service calls that I had to pay 100% of the costs of. But the real insult came recently. The CHEAP, and by that I mean flimsy plastic parts that are used on the upper and lower racks started to break or malfunction. Called Electrolux to order replacements and while they are CHEAP plastic the cost of the parts is quite high. Over a c-note for what should be no more than a Jackson. And the attitude of the customer reps? That depends, some say "that's the way it is, take it or leave it", or "yeah, I don't know why this company treats customers so badly".
Well, they and Frigidaire, White-Westinghouse and Kenmore, all made by the same company won't be able to treat this customer that badly ever again.

product_title: Electrolux EI24ID50QS IQ-Touch 24" Stainless Steel Fully Integrated Dishwasher - Energy Star
review_text:
This dishwasher was purchased last October from the Brick. The first service call was in May of this year. It was purchased with an extended warranty!!! To date this dishwasher officially has been looked at six different times to my account. According to TransGlobal there has only been 4 service calls on it. What I have learned that many of this companies (Sears, The brick, Homedepot) will use different service providers at different times in order to get around their "3 major service" protocol before we replace or credit you the cost of the dishwasher.
Back to the washer>>MAJOR DESIGN FLAW that keeps on giving the repair man a run for their money!! It has to do with the bubble on the upper right hand of the tub. Essentially it draws out the steam when drying (steam)!! Rather then venting out towards the counter, the side vent, this one runs from the top right side of the tub down the side and onto a "drain reservoir" Now remember steam is supposed to come out and there should not be no trouble the repair man said!!!!Instead the float comes into contact with the water "steam" and the drain sensor is SET OFF
I have read the I30 message on the board countless times. I have tried to reset the dishwasher, both by manual instructions and flipping the power switch on and off!!!! Until the water has been completely removed and the float no longer makes contact with the water, the dishwasher will not resume it's normal function. So, I have come to the end of the road with this dishwasher!!! I now wait for a decision to be made on a replacement or credit from The Brick. This appliance uses a ton of water and I mean a ton!! Never really had a problem with clean dishes. Drying cycle is super long too, but I guess we can't change that either. So you know I had to ask the repair man what his choice would be if he had to replace it!!
Bosch or Kitchen Aid he says. Bosch will be my choice moving forward I hope. I have learned a lot of things throughout this long painful process, but yet the most important one is to always spend the extra bucks and buy yourself an Extended Warranty!!

product_title: Electrolux EI24ID50QS IQ-Touch 24" Stainless Steel Fully Integrated Dishwasher - Energy Star

product_title: Electrolux EI24ID50QS IQ-Touch 24" Stainless Steel Fully Integrated Dishwasher - Energy Star
review_text:
I had low expectations for this dishwasher based on the sordid reviews, but after two months of ownership I don't have a single gripe. I'm guessing the control board quality problem was fixed.

My dishes get clean and it's extremely quiet. The silverware tray is fantastic. I can put all my flatware on top and have a ton of room for pots and pans in the bottom. It took some time to figure out the best way to load, but I'm a pro at getting everything in now.

The bottle washers are a bit cheesy. My baby bottles get mostly clean but the clips themselves have a cheap feel and they are too close together to arrange the bottles side by side (Tommy tippee). More trouble getting them on the clips than it's worth.

One star off for racks not rolling as smoothly as some competitors and the chincy bottle wash feature already explained.

I asked for purchasing advice from my appliance repair guy and he said it was a good choice - he has no more or fewer service calls for this than any other. He said all appliances are going to break. They don't last 20 years anymore. The trick is to buy a brand that has inexpensive and readily available replacement parts. He also explained that many performance problems we encounter with today's dishwashers have more to do with epa regulations than the actual appliance. He suggested throwing in a cup of vinegar every fifth wash and running a an empty cycle with just one cup filled with vinegar in each corner once a month. So far so good.

Overall I'm very pleased with my purchase and feel I got good value for my money. I would recommend to friends and family.

product_title: Electrolux EI24ID50QS IQ-Touch 24" Stainless Steel Fully Integrated Dishwasher - Energy Star
review_title: Bad engineering! No spare parts! Lasted only for 6 years!
review_text:
I will never have an Electrolux dishwasher again! The reasons:
1. You can't find simple parts like door seals and hinge brackets. For example, the door bottom seal is not sold separately (~$25). You would need to buy the whole door liner for $350.
2. The metal brackets attached to the hinges rust too fast! In 6 years I got it completely corroded, so it started leaking at the door bottom. Both detachable metal brackets need to be replaced to stop the leak but you won't find this part.
3. Electronics periodically get into a glitch. The display indication periodically won't come up. The power cycling helps to reboot the internal microcontroller and get it working again. We dealt with this issue for 6 years pretty much on weekly basis.
4. The dishwasher has a touch control panel which is nice but the internal speaker is very quiet, you'd need to put your ear close to the door to hear it.

OVERALL IT'S ALL BAD ENGINEERING! STAY AWAY FROM ELECTROLUX DISHWASHERS! DON'T WASTE YOUR MONEY!

product_title: Electrolux EI24ID30QS IQ-Touch 24" Stainless Steel Fully Integrated Dishwasher - Energy Star
review_title: Great washer, as long as you remember to do monthly maintenance.
review_text:
After 15 months of use, this machine still works like a charm. I do agree that the installation is not as straightforward as other dishwashers I've installed, but there's nothing "impossible" about it. Dishes are especially clean. Read the owner's manual. You can adjust he amount of rinse agent to match the hardness of your water. If spotting is taking place, just bump up the release level. Use a machine cleaner each month to keep the stainless steel from developing a film! Only one design problem- if you use gelatin-based detergent pods (the soft bricks of cleaner): The detergent dispenser must be 100% clear of obstructions or the pod won't dissolve completely. No such problems with hard powder detergent capsules or gels you squeeze from a bottle into the dispensing drawer. Make sure you clean the 2 filters or you'll get redeposit problems in about a month or so. Cleaning filters is easy with an old toothbrush. Remembering to do is tougher. Freshly soiled dishes can use the 30 minute cycle and it works well- just don't put anything left out for hours on that cycle, The brief timing can't soak off dried on gook. I got ALL Thanksgiving dishes/pots/silverware done in three 30-minute cycles and it all came out clean!

2020 Update: it only lasted 2 years before electronics went bad.

review_title: you mean I wasted a whole day's vacation so you could ask me ...
review_text: On March 16, 2016, I called Electrolux to request a warranty repair of my then 10-week old dishwasher.  The phone rep asked numerous questions, including what, exactly, was wrong with my dishwasher.  She then instructed me how to try to "reset" the dishwasher (which failed), and then she scheduled what I thought was a repair appointment, five days later on March 21.  The rep asked me whether I preferred a repair time window of 8:00 a.m. to Noon, or Noon to 5:00.  I said I preferred morning as I had an afternoon appointment.  The rep then told me that Whitman Appliance Repair would contact me the day before to tell me my specific appointment time.  The day before, sure enough Whitman called, only to tell me that would see me between 10:00 a.m. and 2:00 p.m.  I said that Electrolux scheduled me for 8:00 a.m. to Noon.  Whitman said they could come between 10:00 and 2:00, or they could reschedule for a later date.  So at the last minute, I had to schedule an entire vacation day off work, and reschedule my afternoon meeting.  On March 21, Whitman arrived as scheduled.  The repair technician walked into my house, looked at my dishwasher, and said, "what's wrong with it?"  I said, "didn't Electrolux tell you?"  The technician said, "they don't tell us nothing."  I explained the problem.  He then said, "you need a new blah blah blah" (a part).  "We'll have to order it, it will arrive in 3 to 10 business days.  Then we will call you to schedule the repair."  He then took a few pictures of my dishwasher, including a picture of the serial number.  He was in my house for all of about 30 seconds.  I said, you mean I wasted a whole day's vacation so you could ask me the exact same question that I already answered for the Electrolux phone rep?"  He said, we'll, I needed to get the serial number."  I said, "I needed to tell the phone rep the serial number before she would schedule the repair!"  He said, "I also needed to take pictures of your dishwasher to document any pre-existing damage, so you can't sue us to fix something that wasn't our fault."  Great!  I blew an entire vacation day so that Electrolux and Whitman Appliance Repair could cover their butts.  Finally, on March 29 -- 19 days after I called Electrolux, I got to schedule yet another vacation day and my dishwasher was finally repaired.  The complete lack of even basic communication between Electrolux and Whitman and the long (half-day) appointment windows for repair convince me that Electrolux and Whitman Appliance have absolutely no regard for customer service.  I will think long and hard before I ever buy another Electrolux appliance.  NEW TOPIC:  The dishwasher I replaced was a very low-end model.  The Electrolux was, at $888 retail, what I thought was a mid-to-high range model.  It has a stainless steel interior and a third rack, which I liked.  However, I learned the expensive way that a more expensive dishwasher does NOT clean my dishes any better than a cheap one.  The ONLY real difference between my old dishwasher and the new Electrolux, is that the Electrolux is quieter when running.  However, the noise level of my old dishwasher never bothered me or my family.  Or bedrooms and TV room are separate floors from the kitchen, so we rarely heard the old dishwasher.  And even if we were sitting nearby, we could converse or play music or do whatever without ever being bothered by the dishwasher.  If I ever have to buy another dishwasher, I'll choose a cheap one (and very lucky NOT an Electrolux).

product_title: Electrolux EI24ID30QS IQ-Touch 24" Stainless Steel Fully Integrated Dishwasher - Energy Star
review_text:

2. Inside of cups will often have food debris.
3. Does not always dry the dishes even when set to max.
4. Leaves streaks on dishes - especially plates and on sides of bowls.

If the rating was based on quietness and delivery alone it would get a raving 5 stars. Because of it's inability to clean effectively, it drops it down to a 1 star. review_title: Overall good quality but wimpy timer alarm
review_text:
Our Thermador double oven gave up after 25 yrs of use, albeit the last 15 yrs we lost some features that Thermador wouldn't fix. Due to Thermador's policy of not supporting parts or service after about 10 yrs. we looked at Bosch and liked their warranty service and reliability on their dishwashers, of which we've had two over the past 30 yrs.
So, this 27" double oven works just like we expected, we like the "proof" temperature settings for dough rising, the "preheat" feature, and the fact that there are no heating rods in the bottom of either oven, leaving a cleaner look and better "self-cleaning" for cleanup. But there are three features we're not pleased with; 1. Why not feature both ovens with identical features? Makes no sense to me. 2. Only one "sliding rack" is included; you purchased double ovens; why not include a sliding rack in each one? It makes Bosch look cheap. And 3.. most importantly, the "Timer" function alarm is useless; it's such a pathetic, weak alarm that you can barely hear if you're in the kitchen, and forget hearing it if you're in another room. There are 3 settings for the alarm and they are all barely indistinguishable from another. The highest setting is simply not loud at all. This is very important to me because we use the timer for all sorts of events, and I especially want to hear it when doing chores in another part of the house. Our old Thermador had a timer alarm you could hear at the other end of the house. I consider the weak, practically useless alarm on the Bosch a true design flaw and defect, it is so weak.
Despite this, I'd purchase the Bosch 27' Double Oven again, for customer support and reliability, just wish they'd address the 3 concerns above.

review_title: Company says I’m on my own for known drum cracks
review_text:
Bought a Samsung washer and dryer unit in this series 4 years ago after buying a home. My home which needed renovation took me two years to move into, thereby leaving the washer and dryer unit sitting wrapped in the original packing/shipping boxes even some time after moving in. Please note I also have a smaller Frigidaire unit located on a different floor in my home which is used mostly because of its proximity to the bedrooms. There are only three adults within my home and NO children, so washer and dryers are not used as frequently.

We started hearing a loud pounding noise with the dryer mid to late October 2018. We discovered the issue yesterday; a cracked drum. Since we NEVER allow shoes of any kind in our units and the heaviest items to go in the units are blankets, we were dumbfounded to find this issue. We’ve since done some research and found other customers complaining about a cracked drum as well as a current class-action lawsuit against the manufacturer (Samsung) for this known issue.

Samsung refuses to fix the drum and will only set-up an appointment if I pay for it. They’ve advised me that even if my dryer was still under warranty, that they wouldn’t cover it regardless because it’s considered a cosmetic issue.
I’ve had many washers and dryers over my lifetime, including the “work horse” Frigidaire washer and dryer on my second floor, yet I’ve never encountered this issue. This is a defect with the manufacturing of this product and Samsung absolutely refuses to make it right.
This will be my last Samsung washer and dryer unit. Other than that I very much enjoy my Samsung TVs and tablet. Samsung gets an A for electronics in my book, but not so much for their washer and dryer units.

product_title: Bosch B22CT80SNS 800 21.8 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel Counter Depth French Door Refrigerator
review_title: There's a few things I would change but so far we are pretty happy with our purchase.
review_text:
So far we are pretty happy with this fridge but there's a few things to be aware of:
- The shelves have little in the way of adjustment options, up or down and that's it. None of the shelves slide out or fold up, this is a nice feature in much cheaper brands and models.
- No butter bin!
- The very top of the fridge tends to freeze whatever is up there, in our case that would be our eggs. This happens when our fridge is set at 38 degrees even, which happens to be the recommended and preset temp from the manufacturer.
- The produce drawers are very shallow, this is a trade off for having a water dispenser in the fridge, the reservoir (keeps the water cold) sits behind the drawers. I'd say you lose a good 4" of drawer depth from the reservoir... but the water dispenser is pretty awesome (more on that later).
- Has adjustable feet instead of adjustable rollers, that means when you adjust the feet it lifts the rollers off the ground. Pain in the butt if you need to pull the fridge out for some reason, not like you need to do this often but still a minus none the less.
- Lighting is not the best we had seen in our search for a fridge, All the other brands had lights all around to eliminate shadows and dead spots. This has two lights at the top which are blocked easily by eggs or pizza boxes.
- The left door is a bit harder to close than the right one since the door spacer is on that side. Which is a pain since the water dispenser is on that same side. If you open both doors at the same time it's not an issue. Wish the spacer was on the right side.

Okay on to the things that I love about this fridge:
- It holds magnets! Love putting our kids artwork on the fridge and our GE profile fridge didn't allow for that.
- From the time we plugged in it was cooling groceries in 4 hours. This thing keeps food COLD, notably our lunch meat which has an extra three days of life (8 days total) over our last fridge.
- Ice! This thing cranks out ice like I've never seen before. 18 hours after I plugged it in we had a full bin of ice. It breezed through our last dinner party where most were drinking mixers. Love the ice maker, which btw comes with a built-in scoop holder and scoop and with the flip of lever it attaches to the door so it slides out upon opening.
- Water dispenser rocks. We used to buy bottled water since our tap water tastes so gross, not anymore. Water comes out cold and it tastes like deerpark water.
- It's a beautiful fridge and it fits like a glove in our cabinet cut-out.
- All the drawers open and close smoothly, including the freezer drawer and inner storage.

If you add up it up appears that the negatives outweigh the positives but I don't think so. We went into this knowing that every fridge we considered would have it's drawbacks. I only found one negative review in my countless hours of research and that is worth peace of mind to me. It seemed that for every good review I found of another brand there was an equal amount of negative reviews. We are a family of four with a 5 and a 2 year old and it's plenty of space for us at the moment, we do have another fridge in the basement that holds a decent amount of frozen goods though. No regrets here I would buy this fridge again for sure.

As a side note this is the same fridge as the kitchen aid architect II series and another jen airr model. Tried finding the differences between them but I could not.

product_title: Samsung DV42H5000GW 7.5 Cu. Ft. Front-Load Gas Dryer with Smart Care, White
review_text:
After a significant amount of research and toiling over the seemingly excessive prices for dryers (it seems like they've doubled in the last 10 years), I landed on this model, primarily due to a high Consumer Reports rating, an extremely big discount from Best Buy, and because it looks very similar to a Kenmore Elite I replaced. In fact, it fits the Kenmore base perfectly and, at a glance, is a very close match to my old washer that it sits next to. I have had it for 3 months now, and I'm at a point where I can say I definitely don't like it.

There are several significant irritants with this dryer. First, it balls-up almost all large items like no other dryer I have ever used. Sheets, towels, and even jeans are ALWAYS wound in a tight mess of a knot, along with everything else that gets caught in the wrath. This happens within a few minutes into the cycle. In particular, drying sheets requires at least 3 complete removals and unwindings during the 1+ hour of drying time. If you forget to do this, you'll easily triple the dry time, having to unravel and restart the load--they'll be wound so tight that nothing will dry. I don't know if it is the speed of the drum, the odd paddles (they're shaped like none other I've seen before), or what.

Second, it developed an annoying rattle inside, toward the back, after a few months of use. I read another review that mentioned a "scraping" noise, which may be the same thing I'm experiencing. It sounds more like a rattle, in my opinion--probably some metal object that has become loose inside. This isn't a huge deal for me, as my laundry room is in the basement, but it is extremely annoying.

Those aside, there are a few other minor annoyances, like when checking clothes mid-cycle (or unraveling, per my earlier comment), there is a chime to indicate that the door is open, just like on a car when you leave the keys in the ignition. This is a completely unnecessary and annoying feature. Also, the unit has to be turned off and on between loads. It takes several seconds to turn on (very much like a Samsung TV, in fact). Why can't I make my selections and push "start" like every other dryer I've ever owned? I mentioned the dry time for sheets--it seems long, but judging from my last dryer, it takes about the same length of time.

The plusses? It looks nice and has very good capacity for the size. It does dry thoroughly if you use the "more dry" setting and don't overload it. However, the benefits do not outweigh the problems. In hindsight, I would have gladly paid another $200 for a dryer without these issues.

review_title: Save yourself some emotional angst and do NOT buy this dryer
review_text:
Glad to know I'm not the only one with issues with this dryer. Thirty minutes after it was hooked up (and the delivery guys were back on their way), it started making a sound like the bearing in the motor had gone bad. I timed it, and the "click, click, click" was 60 times per minute. Fortunately, the merchant offered an exchange.

Then Problem #2 began, and it's actually a much bigger problem.

Whomever designed this overpriced appliance did something wanky to the baffles in the drum, because I didn't have this problem with my old (Samsung) dryer. I can not dry any bedding in this new dryer (purchased 8.2015) because it tangles up everything into such a tight ball that my sheets are ruined. My new policy is to stand at the dryer and open the door every 1-2 minutes, remove all the sheets, shake them out and re-insert. review_text:
After much research we elected to replace our aging Maytag with this unit. After having to remove doors to get the unit into the house because the published dimensions are incorrect, we had the unit installed, programmed and the wireless unit up and running. The wireless setup was painless.

After about 36 hours, the temperatures started to rise in the freezer. The freezer rose 18F and the fridge 8F. We called Samsung support, which itself took an act of congress to get a body on the phone. After and hour discussion, I was told I would have to wait 24 hours for a call back - really now? So we opened a case and 24 hours went buy with no call back. Later the next day the temperatures started to rise dramatically and quickly. There was no cold air blowing anywhere. The fridge rose from 35F to 45F and the freezers went form -8F to 30F in a matter of 15-20 minutes. We started moving food to other boxes. I called Home Depot, who was very responsive, and they got Samsung on the phone immediately.

Samsung had us power cycle the box. The box started cooling again the way it should. I was told the fridge had a glitch - a glitch - c'mon - seriously!!! Yes they said the published fix was to power cycle the box whenever this happens. Since then I have talked with a couple of Samsung tech reps. The Glitch is well known yet they will not fix it.

I am 64 years old and have owned many refrigerators/freezers and the most I ever had to worry about was loosing power. Now I have a full house generator and that is no longer a concern.

They said the unit will do this glitch if there is a momentary power interruption of voltage fluctuation. Silly my Sub-Zero and my Maytag seem to be immune to these issues.

The correct response would have been, "Yes we are aware of the problem and working diligently to fix it. You will be notified when there is a fix. Thank You."

But not Samsung - if you buy this then you deserve what you get. You say I have sour grapes - you betcha! A $6,000 box should at the minimum be reliable.

review_title: Everything it's cracked up to be
review_text:
I was able to secure this refrigerator via Best Buy (I also bought the Chef Collection dishwasher through them). The price was the best I have seen to-date. $4,300. I havent seen it at this price-level since then...though it is bound to drop in price as time goes on. Unfortunately you do get what you pay for as Best Buy has proven to be near-impossible to deal with on this and even more so on a separate Samsung dish-washer purchase.

This refrigerator was wooed-over at the Consumer Electronics Show in January 2014 with one startling "preview-review" after another, plus Samsung has trotted out a bunch of celeb-chefs to make food that has little to do with their product to help grab foodies' attention. After cutting through the marketing mumbo-jumbo we have a refrigerator with an impressive spec sheet.

Plenty of capacity, extremely high functionality of space, amazing looks inside & out, and sparkling water built-in.

The capacity numbers in cuft are impressive and it follows-through with highly usable space everywhere. This model is very deep and also offers plenty of height where you need; along with the requisite flexible shelves to add even more head-room for tall things. But it doesnt stop there. For example, compared to last year's sparkling water model, this one better utilizes the space on the water-side door. There's top-to-bottom capacity utilization on that door. And then there is the bottom right quadrant with its flexible fridge/freezer settings. As opposed to the main fridge and freezer which can be set at one-degree increments, the flex space has four settings. We use it as a 30 degree fridge for leftovers, berries, meats and other items whose freeze point is lower than 32 degrees. I've found the temperature to be very accurate. We are currently at 39 degrees in the main part of the fridge. When using the bottom right for fridge space most people will be awash in extra space during all but the busiest family gatherings.

The exterior is a noticeable step up vs anything Ive seen on the market. A beautiful, dark stainless steel with horizontal grain and an extra coating to prevent fingerprints. Minimal controls on the face; most are concealed on top of the bottom right drawer. And there's a slick LED temp display that lights up only when engaged or when the door opens. There are no extruding door handles which is also a plus. Then on the inside the stainless backing that is meant to maintain temp consistency contributes greatly to a super-sharp looking interior.

The sparkling water function is one that we use daily. Well, hourly : ) We're zealous sparkling water drinkers and this machine has been a god-send in this regard. We love a certain mineral water, but we're tired of the bottles everywhere so we cut that back to only the more serious meals of the day and use the Samsung every other time. It's so nice to be able to poor a smidgen of fizzy for when you need to take a pill, etc. It's worth noting that it does not produce hyper-bubbles even at its highest setting. We like it that way, but I dont think those that prefer Perrier or those that are looking to make copies of sweetened sodas, for example, will be pleased with the carb-level. So take that into consideration.

The little extras like the marination trays arent all that useful as they do not come with a cover and are not very heavy gauge. We'll certainly use them from time-to-time, but it's not a feature that should sway a purchase decision.

Overall were thrilled with the machine and look forward to years of use...

product_title: Samsung RF34H9960S4 Chef Collection 34.3 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel French Door Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_text:
After (30) years it was high time to replace my aging GE 2 door fridge (24 cu ft) which still runs great. This was a project I have been postponing for years as the old GE fridge was set up inside a custom made niche (or cubby) back in 1985. Essentially the old GE fridge sat inside the adjacent laundry room. With the advent in technology, fridges too I realized have grown a lot in volume & features. So eventually I demolished the old cubby & rebuilt it to house this specific Samsung fridge that I bought through Amazon from US Appliances.com. I visited Best Buy to get a hands on feel for this fridge & compare shop with others. This Samsung fridge is the Bentley of all fridges.I compared it to Sub Zero, Viking, Kitchenaid, Thermador which at far higher prices were far more shallower in depth. Nice facade. But not even close in volumetric capacity to the Samsung (34.3 cu ft). My old GE was the top of the line back in 1985 and I was about to do my last fridge upgrade until I die. (I am in my mid 50s). So I wanted the best in class regardless of brand name & price. This Samsung I assure all is the very best in its class and is a bargain for everything it does and offers. The Vikings and Sub zeros at double the price can not hold a candle by it.
Ok. I purchased it along with the Gas Samsung Chef Collection cooking range & micro wave from US Appliance.com for a full make over in my kitchen. I did not buy the dishwasher as my GE profile dishwasher in bisque matches the Kraftmaid ivory/cream cabinetry. And I hardly ever even use it. So left it alone. Blends in well. Btw, the Samsung Gas slide in cooking range is a pro unit and seriously recommended. It has a power burner that does pan broiled Tender loin and NY strip steaks to absolute divine perfection. Talks the walk and walks the talk. It is excellent.

Back to the Samsung fridge. This is a 4 door fridge. It has 2 compressors and 3 evaporators. This is not for the faint of heart. This is the Chef Collection fridge. And Highly recommend you shop around as Best Buy and Home Depot sell this for $5500/ less 10% plus sales tax. US appliance had the best price.Hands down.

Fridge arrived as scheduled and was dropped off with the other appliances by truck on my back deck via my back yard alley access gate. I had to down load the manual to "study up" and understand this fridge. I had to dismount the 4 doors for it to go through my standard 36" wide front mahogany & leaded glass door. It would not fit through my back Pella sliding door. I made these discoveries somewhat in aftermath after the appliances were delivered as I was overseas on business and had no time a month earlier when purchased online. My fault. This is a VERY BIG fridge. I did have its dimensions embedded in my mind from several trips to Best Buy and online too as I had to totally remodel the fridge cubby or niche with the carpenters and sheet rock guys. That was a $1200/ job labor & materials in itself. Remember: No more fridge upgrades until I die.OK

I decided to tackle the Samsung installation myself and hired 2 supermen: Caveman and Samson from a friend's shop. I borrowed a friend's fridge dolly with strap. We moved the Samsung around the block to the front door of my house "doorless". I removed all 4 doors myself. Reasonably easy and straight forward. I did follow the online downloaded print out instructions very carefully. The top left door is heavier than the others. Several electrical wire connectors had to be disconnected. At the bottom corners there are 2 plastic covers held in place with 1 screw that hides the wire connectors. These were also removed to access the connectors.

It was quite a job to roll in this Samsung through my front door, living rm, dining rm and finally kitchen. It got stuck at the 32" wide dining to kitchen door. Mind you that door was already removed off its hinges. This fridge is actually wider than stated without its doors. I had to pry out the frame door stop trim for it to enter the kitchen. It was a Herculean task but I handled it well and was in full control. The fridge was finally docked into its custom cubby. Plugged it in and got it running. The bottom half failed to go down in temp. Interior lights bottom half did not come on. Upper half which is all fridge worked fine. Also door ajar alarm was going off continuously. Left side doors did not align with right side doors. Many issues and more. Called US appliances who summoned Samsung who scheduled a Samsung tech visit. He was dismayed with the issues and recommended replacing it by US appliances. US appliances did not want to have anything to do with this fridge and its issues. Long story short Samsung tech ordered many parts inc a control board & returned in 4 days to fix all issues. Samsung tech initially had no knowledge of this model but when he returned he did. He refitted the small plastic feet covers at bottom corners and leveled the front feet & this fixed all issues.I held off on refitting the plastic covers at bottom corners as fridge leveling needed tweaking. He educated himself & me that there are small magnets inside these plastic covers that make the difference to the bottom half working as designed or not. Would have never thought so. But true. Also handbook found inside fridge makes no mention of the importance to refit bottom plastic covers.I had to buy the CO2 soda stream cylinders from Amazon subsequently and it has now been installed (very simple to do).
Samsung tech was here a week ago and the fridge has been working perfectly ever since. It is very quiet and I have tested and monitored all functions and temp settings. The upper half is all fridge and temp can be set from +34 F to +44 F and its amazing. Also very, very spacious inside. The bottom left is only a freezer and works perfectly. Temp can be digitally and precisely set between plus 5 F to minus -8 F. The bottom right has 4 settings: Freezer (aligns itself with the adjacent Freezer temp settings of +5F to - 8F), Soft freeze (+23F), Chill (+30 deg F), Cool (+41 deg F). This is so awesome. It offers immense flexibility to customize this bottom right corner in so many ways. For perspective: 32 degrees F = 0 degrees Celsius which is the temp at which water turns to ice. With this fridge we have precise control of each compartment. And what a difference does this make to the food we store and marinate prior to cooking.
Then it has the "Power freeze" function that allows rapid cooling down. And has the E function where you can monitor and control several fridge functions remotely via your smart phone (with a downloaded app). And marinating stainless trays; and cleverly designed pull out shelves, trays, bins and what have you. My old GE sounded like a Peterbilt diesel truck every time it cycled on and off. It was LOUD. You can NOT hear this fridge. It is whisper quiet. And again: it is CAVERNOUS and CAPACIOUS. And subtle and modest on the front/outside. Neatly tucked in handles. And the starlight temp display is very cool too. I did buy the extended warranty and with so much high technology and electronics and sensors inside its sheer good sense to get the extended warranty lest some thing goes awry after the first year which is fully covered by Samsung.

review_text: I bought this at Lowes actually lol,  because they had one in stock at my local store and were able to deliver the next day.  Long story short, a rat got into my house,  i was able to trap it in one of the kitchen cupboards.  i created a path out the back door and opened the cupboard, but what does it do,  it runs under my oven.  So to scare it out, i turn on the oven, and what happens next???  You'd think a rat would come running out and scamper out the door.  Nope, i smell burnt rat hair or flesh,  so i turned off the oven and i think the rat died in the hot air vent that leads up from the broiler to the oven.  So gross, so not wanting anything to do with my old oven i bought this one haha.  So far this oven has been great.  I love the large metal knobs, they ignite easily and are at the high setting at first, and you turn the knob left to go down the lowest setting which is a very small flame.  So don't forget to turn off the burner, sometimes i think it's off but it's on it's lowest setting.  But i do like the range of settings for each burner which should give you good control of your cooking heat.  There are 5 burners, a large oval burner in the middle for stock pots, or an included griddle.  This range doesn't come with a wok attachment, but there is a whirlpool one available here at amazon for 32 bucks i think it was, and fits.  I just ordered it, so looking forward to doing some stir fry soon as well.  The electronic oven panel is easy to use,  it's pretty intuitive once you try it.  It has 3 avail self settings so you can program things you cook the most, which is convenient.  It has 4 presets like pizza, bread proofing, slow cook, and dehydrate.  It has a bake/broil button, and a convection bake and broil buttons as well.  I tried the convection oven to bake some bread and it worked well, evenly browned, i cooked at 25 degress lower then normal on the convection setting and it came out well.  It has a timer setting,  clock,  or you just set the bake time, temp,  and you can set a pre time, to bake at a later time, in which it turns on the oven at that time, bakes your food and turns off.  The oven works great in my opinion, and some have stated the edges and sides get hot after an hour of baking.  Not even, all my oven handles,  burner knobs were still safe to touch, but the oven vent is centered right under the control panel display, so if touch the metal under the display, it's burning hot.  The panel itself stayed relatively cool, and i was still able to touch it without being burnt.  I also like the large oven, for when i cook my thanksgiving turkeys, can't wait to try the convection setting on it this year.  Oh and the oven has a burner at the top to do broiling in the oven, the bottom drawer is just  storage.  The  range burners are set deep, like down an inch or more, so if you spill it gets trapped and the black surface was somewhat easy to clean so far.  The panel is a fingerprint magnet, so is the stainless brushed areas, seems to like finger smudges, but overall the oven looks nice,  the sides are black, the top of the range is black, the whole front, doors, and display panel are brushed steel look, so it's attractive.  I think the only thing i didn't like is, the autolocking oven door.  I have to read up and see if i can disable it since i don't have kids in the house.  After baking some bread,  the door was locked until it cooled down to a safe level.  Well, i wanted to take out my bread at that moment, not when the ovens save to open lol.  So not sure if there is a bypass for the lock, but that's the only thing i didn't like.

It has a center griddle for pancakes, eggs, sausage, hamburgers, etc.  and the oven is digital controlled. It works. Check back with me in 20 years and see if my opinion changes. product_title: Samsung NX58H5600SS 30 In. Freestanding Gas Range with Custom Griddle and 5.8 Cu. Ft. Convection Oven, Stainless Steel
review_text:
A very good stove for the money, though it is not true convection, it is fan convection, which means the convection fan does not have an electric heating element. All gas convection stoves only have the fan going when the flames are off, true convection has the fan on more and the flames on less (after pre-heating) because of the electric supplemental heater. So true convection is a little better at browning meat and cooks a little more evenly (than fan convection), but most stoves with that cost about $500 more. Not worth it! (to me). Any convection is way better than any non-convection for even cooking and browning roasts. It works great.
This is free standing. Slide-ins are nice because you get a little more stove top area than a free standing. Again, about $500 more, not worth it! (to me).
The best stove I have ever had, a major upgrade for me. If you are a very serous cook and want it all, and money is not an option, get a slide-in (if you have counters on both sides) with true convection like NX58H9950WS, but be prepared to part with about $1000 more.
Does anyone know what the actual difference is between the bake and roast settings? I watched my cooking for bake and roast, both ran the lower burner with the fan going between firings. I could see no obvious difference, I thought the roast setting might turn on the top burner for some cycles but it never came on. I could find no real explanation of what the oven is supposed to do that is different.
The griddle is great. I thick slab of aluminum so it heats perfectly evenly when paired with the oval burner. For those that think the griddle is too thin, remember that aluminum has 3 times the thermal conductivity of cast iron. The griddle burner does not get it very hot because the oval burner has a moderate flame, making bacon took a bit longer that when I made it in a frying pan. However, the bacon comes out better because it is more evenly cooked. A great design, keeping the heat moderate will make the teflon last long time. Too much heat and metal spatulas are what kill teflon. I like the Teflon coating so it is easy to clean. Fits in the dishwasher.
