review_title: Great unit with convenient features for small apartments or condos
review_text:
We live in a small condo built in the 1960s with old plumbing and very expensive coin laundry. To fight the good fight against the man, we installed this Washer/Dryer unit in our bathroom and could not be happier with the unit!

When I was researching this unit, here are the things that I was wondering about that I hope will save you some time:

- The washer/dryer plugs into a standard 3 prong U.S. outlet. The same outlet that charges your iPhone will power your washer/dryer.

- It doesn't need to vent to the outside! Every other week, you drain out water and anything else that your washer/dryer has collected to keep the loads fresh and not stinky. It takes about 3 minutes.

- You can put in a load of laundry, have it wash, then dry on its own without having to push buttons or move anything between cycles. It works with 80% of cycles with few exceptions (bedding mode being one of them).

- Washing is normal speed, drying takes forever. While washing might take an hour, it could take 4-5 hours for the load to dry. It's not uncommon to have a wash/dry load take 5.5 - 6 hours. For me, I don't really care because I put in laundry before I go to work or before I go to sleep and open the unit up to find a done load. You can easily do one load a day and not worry about moving it.

- As noted above, drying takes forever. If you care about speed, look elsewhere. If you care about convenience and don't want to move loads while you're out and/or sleeping, this is perfect.

- It washes clothes really well. It cleans as well as high end front loading LG washers that I had at my previous place.

- Uses high efficiency detergent and is also extremely energy efficient.

- It is not loud at all. It sounds very similar to a dishwasher.

- While I can't make any guarantees for your set up, we have a 1.5" drain pipe instead of the standard 2" because of our old building. Our washer/dryer has absolutely no problems draining in the smaller pipe because of how efficiently the unit uses and drains water - not even close to overflowing the drain. Our contractors did some creative piping, but probably didn't have to because the unit doesn't ever do a waterfall-like drain where it empties the whole tub in a spin cycle. The water always comes out at a reasonable pace.

- Get vibration foot pads for the unit. It will keep things running even quieter and make sure that your washer/dryer doesn't dance while you're at work. If you live in a condo or apartment and live above someone, definitely invest in the vibration pads.

If you live in a small apartment or condo, this is a fantastic unit that holds a lot and does a lot. If you really need your laundry done fast, this isn't the unit for you. If you sleep and/or work and don't foresee doing more than one load of laundry per day, the convenience of being able to do a complete load of laundry without switching anything couldn't be better. We love this unit!

Tips:
- To avoid wrinkles and not fully dried loads, only fill the tub 1/2 to 2/3 full with laundry. You'll be tempted to fill it to the top, but don't do that.
- Use liquid fabric softener or little scent boosters. Since you don't have the opportunity to put in a dryer sheet, this will keep your clothes smelling fresh through the dry cycle.
- Clean your unit as directed!

I've now owned this for 2.5 years and I regret purchasing it.  I've had the following problems: (1) I have to snake the drain about once a year.  The machine has a "lint trap" but it really doesn't work.  All the loose fiber washed out of your clothes, and there is a lot of it, goes down the drain (or gets stuck around the door opening - but 99% of it goes down the drain); (2) the rubber pad that you press to open the door split and ripped off.  You are only able to put your finger tips in the door.  Yet the pressure of my finger tips alone ripped off the door pad.  This happened within the first month of owning it.; (3) I recently had to call out a handyman to replace the pump.  That was a $340 expense;  (4) I now have to call out the handyman again because I'm getting a dE error  - the little research I did indicates that the door sensor is no longer working;  (5) The sensor for drying the clothes does not work.  NORMAL =  wet clothes coming out of a traditional washing machine.  I have to set the dry time for each load at 120 minutes (2 hours) and that doesn't dry my clothes.  I have to manually come back and set it again for another 120 minutes.  That's a 4 hour wash and dry time - don't be in a hurry for your clothes; (6) the machine drying at high speed makes a lot of noise - shaking.  In this old building with thin floors I'm worried that it's bothers my downstairs neighbor so I only run the machine during business hours while they are at work. Washing: Does a great job of cleaning our clothes, does just as well as a typical washer.

Drying: If you keep in mind that it is smaller than a normal washer and size your loads accordingly, you will have no problems. If you try to fill it to the brim, it probably will leave your clothes damp. The one major flaw to this is it leaves you clothes WRINKLED. Load Size: I would estimate that it can handle 2/3 what a normal washer can.

Cycle time: It takes a little longer than a normal washer to wash the closes; it take 3-4 hours to dry them. This is not a big deal for me since I just run it overnight and wake up to clean clothes.

Noise: Moderate noise, the spin is particularly loud. However, it is no louder than a normal washer, and in general is about the same noise level as my dish washer.

I expected to find an adapter kit so you could plumb it to your sink, but I couldn't find one. I ended up getting some tee connections to split off the for the hot and cold connections under my kitchen sink and ran some long dishwasher hoses to it, picked up some adapters from the local hardware store that converted the dishwasher hose to the washer hose. For the drain, I bought an extension hose and a double air gap and ran it to my sink. I have been using this set up for more than 6 months with no problems. Definitely recommend this for small places.

product_title: LG WM3477HW - 2.3 Cu. Ft. White Electric Washer/Dryer Combo
review_title: Buy From Somewhere With An Excellent Return Policy
review_text:
We read the good and bad reviews, and bought with caution from a local dealer with a 30 day return policy, including delivery and pickup.

On the pro side, you never have to load clothes separately into a dryer and it's compact, with room to install shelves over it since there's no stacking required. We found the drying function to be totally fine, even with heavy loads including jeans! It does take a long time to dry, but we had done our research and expected this. The ventless drying didn't heat up our bathroom, by the way.

BUT, despite having our unit carefully installed, and having the installation crew come out a second time to make sure the machine was absolutely level, the machine is virtually unusable. We installed the anti-vibration pads LG recommends. We did not leave the shipping bolts on the back! Yet it vibrates unbelievably, and makes an incredibly loud knocking sound. If we press and hold the door while the machine is in its spin cycle (which is short) the loud banging abates, but this means that we have to be home, awake, and willing to dash in to support it in order to do laundry. I believe the problem is with the door, and specifically the lower section of the door (LG, are you listening??). But it's beyond what we or our condo neighbors can tolerate. I also think that level of vibration would ultimately lead to other repair problems as well.

In general, this is a higher maintenance unit than some may be used to. You really do have to wipe the lint out of it after every cycle, and follow the instructions about running a cleaning cycle and the like. Still, that's a lot easier than going to the laundromat!

If space is really tight, or if you can't get the electrical work done to put in a 240 volt line, I think this machine is worth a try. Their manufacturing process must simply be uneven. Some of these units must be fine if there are so many positive reviews. But purchase it from somewhere that has an excellent return policy.

Other brands of ventless, 110 volt combo washer/dryers to consider--with a slightly smaller capacity--are Haier or Edgestar. In the end, I didn't really want to deal with wiping lint out of a combo unit. I'm also not sure that the technology is 100% there for these yet in terms of long-term reliability. We do have the vertical space, so we returned the LG and bought vertically stacked, ventless, separate compact units from Bosch. Alas, this meant I also had to have an electrician come in to do the 240 volt wiring. The two Bosch units together cost us about $650 more than the LG combo machine. If we had more money, we would have purchased the Miele models (which are less deep and would have fit more nicely in our bathroom) but saving an extra two inches for $1,000 over the already high cost of the Bosch was beyond what I could justify.

Good luck to all of you other small space dwellers out there. I hope you find a solution that works well for you.

product_title: GE PT9800SHSS Combination Wall Oven
review_text:
We have now been using this unit for over three years. I did not learn there are different power versions of Advantium until I got this in and working and did not seem to work as well as my sisters Advantium. She has a standalone Advantium not part of a combination. Those standalone are more powerful and cook faster. Thus, have not seen much difference in this Adavtium and using convection in main oven. It does requiring swapping out the turntable and realize the metal turntables are not cheap if you have to replace—over $100. A special coating on the metal. They are nice to use to minimize having to preheat or heating up kitchen during the summer. We have found we don’t use the feature much. There are a number of preprogrammed food settings for speed cook but you may need to experiment or look up online for other types of food not programmed in to create a custom setting. Really just wish advantium oven smart enough to just figure it out with some AI and sensors. We use as a microwave the most.

As a microwave it is the equivalent of 800watts so not as powerful as 1000+ ones out there. Just need to add more time for cooking. Wish it had more power. Also, just like our prior model, the glass turntable chips easily on edge so be careful swapping with metal pan. If I had to do over I would rather have more powerful microwave and drop the Adantium feature. Would rather get a turbochef that has a better speed cook function and used in commercial kitchens but they make a pricey home version. Another annoying feature is when the oven or microwave is done you have to push the clear button. It should clear once you open the door automatically. The done or timer chime is soft but you hear just fine while in a large kitchen 30 feet away. But you will not hear it well if in another room or watching TV. Newer models are now coming with apps to let you know.

While on and after cook it has a fan that helps cool the electronics so it makes about 40 DBs of noise while running and cool down. Not a big deal. I do like that the microwave door folds down to take out food to evaluate its doneness. Microwave is not very tall but so far no issues cooking anything. We use the 30 second feature and then roll the knob to add time or press the add 30 second time what we need timer to goto. Defrost works as expected.

No service issues in our 3.5+ years. When power goes out have to reset clock which is quick and easy but wish had battery backup.

The convection oven works great and we use it all the time. Steam function did not seem to clean well so just put on max self clean and that did it. Since self clean is high heat it is not recommended to do this but a couple times a year since it will shorten the oven life span. Note when in self clean you can not use the microwave. Roast works fine. Have not used proof function. Like the keep warm function for keeping holiday meals warm until ready to serve.

The oven glass on the inside is a challenge to get clean with windex—just seems to have a amber stain all the time but not noticeable on outside. Only on shelf has a ball bearing glide and had to lubricate with graphite once so far. Wish at least one other rack had glide. It came with three but we only use two—one lower and one high for broiling. Broiler is ok for electric oven and on high gets hot so have to watch what you are cooking closely.

Overall, there are many programs and a probe for cooking that make it a great oven, but just needs a more powerful Advantium, and microwave to be a five star choice for the price we paid $2898 plus delivery and install was $160.

review_text:
I originally wrote this review for GE's website, yet they rejected it for being too critical. Hopefully posting it here will still be useful for potential purchases.

The previous model of this fridge, PFE29PSDSS, has twice as many sensors for the autofill function. This model's autofill worked so unreliably, and not at all in many cases, that I returned it for the older model. Additionally, the older model has five settings for the large pull-out tray with an LED temperature display while this model only has three settings and no LED display. Comparing the energy efficiency between the two, the older one is also more efficient. To support the extra ice maker, the water filter was moved from being hidden in the door in the older version to being inside the fridge compartment, thus slightly reducing interior space. The only advantages I see to this newer model are the extra ice maker, removable liners on the door trays, and the lighting in the large pull-out tray changes color when you change the temperature setting.

I also had a problem with the compressor making way too much noise and had multiple service appointments before I was able to return it. If you weren't aware of the advantages of the previous model, and you don't have a manufacturer's defect like I did with the compressor, then overall this is actually a very good fridge. It maintains the temperature well and keeps food fresh longer. The bright lights make it easy to see all the contents and there is a lot of interior space and flexible compartments.

review_title: How amazing is it to buy a refrigerator online?
review_text:
How amazing is it to buy a refrigerator online, btw?

We've had it a year, and it's been problem-free. It's really good refrigerator overall. Things I don't like are how anal it is about the water filter (it basically prevented me from doing anything until I changed it...so I just put the bypass "filter" back on to shut it up and decided I'm never gonna buy filters for it...plus, I already have an inline filter for the water line); also not a big fan of the ice maker...it's small (as one might expect when mouted to a door), but it's also pretty slow to make ice. Also somewhat expected since the icemaker isn't in the freezer, but still...

Like any refrigerator, there's always something that doesn't fit somewhere, and this is pretty good about making room. It does have one shelf that can be "halved"...half of the glass shelf slides underneath the rear half to allow taller items.

Well lit, bright LEDs. Not sure I need the lower tray to go between red, blue, and green to indicate food temps that vary by a few degrees, but the kids like seeing the colors change when the press the button.

I was hoping the lower chest freezer door was a little tougher to open, as my toddlers figured out pretty quickly how to throw their weight and get it open. There are obvious safety concerns about this in general, so just be mindful when considering a bottom freezer in general. (There are universal kid-safety kits for latching it closed, btw.)

----------------------
...fast forward to 3/9/17....2-year-ish update:

All systems still functioning. The brushed finish has held up remarkably well to my monkey-grip kids, who have literally climbed the lower freezer door to access fridge items. All LEDs are still nice and bright.

Other things observed:

1. It gets exceptionally cold on the top shelf of the fridge near the "TwinChill" ports, despite the temperature setting being set at the recommended 37° or 1-2° higher. As such, some items in that area have been partially frozen if left there too long.

2. If the humidity inside rises, it prevents the ice cubes from falling further into the bin so that they can be dispensed. They basically stick together a little, and the bin is pretty narrow, so it's rather easy for the ice to stay towards the top of the bin, while dispensed ice creates a void underneath. Nothing is broken in that regard, but it just prevents new ice from being made...and considering it's a small bin as-is, it's always nice to have as much ice available as possible (I use ice often).

3. The Precise Fill mode is a bit picky and will stop filling automatically (as a precaution) if it thinks the container it's filling is too full. My thought is this: There's already an Auto Fill mode...the behavior I just described seems fitting for that mode. In Precise Mode, I'm telling it precisely how much water I want, which should imply that I know how much water the container can hold. For example, I have a 2qt pitcher for making 2qts worth of a beverage...the pitcher, of course, holds just a little more than 2qts. Sometimes the fridge stops at 1qt, and sometimes at 1.75qt, because it's sensing the water level and stops filling. If it's not going to put the precise amount I ask for, the button may as well say Almost Precise Fill. Alas, I can live with holding the button to continue filling.

4. Noise isn't too bad. Every now and then, there's a "what was that noise?" moment, but it's nothing compared to the ghosts that keep opening and closing my closet doors.

All things considered, still a good fridge.

review_text: My wife and I purchased this refrigerator and several other GE Profile appliances as part of our kitchen remodel in November 2015. I would strongly encourage others to avoid this refrigerator.

product_title: GE PYE22PSHSS Profile 22.1 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel Counter Depth French Door Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_title: Poor service and lack of integrity by GE threatens medically-fragile daughter's health
review_text:
Our GE Profile french-door, counter-depth, stainless steel, and much-loved refrigerator, purchased from Home Depot in September, 2015, suddenly began to freeze everything just 10-11 months later. It has been a nightmare trying to get GE to stand behind their product. An even worse "replacement unit" is sitting in our home right now because of the run around from GE's customer service department. This is the letter sent to them tonight...

Good evening, GE,

You have written of a refrigerator with a Keurig, indicating that you believe this is my overriding concern. You are correct that my first complaint with this replacement unit was that it is not the one I believe I asked for verbally, but you have missed what has occurred since then. That concern has long since been superseded by the fact that this replacement unit sent by GE is freezing everything solid since 24 hrs after installation, and I am having to throw things away every time I open the door. Secondarily, each day, it seems, one of us notices another flaw not noticed at first.

However, these are now just side issues. It seems I need to be extremely clear and straightforward: This "replacement" unit began freezing everything in the refrigerator section within 24 hours of being installed.

If my only complaints were that I requested and expected the model with the Keurig; or that there are a number of scratches on the front of the fridge (some of them deep enough to feel when running fingers lightly over the door) when our own unit which we'd had for one year looked new, by comparison; or that the door to the freezer does not glide as it did on my own unit, but sticks and makes the door difficult to open, requiring we wrestle with it each and every time we want something from the freezer...these would all raise serious concerns about GE's choice in a replacement unit, as this fridge isn't worth anything near what mine was worth.

But, those are all secondary concerns. The overriding issue at hand is that the fridge does exactly what my own, superior quality fridge was doing...it is freezing everything from produce, to dairy, to thousands of dollars worth of my daughter's medications which contain live enzymes and require stable refrigeration. Worse, the replacement unit GE sent us has been freezing from the time it was installed in our home. Within 24 hrs, items were found frozen in the refrigerator section. My own fridge didn't began freezing anything until after nearly a year of use.

I no longer care one whit about a Keurig, although I do care that this fridge is not what I asked for (cannot trust GE), is not new (GE has no integrity and cannot be trusted), AND is freezing items (a health hazard for my daughter). The replacement unit sent by GE, promised to be "of comparable quality," is clearly defective and I have no idea why GE felt it could be dumped on us as a replacement, but it must be removed and I must purchase a new refrigerator. My medically fragile daughter's health is at stake. Her pharmacist is doing some research to determine whether the thousands of dollars worth of medications in this defective fridge must be thrown in the trash or if they're safe to use. Of greatest concern is the respiratory medication which comes in vials for use with the nebulizer, and which has live enzymes. However, I will ask the pharmacist tomorrow about the many other medications she has which are also stored in the refrigerator. Her medications are paid for by insurance, are strictly accounted for due to insurance rules and regulations, and are so costly that I cannot afford to replace them. I will not risk her life on allowing GE more time to play around with her health. You have removed our quality refrigerator which had no flaws other than the freezing, and replaced it with a damaged floor model, a second, a refurbished unit. I don't know the history behind this "replacement" unit which I was promised would be of comparable value, but it most definitely is not comparable value. If GE did, indeed, have our refrigerator crushed, as Pardini Appliance claims, then your company is extremely foolish. Ours was a beautiful unit with ONLY the one flaw that it froze things. GE did not send a repairman to our homefor that fridge, saying it was impossible to find an available repairman. Instead GE replaced our beautiful refrigerator with this ugly, damaged monstrosity which ALSO happens to freeze everything, and now GE wants to repair this damaged unit, which was damaged long before it arrived here.

I don't know what is wrong with GE that there is no integrity, no compassion, no willingness to stand behind GE appliances. All I know, all I care about, is that GE has seriously compromised my daughter's health and risked her life by creating this huge mess. My daughter is sick now as I write, has been for a little over a week, has visited the E.R. just a few days ago, and has an appointment with her pulmonologist (3 hrs away from our home) in a few days. I have no time nor energy to "fight" with you over this refrigerator. The fact that nobody at GE cares even remotely about my daughter's health or her life is appalling. Whatever it takes, I need this defective refrigerator out of here ASAP so that I can put a working refrigerator in our house. I will never buy GE again.

You have written, "We understand your frustration in dealing with this matter." Unless you have a 23 year old daughter with global developmental delay due to a young, homeless birth mother trying to abort in late pregnancy by running into walls and throwing herself belly first on the floor, a beautiful baby girl who you brought back to life several times in infancy with mouth-to-mouth resuscitation when she stopped breathing, a child who has direct and silent aspiration (smiles at you as liquid runs into her lungs instead of her stomach), a beautiful daughter who was injured through no fault of her own and who has lived with respiratory failure and frequent pneumonia from infancy, a child who also lives with bronchiectasis, choreoathetoid cerebral palsy, chronic gastrointestinal problems, obstructive sleep apnea, asthma, corrected atrial septal defect (open heart surgery and several weeks on life support in the ICU, all before her 1st birthday), unless you know what it is like to watch your beautiful, non-verbal child struggle to communicate, trapped in a body that won't work, a sweet child who's brain was damaged by a hurting, frightened, birth mother who was also a mere child...unless you are the parent of someone like my sweet daughter, a beautiful young woman who came to our family at 3 months diagnosed "failure to thrive," fed by me for months every 1-2 hrs around the clock with an eye dropper, unless you have lived through long hospitalizations trying to sleep at your child's bedside 24 hrs/day in uncomfortable vinyl chairs and the occasional cot with nurses and physicians traipsing in and out at all hours...unless you have learned to give your child the life-saving medical treatments necessary to keep her alive and then spent years educating your local physicians in their offices and at the E.R. because no one in your area has ever heard of most of your child's medications, medical equipment, or complicated daily treatment regimen...unless you are also the mother of a precious child like my own who blesses the world with her sweet, tender spirit, her gentle touch on the arm of a stranger, her eyes that speak volumes of love and draw in people everywhere she goes, a child who inspires total strangers to approach you, the parent, to say how she has just blessed that person with her loving smile and her gentle touch...unless you are a parent to a daughter like mine, you have no idea. This is not frustration. I have fought to keep my daughter alive for 23 years and have succeeded. I have called Medicaid directly when needed medications were not approved, and I have obtained that approval. I get up in the middle of the night to adjust her respiratory support, to give extra treatments. When she is sick, I give 4-6 hrs of respiratory treatments daily that involve 5 respiratory medications, percussion, in-exsufflator, nebulizer, and suction...treatments she cannot get in the local ICU unless I take her equipment and medications with me. At night she sleeps with respiratory support, oxygen when needed, and is monitored all night, every night, with an oximeter which has a loud alarm to wake me when her O2 drops dangerously low. When she is well, I give 2 treatments a day, which still take 1 hour each. We are blessed that the local doctor in charge of our E.R. has immense respect for my knowledge of her needs and tells me he will follow my lead in a medical crisis. We were just there on Monday, as she is showing symptoms of an infection we have never seen before in her 23 years of life. If this infection has anything to do with the constant problems maintaining proper temperature in the fridge...if this progresses to a life-threatening stage...you can bet I will not be silent about GE's part in making her sick. What on earth is wrong with your company? Do not tell the mother of a child like my beautiful daughter that you "understand" her "frustration" unless you want a mother's rant.

You want photos of the scratches and other damage on the fridge. Sheesh. Two of my other kids have taken on this challenge. I have no time for that. Hear me now...this replacement unit is defective, a second. It began freezing everything immediately. My daughter's health is deteriorating. I am an extremely busy working mother...why on earth do you presume you can call my house and reach me without an appointment? Do you think I have nothing better to do than sit by the phone watching for a phone call from GE? We walked in the door this evening, exhausted after a long and busy day, only to discover that you tried to call me at home today...despite the fact that I specifically wrote this morning and said I would not be near the phone. I am as honest as the day is long and place great value in personal integrity. It's a shame that GE does not also place similar value on it's own integrity.

I need this fridge out of the house. I need the money refunded. I don't want another replacement unit from GE. GE has had weeks to get a working fridge into our house and totally bungled it. My daughter's fragile health has no more time for GE's games. I am a single, working mom whose work day never ends. I have no idea how I will accomplish this, but this refrigerator must be out of this house ASAP to make room because I MUST purchase another refrigerator. The only thing I know for sure is that it will NOT be a GE. I will be going to Home Depot, where I made the original purchase. They have met my daughter. They are compassionate people and care. You have written as if having a Keurig was still the issue. Believe me, I have lived without a Keurig just fine and can easily continue to do so. Please see above and re-read this entire email if you or other GE representatives are still unable to understand my concerns. This problem with the refrigerator in our home freezing everything has been going on for a month because GE replaced our beautiful fridge which froze things with an ugly, second-hand fridge which freezes things. If there is even ONE person in GE who actually cares, my daughter needs that ONE person to contact us and make this right.

This refrigerator needs to be removed immediately and a check needs to be issued for the original purchase price of the unit we chose as a family with such high hopes last September, 2015. I realize GE is trying to drag this out until the 1 yr coverage expires on September 24, 2016, but my daughter's health doesn't have that kind of time for game-playing and delays.

Please. My daughter needs one person who cares. I will not consider repairs to this defective unit nor will I consider another replacement unit. A defective monstrosity, otherwise known as a "replacement refrigerator of comparable quality", sits in our kitchen taking up space and continues to force us to throw out costly food items that have frozen every time we open the door for another meal, another respiratory treatment, or for my daughter's needed thickened water. It seems I now must determine how to pay to have this monstrosity hauled out of here and how to find the funds to purchase a new unit and pay to have it installed, as GE refuses to do so.

In the meantime, I'll try to find time to compile and attach photos and send via email on the cellphone...just as soon as I can find a spare moment. It's nearly 10 pm. My daughter mentioned above is finally in bed on respiratory support after her last treatment regimen for the day. There are dishes to wash and two jr high siblings who need my assistance with homework. Tomorrow will start way too early for my tired body and brain, just like the majority of my days. I do it all for love and I love what I do. There is no more time in our world for all this game-playing by GE. My daughter needs and deserves to have a working, reliable refrigerator. I paid somewhere around $2,700 to be sure she had what she needs and deserves for her expensive medications. Now, just when I need to spend $1000 on winter tires for our vehicle that gets us in and out of our slick, steep, and icy driveway and safely to and from our many responsibilities, such as school, physicians, and specialists in the city, it seems I'm out that $2,700 for my still new refrigerator and must begin to figure out how to pay money I don't have and cannot afford to spend for another unit, because I will not accept another replacement unit shipped blind from GE. My daughter has no more time for your games. I will not allow GE to continue to take risks with her life this way. I have no idea HOW I will meet her needs without GE backing us up, I just know that my daughter needs this and I WILL find a way.

A mother who cares

product_title: GE PT7800SHSS Microwave Wall Oven
review_text: The oven/microwave look and perform exactly as expected. So far, no complaints whatsoever.

product_title: GE PT7800SHSS Microwave Wall Oven
review_text: Broke after minimal use. Repair guy has been out twice now and still no working oven. Not sure how long you are supposed to go without a working appliance.

product_title: GE PT7800SHSS Microwave Wall Oven
review_text: We've had this for a while now and really like it. It is stylish, everything works great and a good buy from Amazon. The microwave/convection oven is the best and huge inside with polished stainless steel that looks great. The cooling fans are very quiet and we don't even notice them being on after cooking. The beepers are low toned and not invasive. The main oven has a great easy slide rack that is effortless to pull on. Lights in both ovens. We weren't sure about the control panel but love it after using it for awhile; easy learning curve with simple controls. Shipping took about two and a half weeks but we new that. Very modern looking and a breeze to install.

product_title: GE PT7800SHSS Microwave Wall Oven
review_text:
First off I am far from an expert on ovens. We rarely bake anything and I use a smoker for most all our meats. We have only got to use this for a couple of weeks so far but I am very happy with it. First off it just looks really good. The fans are much quieter than the oven it replaced. I have used the convection microwave and really like it so far. Only thing I have baked in the oven is a take and bake pizza but so far so good. I know some people complain about the controls but they are really easy once you get the hang of them. I love the sliding rack and the fact that you don't have to remove the grates when you clean the oven. The inside of the microwave is huge and with the convection feature you can use it for some baking during the holidays. This replaced another GE oven that gave us many years of trouble free use and only got replaced to update the kitchen.
I installed the oven myself and it was really easy if you have a few handyman skills and are comfortable hooking up the electrical connection. It is too heavy to lift into place with one person but with me on one side, my wife and her friend on the other it popped right in .

product_title: GE PT7800SHSS Microwave Wall Oven
review_title: Good product except for door opening on microwave
review_text: Great oven and microwave. Took a second to get used to all the buttons and knobs, but not much longer. I love that it has setting for softening butter, and other features my old one didnt have. I like that the timer bell is not annoying loud, but at first wondered what that teeny beep was when I forgot I had put something in there! If there is a lot of noise I can see how you might not hear it.  But the reason I can't give it 5 stars is the oven door pull down instead of side opening.  I cannot reach the back of the microwave to clean that beautiful stainless steel without getting a step stool. Now I am short and therefore also have short arms... but really??? sometimes I think they forget who will be using these products in the home.. and we are not all 5'6 and up!  But otherwise, I like it after a couple months of use. I just am careful to not cause a mess in the microwave!

product_title: GE PT7800SHSS Microwave Wall Oven
review_text: Fantastic drop in replacement for the outdated unit I had The controls are super easy and superior to the up/down push buttons we were used to. Very quiet and simple operation.

product_title: GE PT7800SHSS Microwave Wall Oven
review_text: Owned it for a month now and really am impressed with added features this dual oven/microwave offers. So far no issues.

product_title: GE PT7800SHSS Microwave Wall Oven
review_text:
Great looking oven. The controls are clean and minimalist. There are no numbers, you change temp, time etc. with the dial. It takes a little getting used to.

We've never had a convection oven before, but it seems to put a substantial amount a heat into the kitchen when in convection mode. The smaller top oven preheats quickly.

product_title: GE PT7800SHSS Microwave Wall Oven
review_title: It works, it's quiet, and it's easy to use.
review_text:
I replaced a 2 year old KitchenAid wall oven that came with our new home with this model. Both are convection oven / convection microwave built-in models. What drove me to change it to this GE model was the constant cooling fan noise that blasted out once the cabinet got warm. Additionally, the convection fan worked poorly as all the food near the back of the oven near the fan was overcooked. We only used it in bake mode. I have had this one for three weeks and cooked all the Holiday meals in it. The convection works as it is supposed to work on multi rack baking. Even more wonderful is the fact that the oven is almost silent on all modes. I could not be happier and am heartbroken the builder model was not of this quality.

The only negative was that they guaranteed in their description it would fit into the old model's cutout. It didn't. The new oven was 3/4 of an inch taller. Took me a little effort to open up the cutout but once that was done, it slipped into the cutout and several screws later was ready to go. The installation was screwdriver easy assuming you can connect the pigtails on the wiring to your electrical service.

The knob is a joy to use as we were forever turning off the older oven every time we went to use the timer or microwave while cooking and the controls are much easier to use.

product_title: GE PT7800SHSS Microwave Wall Oven
review_title: A great deal on a great product
review_text:
This double oven is one if our best kitchen buys of all time. My wall oven broke a couple of weeks before Thanksgiving and we couldn't find a decent wall oven in any store. So we found this great deal on a highly rated & reviewed oven on Amazon and the No extra cost shipping was great with a call from the crew when they were getting close. Easy install - it fit into the existing space we had for our single oven This double oven has been in use ever since.
It's so nice to have a large and small oven as well as a microwave.

product_title: GE PT7800SHSS Microwave Wall Oven
review_text: This is a fantastic oven.  It is worth the price premium to have both an oven and microwave in the same unit.  It saves space and handles all our needs.  It feels like it's of very high quality, and I really like the controls.  I'm a believer!

review_text: GE ovens are designed with a fatal-flaw. The broiler flame cycles on and off. product_title: GE PT7800SHSS Microwave Wall Oven

review_title: CAUTION: Burn hazard in microwave & GE refuses to warranty stains on the interior of the microwave
review_text:
Update (see original post below); In trying to clean the inside of the microwave my arm rubbed against the area covering the internal light. The burn shown above was the result. I saw no warning in the users' manual.

Original post:
I have been using the microwave in my oven for about 2 months. I have only cooked conventional foods. Nothing exotic and certainly nothing other than food.

After some stains appeared on the walls of the microwave I contacted GE service who suggested I buy a product called CeramaBryte Stainless Steel Cleaner to remedy the stains. The product did not do the job.

I called GE again and was told they only had a 7-day warranty on what they call "cosmetic flaws". They could not point out any such exclusion in my warranty. They suggested that maybe something I had cooked had splattered and caused the stains. Yet there was no warning in the manual about splatters damaging the microwave.

I believe the material used for the microwave interior was defective. Why else would stainless steel stain?

While the unit functions normally I am concerned that someone looking to buy my home could be put off by these stains perhaps thinking that we did not properly clean our home.

The best GE could offer was a roughly 50% discount on a new unit. I believe they should replace it at no cost to me since there is an issue with the materials they used.

product_title: GE PSB48YSHSS Profile 28.6 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel Counter Depth Built-In Side-By-Side Refrigerator
review_text:
We bought a GE/ Hotpoint Refrigerator, model number PSB48YSHSS, serial number TF595038. The refrigerator did not work from day one. The temperature of the freezer varies wildly from 22 degrees to 54 degrees despite being set to 0 degrees as instructed. The refrigerator also varies in temperature wildly. We lost 100% of our freezer food and refrigerator items.

We called for service and it took a week for a technician to report. When he reported he claimed the appliance needed parts. They scheduled the repair for a week and a half later. 10 days later they arrived without the parts. Upon research, GE sent parts in the mail and the parts arrived AFTER the technicians (2). They could not schedule the fix for another 8 days. When they arrived 8 days later, they opened the box and the part was missing! They scheduled 5 days later. When the technician arrived he could not fix the appliance.

I couldn't be more disappointed with GE. The technicians were great but totally useless since GE didn't send the parts half the time. Turns out that the appliance isn't even a GE, it's a Samsung - so they can't run normal diagnostic tests.

Spend your money elsewhere, the product is a lemon and the service is dismal.

review_title: Quietly just does its job...I guess that's one of the best compliments you can give one of these things.
review_text:
I owe this beverage center a review after several months of issue-free operation. I was hesitant to do so too quickly after another brand/model failed miserably on us after only a few months.

As mentioned, we have had no issues with this unit at all. It is impressively quiet (especially compared to the other equally expensive unit it replaced) and gets the job done. I guess that's one of the best compliments you can give one of these things. You don't really notice it until you need it.

We removed the top half-shelf, which makes it much more functional for our needs (including beer bottles and other items that height).

A minor nit is that I wish there was an option to simply leave the LED light on at all times. Instead, the maximum is a few hours. Energy efficiency thrust upon you, I guess, but LEDs are not exactly power hogs.

I will update the review if and when we ever have problems, but here's to my not having to ever do so!

[[UPDATE (September 1, 2016]]
As promised, I am reporting back with an update as to an issue that has later arisen. Overall, the unit is still performing very well and quietly. One odd issue that has popped up though, is that the unit sometimes gives off an open door alarm when the door is quite clearly closed and sealed. So, it is a sensor (not operational) issue. A repair company came out (entirely free via warranty) and said it is just a metal piece along the bottom that becomes unaligned (he made it sound like this was not the first time they have dealt with it) and the sensor doesn't think there is contact with it. Unfortunately, the alarm is still occurring intermittently, but it doesn't shut down the unit, so it is more of an annoyance than anything. Would certainly still purchase and recommend this product but they need to take a look at this design issue.

[UPDATE (December 8, 2016)]
The false (door ajar) alarm was continuing intermittently so we called out the repair guy again. This time I was there to see exactly what he did. It really is as simple moving this piece of metallic tape back down, at the bottom lip of the fridge. It just kind of shimmies up and doesn't connect with whatever is in the door to tell the unit it is closed. A very simple fix that has worked. Still going strong (and quietly!) with no other complaints.

[UPDATE (October 3, 2017)]
I am reducing my rating to 4 stars because this door sensor issue will not go away. See my comment of this same date in response to someone having the same problem, but bottom line is that this method of sensing whether the door is closed is problematic and seemingly very shoddy compared to the rest of the unit. As I mention in my comment, I have furniture wedged up against this thing to press the door closed (and initiate the sensor) until I can once again get someone out to (maybe??) fix it. They need a better system or some sort of sensor redundancy. Otherwise, it is still operating quietly and very well. I don't regret the purchase but this has been very frustrating.

review_title: Door sensor keeps failing: HOW TO FIX IT
review_text: I purchased this from another online appliance place back in late 2014.  After maybe 3 years something I had in the fridge went bad and rotted/oozed while I was on vacation.  I think its that Kambutcha junk my wife drinks.  No big deal - cleaned it up but after that the fridge was never the same.  The summer after that water would always pool at the bottom of the fridge and spill over.  I thought I had wine that was not corked shut but it turned out to be that the evaporation system was not working right ans water was pooling instead of being evaporated properly.  In the back is a small drain that was plugged up with some nasty sludge - it seems that my wife's Kambucha had evolved to something more nasty than what comes in the overpriced jug from Whole Foods!  I needed to clear the sludge plugging up the drain but to clear it completely you really need to disassemble the entire back of the fridge!  After disassembling the back (about 16-20 screws) I used an air compressor and pipe cleaners to clean all that nasty stuff out and the water could freely drain properly - my water/evap issues were solved.  Soon after my fridge would continuously alarm that the door was open and the light would come on (as if the door was open).  There was no mechanical switch to be seen so I assumed the switch must be magnetic.  As it turns out it was.  Apparently the water from my previous problem had pooled inside that folded metal seam at the bottom, rusted, and swollen that folded metal so that magnet sensor in the lower left of the fridge front could no longer sense the magnetic gasket on the door when shut.  For about a year I could wipe this all down with soapy water and it was often enough to make a better seal and trigger the sensor but eventually the rust became too much.  In the end I had to take the bottom plastic trim off and it you look top the left (if you face the fridge) on the bottom is a thin pair of wires that go to the sensor.  They un-clip easily.  If you take the longer end that runs into the computer circuit and just short out those two wires it tells the system that hte dfoor is shut.  An old school PC jumper worked perfectly to short these 2 pins for me.  The door is always shut now as far as the fridge is aware so no alarm ever.  However there is no automatic light when the door opens. but you can choose to have the light on all the time (3 small LED lights do not use much power) or leave it off all the time - or manually turn it on and off as needed with the bottom on top.  Its annoying but a lot better than contestant door open alarm beeping.  I'm annoyed that a $2K small fridge was designed in a way that this could happen.  If they just sealed that bottom lip where the sensor lived water would not have been able to get in and start to rust, however I knowledge that it started with a spill that I was responsible for (darn that Kambucha).  What did I learn?  It doesn't pay to buy higher quality appliances because all are for the most part poorly designed and there is no value in paying for an appliance brand name.  When this breaks I plan to toss it in the trash and buy the cheapest replacement I can find at Sam's or Costco, assuming it will fail in 5 years or so anyway.

product_title: GE CYE22TSHSS Cafe 22.1 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel Counter Depth French Door Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_text:
We have had this refrigerator for about 4 months now. It was a replacement to a TINY refrigerator. We reconfigured our kitchen, and were able to utilize a new area for a fridge, so happily, got to go significantly bigger. Still had to go counter-depth and smaller than I would have wanted, but that being said? I love this refrigerator.

Counter-depth does cost you a lot of cubic feet in storage, but I love the way that it feels more built-in. And it's hard to get to the back of a deep refrigerator anyway - things can get lost. In our situation a standard depth would have extended beyond the door frame into the living room, which was not an option. We have a small home over all, and a small kitchen. This unit allowed us to get all of the bells and whistles we wanted, and still have decent storage capacity in our somewhat limited space.

This refrigerator is BEAUTIFUL, and has lots of great features. I love the way the ice maker is "hidden" behind storage inside the door. So many others that we looked at had a ugly, obtrusive ice maker as the focal point on the door. It WAS very slow making ice for about the first week. But since then, no problems. It DOES make some funny noises every once in awhile, but it is NOT noisy. Just odd noises periodically. Great versatility in the way you can configure trays and shelving. The only negative to me is the two smaller (for fruits and vegetables) storage drawers. They are too small in my opinion, so I have to store a lot of my veggies outside of the drawers. They are fine, so it's not a big deal to me, but I would have preferred a larger capacity. TO me, that's the only negative.

I LOVE the Temp Select Zone Drawer. It is full-width, spacious, and allows you to change temperature for either meat, beverage or deli. The drawer lights up red, blue or green (changing to bright white) depending on the setting you have chosen. All of the spotlight lighting in both the fridge and freezer is amazing. No way that anything can hide, because the entire refrigerator is beautifully illuminated. Even the freezer, which is nicely compartmentalized, and has a great pull out drawer at the top for items you want to reach quickly.

As you can see we are right up against the wall on the left side, and cannot open the door past 90 degrees. It doe not limit us in any way. All of the drawers open fully due to the smartly configured shelves on the doors.

I thought that the photo viewer was a silly idea, but I have to admit that it's kind of fun to watch our doggie's slideshow on the door!! The exterior light on the dispenser area is very pretty - acts as a nightlight in a dark kitchen. The only idea that escapes me is the hot water dispenser. It takes 5 minutes to heat enough water for a mug. Just use the microwave.

I HIGHLY recommend this refrigerator, especially for folks with limited space available to them. It's gorgeous, and will give you all the fun features you want in a modern fridge, just in a smaller package!!

Because the compressor had now gone to crap, I demanded a new unit, which they agreed to. Additionally, the new unit is way louder than the first. Our kitchen is right off of the living room,and if someone tried to sleep on the couch I bet they couldn't.

For the amount GE charges for this thing, it should work. But it doesn't. Total POS. Get something else and save yourself the headache.

product_title: LG WT4970CW Wave 4.7 Cu. Ft. White Top Load Washer - Energy Star
review_text: BEWARE: MOLD! We have had this washer for just under three years and I noticed our clothes were getting strange smudges on them. I did a tub clean cycle and stopped it momentarily to throw in some vinegar and there I see FILTHY water FULL of chunks of mold and mildew. No amount of tub cleaning, washing, and even straining out the water is stopping this machine from pumping what seems like pounds of mold into the tub/water. I've been washing my clothes in mold for who knows how long - and developed severe allergies because of it. This machine has a design flaw that allows mold to grow and and grow into pounds of sludge underneath the tub that is forced back into the water every time you wash. AVOID THIS MACHINE. You'd be better off washing your clothes in a bucket of river water!

review_title: GE JK3800SHSS 27" Stainless Steel Electric microwave and oven combination
review_text:
We bought this GE combo. to replace one that was too old to get parts for repair. We ordered a 27" since the repair man said to do so. Amazon did not give the dimensions so I looked at the same one on the GE home site. When it arrived it was well packaged and arrived with no damage, etc.; however, it was one solid, very heavy, 170 lb unit, rather than two pieces like our previous one. It also was much smaller than the dimensions stated in the GE site. Our cabinet had to be reworked and repainted to fit the larger hole that existed. It took a great deal of work to prepare the cabinet and then to bring into the house, lift into the spot and connect.

I have not had the unit installed very long - - - and have used it only a few times thus far. The price was the best I found while researching. If the oven cleans as the advertisement states, I will be delighted.

Besides being smaller than the stated dimensions that GE gave, being one single unit fused together made the installation very difficult. I am not happy with the timer sound. It is very soft and there are only 2 settings - - - mute or normal which is very quiet. I have to use my own timer to make sure I know when the cooking process is complete.

The unit is attractive in the stainless steel and goes well with my other stainless and black appliances. I expect to really enjoy this new oven combo. and it's steam-clean or self-clean options.

review_text: I have no issues with the service provided by Amazon but I am not at all happy with the quality of the appliance. After being sent to the Customer Relations department, I was told that the transit charge would be removed, then after speaking to the manager, I was told the parts charge would be removed but I still had to pay for labor. I refused because this was supposed to have been fixed in February. Do not buy this unit; I would also never purchase an appliance from GE; this was my first and my last.

product_title: GE CFE28TSHSS Cafe 28.6 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel French Door Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_text:
We purchased this refrigerator thinking that it would preform as well as the 3 GE refrigerators we had in the past. Boy, were we wrong. The unit is 1 1/2 years ago, installed when we built our new home. Since then we have had issue after issue. First, it was the water was dripping from the water dispenser, at first the tech blamed our plumbing. Still dripping a month later, we called the tech back, this time he found a service bulletin for the source of the problem, ( I guess that we weren't the only buyers with the same problem). So he replaced the filler tube with a longer tube. Problem fixed. Next, we called again about a loud clicking noise, the tech comes back and replaces a fan motor for the meat/ cheese drawer, not just a motor but a large piece of foam was part of the assembly. The list goes on, with other minor issues. The last time the tech told us that this model was the new revised model, that is why there are so many issues. So we called GE to complain about the poor workmanship and asked to have the refrigerator replaced, they offered to replace it with a discount that would have cost us more than we paid for the first time, so we asked for an extension of the warranty. They gave us an extra 1 year warranty. Now, we are hearing a motor running way too fast, it sounds like a motor being over worked. We just called again and are still awaiting for the tech to come back. We are very sorry for buying this overpriced piece of junk. So much for Brand Loyalty! I almost forgot, if you think the hot water feature is instant as I was led to believe, it is not. It takes up to 5 minutes to get the water warm enough for coffee. A Quick Drip coffee maker is much faster, and much cheaper!
We are hoping that someone at GE can read this review, and help us get the bad taste out of our mouths.

product_title: GE CFE28TSHSS Cafe 28.6 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel French Door Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_text: First off I want to mention how much I like General Electric products, and this purchase continues to reinforce my dedication. Auto temp control..., GREAT! Auto filter change notification ...., GREAT! Auto lock, to keep young kids from dispensing water or ice, FANTASTIC.... The touch screen, knobs and buttons are all sturdy, the on screen instructions easy to follow.The electronic picture on screen display...FUN. Finally, play around with how you place the shelving, because once you get it right you'll know it and that makes a huge difference on how much you will enjoy the refridgerator.

review_text: Despite a few bad reviews, this is a VERY awesome Frig and I'm overly impressed!! product_title: GE CFE28TSHSS Cafe 28.6 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel French Door Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_title: The filter is a total scam
review_text:
First, it is the loudest appliance I've ever owned. The thing that angers me more, is the water filter. They've build a NFC chip into the filter, so you can not get any after-market filter, you must pay their crazy high price. More importantly, it decides when the filter must be changed, and cuts off the water flow until you do! We barely use ice, and have excellent tap water... our last GE Profile refrigerator would alert you that it MAY be time for a filter change, but if the water was still flowing at full stream, you could override that and reset the clock... This one demands it. So I tried cutting the NFC chip off the filter to get past it... the system says it detected an unauthorized filter, and to prevent the possibility of a water leak, it shut down the whole water/ice system!

What a crock!

product_title: GE CFE28TSHSS Cafe 28.6 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel French Door Refrigerator - Energy Star

product_title: GE CFE28TSHSS Cafe 28.6 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel French Door Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_text: I bought a new refrigerator approximately 8 months ago, just after GE launched their new CAFE line. Since the beginning refrigerator was giving me issues, occasionally spoiling my food. To help solve this issue I would lower the temperature further. Occasionally I would get a notification on my GE application stating again that there was a temperature increase. Roughly one month ago I woke up to a not working ice maker and leaking fridge with melted food inside, I called GE and they scheduled a technician to come to my house. The technician changed the motor,  during the visit the technician was making comments such as, that an ice maker is considered a luxury, as well as, that we live in an area where it is hard to find parking so he no longer wants to come here and will never come again because my refrigerator caused him such a headache. Exactly two days later my ice maker AGAIN stopped producing  ice,  I called GE again, and now they ordered a new ice maker and set up an appointment with a technician to come install it. Technician NEVER showed up to the previously confirmed visit and even texted me that he is on his way. Then after me sitting and waiting at home ALL day, taking a day off of work, I got a message stating that technician left because there was nobody home and he even tried to ring the doorbell multiple times, I checked my buildings camera footage and no technician ever showed up. I called to reschedule and it is happened AGAIN the following day. I wasted two day off from work while my patients are depending on me to come. When I finally decided that enough is enough, I complained about this technician to GE. They scheduled another technician to come to my house, after he finished he ran some tests, stating that the temperature in my refrigerator is 68 degrees and his computer is showing that I keep my refrigerator door open for more than 20 minutes at the time, after I stated that this is absurd (it is nearly impossible to leave door open in this smart fridge considering it would beep endlessly and close on its own) The technician stated that we probably don't notice that it is open and I stated again that it's impossible because of the magnet that pulls the doors shut, I asked him to demonstrate how I could possibly leave this fridge open, he got angry and bursted out telling me to relax, in Russian. He left and wrote a note that customer yelled at him and to order MORE parts. During that time I called GE endlessly, spoke with countless supervisors/managers, everyone keep telling me that unit has to be labeled as unrepairable in order to exchange the unit . As a customer I have a right to buy PROPERLY working products and not be given defective units who from the get go need to be repaired. This unit was from a new collection, not on sale, not floor sample, very expensive, I feel my rights were violated, I have expensive food loss, GE provided me with a check for $100 and stated that I can go to Walmart and temporarily buy a portable fridge until they fix this one. I have already had two part replacements, FOUR times a technician has come to my house and GE scheduled ANOTHER visit next week where they plan to replace the thermostat. I AGAIN have to take a day off of work to wait for a technician that may or may not show up with no reimbursement for my profit lost. GE has no limit for the amount of visits until they admit that unit is not repairable. This is basically stating that if you are not lucky enough to buy a good unit that they are going to service this unit until the warranty expires and later you are on your own. This is a violation of my customer rights and I feel that such a company as GE has to take a responsibility and stop torturing their customers. I have to continue to open my house to strangers who force me to spend entire days at home, I feel extremely uncomfortable seeing another stranger in my house as as single female. I spent endless hours with helpless representatives on the phone, I feel as though sometimes they put me on mute, no one is listening. I am living a nightmare, I don't understand why I have to repair a defective unit.  I will not purchase GE again, none of my friends will purchase GE, none of their friends will purchase GE. product_title: LG LFXS30766S 29.6 cu. ft. Smart Wi-Fi Enabled French Door
review_text:
We recently purchased this french door refrigerator to replace a side by side. This review only covers initial impressions of design and functionality, not reliability. I gave this four stars due to the unknown reliability factor.

Ice maker - The in-door ice-maker saves space in the refrigerator. Most of the other brands currently have the ice maker located in the left upper corner of the refrigerator. That said, the ice storage in the door is limited. There is a ice container in the freezer for additional ice storage, but of course you have to transfer it down there.

Water dispenser - Dispenses cold water. No issues with water dripping down after releasing the dispenser. The filter seems to be of good quality. We do not like the taste of the tap water out of the sink, but the water dispensed from the refrigerator tastes close to bottled water quality.

Storage design - This design makes good use of available space. Due to the in-door ice maker design, there are no odd shaped door bins like some other models have in order to accommodate the ice dispenser. The right door can be opened to only allow access to the bins. We keep all our condiments here, so it is easy to open the outer door when only getting items stored in the door. If you're getting items from the refrigerator side of the door, you would need to open the back 'cold saver' panel. The four refrigerator drawers allow separate storage for produce, deli, meats, etc. The bottom one that spans the width of the refrigerator can be set to different temperature settings based on the storage item.

Quality - Seems to be of good quality materials. The bins and shelves are sturdy and the drawers slide smoothly. Of note, the metal material that you push your glass against to dispense water scratches easily. I noticed several other models have a plastic piece here instead of metal. Despite the resulting cosmetic scratches, the metal type seems sturdier than the plastic ones I saw in the store. LED lighting inside refrigerator and on water dispenser is a nice feature.

Stainless - Front is not magnetic like my other stainless appliances. Shows finger prints very easily. As long as you use the door handles to close it, an occasional wipedown with stainless steel cleaner is sufficient for us.

Freezer handle - Handle bar lifts up to release latch for easy opening. This was a big plus for us as some models don't have this and require a tug to open the freezer door.

Control panel - More functions than I will ever use. Switches between crushed/cubed ice, sets temperature of freezer and refrigerator, door alarm lock, connects to smart grid, etc. Temperature display only shows what it is set to, not actual temperature. Using my own refrigerator thermometers, temperature readings I took showed the freezer temperature accurate, and refrigerator about two degrees warmer than display. Since it connects to the "smart grid," someone could feasibly hack into your refrigerator settings from the internet. In my opinion, a down side for refrigerator function. Of note, the control panel has to be unlocked in order to switch ice form.

Depth/Height - Extends beyond counter-depth about 10" w/out handles/12" including the handles. Since it is on the end of our kitchen, it looks alright, but if located elsewhere I would have chosen a counterdepth model.

The biggest down sides are the price and only 1-yr warranty. I chose an LG brand because of it's comparatively better reliability by Consumer Reports consumer surveys. As a consumer, for a major household appliance, I expect a longer warranty than one year.

Note: I purchased the LG LFXS30766S locally, not through Amazon.

7/4/15 Update: After owning this refrigerator for 6 months, it began not cooling sufficiently. It began cooling only to 44-50 degrees, even when set lower. Since it is under warranty, I submitted a service ticket on the LG website. The response received was an email advising the customer to level the refrigerator. We verified the level, with slight modifications which did not help the cooling problem. We followed up with a phone call to LG customer service. My husband was on hold for 4 hours, after which he was told they can't schedule more than 3-5 days out and that he would be contacted in 3-5 business days. On the 5th day, having yet to hear from LG, I called back to check the status, which took about 5 minutes, and we received a call back with an availability of a service technician to come out a few days later. Upon arriving, the technician seemed to immediately know the problem was due to a faulty component that had been recalled by LG. After defrosting the freezer and replacing the component, the refrigerator now seems to be cooling properly. Overall we are happy with the functionality and design of this refrigerator after 6 months of use. However, due to the product malfunctioning within 6 months of ownership, I am not confident in the reliability of the product over the long term. A manufacture that offers quality products in this price range should stand behind their product by providing longer warranty coverage.

review_title: Love it, with only one issue (to date)...
review_text:
I've owned this refrigerator for about 2 months now. Purchased it brand new from a local home improvement store (The Blue one, not the Orange one). They delivered it and hauled the old one away. In delivering the new one, they dinged the side of the freezer (bottom, right), so they gave us 30% off for the damage.

For the water, we have well water, bad well water. So I bought a FloJet BW4000 Bottled Water Dispensing System, cut a hole in the cabinet next to the refrigerator and inserted a 5 gallon bottle of water in, hooked it up to the refrigerator and it works great (though the first pump died within 3 weeks and had to be replaced). I've attached a photo of this setup.

4 days ago, I opened the freezer and heard the fan disengage, making an odd sound. So I closed it up and waited for the compressor to kick back on, then opened it again to listen specifically for the fan, and sure enough, there was a problem. Later, I could begin to hear it in the refrigerator as well.

We called LG and they sent a repairman out within 24 hours, after hearing the noise, he knew what it was. Took everything out of the refrigerator, all shelves and drawers, everything. There was frost forming in the lower, left quadrant. He took the inside, back panel off and the elements were all frozen up. (Same issue when he took the freezer back panel off as well).

He had to use a steam gun of some kind, to melt the frost, then bend the pipes back away from the panel. He also moved a sensor. He explained that this was a known problem, that most refrigerators were fixed before being sold, but some slipped through to the public.

We'll see if the issue is resolved or if it continues.

That issue aside though, we love the refrigerator and the deal that we got couldn't be beat. ($1595 after the damage discount, coupled with a Military Veterans discount, coupled with it having already been on sale).

So, frosting issue aside, I'm still going give this refrigerator 5 stars. If the frosting issue becomes an issue again, that may change. But so far, it's an awesome refrigerator.

review_title: Worked great for 4 years, then needed major repair
review_text:
Important note before I start my review: check the label on your refrigerator that is on the top inside right of the fridge. If the manufacture date is between June and Dec 2014, the fridge has an issue with the defroster that needs to be fixed (needs to have a new motherboard or a flash update of the software on it. FYI, you will have to empty the shelf area on the repair day as all the shelves need to come out). You can remove the large bottom drawer and look underneath, if you see ice buildup then you probably have this issue (assuming it's not due to something else).

OK onto the review. Just remodeled the kitchen and was wanting to get the biggest refrigerator I could find. This one is one of the larger fridges out there, and the installers had to remove the doors to get it to fit through the front door. Bought in early Jan 2015, upgraded from a side by side that I bought in 1991.

Took some getting used to the new setup, especially the freezer, but so far the french door type arrangement is growing on me. You can fit quite a few things in this fridge and freezer once you get the shelves adjusted correctly, with a few exceptions (noted in cons).

The biggest shock to me was how little you can store in the door area. On the side by side I had a lot of things in the door, on this thing some of the door storage is a joke, it can barely hold anything at all.

The door in door is alright. I don't think it will be something I ever get again if/when I get another fridge.

I haven't tried their smart phone app yet to see if it's something worth having. It sounds like you have to connect it to wi-fi to use the app which I don't really want to do, I'd rather just use bluetooth to communicate with the fridge. Not that I don't trust LG (well maybe kinda don't trust), but giving the fridge access to the internet or outside internet access to the fridge doesn't appeal to me.

Pros:
Lots of light. Very easy to spot things. LED lighting too so should last a very long time.

For the most part it's very quiet when it's running. My old fridge was freight train loud by comparison. However it does make some loud noises from time to time (see cons).

It does seem to use less electricity compared to old fridge. I noticed my electric bill went down about $10 the first month. I'll have to get on the SCE website and see if I really am using less electricity than I did a year ago.

I like the water dispenser, can put large containers there with no problem and refill water bottles easily as well. It has an LED light that comes on too so you can see what you are filling. It gives you about a second where the light comes on before the water starts coming out, so if you are refilling a water bottle at night you can line it up better if you are quick.

Cons:
At first it was extremely quiet for a few months, and then it started making some *very* loud popping/banging noises all the time. I was very concerned about this, web searching trying to find the answer and the only one is it's the defrost heater... I'm just hoping if it's something wrong that it will break before the warranty expires. Maybe it's due to the defrost issue and the ice buildup that was in the fridge, just got that fixed today (10/10/15) so we'll see how it goes.

The ice maker capacity is fairly small. You won't be having any good sized parties depending only on this thing.

LG customer support stinks. I got a letter from LG via Costco in March saying there is a problem that needs to be addressed (ice buildup behind the crisper in fresh food area - the issue I mentioned at top of my review, that's how I know the date range), I called them about it and they gave me the run around even after sending them a copy of the letter and never heard back from them. I was very displeased how defensive they became about the whole scenario, completely denying there was any issue with the fridge that would cause them to send a letter out. My wife did finally notice there was ice/water on inside bottom of the fridge under the large bottom drawer (there was almost a 1/4" ice layer) so when I called back again 6 months later they finally sent someone out to look at it and sure enough it was due to the defrost issue, and it turns out it is an issue they are fully aware of!

As someone else noted, there is very little storage for 2 quart or gallon sized type containers in this fridge. I've re-arranged the shelves a few times (without sacrificing storage for other items) but can't seem to make it work to store more than a few. I think the folding/sliding shelf is going to have to go. That's too bad, because had they done a better job on the door storage that wouldn't need to happen.

The OEM water filters are very expensive. You can find aftermarket filters for this by other manufacturers, I'm getting ready to try one out here soon will update my review later. Either that or I may put the bypass back in and switch back to the external water filters my old fridge used, they were only $10 and worked great.

Attached a picture of my shelf layout, works good for me maybe it will for you too. I put the sliding/folder shelf on the top right. I kept the shelves even with each other as if they are not at same level can't help but imagine something falling off and cracking the glass on the shelf below. If that doesn't bother you then you could raise/lower the shelves to fix the lack of quart/gallon container storage.

Update 6/25/16: So far the loud popping/banging noises have not returned. It must have been the ice buildup, when the defroster would kick in it was the sound of the ice breaking up. There was a LOT of ice there, it took the tech a long time to get rid of it with his heat/steam gun.

One bad thing with the shelf layout I showed in the picture is the top left shelf will have to be removed to change the water filter.

I tried the WLF-01 water filter and so far not impressed. Bought a 2 pack, the first one started giving out about 2 months later, the water started tasting weird. The only thing that happened was we went on a 2 week vacation, it was fine before we left but when we got back noticed the bad taste and it never got better after 3 weeks of using it. Swapped in the second filter today and will see how it goes.

The white paint on the glass on the "Glide N' Access" shelf is cheap. We spilled some cranberry juice on it and didn't notice it till an hour or so later, when we wiped it off the paint came right off.

Update 4/23/17: Fridge is still working well. I switched back to factory water filters (good prices on Amazon) and all seems good now.

One issue that happened with us, my wife accidentally had something sticking up in the freezer that didn't allow the door to close all the way, it left a little under a 1/8" gap all around the seal. The door open sensor didn't detect it and it was open like that all night long. The next morning got something out and noticed the food in the top drawer was thawing out, found the problem and closed it back up. It did eventually freeze things again but then a few days later noticed food was thawing out again. Looked in the back and noticed the air vents were covered with ice.

Unplugged it and took off the front freezer door and removed the drawers (instructions are in the owners manual). On the left side there is a drawer guide you can remove. The back cover simply pulls off, I started on the top left side. Unplug a couple plugs and you can remove the cover. The evaporator was about 1/3 covered in ice, used a heat gun to melt the ice on the evaporator and a hair dryer to dry out the cover. Plugged it all back in and it works great again.

I guess you could simply open it up and let it thaw out if you wanted but I didn't want the food to unfreeze any more than it had as that may have taken hours.

Update 1/15/19: Noticed food in the freezer seemed to be thawing out right before heading out on a 3 day trip. Came home and found everything thawed out and both sections of the fridge were warm. PTL and thankfully LG agreed to a 1 time warranty extension repair (Costco may have helped with that too, I called concierge service and they called LG on my behalf) and now it's working great again.

If you're in the Los Angeles area DG Appliance Service is the best, they came out and replaced the entire sealed system in about 3 hours (FYI, all the shelves and drawers need to come out of the entire fridge for this kind of repair). Dmitry was very professional and brought all the needed parts with him. Hopefully it will last longer than 4 years now. Had LG not agreed to that warranty extension repair, I'd probably give it 1 or 2 stars. The GE fridge I bought in '91 was still going strong 24 years later and I must admit I was bummed I sold it when this thing died. This LG fridge is a really nice fridge, but if it's only going to last a short amount of time then that's not acceptable.
