review_title: My biggest regret in life is buying an LG fridge.
review_text:
We enjoyed our LG fridge for about six months. Then, the never-ending battle began.

First, we heard a knocking sound. After answering the door to no one for the tenth time, we realized it was the fridge. I Googled. I read the manual. I scratched my head. “Unplug it,” everything more-or-less told me. Great; restart it. Hold down CTRL+ALT+DELETE at the same time. Got it.

I left it unplugged for the recommended four hours. Then I powered it back up and the knocking immediately commenced. A few days later, we got the IF error code.

Error code? A refrigerator has an error code? Seriously. This was too complicated already. Once again, I turned to Google, the manual, and my scalp. “ I called the store. After all, they had strongarmed us into a warranty I didn’t want, and I’m so glad they did.

So the repairman came out. He told me that these fridges were notorious for breaking down. Then he proceeded to show me how to repair it myself because, “This isn’t the first time and it won’t be the last.”

We took the entire freezer apart to get to the ice blower fan, essentially. It gets frozen solid. Every three months like clockwork.

Was it manageable? Yeah. First world problems and all that. But then other stuff started going down:

-The large mechanism that slides into some other cheap, plastic part did something stupid, so the door wouldn’t always close. So guests would shut our fridge but not shut our fridge, which resulted in …
-A ripped rubber door seal.
-No matter what temp the fridge was set at, food sitting directly on the glass shelves or in two of the three produce drawers would freeze. And we’re not talking about some delightful icy crunch. Entire pieces of fruit, meat, even cheese would freeze solid. Did you know cheese could turn into ice? It can. We cannot store food in half of our fridge. (However, I lined all of the shelves in newspaper, which seems to have helped. Plus, I can now read about the local elections from a year ago every morning while I get the orange juice.)
-The freezer fan clogs with ice so often, I have to mention it …
-… twice.
-The water dispensing button is starting to stick.
-The ice dispenser clogs on a daily basis. We keep a knife honer nearby to stab into the bin. I repeat, this happens daily.
-It gets fingerprinted to he77. I know this is a hazard of being an appliance in a home where the occupants have hands. But I hate this thing and now I’m just searching for more to add to the list.
-The water valve that connects the water line to the fridge wore out. So now we don’t even get water or ice until I replace it.
-And now the ice maker is broken. That's a $120 part.

We have a second fridge in our house. We got it for free from an apartment complex that was throwing them away. We keep it in the garage as a beer fridge. Dudes, this fridge (I don’t even know the brand) is probably 20 years old (at least), is ugly as sin, and is chugging away like we do on beer.

Meanwhile, my $2,500 LG heartache mocks me with a frozen water melon, incessant ticking, and dripping water.

This is ridiculous for the price that I paid on this very low quality product.

Everything that my parents bought from them broke within a few months of use. STAY AWAY. They tricked me with their rebranding into LG and untrue slogan of "Life's Good".

The next step, I can pay over $300 to their out of warranty department to resolve my issue. Or I can go to an authorized service provider and pay $78 for a service call to my home. From there, the authorized service provider can call the LG technical support line to help troubleshoot. Why can't I do that? I'm mechanically inclined and I can work a phone. Nope, can't further extort money from you if they do that.

I tried escalating the issue to a US based representative, who did not offer anything other than what the front line agent did. In fact, the escalation person I spoke to didn't believe me that the unit did not have a filter, despite confirmation from their agent that my unit does not use a filter.

If you already own an LG appliance, I would contact them before the warranty expires to make sure every little bit is satisfied, because once that initial term passes, you may as well be stranded on an island. review_text:

It's now the 3rd week in February 2017 and the freezer just failed. Thawed our food and now I can't get the temp to go below 20 degrees even though the digital readout shows -1. Ice makers quit also. Contacted LG customer service who advised 3-5 days just to have a tech come look at it. While I may be jumping to conclusions on how this will all pan out I am not feeling real good at the moment. After the failure I searched online for information and discovered a boat load of negative reviews over the past 12 months for this LG fridge. Many of the reviews start off the same way as my story here and end up costing people a chunk of money. If, after tech support comes out, I find that there is a simple explanation for the freezer failure I will certainly update my review. For now, I just want to caution others that this fridge with the glowing reviews may not be all it's cracked up to be.

EDIT: 2/22/17 Well the fridge is now dying. Won't cool below 45 degrees even though it's set at 33. Rude account executive out of Alabama didn't care at all and just said 3-5 days to contact a repair facility. Won't give us her supervisors information for followup either. Spoke to a couple repair facilities in our area and they advised that they don't do LG warranty repairs because LG fails to reimburse them. Family of 6 with no cold food in the house and no repair timeline....This should go well.

EDIT: 3/17/17. Repair man finally came out the 1st week in March. All the freon leaked out of the sealed system into our fridge. His recommendation was a replacement fridge. He said that since it's a sealed system it is irreparable. LG refused. They want to send another service tech out to fill the system with new freon and a dye so they can see where the leak is at. We are still waiting for that guy and any parts. Worst experience ever with an appliance!

review_title: Good fridge, but only for 1-2 years
review_text:
We purchased this refrigerator back in 2017. It had been working fine for almost two years, however with one exception. The fridge is Wi-Fi enabled, and there's LG app called "Smart ThinQ" that connects to it. The app is pretty much useless, all it does is tells how many times you opened the fridge compared to the average in your area; but it has one useful feature: if someone left the fridge door open, and did not react in time to the fridge itself beeping, the app shows an alert on your phone. This actually helped us 2-3 times when the grandma did not close the door and did not hear the beep.
The problem is that the fridge every now and then loses connection with the home network - the interval is from several days to several weeks. When this happens, you have to unplug it from the power and re-plug, and then it reconnects and stays connected for the next interval.
We tried to address this with LG while the warranty was still effective. LG was sending one tech after another, but they were not trained to address anything with the wi-fi, they did not know what is firmware, they blamed the phone showing the messages, and so on. Couple of times we called LG office, and that's when we found that LG is probably unsurpassed in hostility towards the customer and in their associates' ability to lie. I eventually gave up with this - after all, wi-fi is not the most important feature you expect from the refrigerator.
In the important features the refrigerator was doing fine, however. We have measured the temperature inside in various places of it, and it was never off by more than 0.5°C from the set target temperature - very respectable result.
This all lasted almost two years, at which point the refrigerator stopped cooling, and needed replacing sealed system plus compressor plus system board. The standard 1 year warranty has already expired, but sealed system has 6 years warranty, compressor 10 years, so it was all free of charge, including labor and initial diagnostic visit (we have yet to receive the reimbursement for the latter, but so we were told).
The tech who was doing the job has shared that this model now fails left and right, he sees 2-3 of them every week. There's already class action lawsuit in works against LG about this problem, and according to the materials of the lawsuit (you can easily find it on google), LG knew about it for years, but refused to address. Indeed, in our case the tech has replaced the compressor with the exact same model (the compressor is the point of failure), and it looks like this is not the end: 2 days after, the temperature inside is 10°C higher than what's set. LG is sending their own technician. Remarkably, during all this disaster, "smart" LG app runs its "smart diagnostic" and says that everything is perfect.
Yet another notable nuance: according to the tech, his LG-authorized repair center is only one of the two in Chicago area who are still doing warranty work for LG. With all the others, LG is on credit hold. Draw your own conclusions.
Some other features of the refrigerator. Double door. The idea is to put most-used products in the front compartment, so in most cases you open only the external door, while the main big compartment remains closed, saving the cold. Good on theory, but on practice this feature probably requires more discipline and better memory than we have: we found that in most cases we open both doors, first one, then another, in order to find out where is what you need.
Water filter. Our filter failed much sooner than expected, probably clogged, and we replaced it with the plastic insert LG provides for those who don't feel that municipal water needs any extra filtering.
Overall, with this global compressor problem, this LG refrigerator in particular, and with LG reaction to in in general, probably all LG products, is absolutely the worst money can buy.

review_text:
Purchased this refrigerator on 14Mar2018 at a big box DIY store to replace a Samsung that failed in less than a year. Fast forward to early October 2019 and we have compressor failure. Currently waiting on a fourth service call to repair. The LG tech told me he is going to replace the compressor, condensor and drier and possibly the evaporator. So do your homework before buying this model (or any LG refrigerator anywhere) as compressor failure is a "common" failure point.

The good about this refrigerator is that is is a good looking unit with a good amount of usable space. I like the lighting as it illuminates the interior well. That's about all the good.

The bad list is longer and since I have a dead unit I am motivated to post reviews. I have an unusial case because I bougnt a store ESP when I bought the refigerator. Shortly after that LG announced that they were extending the coverage on the sealed system to 5 years on units purchased after January 2018. But the ESP gives me $300 food loss coverage.

I have to ding it on space because the interior top losses some space at the outer edges so you have to put your shorter bottles and container of the outer edges. Additionally the top shelf with the drop-down front section has a cross bar with restricts the height of items you put on the shelf below it.

Now on to my saga. After my wife noticed that the refrigerator seemed warm I called the ESP service number and they sent out an indie company tech. He poked around and ordered a new evaporator fan and controller board. A week later he came and installed the parts. At which point he told me that this was all he was allowed to do as the sealed system was off limits. A day later with no change in temps I called the ESP number again. This time they sent out a LG tech. He replaced the compressor and reprogrammed a board. Still not cold enough - some cooling but frige is 3 degrees higher the setting (38 - 40, set at 36) and freezing not betting below 27 degrees (set at -4).

So a third service call later the tech tells me that he is going to replace the sealed system - new compressor, condenser, drier and possibly the evaporator coils. I asked if that was the most economical solution and he told me that it was the way LG wanted to do it. Now I have a couple of more days using a loaner refrigerator and ice chests to keep my food cold. Keeping the local store in business buying ice, LOL.

All in all LG does not seem to care about my inconvenience but I still have to call the ESP compnay to update them. It may be time to push tem for a new refrigerator. And that 's my sad tale - for what it is worth.

Bottom line - if you care about looks then this might be your jam. If you want reliability - I would look elsewhere (like Whirlpool had a bad experience with Samsung and when they delivered the loaner unit the guy told me that they were bringing a lot of GE's back). If you do purchase this refrigerator I would highly recomend an Extended Service Policy for peace of mind and food loss coverage,

review_title: This fridge will put me into an early grave.
review_text:
We enjoyed our LG fridge for about six months. Then, the never-ending battle began.

First, we heard a knocking sound. After answering the door to no one for the tenth time, we realized it was the fridge. I Googled. I read the manual. I scratched my head. “Unplug it,” everything more-or-less told me. Great; restart it. Hold down CTRL+ALT+DELETE at the same time. Got it.

I left it unplugged for the recommended four hours. Then I powered it back up and the knocking immediately commenced. A few days later, we got the IF error code.

Error code? A refrigerator has an error code? Seriously. This was too complicated already. Once again, I turned to Google, the manual, and my scalp. “ I called the store. After all, they had strongarmed us into a warranty I didn’t want, and I’m so glad they did.

So the repairman came out. He told me that these fridges were notorious for breaking down. Then he proceeded to show me how to repair it myself because, “This isn’t the first time and it won’t be the last.”

We took the entire freezer apart to get to the ice blower fan, essentially. It gets frozen solid. Every three months like clockwork.

Was it manageable? Yeah. First world problems and all that. But then other stuff started going down:

-The large mechanism that slides into some other cheap, plastic part did something stupid, so the door wouldn’t always close. So guests would shut our fridge but not shut our fridge, which resulted in …
-A ripped rubber door seal.
-No matter what temp the fridge was set at, food sitting directly on the glass shelves or in two of the three produce drawers would freeze. And we’re not talking about some delightful icy crunch. Entire pieces of fruit, meat, even cheese would freeze solid. Did you know cheese could turn into ice? It can. We cannot store food in half of our fridge. (However, I lined all of the shelves in newspaper, which seems to have helped. Plus, I can now read about the local elections from a year ago every morning while I get the orange juice.)
-The freezer fan clogs with ice so often, I have to mention it …
-… twice.
-The water dispensing button is starting to stick.
-The ice dispenser clogs on a daily basis. We keep a knife honer nearby to stab into the bin. I repeat, this happens daily.
-It gets fingerprinted to he77. I know this is a hazard of being an appliance in a home where the occupants have hands. But I hate this thing and now I’m just searching for more to add to the list.
-The water valve that connects the water line to the fridge wore out. So now we don’t even get water or ice until I replace it.
-And now the ice maker is broken. That's a $120 part.

We have a second fridge in our house. We got it for free from an apartment complex that was throwing them away. We keep it in the garage as a beer fridge. Dudes, this fridge (I don’t even know the brand) is probably 20 years old (at least), is ugly as sin, and is chugging away like we do on beer.

Meanwhile, my $2,500 LG heartache mocks me with a frozen water melon, incessant ticking, and dripping water.

product_title: LG LMXS30776S30.0 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel French Door Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_text:
I am very hesitant to write a review on this fridge so soon after buying it (Thanksgiving 2015) as the anchor for a complete suite of new kitchen appliances. Sooo many poor reviews of both the fridge and LG customer service (or lack thereof). But, it it tanks in the future, I will certainly add updates and change my rating accordingly. Now for my three months experience with it.

This is a huge fridge - 30 cu ft, the biggest I've ever owned! There are only the two of us, for God's sake. But the wife insisted, and you know how that usually plays out. Surprisingly, it's only an inch wider than the old 26 cu ft GE Profile. It's also only an inch taller. The big difference is the depth - almost four inches deeper than the old one. I figured it would make things in the back hard to reach, but not so. I think, maybe, the shelves themselves are about the same depth as the GE, made necessary by the amount of space the inner door bins take up in the interior cavity. The brilliant LED interior lighting certainly makes things in the back easier to see in there, so maybe that's why I don't notice how deep it really is. At the end of the day, it DOES hold much more than the GE. That one tended to get stacked up with all sorts of small plastic containers and zip-loc bags for leftovers and otherwise. But not this behemouth. It seems to swallow anything and everything that we throw at it.

As I said, the LED lighting is excellent. There are no shadowed spots anywhere - not only in the main cavity, but also in the custom chill drawer and the freezer drawer. Speaking of the freezer, a friend cautioned me about buying one with a bottom freezer. Said that everything stays disorganized in it, and you have to almost stand on your head to find a particular item. To be honest, I can never find a damn thing I'm looking for in there. But once again, the wife overules, and proclaims it to be great! In its defense, it does have two upper pull out trays that thin items like frozen pizza can be stored in, and that does help to some degree. And, as with other interior areas, the LED lighting is fantastic and helps in locating that runaway chicken pot pie. At least until this week when the light bar went flakey on me. It no longer immediately comes on when I open the freezer drawer, at least not without a light tap on the LED panel. I suspect a loose connection or a bad switch. Regardless, I had enough foresight to buy a protection plan for this thing (I mean, $149 for full 3-year coverage on an appliance that cost $3000 with TT&L is a no-brainer). Got a service visit scheduled in six days, so hopefully the light issue will be quickly resolved.

This fridge really is quiet, unlike those of one particular brand whose name evokes circular eddies in the ocean. Yes, it gurgles and whizzes occasionally, but not objectionably so. They all seem to make some degree of noise, if for no other reason than to confirm that they're still working.

So far, I've not experienced, unlike some reviewers, interior frost build up, frozen items in the fridge compartment, water leaking onto the floor, or condensation on the doors. Yep, the stainless steel fingerprint issue can't be escaped, and this appliance is no different than any other. The good news is that this stainless has a higher sheen than most, which I believe makes it easier to wipe off fingerprints, greasy smudges, and errant food residue deposited by the cook's hands. I'll say no more about that, 'cause SHE may stumble across this review at some point in my lifetime. I've grown accustomed to sleeping indoors and eating regularly, so discretion is a requisite.

The controls are extensive, and pretty straightforward. The exterior information panel is a nice techno-touch, and functionally, it cools, chills and freezes effectively, and as hoped.

The icemaker and water dispenser so far have functioned flawlessly. And even though the door-mounted icemaker is necessarily smaller than traditional top-mounted units, just the two of us have never had to go without frozen H2O. The dispensers spit out their contents on demand, and without complaint or hesitation.

The middle custom-cool drawer really is a neat feature, although when we were shopping for a fridge I didn't realize how useful it could be. As a later middle-age fart, I tend to not remember things like what I had for breakfast, and where I squirrelled away the deli-sliced ham. But once I accepted that the drawer is where stuff like that should go, I immediately appreciated it. I'm sure it adds to the energy efficiency of the fridge, because I don't have to open the the main compartment and let all that expensively cooled air escape just to make a lunchtime sandwich. All the above also applies to the door-in-door design - the soft drinks, milk and OJ are right there, without having to fully open the fridge compartment. I do, though, dislike the light weight of that door. I find that I have to conciously push it closed. I can't just half-heartedly swing it, and expect the gasket magnets to grab. All too often, within a minute or so, the alarm sounds reminding me that the door is still open. I AM an old dog, but occasionally I DO learn a new trick.

Except for the curious issue with the freezer drawer light, I am very pleased with this refrigerator. I may have more to add, however, as time goes on . . . particularly after the three year protection plan expires.

NOTE:
If you don’t find this review to be helpful, please leave a comment telling me why. Otherwise, if you just don’t like the review, for whatever reason, I challenge you to write a better one. I attempt to help others make informed buying decisions. What have you done lately?

UPDATE 3-8-2016
Service techs showed up bright and early (from my retailer, not LG). They were actually a week late, but only because the parts they ordered (a magnetic switch and an LED light strip) were on backorder. Took about thirty minutes to track down the source of the lighting issue, because replacing the LED strip didn't fix it, and the original switch was still working. In fact, the controls on the center pullout drawer, unknown to me, had also stopped working. Turned out to be a loose electrical connection behind that same drawer. He re-inserted the plug, and that fixed it immediately. All is well for the moment. But I'm still keepin' 'em crossed, hoping that some of the other common issues don't develop.

product_title: LG LMXS30776S30.0 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel French Door Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_text:
We bought this fridge a month ago after a LOT of research and we are very happy with it. It is so bright inside, and we use the door in door feature all the time--so handy for grabbing things like milk or condiments. The only problem to note with the door-in-door is if you don't actively push it closed, the outer half of the door won't latch onto the inner part of the door. Unlike a full-on fridge door that has enough mass to swing all the way closed if you just nudge it in the right direction, the outer door is light and doesn't have the mass needed to latch itself. My husband gets the fridge-door-open beep all the time as a result because he forgets it won't latch itself!
As for the general style of this fridge, my husband and I are both tall so it's so nice having everything we use regularly--i.e. the stuff in the fridge, not the freezer--up higher and easier to access. The in-door ice maker is nice since it doesn't take up any space in the main area of the fridge, though the shelves on the ice maker door are laughably small (both depth-wise and height-wise--jars of things like horseradish are about all that will fit there). So far we haven't had problems with running out of ice due to this ice maker's smaller capacity, but it's just my husband and I. One thing to note that I really did not think about before buying (this would obviously be a problem for all fridges of this style) is how short all the shelves are in general. I struggled finding places tall enough for things like bottles of ketchup or salad dressing. Without adjustment (making one shelf very short), literally the only place something as tall as a jug of milk will fit is in the door shelf. Knowing this wouldn't have changed my decision to buy this style of fridge, it was just something I hadn't really thought about beforehand. Overall we love this fridge and would make the same choice again if we had to do it over.

review_title: Great oven but has a drawback...
review_text:
I purchased this oven locally over a year ago for $2200 and have not regretted it for a moment - it is by far the best oven I have owned. The cooking options are numerous: Bread Proofing, "Perfect Turkey", Defrost and Dehydrate are a few of the more unusual settings that are not found on the typical oven. There is also a "fast heat" setting that I use frequently but the temperature on this one is only guaranteed at the center rack position. If you frequently bake the same item, you can store the settings under "My Favorites" to keep from having to enter the same information in repeatedly, too.

The oven is easy to keep clean for the most part (there are 3 clean options to choose from) but you do have to remove all of the grills and racks before starting the cycle. I have cleaned it several times and have not had the front glass explode which is a common complaint. The only negative I have found is that grease/dirt can get trapped between the 2 panes of glass and it is not an easy task to access it for cleaning. I have read that you can take the door off and disassemble it but I have not been that adventurous yet. My unit also came with (2) "easy glide" racks which are wonderful (except when it comes time to scrub them) as well as (4) standard racks. You can also delay cooking so the oven is Sabbath friendly.

All in all, this is a fantastic and versatile oven - I would purchase one again. However, I did deduct a star because I always feel that I have to run the clean cycle when I am at home and can monitor it due to all of the reports of the glass fronts breaking/exploding. Between those complaints and the dirt build-up that I am experiencing between the panes of glass (and other reviewers have commented on, too) , 4 stars it is.

review_text: Samsung must be acutely aware or the design defect in this and related models.  In brief, the drain line below the condenser, inside the refrigerator, freezes up. The design fix is simple but Samsung provides no help, except under warranty.  Unfortunately the owner is unlikely to discover the problem within the warranty period.  But, the problem is not a “malfunction” in the sense of something going wrong, and normally covered by warranty. Rather it is an entirely predictable result of the defective design, and it is likely to occur in every product sold.  Because Samsung fails to acknowledge the problem or disseminate repair instructions, your repair person (even one referred by Samsung) is not likely to correctly diagnose or effectively repair the problem.  I cannot recommend this Samsung appliance. And I will consider this In all future appliance purchases.

review_title: and so far am happy with it
review_text:
Have had this unit for almost a month, and so far am happy with it. Buying a fridge this size was intentional for purposes of wasting less. Why I love it: it's beautiful; it's just me and my husband so the size* is perfect; the freezer and fridge temperatures are easily adjustable; shelves are easily adjustable; am surprised how much more room I have in my freezer compared to my old traditional fridge; it's quiet; my guests love it (once they enter the kitchen it's an attention getter, they all touch it and say they love it); and I waste less food. With the regular sized refrigerator, I would forget about some of my food and it would go to waste. I cook every single day and I've had to rethink how much I cook = less food wasted. It's contributed to helping us cook healthier and eating fresher foods because we make one more additional trip to the grocery store to buy more veggies and fruits. Also, this unit helps me keep my condiments to a minimum.

I wanted the Liebherr refrigerator ($3000 +), but it has awful reviews. Even the salesperson said it would break down in less than a year. So I compromised and almost bought the Summit ($1200+), which has great reviews, but I couldn't see this unit in person. I have to touch and see before buying. I called Summit and they say I can see it at the Home Depot in Manhattan. I live no where near NY. Then I was taking a stroll at the local Fry's while my husband ran an errand and look what I saw! This slim, clean modern unit. I have searched and searched for reviews, and found none, so I took the risk and bought it and so far no regrets.

I recommend buying a flat plug in extension cord. The fridge's extension cord doesn't allow you to really push the unit back so it sticks out quite a bit. Buying the flat plug in will solve that.

*We recently bought an under counter beverage cooler for our beer, wine and mineral water. This was on our shopping list before we decided to buy a slim counter depth fridge. We have more room for other items in our slim LG fridge. So it worked out well.

review_text:

I suppose if you're coming from another front loader or HE washer your perspective will be different but for a first HE front loader this machine has met all my expectations. I give it 4 stars because I do think these products tend to be way overly complicated for what they are intended to do and thus sacrifice reliability for "features" (and I'm a software engineer). Some things are just better left simple, I go to work and deal with tech all day and go home to have to deal with error codes to wash my clothes. Technical support is now required to wash clothes, F%&#. This also makes it difficult for non-english speaking users to use the product at all.

Because it's so feature-rich UI could use some improvement to allow for use by a larger list of localities. Other than this, it really does seem like a great washer so far. If the computer within doesn't die within the next 1-2 years I'll update my review to 5 stars.

review_title: My biggest regret in life is buying an LG refrigerator.
review_text:
We enjoyed our LG fridge for about six months. Then, the never-ending battle began.

First, we heard a knocking sound. After answering the door to no one for the tenth time, we realized it was the fridge. I Googled. I read the manual. I scratched my head. “Unplug it,” everything more-or-less told me. Great; restart it. Hold down CTRL+ALT+DELETE at the same time. Got it.

I left it unplugged for the recommended four hours. Then I powered it back up and the knocking immediately commenced. A few days later, we got the IF error code.

Error code? A refrigerator has an error code? Seriously. This was too complicated already. Once again, I turned to Google, the manual, and my scalp. “ I called the store. After all, they had strongarmed us into a warranty I didn’t want, and I’m so glad they did.

So the repairman came out. He told me that these fridges were notorious for breaking down. Then he proceeded to show me how to repair it myself because, “This isn’t the first time and it won’t be the last.”

We took the entire freezer apart to get to the ice blower fan, essentially. It gets frozen solid. Every three months like clockwork.

Was it manageable? Yeah. First world problems and all that. But then other stuff started going down:

-The large mechanism that slides into some other cheap, plastic part did something stupid, so the door wouldn’t always close. So guests would shut our fridge but not shut our fridge, which resulted in …
-A ripped rubber door seal.
-No matter what temp the fridge was set at, food sitting directly on the glass shelves or in two of the three produce drawers would freeze. And we’re not talking about some delightful icy crunch. Entire pieces of fruit, meat, even cheese would freeze solid. Did you know cheese could turn into ice? It can. We cannot store food in half of our fridge. (However, I lined all of the shelves in newspaper, which seems to have helped. Plus, I can now read about the local elections from a year ago every morning while I get the orange juice.)
-The freezer fan clogs with ice so often, I have to mention it …
-… twice.
-The water dispensing button is starting to stick.
-The ice dispenser clogs on a daily basis. We keep a knife honer nearby to stab into the bin. I repeat, this happens daily.
-It gets fingerprinted to he77. I know this is a hazard of being an appliance in a home where the occupants have hands. But I hate this thing and now I’m just searching for more to add to the list.
-The water valve that connects the water line to the fridge wore out. So now we don’t even get water or ice until I replace it.
-And now the ice maker is broken. That's a $120 part.

We have a second fridge in our house. We got it for free from an apartment complex that was throwing them away. We keep it in the garage as a beer fridge. Dudes, this fridge (I don’t even know the brand) is probably 20 years old (at least), is ugly as sin, and is chugging away like we do on beer.

Meanwhile, my $2,500 LG heartache mocks me with a frozen water melon, incessant ticking, and dripping water.

Because of the GE/Bisque and the SIZE (this is a larger refrigerator) I was forced into this model.

I contacted LG customer service and they ran the diagnostics which seemed to solve the problem - but it was only temporary; the loud fan noise returned three weeks later.  I contacted customer support again and they dispatched a technician the next day. I asked the tech why the unit was so loud?  He informed me that the newer LG refrigerators were, in fact, louder.  He told me LG had increased the torque of the three fans inside the unit. This change was intentional, to make the unit more efficient in cooling. We emptied out the freezer and took the back off to reveal a major ice jam on the defrosting coils. The tech called the LG factory and he was told this was a known issue (defect!).  At this time, LG does not have a fix for this issue - they have not published a bulletin with the affected serial numbers.  All the Tech could do for me was to melt the ice jam using a heat gun and hope it does not happen again.  He instructed me to contact customer service if the noise returns.  Obviously, this is not acceptable; I plan to escalate until LG either fixes my new fridge or gives me a refund.

review_text:
Let me start off by saying that I bought this from another retailer. I initially loved the look and functionality of my new fridge. Now 10 months old this is what I just experienced:

My 10 month old french door refrigerator's fan starting making a loud noise. I looked up my problem on the internet and found that my unit has a know frost buildup issue. I called LG since it was still under warranty. They diagnosed the unit over the phone and scheduled a service appointment for me. A new control panel was mailed out to me. The tech was supposed to be at my home between 8 am and noon yesterday. I received a phone call the night before confirming him for between 10 and noon. The tech did not show up until 1:05. He then proceeded to empty out my fridge, remove all of the shelves and the bins. The vent behind the veggie bin was encrusted with ice which he melted and chiseled away. Then the back panel inside was removed which revealed the entire coil frozen and encrusted with ice. It took until after 3 PM for him to melt all of the ice which resulted in my having towels both wet and dry all over the kitchen, a bucket for the excess water, not to mention my food, bins and shelves strewn about. The tech pulled out the fridge and replaced the control panel on the back. Then came the process of putting everything back together and putting all of the food back in. I then had to wash a load of towels and clean the fingerprints and streaks off of the stainless steel fridge. Well the first thing that I noticed was the once firm and solid bin holder now wobbles. But that is not the worse part, the worse part is that today, one day later, the fridge has begun to make the same sound and the ice is already forming around the vent. I was assured the the control panel (brain) would fix the problem. Well it seems to me that this is not the case and I know have to go through this again not knowing if the LG tech can figure out what actually is wrong. I called for another appointment and was told that as of now none is available for Monday or Tuesday so I have to call back on Monday to see when the next available appointment will be. Why should a new appliance have these issues? Why shouldn't an LG tech be able to diagnose and fix the problem on the first business? Why shouldn't I be able to get an immediate appointment for a return visit to rectify the problem? I'm regretting my decision to go with LG. I should have purchased a Samsung refrigerator. I own an LG Phone an LG smart TV and this refrigerator. I will never purchase another LG product again. Am I expected to miss another day of work to be available for service, suffer the mess and inconvenience of the repair process and then not know if after the second visit if it will be fixed or not?

review_title: Top Notch for Style and Operation
review_text:
We purchased this refrigerator, even after reading the numerous negative reviews on Amazon. We did it because it was truly the largest cubic feet available in counter-depth french door refrigerators and also because in particular we liked a) the in-door icemaker; b) the several sliding compartments in the freezer.

We have now owned the LG a month and have experienced none of the issues that others have mentioned. No noise, no shaking, no imbalance, etc. I wake up in the middle of the night often and I hear NO NOISE whatsoever while the entire house and neighborhood is quiet.

The in-door icemaker is a dream. When we had a party, we could EASILY remove it, pour out ice there into the bucket provided in the freezer itself and then have another round of ice made. And when we didn't use all the ice and wanted to free up the bucket after the party to store stuff in the freezer, we could easily pour the extra ice back into the icemaker and turn off the ice-making until later when we were out of ice again.

The front door interface is clear and easy to use. Yes, the water dispenser is a bit odd and guests could easily mistake how to obtain the water (instead of the ice). But your family won't, just as it will quickly learn the interface on the front door. Not only does having the icemaker in the door make that easy to use, but the extra cubic foot of space freed up in the refrigerator makes the whole thing seem way more roomy. The LED lighting is wonderful. Drawers in the refrigerator slide in and out easily and can be quickly removed with one hand if there's a spill and quickly inserted back after the clean-up. Yes, the compartments are too small for celery stalks so we had the very difficult task of cutting them in half (I'm joking, it's not difficult to do, nor can I think of a recipe that requires full celery stalks). Yes, you have to open both doors to pull out the one large sliding drawer in the refrigerator (although for nothing else). But as people who had a side-by-side before this, I have to say that we quickly learned on which side in the refrigerator different items were, so that mostly we open only one of the two doors.

As for all the complaints, I have no doubt that there are "lemons" in any product line, but we don't have one, so our experience with this item has been exceedingly sweet, and not sour at all. Hopefully, this will continue for the decade or so that we can expect to own it.

The interior is very spacious, especially the refrigerator portion.  A few items we encountered:  This model is taller than our previous LG, at 70+ inches. review_title: Design issues and not quite worth the money
review_text:
[[VIDEOID:a3535f318dbdbdcf8d894ecc6f4bf10d]] It looks good and works well, but the ice maker and the water dispenser are atrocious. In a quest to gain an extra cubic foot of space or so, they made the ice maker very very small. That means you get about a tall glass full of ice from it and it's done, you must wait for more. Making a pitcher of margarita or some other icy drink is not going to work with this model.

The design choices they made for the water dispenser are also baffling. On my old LG fridge, water and ice came down the same chute and the dispensing was triggered by the same big rubber-covered button - a simple and effective design. On this one, the dispensers are separate, ice comes out from the normal spot, while water comes out of a small dispenser above the ice chute. This is dumb to begin with as one has ample space to position a glass/cup under the ice chute but not under the tiny water dispenser. Also, the water dispenser does not seem to be mechanically activated (i.e. pushing the dispenser button opens the valve directly) but rather it seems to have an electrically-controlled valve (i.e. a valve actuated by a solenoid or such). The problem with this is that the water valve opens abruptly, just a fraction of a second after the water pump has started building up pressure. Water does not just drop into the glass but rather it shoots into the glass with too much pressure, causing a spill almost every time. Pouring water into an empty glass at just the right angle (such that the water slides down the side and then bounces off the bottom of the glass) virtually guarantees that the first ounce or so of the water stream will shoot back up onto the refrigerator door and the floor (see attached video for a more bening.

Aside from the above, the surfaces that one must press to activate the dispensers are neither rubberized nor metal, rather they are painted hard plastic. They will end up scratched rather quickly if pressed normally with a glass or cup.

The water filter is very small, probably half the volume of the filter in my previous LG refrigerator. I don't know this for a fact, but I'm willing to bet that it consequently has less filtration capacity and therefore must be replaced more often, at a likely higher cost over the long term.

My unit came with some small cosmetic manufacturing defects (the sheet metal isn't bent quite right in two spots around the edge of the top shelf) and with misaligned doors, so the QA process is not that tight either. Yes, there's an alignment procedure described in the manual but why not take care of that properly at the factory?

Anyway, we can probably live with the issues described above but this new refrigerator is a clear functional downgrade from our previous LG. It provides less or worse functionality and looks pretty much the same but it's nearly twice the money. Hopefully it's as reliable as the previous one (which, now at 10 years of age, is still working fine).

review_title: I hate my LG fridge. Hate. Hate. Hate.
review_text:
We enjoyed our LG fridge for about six months. Then, the never-ending battle began.

First, we heard a knocking sound. After answering the door to no one for the tenth time, we realized it was the fridge. I Googled. I read the manual. I scratched my head. “Unplug it,” everything more-or-less told me. Great; restart it. Hold down CTRL+ALT+DELETE at the same time. Got it.

I left it unplugged for the recommended four hours. Then I powered it back up and the knocking immediately commenced. A few days later, we got the IF error code.

Error code? A refrigerator has an error code? Seriously. This was too complicated already. Once again, I turned to Google, the manual, and my scalp. “ I called the store. After all, they had strongarmed us into a warranty I didn’t want, and I’m so glad they did.

So the repairman came out. He told me that these fridges were notorious for breaking down. Then he proceeded to show me how to repair it myself because, “This isn’t the first time and it won’t be the last.”

We took the entire freezer apart to get to the ice blower fan, essentially. It gets frozen solid. Every three months like clockwork.

Was it manageable? Yeah. First world problems and all that. But then other stuff started going down:

-The large mechanism that slides into some other cheap, plastic part did something stupid, so the door wouldn’t always close. So guests would shut our fridge but not shut our fridge, which resulted in …
-A ripped rubber door seal.
-No matter what temp the fridge was set at, food sitting directly on the glass shelves or in two of the three produce drawers would freeze. And we’re not talking about some delightful icy crunch. Entire pieces of fruit, meat, even cheese would freeze solid. Did you know cheese could turn into ice? It can. We cannot store food in half of our fridge. (However, I lined all of the shelves in newspaper, which seems to have helped. Plus, I can now read about the local elections from a year ago every morning while I get the orange juice.)
-The freezer fan clogs with ice so often, I have to mention it …
-… twice.
-The water dispensing button is starting to stick.
-The ice dispenser clogs on a daily basis. We keep a knife honer nearby to stab into the bin. I repeat, this happens daily.
-It gets fingerprinted to he77. I know this is a hazard of being an appliance in a home where the occupants have hands. But I hate this thing and now I’m just searching for more to add to the list.
-The water valve that connects the water line to the fridge wore out. So now we don’t even get water or ice until I replace it.
-And now the ice maker is broken. That's a $120 part.

We have a second fridge in our house. We got it for free from an apartment complex that was throwing them away. We keep it in the garage as a beer fridge. Dudes, this fridge (I don’t even know the brand) is probably 20 years old (at least), is ugly as sin, and is chugging away like we do on beer.

Meanwhile, my $2,500 LG heartache mocks me with a frozen water melon, incessant ticking, and dripping water.

product_title: LG LMXS27626S French Door Refrigerator, 27.0 Cubic Feet, Stainless Steel
review_title: Reviewing after about a year of use and I still love it.
review_text:
We have had ours for about a year now and felt I should leave my thoughts here.

The french door style is the way to go. You can use just the single doors or open both and store large items like cakes that I had issues with on our old side by side.

I absolutely love the icemaker being located inside the doors. This is an awesome space saving feature. It does create slightly smaller cubes and quite a bit less than most older ice makers with the large buckets. I think for the average family of 3-4 this should be plenty with it. There is an express Ice making mode that runs for 24 hours that makes it colder allowing you to make more ice faster at the expense of some energy savings. There is a large tub in the top freezer drawer that additional ice can be placed for parties (we just go to walmart and get a bag for less than $2). We have also planned ahead and dumped ice into tub before we went to bed the week of the party. For me the added space is much more valuable than having less Ice.

The chime when the door is left open can be annoying, but it can be deactivated. The air filter is a really nice feature that helps food stay fresher and more importantly removing bad odors. This beats the ole baking soda any day. The water filter is much easier to replace than our old fridge where it was located on the bottom grille. There is also a sliding shelf in the fridge that can be pushed back to stand up drinks or other taller objects.

The two freezer doors is a nice addition to this model. Most have 2 sliding shelves inside one door. With the one door design you will have a shorter top shelf. The two door design has both drawers being the same length which is nice.

The fridge is also remarkably quiet to me. The compressor is pretty much silent. This is awesome considering our old fridge was super loud. It was a 10+ year old fridge so I can not compare the sound quality of this to other new models.

Some things I wish were improved on would be light installed in the bottom freezer drawer. There is only a light for the top drawer which I am assuming that is intended to be the primary freezer so you don't have to bend over as much. The smudges can be annoying on the stainless steel. This is easily fixed with stainless steel wipes at walmart that work excellent. I also wish the bottom drawer in the fridge was split into two like the two drawers above it (for fruits and veggies). This is more of a personal preference so I don't have to open both doors to access.

Overall I love this fridge. I did a TON of reviewing online before purchasing this at Lowes and this one had the best reviews of any. I know several people have complained of issues (every fridge does), but mine has worked fine and I can only tell about mine has functioned. I have had no issues with ice maker or any leaking.

If you have any questions about my review or this fridge please feel free to contact me via comments or clicking on my profile. I always try to give as thorough of a review on an item as I can based on my experiences. I put a lot of faith in others reviews and I try to make sure my own reviews reflect that.

review_title: Everything about this range is beautiful. You'll want to buff it daily like a ...
review_text:
This appliance is a work of art. Everything about this range is beautiful. You'll want to buff it daily like a new car's chrome. The upper oven is small, but that works to our advantage. It actually heats up quicker than our toaster oven. It's so much better, that we have replaced our toaster over with a basic toaster since anything that needs to have a small oven can be done here. The lower oven is great especially when you need to cook two things at once. For example, we've used the top oven to defrost a couple of frozen dinners and a pizza for picky guests while the bottom one cooks a ham for the rest.

The stovetop is in a class by itself. It needs its own paragraph. The induction method is without a doubt the best way to cook. If this is your first induction, stay away from stainless steel, as it's really only for cooks that really know what they're doing. Best bet is an aluminum set made for induction with nonstick interiors like the epicurious from jcpenney. Once you use the induction, you'll never want to use standard electric again. ART and function have met.

review_title: Get ready to blow your mind
review_text: If you don't like to cook do not buy this stove. It's way too expensive to just be a decoration. If you do love to cook, this stove is for you. It heats on the stove top very quickly and evenly. The temperature control knobs for the range top are big and bold and there is an additional display on the stove top showing a digital display for each burner with a range of 1 - 9. Don't be afraid to put your cast iron skillets on the surface, just make sure you have the bottom cleaned very well and don't move them around while cooking. I cook home brew and this range has reduced my overall brew time by 30 minutes. The first time I brewed with this range I could hardly keep up, it is that fast. This is plain and simple a cooking workhorse. I continue to be amazed about the performance of this range every time I use it. I have used the convection oven for slow cooking and it seems to handle consistent temperature control pretty well. My wife will probably use the convection oven more than I do but she loves the option for dual-oven temperature control. There is a separation rack that allows dual oven operation and it has a very nice storage position in a slot directly above the warming drawer. The range top also extends over the counter on the sides which gives it a sleek professionally installed looked. Speaking of which, you will need a 240v range cord which is not included and professional installation is recommended. I installed it myself and my best advice is to check range top gap vs. counter top height constantly as you slide the range into position (you do not want to crack the range top). Best range/oven I have ever purchased and I would recommend it to anyone that loves to cook. I did attach part of the cautions included in the owners manual, they are pretty funny.

review_title: Daily users beware, some fatal flaws with this unit.
review_text:
Reviewing the Flex-Duo version of this with induction top.
Let me start off by saying that I really wanted to like this - I had saved up for two years to replace my old electric coil stove, which was slow to heat, difficult to clean, and had non-level burners. This Samsung range seemed like the best unit other than viking, dacor, etc where they start at $5000. I ordered this unit from a big box store with free delivery, and haul-away of my old stove. That all went painlessly, and I have been using the stove at least twice per day for the past month.

Let me start with some pros:
- The unit looks very nice and modern
- It is very easy to clean
- It boils water very quickly and heats evenly
- Dual-oven divider is handy and allows the smaller top half of the oven to be used like a toaster oven, very quick to melt cheese etc using broil setting (but some issues with this feature as well)
- Oven heats quickly and bakes evenly (Edit - there are issues with the oven, see below).

Now the significant cons:

- It's noisy. There's a fan that runs even when just using a small burner on low heat, and it is loud enough to be obvious. Also, there are frequent clicks from somewhere within the unit, it drives my wife crazy. Sometimes there is a weird ultrasonic sound when placing a pan on the burner. All around, a bunch of annoying electronic and whirring noises. My old coil stove was much quieter, and even that one had a noticeable hum.

- The temperature control is digital, so there are only 10 discrete settings from low to power boost. I find it frequently impossible to get the right simmer temperature, setting 2 doesn't simmer at all, setting 3 simmers too much. Additionally, with my old coil stove (which was infinitely variable), I could put a pot of water on and use it is a souse-vide style cooker at very low temperatures. This is impossible with this unit and it a huge let down, now I need to buy an immersion cooker to do what I used to do with no problem and no extra equipment. Samsung should have at least provided half-stops so there could be twenty settings instead of ten. 10 discrete settings is like cooking in 8-bit mode.

- Power boost does not work if you have another burner active (at any power level - WTF??). This kind of makes it barely useful, since in the most frequent case of boiling water for pasta, you may already be preparing a sauce. So you can have the burner at "9" but not power boost, which takes quite a bit longer to get it boiling. This is unacceptable behavior, firstly there is plenty of power overhead to support many burners active at once, and in the rare case where there is not enough overhead, the stove can be intelligent enough to determine when it can and can't support power boost mode. Not being able to quickly boil water when I also have a small pot on a low simmer setting is a ridiculous design oversight.

- The "burners" are very sensitive to the size of pan and type of cookware. The large burner, for example, has a minimum pan diameter of 7.5" in order to work. Well my 10" "everyday pan" has a bottom contact area of just about exactly this size. As a result, it only works about half the time, and I have to constantly jiggle it around so it registers. Another inexcusable design oversight. A 10" frying pan should have no problem using the large element. As it stands, about 40% of the surface of the stove is now only useful for boiling water or making soup, since my large saucepan seems to be the only thing reliably "compatible" with the large element. Edit: I bought a different 10" frying pan, and it works more reliably on the large burner. So be prepared to spend time hunting for just the right cookware.

- Only one oven rack is on roller glides, the rest are the crappy usual style that jam up and have to be jostled around and scrape up the oven paint. For a $3K product, all of the racks should be on rollers, or at least designed to bind up less often than they do, and certainly not a friction mount. In addition, two of the three racks have a metal bar that prevent you from being able to slide out oven pans without lifting them up over the hump. This means one-handed operations are now two-handed, and it's less safe because I have to maneuver around a protruding piece of hot metal that would be very easy to bump with my forearm. I honestly don't know if they QA'd the product design at all.

- You can't broil something on high in the top oven and bake something in the bottom oven. If you can't actually use it like two ovens, don't market it as such.

- Speaking of the oven, I recently discovered that my oven will not hold temperature in bake mode. It preheats fine (verified with an oven thermometer), but then slowly loses heat after preheating, and I mean loses a LOT of heat. I was trying to cook a pizza today, and had the oven preheated to 475. Put the pizza in, and it was in for a long time and still did not seem to be cooking properly. So I stuck an oven thermometer inside and it was only at 350 degrees - WTF? Bumped the setting to 480, oven heated again to the correct temp, then started losing heat again once it reached the set temp. This is obviously a defect and renders the oven useless, will report after trying to have it serviced. THIS SHOULD HAVE BEEN CAUGHT BY QA BEFORE THE PRODUCT LEFT THE FACTORY.

- The touch control panel sucks. There is no force-feedback, and it goes haywire when you wipe it down with a rag. Seriously? You have to engage the control panel lock in order to wipe it down without accidentally turning on all the ovens. Additionally, sometimes just by brushing past it, it will turn on the warming drawer?! The button layout is also needlessly complex and non-intuitive.

So it's fair to say I'm quite disappointed in this unit. Some serious design flaws significantly reduce the utility of some of the standout features, and I almost miss my crappy old coil stove on account of it's super simple operation and reliability. I hope that Samsung takes this feedback and improves their future products.

product_title: SAMSUNG NE58H9970WS Slide-In Induction Range, 30-Inch, Stainless Steel
review_title: As close to gas as you're going to get if you're stuck on electric
review_text:
First off electric cooking in general stinks compared to gas. If you don't have gas, induction is as close as you're going to get and arguably in some ways better (except a gas stove will last a lot longer for sure) . We're not big cooks, just normal fare to get the kids fed, just picked this up as wife wanted a slide in and if I'm going to spend a grand on elements may as well spend a bit more and get the latest. The safety of the cooktop attracted me as the kids grow older and they help make dinner. Also I like knobs this has them.

We've had this unit for about 9 months now so keep that in mind, it's not a long term review. Also ours was not purchased on amazon but that's one of the places people go for reviews. Before purchase I read every review and article I could find...let me hit the high points

* does it make noise, yes a very slight hum on the burners, and there's a fan that runs for a bit to cool circitry. The hum, I don't even hear it maybe just a little...in hindsight I can't believe the nonsense I read in reviews on that, I have two sets of cookware calphalon (which a few are induction ready) and cruisinart induction ready try-ply. From the reviews I thought it was going to sound like Nikola Tesla was performing experiments or something in the room.

You will hear the fans that cool the circuitry, pretty soft, maybe about the same level as low on a quality non birdcage motor vent hoot.
Convection does make noise from the fan, any convection does. Convection is awesome, everything is cooked properly from kids pizza, corndogs whatever that stuff is to real meals we cook...the kids stuff used to always not seem 100% or you weren't sure. . We don't have the flex duo model.

* knobs are sensitive you just bump the range and turn something on lol, anyways no biggie the burners shut off after a period of time if no pan is put on them. A real nice bonus.

* burners do require a certain coverage to work, otherwise they'll shutoff with a beep notice. I thought that was going to be a big deal but it wasn't at all, I never have any problems.

* heat up time is as good as they say, it is crazy FAST, I don't wait more than a minute for anything to get up to temp or so I don't time it I just know I can't go off for 10 minutes like I used to with old electric waiting for heat time. A small pan of water is boiling in under 2 minutes? or so. Burner temp much more like gas, reduce the heat it's reduced....no waiting for elements to cool down so you tend not to overcook if you're in a rush. I feel the induction burners are tons more controllable than elements, low feels like low instantly, medium simmer all work very well and more like gas in terms of reaction.

* we cook with paper towels on the top all the time sauces, bacon,etc makes cleanup much quicker.

* keep in mind the absolute minimum height for this stove is 36 inches. that's a standard cabinet height + 3cm granite. If you've refloored around your cabinets and have a 3cm (~1 1/4inch) granite, you'll be ~ 1/4 inch short from touching the counter top. We found the easiest way to remedy that was to cut the pads off the feet, that gives you more than the 1/4 so you have some play, cutting out the floor will make it too difficult to slide into your spot.

* I read a few reviews about people breaking tops. I'm pretty convinced from reading reviews on all products and working in technical support *no* one reads a manual, the glass lips are supported under the edge by steel but there should be a 1/16 space above your counter all around. I suspect people are slamming pans, or overheating pans or something. I can't say for 100% but I'm not worried about this after 9 months.

* the wifi thing...really? I didn't research this and don't care about it but from a quick glance at the manual it requires the Samsung hub things.

* the led flames *are* cool when used with stainless. I really got sucked in by those lol. In hindsight with induction I find myself putting down paper towels all the time and cooking over those. so I don't have to do post cleanup. So in the end the led's weren't that big of a deal but still nice indicator. 1 month later I forgot they were there.

* I'm hesitant about long term reliability but induction has been around a long time, examining the parts diagrams look reasonably ok to repair diy of course as nothing is worth calling repair folks in for these days. review_title: My LG fridge may put me into an early grave.
review_text:
We enjoyed our LG fridge for about six months. Then, the never-ending battle began.

First, we heard a knocking sound. After answering the door to no one for the tenth time, we realized it was the fridge. I Googled. I read the manual. I scratched my head. “Unplug it,” everything more-or-less told me. Great; restart it. Hold down CTRL+ALT+DELETE at the same time. Got it.

I left it unplugged for the recommended four hours. Then I powered it back up and the knocking immediately commenced. A few days later, we got the IF error code.

Error code? A refrigerator has an error code? Seriously. This was too complicated already. Once again, I turned to Google, the manual, and my scalp. “ I called the store. After all, they had strongarmed us into a warranty I didn’t want, and I’m so glad they did.

So the repairman came out. He told me that these fridges were notorious for breaking down. Then he proceeded to show me how to repair it myself because, “This isn’t the first time and it won’t be the last.”

We took the entire freezer apart to get to the ice blower fan, essentially. It gets frozen solid. Every three months like clockwork.

Was it manageable? Yeah. First world problems and all that. But then other stuff started going down:

-The large mechanism that slides into some other cheap, plastic part did something stupid, so the door wouldn’t always close. So guests would shut our fridge but not shut our fridge, which resulted in …
-A ripped rubber door seal.
-No matter what temp the fridge was set at, food sitting directly on the glass shelves or in two of the three produce drawers would freeze. And we’re not talking about some delightful icy crunch. Entire pieces of fruit, meat, even cheese would freeze solid. Did you know cheese could turn into ice? It can. We cannot store food in half of our fridge. (However, I lined all of the shelves in newspaper, which seems to have helped. Plus, I can now read about the local elections from a year ago every morning while I get the orange juice.)
-The freezer fan clogs with ice so often, I have to mention it …
-… twice.
-The water dispensing button is starting to stick.
-The ice dispenser clogs on a daily basis. We keep a knife honer nearby to stab into the bin. I repeat, this happens daily.
-It gets fingerprinted to he77. I know this is a hazard of being an appliance in a home where the occupants have hands. But I hate this thing and now I’m just searching for more to add to the list.
-The water valve that connects the water line to the fridge wore out. So now we don’t even get water or ice until I replace it.
-And now the ice maker is broken. That's a $120 part.

We have a second fridge in our house. We got it for free from an apartment complex that was throwing them away. We keep it in the garage as a beer fridge. Dudes, this fridge (I don’t even know the brand) is probably 20 years old (at least), is ugly as sin, and is chugging away like we do on beer.

Meanwhile, my $2,500 LG heartache mocks me with a frozen water melon, incessant ticking, and dripping water.

Unlike most other refrigerators with icemakers, this one does not use up any significant internal space with the ice-maker. I called LG and they claimed it meant that the water pressure was too high and that the ice tray was overfilling with water... I said that makes no sense, the sensor isn't sensing that the ice is piling up!!! Because my fridge was outside of the LG warranty and outside of the 3-year Geek Squad extended warranty that I purchased like a good girl, I could not get it repaired. So now, if I want ice, I have to turn the ice maker on and then make a mental note to turn it off within a few hours.

Now, October 2019 my fridge and freezer stopped cooling. Within a matter of 11 hours my frozen food was thawing out and the products in the fridge were almost warm! I just stocked my fridge a few days prior and over half of my food was spoiled. Unreal! If the power had gone out my food wouldn't have spoiled that quickly!! When I went to bed the night before my food was cold. Waking up in the morning my food is almost warm?! When I called LG they said the fridge was outside of warranty but they would repair this as a "courtesy" since it is a cooling problem. What they failed to mention was the lawsuit against them about these two KNOWN, RELATED ISSUES!! I paid somewhere around $2500 for this soon-to-be obsolete boulder. Buyer beware!!!

review_text:

After a couple of weeks the LG repairman finally came out and replaced the sensor in the door. All was well for a while. Last night it happened again. Here is what I think is happening; if you are not SUPER careful to keep food from blocking the air vents, ice builds up behind the panel. The fridge stops cooling and the alarm goes off. The fridge is cooled by the freezer. I removed the freezer food and used a hair dryer aimed at the vents to "defrost" the freezer. The beeping stopped, the fridge is cooling again. The door alarm is really annoying. It can't be disabled, so when you are loading food from the store or cleaning out the fridge, the beeping will incessantly continue. Two more things I don't like; the white surface is so delicate, it got scratched up from tiny magnets we used, and your toenails will be ripped off if you open the door barefoot, since the door is so low. We put masking tape on the floor as a reminder to step back when opening the door. Not attractive. If you buy this fridge, get an extended warranty!

review_text:
Our old Gibson freezer lasted 46 years, and was still working when we go this new frost-free freezer. The only reason we stopped using the Gibson was that it had to be defrosted manually several times a year. This Frigidaire model FFFH20F2QWC died after just 2 years and 9 months of use. While it worked, it was extremely loud. The compressor ran constantly. Today when it died we discovered the door gasket was loose at the bottom, which probably caused it to run too much and burn itself out.

UPDATE: As stated above, I discovered that the door gasket had come loose at the bottom, allowing cold air to escape, and causing continuous running of the compressor. I unscrewed the screws at the bottom of the door and re-tightened the gasket. after letting the freezer "rest" for a day or so (we put some frozen stuff in the refrigerator freezer compartment and threw out the rest), I tried starting it up again, and it worked! Now it doesn't run constantly, and it seems like it may even be less loud than it was before. I will upgrade my rating from one star to two.

review_title: Shameful customer support. I would not recomend them to an enemy.
review_text:
Off the bat - the worst customer support I've ever experienced, and I am referring to LG Electronics, not Amazon.

We had this refrigerator for less than 20 months before it died on us or a weekend we were out of home, wasting TONS of expensive grosseries and more importantly a lot of frozen expressed milk that we were storing for my 9mo. Months worth of supply, that takes a lot of commitment to save up. This is irrelevant to the LG unit and not their responsibility, but the grief was real.

I don't have to elaborate on the fact that machines break. Sometimes too soon, but what can you do? It is not about the fridge, it is about the customer support and their insulting INDIFERENCE to their customers.

Nov 18, 2017: After calling LG Support, they referred us to an authorized contractor to perform the service. Of course, there was no appointment available before the next weekend. A week wasted and left to micromanage our own and the 9mo's life without a working fridge.

Nov 25th: Appliance technician (Ben) visits, diagnoses a working compressor but probably a malfunctioning sealed system. Quotes north of $1800 repair after parts and labor.I follow up with a call to LG Service # on the LG.com webpage, which leads me to an out-of-country calling center apologizing on their system being down, wasting 30+ minutes in the process of me waiting for a human response. Next call on the Phone # provided on the Refrigerator's manufacturer’s label gets a faster response. 10 min later the lady I spoke with understands my frustration and promises me to do her best to secure free parts and cover the labor cost through the contractor. Offers to call the company herself, but by the time of the call (it was early afternoon, perhaps 2PM?) the service contractor who by that time reports off for the day. She promises to follow up on Monday, Nov 27.

Nov 27th: I call the service contractor around noon, asking whether LG had contacted them. It is a negative. I decided to give them some time. Mistake.
Nov 29th: I call LG support again, asking for any progress. I am notified that although there is a written notice on my case on the issue with my fridge and the promise about free labor + parts, it case was not forwarded by the caller internally. I am also notified that I would need to provide the proof of purchase for my case to proceed only after I upload pictures/scans of proof of purchase. I am also notified that I am covered to request a replacement instead of a repair as the fridge has been out of order for more than 10 days. I choose that as the preferable option and I upload the purchase receipt through the link provided on the same day. The system assigns me a case number, apparently for the 1st time, cause they did not care for that before. Mistake.
Dec 08: I chat with LG Support after hearing nothing on my case and having no updates through their online case portal. I am notified that my case was “rejected because it was lacking information”, the information being the receipt and diagnosis that Riddle Appliance technician provided - but was never asked for by LG support: they’ve only requested the proof of purchase and actually had verbally promised to contact Riddle Appliance themselves ASAP. Never happened apparently, and I am to blame. I am assigned a new case number, which further down the road they will use as an excuse because each case # apparently gives them the right to postpone responding to me "3-5 working days".
Dec 12: I chat with LG support again. No updates, I am told it would take 3-5 days after the Dec 8, so I should hear back from them by the end of the week. Guess? Did not happen.

Dec 15: I chat, I call, "3-5 days did not pass", nothing we can do. Each call or chat is roughly 20-30min long between waiting for a human responce btw, good luck if you happen to work in the day.

Dec 18: I call again, I demand a response right there and then, wasting no less than 2hr on the phone bounced from one person to the other, I get an appointment with the "Authorized Tech dept". You know, the one that they should have appointed me to DAY FRIKKING ONE and was NEVER mentioned. What I had mentioned IN WRITING, is that I should have the unit REPLACED. But no, they would have to diagnose it 1st.

Dec 19: I have to take the day off, wait for the technician. He comes, takes his time to bash the contractor they've sent me originally - the one I was referred to by HIS COMPANY - he insists that they - in general, not just the one I had over - are the worst and that he doesn't understand why they use them. Great. Thank you.
He proceeds with the repair. My now 11mo baby is around. I had to ask whether it was safe. He says it is safe, but I will "burn, so maybe not in the room, open all the doors and windows". "Burn" Apparently meant melt away the connections with copper piping for the compressor. The process produced thousands of molten plastic like particles that filled up our kitchen, every inch in the lower floor of our townhome. These are very soft and smear on touch, making a HUGE mess. I am not a hypochondriac lunatic, but I bet this is not good to be on EVERY LITTLE BOTTLE of the baby I washed this morning, every inch of the floor he rolls and crawls and walks all day and EVERY LITTLE toy he has in the house, or his pen, or his bed, or our furniture fabric. Stained, whole house needs to be cleaned.
Because "professional".

I will have to boycott any LG appliance from now on. The Fridge was fine looking, we would not pick it otherwise, but please, from the outsourced calling center in India and who-knows-where that had a disconnect with the main offices, to multiple case # and whatnot, I cannot blame individuals, I can only follow the money and who benefits from the lack of customer service, which is noone but the company for their tactics.

review_title: If you have momentary power disturbances, expect to lose a lot of food.
review_text:
I have very mixed feelings about this freezer unit.

The good: I'm a professor of electrical engineering, and not much into aesthetics, but this is really a beautiful freezer, inside and out. 20.5 ft^3 of space is a lot of room and lets my family cook many meals in advance and store them ready for particularly busy weeks. The outside does not get noticeably warm even during defrost cycles. It has a large LED display showing the desired set temperature.

The bad: The LED should, in my opinion, show the actual temperature, not the desired set temperature. I want to know what the fridge is actually doing; I already know what I'd like it to do! So you still need to purchase a separate thermometer for the inside of the fridge.

But the biggest problem is how it handles power brownouts. If the freezer experiences a power blackout, it will reset as expected and continue to cool once the power is restored. But if your area experiences a brownout (for instance, a momentary drop in voltage by about 20%,(as commonly occurs just before or after a blackout), the electronics do not reset; instead the control board displays an error condition and locks up, allowing the food to spoil. It is easy to manually reset by unplugging/plugging the freezer, but easy to miss if the freezer is in the basement and you were at work or sleeping during the brownout. Thinking I just had a bad control board I replaced it, but it has the same problem. It's easy to duplicate if you have a VARIAC to simulate a brownout, but you cannot duplicate it by plugging/unplugging because it is only triggered by significantly reduced voltage levels, not outages. This is the kind of poor design that should have been caught during quality control testing, and is reflected in complaints other owners have posted in online forums.

You can fix this in one of several ways. The simplest is to buy a remote freezer temperature monitor/alarm. That's not ideal since it requires monitoring, but better than not monitoring it. A timer that automatically cycles the freezer off for a few seconds and then on every 6 hours or so would also work, but would not be good for the long-term health of the compressor. A better way is to build a device that automatically cycles the power to the freezer a few minutes after power is restored following any power disturbance. If you are electrically-inclined I'll send you the schematics, PCB files, and code for mine. Frigidaire: we shouldn't have to engineer things like this for a 1k freezer - just spend the $0.75 to add a capacitor and a power-management IC to your control board and eliminate the problem.

I decided to buy a new refrigerator rather than take the chance that I would have to poor money into repairs only to have a buggy refrigerator. This refrigerator cost almost $3,000 and now only two and a half years later I am buying another one.

I got a letter from a law firm a few weeks ago telling me that as an owner of an LG refrigerator I was party to a class action suit regarding the unreliability of this product.

All in all dealing with LG has been a very expensive and unpleasant experience. I feel that I have an obligation to my fellow consumers to share my experience so that you may take this into consideration before you spend a lot of money on an LG refrigerator that may not live up to your expectations.
