CONS:  The delivery people said the power cool feature would shut off automatically once it reached the pre-set temperatures.  That didn't happen & I had to call customer service to ask how to shut it off.  Also, the Samsung customer care people while friendly are not very good at explaining the control panel and the manual does not explain the control panel well at all.  For example, for the "ice off" feature to be in the off position, a cup icon lights up on the control panel.  The book does not explain this and customer care kept saying when the "ice off button lights up it is off" and when it is not lit the feature is on.  ????  The button does not light up.  Icons show up or disappear in the control panel depending on what button you push and the manual does not identify the icons nor explain them and customer care does a poor job of explaining them.  After much painful discussion, I was able to confirm that the cup icon in the control panel lighting up after pushing the ice off button means the ice making feature is off. Kind of backwards thinking technology but okay, and I hope they are correct.  So, another con is an obscure manual and unnecessarily complicated control panel.  I also want to note that I purchased this item sight unseen, over the internet.  I was not sure what "stainless-look" would actually look like.  The housing of the unit is like a silver vinyl material like a regular fridge and the front and doors are stainless and they DO get fingerprinted easily!  Another con.  But the item description on the site where I purchased it said it was not energy star rated and it is according to the accompanying packaging materials an Energy Star appliance so another pro.  Overall, it's just attractive, affordable, it holds a lot and is quiet.  I'm happy! Never wrote a review before but had to recommend this item!

product_title: LG WM4270HWA TurboWash 4.5 Cu. Ft. White Stackable With Steam Cycle Front Load Washer - Energy Star
review_text:
This washing machine is a bit of an enigma. It is one of the few front loading washing machines within my price point that has three, yes three, additional rinse cycles and this alone was critical in my decision making process as I have severe allergies. So LG won major points here! And while it throughly cleans clothes extremely well (as with all new HE washers), it has one major flaw....if you home has high water pressure you will have the infamous "water hammer"! This is a major design flaw with many new HE front loaders and if you purchase this one, you must also purchase a water hammer resister to keep you pipes from thumping when the machine is cycling. Water hammer resisters are only $10.00 each but it's the principle that matters. I would have given this machine 5 stars as it cleans like none other, can accept a large volume of clothing articles; will save on water, electricity, and offers a myriad of wash cycle options to include its on onboard water heater, but it's the need to purchase additional equipment that influenced my decision.

Update 5.8.2017: I am updating this as a forewarning to potential LG customers. I've had this washer now for a less than 2 years of time and the design flaw reported which did not properly address those with high water pressure finally gave way. Thank God I purchased the extended warranty as my "intake cold water valve" gave way several weeks ago. It's amazing that LG's replacement part was redesigned. Hmm imagine that! I believe that LG redesigned this part due to a plethora of issues with this washer. The kicker is that my infamous "water hammer" issue has been minimized by the replacement part. This machine cleans very well and I really like the customized wash settings but before you even think about purchasing any LG (or other brand for that matter) do your homework! Hope this helps!

review_text:
Best machines on the market at this price bracket.

Before I go in to my own review, I want to point out (as per the comments on both his reviews) that Amazon reviewer "Steve" who has posted two identical negative reviews actually own a DIFFERENT MODEL (WM2650HRA, a cheaper and older unit). It seems he's cluster bombing any LG models on Amazon with this review and posting it twice - While he may be frustrated with his models, it's completely misleading for anyone looking at these machines because they are incredible.

My review: We needed new machines for home and I just wnated the best of the best. Sadly, since Maytag flooded the market with cheap machiens the high end of the market has narrowed considerably. I was advised by my local appliance store to buy Electrolux units (EIFLS60LT Washer & EIMED60LT dryer). It turned out to be the single worst purchase of any device in my lifetime; I won't go it in to here but after a year long battle with ElectroSUXS, 11 technician visits and 60+ hours of my life I'll never get back, they finally and begrudgingly sent replacements....which turned out to be BROKEN.

Thankfully the silver lining of this was the opportunity to get my money back from them! After a lot of research, which firstly involved talking to the various technicians that were coming to attempt to fix the Electrosuxs units, every single one said "LG", without even hesitating "easy and cheap to fix, if they ever need it" was the same response from each one.

So I got these units from LG (WM4270 range) and after 4 months of use, I could not be happier. So much, that I just ordered a second pair for my business, even though the warranty doesn't cover commercial use. I don't care - they're that good.

Firstly, HUGE drum size, yet small overall unit footprint. I can do 15-20 large, soaking wet towels without them even flinching. They also have a ton of of programs but they keep it simple on the dial. If you want to customize the programs then you can easily, using the little matrix buttons for each setting (temp, soil, spin speed etc) and a nice touch is that if you try to go outside what is sensible for that setting it won't let you (i.e. you're trying to to go max temp on a delicates setting). Simple things like this make it a real breeze to use if you just want it for basic functions but then you can also get really advanced with completely customized programs if you need (I haven't bothered yet).

These units are also really fast. Sub 20 min wash cycle and the paired dryer unit will dry a huge load of heavy clothes in around 45 mins.

I could go on and on, but honestly, these are incredibly machines, period.

The only single issue that these have (the entire LG range have it) is that the internal valves for the hot and cold water feeds open and close very quickly. This can lead to water hammering (google it) in older houses where pipes aren't strapped or very long pipe runs, but this doesn't bother me as I have strapped pipes and hammer arrestors installed.

I use liquid HE detergent so this hasn't been a problem, but I wonder if powders or pods would completely dissolve in such cool/cold water.

review_text: I needed a washer and dryer that would fit into a space of about 28 inches deep and 25 inches wide.  This is hands down one of the best units I could have purchased.  I have a family of 5 and the laundry is constantly going.  I needed something that would handle everything I could throw at it.  This unit does exactly that.  I am a second floor condo unit.  I do not have a dryer vent pipe and really didn't want to deal with putting one in.  The unit is stacked (the stacking kit comes with the dryer) and we drain the dryer condensation through the drain pipe.  Some people are concerned the drying time is longer with these condensation units however I find the drying time very comparable to a full-size unit.  With the exception of drawing water, the washer is very quiet.  Regular size washing pods are too much for these little guys.  I have done a few loads and find it's simply too much detergent.  Now, I place a tablespoon of H.E. detergent in the plastic cup that comes with the laundry soap, and I throw the whole cup in the washing machine. review_title: DO NOT EVEN CONSIDER BUYING AN LG PRODUCT
review_text:
I bought this unit last Aug. We bought all LG appliance for our new home, spending double what we would have paid for American products. I started getting fan noise from the upper section. The problem turned out to be ice build up from LG setting the defrost cycle thermostat incorrectly. LG sent out and "LG certified" technician about a week after I called. The guy was an idiot. Because the refrigerator fan was not making the noise when he arrived, he decided the refrigerator was too close to the wall. He opened up the unit behind the refrigerator to show me the fan there was running without making any noise, then moved the refrigerator a foot into the kitchen and told me it needed more room in the back to keep ice from building up. Three days later the refrigerator failed completely with and error code of "E rF", which LG informed me meant the refrigerator fan had failed completely. LF referred me to a different service provider since the first was was incompetent. A new guy showed up, explained what was wrong, then disappeared. I called at least 20 times a week for two weeks with no response from the service technician. LG referred me to another service center, but I got no response from them after leaving multiple messages on their business phone. LG finally found another service technician who is not in network with them. They sent him a work order (a five day process), and he showed up. This guy is great! He knew what the problem was, and called LG support while at our house to have the part shipped. He was a finally able to repair the unit. The whole process took two months! I was furious that I paid $3000 for a refrigarator that failed five months after buying it, and we went two months without a refrigerator.

I hoped that was the end of our problems, but no such luck. On June 30 I came home to find the refrigerator was completely shut off. It had tripped the breaker, and would not power back up when I reset the breaker. I confirmed there was power to the outlet, then called LG tech support again. I insisted they issue a repair order to the technician who was able to fix the unit before. He came and determined that the main control board was bad, with a blown component visible on the board. It took three weeks for LG to issue the order to the technician and ship the part. The service tech replaced the system board and stayed long enough to confirm the refrigerator was powered up and going through the appropriate cycles. Unfortunately, the refrigerator failed four hours later, again with the "E rF" error code.

So, we're not another four weeks into a dead refrigerator after already having it not working for two months earlier this year.

I will NEVER EVER EVER EVER EVER buy another LG product.

review_title: DEAD After Only 14 Months! -- More Expensive To Fix Than Replace.
review_text:
My previous machine was a KENMORE Top-Loader that lasted an incredible 18 years. Then, when it was necessary to replace this antiquated laundry hero, I considered a newer high efficiency machine, and ultimately settled on a not-so-cheap LG WM3370HWA, which lured me in with its advanced features. I felt it might provide an edge cleaning set-in stains, and handling sizeable loads, while reducing impact on the environment.

After four months, problems began, with the washing machine and matching dryer, so I called LG support, and they had me place my telephone against the machine and push some buttons so they could listen to tones the machine produced, to find out what was wrong. Okay, so it told them I needed to change detergent amount and settings. Problem solved. Temporarilly. Another 10 months... right after the washing machine was off warranty, it began screaming, as loud as an abnoxious high-pitched piercing siren every time it spun the clothes! I contacted SEARS, where I purchased the LG Washer and they callously informed me... "Well, these machines don't last forever, seems to me, you were just unlucky with the machine you bought, and you just got a bad one, there's nothing we,re going to do about it!." They refused to help me further, refusing to accept any additional calls I placed to SEARS.

I then tried to contact LG directly, and found their support line required that I input a cell phone number where I was willing to receive regular text messages (advertising?) from LG. The automated LG system then announced if I refused to leave a phone number where I was willing to receive text messages, the call would then end. I did not respond, and the LG voice responded in a very abrupt, loud tone, GOOD BYE---...

I then checked with a local repair center and duscovered bearings go bad, with corresponding cost equal to what I paid for the washer new. Unfortunately, since the machine was still fairly new, many of the parts are not yet available on the market and I would have to wait another 3-6 months, for them to be made available by the manufacturer, according to this repair shop. This simply emphasized the mistake I made in purchasing an LG Washer.

I strongly advise against anyone considering either an LG WM3370HWA, or any LG product, period, due to observed inability to assure quality, poor longevity and value for the price paid, and for inadequate or non-existent customer support to enable post-sale repair problems. It concerned me with the WM3370HWA, that following my initial contact, I was not able to locate a single LG Customer Support center, other than the one described.

For these reasons I will not recommend LG under any circumstance.

review_title: An outstanding performer plagued with technical and quality control complications!
review_text:
Bottom line: if you want a french door fridge with no water dispenser (they get bacteria & grimy + also not kid friendly), this the model to get!

I'm pretty annoyed at the Con's listed below, so I can't rate this otherwise awesome fridge five stars.

UPDATE (Jan 4, 2016):
I've had to get the fresh food fans replaced twice now in 11 months. Luckily all free of charge through 1 year GE's warranty service. There was a known issue with the original fans, and the initial replacement fans were even more faulty. Faulty fans can make the fridge noisy, can spoil your food, can freeze your food, and can even cause an error state that the entire fridge shuts down. Just got my 2nd replacement today and the service tech assured me these will work and have been in use for a while. This is so widespread of an issue that technicians now place a sticker on the fridge stating "the fresh food fan has been upgraded." Have I gotten free updates? Yes. But I've gone through a lot of headaches getting it fixed, scheduling service, and frankly I'm annoyed GE isn't more proactive. They don't contact customers when there is a widely known defect. At the very minimum I want a red LED indicator for me to call GE when an error condition initially occurs, not waiting for a serious system failure. The tech said my problems were happening for a while. This fridge has a computer inside of it, unfortunately you can't access it's detailed information without a GE technician. When the fridge works, it works great. GE service quality has been great. I'm left disappointed with the overall experience unfortunately, which could be easily remedied with more upfront information provided to users.

Pro's:
+ Quiet!
+ Ice produced fast. Large ice tray.
+ Several LED lights illuminate the whole fridge from multiple angles. Most fridge's just have one bank of lights that limit lighting.
+ Extremely deep door trays. E.g. you can fit two 1-gallon juice jugs in just one door tray.
+ Easily configurable shelves.
+ Lots of freezer space. The comparatively additional space in this 28.5 c.f. appliance was put into the freezer compartment.
+ The french door's mullion strip works great. I like that it's attached to the left door since I use the right door more often.
+ No chemical smell in the fridge when first opened! That makes me feel my food will be safer from leeching chemicals. I still initially washed down the insides with a mixture of lemon juice and white vinegar for sanitization.
+ The fridge & freezer drawers slide and align much better than competing refrigerator models.
+ There is a water filter bypass plug included that can be used if your water is already filtered. I already have a whole-house water filter so I loathed having to purchase separate consumable fridge filters that competing models require. GE's manual even recommends you NOT use the fridge filter if you have an external filter! I appreciate the honesty.
+ The fridge's sticker with model & serial numbers has a QR code that makes it simple to register the product using a smartphone. This is just a little thing that made me happy- it's clear that GE has more brains!
+ The top of the french doors have recessed handles built-in, making it easy to swing doors. I'm 6'2" so shorter folks may never think to reach up there, and I never noticed I naturally did this until I felt the handle. Another small detail that makes me appreciate this fridge.

Con's:
- No dairy bin for your butter. Enclosed dairy bins keep your butter slightly warmer than the rest of the fridge so it's easier to spread. Promotes good fridge organization, too. GE doesn't even make a dairy bin part for this model so you can't even order one.
- There are only three trays provided for each door. The doors clearly fit four trays per side and the extra two really should have been provided. I want the extra storage space so now I have to pay out more money to GE Parts in a separate order. Manufacturer cost cutting at it's worst!
- Fans can get noisy. No way of knowing it's a fan issue or your imagination without an official GE technician visit.
- High number of fan failures for this model. See "update" note above.
- There is a buildup of solid ice at the back of the ice drawer. Tech said that new fan may take care of this. I'll update this if the issue goes away.

Other's:
~ Be careful unpacking! The glue on the Styrofoam blocking is very strong. Normally not an issue when it's attached to the plastic wrapping, but if it comes off and attaches to your floor (mine did) or the unwrapped surface of the fridge (mine did also) it may never fully come off!
~ The french doors were uneven on my initially delivered model, the door seal wasn't appropriately applied, and some of the plastic wrap is still stuck in crevices. (Delivery guys banged this one up a bit, too.)
~ I'm getting a replacement for the manufacturer defects listed here and I'm hoping the new model won't have these issues. I'm honestly really disappointed in GE's quality control on the product that I received. Update: new replacement doors finally fixed my Styrofoam issues. Took two replacements to get it right.
~ GE is now developing a WiFi device to retrofit older GE fridges if they have a RJ45 port in order to connect their refrigerators to smart home systems. I don't think this model has a network port; if you're into integrating smart devices you may want to consider this when buying a fridge. NOTE: GE customer support has no idea about this program. I wouldn't count on this model having the connected sensor.
~ Minor inconvenience: when you lock the door temperature controls, the temperature reading is limited to the fridge sensor. I would like to press the freezer button to at least see (not change) the freezer temperature, but you can't without first unlocking. It would have been much better to just display both temperatures at once so you don't even have to jump between fridge and freezer settings. The engineers missed this detail.

product_title: Frigidaire FGGC3645QS 36" Gas Cooktop, Stainless Steel
review_title: Its a very good cooktop for $700
review_text:
For $700 I think this 36 inch wide cooktop is an excellent value. Its not a high end, super fancy cooktop, its a basic cooktop. It has one large burner in the middle, one med/large burner front/right, two med burners on left and one small burner back/right. The stainless deck is not especially thick metal so the unit feels a little on the cheap side when you go to install it, but its perfectly adequate. Now the grates on the other hand are super beefy and give the unit a high quality look. All 5 ignitors worked and all the burners have adequate control range from full blast down to simmer. It comes with a new pressure regulator valve and its factory jetting for natural gas (and includes propane jets). My original gas flex hose fit fine. Overall I'm very happy with the purchase.

Now the installation was another story. My old cooktop was a 36" Dacor, it lifted out easily enough. However I soon discovered that although the counter top cut out width (left to right) was OK, the front to back depth was too narrow by about 1/8 of an inch. Not only that neither the front nor back cut out was straight. This was the fault of whoever built my house 30 years ago, not the cooktop's fault. It took me about 2.5 hours using a rasp to remove enough of the plywood and tile grout to allow it to drop in. I must have lifted it in and out a dozen times, each time removing a little more plywood and grout, etc to get this unit to fit, but it fits perfectly now.

review_title: It had absolutely the worse possible condenser ever put on a refrigerator
review_text:
I have had this fridge for 5 years. I decided it's about time to clean the condenser coils. I am a former refrigerator service man. They're supposed to be cleaned yearly, every 6 months if you have pets.
I pulled off the back panel and was completely dismayed! It had absolutely the worse possible condenser ever put on a refrigerator! I didn't even know they made these anymore!
It is a tight coil of tubes covered in aluminum bristles. Like a bottle brush wound in a coil, then air blows thru it. It picks up every piece of lint, hair or dust. There is no good way to clean it. Vacuuming only takes off the lint on the surface. I used to condemn to the junk pile every refrigerator I found with this type of condenser, because they were always clogged and have long since hammered the valves out of the compressor rendering the whole unit a piece of junk.
And to top it off when I looked to the left there was not a new style linear-scroll-loaf (whatever they call it) type compressor. In it's place was an old style reciprocating compressor! Which are not as energy efficient or dependable as a new style compressor.
Today I will drag an air hose in from the shop and blow out the condenser with 120 psi compressed air. Then spray the condenser with Awesome Orange cleaner from Odd Lots to eliminate the kitchen grime that makes dirt stick. Then blow that out with compressed air.. Then I will clean up the huge freakin mess! Then I will repeat the entire process in my tenants home and in my camper. YES! I was stupid enough to buy three of these! And I can look forward to repeating the process every year!
I don't know if every model Samsung has this cheap condenser. I saw in a video where LG has them too!
So BEFORE you buy a refrigerator, peek in the vent slots in the back and if you see some coils that look like a bottle brush made from aluminum, about one inch in diameter...just walk away. Look for one with black smooth condenser. Sometimes they're flat, sometimes rolled in a coil. But t least the dirt comes off. And a long, not round compressor.
Manufacturers sometimes call these SELF-CLEANING simply because there is no way to clean them.

review_text: We love to entertain, and take drink making seriously. I was immediately disappointed to discover that despite the "cubed/crushed" settings on the dispenser, the cubed ice comes out a mixture of cubed AND crushed. I assumed the unit was malfunctioning, but a call to Samsung taught me otherwise. I was told that this is just how they work, and that replacement or repair of the ice-making unit would not be possible. This may seem a small inconvenience, but since this was the sole reason for replacing the refrigerator, and since it is impossible to make shaken cocktails with crushed ice, it is nothing but a huge and expensive disappointment. I've never encountered this in any other ice-making refrigerator I've ever owned, and have no idea why Samsung refrigerators are incapable of dispensing just cubed ice, but they are not, and they fully acknowledge the fact. Based on my conversation with Samsung, this "feature" is not model specific, so if this is a factor in your refrigerator purchase you might want to look at another manufacturer.

product_title: LG DLGX3371W 7.4 Cu. Ft. White Stackable With Steam Cycle Gas Dryer - Energy Star
review_text:
My typical use is to dump the clothes in, select "cotton/normal," select start, and come back in 75 minutes or so to unload the dry clothes.

5 months after purchase, I performed the same operation, and when I came back, the clothes were still wet. I restarted the same cycle, and could feel no heat at the vent. I started a support chat with LG, who told me that when the "energy saver" mode is operational, which is the default and cannot be permanently disabled, the dryer will not apply heat to the load. Now, I've used this dryer for 5 months, and I have never experienced this behavior, so either she is incorrect, or the machine was not working as designed for 5 months, but suddenly as of today it is. The user manual says use of the energy saver mode will increase drying times (from minutes, to days or weeks, apparently), but nowhere does it say heat will not be part of the cycle.

To add insult to injury, the support person told me that if a service call was created, I would be charged, even though the machine is under warranty, as it's an end-user issue.

Summary: if you wish to use heat in your drying cycle with this machine (apparently not a normal situation, per LG), you have to manually disable the energy saver mode each and every time you run the dryer on one of the default cycles. Basically, take the behavior of every other dryer ever made, and do the opposite of what you'd do on those, and you'll be in good shape. I can only guess that their washing machines may have a "water saver" mode as the default, where you have to manually specify each time that you want the load to use water in the wash cycle.

6 months after purchase, and now it's showing error code TE1 on the display and refusing to finish a cycle, so I have to call for service. 6 months! Is there anyone in the world that thinks this passes for quality? Not that I think any other manufacturer is any better - the mechanicals on all of these appliances are fine, it's the super cheap electronics, which serve no functional purpose other than make it look fancy, that are the Achilles' heel.

With a large household, I believe we have cut our time in half at least for washing and drying and the cloths look and smell clean.  The units are very quiet; our laundry room is next to the kitchen, next to open den and you cannot hear them during operation.  At first we did have a rocking motion from the washer; however, we failed (at first) to level with a level and very important on the feet of the washer and dryer is to adjust the feet, level and use the locking bolt on each foot.  Once we leveled the machines and used the locking bolt to lock each foot in place, we had no additional rocking problems from the washer.  We are following all of the operation procedures for the machines, if you have not owned a front loader before there are a few additional maintenance/clean out producers one must incorporate in bi-weekly and monthly routines, but other than this they work as expected and above.  I hope this continues for many years and maintenance and breakdowns do not plague us as I have read about on a few reviews.  My two sets before this LG Pair was Roper sets and they each lasted over 10 years each with few easy maintenance problems (a couple of replaced heating elements on the dryer; very simple to perform on a Ropers).  It may be unrealistic, however, I do hope to come close to 10 years of few maintenance problems with these LG's also (I realize there are more parts, digital, etc).  They look and feel quality made.  For the present, I am very happy with the pair and their performance.

review_title: Just spent ~$700 on this horrible, very bad
review_text:
Save yourself! Just spent ~$700 on this horrible, very bad, no good washer to match the O.K. dryer. Hate it, hate it, hate it! (Don't tell my husband.) Uses so little water that there's no point in the drum rotating; it does not agitate the clothes, it soaks them. I can do a better job in my laundry tub by hand. It takes 84 minutes to run a "Normal" load; 120 minutes--TWO HOURS! to run a "Heavily Soiled" load. You're not allowed to wash bulky items on "Extra Hot," which is one thing you'll need to get ANY kind of load clean. There is a "water plus" feature but you are not allowed to use it with the "Extra Rinse" feature, which is necessary--your clothes need all the help they can get. You're not allowed to set the washer for a hot rinse. This is all stuff it's not easy to find out in the showroom when you're under the gun for a new washer, quick.

Essentially this washer "works" by soaking the clothes in a minimum of water, and using the spin cycle to remove the (somewhat) dirty water. I'll have to start my loads of "Heavy Soil" loads before I go to bed, and run an extra 15 minute "Speed Wash" first thing in the morning. EVERY night. Or maybe get up in the night to run an entire extra cycle. I know the "Energy Star" people think they'e doing us and the environment a favor by mandating standards of minimum water and energy usage, but if you have to run your clothes twice in boiling hot water, that's not really a savings, is it? Stinks, stinks, sticks! Zero stars!

product_title: LG DLHX4072V 7.3 Cu. Ft. Graphite Steel Stackable With Steam Cycle Electric Dryer
review_text:
This machine has many nice features, and as green folks we love the concept- but it has one serious design flaw which causes it to leak water onto the floor after a few month's worth of use. We've seen over a half cup of leakage with heavier loads. In short: this machine may ruin your floors and require frequent visits from LG technicians and a lot of frustrating time on the line with customer support affirming that yes, indeed you do clean your lint trap, (we do, religiously), and no, the vent is not clogged.

So here's the issue: In a conventional dryer, most of the lint gets trapped in the lint trap, with the remainder going out the air vent (this is why you need to clean your dryer vent periodically). In this machine, the residual lint that evades the trap clogs the evaporator (a component of the hybrid system) and never makes it to the air vent. After the evaporator gets clogged with lint every few months, moisture gets trapped and condenses inside the machine and water droplets blow out through the back of machine where the air vent attaches.

We had a technician out, who discovered the cause of the problem. After he cleaned the evaporator, the machine functioned without leaking for a couple of months and then started leaking again. The technician came out again and found the evaporator clogged again. We suspect that the cleaning will become less effective over time as there are areas in the fins and inner surfaces of the evaporator that are hard to get to.

LG has yet to come up with a solution other than sending the tech again. Our warranty expires soon, and we have gotten uncertain information on whether LG will continue to service this design flaw without charge. In any case, it does not seem like a viable long term solution.

We appreciate that LG is trying to adopt a greener technology that has been available for many years in Europe. However, this is a new technology for LG . We did not realize that we were such early adopters of the LG product, and as such have learned the hard way that this early model has a major design flaw. We'll update again if we get a satisfactory solution.

review_title: Super flexible, great looks, trouble fitting normal items into the shelves
review_text:
This fridge really struck me in the store and I am very impressed by the build quality and the innovative freezer storage compartments. The layout of the 4 door is absolutely amazing and wonderful to work with. All my food is perfectly eye level... which might be dangerous for me in the long run!

My first issue when filling this unit was that I kept running into areas where my things did not fit. It is amazing how many items were about 1 inch too tall to fit in a bin, or on a shelf. The flexible shelving is awesome, but 100% necessary to fit a normal jug of OJ, a wine bottle, a 2 liter, etc. I had a lot of condiments that also did not fit into the door bins due to height. Maybe I will need to buy smaller condiment containers (not family size) to remedy this issue. Still trying to figure out exactly where to put everything to maximize storage options...

Here is my biggest suggestion on this refrigerator - If you can fit the bigger 30 cu ft version in your space - Do it. While this feels like there is a lot of storage, I am limited with too many items that are too tall - and having more cubic footage would be awesome. The larger model will have more than enough storage space and the price is the same. I opted for looks over volume... (Counter depth) make your own decision here.

Also, the flexible unit in the lower right is FANTASTIC. I set it up at "chill" which sets the unit to 30 degrees F (-1C) which is just below freezing. I find this perfect for beer, soda, and other beverages. You actually get that crisp cold cola thing! Only water will freeze at this temp, so alcohol or sugar laden beverages will be just fine. The regular fridge is recommended to be set at 37 degrees F. I enjoy keeping food up in the fridge, and beverages in the lower right section. Looks awesome, and makes it super easy for anyone to find the right beverage.

My unit was delivered through a *BIgBox Store* because I was concerned about having a dud and needing to have it swapped out. My local hub had over 100 of this model in stock. Delivery was a breeze. It literally took them less than 10 minutes to unbox and carry the unit into the house. I paid for "hook up" but apparently they only hand you a 1/4" PEX line to hook up yourself. bummer. My RO system requires 3/8" line, so I had some work ahead of me anyway. No issues at all. It fired up, lit up, and chilled down in less than 2 hours. This process could not have been easier in my opinion.

last note - It has an anti fingerprint coating that isn't so anti fingerprint. Oh well.

On the whole, I am truly enjoying this upgrade in the kitchen and look forward to years of use. At least I will be once I figure out how to organize everything in the right places...

product_title: Samsung RF23J9011SR 22.5 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel Counter Depth French Door Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_title: **UPDATED** I love this refrigerator but don't recommend it!! Started having ice maker problems
review_text:
This review is for the Samsung counter depth refrigerator model number RF23J9011SR/AA.
*** UPDATED 9/28/15 with photos***
***UPDATED with some newly found issues: 8/19/15***
***UPDATED 2/6/2019 Downgraded to 3 stars. Started having ice maker problems a few months ago: Needs defrosting and ice gets jammed ejecting from ice-tray and into the bin preventing new ice from being made. No other mechanical problems so far (3+ years). For the price, I expect a perfectly working ice maker for decades (like my last refrigerator).

Original review
We've had this refrigerator for about two weeks. Overall, we absolutely love it. We are a family of 4. We do not stock up on food. We tend to shop several times a week as we live very close to a grocery store. So the counter depth design not only looks great, it has plenty of space for us. So much so, that we have yet to come close to filling it. I believe it would be fine for families of our size that tend to stock up. The refrigerator section is wide and shallow keeping everything within easy reach and view. Hopefully this will cut down on forgotten leftovers hidden in the back that come to resemble biological experiments. The ice maker makes ice cubes at a rate that is on par with every other ice maker on the market including Sub-Zero (I'm getting about 160 cubes/day). The French door freezer design was my #1 reason for purchasing it. Each side of the freezer has two good-sized pull out drawers, a top pull out shelf and shelves in the door to keep everything organized. Each side of the freezer can be set to a different temperature. We use one side as a standard freezer for things like frozen veggies. The other side we set to "Soft Freeze" and use for meat, fish, and sandwich meat. The food doesn't freeze solid, but is kept really cold and fresh! So we gain more refrigerator space as we don't store any meat in that section. I love not having one, giant freezer drawer so that I don't have to bend over and dig for frozen food. Freezers with one big drawer also collect debris on the bottom: crumbs and hair. Yuk!

There are a few, annoyances that, all tolled, keep me from giving it 5 stars:
1) The doors are not smudge/fingerprint free and require frequent wiping.
2) The recessed door handles, while they look stylish, are a bit of a pain. You can't grab them naturally with either hand. My 10 year old son was the first to point this out. You either have to open the right door with your left hand and vice versa or you have to twist your right hand with your thumb pointing down to open the right doors and similarly with the left.
3) None of the drawers pull out far enough. They all have a stop which I feel is too short.
4) This one is probably the biggest issue for me: With the ice dispenser in crushed ice mode, a lot of crushed ice flies all over the floor unless you have a very wide mug or wide mouthed glass that are pressed right up to the opening. For normal sized glasses, ice goes all over.
5) There is a function on the control panel to lock it out so that someone can't change settings by accident (say, inadvertently touch the freezer temp control and change it). When I use that, then the ice and water dispenser stop working!!

I'll be contacting Samsung about items 4 and 5 for sure. Hopefully they are defects that can be addressed with a service call. Lastly, and this one is very very minor, while it is generally very quite, it does emit a gurgling sound on occasion. I know for sure that it is not the water line because it made that sound before we even hooked it up.

To address some issues I've read about in other reviews (from many different sites)
Issue 1) "It only lasted a year and a half.": 2015 is the first year this model was released and there were no previous versions of it. So these reviews must be for the non-counter depth version of this model. The /AA in the model number indicates country of manufacture which is the USA. So the AA is not a version indicator.

Issue 2) "The outside sweats and drips water all over the floor.": The manual clearly states that if this happens, turn off the "Energy Saver Mode." This could happen in humid environments.

Issue 3) "Ice cube making rate is slow.": There are several issues here clearly addressed in the manual. First, upon installation, it may take several days before it makes ice cubes at its normal rate. Secondly, the rate is dependent upon the temperature to which you have the freezer set. Initially, our freezer was set to 0 degrees Fahrenheit and the rate was slow. I set it to -2 and am getting a rate of about 140-160 cubes per day which is the same as every other refrigerator on the market.

Issue 4) "You can't pull out the ice maker bucket to access the ice cubes en bulk." This one is just not true. Maybe they didn't pull hard enough or they are talking about a different model.

About the attached photos: Upper section: There are about 20 condiment bottles on the 2 top-right door shelves alone with room for a couple more. The pot on the bottom-left is an 8.5 quart Calphalon dutch oven. The bottom-right shelf has 3 half-gallon milk containers, 1 one-gallon milk jug, a 90 oz jug of OJ and several other assorted bottles of water and gatorade. Egg cartons fit nicely under the icemaker. Bottom section: Bottom-right: Set to chill. We use it for meats, beer and other adult bevs we like ice cold. Bottom-left is freezer. Mostly frozen veggies and ice cream.

review_text:
Update as of July 2019:

After owning this fridge for four years I honestly and sadly can no longer recommend it or any other Samsung products to anyone. Samsung, I've been a loyal customer and fan going back long before the Note 3 phone.

The ice maker in this fridge is beyond terrible. Over a year ago it stopped making ice. There are multiple defects with the in-door Samsung fridge ice makers. A quick search online and you'll find thousands of complaints scattered across TV news programs, YouTube, and many repair boards and blogs. Samsung is clearly aware of this ice makers manufacturing defects but is unwilling to recall it and make repairs. It appears at least one class action lawsuit has been filed against them. Advertising for this fridge and directly ON the ice maker states it makes 3× the ice of its competitors. If it is broken more often then working it would seem this is false advertising and ripe for another lawsuit.

To get ice from it I have to constantly, every one week or less, pull out the ice maker and defrost it with a hairdryer. A very messy and time consuming process. I've attempted some of the other remedies suggested by Samsung fridge sales people, appliance repairman, and found online with no long term success.

Add my terrible experience after owning two prior Samsung phones and then getting not one but two of the exploding Note 7's before they took the 2nd one back. I've had Samsung tablets and TVs and having spent a good deal on this fridge no longer feel Samsung as a company has the integrity to stand behind or in front of their products. I imagine the employees and people running the company are no longer proud to be associated with it.

Original review:
I've owned this refrigerator since the end of March 2015. I was looking for a replacement water filter and came across the frig on Amazon and out of curiosity read the few reviews on here.

Here are my thoughts after owning it for nine months:

The configuration for my family of four including two small children is wonderful. Having four doors with bins and adjustable shelving allows us more flexibility then any other refrigerator I've seen.

With the flexible shelves in the frig and doors you can pretty much fit items of any height and most widths. As it is counter depth with an ice maker and THREE compressors fitting deep items in it can be trickier.

Looks great but smudges easily. Magnets can be put on the sides but not on the front. Even if they could magnets WILL scratch almost ALL stainless steel.

Our frig is pretty quiet the vast majority of the time accept an average sound level for a frig when water is entering to make more ice.

Ice maker produces ice as fast or faster than most in-door ice making refrigerators. Downside is that you need to use a wide mouthed cup held close to the dispenser top to avoid crushed ice and even cubes when they first come out from missing the cup.

Appears to be far more energy efficient than most other similar refrigerators.

Water comes out of the dispenser at high pressure. The good is that it fills things fast. The bad is shallow cups, measuring cups, or cups with narrow openings often lead to splashing. I find I often use a large cup and then pour the water in to a measuring cup or a bowl for things like oatmeal.

The frig has no protruding handles so there is nothing to break off or catch on when walking by it. The are recessed and a part of the door. I have not found them particularly difficult to get used to opening and my wife and kids including my 5 year old adjusted quickly to them.

As a prior reviewer also pointed out if you use the control lock feature it disables the water and ice. Having small children I think this may have been intentional as my youngest likes the idea of being a big guy and filling his own cups but is too short to see what he's doing and if we're not watching him could make a huge mess of water and ice. However, we have not used the control lock function as he has not attempted to use it without us...yet.

In summary it's a great fridge with a few small issues. My wife loves it as it replaced a traditional French door with the bottom pullout freezer drawer she learned to dislike which we sold with the house when we moved. Those bottom drawers make things difficult to find under layers of frozen food and do collect all kinds of dirt at the bottom. Having the double doors on the bottom with bins and shelves fixes that problem. If the full size version will both fit and look right/good in your kitchen then I recommend purchasing it at about the same price as it will offer you not only more storage space but more storage depth.

review_title: Most Expensive Paper Weight I've Ever Had.
review_text:
We've had this fridge for 10 months. In that 10 months it's worked wonderfully. NO issues that you see with the icemaker that so many other experience. It's a wonderful looking fridge! Everyone that comes is amazed that it has 4 doors and different cooling zones, etc. It just looks different. I was super excited to get this fridge and considering the original price at almost $4k you would expect it to last.

Two weeks ago the bottom portion of the freezer/fridge stopped working. It happened on a Friday and since we were not home on the weekend we came home on Monday to find that everything in the Freezer/cooling zone was bad (that was a nice mess to clean up). Ok, things happen and things break. That's life. However multiple attempts to contact Samsung in this matter ended with sending multiple techs, who flat out told us "we can not fix this" we will put a trouble ticket to Samsung and they will call you. Guess what? They didn't call. Their customer service is on par with cable companies... IE: HORRIBLE. They read from a script and transfer you to multiple people. My wife was on the phone for 2 hours today trying to get a resolution on a fix. They don't seem to grasp that most people can't be without a fridge, especially if you have young children in the house or a new born baby...

I don't have a problem if someone can't fix something, but ultimately there comes a resolution that is quick and responsive, what bothers me is that either my wife or myself have to call off from work because the tech is coming only to be told on the day they should be arriving that "we do not fix that problem, we will contact Samsung for you"... Taking days off cost money, and depending on what you do can be very expensive, so doing this 3-4 times and what you end up having is the cost of the fridge in days that you have missed work.

Now our ice cube maker doesn't work, along with the entire bottom portion of the fridge not working. I'm sorry but for as expensive as this unit is, that is completely unacceptable. We have a "builder" grade fridge that is in the basement that is over 10+ years old AND it's been moved multiple times to different locations and it works, it just keeps chugging along.

If you are looking for a beautiful looking fridge that will WOW people when they walk in but then not work and have to deal with horrible customer service and techs that are unable to fix the fridge, this IS the fridge to get!! I can't stress that enough!

I LOVE Samsung products, I really do, we have a WHOLE slough of their products from TV's, electronics, computer hardware, etc. And I can honestly say this whole experience with their fridge has put such a sour taste in my mouth that I am very reluctant to ever consider them for appliances in my lifetime or recommend them to anyone again.

I will never buy another Samsung product again. I don't care if it's a TV, Phone, Fridge... NEVER AGAIN!

product_title: Samsung RF23J9011SR 22.5 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel Counter Depth French Door Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_title: Nothing but trouble... but eventually fixed by Samsung
review_text:
We got our Samsung RF23J9011 from Home Depot in September 2018 for about $2700 give or take. Man o' man, do I wish I had read the Amazon reviews first! Who thinks about Amazon for large home appliances?

Wee bough the RF23J9011 based on its list of features, which are impressive. We were limited to a counter-depth style and wanted French Doors. We didn't want to pay for Wi-Fi, or some fancy video see-though. The RF23J9011 had exactly the features that we wanted and none that we didn't.

Pre-Covid, delivery was a snap and we had our new Samsung within a week of ordering it. We loved it for about a month.

The first thing that disappointed us was the limited capacity of the icemaker. With only 3 of us we noticed that sometimes we would run out of ice. Not terribly often, but disappointing for a new $2700 refrigerator that we would have for the next 10-15 years. And then after about 3 months, not ice at all. A quick inspection revealed that the ice maker had frozen up, as if there was a leak in it. We chipped away the ice build up manually and the ice maker started working again. We never did find a leak. Then it happened again about 5 weeks later. Exactly the same. A quick check on the internet revealed that almost all of the RF23J9011s had the same problem. A design flaw. Then we started to read about other problems.

When it was 18 months old, the freezer compartment started going wonky. I bought a thermometer to monitor the temperature. Over the course of a couple of weeks it varied from about 10 degrees F to 30 degrees, all the while being set a t (and reading) -5F. I tried unluggingi it to reset the computer. No go. Then it stopped working altogether intermittently. We looked for a local repair service to fix it, and could only find one that worked on Samsungs. They told us some very scary things about Samsung refrigerators, but came out and use an infrared temperature gun to determine that the cooling was OK, but the fan was probably bad. It took a week to get a fan and $262 later the repairman left and said wait 24 hours and call in the morning. The fan didn't fix the problem and the repair guy said he would have to replace the motherboard, but that parts from Samsung were notoriously hard to get. By this time we had long ago transferred everything from the freezer compartments to the large chest freezer in the garage, so things weren't so bad. But after waiting about 3 weeks, the refrigerator started to die.

Now I'd had enough and called Samsung. They gave us the number of the only authorized Samsung repair service called Service Quick. It took me over 2 weeks to get an appointment. When the guy finally shows up, the refrigerator had been completely dead for 10 days. We used bags of ice to keep stuff inside cool. What a mess. It only takes him 15 minutes to tell me that this was a "sealed system problem", meaning everything was still under warranty, and that he's pick up a compressor and be back --- in about 2 weeks. When there was no return call from Service Quick 3 weeks later, I wrote a very long and nasty letter to the Corporate Offices. Two days later I got an email and a phone call from one of the Vice-Presidents, telling me how sorry he was, and promising to call Service Quick and get them out to the house ASAP. A week later I called Service Quick to find out what was happening and they asked me if I wanted schedule a service call. I nearly had a stroke. After scheduling a service call (for about 15 days later), I emailed the Samsung VP back and also tried to call the direct number that he'd given me in the first email. I left a message.

Then I ordered a tiny refrigerator from Amazon I(RCA RFR320-B-Black-COM RFR321 Mini Refrigerator, 3.2 Cu Ft,
$144.99 that arrived in 2 days. I called the VP back he was very apologetic and promised me a full refund. That was a week ago and I've heard nothing back since.

The Service Quick guy is scheduled to come back in 5 days so we'll see. If he can't fix it, I'l order something else. Why haven't I done that already? Same reason that the Samsung VP didn't offer me a new refrigerator. Almost everything seems to have a 3-6 week wait because of Covid.

So Samsung refrigerators suck and it is virtually impossible to get them repaired.

DO NOT BUY A SAMSUNG REFRIGERATOR

JM Tepper

ps. a year and a half later. Not too long after I wrote the original one star review, the refrigerator section completely quit. I had had enough. I called Samsung Corporate offices directly and got the email address of the President. I emailed him the whole story up to that point, demanding a new refrigerator. Within 24 hours I got a reply from some senior VP who promised to send a Samsung team out to me and guaranteed that if they couldn't fix all the problems with the refrigerator, that they would indeed replace it with a new unit.

The Samsung crew arrived a few days later right on schedule and after about 30 minutes, diagnosed the problem as a "sealed system" problem meaning that the guts of the cooling system had a leak or blockage. They were able to isolate the block, drained the whole system, cleared the blockage, checked the tubes for leaks and refilled it. Problem solved. They also replaced the entire Icemaker. All under warrantee, didn't cost me a dime (except for all the food that went bad earlier).

Now, about 1.5 years later, the refrigerator has been working like a charm every since Samsung was here. The moral of the story is that if you have a problem with a Samsung refrigerator, don't call Sears, don't call a local repair shop, go directly to Samsung.

On the basis of this, I changed the original 1 star rating to 3 stars.

product_title: Frigidaire 242115279 Refrigerator
review_text:
Was a snap to install. its a little funky getting the wires snapped in but overall anyone can do it. I am on my six evaporator motor, well at least I thought it was the evaporator motor. Since about 5 years ago my fridge had a SY EF error. I replaced the fan motor (also easy) in my Frigidaire French door fridge which solved the problem. It worked for about 1 year then every year since I have been having to replace the fan motors. In fact the last time I bought a spare so I can just swap it out. Well, this time the motor swap did not work.
Here is what I learned. There are 4 wires coming to the motor. Original motor has a Red, Brown, Yellow and Red some replacement motors use a white wire instead of a brown. The Brown (or white) wire is ground. The red is +12VDC the Blue is a tach feed back telling the control board the fan is actually turning. The yellow is the on/off wire. If you cut the yellow wire and tie it off to the red going into the fan motor the fan will run fast constantly. Worked for a week until I was able to replace the control card. In fact you could probably leave it this way if it is your last resort. But be aware, the fan runs all the time so during defrost cycles its running so it may not be an ideal fix for the long term. The error did go away though and the fridge temp came down.
Once I installed the new board however, I went and tested my collection of bad motors and only found 1 that did not work. Ironically the new motor I purchased with the control board was DOA but the motor that was installed worked just fine, so my fridge is working once again. Thanks Amazon! Be happy to answer any questions that you may have so just send a note.

review_title: Nice looking, but poor quality, electronics, materials - potentially dangerous
review_text:
We bought this stove looking for a reasonably priced prof. model. Frigidaire promoted it months before they manufactured it and I believe rushed it through production.

So far, we have had three electronic panels as the first two would not work. The touch panel is very sensitive and not all of the features worked on the first two. The last panel has worked for the past six months. We are hoping they finally sent us a good one.

We had the "stainless steel" top replaced because it rusted. The metal top is so thin and the production process apparently scratches / buffs through the metal leaving micro grooves where water from a sponge rusted the top. Amazing because stainless steel does not rust.

But our biggest concern regards the knobs in the front. My wife is 5'2" and when reaching over the stove to put something in or out of the microwave, she leans against the knobs and 20-30% of the time, they turn on, letting gas escape. If she is not paying close attention, the house fills with gas before she notices. She has not lit the burners in this manner, yet, but that is a possibility.

Note: Also, this unit is not designed with a delayed baking (time - bake) feature.

The oven works fine, but like many gas ovens, one has to adjust cook times for various things like cookies or cakes, but once you figure that out, you make that adjustment each time you bake something.

I do like the appearance, the price and large oven capacity as I can bake a very large pizza in it, but I not recommend this product. I will not purchase Frigidaire appliances again, at least not in the near future. Perhaps they will take these and other comments to heart and realize that they cannot hope to succeed without repeat customers, those who recommend their products.

BTW - my one-year warranty is up in a month or two so I am hopeful that the panel will continue working from now on. I can only hope.

Also, the repairman just left after replacing the control panel on the Frigidaire Professional Refrigerator - the match to the stove. :( This one appears to work much better.

- Rubber feet on the cast iron range grates protect the stainless top from scratches, at least they would had they not disintegrated within a couple of months.

- Range burners don't light reliably despite the burner heads being seated properly, absolutely free of moisture and debris, and in a draft-free environment.
- Oven temperature drops at least 50 degrees, sometimes as much as 75 degrees, below the set point before the burner comes on again. Successful baking with that kind of variation is a game of chance.
- The temp probe function has now started to malfunction even though it has never been used. The probe icon comes on intermittently all by itself, then switches itself off. Often it keeps cycling on and off every few seconds for several minutes, even when nothing else is on and "cancel" has been repeatedly pressed. And if the broiler is on when the probe function acts up, it shuts down.
Note that the oven is barely two years old (purchased in 2016) and gets relatively light use in a household of two. But if the probe fix costs more than a few bucks, this oven is going to the recycler.

Bought a Samsung washer and dryer unit in this series 4 years ago after buying a home. My home which needed renovation took me two years to move into, thereby leaving the washer and dryer unit sitting wrapped in the original packing/shipping boxes even some time after moving in. Please note I also have a smaller Frigidaire unit located on a different floor in my home which is used mostly because of its proximity to the bedrooms. There are only three adults within my home and NO children, so washer and dryers are not used as frequently.

We started hearing a loud pounding noise with the dryer mid to late October 2018. We discovered the issue yesterday; a cracked drum. Since we NEVER allow shoes of any kind in our units and the heaviest items to go in the units are blankets, we were dumbfounded to find this issue. We’ve since done some research and found other customers complaining about a cracked drum as well as a current class-action lawsuit against the manufacturer (Samsung) for this known issue.

Samsung refuses to fix the drum and will only set-up an appointment if I pay for it. They’ve advised me that even if my dryer was still under warranty, that they wouldn’t cover it regardless because it’s considered a cosmetic issue.
I’ve had many washers and dryers over my lifetime, including the “work horse” Frigidaire washer and dryer on my second floor, yet I’ve never encountered this issue. This is a defect with the manufacturing of this product and Samsung absolutely refuses to make it right.
This will be my last Samsung washer and dryer unit. Other than that I very much enjoy my Samsung TVs and tablet. Samsung gets an A for electronics in my book, but not so much for their washer and dryer units.

product_title: Samsung DV40J3000EW 7.2 Cu. Ft. White Electric Dryer
review_text:
This purchase was a regrettable mistake that I made. I bought the Samsung clothes dryer because I had such a good experience with their TV. It does dry clothes, but what a pain to use, and a risk to my clothes.

The sensor dry in my opinion has only been useful when drying towels or large loads. It doesn’t work nearly as well as my sensor on my 40 year old kenmore that I got rid of.

I have used this machine for over four months now and am totally dissatisfied with it. It’s a hassle to use because the sensor dry feature in my experience is super sensitive to fabric weight and load size. I mean SUPER SENSITIVE, and if you don’t get it right you have to fiddle around trying to finish drying, or worse it may just shrink the clothes by frying them. Mine is biased to over drying the clothes big time and Samsung advises that is my fault for not getting the load size figured out correctly. And,I can not envision myself ever needing to use “very dry” or “more dry”.

The thing that makes it worse is that the manual timer is extremely limited. It’s called manual, but the only four choices you have are 20, 40, 60, or 80 minutes. So, I tried using damp dry so as not to shrink my long sleeve shirt sleeves. I’ve had a lot of experience washing and drying over a thousand loads of laundry and I’m pretty good at estimating the amount of time a “not dry enough yet” load will take to finish drying without shrinking my shirt sleeves, but there is no way to select anything less than 20 minutes with this machine.

When I first started using it (before I knew I had to be careful) the dryer shrunk a load of my long sleeve shirts, and fried a load of my underwear. I always wash my shirts separately and my underwear separately.

In summary, The automatic sensor dry is not something that can be relied on to take the effort out of drying your clothes, and the manual timer is very limited. It’s a real hassle to dry anything other than towels or a big load of rugged clothing. My poor experience with Samsung service will be considered when deciding on whether to purchase other Samsung products.

For those who are interested there are more details below:

I am very dissatisfied with the performance of the automatic sensor dry. I tried to return or exchange it with “Best Buy” right away but they would not do an exchange, and referred me to the manufacturer who I promptly called. Samsung quickly sent a repair tech out, and the only thing he did was start the empty dryer…watch as it ran for a brief time and shut off. Then he said it was operating normally and there was nothing wrong. That was it. He did not test anything more, and never even brought a tool box or any instrument in. I continued to call Samsung and was eventually, after much time on the phone, placed in contact with a supervisor, who continued to tell me it was operating as designed and they also denied my request for an exchange.

A minor annoyance that was not noticeable until I began to use the machine is that when it’s leveled properly nothing will stay on top of it while it is running. The top tappers off quite a bit at about 9 inches from the from of the unit and there is no lip at the edge. Anything set on top will fall off the front. The paint durability of the top from a scratch perspective is poor. It is really very soft and the top of the machine scratches so easily. I bought a rubber mat with enough friction on the bottom of it to stay put, as well as to protect the paint from scratching and that issue is solved. Samsung obviously doesn’t want me to set anything on top of the machine.

On the positive side, the filter size is generous and is easy to clean, the machine is an attractive design, the wrinkle prevent is a convenient feature and works well, and the paint color is a pleasing modern white.

review_title: Cracked Drum, Company tells me I’m on my own.
review_text:
Bought a Samsung washer and dryer unit in this series 4 years ago after buying a home. My home which needed renovation took me two years to move into, thereby leaving the washer and dryer unit sitting wrapped in the original packing/shipping boxes even some time after moving in. Please note I also have a smaller Frigidaire unit located on a different floor in my home which is used mostly because of its proximity to the bedrooms. There are only three adults within my home and NO children, so washer and dryers are not used as frequently.

We started hearing a loud pounding noise with the dryer mid to late October 2018. We discovered the issue yesterday; a cracked drum. Since we NEVER allow shoes of any kind in our units and the heaviest items to go in the units are blankets, we were dumbfounded to find this issue. We’ve since done some research and found other customers complaining about a cracked drum as well as a current class-action lawsuit against the manufacturer (Samsung) for this known issue.

Samsung refuses to fix the drum and will only set-up an appointment if I pay for it. They’ve advised me that even if my dryer was still under warranty, that they wouldn’t cover it regardless because it’s considered a cosmetic issue.
I’ve had many washers and dryers over my lifetime, including the “work horse” Frigidaire washer and dryer on my second floor, yet I’ve never encountered this issue. This is a defect with the manufacturing of this product and Samsung absolutely refuses to make it right.
This will be my last Samsung washer and dryer unit. Other than that I very much enjoy my Samsung TVs and tablet. Samsung gets an A for electronics in my book, but not so much for their washer and dryer units.

review_title: Now if you are in the same situation I am in here is what I have found out and recommend. ----- problem history and details ----
review_text:
Alright I get to leave the first review to tell everyone how much I loathe this washer.

I have been going back and fourth with support for over a month now. The washer doesn't properly wash the clothes.
Now that is past the 30 day return policy I cannot return the waster and I'm stuck with it.

My recommendation to everyone here is if there is a problem,

--->>> DON'T CALL FACTORY SERVICE! <<<---
(seriously the dumbest thing I did)

Instead quickly return it within the 30 day window to save yourself time and money!

TRUST ME! I'm stuck with a washer that hardly works and will have to throw away money to get a properly working one.
I even tried contacting customer service and corporate with no luck.

Now if you are in the same situation I am in here is what I have found out and recommend.

----- problem history and details -------

It all started when I first noticed random stains on my clothes after washing them. I watched the wash cycle closely by pausing and watching it.
Clothes aren't moving from bottom to top and back down again. Any clothes on the top would never get submerged to get washed. It's supposed to be an high efficiency washer

(see image. the sample sock and my undies never went under water and just floated)

(I recommend anyone try the same test themselves. Put a white sock on top and pause the wash every couple of minutes to see if it moves.)
Now the "tech line" said that this was normal opperation. I watched quite a few videos online and how high efficency washers work and them in action.
All the videos I saw did rotate closes from the bottom up.

Now the workaround.
Always use the deep water (half load) or heavy load (3/4 load) wash. This will make sure there is enough water to cover the clothes.
What I do and recommend to give you clean clothes is pause the wash cycle every 5 minutes or so and pull the clothes on the bottom to the top and unpause the cycle.

I hope this helps any of those who bought this washer having the same issue I am.

review_text:
Whirlpool was the brand of choice for washers and dryers for decades. As proof, CONSUMER REPORT consistently rated highly, and the prices were very good. Like Magtag and all other reliable products, everything went downhill; and Whirlpool was no exception.
.

.

.
.
======================================================================================================
.
.

product_title: Whirlpool WTW7000DW 4.8 cu. ft. Cabrio HE Top Load Washer w/Exclusive ColorLast Option
review_text:
I had my whirlpool cabrio for 5 painful years. I finally, celebratory, took it out to the curb today. First of all when we first got it the thing would finish a load and then start the load again after 2 minutes. So if you started a load and left the house (not uncommon) it would wash the load OVER AND OVER again until you got home. It gave you about 30 seconds before restarting. We called Whirlpool customer service and gave them the code it was showing "LE" on the display and they told us we needed to call an appliance repair man. We did. We called 5, in fact. Each of them told us that they did not work on Whirlpool Cabrio machines because they were either too hard to work on or they were "pieces of ****." Mind you we paid $799 for this machine.

Finally a friend of ours came over and found out that the only problem was that it was still on Demo mode. There was NOTHING in the manual about this, nor could Whirlpool tell us this. The friend fixed it.

2 weeks later the lid lock broke making the machine completely inoperable. Knowing that no one would work on it, I ordered a new lid lock mechanism and replaced it myself, which took me about 6 hours. That was a fun Saturday. I did get it working again tho, to the extent that it ever did work.

The basic function of a washing machine is to take dirty clothes and make them clean. I'd say about 50% of the time the machine left the clothes smelling musty, even if we removed them IMMEDIATELY after the cycle was done.

Recently the machine stopped filling with water. It would pour water in, and the water would immediately drain out, and it would wash our clothes completely dry. We'd have been better off putting them in a big bucket, pouring some detergent in there, shaking it around a while, and throwing them into the dryer. We again called several washing machine repair men and all of them said that either they don't work on those machines, or that it's better to just go get a different machine.

We did. We went online and found a nice used GE machine for $160 and I can not tell you how far superior this used apartment complex style machine is at the basic function of washing clothes. PLEASE save your money. Stay away from the Whirlpool Cabrio, and Whirlpool in general.

product_title: Samsung NE59J7850WS 30 Self-Cleaning Freestanding Electric Double Range
review_title: Looks nice, and ok performer, but unreliable
review_text:
I bought this same model in 2016. I've experienced four problems with this unit. First, and probably my biggest gripe, reliability. But before I get there, let me start with the good.

Stove performance is exceptional. The 3000W speed burner does what it says- things heat up FAST. The warming area is very useful. Its a very nice looking unit. Two built-in timers, and easy to understand controls.

Next... the bad. First, reliability. In the five years I've had this range, something has broke 3 of the five years. Glad I'm a good DIY-er, or the cost of repairs would have been almost the cost of the unit itself. The bearings on the convection fan went bad after about 2 years of use. An infinity switch went bad a year later. The triple-burner broke just this week.

Some of day -to-day issues include poor temperature control in the oven; the "hot stovetop" lamp dislodges and falls into the back of the unit (need to pull the unit from the wall and open it up to put the LED back in place); and any stove-top drips find their way between the oven glass, making a mess.

That said, the range was never completely out of commission (i.e. unusable until repaired). The fan made noise, which is livable (but not efficient). The infinity switch problem knocked one burner out, but we still had 3 burners to hold us over. And the bad burner... well, similar.

Overall, performance is great (stove), and ok (oven). But most importantly to me, an unreliable headache isn't worth the performance benefits, especially when that performance is... meh.

review_text:
I got this Frigidaire cooktop to replace the Whirlpool 4-burner installed by our builder over 19 years ago. The old one was a black glasstop unit, and frankly I was tired of it and wanted a 5-burner. I shopped all over and found everyone was out of stock and backordered, so I was surprised to find it iton Amazon! Not only that, but it was significantly cheaper than at the big box stores and appliance stores in my area, so it was a win-win.

I chose to install it myself. Installation involves only two connections, gas and electricity, and the electrical connection in most cases is just a standard 120v plug. the gas will involve some wrenches of the right sizes, and may entail some fittings to complete the connection. Most gas connections these days are pretty standard, so you should be able to use the ones on the old unit you're replacing. Just be sure to use pipe dope or similar sealant on the gas connections, and test them thoroughly with soapy water after hook-up.

Performance is excellent, and the BTU output of the burners is better than the old one, so I'm happy. The grates are heavy-duty and continuous across the top of the cooktop, making it easy to move pots and pans around with no snags. Nice.

The only negative I have is that the burner control knobs are plastic and are shiny like chrome, while the rest of the cooktop is a brushed stainless finish. but I will say that more expensive big-name units I looked at also use similar shiny knobs.

I like my new cooktop, and will be replacing my oven and microwave shortly with use matching Frigidaire products. 5 stars.

product_title: Haier HLP24E 1.5 cu. ft. Portable Washer with Stainless Steel Drum and Pulsator Wash System
review_text:
I bought the HLP23E, which is the same machine for all intents and purposes, this is the "new and improved" version. I hope so! After less than two years, the internal exit hose clamp broke and I had to pay $88 to have it replaced, as the washer had to be opened and a different, stronger clamp had to be installed. The clamp cost $2. I was slightly irritated. After 2.5 years of normal use by a single person, the buttons broke. They are cheap, cheap plastic. The entire top has to be removed and a new one put in it's place...two hours work ($250)...and then there is no new face plate, so the old one had to be peeled off and half stuck on the new one, so I have to pull the face plate taught with my thumb before pushing the buttons. The machine is now 3.5 years old, and the buttons are less than one year old and they are hesitating...meaning they are pressed and nothing happens. If you just push harder, they will break. Now, I have to start looking for a new washer, and the only portable ones available are cheap plastic buttoned ones.

Now, other than that, I love the machine, but I have paid for an entire second machine and it still won't function free of extreme maintenance for five years. It's an arbitrary number, but the sign of a better quality machine.

I have seen glowing reviews about Haier portable washers, and I agree, when they are first purchased, but nobody else has returned to tell you if they worked long term.

I am looking to get the smallest normal washer I can find, as they say a Y-hose can convert any washer to a portable. I just want to be able to wash my clothing and hang it on my dry racks in peace without having to have the washer fixed constantly in the middle of winter.

I wish these were better made as I love it, and I don't want a huge monstrosity permanently next to my kitchen sink in my tiny apartment, but I have little choice, and the cost of a regular machine will be something I can't really afford, but laundromats are not cheap either and you risk your clothing being less than fresh smelling as they are never cleaned.

I am deeply, deeply disappointed and the company could care less. I have called them multiple times over the years...too bad, there is nobody in management to contact.
