product_title: Haier HLP24E 1.5 cu. ft. Portable Washer with Stainless Steel Drum and Pulsator Wash System
review_title: Delighted with this washer so far!
review_text:
UPDATE:
I've used the washer for 7 months now and it's still working great! Because I like fabric softener since I often hang my clothes outside to dry, I've started to add the fabric softener along with the detergent in the wash cycle. This way, I don't have to babysit the machine and catch the rinse cycle. It works!

I'm moving across the country at the end of the week and really hope the washer makes it through unscathed! I'll be adding the small dryer when I'm in my new home.

I received my washer today and have been merrily washing since we set it up. I LOVE it, it seems well-built but, in case something goes wrong over time, I did purchase the extended warranty. My washer was delivered within the shipping window and arrived in perfect condition. I had read the manual online so I knew what to expect and had arranged my bathroom so that it had a permanent resting place within 3 feet of the faucet/sink and within 4 feet of an electrical outlet. I also had removed the bottom piece/aerator from the faucet. When the washer was delivered, we were good to go!

And it literally only took a few minutes to set up. The washer comes with a piece to screw into the bottom of the faucet (remember that the aerator needs to be removed). We tightened that with a wrench and hooked up the water inlet hose to the top of the machine and the other end to the faucet adaptor. After that, we attached the draining hose to the bottom of the washer. I decided to remove my sink's drain plug thingy and put the end of the washer's hose securely into the drain, hoping it would be secure when the washer pumped water out. (It is! This works perfectly!) The washer comes with a hose clamp but the shape of it and the hook didn't work with my sink or vanity.

We plugged in the machine and ran a test wash with 2 old hand towels. The manual suggests running an initial wash without clothes but I figured putting 2 small towels in would help clean the machine and help remove the "new washer" smell. We set it on a quick wash and the water level on medium, added detergent, and let it go. The machine performed flawlessly. I then started to wash clothes, sticking with the "Quick" wash. That cycle lasts 23 minutes and gets clothes very clean! It uses less water and electricity, too! I did another medium load consisting of 10 pairs of socks, 10 pairs of undies, a good hand towel, and 2 pairs of jammies. I also did a large load and it fit 2 pairs of sweatpants, 4 sweatshirts, and 2 t-shirts. (If this helps, I'm 5 feet, 6 inches tall and wear a Size 6 so smaller people could fit more of their clothes and larger people fewer clothes, I guess.)

I am delighted with how well this little washer cleans my clothes, how much it fits in a load, and how efficient it is! There are 2 lint filters inside the machine and it's amazing how much lint accumulates in them. (Well, maybe it shouldn't be. I do have pets, heh.) The manual recommends cleaning them after each load and I'd agree. It's simple to do. There's only one drawback -- no fabric softener dispenser. It wasn't mentioned in the manual so I just keep an eye on it and add fabric softener to the water during the rinse cycle. The Quick cycle only does one rinse so that's easy enough to figure out without having to watch it constantly.

I bought this washer after my full-sized front loader broke. I'm going to be moving later this year, building a cabin and using solar power so I decided I may as well buy a washer that would work now and also be an energy-efficient, smart appliance for the cabin. This is a winner and I hope it lasts a long time!

product_title: Haier HLP24E 1.5 cu. ft. Portable Washer with Stainless Steel Drum and Pulsator Wash System
review_title: Leaked, No wheels $$ to purchase dolly, no thank you Haier
review_text:
Where do i start, let's go the traditional route of my reviews. Here it goes:

Pros:
*Almost the same size of a regular washer but slimmer and narrow from top to bottom. Regular washers are wide.
*Can hold a lot of clothes, but you MUST be careful not to overload or the machine will stop functioning. Clothing/Blankets weighing too much is not a good idea.
*if loaded properly, it'll do a good wash but nothing near a real washer at home or going to laundromat. This is perfect for baby clothing, single people or people with patience who can spend hours doing very small loads of laundry. We primarily got this for our 5 month old who goes through clothing like nobody's business.
*not quiet, but not loud. Was in bathroom, so if i closed door it was silent (^_^)
*overall, i'd give this an 8/10 which is in line with other professional reviews you'll find inf you search google. Let's move unto the cons shall we?
*Customer support was quick and responsive. When i needed help, their repair shop called right away. It's not American so don't expect anything, but in the least you get to speak to a real person on the other end.

Cons:
*Leaked from the bottom, no idea from where. I'm guessing it was probably the drain pipe which is located in the bottom side. We made sure the drain pipe was in there, utilizing the clamp provided. No avail, still leaked from bottom.
*this is not a fault of the unit, but if your bathroom faucet has old plumbing that cannot handle running cold water for too long, you will experience leaks for your underneath your sink. I think it's best to install this in a kitchen if your faucet has the proper connections. What is fault of the unit is that it can only take cold water, what kind of washer only takes cold water? what if i need to do a warm wash? using warm water will fog the entire inside and i'm assuming the steam can affect the electrical in the machine (don't know from experience as I've had washer only 2 days before sending it right back)
*leaked all over our bathroom floor and cleaning was pain. The very first problem with this unit is that you must press the play button for any water to fill in the drum. if you don't, no water will come. can't open the lid, gotta leave it closed and let water fill before adding soap.
*soap dispenser may be worthless b/c we've added a lot of tide liquid detergent and I've never seen suds. best way is to fill in drum, add your liquid detergent directly.
*it's feakin' HUGE no wheels ZERO portability. This sucker was literally made for homeowners with little space for a regular washer and need something slimmer to fit right in. It's meant to connect and never take off. Buying a separate dolly or wheels or a unit that costs $300 is unacceptable.

Summary: i wish i had researched this more. For my needs the machine itself is great, but due to the leaks and size it is not a good choice for my apt.

review_title: Compatible 10-ft drain hose: Frigidaire 154225602. The Haier HLP24E is the nicest washer I've used!
review_text:
I've owned the Haier HLP24E portable washing machine for three weekends now, and have used it for 2-3 loads per weekend with zero problems.

Before I was able to use the washer however, I needed to find a 10-ft drain hose. Haier only supplies a 5-ft drain hose. However, there are 15 inches of countertop between the right side of my kitchen sink and the space that I could place the washer, plus the drain port on the washer is on the far side from my sink (on the right side of the washer, at the bottom and near the back). I carefully measured, and determined that I needed a drain hose no less than 10.0 ft.

The drain port on the Haier HLP24E portable washer is 1.0" O.D. (1. inch outer diameter), so the drain hose must have a connector that is 1.0" I.D. (1.0 inch inner diameter). The Frigidaire 154225602 (the "Electrolux 154225602" as per the packaging) Drain Hose has a 1.0" I.D. at both the 90-degree connector and at the straight connector. I connected the 90-degree connector to my washer and routed the hose around the back and then over to my sink.

The hardest part of finding a drain hose that would work for my new washer and kitchen layout was that every website that I was able to find that sells drain hoses (including Amazon) does not, in the vast majority of cases, list the inner diameter of the hose connections and the overall length of the hose. It took me days of searching until I found that the Frigidaire 154225602 (aka. the "Electrolux 154225602") fits the Haier HLP24E portable washer, and is 10 ft long instead of the OEM hose which was 5 ft long.

One thing that is nice about this hose for portable clothes washers or portable dishwashers is that it is transparent, so you can see the water level inside. That makes disconnecting it from your sink easier to do without spilling any water on the floor, because you can see exactly where the water level is inside the hose while you are relocating the hose after using the washer.

The washer itself is the nicest washer I have used in 36 years. Literally. There is no agitator inside, so there is actually quite a bit of room inside for laundry. I am 6'1" and have a larger-than average frame, so my articles of clothing are larger than average as well. But I can just fit 7 days of my "lights" in one load, and 7 days of my "darks" in a second load. That is similar to the capacity of traditional full-size washers with the agitator.

All of the controls are digital, allowing the engineers to be able to design very intelligent steps in the wash cycles. I use the "Heavy Duty" cycle, because the water in my town is hard (full of minerals) and therefore clothes don't rinse free of detergent very well unless you use warm or hot water to dissolve the soap and then later use a second rinse cycle. One extra-nice feature is that as the washer is filling with water each time, it repeatedly spins the wash basket a little, to get the clothes at the sides equally wet. That wasn't a feature in the previous washers I've used.

The wash basket also contains two lint traps which work very well. I've used too many washers without lint traps; those washers leave debris on your linens, essentially requiring you to then run them through a dryer to remove the lint. In contrast, the lint traps in the Haier HLP24E do such a good job that I don't need to use a dryer to remove lint, allowing me to hang-dry all of my laundry on two laundry racks that I have in my apartment. Just keep at least one or two windows open 1 inch or a half an inch, and the washer gets the clothes so dry that 24 to 36 hours later, all of my laundry is completely dry. That saves me a lot of money by not having to use the dryer each week, it saves me hours of each weekend, and my clothes last a lot longer too and never shrink.

review_text:
I purchased this from another retailer that also offered a 2 year warranty that begins AFTER the manufacturer's warranty which kicks up the value level significantly. I've been using this Haier HLP24E 1.5 cu. ft. Portable Washer with a stainless steel drum for about a month now. Can you easily wash three pairs of jeans, 3 shirts and boxers? Easily. One thing I like about this washer is it's spin feature. For one it spins as well as a full size washer. Secondly it hasn't complained once. With such a relatively small basket it is kinda hard to load it incorrectly. I think this may be due to the lack of the traditional agitator that reduces load size in full size machine. Those machines force you to load around it increasing the odds of an unbalanced load.With this washer you drop the clothes in, set your desired fill level and wash cycle and press start. Easy. If you wash the same amount of clothes that the super/normal accepts then after your first setting you can simply load and press start. The sink faucet adapter that is included might have some issues with your faucet. They incude a rubber washer that is necessary with most water hoses. Your faucet probably has one as well. When you try and install this with the included washer as well as the one in your faucet you might run into an issue. If it won't screw on simply remove your faucet's rubber washer and install the new washer in its place. Removing the quick connect adapter may make installation of the sink adapter easier. About the only thing I do not like about this washer is its communication skills. Sure, it can complain with beeps if it has an issue but you've no clue how long until the next cycle. You can time each cycle so you will know but it would be nice for the machine to have that info ready. By the by if you have an issue with adding softener you can set a separate timer or purchase detergent with softener included.

6-21-2018 Still working. I did purchase that additional warranty that covers the washer for 2 years.They will come out to my house and repair or replace the washer. When I'm investing nearly $400 with tax included the extra $40 I invested is worth it, to me. That adds 2 years protection that Haier does not. They only offered a 1 year warranty and from what I heard they are greedy and only offer partial refunds after a certain amount of time.I don't want a half-(censored) solution.

BTW, if it looks like your washer has been used before SEND IT BACK!!! This didn't come straight from the manufacturer and as such there will be more inventory issues. review_text:
I've owned one of these machines since 2014. Not too long after arriving in my home it started to have some buyers remorse.

1. If you open the lid to remove the clothes in the final seconds of the cycle (during which it sits and does nothing really except maybe run the end of cycle beeps), toss the laundry in the dryer, the unit must complete it's cycle or it will beep about every 90 seconds until you close the lid and let it complete the cycle. At the end of the cycle it beeps something like 10 times. If you interrupt that, it will continue to alarm until you close the lid. Those ten beeps are so darn important it will not stop until you close the lid. That alarm is similar to a smoke detector low-battery chirp.

I have to unplug it and let it sit for a while then re-try and maybe it will work. This problem is getting worse but there is no mention of code E6 on the sticker on top of the machine. I guess it's a big Haier corporate secret.

3. This machine will do nothing with the lid open because you may be stupid enough to stick your head inside the drum while the its spinning. You cannot start the fill cycle then add clothes or detergent. If there was a easy way to defeat the lid-open switch, I would do so.

4. All in all, it does a reasonable job of washing clothes, blankets, towels, etc., but I would not purchase this again. This washer is larger than it appears in photos.

review_title: I love my Haier washer, and my Haier dryer!
review_text: I purchased this washer several months ago, and I love it.  Years ago, I owned another one of their earlier models, but this one is even better.  The manufacturer seems to really listen to their customers.  It works well with no problems whatsoever.  It is important to remember to drain the emptying hose very well, as it holds about 2 cups to water after the machine is turned off.  I keep a small decorative metal pail (from JoAnn's) next to my sink, which I use to empty the water into after each use.  I place the bucket on the floor and place the hose slightly along the floor with the end of it pointed up, and a couple of inches up from the floor, so the water won't drain onto the floor.  This allows the water left in the machine to drain into the hose.  Then I point the end into the bucket and lift the hose slowly from the machine connection point, so the water will drain into the bucket.  You have to do this several times, as the hose holds quite a lot of water.  The hose connected to the faucet, I empty into the sink and place it in the machine when not in use.  Don't forget to clean the lint filters, and remove them carefully.  And I use cold water only - I'm not sure if the hoses can handle hot or very hot water.  Evidently Haier is the largest small appliance company in the world, and they have recently purchased General Electric's (a very old company) small appliance section.  Their headquarters are located in China, and they are a very good company, and have improved with time.  I will always buy Haier.

It washes, rinsed and drains  like a full size washer,  just the capacity is smaller.  I washed baby clothes to small blankets,  sheets,  men's size 40/32 jeans ECT.  You only need 1/4 of detergent or fabric softener.  It has 2 lint traps that work vey well.  The only down sides are, the plastic piece where the drain hose is at the bottom is not made well if you don't keep the hose completely straight it will leak. Also you  you have to put a bucket where the drain hose is and drain the water out after you disconnect the hose from the unit.  Otherwise it will leak out when you move it.  The drain hose is made well,  but you can purchase a better one,  and the rubber hose is short. Overall I'm very happy with this washer and company I would definitely recommend it and I will definitely purchase from this company again.

product_title: Haier HLP24E 1.5 cu. ft. Portable Washer with Stainless Steel Drum and Pulsator Wash System
review_text: This is a great little washer. It manages to do quite a large load for it's size. The washer is fairly quiet and doesn't vibrate (unless the load is unbalanced). The spin cycle is super fast and gets the clothes about 85% dry. It's easy to hook up and use. I've had it for about a month now and use it at least twice a week. I live in an apartment and not having to use the filthy washers here is a good feeling. I would give this washer five stars if it weren't for the fact that it showed up damaged. The box itself was intact which leads me to believe the damage was caused at the manufacturer before it was packaged. The part that was damaged is a flimsy piece of silver aluminum that covers the back side of the washer where you access the motor and internal wirings. I was able to remove it by taking out a few screws and carefully hammering it back into shape. It looks like nothing ever happened to it now. Attached are some pictures of the damage and the washer. Other than that the rest of the washer was in perfect shape and working fine. I did find however that the drain hose that comes with this washer is fairly short. I believe it's only 5 feet long. I saw another reviewer on here that mentioned a 10 foot hose for a Frigidaire dishwasher that fit this washer perfectly. So I bought it and sure enough it works great. The 10 foot hose part number is Frigidaire 154225602 Drain Hose.

product_title: GE Cafe 30" Built-in Induction Cooktop Flagstone Gray CHP9530SJSS
review_title: Very satisfied since unit was serviced
review_text:
(See service updates at end of review, as well as the comments for a complete picture)

Mar 2018 Update: No changes since last update--still works and looks brand new with not a scratch. I am always worried we are going to crack the glass since we use very heavy enameled cast iron a lot, and once the spouse dropped it after grabbing it while hot, but it survived.

Jan 2017 Update: Operation has been flawless since service last summer. No scratches--still looks brand new because it is so easy to clean. Very fast to get cookware up to temperature or boil water. Sad to see others reviewers still having issues. I would hate to have to go back to gas if this actually were to fail out of warranty. For now, upgrading back to 5 stars based on months of excellent performance.

Original review:
If Dynamic Deals is selling this for several hundred less than the going rate, it is a great deal (even cheaper today than when I bought it). If concerned about the warranty, just buy an extended warranty and you'll be better off than paying the full price while depending solely on the one year GE warranty. Mine arrived in new and flawless condition, and all the features work. Since I have had mine serviced already by GE, you can factor that into your calculus about where to buy this, since there is that other reviewer who didn't want to buy from a non authorized dealer.

In case you didn't know, this particular model is the Consumer Reports #1 rated induction cooktop. In their brand reliability survey, GE is only second to Kenmore, on par with Whirlpool, but has half the reported problems as the worst (KitchenAid). And if you haven't been paying attention to the financial news, it is not exactly a smart move to be investing in anything (Kenmore) associated with the Sears brand these days, given the death watch that company is on.

Fast boiling, completely flush surface with no knobs to trap grease, griddle burner sync feature, much cooler in the kitchen in contrast to an open gas flame, beautiful gray color looks much better on a white countertop than a black surface. (If looks are important, the last reason is a no brainer). The obvious downsides are that you may not want to just drop a heavy pot onto the glass counter, like you can easily do with a gas cooktop. And maybe not all your cookware will work. A large non-induction Cuisinart skillet didn't work, and all the Lodge cast iron pans have been retired to prevent scratching of the glass. Below is a list of induction capable pans we have used successfully on this. The 12" Cuisinart fryer is great for maximizing the real estate of the larger burner, though it is definitely heavy, so I wouldn't recommend to someone who can't handle the weight, since the surface is some kind of glass:

[[ASIN:B00421AYJK Cooks Standard Multi-Ply Clad Stainless-Steel 10-Piece Cookware Set]]
[[ASIN:B001V9K6LC Cuisinart CI45-30CR Chef's Classic Enameled Cast Iron 12-Inch Chicken Fryer with Cover, Cardinal Red]]
[[ASIN:B00VLPCVSM La Cuisine Cast Iron Skillet with Integrated Cast Iron Handles and Enamel Finish, Red, 10"]]

Another downside is that this cannot be flush mounted with the counter--the beveled edge is supposed to lie on top of the counter, although it does have a very low profile which almost appears flush from a distance. If you want a true flush mount, apparently you need to upgrade to the GE Monogram line, which means spending even more, so you'd have to evaluate if that is worth the extra dollars. Also, I was a little disappointed that the built in timer does not sync with the burners, so it doesn't appear that you can turn off the cooktop using the timer, like you can with an oven. If replacing a gas appliance, you may need to hire an electrician to run a 220V circuit, which will further add to the hidden cost of this. There is a youtube video that shows how to shut off a gas line, but basically you can get yellow teflon tape (yellow is rated for gas, unlike the common white tape) and a cap from HD. That tape requires four wraps if I recall, but you'll want to read the instructions on the tape.

Electric is probably more expensive than gas or propane to operate, but it's much cooler and easier to clean, so you'll have to justify any extra operating expenses with those benefits. (If you can afford this, you probably shouldn't mind paying an extra few dollars a month to operate it). It comes with a sample size of cleaner, which is very effective at getting off the residue that builds over the burners. It is pricey on amazon, so I'll have to shop for these locally to compare pricing. But it really only takes a drop to clean each burner, so it should be quite long lasting.

[[ASIN:B01KCCP6C2 Best Value Kit: Ceramic Cooktop Cleaner 28oz Scraper 11 Pads ...]]
[[ASIN:B01CO2LA6O Cerama Bryte GVI209282W Cerama Bryte Ceramic Cooktop Cleaner 28 Oz]]

July 2016 update: After having a number of instances of the burners turning off in the midst of cooking, I had to call GE support. (This was installed in May 2016). The problem was intermittent and apparently due to too much heat for it to handle, though if you can't cook food normally without worrying about overheating, that makes this not so useful as a cooktop. The correct GE number to call is the answer line, and not the repair line. The first rep tried to tell me that a cast iron pan may not be ideal for this! Really? They seem quick to blame pans for issues, probably because too many people are using either incorrect or inferior cookware. The next rep finally understood the nature of the problem after I described the symptoms and dispatched a GE tech and attached a diagnostic tool to the cooktop underneath and discovered some codes suggesting the visible cooktop and its electronics needs to be replaced. Similar to an OBD port in a car, with fault codes and recent history of uses, so fortunately he didn't have to rely on just my explanation. I had captured a video of boiling water to demonstrate the problem, and unfortunately he tried to convince me that boiling water for more than a few minutes was not a reasonable use of the cooktop. Guess that rules out hard boiled eggs! I had to reiterate that the problem extended well beyond boiling water, and later that it applied to multiple burners. I found you need to be very clear and succinct with the problem description, because too much information was not really processed well. (Also, if you boil water and evaporate all the water, it makes sense that overheat protection will kick in and shut down the burner, which is a nice feature you don't get with gas).

Anyway, the replacement cooktop surface was broken in transit, so a new one was ordered. For now am wondering if this was a good purchase, but at least their support is on top of the issue. Fortunately, it is covered by a one year GE warranty and a Squaretrade warranty too. If you register on the GE website, you'll soon get hammered with email offers for an Assurant warranty, which is quite comparable if not better than the Squaretrade warranty since you can get an extra year for a small uplift in cost. Either way, I'd definitely budget an extended warranty into your purchase cost. And be sure to register your product with GE, in case you do need service.

August 2016 update: Backordered parts arrived and the service tech returned on schedule. Unlike that other reviewer's experience with their service tech, I have no issues with three separate appointments--he is quite reliable and honest when he can't answer a question. (Four appointments actually, but one was rescheduled due to sickness, but I was notified by the call center). My initial impression is that the overheating problem was fixed, as I just boiled water for an hour on two burners to test it. The problem seems to have been with an electronic module. Perhaps it was the cooktop surface itself, since that was replaced too. But since the problem was somewhat intermittent, I'll need another few weeks of cooking to confirm the problem has been fixed. Hopefully, it is not a problem that develops with use, because I don't recall if this ever had a problem within the first month of ownership. If the problem recurs, I'll update this review again.

Sept update: No issues thus far. Interesting to read Lisa's review with the same shutdown problem, so it appears there is a defective batch of product still in the pipeline. Hopefully, my replacement parts will continue to hold up over time. I guess I will downgrade to four stars due to the lingering concern for now, and lack of confidence after hearing of others with serious issues. But as of right now, it works excellent, and the gray is really an awesome looking color for a cooktop.

product_title: GE Cafe 30" Built-in Induction Cooktop Flagstone Gray CHP9530SJSS
review_title: Don't buy!. GE will not honor warranty
review_text:
Do Not Buy. I'm working with GE Executive Customer Service to fix my cooktop that's not working as designed. The large burner (3700watts) is very weak, I have to use the medium burner (2500watts) to cook if high heat is needed. If I try to saute food on the large burner, I get very little heat. I immediately switch to the medium burner and bam, I've got lots of heat.

GE techs don't know how the cooktop works and refuse to say it's faulty because the burner does heat to some extent. They claim that a burner with more wattage doesn't necessarily mean it will heat better. It's ridiculous!. They claim to not be engineers and cannot explain it but that's not it. It's absolutely deceptive advertising. Who wouldn't think that more wattage means more heat, give me a break.

They refuse to diagnose the unit with the port on the bottom because their tool is broken. They won't even come back once they fix their tool.

Worst of all, the Executive Service will not listen to the customer and they choose to place their trusts their untrained factory Techs that tell me that they don't know how the cooktop works and agree that something looks wrong.

This is the last GE product I will ever buy.

If GE could intelligently explain how that the cooktop is working as designed, I would feel better. At least I know it's not broken and that the advertising was deceptive. Unfortunately, I think it's much more likely that's it's broken and they are claiming that's nothing's wrong. So frustrating.

product_title: GE Cafe 30" Built-in Induction Cooktop Flagstone Gray CHP9530SJSS
review_text:
Dislike:
- The analog dial controls are a major reason why I bought this model. .. They work, but just barely - and if you have the least bit of moisture on your finger, forget it.

- The hot burner warning sb a red circle around the entire burner instead of that itty-bitty light on the burner temp control. Not so bad if you are just boiling water, but they get flesh-sizzling hot<if you are, for instance, using a frying pan.

- The timer is pathetic. Nothing more than a rather inconvenientially-implemented countdown with barely-audible alarm. I expected to choose a burner, set a time, and have the burner turn off with a nice loud alarm when the timer hits zero.

- I have been unable to get a straight answer out of anybody on BoilDry protection. i.e. What happens when somebody puts a pot on to boil, walks away, and forgets about it for two hours.

- I have been unable to get an answer on pot-burner size mismatches. .. Apparently, on some stoves putting a 6" pot on an 11" burner is asking for trouble.

Likes:
- This thing is seriously-easy to clean.

- People comment on how nice the grey looks compared to black stovetops.

- Don't dis the Hestan frying pan that comes with it. I had the same experience as some others at first: I just could not get the thing to work, but after 30 minutes on the phone with Hestan support I have to say that, for the non-cook, the Hestan pan and accompanying app are the greatest thing since sliced bread...Lots of recipes (16 just for salmon) and they lead you through each process in the most excruciating detail - no assumptions, no "Well, everybody knows *that*..." .. And it automagically controls the burner temp throughout the process .. .. It's Cooking For The Complete Idiot and this idiot really likes it.

product_title: GE JVW5301SJSS Wall-Mount Pyramid Chimney Hood
review_title: Master chef look, not quite the quality
review_text:
So moved into a 20 year old house with a 20 year old under cabinet, non-vented range hood. Every time I did steaks or cooked with a wok I had a 3 alarm fire alarm go off. I knew I needed to get a more powerful exhaust hood that exhausted to the outside. It ended up being a big job and I hired a contractor to remove the cabinet, install the hood and create a vent to the outside wall. I got GE b/c you just see it everywhere in new home builds and it looks good. It also matches the slide-in range.
It has the classic, prototypical high end range hood look. I also didn't want any hassles in that I didn't want to have any service issues which is another reason I went with GE b/c I figure I could get service anywhere. Delivery was fast. Box was damaged but I checked prior to signing and everything was well protected. On the positive, it looks awesome and works super well. Since I have a gas range, I put it always on at least low anytime I use the oven just in case for carbon monoxide. For wok cooking, even with high oil frying, not a peep out of the fire alarms. Don't have to even open windows/no smells. I was a little worried I needed more CFM but it's more than enough and never even had to use the boost mode. Very high quality look with nice lighted buttons. However, the stainless hood seems like it has some minor imperfections in the bends but only really noticeable to OCD people like myself. My big knocks are it really is expensive at $450 on sale and I had to spend $130 extra for the extension for a ceiling that I don't consider very high.

***Update
So less than a year later the fan blower motor is shot. It’s developed a high pitch whine like the bearing has gone out and fluctuates from a grinder noise to a high pitch cat whining. Very disappointed in the lack of longevity. Good news is after contacting GE warranty, they sent a tech and he’s going to send me a new blower that I an install myself. Very easy, one plug and two screws. In any case, very disappointed that a fan that is supposed to last 10+ years doesn’t last one year. So I’ve had issues with most everything I buy now days and these are all well known brands GE, Google, Viewsonic, ...all expensive products with not how they used to build them quality. So now I realize above everything make sure the company has a good warranty. All have been addressed through warranty service.

review_title: Had To Replace Fridge Right After Warranty Expired
review_text: I bought this brand because it was rated the highest in reliability. But shortly after its extended warranty expired, it stopped cooling. We had to throw all our food out, a $300 waste. When the repair tech pulled it away from the wall he had me touch the back coils on the heat exchanger. They were cold. They should be warm. He then pointed to the 3 foot vertical rust and ice line on the back metal wall of the f.ridge. He said I have a coolant leak spraying the inside back wall. It stopped cooling because it ran out of coolant. Because it is an internal sealed system it was not repairable and we had to buy a new fridge. It irks me that friends with cheap fridges have lasted 20 years but this premium brand only a couple of years. If you buy this fridge, set an alarm on your smart phone for a month before your warranty expires and check the back for rust lines. Demand a replacement if you have them. Don't wind up like me.

review_title: Nice machine, with a couple flaws
review_text:
Looks great, apparently it might not be real stainless steel, but I don't really care because it does look good. The control buttons are all hidden, giving it a very clean look.

This machine is very quiet and does clean the dishes well. We put whatever is dishwasher safe and will fit so it gets a lot of random items, cleans everything in the the two racks very well. The top rack as a weird multi level section which is a pretty poor design, makes it so items tip or regular glasses just don't fit.

I mention the two racks because the silverware does not clean perfectly. There are usually two or three items which didn't clean. Not a big deal, they just stay in the machine for the next wash. My main issue is the silverware does not dry well, even with heated dry selected. I end up taking the silverware rack out and putting it in the sink to finish drip drying. I haven't tried moving the silverware to the lower dish rack because the space is used for dishes.

This machine does take a long time, 3-4 hours depending on the cycle you select. Also doesn't have a true quick wash or rinse option. I don't care, but other people will. Just fill the machine, turn it on in the evening and it will be done in the morning.

Looks great and cleans well. I won't be replacing it (builder chose this one in my new house) until it actually breaks, not worth the expense.

The knobs are beautiful too.  Overall the cooktop itself should get 5 stars.  I am giving it a three star because of the imperfections with the downward draft. I clean it with the recommended cleaner and pad. No scratches or issues so far - I use cast iron pans, steel wok, a very heavy steel griddle. Just keep it clean and don't drag your pans over the top. Clean it right away if rice boils over or it gets greasy - using it while dirty will make cleaning much harder later. I also use a razor blade to carefully remove chunky burned on stuff. product_title: GE Profile Series 30" Downdraft Electric Cooktop Black Glass with Stainless Steel Trim PP9830SJSS
review_title: Design Could Be a Lot Better for Installation and Maintenance
review_text:
On Guaranteed Drop In Fit: It is not a drop in fit to my earlier GE electric downdraft model JP385R despite the claim of 'Guaranteed Fit'. The blower discharge is 3.25" x 10' and sits very low in cabinet such that there is only 9" clearance from the cabinet floor. The earlier model JP385R had a 5" round discharge which sat much higher in the cabinet allowing for a 5" offset elbow to fit into the discharge vent in the cabinet floor. In the current model, the transition suggested in the manual (3.25"x10" in to 6" in round) is too large to fit inside the cabinet i.e. GE recommended solution is not going to work in standard cabinets with floor vent. At the minimum, the blower discharge should have options for a 6" round OR 3.25" x 10' discharges. Now, it requires some custom duct work to make it work. This is expensive.
On Electric Connections: My earlier GE model JP385R had a terminal box to which one could screw on the supply wires terminals. In the new models, the supply wire terminals had to be cut off and installed by wire nuts (not provided) to the cooktop wires. 'Wire nuts' is a poorer installation mechanism as compared to terminal box. Also, the cooktop connection wires were relatively short for a convenient wire nut installation. A conduit connector was also not provided. The sheet metal work in plenum, blower housing etc. is sharp and can cause injury. It is also thinner material than the older model. It leads to an impression that GE is penny pinching at every step with a lighter quality product and a lesser interest in great quality product design.
On the plus note, the unit looks nice and seems to work well. Functionally, it will require more babysitting since it is prone to easily scratching and breaking the glass top i.e. it is going to be the proverbial prima donna. All these deficiencies should have been designed out.
The central down draft grill does not fit well in its slot.
This review is respectfully brought to your kind attention.
P.S Two pictures are posted. First pic shows the difficulty of downdraft connection. It will require a custom plenum (I think to make it work) since the 3.25"x 10 in transition proposed by GE is was useless advice. The second pic is of my old connection to downdraft. The expectation was that new GE unit will connect similarly to the the downdraft as the older GE cooktop unit did.

I tried to post the above review (in multiple reduced versions) at the GE site. They keep disapproving it for the following reasons:
"While we appreciate your PP9830SJSS review submission, unfortunately, it doesn’t meet the guidelines for posting to our site. We hope you’ll resubmit so other owners can benefit from reading your experiences.
Try reviewing our guidelines below, updating your review, and then resubmitting.
When submitting your review, please:
Keep your review focused on the product.
Avoid writing about customer service, contact us instead if you have issues requiring immediate attention.
Refrain from mentioning competitors or the specific price you paid for the product.
Do not include any personally identifiable information, such as full names."

I could not see any conflict of my review with their stated policy. I wrote back to GE to ask what the conflict was. GE did not respond. I tried to edit and reposted. It was rejected again with the same policy statement but no guidance to where the policy conflict is. I have now tried a few times and giving up on GE review site.
Can anybody please enlighten me/other GE reviewers what the policy conflict is?
BTW, some other users at GE site have also posted frustration on downdraft connection - as I did. To those customers, GE Customer Service simply apologized and failed to provide any support or solution to back up their claim of 'Guaranteed Fit'. My phone call to 800 GE CARES found the agent to be unaware and unable to understand the issue and unable to help. She directed me to 'Parts' who could not help either without a part number.
Bottom-line: In my experience, GE Customer Service is very difficult to work with. There were nested menus (if you have yet to register your product with the number you are calling from) which don't release you to an agent easily.
Finally, there appears nothing to back up their claim of 'Guaranteed Fit'. There appears to be tendency for cost cutting to the bone on GE's part. I could 'recommend' the new unit to a prospective buyer, but only with all the caveats noted above.

review_title: A Great Unit with Several Issues...
review_text:
Absolutely beautiful refrigerator and the black stainless finish really sets it off. There is an abundance of room in the upper refrigerated section and the door-in-door feature is certainly a plus. The ability to change the temperature in middle drawer allows you to have additional storage space based on a particular need. Based on these features alone I would have rated it five stars; however, there are two design issues that knock it back to three stars.
My biggest complaint is that the icemaker is substandard for such a well designed refrigerator. I never thought to look at the ice bin capacity during the buying process and shame on me for not doing so. The ice bin is exceedingly small...or should I say shockingly small. We find ourselves constantly running out of ice and the icemaker simply can't keep up with demand. Fortunately, we kept our old Kenmore Elite, which has a great icemaker, and placed it in the garage. This allows us to supplement our needs; however, we would be buying bags of ice had we not kept the
Kenmore.
The second issue is the door-in-door design. To open the outer door you press a small latch that is built into the handle. No problem there...until you try to close it. You have to push the door to the fully closed position and listen for the sound of the latch clicking in place. If you don't, the door just swings open and it will stay open until you go back and close it properly. Fortunately, the unit has a warning alarm that beeps if a door is open for any extended period of time. However, the alarm is not all that loud which could be a problem if you immediately exit the kitchen after you close the door. This is not a huge problem but it is one you would not expect in a unit at this price level.
All in all we are pleased except for these couple of issues. This unit should have earned five stars but the sub-par icemaker and storage bin take
the rating down to three stars.

review_title: Really nice fridge, but needs redesigns to get 5 stars from me.
review_text:
We researched quite a bit to find the fridge we wanted. Guess I should have spent a little more time with this one in person.

PROS:
Don't get me wrong...it's a great fridge. The black stainless on this LG is like a high-dollar paint job on a luxury car. Very deep and shiny and does NOT take fingerprints at all like regular stainless. You also can't use magnets on it. So no matter how many sticky-fingered kids you have in your house, this fridge will look like brand new for a long time.

There is tons of room in the fridge portion and the adjustable everything makes it easy to customize the interior for your organizational style (we all have one...milk and juice on the upper right, condiments in the door, beer and sodas on the left). Many options to play with. Also, the lighting inside is the best I've ever seen in a fridge. With the glass shelves and bright light, nothing can hide or get lost. That can really help cut down on wasting food you have to toss because it was not seen or forgotten.

I've never had a french door fridge and this one also has the pull-out drawer. THAT is a really nice feature. Both the compartments and the temperature of the drawer are adjustable for whatever your needs. I still can't decide what I want to put in there but I know it'll be fun to figure out.

Freezer on the bottom is what you would expect. It does have a slide-out tray in the top of it that is good for pizzas, bacon, other flat frozen items. The drawer is deep but like any drawer freezer, things can get piled up and tossed around in there. Not as easy to find things in a drawer freezer than a side-by-side or top. But it suits it's purpose. Drawers glide very easily too.

CONS:
The ice and water system is the only thing I'm not thrilled about. It really needs a re-design and here's why. We're all familiar with how these things work. You push your glass against the concave paddle that cradles your glass and ice or water falls in. Simple. But LG had to try and fix it. And their fix needs fixing.

First, the paddles for water and ice are flat and are coated with the same slick paint as the doors. I know it sounds picky, but it takes some effort to hold the glass still while pressing these paddles because it slides around. For ice, this isn't that much of an issue because the ice area is 'in' the door and has the little tray/drip pan underneath.

But the water spout is in the worst place and is as poorly designed as it could be. It is not 'in' the door but is more even or flush with the front of the door but above and outside of the little niche where the glass is supposed to go. So if it drips after you fill your glass, it drips straight onto the fridge below or on to the floor. Moreover, the spout the water comes from is too short and angled in a way that makes it so you cannot put the lip of your glass under it. And if you use a Bubba 52 mug like me that's rounded, it's nearly impossible to fill without making a mess because the cup slides all over the place on the slick, flat paddle and you have to tilt it a bit so the water even gets in the cup. I can never get Bubba 52 completely filled.

Lastly, this fridge is very deep. It sticks out from my countertop at least 6-8 inches and my countertop is standard depth. A fridge this deep would look much better in a built-in section with sides and a top than just in a space at the end of a counter.

Hope those comments help.

review_title: WARNING: NEVER BUY LG. You will regret it!
review_text:
Dear Mr Riddle,

It it with disappointment that I am writing you about my experience with my LG french door refrigerator. I purchased this refrigerator from Home Depot on 12/7/15. It was installed in my new kitchen in April 2016. I liked refrigerator and all of its features so I was upset when it started intermittently making a loud vibrating sound in July. The sound was coming from the fan behind the filter. As the appliance is covered under the one year manufacturers warranty, I called LG customer service and was told to call a local appliance servicer called "Reliable Appliance Service" myself. The noise stopped by the next day and everything seemed to be working so I never called the service center.

Then, sometime during the week of August 22nd the noise started again. Within the week the fan stopped working. All the food on the top of the fridge was warm and everything on the bottom froze. Additionally the ice and water dispenser stopped working and the letters "E rF" were displayed. I called customer support hoping they could tell me what was wrong. They again told me again to call Reliable Appliance Service. I called Reliable Appliance Service and they said that LG needs to schedule the repair or it will be treated as a cash ticket. I called customer support again and was told that they need to submit a request to their service locator team. Several days passed and I heard nothing. By this time all of my food was spoiled.

On Friday September 2nd I once again called customer support and was told that they still haven't found a servicer. They would prioritize my case with the service locator team and would return my call on Tuesday, September 6. I never heard back so I called customer support again on Thursday September 8th. I was told that they were still trying to find a servicer that would be willing to come to my house 40 miles from Anchorage, Alaska, and that there was nothing more that they could do.

Needless to say by this time I am angry and exhausted. My refrigerator has been broken for over two weeks and your company has conveniently absolved themselves of any duty to fix the problem. Thankfully, Home Depot is willing to pick up the refrigerator and give me a refund. They will be here on Saturday September 10. I will then buy a GE refrigerator.

In the mean time I am telling everyone I know to avoid LG products as the appliances are very unreliable and customer service is unwilling to help. I am sure that you have an interest in keeping your company reputation in good standing with potential customers and therefore I am hoping that by informing you of my experience you can assist your team to make a better product and improve customer service.

At the very least your company should have been willing to pick up the appliance from my home and take it into servicer. Instead I was offered no help what-so-ever. I have spent hours on the phone with absolutely no interest on your company's behalf of helping. If there is one thing that I can hope come of this is that no one who I know buys an LG appliance. This has been literally the worst customer service experience of my life.

review_title: A nightmare story of LG service
review_text:
On November 23rd I had called LG because my french door refrigerator had stopped cooling a few days earlier. I was told that since it was past the 1 year full warranty I would have to pay for the labor but the parts would be covered. So they charged me $350 and said I would get a call in 24 hours to schedule service. a few days later I got a call and scheduled a repairman to come out a week later.

When the repairmen came out he examined the fridge and said that they compressor and closed cooling system would have to be replaced and that he would have to order parts. A week and a half later he came back to repair the fridge which last for about 6 days and then completely stopped cooling again. On December 29th I called LG and explained that my fridge wasn't working and they told me that they would set up an appointment to have someone come out. I asked them if they could get the parts out quickly since this would be the second time they would have to fix it but the LG rep told me that the do not do expedited shipping for anybody and that I would have to wait. The repairman came out on January 3rd and said that they compressor may have been bad and that he would have to order a new one.

It is now November 26th (almost a month since the repairman came out) and after leaving messages with the repairman that didn't get returnedI called LG to find out what was happening. after waiting on hold for 45 minutes I finally spoke with a customer service representative who said she would call the repairman to see what was happening. when she got back on the line she said that she spoke with the repair company and was told that they do have someone who could repair closed cooling system refrigerators and that they never bothered to call me and tell me this.

The LG rep told me that the repairmen was going to file a claim with LG and that they would have to refund LG for the money they were paid for the repair. I asked the rep if they were going to send out another repair person and they said that they would have to be refunded first and that the person at the repair company said they would do it in 24-48 hours. I then asked the LG rep what would happen if they did not call LG back and refund them, the rep told me she was told they would do it in 24-48 hours. I asked them again "What happens if they don't do it?" and the rep did not give me an answer. so basically, even though I did nothing wrong I have to wait and hope that the repair person refunds them, while I get nothing for the $350 I paid 2 months ago. And since the fridge still needs to be repaired I expect that it will take another week or two for a repairman to come out (big IF on that on) and then another couple weeks for parts to come in since LG won't help out getting it done quickly.

I expect that I will have to wait another month to get my refrigerator serviced and that it will be 3 months of not having a fridge. LG was more than happy to take my money but they could care less about actually following through with their customers.

product_title: LMXS30776D 36 Freestanding French Door Refrigerator with 30 Cu. Ft. Capacity CustomChill Drawer Slim SpacePlus Ice System Premium LED Lights Multi-Air Flow in Black Stainless Steel
review_title: Probably one of the best refrigerators currently on the market, buy with confidence!
review_text:
I did not buy my LG LMXS3077D from Amazon but felt compelled to post this review to help you in your shopping/decision process...

Just 3 years ago we purchased the then top of the line Samsung refrigerator. From day one my wife complained about the layout, the freezer access, the ice maker, etc, etc. After leaving a door open a few times she had enough and started shopping for something new.

Alas this LG refrigerator. I could write a novel but if you're like me you just need the quick details so here it goes:

My wife LOVES this refrigerator. Some of the features I thought were gimmicky but now that I'm using them I do agree they are handy. This includes the extra door that opens just the very front of the right hand door allowing you easy access to milk and other thinks not stored deep inside the fridge. The reason why this is so handy is that the doors are a bit heavy but opening the front "thin" door is very easy.

Next is the extra pull out drawer. Didn't think too much of this either but I see it a a whole extra storage space when the main compartment is full. With its custom temperature this becomes very handy also.

In the freezer there are 3 levels. The top level is a "pull out drawer" perfect for most ice cream tubs, frozen waffle and other breakfast boxes and other stackable boxes. The middle roll out shelf is shallow but perfect for pizza boxes and other low height boxes. The basin is, never ending, or a at least it seems that way. Great for large items, a frozen turkey, bags of frozen vegetables, etc

Now one of my favorites, the in door ice maker. I'm a daily user of ice and my only condition in buying a new fridge is it had to have door dispensable ice. Why? First and foremost I like fresh ice. Ice sitting in a freezer bin quickly goes smooth and adopts the smells of all the food circulating through the system. The in-door design of this ice maker mean there is not some big box taking up a portion of the main cabin (like my Samsung did) and the ice stays nice and fresh because it's in it's own sealed and small box. Even though it does take up a portion of the left door, LG included shelves large enough to hold salad dressing bottles, whipped cream, etc and really it's somewhat unnoticeable. A few have commented that the ice maker is small and yes it's smaller than a traditional ice maker but it makes ice fairly quickly and unless you are hosting a large party you probably will not run out of ice.

My next comment can be taken good or bad. The black stainless steel is non-metallic which means you cannot cover your refrigerator with papers using magnets. I absolutely love a clean looking fridge. You may consider this a negative if you really like a fridge full of papers and photos and things. And in case you're wondering, it hides fingerprints very well.

The control panel and LED display is well done. After a few seconds the numbers and other images disappear into the panel but quickly come back with a touch of a button.

How's the performance? We've had ours for 3 months now. This fridge maintains a very constant temperature and is extremely quiet.

Would I recommend this to a friend? Absolutely, hands down. Samsung and most of the other manufacturers make good products but this particular product goes above and beyond anything else we've seen on the market. Would I buy the same refrigerator again? Absolutely, I have no complaints whatsoever!

review_text:

The first time was under warranty and I had no troubles getting it replaced. The second time the fan, ice maker, and 1/2 of the parts for the freezer were replaced. review_title: Would I buy this one again? Yes! Would I recommend it to a friend? Yes!
review_text:
I have had mine for two plus years now. We replaced a huge full size side by side fridge with this counter depth fridge. It is true that the ice maker is small and doesn't make much ice; but, if I had a choice I wouldn't have an ice maker inside my fridge anyway. This one doesn't take up valuable space inside the main compartment. The freezer bin and its drawers are so well designed that I can keep as much frozen food as my old side by side freezer held. The doors easily shut without having to check on them. We have a different brand French door fridge in our camp house on which the doors don't "grab" and I would replace that brand with Another of this exact model if I could afford it. The full drawer in the middle allows me to prepare a huge tray of appetizers. The depth is the full depth of the fridge, so when other counter depths might interfere with entertainment, this ones does not. The middle drawer can be a diff temp from the upper fridge section too, so we have used it for ice cream (cold enough to have it soft and not rock hard, for beer, for white wine that is chilled but not too cold, etc. we get our use out of this. I probably won't ever go back to a side by side. And the drawer feature is on my list forever too.

The diamond black color is actually better than the shines black one I had before. I was uncertain about the color, but I wanted black and appliance manufacturers apparently decided true black was out of style (not). The diamond black works fine with my other solid black appliances, and it doesn't show fingerprints and smudges quite as bad as the pure black or stainless steel surfaces do.

Would I buy this one again? Yes! Would I recommend it to a friend? Yes!

review_title: Most cons mentioned by other reviewers are actually good things
review_text:
I own this dryer (though I didn't buy it from Amazon… I got mine from Lowe's and I DON'T recommend them). I have the electric version. Yes, it's true that clothes aren't baked so they're too hot to touch, but that's not good for fabric anyway. Condensation dryers don't do that. Personally speaking, I'm fine with that (and the energy savings that I gain, let alone the decreased environmental impact).
Not to contradict other reviewers, but I personally do not find it difficult to set things the way I want them to be. There are 12 "standard" programs (e.g., Cotton Dry and Extra Dry; Perm P Damp, Dry and Extra Dry; Delicates, Timed Dry Variable)—a plethora of choices! And there are four "special" programs (Towels, Sanitize, Jeans, and Bulky/Large Items). Beyond that, you can adjust the settings for dryness level (+1, +2, or +3), wrinkle block (+60 min, +90 min), and more. One of my favorite features is the ability to set a "finish in" parameter, i.e., if you don't want to disturb your downstairs neighbor after, say 11PM, but want to finish a load so it's ready in the morning, you can set a finish time for, say 8AM. Result: no annoyed downstairs neighbor AND freshly tumbled, non-wrinkled clothes the next morning! (And I'm not saying the dryer is loud at all; quite the contrary. I just have neighbors who are extremely sensitive to noise after 11, so I try to accommodate them as much as possible.)
Another thing to note is that there is some additional maintenance with condensation dryers: you have to clean the heat exchange unit every month or so, depending on usage. But this is drop-dead simple to do on the Bosch: just slide the lunch-box size unit out of the dryer and rinse it off to clear the lint/fluff that accumulates (see photos). The (positive) flip side of that is that there's no dryer vent to clear, so no worries about blocked vents or potential fires caused by the accumulation of lint.
I want to reiterate that everyone has things that they can deal with and things they can't. I'm a techie and a geek, so I enjoy playing around with all the doo-dads and features on things I buy. Having written user documentation in the past, I'm also one of the few people on the face of the earth that actually reads that stuff (and it's simply AMAZING the things you can learn by doing that!! LOL).

product_title: Samsung RF26HFENDWW 25.5 Cu. Ft. White French Door Refrigerator - Energy Star
review_text:
Have owned this refrigerator for 2 1/2 months and it consistently bangs and clanks (loudly). product_title: Bosch WAT28400UC 300 2.2 Cu. Ft. White Stackable Front Load Washer - Energy Star
review_title: Not perfect, but pretty darn good
review_text:
We're on our THIRD attempt at compact laundry that works for our condo. We first bought the LG combo washer/dryer. We must have gotten a lemon--it was really a disaster in terms of vibration. I thought it was going to take out the whole floor! The thing was terrifying, even though we had the service department come out to level it twice (and yes, the shipping bolts were removed!) The drying cycle also took an incredibly long time, and it smelled as if our clothes were getting cooked. In reviews people seem to either love or hate this machine.

We replaced this with a stackable compact Bosch set, which is great, but still has some vibration. It's WORLDS, even whole UNIVERSES better than the LG combo, but it's noticable to my downstairs neighbor. With some loads the pans hanging from her ceiling and the paintings on her wall vibrate, and we can't figure out which load-type will cause it. You should expect that the dryer will off-load heat into the space, but that was true of the LG as well. I think that's the case with all non-vented condenser dryers. The Bosch set has seemed well-made, and were it not for the slight vibration bothering our neighbor, would suit our needs perfectly as a family of 3.

We're having the Electrolux compact stackable set installed this weekend, primarily because it has a second floor noise and vibration guarantee. I was surprised to see that it's rated the same as the Bosch set in terms of vibration by CR, though. If it has the same level of vibration as the Bosch set, it's going back for sure. But if it's better, out of consideration for our neighbor, we'll keep it and eat the cost.

product_title: Bosch WAT28400UC 300 2.2 Cu. Ft. White Stackable Front Load Washer - Energy Star

product_title: Bosch WAT28402UC 800 2.2 Cu. Ft. White Stackable Front Load Washer - Energy Star
review_title: Lots of improvement over the old model

The new feature of "clean the drum" is what we are looking for years. All the other vendors and stores will take 3-4 weeks to deliver this washer. Shipping is free and no tax (outstate).  The only shortage is that we have to install it ourselves, but it is very easy for us because it is a replacement of our old Bosch washer. We just need to plug the electrical plug to the drier and hook up the hoses and drain pipe. The washer comes with hoses, but it was originally designed to be used in conjunction with the tab water which is closed most of the time. review_text:
My partner and I live in a 30 year-old condo in which we are slowly upgrading mostly-original appliances. Just before my birthday this year, the oven handle and (large) pieces of plastic fascia fell off our coil stove while I was trying desperately to cook dinner. Being a kind soul, he took me oven shopping. I've been buying pieces of tri-ply and enameled iron for years in preparation for THE FUTURE (read: Induction), but it wasn't in the cards. We don't have the moolah.

What I really wanted, and what we could afford, was a dual oven. I've taught a few friends to cook, and one of those acolytes bought a house with a convection oven. Saying I covet his setup is understating what I'd like to do with his Jenn Air. Despite some of the "lower-end" finish options on this stove (exposed oven coils, controls on the backsplash), I decided that the benefits outweigh the drawbacks. Frankly, I don't need fancy touch controls as long as the burners work, and the oven(s) bake as advertised! For the most part, this stove is quite impressive. The detractors are limited to the two 6" back burners. So, I'll get to that, but I'll start with the positives, which frankly outweigh the negatives.

I am a holiday cook. By this, I mean that when I do Thanksgiving, it's done properly. When one is trying to heat seven dishes at once and roast a Turkey, one rapidly becomes overwhelmed with the calculus of burning vs. reheating. That problem is now, thankfully, gone. With two separate cavities that can be heated to different temperatures, ya don't have to choose what's going to be beautiful and what's going to be burnt, anymore... Without spending $3,500.00 on a double wall-oven (which wouldn't fit in our kitchen, anyway). Further, the upper cavity heats up very quickly. 350 in at most five minutes. The lower oven is a bit more... sedate, but by no means slow. Also, the convection option makes for great, evenly-browned roasts, and evenly caramelized bakes! I'm still figuring out convection mode, but it works as advertised, as long as you're willing to experiment with a fast-read thermometer and cooking times.

Now, more positives! The two dual burners are awesome. I haven't been a huge fan of electric elements over the years. Mostly due to my history of coil-stove rental cooking, I have developed a healthy loathing of the genre, and gone misty-eyed over my memories of cheap, burn-ey gas stove realness back in Michigan at my parents' home. Short story, we don't have exterior venting in our condo, so... Electric range it is! Again, I've been chomping at the bit for induction in the US for a decade, but affordability hasn't been forthcoming. Say nothing about the fact that I can get a 7" $50 1,800 watt burner from IKEA (or say something!), a stovetop solution is still rather more expensive than my budget. I prefer large-capacity pans, so having a 6/9" burner and a 9/11" burner is perfect. I only have two pans large enough to take advantage of the 11" element, and all my other pans are 9" compatible. I can properly heat the big pans, and there is still the option to step down the smaller burner to a very powerful 6" element. They heat quickly, the heat is concentrated, and on my pans, I never have to go above the '7' setting, unless boiling liquid. And, boil it does! Quickly... Enough. So, you know, enough said.

Now, the detractors. The two back elements are an enigma. For pots under 2 quarts, they heat as quickly as one could wish. For vessels over two quarts? Not so much. I tried to boil water in a four-quart pot for pasta, and 12 minutes later, there was no discernable boilage. The pan couldn't sit fully on the burner, to be fair, because the control knobs and backsplash jut out too much, but it was a tri-ply conductor. At the end of it, I could still contact the surface of the water with my finger without blistering. My old coil stove, falling apart as it was, could boil water in 10 minutes on a small burner. This is disappointing. Very disappointing. I don't really understand why $300.00 more gets you both a bridge-burner AND hidden coils in the ovens? Seriously? I think there's something wrong here.

Granted, I'm more impressed than disappointed. I wouldn't give up the dual ovens for induction, at this point. I love this stove! I really, really do. There are small problems, but I'm besotted. It does what I want it to, and, frankly? There is no true reason to use 6" burners, apparently. I'll just buy another IKEA hob.

Finally, an addition! I understand the folks who hate a ceramic/glass cooktop, but this one is pretty good, considering. Yes, you will spend WAY more time frowning, spraying and cleaning, but when you really think about it, how much filth were you ignoring below coil burners all those years? For me, the amount was a whole lot. And, if you use a nice ceramic glass cream cleaner with a no-scratch pad once every other time cooking, and an all-purpose cleaner the other half of the time, you'll be more than OK. It's possible that the stovetop 'can' delaminate, but it hasn't happened with mine. And, I've cooked a great deal in my month of ownership. It's been a great month of learning about convection modes and finally getting how to use the back burners properly. They are still underpowered, but I'm more at peace with that now. If anything, I love this stove more than I did before.

Here are some of the problems we have had:
1-the oven is not at a true temperature and doesn't cook the food. It takes much, much longer to cook than any recipe says it will. I have to build in extra time. I could probably hand that, but the next two are NOT acceptable for a 3 month old stove (yes, only 3 months old).

3-We had burner refuse to go off. All of the nobs were off, but the burner on light and hot cook top light remained on. We tried to turn the switches on and off again, but it remained on. We waited to see if it was just a matter of time to cool down... nope - it was still hot 30 minutes later. The only way to turn it off was to go to our fuse box and shut it off from the main switch and reset the fuse (!!!!!)

When you call GE, you get a robo line. They did send someone out with little interest and he "couldn't replicate the problem."

I hate this oven and I wanted to badly to love it. I wish I had just gone with a single standard oven. More options, more to break. I feel like I have a $1200 lemon.

product_title: GE GDF610PSJSS 24" Energy Star Built In Dishwasher with 16 Place Settings in Stainless Steel
review_text:
(Our model number is GDF610PMJ0ES, so may have a few differences. Check it out, first. They appeared to be identical, in the store.)

INTRO
We replaced our dishwasher, range, and microwave together, and went with GE (slate finish … LOVE it.). We have reviews for all three. The slate finish is classy and makes our kitchen look like it came out of a magazine. The purchases were made as a ‘package’ at Lowe’s in Lafayette, IN, and came in only $100 over what we’d planned to spend. Nice. We can’t say enough good things about Lowe’s service. From the staff in the store (who kept us informed at every step) to installation: excellent.

The only problem we have with all three appliances is – oddly enough – the end-of-cycle alarms (and stove timer) are very quiet. It would be nice if we could set a timer loud enough to be heard in the next room, when necessary. However, we now have kitchen appliances that don’t scream at us, so I guess that’s a decent tradeoff. (Note: you can set the microwave ‘buzzer’ from mute to a third level of loud, but the highest still can’t be heard very far away.)

Our reviews are for:
Dishwasher: Model – GDF610PMJ0ES (plastic interior; controls on outside of door)
Range (Gas): Model – JGB700EEJ1ES
Microwave: Model – JVM6175EF1ES

PROS
Cleaning is excellent, the unit is quiet, and the controls are where you can see them (and keep an eye on how much time is left on the cycle). However, there is a model with hidden controls if you like opening the door to check them. We figure we’d rather have at-a-glance access, and why wear out a latch?

Little things mean a lot, and this dishwasher has a lot of good, convenient ‘little things.’ The bottom of the door (inside) is configured like a ramp, not a wall. This allows all the water to drain off after the cycle or if you happen to dump something in there. Nice feature.
Although you can adjust the top shelf, we’ve found no need. It’s positioned so well you can get surprisingly large items on top, should you need to.
This unit seems a bit smaller inside than our old one, but the layout is so efficient, we get more in it at one time. GE has eliminated the #1 problem we had with our old dishwasher: the large ‘hump’ on the underneath side of the TOP basket, which prevented us from placing large items in the middle of the LOWER basket. (I think it was part of the water system.) In this unit, we can line dinner plates up all the way across without an issue. Perfect.

You can place the cutlery container* on the door or on the lower basket. There’s also a convenient accessory basket for small items*. You can sit it pretty much anywhere, but it’s designed to hook onto the inside of the top shelf. It takes up a lot less space than the basket we purchased, for our old dishwasher, from a baby department at a store.

A nice touch for the cutlery basket: unlike the one in our old dishwasher, this one has a totally flat base. It sits up straight, outside the unit, without your having to prop it up against something. We remove it after the cycle to air dry, so this is a big plus for us.
Loading this unit takes a little getting used to, but GE has certainly thought of everything. You may be surprised, as we were, how easy it is to get plates to NOT knock against each other. The way they’ve designed the ‘spines’ throughout = the most efficient dishwasher we’ve ever owned when it comes to space and what you can get in there.

*These baskets both have covers with slots in them so you can put the stem of flatware or even a toothbrush in them. The covers can also keep small items in the baskets, but they do not have to be closed during the cycle.

CONS
Odd pulsing of the motor as it drains water. It’s something we’ll get used to, but right now it’s a bit annoying if we’re watching TV (can you tell our home is the dreaded “open concept”?) No biggie.
One of our wine glass stem holder units won’t stay in the up position when we’re trying to load the top shelf. We usually keep it down and place smaller items underneath and things like grill tools on top of it. So, “down” isn’t a big issue. Just inconvenient when you’re trying to place things beneath it.

We air dry and take the cutlery basket out immediately after the load finishes. For some reason, the basket doesn’t dry very quickly, and it takes a long time for the silverware to be ready.

review_text: I've had nothing but problems since the day this was delivered and the worst part is that LG has the WORST customer service department I have ever had to deal with. A recent chat representative even wrote that she will go "one step a time for me" while reading from the manual. I have a masters degree in nursing, I can read directions!  The stove comes set up for natural gas and it took 2 technicians almost 2 hours to get this set up and installed.  Cost me an additional $320 and yes, these were experienced technicians from a reputable company, but very little is known about this model.  First issue was that the ultraheat burner would not ignite and had a flair up issue when it did.  I had to get "approval" from LG for a service call and again, even the company of their choice knew very little about this stove.  He had to call LG for help and their technicians talked him through the repair.  The upper oven was burning just about everything I tried to bake so I asked him to check that.  The oven was set at 350 and his professional digital external thermometer was reading 425 degrees AFTER the preheat cycle and took forever to come anywhere near 350 degrees. The instructions tell you how to adjust the oven temps, but the (+) does not appear on the digital display, as stated in the manual, so you have no idea if the adjustments your making are even effective! After burning lots and lots of food, I finally got the oven to semi work. I put a high quality thermometer in the oven and it was all over the place, 300-425 degrees during the baking cycle. Now lets talk about the lower oven. From day one there was a terrible odor which I was told was from it being new.  Again, it burned just about every thing I put in so I started playing with the adjustment feature.  It got to a point where some rolls were golden brown on top, but the bottoms were barely done, but at least they weren't burnt! Not to mention that this thing sounds like you have a jet engine running in your kitchen! Now, here's the real kicker. This morning I opened the lower oven to move the rack and the entire inside was black, covered in soot (see photo of rag I used to wipe just the bottom.)  I Called LG but they refused to let me speak to the technical department to see if this was normal for a new oven or if I needed yet another service call.  I was told "this department only speaks to other technicians."  I called Lowe's and this piece of junk will be on it's way back to the store later this week.  Thank heaven I purchased it from Lowe's, at least someone stands behind the products they sell.

review_text: The oven is calibrated at 350 degrees and cooks fine at this temperature. However, when I set the cooking temperature to 400 degrees the internal temperature is actually 450 degrees and I burn things. If I try to cook at a lower temperature the calibration is off in the other direction. I had a technician come out to fix the problem. He confirmed my calibrations and told me there was no fix because the ovens were designed this way. His statement was confirmed by several LG employees by email and phone.  The technician suggested I get a remote read cooking thermometer and use that for my oven temperature. Would not recommend this oven. I generally had a good impression of LG before this. UPDATE:I I got an external reading thermometer and tried to calibrate the oven for use,. The problem occurred between 350 and 352 deg. The internal temp went up by 50 deg with this 2 degree change. LG still would do nothing. I had a local repairman confirm my calibration. He talked with an LG tech and both said it needed a new electronics board. $375 later the oven is working  correctly. After initially offering to help, then denying there was a problem, they will still not help offset the cost.

I have to get in there and scrub with a cloth or sos pads to get the drippings picked up. I also noticed within the first few months of having it, that the inside enamel has a chip in it, has started to rust, and that the underside of the knobs are corroding and rusty. I cook a lot of meals and the oven gets dirty very fast so I have to break down the top range quite often to get into the nooks. It's not so easy to wipe down. Plus, the covers of the gas burners are stained and I cannot lift those stains off at all. The stainless steel shows everything until you cut through all of the splatters thoroughly.
Cooking rack has to be in the center on the top or it burns your food quickly if on lower rack (which is preferred because otherwise your food touches the top and doesn't fit. Cooking has been uneven in the bottom. If I use the top rack, sometimes the item doesn't fit and so I put it on the bottom rack of the bottom oven and it takes longer.
