review_title: Broken, Leaks Gas; LG Won't Help
review_text:
Three months after purchasing this range, we smelled a lot of gas in our house. On an emergency visit, the local gas company determined that the range was leaking gas, that it is unable to hold gas pressure, and that it is a hazardous appliance that could result in serious injury or death if operated. The gas company turned off gas to the LG Range.

The LG Range was well within warranty, so I contacted LG expecting them to take care of it. Instead, they sent a technician who decided he was smarter than the gas company, and there was nothing wrong with the range. Neither LG nor the technician used any common sense or independent judgment, and they refused to do anything. After numerous calls and emails, I have managed to reach other people at LG, who have only continued to punt the issue down the line without offering or providing any resolution at all.

And it's been more than two weeks, with a family of six trying to make school lunches and dinners using nothing but a microwave.

Apparently, LG was content to let us continue using a hazardous range that leaks gas and could seriously injure or kill us, and now they are under no hurry whatsoever to even respond appropriately and help us. This has been a disastrous experience. So much for that warranty.

review_text: I was excited to get this range as part of a new Samsung appliance suite for my kitchen. Huge hassle, especially after using the oven for a year or two after purchasing it new. It does cool down very quickly and the LED lighting is nice but they neglected to take the lighting to the rear of the unit. When you have such a large refrigerator, the lack of lighting is an issue. It is extremely quiet. We didn't even realize it was running when we first plugged it in.
Now the cons: as stated, the lack of lighting in the rear of the inside, no auto nightlight at the water and ice dispenser, the ice maker is SLOW. It is slow making ice as well as you have to stand there forever to get a glass of ice whether it is cubed or crushed, and there isn't a flat grid to sit your glass on while waiting for the ice to finally fall. Also, the water lever behind the ice one is annoying. I would advise people with children or teenagers not get this unit as the doors will not close easily and if not shut firmly will slowly open back up, making it hard for children and teenagers wouldn't notice.

review_title: A few quirks, but overall its been amazing so far.  Owner for a month.
review_text:
First of all, I love the way this fridge looks, its very nicely designed from a visual perspective. I opted for the black stainless steel which has a grey look on the doors and is very nice! The sides and top are a textured black semi-gloss finish. The controls are intuitive and easy to operate, the handles are easy to install on the door and easy to operate. I LOVE the easy access door to all of my frequently used items!

A few lessons learned after purchase:

1. This is a fairly large fridge, we have a small kitchen and this unit fits but its its definitely deeper and wider than some spaces will allow for. I forgot to measure everything else but height and was surprised how much deeper this model is than my old fridge. This is not a negative mark on the fridge, just a lesson learned for prospective shoppers considering a new fridge in general.

2. Definitely follow the instructions in the owners manual (get it online, it may not be in the box on delivery). I thought something was wrong when the water dispenser in the left door was leaking quite a lot of water. I discovered that you have to run a few gallons of water through the system to flush out all the air in the lines which is what causes the leaking. After doing that, it doesn't even drip at all now. All of the YouTube videos complaining of the drip are from people who didn't read the manual.

3. The only negative mark I can think of for this fridge is the static drawers/shelves in the quick access door. You can fit a few tall items in the bottom shelf, but forget it for the other two. It would be super nice if the heights of the shelves were adjustable on the top two. Not a deal breaker, but definitely a frustration point if you want to store more than two one-gallon jugs of something in the door, it just won't fit in the other shelves at all.

4. You will need to customize the shelving heights inside the main body of the fridge. Samsung has a few convenient features of the shelves that are very nice, but the default configuration is likely not going to work for many people without some adjustments. Plan to spend a few minutes stocking this fridge and re-arranging items several times to figure out the best way to arrange everything.

5. The quick/power modes on the fridge and freezer functions is very convenient. We used this option when initially stocking the unit with food. Having the doors open a lot and adjusting things as you stock it causes the inside to warm up quite a bit. The temp indicator said we got up to 42F inside. It only took a couple of hours for everything to stabilize back to the 37F I had the unit set to. I then re-enabled energy saver mode and put the settings back to normal.

6. I LOVE the LED lighting inside this model. Its a very good spread of light, you can definitely see better whats inside and it just looks cool!

7. Wish list - motion sensor on water dispenser area light. You can turn on the water dispenser light or turn it off, but no in between. I would love to see manufactures start putting a motion sensor in this area to save energy but also make it more night time friendly in open floor plan homes. I want the light in general, but at night I don't want to have to remember to manually turn off the light before bed every day!

8. Nit-pick - the divider in the convenience flex tray is nifty but not a solid wall. Its just two bars and food items and packages of things can still slide between the gaps in the rails. Its a cool idea, but more divider surface would be a little more effective at keeping things in place.

9. Its going to take me some time to adjust to the water flavor through this model. This is my first Samsung Fridge and my previous unit had a PUR filter which made my nasty town water taste good. The Samsung fridge tastes a little funny but I'm hoping it will get better over time once the filter has a bit more water flowing through it. Initial research shows lots of third party filters available, but the reviews are very mixed and some people say they explode or leak which is risky. Samsung recommends using only their branded filters. Still, I wish PUR made a compatible filter for this fridge. I did end up buying an "in-line" water filter to connect behind the fridge, connecting it to the water line. This has helped to improve the water flavor quite dramatically. So that took care of the issue, you may need a second high flow filter to help supplement the Samsung filter to compensate for bad tasting town water.

Overall, I really like this model fridge. Of all the demo units in the store we looked at, this is the only one that really caught my eye. The design is just so modern and cool, the lighting is near perfect, the size is good for a family of 5 and it was on sale.

No appliance is perfect, there are moving parts so wear and breakdown is just part of the owner experience with pretty much anything. So I bought an extended third party appliance warranty just in case. Time will tell how good this fridge holds up to my children! But it sure looks good and seems to work really well so far. I'm impressed and would recommend this model to others.

product_title: Samsung Appliance RF28JBEDBSG 36" Energy Star Rated Food Showcase French Door Refrigerator in Black Stainless Steel
review_text:
I agonized for months over choosing a new refrigerator because I wanted modern features (such as an ice maker and water dispenser in the door, French doors, and so forth. But if you read the reviews of the higher-end refrigerators (like this one and other Samsung and LG models), you'll find about 75% five star reviews and about 25% one star reviews. What gives? For the most part, the five star reviews (like mine) are from people who just bought the fridge, they love the features, and everything still works fine. For the most part, the one star reviews are from people who have had their refrigerator longer and are having problems with it.

I've read numerous articles about how to buy a refrigerator and have perused the user forums at length and the impression that I'm getting is that these high-end refrigerators have all sorts of bells and whistles to attract buyers and justify their high prices, but the more technology that goes into a product, the greater the chance that something is going to fail. And a refrigerator is not like a computer in that you can't just toss it in the trunk and take it in for repairs. You have to pay someone to come out, just to look at the thing. The advice that I've gathered from all of this reading has been to buy a very simple refrigerator and freezer that has no ice maker, no digital display, etc. You know, the refrigerator your grandparents had. In fact, some people recommend buying an old, used refrigerator from a reputable manufacturer who still has parts available. I couldn't bring myself to do that. The features of this awesome fridge were too much to resist. So I bought this fridge and paid for the extended warranty through an appliance chain.

It's been a month now and I still love the thing, but I don't expect problems with it for a year or more, so I'll be back to revise my review if my positive experience with this unit changes. On to my review of this particular refrigerator:

POSITIVES
1) The ice maker and water dispenser seem to work just fine. Plenty of ice and cold water.
2) The door-in-door feature is really cool. I can store drinks and things that I want quick access to in that outer door without having to pull open the entire door (which is heavier, and therefore takes longer to open) and let the cold air pour out of the fridge and onto the kitchen floor.
3) The storage space is HUGE! This refrigerator doesn't take that much more space up than did the fridge it replaced, yet it seems to have a lot more room in it.
4) Every little bit of interior space on the doors has shelves, even if they're tiny in spots. Those are perfect for small condiment bottles (like Tabasco).
5) My favorite feature of all is the temperature-configurable central drawer. I like my drinks (beer and water) ICE COLD! I've set the temperature on this center drawer at the "Cold Drinks" setting (which is one degree above freezing) and that's where the beer and water go. No more putting a beer in the freezer so I can have a really cold one later, and then waiting too long and discovering that I've created a frozen beer-pop. Now I've always got ice cold drinks any time. This center drawer also has a movable four-way divider that's great for keeping the beer bottles lined up in neat rows with their labels showing so my friends can see all of the beers I'm offering them without having to hunt around. And the center drawer's temperature can be set for freezing, keeping drinks icy cold, chilling party trays down just the right amount, etc. Love this feature.

AREAS FOR IMPROVEMENT
1) I tested the filtered water that is dispensed for TDS (Total Dissolved Solids). You want the amount of total dissolved solids to be as low as possible, as the dissolved solids are minerals and (possibly) contaminants. The results were that the water filtered by this refrigerator has total dissolved solids about halfway between straight tap water and water that's been filtered by a Brita Pitcher. That was disappointing. It means that the water filtration is not really all that thorough. I'm going to recalibrate my two TDS testers and try again, and I'll post an update if my numbers change. My solution is likely going to be putting another water filter, in-line with the tubing that goes into the fridge. Then the water will be double filtered and I should be able to measure lower TDS values.
2) As I said earlier, I really love the configurable center drawer, however the drawer only allows the user four settings:
a) Wine & Party Dishes: 42°
b) Deli Snacks: 37°
c) Cold Drinks: 33°
d) Meat & Fish: 29°
This is great, except that I've measured the actual temperature and it's always a little higher than what you've selected. So my "Cold Drinks," which should be one degree above freezing, at 33°, are instead at 34° or, more often, 35°. I wish that in addition to the four settings, the user could make their own custom setting or two at whatever temperature they'd like. I'd make mine, "Truly Icy Drinks," and set the temperature at 31° or 32° so that the actual temperature would be 33° or 34°. I still do find myself taking a cold beer out of this drawer and tucking it into the freezer for 5-10 minutes just to give it a little more bite.

So, my initial perception of the quality and features of this refrigerator is very positive, but the truth will be revealed in how well it holds up over time. I will revise my review if things change. Thanks for reading and good lucking picking a good fridge.

review_title: This is the best range I have ever used!
review_text:
[[VIDEOID:4601dc96ddf6bbf286fbed0554486eeb]] We replaced a coil cooktop and oven (installed one over the other, but separately) this free-standing range. I've been using it the past 4 days and am very pleased with this purchase. I once believed I would rather have a gas range in comparison to electrical units, but this range has totally changed my mind.

I read reviews for several days from all types and manufacturers. I paid close attention to the negative comments on this range and the only one I agree with is that it is very easy to accidentally turn on the front knobs by leaning into or brushing over them. At least one person said that the range should have a lockout feature to keep from turning it on accidentally. This range DOES have a lockout feature so I can rest assured my grandchildren won't hurt themselves. But, while I am cooking I do have to make sure I haven't accidentally changed the knob settings. I'm aware, so that is good.

There are some fun options for this range! First, I love the interior color. I know it's blue, but in my kitchen with my lighting it appears purple. And I love purple, so I am super motivated to keep Mrs. Potts (that's what I named the range) very clean. Second, instead of the old buzzing timers or beeps that alert you to various things (e.g. reaching the set temperature, timers, door/s left open) there are some fun melodic tunes which play. The volume of these can be adjusted in settings. By the way, I spent hours reading the owners manual and you should, too. How do you know what you're doing if you don't take the time to read and understand its advanced features? (I've been cooking 40 years and still learn new things.) The range even comes with a coated sheet (with an attached suction cup) you can attach nearby to help you as you learn how to set the oven and knobs.

There are 5 burners (but one is just to be used as a warmer) and the two larger ones in front have special capabilities. The one on the left allows for two sizes of pan bottoms and features an UltraHeat Power Boil setting. The right front burner allows for three pan bottom sizes. If you don't read the instructions, you will not understand how to use the knobs for these two front burners. Their corresponding knobs cycle from one size to the next, all on the same knob.

The oven controls are located in the back panel and again, if you don't read the instructions, you will probably have a little trouble setting the temperature or timers. I learned you have to tap the timer twice if you want to plug in minutes, or only once if you are doing an hour, or more. Regarding the settings, while the oven is preheating, you cannot make any changes to the settings. It simply won't respond. It's not broken. Read the instructions.

Some complained about the accuracy of the oven temperature. I bought a portable oven thermometer and placed it in the top oven and set the temperature for 350 degrees. I was disappointed when the portable thermometer reached only 300 degrees. After reading the instructions, adjusting the calibration settings, I started by adding 15 degrees (I don't know why I couldn't select 50 degrees, but it turned out it was unnecessary.) and then retried preheating the oven to 350 degrees again. This time, when the oven reached 350, both it and the portable thermometer were in agreement! Then, it was time to check the lower oven. It needed no changes. It was perfect!

The reviews have been mixed on how hard (or easy) it is to clean the range top. Ours came with a sample sized bottle of heavy-duty cleaner and a scrubbing pad for the top and a very fancy squirt bottle for the oven. So far, I have only cleaned the top. I went to the store, found and bought the same cleaner, but in a daily strength squirt bottle. I have used it every time, according to the directions, I've cleaned up the kitchen and have found it to work great. I have not had to clean the oven yet.

I was pleasantly surprised by the bigger size of the oven. I was able to bake 2 11" X 13" enchilada dishes at the same time, on the same rack, in the smaller upper oven. Later, I wanted to try out the ability to bake on all three racks (using both ovens) so I made chocolate chip cookies. I prepared three large cookie sheets. I preheated the upper oven and then I used the convection setting on the lower oven (convection is only available on the larger, lower oven). It automatically lowered the temperature on the lower oven to allow for all three racks to cook for the same time. I put all three cookie sheets in at the same time, set the time for 9 minutes, and the cookies were perfectly baked and were all exactly alike!

I will update this review if I should come across anything that needs to be brought up later.[[ASIN:B014CYYXF2 LG LDE4415ST 30" Freestanding Double Oven Electric Range with 5 Cooking Elements in Stainless Steel]]

product_title: LG LDE4413ST 30" Stainless Steel Electric Smoothtop Double Oven Range
review_text:
LG electric range LDE4413ST

This range and model LDE3037ST are LG’s 2015 top of the line electric ranges – these ranges have the same features except this model has front burner knobs and the controls on the LDE3037ST are on the back panel. This model (LDE4413ST) could be dangerous around small children, because a child could turn a burner knob on and be seriously burned by touching the glass top. The left front burner for example, reaches skin-destroying temperatures in mere seconds. We have no kids and preferred (front) burner knobs because you don’t reach over hot pots/pans to change settings, plus it’s easier, faster, and visual, to turn a knob rather than punching in multiple commands on the back panel.

Pros:

- having two ovens is a terrific feature, especially for the added capacity, or if cooking a meal needing different temperatures, modes (convection AND infrared broil in another, say), times, etc..

- very attractive appliance. Those big knobs result in a pro-range look and the range coordinates perfectly with our other stainless steel and stainless / black appliances.

- each oven has a traditional very-high-heat self cleaning feature and LG’s “easy clean” for less severe grime. It works pretty well.

- the 3200 watt front left burner gets super-hot very fast for quick boiling. It’s also dual sized – heat just the inner (smaller) space or also the larger circle space. It takes 10 minutes to boil one gallon of room-temperature water in a large covered pot. Our previous range took 14 minutes to do the same thing.

- the 2700 watt right front burner gets almost as hot almost as fast and its triple sized. I.e., you can heat the inner, the inner and next larger, or all three rings for large pots/pans.

- the rear glass-touch control panel works perfectly. There are lots of features such as dual timers, a clock, broil, bake, convection, choice of oven, etc.

- the infrared burner at the top of the upper oven is worth the additional $200 over models with a standard broiling element. Meats cook faster and taste better at the higher cooking temperatures, similar to a charcoal barbeque being super hot. The infrared element is installed in lieu of a typical heating element.

- the oven door must be closed when broiling or the heat will turn off. Our last range required the door to be opened, which heated & smoked up the kitchen.

- the oven vents along the entire width of the range, with fumes etc. exiting at the base of the rear glass control panel – spreading the exiting hot air/fumes over a wider area.

Cons:

- the hot surface indicator is a single LED. Our previous range (a Kitchen Aid) had a warning LED for each burner, which is better and safer.

- There is no meat probe. Our old Kitchen Aid had an accurate meat probe. Insert it into a roast and the internal temperature would show as it cooked, or program the oven to turn off when it reached the desired temperature. We miss that feature.

- the upper oven has two rack positions, but the lowest position is 3" above the oven bottom, and the other rack position is a mere 2" above that. There was sufficient vertical space in this oven for LG designers to have separated the two racks by 3" which would have greatly increased the utility of the smaller oven. As it is, if both racks are in place, anything placed on the lower rack has to be under 2" tall, such as a cookie sheet.

Other:

- the lower oven read 325 when it was only 300 degrees, but there are a set of commands for you to adjust the built-in thermometer to match the actual temperature.

- a “beeper” signals for either timer or when an oven reaches the “set” temperature. It can be set to loud (for hard-of-hearing customers), normal (for most people), or off.

- as shown in the Customer Image, there isn’t a whole lot of room in the bottom rear of the range for the electric cord and receptacle. Our receptacle was on the floor facing up, and we used a yard stick to push the cord down and out of the way as the range was slid into place. The cord and connection will be a 3-wire or 4-wire, depending on whether your home was wired with 3 or 4 conductor (8 gauge) cable to the range. E.g., our range is on a 50-amp 220 volt circuit, with a 50-amp receptacle, and a 50-amp 3-wire cord.

- take the time to properly level the cook-top surface, side-to-side and front-to-back, via the four leveling feet. To adjust (screw in or out) an adjusting foot with your fingers, temporarily prop up that side of the range on a block of wood. With the top leveled, the ovens were also level. If a vender is installing the oven, insist that he levels it, and stand right there to verify that the level’s bubble is perfectly centered left to right and front to back.

- before installing the included LG tip-over bracket, determine if the tip-over bracket from your previous range works with this range (as ours did) – slide this range into place, open the lower oven door and press down on it. If the old bracket works, the range won’t rock or tip forward.

- some Amazon reviewers of similar LG models were bothered by a clicking noise (electric relay opening/closing) when a top burner was set to less than maximum; and colored streaks in the oven door glass. Our range “clicks”, but the sound is extremely faint and unless we’re paying close attention and are right next to it, we don’t even hear it. The glass in our oven doors has no colored streaks after months of use.

- some LG electric range reviewers complained about LG’s 1-800 warranty number and the technicians they sent out. We bought our range from Best Buy with their 5-year Geek Squad warranty ($149 option). They and most local dealers will haul the old range away, and install it as well if you buy a new range cord from them. If the range fails, their Geek Squad repairs it on-site.

Summary:

In spite of the cons, this is a great range. We like it a lot.

review_text:
[[VIDEOID:f9a2157e17c48b37e50ecc27d718202a]] [[VIDEOID:6caf2c673cad178681f5b192e0fd969d]] The troubleshooting section of the manual states that if the problem is 'Washer seems too quiet', then the possible cause is 'Quiet by design'. Clearly, these are not technical writers, but comedians.

The sounds generated by this machine are perturbing and loud. How loud? At 1 meter in a tiled hallway, the sound pressure levels I measured were:: wash: 77 dBA, spin: 72 dBA. That's as loud as my cyclone vacuum cleaner at full power. The difference is that the GE sounds like power lawn equipment. My prior 4 washers were much quieter. My LG spins at a much higher speed than this GE, and it stays relatively steady. During spin, the GE, even with no load, shakes excessively and rattles. The machine is leveled along 2 axes, and all 4 feet are in contact with a hard floor. I attached a short video of the GE washer during wash and spin cycles.

This washer has a tendancy to go off balance with small loads. There is no sensor to stop the motor when this happens. The basket continues to spin, and bangs against the side panels. The GE technician told me this was not a defect, just the design. It is inconvenient being on standby when doing laundry. Other washers I've used hardly ever have this problem, and in addition they have a sensor to detect the off balance condition.

This machine does have some features that many new HE machines do not, such as deep fill and warm rinse. But I consider them non-features since they negate the energy efficiency of an HE machine, and other top rated machines clean clothes just fine without them.

Based on professional reviews, the top scoring washers were from Samsung and LG. However, actual consumers, having long-term experiences, reported issues with those brands, ranging from machines getting stuck trying to balance the load, to machines that exploded. I settled on this GE as a compromise, since it has pretty good reviews from professionals and pretty good reviews from consumers.

Thus far, this GE looks like a loser. It's not as good as my LG washer, and not as good as my retired "real" Maytags made in Newton, Iowa. In summary, the various symptoms of this machine point to larger design flaws, and I don't expect it will be as durable as my previous machines.

product_title: GE GTW680BSJWS Top Loading Washer with Stainless Steel Basket, 4.6 Cu. Ft. Capacity, 14 Cycles, White
review_text:
After reading many reviews about washing machines before making a decision, I decided to purchase this GE washer. I've always liked GE products, but after owning one of their previous HE models for about four years and being terribly disappointed with it's performance I almost purchased a competitor's product. I'm happy that I didn't.

Note that this is not a paid review.

Now for the review:

Cleaning - 4 stars. This top load HE washer gets clothes clean. I would rate my previous GE HE at two stars, so a great improvement. I considered going back to an agitator washer but worried about capacity and the detrimental effect that an agitator has on clothing. The only reason I didn't rate a 5 is that I haven't tried to clean grass stains yet. It's winter time here so I have no grass stains to work with.

Capacity - 5 stars. The 4.6 Cu. Ft tub has plenty of room for larger articles, including a king size quilt that I recently washed. The last load washed consisted of 4 pairs of jeans, a pair of work pants, 6 shirts, including a 2X flannel shirt and a 2X sweatshirt, and a few pairs of socks. There are settings on the washer for washing jeans separately from other colored articles, but that isn't the way we wash laundry in our household.

Features - 5 stars. As mentioned above, there are plenty of settings for your laundry, 13 total, including one to sanitize with Oxy. There six water temp settings, four levels of cleaning (light through extra heavy), and four levels of spin cycle from no spin through max. All are controlled with easy touch buttons. If that seems like a lot of choices, no worry. You can set the "my cycle" button to remember your settings. I especially like the slide out detergent and softener dispenser tray located at the top of the tub that mixes the detergent with the load as the washer fills. This also makes cleaning easy, although I've washed more than 30 loads and there is no residue showing yet. If you've experienced clothing stains in the past from fabric softener dispenser build-up, worry no more. For those who remember warm water rinse, that feature has also returned with this model. There is also a "deep fill" button, which I use frequently. Press that button and 5-6 more gallons of water are added. I like to see my clothes bathing in water. Also included is a "deep rinse" button, recommended for use with fabric softener. This uses a bit more water and increases cycle times over the 34 minutes they boast about, but I feel more at ease. The glass top makes it easy to see what is going on in there.

Noise - 3 stars. This compares to 1 star on my previous washer. I don't worry a lot about noise as my washer isn't setting next to the television. It does make some odd noises during the wash, also not a bother to me.

One drawback is the dreaded walk that washers sometimes do. The only time I've experienced this issue is when the load became unbalanced on the king size quilt. If this happens, press the pause button and wait about 30 seconds for the lid to unlock to situate the items in the tub.

The washer "walk" and the fact that I haven't tried to clean grass stains yet is my reason for rating at 4 stars instead of 5. I could have spent up to $200 more for another competitor's top load or twice as much for a larger capacity front load but I'm happy that I didn't. We aren't a large family and the 4.6 capacity is plenty enough for us. If you fall into that category, do some shopping for the lowest price and I think you'll also be pleased.

I am using it correctly, the right settings for the types of laundry, but the clothes don't come out as clean as they did in my old Maytag which had manual settings.

review_title: This machine does not live up to its name or function
review_text: In the stores and reviews, this appeared to be the best machine for saving water and energy within a moderate income.  I've have the machine for over a year and regret the purchase almost everytime I use it for more than a small load of shirts and delicates.  On the regular cycles, water only sprays on the clothes....the ones at the bottom get wet; those on top may get wet or stay dry.  The clothes only swish back and forth so the material on top never gets close to the water with the detergent.  When doing sheets and towel or any larger item, I always use the deep fill cycle so that there is sufficient water to cover and clean.  It is also necessary to use the additional, second rinse function since the detergent does not seem to dissipate in the normal rinse cycle.  Due to its design, any larger load, such as one set of sheets or two towels will cause the machine to go off balance during the spin cycle and either "walk" or clunk frantically and stop.  At the end of the spin cycle, the sheets and towels are too damp and are usually hung to air dry for an hour or more prior to being added to the dryer.  The multiple functions appear to be a selling point, but it is not possible to reset any dials to lengthen the wash cycle or add a second spin.  It is programmed to do only what it does and will not allow for human intervention to lengthen a cycle once the sequence has begun.  I thought I was being a wise and ecologically mindful consumer when purchasing this machine, but have discovered that it does not live up to its function of adequately washing larger items or loads.

I was forced to add additional water by bucket -- then be available for rinsing to add buckets of water so the dirt & soap would rinse out. The agitator of this machine was so rough that it tore sleeves & pocket flaps off new shirts, twisted sheets into ropes & knots so that it was impossible for them to get clean & agitated the edges & hems from towels to shreds. This machine was definitely good for the garment & towel industry--needed replacements in about 1/4 the normal life of the garment. Family clothing became grey, stained & shredded.
I complained to the GE Dealer who proceeded to send out repairmen to educate me on the proper setting for this machine (their Best Machine) while totally ignoring the poor design -- assuring me that all machines operate this way. Also, the Spin was SOOOOO fast & loud that we COULD NOT decipher a low flying helicopter from the sound of this machine spinning down our basement as it walked about over the concrete floor and rubbed the paint from the side of my dryer. I agree all of THIS GE Model washer work similar( my son's family had one identical to mine and It worked the same but additionally failed to spin the water out of his family,s laundry. I can not believe that I spent nearly $750 for a new modern machine that was worse to operate than the Wringer Washer that I helped my Mother carry & fill with 5 gallon buckets -- 50 years ago. My Sons Family and I finally gave up trying 'to adjust to new technology' -- and junked these machines after 1 year while still being covered by 4 year Extended Warranty-- GOT new Maytag Deep Fill Washers and are now Quietly suffering thru LOOOOONG Gentle Water-Covered wash cycles--our clothing is steadily getting BRIGHTER with each wash.
SHOP BEFORE YOU BUY A NEW WASHER -- CONSIDER REPAIRING YOUR OLD WASHER.

product_title: GE GTW460ASJWW Top Loading Washer with Stainless Steel Basket, 4.2 Cu. Ft. Capacity, 14 Cycles, White
review_text:
Don't believe the hype on Lowe's website where this washer gets nearly 5 stars. In fact, this washer may be the worst purchase of my adult life. The reason I feel this way is the false advertising. GE advertises this washer as 4.2 cu. ft., however on the largest load size setting ("Super") with the "Deep Fill" and "Deep Rinse" options selected, the washer only fills up about 2/3 of the way. This makes the washer approximately a 2.8 cu. ft. capacity (small) in reality. While, GE boasts the washer has “innovative wash action” and that “it can operate with high-efficiency, using less water while still getting the load clean”, I assure you this is completely FALSE. Yes, front load washers can clean clothes effectively with a lower water level, but this top load washer DOES NOT.

This is a big deal for me because I intentionally purchased a “large capacity” washer so I could clean my king size bedding and wash large loads of laundry at end of week. What is the point of owning a full-size washer that can’t handle large loads? For instance, the water level is so low I can't wash a king size comforter effectively. When I try washing a king size comforter (on the largest load setting & and deepest fill option), portions of the comforter barely get wet so they certainly aren't being cleaned. In the attached picture you can observe that portions of the bedding are still dry!

However, king size comforters are not the only problem. The washer can't handle large loads of clothes either so I end up doing multiple small loads so my clothes actually come out clean. Lastly, the super low water level makes using fabric softener totally impractical. Even on the "Deep Rinse" setting, fabric softener just dumps onto your clothes (staining them) and doesn't mix into the water.

My final thought is that I do not recommend this product and strongly suggest you look for a better brand. Even though this washer is rather new I'll likely leave it behind when I move and buy a real one.

product_title: GE GTW460ASJWW Top Loading Washer with Stainless Steel Basket, 4.2 Cu. Ft. Capacity, 14 Cycles, White
review_title: Owned for 3 years and did some repairs
review_text:
I actually like this washer. I find the new High Efficiency (HE) front loading washers do not clean as well as an agitator does. This was the only HE agitator washer we could find. I had my doubts at first, but it slowly won me over. Things I like
1) HUGE tub
2) Fast wash cycle (< 0.5 hours)
3) The numerous settings for laundry type, level of soiling, water temperature, and options (delay wash, 2nd rinse)
4) They used screws to assemble this thing! That means a tinkerer like me can actually fix things as they break.

Things I don't like.
1) it tends to twist our king size sheets which causes an unbalanced load. I have to untwist the sheets mid-spin cycle about a third of the time. This occurs even when using the Towel/Sheets setting
2) The Precise Fill setting. To me, it always looks like too little water. Never really did a test, just a gut feeling.

About repairs. Over the 3 year period, the washer didn't drain two times. The first time, I downloaded the Technical Service Guide (a MUST have), and went through the Diagnostics (which actually worked like they described). It said the drain pump wasn't working. The TSG also lists a series of tests for many of the washer components. I ran the drain pump test, and guess what, it failed. Before ordering a new part, drained the washer (unplug it and just take the drain hose and place the end in a bucket, it pretty much drains itself). I flipped the thing on its side and the innards are relatively simple and look just like the diagrams in the TSG. The drain pump is held to the drum with 3 3/8" bolts. I removed those puppies and then popped the motor from the pump (2 plastic side clips). Turns out sand got into the pump. I washed the sand out, re-assembled it, and worked like a charm. Took me nearly all day the first time (didn't want to break anything). The second time it happened, it took about 3 hours to drain, dis-assemble the pump, clean and re-assemble.
Should this happen? NO!!! But I AM grateful that they built this thing in such a way that this kind of simple repair doesn't require a $200 service call. The way most things are built these days, they're not repairable (open up a large screen TV; there are like 4 parts, including the screen). This washer is repairable. And since I had it on its side, I checked the motor belt each time. After 3 years, still looks like new.

Call me old-fashioned, but overall, I'm very happy to have a HE agitator washer. I've heard nothing but complaints about cycle time and mildew from my friends with the latest front-loaders. Thanks GE, for still building the agitators.

review_text:

I was a bit concerned about buying another Samsung (esp. given some negative reviews and our own experience) but decided to risk it, as we were matching the new Samsung fridge we had also bought. Having had this microwave now a couple of months, I can honestly say we LOVE it. It has convection functionality as well, which I almost felt might be a gimmick I'd rarely use, but in fact we use it constantly. It has many auto-cook options from "Smart Fry" (to do French Fries, etc w/little oil spray), to reheating for various foods (pizza, chicken, veggies,etc). Again, wasn't sure this would work well but everything we've tried so far has come out great. Not everything you want to heat will be in the list, but we just pick similar items and it seems to hit the mark. (E.g. we just heated some breaded fish fillets under the chicken tenders setting and they came out perfectly in just 8 minutes...the instructions for regular reheat in an oven on the box said 20mins, so this was great). There are a couple accessories that come with it that you need to store but they are how you choose the type of cooking (basically a tray and a couple of different metal shelves to get the tray higher or lower).

MInor complaint is that the internal light is not bright enough, particularly if you have the tall shelf in and food is at the top of the microwave (which we have over-the-range so it's hard enough to see inside normally). But other than that, the microwave works well, the range-lighting and extractor fan are both very good (loud fan at higher settings but we've had it on low and it's done a good job).

So far I'd recommend this without reservations, only concern being our last Samsung lasted 9 months before dying so we don't know the long-term reliability yet.

review_title: Warning:  Front buttons get water in them and the microwave stops working.
review_text:
[[VIDEOID:190c1b1562f75c6887cec7f974b1be2]] I repair electronics and take just about anything someone sends me for repair, that includes occasionally microwaves. I was not familiar with this model until it was given to me to fix and the person stated that the microwave displayed "C-DO" and was unresponsive to all controls, and for this error the manual states that one or more of the buttons is "stuck" in the pushed position. This is apparently a very common fault with these units. I disassembled the door and removed the button membrane, it is stuck on with adhesive. Imagine my surprise when I looked at the backside of the buttons to see that half of them were filled with water. I can only assume that this came from steam from cooking over the stove. This of course shorts the button contacts and makes the microwave think they are being pressed. Getting the water out is almost impossible however I did the best I could with a combination of poking holes in the back and using heat from my hot air station. I was able to dry out 6 of the buttons with water damage and got them working however there were 7 more buttons I could not fix and they were still shorted so I disabled them by cutting the trace. The keypad membrane part # is DE34-00395D however I cannot find it available anywhere online, but you can find the whole door assembly for around $260 which has the membrane already on it. Just be aware if you order a new one, this is likely to happen again. I have uploaded a video to demonstrate what has happened to one of the buttons, all buttons on the left side of the clock were like this. Edit - The video I have uploaded is too compressed by Amazon's site to see what's going on, so I have also uploaded it on youtube. Search under "Samsung Microwave c-do error" and you will see the same thumbnail since I can't link videos in here for some reason.

This is a terrible design flaw to allow moisture from steam to get inside this keypad and ruin it on a microwave that is designed to be mounted over a stove. This microwave was 14 months old, just two months outside of the Samsung warranty. Avoid this thing at all costs.

review_text:
We're VERY HAPPY with this GE Cafe Advantium. It replaced a GE Monogram that we owned for about 10 years. We had numerous microtron tube issues with that oven, and really did not want to purchase another GE product. However, the features for this GE Cafe oven were so much better than competitive brands for the price, and the reviews we read were so positive, that we decided to give GE another try.

So far, so good. Love the LARGE size of the oven...very deep and very wide. We installed it in the same cabinet space as our old GE, and were able to do so without any carpentry adjustment, which was nice...just put it in the cavity, plugged it in, and installed four screws. Even so, the cooking area in this oven is much larger than the old GE, and from what we could find, larger than most competitive brands that fit in the same cabinet space, or even larger cabinet space.

We have not yet consulted the owners manual to operate the microwave. It's that easy to use. Functions are very intuitive, and the cooking quality is great...always the right temperature. We were not sure if we'd like the turn knob, as it looks "analog", compared to the electronic controls, but it turns out that it's really nice to use, and a great way to select functions and options.

The very large turntable is great. One strange thing though...the carriage that is underneath the glass turntable has "TOP" printed on the metal, so when we installed it we made sure that "TOP" faced UP. 'turns out that it would constantly come off the axle that turned it. Our solution was to flip it upside down, and it's been working great ever since.

Another strange thing is that the clock goes to sleep about a minute after showing. We moved through options on the control panel on how to change this, and consulted the owners manual, but to no avail. For us it's not a big deal as the convection oven under this oven also has a clock.

We've not yet used the speed cook or convection cook functions, but Thanksgiving is around the corner, and we're looking forward to giving that a try.

review_title: "It wasn't broke, why did they feel the need to fix it?
review_text:
I've installed around 40 dishwashers in personal residences and rental units over the last 50 years.

Every one, including every other Bosch I've owned, had a simple, reliable water connection readily accessible, inspectable and serviceable for the front of the dishwasher.

This one, however, requires a garden hose connector with a 90 degree bend (not supplied) which must then be adapted to the type of water supply line you are using.

The 90 degree bend, of course, insures that as the dishwasher is pushed back into the opening the bend can function as a "wrench handle" to slightly unscrew the garden hose connector, creating a leak *at the back of the dishwasher*, where it cannot be tightened.

Why, Why, WHY?

There is a perfectly good method of performing this connection which has worked well for 50 years.

The connection can be performed *after* the dishwasher is in place.

The connection can be readily observed to determine if there is a leak.

If there is a leak, it can generally be stopped by simply tightening the readily accessible connection.

WHAT SORT OF IDIOT WOULD CHANGE THIS CONNECTION TO A LOCATION AND TYPE WHERE IT IS SUBJECT TO DISTURBANCE DURING INSTALLATION, AND WHERE IT CANNOT BE OBSERVED OR SERVICED WITH THE DISHWASHER IN PLACE?

Obviously, the same sort of idiot who assumes that I will ever buy a Bosch Dishwasher again.

review_text:
Remember that you are not just purchasing the product itself, you have to deal with the company when things go wrong.

I purchased this product back in late March of this year. In July, the washer started to spill water all over my floor. Called LG who scheduled a service appointment for the next day - which was great. No show. No call. After I spent a week calling LG, the service provider's tech showed up randomly. He also advised us to fix the issue the next time by unscrewing the top of the machine adn fiddling with it ourselves. Obviously this would not be advisable. That meant a 3 to 5 day turn around time for them to find someone to set up an appointment...unacceptable! review_title: My 6 year old refrigerator is useless now, and it has been 3 weeks (and ...
review_text:
My 6 year old refrigerator is useless now, and it has been 3 weeks (and counting) that I've been waiting on LG to take care of it as it is still under warranty.

3 weeks ago my fridge/freezer stopped working (it was warm inside). I got an outside repair person to look at it for $70 who told me the evaporator unit died and had leaked out all the coolant. The part was still under warranty (year 6 of a 7 year warranty) so I needed to get LG to take care of it.
I called LG, told them the part I needed to have replaced. Their technician could not come to my house for a week and 2 days. So we sat for 1 1/2 weeks with no refrigerator/freezer, and we are a family of 5.

When the technician arrived, 2 minutes into the $125 visit, he told me that we needed to replace the evaporator unit (which I already knew and told them a wee prior) and that the part was discontinued and out of stock. So - basically, we have a totally dead fridge.
He told me that they would buy the refrigerator back from me (original price about $1,500) but it would take 5 days to process the paperwork.
We couldn't go another week without a refrigerator so we bought a Whirlpool from Best Buy (love Best Buy, great people!).

After the 5 day wait to be reimbursed for our useless 6 year old fridge, LG never called. So I contacted them to see what is happening, and they say they will give us $600 and are NOT going to haul away the dead fridge. Huh?
So 6 years ago we spent $1,500 on a new fridge, and we paid $195 on servicing it and will need to now pay to have it hauled away and disposed of, and the warranty pay out is $600.

OH - and it is Monday and they don't cut checks until Fridays, so you guessed it, we have to wait yet another week for our check.

WHAT A JOKE!

review_title: So much better than KitchenAid! After 4 years, I still love it.
review_text:
I'M UPDATING THIS REVIEW TO SIMPLY SAY THAT EVERYTHING IN THIS REVIEW STILL HOLDS TRUE AFTER 4 YEARS.

There. I said it. I actually love my dishwasher.

A year ago, we "upgraded"; from a top-of-the-line KitchenAid to the equally top-of-the-line 800 series from Bosch. I have a few frustrations with Bosch usability -- small, simple, things that give the Bosch more of a "learning curve"; than should be necessary -- but after living with it for a while, I honestly marvel at how we put up with the KitchenAid for so long.

WHY WE CHOSE BOSCH OVER KITCHENAID

Bosch middle and third racks are functionally much deeper than KitchenAid's. With the Bosch, I can lower the middle rack to its lowest position and still fit dinner plates below with plenty of room for the water to circulate. This is because of Bosch's slanted racks, and the lack of an exposed heating element. So the Bosch middle rack can handle all types of taller items, and the third rack is outstanding -- it can fit spatulas, tongs, ramekins, wisks, even 10" chefs knives on their sides... all with plenty of room left for silverware.

With all that room up top, you don't even need silverware baskets most of the time, but the Bosch Duo-Flex silverware baskets are another reason we chose Bosch, because they are built like a tank. By contrast, our KitchenAid baskets had to be replaced every 3 years or so, as the plastic broke and developed holes that silverware would fall through.

The Bosch is much less likely to melt your plastic items, even on the lower rack (because there's no exposed heating element).

All the objections we heard about the Bosch -- even from appliance salesmen -- proved to be misinformed. If you understand how to use it, then dishes DON'T come out wet, and the dishwasher DOESN'T smell, and rinsing the filter is not an every day -- or even every month -- necessity.

And finally, several friends with Bosch dishwashers report years of quiet performance, while my $1,100 KitchenAid dishwasher turned out to be a piece of junk. It stopped cleaning effectively after only 7 years, and the racks lasted even fewer years, because the plastic parts holding them together couldn't stand the heat.

WHY WE CHOSE THE 800 SERIES OVER THE 500 OR THE BENCHMARK SERIES

The 500 series is probably the best buy. It is highly rated, and is functionally the same dishwasher as the 800 series. I was just personally nervous about the raised buttons on the 500 series, which didn't seem as likely to handle years of moisture as the flat touch buttons on the 800 series. Also, most of 500 series models do not have those built-like-a-tank Duo-Flex silverware baskets.

The Benchmark series has all this and more, such as a flexible top tray and a TimeLight that projects the remaining cycle time on the floor, but the price difference just didn't seem worth it.

WHY WE CHOSE THE HIDDEN CONTROLS (Bar or Pocket Handle) OVER THE RECESSED HANDLE VERSION

The visible controls on the recessed handle model are unobtrusive enough to blend into any kitchen, and you might like having a display showing how much time is left in the cycle (by all accounts, it's also more accurate than the KitchenAid version). However, some reviewers here on Amazon said that the label markings on the exterior of those models start to wear off with repeated use, making your perfectly well-functioning new dishwasher look like something old and beat up in your kitchen. People experiencing this are not happy. So we went with the bar handle with the hidden controls, which looks great. If I want to know how much time is left in the cycle, I just have to open the door and interrupt it.

WHAT'S THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN ALL THESE MODEL NUMBERS?

I know, right?

First 3 letters: SHX=bar handle, SHP=Pocket handle, SHE=Recessed handle, SHS=Scoop handle

Next 3 letters: 63T=300 series, 65T=500 series, 68T=800 series, 7PT/8PT/9PT=Benchmark series, N8U=Exclusive model sold through distributors

The next 3 letters are a lot more confusing, but the biggest differences are around which cycles are offered. Bosch has a confusing array of cycles and options, ranging from 4 cycles/4 options on the 300 series, up to 6 cycles/6 options on the some 800 series models, but more remarkably the names and types of cycles vary, representing a variety of different combinations from 10 different possible cycles and 8 different possible options! In other words, my six cycles aren't the same as your six cycles.

Focusing on the 800 series, the differences are mostly whether the model has a built in water softener, or whether it has the Eco Cycle, or the Extra Shine or SpeedPerfect options. I chose the SHX68TL5UC because it does NOT have a water softener (which I don't need), and because it had both the Extra Shine and SpeedPerfect options. Explanations:

ECO CYCLE saves energy by running at a lower temperature. Works fine for lightly soiled loads. Doesn't dry as well.

EXTRA SHINE OPTION makes the final rinse hotter and extends the drying cycle. This helps make up for the lack of an American-style exposed heating element, but it extends load time and uses more energy.

SPEEDPERFECT speeds things up by heating the water more and using more water. It also uses more energy.
Keeping the SpeedPerfect, ExtraShine, and Sanitize options on basically turbocharges your Bosch, but kills the energy efficiency.

If all this seems confusing, one thing I like about the Bosch is that it remembers your recent settings and makes that the default for your next load. So you just hit START and it'll do the same options as last time.

NOTE: If you like your dishes to come out piping hot and bone dry, like American models, you can get this easily with the Bosch. Just get this model or any of the others that have the Extra Shine and Sanitize options. When you set up your dishwasher, follow the user manual to turn on "Intensive Drying" (see #6 below) then to give it an extra boost you can run the dishwasher with the Extra Shine and Sanitize options. Your dishes will be bone dry and piping hot, and if you add the SpeedPerfect option as well, your normal cycle will still be well under 2 hours. I used the Extra Shine option a lot initially, but have realized that my dishes get perfectly dry without using it.

WHAT DON'T WE LIKE ABOUT THE BOSCH?

1) It's not intuitive at first. You shouldn't have to read a manual to use a dishwasher, but you definitely need a tutorial if you want your Bosch to do a good job. It's certainly required to understand what all the cycle options are; but it's also things like the middle rack -- when loading, if you don't push it all the way in until it clicks, then the hose won't attach and the middle spray arm won't effectively distribute the water during the cycle. So you definitely can't use the door to push the racks in, and you have to explain that to anybody who's going to use your dishwasher.

2) No CANCEL button. If you start a cycle and want to cancel it, my old KitchenAid had a CANCEL button. On the Bosch, there is none. Lacking such a button, the intuitive thing to do is to hit the ON/OFF button to turn the whole dishwasher off, then start over; but doing that DOESN'T cancel the cycle. You have to hold the START button down for 3 seconds, then close the door, then wait about a minute. NOT intuitive.

3) Rinse Aid dispenser. It's small, and it's hard to see when it's full, which leads to spilling (KitchenAid has a clear fill level indicator).

4) Touch buttons. I figured it out finally, and they are slick, but you have to explain to others that you press right in the center of the button, and don't use pressure.

5) Those heavy duty Duo-Flex silverware baskets that I loved? They are narrower than the KitchenAid silverware baskets, so long items like tongs or slotted spoons or ladles stand up straight and are therefore too tall -- they HAVE TO go in the top rack. [UPDATE: As solid as those baskets are, we stopped using them because EVERYTHING fits in the top 3rd rack, and taking them out cleared even more space for pots and pans in the bottom rack.]

6) Cryptic configuration menus. You can customize a lot of things about your Bosch dishwasher, but don't lose that owner's manual, because it's hopeless otherwise. Here, for example, are the instructions for turning on "Intensive Drying"; (boosts the heat for better drying results): 1) Press the [On/Off] button. 2) Hold down the “A” button (which is the “Normal” button on this model). Press [Start] until the display indicates “d:00”. 3) Release both buttons. 4) Press the “A” button until the display shows “d:00”. 5) Press the “C” button (which is the RINSE button on this model) to turn intensive drying on or off: “d:01” = ON and “d:00” = OFF. 6) Press [Start] to save setting. To be fair, you should only have to customize these things once.

With any dishwasher, one of the wild cards is whether your dishes fit. If you have thick American stoneware, or really wide glasses and mugs, then they might fit better in an American dishwasher. If you're concerned, grab a few placesettings and head to the local appliance store to make sure they fit.

review_title: Dryer had an internal short.  GE doesn't care.
review_text:
I received this unit two hours ago and am really regretting this purchase. After the install guys left, I reached behind the dryer to check that the air discharge duct was properly attached and received a strong electrical shock when I touched the unpainted metal on the back. I put a multi meter between the casing and a common ground and measured 122 volts passing through the case.

This is an incredibly dangerous production error, and could easily have resulted in fatality if my body had been grounded (this is in a laundry room with water and plumbing), I would have had the current pass through me with no GFI protection. The dryer plugs into a 220-volt outlet on a 30-amp breaker.

I am completely stunned that GE would allow this to happen to a major $600 appliance. To add insult to injury, I am now being told that GE won't send a tech out to look at the issue for another 5 days. I have a family of four - we generate a ton of laundry, and I have a wet load in the washer as I type this.

The fact that this dangerous situation occurred is one thing. I get that errors happen regardless of best efforts to prevent them. GE's handling of the situation is unforgivable. They obviously don't care about the customer once the sale is made.

product_title: LG White Front Load Laundry Pair with WM3370HWA 27" Washer and DLEX3370W 27" Electric Dryer in White
review_title: Impressive, and my clothes are clean.. faster.
review_text:
Both are working great three weeks in.

The washer had a little rattle on the back panel but I was able to bend it slightly in so it fit snug enough on the back to not rattle.

Oh yeah.. the other reviews might say it made a bad sound when they first started it. Pretty sure those folks didn't read the instructions. There are four nylon screw bolts on the back of the washer to support the drum in shipping. They MUST MUST be removed before you use the washer. You even have to unscrew one at the bottom just to free the electrical plug.

I have not owned any front loading washer / dryers before this so i'm new to the game. They are the quietest set I have ever owned. Some people said I might need water arresters to help stop the pipes banging, but I have not heard any thuds or annoying sounds. The washer definitely turns the water off and on more times than my old washer. It sounds like it runs some water in, then drains some, then runs more in. Anyways so if your pipes bang when your current washer finishes filling, you might want to look into a set of water arresters for this.

The washer spins fast enough that it has become my cat's new obsession. He sits in front of it and just watches it go around. It does have a very good balance too.

I have heard about front loaders smelling bad from the buildup in the door and seals. Mine isn't smelling bad. I dry the door seal and glass with a towel and then leave the door open. This one does have a little notch where the door isn't closed but it isn't open enough that your pets can get in it.
The manual says to run washing machine cleaner though it once every two months, so we picked up some at the store, have not used that yet.

The dryer seems impressive too. You can just set it to normal and it will estimate the time remaining. It will increase or decrease the time based on how dry the clothes are.. pretty cool. And it has not made our laundry room humid or anything like that.

Both sing songs when they complete their tasks. I can see how some might get annoyed by it but for me it just reminds me to get the clothes out of the dryer.

review_title: This is a pretty decent freezer.
review_text:
We picked up the Haier 5.0 c.u. ft chest freezer about a month ago, and it has been pretty awesome to use. It gets nice and cold just as you’d expect. The 5.0 cu is more than enough for our family of three when combined with our normal refrigerator. We were able to store half a pig, a large turkey, a couple whole chickens, and we have plenty of room left. We actually have several gallon jugs of water in there too and we could still fit another half pig or more in it.

It is fairly light weight. I was able to get it up our porch stairs by myself with a dolly. It is also small enough that it can fit in some pretty tight spaces. We have it in a small mechanical room attached to the garage and we had plenty of room for it. It gets a good seal, and it runs quiet. We added some gallon jugs of water (90% full) to it in order to help keep it from working too hard. I’ve always heard full freezers work best. I did have to use an extension cord, so I used a 12 guage cord and so far haven’t noticed any issues with the cord getting hot.

The only problem I’ve had is that there were some dents in the side from shipping. They weren’t an issue for me so I accepted it and went on. I plan to add a wireless thermometer with an alert though since it isn't in a common area where we'd notice failure quickly. Just in case.

review_text: I have had this 5 cuft unit for longer than I can remember (maybe 2006)...moved it three times to different homes and it has been reliable and easy to clean. It was the perfect size to sit in my two mobile homes in place of a dryer, and it's now in my garage here. I empty and clean it about twice a year. It does develop some frost over time, but cleaning it on a schedule takes care of that. I just move it outside of my garage, pull the drain plugs, let it thaw, then hose it inside and let it drain some more. Then I use some all purpose cleaner and sponge and rinse it with the hose again and towel dry it well. You want it very dry before starting it up again. I keep a gallon bottle of water on the lid to compress the gasket tight. This is part of my frugal plan to not have to go out shopping so frequently. This and an ample pantry saves a lot of running around.

review_text:
It's amazing to me that in a modern manufacturing world, a company like whirlpool could create such an absolute dud of a product.

1. This thing takes forever to come to temperature. If you happen to put food in early or drop too much temp when putting in food, this oven can *never* recover the temperature loss. review_title: Life's Good But LGs Customer Service Sucks
review_text:
My LMX28988ST /04 broke down (purchased Oct 2012). According to the owner’s manual parts are covered for seven years and the compressor for ten but not the labor. At first, I called several local repair shops, and all declined to work on it because they were not authorized LG repair shops. I then decided to call LG's 1-800 number. The lady at LG told me to contact Sears Repair for service. Sears were booked solid and I had to wait around 10 days for an appointment. Finally, the day came, and I was told by the Sears repairman that they are not authorized to do LG warranty work. In any case he did the diagnosis and said my compressor, condenser and dryer were bad. The estimate came out to over a thousand dollars and Sears would need to contact LG before any work could be done or I could pay the full amount and try to get reimbursed for the parts than came under warranty. The repairman charged me $99 plus tax for the house call. He gave me a 10% coupon and told me I could recover my house call bill by buying a new refrigerator from Sears that cost a $1000 and up.

I contacted LG again and “Nick” at LG told me Air Tech Hawaii does the warranty work in Hawaii. Why wasn’t I told about that in the first place. Being the frig initially cost me over $2,500 on sale from the NEX (Navy Exchange), I decided to pay the flat rate of $535 plus $25.21 tax to have it fix. According to Air Tech Hawaii, Sears took a swag (scientific wild ass guess) and diagnose that both the compressor and condenser were at fault. Air Tech Hawaii added a valve to attach test gauges to determine the problem. Turns out the condenser was still working. Unless it was leaking, it would not be covered.

No matter how much I presented my case, LG would not reimburse me for their misdirected service call. I own a couple large LG TV and an electric range but never again. “Buyer Beware” a large corporation like LG would be stingy about 100 bucks. My beef was all about the “principal.”

review_title: WARNING: NEVER BUY LG.  You will regret it!
review_text:
Dear Mr Riddle,

It it with disappointment that I am writing you about my experience with my LG french door refrigerator. I purchased this refrigerator from Home Depot on 12/7/15. It was installed in my new kitchen in April 2016. I liked refrigerator and all of its features so I was upset when it started intermittently making a loud vibrating sound in July. The sound was coming from the fan behind the filter. As the appliance is covered under the one year manufacturers warranty, I called LG customer service and was told to call a local appliance servicer called "Reliable Appliance Service" myself. The noise stopped by the next day and everything seemed to be working so I never called the service center.

Then, sometime during the week of August 22nd the noise started again. Within the week the fan stopped working. All the food on the top of the fridge was warm and everything on the bottom froze. Additionally the ice and water dispenser stopped working and the letters "E rF" were displayed. I called customer support hoping they could tell me what was wrong. They again told me again to call Reliable Appliance Service. I called Reliable Appliance Service and they said that LG needs to schedule the repair or it will be treated as a cash ticket. I called customer support again and was told that they need to submit a request to their service locator team. Several days passed and I heard nothing. By this time all of my food was spoiled.

On Friday September 2nd I once again called customer support and was told that they still haven't found a servicer. They would prioritize my case with the service locator team and would return my call on Tuesday, September 6. I never heard back so I called customer support again on Thursday September 8th. I was told that they were still trying to find a servicer that would be willing to come to my house 40 miles from Anchorage, Alaska, and that there was nothing more that they could do.

Needless to say by this time I am angry and exhausted. My refrigerator has been broken for over two weeks and your company has conveniently absolved themselves of any duty to fix the problem. Thankfully, Home Depot is willing to pick up the refrigerator and give me a refund. They will be here on Saturday September 10. I will then buy a GE refrigerator.

In the mean time I am telling everyone I know to avoid LG products as the appliances are very unreliable and customer service is unwilling to help. I am sure that you have an interest in keeping your company reputation in good standing with potential customers and therefore I am hoping that by informing you of my experience you can assist your team to make a better product and improve customer service.

At the very least your company should have been willing to pick up the appliance from my home and take it into servicer. Instead I was offered no help what-so-ever. I have spent hours on the phone with absolutely no interest on your company's behalf of helping. If there is one thing that I can hope come of this is that no one who I know buys an LG appliance. This has been literally the worst customer service experience of my life.

review_text:

When it died over a 3-day holiday and repair estimates were about $800 plus a long wait to get parts, we decided to buy new. product_title: GE APPLIANCES GNE25JSKSS, Stainless-Steel
review_text: This is my second experience with a french door refrigerator. I like this much more than the comparable Whirlpool. 1. This GE you can open and close either side of the french doors independently of the other side and no worries of accidentally snapping off the seal that bridges the two doors. 2. the full width crisper drawer is easier to open and access the contents as it doesn't have a cover that pops up. For some reason that cover always annoyed me. 3. The lighting is brighter and color temperature makes refrigerator contents look more appetizing. 4. The freezer baskets are solid (not wire grid) and the top basket comes out easily for cleanup of spills/crumbs. I do prefer a side-by-side freezer better for easy access to contents and laying trays flat for freezing, as well as easier door opening. The bottom freezer door is heavy to open and I find myself wanting to rest my elbows on the freezer door top when I'm looking for stuff in the bottom basket. However the french door refrigerator compartment is way better than a side-by-side at keeping foods on all the shelves an even temperature. Also, if you are purchasing this refrigerator for a home with roommates or airbnb guests the french doors can be great so one person uses the left side and one the right side. I gave this 4 instead of 5 stars because of my issues with the freezer. I have had this refrigerator for just a few weeks so we'll have to see how I adjust to the freezer over time. As of right now I would buy this again as the positives outweigh the negatives

review_title: This is a good downdraft cook top for a 30 inch opening BUT safety issue
review_text: This is a good downdraft cook top for a 30 inch opening. A lot of the cook tops out there are too big and have 5 burners. I didn't need that -- I've hardly ever used 4 burners at the same time, so it didn't make sense to use up island space with a 36 inch unit. This unit works very well as far a cooking goes. I was concerned about other reviews stating the flame is sucked into the downdraft. The downdraft is indeed pretty strong (which is a good thing) but the flame-pull issue does not seem to be a problem at all on my unit. You can see a little slight tug of the flame, but no problems -- the heating is fine. Here are the reasons I gave only 4 stars: 1. Once when the water boiled over, it knocked out the flame. If I hadn't been standing there to notice what had happened, I'd have been none-the-wiser with the gas coming out. 2. If you turn the cooktop knob too fast, it bypasses the lighting of the flame, and then again, just gas is coming out. (My husband did this. He had too quickly turned on the cooktop to pre-heat the pan, but he never noticed that there was not an actual flame lit under the pan.) These both seem like safety issues to me. My previous gas cooktop had a continual clicking when the flame was either knocked mid-cooking out or not lit at start up. Therefore, you knew there was a problem and did not walk away until resolved. I feel people should be aware of this safety issue.

At this point we are looking at going a full month without a working washing machine. Taking our clothes to the next town over to borrow someone else's washing machine is not exactly how we imagined spending our weekends less than a year after spending a thousand dollars on a new washer.

All the features in the world aren't worth a thing if a washer can't fulfill its most basic function.

review_text: I've been pretty happy with this washer-dryer pair.  I've had them for 1.5 years now and no serious problems.  They clean the clothes efficiently and the LED readout that tells you how long the load will take is very handy.  These have larger capacity than normal, which is helpful for bedding.  The downside is that the washer is too big for the standard drain pans.  I had to find an outfit online that makes metal drain pans to order.  On the other hand, a metal drain pan is more likely to still be serviceable when you need it so not unhappy about the extra cost and trouble.  It did hold up the installation waiting for the pan since I didn't realize ahead of time it would be needed.  My only substantial niggle (which brought it down a star) is that the water tends to accumulate in the rubber gasket of the washer, resulting in mildew and gunk.  I think you need to just dry it out with a towel after every usage and to leave the door open to dry.  There doesn't seem to be any fix for this.  It's also very quiet and reasonably vibration free.

product_title: Samsung Appliance Onyx Front Load Laundry Pair with WF56H9100AG 30" Washer, DV56H9100GG 30" Gas Dryer and 2 WE302NG Pedestals
review_title: Consider yourself WARNED: CUSTOMER SERVICE WILL BURN YOU
review_text:
So we ordered the flex wash washer and dryer, and after set up tried to run our first cycle of the washing machine. The machine lost all power shortly after starting up. Now queue the samsung customer service nightmare.
Day 1: called samsung customer service (on a wednesday) and was told we couldn't get a technician out to look at the machine until next tuesday.
Over the next two weeks, i have had to wait for 5 service appointments, arranging schedules to be available, I have spent at least 15 hours telling the same story to Samsung customer service, and have gotten nowhere.
Two weeks later: after 5 service calls from technicians with no solution, during which time Samsung refused to assist us with a replacement or refund, we still have a non-functioning machine. Samsung customer support insists that they require some form 7000 from the service technician. However, Samsung won't facilitate this project so i am essentially attempting to act as a general contractor between Samsung and its own service technicians. While the technician acknowledges the machine is a total lemon, Samsung technical support refuses to accept this conclusion and is advising continued service calls.
So ESSENTIALLY, SAMSUNG REFUSES TO ACKNOWLEDGE AFTER FIVE VISITS THAT THEIR MACHINE IS BROKEN AND AGREE TO REPLACE, but instead prefers to hold on to my money while it tries to salvage its broken product.

SO, if you are willing to gamble never getting what you pay for, then this machine is perfect for you, otherwise, I strongly advise you do not purchase any Samsung products.

product_title: LG Graphite Steel Top Load Laundry Pair with WT5680HVA 27" Washer and DLEX5780VE 27" Electric Dryer
review_text: Nice machines.

review_text: This is simply the worst dishwasher made. It's the first one I've owned new (I didn't choose it, it came with the house, which had been flipped) and it doesn't clean as well as the failing one in my old condo, that we 10 years old.
