product_title: LG LDCS24223W 24 cu.ft. 2D Bottom Mount, 33" Wide, Drawer
review_text: I did not like this unit right from the start , the fan was noisy starting and stopping, the magnetic latch was so hard you had to jerk it, if you just pulled easy you would move the whole thing.  I purchased mine from Home Depot on July 1 2017.  I bought it because it was the only large refrigerator I could find that would fit My spot.

product_title: LG DLGX7601WE 27" Gas Dryer with 7.3 cu. ft. Capacity, in White
review_text: The LG DLGX7601WE is the highest rated dryer by Consumer's Report which is why we purchased it.  I remember reading a review online where someone said it didn't dry the clothes well and I thought, well...that can't be true, they must have just gotten a lemon.  Our experience after owning if for a month is that the sensor does not work well. Our clothes come out partially dry on numerous cycles.  The thin easy to dry clothes are dry the thicker clothes are damp. In the case of drying socks the dryer kept turning off after 5 minutes because we were told we didn't have enough in the dryer.  We found LG after running through tests telling us that it was just fine if we took it off energy savor. That is not the case.  The clothes still do not dry on sensor mode.  The only sure way to get the clothes dry it to use time dry.  We are stuck using only the Timed drying mode which is a bit like going back to our dryer 30 years ago after paying heavily for "up to date" technology.  After spending that much money we are surprised at the bad design and lack of support by LG to address the core issue: a sensor design that is ineffective. Put in a load of socks to dry and you will be very disappointed. Consumer's Report got this one wrong to our experience.

product_title: LG DLGX7601WE 27" Gas Dryer with 7.3 cu. ft. Capacity, in White
review_title: Takes 2.5 hours to dry a load and some items are still damp
review_text:
Pros: can control and monitor remaining drying time in the LG ThinQ app. 2 way door is somewhat useful.
Cons: takes too long to dry even half a load, the app will tell you 12 minutes are remaining but 12 minutes later, it'll say 15 minutes are remaining, this will keep happening until you've waited about 2.5 hours for a load to finish and some items to still come out damp. I suspect it turns off the heat frequently in the middle of the cycle and air tumbles the load, because when I open the door to take out some quick dry items, the dryer will be lukewarm, in fact I've never had the inside of the dryer feel 'hot'. This is for a new install in the garage with a new very short vent hose to the outside.

I replaced a 2 year old Kenmore junk dryer but that one at least took about 1.5 hours or so to dry a load before it failed.

product_title: LG DLGX7601WE 27" Gas Dryer with 7.3 cu. ft. Capacity, in White
review_title: Error code because it's too cold outside
review_text: Do not buy this dryer.  It's been installed 11 months, and we got error code "TE2".  Arranged for LG Direct to repair it.  The day before the technician is scheduled to arrive, LG informs me that the error code is probably due to the cold weather in Chicago.  Let me state again - the agent confirmed on a recorded line that there is a good chance that the error code is showing because the weather outside is too cold.  To fix it, I should run a speed dry cycle before running my normal dryer sensor cycle.  Oh, and if he comes to fix it and it's not a defect, I will be charged around $100.  Poorly engineered device.

This nightmare ended with Samsung failing to follow through with the haul-away service that numerous support people promised.
Do yourself a favor and don’t take a chance. This fridge and its service under warranty are sheer sh**.

product_title: GE PFE28KSKSS freezers, Stainless Steel
review_text: First off, I didn't actually buy this unit from Amazon, we bought from an independent local dealer.  We are pleased with its appearance, features, performance and spaciousness, but we are very disappointed with how noisy it is.  This refrigerator replaced a 2001 Kenmore and that one was actually quieter than the brand new GE.  When you pay this much for a refrigerator you expect it to be as quiet as a mouse, this refrigerator sounds like a small airplane getting ready for take off.  The noise seems to be coming from the evaporator fan(s) for the refrigerator section, as opposed to the freezer section, and a little more in depth online research will tell you that GE has been having issues with these fans for various reasons for quite a while.  They obviously haven't solve the issue yet, which is disappointing when you pay this much for a fridge.  If you're at all sensitive to appliance noise, steer clear of this one.

review_title: Worst fridge we have ever owned
review_text:
Worst fridge we have ever owned in 40 years. It is so loud that I can hear it buzzing all the way at the other end of the house. There's nothing wrong with it; that's just the sound it makes when operating normally. It has completely ruined the peaceful atmosphere in our home. Want to sit quietly in your living room and read a book? Impossible, because this monstrous machine is always humming and buzzing and raising everyone's blood pressure with useless noise.

The ice maker is another thing. If you have three adults in your house and they all want a tall glass of tea with ice, forget it. There will not be enough ice. If we have even a single guest over to the house we have to buy a bag of ice and get an ice chest because we know this horrible fridge will not even make enough ice for one guest.

The filter is a scam. Trying to rip people off by charging for a filter no one needs.

I bought GE because they used to be good. They have destroyed what was a great company. This fridge is garbage.

product_title: GE PFE28KSKSS freezers, Stainless Steel
review_text:
So if you're wondering like I sometimes do....you can 100% believe the reviews that are here....this company is completely worthless. I have never used a refrigerator so loud in my life....when you open and close the doors they slam heavily, no way to quietly close. The cheese drawer sounds exactly like a turkey call every time it's opened and closed. The ice maker has no sensor that stops it making ice when full so the ice is constantly going everywhere, including behind the freezer drawer...husband has to clean soooo much ice out regularly. It's just such a piece of junk and was so expensive...such a disappointment. You cannot write these reviews on the GE website, they won't allow any bad ones....extremely unethical! I registered it with the provided card at install. After NINE MONTHS of dealing with their manufacturer defect and slip of quality control, I am finally taking the time to call, and they will not send me a new basket! UNBELIEVEABLE! I am looking at my online profile where I registered it and it says the warranty is still good - they claim they don't go by that....then WHAT is the point of registering it?! GE I have now learned is just another company that cares nothing about customer experience and is happy to lose a customer buying five grand of appliances at a time over a $50 dishwasher basket. The customer just wants to feel valued! I'm disgusted! Lesson learned. Oh, and one more thing.....several months ago I got an email from them inviting a review. I wrote an honest and mostly positive review that also included a few negatives...THEY WOULD NOT PUBLISH IT!! I was shocked. I went to the website and saw nothing but glowing 5 star reviews, not a negative in sight. SO BEWARE of trusting the reviews on their site - they are filtered! Horrible, unethical company!!

review_text: The refrigerator is for the most part it is fine except the ice maker which is slow. product_title: GE GFE28GMKES French Door Refrigerato
review_title: The exterior control panel on this is so annoying.  It's almost impossible to read the touch labels without a flashlight!
review_text: Sometimes it’s the little things that turn out to be the most annoying!  With this unit- unfortunately you’ll need a flashlight to use the external control panel.  We bought this refrigerator/freezer based on the french-doors, freezer door, price, size, color, interior compartments, external controls, etc.,  but there’s one surprise that we weren’t aware of that made this choice a very disappointing one... and it’s the control panel/dispenser on the outside of the freezer door.  On that panel you’ll see that there is a little line lit-up just above one of the two of the selections (water & auto fill), but that’s it!  So if your kitchen is very well lit, or if you use a flashlight, then you can find the other 7 control selection/labels that are in the touch panel.  Since the control labels are a dim, subtle off-white color, embedded into the clear plastic panel, they literally blend in with the Slate background making it extremely difficult, if not impossible (depending on the kitchen lighting or angle from which you may be looking) to see where you are suppose to touch for those 7 other controls!  The French-door refrigerator is great, but the design of the exterior control panel make it difficult to use.  It’s disappointing that something so obviously user-unfriendly was over-looked by design.  I just want to warn you, before you own it.

product_title: GE GFE28GMKES French Door Refrigerato
review_text: I won't show as a verified purchase because I purchased mine through Home Depot.  I love this fridge.  The 4 stars instead of 5 is because of little things, like the fact that the bottom drawer in the fridge doesn't remove easily.  For me, that may be because it is in a tight space and I am unable to open both doors all the way back, but IDK.  I never actually thought I needed theater LED lighting in a fridge, but I must confess it is actually nice and helpful.  I saw the review about the panel and not being able to see it, but I don't have a problem at all with that.  The filter is expensive, about $50, for the water and ice, which is about $15 more than my last Frigidaire. The fridge itself doesn't show fingerprints much at all, but I find myself wiping the handles at least once per day because they show everything. (Same for the matching oven and dishwasher.)  The tab that you press against for water and ice stays spotted and is hard to clean. But I really like this fridge and would not hesitate to recommend it.

review_title: Horrible lemon and horrible customer service
review_text:
DO NOT BUY THIS PIECE OF CRAP

I'd buy some beat up Kenmore or Whirlpool beast off the back of a trailer for $200 bucks and they'd work fine -- until they didn't. So at 40 some years old, I said, what the heck, I'll buy a new one. I end up using the large (not regular or extra large) setting because I do all my colors and all my whites in two loads. And it fills up the tub. Ironically, you get better performance if the clothes are just barely covered by water -- even if you use lots of detergent. A small load is a "regular."

It works fine for me. But using the standard measures I'd say on scale of 1-5:

Washing performance: 3-4 (again depending upon the water level and detergent)
Features: 3 (there's no soak feature)
What else? Looks? 3 i guess

Mine doesn't move around on me. The spin cycle does have clicks and clunks. But whatever, I'm not annoyed by that. The spin cycle does seem to take a while.

GE Dryers? I LOVE the GE Dryer i bought with this. The GTD42. Perfect.

Also, the one other complaint is that the shelves in the left side door (the one with the ice/water machine) are so shallow that they're almost useless. You can really only fit very small bottles or whatever in those (the top one is slightly deeper, but even still is pretty shallow - I can get a dijon mustard bottle in it, but nothing larger, and the two shelves below that top one won't even fit that).

This is critical to know, given the fridge weighs 360 pounds in the box, and it's wide enough that for us, it only fit through our front door. We were able to have it installed by the appliance folks who built our house, and two guys used appliance harnesses/belts to get it into the house, but it's a pretty serious thing to move around (this is not specific so much to this refrigerator, but more to purchasing it via Amazon and so on).

review_text:
I just purchased this a WM on sale. It was purchased to downsize from a Magic Chef MCPMCIM30SST model. It's used in a motorhome, as the refrigerator doesn't have an ice maker, (they take up 45% of the freezer space). The huge Magic Chef took up alot of space and lived where the washing machine would normally go! I wanted that storage space, so I'm now a content owner of this Igloo ICE108 model. It fits perfectly on top of the kitchen counter right next to the coffee maker!

Pay attention to the setup instructions!! In particular the part about not tilting it more than 45 degrees, an d letting it sit for at least two hours.

I completely disregarded the instructions. I actually tilted the box at the checkout line to scan the barcode., and it was placed on its side to get it out of the box. As soon as I cleaned out the inside with soap and water followed by diluted vinegar, then promptly plugged it in and filled it with water. Immediately after the water pumped, the compressor sounded like a small cat was being intermittently choked and let go. It was way too loud. It was much louder than the old much larger Magic Chef that it replaced. I watched some YouTube reviews to try to listen to their ice maker's noise level. One woman on YouTube mentioned how quiet her ICE108 was!

So, I exchanged it, (cant do that easily online)!

Machine two was carefully kept upright from the store shef to my kitchen counter. I plugged it in, and it was so much more quiet! Just a humming when the compressor is running, and a little mechanical noise when the ice drops and the system cycles.

I would give it five stars but it really makes very little ice at any one time. The entire full basket of "Large" ice bullets barely fills one large Tervis cup. If you are going to need a large quantity of ice for an event, (frozen margaritas, several drinks, etc.), you're going to need to stockpile the output in your freezer.

review_text:
This is a review of the Samsung 28 cu. ft. 4-Door Flex™ Food Showcase Refrigerator with FlexZone™
_________________________________________________________________________________

After twenty long years with a durable Kenmore side-by-side that just wouldn't die, it was time to move on. Despite the immortal quality of the Kenmore, it was a white color model and had started to yellow. We also needed/wanted more storage space.

So we were looking for a unit that had more storage space and we also wanted to take advantage of some of the newer design features we've been seeing crop up in the newer refrigerator models. We liked the French Door design of many of the newer models, but what we didn't like was the big roll-out freezer drawer sections. It just seems like you end up piling stuff on top of other stuff in the freezer drawer and then have to dig around later to find items. So it was quite a pleasant surprise to walk into a showroom and discover this new design by Samsung ... the double French Doors! Not only does this unit have the easy-to-use double French Door design, but this Samsung refrigerator features the FlexZone. Which means essentially that the bottom right compartment can be used either as additional refrigerator space, or if you need it, additional freezer space. This was perfect for our needs. We typically don't need a ton of freezer space and were looking for as much refrigerator space as possible. This design gives you the best of both worlds. You suddenly need extra freezer space for upcoming holiday cooking? No problem. Push a button or two and that FlexZone becomes a freezer section. After the holidays, no problem, just switch the FlexZone back over to a refrigerator section. With the double French Doors it also eliminates the hassle of having to dig through a big freezer drawer for items that all stacked up on top of each other.

In addition, this unit offers a Food Showcase door. Open it with the bottom handle and you have immediate access to three shelves without pulling the entire door open. It saves energy and is super convenient. Also, in the FlexZone section, there is a built-in wine rack. This was a very welcome addition for my wife who previously always had to fight to find space for her wine bottles. Most refrigerators never seem to account for the size of wine bottles and you end up having to use up all the tall shelf space you have. The wine rack, for us, was a godsend. It stores wine bottles perfectly, on their side, slightly tipped down toward the top of the bottle. Not only does this create perfect dedicated space for wine bottles, but by doing so, it frees up so much more space for everything else in the refrigerator.

Another welcome feature is the Power Freeze / Power Cool capability. This allows the additional use of energy to rapidly cool down sections or get them to an adequate freezing temperature very quickly. Which comes in handy if you end up using the FlexZone and changing from a refrigerator compartment to a freezer compartment or vice versa.

Inside, the shelving is very well designed and thought-out, with some of them able to slide or lift away depending on the size of containers you are putting into the unit. Everything feels extremely well-built and solid. The entire unit is almost entirely soundless. The space is cavernous. The lighting is bright and efficient and makes everything super easy to find.

Inside, due to the FlexZone technology, Samsung uses three evaporators to cool the unit, which makes for very consistent, even temperature throughout. On the outside, the entire unit with it's treated stainless steel veneer is gorgeous. I have to say, the "fingerprint resistant" coating doesn't seem to do much of a job in eliminating fingerprints and smudges. But just after a few weeks, I found that I quickly started using the recessed door handles without even thinking about it and 90% of the time I don't end up touching the outer surface of the machine. When smudges do appear, it's very easy to take a clean rag or paper towel with some plain water and wipe away any prints, smudges or marks.

Another quality feature is the water filter which is designed INSIDE the refrigerator nestled between the two crisper drawers ... and creating easy access so that when the filter needs replacement there's no need to get behind the giant unit. You just open the refrigerator, then open the water filter compartment and swap out the filter. Additionally, if you decide to NOT use a water filter, the water dispenser will still work!

I read that some people have had trouble with their ice makers and this gave me some pause before purchasing. However, upon further research, it turned out that several manufacturers have had trouble with their ice makers as well. So far, after a couple months, our ice maker has worked flawlessly. Installation was only tricky because we live in a vintage home and the doorways are generally 31 - 32" wide. The installers were JUST able to get it through the last door into the kitchen. Otherwise, it hooked up quickly and despite being told it would take 20 - 24 hours to cool and freeze all the way to operating temps, our unit hit the operating temps within 4 hours.

Overall, the unit is beautiful, spacious and efficient with many excellent new design features. Just the exterior alone has made our kitchen look that much nicer. My wife and I have found ourselves staring at the unit in admiration. And when you open it, it is even more impressive in terms of space, light and design. The retractable and sliding shelves are easily overlooked, but they are by themselves, a fantastic design feature. We simply could not be happier.

review_title: Great fridge, with a very annoying design flow Samsung CAN FIX
review_text:
This refrigerator is great. It has one important human interface design flow Samsung CAN fix:
The control panel at the front of the fridge has both critical controls, and every day ones.

The critical controls include the temperature settings desired for the upper half, the bottom left quarter and the bottom right quarter of the fridge. The every day controls include the spout / lever you press to have water pour into your cup and a cube/crushed ice selector.

The entire panel has two modes: locked and unlocked. In locked mode the entire panel does not react. Can't change compartment temperature by accident (good), but also can't get a glass of water (lever will not respond when panel is locked). This I suppose is useful for parent of young children (even though the panel is quite high up the fridge door). In unlocked mode the entire panel works. You can just as easily get a drink of water, as you can accidentally dial away the temperature of the different compartments.

There is no intermediate sensible setting: water spout and ice type selector controls are on, and the critical temperature controls are locked.

This is particularly important in this fridge where the bottom right quarter will switch from fridge to freezer temperature in one control touch. This I say from experience because we had that compartment full of produce (inc eggs, vegetables etc), when one of our guests inadvertently switched it to freezer mode. The entire content was frozen solid by the time we discovered it, and had to be thrown away.

So now we keep the panel locked down, which is a hassle every time you want to just walk to the fridge and get a glass of water.

Samsung, if you read this: This is easily fixable. This model connects to the internet. Give us a firmware that adds a third lock stage: lock critical controls, but keep every day controls usable. Or find another logical solution and push it to our fridges.

Hope this gets through to them.

review_title: The Good, the Bad, and the Ugly
review_text:
I have had this stove for a year now. It has some good features, and some really horrible features.

The good: The double oven works great. We use it all the time. I store iron skillets in bottom half, so makes it easy if I just use top half, saves electricity, and is simple to use once you get the knack. Also, the range looks great. There is a high powered burner with three sizes -- large-diameter, medium-diameter and small-diameter. It heats quickly.

The bad: The stovetop only has one large diameter burner and that is the high powered burner. This means that it doesn't have a large burner that you can simmer on. The one large burner is high powered, and even when set to low, water still boils on this burner (!!!). Everyone in my household burned everything for three months. My husband now refuses to use this burner. What all this means is that there is no large burner that offers simmering capability. I just have to move large pots to smaller burners when I want to simmer. When sauteing meats, I start at high to heat the pan quickly, add oil and then turn it down to 4 or so, add meat and then turn it down to 2 or even Low.

The ugly: The stove knobs turn far to easily. If you lean against the stove, you can change the cooking heat on the high powered burner from low-small diameter burner to high-medium diameter burner (or from low-medium to high-large) in an instant. I consider this range to be a high fire hazard.

review_text:
This range has been on my Wishlist for years. They discontinued it and I was heartbroken. I didn’t want the newer model because they removed some of the features. The pictures are taken after I finished seasoning the oven. This would be your first step before ever using the oven. Please always remember to remove your divider and all racks before seasoning or cleaning your ovens. The Seasoning process puts a heavy chemical smell in the room. Please ventilate the room. It also gets very hot in the room. Keep all children and pets away from the kitchen. This step is important so you won’t pass these chemicals on to your foods. Overall I lucked up after years of continuous searching and found my dream range in the second largest appliance store in the US. It was way in Colorado and I am in Florida. It took a while but that was on the freight company. It was crated and palletized and in perfect condition. I already have most of the parts to my Samsung Suite but have one more piece to add and I am definitely purchasing it from them. They calmed my mind when I was concerned and communicated with me. They would get 10 stars from me. I don’t know if I am able to say their names but I do favor them now!

The Pros:
Works independently as a single or double oven with the divider in place.

There is storage above the warming drawer for the divider when not in use.

Yes, I said correctly, the bottom drawer is not for storage but it is an actual warming drawer with not just 1, but 3 settings for it.

Cleaning: There is not only a Steam Clean Cycle but, there are not 1, but 3 Self Clean Cycles.

Convection in both ovens

Amazing oven racks, 3 and each is different. (The gliding rack is the ultimate best.)

There is a Delay Setting

The oven is Smart, and can be controlled remotely.
You will know any time an element is on because the knobs will highlight blue. ( As Shown In a Picture).

Once the divider is in place and you use both ovens, you can truly bake in each oven using different settings.

The Cons:
The cooktop has to wiped immediately with any spills. (Please always use a clean cloth)
The digital control panel comes on just from sneezing (Just Kidding). It comes on truly from standing in front of the range cooking, sometimes without you being aware of it. Always pay attention to what is highlighted in the panel. When I first got my range I made the warming drawer come on and didn’t know how to use it yet. I just happen to press it until it went off. Scary. This may be the reason this range was discontinued. That could be a fire hazard.

You have to be very careful to never under any circumstances slide a pot or pan to another element. You will ruin the cooktop. I have always lifted my cookware from one eye to another.

Learning to use the multipurpose knobs is a learning curve. ( like the triple element and the bridge ) The bridge is controlled by 2 knobs but the knob for the front element has 2 positions, 1 for the front element only and in the 2nd position it will light the front element and the center between the front and back elements to make it a bridge. review_title: A nice machine with some annoyances
review_text:
Good machine, generally. I can say that because after 18 months (now 4.5 years as of late 2020), mine hasn't required repairs, nor the matching dryer. It was a replacement for an inexpensive top-loader. I opted for the 6500-series for the aesthetics and because it was on sale; otherwise, save for a bit of extra space, I see no good reason to choose it over the 5200-series.

It cleans as well as you want it to. With shorter cycles, some synthetic garments that retain smells aren't cleaned. A three-hour steam cycle cleaned a camping item that had been sprayed with cat urine impervious to a half-dozen other remedies.

It's fairly well-balanced. Not exceptionally so; you can still get it to vibrate with an offset load, but it has a motion sensor to self-limit speeds. This can make getting the water out of something big and heavy, like a comforter, challenging. Oversized clothing loads have no such problem. Noise is audible and mostly inoffensive, though it probably would annoy a light sleeper.

Like most front-loading machines, this Samsung retains water around the rubber seal. I've left the door askew on mine from day one. No smells or buildup. I suspect this would be less true if I closed the door, though I haven't had to sop water with a cloth or apply any other prophylactics.

The little add-clothes drawer is mostly a nuisance. I once opened it frequently to air the machine out, but the plastic catch would periodically jam for no reason I could discern. The washer is vigilant about locking both doors. Chances are, if it'll let you open the small door, it'll let you open the big one too.

Digital controls are a mixed bag. You get a nifty timer that's moderately accurate for an average-sized load. However, and this is inexplicable: there's no true custom setting. You can create a saved personal wash, but it has to be based on the presets, which arbitrarily lock things out. No hot water for this one, no fast spinning for that one, too short a wash time for another. It's maddening; just let me pick what I want!

That aside, it's a capable, forgettable, stackable machine that's light on power and water. Hard to argue with that if it continues to hold up.

review_title: Starts to smell like a damp locker room
review_text:
We’ve owned this washer for 6 months. Prior to this one we had a GE top-loading washer that was fairly basic, but that worked wonderfully and that we miss dearly — we left it when we moved and thought we’d give this Samsung washer a try.

Why did we try this washer? Well, it looked nice and seemed like the front-loading form would be easier to use. Big mistake.

We quickly discovered that for some reason the designers could not figure out how to keep water from pooling in this forsaken device after washes. So after each wash you have more work to do: wipe down the inside of the door, wipe the large ring interior around the door opening to soak up the remaining water, check the trap for gunk, then leave the door and the detergent module open for about 30 mins until everything air dries the rest of the way, ideally in a well-ventilated room or with a fan blowing on it. Then occasional also run the self-cleaning cycle. (Hopefully you are also using high-efficiency detergent in the right quantities.)

If you do all of that, you MAY be spared the stench, but possibly not. We haven’t been. Now as we walk past our laundry room we often smell the mildew odor while we’ve left the washer door open for it to dry... even just today and we’d run the cleaning cycle yesterday.

I’m so upset at this garbage washer. To have paid more for a machine that is more work and yet doesn’t work as well is so frustrating.

Also, this machine has turned itself off automatically on 2 occasions with no explanation. We came back the first time to find sopping wet clothes. The other time we found it full of suds still.

How does a dryer like this pass any kind of internal design review and quality assurance? Do not buy.

review_text:
[[VIDEOID:9b694a05f9a40cde417e280a2a295062]] Never, ever, buy an Electrolux washer and dryer! My husband and I purchased an Electrolux washer (Model EFLS617SIW) and dryer (EFMG617SIW) in September of 2016. We have had nothing but problems with them. We first had them looked at in April, through a place recommended by Electrolux. The repairman ordered parts for the dryer (new board and switch) but did nothing for the washer. Electrolux denied the claim that we need new machines. We don’t want new Electrolux machines! We want our money back! Electrolux Customer Service is a joke. They just say they are sorry about the problems and understand our frustration. No they don’t.

We are so disappointed in these machines. They aren’t even a year old! Our old washer and dryer lasted about 16 years and never needed serviced. We consider these machines to be lemons. review_text:
I bought this expensive washer and dryer to replace ones that lasted 25 years with the hope paying up front would give me the same good service. For what these cost they are disappointing. All the bells and whistles of the washer do not seem to improve the outcome so I usually use plain vanilla. For those who want a lot of options this machine has them. The only way you get really hot water from the beginning is to use the sanitize setting. This is an EPA ruling and you will find "energy" saving features on all new machines. The max spin is great for towels, but be aware it will cause clothes to wrinkle so I use a slower spin which is fine.
The dryer is my main dislike. The clothes are thrown forward and revolve in a tight circle near the door and thus really wrinkle and take longer to dry because they are in a tight ball. I called Electrolux to ask about this. They were extremely pleasant to deal with and set up a service appointment. The service man said this was the way it was designed to keep clothes away from the heating element so they won't burn and the exhaust (where the lint screen is located) pulls the clothes forward. I don't think so! I showed the service tech with a wet load of wash what happened. He also said that was not right. What was the supposed fix, raise the front leveling legs to throw the clothes back. That helped, but did not cure the problem. In my opinion this is a design failure. I would not recommend these expensive machines.

product_title: GE GDF650SSJSS Built In Dishwasher
review_text:
Had a brand new one installed by GE in 2017. One month out of warranty, it failed due to the water pump failing and it burned up (no fire, but you know what I mean). Repair was going to be $500.00. Such a high end machine should not fail! Customer care gave us 50% off of a brand new one and gave us a two year warranty, which was better than nothing.

New one was purchased an installed by GE in April of 2019. On December 15, 2020 the same thing happened, bringing 2020 to a totally sucky end. They could not send anyone until January 5, 2021 to even look at it “due to COVID”. Riiiiiight. Hand washed dishes through the holiday. Repair guy from ge showed up on Jan. 5, but did not have a pump on the truck to replace it. Scheduled another visit on Jan. 15. Another day off from work to let him in. Tells us that dishwasher is “unrepairable” and gives us a number to call for customer service at GE. Great, I love sitting on hold for 55 minutes-AGAIN.

Finally get through to a rep who tells us that the service number for this GE dishwasher is not handled by her office. She puts me on hold to see if she can find someone to help. After a short wait she comes back and says that the service rep had not put his diagnosis into the computer system yet so there was nothing she could do to help me. She said someone will call me back on Tuesday because of course they don’t work over the weekend and Monday is MLK day. I put money down betting that nobody calls me on Tuesday because every call back I was supposed to get doesn’t happen anyway. Long story short, do not buy this model of GE dishwasher. If you search hard enough you will find that about 50% of the one star ratings out on the web for this machine or do the pump failures.

After spending over $1000 on a dishwasher and having two of the exact same machines fail in three years or less, coupled with the horrific customer service, should be a good indicator of avoiding this model like the plague. So today, as a RN, instead of volunteering in our local Covid vaccination clinic where I could’ve vaccinated 100 elderly residents, I sat at home for this. I am pretty disgusted.

review_text:
I would give this machine a zero if I could. I hate when other people use that line in a review, but i hate this washer so much that this remark is justified. I have had this machine for just under 2 years. from about the third month on, this machine has made my clean laundry smell like mildew, sulphur and rotten eggs. yes, I've tried various methods of tub cleaning methods, all to no avail. this washer's design includes a water reservoir that collects water. the manual says you should empty the reservoir every 3 months, but in actuality you will need to empty it every day if you want your clothes smelling even remotely palatable. and don't expect emptying the water to be a cake walk either. there is a 2 inch tube coming out of the Reservoir about 1 and a half inches from the ground. The water uses gravity to drain, so you will need to find a large shallow pan to stick under the hose every time it needs to be emptied. Then you will need to wait three or four minutes for the reservoir to drain completely. Then you will need to balance foul-smelling water in your shallow pan to your sink and hope it doesn't spill on anything else on the way there.

If you don't remove your clean clothes within a couple of hours, expect the load to smell like you forgot it while away on a week long vacation.

The stain removal quality of the washer is not as good as my last washer which was a whirlpool Duet.

Additionally, if your load becomes unbalanced and you need to re-spin the clothes make sure you don't miss the auto re-spin cycle. Because if your cycle times out, you will need to re-rinse your loads in order to re-spin it. There's no "spin only" cycle setting.

in conclusion: of you want a stress free laundry experience that gives you clean looking and smelling clothes, don't buy an LG washer.

review_title: The oven bakes impossibly uneven.  And Samsung considers this to be normal for this product!
review_text:
I gave 2 stars because the cooktop is amazingly good. I bought and had this oven installed in November of 2017. The stainless steel on the cooktop is easy to scratch and shows every crumb, but that is a minor problem.
The real problem is the oven. This range has the most uneven heating I have ever experienced in any of the ranges I have had over many years. I have had Samsung repair out twice now - first time the thermostat was burned out so they replaced that. No improvement in the oven. Using a good quality oven thermometer, I found out just how uneven the heat is. When I set the top oven on convection at 450 degrees, instead of heating to 425 - which is normal for convection - it went to 460 and burned the food. When I turn on the bottom oven, to convection heat of 450, it chimed when it said it had reached 450. But the thermometer registered 300 degrees! It actually took 25 minutes to get the oven to 400 and it never went higher. I learned from one of the repair men that both ovens actually chime when the HEATING ELEMENT reaches the set temperature, Not the oven cavity! WHAT??????? That is insane.
After the repair man saw all this he called the repair center and was informed that a it is acceptable in this oven for the temperature range to be off by anywhere from 25-40 degrees!!! And Samsung had no intention of doing anything about it.
I called the Escalated Customer Support and a third repairman is being sent out. I am SOOOOO sorry I ever bought this range and I can't imagine ever buying from foreign-made Samsung again. If this won't be fixed by Samsung, I plan to try to get Lowes to back me up. They have excellent customer service and I am hoping they will work with me on this.
The takeaway form this story is: NEVER, EVER BY A SAMSUNG KITCHEN APPLIANCE!! THE QUALITY IS UNBELIEVABLY BAD and YOU WILL GET VERY LITTLE HELP FROM SAMSUNG!!

review_title: Built-Ins, like Children, Should be Seen and Not Heard
review_text: This is a good looking, understated built-in with some nice features such as easily adjustable door bins, a space saving ice maker, and NFC communication so you can diagnose your appliance using LG's smart phone app.  But after owing a Kitchen Aid for 15 years, I think I prefer Kitchen Aid.  This unit boasts an Energy Star certification, and a sale rep assured me that it was also a very quiet unit because of LG's "linear compressor".  Well, if this is quiet, I would hate to hear loud!  This unit is louder than the laboring old compressor on the Kitchen Aid it replaced.  The ice & water dispenser is nice to have, but it only has a single dispensing outlet (meaning you must toggle from ice to water using the selection button.) I would have preferred separate dispenser outlets for ice and water in the door.  It does maintain its temperatures in the freezer and cold food areas nicely, and the soft close doors and crisper drawers are a nice touch.  Lastly, you can set the chosen freezer and refrigerator temperature digitally, and that number is displayed on the LCD display whenever you open the door) but those numbers are NOT the actual temperature readings from inside the unit- they are merely the temps you set. So you will need to buy an after-market thermometer and place it inside the unit if you actually want to know the REAL temperatures inside. For me, I've found setting the unit @ 2 degrees (F) nicely holds the freezer at 0 degrees or just below.  I think the lack of real-time temperature readings is a missing feature I would have liked to see.  So overall, it performs well, seems to be energy efficient, and versatile -- but don't expect it to be silent operator.

product_title: LG LFCS25426D 36" French Door Refrigerator with 25.4 cu. ft. Total Capacity, 4 Glass Shelves, 7.8 cu. ft. Freezer Capacity, in Black Stainless Steel
review_text:
Purchased this model several months ago, and have been quite happy with it. I agree with another reviewer in that it is difficult to find a refrigerator without the ice-maker on the door. We have friends and family that have constant problems with said external ice-makers.

There are minor dislikes. For example, all three doors don't shut easily. Yes, there is the open door alarm. However, I am often out of the kitchen before the alarm begins. On the other hand, this seems a very substantial appliance. Perhaps the weight of the doors contributes to the fact that often the doors stop before completely shutting. According to the installer, it is properly balanced. And, yes, I do occasionally dislike having to open both doors to pull either of the two veggie drawers.

We did have a problem with the ice-maker in the freezer. We tend to drink a lot of iced water. For the first month, the ice maker stopped working several times a week. The manual said that we should clean the sensor to solve the problem. This would solve the problem for a short time. We had been using the "make more ice" control. We decided to stop using said control, and the problem went away. Btw, it would be nice if the manual actually showed us where the sensor is located.

Now, for the positives. Wow, a 25 cubic ft fridge is a LOT bigger than our old 19 cubic ft. We also like being able to put a gallon of milk in the door tray. I wasn't sure we would like a French Door model, but was swiftly impressed with the ease of getting things out of the freezer. And, as I said earlier, it is a very substantial, quality product. Interestingly, when we told the installer that our old fridge was 22 years old, he commented that we would never get that many years out of any new fridge.

review_title: Life's Good But LGs Customer Service Really Sucks
review_text:
My LMX28988ST /04 broke down (purchased Oct 2012). According to the owner’s manual parts are covered for seven years and the compressor for ten but not the labor. At first, I called several local repair shops, and all declined to work on it because they were not authorized LG repair shops. I then decided to call LG's 1-800 number. The lady at LG told me to contact Sears Repair for service. Sears were booked solid and I had to wait around 10 days for an appointment. Finally, the day came, and I was told by the Sears repairman that they are not authorized to do LG warranty work. In any case he did the diagnosis and said my compressor, condenser and dryer were bad. The estimate came out to over a thousand dollars and Sears would need to contact LG before any work could be done or I could pay the full amount and try to get reimbursed for the parts than came under warranty. The repairman charged me $99 plus tax for the house call. He gave me a 10% coupon and told me I could recover my house call bill by buying a new refrigerator from Sears that cost a $1000 and up.

I contacted LG again and “Nick” at LG told me Air Tech Hawaii does the warranty work in Hawaii. Why wasn’t I told about that in the first place. Being the frig initially cost me over $2,500 on sale from the NEX (Navy Exchange), I decided to pay the flat rate of $535 plus $25.21 to have it fix. According to Air Tech Hawaii, Sears took a swag (scientific wild ass guess) and diagnose that both the compressor and condenser were at fault. Air Hawaii added a valve to attach test gauges to determine the problem. Turns out the condenser was still working. Unless it was leaking, it would not be covered.

No matter how much I presented my case, LG would not reimburse me for their misdirected service call. I own a couple large LG TV and an electric range but never again. “Buyer Beware” a large corporation like LG would be stingy about 100 bucks. My beef was all about the “principal.”

If I can prevent one person from buying from this lousy company, I'd be happy.

review_text:
Our LG linear compressor top of the line died after four years and 7 repairs, a real nightmare.
I am now comparing this machine to the Korean, same features:
1. GE has quality hinges that match the cabinet color and are height adjustable, LG were cheapo shiny intrusive stamped out affairs, the thread on the adjuster bolt was worn off from factory.

4. GE steel is darker and less telling of fingerprints, LG was shiny and we were constantly wiping at it.
5. LG became very loud and droning worse after each repair. Quiet linear compressor is just a marketing gimmick, loud to stop a conversation.
5. LG is $4k, GE non-Profile is $2k.
Negatives: loud, but not terribly. Adjusting the stabilizer feet helped, especially once the front of the top frame became locked into the cabinet (photo).

I am looking forward to 20 years with this machine, will be vacuuming the condenser coils regularly.

Still very happy two months later, I managed to elevate the front frame on the stabilizer feet to lock tight on the edge of the cabinetry (photo) this way it became even quieter, droning went away completely.

ONE YEAR UPDATE:

Continues to work well. Intermittent droning an issue, but cooling well. I don't dare call a tech as so far the senile amateurs that make the rounds in our area are mostly clueless. If the noise gets worse I will call my trusty independent repaiman who has a functional brain and skills as opposed to the warranty clowns we had working on your defunct LG.

Taking it down to three stars.

review_text:
First - just a note: You can purchase this product new at Lowe's or Home Depot for approx. $2100 (delivered).
Second: The refrigerator looks nice and has some good storage options.
Next: This is likely in the top 3 worst products that I ever made the mistake of purchasing.
It has a known icemaker design failure. It will take you about 4 months of ownership before this failure becomes noticeable.
There is presently a class action suit against Samsung regarding almost ALL of their "French door" style refrigerators. See it at classAction.org.
The icemaker (located in the refrigerated compartment) constantly freezes up - makes no ice - and instead, leaks water into your refrigerator compartment. This is apparently unfixable. Samsung has no solution, and yet continues to fight their lawsuit AND sell the failed product.
When I contacted a Samsung certified repairman, he told about the known issue - and said there would be no sense in him coming to repair it, as it is "unfixable".
On it's best day - this refrigerator may produce a dozen or so ice cubes. On it's worst day (for me - about 3 times a week), we have to thaw the inside of the icemaker with a blow-dryer (which we just leave sitting beside the fridge) to free-up the frozen lines and components.
If this sounds like your idea of a good time -- go for it!

review_title: Drain hose will get punctured and leak and flood house!  Design flaw!
review_text:
Bought the matching pair. The dryer didn't work from the start and I had to have repair come in, after I bought a lint cleaning kit to clean the duct as they won't work on it without doing that first. No debris and new house but they didn't care...dryer had part not assembled internally causing D80/D90 fault codes...he fixed that and dryer was good.

Now onto the washer...It has a drain hose that runs vertically up the back (inside the machine) and out to your drain. The hose is right behind two sharp plastic tabs on the motor for the drum. This drum moves freely as it washes as it should, and that makes the tabs on the back of the motor poke into the drain hose on the back during normal washing. review_title: Our LG Dryer caught fire during the warranty period!
review_text:
Our LG dryer caught fire 10.5 months after we bought it new from an authorized dealer. There was extensive smoke damage and, obviously, our home and the safety of my family (wife, two daughters and a dog) were imperiled. Luckily, in the end, only the dryer was dryer was ruined. Who knows what chemicals we were exposed to from the smoke?! The WORST part of it all was how LG ducked and weaved and finally turned their backs on us completely. The only thing they would offer to do was repair this faulty, dangerous unit. I told them I don't care if 10 NASA scientists came to our house, fully disassembled and put the unit back together again, it will NEVER be used in our home EVER AGAIN. Who knows if it will catch fire again?! Who knows what chemicals are in the smoke that was created?! LG was completely unsympathetic. They said we were refusing their help and washed their hands of us. And we were contacted by someone in the "Presidential Liaison Office" who said she was the ultimate authority. One of the most unhelpful, unfriendly customer service people I've ever talked to. A heart of ice. And, for the record we're adults and we know how to use a dryer properly, clean the lint filter, etc. The technician who LG sent used a special airflow meter to confirm that the vent and duct were clean.

LG refused to help us in any kind of meaningful way when its appliance caught fire under warranty in our home, putting our safety and possessions at grave risk. It took days for them to address the issue and I spent hours begging and pleaded various customer support agents in Manilla to escalate this. Finally, someone from the highest levels of the support organization, a "Presidential Liaison" contacted me. She was unfriendly, unsympathetic and utterly unhelpful. The only thing she would offer to do was to give me 20% of the value of the unit or have it repaired. I'm not crazy. NO ONE wants a faulty dryer that has caught fire repaired! Who knows what was burning in that unit (plastic, wiring, etc) and what dangerous chemicals were created?! Who knows whether it will catch fire again?!.The idea that we would keep this appliance in our house, given the fact that it put my entire family and home at risk, is completely ludicrous. But the Presidential Liaison was like a robot, just repeating the same thing over and over. I asked her if she was OK with me leaving our interaction furious with LG and ready to yell this story from the mountaintops (ie. social media, review sites, BBB, Consumer Affairs, UL, etc.) and she said she was fine with it. What kind of liaison is that?! What is clear is that the culture of LG and LG Support is completely unsympathetic, completely focused on the bottom line instead of the customer, perhaps even jaded and uninterested in the reputation of LG itself. It is the reflection of a sick company and a cynical corporate culture. For such a widely praised company, it was shocking and hugely disappointing. Needless to say, we will NEVER use LG products again and we will make sure to tell this sad story to everyone we know and care about.

review_text: We purchased the LG washer and matching dryer. The circuit board on the washer malfunctioned, and the washer is now useless. We hired a service technician to service the machine. According to the site, as of this past Tuesday, it would be available in 14 days. Day-after-day, the 14 day estimate remains, and the anticipated availability date gets pushed back. Not hard to see where this is going. Of course, all the while, we have a useless washer with no repair date in sight. I've contacted LG (repeatedly) and got bounced around from department to department to department. Apparently, no one in the entire company knows if or when this part will be available. I wrote customer service twice complaining that no one would answer my question (if/when the part will be available) noting I was being bounced from person to person. They promptly responded by referring me to a number I had already called with no success. BOTTOM LINE: We bought thinking that higher priced appliances are better and would last longer. That is not correct. This LG product has been dismal. Be extremely weary, LG does not stand behind its products, and you can easily end up where we are, living in a very expensive house with a very expensive washer, hauling your clothes to the local laundry mat. My strong advice is to avoid LG at all cost.

review_text:

There is no real agitator and it underfills so clothes never get fully wet. The agitator is just a bottom spin plate with humps on it. If you do manage to get it to fill enough then the clothes do not circulate. Nothing gets properly clean. The only way to get clean items is to never put more than 3 inches worth of clothes in it. If washing sheets you have to wash them one at a time or they balloon up and never circulate.

If you try to change the setting during the wash it then goes through a re-sense mode to judge the weight which now includes wet clothes. That causes it to fill to the maximum level regardless of many clothes are in the machine. When that happens you have to reset it to spin only and start over which results in the machine being the biggest waster of water ever.

If you pay for water usage expect your water bill to at least double.

product_title: Whirlpool W10882923 Ice Maker
review_text:
Update: After 2 years and 9 months still works great!

After some research this seems to be the only diy option for repairing your w10377151 ice maker. Like many other victims, my ice maker blew a pin clip within the control board where it hooks to the heater element. Although there is an interesting youtube video of someone making this fix with a bullet casing, I figured I would go the more common route of replacement. Like many other reviewers, I was hoping to find a plug and play ice maker assembly that could just be popped in and done. This isn't the case as I believe the manufacturer has changed its design after realizing the fatal flaw. Be aware because of this design change the new assembly will have the dial on the front and a white water cup instead of the blue one. This is supposedly an upgrade and will work as a replacement. Also, the new part number on the item will say w10300024 which denotes the repair kit. This does not mean you received the wrong part.

Unfortunately, this redesign involves replacing the wiring harness. Two separate wiring harnesses are included but you only need one. You can quickly identify which one is needed by comparing the wire colors and connectors to the one that is currently installed on your ice maker. The new one should almost be identical. Also included are two plastic covers. One has a hole cut in it for the power switch and one does not. This is because some models have the power turned on from the front panel of the refrigerator. If, like me, your ice maker has a power switch, you will have to transfer this over from the old cover to this one.

Also included in this kit is the metal portion of the fill level arm. This arm is a different shape than my original one. My kit did not come with instructions so I was unsure of which one to use. Since it is provided with the kit, I assumed it was the correct one to use. They do not include the plastic flapper piece, so this will have to be transferred over from the old one. After installing the new arm, I realized that it did not allow the arm to be moved up and down like the one on the old ice maker. I put the old arm back on and found that although I was still unable to move the arm down, I was able to click it up into another position. This reminded me of a different style of ice maker where you would lift the lever up to permanently shut it off and click it back down to turn it back on. Since this ice maker has its own power switch, I determined that this may be why this kit includes a new arm that is bent differently and does not allow this movement. This also may be why another reviewer had an issue where he had to reset the ice maker each time it made a full bin of ice. So I put the new arm back on and hoped for the best.

As for the harness transfer, like others have said, as long as you take pictures you should be able to transfer the harness without much difficulty. I have attached the pictures I took in case anyone misses that step and ends up stuck. I also put some automotive style terminal dielectric grease on most of the connector contacts to try to prevent corrosion. I also opened up the front of the control box and applied some grease to those pins as well to further attempt the original issue from repeating itself. This was a fairly new ice maker so not many of the connections were corroded, but I did notice some on the on off switch located on the front cover.

I slid the ice maker back in, gave it an extra push to get it past the water line, reconnected the connector, turned it on, pressed the door closed button and heard the wonderful sound of the ice maker filling. A little over an hour later the machine dropped its first batch of ice. Success!

In case you were wondering, after powering the unit up, the fill arm dropped to the expected position and all is well.

Also, the hardest part for me in the whole evolution was trying to figure out how to disconnect the main connector prior to removing the maker from the fridge. All you need to do is press on the center of the ice maker side of the connector where the tab is and the connector will pop right off. I will not disclose everything I tried before figuring this out.

Another note, don't get discouraged if after completing the transplant and flipping the power switch to no avail, remember that, at least in my case, the door needs to be closed in order for the magic to happen. You can bypass this by pressing in the button that tells the fridge the door is closed.

review_title: Cheap and easy replacement for your ice maker!
review_text:
I ordered this ice maker to replace the broken unit in our fridge, the first time it went out I tried to go cheap and just replace the thermostat. By the time I paid for the thermostat and special adhesive it was only about $20 cheaper than this whole kit and it only lasted about four months. If your ice maker has gone out, don't waste your time trying to replace individual parts that may or may not be a long term fix, just get this kit and be done with it. When I ordered it I thought was just going to be able to swap the ice maker part out and not mess with the wire harness(es) but I'm glad I read some of the other's posts about it since the new unit is an upgrade and requires the harness to be changed out.

The kit comes with two harnesses and two plastic caps but you only use one of each (you match the old wire harness colors at the main plug to one of the new harnesses and that's the one you will use. This is an upgraded part so changing the harness is a necessity, but it's not difficult. Take a picture of all the where all the connectors plug in before you remove the original harness so you can plug the new ones back in the correct location. A word of caution since all the parts are loosely strewn in the box, check your unit before you install it, mine had a small metal clip that had worked itself under the ice fingers and would surely have messed something up if I had missed it.

The whole repair only took about an hour, but in fairness I had taken it apart before, if this is your first time taking the ice maker apart, take your time and watch some videos before you start, it will be helpful.

review_title: Product Works Great But No Instructions
review_text:
Purchased the refrigerator (Whirlpool Model GI6FDRXXY04) in 2012 from a local scratch and dent store. Various parts have failed throughout the years and it was now time to replace the ice maker. A big thank you to my deceased father for all those years of making me "hold the light", it seems that time was worth while after all. The replacement part came quickly and though I initially thought it was dirty or used, it seems that the grease is simply lubricant. Without any instructions I availed myself of the University of YouTube. The original support clamps are no longer in use for this model as it appears there was a manufacturing change at some point and the supports have been replaced with an under carriage that is not documented or videoed anywhere that I could find. Three bolts later I was at least able to loosen the original part and wiggle it out of a resting position. The new one easily connected to my existing electrical harness so the two that came with the replacement were not needed. A couple of more wiggles to get the new part in and we were off to the races. The key part here is to get the intake funnel (the part that transfers the water from the refrigerator into the ice maker) aligned without having the shutoff arm come out. In my case I'm pretty sure I only got it "close enough". Return the three support bolts to the under carriage assembly and turn the refrigerator back on. About 6 hours later I heard a sound I had not heard in a year. The whole family looked up in amazement as we realized the house was not being broken into, our first produced ice in a year had finally come!
A side note, this refrigerator also had a bad water inlet (part Whirlpool W10498990 Water Inlet) which I had replaced previously. In my case the ice maker had stopped a year ago followed by the water dispenser six months ago. Although, replacing the water inlet did not fix the ice maker directly, I am pretty sure that this was an indirect cause of the ice maker failing.
One thing is for sure, Whirlpool makes you a more educated home repairman. Thank you for that and thanks Dad for always insisting on fixing our own things rather than calling out the experts. I may not have appreciated it at the time but I understand now...and insist my own son holds the light. Guess I've leveled up.

review_title: Not a direct replacement from original, but a definite improvement!
review_text:
As noted in many of the other reviews, there appears to be a flawed design in the ice makers from some of the Whirlpool and similar refrigerators, so much so that the entire unit needed to be redesigned. This replacement part includes the redesigned ice maker, 2 different wiring harnesses, and 2 new caps for the front of the unit. The parts used will depend on whether or not your ice maker has a power switch incorporated into the unit, or like mine, has the control built into the front panel of the refrigerator.

Following some of the mentioned YouTube repair videos, I was able to disassemble the main unit and confirm that my original ice maker had a melted connection underneath the front cover where it attached to the heating element. I did not do any additional troubleshooting and just "rolled the dice" that this part would be what was needed to repair. After doing some comparison shopping, I found that Amazon offered this at a significantly lower price than many of the parts stores I typically use, and also had free 1-day shipping.

The part arrived next day, and since I already had the majority of the ice maker disassembled, the total installation time was less than 30 minutes to put back together. Once back together, the first batch of ice dropped within about 90 minutes, and when I woke up the next morning the tray was full. A few things to note:
- There is a ground wire which attaches underneath the motor in the back that drives the auger to dispense the ice. I did not have a wrench that could reach the screw to remove that wire with the motor in place, so I needed to remove the motor to access that screw.
- The wiring is rather stiff, and takes some coaxing to get into place.
- When reinstalling my ice maker unit into the freezer compartment, the fill hose appeared to be hanging down further than what would allow the unit to slide in. I ended up needing to use a thin aluminum yardstick to wedge in between to push up on the fill hose, allowing the unit to pass by.
- I did swap over the flap from the bar on the old ice maker, but used the bar that came with the new ice maker. I also was unsure if I should reuse the white cap from my old maker or to use the one that came with the new one. I opted to use the new one but hung on to my old one just in case!
- On the box it was stamped that it was a new part, manufactured in 12/18. Much nicer than getting stock that could be years old!!!

5 stars as of now as it was a quick, relatively simple repair, and hopefully will buy us a few more years of use of our refrigerator.

review_title: It works but is a head ache to install
review_text:
I can't complain to much I guess. I was able to figure out how to install the new wiring harness. I had ice after a few hours. that is what I wanted.
It is very strange to me that a seller would send out an item like this without instructions of any kind. Heck I bought a brick to charge my phone and it had instructions. It is really not so much for the wiring. It didn't take long to figure out which harness was needed. It took longer to work my way past the grommets than to actually attach the wiring. In the end the only wire with an issue was the green ground wire. It is not possible to get to the screw. I decided to cut it and add a splice. which worked quite well. The sensor wire bracket from the old unit is attached with a screw. the new one just sits in place and is held by the cover. I only know this because I saw no other choice and it did work after doing it that way.
The new unit comes with a different shut off arm. It is bent entirely different than the old one. I never was able to determine now to properly put it in place. I was able to transfer the plastic flap though. I installed it the best I could. I waited a few hours and never made any ice. I finally took of the arm and it immediately started working. After about 24 hours I had a full bin of ice. I dumped it out and am letting run again. My only concern is if it will continue to make ice after the bin is completely full. I guess time will tell. Maybe that would be good information to put into the non existent instructions.
So far it has done what I bought it for. For that it deserves 5 stars and I rarely take away stars for a product that works but come on guys. You are not selling these thing to tech shops, you are selling them to the public that needs INSTRUCTIONS. Before I got old enough to develop a little patience I would have just returned it for credit and told everyone it was a terrible product and not worth buying.

product_title: Samsung NZ36K7880UG Cooktop
review_text:
samsung

First, let me say I did not buy this from Amazon, I bought if from Best Buy, summer of 2017. That being said, it is my goal to put my review in any place that sells this item so that no one else has to go through what I have been through. The only good things worth mentioning about this induction cooktop is that it is aesthetically beautiful, with its blue glowing "flames" and implied functionality of using a griddle. I say implied, because it doesn't work.

Firstly, this cooktop is one big mess. I scarcely even know where to begin. I will start on the left side, the elongated flex-burner where I should be able to confidently put my Le Creuset griddle and assume that it is going to cook somewhat evenly. Nope, not even close. The flex-zone implies that I can use one button to basically turn this section into an area that I can control with one "control", instead of having to adjust them independently. My griddle fits this area perfectly, yet, it cooks so unevenly that I have to shift food constantly as I am cooking. Pick one up slide it down, slide another in its place. The centermost area seems to cook the most efficiently, with the front end getting the least amount of heat. Again, my griddle does not hang over these burners, yet the frontmost portion of the griddle simply warms the food such as pancakes or grilled cheese sandwiches until I slide them down to another section, so I spend all my time rotating food. Even when using these burners independently, sans the flex-zone, the front burner is definitely weaker. As if that wasn't enough, a few weeks ago, out of the blue, after I had browned a roast on this left side, the glass just cracked. Nothing dropped on it, not so much as a wooden spoon, and yet it cracked. An appliance repairman who was here for something else said it was obvious that the crack came from within, so there's that.

Now we will move on to the center back burner. I have several pans that are the same size as this burner and I was so looking forward to having a large burner. WRONG! If you look at the photo of the water boiling in the skillet and the quesadilla browning in the skillet, you will see that it is as if they just painted a bigger burner image over a 5 1/2 inch element. Whenever I have to brown any kind of food, I again, spend all my time moving it from one place to another in the pan. The only part that browns is that little circle in the middle. meanwhile that tiny center circle of heat burns in my pan because it is so much hotter than everywhere else, no matter how hard i try to avoid it by shifting food, moving the pan etc. I use high quality cookware, All-Clad or Le Creuset. This is not pan problems or user error. I have been cooking since I was a young teenager and I am 61 years old. I am also well adjusted to the digital world. I use iPhones, iPads, computers with Windows, a MacBook Pro. I am the person in our house who sets up the mesh wifi, the modems etc. I am no rookie when it comes to electronics. Moving on…

The back right burner works as expected because I don't expect much from it. It's a small burner, I use a small pan.

The front right burner is once again under-powered for the size of its “paint job”! It looks to be a 9 inch burner, and it is okay, although still does not induce even heat under a $250.00 pan. The burning of the deeper, beige pan was an accident. There was a little water left in my rice and I wanted to quickly boil it out. I walked away and when I realized I had left it on, I quickly returned. When I poured the rice out into a wide pan to stop it from cooking, this was what was on the inside of the pan. Yes, it was my fault it burned, but this pan was completely centered over that 9 inch burner and sits flat on the burner and this is what I found in my pan. Evidence that this burned certainly does not "burn" nor cook evenly.

Best Buy has been to my house several times, Samsung has been here several times. Best Buy changed out the parts for the back center burner and it still does the same thing. They replaced the cracked cook top, but I found a big long scratch on the new one. Not Best Buy's fault, I saw them take it out of the box it was shipped in. Today was a revelation in that I truly believe they, Samsung, think a small 5.5 inch induction magnet is going to excite the molecules in the bottom surface area of an 11 inch pan. Both the employees of Best Buy and Samsung have been as nice as they can be, but they are unable to fix this problem. Do yourself a favor. DO NOT BUY THIS COOKTOP UNLESS YOU NEVER ACTUALLY COOK. After all, it is pretty. Personally, I am leaning toward going back to a conventional glass cooktop. With them you can at least "see' the heating element. it will however NOT be Samsung!

One last thing, and it is of great aggravation. Those nifty little "use your fingers to slide the burner control to the temperature you want" controls are terrible. They may be that way on all cooktops, but I am reviewing this one. I cook. Real food. So there are spatters and drips and sometimes a greasy finger. You can not change these controls unless they are wiped down and relatively oil free. Now, I understand that in a perfect world, that makes sense, but when you have four pans going and you lift the lid from one and the steam dripping from the lid lands on one of those buttons, it will change it. It will turn them off. It will turn them down, it will turn all the burners off at one time if it lands on the power button. Then you have to remember what you had everything set on before you were so careless and dripped a drop of water from a lid on your cooktop if you realize it right away. Sometimes, it is a few minutes before you realize you have turned something off with a water droplet. But you know what else it does, it TURNS THEM UP! So the chicken you have been working so hard to evenly brown in your tiny little 5 inch spot of heat is now burnt black because after all, this is induction. What happens, happens immediately! So if a drip of steam/grease/water falls on your control and the control thinks that warm water is your finger and it just so happens to land on power boil, or the highest setting area on the slider, you are SCREWED! It happens so quickly you scarcely have time to respond, even if you are aware of it.

Yes, it has a lock button and I use that when I only have one pot on the stove and to keep it from coming on when my cat inevitably walks across it with her warm little paws at midnight. But when you have four pots of food going and you need to adjust temperatures as you are cooking in real time, that lock button is a pain to deal with.

review_title: This fridge sticks out the least, is actually counter depth
review_text:
I recently purchased this refrigerator from Lowe's. I actually tried to shop for it on Amazon but it didn't come up when I put in the search variables. I later saw this listing. I'm glad I got it on sale from Lowe's, because otherwise I would have paid too much.

Amazon has this refrigerator listed at 16 cubic feet. Hair lists this model number as 16.4 cubic feet. Amazon lists this as 27 inches deep. Haier lists it as 26.5 inches deep. The doors curve out, so on the edges it is only 26 inches deep, maybe a quarter-inch less. The width is 32.75 inches. The reason I'm sharing these is because I needed to get it into a fairly small hole and I figure other people might want the information, too.

The hole I had to put this in was 33.25 inches, which was too narrow if I wanted to push it back all the way. So I had to pull the refrigerator away from the back wall so that the door wouldn't hit the cabinet. The doors are hinged so that they can fit in a small place, but even so you will need a 34-inch hole if you want to push this all the way back against the wall. I had to pull it out an inch so that it is 27 inches from the wall on the edges and 27.5 inches or so in the middle.

There are a couple of things I don't just love. The bottom freezer area has drawers that are only 10 inches wide. This isn't wide enough for a frozen pizza. There is a space at the top of the drawers that could have taken a shelf so that it would hold a pizza, because each side of the freezer is 12-inches wide. I think it will be a simple matter to cut out a shelf from corrugated plastic and simply lay it atop the drawer framework (there's actually plastic there to hold it, so the drawers will still be operational). This is an easy fix, so I'm surprised the manufacturer didn't do something along these lines.

The other thing I don't like so much is that there are only three shelves in the refrigerator. Only one of the shelves can be adjusted, essentially giving a choice between having the tall stuff on the bottom shelf above the vegetables or in the middle. I would very much like to have four shelves, so that two of the shelves could be fairly narrow in height, which is perfect for soda cans and just lots of stuff. As things are now I have a lot of dead space over the stuff I put in the fridge. With my configuration my shelves have a clearance of 7.75 inches, 7.25 inches, and 10.25 inches. Given that most jars and cans are only five-inches high and stuff like hamburger meat is only two-inches high, it would be really nice to have an extra shelf and less dead air space.

Also, there is no ice maker, but I knew that when I ordered it. If I could have found an equally shallow refrigerator with an ice maker for the same money I would have bought it. And that's really the selling point on the fridge. It's more shallow that any other model I could find at this price point. Every other so-called "counter-depth" refrigerator stuck out an additional three or four inches. I was important for the way my kitchen is laid out not to have a giant fridge sticking out, otherwise I wouldn't be able to open the back door. So despite the things I don't like, the fact is that this refrigerator looks good, is quiet, and really does what I want it to do. I would buy it again.

Great Price!

Instead of trying to attach the end of the drain hose to the faucet attachment, just use the curved clamp to hook around the faucet base. Definitely put the wheel locks on when it's running or it will try to roll away potentially damaging the faucet and attachment. As a portable, you get an extra faucet hose if ever needed. When washing with warm water, wait until it's filled and then turn off the warm water and turn on the cold water for rinsing. When it's done I just stick both hoses inside the washer which leaves the door slightly open to dry out. The manufacturer said this model is discontinued so you shouldn't wait while they're still in stock.
Complaints:
Too much styrofoam packing material! There shouldn't be any since styrofoam does NOT recycle. Separate it from the recyclable cardboard forms and bag the nasty stuff for the landfill.
