review_title: Never Buy AN LG - You Will Regret It
review_text:
My LMX28988ST /04 broke down (purchased Oct 2012). According to the owner’s manual parts are covered for seven years and the compressor for ten but not the labor. At first, I called several local repair shops, and all declined to work on it because they were not authorized LG repair shops. I then decided to call LG's 1-800 number. The lady at LG told me to contact Sears Repair for service. Sears were booked solid and I had to wait around 10 days for an appointment. Finally, the day came, and I was told by the Sears repairman that they are not authorized to do LG warranty work. In any case he did the diagnosis and said my compressor, condenser and dryer were bad. The estimate came out to over a thousand dollars and Sears would need to contact LG before any work could be done or I could pay the full amount and try to get reimbursed for the parts than came under warranty. The repairman charged me $99 plus tax for the house call. He gave me a 10% coupon and told me I could recover my house call bill by buying a new refrigerator from Sears that cost a $1000 and up.

I contacted LG again and “Nick” at LG told me Air Tech Hawaii does the warranty work in Hawaii. Why wasn’t I told about that in the first place. Being the frig initially cost me over $2,500 on sale from the NEX (Navy Exchange), I decided to pay the flat rate of $535 plus $25.21 to have it fix. According to Air Tech Hawaii, Sears took a swag (scientific wild ass guess) and diagnose that both the compressor and condenser were at fault. Air Hawaii added a valve to attach test gauges to determine the problem. Turns out the condenser was still working. Unless it was leaking, it would not be covered.

No matter how much I presented my case, LG would not reimburse me for their misdirected service call. I own a couple large LG TV and an electric range but never again. “Buyer Beware” a large corporation like LG would be stingy about 100 bucks. My beef was all about the “principal.”

If I can prevent one person from buy an LG, I'd be satisfied.

product_title: Samsung NQ70M7770DS 7.0 Cu. Ft. Stainless Combination Electric Wall Oven
review_title: Roller Rings Always Fail and Don’t Last Longer Than Two Weeks
review_text:
I purchased a Samsung model #NQ70M6650D combination microwave/convection oven in December 2019 from BestBuy. It was installed just before Christmas of that year. The price was slightly higher than what I wanted to spend, but I was impressed with the clean lines and all the optional ways of cooking. My family typically uses the oven maybe once a day and the microwave about three or four times per. After six months of daily use, I have formed a “less-than-enthusiastic” opinion of this product. Essentially, it should not have developed significant problems so soon out of the box.

First, the convection system does not cook evenly throughout the interior. The oven has a significant hot spot towards the front right. Also, if you have multiple racks of food cooking on the convection setting, the top rack will actually burn well before the bottom rack comes anywhere close to finishing. I didn’t expect to see this since the oven is equipped with a total of two (2) convection fans instead of just one (1), as the competition provides. Apparently, Samsung’s fans aren’t moving any air. Although I’ve never seen temperature non-uniformity anywhere near this bad from Samsung’s competition, it’s not that big of a problem and can be easily compensated for. You just have to remember to move the food around inside the oven, switch racks occasionally, and add a few minutes cooking time.

However, the most serious problem with this combo system is with the device that rotates the glass turntable inside of the microwave oven. This device ensures that whatever you’re cooking is evenly heated. If it fails, your food remains stationary on the turntable and part of it will be microwaved to a crisp while the rest could still be frozen. The device is identified as a “roller ring” in Samsung’s service manual. The roller ring is made out of brown molded plastic and has three small white rollers towards its outer diameter and a keyed hub in the center. The hub slides over an output shaft of an electric motor which provides the rotational movement. The problem is that the ring is made out of very low quality plastic and when it eventually cracks and breaks, everything stops rotating. I have attached three (3) photos. The larger two are of a failed roller ring assembly showing the overall size of the part. The third photo shows a close-up of a cracked hub. They always break the same way.

Luckily, the roller ring can be easily installed and removed without tools. Unluckily, it appears to break every two (2) weeks. This is an average based on the four (4) rings that have broken in my oven since December. After the first one broke, I contacted Samsung’s Customer Service. They were very helpful and sent a replacement part free of charge. I liked that. What I didn’t like was that it lasted just two (2) weeks. I also purchased two (2) additional replacements from Samsung for $35 each (part #DE94-04028A. Save the number – you’ll need it). They each lasted no more than two (2) weeks. Each part’s hub cracked in the exact same way every time. Note that by this point, my family had refrained from putting anything heavier in the microwave than popcorn. So essentially, the microwave was useless to us. Brand new and useless! So if you purchase this oven, be warned that you will need to spend an additional $35 every two weeks to fix it.

In an odd twist to this story, I still have a broken 20-year-old GE microwave in the garage. It was part of the old combo unit I had removed so the new Samsung could be installed. It originally came with a roller ring too. The GE ring is old, slightly discolored, in good working order, and almost identical. Believe it or not, the ancient GE ring actually fits beautifully in the Samsung oven and functions just fine. I’ve been using it since March (about 16 weeks now) and it performs flawlessly. It rotates and does not crack. So if you decide to buy the Samsung oven, I highly recommend you get your spare roller rings either from GE or a junkyard that has a lot of old GE equipment in it. Apparently twenty years ago they figured out how to mold a $35 piece of plastic that lasts longer than two weeks without cracking.

Other than that, the Samsung’s steam bake feature is very nice and gets used. The convection feature in the microwave is also nice and gets used too. But all in all, the microwave is the weak link and it seems the corrective action would be so incredibly simple to implement. Just mold the roller ring out of a more durable plastic material like GE did. Done! Until then, Samsung has an inferior product with an avoidable nuisance problem that is going to upset absolutely everybody who uses it.

If Samsung would like to respond to me (or send out a case of replacement roller rings), the serial number for my oven is #OB187WCM700269X. I can be contacted at the registration address.

product_title: GE JVX5300SJSS Venting System
review_text:
Let me start with the good. It moves a lot of air and it isn't too loud. The controls are simple and effective.

The bad: 1) the mounting brackets are very sensitive to the inside dimension on the underside of your cabinet - and this will vary from one cabinet to another depending on material thickness and method of construction. The mounting brackets also have a cheaply punched set of holes when they really should have tapped holes. The screws provided are barely self-tapping and easily stripped. The corresponding holes in the underside of the hood have a stamped flange with beveled edges that get in the way of these screws. You are much better simply throwing the flimsy brackets away and putting in a little bit of wood blocking under your cabinets then using screws with washers under the heads to mount the hood.
2) At this price point, it would be nice to have LEDs rather than halogen lights.
3) Most people will use this as an exhaust hood, not a recirculating hood. But GE puts in vent louvers facing the user for those people who want to use it in a recirculating fashion. The louvers are ugly and most people won't use them. So why should we all suffer the sight of them?
4) The stainless finish was 'protected' by a blue plastic film. However the film was cut away in a few places around the controls. The problem is....when the factory cut away the film, the knife they used scratched the stainless perpendicular to the direction of the brushed finish. The film that was supposed to protect the finish ended up ruining the finish because someone in the factory cut away portions of it. It took several minutes with a Scotchbrite pad to obscure the perpendicular scratch.
5) The manual is written for every possible variant of hood, with all sorts of comments like "your hood may or may not have this feature. It might look like this, or it might not." If they can make multiple models of hood, can't they print multiple instructions manuals?
6) The blower is off-center, meaning it will only pull smoke from one side of the range.

These are the sorts of mistakes I would expect of a 'cheap Chinese import' but not of an icon of US manufacturing. I use the quotes because I've actually been very pleased with no-name Chinese products lately. They show an attention to detail, craftsmanship, and a drive to excel. This GE product showed only a lazy US attitude.

review_title: The "no frost" part is a lie.
review_text:
Supposedly, it's "no frost", but we had to call a guy out to defrost it manually after 6 months. And every 6 months after that. So, apparently, the frost melter does not do it's job. We bough tit through Home Depot and got an extended 5-year warranty through a company called Asurion. After the first year, we called GE and asked for a permanent fix or product replacement. They sent us to Asurion, basically a kind of insurance company and only sees issues in terms of an actuarial table. They don't seem to care if the product works or if the customer is happy. It's just about cost. They refused to cover preventive repairs, and told us to call the next time it failed. So, to be clear, they would rather wait for damage, spoiled food and an angry customer before reactively fixing anything. (We've been lucky that it's only failed while we were home. If we'd been out of town, it would have been worse.)
In the mean time, we defrost the system ourselves about twice a year, about as often as we'd have to defrost a regular freezer. But ... we paid extra for the "no frost" tech.
I have to wonder if the engineers at GE have visibility to this. If I were one of their engineers, I'd be appalled. But they are insulted from customer satisfaction by two or three degrees of bureaucratic separation.
My advice? If you get this freezer, at the first sign of defrosting failure, just take it back. Because once they have your money, they will stop helping you. And you've paid Mercedes prices for a Yugo.

review_title: Excellent Model but Read the Manual for Best Results
review_text:
So, I did not buy this on Amazon. Decided that I wanted a local store so any problems would be easy to handle or return. Consumer Reports had this listed as highly rate. My brother also owns an older Bosch but very similiar and has had good results and no problems. I am very happy with my purchase!
I agree that the tines are a bit close together but my dishes do fit. Besides, each row can fold down if needed. In fact pretty much all racks and rows of tines are adjustable every which way. I love the 3rd shelf for silverware; the silverware baskets that that came with the it are in my pantry (don’t need them). I was concerned about washing ability due to some of the reviews. But like I said my brother’s Bosch works great. VERY IMPORTANT - read the instructions!! You need to use good dish detergent (I use Costco’s packets) with a liquid rinse aid. Make sure your hot water is hot enough and run the kitchen facet before starting a load. The salesman said all the seating I need is “Auto” + “Sanitize”. He was right.

Do not, I repeat, do not rinse your dishes. Doing this will give really poor results. The dishwasher has a dirt sensor and rinsed dishes will make it think the dishes are not dirty and not clean long. Also, the detergent has enzymes that require food to activate. Just scrape off the food. That is all you really need to do. The water jets in the bottom are pretty powerful and can easily flip anything small and light like a plastic 1 cup container. Use the middle rack for these.
Plastic do not come out totally dry but everything else does. Just the nature of the beast as plastic does not retain heat well and this effects drying. I run a load and let the door open for a while. Oh, and it take about 2.5 hours to do a load. Not happy about that as my old one took about 70 minutes. Also, you have to manually clean the food filter. Not a big deal as this is needed in my case bout once a month.
This model can hold a lot of dishes. My service for 10 is in and the dishwasher is only half full. Six months of constant use and no issues. All told I am happy with my purchase and would recommend this model.

product_title: SB1-Front Control Dishwasher with Stainless
review_text:
I did not buy this machine DW80J75 series from Amazon. I got it as a floor model when HHGreg went out of business. I installed it myself (rank amateur). It has worked flawlessly for me for over a year. I use it a lot. I have found waiting to "fill it up" before use just makes me wash dishes by hand, so I use it every day or every other day.
This machine gets very low ratings everywhere you look for various reasons. Here is my experience and reactions to these criticisms.
I installed it flat on the floor without using the leveling legs, since one was broken in my floor model. I got the thing level using shims and a carpenter's level. I do not know if extending the legs a lot as it usual would result in issues due to instability, since the legs are cheap plastic. I can easily seen numerous issues arising if the machine is unstable or off level.
"Cleaning is bad": My dishes clean well. When they come out bad, it is because something has fallen out of a rack and is blocking the moving cleaninghead at the bottom, or a dish or utensil is too tall and blocks the rotating head. There is surprisingly little vertical height available in the lower rack. I had the latter problem a lot until I looked carefully.
"Dishes are wet": There is a "Dry" button to push on the control panel, which works well. Make sure you have rinse agent in the machine. My dishes come out perfectly dry, except for the plastic stuff.
"Long cycles": The 60 minute cycle works fine.
"Blue light is too dim in daylight": Mine is plenty bright. If you read the service manual, there are instructions for adjusting that light.
Bad service: I cannot speak to that since mind has only stopped working once. I got the OC error (overfill), and the booklet said to turn everything off and call a repairman. The online stuff talked about a big repair job. Actually, my discharge pipe was blocked by a wire bread loaf tie which somehow got into the drainage.
So, I have been very happy with this machine. It looks nice and is fairly quiet. Since I am a DIY'er, and I won't have to hassle with the warranty stuff and the repairmen.

========UPDATE ON THE WATER WALL WAND==========
The lower moving arm is tricky. It does not move back and forth continuously during the wash cycle, so, it is easy to think that is it not moving at all. This arm moves once at the very start of the cycle, as a self test, so try and catch it there to see if it moves. If you block it with an object in the lower rack extending beneath the basket, the machine won't cycle, but will blink on and off. Putting a big dirty bowel in the lower rack is also a way to test the lower arm.
There is way this arm may not work and be hard to figure out. There is a magnet in the arm which, when the arm is fully back at the rest position, tells the machine where it is. Magnets may degrade over time and the machine may not detect that the arm is fully retracted. I put two of those small, silver, "super magnets" on the bottom of the arm where the factory installed magnet is. They just stick there. Having done that, and being careful about objects in the lower rack not extending through the basket and blocking the arm (they may get dislodged during the cycle and block the arm), I have not seen issues with the "water wall" wand.

============Update Fall 2020======================
The water wall arm stopped working. The motor that drives it was broken. There is a good U-tube video about this There is a cheap plastic part in the motor casing that breaks, disconnecting the motor from the moving arm. Unless you have the ability to take the motor apart and glue the plastic thingee back together, and then weld the motor case closed again, you are stuck buying a new motor. That is what I did. I replaced the motor myself. Not too hard. There are openings in the back of the machine to allow access to the screws that hold the motor in. Good luck. It is fixed and working nicely again.

review_title: BOSCH is luxury lifetime quality and technology that the industry will one day catch upto
review_text:
I am a previous BOSCH owner of washer/dryer and dishwasher.

I owned all three and over a period of 10 years I never had a single service call so I am a Bosch customer for life.

I was hesitant when I read the review here on Amazon on these. I went to Bosch-home.com and read that these were the latest technology that was being manufactured and called customer service to ask questions about what I read here on the dryer.

I have used for three loads of laundry both washing and drying.

I found the washer to be outstanding and was very quiet.

I found the dryer to be incredible technology and had no issues with jeans, socks, linen, t-shirts and synthetics and drying times were as expected in any dryer and perhaps a little quicker.

For anyone questioning why the mixed review and how is my review any more valid.. Here are a few items to consider:

1) Yes, there is a learning curve associated with Bosch because these are so technologically advanced that there are programs that are necessary when you use various articles of clothing.

You cannot just throw a bunch of laundry in and press a button, you need to be aware of what your washing and what program is the best to use.

2) The dryer is absolutely incredible and I agree with Bosch that this is the future technology for drying because of the incredible savings and efficiency!

With that being said, it is high maintenance in the sense that you cannot just clean a screen every once and a while.

You MUST clean the screen, but EVERY LOAD and once a month need to clean a heat exchanger as well. If you don't mind and are capable of making sure you screen is clean each load and clean the exchanger once a month you will be EXTREMELY HAPPY with your electric bill and insane technology used and how much better your clothes will come out and be protected!

Here is the link to copy and paste for going directly to Bosch to read about both waster and dryer technology and quality:

http://www.bosch-home.com/us/products/compact-laundry

One last issue here is a review about the outlet needed or a "four pronged" plug. I live in an apartment and my apartment is in Springfield, Mo. and the outlet needed was already here, this means that the 220v outlet that is needed is what current electric code calls for, the reviewer on the issue with claiming it was not for the USA must have wiring from 30-40 years ago. If you have old wiring than just update your outlet by a simple run to Home Depot or Lowe's. Do not be worried about this set for any reason!

I was just asked about cleaning the exchanger and what is involved in it. I couldn't be simpler or easier to maintenance.

1) Front Lower Left Door in photo
2) Open Door (Flap)
3) Two little levers, open
4) Slide heat exchanger out, rinse
5) Let dry before next use
6) Insert heat exchanger on next use
7) Secure heat exchanger

The heat exchanger is aluminum and very lightweight, it is not difficult whatsoever to handle or maintenance and the time involved is less than 5 mins.

review_title: ONE HOUR OF POWER! It's a blessing to have a dishwasher like this!
review_text:
Let me begin by saying that no dishwasher is divine, so to speak, so defects and problems can develop. It doesn't matter what mechanical or electronic device you purchase, be it a car, computer or dishwasher, there will always be potential failure within the overall scheme of working parts. That just the way things go. So let me speak to those of you who have had some kind of trouble with your dishwasher, perhaps a faulty valve or leaky hose, etc.... IT'S NOT THE END OF THE WORLD! So just relax and breath easy. Be thankful that you live in such a great and prosperous country that you are able to even buy and operated a dishwasher. We are so blessed to have so many convenient devices to help us manage our lives compared to many people throughout the world, and especially in past generations.

What do I think of this Bosch dishwasher? Well, it was a bit challenging to install, as the installation procedure and setup was quite a bit different than my old Maytag that recently gave up the ghost, so it required some extra parts and effort to get things in order. But now that it's installed I can honestly say that I really like this dishwasher very much.

Pros:

- It is very, very quiet - amazingly quiet.
- Despite being energy efficient, it cleans very, very well.
- I love the speed 60 setting, which I use most of the time, as it is more than sufficient to clean almost everything. The water coming from my boiler is nice and hot, which I believe makes a huge difference in its cleaning efficacy. I don't really see the need to use the "sanitize" option, as it does such a great job cleaning exclusively on the speed 60 setting.
- No need for an internal food chopper, as the filtering catch does a great job filtering out large pieces of food, and only needs to be cleaned periodically.
- I love the silverware rack up top. It cleans so well we rarely ever need to used the standard silverware hold, making even more room for pots and pans.

Cons:

- Due to the third rack up top, large cookie sheets don't fit. And even if there were room, as there was in my old Maytag dishwasher, the rack prongs don't allow for easy placement. No big deal, as I don't mind hand washing bigger items.

- I'm not a big fan of the water feed hookup. I wish it were made of solid brass instead of nylon/plastic. The elbow joint needed for hose attachment must not be tightened too much, otherwise the rubber washer might be compressed too much and fail. It also cannot be tightened too little. The washer on the first elbow joint I purchased was too thin and apparently failed due to it being compressed too much, but the second elbow purchased had a much more robust and thicker washer, enabling me to tighten the elbow up without issue. When the first elbow leaked, the water activated the internal emergency shutoff sensor, forcing me to tip the unit back and drain the internal water out in order to reset the machine, etc. Anyways, I highly recommend making sure your installation elbow which attaches to the washer and water supply line, has a nice robust washer in it!

I'm not a huge fan of the rack layout. I personally liked my old Maytag rack a whole lot better. But I'm just being picky in this regard.

BOTTOM LINE:

THUS FAR IT'S BEEN A GREAT DISHWASHER, AND I HOPE THIS TREND CONTINUES. BUT IF IT FAILS, WELL, THAT'S JUST THE WAY THINGS GO AT TIME. I'LL EITHER FIX IT OR GO BUY ANOTHER UNIT AND GET ON WITH LIFE. WHAT A BLESSING IT IS TO HAVE A MACHINE THAT WILL WASH MY DISHES FOR ME!

The good book says: "In everything give thanks!"

Worst of all, after having the dishwasher for only a couple months, the detergent dispenser cover wouldn't close.  This stopped use of the dishwasher, and the repair man won't come for two weeks. review_text:
Same model purchased and installed locally.
Pros: Fairly quiet, but far from silent. Gets the dishes very clean. The top rack is good for things like a cutting board that may not fit anywhere else.
Cons: 1. The wide variety of racks might seem a plus, but it degenerates into a puzzle contest. This will go here, but not there or there, and if it goes there something else won't go next to it, so better put it over there, but wait It doesn't fit there, or if it does it will bang into the plate or glass next door. I enjoy the challenge, but my wife does not.
2. Something as simple as terminating an accidentally chosen custom wash cycle and choosing another will require consulting page 33 of the manual because you will never figure it out on your own.
3. It gets extremely hot during a normal dry cycle. This may be related to two thermally insulated glass coffee cups that shattered or exploded. Those cups survived hundreds of washings unscathed in our previous non-Bosch machine.
And a final note -- The very long machine serial number, which you will need to activate the warranty, is located only on the right edge of the door. The design of our kitchen has that door edge, when it's open, about three inches from an adjacent cabinet door. Getting the number required removing the cabinet door and using a mirror. The mirror was suggested by Bosch customer service who had obviously heard about this problem many times before -- which raises the question, why doesn't Bosch put it somewhere else? Grrr.

product_title: Bosch SHEM78W55N 24" 800 Series Built In Full Console Dishwasher with 6 Wash Cycles, in Stainless Steel
review_text:
I believe this is the model I bought. Looks like it, the price is about the same. The reason I can not tell you if it's the exact model number is because I
had it removed the next day. The horrible, chemical burn smell that came from it was atrocious. I wish I had done some research first; I just blindly went by price and options, which I hope I never do again. About halfway through the heating process, this asphalt, chemical smell came out, filled the kitchen, and I had to actually leave the house. Eventually I had my neighbors, who are electricians and plumbers, remove it. Pieces were melted, but that wasn't the problem. I checked the internet to see if anyone else had my experience. Not only did Boesch have a history with recalls, but apparently the problem was not fixed and passed onto later models. The problem is called Bitumen, and scores of horrified consumers have posted their experiences with this noxious out-gassing material, which does not just "go away in time". One woman removed her children when she ran the dishwasher, another man said he would rather have a noisy dishwasher than a noiseless one that was trying to kill him. Is Bitumen dangerous to your health? I don't know, but I'm not going to be their guinea pig. HORRIBLE PRODUCT, and it does not seem limited to just one company. My old stainless steel dishwasher did not have all the bells and whistles, but I'd take it back in a second, if I could. My advice is: do your research, and if you have a problem, don't "wait it out for a few weeks, and see if the smell disappears" as one consumer was advised by customer service. Me, I'm going to re-examine the old-fashioned way of hand washing, until the companies remove the Bitumen, if they ever want to, or more likely, are forced to.

product_title: Bosch SHEM78W55N 24" 800 Series Built In Full Console Dishwasher with 6 Wash Cycles, in Stainless Steel
review_text:
The Bosch SHEM78W55N replaced a 9-year-old Whirlpool dishwasher that had developed an erratic motor and seemed too expensive to repair at its age. Here is my evaluation of the new Bosch after a month of use and several wash cycles. I usually run it every 2-3 days and lightly rinse dirty items before placing them in the dishwasher.

CONTROLS: One reason I chose this model was that its controls and status displays are clearly visible when a cycle is running. I suppose some folks prefer the esthetic simplicity of hidden controls, but I like to see what's happening at all times. The countdown clock showing remaining time in a cycle is especially useful. My only complaint is that the touchpad buttons don't always respond to a light touch and sometimes need an extra heavy poke.

LOADING: The Bosch's configuration of racks is quite different than my previous Whirlpool, which requires a new set of loading habits that I'm still developing. The third rack on top, which takes up very little interior room, is great for a lot of silverware, flat cooking utensils, and shallow bowls. The other two racks have variously spaced tines, some of which are adjustable. I'm not sure if they can hold quite as many glasses, cups, plates and bowls as the Whirlpool did, but with a little fussing I can squeeze in an adequate number. The one-piece silverware holder that sits on the right side of the lower rack is usually unnecessary due to the third rack on top, so I almost always remove it before running a load to make room for more plates or bowls.

NOISE: Amazingly quiet. The old Whirlpool was pretty low noise, but I'd hardly even know the Bosch is running if it weren't for the lights on the door.

CLEANING: Using the Automatic/Sanitize cycle with a Finish tab and liquid rinse agent, dishes, glasses, and silverware come out consistently clean and film-free.

DRYING: Although Bosch's lack of a metal heating element ring on the bottom of the interior is notorious for leaving dishes (especially plastic items) somewhat wet at the end of a cycle, I have not found it to be a major issue with this model. I use the Extra Dry cycle, which adds a few minutes and possibly hotter water at the end, as well as a liquid rinse agent. By opening the door after the cycle ends to let dishes cool for a few minutes, most dishes are dry when I'm ready to put them away, and the few plastic lids that have some residual water are no worse than I experienced with the Whirlpool.

CYCLE TIME: While my previous dishwasher typically took 3 - 3.5 hours for a normal cycle, the Bosch clocks in at 2.5 - 3 hours for the Automatic (dirt sensitive) cycle, even with the additional time for the Sanitize and Extra Dry options. I consider this pretty good for a high efficiency appliance.

ODOR: With my old Whirlpool, leaving a partial dirty load overnight rarely caused an odor problem. However, the Bosch seems a bit worse on occasion, which can be helped by running a Rinse cycle. I have not noticed the consistent strong odor that some Bosch reviews mention.

Overall, though this is not the least expensive model available, I'm generally pleased with the choice, and hope to get many years of trouble-free service from it.

review_text:
Shortly after purchasing the dishwasher, I noticed that the dishwasher left an invisible soapy detergent residue on all items after a normal wash cycle. I tried 3 other different kinds of dishwasher detergent, from tablet to liquid, but still the problem remained. I called customer service who seemed very annoyed to help, and trying to deflect blame on the water hardness in NYC, as if other dishwasher brands couldn't compensate either. I know for a fact that other neighbors in my building did not encounter this problem.

The other thing is with the model's condensation drying system, which is very high maintenance when running a dishwasher overnight. Again, the customer service representative seemed to scold customers as if scripted to make sure to unload dishwasher within an hour and half after wash.

These are characteristics from my experience (both the dishwasher mechanics and the customer support) that make the dishwasher and brand not only very expensive relative to value but also very untrustable and unreliable.

This Bosch washer has performed well for me for just over a year. I installed it myself without too much issue. It is very quiet as advertised.

I would say that it does sacrifice cleaning ability to stay quiet. It's not going to clean baked on/hardened foods without some pre-wash/scrubbing beforehand. The top silverware drawer is the same - spacing out the spoons and forks a bit is required.

review_text:
My Bosch worked perfectly for 3 1/2 years. It is super quiet. So quiet that they have a small red light that shines on the floor to show you it's running. It also cleans everything very well and I've not seen any food particles on the glassware and don't need any "shine" additives. Just what I wanted. (It was the model on recall but NOT in the range of serial numbers that had the problem.)

Cons: I guess that in order to make it so quiet they had to seal it well. They sealed it so well that it everything wet - silverware in particular. I've learned to leave the door open for a couple of hours when it finishes running and while everything is still steaming hot; otherwise, everything needs hand-towel drying.

The other problem is the plastic handle and the plastic button surround both cracked within the first month or so. For such a well-designed machine why they skimmed on this is beyond me.

The big problem: Yesterday it flooded the kitchen. It would not drain. It kept running, washing and rinsing, but without draining. If you weren't aware, the wash part of the cycle foams. Since it didn't drain, the following rinse bit just over foamed and created enough pressure that the foam oozed around the door seal along with the rinse water. (The drain filter was not plugged up, this is a failure either of the mechanical or electrical circuitry.)

Yes, you could say it looked funny, like in a frat house comedy, but then you didn't have to clean it up!

Called to have it repaired and the service manager made it sound like he's been there and done that too many times. He knew what parts to order seemingly without needing to look anything up. I'll find out in a week what this is going to cost. And, yes, I know a broken dishwasher is a first world problem but for the price I paid and only doing an average of 3 or 4 loads a week, this thing should have lasted much longer.

review_title: Consumers report consistent water pump failure and filter clog issues
review_text:
We purchased our Bosch dishwasher only 2 years ago for about $700 from a local appliance store (not Amazon) and it worked great...until it didn't. We loved the 3rd tray on top for silverware. There is no heating element in the bottom which is great so you can put anything anywhere and not have to worry about melting and fires. The water is so super hot, the dishes are usually completely dry at the end of the cycle and it's super quiet.
Then we started getting the E15 error message indicating there was water in the machine tray that wasn't draining out fast enough so the machine stops. Then the E22 error message indicating the filter was clogged. The appliance store sent a technician and $400 later we have a new water pump. Apparently the original one had a small crack/leak in it. I contacted Bosch, submitted the requested receipts and invoices but they offered no assistance or compensation. Their response was "the electronic components have a 5 year warranty, the pump has only a 1 year warranty, you should have purchased an extended warranty".
In the future we'll be going back to Kitchen Aid or Maytag for a fraction of the price and way more reliability and customer support.

Well, 9 months ago I purchase the previous model to this dishwasher and it was awesome, no issues - however then we had the 1000 year flood and it was the only appliance that got damaged.  Since the warrantee does not cover flood damage - quite understandable - I took it to get repaired on my dime and come to find out you can't get parts for it any longer.  In fact, my 8-month old dishwasher has been end-of-liffed and can't be repaired.  I am getting less and less excited about this awesome dishwasher due to logistical missteps by Bosch - a bit sad.  So now i am working to set up an appointment in two weeks to get someone to look at the dishwasher and try to figure out why i have a dud and hopefully fix it.

review_title: Make SURE this can replace your existing dishwasher!
review_text:
Bought this from the big box store after reading dishwasher reviews ad nauseam. I like the look, performance reviews, scooped handle/hidden controls, third shelf and most importantly - the quietness. Got a great deal that included free delivery and installation. Date arrived and when the delivery guys showed up, never took it off the truck, immediately took a look at our old dishwasher, the space it would be going and proceeded to tell us that we were hooked up for dishwashers that have the pipes and water supply coming from underneath the unit; Bosch hooks up on the backside. That was enough that they told us we would have to call the store again to solve the problem and they promptly left. I would have assumed that the unit could be adapted to fit, was even willing to help them out as I like to take care of problems around the house myself. But they simply said it wouldn't work, all Bosch's have a closed bottom (which results in the quietness) and that I would have to get a model that hooks up on the bottom.

I went to the store and spoke with the salesman in the large appliance dept. Despite his (supposed) 20+ years selling dishwashers, he had no idea what I was talking about with regards to a closed bottom dishwasher vs a open bottom dishwasher. Also said for large appliances, I should never buy online because "you don't know what you're getting."

Well long story short, after doing some quick research online, I found out Kitchenaid makes the type of dishwasher I needed and fortunately when I went back to the store to make an exchange, I found a better salesperson who knew what they were talking about and helped fix the problem. Was even able to find a Kitchenaid model with just as good reviews, same price and even free delivery/installation.

review_title: Doesn't dry plastic items. Doesn't rinse well. Manual clean filter.  Long cycle. NOT recommended.
review_text:
Our Bosch 300 does a good job of getting food off ceramic plates. But it has several serious issues we don't like:

1. It doesn't rinse well. I washed a pan I cooked bacon on, and at the end, the dishes had a greasy feeling. My wife washed a coffee grounds contained that she had emptied, and at the end there were coffee grounds on plates.

2. It dries ceramic plates ok, but it leaves plastic items dripping wet. We have to wait for them to dry to put them away.

3. A normal "Automatic" cycle takes 2:30. Pressing the "Half load" button cuts it to 2:00. That's a lot of washing to end up with greasy dishes.

4. If you don't use a rinse agent, it adds an extra 30 minutes to the total time. I don't like having chemicals in the final rinse, so I use water as the rinse agent. None the less, the plates often have a slippery feeling at the end like soap wasn't fully rinsed.

5. It has a filter that you have to kneel down to remove and clean. A replacement filter costs $20.

We regret buying a Bosch, and we won't make that mistake again.

review_title: TERRIBLE dishwasher, didn't work after 4 uses - DON'T BUY IT
review_text:
After using my brand new dishwasher for four times I noticed that the silverware in the cutlery tray was dirty. It's not just that it wasn't properly clean. It was dirty, greasy and you could even see the color of the food. (I don't think I put anything in the cutlery tray the first times I used the dishwasher). Some of the dishes in the lower tray (including a tall glass) are somewhat dirty too. I called Bosch customer care and was told that the dishwasher needs rinse aid in order to wash (so just adding dish washer detergent doesn't get you clean dishes) and that they will charge me for the work of the technician if lack of rinse aid is the problem. Note that the product information doesn't include that it only washes if rinse aid is added.
I'm now washing the same load of dishes now for a third time on a row in the hopes that it solves the problem but bottomline is (1) a dishwasher should be able to wash dishes only with adequate detergent, (2) if additional items are NEEDED for the dishwasher to wash this should be clearly stated as part of the description of the product, and (3) nothing excuses rude customer care that passes customers the burden for problems with brand new items.
In a subsequent call to BOSCH customer care I was told that the dishwasher should work without rinse aid. A technician came to check my unit and he said that this washer ONLY works with dishwasher tablets, even if that's not written anywhere and the guide that comes with the dishwasher says you can use liquid dishwasher. I still don't know if it'll work with those (he refused to try it and just left), but at any rate if this dishwasher ONLY works with these items, that information must be provided upfront so you decide if you want to buy it or not. I feel like I've been sold a car and later been told that the car only works if I wear a red shirt.
You can see in the picture what items look like AFTER THREE CONSECUTIVE WASH CYCLES!

review_text:
We absolutely love this dishwasher. It's amazingly quiet, and does a terrific job cleaning. One review had said that it was not quiet. When it is being installed, there is a foam/fabric blanket that fits around it. Do not let your installer remove that. It is the sound dampening material that makes it quiet. They scrape food into the trash, but aren't scrubbing. You have to put your ear to the outside front of the dishwasher to hear any sound at all. review_title: Quiet, but cannot get the basics right
review_text:
Yes, this dishwasher is quiet, but it falls short in so many other ways I have to give it 1 star. I cannot believe I paid almost $1000 for this; it is absolutely not worth it.

Yes it is quiet. I wanted a really quiet dishwasher, so I bought it. But it can’t get the basics right.

One reason it is quiet is because - I assume - that it doesn’t have the vent that many dishwasher have. This brings me to the first major pain with this dishwasher. If you don’t open the door and prop it open after a cycle the steam doesn’t dissipate and instead condensates on everything, leaving your dishes wet. It doesn’t matter how long you wait, if you don’t open the door after the cycle finishes you will come back hours later to wet dishes.

They could at least have worked round this fundamental flaw by alerting you when the dishwasher has finished, but this has been botched too. When the cycle completes, it makes a few quiet beeps, and then goes silent. These should quietly repeat periodically for a couple of hours until you open or turn it off. It’s way too easy to miss the existing beep.

They boast that the dishwasher also has an “InfoLight”. Apparently this is a registered trademark. Did they also patent this? I really hope not. It’s garbage. The light shines when the dishwasher is on. Once the dishwasher is finished, the light goes off. So, given that I usually use a 1.5 hour cycle, for 22.5 hours per day, the light is off. Off means one of two things: the dishwasher has finished a cycle, or the dishwasher is off. If you don’t hear the finishing beeps, the light being off sure isn’t going to remind you to open the dishwasher. And remember that if you don’t open it immediately, you end up with wet dishes. This light could actually be useful if it turned GREEN and stayed on until you open it or turn it off.

The only other thing the InfoLight does is flash if you open the dishwasher mid-cycle. If you close it again it will flash to alert you that you need to turn it back on. This is meant to be helpful, but what would be a LOT more helpful is to do what literally EVERY other dishwasher I’ve ever used is to automatically start up again once you close the door. Instead, for some inexplicable reason you have to press the resume button to resume. WHY?

Finally, if you do open it midcycle or forget to turn it off after the cycle completes and have the door open in the horizontal position, the slightest brush of your clothing against the touch-sensitive buttons will activate them. This can change the cycle or some how screw up the mid cycle so that even if you do press resume and then close the door the red light will mysteriously continue to flash.

With a few small software changes this dishwasher could be better. But I’m stuck with this expensive machine now. I really really wish I hadn’t bought it. DO NOT BUY!

review_text:

This was a lot of money for us but we missed having a double oven over the holidays.

Things I like about this single/double: it fits in the cabinet space perfectly where our previous GE single oven was. It was pretty easy to install, although it is much heavier than a single oven. It looks really nice and it works well - cooks evenly. It is nice to have 2 spaces for cooking since there is no substitute for that. We do try to use the top oven as much as possible; I'm assuming it uses less energy to do that, but I don't really know for sure.

Things I don't like: The racks, for several reasons. Yes, you can cook a turkey which was great, but you cannot pull out the rack when it is at the bottom level. So for basting, etc, it was difficult. It can only come out a couple inches before it hits the door. The other thing I really don't like is you cannot switch the racks between the top and bottom oven. So, when you take out the glide rack (which is not as nice as some glide racks) to cook a turkey or angel food cake or roast, you have to find somewhere else to put it because it is narrower than the top oven. And, because it's a glide rack I often cannot keep it together while moving it (my problem). Also, you have to type in the temperature when you hit "bake" (it does not default to 350 like most ovens; perhaps some prefer this, but I don't) and it times out very quickly if you don't type something.

The fan runs from the moment you turn on the oven, but it also turns off almost immediately after you are done using it. My old oven turned on the fan after you turned off the oven. This probably needs to happen because the oven fills the entire cabinet space and so I would rather have it be safe. You can hear the fan, but it is not terrible.

If I had it to do over, I would probably spring for a double oven and spend the money to rework my cabinets. I had only seen the single-double ovens in person in a range as no one but GE carries this product yet and I haven't seen it in any stores near me. I had assumed it would be about the same as the range ones, but had I read things more carefully, I would have realized that both these ovens in the built-in are smaller than the single-double range ovens.

My recommendation: If can create the space, get a double oven. If you cannot, this is a fantastic way to have 2 ovens in a small space.

product_title: GE PT9200SLSS Electric Double Wall Oven
review_text:
The home we purchased three years ago came with an ancient single wall oven and a built-in microwave, leaving us with few options to upgrade to the double oven of my dreams. The GE Profile PT9200SLSS seemed like a great compromise - a double oven in the space of a single. Although we couldn't find a floor model anywhere, we decided to buy it after reading the great reviews for this model and the previous version.

So far I have been thrilled with its features and performance. The top oven preheats very quickly and is perfect for many of the items I bake - pork chops, cookies, biscuits, etc. We've enjoyed the pizza settings on the upper oven and convection bake on the lower oven. I've slow cooked roasts in the lower oven that are amazingly tender and delicious. The whole chicken I roasted on the convection setting with the probe was cooked perfectly.

The biggest question we and many others have had is whether the Thanksgiving turkey will fit inside. The 19 pound bird we have does not fit in my Calaphon roasting pan with V-rack, but as you can see from the attached picture, the turkey does fit (with room to spare) using a disposable aluminum roasting pan. We have a smaller turkey - 13 pounds - that fits in the roasting pan on that V-rack nicely.

There are a few cons to the oven, mostly that the rack in the top oven does not come out far without hitting the door, so getting dishes in and out can be a bit tricky compared to a full-size oven. This is a minor quibble, and certainly doesn't outweigh the incredible convenience of having two ovens. I am so thrilled to be able to roast a turkey and bake my pies, rolls, and other holiday side dishes. The only other con is that modern ovens are smaller than old ovens, so we had to have a filler strip custom made to cover the gap in our cabinet. However, we would have had that problem with any new oven.

For anyone who wants the versatility of a double oven without having to do a kitchen remodel, I can't recommend this oven enough.

The functions it will perform work perfectly from probe cooking to slow cooking to the warming function and many more. I will agree with another reviewer about the racks not being interchangeable between the top and bottom oven. It would have been better to have that design. I have taken the easy slide out rack and just put it away. I don't see where it's needed IMO. If i'm cooking 2 racks of cookies or something like that then i'd put it back in.

the lower oven is big enough for thanksgiving and the upper oven is great for pizza and it's warming functions to keep dishes warm before serving. It all just works for me and i have nothing but praise about 'how' it operates. The one thing I wish would be different was more contrast on the touch screen labels so they stand out better to read in low light.

the ovens are easy to keep clean and they hold temperature consistently. Convection baking and roasting and probe cooking are spot on for me. I get consistent results time after time with this oven on baked goods and breads as well as roast and slow cooked ribs and brisket.

It's terrific IMO.

If you put in even a tiny amount of HE soap or softener more than recommended, the machine will leak, setting off an LC1 or LC2 error code. The tech did nothing to correct the problem, which was caused by dried up soap and softener in the upper and lower filling cups. I will replace them with what has worked for us for nearly 20 years without a problem - a Maytag top loader and matching dryer.

product_title: Samsung White Front Load Steam Washer
review_text:
After about a year, the cycle times started getting longer and longer. When you start the load it tells you how long the cycle should take, about an hour. SO I would set an alarm on my cell phone for whatever time was on the washer. All went well for about a year. Then upon returning to change the load, there would still be 10 minutes left on the timer. Next week, there would be 25 minutes. Soon, a load was taking over two and a half hours. SO I watched what was happening. It would try to spin and it would go off center, stop, go slowly for a minute, back and forth, then try to spin again, and go off balance. I tried opening it up and rearranging the clothes inside. Same result. I tried it with an empty machine. Still same routine. SO I called in a certified repairman. He couldn't figure out how to fix it. I paid him. I called in another professional repairman. After an hour of diagnosis, he said he would have to research the problem. Got a call. He said that there are two fluid containing ballast weights on the front of the machine that had probably leaked and would have to be replaced. Estimate, $500. Bad thing was that he wouldn't guarantee it because it was a design flaw. The same thing would probably happen again. He recommended that I scrap the machine. So I lose the purchase price. I lost the cost of two repair visits, over $200. and I've been without a washer for over a month while we tried to diagnose the problem.

Called Samsung. They refused to do anything because the washer is more than 12 months old.

review_title: Caution - Does NOT have a regular bake feature.
review_text:
We purchased this oven because it has both convection and conventional bake settings -- or so we thought. It turns out that the 'regular' bake is convection as well (using circulating air and the convection fan to heat the oven) and requires the exact same adjustments to recipes. Yes, we've read the manual. Yes, we've talked to Samsung. Yes, we've had it looked at. Turns out that's what it's /supposed/ to do, and, silly us, it's our fault for not adjusting all our family recipes, including the ones that will /never/ work under convection, to their super-special not-so-conventional 'regular bake' setting. Oh, and regular broil isn't really regular broil, either. It's... wait for it... convection.

Since it's our fault for not appreciating the change, and the unit is working the way they designed it, we're out of luck -- a near-new expensive appliance that is a total financial loss. We really have no choice but to re-buy a different one if we want a functional oven in our kitchen.

If you like using convection-baking only, this might be a great appliance for you. But if you want an oven that actually has settings other than convection-bake, run, don't walk, away from this one.

product_title: Samsung NZ30K7880UG Cooktop
review_title: We've owned this model for more than a year
review_text:
I did not buy this cooktop from Amazon but I rely on these reviews so heavily that I wanted to weigh in with my own experience (so far) with this exact model of appliance. When I bought this a year and a half ago, there were only two companies that made models like this. This cooktop offered more options for versatility. There were few reviews out there about Samsung's model but we bought it with some apprehension. I'm going to try to address all of the questions we had initially but couldn't find mentioned in reviews.

My husband and I are both glad we got it. Note - it DOES take a bit of time to get adjusted to it but the perks are so significant that we'd do it again...so far. It hasn't given us any of the problems others have complained about. The controls are easy to use, just different from what you're used to. We don't use the magnet knob...we just gently tap the control spot and it adjusts up or down, tap again to fine tune it. You can also adjust it with just a finger gently rubbing the circle of the control. It doesn't need a hard touch, in fact, it works better without a firm touch. It's like the touch screen on your smart phone. I'm glad to be done with the knobs that take up space or gather gunk under them.

I love the rectangular units to the left that sense the right number of spaces to activate. I have an oval enameled iron dutch oven that uses three of the spaces. I'm able to adjust the spaces so that I can use it as a slow cooker. You can put a pot on each of the four spaces if you need - they will individually work. The fast heat is amazing - the water boils faster than my hot pot. One thing that is either good or bad, depending on how you feel about it...when the pot boils over, the burner automatically turns off and with that, the contents of your pot immediately stop boiling. It's not like the other electric stove - it's more like a gas stove in this way. You are not likely to make such a mess. Nothing gets cooked on it as the burners don't get as hot as other types of units. It's the pots that get hot. The glass does get very, very warm but not enough so that you'd blister if you accidentally touched it or ruin it if you spilt sugar on it.

With the controls, I have discovered a greater range of temperatures with this cooktop - the low is cooler and the high is hotter. I find I've had to be careful of the temps I choose as I can easily burn food. I don't cook things on the same temp as I used to, I choose a cooler setting. Until you get used to it, start cool, slowly adjust up, then stay with it for a minute.

The burners are just as flexible as a gas stove without the sticky, smelly gunk build up from a gas unit. It also won't set your kitchen or hair on fire. I was watching a friend with a gas stove cleaning her top...way more trouble than this. The induction is VERY easy to clean...soap and water with a microfiber cloth dry. Again, things don't get burned onto the glass.

I have a little 3 yr.old with fingers that explore. You can lock the cooktop on or off. If the lock isn't on and she touches the control, a burner doesn't begin to heat if a pot isn't on the burner. If the burner doesn't sense the pot, it turns itself off without heating. This is so much safer than gas!

The pots are not hard to find nor terribly expensive. C05TC0 carries a very nice set and they frequently go on sale. Enameled cast iron works great on them. Cast iron works, too, but I'm a bit hesitant to use it as it might scratch the glass. Oh, by the way...be cautious of sugar or salt being left on the glass and then putting a pot on it and sliding it - the crystals will scratch. This is the same as the electric cooktop we used to have. A friend of mine had a glass top a number of years ago, scratched it and it cracked. I leave a microfiber cloth near the stove and wipe it off occasionally. Again, it just stays clean sooo easily!!

So far, I'd do it again. I simply can't see any advantages to other types of stoves. Over the years, I've owned and used so many stoves: the old ring elements, gas, glass cook top and I really enjoy cooking on a wood stove during the winter. This is my preferred way to cook in the kitchen. The only down side we see with this is that this cooktop requires a Samsung specialist with parts from the parent company. I'll update this if we have problems.

An update-
One of my fears of getting this cook top was that I wouldn't be able to can my garden bounty any longer. Well, I've just been very successfully canning on this Samsung induction. I used a hot water canner that is found on Amazon. (Key words: Stainless Steel Multi-Use Canner Victor.) The main thing is to be careful to not drag the canner across the glass, thereby scratching the glass. This is tricky as the canner is heavy. I took a clean terry cloth dish towel, placed it very close to the boiling canner and pulled the canner up onto the towel. I love, love, love that I can get a towel so close to the burner!!

I'm noticing I'm mentioning scratching the glass a lot. Huh...actually, while cooking - or otherwise - I don't pay that much attention to scratching. It's not THAT big a deal. I would definitely get this again if I had do overs.

Year 2: Still love it, still prefer it, still looking nice, still working fine with no problems. I'd buy it again with no qualms.

product_title: Samsung NZ30K7880UG Cooktop
review_title: If you really want to be a beta tester...
review_text:
Short review: Don't.

Longer review:
You might be tempted to see all of the negative comments about quality control and failure rate on this cooktop and think "sure, but I bet I'll be fine." That's what I was hoping for. Unfortunately, you might get one free of defects, but you won't get one free of design flaws.

"Flex Zone" double burner on the left side was broken right out of the box. The sensor that tells it a pan is there is defective, straight from the factory.

The outer ring in the large burner doesn't work, and again, never worked. So if I want to cook something on the innermost 6" of my great big 12" cast iron braiser, things are great. For even heat across the whole pan, not so much. Nothing at all.

But here's the thing: even if everything worked as designed, it was designed to be an admittedly beautiful movie prop and not a functional home appliance. If you get ANY water, oil, or food on the top, the touch "buttons" freak out completely. I've dripped condensation and turned a burner from 13 down to 2, turned a burner off, turned the entire stove off... Imagine trying to use your phone with water drops on the screen, and you kind of have the idea. But hey, Samsung has your back! There's a single magnetic knob that you can control any one burner with in case your hands are wet or the surface has stuff on it! Looks cool, sounds cool, makes for a nice looking kitchen in a movie... does NOT work. The most I can say is that if you rotate it clockwise, the odds are better (like, 70%?) that the temperature will go up than that it'll go down. As far as HOW MUCH it moves, or what speed, or whether anything at all will actually happen? Find some kitchen deity to pray to and see what you get.

If you're staging your house so it looks cool, and you're about to sell it and move, AND you're a bit of a misanthrope... actually, just save money and get an actual prop.

It's on its way back, and whether it's just an outlier/lemon or not, we'll never know, because we're buying something else.

product_title: Whirlpool WDTA50SAHZ Built-In Fully Integrated Stainless Steel Dishwasher WDTA50SAHZ
review_text:
Really nice dishwasher! We chose this model (WDTA50 series) because we found all the features we were looking for:

1. Silverware basket can be hung on the door. We like this---it saves lots of space in the
lower rack. Some don’t like it, but you can place it in the lower rack if you want.
2. Quality. This one felt like it was built better than others in this price range.
3. Pocket handle and a nice, clean appearance (ours is white).
4. Positive reviews from users, especially regarding drying performance.
5. Reliability. Whirlpool has the best reliability record and is built in the USA. We loved our
old Whirlpool.
6. Tall tub and nylon rack, with a simple internal design. We don’t need folding rack tines or
special compartments. We removed the stemware holders.
7. Heated dry.
8. “Middle-tier” in terms of product line. I’d judge this one as near the top of its class.

We are happy with our purchase (and did a lot of comparison shopping). After 60 days, these things stand out:

Positives
• Gets dishes sparkling clean, especially Sensor Wash cycle. No re-deposit issues with Sensor Cycle. Best results seem to be with Cascade pods (as recommended by Whirlpool). If dishes are coming out of this machine dirty you’re doing something wrong or have a lemon.
• It is very quiet. And we like the tiny blue – red – white light that signals its operation.
• Rack design is better than our last dishwasher (which we liked). It seems to hold more dishes and is easier to load.
• Control panel on top is easy to use and very easy to clean.
• We think this machine performs better and is nicer to use than a friend’s Kitchen Aid that cost almost 3x as much.

Negatives
• 1-Hour Wash cycle leaves some re-deposit, even though we rinse dishes. I doubt we’ll use it to wash dishes unless the load is small and only needs a light wash. Maybe as a rinse-hold cycle (with no dry) but it uses more water than a regular wash.

• Whirlpool changed the size of the slots for silverware in the basket from earlier models. The front row slots are now too narrow for our dinner forks. Annoying, but we just put them in the 2nd row, which works.

• Regular dry leaves too much water in places like behind the silverware basket. Extended dry helps. Dishes are plenty dry but there is water on the walls. Expect to wipe out small amounts of water in the cupped bottoms of some items, which is common in most dishwashers.

Finally, I don’t understand negative reviews from people who purchase machine with visible features (silver basket, folding racks, etc) that they don’t like. Do homework beforehand, and go look at machines at a store, or do some online research. Buy one with the features you WANT and you’ll likely be happier with it. We are happy with this machine largely because it has features we were looking for. We checked them out in the showrooms of local stores.

By 6/2021, excessive water on interior after cycle ended; 1st warranty guy said it was because I have a water softener and should not be using rinse aid (softener installed 2002 & never a problem).  He also said I should try other brands of detergent.  He also said it might be the tankless water heater.  Water heater serviced: no problems, working perfect.  12/2021 after using every brand available, interior and dishes were completely wet, even 4 hrs after cycle ended.  1/2022 2nd warranty call, different company sent out.  He said I have extremely hard water and should only use liquid detergent (only 1/2 amount in tray) and must use rinse aid.  He said I should have softener serviced since it appeared to not be working.  While waiting for service, I added rinse aid; should have helped since people without softener have hard water.  Softener filter changed, but no problem found with softener.  He had a Whirlpool like mine and said he had same problem; it was a bad pump not draining properly.  I've spent $400 on unnecessary service calls for water heater and softener and dishwasher still doesn't work right.  So, I have 10 months left on extended warranty and I'm calling again!  I see this model is discontinued.  Wish I had my old black dishwasher back since it was working fine at 10 yrs old!  Won't be buying Whirlpool again ever.

review_text:
I purchased this from another retailer but wanted to post somewhere regarding additional items needed for the installation. You will need

1. A 14 gauge replacement power cord. The manual does not recommend using the standard 16 gauge dishwasher power cords carried by Lowe's/Home Depot. I suggest ordering ahead. https://www.amazon.com/AWG-Replacement-Power-Cord-Open/dp/B082FMNR8T/

2. 3/8 electrical connector like this one - https://www.amazon.com/Sigma-Electric-CECOMINOD032747-Cable-Connector/dp/B004ITFA0Y If you go to home depot you can get just a pack of 2

3. You will need this also - https://www.amazon.com/Kelaro-Universal-Dishwasher-Compression-Connections/dp/B07WZRW5ZS/

4. Four-6 wood screws to mount the power junction box (i think that's what they call it) and a plastic part to mount the drain hose in your cabinet. You can find details in the install manual

I highly recommend downloading the installation manual ahead of time so you are sure you have everything you need ahead of time, including the parts, etc.

Installation tip. the power junction box goes underneath your sink not behind the dishwasher. Loosen the leg adjustment at the front of the dishwasher and adjust as best you can before pushing it into position. Otherwise they will be a pain to adjust. They are a pain to adjust anyways, it's a plastic leg that is very difficult to move, bad design for such an expensive piece of hardware.

review_text: This Gold Series Whirlpool dishwasher was the "builders' special" that came with the condo bought in 2012. I didn't expect much, since I'd previously gone with high-end brands like Kitchen Aid. This was also the first "Energy Star" dishwasher I had. However I've been pleasantly surprised with Its performance: It gets the dishes cleaner than any dishwasher I've had (I've had 10 over the years) and is as nearly perfect as it could  be. It is relatively quiet, and has to be, because my kitchen is part if the condo's great room. On the down side, it takes over two hours on the "normal" and "sensor" settings. It does have a one hour cycle that I don't use. It does not have a "rinse and hold" feature, and does not need one--I never rinse dishes beforehand, I only scrape. Also, I should note that it gets light duty, as I run it  about 3 times a week.  Bottom line, after 4 years, the best dishwasher I've had over the last 56 years.

review_text: We have always had Whirlpool kitchen appliances and this dishwasher replaced a 19 year old dishwasher that still worked because I wanted to switch to stainless appliances.  They definitely don't make them like they used to!  Based on features, this one looked like an upgrade to what we had before.  The first few months I loved our new dishwasher.  It was super quiet and the dishes were clean.  It was much easier to load than the old one that had a cone shaped plastic piece in the middle of the bottom  tray.  Even on the extra drying cycle, the dishes still come out wet but I can deal with that.  However, after the fully loaded bottom rack came off the tracks for about the fifth time and I had to wrestle with the weight of it to get  back on the track, it started to bother me.  The plastic parts are so much thinner and cheaper than the old versions.  The silverware holder just rests on two little pegs on the outside of the bottom rack so it often  comes loose and bumps the button that dumps the  clean  silverware all over the floor as you are trying to lift it out.  Also, the plastic pegs that separate the plates on  the bottom rack are too short.  So, if you put dinner plates in, they stand up straight until you move the rack and then they all fall over about 30 degrees and hit the plate next to it.  The dishwasher had a 12 month warranty and at close to 15 months, the motor gave out.  I called Whirlpool and they did come out and replace the motor under the warranty so I added a star for that since they stood behind the product.

review_text:
I recently had this gas-on-glass unit installed. I was hoping to avoid the difficulty of keeping a stainless unit clean, we have had gas-on-glass before, so we wanted to get it again. In the pictures, it looks great. We could not find it in any store, so we bought it sight unseen. It's a GE -- what could go wrong?

Unfortunately, there are some problems that are not evident in the pictures. The knobs are light, cheap plastic and are not heavy and solid like I had hoped. There is one middle grate that is hefty and solid, but the two other side grates are thinner. It does look nice once you clean and windex it, but it is starting to develop spots that I cannot seem to get off (and it has only been a few weeks). This is even though I am diligent about cleaning it promptly.

There is also a safety concern. When you turn the unit on, it clicks until it lights. Once it lights, you adjust the flame and are good to go. Well, one time I turned the knob to ignite, but apparently it did not ignite but the gas kept coming out. I could not see this because of the large pan that blocked my view of the flame. After a few seconds I noticed that it had not ignited and adjusted the knob to get it to light. The spark ignited the gas and flames shot out toward me. Had I not noticed the ignition failure quickly, I wonder if a bigger gas cloud would have ignited. I do not recall this ever happening with my prior gas cooktop. So I now have a cooktop that has plastic knobs that might someday injure someone because of the ignition mechanism. If I had it to do over, I would buy something else.

review_title: Induction is the way to go.
review_text:
We have had this induction range for 4 months now,a nd it has exceeded all expectations. I have always used a gas range, but when we bought a house with a 25 year old electric, we had to replace it. I planned on gas again, but after doing some research, decided to go with the induction range. The GE PHS930 is a great buy. It heats so much faster than gas, and doesn't heat up the kitchen. The multiple levels of power allow a pot to simmer very easily. The response when you change the heat level is immediate. The oven is solid with easily movable racks, and the convection oven makes for a very even heat throughout. I have seen people complain about noise when the burners are on, but that certainly is not the case with mine. The best thing is the cleanup is a breeze, because nothing burns onto the glass, and it is entirely smooth. We were warned by friends that the glass top will scratch, but that has not been the case at all. The only downside is that most of our pans did not work, but fortunately, they had a special where they included an entire set of Chantel pots and pans with the purchase, and they are very high quality. If you are considering induction, I highly recommend an induction range. I can't speak about other brands, but this one has far exceeded our expectations. I will never go back to gas or electric again.

Edit: We have had this range for 3 years now, and everything is still great. Works great and not a single scratch on the surface. It still looks brand new, and we cook on it multiple times a day.

review_title: GE PHS930SLSS 30 Inch Slide-in INDUCTION Electric Range
review_text:
Never owned or cooked on an Induction Range before. However, as an electrical engineer I fully understand the benefits of it. Efficient, evenly distributed heat that allows cooking where the whole bottom of the pan is heated to the same temperature.

We had a gas range before and this induction range blows GAS and resistive elements out of the water..

Major problem with GAS is hot spots in the pans, danger when Flambéing and if you are cooking 1 piece of fish you’re ok with gas but try to cook 3 or 4 and have all of them come out with same golden crust? Well that is not possible with gas.

However, with Induction cook top it was so easy, no moving the fish around in the pan to get that even crust, just let it sit where it lands because it's is the same temperature everywhere.

Boil overs, Okay, so we were kind of worried about how flat the top of this range was. I finally experience my first boil over doing a celery root puree for salmon. This puree requires equal parts milk and water and I put the lid on without thinking first and of course boil over. I was panicked for a moment running to the other side of the kitchen to get paper towels and upon my return I was pleasantly surprised to find both the left and right edges of the of the stove top have a inclination right along the edge so fluids don't dribble down the sides of your stove! GREAT!!! THANK YOU GE!!

Boils water almost as fast as my microwave within 30 seconds or so with 1 cup of water in/on each. In fact I make my own stocks, beef and chicken. There is NO better way than with an induction cook top, reason? Simple, the induction cook top puts out as electric field that not only encompasses the entire bottom of the pans and beyond, but partially up the sides,(a few inches), of the pan as well. 30 Qt boiled fast because of the XTRA heated surface area that induction brings to the game.

Instant heat, like a gas burner only without the danger or hot spots in pans, you don't have to stir or move food around as much when doing a saute.

Easy to clean, unlike our gas stove which would take 60 minutes at least and if you had a boil over even longer! We cook right on those Silpat's they are silicone baking pats for small personal pizza's and work great for keeping the induction element area's clean, unscratched and the bottom of your pans like new.

UI - User Interface intuitive and easy, didn't even need to pull out the manual to set the clock!

1 Con - GE put a warming spot in the back center that uses a standard heat element i.e. resistive element not inductive bad idea, if you have a paper towel or something else down to keep the glass nice and clean around the inductive elements then it could melt or catch fire. So we don't use it ever, if it were inductive we would use it and love it.

We will never go back to resistive or gas range again!

review_title: this stove WILL NOT FIT in a 30" opening
review_text:
Do not buy this stove unless your stove opening is wider than 30"...

Full disclosure: I bought this stove at Lowes in March, 2019. However, based on my experiences below, I'm pretty sure all these stoves have the same defect), and I'm putting this on all the sites that carry it so everyone will be aware of my experiences...

The short version:
The bottom of the stove is WIDER than 30" at the bottom (more like 30-1/8"), so it WILL NOT FIT in a standard 30" opening.

The longer version:
This was confirmed on the original stove I purchased, a replacement stove that was delivered to me, AND a display model at a local Best Buy (none on display at Lowes). All stoves have the same visible "flare" at the bottom: 29-7/8" at the top, and +/- 30-1/8" at the bottom where the drawer is. This may not seem like a big deal, but it means that if your stove opening is constructed to be exactly 30" (e.g. Per GE's written installation instructions and most kitchens), the stove won't slide in all the way. In my case (brand new kitchen, opening made based on GE's instructions), there is a 3" gap between the back of the stove and the edge of the countertop - pushing it back farther would have damaged the cabinets and (likely) the stove, not to mention I'd never be able to get it out again.

The Lowes and Best Buy associates I worked with on this have informed me that the will no longer recommend this product based on this information.

After a month of "back and forth" with GE customer service (my experience was better than some other reviews on here), they are buying back my stove because they cannot guarantee the a third replacement stove won't have the same defect.

The other features on the stove are OK (the touchscreen controls are a little hard to deal with - they only work about 80% of the time with my wife's fingertips and the oven is slower to preheat than other stoves I've had). One good thing is if you're OK with damaging your old cabinets to cram it in, GE does offer an up to $300 "fit guarantee" for your efforts (only applies when you're replacing a stove in an existing kitchen, not putting a new stove in a new kitchen)...

consider yourself warned...
