review_title: I love this stove--when it works.......
review_text:
I purchased this GE profile induction stove early in 2016 From Sears appliances. It worked great for the first 18 months or so. Induction cooking is great--heat controlled, easy to clean, fast--I don't think I could go back to gas (using the smoke detector for a cooking timer) or regular electric (waiting for the unit to finally heat up, then cleaning all the unit pans from the boil-overs and grease splatters that inevitably happen). BUT, after the first 18 months, this stove has been on about a 3-day work week--it cannot be depended upon to work on any given day or time. It intermittently shuts itself off and refuses to work, then a day or two later will magically agree to come to work for no apparent reason whatsoever. Just try to invite friends to dinner and the stove will go on vacation. Christmas dinner was an adventure.

The circuit breaker for the stove has become my best friend. Sometimes, I can turn off the breaker for a minute or two, and the stove will work. Sometimes I get error code FA92. Thank goodness I purchased an extended warranty, because the repair folks have replaced the big "motherboard" that makes the whole thing work twice, replaced the fan once, and the components for the big stove top unit is coming in a couple weeks. There was another repair for the panel under the touch panel. I'm sure the cost of these repairs (under my extended warranty) cost more than the stove in the first place, so if you buy one of these, be sure to get the warranty!

So in a nutshell, I really like induction cooking. Its clean, safe, and controllable. The downside is that it is a giant computer and if one thing shuts down, the whole stove is dead (except sometimes the oven will work---sometimes) Repair people can only replace components, not really track down problems other than looking up the error code and hope they guessed right.

I am hoping that my stove is just a lemon, and that other stoves, even of the same model, work flawlessly for years, because my next stove (and I don't think this one will ever get fixed) will also be an induction stove.

product_title: GE PHS930SLSS Smoothtop Cooktop
review_text:
We have had the PHS930SLSS GE Profile induction range about 6 months, and are generally very pleased with it. We finally took the plunge into induction cooking, and don't regret it a bit--much happier with it than with the glass top range it replaced.

Of course, you need induction-ready pans, but one thing we didn't realize is that all induction-ready pans are not alike! We noticed that some pans-usually lighter ones--heated up a lot faster than others, so I did a little experiment and found that to boil 16 oz of water took between 1.5 and 4.5 minutes. The fastest times were pricey, quality stainless-clad pans and the slowest were light, inexpensive pans from that Swedish household goods superstore. They work, but just are not as efficient or responsive. I'm assuming that it has to do with the amount of iron or steel in the bottom of the pan.

Here are the Pros for this range:
--Easy to clean top. Because it doesn't get nearly as hot as a radiant glass-top range, all that scraping and scrubbing is gone! Ten times easier to clean than any other range we've owned.
--Stylish, modern design. It's a beautiful appliance.
--Interface of the control panel is excellent. Very intuitive and quick and easy to set.
--Good convection oven. The temperature differential (called "Auto Conversion" in the manual) between convection (usually 25° lower than non-convection) can be adjusted or eliminated. I turned off the Auto Conversion and the baking times are more realistic. Baking is even, and preheating is not terribly fast but not a problem either.
--The Warming Zone, the middle back "burner," works well. It is thermal, not induction.
--Proofing feature of the oven is handy for bread making.
--The oven probe works well on cooking meats and is easy to set up.
--Visibility into the oven is good.
--Range has internet connectivity, but we do not see a need to turn the oven on or off and set the temperature remotely. A solution looking for a problem. Also, GE asks for a lot of personal information to use the app.

Cons:
--The beeps of the timer and oven preheat are way too soft. Even set at the loudest setting, they can be inaudible.
--The broiler requires that the oven door be closed. Many cooks like to have the door open a bit to broil.
--The glass control panel gets messy because of splatter, and must be turned off in order to wipe it clean...otherwise, the cleaning cloth activates the various controls. Not a big issue, but an inconvenience.
--The oven light stays on forever. I much prefer a time-out on the light after an adjustable time so you don't find the light on the next morning.
--The "soft close" drawer under the oven required some adjustment when we got the range, and it only works when the drawer is within an inch of closing. Just as easy to close it all the way yourself.
--Very few accessories are available. GE only offers broiler pans and more wire oven racks. I would love to see optional deluxe oven racks that have drawer-slide mechanisms which pull all the way out without tilting and maybe spilling oven contents. Many higher-end ranges have these, and I would like GE to offer these as an optional accessory.
--There is a slight hotspot in the middle of each induction burner. This may be the case with all induction ranges, but the evenness of the cooking area could be better. This is mitigated by a quality pan which evens out the heat across the surface of the pan.
--No printed manual. Come on, GE...this kind of money for an appliance and no printed manual?

Even with these cons, it's the best range we've ever owned.

review_title: After a solid decade of service, we decided to ...
review_text:
After a solid decade of service, we decided to replace our slide-in GE Profile range with a Café series model.

Pros:
- Oven heats up more quickly than previous ones
- More burners than the Profile that we replaced
- Burners are higher-output, and the dual-ring high output burner has a smaller flame ring, so you can turn it on full blast on slightly smaller pots and pans
- Installation was a cinch
- Includes a cast-iron griddle for use over the middle two burners

Cons:
- The range is a little bit deeper than the old GE Profile I replaced by about an inch and a half. While it fit in perfectly width-wise into the counter's cutout, it sticks out a bit more than the older range.
- The warming drawer is smaller than the storage drawer on the GE Profile.
- Cleaning the cooktop is a bit trickier with this range -- the old Profiles had a glassy ceramic top which you could scour with your usual ceramic cleaner and use a razor blade for super-stuck on stuff. This one is all metal, and there are no removable trays which you can replace. Warm soapy washcloths and stainless steel cleaner are your friends.

Indifferent:
- WiFi/Bluetooth (do I really need the ability to preheat my oven while sitting on the couch? Is it a selling point that I don't have to reach up to press a button to turn on my range hood when turning on the stove?)
- The Café series is definitely a "musical" range in terms of the sounds it makes to let you know your oven is pre-heated, or your timed bake is over, etc. A definite change from the single kind of "beep beep" the Profile made.

review_title: Good features, good design, good quality
review_text:
I like this unit. It is attractive and after a month of use I find it well designed. I learned the hard way there are several key features in this kind of range (dodged a bullet with the purchase and then before-15-day return of the Jenn-Air version).

The front panel must be more or less vertical, not horizontal or you can't see the clock from across the room, it gets covered in cooking grease and the knobs get uncomfortably hot to touch when the front burners are used. Check.

The griddle must have sufficient burner power or it is semi-useless and this unit has the best solution of any in its price range with a total of 6 useful burners rather than the more standard 4 useful and 1 oddly shaped useless one. Check.

I did not give it 5 stars for two reasons.

The first is that while the stock griddle is a wonderfully solid chuck of cast iron it comes with a surface so rough it would take years to season, so I had to spend an entire morning grinding it smooth with a power sander.

Second, and this is a problem with the entire market of these kinds of ranges, the cooling fan (not the convection fan) is very loud, on the order of 75 decibels. I got the level down to a more ignorable 70 db by taking the back sheet metal off, installing sound deadener on the fan shroud and replacing the sheet metal while ensuring it was tensioned against itself. Further quieting could be achieved by a little more careful engineering of the intake surfaces. I feel like for $3000 GE should have done this engineering (and ground down the griddle) for me.

After three months of owning the GE Café Dual Range we have multiple problems with it. First, the tri-ring 21000 BTU burner stopped working properly. When turned on, the flame would only come out of half the burner. Secondly, the ignitor on the two middle burners started attempting to ignite even though they when not in use. I confirmed the burners were in the off position, and yet the burners were attempting to ignite. This is a particularly concerning and dangerous malfunction for a gas stove. review_title: Don’t Waste Your Money and this is not the 500 Series.
review_text:
First off I would like to say part of my disappointment is that when I was searching for what I wanted on amazon I searched specifally for this product line BUT the 500 series not the 300 which is what I got. When it’s the first things that comes up and NOTHING else about the ad itself tells you that your looking at the 300 and not the 500 it’s very hard to know. I even expanded the pics that were available but when you bring them up large enough to see the words and numbers it for to blurry to read. I feel like maybe this was a little intentionally deceptive on the sellers part and I should’ve done more research.
Bottom line these pair is an expensive disappointment. Washer claims to be a high capacity yet low profile machine that can hold up to 16 lbs of dry clothing. I challenge you to try to get that much into this washer without stuffing things so tightly they don’t get clean. The washer however otherwise works fine. It runs quietly and cleans just as well as you would expect at this price point and for a Bosch product.
The dryer....ugh what can I say that’s positive? Not a lot sadly. If you’ve watched any of the YouTube videos featuring the 300 series then you already know where I’m headed and why I was trying to avoid purchasing this in the first place. The dryer basically has two filter/lint trap areas that you need to be concerned with. The first is the typical in dryer type that you take out and clean after every use, no harm no foul it works fine. The other is this contraption on the front bottom of the dryer on the left hand side as your facing it. This thing is a giant POS. The brochures tell you this needs maintenance less often that your in dryer lint trap to keep it working but oh how untrue this is. The dryer will basically stop drying before your clothes are anywhere near ready with pretty much every load and it’s because this filter gets even the tiniest debris in it and causes the dryer to presumably over heat I’m actually not sure how the mechanism works but bottom line it just stops drying all the way. At which point you will have to take this thing out and get ready because the compartment is filled with sitting water that for some reason didn’t drain all the way and as you pull here comes the water steaming down the dryer onto you, the floor, your clothes. Sometimes as much as 3/4-1 cup of water. Then you stand there staring at this filter that for all intents and purposes looks totally clean other than dripping water everywhere. So you go through the motions of shaking it, putting your hand into the filter compartment to loosen the other little flap at the back that the manufacturer doesn’t even tell you is the actual problem in an attempt to find sometimes up to a sliver of sopping wet lint that you hope and pray is the problem but is inevitably not becaue a load and a half in your dryer isn’t drying again.
I’m giving one star because the units are nice looking, compact as promised and other than being really low capacity the washer does clean really well.
My suggestion just get one of the typical white top loading washer dryer stacking sets you use when you stay in almost any vacation condo. They’re cheaper, hold more clothes and work better.

review_title: How to fix a noisy Frigidaire fridge
review_text:
Bought 1 new from Lowes. Same day it was delivered I heard a loud humming noise. Called Lowes, they said it would be a month before they can replace it. Everyday until the new fridge arrived I'd have to turn off then back turn on the fridge to get the noise to stop. The new fridge arrived. Later that evening, I heard the same humming noise coming from behind the fridge.

FIX:
I'm not an electrician or mechanic or even "handy". I just got tired of the damn noise.

*Do not do this if you do not feel comfortable working in and around exposed wires.*

While the fridge is making the noise, remove the lower panel behind the fridge. Should be 3 or 4 screws holding it in place. You'll see in the bottom left a roundish looking device. That's the compressor. Next to mine is a plastic box almost touching the compressor. Whenever the compressor would kick on, it would vibrate this box, which sounds like a "humming" noise.

Brace the plastic box by putting something between the compressor and plastic box. Could possibly use duct tape to tape the box to the compressor. I didn't look, but there's probably a screw securing the plastic box that has come loose.

I hope this helps.

product_title: Whirlpool WRS588FIHV 28 Cu. Ft. Black Stainless Side-by-Side Refrigerator
review_title: What you may not know already...
review_text:
I've had this WRS588FIHV fridge for a few weeks now I won't go into the details you can read in other reviews -- for example, someone posted that this thing sounds like a Harrier jet. Yeah, that's about right (when the compressor is running). But, I want to let you know about some things you probably don't know.
(1.) It does not have a "dairy bin" at the top of the fridge door. It is obviously made to support one. What the heck, Whirlpool? Why not include that? I did much research trying to find one. I even called Whirlpool parts and spoke with someone directly. They suggested a part that would obviously NOT work and definitely wound NOT match. Frustrating. I read all the reviews on Whirlpool's site, and one of the last ones I read suggested a part would fit that cost $32.90 (thanks for posting that!!). I want to let you know that this is indeed true, the part number is WPW10324760. It fits perfectly.
(2.) After much frustrating research looking for a dairy bin, I came to the conclusion that the interior of this Whirlpool fridge is basically exactly the same as a Kenmore Elite 51773. I can't tell you how many hours that took to determine.
(3.) After realizing that the interior of this fridge the same as a Kenmore Elite 51773, I saw that the Kenmore Elite 51773 comes with a wine rack. Yup. The part number for that is W10478548. It fits perfectly. It basically sets from the shelf brackets and then the shelf itself sits on top of it It's made of metal and is pretty sturdy with four bottles on it. I placed it on the first shelf bracket above the deli drawer. I can fill the shelf atop the deli drawer with 16-oz water bottles and still have the wine rack fully loaded above it.
(4.) The Kenmore Elite 51773 also comes with a "can rack" that can be added to the door. I couldn't find this specific part, but I didn't really want one anyway. Maybe someone else can do that research and post.
(5.) In conclusion, for about $100, you can add a dairy bin shelf to the top of the fridge door and a four-bottle wine rack to the main shelves in the fridge. It may also be possible to add a can rack to the fridge door.

review_text:
So I should preface this review with the fact that I've never owned a new fridge before. It's always been hand me downs and/or what came with the place I was living. So, when I happened on a deal to buy this fridge from home Depot for $1800 I jumped on it.

I loved the design from the moment it was delivered and I had zero issue setting it up and connecting it to the existing water line.

I had chosen this model because it had very few complaints about the ice maker when compared to previous models and other than being a bit on the loud side, I really can't complain about it one bit.

The flex drawer, is hands down my favorite feature of this fridge and everyone in the house gives it a real workout daily since it's where we tend to keep drinks.

Having come from a side by side style fridge and freezer unit makes this units freeze feel massive. I really thought I'd like the basket design more than I do. But it functions very well and holds more then any of my previous freezers so again I love it.

Thankfully I haven't dealt with Samsung customer service yet. But for anyone struggling with them, I highly recommend contacting the credit card company you purchased your fridge with, if you used a credit card. Most major credit cards will fight for you or credit you a lot faster than Samsung support will. Then they'll deal with Samsung in their own time.

Update: I did have the ice maker stop working for me once now. It had frosted over and caused the ice to stop falling into the tray. I took the ice maker apart a little and used a hair dryer on the lowest setting to defrost and dry out the unit. Checked all the seals and reset the ice maker like in the instructions and haven't had and issue since. I'm about two months past that single freeze up. That's the first minor inconvenience.

review_text:

PROS:
The washer has 3 adjustable racks that I found sturdier than other brands. I found it very modeler and easy to accommodate different size dishes.

Quiet - It is not silent, but it is definitely way quieter than other models we had. The really time that you hear it is when it is pumping out the water through the disposal, and that isn't going to get much quieter.

CONS: System has only a 1 year warranty. I would not recommend without a 3 year warranty.

The button on the door easily break. The whole right side of my washer stopped responding and support is useless. The next available tech is several weeks out. Most parts are at least 2 weeks+..
- The primary control that runs the system has been replaced with a different model.

They have a feature called Smart Thinq. This gives a push notification when the Dishwasher is complete, not that you could start as the dishes would be too hot at this point to put away. You can download from choice of 4 download cycles. This gives you options for "Pots & Pans, Casseroles, Glassware and Night Care"

You cannot schedule the dishwasher or remote start it from the app. You cannot make any mode selection changes with the app.

You can also check the estimate cycle time with your phone.

The smart diagnosis is a joke is not very helpful and displays the same information you would get if you looked up any light / or Error codes displayed on the 3 character LCD.

---
If you are looking at this because you like the drawers and sound, it is a very good. Do not buy because of the Smart Thinq. Buy with at least a 3 year warranty as I expect further problems.

review_text:
We were inpressed with how quickly the induction range brings water to a boil. There are a few things you need to be aware of if you plan to buy this stove.
1) The range has 4 "burners", 3 of them work as you would expect. The largest burner is very sensitive about the pots and pans that will work with it. Some large pots that will work with the other 3 burners (and are 100% induction compatible) will not work on the large burner. We had a service man come out to look at it and he couldn't explain why this was the case even after he spoke directly with the factory. The answer from Frigidaire was that even if he replaced the range top the results would be the same. Unfortunately the large burner is the front-right burner, which with our kitchen setup is the most used burner.
2) All four burners say "Auto Sizing" and have rings showing different pan sizes that work with that burner. The repairman and the factory representative said that "Auto Sizing" doesn't mean "Auto Sizing" - the range does not sense the size of the pot/pan being used, it just senses that it is induction-compatible. So, what does "Auto Sizing" mean? The repairman couldn't explain it.
3) Are you used to having an aluminum drip pan in your oven to catch drips? The instructions tell you not to put anything in the bottom of the oven, so anytime you get drips you have to a) live with it, or b) clean your oven.

If you don't mind getting by on 3 burners then you might be very happy with this stove, if you need a large burner or all 4 burners from time to time then I would look to another brand.

review_title: Accurate  temperature settings, high quality materials, and the French door feature is a major plus
review_text:
Our last oven had excellent ratings from consumer publications but was an absolute piece of junk from day one. I was determined to take the time to deeply research our next oven purchase...and shell out extra dollars, if necessary, to get a higher quality appliance. After all, we’d already spent over $ 7000 on 2 inferior wall ovens. Each lasted only a few years.

Since installation of the Cafe oven, I’ve cooked bread, roasts, casseroles, cookies, cakes...you name it, Everything came out perfectly. I tested the accuracy of the temperature settings with a professional oven thermometer. They were spot on. In other words, if I set the oven to 450, the thermometer read exactly 450. Impressive.

The French doors are of course a major feature and far more than just an attention getter (although they certainly look stunning). I find them far better than traditional doors. You open both upper doors at once by using only one hand and simply place your baking dish straight into the oven. . There’s no bending, no stooping, and no risk of getting drips on an open door.

I do suggest rubbing some graphite, provided by the manufacturer, on the racks so they roll smoothly from the start. Otherwise they are a bit hard to slide...or were for me. I also had a learning curve when taking racks out of the oven. They come out very easily but it took practice to learn how to replace them. But this was a minor bump in the Road.

I got exactly what I wanted: a sturdy oven with accurate temperatures, french doors, and an appliance that adds unique style to my kitchen.

review_text:
Update: 18 months after my purchase the cooktop failed. The knobs on the left glow when turned on but no heat turns on. The knobs on the right don't even glow. My wife called GE support and they told us it was out of warranty and wanted to charge us an unknown amount to send someone out to look at it. We had no idea if they were talking $50 or $2000 to repair it and it's practically brand new so I decided to write letters to their executives and engage them on social media. I understand that appliances fail, but I expect free repairs on a brand-new appliance. I engaged GE on social media first and they seemed a lot more willing to help.

But I ended up fixing it myself. While I was driving home from work I was thinking there's probably a computer in this thing and maybe it needs to be rebooted. So I fixed it by turning it off and back on at the breaker.

Because GE phone support was not empowered to stand behind their product when my wife called I am dropping my rating from 5-star to 1-star. While the social media team seemed willing and may have helped us out, I shouldn't have to waste timing engaging manufacturers on various platforms to get a reasonable response. That said, I am still happy with the product. Just not the warranty or the service.

Original review is below:

I bought this for my wife and she loves it! Until now we both preferred gas, but our house doesn't have a gas line so we've been using a regular electric range that came with the house until it finally died so we just replaced it with this model. My wife cooks almost all our food from scratch due to dietary restrictions, so a double-oven is almost a necessity and my hope is it allows her to do her baking in half the time so she's not spending all day in the Kitchen. I'm also going to supplement with an over the hood convection microwave oven to get us up to 3 ovens.

Things I like:
- Real physical knobs, this is superior to touch interfaces where you have to take your eyes off the food to adjust the heat. Real knobs are just so much better, you just turn them. No trying to figure out which burner you're on or where your finger is. Really the reason I went with this instead of some less expensive models is for the knobs.
- The Induction cook-top is fatastic, it heats up very fast, faster than any electric that I've used. Also this gives quick precise heating control with our stainless steel pans (less so with cast iron) which we didn't have with electric. My wife says this is the best feature over an electric and she likes induction even better than gas. ...she's completely right, with our traditional electric we'd always take the tea kettle off the burner when it started boiling... now with our induction cooktop turning off the burner stops is from boiling immediately.
- Double oven, top oven is normal, bottom oven is convection. Today I was cooking a King Cake and my wife was doing Birthday Cupcake, at first she was trying to coordinate who would use the oven when but smiled when she remembered it was a double oven! We baked both at the same time.
- The convection is nice, the auto-adjust feature automatically lowers the temperature (so if you set the oven to 350 deg it is actually at 325 in convection mode) but you can turn that feature off if you want to control the temperature manually. It also seems convection is more energy efficient since you're cooking at a lower temperature or shorter time to do the same amount of baking.
- Electrical wiring instructions were easy, I was able to do the install myself without issue (did have to run down to Home Depot to purchase a power cord).
- Reading though the manual you can actually adjust the temperature by having the oven automatically add or subtract degrees to whatever you set ... mine is right on but it's a nice feature to have if after 10 years it's baking too hot or to cold, or want to adjust it for altitude.
- Intuitive touchpad control for the ovens
- Child lockout--locks out the range controls when not in use.
- The led ring around the knob glows when that burner is active to let you know it's on.
- The induction element automatically shuts off, or doesn't turn on when it doesn't detect a pan over it.
- Came with a wooden pallet. Always nice to get another pallet.

What could be better:
- The warmer in the back middle is not induction, it's a regular heat element but it can only warm, not cook. I think it would have been nice to make that a normal electric burner instead of just a warmer for the one or two pans we have that didn't work with induction.
- I was a bit disappointed in the high cost of matching GE Cafe Microwaves, the GE Profiles don't really match the style that well so I ended up going with another brand which of course won't work with the Chef Connect feature.
- I really wish kitchen appliances manufacturers would get together and come up with open standards so that any branded range can communicate with any branded microwave instead of each manufacturer doing their own thing.
- Only 1-year warranty. For this price-point I would expect maybe a 3 to 5-year warranty. I will be disappointed if I don't get 15 years out of it.
- Really a minor point but nothing on the cooktop glows...I think it would be cool if some rings around the burners glowed when active in proportion to the heat you're outputting there. The rings glowing around the knobs aren't as good a visual I don't think.
- The sound volume for alerts (like done pre-heating, timer done, etc.) is too quiet, I have it on the highest setting and can't really hear it if my son is awake unless I'm in the Kitchen.
- I haven't tried the phone app which may have provided an alternate way to get alerts, but it want me to sign up for a GE account... I really don't want an account with GE or my appliance phoning home so stopped there.
- There's only one timer... I think there should have been two timers (one for each oven).

A few notes:
- Probably just me but I feel like I have to be very careful putting heavy cast iron pans on it... it just feels weird doing that on a glass top! I guess I just have a fear of it cracking.
- Some pots vibrate and make a little noise when the on high--especially when interacting with other pots. Doesn't happen too often but it does happen. It's not too loud or bothersome.
- There seems to be an undocumented Ethernet or serial port on the back of the oven. I can't find any information on it.
- You do have to bend down pretty low to use the lower oven, not an issue but something to be aware of...conversely the smaller oven on top is easier to access than most ovens.
- The LED display is white, maybe a tad blue, fortunately it's not super bright like some blue LEDs which light up the entire house at night keeping you awake. There is also a dot-matrix area in the display which is nice to give you very detailed instructions making the interface easy to use.
- Only the bottom oven is convection.
- With induction some pots and pans won't work. So far we've found 2 in our collection that won't work. A glass tea kettle and a stainless steel pan made with aluminum inside (stainless steel with copper inside do work very well with induction) good way to test your existing cookware is try to stick a magnet to the bottom of it.. if attracts the magnet you should be good.
- I bought from 1-stop Camera and Appliances. Smooth transaction, and the delivery company called the day before coming. The truck that delivered mine only had a liftgate and was really not equipped to do more than drop it off in my driveway (I could have gotten installation service but declined). It came in the middle of a winter storm so my driveway was very snowy and icy. I got out my dolly and straps and the driver was nice enough to help me push it up my slippery driveway to get it to my garage. My wife and I took it from there... it is a little heavier than most ranges I've moved.

This is a good range, my wife loves it, I think it was a good value considering it has knobs, is induction, a double oven, and convection. I hope to get many years of service out of it.

review_text:
First, about the product. When we opened the box, it was dented, bent and bowed in multiple places. Our remodeling team installed it anyway, and we attempted to use it. We learned that both ovens would shut off after the temp rose over approx 160 degrees. We also later learned that the cooktop burners (are they burners on an inductive?) also shut off without warning after a while. So, our product, out of the box, was both damaged and defective. The positive: it looks great in our kitchen, if you don't look too hard for the damage.

The refund/replace/repair saga. We purchased our range for a kitchen remodel about two months prior to remodeling team getting started (big mistake). We did not open the box (even bigger mistake) after delivery, and it remained in our garage unopened. Seems that Amazon has a 30 day refund/replacement policy. When I reached out to the seller, Dynamic Deals, they declined my refund request because I purchased it, at that time, 70 days prior, and told me to contact GE. OBTW, they did not offer any contact information; they put that on me to figure out the rest. No help whatsoever. I then filed a claim with Amazon, and they also declined my refund request, citing their policy. So, I reached out to GE, who dispatched a repair tech. They are replacing the damaged and defective parts next week, but they also declined to issue a refund, stating that it was repairable. With no other alternative, I agreed to a repair. I will update this later, if the repair doesn't remedy the problem. I want to love this range, but I'm not holding my breath.

Lessons learned. Don't buy appliances via Amazon. The return policy states that you have 30 days, that you are on the hook for shipping charges and often a 20% restocking fee if the product is opened. Companies in your local area have a reputation to uphold or they go out of business. Dynamic Deals, the 3rd party seller, didn't care, even after I gave them several opportunities to make it right and save the relationship (and earn a good review). Save yourself the headache and buy local for major appliances. Quite frankly, I was surprised by Amazon's response. For as much as I purchase from them, I expected more. Costco would have given my money back no questions asked. Even Best Buy would have done the same. I won't make another expensive mistake like this again. I hope you can learn from my mistakes. Buy local. If you don't, open the box and inspect everything immediately after delivery. Don't buy more than 30 days before you intend to install and use it so that you can ops check. Finally, don't wait to contact the seller and/or Amazon if something is amiss. They will stand on policy, and then its your problem.

Good luck.

review_title: Only good for cooking one item at a time -
review_text:
This dual oven is anemic at best. It takes 15 minutes to preheat to just 200 degrees. 400 degrees can take over half an hour. Not sure why they claim it has powerful heating elements. Had to adjust top oven by 30 degrees to get it to heat even close to set temperature. Most oven settings claim you should only bake, roast, etc one item on the middle rack at a time - but there are 3 oven racks. So they have a Convection, Bake, Multiple rack setting that supposedly accommodates placing more items in the oven - and they warn you that it may take longer to cook all levels. But what we found is that different levels cook at different rates, and we have to move items around in the ovens multiple times in order to get them all cooked somewhat evenly. The oven in their ads looks like it is capable but somehow the wizards that designed the features must have never actually tested a live unit with real foods to bake, roast etc. I am VERY disappointed in the overall oven - I think they tried to make a "smart" oven but whoever programmed the functionality seems to have forgotten that real cooks know the temperatures they want to cook at and don't need some fancy software to override the cooking process with gimmicks. What would be wrong with having an accurate temperature setting, that cooks at a consistent level no matter how many items are in the oven? This oven does not do that. I replaced an older oven that was getting beyond repair with this oven. The old oven could heat to 450 degrees in 10 minutes. It maintained an accurate oven temperature no matter what or how much we were cooking in the oven. And I could adjust the to my choice of temperature settings in 1 degree increments (allowing ME to make any cooking adjustments for the amount of food in the oven), and it cooked equally well on each of its three racks. Now there is a goal for the designers of this oven to reach.

product_title: Bosch SHPM98W75N 800 Series 24 Inch Built In Fully Integrated Dishwasher with 6 Wash Cycles,in Stainless Steel
review_title: Worst dishwasher I have ever seen
review_text:
I bought this from a different store but thought I should warn others about this dishwasher. This is a decent looking dishwasher but that is the only good point. In short we returned this so-called dishwasher because it 1) does not clean; 2) leaves the dishes soaked; 3) does not load well despite having a rather nice third rack; and 4) the inside stinks of plastic despite having been run at least 8 times on maximum wash and rinse to clear out the odor. There are also some issues with how quiet it is that I will describe later. They may or may not be a problem for you, but you pay quite a bit more to get the extra quiet of this model over a similar one that is only a bit noisier.

The instructions say you should put the dirty side of the dishes facing the wash arms but the spacing and angle of the rack pegs means that if you put the dishes in that way you can't get very many dishes in. If you do it that way with lots of space between the plates etc. the dishwasher will mostly clean them. If you load it as shown in the pictures so you can get all of the 12 place settings in, forget it, nothing will get clean.

The dishwasher has no heating element and is supposed to dry the dishes by condensation of the hot rinse water onto the walls of the dishwasher where it then drains away. I live at high altitude and normally things dry very, very quickly but this dishwasher has no vents and the condensation drying does not work so even 10 hours or more after the cycle has finished on the "extra dry" setting, things are still wet. It is so dry here I have always turned off the drying cycle on my previous dishwashers and everything was dry a few hours after the cycle, but my other dishwashers have vents. This is a really stupid design.

There are several sites on the internet devoted to stink problems with Bosch dishwashers. Some people have problems with the drain installation where they get sewer gasses into the dishwasher. Proper installation should fix this. Some people have a bad smell from the bitumen in the outside insulation. We had a nasty plastic order from inside of the dishwasher. It might be a defect in ours. We did find some nasty oily red stuff in the filter so a seal on the motor might have failed but this is a brand new dishwasher. Whatever the cause, it does not go away and can impart a bad smell to items that the dishwasher is supposed to clean.

Finally, the dishwasher is supposed to be very quiet at 39 dBA. Well that is sort of true at quite a cost. To keep the sound down while it is running, they have eliminated the grinder that minces up and disposes of any food particles that come off the dishes, so you have to clean out the filter by hand every month or so. That might be OK, but when the dishwasher drains, it is very loud so you have the extra inconvenience of cleaning the filter and the dishwasher isn't all that quiet.

There may be better Bosch dishwashers but I think the stupid condensation drying is now their standard as is the annoying manual-clean filter. There seem to be several stink problems and I don't know if some models are better or worse on that. I certainly will never have another Bosch dishwasher.

product_title: Bosch SHPM98W75N 800 Series 24 Inch Built In Fully Integrated Dishwasher with 6 Wash Cycles,in Stainless Steel
review_text:
We bought one of these dishwashers in April. It took 8 hours to install because it DOES NOT fit into a standard 34 inch opening- although the Jenn-Aire and LG had no problem in or out. This is due to the solid plastic (not metal like real dishwashers use) bottom structure- it requires an absolutely flat surface. We had to drill and grind the concrete and tile to get it into the opening. Our previous dishwashers (LG- 14 years, and Jenn-Aire, 13 years) ran well and quietly until they just gave up. The Bosch is:

1) noisier- I measured 54-55dB at 1meter with my calibrated instruments- stand measuring conditions. 10dB means 10 times louder than advertised.
2) the levelers are soft plastic- just deform rather than raise or lower. The LG and Jenn-Aire use steel rods with locking nuts.
3) Does not clean dishes unless we wash them first. Our water is softened and filtered. We use Finish tablets and anti-spotting solution.
4) Rarely cleans silverware unless it is perfectly cleaned by hand.
5) Does not clean glasses if they are spanning the water feed bar in the upper part of the washer.
6) Does not start when we push the buttons. My wife can get it in 3 to 4 tries, I give up after 5.
7) the anti-spotting solution cup is a ridiculous design- the solution dribbles all over the door inner panel when trying to fill it, and there is not a functioning fill indicator like the LG units have.
8) the bottom rack always (read: ALWAYS) derails due to bad design.

This is not an isolated case- we have a friend in Massachusetts that bought one recently- she has the same problems. A friend in Ohio just bought one- they are returning it to the dealer for a real dishwasher. A friend in Colorado was given one after his old Bosch unit was recalled for being a fire-hazard. His new unit has the same problems as ours.

I finally became frustrated today when the silverware was dirty after a cycle. See the images- much of the grate area is blocked by casting flash which prevents water from getting to the silverware from below. This is just lousy quality control (if there is any). For a $5.00 part (maybe less) the entire $1300 dishwasher is compromised. Also, the grates in the LG were much more open than the Bosch, so it is again design to begin with (poor English sentence structure, sorry).

So, our new solution is to wash the dishes in the sink, rinse, and put them in the dishwasher racks to air dry. Costs less electricity and we know the dishes are clean.

review_title: A nice well build french door fridge from LG
review_text:
Finally bought a new french door fridge. I went with the LG brand as I have heard they are a good brand and last. My previous fridge was a side by side and a Maytag, but it junked out on me. This model has it says a dual ice maker, but it is really just the icemaker in the door and you can dump the ice in the door manually into the tray for ice in the top freezer under it. There is a second freezer as well under it. The bottom one is bigger.

The fridge part is massive! It has so much more room than my old one. I also like how it is open all on top and there is no divider as found in the side by side models and the fridge part is eye level and I do not have to lean down to get things out of the fridge. Really makes you think why no one invented these french door fridges sooner!

The water filter for it I noticed is rather pricey, that is one concern about it I have had. I may see if I can just take it out later, as that was what I did with my Maytag and never had any problems being on city water.

A nice feature with this is the ice cubes are smaller than the only type, which I also really like. It also has wifi so you can connect it to your phone to see the temperature, but it is more a fun feature than having any real benefit as far as I can tell.

It has a quick ice feature to make ice faster if you are having company come and turn it on a day prior, so it makes ice faster to start to fill the lower tray manually by unloading the ice from the top tray as it is made. However, I would just go buy a bag of ice for a few dollars for that, as the water filter on these is expensive and I suspect that just buying bags of ice for parties would be more cost effective as well as easier to do.

There is also a shelf that will slide in when you open the doors, so if you have something taller you can put it in the fridge. The doors have space to store items as well on the insides. The left side will only old small things like a bottle of ketchup. The right side can holder larger things like a gallon of milk.

There is a fruit and veggie drawer, although you can set them to either. Both can be fruit or veggie, or swap them at any time. Under it is a small long storage drawer as well for smaller snack items.

product_title: LG LMXS28626S 28 cu.ft. 4-Door French Door Refrigerator - Stainless Steel
review_text:
My LMX28988ST /04 broke down (purchased Oct 2012). According to the owner’s manual parts are covered for seven years and the compressor for ten but not the labor. At first, I called several local repair shops, and all declined to work on it because they were not authorized LG repair shops. I then decided to call LG's 1-800 number. The lady at LG told me to contact Sears Repair for service. Sears were booked solid and I had to wait around 10 days for an appointment. Finally, the day came, and I was told by the Sears repairman that they are not authorized to do LG warranty work. In any case he did the diagnosis and said my compressor, condenser and dryer were bad. The estimate came out to over a thousand dollars and Sears would need to contact LG before any work could be done or I could pay the full amount and try to get reimbursed for the parts than came under warranty. The repairman charged me $99 plus tax for the house call. He gave me a 10% coupon and told me I could recover my house call bill by buying a new refrigerator from Sears that cost a $1000 and up.

I contacted LG again and “Nick” at LG told me Air Tech Hawaii does the warranty work in Hawaii. Why wasn’t I told about that in the first place. Being the frig initially cost me over $2,500 on sale from the NEX (Navy Exchange), I decided to pay the flat rate of $535 plus $25.21 to have it fix. According to Air Tech Hawaii, Sears took a swag (scientific wild ass guess) and diagnose that both the compressor and condenser were at fault. Air Hawaii added a valve to attach test gauges to determine the problem. Turns out the condenser was still working. Unless it was leaking, it would not be covered.

No matter how much I presented my case, LG would not reimburse me for their misdirected service call. I own a couple large LG TV and an electric range but never again. “Buyer Beware” a large corporation like LG would be stingy about 100 bucks. My beef was all about the “principal.”

The second time it failed they replaced the entire icemaker module because LG found a design fault in the original design. Now, as of yesterday, the compressor has failed. review_text:
I purchased the product (Fridge) elsewhere, exact same model.

Pros: It works well, the items in the back of the fridge are at the same chilled level as those in the doors.
The layout is well designed for the way we use a refrigerator and freezer (the bottom drawer holds more than one large turkey if that matters to you). The controls for the refrigerator are on the door, and some are in the app. There is a lockout for the water and ice dispensing. There is also room to fit a pitcher and tall glasses into the dispenser.

Cons: Opening the doors with their opening both sides is an issue depending on the layout of your kitchen. For us, the right door goes up against a wall that comes out far enough to impact how wide that door can open. The refrigerator fits fine into the space, this is just an issue with the way the two doors open in the middle of the fridge. Our old fridge that opened on the side (top freezer model) and was 10 cubic foot smaller had the same issue with that wall. The thing is, our kitchen design is a standard design (I am thinking it's time to remove that wall).

The lockouts work for the dispenser but not for the controls. We have a fairly innovative kitten when it comes to things. Let's just say that waking up to the freezer no longer set to 0 degrees, but instead to -8 degrees, and the refrigerator no longer set to 40 degrees but to 48 degrees had me setting up an interior surveillance camera, and now wishing we had full lockouts after watching how the kitten was doing it. Same for the LG model range, the lock outs do not do enough when it comes to this kitten.

The other issue is delivery. I'd measured the doorway and all spaces involving bringing in the refrigerator. I paid for delivery knowing there are issues in how a refrigerator is handled. I was prepared when the delivery folks arrived, looked at the door and said they couldn't deliver it. I said, flatly, I had measured, and they could. I proceeded to remove the storm door, front door, and all latchings from the frame. It barely fit through sideways with the doors removed. The issue are the drawer brackets stick out over an inch out. Those made it almost not work, and were not included in any measurements I found online.

Once past that point, the delivery went fine, the doors went back on no issue. My feeling is all refrigerators are overpriced for what they do. But, this one is doing the job well. And, I'm glad to have opted for this model. I may well purchase the extended warranty from LG for this and the dishwasher if possible. Not sure if I'd concern myself that way on the stove, but both the dishwasher and refrigerator use the wifi and app. Simply, there is more that can go wrong with them than I'd want to deal with personally.

review_text:
I bought this through a local retail chain, based on the online description and in consultation with a friend's son-in-law who worked at the store.

First, xxx disappointed in small amount of ice produced each cycle. We're just a 2-person household though home most of every day, so we empty out the ice daily. Fortunately, the dispenser handles the cubes I make in ice cube trays, will even crush it.

Our prior fridge died suddenly late on a Sat. afternoon a few weeks ago. Although it also had the ice maker in the fridge (stupid idea), we almost never ran out of ice. Nor did the chilled water line ever freeze in the last 5 years of life (it came with the house at purchase; it was about 14 years old and the very pricey electronic control board quit).

I quickly researched online and narrowed my choices to just a few brands/models. The alcove limited the size, so that was the first consideration. One of the *truly terrific* features on this model is a full-width, lighted "deli" drawer, and if need be, the veg/fruit bins can be stacked to provide xxx-high storage on one side.

The interior lighting really is great. Having the veg/fruit bins well lit helps remind you of the contents every time you open the doors. The exterior lighting, however, is almost non-existent. It's almost impossible to see where to push for water and ice cubes, even with the very strong kitchen lighting I have. I ended up putting round adhesive dot labels over the spot to press for dispensing. The factory labeling looks like it should be lit, but isn't.

The freezer lighting and depth is fantastic, but the fridge door shelves aren't deep enough to prevent bottles from falling forward when the doors are pulled open. All the shelves are glass; I miss having one that's vinyl-coated wire that helps cool recently cooked food.

I knew that this model had a number of negative reviews on various sites, but given our space, budget, and need, figured we'd take a chance. One thing that may help if there's trouble: the store sends its own repair techs out - - and we did buy the extended warranty.

The smudge-resistant "Gallery" finish is very, very nice tho the sides are a traditional pebble finish in a dark grey paint - - be aware if yours will be exposed. The handles do show smears.

review_text:
I bought this LG Dishwasher in October of 2017 from Home Depot. In March of 2019 (less than a year and a half later), the electrical control panel stopped working so I was unable to use the product. Since it was 5 months past the warranty, I was charged $135.31 for a technician to come out and diagnose the problem. I was informed that I would then have to pay for the repair and labor after the technician ordered the new part. When the technician arrived, he had a new electronic control panel (so he already knew what the problem was before even looking at the dishwasher) and told me that I would not be charged for the repair or labor because this was such a common problem - that they had the NEW MODIFIED electrical control panels in stock. He said that in the NEW MODIFIED control panels, they have added a moisture barrier because in the old version, moisture from steam would get into the control panel and ruin the electrical system. I asked him why there hasn't been a recall on this product since it was so common, and he said that he didn't know why but there has been a "Service Bulletin" released regarding this same issue. I then called customer service to get a refund of the $135.31 that I already paid, and they would not give a refund even after being escalated to a supervisor. I asked to be escalated again and was informed that he could not do that. I tried to call the President of the company and got no answer and no way of leaving a VM or email. Considering this is a COMMON DEFECT in the product and a modified control panel has been created for this issue, there should be a recall and all expenses paid. I want my refund of $135.31 since this was LG's defective product and not anything that I could control! A complaint with the BBB has been filed and I will continue to let people know that they should stay away from LG products.

* Update* I finally got a refund for the service call, but only because I slammed them with bad reviews everywhere I could think of. Amazon, Home Depot, Lowe’s, Twitter, Facebook, BBB, and many more. After leaving several bad reviews on FB, a representative reached out to me and got it approved - but it took almost three months after it was approved before I saw that money. The refund wouldn’t have happened had I not been persistent. I urge people to not let companies like LG take advantage of you. Escalate, go to social media...whatever it takes. To date, this dish washer has still not been recalled.

review_title: Broken after 2 months and Whirlpool service is absolutely terrible
review_text: DO NOT BUY THIS PRODUCT - (purchased at Home Depot, but warning people on Amazon). I don't usually leave reviews but want to stop you from wasting money, time and food (and a lot of patience). I had it for less than 2 months and the refrigerator side of the unit froze everything solid with no way to stop it from happening (yet having to continue to run it to keep all frozen items frozen). I adjusted the temperature to all different settings and went through the manual with all recommended fixes (air vent clearance, etc.). The manual actually states the top shelf of the fridge will be colder (because it's vented/cooled from the freezer near the top of the unit) and there's no way to change that. I scheduled service after navigating an atrocious automated call system. It was more than a week out for a technician to come to our house (they only set aside 1 day week for areas and at the time of scheduling will only commit to a window of between 8a.m.-4p.m.). When the technician arrives, if they do not have a part on hand, you're likely looking at additional multiple weeks before they can come back. I'll likely not have a working refrigerator for about a month. With a baby at home, it's especially inconvenient. Also, the Whirlpool standard warranty does not cover food loss, so you're out that cost as well as the time off from work for the service appointment. Oh, and you cannot return major appliances to Home Depot, so you're completely at the mercy of Whirlpool. I worked at Whirlpool headquarters in Benton Harbor, MI, and have actually had a soft spot for the company in the past. Their call system states, "For over a century, we've believed in everyday care." The problem is it's just marketing lip-service to chase the current customer experience trend. There is no operational orchestration to meaningfully support and quickly resolve customer issues. If you need any proof defects are expected in their products, look at them not covering food loss in the first year warranty - the belief is there's financial risk to the company and that can only be the case if Whirlpool believes there's a decent chance a percentage of the product will be defective. Seriously, do not buy this product.

review_text: This refrigerator came with my new home.  The ice/water dispenser area is so small you will most always hit the water dispenser when you're getting ice.  Soon to be the garage refrigerator.

product_title: Whirlpool WRS325SDHZ 25 Cu. Ft. Stainless Side-by-Side Refrigerator
review_text: The ice maker works really well - better than my last Frigidaire.  So far (about 6 months) I have no complaints.  Living up to my expectations.

product_title: Whirlpool WRS325SDHZ 25 Cu. Ft. Stainless Side-by-Side Refrigerator
review_title: You had one job refrigerator, and you FAILED!
review_text: I bought this fridge after my two year old LG died due to the bad compressor problem that is ongoing for that manufacturer. This one  had pretty good reviews so I bought it as a replacement. It was delivered a week later. The freezer section is fine. It is holding a steady -1 degrees F on setting three of five. The fridge, however, is another story. I put thermometers with memory in all of the drawers. On setting 4/5 (five is coldest), the top shelf is usually below freezing. The next shelf is about 39 degrees. The shelves below that average at 42/43 degrees. The bottom two drawers which act as crispers average at 45 degrees and range 44/48 degrees. The seller has agreed to give us a refund as a brand new refrigerator should not be like this. However, I don't see how it could be any other way as the only vent in the fridge is at the top of the unit and blows air down from there. Thus I would think this would be the default situation - frozen top shelves and balmy lower ones. Completely unsatisfactory. As for the noise, yes it is louder than other units, but it is not overpowering or something that would keep you awake at night. If it weren't for the fact that this refrigerator is not refrigerating, I'd keep it and likely be OK with my purchase.

product_title: Whirlpool WRS325SDHZ 25 Cu. Ft. Stainless Side-by-Side Refrigerator
review_title: We've had it 6 months and now we're selling it!

The water dispensing tube is in line with the front of the door, so when you get water and the tube drips, it runs down the front of you fridge onto the floor. The ice dispenser is super noisy and ice gets caught in the dispenser door, only to fall out later when partially melted onto you floor. If you have a wooden floor forget it. This will ruin your floor. Even if you don't, you have to constantly wipe the water off the front of the fridge and still wipe up the water off the floor. The veggie drawers are small and do not slide easily. We had a low cost GE fridge before we were perfectly happy with for 15 years. The fridge does maintain good temperatures in both the fridge and freezer. I've hated this thing for some time now but didn't say anything. This morning my wife said, "We need to talk and you're not going to like this. I hate  that fridge!" To her surprise I said, then we'll get a new one. We don't really have that kind of money but life's too short to be pissed off every time you go to the fridge.

product_title: Whirlpool WRS325SDHZ 25 Cu. Ft. Stainless Side-by-Side Refrigerator

review_text:

The shelves cannot be raised or lowered, but we knew that before purchasing it. There is an annoying problem with the ice maker, where it shuts off when full and then won't turn back on. Also worth mentioning that you can't open the ice maker door to lower the arm without dumping ice all over the floor, because it gathers against the door.

The other problem we've had is likely a manufacturing defect. Only one door can be moved to level the doors, but when we leveled ours, the door we had to raise the door so high that it rubs on the hinge and this prevents it from closing by itself. So, we were presented with a choice between a rubbing door that won't close well or settle with doors that look awkward because they sit at different heights.

product_title: Whirlpool WRS321SDHZ 21 Cu. Ft. Stainless Side-by-Side Refrigerator
review_title: Whirlpool WRS321SDHZ 21.4cf Stainless is a Great Fridge
review_text:
My WRS321SDHZ Stainless 21.4cf (33”W 66”H) was installed 12-7-18. It’s 10 days later, and I’m 100% thrilled with it. Here are my observations:
SOUND: This is a quiet fridge. After reading some reviews (just a few), I was fearful of a freight train coming into my kitchen. I was incredibly relieved at how quiet this fridge is. It hums and makes noises here and there, but a fridge can’t be totally silent. Do NOT worry about this as I did!
ICE MAKER: Awesome. So very easy to dispense water and ice. The Water lever is up front, and very easy to use, and I’ve not yet had a single drop fall into the collector after removing the glass. The Ice lever is in the back, and works perfectly. Nothing yet has even touched the little tray collector at the bottom so far.
SHELVES: They’re not adjustable, but that has caused me zero problems. I’m amazed at how much room this 24.1cf fridge has vs. the 12yo 21.7 Kitchenaid that it replaced. I removed the in-door Can Caddy to give more room there – that’s where all the milk and juice gallons and ½ gals. and tall things go.
TEMPERATURES: Perfect. I left the temp. settings as from the factory (middle settings), and I’m getting -3/-4 in the freezer, and 35-36 in the fridge consistently.
LOOKS: My WRS321SDH is a work of Art, as far as I’m concerned. It’s gorgeous, inside & out. The inside lightening is beautiful and the shelves are handsome – so clean-looking. The outside look is stunning.
WHEELS: Non problem. I was a little worried about the wheels that you can’t lock. BUT, I am getting zero rolling when I open and close the door. I asked the install guy before I knew there was no problem, and he said buy little furniture studs if you need them.
DOOR ALIGNMENT: Perfect. They looked good initially, but the installer did do a minute or so adjusting (with a little wrench I think) for total perfection.
BOTTOM LINE: This is an amazing fridge and I’m happy as a lark with it. If something should change or I find something I don’t like, I’ll come back and post an update.

product_title: Whirlpool WRS321SDHZ 21 Cu. Ft. Stainless Side-by-Side Refrigerator

product_title: Whirlpool WRS321SDHZ 21 Cu. Ft. Stainless Side-by-Side Refrigerator
review_title: Shelves are non-adjustable and will not fit milk, 2L, juice, etc.
review_text:
I purchased this Whirlpool fridge today, so I cannot speak to the longevity, but I felt compelled to write a review almost immediately, for several reasons.
First the Pros:
- Looks sharp!
- Easy setup (Note: my previous fridge had a different connector for the water line (push to fit), but this one needs a ferrule and nut (and probably tubing if you didn't already have it) purchased separately. The documentation is hard to find, but you need a 1/4" compression fitting with 1/4" OD copper or polyethylene tubing.
- It is under 68" tall - usually these are the basic college-dorm type refrigerators, but this side-by-side is a very nice upgrade for this size. If you need a smaller refrigerator, this is a very nice one! I have only found two that I would consider purchasing...this one and the LG LFDS22520S (french door style with freezer on bottom).
- Cools to temp ridiculously fast! We set it up, plugged it in. I went to pick up nut & ferrule, returned, attached plumbing, and had the first load of ice in under 3 hours. I was super impressed, so I started transferring my food back into the fridge (from coolers, since last fridge died unexpectedly), and here is where the cons come in.
Cons:
- SHELVES IN FRIDGE ARE NON-ADJUSTABLE AND WILL NOT FIT A GALLON OF MILK!
I started unloading the coolers, putting condiments away, thinking, 'wow, there is a lot of door space for all my condiments'. Then, I went to the next cooler, and grabbed a gallon of milk, and lo and behold, it would not fit on any of the shelves. My family goes through three gallons per week, and that will take up about half of the door space...in my previous fridge, I lined them up one behind the other. It is much easier reaching back in the fridge to pull out a new gallon of milk than it is to dig on a shelf for a bottle of ranch dressing in and behind 4 other bottles of dressing and bbq sauce. I knew the shelves were non-adjustable shelves, but I had no idea it would not fit a gallon of milk. What in the world?!?! This is quite possibly the worst design possible! 2L soda? Won’t fit. Bottle of apple juice? Won’t fit. Basically, any beverage that is larger than a 20 oz soda has to go in the door. The maximum height for the largest shelf is 9 7/8 inches. A jug of milk? 10 inches. We were torn between an LG and a Whirlpool, and had I known this, I would have paid the extra $250 and gone with the LG (even though the LG has a water dispenser and an ice maker, not an ice dispenser).
-Temperature adjustment buttons are in the same spot as the 'crushed/cubed' selector button, so it is very easy to accidentally change the temperature of the fridge. Using the 'Lock' feature locks everything out...it won't change the temperature, but it won't dispense water or ice. Poor design, in my opinion.
-It is my first 6 hours of owning this fridge, but I need to investigate if there are locks for the wheels, as every time I open the fridge, the entire unit rolls forward. I have to hold the fridge with my left or right foot, or other hand, depending on which side of it I am opening. That means that it seals well, which is a very good thing, but it seems silly to have to wedge a new fridge without wheel locks or leveling feet that lift them up.
- Freezer is small for this size fridge. I was upgrading a 19.? CF side-by-side to this 21.4 CF side-by-side, so I expected it to be larger. Instead, the ice maker and water dispenser (which my previous fridge had), takes up the top 1/3rd of the freezer. There is a tiny shelf that literally measures 4" wide and 1 3/4" deep on the back of the water dispenser which screams "our design is so bad, you will be thankful for this extra 7 square inches of space! My wife's comment was "We have too much stuff in the freezer anyway." Well, that will not be the case anymore, as I estimate the freezer space to be about 75% of my previous smaller fridge. The specs say it has 6.7 cubic feet of freezer space, for what it is worth.

I want to give this fridge 4 stars, docking one for freezer space, which is visible when you buy it, so you know what you are getting. I think that this is a decent fridge if: you need a fridge under 68" tall, you don't need a lot of freezer space, you don't have a lot of condiments, and you don't drink much milk or other refrigerated beverages. If any of the above 4 statements for you are not true, then look elsewhere. Because of the blatantly egregious design flaws (make your shelf adjustable or 1/8 inch lower!, a 7 sq in shelf - really?, rolling wheels), I cannot recommend this refrigerator to anyone because it makes me question what 'under-the-hood' design flaws may exist that I can't see. Literally, 1/8 of an inch of shelf space cost this refrigerator 3 stars…I would have rated 4 stars if you could fit beverages in it. For some people's lifestyles, this may be a great fridge...for my family, not so much. I just wish I had known before buying it, so now you do.

product_title: 'LG Graphite Steel Top Load Washer'
review_text:
We purchased the LG top loader 5.0 washer in November 2019 and had issues with it from first use. The soap/rinse dispenser was not draining or flushing the soap through to adequately clean the clothes. It was overflowing with water after use, but the clothes were often no clean. Often they were not even wet in the middle where they often twisted into knots. We contacted LG and were told that we had a water pressure issue and to hire a plumber. $300 later the plumber and a contractor tell us our water pressure is still fine.
We call LG to request an exchange or return and are told that we could only get a service call. 3 months later, 5 service calls (only two actually show up with a 5 hour window on week days!), countless phone calls without ever getting a return call, two new parts replaced, the issue still exists and LG still refuses to take back or replace the washer! We were very frustrated-stuck with a $900 washer that does not work and LG will not take responsibility. It was under warrantee and we purchased the 3 year extended warrantee. They instead insist on repairing a brand new appliance until it works.
Finally, after threatening legal action and at least 100 phone calls with numerous unsupportive staff, very poor customer service and recording of the issues, we got Home Depot to pick up the defective product. It was a poor experience with both companies, so beware that if you are part of the 20% of LG washers that do not work properly (as stated to me) you will be stuck with it! I highly suggest you consider another company with better product and customer service. Fingers crossed you do not need it and do not have to waste your time with this experience or 4 months without clean clothes.
Also note, the drawer dispensers are poor quality and flimsy, they do not drain water well. I was told by multiple sales people that there is often water left over in the drawer system which can contribute to mold issues. Several appliance stores in Seattle have even stopped carrying LG due to issues with service and need for 'repairs.'

product_title: LG WM9500HKA SIGNATURE 5.8 cu. ft. Mega Capacity Washer in Black Stainless Steel
review_text:
Has all the features and capacity you could want. God forbid you should need warranty service. Our washer stopped working at 13 months with light use (just me & my wife), so we called LG service. After an initial visit to determine the problem, parts were ordered. Two weeks later the parts and technician showed up and he installed the part. Still did not work. More parts ordered and 2 more weeks passed. New parts installed. It still did not work. Round 3, same routine, still did not work. We are now at 1 and a half MONTHS with no washer. On this 4th visit I got involved with the tech and insisted he check the cable to the main motor for a break, That was the problem all along.

The tech was incompetent just threw new parts at the problem. I (homeowner) repaired the cable and the machine worked again.

Fast forward 2 years. The washer would not drain and there was a racket when the pump was running. Called LG and told them the drain pump was bad and to please dispatch a tech WITH A PUMP. Tech arrived a week later with NO PUMP. Now I'm waiting 2 MORE weeks to get the part and service.

I had expected better quality and longevity from a $2000 washer. I also expected better service from a big company like LG.

Think twice before buying LG.

product_title: LG WM9500HKA SIGNATURE 5.8 cu. ft. Mega Capacity Washer in Black Stainless Steel
review_text: I bought a similar unit for my rental house. The first one I had delivered turned on but would do nothing else.  Under warrantee, so the vendor removed and replaced the unit.  The second machine left a gallon or so of water sloshing under the revolving drum.  Vendor sent repairman - said I was using too much soap, or had too heavy a load, or . . . the machine did the same thing using NO soap and NO clothes.  Vendor told me they could do no more repair calls but would write letter I could share with LG to support my claim, but in their experience "LG would just laugh at me".  Go on line and trype "LG washer trouble" to see this is long-standing defect.  If you buy this you've been warned.

product_title: LG WM9500HKA SIGNATURE 5.8 cu. ft. Mega Capacity Washer in Black Stainless Steel
review_text:
We have a large family and I do a lot of laundry. When it came time to replace my "exploding" Samsung top loader under their recall replace/buyout, I decided to try a front loader machine. Problem is, most front loaders are smaller capacity than top loaders. After 6+ months of research I chose this LG WM9500HKA and matching dryer. It was the largest machine on the market at the time (January 2020), I'm fairly certain it's still the largest machine available without adding a separate mini machine. Initially I liked the machine. My biggest complaint was it has an extra rinse cycle option but no extra spin cycle option. This isn't always a big deal, except the drain pump motor failed in January 2021, one day after our manufacturer warranty ended. Thankfully I had purchased through Costco and had a 2nd year warranty added. LG sent a repairman out and the drain pump motor was replaced within a couple days. However, after replacing the drain pump motor, if I ran the washer on high spin cycle even for small loads, the machine would leak from the front.
Fast forward to December 2021 and the grinding noise from the drain pump motor started again. January 2, 2022 the drain pump motor died again. The original drain pump motor lasted less than a year, the replacement lasted less than a year. Managed to get LG to send a repairman out to replace the pump motor again. Repairman starts complaining as soon as he gets out of his truck, complaining about everything, opens the machine lid and states the warranty is void and he won't complete the job. He eventually said he would leave the part, the drain pump motor, for us to install on our own. He didn't even turn the machine on to listen to it, did nothing to troubleshoot or attempt to diagnose the problem. Went completely on my diagnosis of the problem. We installed the pump motor we were given by the LG technician, reassembled the machine and the drain pump motor is making the same grinding noise and the machine won't drain. Now we don't know if we were given a faulty part or if this isn't actually the problem. To make matters worse, outside repair companies won't attempt to repair the machine because we took the machine apart and attempted the repair and it didn't solve the problem. So we have a $2,000 machine that isn't quite 2 yrs old, it won't drain, no option for a spin cycle without adding water so even if we manually drain the machine it won't spin the laundry. (We ordered on 1/2/2020 but delivery took 2 weeks, then dryer had to be replaced because it smoked, so we didn't actually having a working washer/dryer set until 2/15/2020 - absolutely ridiculous that the warranty starts on date of purchase not delivery.) review_title: Loud annoying grinding sound during agitation cycle - perfectly normal, though
review_text:
I've had this a week and done half a dozen loads. This is a nice looking and well-operating machine. There is one significant problem.

The agitation cycle is annoyingly loud and jarring. The washer makes this grinding noise as it swishes back and forth. I've been around washing machines for half a century and I've never heard a washer make a noise like this. Normally, the washing machine sounds kind of blend away into the background and become like white noise. With this machine, you definitely know it when the machine starts agitating. And it does this agitation more than once per washing cycle, so it becomes very distracting.

At first, I thought that there was something wrong with my washer. But no, GE has on its website (accessible through a QR code that you scan) audio of the washer making this noise. I'm sure they do this precisely to reduce the number of customer service complaints they get about it.

I find a few things about this interesting. First, that GE obviously knows that this noise is a problem. However, instead of doing some actual engineering to try to fix it, they direct you to their website to listen to it, to avoid the inevitable customer service calls. Second, this unit is a replacement for a previous stacked GE unit that must have been around 15-20 years old. The old unit didn't make this sound - no other washer I've ever heard during my entire life ever did. This is progress?

That being said, the washer and dryer work just fine. Clothes come out clean and dry. Speaking of actual engineering, they did a couple of nice things to improve the dryer in the 15-20 years since my last unit. The old unit could only be set to dry for 50 minutes, which was never enough to get the clothes fully dry. You can set the new one to 90, which is enough.

When the old dryer was done with its cycle, it used to make this very loud annoying buzz - EHNNNNNNT - like on a game show, but only if the game show really wanted to make fun of a loser. The new dryer doesn't make any noise when it stops. Also, they've moved the lint collector to the front of the dryer instead of being waaay in the back. This makes removing lint much easier.

review_title: Don't Buy!  Failed after 13 months.  JUNK
review_text:
After about a year, the cycle times started getting longer and longer. When you start the load it tells you how long the cycle should take, about an hour. SO I would set an alarm on my cell phone for whatever time was on the washer. All went well for about a year. Then upon returning to change the load, there would still be 10 minutes left on the timer. Next week, there would be 25 minutes. Soon, a load was taking over two and a half hours. SO I watched what was happening. It would try to spin and it would go off center, stop, go slowly for a minute, back and forth, then try to spin again, and go off balance. I tried opening it up and rearranging the clothes inside. Same result. I tried it with an empty machine. Still same routine. SO I called in a certified repairman. He couldn't figure out how to fix it. I paid him. I called in another professional repairman. After an hour of diagnosis, he said he would have to research the problem. Got a call. He said that there are two fluid containing ballast weights on the front of the machine that had probably leaked and would have to be replaced. Estimate, $500. Bad thing was that he wouldn't guarantee it because it was a design flaw. The same thing would probably happen again. He recommended that I scrap the machine. So I lose the purchase price. I lost the cost of two repair visits, over $200. and I've been without a washer for over a month while we tried to diagnose the problem.

Called Samsung. They refused to do anything because the washer is more than 12 months old.

review_title: Complete junk. Huge waste of money.
review_text:
We have had this washer for a bit over 2 years. Started out needing 3?, 4? service calls just to make it STOP LEAKING water all over the floor. The lack of an agitator and large tub is a nice idea, but a complete fail in application. Not only does it not clean clothes nearly as well as a machine with an agitator, but the extra space this allows is intentionally not used by the washing machine. It simply will not fill up high enough with water to wash blankets, or anything else relatively large that still easily fits inside this huge and beautiful looking tub.
This is all about looks, not function. Lots of bells and whistles... oh, and beeps. Pretty little sing-song beeps. This is what the engineers at Samsung think cleans clothes. They spent their time on pretty little beeping noises. I would rather have an ugly, 20 year old washer that actually works.
