review_text:
[UPDATE 2018-11-26] I posted the review below to Frigidaire's website, and this is what they responded back with. Hilarious.

Thank you for choosing Frigidaire. As a valued owner, your opinion matters greatly to us and to other customers. We enjoyed hearing your thoughts and appreciate you taking the time to write a review. Unfortunately, your review could not be posted for the reason listed below. Please take a moment to update your review so we can post it on the site.

Thanks again for your valued feedback.

Mention a competitor
Directs business away
Includes personally identifiable information
Mentions shipping complaints
Including inappropriate media
Contains a URL
Is vague or needs more detail
Includes profanity

[ORIGINAL REVIEW]

I am purposely taking 30-45 minutes of my time to write this review and create accounts on every website I can find (Frigidaire, Sears, Home Depot, Amazon, Lowe's etc.) that sells the Frigidaire FFLG3900UW0 Washer-Dryer combo to warn others of the incredibly low quality and unreliable and poor operation of this machine.

From how nonintuitive and backwards the controls are, to how finicky the load balancer is and how aggressive the lid lock is, those who purchased this machine should be issued refunds and the engineers responsible for the design of this machine should be sent back to school and/or fired.

Regarding the controls: settings changes (e.g. from cold to warm to hot, from low to max fill) rotate in the opposite direction (from top to bottom instead of bottom to top) and the cancel buttons don't cancel any cycle immediately, but take an unrealistically long period of time to cancel. How long? Who knows. Apparently I have all day to sit around and wait for the machine to cancel before I can fix a problem, like an unbalanced load. Which leads me to:

Almost every load goes out of balance. I've been using washing machines for 30 years, and never have I encountered a washer that was as finicky as this one when it comes to load balancing. Almost. Every. Single. Load. Regardless of the materials, how careful I am to place them in the tub, or fill level, this machine must apparently be as balanced as a gyroscope on the Hubble Space Telescope. What have such tight tolerances? This isn't astronomy or a rocket launch, this is laundry.

Which brings me to the lid lock. When a load is out of balance, when does lid lock disengage? Who knows. The machine will beep at you and flash "Unbalanced Load", but when you try to lift the lid you encounter the lid lock. Which. Won't. Disengage. Ever. Well, maybe after 20 minutes, but again, I don't have all day to sit around in 2018 and fix problems on what's supposed to be an automated machine.

So, in summary, if you value your time and sanity, look elsewhere, as this machine was designed by second and third class engineers and wasn't field tested properly, and as such should be recalled and scraped.

product_title: Electrolux EFME427UIW 8.0 Cu. Ft. White Electric Dryer with Steam
review_text:
First and foremost this was not the dryer of my choice. My partner wanted us to get a dryer to replace the 30yr old one I had and left it up to me to pick but once I did pick, he seemed a bit disappointed that what I picked was half the price of this dryer, and he gave me a spending limit which was more than this dryer. He decided to pick this one due to what I would consider bells and whistles which I know I would never use and I am the one who does the laundry. As to why my first choice was something a bit simpler but still a large dryer.

The first one we received sadly has an issue. The panel behind the buttons must of been slightly off because the start button only worked 10-20% of the time. Every other button worked 100% to the lightest touch but the start button would not even work if I covered it will all my fingers. The few times it randomly ran it worked perfectly. It never gave me the error for the flint and it dried everything all the way through without stopping way too early. But not being able to get it to ruin 80-90% of the time made it impossible for me.

Luckily the seller was quick and kind enough to help us with the situation, and was happy to get a new one out to use once the one we had was picked up. The seller made the transaction easy, simple and was very quick to respond. So majority of the good review on this is the seller.

We got our new one and all the buttons work. But....now I have to deal with the flint error. I decided to wash a fluffy queen bed cover and the dryer kept alerting it was the filter about every 10 minutes, and the blanket was still damp. I felt like i was stuck babysitting the dryer to make sure it dried this one blanket. I still had 2 bed covers, 3 sheets and another queen blanket ready to start drying in my washer. My work desk isnt far from my garage so I hear it as soon as the warning lets off and I work from home, so for me its irritating but I can work with it. For someone who has to trust a dryer running while they leave home for work or etc, you cant trust to leave this dryer going cause you might come home to linen still damp.

I Just put in a load of clothes and I have to run everything on the heavy cycle because I feel it will never get dry after repeat restarts. I even check the filter and clean out what little if any is in there. I had just checked the time at 10:23 as I walked into the kitchen and by 10:29 it was beeping saying flint build up. I cleaned it out and started it again. 10:40 it is beeping again and I know it hasnt past 60 minutes from when i start it the first time. From what I felt the clothes feel mostly dry, and the issue is when they get slightly dry the move around a whole lot more so more of it begins to pile in the front over the filter region. But at times there may still be damp clothes towards the rear. Due to this bad design it causes the dryer to turn off and sound the alarms. Had the company designed the glass to slightly go in at a slant a bit, not causing heat build up over the flint compartment but to at least keep buildup from happening over it, im sure these dryers would work amazing. Sadly I am not sure as to why they chose the design they did. So even if the tub might seem huge, its not really worth putting a large amount or even one single large blanket in it which really is sad.

Pros: If you have cats &/or dogs that shed a lot, this dryer is amazing. I retired a very well kept 30 yr old dryer that was handed down to me but I had no idea what I was missing out on with a newer dryer. This thing gets all the fine hairs out and one dryer sheet does the job at making everything smell amazing.

Con: The design causes a huge annoyance with larger blankets or larger mix loads due to its fidgety flint sensor. If the company created an item that could easy snap or rest into place above the filter which would keep air circulating and keep clothes off of it, I would be happy to buy it in the heart beat. But sadly dont think anything like that exists yet. Here is hoping

product_title: Bosch 24" 100 Series Stainless Steel Dishwasher
review_text: After a lot of research and pouring over Consumer Reports ratings I settled on a Bosch dishwasher and then visited a number of appliance dealers.  I do not cook a lot so rarely have large pots and pans or large loads so I settled on the price and performance of the 100 series and this one (SHEM3AY55N) stood out immediately and I chose to let the store (Lowe's) deliver and install it.  The installer had my old one out and this one in and up and running in ~30 minutes.  A lot of reviews had commented that the dishes weren't dry (no heat element !) but if you follow the recommended AUTO + SANITIZE setting and use a rinse aid (Finish is supplied but any brand can be used) the dishes come out hot and dry.  The run times are much longer than older machines, 2 1/2 hours for the above setting but the machine is so quiet I had to feel the door to make sure it was running.  Apparently the longer run times are part of the energy efficiency feature. Other reviewers noted a strange smell, probably due to some of the test water being left in the pipes of the machine, and it was true but I ran several empty loads, left the door open all day to help air it out and put a box of baking soda in it when I closed the door at night and the smell is gone.  I've had it almost 2 weeks and have run it several times on a variety of settings just to test it and so far I am delighted with the performance but if you want your dishes dry when it finishes use the AUTO + SANITIZE + rinse agent.  The manual says it will not start if the rinse agent container is empty but that's wrong, it will.  It is attractive design and fits in the standard 24" x 34" opening for most dishwashers but be sure to measure just in case.  Bosch is the quietest dishwasher on the market and I love this model.

product_title: Bosch 24" 100 Series Stainless Steel Dishwasher
review_title: Disappointed - dishes not clean or dry
review_text:
Sadly, I’m disappointed with my Bosch dishwasher. I had high hopes. When my last dishwasher died a spectacular, fiery death I decided to get a dishwasher from a high-end brand. Bosch topped all of the lists at Consumer Reports, so the choice was obvious. My old dishwasher was a mid-range model from a cheap brand, so while it didn’t always perform well, that was no more than what I expected. Unfortunately, my new Bosch doesn’t even work as well as my old dishwasher and cost twice as much as some of the alternatives.

I’ll start with the good first. My Bosch looks nice. It’s very quiet. I like the controls on the top. It’s probably as energy-efficient as claimed (I have no way to check). It’s well designed for installation and maintenance, though some parts are plastic that should really be metal.

Now for the bad.

1) It doesn’t get my dishes clean on normal mode. When I put it on heavy clean it does alright, but not quite as good as my cheap old dishwasher. The acid test is the saucepan with eggs. The Bosch takes three times through to clean it while the old one only took two.

2) It doesn’t dry the dishes, unless maybe you put in rinse conditioner. My dishes always come out wet. My old dishwasher got everything dry without any added chemicals. I expect new appliance to be convenient, not require more effort than antiquated ones.

3) Three hours to wash the dishes. Seriously? I should mention that’s with heavy wash and sanitize, because as I mentioned, regular wash doesn’t get the job done, and who would want unsanitary dishes?

4) This one is trivial, but since I’m on a roll I’ll mention it. All of my appliances play a short pleasant tune to signal they’re done. Not my dishwasher. It just kind of beeps.

In conclusion, I cannot in good conscience recommend this dishwasher.

review_title: Do not buy Bosch dishwasher if you want to drain through an air gap
review_text:
I had a terrible experience using the Bosch dishwasher.
I bought the Bosch dishwater SHEM3AY55N/28 in January 2022. The drain has always been problematic (error code E24). I installed the dishwasher with the drain hose connecting to an air gap, then to the disposal – a standard connection setting. At the beginning the drain cycles may succeed 50% of chances but now down to 10% chance.
Recently I called Bosch customer service. The tech came my house and verified the problem. He said Bosch dishwashers always have problems to drain water completely if the hose is connected to an air gap. He suggested to connect to the disposal directly. He said even an expensive model has the same problem since all Bosch dishwasher uses the same pump, which is not powerful enough. The following is his comment on the service report:
“Client had error code of e24, when I arrived I found in the unit so I had some water and initially tested the drain cycle ensure enough it was draining very slowly. I did not find an installation issue everything was good including the loop for the drain hose. After tracing down where the congestion was, found that the unit drain fine with disconnected from the air gap even though the air gap had no debris inside, advised client that the drain cycle and pump were not designed for a run that long, he should disconnect from the air gap and go straight into garbage disposal as the unit has no issue pumping water out that way”.
So, it is a design issue. How can you have a dishwasher not able to drain through an air gap. No where of the machine’s user manual mentioned it should not be connected to the air gap. I called customer again and try to find a resolution. They do not want to help. The supervisor (Chris) said “it is your installation issue”, shamelessly.
I am going to connect the drain hose directly to the disposal and see if it drains properly and if it leads to backflow (since not using air gap). I will keep you updated.

And on top of all that, it doesn't dry the dishes properly, so we have to empty the contents all over our countertops so that they can dry before we put them away.

The good news is I've learned my lesson: always read user reviews first. And never buy a Bosch dishwasher.

review_title: Bought And Returned This Compact Washer For NOT Being Compact
review_text:
The most important piece of information concerning this washing machine was misquoted, by the vendor specifications, at the store where I bought this unit. A 2.1 cubic foot washer is the best compact available, and of course is unavailable so, given no other option for something that could fill enough to properly wash a Queen comforter, I purchased the new, GE 2.8 cubit Foot top loading washing machine, thinking it was the next innovation. I assumed, based on specs, that the washer was slightly taller, with a slightly deeper basket, resulting in a 2.8 instead of a 2.1 cubic foot load capacity, as widening the machine would be madness.

Given that the width of door frames in the average bathroom in the 1960s, 1970s and 1980s built apartments, condos and houses was between 24 and 28 inches with the 24 inch door size in very common use, more common than the other two options, it would make no sense to produce a compact or portable machine that had a width precluding use. This unit is 24 inches by 24. 5 inches, with no wiggle room. Even with the door to our bathrooms off their hinges, this machine would never fit in any of them, so back in the box and back to the store this went.

The specifications have been updated, where I purchased this, again, 24 x 24.5, and hopefully the same thing won't happen to anyone else, however, for anyone looking at this machine, please be advised that it is too large to fit through any bathroom door in our house, built in the 1970s and, after measuring at a friend's 1960s home we found their doors also measured exactly 24 inches, with about 23.3 between the door frame stops on either side.

Given that a 23 inch machine is the maximum that can fit through what was, for decades, the standard bathroom door size, this machine is simply not workable unless you are using it in a large, standard size washing machine slot in a garage or laundry closet and, if you can fit a 24 inch machine with a low 2.8 cubic foot capacity, you can probably fit a standard 27 inch machine, why bother with a machine that washes so much less and doesn't fill enough to wash a large comforter? It just makes no sense.

I can't recommend this for anyone seeking a compact washer, as a 23 inch width is about as wide as it could be in order to be considered compact, for use in a bathroom with a sink hookup. I also don't recommend this for anyone seeking a washing machine who can accommodate a larger size washer, such as a 27 inch, because the capacity on the 27 inch GE washer far exceeds this and that washer comes with a functioning Deep Fill button, as of 2019. With any luck, someone will design a 2.5 or even a 2.8 cubic foot washer that utilizes a slightly taller tub in a housing of 22 to a maximum of 23 inches, so that I can finally replace my dead Haier 2.1, which was so useful for so many years.

I hope this helps you in your search. I must continue mine for a good 2.1 cubic foot portable. If Ge ever considers a redesign on this, making it a bit taller and thinner, to make it workable for anyone living in an older home, I will post the information on that new machine in this review and will recommend the machine.

product_title: SAMSUNG RF28NHEDBSR / RF28NHEDBSR/AA / RF28NHEDBSR/AA 28 Cu. Ft. Stainless 4-Door French Door Refrigerator
review_text:
I just purchased this (granted, I did it from Lowes, but the review is important) and I couldn't be happier with it.

Also, if you're looking at reviews on Amazon, especially with refrigerators, MODEL NUMBER IS CRITICAL. The manufacturers not only have umpteen models, but some are exclusive to vendors. Don't just read a Samsung, LG or Whirlpool review and think that review is for the exact model you're interested in. Save yourself the hassle and ALWAYS specify the model number in any search, even on Amazon.

I've had the unit for about 2 weeks and I'm amazed at how often my family uses the LED display which is massive.

I financed it since it's what I would have wanted when we finally get around to remodeling our kitchen and I've realized that no company makes a "suite" where one or more parts are crappy and one or more parts are top notch, so I'm going with a mix and match approach to get what I need, anyway.

So several things.

1) I did tons of research as befits a former network engineer and I was amazed at how many top end refrigerators had significant issues with the ice maker and or had issues with the compressors. This Samsung model has been fantastic in that regard, cooling quickly upon initial installation and remaining cold. The ice maker makes GREAT ice at a decent rate. If you need tons of ice, I dunno if any new refrigerator is gonna help you because none make tons of ice quickly. That's just what's real. Those models which might...have issues which may be disqualifying to you. They were with me.

2) I'd never had multiple drawers on the bottom and the configurable drawer (configurable using the LED which can be easy to miss in the novel sized documentation) is wonderful. We use it as the lunchmeat drawer and it really reduces the times the doors are opened.

3) The water filter is top notch and my family actually started drinking the water due to it's much improved taste.

4) The LED does turn off and the brightness can be adjusted. It does not just blast the room with light 24/7. That was a concern for us.

5) The water fills really quickly which is great for me as I use a 30 oz YETI tumbler for my drinks and my old fridge took forever to fill it up. However, the light in the dispenser well is super weak and doesn't really do anything at all.

6) The shelves on the doors are a little narrow so while they fit the standard milk container, in order not to bend it, you need to raise the other shelves which limits what can be stored on the door. If you use the collapsing shelf, you have tall things in front of shorter things and end up playing Refrigerator Tetris. We're new to the fridge, so some of that is on us to better figure out how to configure what we have and to best maximize the space. If you come from a single door or a 2 door french door model, this configuration takes a little getting used to.

7) The LED is Android based, and has Pandora preinstalled which was nice. I just logged in and streamed Pandora while I did the dishes which meant I didn't need to leave my phone out where it could get wet. Not the greatest speakers, but surprisingly nice. If I was going to make my all day spaghetti sauce again or do Thanksgiving, I'll probably break down and get a Bluetooth speaker and pair it with the fridge. I was able to pair my iPhone XS Max to the fridge and stream Pandora with it as well. If you don't want to try to install apps on the fridge, that's a great way to listen to audio books, Spotify or even YouTube. And yes, you can play YouTube in the provided browser.

8) The refrigerator is relatively quiet with the odd knock which is normal. It is not loud, no whine (it's more of a low hum).

9) My family has been very mindful when closing the doors, but if someone carelessly just slams the door, it can pop the other ajar slightly. We haven't tested if the fridge will sound the alarm in this case, but my kids are all adults now, so it's not an issue for them to pay attention to such things.

10) The interior lights are bright LEDs and unless the fridge is packed, there's plenty of light.

Conclusion: The unit looks the part, it functions the part and we couldn't be happier with it. I used to think an LED on a fridge was the height of silliness, but the utility is hard to argue with. It's not frivolous at all.

I also bought the Ring video doorbell and that will allow me to see who's at the front door on the fridge which is nice when I'm waiting on a package (none of the Fedex, UPS or USPS delivery guys knock let alone wait for signatures) or if I'm cooking.

EDIT 4/27/20: After a year of use in a busy household that now numbers 7, I can’t be more impressed. It still looks like new, is far easier to clean the inside than our old fridge and it’s definitely the highlight of our kitchen and the way it’s holding up, we should have this appliance for many, many years.

review_title: Here is my anecdotal experience with Electrolux front load washers
review_text:
I spent a day and a half trying to fix my 6-year-old Electrolux model EIFLS60JIW1 which we inherited with our new home 3 months ago. To summarize quickly, I am now in the market for a new washer because I was unable to fix it and may have hastened its demise. So if you are curious, continue reading for details.

Also, let me say I think getting 6 years of this unit seems ok but I googled around to try to get a sense of how long these units should last and came up with estimates between 10-14 years, but to be fair I think in my case I probably went about the repair wrong in the end and this is one of those regrettable times where I may have actually caused my unit's demise too which is why I am conflicted about how many stars to give. Also, since they no longer make this version I am listing it with the new models above, not so much to warn other consumers like me but maybe to just inform everyone of my anecdotal experience. Besides, from what I can tell looking around on the internet, the Electrolux brand seems to still be highly rated or at least advertised strategically very well because I am no longer sure what to make of all of those "consumer report" websites which seem more and more biased lately after you google, "best front load washer to buy."

Ok so back to focusing on the washer; so it was apparently purchased by the previous owners in July 2015 and appears to have worked fine until now as far as I can tell basically for 6 years. I noticed there was a very small pool of water under and in front of it over the past few days doing 1-2 loads per day. On closer inspection, I saw the door seal had a small part missing portion of rubber where the glass door presses into, spanning about 2 inches in the lower-left portion of the seal so ordered the part from Amazon and replaced it (more on that later). What really prompted us to act was after the small leak got bigger and I noticed at the same time the clothes were still soaked at the end of a cycle. After watching a full 14 min rinse spin cycle finally determined that the thing was not agitating or spinning at all but towards the end of the cycle could hear the motor kick on and sounded like it turning at full speed but still not spinning. Using a very helpful, I have to admit set of videos from repair clinic and appliance parts.com on youtube as a guide, I took back panel off and saw belt had fallen off. After inspecting the belt for cracks I decided to re-install the belt back onto the rotor wheel (mistake perhaps?..should have ordered a new belt, and wheel probably) which was finally feasible after attaching a zip tie to hold a portion of the belt onto the wheel and stretching the rest on. Of note, the wheel itself was also wobbling so found the bolt had loosened and assumed this was responsible for belt eventually falling off in the first place. After tightening the bolt, put back panel on and it worked great again for 4-5 loads then the same problem occured again.

As an aside, while working on this portion of the washer, the door boot seal also came in the mail so I also took off the old rubber seal and reinstalled the new seal. To my disappointment, it still seemed to leak even with the new seal. I do not know if this was due to a defective seal or leaking from a different portion of the washer underneath (related to the stuff going on in the back) where I can't see but I did a double-take and re-inspected my installation for what its worth to confirm that the seal and springs holding it on appeared snug. Anyway, for this reason, I am recusing myself from writing a review on the boot seal since I am not sure on the cause of the leak.

Fast-forwarding backs up to the back of the washer with the belt falling off. So reading online the most common causes seemed to be worn chewed-up belts, a loose wheel (despite re-tightening), or bearings going within the tub itself. I found the wheel itself was loose again and this time there was a lot more black powder-rubber dust stuff all over the back of the tub. Looked like the belt had been rubbing against the back of the plastic tub and the metal wheel itself had actually cut deeply and completely through the tub like a blade near the top portions of the tub. There was now evidence of water dripping out of where the cuts were and pooling in the tray in the back of the washer! I think in retrospect, I should have probably tried to replace the wheel itself and the belt too because thinking back, the wheel was difficult to wrench back on, and even after tightening there was ever so slight bit of play where the wheel attached to the nut.

In conclusion, I like to do my own repairs when there is time to learn more and tinker, and admittedly I sometimes struggle with "repair guy trust issues" (my own demons I am working through), but looking back this was a "penny-wise" move on my part not getting an appliance professional in to do the repair because now the cost of fixing this will approach just replacing the unit.

Also, I want to apologize to the Michigan-based repair clinic and appliance parts .com. I used their youtube videos to do the repairs which were excellent. I thought about it and SHOULD have bought the parts from them as well and not gotten cheap and got the less expensive part from Amazon (97$ vs 140 + 27 one day ship). My laziness is why Amazon is getting too powerful so maybe need to suck it up and pay a little more to support other US companies more often. Again though I have a tough time when I can click once vs type in my address... find credit card... enter card number each time there is a new website but Karma has burned me this time for sure in this case.

review_title: Functional and nice-looking 30" Black Gas Cooktop
review_text:
UPDATED Sept 2020:

After owning this cooktop for over a year, I have some observations to make.

1) The grates and the iron disks that set over the burners look ugly at this point. They are not a porcelain finish so they discolor very easy from cooking splatters which inevitably happen no matter how careful you are. No amount of cleaning will remove these awful discolorations that are bonded to the surface of the iron. It looks bad and friends will ask why you don't clean your cooktop. You can put them in the dishwasher set to 'sandblaster' mode, but it doesn't help much. You can spray oil over the entire grate in an attempt to get it to look more uniform and it will. But when you cook with it, the heat will turn the grate a dark brownish black from the burnt oil and that is just as bad or worse than what you were trying to hide. Face it, there is no practical solution to this problem.

2) The bright aluminum gas distributors that the iron disks set on also get discolored from food splatters and from cleaning agents that you may spray on your top to clean it. Some splatters come off; some discolor the aluminum. Don't make the mistake of putting them in the dishwasher to clean. The detergent will oxidize the aluminum and then you will be really sorry. Yes, I learned the hard way.

At this point, I bought a cover to hide the cooktop. It used to be spectacular when it was new, but now it is just a seemingly well-used cooktop. It does perform well which is the most important consideration, but it is no longer nice to look at. I have to give it 4 stars since it does serve me well. Would I buy again? Hmm, maybe. I have looked at the other brands and most of them have the very same materials which means they will discolor also. I am kind of missing the porcelain coated grates that my former KitchenAid cooktop had. But this Samsung still works much better. ###

========================================
May 2019. I have now owned and used this Samsung Black Stainless Cooktop for 7days. Here are some details that are not specified:

1) Only the control area is Black Stainless. The burner area is black porcelain. This is a good thing since the porcelain is easy to clean. The Black Stainless is also easy to clean and looks very attractive. BTW, it truly is fingerprint resistant.

2) The instructions recommend not to put the Iron Grates into the dishwasher. They are coated, but not porcelain coated. My previous KitchenAid had porcelain coated iron grates that looked nice but they eventually chipped and became dulled with scratches on top. I like the Samsung grates and find that cleaning them is not difficult but I have not burned cheese on them. Also, the Iron Grates have small, silicone rubber feet with inverted dimples that sit snuggly on the small dimples of the cooktop for a firm footing that keeps them in place without scratching the cooktop. Those wipe clean easily.

3) The burners are quick and easy to disassemble for cleaning. They are just 2pieces each except for the middle burner which is 3pieces due to the combination small/large burner-in-one.

4) The controls work smooth and easy. The control for the middle combination burner has a bit of resistance to turning whenever the transition is reached between just the small burner operating alone and both small & large burners working together. It is nice to know when that point is reached so looking under the pot is not necessary.

5) The Blue LED glow that emits from under a control knob whenever it's respective burner is operating is a great feature. It is quick and easy to determine from a distance if all the burners are off! The knobs are easy to remove for cleaning and the underlying Blue LED assembly within the cooktop is protected by a clear rubber gasket. It looks stunning whenever any burner is on with it's hot blue flame and matching Blue LED lighted control.

6) The burners all operate with a distinct hot blue flame and have more than sufficient BTU output to prepare whatever one may desire. That 19,000BTU middle Power burner will definitely heat a large wok for quickly searing vegetables and meats unlike so many smaller BTU output competitors. If one wants access to home cooking power, this is it. Good job Samsung for making a decently BTU powered cooktop. BTW, I have read some reviewers that complain about gas cooktop grates being too high. Hogwash. It absolutely is not necessary to have the burner flames on the bottom of the pots. A small distance between is ideal unless one is trying to smelt lead in a smelting pot! Not!

7) NOTE that the Wi-Fi module at the back right of the cooktop IS REMOVEABLE! It is a simple matter of removing 4 cooktop corner screws and the cooktop mounted burner screws (2 for each burner except the middle that has 3). These screws are all lightly tightened so they come out easy. Slightly separate the cooktop at the back corner and slip the module out. It has a small connection cable with connector that disconnects at the module. Insert the connector into a Module Blank Cover from the provided accessory pack. This module blank cover is then slightly snapped into place. Easily reassemble being sure to GENTLY tighten the 4 cooktop screws and 11 burner screws. It takes about 5minutes start to finish. When finished the Wi-Fi module is gone and no longer protrudes while the cable and connector are held in-place by the Blank Cover. Pretty simple.

That is the summary. This unit looks great and functions perfectly. I don't use the Wi-Fi feature. I would purchase it again. I also own a Samsung refrigerator and a Samsung phone and a Samsung monitor. I have other electronics by Sony, LG, Onkyo, Apple, etc. My other appliances are by KitchenAid. I chose the Samsung cooktop over the KitchenAid cooktop since I wanted plenty of cooking power and I like black in my kitchen for accent. I also wanted the Blue LED controls for easy determination of whether in operation. Oh, I really like the included non-stick Flat Burner Plate that securely attaches on the grate of the left 2 burners. I used it for pancakes and was impressed with the even cooking results. ###

I had to use an angle iron and a 40$ granite cutting wheel on 3 sides to make it fit. 30' units vary in inset size. Lit knobs are awesome, grates fit perfectly and don't slide at all. Burners light immediately and flames are well distributed to avoid hotspots while cooking. I researched this unit pretty well before purchasing and the most common complaint was it's difficult to clean and it discolors over time. I can't speak to that yet but no gas range is ever easy to clean. Regular price almost 1800 dollars for 899...... Lemme 🤔.. Sold! PS. I removed the wifi function, if you can remember to check your phone to see if you shut the range off, you should be able to remember to turn it off before walking away from it. Or..... Check yourself into assisted living and don't cook.

product_title: Samsung 30" Fingerprint Resistant Black Stainless Steel Gas Cooktop
review_title: Nice cooktop, but you have to take some care to keep it looking like new
review_text:
During a recent countertop replacement, we decided to replace our existing cooktop and wanted to try a black model instead of stainless.

The Samsung cooktop looked to be a good choice and arrived in a box that was well packed and contained all of the various parts needed. Note that this cooktop comes with its own pressure regulator which transitions the smaller 1/2" gas line on the unit to the more standard 3/4" gas fittings you use for these devices. Installation was simple enough and I only had to figure out where to cut a new hole for the gas line to emerge. Provided is a foam double-sided sticky tape used to hold the cooktop in place - and I added clear silicone sealant around the rest.

In operation, the cooktop is great! Several different burner options to simmer, cook, and fry anything from small pots to large kettles. My wife and I LOVE the light on the knobs as it looks cool, but more importantly lets you know if a burner is still on.

My only ding - minor - on the product so far is that while it says "fingerprint-resistant", pretty much any spills or drops show up fairly clearly. As well the burner tops also discolored quickly under higher heat. Some of this may be filed under "Ok, it is a Stove" and these things happen, but if you want it to look great you'll just have to keep up with the drips, etc. It's not a big deal, but it looks so good when installed we want to keep it that way.

review_text: My washer is 8 months old and I really loved it until it started to act glitchy about 2 months ago. Finally it started to make a trotting sound, the drum was immobile and I could not open the door or finish the cycle. Pressing the off button did not stop the trotting sound, it had to be unplugged. Electrolux got service for me the next day and the tech got the soaked clothes out and brought in a new computer and latch on technical supports recommendation.  He replaced the parts the following day and the drum still would not move and the trotting sound persisted. He located the sound by the motor and with the machine off, placed his hand on the motor casing to locate the source of the sound. He was thrown against the wall. The whole motor casing was live, the Electrolux rep confirmed the machine did not have the ground wire and ground screw that was supposed to be there. Additionally, there were toy Euro coins inside the back of the machine. It was obvious the machine was not inspected before it left the factory. I am lucky the house didn't go up in flames knowing the has been power going through it without casing since we bought it.  Naturally, the motor is burnt up. I did not feel comfortable just having the motor and power casing replaced as this machine was not constructed properly and I cannot trust it. I went all the way to a corporate supervisor and was told they totally understand how I felt but they would not fix a defective from the start machine. I wonder how they would reply if the tech would have died because of their neglect?

You can adjust the feet by turning the wrench underneath the washer even if it is already stacked with the dryer. I was very happy with the wrenches.  After leveling it works wonderfully. review_title: Buy a range off of Amazon?
review_text:
We were desperate for a new range, as our current one was no longer working and was going to require a costly repair. We plan to do a complete remodel of our kitchen in the next couple of years, and a double oven range was a must. Yet, due to the pandemic, none of the local stores could get us this range for at least 6-8 weeks or longer.

I was a bit concerned ordering this off Amazon, from a retailer several states away. Definitely had to call my credit card company to explain this wasn't a fraudulent purchase on my card! But once they approved the purchase, it all went very smoothly.

It was 3 weeks to the day from order to our door. It was easy to check the progress of our shipment by calling the dispatcher with the shipping company. They always knew where our range was.

My husband met the delivery truck and was very impressed by their detail and work. Before even taking the range off their truck, they examined the route to our kitchen very closely, including measuring narrow spaces and taking pictures of the doors and walls. They unpacked the range, carried it in, and helped my husband get it positioned correctly.

I love having two ovens!! Have been wanting this for years. But due to the small size of our condo, knew I would never have the space for two wall ovens.

I've always thought all appliances were pretty much the same. But this LG range seems so much more "solid" than our last two ranges. It's the same size, but the ovens heat up quicker and the stove elements heat more quickly as well. In addition, the smooth stove top cleans like a dream. My last one was a real challenge to get clean...always had streaks that wouldn't come off. And LG has filled in the little groove around the edges that so easily catches dirt and crumbs.

All in all, this was an easy purchase and I absolutely love this range!

The real problems start when you want to use the oven or even worse, WAY worse, the timer. I would love for whatever ex game coder came up with these things. If you want the oven on, you have to turn the knob in any direction, then look, carefully if you are on the upper or lower oven half of the dial, then stop on the desired function. Then you set the temp and press the start upper or lower button depending on which oven you think you dialed to. If you miss any of this you get to start over again in a few seconds. But the timer is like a testimony to dumb programming. You hit timer, then the + button to start the panic to higher numbers, when I say panic, I mean after you hold the button for a second, it goes to 1 minute, then as quick as you blink, it's at 40 minutes, then you use the - button and try not to blink, then you are at 10 minutes, so wanting 22 minutes, you figure your only chance is to just tap the + button another 12 times. Yep, that gets you there. Only good thing is it makes the glass of wine feel like a reward instead of a guilty pleasure. You develop almost a PTSD about having to set the dumb thing. Biggest deal is it doesn't need to be that hard.... Anyway, excuseless-ly dumb, how many folks really don't have the extra 2 seconds if they have to get to some astronomically high timer setting???? Don't most timer setting hover around the hour mark or lower? It's just annoying every time.

So if you want a range that operates like a range, has UI designed by a coke addict and a miserable glass top to spend hours every week scrubbing on, then you have hit the jackpot with this one.

product_title: Samsung 36" Stainless Steel Gas Cooktop
review_title: You can remove the WiFi dongle.
review_text:
This is an excellent cooktop. Top-rated (by that un-nameable consumer ratings organization), great looking, and lots of burner options, from excellent low-heat burners (for delicate sauces) to a 22,000 BTU intense-heat central burner with an included wok stand that gives Asian food that instant stir-fry quality. I also like that the griddle (at least on the 7755, high-end model) is cast iron, as are all of the cooking grates. This makes the unit quite heavy; it took two big guys to even pick up the box.

The Wi-Fi connectivity is worthless, a gimmick for people impressed with anything "high tech." Of course, you can't use the app to turn on a burner (that would be incredibly dangerous, starting a fire remotely!), or to turn off a burner, but only to see "status". Well, if I'm cooking, I am paying attention to the food (and the burners), and I have all the "status" I need right in front of me. Worse, the Wi-Fi "dongle" (interface add-on) sticks out the back of the unit by a couple of inches, which makes installation almost impossible for most kitchens. I have never seen that much clearance between the back of a cooktop and the backsplash on the wall, so if you want to keep the Wi-Fi appendage you will need to cut out an inch or two of countertop material in the front. If that's granite, that's HARD WORK. And worse, you might end up with an exposed gap in the rear, which will need some sort of cover plate. That's an ugly solution.

Fortunately, it only takes a couple of minutes to remove the Wi-Fi dongle, and the instructions are in the installation manual. (Clearly, Samsung realized that many people will want to do this.) They even include a plastic coverplate to seal the hole that remains after you remove the dongle.

In my case, post-pandemic "supply chain problems" delayed delivery of the unit by almost 10 months, but fortunately my previous cooktop was still functional (with a few anomalies), so I could live with the delay.

product_title: LG LFXS26973D 26.2 cu. ft. Smart Wi-Fi Enabled 3-Door F
review_text:
We bought this refrigerator a few months ago, and while it is attractive, roomy, and fairly well-designed, it does have a couple of problems, one of which is annoying as hell. First, the in-door ice maker jams constantly. We have to open it up and unjam it practically every other day. Second, the surface is so painfully delicate, it scratches if you look at it wrong.

But neither of those is the worst thing. No, that would be the unbelievably annoying “ding-dong, ding-dong” sound that emits loudly every time the door is open for longer than 60 seconds (and yes, I timed it). It is the Alarm From Hell, and while its purpose is to alert you if you leave the refrigerator open, the mentally-deficient engineer who designed it has apparently never had to put away groceries or clean out a refrigerator. I cannot stress strongly enough how infuriating it is to lug in a bunch of groceries, and then to be electronically bitched at the whole time I'm putting them away. I have literally taken to putting two items in, quickly closing the door, opening it again to put away two more items, quickly closing it again, repeat, repeat, repeat ad nauseum.

My husband did a search online to see if there is any way to adjust the amount of time you are given before it starts shrieking, but apparently there isn't (that would make far too much sense!). Evidently, 60 seconds is believed by LG to be the maximum length of time needed to put away a trunkload of groceries. If you buy this damn thing, I hope you are faster than I am!

review_text:
I replaced a $1200 Thermador cooktop with a $389 Fridgidare and so far I'm happy that I did.

Installation was more difficult that I expected; they didn't bother to install brackets for my previous unit, so I had to install brackets on my granite. I didn't like the suggested method (silicone only) so it added a day to the process to do it more securely. I also had to cut a hole in the wall because the genius installers left the box exposed for the wiring, but there was no way to get to the clamp. Patching that is another project in my future.

The reason I like this unit was 1) It was crazy cheap 2) It had a low powered and high powered element in the front, which fits my cooking style. "Quick Boil" is 3000 watts; I do my boiling in an instant pot, but the extra power is useful when stir frying or searing steaks. Even the smaller inside element is 1600 watts. My previous cooktop had 2 1200 in the front and a 2500 and 2000 watt in the rear. You can't stir fry on the rear element easily.

I feel like this unit is a bit more "glassy" than my previous unit; a bit more fragile. Time will tell how it holds up.

A downside is that I have to re-learn how to cook my favorite dishes, as the settings and power is very different. The Quick Boil element will burn fried potatoes on 3 in a couple of minutes. On the bright side is that the wok heats up in half the time.

review_title: Major brand makes a big difference

Amazon eventually credited me after pushing hard and escalating due to the safety and fire hazard even tho I had the cooktop for months before trying to install it and seeing the problem. This unit just feels more substantial and durable. The wiring is perfectly suitable for most American houses and the instruction manual actually makes sense.

As for performance, wow. I had LP gas for many years and havebt used electric for a long time. I was not looking forwsrd to the slow responsiveness compared to gas, but this aspect has come a LONG way. The burners are precisely temped and respond quickly to input changes. The rapid boil/ hi on the bottom right high input burner is FAST. I tested cooking bacon on high and no joke, 2 or 3 minutes and done.

So happy with my cooktop.

I bought this cook top back in January. One of the reasons I bought it was because it's a Frigidaire. I love the cook top, but one of the burners stopped working after only a couple months. review_title: Just impressive. Fast, clean - much better than gas or conventional electric
review_text:
I have always been a fan of cooking with gas. Just hate electric coil stoves. So while induction is not really new, I had no experience with it and wondered if it could really be better than gas. WELL IT IS. This thing has both a lot more power than my gas cooktop did, as well as much finer control on lower settings, as well as absolutely instant response to control changes. I love having a fixed number to press, rather than just vaguely twisting a knob and peering under the pot to set the flame height by eye. This boils water almost twice as fast as any gas or electric cooker I've ever seen, yet at the same time has much lower and more consistent warming settings. I cooked some spaghetti (quickly) drained and then added sauce, keeping the whole pot on the stove on setting 1 and it kept perfectly warm for 40 min without burning or crusting at all to the bottom of a stainless steel pot. Let me tell you, that would not happen on any other range I've ever used. To cook rice I used to have to place an additional gas burner grate on top of the other to get the pot further from the flame, because low was not quite low enough. On this, after boiling on 9 I just set it to 2 and let it simmer for 20 min never lifting the lid - perfect as a rice cooker.

Instead of paying twice as much for a Bosch or a Samsung, I decided to get this and a couple of really nice French induction capable copper pots. (De Buyer Prima Matera.) Yep, I had to get rid of a set of non-induction ready stainless cookware. But I decided that having two really great beautiful evenly cooking pots rather than a whole set of things I hardly ever use was a good trade. The cast iron I use works great, as well as an All-Clad saucepan and another big stainless stockpot. I used a magnet on the bottom to test all my pots before getting this.

A few minor cons:
The huge round burner in the center is a little puzzling, I don't have a pot or anything nearly that big in diameter (a full 12"). Seems like a bit smaller and re-positioned more evenly would be a better trade but it works.

There is a bit of a buzz hum as well as a small fan noise, but it's fairly low and not really objectionable. It is loudest on P or "power boil" but still not that bad. I'm really sensitive to noise but honestly whatever you are cooking with it's steaming and bubbling and frying sounds will be louder than the hum.

There are really only two power supplies, each split and supplying two of the burners. This means if you want two things to heat up really fast, you need to choose two burners not sharing the same power supply. They also recommend setting one on max and waiting a bit before setting another one on max. This is explained in the instructions, but better to know this limit before you buy. I don't know, maybe the more expensive types don't have such a limitation. I seldom use more than 2 burners at once so it's not really an issue. Not sure I've ever used all four burners at once but I'm sure some people do.

On low settings it is true that the power cycles on-off. However unlike the old style electric coil burner, or a microwave, the cycle is fast like once or twice a second, rather than once every 20 sec or something. The result is even heating and no noticeable pulsing billowing and overheating as with coil elements. And the noise while cycling is fairly faint.

The black glass top has a fine pattern of silver dots and lines, which I guess I didn't really notice from the photos. The pattern may hide slightly the streaks on the glass. It is easy to clean the glass of spills and oil but pretty hard to get it perfectly rid of streaks. At any rate is a huge improvement over all the grates and cavities and wells and white (why!) surface of my old gas cooker that was just a nasty job to clean.

I am getting some silicone burner covers for this to help prevent scratches from the heavy pots on glass. None so far but seems inevitable.

I did get an AMZ extended warranty, but in the box is a card with a much cheaper ext. wty program from Frigidaire. Wish I had know this before hand. It's like 3 extra years for $30. The one I got was I think 4 yrs for $100. Oh well.

Only had this for about 10 days but will edit this if anything goes amiss.

All in all, a very reasonable cost to get into induction cooking with a lot more pluses than minuses. If that seems like a lot of cons they are really only minor considerations because this is still twice as good as any cooktop I've ever used.

review_title: Great cooktop, great price, here's the opinion of a first-time induction user
review_text:
I am extremely satisfied with my Frigidaire induction cooktop. I looked at a lot of options that were cheaper but the reviews were too hit or miss to make me comfortable, so instead I spent a few hundred extra to go with this option and I'm very glad. Here is an in-depth review from a first time induction user:

I remodeled my kitchen and was really opposed to keeping my electric cooktop; I just didn't like it. I didn't have much room in the budget to pay someone to run gas lines so I did some research and was drawn to several features of induction; namely, the speed with which it boils water/liquids and the energy efficiency (no wasted heat like you get with gas). Secondarily, I liked that the burners don't get super hot. Scraping burned-on food off of the electric cooktop was one of my least favorite tasks ever.

I did stop by a kitchen showroom to look at the induction options and luckily they had several models that I could demo and they also had pans of water to try out the boil function. When I saw for mine own eyes water that boiled in less than a minute, I was hooked. The cooktops I saw were 3-4 times as expensive as this option. I do not regret for a single moment not paying the extra money. I also do not believe that the difference in functionality reflects the difference in cost; this model does not work exponentially worse nor did the expensive ones work exponentially better. This cooktop is a great value.

First I'll address the noise that some have complained about. Yes, from time to time, the cooktop can be noisy. Sometimes a fan comes on, other times you can hear buzzing, particularly when using power boil, and very seldom I have heard some screeching but it is usually remedied by going up or down a power level or even just simply adjusting the pot on the burner (I noticed all of these things with the $2000 models in the showroom as well). Generally speaking, the noise is no louder than the sound of the food that's cooking. Sure, an electric range will not make the same amount of noise but electric ranges don't cook nearly as well. Gas ranges also make noise. So does basically every other appliance in your kitchen when you use it.

I find the layout of the burners to be very smart. The large center burner is big enough to fit my cast iron dutch oven which I cook with regularly but I can also use smaller pots on it, as the burner will adjust to only heat the area that it is in contact with. That's the beauty of induction. With electric, if your pan is too big or small for the designated burners, that's too bad, you either have to try not to roast your fingers over the exposed parts of the burner or deal with the edges of your pan not getting directly heated.

Another great feature of induction is that the burner will not get too hot to touch. While it does get quite warm, I have touched it shortly after removing a pot and not gotten burned. This is really convenient when food spills because it will not burn onto the cooktop. I simply remove the pan, wipe things down, and put the pan back. The cooktop also conveniently pauses heating when a pan is removed and resumes automatically when it is placed back. It saves energy by automatically shutting off if no burners are on or if no pan is placed on a burner for longer than 30 seconds.

You will have to purchase induction-compatible cookware. This was not a downside for me as I'd already planned on purchasing a high end set to replace my 10 year old non-stick pots and pans that were starting to flake. If handled with care, a few high end pans and a cast iron or two will meet your needs well and last for a long time (hand wash, no dishwasher, no metal utensils).

I think the only complaint I can think of at this point is that the cooktop does not respond instantaneously to touch. There is about a half-second delay between touching a button and the change occurring. This was primarily an issue as I was getting used to what heat levels to use and accidentally boiling pots over a few times (don't leave the power boil on once the water is boiling or you'll have a mess, turn it down a few notches and it will continue to boil). Now that I understand how to use the cooktop properly, I can anticipate when something might boil over or splatter and turn the heat down ahead of time.

I hope this info was helpful. The bottom line is, this is a great option at a great price. If you're considering it, just do it. It's worth it.

Turns out there is a very easy fix to the uneven cooking that many are experiencing.

Option1: dont call the manufacturer, this is a waste of time. Call any authorized service in your area. Once they come to your house, look for option2 below to help them fix it

The cooktop will now perform as designed.

Interestingly, Frigidaire now glues these little legs so they dont move.

Very uneven cooking. You will be rotating pots as the largest burner is incredibly uneven in temperature. Eggs on one side of the pan will burn to coals while the other side just starting to get warm. It is that bad.

Purchased this to replace an older radiant cooktop.

PROS:
* Installation was super easy - took less than 30 mins

* Temperature control is much faster and more precise than a radiant cooktop
* Mostly no burnt-on food if something boils over. If you're cooking something for a long time, the cooktop will eventually get hot enough to cause some foods to stick, but it's not nearly as bad as a radiant cooktop.

CONS:
* When compared to a dial, the touch control can sometimes be hard to set exactly where you want it. You have to drag your finger and sometimes it can take a few tries before you get it to the power level you're looking for.

* The middle (i.e. largest) element seems to heat a bit unevenly. I used a 12" skillet to cook breakfast sausage patties and noticed that the sausage in the very middle of the pan cooked much faster than the sausage located around the perimeter.
* Although it's much easier to clean than a radiant cooktop, it's not as simple as "wipe it with a sponge after cooking and you're done". If anything boils over or splatters, you'll still need to spend some cleaning it.

Overall, I would buy this again because it represents an excellent value and the cons I listed are mostly minor things that I can work around.

First of all, the controls are weirdly positioned. In most cooktops in my life they use those little icons to identify which switch controls which burner. Here it's not the case. Yes, you can easily figure it out, but it was weird to see it like that initially.

Then, there's a power switch which controls everything... Including the timer. There are times when we used our old cooktop's timer for other things, such as when we had something in the oven for instance. Here, if the cooktop is not "on", every time you want to use the timer you have to first turn it on, which is annoying. And talking about annoying, the chime sound this timer makes is a pain. OK, it's noticeable. But it's annoying.

Lastly, the physical position of the burners is not great. There's a HUGE one in the middle surrounded by the others. We'd rather have them a bit more spaced and maybe have the large one in one side and the smaller in the other, like we had our previous unit.

Again, it does its job, looks great and it's not bad at all. We just wished it didn't have those minor issues.

product_title: FRIGIDAIRE FGIC3666TB Gallery 36" Electric Induction Cooktop, Built-in 5-Burner, Vitroceramic Glass, Black
review_title: Product is very fragile, does not ship well. A lemon arrived at my house.
review_text:
On the plus side, this induction cooktop would have 5 stars if it got here in good functional condition. It worked very well after the first visit by Sloan Appliance Repair, an excellent shop. I look forward to using the completely repaired or replaced configuration, whenever that happens.
Don't order this online. Pay whatever extra it is to a good appliance store which will deliver, install, test.
I don't know if it was bad quality control at mfr Electrolux, shipping damage, or both. If we had not procrastinated 5 weeks as I am an old 155-LB weakling, we could have done an Amazon return/exchange.
It turned out that I could remove our radiant cooktop and install this one. Then when I closed the breaker the indicators went through an almost-normal startup sequence, then it was very hard to get any response from the controls. The most I could get was an error code indicating missing or defective temperature sensor.
Because Sloan is in high demand, the soonest appointment they could give me was 2 weeks out. The technician checked it, opened it, and discovered connections that had fallen apart. Also, the touch-sensing control card was not against the underside of the glass, because the tabs of its plastic frame had broken off. He ordered a new card, and advised me it would take a couple of weeks to come in. We placed a washcloth folded twice under the broken card to hold it in place. After assembly, the unit worked perfectly except that the touch points and indicators were a little out of place.
What I mean by worked perfectly: Functionally this is a very good design, and it's _induction._ I could go on about how well all the features work, but that would be very long.
This includes the basic induction cooking difference: The traditional radiant glass top is sluggish. It heats the glass first to some insane temperature, so the glass can heat your pan. If you get something to a boil, when you turn the heat down, it takes a long time for the glass to cool enough to stop the boil. You have to get in there and move the pan off the hot spot. And then, I'm not so skillful that I can prevent spills. I often spill food or stir it out of the pot. The extremely hot glass bakes spills to a crisp quickly. As I am not a neat freak, my crispy spills turned to sticky char with repeated ops.
An induction top, like a gas stove, lets the pot cool down as soon as you reduce the heat. If some directions say "remove from heat," you can turn the heat off and there you go. The glass is no hotter than the pot, and cools just as quickly. The glass is too hot to touch, and H appears to so indicate.
Today I boiled some water for an instant food. I could see the water start to swirl in seconds. When it came to a big frothy boil, I reduced from Power Boil to 6 and the froth settled right down.
The tech brought the new control card a few days ago. It seemed to work fine at first. The next day, I was buffing the glass with a paper towel and the unit started beeping as it does. I think the control had become sensitive to static charge. I could not turn it on. It worked after I held a moist towel to the glass for a while. This morning when I tried the first few times to turn the unit on, it would only come up in Locked mode. I had to get patient and work out how long to hold my finger on Lock, to unlock. Then I could fry my eggs. Sometimes when I have the one burner going, I can't start another one. I have called on Sloan to come back out.
To summarize--
* When this model works, it works very well. If your local store's installer puts one in and it's good, I think it will work well for a long time.
* This design does not ship well, at least in single boxes instead of stacked on pallets. The first one we ordered was sold through Amazon by a distant appliance store and when the truck arrived, the driver came to my door and explained that he discovered our item was a box of broken glass. The second one, same store, we got a call that the item would not arrive. I got the impression that it broke en route. Amazon disqualified that store and got this possible lemon directly from Electrolux (mfr of Frigidaire). There was a puncture, so I opened the box and saw perfect glass. I should have, as we always hear, reported the damage to the carrier and Amazon.
I am going to ask Sloan if they can just get me a replacement unit.
On the feature ratings below, 5 stars on each of those specifics.

review_text:
I swapped this cooktop in for an Amana conventional Ceran cooktop. It was perfectly good, b weut slow, never seemed to get hot enough, and a pain to clean any spill-over burns. I wanted something better.

Induction is a dream. I can boil water now faster than the microwave. Really! Pasta now in 10min, instead of 40. It seems to cook about 4x faster. The 10 power levels affect the pans quickly so I have a lot better control and less burn. And the food is hot when served. It feels like I cut dinner prep in half.

It's easy to clean because the glass hardly gets hot and the spill over doesn't burn. I did buy a few new skillets, but didn't really need too. I found that most pans on the shelves were Induction compatible.

It is different then a conventional electric cooktop. It does have a little fan inside for the electronics that's noticeable - but not loud. They also can sometimes make the pans "sing"/rumble a bit. I found just moving the pan a bit eliminated the noise.

The could do a better job with communicating the meaning of the chirps & flashing lights. My 1st test was to boil the big pasta pot, but within a few seconds of putting the pot on the burner - the control started flashing "P" what? I didn't see P in the manual. after 30 seconds the burner shut off. try again on a different burner, same. Try the smaller pot - bingo. works. I suspect that the big pot (stainless side with induction bottom) wasn't magnetic enough to work well. The other chirp - happens when the top is off, and I'm cleaning it. I'm still not sure, but suspect that its saying something is on the burner.

I did take peoples advice on install and took off the glass and check the generators for proper placement. 4 of the 5 we're off the locators. repositioning is easy once I saw the locator tabs on the under pan. just re-install the rubber feet in the slots on the generators and then place on the locators on the pan. I suspect the issue is with shipping, if the box is stored upside the generators likely drop off the locator tabs and get moved around knocking the rubbers off.

a few installation comments.

My old cooktop was installed with a foam gasket around the edge. To old to be reused, and nothing similar came in the box, I opted to use a 1/8" caulk rope(intended for windows). was troublesome since it wasn't sticky and fell into the hole when I tried to center the top. Unfortunately the caulk didn't compress well, leaving gaps. I think a better approach would to have used a bead of silicone around the edge of the glass and drop it into the hole and let it squeeze out for a good seal.

The unit comes with 2 wide-angle brackets that screw into the countertop(butcher block here so no issues) and help support the weight of the unit. Once installed, there's 1 screw per side used to tighten the brackets to the bottom of the unit. The installation guide says to install 2mm below the level of the countertop. Its' about the thickness of the bracket.

It's important that the brackets be installed on the exact center line where you'll place the top, so the bracket hole will line up with the hole on the bottom of the unit case. Note that the sides of the brackets have slots so leave some slack with the screws, so you can slide the bracket to align the screw holes.

review_title: Uneven Heating, high-maintenance surface, inaccurate sensors
review_text:
This is our second induction cook-top. Our first one lasted 10 years w/o a problem until it failed. We've used this Frigidare unit for 6 weeks. The burners don't heat evenly, not even close. When bringing a liquid to a boil, it will boil exclusively in one quadrant of the pan. You'd be likely to burn something more viscous if you didn't constantly stir it, even on a lower setting.
Another drawback is that the markings for burner locations are painted on top of the cook-top. They were embedded within the glass on our earlier model. The Frigidare marks will undoubtedly wear off over time. Instructions for this unit caution to not move pans around on the surface, claiming this is to avoid scratching. More importantly, it will probably remove the burner marks. It is natural to slide a pan, particularly when making minor adjustments.
The last disappointment has to do with the sensors that identify whether or not a pot is properly positioned over the center of the burner. They are not accurate. Sometimes it detects that a pot is not centered...burners won't come on in that case...when it is visually centered and simply turning the unit off/on again fixes the problem without moving the pot. Other times, moving the pot off center, visually, fixes the problem...w/o moving it back to the apparent center. Either the marks for the burner locations are off or the sensors or both.

But, the biggest problem: while washing a bathmat, a few towels or any small load, the machine always gets off balance in the spin cycle, begins violently knocking against the outer cabinet, and then, STARTS TRAVELING! After 25% of the washes, the washer needs to be pushed back into position after traveling 6-12 inches away from the wall. THIS IS INSANE! It weighs 160lbs and still travels freely like my self-propelled lawn mower!
I've already wedged it in, taped it to an adjoining cabinet, and tied it to the dryer. The next attempt will be to tie it to the rear wall, e.g. Ikea dressers. Others have commented on the lack of a dedicated SPIN ONLY cycle, which I concur. When put in SPIN ONLY mode, it goes into a cycle of adding water, spinning, and adding more water. Again, highly counter-productive. In short, this machine seems to have a mind of its own. I don't think I'll be returning it. I don't think it will last the 12+ years my last Whirlpool lasted. And, I cannot recommend others to buy this GE model. Please, take this review seriously. I have nothing against GE, but am just passing on my experiences with this washer.

product_title: GE APPLIANCES GTW465ASNWW, White
review_text: I work for an appliance repair company. I deal with washing machine problems every day. This is by far the best washer I've ever owned. NO problems with being off balance (bulky loads will cause the tub to wobble a little but it's designed to do that so it doesn't have to stop the cycle with and off-balance error code like many washers). Loading the washer properly is the key to having it work well.  I love that I can set the water depth and the extra rinse feature is a bonus. A complete cycle of laundry done in less than 20 min. If I have to find something negative I'd say it's not "whisper" quiet like the description states. It sounds like a normal washer. Behind the door of the laundry room I barely hear it. People complaining about the washer being off balance are likely wrapping their blankets, jeans, towels, etc around the agitator (which is the wrong way to load a washer) or they're stuffing it like a commercial washer at a laundry mat. They probably didn't read the manual which explains how to use the washer and recommendations for load size and water levels for each cycle selection. Auto-soak mode does a good job of going after heavy stains

The big capacity is a double-edged sword. If you are below 5' tall getting that last sock will be a strain.

review_title: Lives up to Consumers Reports Best Buy
review_text:
Read every review on Amazon, bought locally with 5 year extended warranty because I was nervous about the negative reviews. Don't think I needed the extra warranty since I am not having any real problems.

I am very happy with performance and cleaning but had to adjust to a little different setup and use:

1. The unit must be mis-leveled. When your level says level front to back/left to right the drum wasn't centered and that's what had to be perfectly centered by un-leveling or it will sound like it will explode. (Just like the manual describes in leveling) You can NOT trust leveling the cabinet for the drum to be centered.

Edit: Hey LG - put a dot or cross hair in the center of the see through top to make the drum centering operation take minutes instead of hours with level, test with heavy load, listen for banging, repeat this until it runs quiet. (Took me 4 repeats)

2. With old agitator washer you could throw everything in a load- towels, sheets, jeans, shirts etc - Now, you really must seperate loads by fabric density/size or the machine will be out of balance, generate more noise, and most likely wear faster. If you do throw everything together - use the bedding cycle - fills tub more.

3. If you don't like the water saving cycles the bedding cycle fills the tub completely- I use this a lot on loads that are heavily soiled or very large loads - not just bedding.

4. I think consumers reports got it right - very good washer and a best buy (2021). It takes a few changes in how you sort loads - but worth that small adjustment.

This model is the lowest priced model with slightly less features but has everything I need.

review_title: Looks nice, quiet, doesn't clean well, quickly failed
review_text:
My old dishwasher broke and began leaking, so it was time for a new one. I wanted a quality unit that did a good job washing, and that had a third rack on the top. I read some reviews, and this one looked like it fit the bill.

Best Buy delivered quickly, and I installed the unit myself. I was impressed with the quality and design, as well as the relative ease of installation.

One of the main features of this dishwasher, being highly energy efficient, is that it pops the door open at the end of the wash cycle, to aid in the drying of the dishes. This worked great...the first four times I used it. Then it stopped working, and it has never popped the door open since. This is a problem, because now your dishes end up sitting, soaking wet, and never drying - unless you happen to be around and remember to open the door manually.

A quick visit to the Samsung community support website and I discovered that there are MANY people who have this dishwasher who are experiencing the exact same problem: it works for the first 3-4 washes, and then never works again. It appears to be a design fault.

A second feature I wanted is the much vaunted "Smart Things" support, where you can hook the dishwasher to your Wifi, and control it via your phone. That way you can start the dishwasher remotely when you need to, or check on its status. This works great...except you have to enable it by pressing a button on the dishwasher. EVERY SINGLE TIME. You can't start the dishwasher remotely, because in order to enable the remote features, you have to first turn it on by pressing a button on the dishwasher. When the cycle finishes, it turns itself off again. This completely defeats the purpose of having remote control over the dishwasher! What an idiotic design decision!

Lastly, and most importantly, this dishwasher does not clean dishes ANYWHERE near as well as my old dishwasher did - a unit that cost half the price of this one. If there are many things on the main upper rack, the things on the top rack hardly get touched by spray, and remain dirty. I am OFTEN finding dishes on all of the racks that are still dirty after a wash cycle, and I end up running the wash cycle twice in order to get things clean, which kind of negates any energy or water savings.

So in conclusion, this dishwasher doesn't wash dishes very well, doesn't dry dishes at all, has major design faults, and the extra money I spent to get the Smart Things remote integration is a waste, because you have to manually press a button on the dishwasher first every time to enable it.

Choose a different dishwasher from a different manufacturer. I wish I had.

UPDATE: Samsung sent out a repair tech to fix the door under warranty. He replaced the solenoid that pushes the door open. He told me that he was "fixing one of these almost every day."

Result: It worked!!! For two whole days. Then it stopped working again. It's obviously a design fault. How did they not catch this widespread problem in product testing?? My original opinion remains: don't buy this piece of junk.

ANOTHER UPDATE: The unit is now 10 months old, the door release still works intermittently, but now the much marketed "linear wash" system has completely stopped working, and as a result the dishwasher no longer cleans dishes. What a PIECE OF JUNK this thing is, I'm sorry I spent my hard-earned cash on it. I'll now be spending even more money on purchasing an extended warranty for this lemon, because clearly I'm going to need it.

product_title: Samsung Appliances DW80R9950UG Smart Linear Dishwasher in Black (2019)
review_title: Incredible disappointment, numerous problems, no support
review_text:
This dishwasher is loaded with problems that Samsung knows about but refuses to address.

It has a "water wall" arm instead of a spinner on the bottom. That is supposed to clean better because it doesn't miss the corners. It also has double the water on the left-hand side that can be optionally added. That's just one more thing to break... and it does. The water wall moves back and forth and the jets are in the back of the washer. They squirt the wall as it moves and the water is deflected upward to the dishes. The water wall uses a magnet to determine its position. Magnets lose their magnetism in heat, so guess what that means... it stops working when the magnet gets weak. If you stick another magnet to the factory magnet, it may get it working again. Search "waterwall magnet" at community.samsung.com to find these problems. That's the site where Samsung tells you to pay for a repair because it's not their problem. You'll see the owner's frustration.

Another problem is the door is supposed to open at the end of the cycle. Two little plungers push it open. They work for several weeks and then stop. They either don't open the door or they get stuck and you can't close the door. Search for "auto release" at the above site to see lots of owners complaining.

Samsung does not have many repair centers and some independents won't work on them. I found one who did, but he said they were hard to work on and some parts are just not available (like the circuit boards). The Samsung parts site has no parts available, zero, zip, nada. Everything shows back-order. I asked the chat-rep and he confirmed they have no parts. The chat rep told me to have their service rep come out (a six hour round trip charge plus the repair charge.) That would cost more than the dishwasher.

I got an error code that said it would not drain. It did drain, however and no water was left. The drain worked fine, but it gave an error code every wash. The service tech thought it could be either the case break or the pump, he couldn't determine which from the codes. Either would be a couple hundred dollar repair and might not fix it.

Samsung should recall these dishwashers and fix these design defects, but they won't even repair them when they break, much less recall all of them and fix them. I would never buy a Samsung appliance again based on the experience with this dishwasher. You'll see lots of folks on the Samsung site have the same opinion.

I told Samsung that at this point, we were not interested in another repair attempt. I requested a refund on the dishwasher so I can buy a different brand. I also sent over the contractor estimate to replace our flooring for the second time.

They want us to procure multiple contractor quotes, despite the current difficulty in finding a contractor available. The claims representative has begun ignoring our emails and refusing to escalate the incident to her managers despite multiple requests.
