review_text: My new french door refrigerator freezer motor sounded odd from the get-go, and completely stopped cooling 4 months after being placed in service.  The refrigerator came with a standard Magnuson-Moss repair-or-replace warranty.  Upon contacting GE I got onto a customer service do loop, in that the website asked for my zip code and then said I need to call GE, and the customer service ARU would not do anything other than text me the website address.  When I finally reached a person, she acknowledged my "urgent" (her word) situation and passed me to a customer "advocate," the first in a long line of recorded messages and unhelpful GE employees I reached after long waits on hold.  This advocate advised that GE had no one to help me in my area (house is in a small town).  I naively thought this meant they would locate a service provider and would actually do so, because honorable people and companies do what they say they will do, particularly when they say it in writing.  Over the next two weeks and 19 telephone calls, all involving wait times, GE sending someone to the wrong address in the wrong town, GE advising me two different times of companies who would be handling the service call who had never heard from GE and who did not service GE appliances at all, GE finally admitted that it would not service my appliance and had no intention of replacing it.  So, two weeks wasted, with no refrigerator over the holiday season, and I was left with a dead refrigerator and on my own to solve the problem.  It would have been possible, at some expense, to send a repair person from a nearby town, or to simply ship a new refrigerator, so the obvious conclusion is that GE does not honor its written warranties if it determines that to be expensive. I contacted GE executives directly and got the purchase price less delivery charges reimbursed, and of course got no sympathy for being left to dispose of the worthless GE refrigerator I'd been left with.

I solved this problem by covering my ice machine with a towel, and when I open the lid I just place the towel over it, when it is in the open position. It works, and The lid no longer unexpectedly closed in the middle of me accessing ice.
Another note for would be owners of this contraption, is that naturally, as the machine makes its batches of ice, the longer it is left to do so, the larger that ice cubes become. I am assuming that this is due in part to the cooling coils becoming more cold after each batch, and also that the water is somewhat becoming more cool, as it is turned into ice , and melted = cold water lol.
This particular machine offers two setting small and large, in reference to the size of ice cube you would prefer. I leave mines on large, and have not tried the smaller setting yet.
These ices cubes are great for use in water bottles, and Hydro Flasks, and will fit in most openings. I have even fit smaller ones into plastic water bottle openings ( one-by-one ).
I have no gripes with this machine, and am glad that I decided to invest in one, I no longer have to sacrifice, frezzer space, nor do I have to buy bags of ice, unless I'm filling a cooler for the beach.

review_text:
Great for my needs! I eat ice. A LOT of ice! This machine is great, but I have some tips to make your experience easier. Bear with me here, it's worth the work.
1 - You will need 2 ice bins for your freezer. 1 for the fresh ice and one for the hard frozen ice. The fresh ice comes out wet and porous and soft. (perfect for eating!)
2 - Put refrigerated water, or even ice water in the machine. The first batch will come out MUCH better the colder the water is!
3 - Stir the fresh ice into some already hard frozen ice until it dries and turns white. Dump half of it in your other ice bin. Keep doing this with each batch or two. This will prevent you from having one big "ice cake" that's a real pain to deal with!
4 - ALWAYS drain and rinse your machine after you use it, and leave the lid propped open. This will keep your machine ice and fresh.

I'm so so happy with this purchase!

review_title: Great while it lasted!  But there should be a smaller setting for cube size.
review_text:
This lasted through 1-1/2 years of steady, frequent use before it died. While it worked, I loved it! I like to chew ice and don't want to damage my teeth. This ice maker has two sizes - Medium and Large. It calls the two sizes Small and Large, but there's not much difference between them and the "small" is too big. When this died, I replaced this model - ICE101 - with the larger Igloo ICE103. The ICE103 has three sizes, so I hoped that the 'small' would be smaller, but I learned that those three sizes are really Large, X-Large and XX-Large. What it calls "small" is the size of the Large for ICE101. In other words, if you pay more, you get more sizes yet even less choice than before! The ICE103 is larger, which would help if you want more capacity, but it takes more space, and I regret buying it. I wish I had simply bought another ICE101 as a replacement.

What broke after a year and a half was apparently the electronics - no matter how many times I reset it, it kept flashing first that it was out of water and then that it was full of ice. Neither of those was true, but it kept going back and forth.

Earlier, I had thought it was broken because it said that it was full of ice even when it wasn't, but I checked other reviews here and learned that this sometimes happens if the ice basket isn't down all the way. This was a pain - it sometimes decided this even though I had not moved the ice basket. since the day before. I eventually learned that it helped to splash some water around the edges of the basket. I don't know if the water helped the basket slip down further, or if it just got the sensors wet, but it helped.

Overall, I would buy this again, and wish I had repurchased it rather than replacing it with the larger ICE103. The cubes were great for chewing - I just wish that the small setting was a bit smaller.

review_text: When I purchased this ice maker it was called 'Igloo' not 'RCA' but appears to be the same machine.  Don't expect the touted 26 pounds of ice per day.  The water supply tank holds about 2 liters; the machine will make five ice cubs in approximately thirteen minutes.  The cubes are dropped into a  basket above the water tank, an unrefrigerated chamber.  The 32 degrees ice begins to melt immediately and drains back into the water supply tank.  You could set up a relay team to harvest the ice as it is made, and whisk it to your refrigerator's freezer compartment.  You will also have to replenish the water feed tank because two liters of water will not produce 26 pounds of ice.  I use this ice maker in the master bedroom.  It supplies enough ice for my 30-ounce thermal tumbler.  Because this ice is at most only 32 degrees Fahrenheit, unlike the ice from your home freezer which is kept at minus five or more degrees below zero Fahrenheit, It quickly melts when exposed to room temperature water or beverages.  If you hate 'warm' tap water like me, it may be worth the expence.  The ice maker has worked without mechanical/electrical problems to date.

review_title: Might Work for a Camping Trip, or a One Time Party...
review_text:
Purchased this item and 8 months later it is useless.

Was very excited to get this and hopeful that the days of buying ice would be over! For the first week it was so neat - a little noisy, and the ice cubes melted incredibly fast - but then, what do expect when they all have holes in them... So there are these rods, and they get super cold, enough to freeze the water around them - so you have these little playing dice sized cubes with a hole in the middle, where the rod was.

Melted REALLY fast, and always kind of watery - the bin wasn't cold enough to keep them frozen for long at all, but it was okay for what we needed... for a bit...

The bin and all the parts inside started getting moldy SUPER fast. We figured with constant use we could go maybe a week without shutting it down and doing a thorough cleaning - but no, we ended up just using the ice to keep the sodas cold. I wouldn't put ice from this machine inside my drink now for anything - there are too many tiny areas that are too difficult to get to and I could never get it completely clean.

But still - it kept our drinks cold, we were okay.

Then today - the red light indicating the bin was full went on, and the bin wasn't full. We've tried everything, gone online and researched it, and basically what we're being told is to just call it dead. While we might be able to get the manufacturer to repair/replace, we would have to pay the shipping and some kind of co-pay that would make it much more worthwhile to put the money towards a better one and call the bit we paid for this one - a valuable learning experience.

Learn from our mistakes. :) Also, I encourage everyone to wait a year before reviewing appliance-type purchases. Lots of things that work great for the first while end up as doorstops, and I think a year is a fair trial to see if the item you bought possesses true quality or not. Just a thought. :)

review_text: I love This!!! I am not the type of person who always marks stuff as 5 stars. The small ice will go into a soda bottle opening easily and will fit in the small opening of a Nalgean water bottle. The ice machine is very quiet and takes up very little space. Also there is an ice scoop for use if your hands are dirty and you don't want to add mud to your drink! I am very pleased with this and would recommend to RVers who want ice, but can't just up and go to a store every time ice is needed or have the room to spare in the freezer for large bags of ice. I am, on the average. an hour or two away from town. I drive a full size I ton dually and am in the mountains with a high elevation gain, so by time I drive to town and back, hoping my cooler does its job and ice loss is minimal, I have pretty much spent the money it cost for the price of the ice maker. product_title: LG WM3500CW 4.5 Cu. Ft. White Front Load Washer
review_text:
We are rough on our clothes washers. We seem to burn them out every 6 years. This was our first LG appliance.
Bought it at Lowes during COVID and brought it home in our SUV.

Total pain to get thru the laundry room door, even after pulling the box off. Remember to buy new water lines with the stainless steel mesh jacket (to prevent massive water leak). Washer came with a discharge tube but we needed to add two additional zip ties to keep it secured without fear of a leak. Use teflon tape on the pipe screw threads to get a water tight seal.

You'll need two 11/16 or 17mm wrenches and a magnetic bubble level to adjust the legs. Spend a lot of time on this to minimize vibration issues.

We stacked our old Samsung Gas Dryer on top and the brackets did not fit like they did on the previous Samsung and Whirlpool washers. Going to have to build a custom wood bracket to secure the dryer to the washer so it won't slide off.

The washer has two cold settings: cold (it brings super cold water up to some determined temperature) and tap cold (it just takes the cold water as is from the pipe. Probably useful in colder climates to get a consistent wash, but meh for here in California.

There is a power button that you have to use to turn on the washer before you can use the dial to choose your program. The screen to the right of the dial is a PAIN to read in low light. I printed stickers next to it for the key settings of OXY (presoak), Delay, Temperature and Cold Wash (darks).

There is a dial setting for "download" that uses your iphone or Android to download LG's ThinQ app. It basically hooks your washer up to WiFi to let you know when the washer is done and lets you create your own preset to make a custom washer setting. Used it a few times but never sure who set it last and what settings it has so I avoid using it. Did not like that the app REQUIRES you to give your location and birthdate info to use. Should be better privacy laws.

The Washer is a lot louder than our whirlpool when filling with water. The hoses move around. I'm guessing it has a smaller intake or too sudden of a shut off. There hasn't been much of a vibration issue so far. All in all a good washer. Will see how long it lasts...

Water would build up inside the body of the unit, corrode the copper tubing as well as the rear exhaust radiator fins. review_title: Ding, Ding! Annoying ear pain! PLUS, Deep Narrow Drum rolls blankets & sheets into tight burritos!!!
review_text:
This dryer makes incessant noise, so I'm too annoyed to decide whether it works well or not.
The drum is deeper than 3 other large capacity dryers I've owned; this is very useful feature if you're trying to put it in a narrow space. If you're under 5'7", have short arms, or a bad back, the longer reach may take getting used to.
I don't know if this dryer can be stacked, but that would help the reach.
My manual, for dve(g)45r6300/dve(g)45r6100, shows how to turn off the end-of-cycle musical tune, but says this: "However, the other sounds stay active." It doesn't divulge how active those other sounds are!
If you have sensitive ears, you need to be prepared. This dryer causes me ear pain with its incessant ding, ding, dinging, to set it, open the door, turn on, turn it off...
I'll try to describe it; I've already turned off the end-of-cycle musical alarm, and the following is what remains! I may be off a ding here or there, but I'm pretty close:
Turn it on: 6 dings
Turn dial from Normal to Time dry: 5 dings (and it always resets to normal after each load).
Press the buttons from high heat to medium heat: 3 dings
Press start: 3-4 dings rolled together
I'm at over 15 musical notes just to dry a few t-shirts.
But wait, there's more!
Leave the door open while getting items out: two dings, repeating. They sort of reminded me of European police sirens. I suspect they'll continue dinging for as long as the door remains open, so I slam it shut as fast as I can!
Close the door but fail to press start! Oh, yeah, I'm just asking for punishment!
8 dings in sets of 2 quick EU police sirens.
These dings may also repeat, but, again, I press start as quickly as humanly possible to avoid additional high-pitched ear-pain! I'm thinking Havana Syndrome!
I've now jammed my fingers several times rushing to stop the dinging! My poor button pushing knuckles may eventually develop arthritis if I can't disconnect the dinging.
I will say that it's a very attractive dryer; if you wear headphones, it might be perfect.

Update: I contacted Samsung customer service via online chat for help with my now loathed new dryer.
I thought Samsung might sell a silent mechanism replacement for their obnoxious buttons/dials, or full silencing instructions; I even asked if there were actually speakers to cover with duct tape, or wires I could cut! Nobody could tell me anything!
I was transferred through two polite Samsung representatives (who only knew how to turn off the end-of-cycle jingle which I'd already done).
A third representative promised to escalate my grievance and arrange for a technician to visit my home. That was a week ago; I'm not aware of missing any calls, but I don't really expect one. So, I will try to return it, but it's been over 30 days and I'll be losing hundreds of dollars.

I think Samsung is rude to force people to hear unnecessary sounds, whether they're annoying or not.
This model number should include a prominent warning label about unnecessary sound-effects; Samsung needs to alert families with babies, light sleepers, students studying & trying to concentrate, musicians, writers, thinkers...
"Warning: This Device Dings/Pings Repeatedly & Can NEVER Be Turned Off!"
However, for people who enjoy the machine noise in casino lobbies played at a much higher pitch, or listening to cheap video games on a transistor radio, they should be fine drying laundry with this model.
Wow! I genuinely hate this product. Where's my hammer?

!!!!! UPDATE!!!!! The deep narrow drum rolls my blankets & sheets into tight burritos that remain wet in the center; we must repeatedly pull them out to unroll them & then stuff them back in to continue to dry. It's an exceptional amount of work.
Considering the expertise & experience of Samsung's amazing engineers & designers, it's almost like this dryer is some kind of bad practical joke! I genuinely loathe it with the intensity of a red dragon. I've never had an inanimate object cause me angst, so this is indeed an unusual experience; however, I wish this dryer would just go wherever missing socks go, never to be seen again. Maybe I'll just take an ax to it and carve up all that wasted money spent. Grrrrrr.

I’m loading this washing machine like I’m decorating a cake sprinkling the dirty clothes around the machine to avoid potential unbalanced load error. Also, I know if I put in a load of towels not to leave the general vicinity of my home as the load will certainly become unbalanced even if I practice the “decorating a cake” method of loading the machine with the towels. So that means I need to reach in and rearrange several soaking wet bath towels and ask the laundry gods to assist in completing the load. I’m not sure how anyone who is either shorter than 5’5” could reach into this washing machine to do this or anyone who has arthritis or any other mobility issues.

review_title: I Didn't Know It Was Possible to Hate a Washing Machine
review_text:
We don't buy major appliances without doing some research. Three years ago, Samsung was supposedly a good brand. What a joke.

This washer claims to be high efficiency and is supposed to conserve water. Yes, when the top section of a load of laundry remains completely dry, I suppose that would conserve water. It won't clean clothes, but in theory it saves water. To ensure that clothes have a chance of getting clean, they have to be soaking wet before the washer is started. Failing to manually add water to the machine results in clothes that are dirtier coming out when they went in. Forget throwing a quick load in before heading to work unless you wake up early enough to walk between the nearest sink and the washer at least three times with a very large container of water. I'm confident that I use far more water to wash clothes with this "high efficiency" machine than I ever did with a standard washer.

This washer has to be continually babysat. It cannot complete a single cycle without stopping, emitting an incredibly annoying beeping sound, and issuing an "unbalanced" message. It will not start again until the clothing is rearranged. Some loads have to be rearranged multiple times. It's useless to try to start a load of laundry at bedtime or before running an errand because you will have to get up and turn the machine off to get it to shut up till the next day or come home from your errand, rearrange the clothes, and start it again.

This is the most labor intensive "labor saving" device I have ever owned. Even with adding water and monitoring every load, it does a TERRIBLE job of cleaning clothes. Clothes some out covered in lint and bits of human hair. A person who does any sort of manual labor outside will not get those clothes clean in this washer. It's just not going to happen.

review_text:
This review is partially complaining about all of the modern washing machine choices because of unrealistic regulations that focus too much on "saving water" ...

I LOVED my previous (1999) Twin sets of Stackable Laundry Centers by Kenmore - Whirlpool. Fast-forward to 2021- it's nice to save water when you can, - to me that's what the choices for high, medium, & low water levels are for. I always used the "low" water setting with my older units whenever it made sense.

but when saving water renders unacceptably dirty laundry & an inability to "soak" -- I am sooo miserable doing laundry ...!

The total cost for my new GE gas dryer laundry center with installation & removal of those 2 older Laundry Centers that I LOVED - was $1,850 - & since there's essentially no way to "soak" with modern Laundry Centers, GE or other brands - I say switch to ANY other good name brand NON LAUNDRY CENTER SINGLETON washing machine that allows a soak cycle, & hopefully indicates a way to direct the machine to provide more water ( I prefer top load - washing machines). The Maytag non-stack top load we ordered for our mountain home around 2017 does allow the basin to fill fuller, if you call the help line & ask them for the ( secret ? ) way to do that -- maybe you put the setting on "bulky item"...? But, Covid-19 caused many "good brands" to have severely back-logged delivery dates at the precise time I needed my machine. Who can bear to wait weeks or months, or "unknown" delivery estimations, when they need new washer / dryer units yesterday...?

Who wants to blow nearly $2 thousand dollars - on a washer with new fangled short washing cycles that you can't even begin to understand how to control...?

I think at least some of these newer machines help you keep doing laundry in User-Friendly ways that you can feel more confident will actually clean your clothing in gentle, yet thorough ways. We Consumers should fight hard for our rights to have clean laundry, & washing machines that are user-friendly - we are smart enough to put water levels on "low" - if the job calls for it..! So this is fight we need to take-up with our Legislators and water-usage Regulators.

When 21 years passed while my 2 previous laundry centers sat side-by-side working VERY WELL, ... I knew the newer technology would take some adjustments on my part - but, I feel like if we can send people to outer-space ; then we ought to be able to offer Consumers washing machines that can conserve water when possible - but that also allow Consumers to elect to use more water, if that's what the job requires, & to allow the Consumer to SOAK certain loads when they want to, whether that's during the wash cycle, or during the rinse cycle.

product_title: Samsung RF28R7351SG 27.8 Cu. Ft. Black Stainless 4-Door French Door Refrigerator
review_title: I hate almost every "feature" of the refrigerator.
review_text:
Full disclosure. I bought this exact model through a local big box store and have been using it in my own house for the past 13 months. It replaced an old school, traditional side by side. Oh trusty side by side, how I miss you. Simple, and ran for 15 years without any issues, and I could stuff you with tons of food. Both refrigerators were generally the same number of cubic feet. There is virtually NOTHING I like about this new refrigerator and I regret ever buying it.

First, most shelf height cannot be adjusted. There is one shelf with a sliding/retractable front half that I found to be a useless gimmick. There is another shelf where one portion of it can flip up to provide a very tall storage space. In 13 months I haven't bought one item that required using that tall space. I'd imagine if you bough a large floral arrangement, it might come it handy if you want to store it in the refrigerator, but other than that, USELESS. Not to mention, if you flip up that shelf, you loose half of the top shelf storage area. NONE of the door storage areas are adjustable. WHAT?!?! The left side door has these odd shaped "nooks" that most items won't fit. If you have lots of tiny, short bottles, ok, but most standard sized condiment bottles and jars, nope. The right side door has 3 baskets, and guess what, NONE of them can be moved up or down. They can be removed from the door and put on the kitchen table, but again, USELESS. Who does that? Progressing inside, on the right side... the bottom shelf can be set to one of two positions. Unless you want to actually store bottles of, oh I don't know, 1/2 or one gallon containers of MILK, Juice, Soda, etc. Thats right, standard American sized 1/2 gallon, 1 gallon, 1 liter containers will NOT FIT on the right side unless you put the shelf on its highest position. Even then, 1/2 gallon cartons will hit the bottom of the next higher shelf, so you have to tilt them to get in/out. Maybe your thinking all those cartons will fit elsewhere? NOPE. That's right, The top shelf, which is not adjustable, does not let you put just any standard sized beverage container. Try to put a gallon milk on top shelf, it's about 1/2" too big. Options? You can put the milk in the bottom right door tray... BUT.. not two, 1 gallon contains... it's too tight of a squeeze. But wait, you can slide the front portion of the bottom shelf back... sure... and the milk will fit better, but then all the space in back... now other things wont fit because when you slide the glass back, it slides UNDER the shelf, reducing the clearance by a good 1".

Now let's progress to the middle storage drawer... it has this very annoying metal sliding divider to allow keeping different types of items from mingling... I ripped mine out after the first month. All it did was get in the way. It also eats of valuable storage space. Even if you adjust the divider to get it out of the way, it still sticks out a good 2" along each side. Simply don't care if my cheese, deli meat, and butter all touch. I couldn't get rid of that thing fast enough. The only thing I like about this drawer is the independent temperature adjustment, which I'll admit is nice, colder for deli meats, cooler for beverages, etc.

Freezer on the bottom. Ok, I don't really see the big advantage. I guess if you don't access the freezer much, then yeah, put it on the bottom... however...the top sliding drawer in the freezer... you SUCK. The rollers are constantly coming off the track and it jams. Every time I move that drawer, I have to fight getting it back into the track so I can close the freezer. It also doesn't slide back enough to let you access the back of the bottom bin. Finding things is always a challenge. Since there are only 2 bins, and they are deep. In order to pack as much frozen food as what in my side by side, you have to stuff the bins... which means food gets buried on the bottom. Plan on constantly pulling out food at the top of the bins, to access the items that got relegated to the bottom. Side by side was never a problem, it had 6 smaller bins and 2 shelves... everything was easy to find, not to mention I could easily get 25% more food into it than in this new Samsung.

Off to the icemaker... which happens to be in the refrigerator. Keep in mind that foods you put next to, or under the ice maker will get VERY cold. I made the mistake of putting cans of soda under the ice maker. Well I had so much other food around it all, that the area with the soda got so cold that 2 soda cans froze and burst in the back. YUCK. Which leaks me to CLEANING the insde. At this point I want to hunt down who designed this contraption. You CANNOT easily remove anything to clean it. The glass in the bottom shelf? you can't just lift it out... that would be way too easy. You have to remove the entire bottom shelf and draw assembly, and then fight getting the glass out. It's the same struggle with the other glass shelves... you can't just remove the glass, you have to remove the entire shelf assembly. WHY! At this point I need a drink so I'll get some ice... maybe I want to make a frozen margarina and I need a lot of ice... I don't want to stand in front of the door for 10 minutes so lets get the ice out of the ice maker... I swear I thought I was cracking plastic to get the ice bucket out of the ice maker. That think is held in there, with no easy way to get it out... no handles or recesses to easily grab... you just have to push up on it and pull... hard... it will sound like something is breaking, but supposedly that is normal. Now you've got it out.. ICE! wait.. where's all the ice? Based on the size of the icemaker, and how much room it takes up inside the refrigerator, you'd think it would be a decent quantity. Nope... there's about enought ice to fill one standard sized , old school blender. If you have one of those large sized Ninjas or Vitamix, your not going to fill it.

Finally we make it to the outer door for water and ice. You can get a very large size tumbler/mug in here... lots of clearance... but the buttons to change modes... they are these new fangled capactive touch things that are picky about how you touch them. If you are wearing gloves.... like you've been in the yard and came inside to refill your bubba-mug... take them off. I couldn't switch between ice/water with gloves on. One thing I really like on my old refrigerator was the ice/water night light. I could turn it on at night and actually see the water/ice opening and buttons when I walked into the kitchen at night to fill my water glass, all WITHOUT having to turn on the kitchen light. You'd think a 21st century refrigerator would have this ancient feature... NOPE. the light only comes on when you press your glass/mug/tumbler against the fill lever... but its dark in the kitchen and you can't see the door, much less the lever to begin with.... so on goes the kitchen light.

Long term use. After 13 months, some things have also broken. The inside door pitcher, which can be used to brew tea, etc... and autorefills every time you remove/replace it. Mine has leaked for the past few months. The gasket around the lid doesn't seal anymore and evertime I take the pitcher out to fill a glass, it leaks. I was going to call for a warranty replacement but I just missed my deadline by 3 weeks. If you can find a replacement, it's going to set you backk just over $100... yes, for a PITCHER!

Do yourself a favor... stick with that trusty old refrigerator you currently have.

product_title: Samsung 24" Built-In Fingerprint Resistant Stainless Steel Dishwasher
review_text:
I couldn’t find many reviews, so I thought I would help future buyers avoid my mistake. I know Samsung has a bad reliability rating among consumers with regards to their appliances. But I have had Samsung washers, dryers and refrigerators for over 10 years without major problems and I like the looks and technology. Saw they started making dishwashers a few years ago and when I needed a replacement I debated between this Samsung and the popular Kitchen Aid with the third rack and low decibels that I had owned a couple years before in a previous home. Went to multiple places and saw it in person. Choose a local appliance center that also services their appliances in case we had any future problems. Although they stocked the Samsung, they said almost everyone bought the Kitchen Aid or one of the other brands. So although Samsung didn’t have many reviews, it didn’t have bad reviews. But their was no in depth reviews on how the Samsung features work.
I really wanted a low DB dishwasher and one that popped open automatically after the cycle was finished to finish drying. I’ve heard to bring your own dishes to test what the dishwasher truly holds before purchasing. Should have listened to that advise and if you are insisting on the Samsung, you must do this before you buy! I noticed in the showroom that the third rack was able to rise slightly. Second rack where you put your glasses had 2 rows of times that you could angle and adjust the width of the rows depending on the type of glass, such as wine, mugs, or standard glassware. Thought this would be adequate, it is not. The rows are so narrow it’s hard to get my small glasses in. I don’t have oversized cups so I didn’t think I would have a problem. The angle just creates more problem, because it gets in the way of the cups, not accommodate the cups. So it takes a lot of time to squeeze glassware in if I want to use the full 5 rows. Otherwise it’s only 3 rows and your cups with scoot around at weird angles because it’s too big. For those with large cups, forget it.
The biggest problem with this dishwasher is the actual usable capacity size. It seems smaller than my old Kitchen Aid and it was definitely smaller than even the builder grade GE dishwasher that I replaced. I would take either of those before this Samsung. I normally don’t like the cheap dishwashers, but I should have saved the money or gone with a different brand. Especially since this Samsung is easily over $1,000 installed. The Samsung would be okay capacity wise for a bachelor or two person household. But for a family of four be prepared to do more loads. I dread when another family visits for a week. Having to wait hours with a sink full of dirty dishes between loads because this washer will not hold enough.
One of the features that I was most excited about and the main reason we choose this Samsung, since few had this option, is the self opening door at the end of the cycle. This has been the biggest let down. It opens fine and a quiet fan runs for about 10 mins after the door opens, which is great. The main problem is the door opens so quickly after the load is done, the dishes don’t get much of a chance to completely dry. I wish there was a way to adjust this setting. It seems like it only dries with the door close for 10 mins after the cycle is finished. It should probably be for half an hour. So unless my dishes are going to air dry for a long time, I still have the old problem of having to shake off the water from upside down bowls and plastics, that are wetter in this dishwasher than others that allow more dry time. We have granite counters so I wasn’t afraid of warping. But if you have laminate, I’ve heard the self opening ones are not good, because of the excess moisture.
The pros of this machine are it’s extremely quiet. I have a great room with tile floor, so I wanted a quiet dishwasher. It’s hard to determine if this is on, its so quiet. It’s slightly quieter than the Kitchen Aid, but the Kitchen Aid was extremely quiet that neither one should bother you. It doesn’t have a large handle sticking out like the Kitchen Aid. Although that handle looked like it would make a nice towel rack, the towel would fall and/or hit the floor every time you opened the door.
One thing that may be a feature or a drawback, depending on your preference is the large electronic numbers displayed in the front of the machine when it’s running. It tells the time left on the cycle. No way to turn it off. It stays lit the entire time it’s running.
So far it runs the way it is designed. It has popped open smoothly and the fan runs quietly. I just wished the designers could have done a better job. It’s like they looked at all the features a dishwasher could have and wanted to include them, but didn’t consider if the features were functional in a real household setting. Unfortunately, this dishwasher is a no buy.

product_title: Samsung 24" Built-In Fingerprint Resistant Stainless Steel Dishwasher
review_text:
I bought this dishwasher at a big box store, the salesman couldn't say enough great things about this dishwasher...which means he's never used one.

First the positives. The thing is quiet. Super quiet and what isn't there to love about quiet? Does it do an adequate job of cleaning? Meh. Drying? Very good.

It's got some problems.
1) My dinner plates are a standard plate size (10.5 inches) and if I lower the second rack so I have more second rack space the swing arm hanging off the rack knocks into the top of the plates and won't spin. Doesn't spin, so the second rack doesn't clean properly.
2) Can't clean bowls on the bottom rack. After an unscientific look into what the problem is, I'm fairly sure it's because the lower swing arm moves back and forth instead of spinning. So if you put bowls on the second rack, that has a typical swingarm that rotates, they get clean, but on the bottom rack they will not get clean. In fact it leaves like a weird residue in them, and then I have to take them out and hand wash them. By the way that bottom arm that travels front and back isn't actually spraying water. There are jets located at the back wall of the dishwasher and those jets spray water into that arm, which acts as sort of a ramp and shoots the water upwards. I think (and this is a big guess) that because of that tech, anything that isn't a flat surface will not get clean and will actually shoot any junk up into the bowls. So if you want to pre-wash your bowls...then this is your dishwasher. If you want your dishwasher to do what it's supposed to do...keep searching.
3) The third rack is designed poorly. This is gonna be a challenge to describe, but because the rows that separate the utensils are at the close end instead of the far end you can not load knives next to forks and spoons (the knife handle is wider than a fork handle, and the rows are too narrow). So the easy solution is to load them on the opposite side of the rack...but wait, if you do that and you want to lower the middle part of the rack to hold, for instance, a large serving spoon, then the knives will slide back and won't stay in their place. Super annoying and is just a bad design.
4) The app is a joke, at least on an iPhone. Sort of works, but is buggy. Definitely not ready for prime time.
5) The buttons you push to choose your cycle and to power and start don't have a tactile response. Again, this sounds minor, but if the button actually pushed in, you would be able to tell you've done something.
Would I recommend this dishwasher as a buy? Nope.

product_title: Samsung 24" Built-In Fingerprint Resistant Stainless Steel Dishwasher
review_text:
Bought this dishwasher from a big box. This listing does not show the model number, but it is a Samsung DW80R9950. Absolutely terrible machine.

To its credit, it is very quiet and it does a respectable job cleaning dishes. However, the "water wall" mechanism is too complicated for its own good and practically guarantees you'll need maintenance sooner than later. The system has a motor driven deflector that moves along a belt on the bottom of the tub to direct powerful jets up. Not the worst idea, but it relies on a delicate magnet and sensor arrangement to accomplish this. If either the magnet or the sensor break or degrade, then the drive motor burns itself out. To fix it, you need to disassemble parts into the tub, opening the door for leaks.

The killer for me, our sensor and motor failed twelve months and two weeks after purchase. Just past the warranty window. The extended warranty would cover the minor cost of the parts, but not the major cost of installing them.

I know they don't make them like they used to, but I don't think it's unreasonable to expect more than a year of service out of a $1,000 machine. Personally, it will be a while before I come back around to Samsung as a brand.

review_title: Want to bake at 500 degrees? Can't.
review_text: I have been baking for 5 years. My new rental apartment came with one of these. My baked goods started coming out much worse than they should. Never even crossed my mind that the oven would have something to do with it because I never had an issue with an oven before. After a long while and trying many different things, it clicked. It had to be the oven. So I ordered an oven thermometer. First, I cross tested the thermometer with my sous vide machine and meat thermometer. All 3 showed the same temperature. So I was sure the oven thermometer was accurate before I tested the oven. I cranked the oven all the way up to 500 in bake mode. When it beeped after 25 minutes, I checked the thermometer and it read 390 degrees! I gave it another 20 minutes so 45 minutes total. It went up to a mere 415. Would it go up to 500 eventually, after maybe a few hours? Not sure, don't care. It shouldn't take hours to reach 500. Nobody has the time or the money to burn for that. If you're into baking, avoid this one.

review_title: No sound comes from this refrigerator! It is quiet and efficient!
review_text:
[[VIDEOID:d56df7c1ecac5f8214c5d85cf22a4933]] I drive an 18-wheeler for a living and decided to get a compact fridge for my rig. After doing a lot of research, the pick for me was this GE compact refrigerator with freezer!

Now this refrigerator sits right next to my bunk so one of the most important aspects that I was looking for in a refrigerator of this size is how quiet it would be.

Wow! And I can say that backwards wow! This refrigerator does not make any sound at all! I was totally shocked! I had to put my ear up to the side of the fridge to see if it was working! Lol

And within a couple of hours it was ready to have food put into it!

I will say this as a word of caution! if you are having this delivered to your home or to maybe a third party like a UPS store or FedEx store!

Make sure it's a reputable delivery service and here's why I say that! Make sure the the carrier of this refrigerator does not transport this product laying on its side! Or after it's delivered make sure that if a third party is holding this for you, that they do not store this on its side!

They need to keep it right side up as indicated on the box! Reason being if you put it on the side oil can go into the cooling compressor and then when you start the fridge it will not cool!

This is bar none one of the best investments that I've made in an appliance! Yes this is a little more expensive than the typical others that are comparable to the size of this GE fridge!

However, if you're looking for a refrigerator that doesn't make any noise this is it!

I even sent an email to the GE headquarters in Louisville Kentucky telling them how happy I am with this fridge! Much to my surprise they called me back! Anyway I highly recommend this refrigerator especially if you're looking for something that will not wake you up at night!

The extra money for this is definitely worth it trust me!

product_title: LG LTG4715BD 6.9 Cu. Ft. Black Stainless Double Oven Gas Range
review_text:
Don't let the low rating on Consumer Reports mislead you. This is a great little range with lots of features - more even if you have a WiFi and cellphone that accepts LG's ThinQ app. The WiFi only works over a 2.4GHz system, and not on a 5.0 GHz system.

One of the included accessories is a meat probe,which only attaches to a port or jack in the lower oven, and not to the upper oven. I spent quite a lot of time looking for the jack in the upper oven before I ever looked in the lower oven. If you want your meats properly cooked or broiled, use the the meat probe.

Another accessory some will find useful is the wok rack. It fits over the burner grate and holds a rounded-bottom wok securely.

One unusual feature is the oven cooking mode, which set by a round dial labeled "Oven Control" on the front of the range, and where you might expect the oven temperatures to be set. Instead, the round dial has cooking modes inscribed on it, and oven temperatures are digitally set in the electronic panel. Turning the "Oven Control" dial changes the information on the electronic display to preset values.

The only negative about the Oven Control dial is that the labeles inscribed on it are hard to read, but if you need to kmow what they are, a handy fix is to pull the knob off and mark the labels on it with a magic marker, then wipe the dial so only the labels are marked.

The only other negative I have on the double-oven range is that the lower oven virtually sits on the floor, and it might be hard to access for some less-mobile cooks.

All-in all, I like this double-oven range, would by it again, and I would recommend it to my friends.

review_text:
LG designs great refrigerators. They're functional, efficient and attractive. Unfortunately, LG uses linear compressors. The LG Linear compressor has a poor life expectancy when compared to different types of reciprocating compressors like the ones typically found in AC units, or the digital inverter compressors used by Samsung and others.

Linear compressors are cheaper and there are a few other advantages for refrigerators: however, none of that makes up for the failure rate of the design used by LG.

The failure rate is so high, LG has settled two class action lawsuits in the last few years regarding the compressor, yet LG refuses to change the design, switch to a more reliable compressor type, or even admit the problem.

All appliances produced now days have reliability issues. Part of the problem is US and European governments forcing companies to make more and more efficient appliances. The more efficient compressors and refrigeration equipment become, the less reliable they are.

For example, AC units that have a very high seer rating (high energy efficiency) fail more often and cost more to repair than low seer units. Any savings on energy is over shadowed by repair costs over the life of the equipment. The government doesn't care how much we spend replacing and repairing appliances because they want to show everyone how much they're doing to help the environment. It's a bogus objective that comes as a very high cost to consumers. And there is more of it coming--water heaters (barely work now), washing machines and more refrigerator crap.

Of course, LG has more reliable options so who knows what their internal costs are and the internal politics. You can bet that LG has looked closely at the economics of replacing the sealed cooling system with a more reliable one versus paying the claims, etc. They do what's in their best interest not yours.

I've personally had two new $3000 LG fridges both fail within 5 years. I don't bother repairing them, I just buy new ones. In my experience, repairing sealed systems using linear compressors is usually a very short lived solution (as in likely to fail again within 2 yrs). But others may disagree.

I won't buy any more LG refrigerators until they change the cooling system despite how much we like all the other LG features.

As an aside: in my opinion Samsung closed systems are better than LG's, but they've got ice maker problems that they can't or won't fix. They've had to settle claims also. The Samsung design is not nearly as functional as the LG, but it may last longer.

We bought this dishwasher a year and a half ago to specifically to match our Cafe Matte White Double Oven and Cooktop; while it looks great, we continue to have issues with dirty dishes and and detergent pods not clearing from the dispenser (Cascade Platinum Pods); we are on our third service call.

The first service call (under warranty) the GE technician told us its because we weren't cleaning our plates properly or that they were sitting in the sink too long and that we weren't using rinse aid; we started using rinse aid diligently as well as pre-washing our plates, but it had no change in the issue.

The second GE service technician came out (still under warranty) and said it had nothing to do with rinse aid, but that there was an issue in the internal water distribution that he had to replace. He replaced it and things definitely improved cleaning; continue to have issues with detergent pods being stuck in the dispenser.

Now a year later, we're back to issues with pulling dishes out with food stuck-n and dried to the plates even though we continue to pre-wash and use rinse aid. (Detergent pods still an issue - Cascade Platinum).

We just had our third GE technician arrive - now out of warranty. It was the same guy from our first call that lectured us again about dishes sitting too long and rinse aid. (FYI - I had dishes sitting in the sink so that he would have a clean dishwasher to work with).

After he was done lecturing us, he told us that the top water spinner needed to be replaced because the holes are clogged. As we are out of warranty, this is now a $270 cost on a dishwasher that has been flaky on cleaning since we got it.

As much as we love the aesthetics of it - that Matte White and Bronze is beautiful - a pricepoint this high for a non-performing dishwasher and the costs we now have to sink into this a year and a half later dont make it worth it. Spend on the money a dishwasher that works instead of this!

product_title: Frigidaire FGEH3047VF Gallery Series 30" Electric Range with 5 Elements, 5.4 Cubic ft. Capacity Convection Oven, in Stainless Steel
review_text:
Purchased from Lowe's (for a lot more than the Amazon price, but with much faster delivery and haul away). The rear trim kit was not included as indicated on their website, so had to do the customer service runaround to get that amount refunded to order on my own. But if you are replacing a true slide in range, be prepared to fiddle around if you are placing in an island. You will need the rear trim and very likely those silicone strips to seal around your range so gunk doesn't fall through.

I have been using this for a week after upgrading from an old electric coil Jenn Air downdraft range. This is my first glass top cooktop and it's an adjustment as it heats SO MUCH faster than my old range, but no complaints there. One reason I chose this particular range was that the manual stated it's fine to use cast iron, and I'm having no issues. As long as I remember a lower initial temperature, it's fine.

The shiny black glass is definitely bringing out a slightly obsessive side to my personality of which I was previously unaware. My Jenn Air range was impossible to keep clean, so I think now that I have something that can be clean, it *must* be clean and shiny all the time. I'm not using anything more than vinegar spray, baking soda, Swedish dishcloths, and an old cotton diaper or linen towel to keep it gleaming. So you don't have to buy expensive cooktop cleaner unless you want to. And I have a new hobby.

The oven is a HUGE improvement over what I had before. It heats quickly and evenly, and the temperature stays consistent. Not impressed with the steam clean option, but I know the high heat self clean option will shorten the life of any oven, so I won't be using that. Haven't used the air fryer feature yet, but I love the convection setting for roasted veggies--just need to drop the temperature from what I'm used to.

We're quickly getting accustomed to the funny 2 and 3-way dials that control the multi-option burners. My kitchen is well lit, but I can see where some folks might have visibility issues with the knobs. Someone here was complaining about the touch panel turning on when you brush up against it. It's true--it beeps like it's turning on, but unless you hit the start button, nothing actually happens, so I don't really see an issue there.

The only features I am missing from my last range are the ability to set the oven super low (minimum temp on this one is 170 so too hot for proofing dough) and multiple timers. Other than these two small things, I am quite fond of this new range.

So far, so good--very pleased with my purchase.

Once that is done, it is almost impossible to remove the bin to melt the ice and restore operation.

The additional problem is finding a repair facility that will work on a Samsung refrigerator. product_title: GE® 21.8 Cu. Ft. Counter-Depth Fingerprint Resistant Side-By-Side Refrigerator
review_title: Works great; quiet, light on the amenities
review_text:
So far this fridge has been awesome:

- Mostly quality feel and construction
- Track rollers (like inline skates)
- Great temp control
- Awesome lighting
- Easily accessible water filter
- Quiet
- Soft close doors (stops midpoint rather than slamming shut, ultimately breaking the door shelves)

What's missing in action for a $2000 fridge (price after taxes):

- Drawer slider mechanisms (as in WHAT drawer slider mechanisms? No rollers-sloppy plastic-plastic tongue/groove setup)
- Cheap looking lenses for interior lighting
- In-door water dispenser angled so far forward it easily misses smaller cups and glasses, shooting water onto the floor unless you're careful
- In-door ice dispenser spews crushed ice everywhere unless your container is right up against the nozzle that's supposed to prevent it.
- No egg tray; seriously?

I've seen reviews saying this fridge is noisy. Not Mine. It makes noises every so often: a sort of purring sound, a sort of winding sound, ice cubes dropping and tray refilling of course, couple of other random noises. Except for the relatively loud ice cube drops, this fridge is mostly supremely quiet, unless you have super-hero hearing, in which case you should get an old-fashioned ice chest.

Except for the disappointingly cheap drawer tracks, cheap-looking light lenses, and cheesy glass shelf mounting design, it's a great fridge. My daughter has a four-door GE Profile; it's clear GE knows how to make a sophisticated looking, feeling, and operating fridge. THIS, IS NOT THAT.

So basically, what used to cost $900$1100 not that long ago- for a decent fridge like this one, now costs $2000*. I would have expected MUCH better detailing inside at this price point from a manufacturer that CLEARLY knows how to do it.

HOWEVER, compared to my Sears Elite, actually an LG ("elite" - that's a laugh) from a few years ago, this thing is like the latest version of the Star Trek Enterprise. I spent the best part of $1500 in parts and repairs AFTER the TWO COMPRESSOR REPLACEMENTS under warranty. It make a helluva racket, and A LOT of that money was spent on expensive replacement drawers that cracked, partly from the doors slamming instead of having a soft close mechanism of some sort, and partly because they were just made from crap plastic that became brittle at lower temps, which is kind of what fridges do.

Would of gave this fridge a 5-star if it cost closer to $1500 "out the door" (taxes/delivery). BUT GE is near or at the top of the reliability and temp control lists, so overall, I'm grudgingly happy w/the purchase.

*Home Depot is having some deals as of this writing.

review_title: I wish I had read the rewiews here first...
review_text:
I didn't buy it here figuring using a local vendor would be more proactive if there are problems, ... wrong again.
First, never have anything delievered on a Friday and possibly on a Monday, salesmen are useless as they are just order takers and are half out the door before Friday lunch and possibly not in until afternoon on Monday. Friday was my mistake.
Second don't buy this unless you have a ton of room around the location for the clunky doors to open as their thickness and the angle they open to is very wide. You cannot box this refrig in and counter depth refrig means nothing. If you expect to put this next to a counter depth side wall it will wind up being 5 to 6 inches away from the rear wall. Ugly is the mild term for how it looks when in this position.
Third, for the price of this thing you might expect a decent or even innovative leveing mechanism, wrong. The leveling mechanism is two, one of each side of the front, typical jackscrews... with cheap nylon nuts that will eventually round off from use. That use will be the fact that you have to unscrew them to move the frig for cleaning. Yes we like to clean under the frig. Adjusting those leveling screws will also damage your flooring as the wrench of your choice will be dragged across the floor leaving scratch marks. If you're buying a house with one these transformer monsters check for flooring damage.
Forth, thhe heated sealing surfaces can burn you. They heat the sealing surfces of the doors to avoid condensation. These are the surfaces between the doors. Normally they are just warm to the touch but recently we had the ocassion to use 'super' mode where the frig and freezer are set to cool rapidly. My wife touched the surface between the refrig and the vegetable freshness section as was burned.
Fifth, there is a bothersome procedure to closing the frig doors. The right door must be closed first and if open the right door only you still have to open the left door then close the right door and then close the left door. A futile exercise if you have teenage children. Not to mention children of a certain lessor height will never get into the frig anyway necause it is too tall for them. So if you have teenage children you will forever be checking to see if the frig doors are closed correctly.
Sixth, Bosch service is non-existent and so is vendor serice for that matter. You're a consumer, you're nothing to them but a source of money, nothing else. Remember, this is Germany providing these things. You're supposed to take it, period. I attempted to call them and was robotically told to wait with no guess as to how long. I suspected many would fall by the wayside before being connected and it would be quicker to fly there.
All in all not a good start to $4000 purchase and definitely our last Bosch purchase AND definitely not the end of future trouble. As a side note to where we came from with this. The refrigerator we replaced was a 1988 Frididaire that never had a problem and was a hand me down from my parents.
All this and we haven't had the thing long enough to know if it's even going to last a year. I gave it two stars so I can come back and update when the thing crashes.

review_title: OK oven, but I wouldn't have chosen this given another chance
review_text:
This oven has lots of fabulous features on paper. And I appreciate LG for trying to make appliances look modern. It's been working stably after two years. However, there're some annoying things about this oven:

1. When the microwave cycle finishes, it keeps beeping every 30 seconds until you explicitly press CLEAR button. Just opening the oven door won't stop this.

2. The buttons are hard to press. It often doesn't register on the first attempt. You have to carefully press the center of buttons hardly.

3. The microwave fan keeps running for a few minutes after every microwave cycle, even when the oven is not hot at all, like after heating the butter for 10 seconds. This is noisy.

4. There're lots of fancy features on the product page but little details on when to use them. Examples:
- There's very little information about what Steam Cook does and when to use it. The manual only described the steps to use it. It's definitely not the Chinese style steam cooking, and there're very few, if any, recipes for this oven's steam cook.
- The product page mentioned infrared heating, but there's no mention to it in the manual and it's not clear how to take advantage of this.
- The Speed Oven is featured on the product page, but the manual just vaguely mentioned that it's good for roasting meat and baking bread, without deliberating the impact to the food and the difference against regular cooking.

5. The temperature probe can be very inaccurate. I find it consistently undercook food. I stopped using it after using it twice.

6. The manual mentioned the firmware update feature with the phone app, but afaik this is impossible with this oven. I wish they had it so that at lease some of the points mentioned above could be potentially improved.

review_text:
This was my first ever DYI d/w install. I built a base out of pine wood (on flat 5mm silicone feet to avoid condenstation and warping) to fix the 1.5" top gap, depth 20" only to clear the kickplate. I was greatly helped by several Bosch 800 series install series videos, especially Barron's Plumbing featuring his despondent reverse bite wife:)

Important points from install:
1. Have someone tilt it backward and unscrew front feet by hand until the wrenchable part is visible, it will save you pain later.
2. Buy a Bosch junction box so you can continue using dishwasher on separate outlet. DO NOT install it behind the dishwasher if your counter depth is 24", but rather take under the sink right above the cabinet hole, read below.
3. If you have to drill holes for drain, inlet, and power make it as close to ground as possible, this will keep the inlet and drain pipes flush with the recessed space under lower back end, especially in a sink-to-the-right install.
3. Drain has to have a very high point above the garbage disposal or it will backflow into machine.
4. When pushing back make sure you keep machine to the side away from sink, that way you can shine light and inspect for kinks, move machine 2", then pull hoses, repeat until done.

Now to use:
1. Use only FINISH brand pucks. I disabled the annoying Rinse Aid
2. For best drying use AUTO cycle, Sanitize(high temp), and Extra Dry.
3. Remove third top tray, glass stem holder from second tray, and utensil
separator grids from utensil tray, throw into trash can. Your life will be much
easier.
4. RTFM and download it on your laptop. The settings are a bit cryptical.
5. Do not despair on the capacitive buttons, they get better as you use it for a week.

Coming from two Kenmore Kitchenaid rebadges this is the Tesla!
German parts assembled in USA.

Kudos to Abt. for shipping via airplane in three days for only $40.

I ended up with a special recessed outlet and the unit barely fits. Second, the water supply line does not fit a standard 3/8 dishwasher supply line. I had to get an adapter to the unit's garden hose thread.

It was frustrating to attempt testing the unit (prior to final installation) which appeared to be dead until I figured out the door must be open to use the controls. review_title: This Stove Makes Our Home Feel Like a Home
review_text:
We used to have an apartment sized gas stove. My wife did most of the cooking on it. The burners were close together, the pilots didn't work, the oven was small, he broiler handle broke off when little Jimmy was climbing on it, but she made it work.

I was working as an assistant fax operator at a copy store in a nearby strip mall. Covid and all, and email, too, there weren't a lot of people coming in to send faxes. One day my boss calls me into the office and says "Well Harold, your fax numbers are down for the sixteenth consecutive month, and I'm going to have to let you go. However, I can get you in as an apprentice assistant at my brother's company, Problem Grease Trap Specialty Cleaning." I jumped ship and landed in slime.

At least I had a job. Eleven children at home was hard, but we liked it. We didn't have beds for them all. We stole moving blankets out of UHaul trucks for bedding. We had to kill the bed bugs with a rolling pin. The kids would spend most of the day foraging for food, like at the dumpster behind Dunkin Donuts. We made all kinds of stuff out of donut dough and Chik Fil A finds, using that little gas oven. Until the burners rusted out.

My wife had had enough. Me smelling like a grease trap, eleven kids, and no stove. She said,"Harold, take the kids. I'm getting a job."

Martha went out and applied for a job as a fashion model in New York City. She was a shoe-in, with 3" spikes. Soon we were able to afford what we needed to support eleven kids the right way.

The first thing we did was go out and buy a Frigidaire FFEH3051VS 30" electric stove, with self cleaning oven glass top, front burners, and a low back. We also buy food at the store, and the kids can go to school. Life is so much better with a Frigidaire FFEH3051VS.

review_title: Overall a good oven but some flaws with control board and company doesn't help troubleshoot
review_text:
I ran into a known issue with this stove above 4 years after I bought it, which is that moisture got under the keypad and it started beeping and giving me an error constantly. I couldn't even use the stove because anytime it was plugged in, it was beeping so much.

the company was not helpful; they just wanted to send a repair guy out, which is 80$ just to come out plus prbly 350-500 to replace the control board.

All you need to do is to peel the cover off and gently clean the contacts below with alcohol and q-tips. There are many youtube videos of how to fix this.

Also, even if you need your control board replaced, it looks very simple (unscrew the back of the stove, plug and play to put the new one in). So check out those options before paying for an expensive repair.

The stove is great otherwise. I'm annoyed that frigidaire a) doesn't have any kind of sealant around the keyboard cover to prevent this common, known issue and b) doesn't provide troubleshooting to help you fix the problem yourself. Also, although frigidaire's customer service did eventually give me the parts numbers (which I wanted in case we did need to replace teh control board), I had to ask them several times and they kept trying to push me to hire a repair guy instead. I finally said "Am I allowed to know the parts numbers?" and then they gave it to me. I wonder if they get a kickback from the repair costs, since they were so pushy about it.

Shouldn't cost a lotta money to fix this, and I"m sure a lot of people pay way too much for the repair.

review_title: Far from what I was hoping.....
review_text:
Unfortunately, the clearance from our cabinet to floor is 1/4" too short for 95% + of the standard dishwashers. After much frustration trying to find one locally (and having to return a new one that wouldn't fit) I ordered this one since it's ADA compliant and as such it would fit. It did. However, there are some annoying and surprising design flaws in this machine.
In no particular order....
First, there is NO water dispensing from the very top (ceiling) of the tub. I'm not sure how the tops of items in the top rack or supposed to be cleaned. Every other DW we've ever had has a circulating dispenser above AND below the top rack. This one just has below.
Secondly, the racks seem to be very poorly designed. The vertical holders on the bottom rack are too short and too close together to hold anything except plates. You can put several plates (though I wouldn't put them THAT close together) but no pots or pans. The top rack is useless for holding light glasses or really much of anything, again due to the very shallow vertical posts on the rack.
Third. It does not dry, at all! We've tried multiple settings including heat dry and everything is still soaking wet.
On at least one cycle the detergent dispenser didn't open and the water didn't drain. We've only used it a handful of times so hopefully this doesn't recur.
Overall dishes do NOT come out clean.
Overall VERY disappointed in the performance and utility of what to us, was far from a 'cheap' dishwasher. I was hesitant to buy something like this online and sight unseen. Sometimes you just have to learn those lessons I guess... Had I purchased this locally it would definitely be going back.
The only reason it got 2 stars instead of 1 is because it is quiet. Significantly more so than our previous one. I suppose if you're not going to do a good job, you can ate least be quiet about it. So I guess that's worth 'something'.

review_text:
I am a Property Manager and have never had this many problems with a brand new appliance before in my life. I am assisting my parents with converting their brand new range to LP and it has been over a month without any success. For starters, the conversion kit that comes taped to the back of the appliance contained defective propane (LP) orifices for the burners. Two of the five don't work. Secondly, the instructions on converting the oven to LP are contradictory. On one side of the directions, it says to adjust the pressure regulator and on the other side it says to replace the oven orifice to work with propane (LP). When I called Frigidaire customer service to find out where the oven orifice is and why didn't it come with my conversion kit, they said they don't sell the conversion kits to customers so I would have to contact a third party certified technician (TPCT). The customer service rep then said that my specific model doesn't need an oven orifice, but she wasn't sure and to check with my TPCT.

I called the TPCT that they referred me to and they said they were unsure of what came with the conversion kit and would get back to me. When they called me back, they said their conversion kit comes with an oven orifice, so I said I'd like to purchase it. They said they won't sell it to me without a service call. I asked how much that would be, they said $100 for a diagnosis, but that amount would be applied to the $225 labor charge to convert my appliance to LP and an additional $25 for the kit. I told them, I know how to convert the stovetop, it's already done except for the two defective pieces, I just need the oven. They said it would still cost me $250 or I can call some other parts and appliance store.

I called the local parts store and told them my plight. They said immediately, this model doesn't need an oven orifice and that Frigidaire and their TPCT should have told me that. It does need adjusting to the oven's pressure regulator and orifice, but it doesn't need a replacement piece.

Finally, someone who actually knows what they're talking about and they don't even work for the company that manufactures the appliance!

This appliance that we have owned for over a month without a single use is not only defective but will cost me half the price of what I paid for it to have a TPCT fix it. I have never owned a Frigidaire appliance before this and now I know why. They are the worst appliances and I will never purchase them again for my own personal use or for my properties.

review_title: This makes the ice but it. does NOT keep it FROZEN!
review_text: I was so excited to get this ice maker. I really thought it was going to be amazing especially for this price point. Don't get me wrong, this does exactly what the item description says it does. It makes wonderful ice and it really is just like Sonic’s ice but there are some huge flaws. So, I am getting everything together to get this process going, First, this only came with a quick start guide. There is not a separate more thorough operations manual or any troubleshooting guide. Set up for me took a bit longer than it should have but having some unclear instructions was a distraction. You have to do a cleaning cycle before the ice. That was pretty easy just fill up the reservoir that is located under the ice bin to the fill line with water. Make sure the switch in the back is turned to cleaning and begin. Once that is done the extra water tank that is attached to the machine only by a magnet (which I do not like) has it's own cleaning cycle but it is not necessary to use the extra tank if you are not planning to make a lot of ice. Once the cleaning is done now it's ready to go. I started my first batch, made sure the ice was forming (it only took a couple of minutes) and went on with my day. I went back to the kitchen for a my first drink with my new ice about an hour and a half later. I see that there isn't any and there isn't any water either. I thought I must have done something wrong. So, I am scrambling around to find an answer to what us wrong. I went to the GE website and there isn't anything other than the quick start guide. Of course you can  contact support if there are any issues. I decided to start fresh so I took the plugs out of the hoses in the back and drained the water out which was trapped in the machine where I couldn't see it. I'm not sure about this but I had to have read it somewhere, I found out why there was no ice after I returned to the kitchen.  I knew the ice was forming and dropping into the bin before I left the kitchen so I know I wasn't crazy. But, this expensive appliance does not keep the ice in the bin frozen. What? The ice machine doesn't keep the ice frozen? So it only does half it's job and the bin is located inside the machine. I could understand if the bin was on the outside of the machine but the inside? So that is what happened it had all melted and the water was already recycling to make more ice. It just can't be seen. The guide states that if the water recycles it will make the ice taste bad. I really like this ice. The little pellets that form into ice make drinks taste so much better than the big bulky ice cubes do. This machine works great but I do not have time to babysit each cycle of the ice-making process. At least not at this price. To have an appliance this expensive do only half of what it should do is crazy to me. So, I wouldn't recommend this unless you gave a lot of cash to spend and a lot of time to waste but for me, this is unacceptable. I can not believe that this machine can make ice but it doesn't keep it frozen!

review_title: Makes ice fast!  But doesn’t store ice.
review_text:
Starts producing some ice within 8 minutes of starting up, and only a few minutes later it has created enough ice for a couple of drinks.

This unit does not need to be plumbed in, and actually cannot be. It has a detachable tank for refilling the water supply, which is convenient. You need to use the best water you can to keep it working well, e.g. water from a RO system, bottled water, etc.

While it has a freezing unit for making ice (fast), the ice is delivered into a clear plastic compartment from which you can scoop out ice with the included scoop, or you can remove the container to pour out the ice into something else. This unit does not have a freezer compartment of its own, so the ice it produces into the clear plastic compartment eventually melts and then is collected automatically to be re-frozen.

This is a very substantial, heavy unit. That has its pros and cons. It’s tall enough that it doesn’t fit under my kitchen counter cabinets, so you need to put it in a place that has enough vertical clearance. It also needs some open space on the sides for air discharge, and on one side for the water container. It’s quite heavy so you won’t want to move it around a lot, but on the other hand, it won’t slide around on its own.

If you accidentally press the single control button while the unit is making ice, it resets and starts pouring water over the ice, melting most of it until it gets going again.

Overall a very nice, substantial unit that makes ice very fast, but you need to keep it operating all the time if you expect to have ice all the time. Uses roughly 300 watts of electricity.

review_title: Fresh Good ice is worth it!
review_text:
This ice maker delivered exactly what we were looking for, the good ice that we could only find at a few restaurants or In the hospital. Though it is a luxury item, out of all the options available, this seems to be the least expensive way to get that good ice made fresh at home.

The ice maker is larger than we thought it would be. Be sure to check the dimensions for where you want to put it. There is some “white” noise when it is making ice, but not too loud. We have not heard grinding or other unusual noises. The loudest thing is when the fresh ice falls down and lands in the drawer.

There is a Bluetooth app that can schedule when your machine turns on. But we don’t really use that feature much yet. We just push the big button on the front of the maker when we want ice and within 15 minutes we have enough for a couple servings. One hour gives us a pound of ice, plenty for a larger gathering. The unit shuts off automatically when the bin is full. The maker keeps the ice cold and usable for 4-6 hours. Then the ice melts away into the maker to be recycled at the next making. Good, thoughtful design makes this very simple to operate and use.

The side attachment for extra water is a “must have” accessory. Since there is not a running water attachment, we have to fill the attachment every 4-6 hours of making ice, or about 5 pounds of ice. But refilling is easy and the fact that it isn’t tethered to a running water line makes it easier to move to different areas for dinner, a party, etc. It is heavy, so we don’t move it often.

We have been using the ice maker for almost one month. I went with the GE model because it was a bit newer version of the First Opal product. We haven’t had a good chance to observe how reliable it is. So far so good for the first month. I still went ahead and bought the small appliance protection just in case something happens to our new favorite toy.

review_text:
I've only been using the ice maker for two weeks but like it very much so far. It arrived in excellent condition and was easy to get it started. I have not yet hooked up the side reservoir so can't speak to how well that works.

I only notice the noise when the machine is actually making ice but it's in a room that's far enough away from the general living area so I am not bothered by it at all. It is a little bit loud but not unbearable but I would not want it making ice in the same room where people are watching tv or having a conversation.

Never had Sonic ice to which a lot of people compare the ice from this machine so I can't say if it is similar or not but I do like the ice produced with the Opal. It is light and crunchy making it easy to chew. Ice nuggets that stick together are very easily separated with a gentle scrape of the scoop.

I am replacing the scoop that came with the ice maker because it is made of plastic and I do worry that it will chip when scooping out ice. I am replacing it with a small stainless steel scoop.

At first I didn't see the point of the drip pan but I tend to make a mess sometimes when scooping ice from the bin and transferring it to a thermos and the drip pan catches some of the ice that misses the mouth of the thermos--my fault, not the machine's. The pan is also good for resting the scoop when not in use.

It looks really good and very inviting when the light is on. When it needs more water the circle on the face of the machine turns blue so I never have to worry about running out of ice unless guests are over and using a lot of it. If the bin gets low on ice it automatically starts making more and it takes about 15 minutes.

Overall, I like this ice maker a lot. At $500+ I'm not convinced yet that it is worth that amount of money and it will take a while to pay for itself compared to the money saved from not needing to buy bags of ice at the grocery. If the machine lasts that long I will be happy.

Best thing about it is that I am drinking a lot more water these days because I like the ice a lot and it is so easy to scoop (grocery ice gets stuck together and requires an ice pick to separate or a hard drop of the bag onto the floor) and always available.

review_text:

It is an insanely expensive item, but the more she uses it, the less guilty I feel for allowing her to make this purchase decision.
Why ice? Why scrape the ice to pack into pellets? If you must have ice, then what is wrong with a $3 tray in the freezer? The post office personnel in our town were all abuzz when it came in. They seemed to know what the heck it is and were excited to see it come through. Weird.
She chews it without harm to her teeth (yep, grabs a bowl and snacks on it) and makes slushy drinks. I do not get it, but to each their own.
The system does not store the ice/keep it cold. It sits in an uninsulated drawer, and as it melts that water is recycled to make new ice.
System requires regular cleaning. The teen cleans it, so I have no first-hand experience with it.
Packaged incredibly well. Not kidding. There was even plywood in there.
