review_title: Made great ice, but quit working after a few months.
review_text:
I was pretty hesitant to order this because of all the negative reviews. However, I had some birthday money to spend, so I decided to go for it. My daughter and I love Sonic ice and we were going through a bag per day. I have been very pleased with this machine. Although everyone’s water is different (which would produce different textured ice), in my opinion, this machine produces better than Sonic ice. It’s soft, the perfect size, and has excellent eating texture. It can barely keep up with our ice consumption, but we let it run almost constantly when we are home and bag what we don’t use. The machine is about as loud as our dishwasher—noticeable, but not annoying or excessive. It gets pretty warm on the outside, so make sure there is proper ventilation on all four sides. I clean it once per week with diluted vinegar and have had no issues with grinding noises, shutting off, or other mentioned issues.

Update: 9 months later it broke. Stopped making ice and constantly flashed the blue light indicating it was out of water when it was actually full. I tried all the troubleshooting tips and tricks and finally called in a replacement since it was still under warranty. They said they were waiting on parts and it would be six weeks before they could ship me a “refurbished” unit. It has now been 9 weeks and I have not received anything. The warranty company does not answer the phone and when I email them for an update I get automated emails saying the same thing (six weeks, waiting on parts, sorry it broke, yadda yadda). I spent almost $600 on this thing and although it made perfect ice when it worked, I would not recommend buying this because so many people are having the same issue as I am.

review_text:

review_text: LOVE, LOVE, LOVE this machine.  I run it for 1 full day and empty the bin into a plastic baggie about every hour and freeze it.  When I get the baggie out the next hour to fill it, I break up the ice in the bag by "whacking it on concrete" and it is no longer a frozen lump of ice.  I get enough ice to fill the bin in my freezer and then I have an extra bag left over for when I need to fill the bin next time.  This way I only run the machine every 2 weeks.  GREAT ICE!

review_text: Stopped working after about a year. Terrible implementation.

review_text: I love this ice maker, however it wasn’t love at first use. When we first got it, it wasn’t working right. After reading many reviews I came across one that talked about pampering it for several weeks. This is what we did: read instructions and set it up properly. Then for about a month run it for 2 hours then unplug it for a few hours. It finally started working right but I was needing to clean it every other day. I was using filtered water but decided to try bottled water from a water store. Once I started using the bottled water, the ice maker started making so much ice!  Now it fills up at least three 1 gallon bags a day.

product_title: GE Profile Opal | Countertop Nugget Ice Maker with Side Tank | Portable Ice Machine with Bluetooth Connectivity | Smart Home Kitchen Essentials | Stainless Steel Finish | Up to 24 lbs. of Ice Per Day
review_text: We have had this ice maker for a year now. It worked great the first 4 months and then started to be problematic. We used distilled water and cleaned it regularly. However, increasingly, it won't function properly. We sometimes had to take it through the cleaning cycle 4 or 5 times to get it to work correctly. This past month, after the cleaning, it stopped working. It would make a thin layer of ice and then stop. We have been trying to get the Opal people on the phone for trouble shooting, but they are difficult to reach and then put you on hold or tell you you have called the wrong number.  We miss the ice, because when it worked the ice was great. However, I would discourage purchasing this machine unless you are mechanically inclined and can fix things on your own.

review_title: It's the crunchy ice you want.
review_text:
[[VIDEOID:ac3c6066f0a65c351b52e0a934ba74b5]] This gives the crunchy nugget ice, that you would expect from certain Fast Food places, in your home. But this is not a cheap basic ice maker. If you want that you are looking at the wrong machine.

It has about the same running noise as my refrigerator. And that is not a bad thing. If you need it to run all day, once again you are looking at the wrong machine.

I normally put in about 5 cups of water, let it run, and have my crunchy ice in 30-45 mins. I put in a gallon of water in the side reservoir today, just to show that it is an awesome machine.

I've had it for months with no complains. I hope it works as well for you also.

Update- after getting a new machine from the company a year ago, it recently stopped working again. Very disappointed, total waste of money.

If you love to chew ice and dream of being able to easily grab a cup anytime your home, this is NOT the machine for you.

I’m super disappointed. I was gifted this for my birthday and it’s been one disappointment after another. My first machine worked well for about 2 weeks before it started leaking out of the back. Unfortunately where I have it I didn’t notice when it started and it dripped off my counter and ruined my wood floor and baseboards.
I contacted customer service. They were quick to respond but slow to send out a replacement. They required a credit card be put on file and good for $300 until I sent my faulty machine back. They quickly withdrew the $300 and were extremely slow refunding it.
I’ve had my (used) replacement for about 2 weeks and it does not keep the ice cold. It leaks out from under the ice holder constantly and I basically have a very watery slushy maker.

What is the point of replacing a faulty machine with someone else’s faulty machine? At this point I’m just going to cut my losses and throw it in the trash. Not with the time and EXTREMELY over priced.

review_text:
This machine works great so far. We have a family of six, and I'd say that with how much ice we use vs. how this machine is able to keep up... it does a great job. By the end of the night, the ice bin is full.

Via the app, we tell it to stop making ice at night, and we bag-up the ice it produced during that day. Those bags will come in handy during gatherings.

Word of caution though. When we first plugged in the ice maker, we had the back and left vent too close to the wall and the machine was not producing any ice whatsoever. After we realized this, we pulled it away from the wall and it immediately started making ice.

UPDATE: Had to bump this down to 1 star... the fact that it makes ice is great, the fact that it screams while do so is irritable to say the least. What concerns me more is that GE knows this is an issue and is doing nothing about it... at least tell us what part to replace, I'll do the repair myself. Buyer beware... read the review comments and you'll see many complaining about the squeals and whines.

review_title: I'd pay $500 to NOT have this experience.
review_text:
My machine worked and produced quality ice for about 3 weeks after I purchased it. We noticed a decline in the amount of ice the machine would make as well as the quality of the pellets in that time. Around the 3 week mark the machine started making a very loud compressor noise intermittently and water would pour down the back of the machine into the reservoir and the machine wouldn't make ice. I wasn't sure why it was doing this but reached out to Opal support and followed their directions for defrosting my machine. This did not work and my machine continued to behave in the same manner, and Opal support told me that they would need me to send them a video of the machine doing this behavior so they could analyze.

After I sent the video to Opal they let me know that my machine was broken and they would need to send me a "refurbished" machine to replace the broken ice machine sitting on my counter. They sent me an email that allowed them to authorize a $300 charge to my card so I could be sent a "refurbished" ice machine to replace my faulty ice maker, which wasn't appealing considering I had not had my ice machine that long, but I authorized the charge and waited.

I am still waiting. I authorized the charge over a month ago. I called Opal yesterday to request a new machine, or to have an update and was called back by an escalation manager today who informed me that if I wanted a refund I would "need to contact Amazon" and they did NOT have any ETA on when I would receive a refurbished machine as they had none in stock and did not know when their shipment was arriving. They quite basically can't help, sorry out of luck. I know this is a first world problem, but I have a very expensive ice machine that is just a paperweight and has been sitting on my counter not making ice far longer than it ever did doing it's job. Frustrating experience from start to finish, I would use this a warning to anyone considering purchasing one of these machines.

Amazon support has told me they will allow me to send in the faulty machine and they will refund me $483 off what was an original $600 purchase price. I am losing over $100 dollars as a consumer simply because I wanted the "good" ice and purchased an Opal/GE Ice maker.

review_text:
[[VIDEOID:2fb7e4b4ad6ccbd96a93c46b03a7498f]] Ice is good, but only a week in and this $500 ice contraption started sounding like a dump truck! You had one job to do GE...one job. Lots of videos online showing the same defect. You'd think for the amount of money they charge for this unit they would listen to their customers, but they don't appear to care. We actually bought two of these and both are going back. Very unfortunate.

<<Update 1/9>>

Trying to go through the warranty support hotline for the problems (on hold for 90+ minutes before someone picked up!). They suggested I "go through the cleaning process again, or use distilled water to make ice". This machine was a month old, our house water supply has softener and reverse osmosis systems. This is not a water quality issue. Anyway, the noise in the video continued periodically and I believe it is being cause by ice jamming up the rotating cylinder, causing strain on the motor. We'll just the other day the machine died for good. I'm leaving my 1star review and will be filing a dispute with my credit card company. I'm an engineer by trade and I can tell you that this machine makes great ice, when it works, but the design is critically flawed. If you do decide to buy this anyway, opt for a 3yr warranty as well and plan on sending it back at LEAST once during that time. This machine was not built to last.

<< Update 8/16 >>

We are now on our THIRD return in 8 months. GE outsources the warranty service to a company called OnPoint. This company is non-responsive, has horrible customer service and an average of 90 minute wait times. My claim was ACCEPTED over 2 months ago and I am still awaiting a replacement. They stopped responding to my messages and it was not until I filed a claim against GE with the BBB that I got a response.

At this point, after reading all the countless horror stories from others who have wasted hundreds, if not thousands of dollars on this garbage product, I am seriously considering a class action suit. Please message me if this is something you'd like to take part in!

review_title: regular maintenance must be done regularly
review_text:
Quality of Ice - great
appearance of machine - great
maintenance - we find that you have to clean the "ice chute" of the machine at least every 2 weeks, often times more regularly than that. Failure to do so will result in the machine making a horrible squeaking noise. The noise is caused by mineral built up in the area right above the ice chute. You must clean the machine to avoid this. To clean, you must completely drain the machine of water (recommend placing the machine near a sink because it is heavy and annoying to move). You have to wipe down the ice chute with either a vinegar or bleach solution and run bleach/vinegar through the system.

I find it really annoying that I have to do this cleaning so often because we have a water softener + an in line water filter in the house and we really do not have hard water deposits anywhere in the house....but apparently those deposits are enough to cause issues to this machine.

The first machine was returned within 30 days because the squeaking sound got really obnoxious despite regular cleaning. We received the second machine...it lasted about 80 days. Could not get a hold of GE customer support. To me, it sounded like the coolant pump was going out. The machine ran non-stop and was louder than our washing machine with a constant clicking sound. I don't know...maybe the refrigerant sprung a leak. Either way, we returned machine number 2 right before the 90 day warranty and are now going to look elsewhere for an ice machine.

review_text: [[VIDEOID:895e29d3b0688a6ccb4eae508dd3830c]] We’ve been wanting an pellet ice maker for years. Every time we go to a restaurant that has pellet ice we state that we want a machine. Well we finally had the money to invest in one and researched several. We were confused why it seems why people either seemed to give it 1 star and complained about the loud noise it makes or 5 stars stating it was not very loud and awesome. We are definitely the 5 star awesome crowd. As you see in the video it makes a low volume hum similar to a refrigerator or dishwasher. I find it calming. However, we believe we have figured out the issue. Once the water cycles through in the reservoir it will try to suck up water to make the ice and will make a loud gurgling/screeching noise. Once you put more water in the reservoir the loud sound goes away instantly. Think of a large mouth trying to suck up a tiny amount of water. Give the poor beautiful machine something to drink people! If you don’t want to make more ice then just hit the pretty, big, illuminated button at the top. We turn off the machine over night and it still has ice in the bin the next morning. Some ice does melt but it the water doesn’t sit at the bottom of the tray because the ice bin has drainage holes in the bottom and the water just goes in the water reservoir. If you want to make more ice and need to fill up the ice machine again then just dump/scoop the ice into a gallon ziplock or another tray to put into your freezer. This thing is awesome and I think it looks great. It fits on most any countertop but is large and it should be for this type of quality. The unit is packaged very securely. It even has a plywood base at the bottom and is bottom heavy to avoid being shipped/delivered/stored upside down (of course you’ll have a dumb dumb put it upside down). The way you have to unbox the unit avoids any thinking of turning it upside down. Please note that if the unit still makes a loud noise and the water reservoir isn’t empty then you may have a faulty machine. We’ve read that if the unit is turned upside down it can damage it. This machine is worth the large price tag and honestly I think it’s a great value for the quality and design of this unit. GE doesn’t make junk. We love love love this ice maker and enjoy the delicious ice it makes. Now go and buy it and start crunching some ice!

review_title: Ineffective and Frustrating Customer Service/Unit Leaks
review_text:
My unit leaks. A lot. I have literally spent hours on the telephone trying to reach customer service. The hold times are incredible. Finally, two months ago, I was able to speak with a customer representative, who informed me that they would simply replace the likely cause of the leak-- the auxiliary water tank. They promised to send an email for me to return with some basic information and then they would send the tank.

Weeks passed without an email. After spending hours trying again to reach customer service to find out why no email, I learned they had a typo in my email address. After correcting their error, I received the email.

Weeks again have passed as customer "support" requests more and more information before they will process the warranty claim. Recently, they asked for a video of the leak. When I told them the source of the leak was not visible from the outside of the unit and thus a video would be meaningless, they refused to proceed further, stating that they had to check a box on the warranty claim, which required a video. So, I filled the auxiliary tank, caused another substantial leak over my counter, took a video and because a video of any length can't be emailed, set up a cloud service so I could share a link.

I doubt they will even download the video because evidently its purpose was not for information but to provide another hurdle for me in my effort to proceed with the warranty claim. Next, I expect to receive another email asking for more irrelevant information before they can proceed.

Putting aside the leaks and lack of customer service, the unit produces great ice. I love the concept. The unit produces ice relatively quickly. It isn't quiet, but the noise is not bothersome to me.

product_title: GE Profile Opal | Countertop Nugget Ice Maker with Side Tank | Portable Ice Machine with Bluetooth Connectivity | Smart Home Kitchen Essentials | Stainless Steel Finish | Up to 24 lbs. of Ice Per Day
review_title: Great concept, but not reliable - the Peugeot or Range Rover of ice makers
review_text:
I'm hoping to nurse ours for another two and half months. Then I've hit my break-even, in terms of the spend reduced to Chick-Fil-A for buying bulk ice or even soft drinks. When the Opal works, it's fantastic! Yes, it's noisy. It's also big and heavy for a countertop appliance. The cleaning process is time consuming, and we do do a monthly wash with vinegar to remove the scale from our hard water. But, like already said, when it works - it is awesome!

Problem. The yield is tapering off ... and, I have no idea why. The overly-simplified interface, and very concisely written directions and troubleshooting offer little guidance except to call customer service. I want to do that about as much as poking my eye with a sharp stick. Service? Seriously?!! It's barely a year old, and at $550 ... well, let's just say I expected a little better performance.

My sister and brother-in-law received one as a gift from his mother, and that's where we were introduced. I researched, after visiting them, and did see a number of reviews suggesting performance issues ... but, optimistically figured it was from cranky customers. However, I'm now fearful that we're facing a similar performance issue ... and I am definitely NOT a cranky customer ... :-) Okay, maybe this is a check on my self-awareness ... but, that's another issue.

So, as they say, caveat emptor. It's a cool product ... when it works. I'm hopeful some good competition will arise, seeing that customers aren't balking at a $600 price point, and provide a better quality product.

review_text:

Well, ours was delivered by a small-framed man, note: it's Heavy and awkward. Ours was on its side on the porch. I've worked with refrigeration, and I know from experience when a freezer or refrigerator is laid on it's side the oils and coolant move and when plugged in and turned on it will make noises and stop working. Damaging the system. There was nothing in the instructions about this, so I let ours sit for 24 hours upright position before plugging it in. Once plugged on I turned it on cleaning flushing the system, with “No”unusual sounds.

The only issue we've found is the ice in the bin is wet so when dumping it into a bag or tray in the house freezer it froze together like one big block of ice.

review_text: The Opal ice machine does make small pellet size ice but after an hour and very little in the way of ice, (keep in mind, it begins melting the moment its dropped into the bucket because it lacks adequate insulation) it entered into a defrost cycle. This lasted about 50 minutes. Then it took another 30 to produce ice again. It did this several times in one day. When it goes into defrost, if you aren't there to notice it and remove the ice, it will be lost as the defrost cycle sends a water stream over all of the ice, melting it. The machine is quiet which was nice and I'd have kept it had it not been for the frequent defrost cycles.

review_text:
I was so excited to get this ice maker. I read the reviews and several had mentioned lack of build quality, and although I was skeptical I was excited to give it a try.
The first day it ran great, ice was great, everything worked. Late that night the ice maker developed a squeak. It sounded like the compressor was freezing up or locking up and causing this squeak noise. I looked up the error online and it said the ice maker needed to defrost, and that this typically happens automatically.
After it continued to squeak for 2 hours I decided I’d just turn it off, and let it defrost manually. Overnight all the ice had melted so I figured this was enough time for a defrost. I turned it back on and immediately it began squeaking.
Support asked me to run a cleaning cycle to ensure it wasn’t related to anything being clogged, that also did not help. I ended up having to return it, which putting a 50lb ice maker back in its original box without the original bands around the box is fun in its self.

review_title: Please do not buy. We went through 2 of them.
review_text:
The first one came. We followed directions very closely to set up. The ice was amazing at first. Then it started tasting horrible. A friend described it well “it tastes like free on smells.” We kept thinking it may be the newness. But we went through gallons and gallons a day since our work guys didn’t notice the taste as much as most of us. It never got better. Then started making a grinding noise. I exchanged it for a new one. I really wanted this icemaker to work. The next one worked about 1-2 weeks and completely quit working. It quit reading it had water. We checked everything a million times. It’s all in line with the other reviews. Not sure how it has 4.5 stars with how many 1 star reviews it has. I had confidence though since it says free returns.

However, they would intially not allow me to return and insisted I must have left plastic on it fir it to taste bad. There was literally nowhere to leave plastic on. With the second they said the best they could do was put me in touch with GE for technical support. She insisted it was my fault it quit working and only GE could help me. She refused to consider a refund and told me she was done speaking to me about it.
When I got to another representative, he read the transcripts from the previous conversation. I asked him why it’s said free returns if it only meant free referral and if I literally can’t return it.

I read the same from other reviews, that Amazon won’t return. I have never had this issue before. I asked them to take the “free returns” off the listing. He then offered me a complete refund.

If you need to return don’t deal with GE “set up help.” Push amazon to honor their advertised free returns.

More importantly don’t buy this in the first place. They last a few months for many other reviewers. I think we use more ice than most so it quick working sooner. I think our first was just defective from the start and second broke after a few weeks.

review_text:
I love chewing ice, and was using the crushed ice feature from my fridge. Ended up scraping off my tooth enamel and with cold sensitivity and toothaches. I get de-hydrated very easily, and chewing ice helps me stay hydrated. It's easier for me than drinking plain water.

Chewy ice (aka "nugget" ice, like from Sonic) does not affect my teeth since the ice is much softer, and I will mindlessly chew it all day without issue, staying hydrated and also satisfying that "light snack hunger". Mixing in sweet tea or soda (very occasionally) give you that nice flavored ice at the bottom of the cup.

Yes, this is expensive. I bought it on Prime Day for $100 off, but still hundreds of dollars for a "nice to have" appliance seems frivolous. However, I go through about 4 cups of ice a day while working from home, which helps me stay hydrated and snack less. Looked at through the lens of health helps it make financial sense.

There are other nugget ice makers out there, but this one has it all - good ice, reliable, quick, and a large water reservoir. They big reservoir lasts my spouse and I about 3 days.

It does make a dishwasher-level of background noise while producing ice. Once the tray is full, it's soundless. If you let the water completely empty, it makes a sound like a weed-whacker, which is very annoying, loud and concerning. Turning it off and filling it up makes the sound go away.

Five stars from me. Highly recommended.

review_text:
The ice is great, no complaints there. But this is now my 3rd GE nugget ice maker (previously branded as "Opal") and all three have the same problems. First, they all eventually start making an incredibly loud and extraordinarily irritating squealing noise. It's basically nails on a chalkboard at about 90 decibels. It has to be turned off so it can "defrost". Once that noise starts on the ice maker, it's there forever. You'll need to constantly turn it on and off to make enough ice while avoiding the need to tear your ears off so you don't have to deal with that sound. I can't be certain, but I've heard rumors the CIA is considering using these things as an interrogation technique to replace waterboarding. I've followed all recommendations - cleanings (with the recommended cleaning solution, bleach, vinegar, etc.). Nothing helps.

Also, this thing seems to grow milden like a lab experiment. I thoroughly clean the ice maker every 10 days or so on average and I'll see mildew starting to build up on the water reservoir in 2-3 days. I use the optional water filter in the reservoir and I only use filtered water in the tank. I've also moved it around to different locations to ensure good airflow. No effect. I won't be buying another one. I'll either find a better option (if one exists) or stick to regular ice until there's something more reliable is available.

I think a lot of the positive reviews are from initial usage - again, the ice is great. But this is the third one for me and they've now ALL had the same squealing death throes issue... that can't be a coincidence. There's a design issue here and it's not worth the relatively high cost for the product.

review_title: Cheap electronic components, pump motors = high failure rate
review_text:
I am an engineer by profession, and am thus cursed with the understanding that things don’t work by magic.

We bought one of these ice makers last month. Two days ago, the pump stopped pumping water into the internal reservoir (from the tank under the icebox into a smaller interior hold tank that feeds water to the cold plenum which forms the ice). Without water available to freeze, the icemaker thinks that it needs water even if it is full.

One of three components have failed: the sensor which tells the control circuit to turn the pump on, the control circuit itself, or the internal pump itself.

I am sure, like most consumer products, the manufacturer selected the cheapest possible components to minimize manufacturing costs.

However, as an engineer I know that paying a few extra pennies for basic components such as capacitors, IC’s, sensors, pump motors, etc., significantly increases the MTBF (mean time between failure) of the product. I doubt any serious MTBF analysis was performed during the development of this product.

These components which seem to have a high failure rate are also not the primary drivers of cost. Costs less up front so it looks good on a power point slide presented internally to the bean counters, but on the back end of the product lifecycle it costs GE significantly more.

I wouldn’t recommend this product until they upgrade the BOM (bill of material) and start producing icemakers more reliable components.

Knowing all that, I purchased the product any way -- I know all products have lemons occasionally, that some consumers aren't realistic in their expectations, etc. I've generally had good experiences, and when the experience wasn't good, the manufacturer stepped up quickly and either refunded my money or shipped me a replacement. A friend of mine purchased an Opal years ago (5? 7?) and has had very little trouble / issue with it, so I thought I'd make the purchase.

I purchased the Opal ice maker and it worked great -- for six months. Then it died. So I started the process for a refund / replacement. I called customer service, who took my information, gave me a trouble ticket number, and told me an e-mail had been sent to me to complete. I was to complete the e-mail and send it in. I was also told not to call back again (!), that all further communication would be via e-mail.

That was a month ago. All I've heard is crickets. No responses to requests for status. I was frankly shocked that a company as large as GE would have such poor customer service. Even a canned message would be helpful, something like: "We know Opal is a pitiful product with a high failure rate, but we are overwhelmed with refund requests and like many companies, we simply do not have enough workers to address the complaints in a timely manner. Please rest assured that we will get to your request as soon as we possibly can. If you haven't heard from us by (date), feel free to call our Customer Service line at 800-XXX-XXXX, and we'll give you a verbal update. Thank you for your patience, and we're sorry for this unfortunate experience with our GE product."

I'll come back and report the results when and if I ever get a response / refund / replacement from GE.

Note: I thought the product worked great those first six months, and really liked the soft ice it produced. But at nearly $600, that great ice cost me about $100 a month.

Hopefully this will be resolved in the near future.

review_title: You had me at convertible drawer
review_text:
I’m very happy with my purchase of this refrigerator on July 15, 2022. It was over $500 less here on Amazon than HD/Lowes and was in stock as well (was not at the others). I’m unsure if their appliances come with free installation though.

PROS:

- The interior lighting is vibrant and adjustable (via the app). LED wall is attractive and useful.
- I’m finding the convertible drawer more and more useful. Initially I was wondering why I had opted for this feature, but I’m glad I did. Perfect location for cold cuts, cheeses, eggs, drinks etc. Far more convenient than opening the doors. The drawer offers multiple temperature options depending on your needs. Just wonderful.
- Ice cubes are smaller than my old GE Profile. Cubes are crescent shaped and approximately 1 inch in length. The smaller size fits easier in smaller cocktail glasses etc.
- Freezer offers a lot of space. Far more than expected.
- Door-In-Door feature is great for frequently accessed items like coffee creamers and the like. I use it 3 times as often as opening the main doors.
- The downloadable app is a nice feature that allows modifying the settings and lighting. Also provides pertinent notifications.
- The auto-fill water feature is a really nice touch. I have RO filters in the house so doubt I will use this often but I’m impressed by the tech :)
- I understand that the water filter will mandate replacement after 6 months on avg. Since I have a whole-house filter I called and ordered the “WR17X33825 filter bypass plug” from GE. They shipped it free of charge and took less than a week to arrive by mail.

CONS:

- Although there is a lot of interior refrigerator space, it feels as if there is less door shelf space than my previous GE. The fixed shelves on the left door are smaller and narrower as well.
- The Door-In-Door shelves are running about 5 degrees (Farenheit) warmer than the interior of the fridge so plan accordingly. I have my interior temperature set to 35 F and my DID shelves run 39-40 F.
- The ice bin is half the size of my previous side-by-side GE. Seems to fill rapidly though so aside from bulk ice for parties, etc., doubt this will impact me at all.

Be advised that “Some Assembly Is Required” applies here. The delivery folks brought the unit into my kitchen (thank you fellas), but I tackled the rest. A lot of packing tape and protective film to remove. That was the lion-share of the efforts. A razor blade works best to remove the film without hanging pieces at the seams. Interior shelves and door handles after that. Finally one needs to properly level the unit, then level the doors so they are even. That was a bit of a project for me as my doors were WAY off. After adjusting both doors fully in opposite directions to get close, I needed to loosen the mounting screws to get the rest of the way there. Overall it took about a day and a half to finish the installation. Your mileage will vary.

I'm giving this refrigerator 4.5 stars. Since there's no option for a half star on Amazon I'll round up to 5. My only complaint was with the doors. Took a lot of effort to get them level at the top and I have a uneven gap between the doors and the convertible drawer due to the maximum adjustment needed. I also have no info on longevity. Hoping for 10 years. I'll repost if I experience issues with reliability.

product_title: FRIGIDAIRE EFIC189-Silver Compact Ice Maker, 26 lb per Day, Silver (Packaging May Vary)
review_text:
I received this as a Christmas gift from my sister in December 2020. It is now September 2021 & the ice maker started malfunctioning a few days ago. It seems like it needs to be recalibrated or something. The timing is off and the water “trough” around the stems isn’t going all the way up anymore to let the ice fall off the stems and be lifted into the basket. I think the air that pushes the ice off the stems may be going off too soon causing the ice to drop into the trough while it’s in motion & still has water in it, hindering it from going all the back & draining the water & letting the ice drop. Instead it goes back a little bit, the ice is getting released into the water & then the trough goes back to the ice making position & starts making more ice on top of the ice already on the stems causing a huge block of ice that only falls off after the machine goes into hibernation mode and quits cooling so it seems. I’m guessing that because the air is perhaps pushing the cubes too soon the water trough thinks they are off & just goes back in ice making position. I don’t know really, I’m no engineer. This is really just through observation. Either way, 9 months seems like a short lifespan and I’m really disappointed. Especially since the “troubleshooting scenarios” in the guide are useless.

Ironically enough though, my husband has a masters in mechanical engineering and he said my observation is correct but he doesn’t know which scenario is the problem, the trough not going back all the way or the air pushing too soon (he doesn’t have the time or desire to watch the ice maker to make a definitive diagnosis;). I’m just going to reach out to Frigidaire and bitch I suppose. 🤔

review_title: Side of the device "melted" and the fan shakes so hard the unit turns off.
review_text:
We were super excited about getting the new ice machine and things were going great, until they weren't.

Received the ice maker approximately 28 Nov 21 - Did not plug it in and put it into service until approximately 24 Jan 22. Hey, we have some neurodivergence in the house so it took a little bit to get there. This ultimately was the "downfall" for being able to return this product as the return time ran out on 31 Jan 22.

The good: This thing pumps out ice at the rate the manual and listing states. It has some cute cubes and they are small enough to fit most of the reusable bottles/cups we use here in the home.

The not so good: After 31-days of use the fan (located on the back right side of the unit) seems to be loose or broken and now, at least once a day will rattle so loud and hard that the unit shuts down. There is, what appears to be, a spot where the unit overheated and "melted" the side, to the tune of an approximate area of 6" x 4" as notated by the picture with the ruler. The unit began to "auto shut off" about 2-weeks into use, but it was not consistent and we could not figure out why, shortly after is when we noticed the melted section. So it seems there may be a defect (possibly just with the one we purchased) in this one.

Maybe this unit does not support being plugged in 24hrs a day? I may have missed that in the instructions. However, for a $129 unit to last 31 days, just long enough to get past the return point, that also does not seem right. We plan to find a new countertop ice maker, likely from a different company, we expected more from a Frigidaire product.

We do hope you have great success with your item if you choose to purchase this product.

review_title: Broke in 5 months and warranty not good!
review_text:
We had a similar model than this one, but it broke a little after the first year. We wanted a similar one, but one that had a manufacture's warranty. This one looked perfect and we spent a little more than the competitors on it.

Five months into owning it and it starts to make a horrible grinding noise when it's used. Not wanting to damage it further, we have stopped using it. I reached out to the manufacture about their warranty. I was required to submit about 6 photos of the unit from all angles and also a video of it making the noise to prove it was defective. After that, they would replace or repair, but only if we paid to have the large and heavy unit shipped to them. I live on the east coast of the US and they require me to pay to ship it to the west coast. The shipping price is close to the cost of a new unit. So, basically, I can have them fix my old one or buy a new one for about the same price.

The unit is defective and within the warranty, but they won't replace it until I spend as much money as it cost to buy it to ship the broken one back. Why am I punished when their unit is defective? The warranty is useless. I would not recommend purchasing this one. If you want a cheap piece of crap, there are identical models you can spend less money on.

review_text: Reviews here indicated that the unit has a high failure rate, so I got the insurance from Asurion for $11.99.  The ice maker worked for 15 months and then the "Ice Full" sensor failed.  (The "Add Water" sensor never worked, and I suspect that reports of the motor burning out quickly were due to customers not realizing that the water reservoir was empty, so we got into the habit of monitoring that.)  The claim through Asurion was easy, so we got to use the ice maker for more than a year at a cost of $11.99.  If I can't find a better option, we'll get the same kind and play the same game again.  The cubes are on the small side and they melt quickly while sitting in the reservoir; not sure what could be done about that, but then I'm not an engineer.  It would be nice to be able to see how far the unit is through a cycle, so that you can time better when to turn it off.

review_text:
Purchased this washing machine and the matching dryer. Got them installed and running last night. I was very disappointed with my initial wash.

Do not wash your clothes on the normal setting. The water does not fill up far enough to completely submerge the clothes and the agitator will shred your clothes. I was told that you can remove the agitator but I am not finding any information in the manual or on YouTube about doing so. I bought it with the intent to remove the agitator because of how it can damage clothing.

If you use powder detergent the normal cycle does not provide enough water to dissolve powder detergent and fully rinse it from your clothes. You must wash your clothes on one of the other settings which will take much longer.

The app is an absolute joke. And LG is so proud of it and certainly does propel them into the standards of technology 5 to 7 years ago. Seems a little late to join the game. But once you use the app you can see that they have no innovative twist or even basic knowledge on how to provide a customer with an easily navigatable and useful app. It's quite complex and not of the modern simplistic design. The features are in reality very few. You cannot remote start a washing machine, the notifications are out of sync with the cycle and there are no other features that are worthwhile. The app does not sync well with the machine. And the machine must be on and Wi-Fi activated each time you wish to use it. All it does is add a frustrating useless step to your normal washing routine.

Six features that need to be added: allow the owner to add more water to the washing bin during a cycle. Add a warm rinse. redesign the detergent bin. It is very difficult to add powder detergent. They haven't located in a very awkward place. allow the owner to remove the agitator. Allow the owner to unlock the lid during a cycle to add more clothes. Fire the team you have working on the app and hire a competent team who is forward thinking. (Or maybe LG is just too heavy handed to allow for any useful innovation?)

Not all of us have kids, or even have kids over to our homes. There's no reason to have the lid locked the entire cycle. Reminder to you overly safety conscious folks out there: not everything in reality is for children.

review_title: Do not buy!  This washer is a finicky piece of crap that doesn't wash and gets easily unbalanced.
review_text:
I am writing this here and publishing it to every site that will take a comment this long. I want you all to avoid getting ripped off. This machine will not make your life easier. It will make a daily/weekly chore far more time-consuming. I hate this thing so much that I'd go so far as to say it's actively anti-woman. (We all know who is still doing most of the laundry all over the world.)

Now, the capacity on this thing is huge. This is one of the reasons I bought it, as we have an incontinent adult child and a lot of bedding to wash when she visits. One problem: You can't put loads of bedding in the washer indiscriminately. Even if it everything fits in a couple of loads.

This machine has a serious issue with becoming easily unbalanced. Sheets hold more water than mattress pads. The sheets get wadded up and you are constantly pausing the cycle and re-distributing things. If you do not, the machine attempts to address the problem itself BY ADDING MORE WATER and swirling things around. If you are offended by wasting water, or your water bill, this is NOT the machine for you.

The same problem occurs for lightweight twin comforters versus a cotton blanket. Cotton blanket gets heavy and unbalances the load. So I am learning what bedding goes best together and babysitting loads of bedding through the washing cycle. This is going to be a problem any time you time you try to run different types of clothing all at once. If you're not a laundry sorter, this is definitely not the machine for you, because you have to be.

And forget about washing just a couple items you really want to wear. Same reason.

Second major issue? The machine fails in its basic job: Washing clothes. Recently, I realized that an unusual number of shirts (our most commonly stained items) were not coming clean with our standard stain treater and same old laundry detergent we've always used. So I'd spray them with more stain treater and rub them together and run them in the next load. I've never had to do more than this with any other machine. But they were still coming out stained.

I now have to pre-wash stains out of clothes before putting them in the wash. Spray, scrub them with a clean toothbrush, rinse, and then put them in the washer. This is a ridiculous waste of time and, of course, my menfolk do not notice they stained their frigging clothes; so things need washing multiple times. The stain becomes more set after it's dried, so we've lost a few items.

This machine machine makes washing an onerous chore, again. Is this how my great-grandmother spent her days?

Just avoid purchasing this at all costs.

review_title: Ice maker will fail and Samsung won't help
review_text:
This is by far the worst appliance purchase I have ever made. I have had countless problems with this since the day it was delivered. First day of use, it won't cool down. Luckily was able to get it replaced within a week with another one. Then after 9 months, the ice maker stops working and the ice maker compartment is frozen over. I called customer service and after a lengthy hold was told that it was because the fridge wasn't level. Told me to defrost the fridge and make sure it was level.

That seemed to work and I forgot about it until six months later, the same problem. This time I was told it was due to air the water line. So I defrost, pull out a few gallons of water to flush the line and I get ice again. A few weeks later the motherboard failed, but now I'm, out of warranty so I keep getting shuffled around over 3 days while my food rots until I give up and pay to have it replaced. Shortly afterwards, the ice maker stops again. Same problem so I decide to have the ice maker replaced.

That works well for about 9 months and then the problems start up again. I replaced the icemaker one more time and that worked for a year before it stopped making ice. I can defrost it and get a few weeks of ice before It fails.

Bottom line Samsung refridgerators have a design flaw that causes ice to buildup around the fan in back of the ice compartment. Once the fan stops, the icemaker begins to freeze over and finally stops working.

There is no solution to this design flaw that I've been able to find. I've tried every repair suggestion and nothing works. And because of the class action lawsuit over this issue, Samsung has refused to acknowledge the problem or do anything to help me.

Be warned, do not buy Samsung refrigerators until this design flaw is solved. Search for Samsung refrigerator ice maker lawsuit for more details

review_text:
I got mine 4 months ago and while there was a problem with the control panel that took a month to replace (they said it was such a new product they didn’t have a large part inventory and it had to come from the factory during COVID), it was repaired without cost and has worked great since then. I think the induction top can boil water faster than the microwave, seconds not minutes! I air fry roasting vegetables all the time. I didn’t get the official basket. I use a black crisper tray set upside down over a slightly smaller baking sheet with some binder clips to prop it up a bit so air can be blown under the basket but the sheet catches crumps and drips without them being blown around the oven. So it’s a smaller, handier, tray to slide onto a rack instead of replacing a rack and adding a catch tray below.
There is a little bit to learn, like don’t preheat your pans much or you risk warping them because they heat up so fast! Don’t drag your pans around or you could scratch the surface, you can actually put a thin silicone sheet in between, or even a paper towel. You can’t pick up a pan for more than a couple seconds or the burner shuts off.
I had a 36” range before, but this 30” seems to have as much room inside the oven as the 25 yr old one. The smooth cool cooktop is another useful space as opposed to gas grates. The oven light goes on and off as you open the door. It has a switch too but they don’t recommend turning the light on during air fry.
The two things I am careful about: NOT leaving pans and kettles on top of the burners. I have leaned on the front to reach something above the range and brushing the controls have turned them on. With no magnetic metal on the burner, nothing will happen. You will hear the beeping and know to check what happened plus there is a lock function to keep children from doing it too -so it is not really an issue. The other thing is no one can tell me how safe it is to pull a hot pan out of the oven and put it directly on the cooktop like I used to on the gas grates...so I always have Big thick hot pads handy to throw down. I know the ceramic glass can handle a lot of heat, but I’m not going to push it. I love how easy it is to clean up and I found gap covers to squeeze between the stove and counter top to prevent anything from falling in between and give it a built in look. You put polish on it like a car for even easier clean up! For reference: that is an 8x8 pan in the picture. I usually have a Silpat sheet on it for extra peace of mind against dropping or scratching...no scratches yet!

review_text:
I grew up and learned to cook on a nice gas cooktop. Also used coil type electric and flat top electric a bit. Really, really preferred gas between gas/electric. Fast forward to married life, no gas available in our subdivision. Made do with a glass flat top for quite a few years, but never liked it. That one finally died, and I decided to give induction a try for a few reasons, but mainly to avoid having to put in LP, and a lack of a hood in our kitchen.

So far really like it. Still slightly prefer gas, as I am a huge fan of cast iron & carbon steel. Both work on induction, but tend to heat a bit unevenly if you are really throwing the heat to them. This can mostly be overcome, especially with cast iron, by heating them up to medium low heat allowing them to become heat soaked before taking the temp higher. They still get hot spots (usually the center) at the extreme upper end of the heat level, but nothing crazy. Good quality clad pans heat very evenly. The biggest thing that is noteworthy is just how much power induction has compared to either gas or electric, and how stable it will hold temps. Mine has settings of L, 1,2...8,9,H, plus a "P" power setting for each eye. Power is for rapid heating of stuff like pasta water. I was skeptical of having notches vs a continuous variable control, but that has proven to not be an issue. Once you get the temp you need to work at dialed in, it will hold it indefinitely. You can also take away heat instantly....for instance to stop a pot from boiling over. Kill the eye, and the boil over stops just as quickly. One common complaint with induction is a "singing" noise between the pot/pan and stove. I have not experienced this with the exception of on the P or high settings. Use of those settings is typically temporary/short, so not something I can't live with. The other big advantage, especially since we don't have a hood, is the lack of heat loss into the room. Makes a big difference in terms of not overheating the kitchen with cooking. Overall I'm a fan. Still like gas a bit better, but its a huge upgrade compared to plain electric. Added safety benefit of the eyes being almost immediately cool is nice as well.

Overall pretty impressed with ordering through amazon. Was about $600 less than anywhere else at the time, and just as fast. Air fry function is pretty neat, but can smoke out the kitchen if you do stuff that is too greasy. Like that it fits a freestanding space, but looks like a slide in. Had to make a small mod to the rear trim piece to work with our countertops/tile backsplash, but that was no big deal. Preheat is as fast as I've seen and overall bake quality is great. Bottom storage drawer is a bit small, but that space is utilized in the oven itself. Overall very impressed for the $.

product_title: GE GDT225SSLSS 24 Inch Built In Fully Integrated Dishwasher with 3 Wash Cycles, 12 Place Settings, in Stainless Steel
review_title: Probably the worst home appliance ever made
review_text:
GE, are you OK? Why do you hate your customers so? I ask because I recently installed this very dishwasher in my apartment, and I can only conclude that whoever designed it genuinely hates all human beings, especially the ones that buy this dishwasher. Either that, or GE simply does not even bother to test out its appliances to see if they are actually something the rest of use can use. Actually, that can't be the answer, because it appears that you have gone out of your way to make this dishwasher nearly impossible to use.

So what's wrong with it, besides "everything"? Let's start with the placement of the detergent holder. Like most dishwashers, it's a small recess into which you put the detergent tablet and then snap shut a door to hold it in. The idea, of course, is that the door opens during the cycle to clean your dishes. So why on earth would you put that recess in a place that it is constantly blocked by the cutlery in the cutlery container that you have placed directly in front of this recess? There are literally parts of the cutlery container that you cannot use because using them would block the door covering the detergent, as I have found out the hard way. How can it be that this was not discovered during some kind of testing period? Or how about the wine glass holders on the top rack? They fold down and are specifically designed for you to place the stem of a wine glass through. Unfortunately, if your wine glass actually has a stem then it will be too tall to actually fit on the top rack - something you will find out when you innocently try to slide the rack back inside the dishwasher and find it has smashed your wine glass. Yes, I said smashed. So little testing has been done on this thing that GE has not even noticed that you cannot place a wine glass in a rack as intended without it being broken. Honestly, I could go on and on. How the places meant for the plates won't actually hold any kind of normally shaped or sized plate. How there is nowhere you can put a bowl. How there is nowhere you can easily place any kind of pot or saucepan. Again... how could none of this been tested?

Oh, and finally, when you do manage to get your dishes inside and the machine on.... it does an absolutely terrible job of actually cleaning them. My washing routine now consists of putting the dishes in the dishwasher, taking them out, and washing them all over again by hand.

Not sure what we have done to insult you, GE... but, please, get yourself some help.

review_title: Our LG Dryer caught fire during the warranty period!
review_text:
Our LG dryer caught fire 10.5 months after we bought it new from an authorized dealer. There was extensive smoke damage and, obviously, our home and the safety of my family (wife, two daughters and a dog) were imperiled. Luckily, in the end, only the dryer was dryer was ruined. Who knows what chemicals we were exposed to from the smoke?! The WORST part of it all was how LG ducked and weaved and finally turned their backs on us completely. The only thing they would offer to do was repair this faulty, dangerous unit. I told them I don't care if 10 NASA scientists came to our house, fully disassembled and put the unit back together again, it will NEVER be used in our home EVER AGAIN. Who knows if it will catch fire again?! Who knows what chemicals are in the smoke that was created?! LG was completely unsympathetic. They said we were refusing their help and washed their hands of us. And we were contacted by someone in the "Presidential Liaison Office" who said she was the ultimate authority. One of the most unhelpful, unfriendly customer service people I've ever talked to. A heart of ice. And, for the record we're adults and we know how to use a dryer properly, clean the lint filter, etc. The technician who LG sent used a special airflow meter to confirm that the vent and duct were clean.

LG refused to help us in any kind of meaningful way when its appliance caught fire under warranty in our home, putting our safety and possessions at grave risk. It took days for them to address the issue and I spent hours begging and pleaded various customer support agents in Manilla to escalate this. Finally, someone from the highest levels of the support organization, a "Presidential Liaison" contacted me. She was unfriendly, unsympathetic and utterly unhelpful. The only thing she would offer to do was to give me 20% of the value of the unit or have it repaired. I'm not crazy. NO ONE wants a faulty dryer that has caught fire repaired! Who knows what was burning in that unit (plastic, wiring, etc) and what dangerous chemicals were created?! Who knows whether it will catch fire again?!.The idea that we would keep this appliance in our house, given the fact that it put my entire family and home at risk, is completely ludicrous. But the Presidential Liaison was like a robot, just repeating the same thing over and over. I asked her if she was OK with me leaving our interaction furious with LG and ready to yell this story from the mountaintops (ie. social media, review sites, BBB, Consumer Affairs, UL, etc.) and she said she was fine with it. What kind of liaison is that?! What is clear is that the culture of LG and LG Support is completely unsympathetic, completely focused on the bottom line instead of the customer, perhaps even jaded and uninterested in the reputation of LG itself. It is the reflection of a sick company and a cynical corporate culture. For such a widely praised company, it was shocking and hugely disappointing. Needless to say, we will NEVER use LG products again and we will make sure to tell this sad story to everyone we know and care about.

review_text:
I love LG products and I want to love this washer but I just can't. We have had our washer for two weeks. It seems to get clothes clean, although because of such small water usage, they come out very wrinkled. The instruction manual is the WORST I have ever seen for a major appliance. It has 14 pages of installation, one-fourth of a page on how to use a top loader washer--not kidding--and 6 pages of trouble shooting. Nothing on the cycles, nothing on the extra options. Even trying to find the information online is hit and miss. The washer is worth 4 stars, but the manual is worth zero. I'm not sure I would buy this model again.

Note added November 2021: We have had this washer for 9 months, and every time I use it, I say "I hate this washer." It is without question the worst major appliance I have ever owned. The water level is ALWAYS inadequate to get the clothes clean; there is a Water Plus button to add more water, but it is always a guess as to how much to add. Also, without an agitator, there is a dead zone in the middle: if a large item gets trapped in there, it never moves with the rest of the clothes. I may make it 12 months before replacing it with a new washer, but my frustration level increases every time I use it. I like other LG products, but this one is horrible.

product_title: LG WT7300CW 5 Cu.Ft. White Electric Top Load Smart Washer
review_text: Just got this washer, installed it (which was easy) and it's doing a nice job of cleaning our clothes.  My issues are with the manual and connectivity.  After a live chat with an actual person, they sent me a link to connect with a tech.  I emailed my issues and they responded the next day.  Why in the world they don't tell you in the manual that the washer's wifi password is the last 4 numbers/letters that show up for the washer in the wifi settings repeated twice, and not your router's password, is beyond me.  Anyway, I got it connected and it sends a notification when your load is done and that's useful.  You use a qr code reader to dl a more detailed manual that walks you through the many cycles and many features of the machine.  Kind of a pain, but it saves paper so I get it.  It's not your parents' washer.  Others have complained about the lack of water in the cycles but the manual does tell you how you can increase the amount of water in the cycle as well as controlling water temp, spin rate, etc.  There is a learning curve but I feel like most new appliances these days are in the same category.  Just clean my clothes and I'll be happy.

review_text: We like to add the Soak cycle to the washer cycles to enhance cleaning results.  We can certainly do that using the control panel on the washer. My LG dryer allows me to push a button and save my dryer settings for reuse.  LG has gone to all the trouble to add WiFi and an app and they don’t even allow the customer to create and save their own cycle definition or allow us to modify one of your pre-defined cycles. product_title: LG WT7300CW 5 Cu.Ft. White Electric Top Load Smart Washer
review_text:
Brand new LG WT7300CW Washer. All the advertisements say that it works with Amazon Alexa and Google Assistant. You have to install the LG ThinQ app on your phone and then link Alexa and Google Home. Siri or the Apple Home app does not support washers at this time apparently. The LG ThinQ app can send a notification to your phone when the washer is finished. Neither Alexa or Google Home can notify us when the washer is finished. At least Google Home can tell me how much time is left on the washer. But Alexa can only tell me if the washer is on or off. LG built a terrible skill for Alexa. They need to hire a good programming team and fix it.

Here are Alexa commands that work and don't work.

Me: "Alexa, is the washer running?"
Alexa: "The top load washer is on."

Me: "Alexa, what's the status of the washer?"
Alexa: "That's not supported yet."

Me: "Alexa, how much time is left on the washer?"
Alexa: "That's not supported yet."

Me: "Alexa, is the washer finished?"
Alexa: "That's not supported yet."

Me: "Alexa, ask LG for the status of the washer."
Alexa: "Sorry, I didn't find a group or device named L G Washer"

Me: "Alexa, ask LG how much time is left on the washer."
Alexa: "That's not supported yet."

Me: "Alexa, what mode is the washer in?"
Alexa: "Top load washer doesn't support that."

Google Home commands that work and don't work:

Me: "Hey Google, what's the status of the washer?"
Google: "The top load washer is on washing cycle and will be done in 53 minutes."

Me: "Hey Google, how much time is left on the washer?"
Google: "The top load washer will be done in 47 minutes."

Me: "Hey Google, tell me when the washer is finished."
Google: "In Greek, that's: εμένα όταν σταματήσει το πλυντήριο."

Me: "Hey Google, tell me when the washer is off."
Google: "Got it, stopping the Top Load Washer." (Oops! Now I need to restart it!)

After several email exchanges I was informed that the pedestal was back ordered and would not arrive until mid August. I called customer relations again on a Friday afternoon to discuss a plan. review_text:
We LOVE this oven! The first gas range we've had. It is a joy to cook with. Very fast to heat. Much faster than our electric range, which this replaced. To date, we've utilized about every feature except broil. The convection bake is very nice. The air fry feature gets a lot of use too. So happy with these features, we got rid of our convection toaster oven and our countertop air fryer.

I converted this to propane, which was a bit confusing. Took a while to figure out the proper burner tips necessary, as the kit I bought didn't quite match the range as far as the instructions were concerned. I was able to locate the proper instructions online which more closely matched the burner configuration.

I checked the oven box temperature with an external probe and the stove and thermometer matched very closely. The oven does rise past the set temp when it first heats up significantly, but once it hits your set temp and the burners shut off, the temperature rapidly falls back to where it should be and maintains very well. It does seem to cook faster than, say, the food box instructions indicate. I've learned to keep an eye on food items such as frozen pizzas, shaving a few minutes off.

Now the con, and it's a big one though not able to be overcome. The top burners are notoriously easy to accidentally turn on. As others have stated, simply brushing up against them can fire them up. I can't recall how many times this happened in the first week just reaching up over the range to retrieve something from the microwave, or a pot (we have hanging over the cook area). The real scare was when I came down from showering to discover one of our dogs, in an attempt to lick a griddle we had cooling at the back of the range, turned the front burner on--sans ignition! The smell of gas was overwhelming. Fortunately, I was home. It hadn't been hissing gas very long and I was able to air out the house. But could have been catastrophic. Apparently, this is not the only gas range to have this issue. A quick search will turn up dozens of articles, exposes', and similar stories. A quick push and flip, and you go right past the piezo ignition straight to gas gushing out. Almost a deal breaker, we made a wooden plank to fit behind the knobs to keep them from being pushed in. Then, after reading an article about gas stoves and this hazard, I found an after-market company that makes safe range knobs that require you to pinch, push, then turn. This completely eliminates the problem. It was, in the end, worth the extra expenditure considering how many other manufacturers' ranges have this problem.

To end, we love cooking with this gas range. It's beautiful, relatively easy to maintain and keep clean, and handles smudges pretty well. I really like the oval center burner, though the flame pattern is a bit wonky on ours unless you actually have a griddle or other piece of cookware on it when it's lit.

review_text: The GE Sensor-dry dryer fails miserably at its basic mission: to dry clothes.  We bought one new and after about six frustrating months had a GE repair person out to fix it because it wouldn't run a full dry cycle without either stopping or finishing with semi-dry clothes.  He explained that sensors in the dryer are spaced so that only clothes in either the front or back are measured for dryness....yet the action of the dryer moves larger items to the rear.  This means that you positively cannot dry jeans with shirts (shirts may be dry, jeans will be damp) or towels with clothes (same issue) in the same load.  In addition, the slightest amount of lint with cause the dryer to beep about once every 45 seconds for an eternity...until you get so tired of listening to it that you come to turn it off or clean out the tiny amount of lint that set off the sensor. The only way to get what you expect is to put every single load on Heavy Duty and pray that whatever you're drying doesn't throw off any lint.  Our guest house has a dryer from a competitor that works like a charm.  The GE dryer is so frustrating that I won't ever buy another GE appliance.

review_title: WIFI is old school and does not work with dual band mesh access points.
review_text: What a letdown, this fridge is all about the tech and you pay a pretty penny for it. The wifi connectivity is 2.4 Ghz, NOT 5 ghz (dual band). Why does this matter? If you have a mesh wifi setup (the kind offered by every major wifi vendor) you have a wireless access point (multiple) that send out both 2.4 and 5ghz sharing the SAME wifi name. This is so any modern equipment can communicate with the access point and work out the best band to use and switch between bands as conditions change. When you have a single band 2.4ghz client, like this fridge, it cannot tell the difference and it more often than not fails to connect or disconnects.  This protocol has been out and common for YEARS (Like Orbi, ASUS Aimesh, Googel Mesh, etc.) To put out such an "advanced" hitech unit out and be incompatible is just shameful. There is almost no cost difference in dual band hardware and no redesign of any other components would be needed to have made the change. Also, the 2.4ghz band if often overcrowded in a modern home and microwaves interfere with that band, you know, that box right near the fridge? Even if you can connect the UI and interface is not good at all, confusing, tries too hard to be cute, does not do the basics well. They released it with a many questionable features that are not the useful but look good in a demo when they should have introduced the basics that work and THEN added features with updates. Also, the Samsung answer to Echo and Google home is Bixby, ever hear of it? Exactly. It is worse than a first gen Echo. Why not include Echo or G-Home instead of Bixby? Oh, the fridge works great, temp is consistent, ice maker has NEVER clogged.

review_text:
This washer is terrible. The washer is frequently unable to begin its spin cycle because starting to spin the wet clothes makes the washer shake with a huge banging. It must pause, try to adjust the wet clothes with a slow rotation, and start again. This inability to progress to spin happens rarely with small loads (~5 pounds of kids clothes), often with medium sized loads (~10 pounds of adult clothes including a sweater or two), and always if anything bulky is included (towels, bed sheets, throw blankets). When the washer has a hard time starting the spin cycle, the best case is that the washer will attempt to rebalance the wet clothes over and over again, not making any progress for ~20-60 minutes before the stars align and spin occurs. Rebalancing by hand does not help. The bad scenario is that among all of the failed spin attempts, the washer will begin to leak water on the floor. It's hard to tell exactly where the water is coming from, but after some experimentation, it seems to come from the overflow vent in the back.

We have called LG service multiple times, but they had no solution for the inability to progress to spin cycle ("try rebalancing by hand" is not useful when gravity inevitably pulls the wet clothes back to the bottom of the drum) and we didn't have the leaking problem until we had owned the washer for 13 months, which is one month more than the warranty. It was professionally installed and balanced, and I have personally confirmed the balance and level installation multiple times.

I wish I had bought something else.

review_text:
The new Samsung 6.3 cu. ft. Front Control Slide-In Electric Range with Convection & Wi-Fi in Stainless Steel is a great oven, but like with everything in life, it could be better.
Let me start by listing the Pros:
Fingerprint Resistant: It does minimize the number of fingerprints on the stainless-steel frame, but it may leave little smudges here or there.
Five heating elements: The power on the heating elements is awesome. It provides fast heat in just seconds. It also includes two dual ring elements to be used with multiple sized pots and pans.
Oven: large 6.3 cu. ft. oven is big enough to accommodate multiple large dishes at once, especially with the holidays coming up. Powerful convention decreases the time for baking, roasting and evenly cooking food. Compatible with SmartThings and any virtual assistance available.

Now the Cons:
Fingerprint resistant: smudges are still visible and will build up if not wiped. Touch screen smudges constantly and it is very sensitive to the touch. Any passing of a cloth on the touch screen will activate any of the features. The locking mechanism is available, but it also locks the oven door and if the sensors do not detect the door, it will take a while for the locking mechanism to work. Additionally, there are no instructions on the usage of the touch screen controls in either of the three manuals that come in the box. To get a detailed description on the touch screen features, you will need to go to Samsung’s website and download the manual for the range.

product_title: Samsung NE63T8311SS 6.3 cu. ft. Front Control Slide-In Electric Range with Convection & Wi-Fi
review_title: So disappointed! Too many flaws, very frustrating
review_text:
After several years of use, our prior range ultimately broke and repairs would have equaled the cost a new one. Unfortunately, it was just a couple of days before Thanksgiving and most stores had big appliances on back-order due to pandemic-related delays. Finding a range that was available for pick-up within a couple of days certainly limited our selection. After endless online and in-person looking, researching, etc. we came upon this Samsung range. We have a Samsung fridge and have had good luck with it for eight years, so we were hopeful for the same with the range. Black Friday sales prices were already in effect, so we were able to purchase for several hundred less than the listed price, but was still around a thousand dollars. Ugh.

Pros: It bakes and cooks. The oven light works well.

Now for the cons:

While we were excited to have the Air Fry feature with the larger capacity this range provides, it has become a cleaning nightmare. The way the fan blows, it blows grease all over the bottom of the stove. The best solution we've found is to wrap the entire bottom shelf in aluminum foil to catch all the splattered grease. You can't just put it directly on the bottom of the oven because the fan will blow it around. It also blows grease on all the sides. Not only will it set off the smoke alarm when you open the door, it means you'll have to use the self-cleaning feature after each use of the air fryer.

We've tried the Steam Cleaning feature, but don't notice a difference before/after. The only effective solution is the traditional self-cleaning feature. We were also warned by sales people to try not to use the self-cleaning feature too frequently because it can reduce the life of the control panel. Great. Fortunately, the steam/smoke vents out the back so that's a slight plus for longevity of the panel, but creates a bit of a smokey mess nearby.

The front touch panel is at an angle and so sensitive that if you or your sleeve or other clothing barely touch it, it activates or deactivates whichever function was breezed by. This has resulted in the oven unwittingly being turned off several times while cooking on the stove top resulting in instances of raw or unbaked food, the oven being turned on unwittingly, and the the self-cleaning function turned on unwittingly.

On the stove top, one of the burners indicate "Rapid Boil" but there is apparently not an expedited feature for boiling using that or any other burner. It has taken as long as 15 minutes to heat water in a partially full tea kettle and boiling water in a mid-sized pot can take 25 minutes or more.

The stove top may be fingerprint resistant, but cleaning it to look like new is not a possibility. After the first use, there were scuff marks that cannot be removed.

The way the burners are positioned, there isn't adequate room for a larger pan in front and medium pan in back, they crowd one off the other burner or touch.

Trying to clean the glass in the oven door is a virtual waste of time. Even after the self-cleaning feature, grease splatters from using the air fryer remain.

The oven racks have wider-than-usual spaces between each section, so if you put a frozen pizza on it to bake, the sides of the pizza will droop over the edges of the section, melt cheese onto the bottom of the oven and back to smoke alarm and self-cleaning again.

Pre-heating time seems slower than it should be too so we resort to turning on the broiler to make preheating go faster.

The timer - you have to hold down for three seconds to activate or deactivate. Despite how sensitive every other function is on the panel, this one doesn't always register. Half the time we give up and use the timer on the microwave or our phone.

Most items have to bake several minutes longer than in previous electric oven.

The drawer at the bottom is smaller than traditional oven drawers, we can fit the piece for the air fryer, a pizza stone and one other cookie pan and that's about it.

There's a gap on both sides where we slid it in and need to purchase caps for esthetic purposes and so smaller items don't fall down the sides.

If you like fire hazards, uncooked meals, and spending an unnecessarily inordinate amount of time cooking what should be the fastest and simplest of meals, and using a self-clean feature a lot, you might enjoy this range. It has provided me with greater resolve to save faster for a remodel of our kitchen to justify purchasing a replacement.

With taxes, etc., we paid over a THOUSAND DOLLARS for this. (We looked at used appliances, but there were no slide-in electric ones available in a 50 mile range at the time.) I'm thinking the outdoor grill or cooking in the fireplace might have been better long-term solutions.

It's best use might be as a very large, conversational paper weight. (And we all know how in-demand paper weights are these days!)

review_text:
LG designs great refrigerators. They're functional, efficient and attractive. Unfortunately, LG uses linear compressors. The LG Linear compressor has a poor life expectancy when compared to different types of reciprocating compressors like the piston or scroll typically found in AC units, or the digital inverter compressors used by Samsung and others. Piston compressors last 20 to 30 years, but the government wants them gone, so companies are stuck with lower life compressors.

Linear compressors are cheaper and there are a few other advantages for refrigerators: however, none of that makes up for the failure rate of the design used by LG.

The failure rate is so high, LG has settled two class action lawsuits in the last few years regarding the compressor, yet LG refuses to change the design, switch to a more reliable compressor type, or even admit the problem.

All appliances produced now days have reliability issues. Part of the problem is US and European governments forcing companies to make more and more efficient appliances. The more efficient compressors and refrigeration equipment become, the less reliable they are. Add that to the poor quality control in Chinese and Korean factories, and the consumer is losing big.

For example, AC units that have a very high seer rating (high energy efficiency) fail more often and cost more to repair than low seer units. Any savings on energy is over shadowed by repair costs over the life of the equipment. The government doesn't care how much we spend replacing and repairing appliances because they want to show everyone how much they're doing to help the environment. It's a bogus objective that comes at a very high cost to consumers. And there is more of it coming--water heaters (barely work now), washing machines and more refrigerator crap.

Of course, LG has more reliable options so who knows what their internal costs are and the internal politics. You can bet that LG has looked closely at the economics of replacing the sealed cooling system with a more reliable one versus paying the claims, etc. They do what's in their best interest not yours.

I've personally had two new $3000 LG fridges both fail within 5 years. I don't bother repairing them, I just buy new ones. In my experience, repairing sealed systems using linear compressors is usually a very short lived solution (as in likely to fail again within 2 yrs). But others may disagree.

I won't buy any more LG refrigerators until they change the cooling system despite how much we like all the other LG features.

As an aside: in my opinion Samsung closed systems are better than LG's, but they've got ice maker problems that they can't or won't fix. They've had to settle claims also. The Samsung design is not nearly as functional as the LG, but it may last longer.
