The new Samsung 6.3 cu. ft. Front Control Slide-In Electric Range with Convection & Wi-Fi in Stainless Steel is a great oven, but like with everything in life, it could be better.
Let me start by listing the Pros:
Fingerprint Resistant: It does minimize the number of fingerprints on the stainless-steel frame, but it may leave little smudges here or there.
Five heating elements: The power on the heating elements is awesome. It provides fast heat in just seconds. It also includes two dual ring elements to be used with multiple sized pots and pans.
Oven: large 6.3 cu. ft. oven is big enough to accommodate multiple large dishes at once, especially with the holidays coming up. Powerful convention decreases the time for baking, roasting and evenly cooking food. Compatible with SmartThings and any virtual assistance available.

Now the Cons:
Fingerprint resistant: smudges are still visible and will build up if not wiped. Touch screen smudges constantly and it is very sensitive to the touch. Any passing of a cloth on the touch screen will activate any of the features. The locking mechanism is available, but it also locks the oven door and if the sensors do not detect the door, it will take a while for the locking mechanism to work. Additionally, there are no instructions on the usage of the touch screen controls in either of the three manuals that come in the box. To get a detailed description on the touch screen features, you will need to go to Samsung’s website and download the manual for the range.
Cooktop: even after the hot surface indicator turns off, the cooktop still stays very warm and will burn your hand to the touch. It does take quite a while for the cooktop to be cold. Cleaning the cooktop has been an issue. Even with the warm surface cooktop, the cloth will stick to the cooktop and will leave a permanent mark on it.
Virtual Assistance: As cool as it is to have an oven that is controlled via Bixby, Google Assistance, Alexa, SmartThings, etc., it really is only good for utilizing the oven feature. The SmartThings App will let you control the oven light and the oven temperature, but you do not have any access to the cooktop. It will let you know that the cooktop is on, but you can not turn it off. If you do utilize any of the virtual assistance voice commands to pre-heat your oven, make sure that there is nothing inside the oven i.e. pots, pans, etc. I believe this feature is only good if you are out of the house and realize you want to cook a frozen pizza and need the oven to be pre-heated. For the bad, the fan inside continues to stay on until the oven is cooled. This wouldn't be such a bad thing except during the heat of the summer it heats up the kitchen and it can become unbearable. The front electronic controls are so sensitive that even a light touch from your clothing or a paper towel can turn something on. But the most frustrating thing about this stove is the incredibly fragile glass cooktop. It scratches like butter. I must include here that we've owned a GE and a whirlpool in the past and have never had such a difficulty in keeping a glass cooktop looking clean and shiny. We're using the glass cooktop cleaner recommended by samsung, and I'm using the polish recommended after every use. Even after all of that, we're still getting light scratches on this cooktop. We even went so far as to spend $400 on a whole new set of pots and pans that are specifically designed for glass cooktops with a smooth flat steel bottom amd we are still getting scratches. The heat from the burners also seem to leave some type of round heat marks that appear like a haze. So whatever you do don't accidentally slide a pan or a pot on this cooktop, don't place a fork on this cooktop, and don't use a higher heat or you'll put a heat haze in the glass. I'm seriously on the fence and whether or not I can recommend this stove. While it works great and it looks great, if you don't want a stove that looks 10 years old after just a couple of months, you might look for another option that has a more durable glass top.

review_text: 2 years of use, no issues.  I got it to replace the crappy icemaker in my Samsung fridge (which is the worst design ever by the way).  Get a flexible OXO scoop which is better than the one that comes with it.  Use descaler solution when you start to see calcium scale in the reservoir cradle or the well beneath the ice bin.  Buy the filter for it so you can use sink water vs your fridge's water dispenser or pitcher (too slow and annoying to fill this way IMO).  Makes ice quickly. I think the multiple indicator lights and plastic housing on the 2nd gen is not as aesthetically clean as the stainless steel design on the 1st gen, but to be honest sometimes it is sometimes hard to see the pulsing/cascading light (during active ice cycle) on the 1st gen, when the kitchen lights are on full bright. review_text:
I sometimes have to dry our clothes twice to get them dry enough after following instructions and not overloading the machine. There are other reason this machine is a waste of money. We have the extra capacity dryer as we have larger blankets and comforters that we wash regularly. Ha! Those items, which usually don’t spin dry very well (see my review of the companion Samsung washing machine) turn themselves into cocoons of wet fabric after five minutes even with the use of tennis balls to help keep things moving in the dryer. So every five to ten minutes I need to go to the dryer, take out the blanket, give it a good shake and return it. If you have mobility issues, arthritis or are an older individual with weak strength, this is not the dryer for you. Along those same lines, I have dryed three or four throw size blankets, again with tennis balls to keep things moving around, and usually one of them remains stuck in the back of the dryer, also in a cocoon of wetness that somehow just never wanted to join the party with the rest of the throws in the dryer. This is after I shook them out from the washer before carefully placing them into the dryer so as not to load the dryer with a bunch of lumpy throw blankets.

Also, I use the fluff or air only cycle on our dryer to dislodge dog hair from the crib size flat sheets I use to cover our dog’s various beds throughout the house during shedding season prior to putting those items into the wash. The first time I used this Samsung dryer to do this, I used blind confidence and after the fluff cycle in the dryer, put them into the Samsung washer. Big mistake: first the washer threw the unbalalnced loand error (again, see washer review) and when I opened the washer to relocate the soaking wet crib size flat sheets, my hand came out covered in wet dog fur. After a look around the wet sheets in the washer, I pulled out at least five clumps of wet dog fur which the washing machine kindly formed for me in the wet sheets. The second time I tried to fluff the dog hair off the sheets before washing, I checked the lint trap which remained clean after a 20 minute fluff (with tennis balls) and for fun, I took these crib size flat sheets outside to give them a good shake and ended up completely covered in dog hair (note to self: stand up wind in the future). Our previous dryer removed 80% of all fur which I could determine by pulling out the lint trap. This dryer might remove eight strands of dog fur.

review_text:

Secondly, the cheese drawer at the bottom that spans the width of the fridge will not shut straight without two hands and several tries. Without a guide, any imbalance of weight inside the drawer causes it to track left and right, even with two hands on the drawer! What a pain.
Thirdly, the temperature gauge is off. We set the inner fridge temp to the suggested temp and all of our veggies froze. We have lowered the inner temp one degree at a time until we’re finally at 40 degrees and we still get partially frozen veggies and ice in our water. I wish I could return it!!

review_title: lasted one year and 3 months before subtle failure
review_text:
Really expected more out of this unit. I bought it mainly due to cost and speed at which it could be delivered to me about 1 year 3 months ago (had no backup garage fridge at the time). Our old LG fridge completely died after about 4.5 years so was hoping for at least that out of this unit but no luck. So the way the freezer dies is not straightforward. While I await the new one from Home Depot (another LG) this one continues to work for the fridge section. The freezer still makes ice actually and on the surface looks like it is doing the right thing. But adding an external temperature monitor shows the issue. The freezer cycles from -14 deg F and back to 6 deg F. I think it must lock up, thaw then repeat causing excessive freezer burn to every item in the freezer. It presents as a thin layer of frost when you open the freezer and on meat/veggies will see a lot of frost/icing. Tried the "simple" fix with replacing the freezer thermistor but no luck (and cleaned coils in back of unit). Anyhow, on the last failure I bought a secondary garage fridge (smart move). I didn't buy a warranty for the Samsung - am torn on this. If something dies just after a year that is supposed to last at least 15 do I really want it? I got a 5 year warranty on the new LG thru Home Depot so will see how that goes. I bought a Thomas 4127 probe based thermometer to keep an eye on the new one. Highly recommend so the minute the temps don't hold range you can call in for service. I think there may be a cascade type problem here with the design where one thing knocks out another but not sure. In closing, calling this POS a loss. Good luck!

UPDATE: The thermal sensor in the freezer section DA32-10104N (used aftermarket, not OEM) that I replaced actually fixed the issue. I think when monitoring with the Thomas 4127 the probe must go into a larger mass that won't move the temp around as quick. I covered the probe with some gel packs and the freezer section is holding a steady temp near 0 instead of the -14 deg F. I think the thermal defrost sensor was just starting to go so the small layer of frost was due to this partially failing thermistor. On the defective one I was getting about 10Kohm in ice water and on the new one about 13Kohm so this translates I think to a difference of about 10 deg F being off. So the computer is told it is hotter and therefore does not defrost like it should and probably stresses other components. Looks like I can cancel the order on the new LG one at Home Depot up to 3 days before delivery. Giving it one more day before pulling the trigger on that. Cautiously optimistic I can get more life out of this and now aware that this thermistor is a wear item. I would not buy a Samsung fridge again but hope this might help someone who already owns one!

The tech told me this model of fridge was a nightmare and there was a whole lawsuit against LG with this because the unit fails and can't really be fixed. He couldn't find the issue, so he tried to report to LG that it was not fixable but they told him to replace the compressor, refill the coolant, and see if it worked. It got better for a couple of weeks then started to warm again, melting all of the ice inside and leaking all of my kitchen floor. I called LG again, hoping they would just replace it but they told me that they would not replace it until there have been 3 failed attempts to fix it, and then they couldn't find technicians to fix it and kept delaying over and over despite the warranty terms. review_title: A very good ange overall, but with 1 main issue
review_text:
I have owned this range for a little over a year now and it has been great, with one exception…the center cooking grate is slightly higher than the 2 outer cooking grates.

Cooktop:
• Burner performance is very good; a lot of options for high heat and slow simmer applications.
• Easy to start and large, hefty knobs make it quick and easy to adjust as you are cooking.
• Cleaning is relatively easy, with respect to a gas stove; cooking grates are easy to remove and put back in place.
• The only glaring issue is the unevenness of the center cooking grate (slightly higher) compared to the 2 outer cooking grates.
o This makes it a challenge to move pots around the cooking surface easily; you have to slightly lift part of the pot or pan…it is not truly a continuous surface.
o Large/heavy stock pots, filled with liquid, are a challenge to move or adjust on the burner, if not placed exactly in the spot you want them.
o Also, when you have a fry pan bridging the center and outer cooking grate, any oil will tend to pool a bit to the opposite side of the pan.
o At first this was a minor inconvenience, but after a year it has become a glaring issue for me.
Oven:
• The oven performance is very good; heat distribution is pretty even and temps seem to be accurate with respect to the corresponding settings.
• Convection performance is excellent and the air fryer setting works well.
• There are a lot of rack locations, so you have a lot of options for cooking multiple items at once.
• Cleaning pretty easy, but I have not tried the self-cleaning option yet.

Overall, I have really enjoyed this range, but wish there was a fix of the uneven cooking grates.

Note: Purchased at Best Buy.

product_title: LG WM4000HBA / WM4000HBA / WM4000HBA 4.5 Cu. Ft. Ultra Large Capacity Smart wi-fi Enabled Front Load Washer with TurboWash 360 and Built-in Intelligence
review_title: ONLY a First Day review... all is good though.
review_text:
We chose this and its dryer mate because the NY Times reviewed it as best for the year model for cleaning cloths, gentleness on cloths, and expected durability and longevity of the product line. This is a DAY1 review.

First the Bad:

1. the manuals are terrible. There is so much missing about how to use the controls it is pitiful. Consider for example that there is NOTHING in the dryer manual to tell you how to use all the potential button settings. None of the buttons worked, until I figured out hours later that you must use the MANUAL selection on the dial before you can change stuff.. If you go to the LG web site, there are other documents you can read but I mean really. As a Software Engineer, if my QA and DOCUMENTATION people wrote manuals this bad about what I build, I would fire them.

2. availability is spotty on both the appliances and their accessories. We had trouble finding the matching dryer, and could not get the pedestal add ones because none were available. Chalk this up to COVID I guess but one outfit said we would need to wait five weeks to the matching dryer. So do some research and shop around to see who has what in stock. If your current washer/dryer are on their last leg, maybe don't wait for them to fail before you but new ones? Just a thought.

3. the washer is louder that both the wife and I expected. OK in fairness, there was never any claim made about how loud or quiet these machines were supposed to be. And the door is still off the laundry room and the room is empty... so there is nothing to muffle the sound. I expect this to reduce significantly once the crap is put back into the laundry room and the door hung. So maybe I am over stating this negative.

4. 4.5 cubic feet ain't as big as it sounds. Compared to our old top loader, it seems the size of loads we are putting in the washer is smaller. It is hard to judge without a side-by-side comparison, and maybe we over stuffed to old guy whish is why it had some problems, and I could in fact stuff more into the new machine if I wanted. But it does seem like the load size smaller.

The GOOD:

1. new looking cloths, fast. I kid you not when I say the stuff that comes out of washer and dryer looks brand new. I am a work-from-home IT guy so I am mostly a sweats and t-shirt man. All my cloths so far look brand new and soft out of the dryer. And the "seemingly" smaller load sizes get done in 30 minutes in the washer unless I pick one of the longer running cycles. We did upholstery covers, blankets and bedding, pillows, towels, slippers, and lots of cloths (yeah they delivered the machines @9:30am and I did 10 loads today) and ALL of it looked NEW after being cleaned by this pair of machines. The dryer takes about 54 minutes to dry whatever you put in it. I used the manual setting for a lot of it which allowed me to reduce heat and dry time to 40 minutes.

2. no-brainer operation. If you are not into all the options worry not, you don't really need them. There are so many presets on the dial, you almost can't fail to find a setting that works for whatever you are cleaning. You just turn the machine on, put a detergent plug into the drum, load, dial up your clothing match, and press the run button. The washer appears to have some AI that checks the washer load to see if any timing adjustment is needed off the baseline you dialed in, but maybe that is my imagination. Point is anyone can use these with great precision without any effort. Kind of makes up for the crappy manuals. Only thing I add is "extra rinse" at the end of the wash cycle.

3. has less expensive versions in the model line if you do not want to spend the money on these. I am guessing of course but I would think "lower end" models in the same product line are really just fewer features but same washing and drying ability and reliability of product. So if you need to save money on your set look at those instead.

Tomorrow is the Wife's turn. If she has any major comments I will add them to this review later. Kevin

review_title: Takes some time to tweak, a pain to maintain. Drys well
review_text:
This is the only washer dryer combo that stacks in the front. If you are putting them on a pedestal you don’t have to assemble both together and lift both up. The ventless is good if you don’t have an existing vent. I preferred my old vented Axxis to this one but Bosch stopped making vented ones.
If you have pets regular maintenance is needed. You have the regular lint trap to clean and since the mesh is so fine and you use dryer sheets you have to scrub it periodically to get rid of the wax build up or it will, clog, overheat, and shut down—requiring a maintenance call to pay someone a lot of money to take off a back panel and push a button. Then you have to periodically clean the condenser which builds up hair and lint. If you don’t, the dryer becomes inefficient and eventually stops drying. Washing the condenser in your sink or tub will wash a bunch of hair down the drain leading to potential clogs. Finally you have to clean the sump—where the moisture from you condenser goes. If not, the pump clogs and the water pools and your clothes don’t dry. This is the trickiest one to clean as it is in the way back and the sump cover is a pain in the butt to open. If you are not handy and own this dryer, you will be regularly paying someone a lot of money to do basic maintenance.
Note: the default dry setting are a bit damp for someone like me who has dust allergies. You can make it dry more by using the “dry level” button. Be careful because your laundry can get hot and synthetics will off gas and cottons can smell burnt.

product_title: FRIGIDAIRE EFMIS164 70 Can, Glass Door Beverage Center Refrigerator
review_title: Looks nice, but it needs a fan…
review_text: Wanted a small beverage fridge that would look nice and keep drinks cold, ended up with that in the end after a few weeks of frustration. First and foremost the build quality is poor. I wasn’t expecting high end, but this is bottom of  the barrel type stuff. They include a drip tray but the “drain” appears to be filled with spray foam. The wire racks appear to be made of the same thickness aluminum that they use in twist ties then covered in several layers of paint. The shelves bend under the weight of a single 12oz can. I’m constantly having cans tip over and fall out when the unit isn’t mostly full simply because they are shifting on the uneven support of the shelf.The fit and finish of the compressor is also very poor, though the unit itself seems to be decent. There is also clearly very little thought in the design of the unit as a chiller. It’s simply stick a cooling element in a box. There are significant amounts of spray foam type insulation (Great Stuff style foam) that are clogging up lots of stuff, including what I assume was supposed to be the drain for the drip tray. I ended up just putting some sponges where it should drain. The thermostat appears to be connected directly to a cooling element, and proceeds to shut the unit off as soon as that element reaches the desired temperature. This results in an air temperature in the fridge of about 55-60 degrees on the coldest setting and just room temperature at any other setting other than max. The unit is rated at 40-60 degrees. In doing some troubleshooting I discovered that placing a battery powered fan pointed towards the back right top corner (when looking from the front) quickly caused the compressor to kick on and continue running. It did not kick off until the air temp was down to 36 degrees. I’ve since replaced the battery powered fan with an adjustable speed AC powered fan running at the lowest speed on the upper rack and have actually had to back the temperature control back to prevent drinks from freezing. In the end I have what I wanted, I just didn’t realize how much effort would be required. I will attempt to add photos - but the fridge is stocked and cold right now, so I don’t want to risk my luck!

review_title: Does NOT hold 70 cans and the shelves are VERY unstable!
review_text:
I never give bad reviews. My mama taught me that if I couldn't say anything nice, I shouldn't say anything at all. The problems with this item, however, have led to me breaking my 50 year nice streak. I couldn't address stars for temp control or style because there are too many problems with this unit before you even get to those aspects. First of all, it is advertised as holding 70 cans, but the loading diagram in the manual only shows capacity to accommodate 60 12 oz cans. This, however, is also incorrect. Loading according to diagram, I was only able to get 45 cans to fit (but not SAFELY). It honestly feels like false advertising and I am very disappointed.
It gets worse. The shelves are REALLY flimsy and there is no structural support for them in the front of the unit, which means that the cans FALL OUT any time there is any movement. The unit itself is level and I have verified the level. The problem is that the weight of the cans causes the shelves to bow in the middle and droop downward in the front. (The grooves holding the shelves only extend about 2 cans deep, so the cans in the front row are not supported and continually fall out.) In actually, the unit only SAFELY holds 35 cans - HALF the number promised. Diagram indicates each level holds 20 cans (which equals 60 - not 70), but the bottom only holds 15 and the top 2 levels only SAFELY hold 10 cans due to said saggy shelf issues.
I am going to wait til tomorrow to decide if I will send it back as I try not to make decisions while I am mad. Why am I mad, you ask? I am mad because I had multiple cans fall out on my feet while trying to load it, and several hit my toes in just such a way as to make me say words that I regret saying in front of my staff. I am going brainstorm overnight for anything I can do to stabilize the shelves to make it safer before making my final decision, but I am leaning towards sending it back due to it also only holding 1/2 of the advertised capacity.
Reputation Disclaimer: this is Lisa - not Kerry - writing the review. Kerry probably would not have cussed when the cans hit his toes.

It's just...defective.

However, because it's over one year old, there is no warranty, despite it being a manufacturer defect.

For comparison, we have five other freezers in our extended family, all different makes and models, bought in different years and even DECADES.

If there's an outage, or someone leaves the door open, that's fine. That's on us. But if we have done nothing, and the product we spent our money on just... DOESN'T WORK, that would seems to be on the company that made it.

We are horrified, and angry.

DON'T BUY THIS FREEZER. Maybe it'll be "a good one", but it could also be a very expensive doorstop.

product_title: Frigidaire FPFU19F8WF Frigidaire FPFU19F8WF 33 Inch Wide 18.6 Cu. Ft. Freezer with Internal Ice Maker
review_text:
Frigidaire keeps deleting this review off of their website, so hopefully some people see it here!

TLDR: Do not buy this freezer unless you are OK with not having a working Ice Maker. I purchased this Fridge and Freezer Pair, and within a month the Freezer fan needed to be replaced, and within the first year the Ice Maker stopped making ice. Please understand if you are considering this unit that the Ice maker CANNOT BE FIXED OR REPLACED! It is an issue with the water line or water line heater that runs through the insulation in a Non-serviceable portion of the freezers cabinet freezing up or breaking. Just read through the reviews and you will see how many reference an Ice Maker or water line issue. They finally paid me back for what I paid for my unit (this took MONTHS), but I am now stuck with a cabinet that is sized specifically for these units, a freezer that has increased substantially in price, and I'm not sure what I will do. From what I've been told, they still don't know why this is happening, or how to address it!

Additionally, for everyone saying their freezer is LOUD, and Frigidaire telling you "that is how a freezer sounds", they are wrong. There is a control board housed in a plastic housing over top of the compressor in the back of the freezer. The plastic housing was not designed or assembled correctly, so half of it opens and falls right onto the compressor. So as the compressor runs, the plastic rattles on it and makes a loud humming noise. They came out and "reattached" the housing, only for it to fall apart again within a few months. But it was quite while reattached. So now I need to pull both of these units out again to try to re-attach this housing. Overall, this Freezer is a lemon and will probably be part of a class action at some point.

The product is horrible, very poorly manufactured.

It's classic tactics to try to frustrate anyone hoping to make a claim. I'm guessing that GE selected OnPoint b/c the product is so bad that they don't want to cover it themselves.

If you ask to speak to someone, they give you the run around
Just avoid, avoid, avoid this product.

review_text:
[[VIDEOID:9230eb9a5fbbeaa4d0abe29447bde041]] In less than two months I have gone through three of theses machines. They all did the exact same thing. Every few hours it would start making an obscenely loud hammering noise for anywhere from 15 to 45 minutes. When the first one did it, I ordered a replacement. While waiting for the replacement, it stopped making the noise and seemed to work perfectly. I received the replacement and immediately cleaned it and got it running. The next day it started making the same noise. The first one was still behaving, so I sent back the replacement. A few days after sending it back, the first one became unresponsive. It would turn on, cycle the water and then shut off. It had only been running for a few weeks and I had only used bottled water in it, so it was NOT due to build-up. I ordered a third one and set it up yesterday. It immediately started with the same hammering noise every few hours, but I let it run to see if it would work itself out. Today it started making the noise and this time it was worse. I took the video and right afterwards it began to smell like it was burning. I immediately unplugged it and had to open the window. The right side was too hot to touch. There is obviously a design flaw. I am so lucky I was home and near the machine because I’m certain it would have resulted in a fire. An hour after unplugging it I wanted to get it dried out for packaging. When I drained the hoses, the water was hot. I just cannot trust another one.
Edit: After several months of not having my nugget ice, I saw the machine on sale for prime day and decided to try it once again. I only had it running for 3 weeks and the pump went out. I was past the 90 day Amazon warranty due to being out of town. working with GE was a nightmare. After several phone calls and emails with repetitive requests for the same information I had just provided, they said they only replaced machines with refurbished ones. Ok, no problem… except the one they sent me looked like the previous owners had it for a year. It was dented, scratched, and had layers of calcium deposits around the dispenser, it hadn’t even been cleaned! I contacted GE again and sent them pictures and said this was unacceptable. They agreed to send me a new one this time. I have been waiting for 2 months now for the replacement. They said they were back ordered, but what they were doing was filling Christmas orders first. I have been without a machine for 6 months now. They won’t refund my money. I even offered to pay the difference to get the new model that came out right after I bought mine hoping they’d worked out the problems in the updated model. Nope. So I am now still waiting for my 6th machine and will only have a partial warranty on it. This has been one of the most regrettable purchases I have ever made.

review_text:
Very disappointed, especially for the very high price of this unit.
The unit lacks an air only/no heat setting, even though the manual recommends a no heat setting for some fabrics. The heat setting only goes to “low heat” but does not have an air/no heat setting.
There is nothing intuitive about this set. The controls are complicated and opaque in function. Some options are unavailable at times, for no discernible reason. The wi-fi connection is not well explained in the manual and I initially had trouble connecting to wi-fi.
The manual refers to additional cycles/settings that can be downloaded via the app. Why? The whole idea of settings and cycles that can be accessed only by download seems to be a gimmick; why not have these settings/cycles available via the unit’s controls?
The washer seems to do a good job and is very quiet. The washer drum is very deep and I need to get down on my knees to reach smaller items, like socks, in the back (and my arms are fairly long). The dryer seems very slow and never fully dries my clothes without multiple cycles, even at the highest dry setting.
The buttons are supposedly touch-sensitive, but they often do not respond until I touch them several times.
One of the selling points of the stacked unit is that the dryer is designed to select appropriate drying settings based on the selected wash settings. However, if you don’t get to the dryer very soon after the wash cycle ends, the unit shuts down and the programmed dry settings are no longer available.
Overall this unit is frustrating and definitely not worth the very high price. I am very disappointed.

product_title: LG LTCS20020W 20.2 Cu. Ft. Top-Freezer Refrigerator - White
review_text:
I bought my LG LTCS20020W top-freezer refrigerator from a local Lowes, so you won't see an Amazon purchase notice. Shrug. I've only owned it for a short while, but here's the skinny:

FREEZER:

The top freezer hits the ideal 0 degrees F in just a few hours by setting the thermostat on the center position. I deliberately bought a unit with no ice maker on the theory that ice makers are notorious troublemakers. DOWNSIDE: there's NO FREEZER LIGHT. I stuck a little Motion Sensor LED Night Light to the freezer roof to fix the issue.

REFRIGERATOR:

The refrigerator achieved 37-40 degrees F in a few hours with the thermostat only on the second position. My fridge is a simple unit with LED light, two crisper drawers, a smallish dairy bin and two shelves. Some units include an optional door alarm and pantry drawer, but not mine.

OVERALL:

This LG top-freezer refrigerator is VERY quiet and energy efficient. The dimensions are excellent for my small kitchen and contains enough food for over a week for my wife and I. This refrigerator is just a tiny bit shorter and narrower than some, which can be a major plus when situating it in some kitchens, especially in older houses. But the refrigerator is an inch or two deeper than some, so measure carefully.

I didn't realize it at first, but the doors are reversible. The fridge comes set up with the doors opening to the right, but even an inexperienced person (like myself) can switch the hardware so the doors open to the left in an hour by following the on-line videos.

LG refrigerators have a some of the best reputations for reliability, so I'm expecting this LG LTCS20020 to outlast me. Five stars.

review_title: Worst Appliance I've Ever Purchased - Bar None!
review_text:
I've owned my Family Hub Refrigerator for four years now. In that time, the compressor has failed twice, and the icemaker freezes up every month. There is truly nothing more frustrating in the kitchen than a refrigerator that stops cooling, ruining hundreds of dollars of food and preventing you from storing perishable food in your home. After spending $4,000 on this fridge, I expect it to, at the very least, continue to keep my food cold. The first time the sealed system failed, it took more than two weeks for Samsung to replace the compressor. That means my children had no access to perishable food in our home for that duration. Adding salt to an open wound, even though the sealed system is still under warranty, I was charged $99 for a service call. Samsung said they could not waive that fee.
Seven months later, the refrigerator has stopped cooling again. Samsung sent out another technician four days ago (for another $99), more than a week after it stopped cooling and ruined hundreds of more dollars of our food. product_title: GE Profile Opal | Countertop Nugget Ice Maker with Side Tank | Portable Ice Machine Makes up to 24 lbs. of Ice Per Day | Stainless Steel Finish
review_title: Don't Buy a G1, and if you do, read this about what to do with the tank.
review_text:
EDIT/Update - Warranty was not a horrible experience and done entirely through the mail. However, when the replacement failed in the same way, as I was cleaning it up a giant 'THUD' from the side tank (that I highly recommend as the regular chamber is teeny tiny) came out. It was having a cavitation vacuum and just not feeding water in. SO, just drill a teeny tiny little pinhole in the bottom-bottom (like, in the general vicinity of the valve) of the clear plastic tank, and it will do 10x better.

STILL, G1s aren't recommended and I still don't like it. But this is way better. I hear the G2 Opals aren't worse.

Original post:

I really didn't do my research on this. I saw a bunch of cheap-o ones, but THIS, this, was going to be the best. And nugget ice. I've always wanted nugget ice.

For the first 3 weeks, it was pretty good. It was the lifestyle change I've always wanted. It was a little power hungry/hot, and the power button just didn't want to work about 2/3rds of the time --- but I could deal.

...then it stopped making ice. ...then the power button would only work after I'd unplugged and plugged it.

I can clean it with straight vinegar if I run the clean cycle on it literally 5-6 times, and sort of get ice production back. It doesn't last long. The power button is/was/will always be, awful.

I can say with pretty good certainty, this is the last GE product I'll ever, ever own. I will make a point in researching any appliance purchase just to make sure it isn't a rebranded GE product. This thing is a maintenance pig and nugget ice was only an amusement to me to begin with.

review_text: I’ve never wrote a review on Amazon before but I do read reviews before any big purchase and I feel like I have to on the Opal ice maker. I was very excited when my husband bought me this ice maker. I love crunching on this kind of ice but it was short lived. I’ll preface that we do have our own water well and we have a water softener for our entire home and the ice maker was filled with this water.  I followed all the cleaning recommendations as described in the instruction manual at least once a week sometimes twice. It’s fairly labor intensive and a definite con to this machine. About 3 months in it started making a metal on metal grinding sound in the rear of the machine and then just quit working. It was still under manufacture warranty so I contacted them and a new machine was shipped to me and the old one shipped back to them. This took about 3 months to complete the process. 2nd machine was setup just as manual suggested and literally 45 days later it too started making awful grinding noises near the motor. **Both machines had plenty of air flow around and there was no dirt or dust in the motor area or vents. I called customer service and the suggested to unplug the unit, do the deep cleaning with straight vinegar as described in owners manual, and then try it again. I did this and then I plugged it back in and all seemed ok at first. I left the house and came back home later to a note from the cleaning lady saying “the ice maker started making a terrible noise and I thought it was going to blow up so I unplugged it”  I reached out to GE and customer support via email and by phone. They said they would get back to me… they never did. So I let this broken machine sit for another 6+ months until the original manufacturer warranty expired and the extended warranty set in and got my refund. Long story short… BUY THE WARRANTY and you can thank me later.

review_title: Lots of room for big pizza boxes or casserole dishes.  Just a couple of deal-breakers, though!
review_text:
LG provides a 1-year warranty for this fridge. I've owned mine for 2 years now, so wanted to provide some insights.

As I mentioned in the title, the entire width of the fridge is spacious and accommodates just about anything you want to refrigerate. The top shelf is closest to the vent from the freezer, so liquids tend to freeze (yes, even though you can set the fridge and freezer compartment temps to the exact degree). Butter, guacamole, and things like that do well up there.

One minor complaint is that you must open both doors to access the full-width meat tray at the bottom and keep those doors out of the way while operating the tray.

My biggest complaint are the door gaskets. No fridge is worth a thing if it can't keep the cold air in! Now, there is an alarm that goes off if the doors are left open for a period of time. The problem is that the doors have to be noticeably open. The freezer drawer was my first indication of weak magnetic gaskets. Even though you push in the drawer and it sounds like it's closed, you need to give an extra push just to be sure. Otherwise, you'll return to your freezer to find the contents frosted over! Trust me!

The ultimate complaint is with the right door. It's *very* challenging to keep this door secured! The alarm won't go off if the door is slightly ajar. The magnetic gasket on the right side is noticeably weaker than the left-hand door. It feels like it's gotten weaker over time. It takes *very* little force with just one finger to open the door! This door will fail to seal if you just close the door and walk away (the air pressure inside seems to not let the gasket seal). Also, closing the left hand door can create air pressure that pops the seal on the right door. Either way, the right door sticks out about half an inch, allowing cold air to leak out and more compressor run-time, I'm sure. So, I'm *constantly* checking and re-checking the right door! With kids in the house, forget it! I've looked closely at the gasket and it is not damaged and it makes full contact all the way around, but it's just *super* weak!

review_title: Our LG Dryer caught fire during the warranty period!
review_text:
Our LG dryer caught fire 10.5 months after we bought it new from an authorized dealer. There was extensive smoke damage and, obviously, our home and the safety of my family (wife, two daughters and a dog) were imperiled. Luckily, in the end, only the dryer was dryer was ruined. Who knows what chemicals we were exposed to from the smoke?! The WORST part of it all was how LG ducked and weaved and finally turned their backs on us completely. The only thing they would offer to do was repair this faulty, dangerous unit. I told them I don't care if 10 NASA scientists came to our house, fully disassembled and put the unit back together again, it will NEVER be used in our home EVER AGAIN. Who knows if it will catch fire again?! Who knows what chemicals are in the smoke that was created?! LG was completely unsympathetic. They said we were refusing their help and washed their hands of us. And we were contacted by someone in the "Presidential Liaison Office" who said she was the ultimate authority. One of the most unhelpful, unfriendly customer service people I've ever talked to. A heart of ice. And, for the record we're adults and we know how to use a dryer properly, clean the lint filter, etc. The technician who LG sent used a special airflow meter to confirm that the vent and duct were clean.

LG refused to help us in any kind of meaningful way when its appliance caught fire under warranty in our home, putting our safety and possessions at grave risk. It took days for them to address the issue and I spent hours begging and pleaded various customer support agents in Manilla to escalate this. Finally, someone from the highest levels of the support organization, a "Presidential Liaison" contacted me. She was unfriendly, unsympathetic and utterly unhelpful. The only thing she would offer to do was to give me 20% of the value of the unit or have it repaired. I'm not crazy. NO ONE wants a faulty dryer that has caught fire repaired! Who knows what was burning in that unit (plastic, wiring, etc) and what dangerous chemicals were created?! Who knows whether it will catch fire again?!.The idea that we would keep this appliance in our house, given the fact that it put my entire family and home at risk, is completely ludicrous. But the Presidential Liaison was like a robot, just repeating the same thing over and over. I asked her if she was OK with me leaving our interaction furious with LG and ready to yell this story from the mountaintops (ie. social media, review sites, BBB, Consumer Affairs, UL, etc.) and she said she was fine with it. What kind of liaison is that?! What is clear is that the culture of LG and LG Support is completely unsympathetic, completely focused on the bottom line instead of the customer, perhaps even jaded and uninterested in the reputation of LG itself. It is the reflection of a sick company and a cynical corporate culture. For such a widely praised company, it was shocking and hugely disappointing. Needless to say, we will NEVER use LG products again and we will make sure to tell this sad story to everyone we know and care about.

review_text:
We were given a phone call about 30 minutes after placing the order, to verify that we understood that we were getting one machine that could do both wash and dry, as well as to set up expectations on how and when my machine would be delivered. This alone I would recommend this purchase.
Delivery was smooth and went as planned, the delivery company called about 3 days before delivery, and the driver called the morning of as well as about 1/2 hour out. Once the driver was here and we got the machine off the truck he did help cut the packaging open as it was damaged, so we verified the machine itself wasn't damaged. Which it wasn't just.
We live in a 5th wheel toy hauler, so space is very limited. This machine fits perfectly in the space we have for it in our garage. This machine is not vented, so when its drying, the "vented" goes down the drain to the gray tank, and the lint is collected around the door and seal, which makes it easy to clean.
Things to know is that with a unvented combo unit, your clothes are supposed to be slightly damp, take them out and give them a shake, this does 2 things, instantly dries and gets the wrinkles out. It does take about 3 or 4 hours to do a load of laundry that is from start to finish. So yes it does take a bit longer, but you don't have to remember to swap machines. I usually do 2 loads of laundry a day, one in the morning before leaving and one at night as we're going to bed. I come home to clean, dry clothes and wake up to clean, dry clothes. the loads do need to be smaller, but I can still wash a queen sheet set in one load, or 4 pairs of jeans or 2 heavy bath towels with a few hand towels.
This is a normal 110 unit, so no special wiring or anything, just plug it in and connect the water and drain.
I was surprised that this machine could connect to the internet, I haven't done it yet, I don't see a need for it, but it's great that I have that option. The manual was written in very good English, that was easy to read and understand, I don't know about the translations.
I would recommend this machine if you are limited on space, water and time. It has lots of washing and drying features including steam and sanitize.

review_text:
This is a nice little ice maker that doesn’t take up too much space, is relatively quiet, and makes a fair amount of ice in a short amount of time.

The ice that’s made is either small or large. The large ice doesn’t seem to be as frozen as the small and the size difference is negligible so you’re better off using the small size… speaking of frozen - the ice is often “wet ice” as in it often melts since this little guy is not a freezer. It’s clever design makes ice, drops that ice into that a tray which is over the water reservoir, and the ice melt is then used to make more ice.… which isn’t really a big deal unless you plan on moving the ice to an actual freezer. If you do move it to a freezer be sure to come back and break up the “wet ice” as it freezes otherwise you will have a giant ice ball.

Still worthy of 5 stars in my opinion. Great little ice maker!

review_text:
I wanted to post an actual timetable for what you can expect out of this machine. The description states "wait up to 15 minutes to enjoy fresh ice" which is incredibly misleading. The actual unit itself is great, which is why I am giving it 4 stars, but I am taking one off because they make it sound like you're going to have a bin full of ice in 15 minutes, but that is nowhere close to the truth. You'll have enough ice for a drink or two in that time, sure, but expect to run this machine for 6 hours non-stop if you need a gallon of ice.

Here is what you can expect ( tested on Large Ice setting ):

1. One complete cycle creates 1 quart ( 4 cups ) of ice
2. Once complete cycle takes just over 90 MINUTES to complete
3. There are 10 batches of ice per cycle, with each batch taking between 9-10 minutes.

Full disclosure: we're using Nestle bottled water in ours. Yet the cubes are clear, taste-free and wonderfully efficient.

I work from home, so there will be days when I make ice all day, filling the water reservoir and emptying cubes. It's not labor-free, but it also beets the old-school trays, and the quality of ice is far superior than what we ever got through our freezer, regardless of filter age.

This product is actually made by a company called Curtis International. Then companies like Frigidaire or Igloo just slap their logos on the front. They don't provide any actual support for the product, but instead forward you to Curtis. Curtis has an extremely cumbersome and onerous warranty process. They only communicate by email. If you call them, they will just tell you to send them an email. They won't respond to your email for 5-10 business days (i.e. 1 to 2 weeks), and when they finally do, it will just be to ask for information you already gave them. This is probably a deliberate tactic to push you past the end of the warranty period or return window.

If you are counting on being able to return this to the seller (i.e. Amazon), beware that many people report being told that this item is non-returnable.

These machines -- again, all countertop ice makers are identical and made by the same company, just with a different case or branding -- are notorious for failing within weeks or months. I was sick of buying 3+ bags of ice a week, and, spending like 7+ bucks a week on ice (our family uses a lot of ice). This machine has already paid itself off. Makes ice fast enough for me, actually faster than I expected it to. I let the machine get full, then, dump the ice into a gallon size plastic bag. I found that if I put the ice directly into the freezer ice tray it will end up in big clumps. So, everytime the machine is full, I take the bag out, hit it on my counter top so all the cubes separate, then refill again from the machine. In a couple hours I have a full ice tray. It sounds like a lot of work, but, it really isn't. Less time and effort than driving to get ice, that's for sure. And, if I am having a few friends over and know we will be using ice, I turn the machine on and we take the ice directly from the machine. review_text:
There are many brands available, all presumably of the same design. We bought one of the first all-white Frigidaire ones, used it every day for 2 years and wore it out… it ran non-stop! It finally stopped all together.

We purchased this copper colored Frigidaire unit and we notice it is quieter and makes ice faster than the first model. There have definitely been design improvements.

This unit keeps up with the rate we drink ice water, which is pretty much constantly. The unit has two speed settings. The faster setting makes a softer chewable ice which my wife prefers. I’m indifferent to that, but we both love the hollow shape of the ice (tubes, not cubes) because the increased surface area chills a drink faster. We also like the ease of walking over to the countertop unit to add ice to the sane glass periodically. It’s effortless.

The ice is just as fresh as the water you use, because there are no refrigerated food odors absorbed into the standing ice.

The unit will accumulate residue over time and it does require cleaning which can be difficult unless you buy a long handled brush to reach inside and clean the mechanism.

All-in-all, we are totally happy with this ice maker… and the copper color is attractive to boot!

I've spent over three months trying to resolve this. Almost daily. You cannot get through by phone, copious information (pictures, videos, documentation) is requested by email and requested again as if it were never received, and there's no response. I suspect this is a stalling tactic.

I finally got an address and mailed the unit back over 4 weeks ago. I follow up every few days with Curtis and get no response via email or phone.

There is no way this can be legal. The unit was defective and there is absolutely no recourse for getting a refund or even a response. Amazon should not continue to offer electronics from this company - essentially, I just spent $140 that I cannot get back.

Heed my warning. Get a machine from a different vendor or at a store where you can return it directly. Many others on the Better Business Bureau web site have had the same issue.

review_text:
First off, I got a red ice maker which was not my first choice. For unknown reasons, when I selected the grey ice maker, Amazon says they can't deliver to Hawaii. Same thing with the silver/stainless model.
Only the red one could ship to Hawaii. Amazon, get your act together!
That aside, this ice maker produces pretty good quality ice in a very short time, although it should be noted the first few ice harvests are not the best. But that's no problem, as this ice melts it drips into the reservoir so it will eventually be turned into ice. As ice production continues, the quality gets better. I've left it on the large ice size, as the small size make ice bullets that are very thin and fragile and are hard to scoop out with them breaking up which you may or may not want.
I've had it running during a gathering of friends and it seemed to keep up with demand.
It does have a tendency to leave an ice bullet caught in the upper left corner, which fools the ice maker into thinking the bin is full.
The water reservoir drain is a little awkward to reach and remove for draining, but after a few times you develop a knack to use. If the finger grips were a little larger it would make use much easier.
Same thing with the water strainer, it's difficult to remover. If it had a short vertical post or tap it would make it easier to remove for cleaning.

review_text:

ice holder every hour or so. Thus making 26 LBS per day means constant supervision of the operation. A refrigerator ice maker can operate for many more hours continuously to make far larger amounts of ice without human intervention. This device makes very wet ice so that when you store it, it becomes an iceberg that needs an ice mallet to make it useful. I have this problem as well with 5 LB ice you get from stores so this is still a little better than using 5 LB ice bags. I find putting the full ice tray output into a zip lock 1 Quart bag to be the best
way to preserve the ice as it is easy to break up the ice and is easy to find a storage spot in the freezer. I would much rather have a refrigerator with an icemaker that provides a much larger storage tray for ice that does not become an iceberg in a few days. Still, the Frigidaire is a nice option to have and I will keep mine rather than go out and spend twice as much for a refrigerator that has the ice maker ability.

review_text:
We did not purchase our GE range from Amazon but from Home Depot. But we want to share our experience with GE as a company and how they stand behind their products.

Less than 4 weeks after purchasing the range it has become inoperable. We used the oven to prepare a meal last night, turned it off and sit down to enjoy the meal with dinner guests. The oven had been turned off for approximately 2 hours when we began to smell fumes coming from the oven. Open the oven to find smoke coming from the vents in the bottom of the oven. Even though it had been turned off for 2 hours the back of the oven was hot. We unplugged the stove it continued to produce fumes and smoke. We turned off the gas and the next morning called GE to arrange for service. This is the week of Christmas so we were told the soonest they could come to do the repair would be the Monday after the holiday. Which means we have no means to cook with for the next 5 days. We live in a very rural area in the mountains. So we ask for different options perhaps a replacement of the stove, we were told the only option was to have service come look at it. I'm sure if it's fixable it will require ordering parts and returning to install parts which means even longer before we have a working oven. It also means for the next 5 days and over the Christmas holiday we are without a stove to cook on.

I'm old enough to remember when companies like GE sold appliances that were reliable and they stood behind them if they weren't. This is the second new gas range we've purchased in less than 2 years of building our new home. The first one was a Samsung. We highly recommend you do not purchase a Samsung! That stove turned out not to be fixable and they would not stand behind seeing that the year warranty had expired. So we had to sell it on Craigslist for next to nothing.

Don't know what the answer is to buying a dependable appliance these days.

review_text:
I purchased this refrigerator, along with matching dishwasher, oven, and microwave in March 2022, and received delivered and installation in May. The freezer stopped cooling properly in late July.

Short review - after dozens of frustrating phone calls with the manufacturer, retailer, and warranty service provider and multiple service appointments, it is now October, the freezer is still broken, and Frigidaire still refuses to replace the unit. It is an unbelievable failure to stand behind their warranty and I'm now trying to figure out which court to file my small claim.

Slightly longer review - I can confirm that the app and the fridge does a good job of alerting you on your smartphone when the temperature is too high in the freezer. I can also tell you that when an alarm goes off on this fridge, it makes a shrill beeping alarm sound every few minutes for several hours. Sadly, someone in engineering decided that the best way for a consumer to reset this alarm is to push ANY button. So if you don't want to be perpetually tortured by this alarm, you have to choose whether you want ice cubes or cold water from the front of your unit until the unit is fixed or until the end of time, whichever comes first. If you change between water and ice you get a new round of shrill beeping. This is truly devastating over the course of 2 months of a failed freezer, topped only by having a freezer fail while storing breast milk for a baby during a baby formula shortage and operating on little sleep. You can see how I am more than a little salty at this point.

The best advice I can give is never to buy anything from Frigidaire. Barring that I highly recommend recording all phone calls with customer service, requesting a reference number for each conversation, and never counting on anyone proactively following up with you at any stage of the process.

review_text: Bought to replace a frigidaire bullet ice machine that started being less than reliable after 7 years. I was hesitant about the nugget machine since I had read many reviews about how load they were. After much deliberation, I pulled the trigger. I read the instructions so I would maximize the machine to operate the best possible. Which meant after unboxing and cleaning the reservoir, I put it on the counter and let it set for 2 hours. This is to allow the refrigerant to settle. Something most people don't understand about anything that operates with refrigerant. Then I put a little water in and ran the cleaning cycle. 15 or so minutes later, I pulled the plug and drained that water. Put the plug back in and filled reservoir and selected ice. Compressor came on and about 13 minutes later I heard the ice start to drop. Amazingly the cycle was quieter than my old ice maker. Maybe 45 minutes later I didn't hear it at all because the bin was full and had shut itself off. Wow, chewy ice. I used bottled water so there was very little taste to the ice other than being ice. Only thing I've noticed is you have to keep an eye on the water level. Because the ice is nugget there is alot in the bin so when it's full the reservoir is about empty. Other than that, it is one of my best purchases. Would not hesitate to buy another.

product_title: FRIGIDAIRE Professional FPGC3677RS FRIGIDAIRE Professional 36'' Gas Cooktop with Griddle in Stainless Steel
review_text:
This was very easy to install. All I needed to do was to buy a flexible gas line kit and it went in very easily.

First, this was replacing an old 30" cooktop so I had to enlarge the opening. Using my framing square and a sharpie with a jigsaw made quick work of that.

Then I had to convert it to propane and that was easy with the included kit. I just had to replace the burner orifices but that was super simple and straightforward with a 1/4" socket set. All I needed was a 7mm and a 3/16" socket to remove the burner and orifice. The orifices come stuck in a card showing their position on the stove and the orifices are also color coded to further aide in identification and installation. Just put a piece of double sided tape on your socket to aide in installing the orifices..

So once the opening was enlarged and the conversion done, it was time to hook it up. The range comes with a regulator. It just screws onto the stub tube in the range. I just applied pipe dope to the stub and screwed the regulator on. It's got an arrow to indicate gas flow. Very easy.

The inlet of the regulator is 1/2" FIP (female pipe thread). I bought a flex hose install kit and it had a 1/2" male pipe thread adapter that screwed right into the regulator and the hose screwed onto it. I just connected the other end of the hose to my gas supply valve and I was done after a quick leak check. The cooktop has a power cord for the igniter.

The the cast iron grates are heavy and stay put. I love the continuous surface with all three grates installed. The included griddle is also heavy cat iron.

This range feels and looks great. Overall, I am very pleased with how it turned out.

review_text:

Just two things that I'd want to improve (that didn't occur to me before buying):
1.) There's no LED that indicates that any of the burners are on. Because the black caps over the burners can somewhat conceal flame that is set on low simmer, it's easy to inadvertently leave a burner on.
2.) Although part of what makes this look like a high-end unit is the profile when standing a few feet away from it, the iron grates are maybe 3/8" too high above the burners. I suspect some heat is lost due to that. While the center burner puts out a lot of BTUs, the spread of the flame on that burner is quite wide so not ideal for heating a small-to-mid-width pan or pot, for example.

Having stated the foregoing, I think it's a good value.

product_title: FRIGIDAIRE Gallery EFIC255 Countertop Crunchy Chewable Nugget Ice Maker, 44lbs per Day, Auto Self Cleaning, 2.0 Gen, Cream
review_title: Fast and compact. Just one wish.
review_text:
The first thing I liked about this ice maker is the small footprint. I have seen toasters with a larger footprint. It's narrow, so it doesn't eat up much counter space. I unpacked and followed the directions for cleaning before use, including running one cleaning cycle. Then I filled the tank with fresh water (we use distilled water in all appliances) and pushed the ice button. It does make some noise, but not much. You can hear the fan most of all, and a little rumble from the pump, etc. Our air fryer and microwave are much louder.

I heard ice being dropped into the tray no more than five minutes after pushing the button. After about an hour and a half the tray full light went on. The nuggets are very nice and resemble the ice you get at many restaurants. The taste was perfect. The one thing I didn't like is that after so much time the ice has melted quite a bit. And that brings up my one wish for this machine. They should have made the ice drawer double walled to provide more insulation. The tray does have slots in the bottom to allow drainage into a tray below, and that water is recycled to make more ice, but to me that is wasted energy. Note that this is not unique to this machine. There are plenty out there without insulated ice bins.

Overall, we love this machine. Our refrigerator ice maker is broken and we use this to make ice and fill the ice bin, which lasts us a few days. We'll also be making ice and bagging it for the upcoming holidays, and it will be nice knowing that we can keep the ice coming if needed.

product_title: FRIGIDAIRE Gallery EFIC255 Countertop Crunchy Chewable Nugget Ice Maker, 44lbs per Day, Auto Self Cleaning, 2.0 Gen, Cream
review_text: We already had another nugget ice maker, but by an unknown brand and it works fantastic however, when we saw this one become available by a name brand I have trusted since I was a kid, I wanted to give them a fair shot.  Make not mistake though, when you order a nugget ice maker, most of them are quite large so keep that in mind when ordering because if you do not have the space for it, best to wait until you do.  That also means clearance space around the unit as these ice makers need plenty of ventilation for the fan to work properly and not burn out your motor.  This ice maker in particularly is fantastic!  It produces ice really fast, easy to set up, instructions are very clear and complete (unlike our last one, that was the only downfall to the other one), this machine is worth every last penny.  We haven't had it long, but so far it is fantastic- 44 lbs of ice in a day and it takes only about 30 minutes to fill up the bin entirely.  The different compartments is very interesting, something we are not used to with any of our other units, but I actually prefer the way Frigidaire decided to construct it this way.  In other brands, usually your ice basket hovers above the water, in this one, there are two separate compartments, with the water container being on top and you just slide it open, lift the little lid and fill.  The reason I like this feature better is because often, if your ice basket is sitting on top of the water, and someone accidentally puts just a little too much water in the reservoir, it melts the ice you just made.  With this unit, that is not even a thing.  I would definitely recommend this ice maker if you are wanting a nugget maker and I am truly glad these are finally becoming more affordable for home use!  I hope you find this review helpful!

review_title: So much better than my last ice maker!
review_text:
I live on a barrier island where the water has always had an unpleasant odor and taste. My ZeroWater takes care of that issue and I've always used filtered water for my ice rather than town water. I'm on my third ice maker in ten years and at least on the short term, this new one is a winner.

product_title: Frigidaire EFIC452-SSRED XL Maker, Makes 40 Lbs. of Clear Square Ice Cubes A Day, Stainless, Red Steel
review_text:
I have now had this for 7 months and found a more than a few pros and cons.

I'll get the company, and not the machine, related stuff out of the way right now. First unit I was sent leaked water from some spot and at first I wasn't sure if this was condensation or what. I returned the first unit because whether or not that was a defect I wasn't going to use a machine that leaked all over the counter no matter what. Second machine arrived and NO leaking at all. So the first unit was in fact defective. However, second unit was obviously a USED machine! I kept the second machine (maybe a poor choice) because it at least did not leak, and the 'used' factor was only noticeable really due to the water spots and a bit of grime in the reservoir. Nothing major, just a good cleaning before any real use, was required.

Let's start with the pros:
Clear ice (keep that machine clean though)
Sheets of ice that last (melting is slow)
Adjustable time to make thicker sheets (cubes)
I run this a few hours every day. 7 months, every, single, day.

Cons:
Most noticeable is the cleaning factor. I have smallish hands for a guy and I still can't reach areas well enough to give this thing a deep clean.

That's really it for cons I suppose. There are some things I can nit pick if anyone cares. Read on if that's the case.

Included scoop is useless. This thing makes 'sheets' of ice that laugh in the face of this minuscule scoop thingy. (not a big deal, but if this kind of thing is important to you, maybe just buy one of those bullet ice machines)
Other people seem to know how much ice this can make with X amount of water. I, however do not. So I would love an option to select X amount of sheets (this thing makes sheets of ice remember) to be made.
Description says it runs on 120watts. Really? I didn't test this with a Kill-o-Watt yet, but I did try and use it with two different portable battery packs that could not handle the initial load. So this thing must spike well over 300watts (seriously, 120watts ??) and only consumes the stated 120 when it's in the 'hey, about to dump this sheet of ice out' stage, or they simply meant it runs on 120v. I'll need to test this for off grid use.

Overall this is a great machine. I'm listening to it in the 'I'm about to dump this sheet of ice out' stage right now as I type. I did encounter a defective initial machine, then the 'here, have a used one' after that, but I am still happy with my purchase. I don't remember the exact reason I chose this over the 'bullet' style machines, but I think it was based on output(?). However, I think I would have been happy either way. Those bullet machines put out individual cubes, which would make the included scoop in this machine actually useful! This machine puts out 'sheets' of ice that you can break up if storing in your freezer or whatever. Personally, I use them in my tumblers. One sheet fits well when broken in half. Solid sheets seem to last longer when used in a cooler for other stuff. I think this all comes down to personal preference but honestly you could simply go with which ever unit was cheaper and be just as happy.

Hope this helps someone reach a decision. Once I get my solar set up in place and see how this machine fits in I'll update my review.

review_title: Good ice maker if you need a lot of clear ice and have a place to put it....
review_text:
My wife was getting hip surgery and was told that she needed to use ice on her hip for at least 3 weeks following her operation. My fridge icemaker was just not going to be able to keep up with the demand, so I started reviewing ice makers. This Fridgidaire icemaker was reviewed well on Amazon, and advertised that it made clear ice. Most importantly, this unit advertised that it could make 40 lbs of clear ice in a day, which is much more than many of the cheaper ice makers. Since I figured it would be nice to use this to make ice in a home bar after she was done with it, I bought this unit.

This unit works by dribbling water over a vertical metal grid that looks like an ice cube tray. The metal is cooled and the water freezes as it pours over the grid. The longer you let the water flow, the more completely the ice cube forms within the grid. You can adjust the thickness of the ice within the grid by a setting on the touchscreen. I set mine to maximum to get solid, clear cubes. When the freezing is done, the water stops flowing and the ice cubes are pushed as a "block of cubes" into a bin.

The Good:
- If you use filtered water, the ice is indeed clear and doesn't have those annoying hollow "holes" in the ice that I associate with cheap ice makers
- The product looks great. I really like the red and black coloring, and it looks good, not cheap.
- It will make 40 lbs of ice in a day if you are diligent about emptying the ice cube bin frequently.
- The ice maker makes about the same amount of noise as a dorm fridge. There is certainly a fairly loud clunk each time a sheet of ice falls into the tray, but the overall ice-,making process was less loud than I expected.

The Bad:
- The ice cube bin holds maybe 4 or 5 "sheets" of ice before it fills up and the machine stops. Since the bin is not cooled, the ice starts to immediately melt unless it is taken out and placed in a freezer or cooler.
- That means about every hour or so, you must go into the machine and remove the ice and put it somewhere cold if you want to max out on the ice production. It would have been much nicer if the holding bin kept the ice cold.

The ugly
- If you fill the unit with water and let it run overnight, you will wake up to 4 or 5 sheets of mostly melted ice in the tray.
- The ice machine works well, but is a bit difficult to drain completely during cleaning. I worry that you could easily leave some water behind which might lead to mold.

review_title: If your Opal quits working or overheats, read this
review_text:
My neighbor had one of these, and it quit working. I like to fix things and I like a challenge. it took me a while to figure it out, but I think I have found an easy fix. I discovered that when it stopped working the microprocessor had quit - the button would no longer respond to touch. These run very hot! On a hunch I added a 120mm "pc fan" to the back of the unit, blowing out, to extract the heat created by the compressor. The ice maker has been working without a problem ever since. If this helps someone then I'm happy. You can find 120mm PC fans just about anywhere (including on Amazon). The one I used is rated for up to 12v. I hooked it up to an adjustable DC supply (also from Amazon) and set it for 12v. The ice maker ran for days without any problems. Then I changed the supply to 9V so the fan is a little quieter, and so far the Opal has been running just fine (four days now). Good luck!
Will

review_title: There is a defect you can fix that will keep it lasting years and years
review_text: We got this machine directly from GE and loved it. Using it daily it went about 6 months and started screeching like other reviews have said.  There is a tank with gearbox.  It has run dry and this causes the screeching.  (if you fix it yourself, the warantee would probably be void)--All you need to do is take off the back panel and side panel and the top panel, find the gearbox and take off the top fan and two screws holding it on and lift it a bit and put oil in it (I used a spay of lithium greese (brand wd 40) and several drops of air gun oil.  It runs and makes ice much better than even when it was new.  Youtube how to fix the screeching and there are a few people showing this process.  On my model, I had to take the top off (which is doable, but you might bend some of the panels in the process).  be careful to not bend the fan/radiator setup as it is right on the back of the machine.

review_text:
Owned this for just over a month now, set up was actually easy, connecting to the app was simple too, in spite of many complaints from other users. Noise is actually minimal, the loudest is the actual ice dropping into the bin, but it's not an issue. Ice production is flawless, and plentiful, with 3 adults in the home, we don't have a problem with running out because it just keep pumping out ice. DEFINITELY get the side tank! It's a godsend in keeping the ice flowing! Cleaning is a chore, I won't lie about that, but it's becoming easier the more I do it. I just wished the cleaning cycle was longer 3 minutes seems short to flush and clean the machine. Just completed a 1 month descaling, and will laborious it was necessary.
Over all I'm extremely happy with the ice maker, I strongly suggest you invest in the replaceable water filters that fit into the bottom of the reservoir, they will slow down build up and make the cleaning go easier, also use FILTERED (we have a Pur filter) water to fill the tank/reservior, your machine will thank you for it. Don't use tap water! Feel that this was a expensive purchase but can totally justify the cost as much ice as we use.

review_text:
I really like that this GE nugget ice maker is super quiet (in comparison to our previous one), that it generates an entire "load" of ice in about 90 minutes, and that the ice is consistent in size, texture and color.

I also like that the lid is insulated (our old one was not and the ice always seemed to melt before we finished it), and how easy it was to set up and begin using (I did not even have to read the instruction booklet). I also like that it fits on and underneath the cabinet -- even after leaving space for heat ventilation on both sides of the unit.

I am impressed at the design that returns melted ice back into the water reservoir -- which is below the ventilated ice bucket -- and is recycled into new ice as the current ice is used and the machine starts up again.

At times we just make a few batches of ice and store it in gallon ziplock bags in the freezer. It appears solid when you later go to use it, but simply drop the bag a couple of times flat on the floor to turn the ice back into nuggets (old flight attendant trick) and it is just as good as the stuff coming directly from this ice maker.

review_text:
I bought this machine a little less than 3 months ago. I didn't read the reviews until AFTER I bought it. I got super nervous because I read several talking about it making a big noise within a month of getting it. Here's what I figured out.

A)DOES NOT COME WITH A FILTER. YOU MUST BUY YOUR OWN. I assume alot of the noise issues were caused by 1 of 2 things. Not putting a filter, and using with hard or hard like water or letting water reserve run dry.

2) It consumes lots of water. LOTS. Buy the extra tank. We go through 2 gallons of water a day with ours.

3) the ice is PERFECT.

4) Cleaning it is super easy

5) I repeat the points about making sure you get a filter and monitor the water level.

There is a nifty app that let's the machine "talk" to you. It tells you what it needs.

I've had no issues whatsoever with this machine. I keep it in the drink room (a converted game/drink room in the garage. The instructions specified not to install it next to a microwave or stove top. This is for heat issues. The machine can get hot, so keep it in a cooler place. Otherwise, I recommend this machine.
