These units require constant, scheduled cleaning. You have to take the tank off, drain the machine into a sink, fill it with bleach and water, run a cleaning cycle a few times and then do a number of rinse sessions. This machine is VERY sensitive to scale and any other contaminates.

After a lot of research, this was the only maker that met my needs. Another caveat is that it sometimes thinks it's out of water. Gotta mess with the tank and lines for 15 seconds to "kick it". Minor and infrequent occurrence. If you can swallow the steep price, I highly recommend this machine.

product_title: GE Profile Opal 2.0 | Countertop Nugget Ice Maker with Side Tank | Ice Machine with WiFi Connectivity | Smart Home Kitchen Essentials | Black Stainless
review_text:
So, I’ve been looking at nugget ice makers for a while. They’re pricey, though, so I wanted to make sure it was worth it. I’ll start by saying that I’m basing my review on the experience with this product but also my experience with another ice maker we have and use regularly. The first thing is that I expected this to be sort of “plug & play.” It’s not. It’s not really difficult but it’s not quick. I also feel that the directions were somewhat lacking and a few things could have been explained more clearly. You have to run a few cycles to clean the machine, so know that going in because it keys some time. Also, it’s a pretty large machine so it takes up some counter real estate for sure.

When you get to the point of making ice, you can fill the reservoir on the side but it’s not necessary. You don’t even need it, really. You can make ice without it by filling the compartment under the ice bin. The directions do not clearly state this, but I guess they think you’ll infer based on the photos. The next thing that’s a little weird but apparently not a big deal, is that before the ice starts making, water drips int the ice bin. I wiped the water out as soon as a few pieces of ice fell because I didn’t want the nuggets to stick together. I think this is a poor design and makes no sense. It does take a while to make a full bin of ice. The booklet says it will start making ice in about 20 minutes, which is true, however, it takes about an hour to get a full bin. I dumped the bin when it was full and out the ice in the freezer. It immediately started another cycle, which was nice. There’s a light on it, which is nice. I have not set up the Wi-Fi yet. While it is a bit louder than our other ice maker, it’s not disturbing, it’s about as loud as the microwave when it’s running. We have an open floor plan with the kitchen and living room in close proximity and it didn’t interfere with watching tv at all nor did it wake us up at night.

The cons are that it’s a bit large, but I don’t think that outweighs the benefits, unless you have a small kitchen or no counter space. Compared to our other, far less expensive ice maker that we use in our camper, it takes longer to make ice but I don’t really think that’s a very big deal and it’s a fair trade for the good ice. The water dripping in the bin is just poor design, but I think it’s necessary because of the the way the machine works. The biggest issue with the water dripping is that it does cause the nuggets to stick together. The biggest issue I see with this particular machine is that the bin is not refrigerated so the ice starts melting quickly. It causes the ice to stick together. If you don’t freeze it pretty quickly it ends up as kind of a block of nuggets, which defeats the purpose.the water from the ice melt in the bin does run back down into the reservoir but not fast enough to prevent the ice from sticking together. That’s really the biggest flaw I see with this machine. Our less expensive ice maker does hold the ice in the bin and keep it cold and as you scoop it out it makes more so I expected similar from a high end machine like this. I would still recommend this machine but I’m not sure that at this price point I would make the purchase again. I’m still deciding on that point. I’m not disappoint in the machine at all, though I do think there are minor improvements that could be made that would make it a 5 star product.
